If Hamlet were silenced, and Claudius and his court were presented in some other plot, the audience would suspend disbelief in the actions on the stage as willingly as it does for Macbeth or The Merchant of Venice. Drama relies on the idea that events and characters are as they appear; otherwise they would carry no emotional power.)

然而，从紫式部夫人开始，每一位小说家最基本的信念都是：事物并非如表面所见；这种信念可以根据小说家自身的感知进行补充或修正。当然，诗人和剧作家也经常表达同样的信念，但小说家必须表达这种信念，因为叙事视角本身就凸显了个人想法与周围人想法之间的对比。那些深受“表象具有欺骗性”以及“自己知道真相”这种感受所驱使的文学艺术家，正是出于这个原因而被小说所吸引。 （相比之下，如果我们考察戏剧《哈姆雷特》，哈姆雷特经常断言丹麦的真相并非表面所见。他指的是克劳狄斯的罪行及其随后的掩盖。他的这一前提也通过诗歌以象征性的方式加以阐述，但他之所以如此频繁地表达自己的观点，原因之一在于戏剧的表象对观众而言存在着与之相反的现实。如果哈姆雷特保持沉默，而克劳狄斯及其朝臣出现在其他剧情中，观众也会像观看《麦克白》或《威尼斯商人》那样，心甘情愿地接受舞台上的情节。戏剧依赖于事件和人物表象的真实性这一理念；否则，它们便无法承载任何情感力量。）

Eighteenth-century English novelists frequently wrote about a plucky or bold or lucky protagonist successfully making his way against a tide of privilege, criminality, and circumstances. At the least, such novels required the conviction that these outcast individuals were worthy of attention; they also required the conviction that their eventual triumph was possible and plausible. The Princess of Cléves , by Madame de La Fayette, illustrates the conviction that women have complex inner lives worthy of analysis. The Tale of Genji , by Murasaki Shikibu, is imbued with the Buddhist ideas current in tenth- and eleventh-century Japan, and expressly imparts them as motives for the characters and as ways of analyzing the meaning of their lives. Sir Walter Scott's The Tale of Old Mortality delineates the ways different forms of religious belief create different personality structures, and how these, in turn, shaped Scottish history. Yukio Mishima's novel The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea is motivated by a different set of convictions about the nature of childhood than is Little Women.

十八世纪的英国小说家经常描写勇敢、大胆或幸运的主人公，他们成功地对抗特权、犯罪和环境的重重阻碍。这类小说至少需要读者相信这些被排斥在外的人物值得关注；也需要读者相信他们最终的胜利是可能且合情合理的。拉法耶特夫人的《克莱沃公主》体现了这样一种信念：女性拥有复杂而值得分析的内心世界。紫式部的《源氏物语》充满了十至十一世纪日本盛行的佛教思想，并明确地将其作为人物的动机以及分析其人生意义的方式。沃尔特·斯科特爵士的《旧日之死》则描绘了不同形式的宗教信仰如何塑造不同的人格结构，以及这些结构反过来又如何影响了苏格兰历史。三岛由纪夫的小说《海贼王》与《小妇人》有着不同的关于童年本质的信念。

Egotistical or self-aggrandizing convictions fuel the novel-writing enterprise as readily as more altruistic ones do. All convictions go back to the novelist's early sense that his inner life is as real and interesting as his circumstances, that his view of things is as valid as the opinions of those around him. His first feeling of conviction might only be that he has to combat external pressure to conform. Writing powerfully embodies and develops the will to survive. The Czech novelist Arnost Lustig was eighteen and had lived in three concentration camps when he escaped from a train heading to Dachau and joined the Czech resistance. His many novels about the Holocaust assert not only his characters’ will to survive, but also his own. The ways in which Rebecca West's economically and socially insecure Edwardian childhood molded her ambition and will are vividly evoked in her wonderful novel The Fountain Overflows.

自我中心或自负的信念，与利他主义的信念一样，都能轻易地推动小说创作。所有这些信念都源于小说家早期的感受：他的内心世界与他所处的环境一样真实而有趣，他对事物的看法与周围人的意见一样有效。他最初的信念或许仅仅是，他必须对抗来自外界的顺从压力。写作有力地体现并发展了生存的意志。捷克小说家阿诺斯特·卢斯蒂格十八岁时，曾辗转于三个集中营，他从一列开往达豪的火车上逃脱，加入了捷克抵抗组织。他创作的许多关于大屠杀的小说，不仅展现了笔下人物的生存意志，也展现了他自身的生存意志。丽贝卡·韦斯特在爱德华时代经济和社会地位低下的童年经历，在她精彩的小说《喷泉涌流》中得到了生动的描绘，塑造了她的抱负和意志。

But convictions change. The paradox of a career of novels is that theories are found wanting, specific convictions dissipate, the novelist comes to see things in a different way. Tolstoy's convictions about marriage when he was writing Anna Karenina were different from those he held when he was writing The Kreutzer Sonata. A novelist can write a string of novels only if he or she is ready to embrace new ideas with as much conviction as he or she embraced earlier ideas. If the conviction simply dissipates or grows stale, the novels do, too. Some novelists have only one real conviction, which they express effectively a few times before the quality of their work declines. Perhaps F. Scott Fitzgerald would be an example of this. In general, the broader a novelist's interests and sympathies, the longer he can pursue his vocation. Great novelists have plenty of convictions. Later novels may contradict earlier ones—when Boccaccio wrote The Decameron he dedicated it to the pleasure of women; late in life he wrote another work that was virulently misogynistic. The theories that change motivate the novelist's ability to do the work because the novelist seizes new theories and ideas with the same enthusiasm every time. He may be consistent only in the passion with which he takes up new theories and applies them. Fortunately, the essential conviction that things are not as they appear is one that almost any novelist can harbor for his or her entire life without fear of contradiction.

但信念会改变。小说创作生涯的悖论在于，理论会逐渐被证明是不够的，特定的信念会消散，小说家会以不同的视角看待事物。托尔斯泰在创作《安娜·卡列尼娜》时对婚姻的看法，与他在创作《克莱采奏鸣曲》时的看法截然不同。只有当小说家能够像接受早期思想一样，以同样的信念接受新的思想时，他/她才能创作出一系列小说。如果信念消散或变得陈旧，小说也会随之衰落。有些小说家只有一个真正的信念，他们能有效地表达几次，之后作品的质量就会下降。菲茨杰拉德或许就是一个例子。总的来说，小说家的兴趣和同情心越广泛，他/她从事写作的时间就越长。伟大的小说家拥有丰富的信念。后期的小说可能与早期的作品相矛盾——薄伽丘创作《十日谈》时，将其献给女性的快乐；晚年，他又创作了一部充满恶毒厌女主义的作品。不断变化的理论激发了小说家的创作力，因为小说家每次都能以同样的热情拥抱新的理论和思想。他或许唯一不变的，就是他对新理论的热情和运用。幸运的是，几乎所有小说家都可以终其一生秉持“事物并非如表面所见”这一根本信念，而无需担心自相矛盾。

And every novelist operates with one other essential conviction: almost from the first moment a future novelist begins reading novels, he realizes that all novels are different from one another, and, much more obviously, different from all plays or all poems. This difference provides him with the conviction that he, too, could write a novel, and with the further conviction that as wonderful as many novels are, none of them is just right. In fact, none of them exactly fits his experience or his opinions or his ideas of form, so he comes up with a theory of the novel, at least a rudimentary one, and puts it to the test: he writes a novel. This conviction is the source of the originality that we prize as readers, when we delight in P. G. Wodehouse one day and in Honor de Balzac the next. As a relatively recent form (and not until more recently a respectable form), the novel allows the nascent novelist's theory an entry. And then, at least sometimes, the form itself changes as a result of the novelist's convictions.

每位小说家都秉持着另一个至关重要的信念：几乎从未来小说家开始阅读小说的那一刻起，他便意识到所有小说彼此不同，而且更明显地，与所有戏剧或诗歌都截然不同。这种差异让他相信自己也能写小说，并进一步让他相信，尽管许多小说都很精彩，但没有一部是完全符合他心意的。事实上，没有一部小说能完全契合他的经验、观点或形式理念，因此他提出了一套小说理论，至少是初步的理论，并将其付诸实践：他写小说。这种信念正是我们作为读者所珍视的原创性的源泉，让我们今天为P·G·伍德豪斯的作品而欣喜，明天又为奥诺·德·巴尔扎克的作品而着迷。作为一种相对较新的文体（而且直到最近才成为一种受人尊敬的文体），小说为初露锋芒的小说家的理论提供了切入点。然后，至少在某些情况下，小说家的信念也会促使小说本身发生改变。

For some years—twenty or thirty at most—the novelist as a living person coexists with the novelist as a literary persona. Inevitably this coexistence is uncomfortable, and some novelists bear it better than others. The requirements and responsibilities of the literary persona and the living person are different. The first truth about a literary persona is that it is equally the possession of the author and the reader; both create it and both respond to it, since it is made by the act of reading and remembering the novels. When readers are disappointed or angered by the living person of the author, it is because they sense a violation of their own creation. Writers who fail to realize that they have spawned another being, different from themselves but connected, are disappointed, too, or angered by the disappointments and demands of readers. In some cases, innate self-esteem and well-learned good manners go a long way to easing the boundary between the public self and the private self: Edith Wharton, for example, who was well schooled by social position to adopt roles that diverged from her personal preferences, showed unexcelled savoir faire throughout her career, all through the First World War, when she did charity work and war work in France, and in her relations with sometimes prickly colleagues, such as Henry James, who was envious of her commercial success. Other novelists, of course, have been legendary boors, which perhaps they would have been anyway.

在长达二三十年的时间内，小说家作为鲜活的个体与作为文学形象的个体并存。这种共存必然令人不安，有些小说家比其他人更能适应。文学形象和鲜活的个体所承担的要求和责任截然不同。关于文学形象，首先要明白，它既属于作者，也属于读者；两者共同创造，也共同回应，因为它是由阅读和记忆小说的行为塑造而成的。当读者对作者的鲜活个体感到失望或愤怒时，是因为他们感到自己的创作受到了侵犯。那些未能意识到自己创造了另一个与自身不同却又彼此关联的个体的作家，也会因读者的失望和要求而感到失望或愤怒。在某些情况下，与生俱来的自尊和后天习得的良好礼仪能够有效地模糊公众形象与私人形象之间的界限：例如，伊迪丝·华顿，她从小就受社会地位的熏陶，学会扮演与个人喜好相悖的角色，但她始终展现出无与伦比的处事之道，尤其是在第一次世界大战期间，她在法国从事慈善和战时工作，以及与一些有时性格古怪的同事相处时，例如嫉妒她商业成功的亨利·詹姆斯。当然，也有一些小说家以粗鲁无礼著称，或许即便没有这些特质，他们也难逃此劫。

But the novelist, too, has a relationship with his literary persona that might be somewhat different from his sense of his living self. The literary persona is a much revised and perfected being. It knows how life works and has a fairly complete theory of human behavior. It knows how to resolve conflicts and bring about appropriate endings. It is eloquent and fluent. It is consistent and logical. It partakes of the wisdom of all literature that goes before, but has the self-confidence to modify it slightly. It has good comic timing, if need be, and a marvelous sense of the appropriate. More than anything else, it is appealing, because a novel is never coercive and always works by seduction, so the literary persona, even if difficult and obscure, is a successful seducer. And when the novelist reads the works of his own literary persona, he must react to them—he has been conditioned to react to literature by years of reading, so he reacts. Some novelists always have doubts about the literary persona—does it say enough, know enough, or is it a pale shadow of what it might be? Other novelists are fully confident, and even fully realized, in the literary persona. Their difficulty is that they don't feel that they can personally live up to the excellences of the literary persona. While the marquis de Sade's literary persona is superhumanly energetic and brutal in his exploitation of women, for example, the marquis himself seems to have occasionally been a nice man—at any rate, he had a faithful woman friend for his entire life whom he does not seem to have exploited sexually in any way. Anthony Trollope, Jane Austen, and Ford Madox Ford apparently enjoyed and learned from their literary personae. When he read The Good Soldier ten years after writing it, Ford was as delighted as if it had been written by someone else; he called it “My auk's egg”—his once-in-a-lifetime masterpiece, so accomplished that even he didn't understand how he did it. Trollope and Austen seem to have written in narrative voices very close to their own natural modes of thinking and talking, which would mean that they actually were quite like they presented themselves.

但小说家与他笔下的文学形象之间的关系，或许与他对现实生活中的自我认知有所不同。文学形象是一个经过反复修改和完善的存在。它深谙生活之道，对人类行为有着相当完整的理论。它懂得如何化解冲突，如何安排恰当的结局。它文笔流畅，言辞铿锵有力。它逻辑严密，前后一致。它汲取了前人所有文学作品的智慧，并拥有足够的自信对其进行微调。必要时，它能把握住恰当的喜剧节奏，并且拥有敏锐的感知力。最重要的是，它极具吸引力，因为小说从不强迫读者，总是通过诱惑来达到目的，所以文学形象即便晦涩难懂，也依然是一位成功的诱惑者。当小说家阅读自己笔下文学形象的作品时，他必然会做出反应——多年的阅读已经让他养成了对文学作品做出反应的习惯，所以他会做出反应。有些小说家总是对文学人物形象有所怀疑——它是否表达得足够充分，认知足够深刻，还是仅仅是其真实面貌的苍白影子？另一些小说家则对文学人物形象充满信心，甚至认为它已臻于完美。他们的困境在于，他们觉得自己无法在现实生活中达到文学人物形象所展现的卓越境界。例如，萨德侯爵的文学人物形象精力充沛，对女性的剥削残忍至极，但侯爵本人似乎偶尔也展现出和善的一面——至少，他一生都有一位忠诚的女性朋友，而他似乎从未以任何方式对她进行性剥削。安东尼·特罗洛普、简·奥斯汀和福特·马多克斯·福特显然都从他们的文学人物形象中汲取了灵感并乐在其中。福特在创作《好兵》十年后重读此书时，欣喜若狂，仿佛这是别人写的；他称之为“我的海雀蛋”——他一生中唯一一部杰作，如此精妙绝伦，以至于连他自己都无法理解自己是如何创作出来的。特罗洛普和奥斯汀似乎都用非常接近他们自身自然思考和说话方式的叙事口吻进行写作，这意味着他们实际上和他们所展现的自己非常相似。

Novelists are fully capable of taking advice from their literary personae, at least some of it bad. I would make the case that F Scott Fitzgerald's bittersweetly tragic worldview, expressed in This Side of Paradise and The Beautiful and Damned , and then reconfirmed as he reread and rewrote and was praised for these same novels, dictated the tragic arc of his short life. Without the self-reinforcing loop of being seduced by his own literary assertions, he might have lived longer and produced more various work. When critics greeted Jude the Obscure with scathing rejection, Thomas Hardy shut down his novelist persona completely and went on as a poet, but in a different and more robust vein than he had written in as a novelist. It is hardly surprising that a novel that climaxes with a suicide and the murder of five children would end a career, whether reviewers liked it or not. In a different way, Choderlos de Laclos moved away from the calculating, libertine literary persona of Les Liaisons dangereuses , even though the novel was famous and successful. He spent most of his life as a happily married family man.

小说家完全有可能从他们文学形象中汲取灵感，即便其中一些是错误的。我认为，菲茨杰拉德在《人间天堂》和《美丽与毁灭》中展现的苦乐参半的悲剧世界观，以及他反复阅读、修改并因此获得赞誉后不断强化的这种世界观，最终决定了他短暂人生的悲剧轨迹。如果没有被自身文学主张所诱惑的自我强化循环，他或许会活得更久，创作出更多不同类型的作品。当评论家对《无名的裘德》的评价尖锐苛刻时，托马斯·哈代彻底放弃了小说家的身份，转而成为一名诗人，但他的诗歌风格与他作为小说家时截然不同，也更加雄浑有力。一部以自杀和五名儿童被杀为高潮的小说终结了一位作家的创作生涯，无论评论家是否喜欢它，这都不足为奇。肖德洛·德·拉克洛以另一种方式摆脱了《危险关系》中那个精于算计、放荡不羁的文学形象，尽管这部小说名利双收。他一生的大部分时间都过着幸福美满的家庭生活。

Literary personae aren't necessarily required to typify wisdom, reason, goodness, or even intelligence—some authors, such as Dostoevsky, take passion, radical innocence, holiness, or strong, honest emotion as ideals—but literary personae are required to observe coolly and in detail, since it is the details that progress the story and make it worth reading. This means that every literary persona is at least in some measure less subject to certain venal emotions, such as envy, resentment, feelings of martyrdom and victimization, embarrassment and shame, pettiness and irritability, than living authors are. Even when a narrator, in the apparent voice of the author, expresses such feelings, he is objectifying and observing them, holding them and himself up to the reader's scrutiny. The result of this is that every literary persona is more judicious than almost every author. Perhaps this difference is the source of the endless literary joke, depicted with great wit in John Updike's The Complete Henry Bech , about how small-minded authors are among themselves. They are no more small-minded, I would bet, than other living persons, but they are always more small-minded than their literary personae. In the Bech stories, Updike very cleverly gets to have it both ways—in so closely observing the shortcomings of his protagonist, Henry Bech, Updike gets to both claim them and distance himself from them. It is his narrative voice that simultaneously depicts Henry's sins (including murders of unsympathetic critics and reviewers) and forgives him for them. Updike succeeeds in gaining the reader as an ally—of course, John Updike would never do what Bech does—without so undermining Bech that the reader refuses to read about him.

文学人物并非必须代表智慧、理性、善良，甚至智力——有些作家，例如陀思妥耶夫斯基，将激情、纯真无邪、圣洁或强烈而真挚的情感视为理想——但文学人物必须冷静细致地观察，因为正是这些细节推动故事发展，使其具有阅读价值。这意味着，每个文学人物至少在某种程度上比在世的作家更少受某些庸俗情感的影响，例如嫉妒、怨恨、殉道者和受害者心态、尴尬和羞耻、斤斤计较和易怒。即使叙述者以作者的口吻表达这些情感，他也是在客观地观察和审视它们，并将它们以及他自己置于读者的审视之下。因此，每个文学人物都比几乎所有作家都更加审慎。或许正是这种差异，造就了文学界一个永无休止的笑话，约翰·厄普代克在《亨利·贝克全集》中对此进行了巧妙的描绘，即作家们彼此之间是多么的狭隘。我敢打赌，他们并不比现实生活中的人更狭隘，但他们总是比他们笔下的文学人物更加狭隘。在贝克的故事中，厄普代克非常巧妙地做到了两全其美——他细致入微地观察着主人公亨利·贝克的缺点，既承认了这些缺点，又与它们保持了距离。正是他的叙述声音，既描绘了亨利的罪行（包括谋杀那些不同情他的评论家和书评人），又原谅了他。厄普代克成功地赢得了读者的认同——当然，约翰·厄普代克绝不会像贝克那样行事——同时又没有过度贬低贝克，以至于读者拒绝阅读他的故事。

Literary personae bear the onus of the author's expectations, and not every literary persona performs as hoped. At the most basic level, not every literary persona gets great reviews and earns lots of money. Some literary personae coincide with the public taste quite nicely, others thrill the critics, and a few transform society, but almost none do all three. Some literary personae are quite complex and hard to understand, such as that of James Joyce. Some are saccharine or sentimental, such as that of Louisa May Alcott. Others are full of contradictions— D. H. Lawrence, for example, is by turns aggressive, salacious, lyrical, insightful, dopey, smart, and embittered. It is important to remember that the author has only limited control over this sort of complexity; his three inspirations—literature, language, and life—combine willy-nilly to create his literary persona, and they may combine in ways that do not at all mimic the way he leads his life or appears to his acquaintances. However, the living author must accept the limitations of his literary persona, and some authors do so more gracefully than others. Few are as lucky as George Eliot, who began life as a plain and deferential country girl and yet was able to educate herself in a way that allowed her to develop a literary persona that expressed such intelligence, compassion, wit, and range of emotion that she achieved considerable wealth as well as universal respect and acceptance in spite of her unorthodox liaison with George Henry Lewes.

文学人物承载着作者的期望，但并非每个文学人物都能如愿以偿。最基本的一点是，并非每个文学人物都能获得好评和丰厚的收入。有些文学人物与大众口味十分契合，有些令评论家为之倾倒，少数甚至改变了社会，但几乎没有人能同时做到这三点。有些文学人物相当复杂，难以理解，例如詹姆斯·乔伊斯。有些则甜腻或感伤，例如路易莎·梅·奥尔科特。还有一些充满矛盾——例如D·H·劳伦斯，他时而咄咄逼人，时而好色放荡，时而抒情，时而洞察力敏锐，时而愚钝，时而聪明睿智，时而愤世嫉俗。重要的是要记住，作者对这种复杂性的掌控力有限；他的三大灵感来源——文学、语言和生活——随意地融合，塑造了他的文学人物，而这三者的融合方式可能与他真实的生活方式或在熟人眼中的形象截然不同。然而，在世的作家必须接受其文学形象的局限性，有些作家比其他作家更能优雅地应对。乔治·艾略特堪称幸运，她出身平凡，是一位谦逊的乡村女孩，却凭借自学，塑造了一个才智过人、充满同情心、机智幽默且情感丰富的文学形象，最终获得了巨大的财富，并赢得了世人的尊重和认可，即便她与乔治·亨利·刘易斯的恋情并非寻常。

As the author gets older and publishes more work, his or her literary persona grows larger, stronger, and more out of control. It may begin to dictate to the author, to limit his freedom of subject and style, even to haunt him, in some sense, especially if earlier work bulks larger in the construction of the literary persona than later work. Readers and perhaps scholars come to know more about the author's work than he does—they might have read and reread a book very recently that the author hasn't read in twenty years, and hold him responsible for sentiments that he not only no longer feels, but can hardly remember. As the oeuvre grows larger and readers come to it differently—almost never, for example, reading the books in the sequence in which they were written—the literary persona takes on more and more layers, made up of more and more things that more and more people have said about it, and also of many things that the author himself might have said in passing to an interviewer, on the radio, or on TV. Many of these layers bear only a glancing relationship to the living author, who gradually diminishes in size relative to his literary persona. The literary persona is a verbal construct but it speaks with a human voice, and to those who don't actually know the author, it seems to be the author.

随着作者年龄增长，作品增多，其文学形象也愈发庞大、强势，甚至难以驾驭。这种形象可能会开始左右作者，限制其题材和风格的自由，甚至在某种程度上成为一种困扰，尤其当早期作品在构建文学形象中占据比后期作品更大的比重时更是如此。读者，或许还有学者，对作者作品的了解可能比作者本人还要深入——他们可能最近反复阅读了作者二十年前未曾翻阅的作品，并因此对作者的某些情感负责，而这些情感他不仅早已不再有，甚至几乎记不起来了。随着作品数量的增加，读者阅读作品的方式也发生了变化——例如，几乎没人会按照作品的出版顺序阅读——文学形象便呈现出越来越丰富的层次，不仅包含越来越多人对作品的评价，也包含作者本人在接受采访、广播或电视采访时可能无意间透露的诸多信息。这些层面中的许多层面与在世的作者只有一线之隔，作者本人相对于其文学形象而言逐渐黯然失色。文学形象是一种语言建构，但它却以人的声音说话，对于那些并不真正了解作者的人来说，它似乎就是作者本人。

The antidote for the discomforts inherent in such a situation is simple but not easy. The author keeps writing; keeps publishing, if possible; and keeps smiling for the audience and the camera. The more intently he or she focuses on the page being written rather than the career that is developing or disintegrating out there somewhere, the better the work and the happier the living person.

应对这种处境带来的不适感的良方很简单，但做起来却并不容易。作者应该坚持写作；如果可能的话，继续发表作品；并且始终保持微笑面对读者和镜头。他/她越是专注于正在书写的文字，而不是关注外界正在发展或衰落的职业生涯，作品就越好，生活也越幸福。

Eventually, inevitably, mortality decides the competition between the living author and the literary persona in favor of the literary persona, and year by year the living author recedes out of currency and out of memory. The documents and facts about his life get lost or cease to be understandable, and he, too, becomes only a literary construct, and now the construct belongs entirely to readers, plus maybe a biographer or a few scholars. This construct should never be mistaken for the formerly living person. The fact is that upon death, the living person is folded into his or her literary persona and is, for better or worse, beyond resurrection.

最终，死亡不可避免地决定了在世作者与文学形象之间的竞争，文学形象最终胜出。年复一年，在世作者逐渐淡出人们的视野，被人遗忘。关于他生平的文献和事实要么遗失，要么变得难以理解，他本人也沦为一种文学建构，而这种建构完全属于读者，或许还有传记作家或少数学者。这种建构绝不能与曾经鲜活的作者混淆。事实上，一旦死亡，在世的作者便融入了其文学形象之中，无论好坏，都无法复活。

# ↩

4. The Origins of the Novel

4. 小说的起源

F rom our promontory atop Earth's big bookstore, the history of the novel looks, of course, much different from the way it looked to those who made it. Some novelists and their novels dominate the landscape—Charles Dickens and David Copperfield , Marcel Proust and In Search of Lost Time , Lady Murasaki and The Tale of Genji. Others are fallen monuments—Johann Wolfgang von Goethe and The Sorrows of Young Werther , for example. Some novelists can be made out with low-powered binoculars—Balzac, Laurence Sterne. Some who once freely populated the landscape seem to have gone completely underground—Madame de Scudry and her fellow romancers, or Ouida and Edna Ferber, popular writers of the mid-twentieth century, or “the horde of scribbling women” who so tormented Nathaniel Hawthorne. Every novel that now strikes us as original itself originated in a social and artistic network of some sort, because the canon is always being made, remade, and expanded by novelists themselves out of the present stock of available books. Henry Fielding and other eighteenth-century novelists loved Don Quixote. Charles Dickens loved Henry Fielding, Tobias Smollett, and Sir Walter Scott, as well as The Tales of the Arabian Nights. Dickens was so influential that later writers shaped their writing in imitation of (or in contrast to) his, and imbibed what he learned from his models secondhand (as well as firsthand if they, too, were fond of his favorite authors). Henry James, who was a young man when Dickens was at the end of his career, gave Our Mutual Friend a bad review. He disdained what he saw as the formlessness of the older man's master-works. When James had become “the Master,” Virginia Woolf was making up her mind about what constituted the best models—she not only revived interest in Jane Austen and George Eliot by writing about them favorably, she also learned things from them. And any woman writing novels in English today has read Virginia Woolf and, no doubt, taken her essay A Room of One's Own much to heart. The tradition of the novel is a living legacy from older authors to younger ones. An author may go out of favor, and even seem to disappear, and then be revived simply by the regard of an influential figure who gets others interested in him or her (a novelist also can kill an ancestor, as Mark Twain killed James Fenimore Cooper). Readers are almost always partisan to some obscure author or another, and so, as long as a book is available in Earth's big bookstore (which I construe as every bookstore and every used-book store and every library in the world), it has a chance of finding a new audience.

从我们这高高在上、俯瞰地球这座巨大书店的视角来看，小说史的面貌当然与那些创作者眼中的截然不同。有些小说家及其作品占据了历史的主导地位——查尔斯·狄更斯和《大卫·科波菲尔》，马塞尔·普鲁斯特和《追忆似水年华》，紫式部和《源氏物语》。另一些则如同陨落的丰碑——例如约翰·沃尔夫冈·冯·歌德和《少年维特的烦恼》。有些小说家只需用低倍望远镜就能辨认——巴尔扎克，劳伦斯·斯特恩。还有一些曾经活跃于文坛的作家似乎已经彻底销声匿迹——斯库德里夫人和她的浪漫主义作家同伴们，或是二十世纪中期的畅销作家欧伊达和埃德娜·费伯，又或是令纳撒尼尔·霍桑苦不堪言的“一群笔耕不辍的女性作家”。如今每一部让我们觉得原创的小说，其创作都源于某种社会和艺术网络，因为经典作品总是由小说家们从现有的书籍中不断创造、重塑和拓展的。亨利·菲尔丁和其他十八世纪的小说家都喜爱《堂吉诃德》。查尔斯·狄更斯喜爱亨利·菲尔丁、托比亚斯·斯莫利特和沃尔特·斯科特爵士，以及《一千零一夜》。狄更斯的影响力如此之大，以至于后来的作家们模仿（或反其道而行之）他的写作风格，并间接地吸收他从其前辈那里学到的东西（如果他们也喜爱他所推崇的作家，那么他们也会直接吸收）。亨利·詹姆斯在狄更斯创作生涯末期时还很年轻，他曾对《我们共同的朋友》给予差评。他鄙视这位老作家在其杰作中所展现出的不成形。当詹姆斯成为“大师”时，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫正在思考何为最佳典范——她不仅通过撰写赞扬简·奥斯汀和乔治·艾略特的文章，重新唤起了人们对他们的兴趣，而且还从他们身上汲取了灵感。如今，任何一位用英语创作小说的女性作家都读过弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的作品，并且无疑都对她的散文《一间自己的房间》深有感触。小说传统是老一辈作家传承给年轻一代的鲜活遗产。一位作家可能会失宠，甚至销声匿迹，但仅仅因为一位有影响力的人物的赏识，就能让其他人重新关注他/她（小说家也可以“扼杀”前辈，就像马克·吐温扼杀了詹姆斯·费尼莫尔·库珀一样）。读者几乎总会偏爱某些默默无闻的作家，因此，只要一本书能在地球上最大的书店（我指的是世界上的每一家书店、每一家二手书店和每一家图书馆）里找到，它就有机会找到新的读者。

It is not what various academic schools consider to be the great tradition that creates the canon, but what novelists themselves read and carry forward when they write. From the point of view of the working novelist, the history of the novel is just this: plenty of models to learn from and enjoy.

并非各学术流派所认定的伟大传统造就了经典，而是小说家们在写作时阅读并借鉴的作品。从小说家的角度来看，小说史正是如此：提供了大量可供学习和欣赏的范例。

Although the novel was invented several times—most notably in 1004 by Murasaki Shikibu in what later became Kyoto, Japan, and once again in the thirteenth century in Iceland, in the form of the Icelandic saga—the modern novel is usually considered to have originated with Don Quixote. Like later novels, though, Don Quixote grew directly out of earlier works, and I think it is productive to look for beginnings of the modern novel right where we look for the beginnings of the modern period, and that is in Florence during the Black Death of 1347 – 51 . As everyone knows, the great plague of the middle of the fourteenth century devastated and transformed Europe, killing between a third and a half of the population of most areas. According to historians, some regions, especially in Scandinavia and eastern Europe, did not recover their pre-plague numbers until the middle of the nineteenth century. Florence, a bustling commercial center, was hard hit. A city of over a hundred thousand, large by standards of the time, Florence lost between two-thirds and three-quarters of its inhabitants to the pandemic. Florence was the home of Giovanni Boccaccio, born in 1313 , author of many works, including The Decameron , a cycle of a hundred stories supposedly told by a group of ten young people over the course of ten days in a luxurious retreat from the horrors of Florence (the characters actually stay out of Florence for fourteen days, but religious duties forbade entertainment on Fridays and Saturdays). Boccaccio called his work a commedia , which in the parlance of the time meant “any play or narrative poem in which the main characters manage to avert an impending disaster and have a happy ending.”

尽管小说曾多次出现——最著名的是1004年紫式部在日本京都（今京都）的创作，以及13世纪冰岛的冰岛萨迦——但现代小说通常被认为起源于《堂吉诃德》。然而，与后来的小说一样，《堂吉诃德》也直接源于早期作品。我认为，探寻现代小说的起源，就如同探寻现代时期的起源一样，是颇具启发意义的，而现代时期的起源正是1347年至1351年黑死病肆虐期间的佛罗伦萨。众所周知，14世纪中叶的这场大瘟疫摧毁并改变了欧洲，导致大多数地区三分之一到一半的人口丧生。据历史学家记载，一些地区，特别是斯堪的纳维亚半岛和东欧，直到19世纪中叶才恢复到瘟疫前的水平。佛罗伦萨作为繁华的商业中心，也遭受了重创。佛罗伦萨是一座拥有十多万人口的城市，在当时算是大城市，但疫情期间，城内三分之二到四分之三的居民都死于这场瘟疫。佛罗伦萨是乔万尼·薄伽丘的故乡，他生于1313年，创作了许多作品，其中包括《十日谈》。这部作品由一百个故事组成，讲述的是十个年轻人为了躲避佛罗伦萨的种种恐怖，在一处豪华的避世之所里，用十天的时间讲述这些故事（实际上，这些人物在佛罗伦萨之外待了十四天，因为宗教习俗禁止他们在周五和周六进行娱乐活动）。薄伽丘称他的作品为喜剧，在当时的语境中，“喜剧”指的是“任何戏剧或叙事诗，其中的主角设法化解了即将到来的灾难，并最终获得圆满的结局”。

∗ L. Kip Wheeler, “Literary Terms and Definitions, Comedy,” http://web.cn.edu/kwheeler/lit_terms_C.html .

∗ L. Kip Wheeler，“文学术语和定义，喜剧”，http://web.cn.edu/kwheeler/lit_terms_C.html。

Boccaccio, thirty-five, was already a noted man of letters with several works to his credit when he set to work upon The Decameron. He was not especially happy in Florence, having been obliged to return from the elegant and learned court of Naples in 1341 to a town we might liken to Dallas as opposed to New York City—a town of money, commerce, and philistinism, where Boccaccio's literary and scholarly predilections didn't quite fit in. Before the onset of the Black Death, Florence was already in turmoil—in 1345 , two of the great Florentine banking houses collapsed when Edward III of England reneged on his loans, throwing the city into a financial panic. Boccaccio had to scout about for patronage, and he went looking in Ravenna, where Dante, a particular idol of his, had died in 1321 .

薄伽丘三十五岁时，已是颇有名气的文人，著有多部作品，才开始创作《十日谈》。他并不十分喜欢佛罗伦萨，1341年，他被迫离开优雅博学的那不勒斯宫廷，回到这座更像是达拉斯而非纽约的城市——一个金钱、商业和庸俗之城，薄伽丘的文学和学术爱好在这里显得格格不入。在黑死病爆发之前，佛罗伦萨就已经陷入动荡——1345年，英格兰国王爱德华三世违约，导致佛罗伦萨两家大型银行倒闭，引发了全城的金融恐慌。薄伽丘不得不四处寻找赞助，他前往拉文纳，那里是他特别崇拜的但丁的故乡，但丁于1321年逝世。

In accordance with medieval convention, all of the strands of Boccaccio's work came from literary antecedents. Compilations of tales were a common form throughout the Middle Ages, and a look at only one of the books Boccaccio is thought to have been familiar with illustrates the multiple traditions he was heir to. The Panchatantra , written in India in Sanskrit before A.D. 500 , was probably familiar to Boccaccio through a Latin translation of about 1270 called Liber Kalilae et Dimnae , or the Directorium humanae vitae. The Latin version, by John of Capua, had been translated from Hebrew, which had in turn been translated in the eighth century from Arabic. Even Boccaccio's depiction of Florence in the grips of the plague, ostensibly a firsthand report, was probably borrowed from (or influenced by) an account of an eighth-century Florentine plague from the Historia Langobardorum by Paulus Diaconus (“History of the Lombards” by Paul the Deacon).

按照中世纪的惯例，薄伽丘作品中的所有元素都源于文学先例。故事集在中世纪十分常见，仅从薄伽丘被认为熟悉的众多书籍中选取一本，便可看出他继承了多种文学传统。《五卷书》（Panchatantra）于公元500年之前在印度用梵文写成，薄伽丘很可能是通过约1270年出版的拉丁文译本《卡利莱与迪姆纳之书》（Liber Kalilae et Dimnae，又称《人类生活指南》Directorium humanae vitae）而了解的。该拉丁文译本由卡普阿的约翰（John of Capua）从希伯来文翻译而来，而希伯来文则在八世纪从阿拉伯文翻译而来。即使是薄伽丘对佛罗伦萨遭受瘟疫肆虐的描绘，表面上是第一手报道，也可能是借鉴（或受到）保罗·迪亚科努斯（Paulus Diaconus）的《伦巴第人史》（Historia Langobardorum）中关于八世纪佛罗伦萨瘟疫的记载。

But the importance of The Decameron as an antecedent of the novel is that it owes as much to Boccaccio's observations of the world all about him, the present life of Florence in 1348 , as it does to its literary sources—he took the old material and worked it in the fire of current events. Florence in the mid-fourteenth century was a unique and not quite medieval city, where the merchant and banking classes were immensely powerful, where citizens experienced what you might call a modern degree of stimulation and change. As a result, The Decameron bears many of the hallmarks of the modern novel—moral relativity, everyday concerns, and uneasiness about, on the one hand, money, and on the other hand, God. It has celebrity named characters in several stories and average Joes (and Josefinas) in other stories. It observes contemporary manners and ideas. The frame provided by the overt depiction of the plague while it is happening provides a solemn and even urgent undertone to the humorous antics of the tales and the sensuous details of the setting. Some of these characters may soon be overtaken by the general disaster, portrayed by Boccaccio as a moral horror as well as a mortal one; the tales they tell of mutability, of jokes and tricks and miracles, prepare them for their fates as well as distract them.

但《十日谈》作为小说先驱的重要性在于，它不仅得益于薄伽丘对周遭世界、1348年佛罗伦萨当下生活的观察，也得益于其文学渊源——他汲取了古老的素材，并将其融入到当时的社会现实之中。十四世纪中叶的佛罗伦萨是一座独特且不完全属于中世纪的城市，商人和银行家阶层势力庞大，市民们经历了堪称现代的刺激和变革。因此，《十日谈》具备现代小说的诸多特征——道德相对主义、日常琐事，以及对金钱和上帝的矛盾不安。书中既有名人故事中的人物，也有普通人（以及约瑟芬娜）。它反映了当时的社会风俗和思想观念。瘟疫肆虐的直接描绘，为故事中滑稽的情节和感官化的场景细节增添了一丝庄严肃穆甚至紧迫的氛围。这些人物中的一些人或许很快就会被这场灾难吞噬，薄伽丘将这场灾难描绘成一场道德上的恐怖，而不仅仅是一场生死之灾；他们讲述的关于世事无常、玩笑、诡计和奇迹的故事，既让他们为即将到来的命运做好准备，也让他们暂时忘却烦恼。

The Decameron , not often read today, is conventionally considered a compilation of erotic tales, but it is far richer than convention implies. Even though many of the plots turn on desire, seduction, and adultery, what makes them interesting and diverse is how the protagonists achieve their ends, and the ramifications of their actions among their friends and associates. The theme of desire is the ground color of the carpet, but ingenuity and idiosyncrasy form the pattern. Some of the tales are quite simple. In the ninth story of the fifth day, for example, a young aristocrat spends all his money futilely pursuing a young woman, who marries another. Now broke except for one cherished possession, an excellent hawk, he moves to a small farm in the countryside. Soon the woman's husband dies, and she and their son move to a large estate that happens to be near the small farm of her former suitor. The child yearns to possess the hawk, and then falls ill. When the woman goes to the protagonist to ask for the hawk, he wants to be hospitable, so he kills the hawk, plucks it, and roasts it for her meal.

《十日谈》如今已鲜有人读，通常被认为是情色故事集，但它的内涵远比人们通常认为的丰富得多。尽管许多故事都围绕着欲望、诱惑和婚外情展开，但真正引人入胜、丰富多彩的是主人公们如何达成目的，以及他们的行为在朋友和同伴中引发的连锁反应。欲望是故事的底色，而巧妙的构思和独特的风格则构成了故事的图案。有些故事相当简单。例如，在第五天的第九个故事中，一位年轻的贵族挥霍无度地追求一位年轻女子，最终她嫁给了别人。如今他身无分文，只剩下一件珍爱的物品——一只优秀的猎鹰，于是搬到了乡下的一个小农场。不久，女子的丈夫去世，她带着儿子搬到了一座大庄园，而这座庄园恰好就在她前追求者的小农场附近。孩子渴望拥有那只猎鹰，之后便生病了。当女子去找主人公要鹰时，主人公想款待她，于是杀死了鹰，拔了它的毛，烤了它做成她的晚餐。

After they have eaten, she confesses that she has come to ask for the hawk, but alas. Nevertheless, the protagonist has demonstrated that even now he would do anything for his lady love. Soon enough the child dies—“whether from disappointment at not getting the hawk or from the mortal nature of his illness no one knew”—and soon after that, the mother tells her brothers that she would like to marry her poor neighbor. They consent, and all of the protagonist's desires are realized.

饭后，她坦白说自己是来求取那只鹰的，可惜未能如愿。尽管如此，主人公已经表明，即使到了现在，他仍然愿意为心爱的姑娘付出一切。不久，孩子夭折了——“究竟是因为没能得到鹰而失望，还是因为疾病本身不治身亡，无人知晓”——之后不久，母亲告诉她的兄弟们，她想嫁给贫穷的邻居。他们同意了，主人公的所有愿望都得以实现。

Other stories are little more than jokes or tricks. In the fourth tale of the seventh day, for example, a man locks his wife out of the house. She pretends to throw herself down the well, and when he comes running out, she sneaks into the house and locks him out. She then berates him in front of the neighbors, who call in her brothers, who beat the husband. After they are reconciled, he promises not to be jealous, and to let her do as she pleases, as long as she does it discreetly. In another tale, three men embarrass an elderly and unpleasant judge by pulling his pants down in court.

其他一些故事不过是些玩笑或恶作剧。例如，在第七天的第四个故事里，一个男人把妻子锁在门外。妻子假装跳井自尽，等他跑出来后，她偷偷溜进屋里，又把他锁在外面。然后，她在邻居面前斥责丈夫，邻居们叫来了她的兄弟，兄弟们狠狠地揍了丈夫一顿。夫妻和好后，丈夫答应不再嫉妒，只要妻子行事低调，就让她随心所欲。在另一个故事里，三个男人在法庭上扒下一位年迈而令人不快的法官的裤子，让他颜面尽失。

In one very famous tale (fifth day, fourth tale), a girl who wants to entertain her lover persuades her father that she wants to sleep outside on the balcony because it is stuffy indoors, and also she wants to hear the nightingale sing. He agrees with some reluctance, then locks the balcony doors and draws the curtain. She receives her lover, who climbs the vegetation to get to her. They make love so many times (“causing the nightingale to sing at frequent intervals,” writes Boccaccio) that they fall into a sound sleep, and when morning comes, the father unlocks the doors and discovers them. He is enraged, and threatens to kill the lover, but is reconciled when the girl and the lover agree to marry on the spot. Boccaccio uses the figure of the nightingale several more times to indicate the joyous lovemaking between the girl and her lover. The tale uses many joke-type conventions—the daughter's attempt to deceive her jealous father, the happy ending, the mother's coolness in contrast to the father's rage, and wordplay. The effect of the story turns not on character but on plot and phrasing. And it is meant to raise a laugh, which it does—in the prologue to the next tale, the narrator reports, “all the ladies laughed so much that it was some time after Filostrato had finished before they had managed to contain their mirth.”

在一个非常著名的故事（第五天，第四个故事）中，一个女孩为了款待她的情人，说服父亲她想睡在阳台上，因为室内太闷，而且她也想听夜莺歌唱。父亲勉强同意了，然后锁上阳台的门，拉上窗帘。女孩迎接了她的情人，他爬上植物来到她身边。他们多次交欢（薄伽丘写道，“夜莺不时地歌唱”），直到沉沉睡去。第二天早上，父亲打开门，发现了他们。他勃然大怒，威胁要杀死情人，但当女孩和情人当场同意结婚时，他才消气。薄伽丘在故事中多次使用夜莺的意象，来象征女孩和情人之间欢愉的性爱。这个故事运用了许多笑话的惯用手法——女儿试图欺骗嫉妒的父亲、皆大欢喜的结局、母亲的冷静与父亲的愤怒形成鲜明对比，以及文字游戏。故事的效果不在于人物塑造，而在于情节和措辞。它的目的是博君一笑，而它也确实做到了——在下一个故事的序言中，叙述者写道：“女士们笑得前仰后合，菲洛斯特拉托讲完故事后过了好一会儿，她们才勉强止住了笑声。”

The sixth story of the ninth day also has wordplay, and a punch line, but it shades rather more toward a story, since it concerns the unexpected transformation of one of the characters. In this case, a young man who loves a young woman persuades a friend of his to help him sneak into the family home, where there is but a single bedroom with three beds and a cradle. When everyone is asleep, the first young man creeps into the bed of his beloved. Soon afterward, though, the second young man goes out to relieve himself. While he is out, the wife wakes up at a sound in another part of the house and goes out naked to check things out. When the second young man returns, he bumps into the cradle and moves it, and when the wife returns, she is misled by the position of the cradle and gets into bed with the second young man, who, as Boccaccio writes, “gave her a cordial reception, and without a murmur, tacked hard to windward over and over again, much to her satisfaction.” The first young man is afraid to fall asleep and be discovered with the daughter, so he gets up to go back to his bed, but, also misled by the position of the cradle, he gets into bed with the father, and thinking he is with his friend, begins to express his delight in the charms of the girl. The father wakes up and threatens to kill the young man. At this point, the mother awakens and realizes she is in the wrong bed. She saves the day by sneaking into the bed of the daughter, then loudly proclaiming that she has been there all night and nothing has happened. The second young man then starts calling out to the first young man to wake up and stop bragging about doing things that he has only dreamed of. The father starts laughing, the first young man goes back to his bed, and the daughter later convinces the mother that nothing at all happened. “And thus the mother, who retained a vivid memory of Adriano's embraces, was left with the conviction that she alone had been awake on the night in question.” Her transformation, though slight, is real—she has enjoyed something illicit and used her wit and discretion to make sure that no ill consequences ensue. Boccaccio's telling gives the whole tale a joyful exuberance that relieves it of its potential for sin and conflict. A later telling, as “The Reeve's Tale,” in Geoffrey Chaucer's Canterbury Tales , exploits the dark side of the material, but Boccaccio's version reveals a great deal about not only his forgiving view of love and sexuality and his comic turn of mind, but also his graceful and efficient literary style. His choreography of what could be a confusing set of actions is clear and humorous, alternating essential details, such as when the cradle was moved and what people said, with homely nonessentials that give the story verisimilitude (the wife goes out of the room to investigate what the cat is doing). Both the women and both the young men are quick of wit, and the father is fooled, but genially so, in the interests of peace rather than exploitation.

第九天的第六个故事也运用了文字游戏和妙语，但它更偏向于一个完整的故事，因为它讲述的是一个人物意想不到的转变。故事中，一个爱上年轻女子的年轻人说服他的朋友帮他偷偷溜进女子的家中。那家只有一间卧室，里面放着三张床和一个摇篮。当所有人都睡着后，第一个年轻人悄悄地爬进了心上人的被窝。不久之后，第二个年轻人出去方便。他出去的时候，妻子被屋子另一边的动静吵醒，赤身裸体地出去查看。第二个年轻人回来时，不小心碰到了摇篮，把它挪动了一下。妻子回来后，被摇篮的位置误导，和第二个年轻人一起上了床。正如薄伽丘所写，第二个年轻人“热情地迎接了她，一声不吭地一次又一次地迎风而上，让她非常满意。”第一个年轻人害怕睡着后被发现和女儿在一起，于是起身想回自己的床上，但由于摇篮的位置让他误以为是朋友，便爬上了父亲的床。他开始赞美女儿的美貌，父亲醒来后威胁要杀了年轻人。这时，母亲醒了过来，意识到自己睡错了床。她偷偷溜进女儿的床，大声宣布自己整晚都在这里，什么也没发生，这才化解了危机。第二个年轻人开始叫醒第一个年轻人，让他别再吹嘘自己做了那些只存在于梦里的事。父亲哈哈大笑，第一个年轻人只好回到自己的床上。后来，女儿向母亲解释说什么都没发生。“就这样，母亲仍然清晰地记得阿德里亚诺的拥抱，她坚信那天晚上只有自己醒着。”她的转变虽微不足道，却是真实的——她曾享受过某种不正当的欢愉，并运用智慧和谨慎确保不会招致任何不良后果。薄伽丘的叙述赋予整个故事一种欢快奔放的气息，使其摆脱了罪恶和冲突的可能。后来，乔叟在《坎特伯雷故事集》中以《管家的故事》为题，挖掘了素材的阴暗面，但薄伽丘的版本不仅展现了他对爱情和性的宽容态度和幽默的思维方式，也体现了他优雅而精炼的文学风格。他以清晰而幽默的方式安排了原本可能令人困惑的情节，将诸如摇篮何时被移动、人们说了什么等关键细节与赋予故事真实感的日常琐事（例如妻子走出房间去查看猫在做什么）交替呈现。两位女士和两位年轻男士都机智过人，父亲虽然被愚弄了，但出于和平而非剥削的目的，他欣然接受了愚弄。

Another tale that Chaucer used (“The Clerk's Tale”) is Boccaccio's hundredth, the tale of the patient Griselda, whose husband puts her through one trial after another to test her obedience and her devotion. His motive for testing her so severely even over the objections of all his friends and relatives is that he wants to make sure she knows the proper duties of a wife. Hers for enduring is perhaps a tad more convincing—she is well aware of her humble origins, and she has never considered the goods she attained at marriage to be hers. There is some implication in the last lines that it is her lowly birth itself that endows Griselda with the fortitude to endure the faked deaths of her children, her apparent abandonment by her husband, and his evident remarriage to a much younger woman. Griselda's tale of goodness (which represents, as well, the proper Christian response to all of the apparently senseless blows life and fate afford) contrasts with tale number one, the tale of the wickedest man who ever lived, a man so wicked that he lies in his deathbed confession, and yet a man who, subsequent to his death, gains a reputation for sainthood and whose posthumous influence actually, according to the story, works for good. In these tales and others, Boccaccio explores complex themes of virtue, vice, salvation, psychological motivation, and forgiveness.

乔叟引用的另一个故事（《书记员的故事》）是薄伽丘的第一百则故事，讲述了坚忍的格里塞尔达的故事。她的丈夫为了考验她的顺从和忠诚，对她百般刁难。尽管亲朋好友都反对，他仍然不顾一切地严加考验她，目的是为了确保她明白妻子应尽的职责。格里塞尔达的忍耐或许更有说服力——她深知自己出身卑微，也从未认为婚后所得的财产属于自己。故事的最后几行暗示，正是她卑微的出身赋予了格里塞尔达坚韧的意志，使她能够忍受孩子被伪造的死亡、丈夫对她的抛弃以及他明显与一位年轻女子再婚的种种磨难。格里塞尔达的善良故事（同时也象征着基督徒面对生活和命运看似毫无意义的打击时应有的回应）与第一个故事形成鲜明对比。第一个故事讲述的是有史以来最邪恶的人，他邪恶到临终忏悔时都撒谎，然而死后却被尊为圣人，而且根据故事所述，他死后的影响实际上造福了世人。在这些故事以及其他作品中，薄伽丘探讨了美德、罪恶、救赎、心理动机和宽恕等复杂主题。

Boccaccio was well aware that he was doing something new—at the beginning of the fourth day, he intrudes to defend his work—both that it is written in vernacular prose and that it is written to appeal to women, not scholars. He defends it, paradoxically, as factually correct and as a natural thing for him to do, since he likes women—prose, that is, is meant to be pleasing and accessible. Artistically, though, the main thing Boccaccio had to guard against was the possibility that the stories would run together in the reader's mind and grow repetitious or jumbled. He used several organizational principles to avoid this, including thematic introductions, commentary by the storytellers, and juxtaposition of contrasting tales to one another, as well as a wide variety of settings and plots. But he also used what have become typical novelistic techniques—names, descriptions, quirks of behavior, and characteristic dialogue. His use of these things is so natural that it seems automatic to us, but in fact it sets The Decameron off from other medieval works, such as Le Roman de la rose and Le Morte d'Arthur , whose authors have little understanding of individual psychology. In those works, characters’ traits are emblems of their identities or roles rather than ways of being. When the emblem is removed, the character is no longer recognizable to the reader. Action exists in and of itself rather than as a result of psychology. By contrast, in every story of The Decameron , the plot grows out of the idiosyncratic nature of individual predilections or desires.

薄伽丘很清楚自己正在做一件新事——在第四天的开头，他便插话为自己的作品辩护，既强调作品是用白话散文写成的，也强调作品是写给女性而非学者的。他自相矛盾地辩称，作品在事实上是正确的，而且对他来说也是顺理成章的事，因为他喜欢女性——也就是说，散文的目的是为了取悦读者，让读者容易理解。然而，在艺术层面，薄伽丘最需要警惕的是故事在读者脑海中混淆，变得重复或混乱。他运用了多种组织原则来避免这种情况，包括主题引言、叙述者的评论、对比鲜明的故事并置，以及丰富多样的场景和情节。此外，他还运用了如今已成为典型小说技巧的元素——人名、描写、行为怪癖和特色对话。他对这些元素的运用如此自然，以至于在我们看来似乎是下意识的，但实际上，正是这一点使《十日谈》区别于其他中世纪作品，例如《玫瑰传奇》和《亚瑟之死》，后者的作者对个体心理知之甚少。在那些作品中，人物的特征是其身份或角色的象征，而非其存在方式。当这些象征被移除时，读者便无法辨认出人物。行动本身的存在，而非心理因素的结果。相比之下，《十日谈》中的每一个故事，情节都源于个体独特的偏好或欲望。

The Decameron became a famous masterpiece almost immediately and retained its allure for hundreds of years. One result of The Decameron's relative “philogyny” (compared with conventional views of women in the Middle Ages) was, for our purposes, the placing of women's concerns at the center of the European novel for the next six hundred years.

《十日谈》几乎立刻成为一部举世闻名的杰作，并在数百年间保持着其魅力。就我们的目的而言，《十日谈》相对“女性化”（与中世纪传统的女性观念相比）的一个结果是，在接下来的六百年里，女性的关注点成为了欧洲小说的核心。

The Decameron was the direct inspiration for Marguerite de Navarre's The Heptameron , the essential transitional work between the medieval story cycle and the modern novel. In many ways, the European novel as we know it today grew directly out of The Heptameron , which is even less well known to modern readers than The Decameron. Marguerite de Navarre was a queen, the older sister of Franois I, who became king of France in the early sixteenth century. Both Franois and Marguerite were exceptionally well educated—Marguerite spoke five or more languages, wrote both prose and poetry, and took an earnest interest in the religious controversies of the time; though a Catholic, she was in favor of Protestant-style reforms. In her early thirties, she was delegated to negotiate the ransom of Franois from the Spanish, who had captured him in battle. A few years later, she married Henri of Navarre (a small kingdom in the Pyrenees now known as Navarra, and part of Spain). Marguerite had a strong interest in literature, and commissioned a French translation of The Decameron , but more importantly, she wrote (or compiled) a set of tales intended to be a Decameron for the new age (the 1550s ). Who made up the tales, whether Marguerite herself or Marguerite and a set of friends, how far she got (all that remain are seventy-two tales, thus the naming of the compilation The Heptameron) , and how the concerns of the tales were to be resolved remain unknown to scholars, but Marguerite stated overtly that the premise of the taletelling was that the tales were all true and that they addressed a single question: is it possible for a woman to know true love and to remain virtuous? This question was to become the central question of most of the novels written in France—and, indeed, in the rest of Europe—until at least the early part of the twentieth century.

《十日谈》直接启发了玛格丽特·德·纳瓦拉创作《七日谈》，后者是中世纪故事集与现代小说之间重要的过渡作品。在许多方面，我们今天所知的欧洲小说都直接源于《七日谈》，而《七日谈》在现代读者中的知名度甚至比《十日谈》还要低。玛格丽特·德·纳瓦拉是一位王后，是弗朗索瓦一世的姐姐，弗朗索瓦一世于十六世纪初成为法国国王。弗朗索瓦和玛格丽特都受过良好的教育——玛格丽特精通五种以上的语言，能写散文和诗歌，并且对当时的宗教争论抱有浓厚的兴趣；尽管她信奉天主教，但她支持新教式的改革。三十岁出头时，她受命与西班牙人谈判，以赎回在战场上被俘的弗朗索瓦。几年后，她嫁给了纳瓦拉的亨利（纳瓦拉是比利牛斯山脉的一个小王国，如今被称为纳瓦拉，是西班牙的一部分）。玛格丽特对文学有着浓厚的兴趣，她委托人将《十日谈》翻译成法语。但更重要的是，她创作（或编纂）了一部故事集，意在成为新时代（16世纪50年代）的《十日谈》。这些故事究竟是谁创作的？是玛格丽特本人，还是她与一群朋友共同创作？她究竟完成了多少（现存的只有七十二个故事，因此这部作品集被命名为《七日谈》）？以及这些故事的主题最终是如何解决的？这些问题至今仍是学者们的谜团。但玛格丽特曾明确表示，这些故事的前提是它们都是真实的，并且都围绕着一个核心问题：女人能否在拥有真爱的同时保持贞洁？这个问题成为了法国乃至整个欧洲大多数小说的核心主题，至少一直延续到20世纪初。

Marguerite named her ten taletellers with clues to what seem to have been the names of members of her circle, including Henri, who appears as “Hircan.” Each tale is followed by a critique, where the tellers do not just react with pleasure, as they do in Boccaccio, but also discuss the characters’ actions and the moral implications of each tale. Far more explicitly than in The Decameron , in The Heptameron , the characters are concerned with the difficulties of salvation—there is no easy pleasure and ready forgiveness in Marguerite's book. Though Marguerite and her friends were Catholics, hers was a world where religious controversies were of major importance and where prevention of sin was all-important because redemption was felt to be problematic. All of Marguerite's characters, but especially her taletellers, were obliged to look within themselves.

玛格丽特为她的十位讲故事者取了名字，这些名字似乎暗示着她圈子里的成员，包括亨利，他以“希尔坎”的化名出现。每个故事之后都附有评论，讲故事者们的反应并非像薄伽丘笔下那样只是单纯地表达愉悦，而是会讨论人物的行为以及每个故事的道德寓意。与《十日谈》相比，《七日谈》中人物对救赎之难的关注更为明确——在玛格丽特的书中，没有唾手可得的快乐和轻易的宽恕。尽管玛格丽特和她的朋友们都是天主教徒，但她所处的世界却是一个宗教争论至关重要、预防罪恶至上的世界，因为人们普遍认为救赎本身就是一个难题。玛格丽特笔下的所有人物，尤其是她的讲故事者们，都必须进行自我反省。

By contrast to The Heptameron, The Decameron , even with all of its dark shadings, seems positively rollicking. Boccaccio may include cruel and misogynistic stories, undeserved cuckoldings, and episodes that modern readers find barbaric, but for the most part he seems to be in favor of and forgiving of the pleasures of coupling. For the characters of The Heptameron , though, life is full of hard lessons and double binds, even for the wealthy and privileged. The ten taletellers of The Decameron escape the plague in a pastoral paradise; the ten taletellers of The Heptameron are stuck in a primitive monastery in the midst of inhospitable and unscenic mountains that are filled with wild animals. The world itself is unforgiving, and human society is no less so. What is more troubling for the reader is that Marguerite's tales have so little variety. If The Decameron seems to be an inexhaustible treasury of narratives and characters, The Heptameron seems more like an obsessive nightmare, where the same characters stuck in the same dilemmas return over and over, though with different names and in different guises, to be investigated again and again for some bit of new insight that never turns up. This is fertile novelistic territory.

与《七日谈》相比，《十日谈》即便充斥着阴暗的色彩，也显得轻松愉快。薄伽丘或许在书中描写了残酷厌女的故事、无端的戴绿帽情节，以及一些在现代读者看来野蛮的场景，但他似乎总体上是赞同并宽容性爱之乐的。然而，对于《七日谈》中的人物而言，生活充满了艰难的教训和进退两难的困境，即使是那些富有特权的人也不例外。《十日谈》中的十位说书人躲过了瘟疫，来到了田园牧歌般的世外桃源；而《七日谈》中的十位说书人则被困在荒凉崎岖、野兽出没的山区深处一座原始的修道院里。世界本身就残酷无情，人类社会更是如此。更令读者感到困扰的是，玛格丽特的讲故事内容过于单调乏味。如果说《十日谈》是取之不尽的叙事和人物宝库，那么《七日谈》则更像是一场令人执着的噩梦，同样的人物困于同样的困境，一遍又一遍地出现，尽管他们的名字和伪装各不相同，人们却一遍又一遍地探究，试图从中获得某种新的启示，而这种启示却始终没有出现。这无疑是一片充满创作潜力的沃土。

The fortieth story is particularly striking in several ways. It concerns a man and a woman most of the taletellers know, the comte de Jossebelin and his beautiful sister, to whom the comte is very close. Although she is of a marriageable age and has many offers, he refuses to allow her to marry. She falls in love with his favorite gentleman-in-waiting; they marry, and live happily, though secretly, for several years. Their relationship is reported to the comte, who surprises them in bed. The husband escapes through the window, while the wife pleads her case—she is an adult woman and her husband is just the man the comte had always said he wished she could marry, and the two of them are married in the sight of God. They have never done anything unvirtuous. Nevertheless, the comte has the husband caught and killed on the spot, and then imprisons his sister in a remote castle, where she devotes herself to religion. The comte's six sons “all die miserably,” and his daughter inherits the estates. The ten critics try to work out some way of understanding the cruelty of the story. Hircan makes the case that the comte must put down the ambitions of the lower-caste servant, no matter what, but the others are more subtle.

第四十个故事在几个方面都格外引人注目。故事的主人公是约瑟贝林伯爵和他美丽的妹妹，这对男女在大多数说书人中都耳熟能详。伯爵与妹妹关系非常亲密。尽管妹妹已到适婚年龄，也收到许多求婚，伯爵却始终不肯让她出嫁。妹妹爱上了伯爵最宠爱的侍从，两人结为夫妻，秘密地过着幸福的生活，长达数年。后来，他们的关系被人告发给了伯爵，伯爵在床上撞见了他们。丈夫趁机从窗户逃走，妻子则苦苦哀求——她已是成年女子，而她的丈夫正是伯爵一直希望她嫁的那个人，而且他们已在上帝的见证下结为夫妻。他们从未做过任何不道德的事。然而，伯爵还是下令将丈夫当场处死，并将妹妹囚禁在一座偏僻的城堡里，让她在那里潜心修行。伯爵的六个儿子“都死得很惨”，他的女儿继承了遗产。十位评论家试图找出理解这个故事残酷之处的方法。希尔坎认为，无论如何，伯爵都必须压制低种姓仆人的野心，但其他评论家的观点则更为微妙。

Two of the women, including Oisille, an older woman who is the most religious, and often the conscience of the group, draw the typical virtuous lesson—every girl must mold her passions in obedience to her family obligations. Nomerfide, though, who doesn't offer an opinion about every story, suggests that the experience of true love and true pleasure compensates for death, because the one is rare while the other is routine. She says, “The pleasure, too, must have been rare, and all the greater, since it runs counter to the views expressed by all wise men, and has in its favor the fact that a loving heart found satisfaction and that a soul found true repose.” Others remark on the injustice of the comte's actions and contrast that to the nature of true love (“though her body was imprisoned, her heart was free and united with God and her husband”). They also point out the political implications of the story—”in order to maintain peace in the state, consideration [in matters of marriage] is given only to the rank of the family, the seniority of the individuals, and the provisions of the law, not to men's love and virtue, in order that the monarchy not be undermined.” Often practical sorts of arrangements lead to marital hell, proposes Dagoucin (who is possibly a priest and an abbot), but not always, agree the others, and the married members of the group then congratulate themselves on their luck and skill in gaining marriages that are loving, pleasurable, and virtuous—“So happy were they all that I think the married couples among them did not do quite so much sleeping as the rest— what with talking about their love in the past and demonstrating it in the present. Thus the night passed sweetly until morning broke” (p. 375 ).

两位女性，包括年纪稍长、最为虔诚，也常常是这群人良心的奥伊西尔，都从中汲取了典型的美德教训——每个女孩都必须约束自己的欲望，以服从家庭义务。然而，诺默菲德并非对每个故事都发表意见，她认为真爱和真快乐的体验可以弥补死亡的痛苦，因为前者难得，后者却司空见惯。她说：“快乐也必定十分珍贵，因为它与所有智者的观点相悖，而且它的好处在于，一颗充满爱的心得到了满足，一个灵魂得到了真正的安宁。”其他人则评论伯爵行为的不公，并将其与真爱的本质进行对比（“尽管她的身体被囚禁，但她的心却自由了，与上帝和她的丈夫合而为一”）。他们还指出了故事的政治含义——“为了维护国家和平，（婚姻）只考虑家族地位、个人资历和法律规定，而不考虑男人的爱情和德行，以免君主制受到动摇。”达古辛（他可能是一位神父兼修道院长）认为，务实的安排往往会导致婚姻的痛苦，但其他人也同意并非总是如此。于是，小组中已婚的成员们为自己能够获得充满爱、幸福美满且美德的婚姻而感到欣喜——“他们都非常幸福，我想他们中的已婚夫妇睡眠时间比其他人少得多——因为他们一直在谈论过去的爱情，并在当下展现爱情。就这样，夜晚甜蜜地过去了，直到黎明破晓”（第375页）。

Story thirty is as strange (and Oisille remarks that it is the strangest story she can imagine), but the taletellers agree more readily upon an interpretation. A woman has a teenage son who is making a play for a servant girl. The girl reports this, and the skeptical mother declares that she will sleep in the servant girl's bed to see if she is telling the truth. The son does appear, but the mother is still reluctant to believe that he means to do anything. She remains quiet, and then, once he begins making love to her, thinking she is the servant, “so fragile was her nature that her anger turned to pleasure…. Even as the dammed-up torrent flows more impetuously than the freely flowing stream, so it was with this lady, whose pride and honor had lain in the restraints she had imposed on her own body” (p. 318 ). The woman gets pregnant. She sends the son off to the Italian wars, gives birth, and sends the baby daughter to her brother, where she grows up. In the meantime, the wars end and the son wants to come home, but the mother is now afraid of her own feelings for him, so she tells him that he can't come home until he has married someone he loves. He visits his uncle, unknowingly meets his sister, falls in love with her, and brings her home as his wife. The mother confesses her sins and their consequences to an official, who gets advice from theologians, and everyone agrees that the woman can never tell the children what has happened, but must do penance for the rest of her life. Part of her penance is the sight she has every day of the love between the married couple— “never were a husband and wife so close. For she was his daughter, his sister, his wife. And he was her father, brother, and husband.”

第三个故事同样离奇（奥伊西尔评论说这是她能想象到的最离奇的故事），但讲述者们却更容易达成共识。故事讲述的是一位妇人有个十几岁的儿子，他正对一个女仆动手动脚。女仆把这件事告诉了她，心存疑虑的母亲却说她要睡在女仆的床上，看看她是否说的是真话。儿子果然出现了，但母亲仍然不愿相信他会有什么企图。她保持沉默，直到儿子开始与她亲热，误以为她是女仆时，“她天性如此脆弱，以至于怒气转为欢愉……正如被拦住的洪流比自由奔流的溪流更加奔腾不息，这位妇人也是如此，她曾经的骄傲和荣誉都建立在她对自己身体的束缚之上”（第318页）。妇人怀孕了。她把儿子送去意大利打仗，生下女儿后，又把女儿送到她哥哥那里抚养长大。与此同时，战争结束了，儿子想要回家，但母亲却害怕自己对他的感情，于是告诉他，除非娶到自己心爱的人，否则不能回家。儿子去拜访叔叔，无意中遇到了叔叔的妹妹，爱上了她，并把她带回家娶为妻。母亲向一位官员忏悔了自己的罪过及其后果，官员又咨询了神学家，最终大家一致认为，母亲永远不能告诉孩子们发生的一切，必须终生忏悔。她忏悔的一部分便是每天目睹这对夫妻的恩爱——“从来没有一对夫妻如此亲密。因为她既是他的女儿，又是他的妹妹，还是他的妻子。而他既是她的父亲，又是她的兄弟，又是她的丈夫。”

The woman's sin, all the taletellers agree, has had its origins in her prideful sense of her own virtue, and anyway, points out one of the women, “nothing should induce a woman to risk sharing a bed with a male relative…. It's not safe to set a naked flame near tinder” (p. 322 ). Interestingly enough, the conversation then turns to the ways in which Franciscan monks employ preaching virtue as a method of seduction, and then Hircan points out that the monks of their monastery have failed to ring the evening bell because they are hiding behind the hedge, listening to the salacious stories.

所有讲述故事的人都一致认为，这女人的罪过源于她对自身美德的骄傲自满。其中一位女人指出，“无论如何，女人都不应该冒险与男性亲属同床共枕……这就像在易燃物附近点燃明火一样危险”（第322页）。有趣的是，谈话随后转向了方济各会修士如何利用宣扬美德来诱惑女性，希尔坎接着指出，他们修道院的修士们因为躲在树篱后面偷听这些淫秽故事，所以没有敲响晚钟。

What Marguerite and her interlocutors are doing in The Heptameron is experimenting with realism and psychology, two essential characteristics of the novel. Whether or not the stories they tell are true, in their critiques, they treat them as if they were. They discuss motivation, social context, and states of mind before, during, and after the action. They situate even the most shocking events in a generally accepted moral context, and use both common sense and religious precepts as guides to interpretation. They also relate the stories to their own lives by reacting to them, allowing the stories to spark discussions of their own histories. Since they are friends, they do something else that friends often do, which is to call into question one another's interpretations by reminding one another of past mistakes or proclivities (though this is always done in a good-natured way and the group is never unfriendly). Because half of the group is women, and one of them is the queen (and another may be the queen's mother), the dilemmas and traps that confront women are taken very seriously. The ways in which women are agents of their own salvation and damnation are discussed in the context of the ways in which women are subject to the will of others. That women have erotic desires of their own is also a given. The opinions of the men do not take precedence, and the opinions of Hircan, the king (Henri was eleven years younger than Marguerite), are often politely overlooked, as if their crudity is to be expected.

在《七日谈》中，玛格丽特和她的对话者们正在探索现实主义和心理学，这是这部小说的两大核心特征。无论他们讲述的故事是否真实，在他们的评论中，他们都将其视为真实事件。他们探讨动机、社会背景以及事件发生前、发生中和发生后的心理状态。即使是最令人震惊的事件，他们也会将其置于普遍接受的道德框架中，并运用常识和宗教教义作为解读的指导。他们还会通过对故事的反应，将故事与自身生活联系起来，从而引发对自身经历的讨论。由于他们是朋友，他们还会做朋友之间常做的事：通过提醒彼此过去的错误或倾向来质疑对方的解读（尽管这种质疑总是以善意的方式进行，群体之间也从未出现不友好的氛围）。由于这群人中有一半是女性，其中一位是女王（另一位可能是女王的母亲），因此女性面临的困境和陷阱得到了非常严肃的探讨。探讨女性如何成为自身救赎与毁灭的主体，是将其置于女性如何受制于他人意志的语境之下。女性拥有自身的性欲也是不言而喻的。男性的意见并不重要，国王希尔坎（亨利比玛格丽特小十一岁）的意见往往被礼貌地忽略，仿佛其粗俗无礼是意料之中的事。

Taken as a whole, The Heptameron is a kind of rough draft for many novels yet to be written; the stories, for the most part simple and plot-based, but dramatic and full of mysteries, are given depth and complexity by means of critical inquiry.

从整体上看，《七日谈》就像是许多尚未写成的长篇小说的草稿；这些故事大多情节简单，但又充满戏剧性和神秘感，通过批判性的探究赋予了它们深度和复杂性。

In fact, strange tales have often inspired novels—Stendhal wrote The Red and the Black following a newsworthy trial, for example, and Dostoevsky was similarly drawn to the real-life episode that inspired Crime and Punishment. Sensational acts arouse moral curiosity. Onlookers become preoccupied with finding a logic for them that allows them to fit into some theory or other of human nature. Furthermore, the religious beliefs of Marguerite and her friends (Catholic, but with reformist leanings) meant that they mistrusted to some degree the conventional system of precepts and moral rituals. Aware of the Reformation and Counter-Reformation that swirled all about them, they were eager to look within and to discuss, to find a basis of right behavior that was logical as well as uncorrupted. There is a strong sense that notions of class, ethics, custom, and morality that had served in the Middle Ages were breaking down in the middle of the sixteenth century to a degree unknown even during the Black Death, and the point of Marguerite's project is to come up with something, even something provisional, that will serve as a guide to the ten taletellers in lieu of what has been lost. This is a common function of the novel.

事实上，奇闻轶事常常激发小说创作的灵感——例如，司汤达在一次轰动一时的审判后创作了《红与黑》，陀思妥耶夫斯基也同样被启发创作《罪与罚》的真实事件所吸引。耸人听闻的事件会激起人们的道德好奇心。旁观者会执着于寻找某种逻辑来解释这些事件，使其符合某种人性理论。此外，玛格丽特和她的朋友们（她们信奉天主教，但带有改革倾向）的宗教信仰意味着她们在某种程度上不信任传统的戒律和道德仪式体系。她们意识到宗教改革和反宗教改革的浪潮席卷而来，因此渴望反思自身，展开讨论，以找到一种既合乎逻辑又纯洁无瑕的正确行为准则。人们强烈地感觉到，中世纪盛行的阶级、伦理、习俗和道德观念在十六世纪中叶开始瓦解，其程度甚至超过了黑死病时期。玛格丽特此举的目的，正是为了找到某种东西，哪怕只是暂时的，来代替那些已经失落的准则，指引十位说书人。这正是小说的常见功能。

Both Boccaccio and Marguerite de Navarre were much interested in individuals. In considering human behaviors and misbehaviors, they gave great attention to motives and idiosyncratic circumstances. They sought to understand how points of view differ from individual to individual, and while they accepted the structure of their societies as givens, they thought that both men and women could act for or against the more brutal tendencies of their societies. They saw both men and women as agents of their own salvation or damnation, and they saw the details of such fates as inherently interesting and illuminating. The controversies of the Reformation promoted a believer's sense of his own individuality—he was responsible for avoiding sin and for feeling and demonstrating the presence of God's grace. This gave him (or her) an awareness of the inner life—first of his own, and then of the inner lives of others. Examples of what to do and what not to do abounded, if only one observed closely enough. All of these habits of mind fed naturally into the rise of the novel, which organizes itself around individuals and pays attention to the inner life and its relationship to the outer life. And the novel requires conflict, especially inner conflict. The inner conflict of the worried, conflicted believer predisposed him or her to a novelistic state of mind.

薄伽丘和纳瓦拉的玛格丽特都对个体抱有浓厚的兴趣。在考察人类的行为和不当行为时，他们非常关注动机和独特的境况。他们试图理解不同个体视角之间的差异，虽然他们接受社会结构是既定的，但他们认为男女都可以顺应或反抗社会中更为残酷的倾向。他们将男女视为自身救赎或毁灭的主体，并认为这种命运的细节本身就引人入胜、发人深省。宗教改革的争论增强了信徒对自身个性的认知——信徒有责任避免犯罪，并感受和展现上帝的恩典。这使他们意识到内心世界的存在——首先是自身的内心世界，然后是他人的内心世界。只要足够仔细地观察，就能发现许多关于应该做什么和不应该做什么的例子。所有这些思维习惯都自然而然地促成了小说的兴起。小说以人物为中心，关注人物的内心世界及其与外部世界的关系。而小说需要冲突，尤其是内心的冲突。忧虑而矛盾的信徒的内心冲突，使他们更容易进入一种小说家的思维状态。

When Cervantes wrote the first volume of Don Quixote , he put together the elements of the novel with an inspired simplicity that achieved a wide and enthusiastic audience. Don Quixote, like every good protagonist, entered into Cervantes's abundance of material and shaped it around himself, but, as with The Heptameron , the invention of the novel in Don Quixote required a great deal of interpretation and conversation among the characters. To many modern readers, this incessant talking gets in the way of the action, but in fact it was necessary to the engendering of the novel as a form. The novel is self-conscious because modern people feel that they are different from past generations. Don Quixote's conversations with his friends almost all revolve around how current adventures and activities relate to received wisdom, often the wisdom of the medieval romances Quixote is fond of. As the conversations progress, the novel's sense of self-assurance solidifies.

塞万提斯创作《堂吉诃德》第一卷时，他以一种充满灵感的简洁手法将小说元素巧妙地融合在一起，赢得了广大读者的喜爱。堂吉诃德如同所有优秀的主人公一样，从塞万提斯丰富的素材中汲取灵感，并将其塑造成自己的形象。然而，与《七日谈》一样，《堂吉诃德》的小说形式也需要大量的解读和人物间的对话。对许多现代读者来说，这种喋喋不休的对话妨碍了情节的推进，但实际上，它对于小说这一形式的形成至关重要。小说之所以具有自觉性，是因为现代人觉得自己与过去几代人截然不同。堂吉诃德与朋友们的对话几乎都围绕着当下的冒险经历和活动与既有智慧之间的联系展开，而这些智慧往往来自堂吉诃德所钟爱的中世纪传奇故事。随着对话的推进，小说的自信也愈发鲜明。

Don Quixote's inseparable and necessary companion is Sancho Panza. When Quixote first ventures away from his home, under the spell of his romantic books and eager for knightly experience, he goes alone, but it is evident to the reader as well as to Cervantes that his solitude does not strike exactly the right note—for one thing, he has to express his thoughts too lengthily and too clearly. They seem less like thoughts than discourses, making Quixote pedantic and inhibiting the flow of the action. For another, he seems both too crazy and too vulnerable. His own navet and incompetence, combined with the casual brutality of the world of seventeenth-century Spain, make him too pure a figure of pity to succeed comically. He needs a buffer and ally as well as a sounding board, and Sancho, who is practical in some ways, though quite innocent in others, serves both functions. Sancho, as a peasant who is loyal to Quixote but skeptical of his theories, stands between the idealism of Quixote and the realism all around, enabling both sides of the novel's inherent binary nature to flower more naturally than they could in The Heptameron. Quixote is in distinct conflict with his world—it is how he is defined. In this, he differs from the characters in The Decameron , especially, and even from the characters of The Heptameron. The variety and richness of those two works paradoxically confirm the social realities that many of the characters of the stories transgress. Even such characters as the sister who watches her brother kill her husband and the mother who is impregnated by her son exist entirely within the social network created by the tales, which in turn are embedded in the social network of the taletelling. The world of The Decameron is in crisis, and the world of The Heptameron is self-contradictory and frightening, but the addition of each tale to the many previous ones reinforces the reality of those worlds.

唐吉诃德形影不离且不可或缺的伙伴是桑丘·潘萨。唐吉诃德初次离家，受浪漫小说的诱惑，渴望体验骑士生活，便独自一人踏上旅程。但读者和塞万提斯都明显看出，他的孤身一人并不尽如人意——首先，他总是冗长而清晰地表达自己的想法，与其说是思考，不如说是长篇大论，这让唐吉诃德显得迂腐，也阻碍了情节的流畅性。其次，他显得既疯狂又脆弱。他的天真和无能，加上十七世纪西班牙社会的冷酷无情，使他成为一个过于纯真可怜的形象，难以达到喜剧效果。他需要一个缓冲、一个盟友，以及一个倾诉对象。桑丘在某些方面务实，在另一些方面又天真无邪，恰好扮演了这两种角色。桑丘作为一个忠于堂吉诃德却又对其理论持怀疑态度的农民，游走于堂吉诃德的理想主义与周遭的现实主义之间，使得小说固有的二元对立得以比在《七日谈》中更加自然地展现。堂吉诃德与他所处的世界存在着明显的冲突——这正是他被定义的方式。在这一点上，他与《十日谈》中的人物，尤其是与《七日谈》中的人物截然不同。这两部作品的丰富性和多样性，反而以一种悖论的方式印证了故事中许多人物所违背的社会现实。即使是像目睹哥哥弑夫的妹妹和被儿子强奸怀孕的母亲这样的人物，也完全存在于故事所构建的社会网络中，而这些故事本身又嵌入于讲述故事的社会网络之中。 《十日谈》的世界正处于危机之中，《七日谈》的世界自相矛盾且令人恐惧，但每个故事都与之前的许多故事相呼应，从而强化了这些世界的真实性。

Not so with Quixote. The question arises with Quixote, as with every strong protagonist: does he shape the world, or does it shape him? This question is present in the mere process of the author shifting his attention from Quixote to the world around him and back to Quixote and back to the world around him, realizing each in ever more detail, fitting each more and more to the other in what you might call artistic unity. This is the essential process and power of the novel— to make one cohesive work of art out of many disparate elements, showing the one character in detail while constantly evoking the many that surround him. Don Quixote is the first modern novel because the reader's experience of Cervantes's mind working over this relationship is the first modern example of undiluted authorial consciousness as it unfolds page by page. As with many great works, the original stroke of genius by the author was coming up with a good, simple idea (a middle-aged gentleman who has read so many accounts of knightly courage that he decides to try it himself). That things are not as they seem is the root premise of Quixote's view of the world, but also the root premise of Cervantes's story, because even though things aren't as Quixote thinks they are, they also are not as they seem to the other characters. Only author and reader know the truth. Layers of reality and seeming—of point of view—build upon one another.

但堂吉诃德却并非如此。如同所有杰出的主人公一样，堂吉诃德也面临着一个问题：究竟是他塑造了世界，还是世界塑造了他？这个问题贯穿于作者将笔触从堂吉诃德转移到他周围的世界，再回到堂吉诃德，如此往复的过程之中。作者对两者的刻画愈发细致入微，使它们彼此更加契合，最终达到一种艺术上的统一。这正是小说的精髓和力量所在——将众多看似迥异的元素融合为一个浑然一体的艺术作品，既细致描绘了主人公的形象，又不断地展现了他周围的世界。《堂吉诃德》之所以被称为第一部现代小说，是因为读者能够体验到塞万提斯对这种关系的思考，这便是现代小说中作者意识最纯粹、最完整的展现，它逐页展开，令人叹为观止。如同许多伟大的作品一样，作者最初的灵光乍现源于一个简单而精妙的构思（一位中年绅士读过无数骑士英勇事迹后，决定亲自尝试一番）。事物并非如表面所见，这既是堂吉诃德世界观的根本前提，也是塞万提斯故事的根本前提。因为即便事物并非堂吉诃德所想的那样，对其他角色而言也并非如此。只有作者和读者才知道真相。现实与表象——视角——层层叠加，彼此交织。

The history of the novel demonstrates that this simple idea—points of view evoked and juxtaposed—is inexhaustibly fertile. What The Decameron and The Heptameron show with their multitude of briefer and sometimes jokelike stories is that before the end of the sixteenth century (at least in Europe), ways of understanding and depicting the inner life were not rich enough to sustain much narrative length. But the plays of William Shakespeare, written in the 1590s and early 1600s , show that self-consciousness and introspection were bursting out all over. By means of asides, soliloquys, prologues, and epilogues, the playwright was pushing against the boundaries of the drama to display and explore the inner life as well as to address the audience unmedi-ated.

小说史表明，这种简单的理念——唤起并并置不同的视角——具有无穷的创造力。《十日谈》和《七日谈》以其众多短小精悍、有时甚至带有戏谑意味的故事表明，在十六世纪末之前（至少在欧洲），理解和描绘内心世界的方式还不够丰富，不足以支撑篇幅较长的叙事。但威廉·莎士比亚在16世纪90年代和17世纪初创作的戏剧则表明，自我意识和内省正在蓬勃发展。通过旁白、独白、序言和尾声，剧作家突破了戏剧的界限，展现并探索人物的内心世界，同时也直接与观众对话。

∗ For further discussion of this point, please see Stephen Greenblatt, Will in the World (New York: W.W. Norton, 2004 ).

* 有关这一点的进一步讨论，请参阅 Stephen Greenblatt 的《世界中的意志》（纽约：W.W. Norton，2004 年）。

The wars, controversies, and religious movements of the sixteenth century required people to look within—life, death, and eternal salvation were at stake. The result was the characteristic rhythm of the realistic novel—action, reflection, action, reflection, action, reflection, for hundreds of pages. It is a hypnotic rhythm.

十六世纪的战争、争论和宗教运动迫使人们进行内省——生死攸关，永恒救赎也岌岌可危。由此便形成了现实主义小说特有的节奏——行动、反思、行动、反思、行动、反思，如此循环往复，绵延数百页。这种节奏令人着迷。

That Quixote is chaste and celibate is also significant, both as a departure from earlier depictions of manly men and as an omen of the future development of the novel. No more rolling in the hay, no more easy acceptance of human sexuality, including the sexuality of women. In Quixote, the opinion of Marguerite's Hircan—that if a woman doesn't yield to his pleasure, he is justified in killing her as a matter of honor—gets tossed into the dustbin of literary history.

堂吉诃德的贞洁和独身也意义非凡，这既是对早期男性形象的颠覆，也预示着小说未来的发展方向。从此不再有风流韵事，不再轻易接受人类的性行为，包括女性的性行为。在《堂吉诃德》中，玛格丽特的情人希尔坎——如果一个女人不顺从他的欲望，他出于荣誉可以杀死她——的观点，被彻底抛弃在了文学史的垃圾堆里。

The religious conflicts of the sixteenth century could not help making sexuality an inflammatory subject, especially since, as both The Decameron and The Heptameron demonstrate, one of the great accusations against the Catholic Church was that while professing celibacy and holiness, its clergy were universally promiscuous—story thirty-three of The Heptameron specifically treats this subject. We may speculate about why Cervantes deprived Quixote of his sexuality, but the effect on later novelists was to provide a model of male virtue that was unusual in its own time but more and more usual in later novels. According to Quixote's friends and the people he meets along the way, his chastity is one of his stranger peculiarities, but as the reader becomes more acquainted with him and grows fond of him, his chastity grows less eccentric and more ideal—evidence of his holy foolishness, as well as of his foolish holiness. Don Quixote was, of course, not the only reason explicit references to sex were dropped from novels, but it set a precedent—two entire books could be written about the inner life of a man who falls asleep whenever discussion of sexual and romantic relationships comes up. An author could make believable a grown male character who has no sexual desires. In part owing to the huge popularity of Don Quixote , the novel gave up a large and fertile subject (at least until the twentieth century), and entered into the idea that because of taboos on sexuality, discussions and depictions of other, more public sides of human nature constituted discussions of all of human nature. The novel, which is simultaneously public and private, published and intimate, has a special capacity to explore the most intimate subjects, but for three centuries it did not routinely explore them, and its avoidance of those subjects made them more and more difficult to discuss.

十六世纪的宗教冲突使得性成为一个极具争议性的话题，尤其因为正如《十日谈》和《七日谈》所展现的那样，对天主教会的一大指控便是，尽管其神职人员标榜独身和圣洁，却普遍存在性滥交——《七日谈》的第三十三则故事就专门探讨了这一主题。我们可以推测塞万提斯为何剥夺了堂吉诃德的性欲，但其对后世小说家的影响在于，它提供了一种男性美德的典范，这种典范在当时并不常见，但在后来的小说中却越来越普遍。根据堂吉诃德的朋友和他一路遇到的人的说法，他的贞洁是他最古怪的特质之一，但随着读者对他的了解加深，并逐渐对他产生好感，他的贞洁便不再显得怪异，反而更显理想——这既体现了他圣洁的愚昧，也体现了他愚昧的圣洁。当然，《堂吉诃德》并非小说中不再直接描写性爱的唯一原因，但它开创了一个先例——完全可以写两本书来描写一个男人的内心世界，他一谈到性或爱情关系就昏昏欲睡。作者可以塑造一个没有性欲的成年男性角色，并使其显得可信。部分由于《堂吉诃德》的巨大成功，小说放弃了一个庞大而富有创作潜力的主题（至少在20世纪之前是如此），并接受了这样一种观念：由于性方面的禁忌，对人性其他更公开的方面的讨论和描写，就等同于对整个人性的探讨。小说兼具公共性和私密性，既是公开的又是私密的，它拥有探索最私密主题的特殊能力，但在三个世纪的时间里，小说并没有经常探讨这些主题，而它对这些主题的回避反而使它们越来越难以讨论。

As suggested above, the two volumes of Don Quixote are not the same. The first volume is a more primitive work altogether than the second. Cervantes is less adept at integrating Quixote and Sancho with the characters they meet along the way, and it shares with The Hep-tameron a quality of disparateness. Shortly after the famous incident of the windmills, for example, Quixote and Sancho attack two friars whom they mistake for kidnappers. They are soundly beaten. Far from an inn, they are taken in for the night by some goatherders, who tell them the sad story of Grisstomo and Marcela—he has died for love of her, and his funeral is about to take place. This story goes on for some twenty-two closely printed pages, and although it is interesting in the context of the preoccupation of the novel as a form with the dilemma of what is to be done with women, it has very little to do with Quixote's adventures. The same is true of the subplot of Cardenio, Dorotea, Don Fernando, and Luscinda, which takes center stage, more or less, for almost a hundred pages (and includes a subsubplot quite similar to story forty-seven in The Heptameron). It is not that these stories are not interesting in themselves, it is that their themes don't fit very well with the themes of Quixote and Sancho's quest. And it is not precisely that Cervantes can't control his material, it is that in the first volume he doesn't realize that it requires control. Quixote and Sancho's quest is meant to be both their story and a frame for other stories. Volume one is more like The Heptameron. Volume two is more like a modern novel—in it, Cervantes has learned how to make Quixote and Sancho central to his novel by deepening their characters and making their adventures grow out of who they are. By far the most important of these is their run-in with the duke and the duchess, which takes up more than half of the volume. Quixote and Sancho meet the duke and the duchess in a wood, and the two aristocrats immediately realize they have indeed met the famous knight and his squire. They then use their wealth and power to devise an elaborate practical joke by which they entertain themselves with the spectacle of Sancho and Quixote acting in character. They tempt Sancho with power—pretending to put him in charge of his own island—and they test Quixote with the charms and blandishments of women whom they have paid to tempt him. He remains untempted, but the unrelenting joke exhausts him, and when he goes home afterward, he has lost heart. On his deathbed, he admits that he had been mad, but now he is sane, no longer Don Quixote, but once again Alonso Quijano. His friends plead with him to resume his cause, but he confesses, makes his will, and dies.

正如上文所述，《堂吉诃德》的两卷并不相同。第一卷整体上比第二卷更为原始。塞万提斯在将堂吉诃德和桑丘与他们沿途遇到的人物融合在一起方面略显逊色，而且它与《七百一十七》一样，都存在着一种割裂感。例如，在著名的风车事件之后不久，堂吉诃德和桑丘误将两个修士当成了绑匪，并袭击了他们。结果他们被狠狠地揍了一顿。他们离客栈很远，被几个牧羊人收留过夜。牧羊人给他们讲述了格里斯托莫和玛塞拉的悲惨故事——格里斯托莫为爱玛塞拉而死，他的葬礼即将举行。这个故事用了大约二十二页密密麻麻的文字，虽然从小说这种体裁探讨女性问题的角度来看，这个故事颇具趣味，但它与堂吉诃德的冒险经历却几乎毫无关联。卡德尼奥、多萝西娅、唐·费尔南多和卢辛达的支线情节也是如此，它占据了近百页的篇幅（其中还包含一个与《七日谈》第四十七篇故事颇为相似的子支线情节）。并非这些故事本身不精彩，而是它们的主题与堂吉诃德和桑丘的冒险之旅的主题不太契合。也并非塞万提斯无法驾驭素材，而是他在第一卷中并未意识到驾驭素材的重要性。堂吉诃德和桑丘的冒险之旅既是他们的故事，也是其他故事的框架。第一卷更像《七日谈》，而第二卷则更像一部现代小说——在这一卷中，塞万提斯学会了如何通过深化人物性格、使堂吉诃德和桑丘的冒险经历源于他们自身，从而使他们成为小说的核心人物。其中最重要的莫过于他们与公爵夫妇的偶遇，这占据了全书一半以上的篇幅。堂吉诃德和桑丘在树林里遇到了公爵夫妇，两位贵族立刻意识到他们遇到的正是那位著名的骑士和他的侍从。于是，他们利用自己的财富和权力，精心策划了一个恶作剧，让桑丘和堂吉诃德扮演他们的角色，以此取乐。他们用权力诱惑桑丘——假装让他掌管自己的岛屿——又用他们雇来勾引堂吉诃德的女人们的甜言蜜语来试探他。堂吉诃德始终没有动摇，但这没完没了的恶作剧让他精疲力竭，事后回到家时，他已丧失了斗志。临终前，他承认自己曾经疯了，但现在他恢复了理智，不再是堂吉诃德，而是阿隆索·吉哈诺。他的朋友们恳求他重拾事业，但他坦白认罪，立下遗嘱，然后死去。

Don Quixote was instantly popular—so frequently translated that one of Shakespeare's late unfinished plays seems to have been taken from the Cardenio material of volume one.

《堂吉诃德》一经问世便广受欢迎，被频繁翻译，以至于莎士比亚晚期未完成的一部戏剧似乎取材于第一卷的卡德尼奥素材。

∗ See Stephen Greenblatt, Will in the World.

* 参见 Stephen Greenblatt 的《Will in the World》。

It was known all over Europe and, no doubt, Madame de La Fayette, who wrote The Princess of Cléves some forty years after Cervantes died, was familiar with, at least, a French translation. But her greatest novel seems to have been much influenced by The Heptameron , since she set it in the 1550s , in the court of Henri II, who was the son of Marguerite's brother Franois. Madame de La Fayette prided herself on the precision of her historical knowledge and her familiarity with court life of her own day; she would surely have known all about Marguerite and her tales (although our modern edition is different from the edition she would have had access to). We can see The Princess of Cléves as a lengthier and more psychologically detailed answer to Marguerite's original question: can a woman know true love and remain virtuous at the same time? Every word and action of the princess, from the moment she first sees her lover to the end of the novel, models both true love and perfect virtue, an unlikely but dramatic path through the minefield of women's roles and risks in the early modern era.

这部作品在整个欧洲都广为人知，毫无疑问，在塞万提斯去世约四十年后创作《克莱沃公主》的拉法耶特夫人至少熟悉它的法文译本。但她最伟大的小说似乎深受《七日谈》的影响，因为她将故事背景设定在16世纪50年代，亨利二世的宫廷——亨利二世是玛格丽特的哥哥弗朗索瓦的儿子。拉法耶特夫人以其精准的历史知识和对当时宫廷生活的熟悉而自豪；她肯定对玛格丽特和她的故事了如指掌（尽管我们现在看到的版本与她当时所接触的版本有所不同）。我们可以将《克莱沃公主》视为对玛格丽特最初提出的问题——一个女人能否同时拥有真爱和贞洁——的更长篇幅、更注重心理描写的解答。从公主第一次见到她的爱人到小说的结尾，公主的一言一行都体现了真爱和完美的品德，这是一条不太可能但却充满戏剧性的道路，穿越了早期现代女性角色和风险的雷区。

The plot is a typical French plot—a woman with some status but limited money and influence takes her beautiful daughter to Paris to find her a husband. In spite of the girl's beauty, she is unsuccessful at first, and when the girl does attract the attention of the right sort of man, it is someone she likes but does not love, Monsieur de Cléves. Out of prudence, the mother, who is in ill health, presses the marriage. Shortly after the marriage, the most desirable man in France, the duc de Nemours, falls in love with the girl. Although she avoids him as much as she can, he is irresistibly attentive, and eventually she falls for him. Her passion is deep and sincere, but as a desperate method of avoiding any compromise to her virtue, she confesses her passion to her husband (with whom she has no children, indicating perhaps that their marriage is sexless). The husband is both grieved by her love and gratified by her confidence in him and by her virtue. The triangle, now positively glowing with the frustrated passion of all parties, persists unstably for a short time, and then the husband dies, leaving the princess to marry her lover if she wishes. She does not, partly because she is aware that the knowledge of her passion had contributed to her husband's fatal illness, but additionally, because she also knows instinctively that should Nemours possess her as his wife, his passion would be likely to diminish. As long as the two remain unsatisfied, their love is equal; were she to yield, inequality, and therefore unhappiness on her part, would ensue. This is simultaneously a mere piece of logic that promotes a virtuous outcome and an astute insight into the nature of romantic love as opposed to marital love. Is the princess right or wrong? She trumps her passions with a choice perhaps more plausible to some people than to others—she declares that she owes her truest love to God, and she is going to solve her emotional dilemma by sequestering herself, praying, and doing good works.

故事情节是典型的法国式爱情故事：一位出身尚可但家境有限的妇人带着她美丽的女儿前往巴黎，为她物色夫婿。尽管女儿容貌出众，但起初却屡屡碰壁。好不容易吸引了一位合适的男士的注意，却只是女儿喜欢却不爱的克莱夫先生。出于谨慎，身患重病的母亲催促女儿成婚。婚后不久，法国最炙手可热的男士内穆尔公爵便爱上了女儿。尽管女儿竭力躲避他，但他却对她百般殷勤，最终她还是被他迷住了。她的爱恋真挚而热烈，但为了避免任何违背贞洁的行为，她孤注一掷地向丈夫坦白了自己的心意（两人没有子女，或许暗示着他们的婚姻并不和谐）。丈夫既为女儿的爱恋感到痛苦，又为她的信任和贞洁而感到欣慰。这段三角关系，此刻因各方受挫的激情而熠熠生辉，摇摇欲坠地维持了一段时间，随后丈夫去世，公主可以自由选择是否嫁给情人。她没有，部分原因是她意识到，丈夫的死因正是因为他知道她的激情被知晓，但更重要的是，她本能地知道，如果她嫁给尼穆尔，他的激情很可能会消退。只要两人都保持着不满足的状态，他们的爱就是平等的；如果她屈服，就会出现不平等，从而导致她的不幸。这既是一种促成美德结局的逻辑，也是对浪漫爱情与婚姻爱情本质的敏锐洞察。公主是对是错？她战胜了自己的激情，做出了一个对某些人来说可能比对其他人更合理的选择——她宣称自己最真挚的爱献给了上帝，她将通过自我封闭、祈祷和行善来解决自己的情感困境。

The Princess of Cléves was a great success, and sparked intense discussion of the princess's unusual strategy for maintaining her virtue.
