Its plausibility was still being argued in the nineteenth century— possibly every Frenchman in the history of reading, including Stendhal, considered the princess's choices strange, but a glance at the seventy-two attempted solutions that constitute The Heptameron reveals just how hard Marguerite's riddle was. Madame de La Fayette understood her novelist's job—willing suspension of disbelief can be achieved without plausibility when the story is interesting enough to make the reader eager to read on, and reading The Princess of Cléves is intriguing and exciting. Each time the princess does an implausible thing, it seems like the only appropriate thing to do in the context of the story, especially, it seems to me, if the reader is a woman. As a young girl unprotected by family, wealth, or influence, living in a world of gossip and intrigue, the princess knows that her position is especially treacherous—it is probable that the duc de Nemours, for all of his desirability, cannot protect her honor, whatever the power of his affections. By age forty-five, with something like thirty years of court life behind her, Madame de La Fayette was certainly a realist about gossip, status, and intrigue.

《克莱沃公主》大获成功，引发了人们对公主保持贞洁的非同寻常策略的热烈讨论。这种策略的合理性在十九世纪仍为人争论——或许历史上所有读过书的法国人，包括司汤达在内，都认为公主的选择十分古怪。然而，只需看看构成《七日谈》的七十二种尝试性解决方案，便可知玛格丽特的谜题究竟有多么棘手。拉法耶特夫人深谙小说家的职责——当故事足够引人入胜，让读者渴望继续阅读时，即使情节本身并不完全合理，也能让读者心甘情愿地暂时放下怀疑。《克莱沃公主》正是如此，引人入胜，令人兴奋。每当公主做出看似不合情理的事情时，在我看来，这似乎都是故事背景下唯一恰当的选择，尤其对于女性读者而言更是如此。作为一个年轻女孩，她没有家族、财富或权势的庇护，生活在一个充满流言蜚语和阴谋诡计的世界里，公主深知自己的处境极其危险——内穆尔公爵即便魅力非凡，也无法保护她的名誉，无论他对她多么倾心。到了四十五岁，在宫廷生活了近三十年后，拉法耶特夫人对流言蜚语、地位和阴谋诡计早已了然于心。

At the same time, Madame de La Fayette had to come up with a technique that would put her story across, and she did so—moment-by-moment analysis of her protagonist's state of mind and emotions combined with incisive depiction of court life under Henri II (who is openly unfaithful to his queen). And because the princess has to keep secrets as best she can—given the constant circulation of gossip, she can confide in no one—Madame de La Fayette was forced to anatomize her inner life for the reader to an unprecedented degree, without resorting to Quixote-like conversations between the characters. She pretty much invented indirect discourse—the technique by which an author plausibly “overhears” her character's thoughts and expresses them in a way that seems idiosyncratic to her character. The result is a novel that is strangely modern in its psychological astuteness, far more detailed in this way than any of the works we have so far looked at, and one of the acknowledged great novels of French literature. At the same time, it is not idiosyncratic in its voice, like Don Quixote. As a narrator, Madame de La Fayette stays out of the way of the story, rarely intruding in her depiction of the characters. Her intelligence and originality come in her deployment of story, character, and theme rather than in her expression of her own personality. The Princess of Cléves was published anonymously. Madame de La Fayette wanted the princess's story to stand or fall on its own rather than suffering or benefiting from any association with her life or her reputation. More important, the novel is not about the princess's eccentricity, as Don Quixote is about Quixote's eccentricity. What it offers is an alternative plot about the struggle to conform to an ideal in spite of temptation and social pressure. An extravagant style is appropriate to the one; a correct but self-effacing style is appropriate to the other.

与此同时，拉法耶特夫人必须找到一种能够有效传达故事的写作技巧，而她也确实做到了——她将主人公的心理状态和情感逐一剖析，并巧妙地结合了对亨利二世统治下宫廷生活的深刻描绘（亨利二世公开背叛了他的王后）。由于公主必须竭尽全力保守秘密——在流言蜚语四起的环境下，她无法向任何人倾诉——拉法耶特夫人不得不以前所未有的程度剖析人物的内心世界，而没有采用堂吉诃德式的对话方式。她几乎可以说是发明了间接引语——这种写作技巧使作者能够“偷听到”人物的想法，并以符合人物自身特质的方式表达出来。这部小说以其敏锐的心理洞察力展现出一种奇特的现代感，在这方面远比我们之前探讨过的任何作品都更加细致入微，堪称法国文学的经典之作。与此同时，它的叙述风格并不像《堂吉诃德》那样特立独行。作为叙述者，拉法耶特夫人始终保持低调，很少干预人物的刻画。她的智慧和独创性体现在对故事、人物和主题的巧妙运用，而非个人风格的表达。《克莱沃公主》以匿名形式出版。拉法耶特夫人希望公主的故事能够独立成篇，而不是因与她自身经历或名誉的任何关联而得失。更重要的是，这部小说并非像《堂吉诃德》那样着重描写公主的古怪性格，而是讲述了一个关于在诱惑和社会压力下，努力追求理想的另类故事。一种风格适合张扬，另一种风格适合端庄谦逊。

The career of Daniel Defoe, who was a child in London when The Princess of Cléves was being published, illustrates not only many things about how novelists take up their vocation, but also a great deal about how the novel was invented and then, as it were, franchised. In the first place, since he was a tradesman, importer, and hack writer, Defoe's class loyalties, daily activities, and sensibility were different from those of his predecessors. In addition, by 1700 , when Defoe was forty, European religious conflicts had more or less been decided. The assassinations, revolutions, wars, counterrevolutions, inquisitions, tortures, hangings, burnings, murders, mutilations, and terror that marked the seventeenth century had subsided into a more or less territorial configuration of Catholic and Protestant countries that now competed for colonial wealth and trade domination. Capitalism was not as free or as sophisticated as it would be by the time Adam Smith wrote The Wealth of Nations ( 1776 ), but it had spread around Europe and was the order of the day in vibrant urban regions. Capitalism, of course, depended upon numeracy and literacy. Defoe was a man of the printed word— he was the first of our originators who depended upon the widespread dissemination of books and pamphlets for a living. As a result, he was drawn to sensational subjects, because they were the most likely to sell. At the same time, Defoe's Nonconformist religious training gave him a sense of sympathetic connection with subjects not previously given serious literary treatment—prostitutes, servants, criminals, working men and women, courtesans, adventurers of all stripes. Defoe knew from going to chapel that all humans could look within and inventory their virtues and defects, and were, therefore, suitable protagonists for novels.

丹尼尔·笛福的职业生涯，在他还是《克莱沃公主》出版时，他已是伦敦的一名孩童。他的人生经历不仅展现了小说家如何走上这条职业道路，也深刻揭示了小说的诞生和发展历程。首先，由于笛福出身于商人、进口商和业余作家，他的阶级认同、日常生活和情感都与前人截然不同。此外，到1700年，笛福四十岁时，欧洲的宗教冲突已基本平息。十七世纪充斥着暗杀、革命、战争、反革命、宗教裁判所、酷刑、绞刑、火刑、谋杀、残害和恐怖的种种暴行，已逐渐演变为天主教国家和新教国家之间相对稳定的领土格局，它们竞相争夺殖民财富和贸易霸权。当时的资本主义虽然不如亚当·斯密撰写《国富论》（1776年）时那样自由和成熟，但它已在欧洲各地传播开来，并在充满活力的城市地区成为主流。当然，资本主义依赖于识字和算术能力。笛福是一位与印刷文字结缘的作家——他是我们最早依靠书籍和小册子的广泛传播谋生的先驱之一。因此，他倾向于选择耸人听闻的主题，因为这些主题最容易畅销。与此同时，笛福的非国教宗教教育使他对那些此前未得到严肃文学关注的群体——妓女、仆人、罪犯、劳动者、交际花、形形色色的冒险家——产生了一种同情的共鸣。笛福从教堂礼拜中了解到，每个人都可以审视内心，清点自身的优缺点，因此都是小说中合适的主角。

Defoe was no less interested in the condition of women than our four previous authors—both Moll Flanders and Roxana deal frankly with the stark choices many women must make between virtue and survival. For his characters, though, the choices were neither sentimental nor abstract—giving up one's virtue was often the only way for a woman to survive, and one of Defoe's pamphlets was a defense of women's rights. His great technical innovation, though, comparable to Madame de La Fayette's invention of indirect discourse, was narrating in the first person rather than the third person. One of Defoe's hack writing jobs was criminal confessions. Criminals were celebrities in early-eighteenth-century England. In the complete absence of a social safety net, theft, murder, and other forms of violent crime were commonplace, and prostitution, child abandonment, and child-selling were routine, even though the laws against all of these transgressions were strict, punishments were harsh, and recidivism was the order of the day. Sensational crimes were written up and published, and when especially famous criminals came to be hanged (in public, as examples), writers such as Defoe composed their confessions. Defoe also was used to writing in his own voice—he wrote essays and polemics on politics, he wrote a travelogue of a journey around the British Isles, he wrote about a haunting. When, nearing sixty, he came to writing The Life and Strange Surprising Adventures of Robinson Crusoe , the first-person point of view was utterly natural to him, but it changed the nature of the novel, plunging it into the subjective realm and shifting the balance between the inner life and the outer life. The narrative still moved between actions and reflection, but now the actions were depicted entirely through the filter of the narrator's mode of reflection. An author need no longer cultivate a particular style that he used to tell many types of stories—varying his tone, perhaps, but retaining his authority. Defoe experimented with different styles—that is, different inner lives—for different narrators. Crusoe approaches everything practically, including his salvation. Moll Flanders is breezier and livelier than Crusoe—although she has been and remains a bit shocked by some of the things that have happened to her, her vitality seems like her natural counterweight to a sense of sinfulness. The narrator of A Journal of the Plague Year is more cautious and precise than either of the other two, almost entirely self-effacing and yet quite particular in his depiction of the catastrophic epidemic. Roxana, the protagonist of Defoe's last novel, is the most complex. She is a realist about what she has been required to do over the years to survive, but she is also tormented by her actions—in particular, at the beginning of the novel, when Roxana's husband abandons the family, she starves with the five children for a while, but, realizing that everyone is going to die, she consigns the baby to the parish and perpetrates a ruse upon her husband's sister (who is more prosperous), to plant the older four children in that family. The oldest daughter is subsequently sent away as a servant by the sister-in-law, but the girl returns to haunt, and endanger, Roxana, who more or less colludes, or at least acquiesces, in her death. It is a dark and complex novel, and the female voice is thoroughly convincing. As a gloss on the theories of Thomas Hobbes and their origins in the social conditions of England, it could not be more convincing.

笛福对女性境况的关注丝毫不亚于我们之前提到的四位作家——无论是《莫尔·弗兰德斯》还是《罗克珊娜》，都坦率地探讨了许多女性必须在贞洁与生存之间做出的艰难抉择。然而，对于他笔下的人物而言，这些选择既非感伤也非抽象——放弃贞洁往往是女性生存的唯一途径，而笛福的小册子之一正是捍卫女性权利的宣言。不过，他最伟大的写作技巧创新，堪比拉法耶特夫人发明的间接引语，在于他采用第一人称而非第三人称进行叙述。笛福的其中一项兼职工作是撰写罪犯的自白。在十八世纪初的英国，罪犯如同名人一般。由于社会保障体系的完全缺失，盗窃、谋杀和其他暴力犯罪司空见惯，卖淫、遗弃儿童和贩卖儿童也屡见不鲜，尽管针对所有这些罪行的法律十分严苛，惩罚也十分严厉，但累犯现象却屡见不鲜。耸人听闻的罪案被记录下来并出版，当一些特别臭名昭著的罪犯被处以绞刑（例如公开处决）时，像笛福这样的作家会撰写他们的忏悔录。笛福也习惯于用自己的声音写作——他写过政治散文和论战文章，写过环游不列颠群岛的游记，还写过关于闹鬼事件的文章。当他接近六十岁时，开始创作《鲁滨逊漂流记》时，第一人称视角对他来说完全是自然而然的，但这改变了小说的性质，使其进入主观领域，并改变了内心世界和外部世界之间的平衡。叙事仍然在行动和反思之间切换，但现在行动完全是通过叙述者的反思视角来描绘的。一位作家不再需要培养一种特定的风格来讲述各种类型的故事——或许会改变语气，但仍然保持其权威性。笛福为不同的叙述者尝试了不同的风格——也就是不同的内心世界。克鲁索对待一切事物都务实，包括他的救赎。莫尔·弗兰德斯比克鲁索更轻松活泼——尽管她过去和现在都对发生在她身上的一些事情感到有些震惊，但她的活力似乎是她对抗罪恶感的一种自然平衡。《瘟疫年日记》的叙述者比其他两位都更加谨慎和精准，几乎完全不加修饰，但在描述这场灾难性的瘟疫时却又十分细致。笛福最后一部小说的主人公罗克珊娜最为复杂。她对多年来为了生存不得不做的事情有着清醒的认识，但她也饱受自身行为的折磨——尤其是在小说开头，当罗克珊娜的丈夫抛弃家庭后，她带着五个孩子忍饥挨饿了一段时间。意识到所有人都将死去，她将幼子托付给教区，并设计欺骗丈夫的妹妹（她家境更为富裕），将四个大孩子安置在她家。大女儿后来被弟媳送去当佣人，但她却回来纠缠罗克珊娜，并危及她的生命。罗克珊娜或多或少地参与了她的死亡，或者至少是默许了她的死亡。这是一部阴郁而复杂的小说，女性视角极具说服力。作为对托马斯·霍布斯理论及其在英国社会状况中起源的阐释，这部小说可谓无可挑剔。

What Defoe was after was not so much sympathy as empathy—not so much “feeling with” a protagonist, but “sensing through” him or her. All of Defoe's protagonists are morally problematic; all have committed sins and crimes, and, more important, all have committed cruelties, but all are also burdened by awareness of not only the sins but also the circumstances that gave rise to them. This moral ambiguity perfectly suits both the novel's focus on the inner life and also the tendency of prose to proliferate, making finer and finer distinctions at greater and greater length. In fact, Defoe's protagonists (with the exception of his first, Crusoe) tend to be so subjective that the world they live in is depicted only in passing. They hardly bother setting a scene or describing a person or a place. Emotions are portrayed and alluded to, but the realest part of the inner life of Defoe's characters is the activity of weighing right and wrong against necessity and desire. And yet Defoe's novels are filled with energy and rarely depressing. There is no ennui in Defoe's characters. They take an active interest in practical matters—Robinson Crusoe, of course, is famous for his enterprise, but Roxana provides plenty of interesting information on many topics, ranging from how to foist your children off upon your relatives (which she must do in a particular way because of parish pauper laws), to how to transfer a large sum of money from one country to another, to how to conduct affairs of mutual benefit with married men. Defoe's characters readily comprehend that survival is a full-time job requiring cleverness and application as well as luck. And because Defoe's women characters are on their own, they have an answer to a perennial European question: what is the purpose of women? It turns out that their purpose is work, same as men.

笛福追求的与其说是同情，不如说是共情——与其说是“感同身受”主人公的感受，不如说是“透过”主人公的视角去感受。笛福笔下的所有主人公都存在道德问题；他们都犯下了罪行，更重要的是，他们都犯下了残忍的罪行，但他们也都背负着沉重的负担，不仅意识到自己的罪行，也意识到导致罪行发生的种种境况。这种道德上的模糊性完美契合了小说对人物内心世界的关注，也符合散文的惯性——即在越来越长的篇幅中，对细节进行越来越细致的描绘。事实上，笛福笔下的主人公（除了他的第一个主人公鲁滨逊）往往都非常主观，以至于他们所生活的世界只是被一笔带过。他们几乎不费心思去描绘场景、人物或地点。情感虽有描绘和暗示，但笛福笔下人物内心世界最真实的部分，在于他们权衡是非对错、权衡需求与欲望的活动。然而，笛福的小说却充满活力，鲜少令人感到压抑。笛福笔下的人物没有丝毫倦怠之感。他们对实际事务充满热情——鲁滨逊·克鲁索当然以其冒险精神闻名，但罗克珊娜也提供了许多关于各种话题的有趣信息，从如何将孩子托付给亲戚（由于教区贫民法的限制，她必须以特定的方式这样做），到如何将一大笔钱从一个国家转移到另一个国家，再到如何与已婚男人进行互惠互利的交往。笛福笔下的人物深谙生存是一项需要智慧、勤奋和运气的全职工作。而且，由于笛福笔下的女性角色都是独立自主的，她们对一个永恒的欧洲问题——女性存在的意义是什么——有着自己的答案。事实证明，他们的目的和男人一样，都是为了工作。

The Adventures of Robinson Crusoe , which was published anonymously in 1719 , was a sensation. Within a year of publication, it was translated into several other European languages in, of course, pirated editions. Defoe's later novels (five in three to four years, along with other books) did not cause quite the stir as his first, and he did not receive royalties—each was a one-off. Defoe died in 1731 somewhat mysteriously, away from his family and hiding from creditors. Did immediately subsequent novelists learn from him? On the one hand, Robinson Crusoe was the most successful novel of the eighteenth century, and Moll Flanders and Roxana went through many editions in which they were cleaned up and morally improved; on the other hand, Defoe's subject matter was so sensational and lacking in respectability that if novelists such as Fielding and Richardson learned something from Defoe, perhaps they would not have admitted it. Intention, though, is not the same as effect. Defoe might not have intended to broaden the audience and the subject matter of the novel; he might have intended only to make money. Even so, he often wrote books with a didactic purpose. His first work, a pamphlet of 1689 , justified the Glorious Revolution (the accession of William of Orange, a Protestant and a German, to the English throne). He wrote The Family Instructor , the two-volume Complete English Tradesman , and The Complete English Gentleman , as well as his essay on the rights of women. In fact, Defoe was so successful in democratizing the English novel that writers of later generations of the eighteenth century—into the career of Jane Austen—expended considerable effort giving the novel a higher tone.

《鲁滨逊漂流记》于1719年匿名出版，轰动一时。出版不到一年，它就被翻译成多种欧洲语言，当然，盗版也层出不穷。笛福后来的小说（三四年间出版了五部，外加其他作品）并未像第一部那样引起轰动，而且他也没有收到版税——每部作品都是一次性收入。1731年，笛福离奇去世，远离家人，躲避债主。那么，后来的小说家是否从他身上汲取了灵感呢？一方面，《鲁滨逊漂流记》是十八世纪最成功的小说，莫尔·弗兰德斯和罗克珊娜的故事也经历了多次版本修改，在道德上得到了提升；另一方面，笛福的小说题材如此耸人听闻，如此缺乏道德底线，以至于像菲尔丁和理查森这样的小说家如果从笛福那里学到了什么，或许也不会承认。然而，意图与结果并非一回事。笛福或许并非有意拓宽小说的读者群和题材；他或许只是为了赚钱。即便如此，他的作品也常常带有教化意义。他的第一部作品是1689年的一本小册子，为光荣革命（即新教徒、德国人奥兰治亲王威廉登上英国王位）辩护。他还著有《家庭指导手册》、《英国商人全书》（两卷本）、《英国绅士全书》，以及一篇关于妇女权利的文章。事实上，笛福在使英国小说大众化方面取得了巨大成功，以至于十八世纪后世的作家——直至简·奥斯汀——都花费了大量精力来提升小说的格调。

Even though writers all over Europe (and the world, if we include The Tale of Genji as one of our most original and influential novels), invented and reinvented the novel, it took hold as an established form in England about two generations before it took hold in France and elsewhere owing to the economic and social conditions in England that promoted literacy. One of the first newly literate groups, for example, was the large class of ladies’ maids who worked from age fourteen or so in wealthy houses all over England, who had a fair amount of leisure time, who lived in close proximity to books and educated employers, and who were themselves required to exhibit a certain amount of refinement, but the growing eighteenth-century audience for the novel was diverse. As a result, each of the great English novelists of the eighteenth century brought something innovative to the new form.

尽管欧洲各地（如果将《源氏物语》也算作最具原创性和影响力的作品之一，那么全世界的作家都参与了小说的创作和革新，但由于英国的经济和社会环境促进了识字率的提高，小说作为一种成熟的文学形式在英国比在法国和其他地方早了大约两代人的时间。例如，最早一批识字的群体之一是数量庞大的女仆阶层，她们从十四岁左右就开始在英国各地富裕人家中工作，拥有相当多的闲暇时间，生活在书籍和受过良好教育的雇主附近，并且她们自身也被要求展现一定的文雅举止。然而，十八世纪小说的读者群体日益壮大，且十分多元化。因此，每一位十八世纪伟大的英国小说家都为这种新兴的文学形式带来了创新。

In 1740 , a London printer named Samuel Richardson galvanized the literary world with his epistolary novel Pamela. Pamela began as a model letter in a small instructional book Richardson had written, meant to show the newly literate classes how to write proper letters on various topics and for various purposes. Pamela's letter is that of a servant girl to her parents about her employment on a large estate. Richardson seems to have quickly understood both the thematic and the dramatic possibilities of Pamela's situation, and, seized by inspiration at age fifty, he became a novelist. Pamela, who is in the Dissenting habit of confessing to her parents to seek their advice on how to live a godly and virtuous life, reports the death of her mistress, and shortly thereafter that her young master, Mr. B., seems intent upon seducing and then raping her. According to Pamela, her sole concern is to maintain her virtue and the purity of her soul for reasons of faith. Mr. B. has her abducted, held against her will, drugged, and pinned down while he attempts to outrage her virtue. He then tries a false marriage. Eventually, though, he falls in love with Pamela and decides to marry her in reality, mostly because he is very impressed with her tenacious grasp upon her virtue and with her literary style, which he has read in her letters. At that point, his sister strongly resists the marriage, and Pamela begins writing about larger issues of the true nature of love and marriage.

1740年，伦敦印刷商塞缪尔·理查森凭借书信体小说《帕梅拉》震撼了文坛。《帕梅拉》最初是理查森所著一本小型指导书中的一封范文，旨在指导新近识字的阶层如何就各种主题和用途撰写得体的书信。帕梅拉的信是一位女仆写给父母的，讲述了她在庄园里的工作。理查森似乎很快领悟到帕梅拉处境的主题和戏剧性，并在五十岁时受到灵感的启发，成为了一名小说家。帕梅拉遵循着非国教徒的习惯，向父母忏悔，寻求如何过上虔诚而有德行的生活的建议。她在信中报告了女主人的去世，不久之后，她的年轻主人B先生似乎意图引诱并强奸她。帕梅拉认为，她唯一的愿望就是为了信仰而保持贞洁和灵魂的纯洁。 B先生绑架了她，强迫她待在房间里，给她下药，并试图玷污她的贞洁。之后，他又试图与她假结婚。然而，最终他爱上了帕梅拉，并决定与她结婚，主要是因为他被她坚守贞洁的品质以及她从信件中读到的文学才华深深打动。此时，他的妹妹强烈反对这桩婚事，而帕梅拉也开始写作，探讨爱情和婚姻的真谛等更深层次的问题。

Upon publication, Pamela was a popular success, which meant that readers all over England and even France (the French polymath and encyclopedist Denis Diderot was inspired by Pamela to try novel-writing as well) could make up their own minds about Pamela's logic. The great innovation of Richardson's epistolary form was a sense of intimacy and immediacy. Modern readers might find the idea that Pamela could retire to her closet and write at length about her adventures, her feelings, and her ideas even in the midst of being pursued entirely unbelievable, but Richardson's contemporaries were willing to suspend disbelief for the sake of enjoying Pamela's spirited resistance. In some sense, an epistolary novel is like a movie—we seem to be watching it while it is happening, and it therefore gains an extra degree of unpredictability and suspense. Other types of first-person novels are necessarily written after the fact, which means that the narrator has survived, and assimilated his experiences at least to a degree. The epistolary novel can more closely resemble the actual passage of consciousness through time, especially in an epistolary age, when average people are in the habit of regularly reporting on their thoughts and reading the reports of their friends. There is no denying that Pamela and her novel are simultaneously ridiculous and compelling. Richardson's novel also had a strong (and possibly unintended) political dimension.

《帕梅拉》出版后大获成功，这意味着全英国乃至法国的读者（法国博学家、百科全书编纂者狄德罗也受到《帕梅拉》的启发，尝试创作小说）都可以自行判断帕梅拉的逻辑。理查森书信体小说的伟大创新之处在于它营造了一种亲密感和即时感。现代读者或许会觉得，帕梅拉即便在被追捕的情况下，也能躲进衣橱里，长篇大论地记录她的冒险经历、感受和想法，这简直难以置信。但理查森的同代人却愿意暂时放下怀疑，去欣赏帕梅拉那充满活力的反抗精神。从某种意义上说，书信体小说就像一部电影——我们仿佛在观看正在发生的一切，因此，它增添了一份额外的不可预测性和悬念。其他类型的第一人称小说必然是事后创作的，这意味着叙述者已经幸存下来，并且至少在一定程度上消化了自己的经历。书信体小说则更能贴近意识在时间长河中的真实流转，尤其是在书信时代，普通人习惯于定期汇报自己的想法并阅读朋友的来信。不可否认，帕梅拉和她的小说既荒诞又引人入胜。理查森的小说也具有强烈的（或许是无意的）政治色彩。

The basic question Pamela asks is: do I belong to my master, or do I belong to God? Is her virtue hers to dispose of, her master's to take, or theirs to preserve? When the subject turns to love, do property and class issues trump emotional ones? Has Pamela proved herself and her arguments? Pamela is openly and directly about power: what are its limits and how are they to be maintained? The very epistolary unfolding of Pamela's dilemma intensifies the importance of these questions—after all, Moll Flanders and Roxana have already lived their lives. Their task as they set down their adventures is to decide whether and how to repent—to decide the meaning of their adventures. The outcome of Pamela's story is not yet decided as she is writing, so part of her task is to come up with strategies for outwitting Mr. B., at first, and then later, reasons for deciding whether his reformation is real. All of these questions, since they are about power, implicitly link the personal and the political; as soon as Pamela gained a multitude of readers, the issues became explicitly political, as highly charged issues in popular novels tend to do. If a reader were sympathetic to Pamela's defiance, might he or she be sympathetic to the defiance of other women to the demands of property and class, not to mention to the sexual urges of men?

帕梅拉提出的基本问题是：我属于我的主人，还是属于上帝？她的美德是她自己可以随意处置的，还是她主人可以夺取的，抑或是由他们共同守护的？当话题转向爱情时，财产和阶级问题是否凌驾于情感之上？帕梅拉是否证明了自己和她的论点？帕梅拉坦率而直接地探讨权力：权力的界限是什么？又该如何维护？帕梅拉困境的这种书信体展开方式，反而凸显了这些问题的重要性——毕竟，莫尔·弗兰德斯和罗克珊娜的人生已经过去。她们记录下自己的冒险经历，是为了决定是否以及如何忏悔——决定她们冒险的意义。帕梅拉写作时，故事的结局尚未确定，因此，她的一部分任务是想出策略来智胜B先生，然后是思考如何判断他的悔改是否真实。所有这些问题，由于都与权力有关，因此都隐含地将个人与政治联系起来； 《帕梅拉》一经拥有众多读者，其主题便立刻变得具有明显的政治性，这在通俗小说中屡见不鲜。如果读者同情帕梅拉的反抗精神，那么他或她是否也会同情其他女性反抗财产和阶级的要求，更不用说反抗男性的性欲呢？

One of Samuel Richardson's contemporaries who was not impressed was Henry Fielding. Fielding began as a playwright, but English theaters of his day were subject to licensing laws, and as a result of one of Fielding's satiric attacks upon the government, his theater was closed. He turned to writing novels, and his first effort was a pastiche that mocked Pamela , titled Shamela , that picked up on some of the sillier aspects of Pamela's story. Fielding had enough success with his short novel that he decided to try another approach, so he wrote Joseph Andrews , allegedly the story of Pamela's brother, also a servant, who has his own troubles with Lady B., Mr. B.'s lascivious sister.

塞缪尔·理查森的同代人中，有一位对理查森的作品不以为然，那就是亨利·菲尔丁。菲尔丁最初是一位剧作家，但当时的英国剧院都受制于许可证制度，由于菲尔丁的一部讽刺政府的作品，他的剧院被关闭了。于是他转而创作小说，他的第一部作品是戏仿《帕梅拉》的《沙梅拉》，这部小说模仿了《帕梅拉》中一些荒诞不经的情节。菲尔丁凭借这部短篇小说获得了一定的成功，于是他决定尝试另一种创作方式，创作了《约瑟夫·安德鲁斯》。这部小说讲述的是帕梅拉的弟弟约瑟夫·安德鲁斯的故事，他也是一名仆人，与B先生风流成性的妹妹B夫人之间有着一段纠葛。

Fielding's masterpiece, though, owes more to Don Quixote , a book Fielding loved. In Tom Jones , his eponymous hero, Tom, is exiled from the estate of his foster father, Squire Allworthy, and forced to seek his fortune on the road to London. At the same time, Squire Western, All-worthy's neighbor, decides to force his daughter Sophia to marry All-worthy's nephew (and Tom's enemy) Blifil, to consolidate the two properties. Tom is an attractive young man, and encounters (unlike Quixote) several challenges to his virtue both on the road and among the worldly aristocrats in London. Finally he finds himself in danger of hanging, but just in time, all of Blifil's schemes are unraveled, and Tom (and Sophia) are saved. As a dramatist, it was natural for Fielding to import conventions of the English theater into the novel, and he did, including wit and comedy, an exciting plot that turns on the villainy of Tom's antagonist, and also the standard comic ending—love, reconciliation, and prosperity (which in pre–Industrial Revolution England meant real estate). Fielding's England was a manly, robust, rough place not that different from Cervantes's Spain, except that a pastoral paradise was to be found in England, among the country estates of such responsible and thoughtful members of the gentry as Squire All-worthy. Fielding was by no means progressive, though he was skeptical of religion and leery of forcing young women to marry against their will. Above all, he was humane. He recognized the temptation for people of privilege to abuse their privileges and overlook their obligations; he portrayed members of all classes acting not only foolishly and ridiculously but also coarsely, selfishly, and brutishly. His dearest virtue (the one that in Tom himself balances all his faults and accounts for some of his mistakes) was openheartedness. But the purpose of the plot of Tom Jones is never to spread the wealth around—it is always to consolidate (country) property and attach it to right feeling. If a certain amount of fun can be had in the bargain, so much the better. Because Fielding was classically educated, and because he made a strenuous effort to do so, he raised the tone of the novel by calling Tom Jones a “mock epic” and including extensive commentary that explicitly linked the story to classical models. Later novelists could read Tom Jones (and Fielding's other novels) with both pleasure and self-satisfaction—he was respectable.

然而，菲尔丁的这部杰作更多地受到了他挚爱的《堂吉诃德》的影响。在《汤姆·琼斯》中，主人公汤姆被养父奥尔沃西乡绅逐出庄园，被迫踏上前往伦敦的旅程，寻求自己的命运。与此同时，奥尔沃西的邻居韦斯特恩乡绅为了巩固两家庄园的所有权，决定强迫女儿索菲娅嫁给奥尔沃西的侄子（也是汤姆的死敌）布利菲尔。汤姆英俊潇洒，与堂吉诃德不同，他在旅途中以及在伦敦的世故贵族中都遭遇了诸多道德上的挑战。最终，他甚至面临绞刑的危险，但就在千钧一发之际，布利菲尔的阴谋败露，汤姆（和索菲娅）得以幸免于难。作为一名剧作家，菲尔丁将英国戏剧的惯例引入小说创作中是自然而然的，他也确实这样做了，包括机智幽默、扣人心弦的情节（围绕汤姆的对手的邪恶行径展开），以及标准的喜剧结局——爱情、和解与繁荣（在工业革命前的英国，繁荣通常意味着房地产）。菲尔丁笔下的英国是一个充满男子气概、强健粗犷的地方，与塞万提斯的西班牙并无太大区别，只是在英国，在像奥尔沃西乡绅这样负责任、深思熟虑的绅士们的乡间庄园里，存在着一片田园牧歌般的乐土。菲尔丁绝非进步主义者，尽管他对宗教持怀疑态度，并且对强迫年轻女子违背意愿结婚的做法感到担忧。最重要的是，他充满人道主义精神。他意识到特权阶层容易滥用特权、忽视自身义务；他笔下的各个阶层的人，不仅会做出愚蠢可笑的行为，还会展现出粗鲁、自私和野蛮的一面。他最珍视的美德（汤姆身上弥补了他所有缺点并能解释他某些错误的美德）是坦诚。但《汤姆·琼斯》的情节目的从来都不是为了分配财富——它始终是为了巩固（乡村）财产并将其与正确的情感联系起来。如果还能从中获得一些乐趣，那就更好了。由于菲尔丁接受过古典教育，并且为此付出了不懈的努力，他将《汤姆·琼斯》称为“戏仿史诗”，并加入了大量的评论，明确地将故事与古典典范联系起来，从而提升了这部小说的格调。后来的小说家们可以带着愉悦和自豪感阅读《汤姆·琼斯》（以及菲尔丁的其他小说）——他是一位受人尊敬的作家。

In 1759 , Laurence Sterne, too, came to novel-writing from another career. He was a clergyman, accustomed to writing sermons, discussing morals and values, and finding general lessons in specific examples of human behavior. But Sterne was an odd duck and not terribly successful in his clerical role. He was also writing at a time when what was called “feeling” but perhaps what we would call “sentimentality” was replacing sharp satire as the fashion. Defoe's Roxana , for example, still in print, was extensively rewritten by late eighteenth-century publishers of new editions to mitigate Roxana's seeming indifference toward her children and her less than satisfactory repentence at the end. And whereas Richardson went from Pamela's two-volume rape in 1740 to Clarissa's seven-volume rape in 1748 , investigating ever more carefully and fully both Clarissa's point of view and that of Lovelace, her abductor, Sterne's protagonists, Mr. Shandy (the father of Tristram) and Uncle Toby, were hardly interested in sex at all. Uncle Toby, in fact, who comes more and more into prominence as the novel proceeds, is of a singularly modest turn of mind, much more interested in playing an elaborate form of toy soldiers in his garden than paying attention to the widow over the hedge. What Sterne cared about, what constituted his innovation, was human, and especially male, eccentricity. Defoe's characters, Fielding's characters, and the characters in Pamela were intended, at least at the beginning, to typify or represent their categories. As the plots of the novels developed, the protagonists individualized themselves, but the dramatic tradition was so strong in England that thinking of human psychology as typology was automatic—in a drama, the actors inhabit the characters and can't help but individualize them, so the author can focus more on the action than on shades of human uniqueness. Sterne, however, as a writer of sermons, did not organize his characters in the same way, and he was not so attached to plotting as an organizational method. He presented his characters as eccentric from the beginning; in fact, the action of Tristram Shandy progresses more and more slowly in part because Sterne's (or the narrator's) theory of psychology is based on uniqueness—the unique circumstances of Tristram's conception (his father cries out in annoyance at the moment of ejaculation) and birth (the doctor presses the baby's nose with the forceps, thereby, by symbolic extension, damaging his penis or his libido). Sterne's ideas have their origins in the vagaries of thought and the contingencies of circumstance. If all novels have two sides—the public and the private—the privacy Sterne explores is even more extreme than that of Richardson because it is more idiosyncratic. Unlike Pamela, Clarissa, and Lovelace, Mr. Shandy, Uncle Toby, and the narrator are not attempting to conform at all. In any novel, what is most original is always what is most intimate (though the converse is not true—often intimacies are related in quite conventional ways, importing the public into the private and showing that an author's ideas of intimacy aren't very original). Sterne significantly extended the private, philosophical side of the novel, as, in A Journal of the Plague Year , Defoe extended the public, documentary side of the novel. The very fact that few authors have followed these two models subsequently shows how demanding and unusual they are, and how much more readily the novel shapes itself to the fairly equal representation of inner life and outer life, of the individual and the group.

1759年，劳伦斯·斯特恩也从另一个职业转行成为小说家。他曾是一名牧师，习惯于撰写布道词，探讨道德价值观，并从具体的人类行为案例中汲取普遍教训。但斯特恩是个特立独行的人，在牧师岗位上也并不成功。他写作的时代，一种被称为“情感”（或许我们今天会称之为“感伤”）的风格正在取代尖锐的讽刺，成为当时的时尚。例如，笛福的小说《罗克珊娜》至今仍在出版，但十八世纪末的新版本出版商对其进行了大量改写，以淡化罗克珊娜对子女的冷漠以及她结尾处不够令人满意的忏悔。理查森从1740年两卷本的《帕梅拉》到1748年七卷本的《克拉丽莎》，不断深入细致地探讨克拉丽莎和绑架者洛夫莱斯的视角，而斯特恩笔下的主人公——尚迪先生（特里斯特拉姆的父亲）和托比叔叔——却对性几乎毫无兴趣。事实上，随着小说的推进，托比叔叔的戏份越来越多，他性格极其谦逊，比起关注篱笆那边的寡妇，他更热衷于在花园里玩一种复杂的玩具兵游戏。斯特恩关注的，也是他创新之处所在，是人性的，尤其是男性的怪癖。笛福、菲尔丁以及《帕梅拉》中的人物，至少在最初，都是为了体现或代表各自的类型。随着小说情节的发展，主人公们逐渐展现出各自的个性，但英国的戏剧传统根深蒂固，人们自然而然地将人类心理视为一种类型学——在戏剧中，演员们融入角色，不可避免地赋予角色独特的个性，因此作者可以更专注于情节本身，而非人类独特性的细微差别。然而，作为布道家的斯特恩，并没有以同样的方式塑造人物，他也不像戏剧作家那样执着于将情节作为一种组织方法。他从一开始就将笔下的人物塑造得古怪离奇；事实上，《项狄传》的情节进展越来越缓慢，部分原因在于斯特恩（或者说是叙述者）的心理学理论建立在独特性之上——特里斯特拉姆受孕（他的父亲在射精的那一刻恼怒地叫喊）和出生（医生用产钳按压婴儿的鼻子，这象征性地延伸到损伤他的阴茎或性欲）的独特境遇。斯特恩的思想源于变幻莫测的思维和偶然的境遇。如果说所有小说都具有两面性——公共层面和私人层面——那么斯特恩所探讨的私人层面比理查森的更为极端，因为它更具个性。与帕梅拉、克拉丽莎和洛夫莱斯不同，尚迪先生、托比叔叔和叙述者丝毫没有试图循规蹈矩。在任何小说中，最原创的总是最私密的（尽管反之则不然——私密关系往往以相当传统的方式呈现，将公共层面引入私人层面，表明作者对私密的理解并非十分新颖）。斯特恩显著地拓展了小说的私人和哲学层面，正如笛福在《瘟疫年代日记》中拓展了小说的公共和纪实层面一样。很少有作家后来遵循这两种模式，这恰恰说明了它们有多么要求高、多么不寻常，也说明了小说更容易塑造出相对平等地展现内心生活和外部生活、个人和群体的形象。

By the time of Sterne's death, the novel was fully invented and, indeed, franchised. It was a popular and exciting literary form. Enterprising dramatists, poets, and intellectuals were frequently moved to try writing a novel or two. More important, novels were regularly published that became all the rage—sometimes because they were so shocking, at other times because they were so funny or moving. Translations were common, so that novels such as Don Quixote and Robinson Crusoe were available to numerous readers who lived in places and at times entirely remote from Spain in 1610 or London in 1719 . Later authors would go on to expand the scope of the novel, to refine its rhetoric, to challenge its readers, to modify how quality in the novel should be defined, but lengthy written prose narratives with protagonists, narratives that regularly alternated between depicting the actions and the inner lives of their characters, narratives that focused on the adventures of individuals and their context within small groups and large groups, narratives that defined reality sometimes as objective and sometimes as subjective, narratives with complex plots and narratives with hardly any plots at all had made their appearance and did not have to be invented again.

斯特恩去世时，小说这种文学形式已经发展成熟，甚至可以说已经形成了一种商业模式。它是一种流行且令人兴奋的文学形式。许多富有进取心的剧作家、诗人以及知识分子都跃跃欲试，尝试创作一两部小说。更重要的是，当时涌现出许多风靡一时的小说——有时是因为它们内容惊世骇俗，有时则是因为它们幽默风趣或感人至深。翻译作品十分普遍，因此像《堂吉诃德》和《鲁滨逊漂流记》这样的长篇小说，在1610年为众多居住在远离西班牙的地方，甚至在1719年为远离伦敦的读者所熟知。后来的作家们不断拓展小说的范畴，精炼其修辞手法，挑战读者的认知，并修正小说质量的定义。然而，那些篇幅较长、以主人公为主角的散文叙事作品，那些经常在描绘人物行为和内心世界之间交替的叙事作品，那些聚焦于个人冒险经历及其在小群体或大群体中所处环境的叙事作品，那些有时以客观视角定义现实、有时以主观视角定义现实的叙事作品，那些情节复杂或几乎没有情节的叙事作品，都已经出现，无需再被重新发明。

# ↩

5. The Psychology of the Novel

5. 小说心理学

Whereupon this worthy knight, whose swordplay was doubtless on a par with his storytelling, began to recite his tale, which in itself was indeed excellent. But by repeating the same phrases, and recapitulating sections of the plot, and every so often declaring that he had “made a mess of that bit,” and regularly confusing the names of the characters, he ruined it completely. Moreover, his mode of delivery was completely out of keeping with the characters and the incidents he was describing, so that it was painful for Madonna Oretta to listen to him. She began to perspire freely and her heart missed several beats, as though she had fallen ill and was about to give up the ghost.

于是，这位剑术精湛、叙事能力同样出众的骑士开始讲述他的故事，故事本身的确精彩绝伦。然而，他反复赘述情节，时不时地自嘲“这部分讲错了”，还经常把人物的名字搞混，最终把故事彻底毁了。更糟糕的是，他的讲述方式与他所描述的人物和事件完全不符，以至于奥雷塔夫人听得十分痛苦。她开始大汗淋漓，心跳也漏跳了几拍，仿佛病入膏肓，即将离世。

— GIOVANNI BOCCACCIO , The Decameron

——乔凡尼·薄伽丘，《十日谈》

T he basic substance of imaginative literature (novels, plays, poetry) is not reason but emotion, which is expressed not by the denotations of words, nor the grammar of the sentences, but through the connotations and colorations of the words as employed by the author's style. Once a story has been put into words, people can analyze it, ponder it, hold it in their minds, come to know it, change it willingly, learn from it. But it exists not as words written in books but as images with feelings attached. To read and then reread a work is to reattach remembered images to unremembered words and to experience again (and sometimes even more sharply) the pleasure of the inchoate becoming specific. Both writer and reader experience the same basic pleasure—something in one form in the mind takes another form on the page, something in one form on the page takes another form in the mind. This is the essential pleasure of literature, ideas going into and out of words over and over and over, any time the reader opens a book, or the author takes up a pen.

想象文学（小说、戏剧、诗歌）的本质并非理性，而是情感。这种情感的表达并非通过词语的字面意义或句子的语法，而是通过作者运用文字风格所赋予的内涵和色彩。一旦故事被诉诸笔端，人们便可以分析它、思考它、将其铭记于心、了解它、随意地改变它、从中学习。但它并非以书页上的文字形式存在，而是以承载情感的图像形式存在。阅读并重读一部作品，就是将记忆中的图像与遗忘的文字重新连接起来，再次体验（有时甚至更加强烈地体验）那种由模糊不清变为具体的愉悦感。作家和读者都体验着同样的基本乐趣——脑海中的一种形式在纸面上呈现出另一种形式，纸面上的一种形式又在脑海中呈现出另一种形式。这便是文学的本质乐趣：思想在文字中反复穿梭，无论读者何时翻开书页，或作者何时拿起笔，皆是如此。

The sheer length and accessibility of the novel, though, changes a reader's experience of this process in specific ways, because the number of words and their connections expand toward the infinite—ideally, in a hundred-thousand-word book, every word could relate to every other word in some unique way, and no conventional forms (as in poetry) or interpreters (actors and directors) are present to limit or guide the reader's intuition. Scholars and critics have despaired of coming up with a method that is various enough for understanding the novel, and their despair is warranted—in a novel such as Rebecca West's The Fountain Overflows , where every word seems to relate to and reflect upon every other word, building layers of meaning and feeling that seem to shift continuously, all critical methods are of only modest usefulness. A lively intuition, though, can make it all out to a satisfying degree. Any reader's list of her ten favorite novels exhausts the interpretive capacities of generations of critics, but is readily accessible, over and over, to the reader herself. In fact, the accessibility of the novel renders critical interpretations superfluous to the reader/author interaction. A novel may be read on all sorts of levels, as articles and controversies in scholarly journals show, but it can be enjoyably and correctly read just to see what happens next and to enjoy the company of the author, the narrator, and the characters.

然而，小说的篇幅和易读性却以独特的方式改变了读者对这一过程的体验，因为字数及其关联几乎无限扩展——理想情况下，在一本十万字的书中，每个词都可能以某种独特的方式与其他词相关联，而且没有任何传统形式（如诗歌）或诠释者（如演员和导演）来限制或引导读者的直觉。学者和评论家们一直苦于找不到一种足够多样化的方法来理解这部小说，他们的失望并非毫无道理——在像丽贝卡·韦斯特的《喷泉溢出》这样的小说中，每个词似乎都与其他词相互关联、相互映照，层层叠加的意义和情感似乎在不断变化，所有批评方法都只能发挥有限的作用。然而，敏锐的直觉却能将这一切解读到令人满意的程度。任何读者列出的十部最爱小说，都穷尽了数代评论家的诠释能力，但对读者自身而言，却可以反复阅读，触手可及。事实上，小说的易读性使得批判性解读对于读者与作者的互动而言显得多余。正如学术期刊上的文章和争论所表明的那样，小说可以从各种层面进行解读，但仅仅为了了解接下来的情节发展，享受与作者、叙述者和人物相处的时光，也可以愉快而正确地阅读小说。

Each of the elements of the definition of the novel has an effect on the psychology of reading the novel. For example, narrative voice is social, and so the psychology of the novel is a psychology of relationships, even if the novel is about an isolated loner such as Robinson Crusoe, or Franz Kafka's Josef K. in The Trial. Since the mere existence of the narrative voice implies a teller, a listener, and other beings who are being told about and implies, therefore, relationships, every reader comes to every novel with plenty of experience that bears upon the reading of a novel. The qualities of the voice are automatically present—is it warm, friendly, knowledgeable, soothing, charming, intelligent, self-obsessed, droning, bombastic, mechanical, silly, beside the point, suspect? The reader perceives and reacts to these qualities instantly, without thinking. If she likes the voice and feels comfortable with it, she may not actually think at any time, except to process the characters and events of the narrative, but such processing isn't exactly cogitating. A novel that is a comfortable fit with the reader, whose characters and narrative voice the reader is drawn to and enjoys, whose jokes the reader laughs at, and whose insights the reader understands and appreciates, arouses a sense of friendliness. With such a novel—let's say Persuasion —the reader's responses feel harmonious and agreeable. She recognizes the crass insensitivity of Anne Elliot's father and sister and the tediousness of Anne's old-maid existence; she understands how the naval officers and their wives offer a welcome breath of exotic practicality to Anne's social life; she follows the subtle changes in Anne's feelings toward Captain Wentworth; she is in sync with the play of Jane Austen's wit. When she retreats from the flow of the narrative into judgment, it is to appreciate scenes or phrases or even to marvel at them. The relationship the reader has with such a novel feels reciprocal though it is not. The reader is supplying both the give and the take that furnish such a reading experience with a feeling of conversational intimacy. Of course, the author is as familiar as the reader with social intercourse; he (or in this case, she) is using the forms and tones of social intercourse to communicate the ideas in her novel because she cannot help doing so. When an author writes, she is communicating with herself; when a reader reads, she is communicating with herself, but when she feels a sense of kinship with a particular novel, she feels that the author is communicating with her.

小说定义的每个要素都会对读者的阅读心理产生影响。例如，叙述声音具有社会性，因此，小说的心理本质上是人际关系的心理，即便小说的主角是像鲁滨逊·克鲁索那样孤僻的独行侠，或是卡夫卡笔下《审判》中的约瑟夫·K。由于叙述声音的存在本身就意味着叙述者、倾听者以及其他被叙述的对象，进而暗示着人际关系，因此，每位读者在阅读小说之前都会带着丰富的经验，而这些经验会影响他们对小说的理解。叙述声音的特质是自然而然地呈现的——它是温暖的、友好的、博学的、令人舒缓的、迷人的、睿智的、自恋的、单调的、夸张的、机械的、愚蠢的、离题的还是可疑的？读者会立即感知并对这些特质做出反应，而无需思考。如果她喜欢这种叙述声音，并且感觉舒适，那么她可能根本不会思考，除了处理叙事中的人物和事件之外，但这种处理并不等同于深思熟虑。一部与读者契合的小说，如果读者被书中的人物和叙述声音所吸引并乐在其中，能够开怀大笑，理解并欣赏其中的洞见，便会唤起一种亲切感。读这样一部小说——比如《劝导》——读者的反应会感到和谐愉悦。她能体会到安妮·艾略特的父亲和姐姐的粗鲁无情，以及安妮老处女生活的乏味；她明白海军军官及其妻子如何为安妮的社交生活带来一股令人欣喜的异域实用主义气息；她能感受到安妮对温特沃斯上校情感的微妙变化；她能与简·奥斯汀的机智对话产生共鸣。当她暂时放下叙事，进行评判时，是为了欣赏某些场景或语句，甚至惊叹于它们的精彩。读者与这部小说之间的关系看似互惠，实则不然。读者在阅读过程中既给予也接受，这种互动赋予了阅读体验一种对话般的亲密感。当然，作者和读者一样熟悉社交互动；她（或者在这个例子中，是她）运用社交互动的形式和语气来传达小说中的思想，因为她情不自禁地这样做。作者写作时，是在与自己交流；读者阅读时，也是在与自己交流；但当她与某部小说产生共鸣时，她会觉得作者正在与她对话。

If the reader doesn't like the voice, though, she starts to think, should I keep reading this, or should I stop? She weighs her boredom or dislike against what she is getting from the novel. With a novel such as Vanity Fair , for example, where the tone of the narrative voice is very cynical and where the characters may be hard to like (and the drawings, by Thackeray himself, might be unappealing), she withdraws a bit from the experience of the novel (maybe even while continuing to read) and concocts an argument about whether to go on and for how long. After another ten or twenty pages, perhaps, she puts the book down and walks away. Sometime later, she comes back and sees the book. Then she makes another decision whether to pick the book up and start reading again. This decision is not unlike choosing to call someone who isn't a bosom friend—will the payoff for picking the novel up again outweigh the discomfort already experienced (and already associated with everything about the novel, including the picture on the cover and the color and smoothness of the paper)? If she picks it up again and goes on with it, she reaffirms her commitment, but this can work in two ways. One way, of course, is that she presses ahead to the end of the novel and finishes it, adding to whatever pleasures she ultimately gets from it a sense of accomplishment and relief. The other is that as her commitment deepens, she comes to resent the novel more and more for being so intransigently itself, and this resentment might cause her to throw down the novel in disgust after two hundred or three hundred pages. If she had simply never picked the novel up again after the first few pages, she might never have felt resentment or disgust at all, just a vague sense that the novel didn't have anything to do with her. Every novel, every narrator can't help offering the promise of a relationship.

然而，如果读者不喜欢叙述者的语气，她就会开始思考：我应该继续读下去吗？还是就此打住？她会权衡自己的厌倦或厌恶感与小说带给她的感受。例如，像《名利场》这样的小说，叙述者的语气非常愤世嫉俗，人物也难以讨喜（就连萨克雷本人绘制的插图也可能不吸引人），读者会暂时从小说体验中抽离出来（甚至可能在继续阅读的同时），并反复斟酌是否要继续读下去，以及要读多久。或许又读了十来页，她便放下书，走开了。过了一段时间，她又回来，看到了那本书。然后，她再次决定是否要拿起书继续读下去。这个决定就像是选择给一个并非知己的朋友打电话——重新拿起这本小说的回报是否能抵消已经感受到的不适（这种不适感已经与小说的方方面面联系起来，包括封面图片、纸张的颜色和触感）？如果她再次拿起小说并继续读下去，就相当于重申了自己的决心，但这可能会产生两种结果。一种结果当然是，她坚持读完小说，在最终获得的乐趣之外，又增添了一份成就感和解脱感。另一种结果则是，随着她投入的加深，她会越来越反感小说的固执己见，这种反感可能会让她在读了两三百页后厌恶地扔掉小说。如果她只读了几页就再也没拿起过这本小说，她可能根本不会感到任何反感或厌恶，只会隐约觉得这本小说与她无关。每部小说，每个叙述者都忍不住要提出一段感情的承诺。

Of course, a reader may begin by disliking Vanity Fair but be won over in the end to liking it very much. The novelist has many pleasures to offer—the unusual pleasure of the exotic, the intellectual pleasure of historical understanding, the humane pleasure of psychological insight into one or more characters, the simple pleasure of entertainment and suspense, the exuberant pleasure of laughter and trickery, the guilty pleasure of gossip, the tempting pleasure of secrecy and intimacy, the confessional pleasure of acknowledged sin and attempted redemption, the polemical pleasure of indignation, the rigorous pleasure of intellectual analysis, the reassuring pleasure of identification with one's nation or people, and the vicarious pleasure of romance. The reader may gradually set aside the discomfort of incompatibility and come to enjoy any or all of these pleasures by the end of the novel, and if the incompatibility stems more from unfamiliarity than anything else, then she has many hundreds of pages to get used to the novelist's way of thinking and of expressing himself.

当然，读者或许一开始并不喜欢《名利场》，但最终却会被它深深吸引。小说家能带给读者诸多乐趣——异域风情带来的非凡愉悦，历史知识带来的理性享受，对一个或多个角色心理洞察带来的人文关怀，娱乐和悬念带来的纯粹乐趣，欢笑和诡计带来的酣畅淋漓的快感，八卦带来的罪恶快感，秘密和亲密带来的诱人诱惑，坦诚面对罪孽并试图救赎带来的忏悔快感，义愤填膺带来的辩论快感，严谨的理性分析带来的愉悦，对国家或民族认同带来的慰藉快感，以及浪漫爱情带来的替代性快感。读者可能会逐渐克服不协调带来的不适感，并在小说结尾享受到其中一项或多项乐趣；如果这种不协调感更多地源于不熟悉而非其他原因，那么她还有数百页的篇幅来适应小说家的思维方式和表达方式。

If the incompatibility comes from a disagreement in opinions, then the reader has hundreds of pages to understand and to learn to agree with the author's arguments. The author can employ different sorts of logic—the logic of cause and effect as expressed in the scenes; the logic of character—whether thoughts and actions hang together and make sense; the logic of theme—whether the author's argument about how the world works makes sense; the logic of structure—whether the parts of the novel work together. There is also a logic of style—how the diction and grammar the author uses at the beginning of the novel prepare the reader for the diction and grammar he uses in later sections (an example of success on this score is Anthony Trollope's The Last Chronicle of Barset , in which the reader is prepared by the way the author discusses the intricacies of a troubled but loving marriage at the beginning of the novel for his analysis of a troubled and loveless marriage at the end).

如果矛盾源于观点分歧，那么读者就需要阅读数百页才能理解并认同作者的论点。作者可以运用不同的逻辑——场景中体现的因果逻辑；人物逻辑——思想和行为是否连贯一致且合情合理；主题逻辑——作者关于世界运行方式的论述是否合理；结构逻辑——小说各部分是否协调一致。此外，还有一种风格逻辑——作者在小说开头使用的措辞和语法如何为读者理解其后文的措辞和语法做好准备（安东尼·特罗洛普的《巴塞特的最后编年史》在这方面就是一个很好的例子，小说开头作者对一段充满波折却又充满爱意的婚姻的复杂描写，为结尾对一段充满波折且缺乏爱意的婚姻的分析做好了铺垫）。

The reader may recognize that the author has set out to manipulate her in a certain way, to use one or more of his available logics to persuade her of his ontological theory—Thackeray may have intended to show the inexorable decline of honor among Englishmen of breeding and education—but as the materials of his novel coalesce, she recognizes elements that are contradictory, that the author didn't intend, hadn't thought of, and possibly never understood. In Vanity Fair , Becky Sharp disappears ignominiously toward the end of the narrative; unlike Lily Bart, in Edith Wharton's The House of Mirth , she is not even allowed the dignity of a tragic death. Without her, the energy of the novel dissipates and the novel's only possible hero, the faithful William Dobbin, discovers himself obscurely dissatisfied with his happy ending. Although Thackeray portrays Becky as a selfish arriviste, a pathological liar who is perhaps capable of murder, and an almost certainly unchaste adulteress, she seems to have certain qualities of insight, intelligence, and vitality not allowed any other character. Thackeray seems to like her in spite of himself, as if only conventional propriety is preventing him from awarding her some final triumph. Did Thackeray intend such a combination of vice and energy? Did he even understand Becky's grandeur? Was she a product of his art or an unintended consequence? A reader can find herself beguiled by the confluence of the authorial intentions and lucky accidents of composition as readily as any other pleasure.

读者或许会意识到作者有意操控她，运用他惯用的逻辑来说服她接受他的本体论理论——萨克雷或许意在展现英国上流社会人士荣誉的无情衰落——但随着小说素材的逐渐融合，她会发现其中存在一些自相矛盾的元素，这些元素并非作者的本意，也并非他所预料，甚至可能他自己也从未理解过。在《名利场》中，贝基·夏普在故事结尾黯然离去；与伊迪丝·华顿的《欢乐之家》中的莉莉·巴特不同，她甚至连悲剧性的死亡都得不到应有的尊严。没有了她，小说的能量便消散殆尽，而小说中唯一可能的英雄，忠诚的威廉·多宾，也发现自己对自己的幸福结局感到莫名的不满。尽管萨克雷将贝基描绘成一个自私的暴发户、一个病态的骗子（或许有杀人倾向），以及一个几乎可以肯定不贞的通奸者，但她似乎拥有其他角色所不具备的洞察力、智慧和活力。萨克雷似乎不由自主地喜欢上了她，仿佛只有世俗的礼仪阻止了他最终给予她某种胜利。萨克雷是否刻意塑造了这样一个兼具恶习与活力的角色？他是否真正理解贝基的伟大之处？她是他艺术的产物，还是一个意料之外的结果？读者很容易就会被作者的意图和创作中的偶然巧合所吸引，如同享受其他任何乐趣一样。

Some authors deploy their modes of seduction more gracefully than others, but what they are all trying to achieve in the reader is what length itself demands: willing suspension of disbelief. There are two halves to this equation: “willing” and “suspension of disbelief.” It is far more difficult to make the second half work than the first, because no amount of plausibility really overcomes the definition of a novel as fiction.

有些作者比其他作者更擅长运用各种诱惑手段，但他们最终都试图让读者达到同样的目的，而这正是小说篇幅本身所要求的：让读者心甘情愿地暂时放下怀疑。这个等式包含两部分：“心甘情愿”和“暂时放下怀疑”。让“暂时放下怀疑”比让“心甘情愿”难得多，因为无论情节多么合情合理，都无法真正改变小说作为虚构作品的本质。

Usually, what puts a reader into a state of willingness is an interesting assertion, such as “It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife” (Pride and Prejudice) , or “Ours is essentially a tragic age, so we refuse to take it tragically” (Lady Chatterley's Lover) , or “It was the best of times, it was the worst of times” (A Tale of Two Cities). But a character may also do an interesting or appealing thing, such as “Jewel and I come up from the field, following the path in single file” (As I Lay Dying) , or “Buck Mulligan came from the stairhead, bearing a bowl of lather on which a mirror and a razor lay crossed” (Ulysses). At the beginning of “The Metamorphosis,” Kafka has Gregor Samsa change into a bug, perhaps one of the most intriguing first premises in literature. However, in teaching this story twenty-two times to undergraduate students, I found that out of every thirty students, one or two were simply unwilling to believe that Gregor could turn into a bug, and for those students, the story offered no charms at all. It was not that the other students believed that a man in Prague in 1915 turned into a bug; it was that they enjoyed the idea and suspended disbelief, and once they imagined Gregor's bugness, they were open to every other idea that Kafka had to offer.

通常，能激发读者兴趣的，是一些引人入胜的论断，例如“凡是有钱的单身汉，都渴望娶妻”（《傲慢与偏见》），或者“我们身处一个悲剧的时代，所以我们拒绝以悲剧的眼光看待它”（《查泰莱夫人的情人》），又或者“这是最好的时代，也是最坏的时代”（《双城记》）。但人物的某些行为也可能引人入胜，例如“我和朱厄尔从田野里出来，沿着小路排成一列”（《我弥留之际》），或者“巴克·穆里根从楼梯口走出来，手里端着一碗泡沫，碗上交叉放着一面镜子和一把剃刀”（《尤利西斯》）。在《变形记》的开头，卡夫卡让格里高尔·萨姆沙变成了一只虫子，这或许是文学史上最引人入胜的开篇之一。然而，在给本科生讲授这篇故事二十二次后，我发现每三十个学生中总有一两个不愿意相信格里高尔会变成虫子，对这些学生来说，这个故事毫无吸引力。倒不是说其他学生相信1915年布拉格的一个人真的会变成虫子；而是他们喜欢这个想法，并且愿意暂时放下怀疑。一旦他们想象出格里高尔变成虫子的样子，他们就能欣然接受卡夫卡提出的其他所有想法。

Willing suspension of disbelief is a strange state of mind—reading nonfiction does not require it and neither does reading poetry, since both are based on logical argument. Many intelligent and educated persons resist it entirely or yield to it only for a brief time, in the darkness of a theater, accompanied by other members of an audience—the world is full of people who are rather proud that they don't read novels. Publishers often lament that the audience for novels is narrowing, and especially that it is losing men. A literary education not only enlarges a reader's willingness to suspend disbelief by extending her range of pleasures, it also strengthens her ability to enter the meditative state, and to be receptive to the influence of another human mind, because it is a state of contemplation that is essential to the true appreciation of the novel. While all art forms promote this state of receptivity, with the novel it is uniquely sustained—it is not possible, for example, to contemplate a painting for ten or twelve hours, the amount of time the average reader would need to read a five-hundred-page novel. Few dramatic productions run for more than four hours, and even that length of time is considered daring. How long is Wagner's Ring cycle? Fifteen hours is perhaps equivalent to reading Anthony Trollope's Can You Forgive Her? , and nowhere in the region of any of the great meganovels such as Proust's In Search of Lost Time.

主动放弃怀疑是一种奇特的心理状态——阅读非虚构作品和诗歌都不需要这种状态，因为两者都基于逻辑论证。许多聪明且受过良好教育的人完全抵制这种状态，或者只是在剧院的黑暗中，与其他观众一起短暂地接受它——世界上有很多人以自己不读小说而自豪。出版商常常感叹小说读者群正在萎缩，尤其是男性读者正在流失。文学教育不仅通过拓展读者的阅读乐趣来增强其放弃怀疑的意愿，还能增强其进入冥想状态的能力，并使其更容易接受他人思想的影响，因为沉思的状态对于真正欣赏小说至关重要。虽然所有艺术形式都能促进这种接受状态，但小说却能以独特的方式持续这种状态——例如，我们不可能花十到十二个小时去欣赏一幅画，而普通读者读完一本五百页的小说也需要这么长时间。很少有戏剧演出超过四个小时，即使是四个小时也被认为是相当长的。瓦格纳的《尼伯龙根的指环》有多长？十五个小时或许相当于读完安东尼·特罗洛普的《你能原谅她吗？》，但远不及普鲁斯特的《追忆似水年华》等任何一部伟大的鸿篇巨著。

For some readers, of course, eight to ten hours spent reading a novel in a receptive state of mind is the only quiet, contemplative time they can afford, and the opportunity to suspend so much disbelief, to follow a single line of thought, is comforting as well as entertaining and enlightening. When the reader accepts the first line of a book, she agrees to think about the same things, and in the same degree of detail and in the same order, that the writer has chosen to think about. While she is reading the book, she is thinking about them simultaneously with the author. Although in book form the novel precedes her contemplation of it and may historically precede her very existence, as a novel it unfolds in the author's mind and her mind simultaneously. The recognition of this effect of the novel, and of its uniqueness in literature, was the revelation that enabled Marcel Proust to write In Search of Lost Time. Proust knew that he could not achieve the sense of reexperiencing important episodes that he sought if he were to write an overt memoir because a memoir has to seem true (both factual and incomplete). He preferred to use the conceit of a memoir but to write a novel, which enabled him to pick and choose aspects of his experience that he found “useful to my theme,” as he said, and to elaborate as much as he wished.

当然，对某些读者而言，八到十个小时以全神贯注的心态阅读小说，是他们唯一能抽出时间静心思考的时光。有机会放下诸多怀疑，跟随单一的思路，既令人感到慰藉，又充满娱乐性和启发性。当读者接受一本书的第一行时，她就同意思考与作者相同的事物，并且以相同的细节程度和顺序进行思考。在阅读的过程中，她与作者同时思考着这些事物。虽然小说以书籍的形式出现时，先于读者的思考，甚至在历史上可能先于她的存在，但作为一部小说，它在作者的脑海中和读者的脑海中同时展开。正是对小说这种效应及其在文学中独特性的认识，促使马塞尔·普鲁斯特创作了《追忆似水年华》。普鲁斯特深知，如果他写一部直白的回忆录，就无法达到他所追求的重温重要事件的感觉，因为回忆录必须显得真实（既要符合事实，又要有所缺失）。他更倾向于采用回忆录的形式，但写一部小说，这样他就可以挑选他认为“对我的主题有用”的经历片段，并随心所欲地进行展开。

Because of the way that the novel unfolds in the mind of the willing reader, she cannot be “wrong” in her response to it—the fact that the novel is created only in her mind while she is reading it gives her sole possession of it. Outside of literature, maybe the closest thing to this is a guided meditation, where the voice of a guru suggests images and ways of thinking that are intended to result in a particular state of mind. Presumably, as he speaks, the guru is meditating on the same images he is speaking of. But few guided meditations go on for twenty-six hours (the length of a full recorded reading of my novel Horse Heaven). Rather, the voice of the guru fades away after a while, having induced in the student's mind an absence of voice or image. A novel, too, induces a contemplative state of mind, but rather than emptying it, it fills it with many different thoughts and feelings. Present with the reader in her mind is the individuality of the writer, whose idiosyncratic phrasing, ideas and emotions, fears and desires are guiding her and influencing her and inviting her to react.

由于小说是在读者的脑海中展开的，因此她对小说的反应不可能“错误”——小说完全在她阅读时于她的脑海中生成，这赋予了她对小说的独占权。在文学之外，或许最接近这种体验的是引导冥想，其中一位导师的声音会引导人们进入特定的心境，并暗示一些意象和思维方式。想必，导师在讲述的同时，也在冥想着他所描述的那些意象。但很少有引导冥想会持续26个小时（这相当于我完整朗读小说《马之天堂》的录音时长）。相反，导师的声音会在一段时间后逐渐消失，并在学员的脑海中引发一种声音或意象的缺失。小说也能引发沉思，但它并非清空这种心境，而是用各种各样的思想和情感将其填满。读者心中浮现的是作者的个性，作者独特的措辞、思想和情感、恐惧和欲望都在引导和影响着读者，并促使读者做出反应。

However, not every state of willing suspension of disbelief is the same. A novel directs the reader's contemplation of it. Even when a reader likes four different novels equally, and is equally receptive to them, she won't read Robert Musil's The Man without Qualities in the same manner that she will read Halldr Laxness's Independent People , or even in the same manner that she will read another great modernist novel such as Ulysses. A page-turner offers the pleasure of suspense (this is one of the pleasures of the tale), but in an epic, more than moderate suspense might be a fault. In an epic, the unhappy outcome of the novel is shadowed forth early on. Relentless page-turning gets the reader only where she knew she was going in the first place, and it gets her there faster, without sufficient time to ruminate upon the qualities of the epic protagonist that make him or her interesting and worth reading about. Novels with a large component of travel narrative, such as Moby-Dick , are meant to meander so that the writer and the reader can gaze at the scenery and appreciate its exotic qualities. One of the problems some modern readers have with Melville is that they don't have the patience to realize that the psychological and plot elements of his stories are intentionally set into a wide landscape that is meant to comment upon and contrast to the narrow intensity of human desires and preoccupations. A novel such as The Man without Qualities is an argument about the nature of modern life presented in a highly figurative and epigrammatic style. If the reader doesn't go slowly enough to follow Musil's argument and think about his analogies—if she isn't as precise in her reading as he is in his writing—then the novel will pass her by almost completely. A romantic novel—let's say Jane Eyre —offers the reader still another dilemma. Everything in the plot and character depictions pulls her toward the climax that is to unite the protagonists, but for the story to be worth reading, the protagonists and their ups and downs have to be depicted and read about with care; the suspense of a romantic novel can actually get very strong even though author, reader, and convention all foreshadow the outcome and even when, in rereadings, the reader knows the outcome quite well.

然而，并非所有自愿放弃怀疑的状态都相同。小说引导读者的思考。即使读者同样喜欢四部不同的小说，并且对它们同样感兴趣，她阅读罗伯特·穆齐尔的《没有个性的人》的方式，也不会与阅读哈尔德·拉克斯内斯的《独立的人们》的方式相同，甚至与阅读另一部伟大的现代主义小说，例如《尤利西斯》的方式也不同。引人入胜的小说提供悬念带来的乐趣（这是故事的乐趣之一），但在史诗中，过分的悬念可能反而会成为一种缺陷。在史诗中，小说的悲剧结局很早就被暗示出来。不停地翻页只会把读者带到她一开始就知道的目的地，而且速度很快，却没有足够的时间去思考史诗主人公身上那些使其引人入胜、值得一读的特质。像《白鲸》这样以旅行叙事为主的小说，其叙事节奏往往较为舒缓，以便作者和读者都能欣赏沿途风光，领略异域风情。一些现代读者对梅尔维尔的作品存在一个问题，那就是他们缺乏耐心去理解，梅尔维尔笔下人物的心理描写和情节发展，都是有意将故事置于广阔的背景之中，以此来反衬人类狭隘的欲望和执念。像《没有个性的人》这样的小说，则以高度比喻和警句式的风格，探讨了现代生活的本质。如果读者不够细细品读，无法理解穆齐尔的论证和比喻——如果阅读不够精准，无法像他写作那样严谨——那么这部小说几乎会被完全忽略。而像《简·爱》这样的浪漫小说，则会给读者带来另一种困境。情节和人物刻画中的一切都将她引向最终的高潮，使主人公们走到一起。但是，为了让故事值得一读，主人公及其经历的起伏必须被细致地描绘和阅读；即使作者、读者和惯例都预示了结局，甚至在重读时读者已经很清楚结局，浪漫小说的悬念仍然可以变得非常强烈。

Novels have protagonists; protagonists, like narrators, have points of view. Point of view is like perspective in a realistic painting—it changes the size and shape, the nature and identity, of characters, objects, and events in accordance with their proximity to the viewer. Since a reader naturally has a point of view, her own, she readily accepts the simple humanity of point of view in a novel. By contrast, because at first glance nothing differentiates the protagonist in a play or a movie from the other humans around him or her, an audience member needs to be told whom to attend to and empathize with. Point of view in a movie or a play is superimposed by language, camera angles, stardom, voice-over.

小说有主人公；主人公和叙述者一样，都有各自的视角。视角就像写实绘画中的透视——它会根据人物、物体和事件与观者的距离远近，改变它们的大小、形状、性质和身份。由于读者本身就拥有自己的视角，因此她很容易接受小说中视角所体现的简单人性。相比之下，戏剧或电影中的主人公乍一看与周围的其他人并无二致，观众需要被告知应该关注谁，应该与谁产生共鸣。电影或戏剧中的视角是由语言、镜头角度、明星效应和旁白等因素叠加而成的。

The novel, of course, shares point of view with poetry, sharing also the quality of perspective. But the poem—at least the modern poem— usually does not excel at narrating events (and since the rise of the novel, hasn't been asked to do much of it). It excels, rather, at making events stand still for a moment so that some meaning or feeling can be wrested from them by ever more precise and evocative use of language, language that is supposed to cause the reader to stop rather than go. Action, all going and no stopping, is for plays and movies—movies that have nothing else have action. Even plays that have nothing else have talk, which is a type of action. The novel is the only imaginative form that must have both action and point of view, suspense and reflection. In this it seems to mimic the way life feels.

当然，小说与诗歌共享视角，也共享透视的特质。但诗歌——至少是现代诗歌——通常并不擅长叙述事件（而且自从小说兴起以来，诗歌也很少被要求这样做）。相反，它擅长让事件暂时静止，以便通过更加精准和富有感染力的语言运用，从中挖掘出某种意义或情感。这种语言旨在让读者驻足思考，而不是匆匆而过。一味向前、一气呵成的动作，是戏剧和电影的专属——电影即便没有其他元素，也少不了动作。即使是没有其他元素的戏剧，也有对话，而对话本身也是一种动作。小说是唯一一种必须兼具动作和视角、悬念和反思的想象形式。在这方面，它似乎模仿了生活的感受。

Every novel, then, is a guided meditation on a common thing, common both in the sense of “mundane” and in the sense of “shared”— action and reflection as perceived from a particular point of view. Perhaps this is the reason novelists are generally run-of-the-mill sorts of people, not experts, not possessed of prodigious resources in any specialized realm. Would anyone read a hypothetical novel by Albert Einstein? We can imagine the publisher's blurb: “In this page-turning, soul-wrenching work of genius, Time and Distance , the smartest man of the twentieth century tells the story of a fascinating marriage, the passionate ups and downs and the numbing but illuminating details of daily life, alongside the exciting adventures of new ideas and the final flight from tyranny!” Or, perhaps, a novel by Donald Trump, “Brick by Brick , a strangely lyrical investigation into wealth, corruption, fame, and fashion.” And yet every day we read and enjoy White Teeth , which was written by a twenty-five-year-old girl; Rabbit Is Rich , which was written by the only son of a schoolteacher from a small town in Pennsylvania; Persuasion , which was written by the second daughter of a minor landowner in Hampshire, England; The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn , by a small-town boy from a small midwestern state; and Dead Souls , written and partially destroyed by the son of a moderately wealthy minor official from Ukraine. It is hard to overestimate the importance of this quality of commonness to the nature of the novel; it enables a reader to relax with a novel as with another person, and also to feel as though the novelist might have something to say of relevance to the reader's own common life.

因此，每一部小说都是对某种寻常事物的引导性冥想，这种寻常既指“平凡”，也指“共享”——即从特定视角感知到的行动与反思。或许正因如此，小说家通常都是平凡之人，而非专家，也并非在任何专业领域拥有渊博的知识。有人会读一本假设由阿尔伯特·爱因斯坦创作的小说吗？我们可以想象出版商的宣传语：“在这部引人入胜、扣人心弦的天才之作《时间与距离》中，二十世纪最聪明的人讲述了一段引人入胜的婚姻故事，其中既有激情澎湃的起伏跌宕，也有令人麻木却又发人深省的日常生活细节，以及激动人心的新思想探索和最终逃离暴政的壮举！”或者，或许会有人读唐纳德·特朗普的小说《砖瓦人生》，“这部小说以一种奇特的抒情笔触探讨了财富、腐败、名望和时尚。”然而，我们每天都在阅读和欣赏《白牙》（White Teeth），这本书的作者是一位25岁的女孩；《兔子发财了》（Rabbit Is Rich），作者是一位宾夕法尼亚州小镇教师的独子；《劝导》（Persuasion），作者是一位英国汉普郡小地主的次女；《哈克贝利·费恩历险记》（The Adventures of Huckleberry Finn），作者是一位来自美国中西部小镇的男孩；以及《死魂灵》（Dead Souls），作者是一位来自乌克兰的中产阶级小官员的儿子，这部小说后来被部分销毁。这种平凡性对于小说的本质至关重要，其重要性怎么强调都不为过；它使读者能够像与人交谈一样轻松地阅读小说，也使读者觉得小说家似乎在讲述一些与读者自身日常生活息息相关的故事。

When NASA sent a capsule into space a couple of decades ago, carrying schematic drawings of a man and a woman, a few mathematical formulas, some music, and several other objects, they did not include a copy of To Kill a Mockingbird. Every single novel is far too particular to be representative of the whole human race, but the paradox is that while every novel is too particular and even humble to stand as an emblem of humanity, the commonness of the novel is its most humane and human aspect. This is one of the effects of prose (one that Boccaccio pointed out in The Decameron when he was trying to justify its existence in 1350 ). People grow up narrating, expressing their points of view, elaborating and embroidering upon incidents, telling stories over and over. They do so because they want to fix events in their minds and remember them by endowing them with significance and discovering their meaning. It seems clear that many species of animals communicate vocally, but no other species of animal has been discovered to tell untrue stories.

二十年前，NASA将一个载有男女示意图、一些数学公式、音乐和其他物品的太空舱送入太空时，并没有携带《杀死一只知更鸟》。每一部小说都过于独特，无法代表整个人类，但矛盾之处在于，尽管每一部小说都过于独特甚至谦逊，无法成为人类的象征，但小说的普遍性恰恰是它最人性化、最富人情味的一面。这是散文的作用之一（薄伽丘在1350年创作《十日谈》时，为了论证散文的存在，就曾指出过这一点）。人们从小就喜欢叙述，表达自己的观点，对事件进行阐述和润色，一遍又一遍地讲述故事。他们这样做是因为他们想要将事件牢记于心，并通过赋予其意义和发现其内涵来记住它们。显然，许多动物物种都通过声音进行交流，但目前还没有发现其他动物物种会编造故事。

Untrue stories, as Proust realized, are worth telling only insofar as they remain distinct from true stories. It is this distinction that gives them completion. We can see this effect in both lies and gossip. Lies, of course, require some sort of logic for the liar to remember them and avoid being found out. The very process of working out a lie so it is plausible, though, is what makes it complete and implausible. Liars become smooth because they must—they are rhetoricians above all. Gossip, not a set of lies but a set of inferences, works the same way. A round of gossip always begins with a person everyone knows (a character) doing something interesting but uncharacteristic (shoplifting a blouse). The purpose of the gossip is to add events to the story as they become known (she gets caught, she cries, she is discovered to have another blouse in her purse, the police are called, she goes to the station, her dad calls the mayor, she gets off scot-free) and to account for the twists and turns in the story by means of psychology (that narcissistic bitch, remember when she took the lipstick out of my purse and wouldn't admit it even though I found it right in her locker?) and motive (she said if she didn't get that blouse somehow, her cousin would buy it, and she couldn't stand that), and then a broader interpretation of character (you know she always has thought her cousin was prettier than she is, and she hates her for that, but you'd never know it because she's so sweet whenever the cousin is around). Once the story is complete—when all the events are accounted for and the logic of the original mystery and its relationship to the character are understood— it becomes boring and the gossips go on to something else. It doesn't matter whether the story, the motives, and the interpretation of character bear any relationship to reality (Do you remember when she stole that blouse? Well, it turned out the saleslady put it into her bag by mistake as she was leaving the store. She had paid for the other blouse anyway.); the compulsion of gossips is to fill in all of the details until the incident becomes a rounded whole.

正如普鲁斯特所认识到的，虚假的故事只有与真实故事有所区别才值得讲述。正是这种区别赋予了它们完整性。我们可以在谎言和流言蜚语中看到这种效果。当然，谎言需要某种逻辑才能让说谎者记住并避免被揭穿。然而，正是精心编造谎言使其听起来合情合理的过程，才使得谎言既完整又荒谬。说谎者之所以能说会道，是因为他们必须如此——他们首先是修辞家。流言蜚语并非一系列谎言，而是一系列推断，其运作方式也相同。一轮流言蜚语总是以一个人尽皆知的人物（一个角色）做出一些有趣但反常的事情（比如偷了一件衬衫）开始的。八卦的目的是随着事件的进展（她被抓住了，她哭了，有人发现她的钱包里还有另一件衬衫，警察来了，她去了警局，她爸爸打电话给市长，她最终逍遥法外）不断丰富故事情节，并通过心理学（那个自恋的贱人，还记得她从我的钱包里拿走口红，即使我在她的储物柜里找到了，她也不肯承认吗？）和动机（她说如果她没能弄到那件衬衫，她表妹就会买下来，她受不了这一点）来解释故事中的曲折离奇，然后对人物性格进行更广泛的解读（你知道她一直觉得她表妹比她漂亮，她因此恨她，但你永远不会知道，因为只要表妹在场，她就表现得那么温柔）。一旦故事讲完了——所有事件都得到了解释，最初的谜团及其与人物的关系也都被理解了——它就变得索然无味，八卦爱好者们又会开始谈论其他事情。故事、动机和人物解读是否与现实有任何关联都无关紧要（你还记得她偷那件衬衫的事吗？其实，是售货员离开商店时不小心把它放进了她的包里。反正她已经付了另一件衬衫的钱。）；八卦爱好者的执念在于要把所有细节都补充完整，直到事件成为一个完整的整体。

Everyone acknowledges that true stories can never be fully known— too many details lack corroboration, too many witnesses disagree about what really happened. Every true story is unsatisfying insofar as it is required to be true. But since the novel is required to be complete (its dispensation from truthfulness), its acknowledged untruthfulness removes it from the world of consequences. The reader suspending disbelief expects a novel to take place in a designated game area (inside a book) under rules that apply only to the game. The rules are agreed upon ahead of time (for example, that it is possible to experience a time and a place very different from one's own). However serious its subject matter, the reader suspends disbelief because a novel is a form of play. Suffering and brutality can begin and unfold without either the author or the reader lifting a finger to stop them. Horrors depicted graphically in a novel are considered to be far less disturbing than the same graphic horrors in a nonfiction account because they are being used in a different way, as part of the logical progress of a game rather than as an unwelcome or irrational intrusion upon life. And unbelievable happy events also can take place in a novel, as a way for the mind to play over and learn from what it might otherwise not have a chance to experience.

人人都承认，真实的故事永远无法完全知晓——太多细节缺乏佐证，太多证人对事件真相各执一词。每个真实的故事都令人感到不尽如人意，因为它必须真实。但小说必须完整（它无需追求真实），其公认的非真实性使其脱离了后果的考量。读者会暂时放下怀疑，期待小说发生在一个特定的游戏区域（书本之中），遵循仅适用于游戏的规则。这些规则事先已达成共识（例如，可以体验与自身截然不同的时空）。无论主题多么严肃，读者都会暂时放下怀疑，因为小说是一种游戏。苦难和暴行可以发生并展开，而无需作者或读者采取任何行动来阻止它们。小说中描绘的恐怖场景，往往比非虚构作品中同样的恐怖场景更不令人不安，因为它们的运用方式不同：小说中的恐怖场景是故事逻辑发展的一部分，而非对生活的不速之客或非理性侵扰。此外，小说中也可能出现令人难以置信的幸福事件，让读者有机会重新审视和体验那些在现实生活中可能无缘经历的事情。

The game quality of the novel gives it meaning and form, because all games begin, have a playing time, and end. It also gives the novel at least a rudimentary raison d'tre, since games are a recognized form of learning for young mammals. The author sets up the game and is required to signal to the reader early in the narrative what the rules are. He does this in part by adopting a certain diction and tone right away— As I Lay Dying , for example, is a game about the lives of people who speak ungrammatically and are likely to do something unconventional; A Tale of Two Cities is a game in which two cultures are going to be contrasted, and the contrasts are going to be marked ones; A. S. Byatt's Possession is a game in which romantic relationships and styles of literature in two eras separated by 125 years are going to be compared and contrasted. A plot game, such as a murder mystery, signals the beginning of the plot right away with some sort of sinister event. A game about the workings of the mind puts off the beginning of the plot in favor of narrative ruminations about the nature of the world. A game about what seems versus what is, such as Kafka's “The Metamorphosis,” begins immediately describing what seems to be happening—Gregor was transformed into a bug, and this is what his little legs waving in the air looked like to him.

小说的游戏性赋予了它意义和形式，因为所有游戏都有开始、游戏时间和结束。它也为小说提供了一个基本的存在理由，因为游戏是幼年哺乳动物公认的学习方式。作者设定了游戏规则，需要在叙事初期就向读者表明规则。他部分地通过采用特定的措辞和语气来实现这一点——例如，《我弥留之际》讲述的是一群说话不合语法、行为可能非常规的人们的生活；《双城记》是一场对比两种文化的游戏，而且这种对比非常显著；A·S·拜厄特的《占有》则是一场比较和对比相隔125年的两个时代中浪漫关系和文学风格的游戏。情节游戏，例如谋杀悬疑小说，会以某种不祥事件开篇，标志着情节的开始。一款探讨思维运作的游戏，会先抛开情节，转而对世界本质进行叙事性的沉思。而一款探讨表象与本质的游戏，例如卡夫卡的《变形记》，则会立即着手描述表面所见——格里高尔变成了一只虫子，而这就是他眼中自己那在空中挥舞的小腿的样子。

To be truly playful, a game requires voluntary participants—if the author does not construct a game that is interesting enough to participate in, the reader is perfectly free to walk away. If she stays to play, then the playful nature of the game frees her to do things she might not be free to do in life—to question, to contemplate, to fantasize, to experience intense emotions, and to feel no guilt about doing so. The participants in a game may learn something that they take away from the game, but they don't have to. This is part of the freedom of playing the game. The novel game, like the baseball game, is thus an exercise in freedom, agency, and choice. The author may attempt at every turn to imbue the reader with certain sympathies or to get the reader to believe in a certain chain of cause and effect, but the reader is always free to object or disagree, or, indeed, to correct the author's misconceptions, as authors of bad reviews frequently do.

真正称得上“游戏”的乐趣在于参与者的自愿性——如果作者构建的游戏不够有趣，读者完全可以离开。如果她留下来玩，那么游戏的趣味性便能让她去做一些在生活中可能无法自由去做的事情——质疑、思考、幻想、体验强烈的情感，并且不会因此感到任何愧疚。游戏的参与者或许能从中有所收获，但他们并非必须如此。这正是游戏自由的一部分。因此，小说游戏，就像棒球比赛一样，是对自由、自主性和选择的练习。作者或许会处处试图让读者产生某种共鸣，或者让读者相信某种因果关系，但读者始终可以自由地提出异议或反对，甚至可以纠正作者的错误观点，就像那些写差评的作者经常做的那样。

The gamelike nature of the novel is built on the literary convention of the conceit. The conceit is a form of metaphor or pretense—John Donne's poem “A Valediction Forbidding Mourning” is full of conceits such as “Our two souls therefore, which are one,/Though I must go, endure not yet/ A breach, but an expansion,/Like gold to aery thinness beat”—in which the poet and the reader collaborate in a logical quest to understand the unique sort of love the poet and his wife share, using metaphors of quiet death, gold leaf, and compasses. The sensuous qualities of the images bolster the logic of the argument. In the same way, Trollope's novel The Eustace Diamonds proposes that the reader and the writer contemplate the character of Lizzie Eustace, whom they will agree to be a beautiful but shallow and ruthless young woman, who will begin the game's train of logical events by keeping for herself a string of valuable jewels that by rights belongs to the estate of a family she has married into. They will further agree that Lizzie has all sorts of relatives and associates who are implicated in her designs in some way or another, to see the effect of Lizzie's ambiguous moral choice upon the social world in which she lives. Lizzie's action works in the social body that she is part of like a radioactive isotope— as it moves around, it illuminates, sometimes in surprising ways, the moral life of the community. Trollope's conceit is that these characters and events are real, just as Donne's conceit is that love can be likened to death, gold, and a compass. The conceit of the poem succeeds if it promotes the logic of the poet's argument and if it is vivid enough for the reader to envision it. The conceit of the novel succeeds if the reader enjoys following it out. But both novelist and reader understand that it is all pretense. No diamonds have been stolen, no men have turned into bugs, no radio station broadcasting wholesome pap from downtown Minneapolis was ever started by a pair of brothers named Ray and Roy, no incognito crown prince has ever pulled a sword from an anvil resting on a stone, no fifteen-year-old French girl was ever subjected to year after year of relentless torture and attack and then killed by a lightning strike. But it is lots of fun to think that all of these things have happened, and more.

这部小说的游戏性建立在“比喻”这一文学惯例之上。比喻是一种隐喻或伪装——约翰·邓恩的诗作《告别辞》中充满了比喻，例如“因此，我们两个灵魂，本为一体，/即便我必须离去，也无需/承受裂痕，而是不断扩展，/如同金子被锤炼至薄如蝉翼”——诗人与读者共同协作，运用静默死亡、金箔和圆规等隐喻，展开一场逻辑探索，试图理解诗人与妻子之间那份独特的爱。这些意象的感官特质强化了论证的逻辑性。同样，特罗洛普的小说《尤斯塔斯钻石》也引导读者和作者思考莉齐·尤斯塔斯这个人物。他们一致认为莉齐是一位美丽却肤浅、冷酷无情的年轻女子，她将通过私藏一串本应属于她嫁入的家族的珍贵珠宝来开启一系列合乎逻辑的事件。他们还一致认为，莉齐的亲戚和同伙都以某种方式卷入了她的计划，从而观察莉齐模棱两可的道德选择对她所处的社会世界的影响。莉齐的行为在她所处的社会群体中如同放射性同位素一般——随着它的扩散，它以有时令人意想不到的方式照亮了社群的道德生活。特罗洛普的构思在于，这些人物和事件都是真实的，正如约翰·邓恩的构思在于，爱情可以比作死亡、黄金和指南针一样。诗歌的构思若能促进诗人论证的逻辑，且足够生动形象，使读者能够身临其境，便可成功。小说的构思若能令读者乐于跟随其发展，便可成功。但小说家和读者都明白，这一切都是虚构的。没有钻石被盗，没有人变成虫子，没有一对名叫雷和罗伊的兄弟在明尼阿波利斯市中心创办了播放健康无聊节目的电台，没有隐姓埋名的王储从放在石头上的铁砧中拔出宝剑，也没有十五岁的法国女孩遭受多年无情的折磨和攻击，最终被闪电击中身亡。但想象所有这些事情都发生过，甚至更多，却是一件非常有趣的事情。

As with all games, the novel game has many levels of play. The lowest level is, perhaps, simply following the sequence of the story and understanding what happens and why. Higher levels move toward greater and greater complexity and efficiency, just as professional basketball players execute more plays more quickly and more masterfully than high school basketball players do. A novel with a very high level of game quotient has more and more internal and external references, a denser and denser net of connections between words and of intuitive meanings, and the result is a higher level of abstraction. In a novel such as Ulysses or any one of a dozen other modern and postmodern novels, no character, no image, no incident stands alone—everything is part of a network of allusions that constantly offers various meanings and reinforces the playful nature of the novel as a form. This high level of play also shapes a novel's claims to verisimilitude, in fact making the question of verisimilitude part of the discussion of that particular novel. Novelists and readers, of course, take greater or lesser pleasure in the game potential of the novel as a form. To some readers, the various and shifting nature of Ulysses constitutes its greatest claim to verisimilitude; to others, the lack of an easily recognizable plot (which is always what makes a novel a public object rather than a private one) indicates self-indulgence on the part of the author. And as any game grows more complex, it becomes more abstract and exclusive—in order not to get lost in the subtleties of play, fans have to be highly versed in the rules and the moves of the game and willing to play the game (read the book) over and over to get everything out of it. The novelist has as many drafts as he wants to enhance the intricacies of the novel; likewise, the patient reader has as many rereadings as she wants to work out the intricacies the novelist has introduced. Obviously, the novel as a game gives itself over to all the tendencies of games to consume insiders and deflect outsiders. Highly referential and inaccessible novels with little plot and very complex characters need help to recommend themselves to normal readers, and so, for example, you can buy a twelve-cassette course of lectures on Ulysses that promises to get you through the book in a way that makes sense of it—and makes you want to read it. If you buy the lectures ($79), perhaps you will commit yourself to the project instead of wasting the money. The lectures and the book, it is implied, will have been worth the effort once the reader discovers the riches of the author's imagination, and in addition the reader will have gained the prestige of reading something great, famous, and obscure. Only a novel at the highest level of play with little evident suspense requires so much promotion by those who enjoy it. Jane Austen novels, for example, recommend themselves because they work perfectly well at lower levels of play (they seem true, funny, and suspenseful), even though there is more to be discovered as the reader grows more sophisticated. The fact remains, though, that the reader possesses the novel, and so if she finds that the residue of truth or insight remaining after the intricacies of an extremely sophisticated novel game have been worked out isn't really worth the effort, she is entitled to her opinion.

如同所有游戏一样，阅读小说也包含多个层次。最低层次或许仅仅是跟随故事的顺序，理解事件的来龙去脉。更高的层次则朝着越来越复杂、越来越精妙的方向发展，正如职业篮球运动员比高中篮球运动员执行更多战术、速度更快、技巧更娴熟一样。一部游戏性极高的小说会包含越来越多的内部和外部指涉，词语之间以及直觉意义之间的联系网络也越来越密集，最终呈现出更高的抽象层次。在《尤利西斯》或任何其他十几部现代和后现代小说中，没有哪个人物、哪个意象、哪个事件是孤立存在的——一切都是指涉网络的一部分，不断提供着各种不同的含义，并强化了小说这种形式的趣味性。这种高层次的游戏性也影响着小说对真实性的追求，事实上，真实性问题本身就成为了讨论这部小说的重要议题。当然，小说家和读者对小说这种形式的游戏性所蕴含的乐趣程度不一。对一些读者而言，《尤利西斯》丰富多变的特质恰恰是其最接近现实的体现；而对另一些读者来说，缺乏易于辨识的情节（而情节恰恰是小说成为公共而非私人物品的关键所在）则表明作者的自我放纵。任何游戏，一旦变得复杂，便会变得更加抽象和排他——为了不迷失在游戏的微妙之处，玩家必须精通游戏规则和各种操作，并且愿意反复阅读（反复阅读小说）才能从中领悟一切。小说家可以根据需要修改无数遍，以增强小说的复杂性；同样，耐心的读者也可以反复阅读，以探究小说家精心设计的种种复杂之处。显然，小说作为一种游戏，必然会受到所有游戏特性的影响：它容易吸引圈内人，排斥圈外人。那些情节简单、人物复杂、引经据典晦涩难懂的小说，需要借助一些辅助手段才能吸引普通读者。例如，你可以购买一套十二盒磁带的《尤利西斯》讲解课程，它承诺能帮助你理解这部作品，并激发你阅读的兴趣。如果你购买了这套讲解课程（售价79美元），或许你会真正投入到阅读中，而不是白白浪费钱。这套课程暗示，一旦读者领略到作者丰富的想象力，这些讲解和书籍本身就物有所值；此外，读者还能获得阅读一部伟大、著名且鲜为人知的作品的荣耀。只有那些娱乐性极强、悬念不明显的作品才需要如此费力地推广。例如，简·奥斯汀的小说之所以能够吸引读者，是因为它们在较低的娱乐水平下也能很好地发挥作用（它们看起来真实、幽默且充满悬念），尽管随着读者阅历的增长，其中蕴含的更多内涵等待着他们去发掘。但事实仍然是，小说的主人是读者，因此，如果她发现，在解开了极其复杂的小说游戏之后，剩下的真理或见解并不值得付出努力，那么她有权发表自己的意见。

So far we have talked about the psychology of the novel from the reader's point of view, but the novelist has a psychology, too. Once he has decided to write a novel, he goes through all the stages anyone else goes through who is attempting to learn a skill (see chapters 10 and 11 ). Just as the novel is read intuitively, it is composed intuitively. Many great authors give themselves over to the process of composition as to madness or vision—that is, they place the reasoning brain in service to the limbic brain, knowing that intuition is a faster, more efficient, but less knowable and controllable method of creation. The length of the novel requires the productive author to do this daily, often for years. An excellent example of this is an account by Charles Dickens's daughter Kate of an occasion from her childhood when she was ill, and spent the day in her father's study. He would sit at his desk writing, then jump up and go to a mirror, where he would make faces and talk quickly in various accents, then run back to his desk and write some more.
