He was acting out the drama and dialogue he was writing, with no sense, she thought, of where he was or of her presence in the room. Every novelist experiences a variant of this. Some theorists of creativity call it “flow.” Robert Musil, in The Man without Qualities , characterizes it quite nicely as follows: “this non-plussed feeling refers to something that many people nowadays call intuition, whereas formerly it used to be called inspiration, and they think that they must see something suprapersonal in it; but it is only something nonpersonal, namely the affinity and kinship of the things themselves that meet inside one's head” (p. 129 ). He is overtly referring to a sense of synchronicity, but what he is describing is the feeling of writing a novel.

到目前为止，我们一直从读者的角度探讨小说的心理，但小说家也有自己的心理。一旦决定创作小说，他就会经历所有学习技能的人都会经历的阶段（参见第10章和第11章）。正如小说是凭直觉阅读的，它的创作也是凭直觉进行的。许多伟大的作家都全身心地投入到创作过程中，如同疯癫或灵感迸发——也就是说，他们将理性思维服务于边缘系统，因为他们知道直觉是一种更快、更高效，但却更难以捉摸和控制的创作方式。小说的篇幅要求高产的作家每天都要这样做，而且往往持续数年。查尔斯·狄更斯的女儿凯特讲述了一个绝佳的例子：她小时候生病，整天待在父亲的书房里。狄更斯会坐在书桌前写作，然后突然起身走到镜子前，对着镜子做鬼脸，用各种口音快速说话，之后又跑回书桌继续写作。她觉得，他仿佛在演绎自己笔下的戏剧和对话，完全没有意识到自己身处何地，也没有意识到她的存在。每个小说家都会经历类似的感受。一些创造力理论家称之为“心流”。罗伯特·穆齐尔在《没有个性的人》中对此做了精辟的描述：“这种茫然无措的感觉，如今许多人称之为直觉，而过去则称之为灵感，他们认为其中必定蕴含着某种超个人的东西；但它实际上只是非个人的东西，即头脑中各种事物之间的亲和力和关联性”（第129页）。他表面上指的是一种同步性，但实际上描述的是创作小说时的感觉。

“The things themselves” Musil alludes to are figures, words, images, and ideas given potency and importance by feelings such as indignation, pleasure, incongruity, sadness, fear, eagerness, and repulsion, and sensations such as coolness, smoothness, speediness, dullness, heat, abrasiveness, and warmth. All of these “things,” which, of course, are not things at all but mental processes, come and go in the mind until something causes their connections to jell, and some set of them links up in a logic that is evident to the writer but as yet unexplored. The jelling catalyst might be any component of the novel. When I conceived A Thousand Acres , the ideas about Lear's daughters and about agriculture had been knocking around in my mind for fifteen years or so, but the exact moment they jelled was when I was driving down I- 35 in northern Iowa in late March 1988 . The landscape was flat and cold, lit by a weak winter sun, and as I stared out the window, the farm fields seemed enormous and isolated. As soon as I said, “This is where I could set that Lear book,” the whole thing came into my mind, and the image of that bleak landscape remained throughout the writing of the book as a talisman to return to every time composition faltered. With Horse Heaven the situation was different—I conceived the book before I knew anything about the subject. A phrase I heard on the radio, “spit the bit,” suggested to me that the language of horse racing must be wonderfully rich. As I began to learn about racing, each phrase or descriptor I then discovered added its own bit of inspiration to my original idea. In one case the catalyst was setting; in the other, the catalyst was language.

穆齐尔所指的“事物本身”指的是人物、词语、意象和观念，它们因诸如愤慨、愉悦、不协调、悲伤、恐惧、渴望和厌恶等情感，以及诸如清凉、柔滑、迅疾、迟钝、灼热、粗糙和温暖等感觉而具有力量和重要性。所有这些“事物”，当然，它们并非真正的事物，而是心理过程，在脑海中来来去去，直到某种因素促使它们之间的联系凝结，最终形成某种逻辑，这种逻辑对作者而言显而易见，但尚未被探索。这种促成凝结的催化剂可能是小说中的任何组成部分。当我构思《一千英亩》时，关于李尔王的女儿们和农业的想法已经在我脑海中盘旋了大约十五年，但真正让这些想法成形的那一刻，是1988年3月下旬，我驾车行驶在爱荷华州北部的35号州际公路上。那里的景色平坦而寒冷，冬日的阳光微弱地洒在田野上。我凝视着窗外，农田显得无比辽阔而孤寂。我刚一开口说：“我可以把李尔王的故事背景设定在这里。”整个构思就此涌入我的脑海，那片荒凉的景象贯穿了整部小说的创作过程，就像一个护身符，每当我写作遇到瓶颈时，它都会浮现在我的脑海中。而《马的天堂》的情况则截然不同——我在对这个主题一无所知的情况下就构思了这本书。我在广播里听到的一句话“吐掉马衔”让我意识到，赛马的语言一定非常丰富。随着我对赛马的了解不断加深，我发现的每一个词组或描述都为我最初的想法增添了新的灵感。在一个案例中，催化剂是凝固；在另一个案例中，催化剂是语言。

Charles Dickens was an avid seeker of names—he read directories and looked for odd names on gravestones. Even though he was almost always writing to a schedule, he was careful to name his characters in ways that seemed to baptize them and begin their journey. Martin Chuzzlewit's plot didn't truly form around him when his name was “Chuzzlerigg.” For Virginia Woolf, the history of Vita Sackville-West's house caused the jelling of all sorts of thoughts about men, women, literary history, writing, nature, and love. For Harriet Beecher Stowe, the death of her own child from an illness sharpened her sense of the meaning of the slave trade, and she constructed her novel of slavery not first and foremost around the subjection of one man to another, but around women losing their children. Fyodor Dostoevsky wrote The Idiot when he was on a lengthy journey in Europe—homesickness sharpened his sense of what it would be like to return to Russia as a perfect innocent. Proust felt Swann's Way jell when he tasted a madeleine dipped in lime-flower tisane and was reminded of Sunday morning visits to his aunt when he was a child. As Musil suggests, this seems like an involuntary process, but I believe that is because it takes place in the same part of the brain where other things take place that seem involuntary, too, such as predilections, affinities, antipathies, a sense of rightness, and other passions of all sorts.

查尔斯·狄更斯酷爱收集名字——他阅读名录，寻找墓碑上那些奇特的名字。尽管他几乎总是按计划写作，但他给笔下的人物取名时却格外谨慎，仿佛赋予了他们洗礼的意义，开启了他们的旅程。如果马丁·丘泽尔维特的名字是“丘泽尔里格”，那么故事的情节就无法真正围绕他展开。对弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫而言，维塔·萨克维尔-韦斯特故居的历史让她对男人、女人、文学史、写作、自然和爱情等诸多话题产生了浓厚的兴趣。对哈丽雅特·比彻·斯托而言，她自己的孩子因病去世，这让她对奴隶贸易的意义有了更深刻的理解。她创作的奴隶小说，并非首先围绕着一个男人对另一个男人的奴役，而是围绕着失去孩子的女性展开。费奥多尔·陀思妥耶夫斯基在欧洲的一次漫长旅途中创作了《白痴》——思乡之情让他更加深刻地体会到，如果自己能以一个纯真无邪的孩童的身份回到俄罗斯，将会是怎样一番景象。普鲁斯特品尝了一块蘸着菩提花茶的玛德琳蛋糕，想起了儿时星期天早上去姑妈家的情景，这时他感到《斯万之路》的意境涌上心头。正如穆齐尔所说，这似乎是一个无意识的过程，但我认为这是因为它发生在大脑的同一区域，而大脑中其他一些看似无意识的事情，例如偏好、亲和力、厌恶感、正义感以及其他各种各样的情感，也都发生在那里。

But it is not all clear sailing for the novelist once he has tasted the madeleine. The reasoning brain often responds to such an experience by saying no, bad job, not good enough, I don't think so, better not, too dangerous, who do you think you are?, and watch out. Practiced and prolific novelists have to be adept at short-circuiting the cautious and reasonable areas of the brain that get in the way of the process while making use of the logical faculties that organize, support, and oversee the composition of the story itself. Every novelist has to withdraw from a state of inspiration at least once in a while to work out the logical steps of plot, character, structure, theme, and style. The sense that an author has thought through the logics in the work is reassuring to the reader, who wants both sensation and perspective, preferably simultaneously. About three-quarters of the way through Halldr Laxness's great epic of Icelandic rural life Independent People , for example, little Nonni, possibly Laxness's stand-in, is taken away from the impoverished family steading to America, where he is to learn a trade. The last person he says good-bye to is his grandmother, who bestows upon him her only two possessions—a kerchief and an ear pick—and gives him her only two pieces of advice: “I want to ask you never to be insolent to those who hold a lowly position in the world. And never to ill-treat any animal.” Nonni is deeply affected by leaving home; the chapter is full of lyrical descriptions of the sound of the birds, the look of the family home, the sunlight. All of this is in some sense inspiration—the novelist surveying his homeland from the distance of many years. At the end of the chapter, though, the intelligence of the novelist enters twice—once in the voice of Asta Sollilja, Nonni's older sister, who says, “Say thank you to your grandmother, Nonni. She's given you the only thing she has.” And then right away in his own voice as narrator, “And he put his hand in hers and thanked her in silence, for he knew no words that could express his gratitude for such a gift; she was giving him the nation's poorest Christmas to cheer him on his way when he went out into the world, and he knew that henceforth she would never celebrate Christmas” (p. 358 ). The scene, which is enormously poignant already, is made all the more so by Laxness's choice to underscore the humane and loving feelings he considers most important with a small authorial intrusion, which reflects upon not only general human conditions, but also, it is implied, what the adult Nonni learned from his humble origins.

但对于小说家来说，一旦尝到了灵感的滋味，创作之路并非一帆风顺。理性的大脑往往会对这种体验做出反应，比如“不”、“写得不好”、“不够好”、“我不这么认为”、“最好别写”、“太危险了”、“你以为你是谁？”以及“小心点”。经验丰富且著作颇丰的小说家必须善于绕过大脑中那些谨慎理性的部分，以免它们阻碍创作过程，同时运用逻辑思维来组织、支撑和统筹故事的构成。每位小说家都必须时不时地从灵感迸发的状态中抽离出来，仔细推敲情节、人物、结构、主题和风格的逻辑步骤。读者会因为作者对作品逻辑的深思熟虑而感到安心，因为他们既渴望感官刺激，也渴望深刻的思考，最好两者兼得。例如，在哈尔德·拉克斯内斯描写冰岛乡村生活的鸿篇巨著《独立的人们》中，大约四分之三处，小诺尼（或许是拉克斯内斯的化身）被带离贫困的家庭，前往美国学习一门手艺。他最后告别的是他的祖母，祖母将她仅有的两件物品——一条手帕和一个耳勺——留给了他，并给了他两条忠告：“我希望你永远不要对那些社会地位低下的人无礼。也永远不要虐待任何动物。”离开家乡对诺尼影响很大；这一章充满了对鸟鸣、老房子和阳光的抒情描写。所有这一切在某种意义上都是一种灵感——小说家从多年后的距离审视着他的故乡。然而，在本章结尾，小说家的智慧两次显露——一次是通过诺尼的姐姐阿斯塔·索利利亚的口吻，她说：“诺尼，替我向奶奶道谢。她把她唯一拥有的东西都给了你。” 紧接着，叙述者以自己的口吻写道：“他把手放在奶奶的手里，默默地感谢她，因为他找不到任何言语来表达他对这份礼物的感激之情；奶奶给了他全国最贫穷的圣诞节，好让他在踏入社会的路上得到慰藉，而他知道，从此以后，奶奶再也不会庆祝圣诞节了”（第358页）。这一幕本身就十分感人，而拉克斯内斯选择用少量的作者介入来强调他认为最重要的人性和爱，更使之令人动容。这种介入不仅反映了普遍的人性，也暗示了成年后的诺尼从他卑微的出身中学到了什么。

And so every novelist figures out a way to circumvent the judgmental, reasoning brain long enough to get the novel moving, but also, to use it to discern and clarify the meaning of the material. Every so often an author is so inspired that the whole brain works at a pitch of efficiency, discernment, and appropriateness that the author himself cannot understand. A novelist in the midst of inspiration does not feel the egotistical emotions—Aren't I great? Look at me!—but the selfless ones—Aren't I lucky? Isn't this interesting? Isn't this fun? This doesn't mean that the egotistical emotions don't intervene whenever they can, especially in relationship to other novelists. But the reader's exposure to the mind of the novelist is so prolonged that she can always tell by his tone when he is promoting himself in some small-minded way or when he is serving his characters, themes, and plot. All good novels, even those about how selfish the author is, what a jerk he has been, and what this says about all the other selfish jerks in the world, strive to attain the grandeur of inspiration over the pettiness of self-promotion.

因此，每位小说家都会想方设法绕过大脑的评判和推理，让小说得以顺利展开，同时也能利用大脑来辨别和阐明素材的意义。有时，作家灵感迸发，整个大脑高效运转，洞察力、洞察力和恰当性都达到了作家自身都无法理解的程度。处于灵感迸发状态的小说家不会感受到自负的情绪——“我真棒！看看我！”——而是会感受到无私的情绪——“我真幸运！这真有趣！这真好玩！”。但这并不意味着自负的情绪不会在可能的时候出现，尤其是在与其他小说家交流时。但读者与小说家的内心世界接触的时间如此之长，以至于他们总能从作家的语气中分辨出他是在以某种狭隘的方式自我吹捧，还是在为人物、主题和情节服务。所有优秀的小说，即使是那些描写作者多么自私、多么混蛋，以及这反映了世界上所有其他自私混蛋的小说，都力求达到鼓舞人心的宏伟境界，而不是自我推销的琐碎。

If the novel is a therapeutic act, as suggested above, then the very form of the novel suggests a possible positive therapeutic outcome for the author first of all. The Hungarian theorist of the novel Gyrgy Lukcs pointed out that while from the moment the curtain goes up on the stage, a drama accelerates toward the climax, a novel begins from the first page to back away from the climax. The essence of the novel is retarded action rather than precipitate action. There are all sorts of methods for retarding the action of a novel, from digressions and detours, to the introduction of new characters, to plot twists and changes of scene. A compelling style itself retards the action by inviting the reader to linger over the words and sentences. Every time the action of a novel is retarded, choice enters, and so, every time, a character can choose again whether to pursue one course of action or another. One result of this retarded action is that the inevitability of tragedy is lost. If tragedy is the inability, in the end, to make connection, then the retarded action of the novel repeatedly raises the opportunity of making connection, and most characters, even in the most dismal novels, end up making some sort of connection. In Leo Tolstoy's “The Death of Ivan Illych,” the reader may think that at last a novelist is going to have the guts to fade to black. Ivan is dying. He has no relationship with anyone. His family life is entirely shallow and commodified. He is isolated by materialism and pride. Nevertheless, at the last moment, on the last page, when he feels that death is like being shoved into a dark sack, he notices that his son is sad at his passing, and the bottom of the dark sack gives way to light. A similar thing happens at the death of Gregor in “The Metamorphosis”—though Kafka was writing out of Jewish tradition (and Yiddish stories are often the darkest at the end), he still has Gregor sense the light of dawn just at his passing. Why is this? Can no novelist be relied upon to tell the unredeemed truth?

如果小说如上文所述具有疗愈作用，那么小说的形式本身就暗示着作者首先可能获得积极的疗愈效果。匈牙利小说理论家吉尔吉·卢克奇指出，戏剧从帷幕拉开的那一刻起便加速走向高潮，而小说则从第一页开始就逐渐远离高潮。小说的本质在于延缓而非急促的行动。延缓小说行动的方法多种多样，从离题和迂回，到引入新角色，再到情节转折和场景转换。引人入胜的文风本身就能延缓行动，它引导读者细细品味每一个字句。每当小说的行动被延缓，选择便随之出现，因此，每一次，人物都可以再次选择是采取哪种行动。这种延缓行动的结果之一便是悲剧的必然性被削弱。如果悲剧最终在于无法建立联系，那么小说中缓慢的情节发展便反复地创造了建立联系的机会，大多数人物，即便在最阴郁的小说中，最终也都能建立某种联系。在列夫·托尔斯泰的《伊凡·伊里奇之死》中，读者或许会认为，终于有一位小说家敢于让故事走向黑暗。伊凡即将离世。他与任何人都没有联系。他的家庭生活肤浅而物化。他被物质主义和骄傲所孤立。然而，在最后一刻，在最后一页，当他感到死亡如同被塞进一个黑暗的麻袋时，他注意到儿子为他的离世感到悲伤，黑暗的麻袋底部出现了光明。在《变形记》中格里高尔之死也发生了类似的事情——尽管卡夫卡的写作深受犹太传统的影响（意第绪语故事的结尾往往最为黑暗），但他仍然让格里高尔在临终之际感受到了黎明的曙光。为什么会这样？难道就没有一个小说家能够说出未经粉饰的真相吗？

In fact, hope exists in the form of narrative itself, because the narrator cannot stop talking. In the end is the word, and as long as the word exists, the possibility of connection exists, no matter how resolutely the author attempts to prove otherwise. Drama can be ended with an action or a curtain, but the novel must say good-bye, which means it lives on after the action is over. It is in the nature of the novel to say, “We are still alive.” Furthermore, the requirement of the novel that the narrator be lucid enough to tell the tale puts a boundary on insanity and other forms of mental disconnection. No novel can weasel out of this hopefulness, because the act of observation removes one, at least temporarily, from the state of being overwhelmed or destroyed by circumstances. For real cataclysm you have to have drama or film.

事实上，希望本身就存在于叙事之中，因为叙述者无法停止讲述。最终，文字依然存在，只要文字存在，联结的可能性就依然存在，无论作者如何竭力想要证明并非如此。戏剧可以以一个动作或帷幕落下而结束，但小说必须道别，这意味着它在故事结束后依然存在。小说的本质就在于表达“我们依然活着”。此外，小说要求叙述者必须足够清醒才能讲述故事，这本身就限制了精神错乱和其他形式的精神分裂。任何小说都无法逃避这种希望，因为观察的行为至少能暂时使人摆脱被环境压垮或摧毁的状态。真正的灾难，你必须通过戏剧或电影来展现。

Sometimes the author himself is the first to react to the hope held out by the very nature of his novel. A character, even the protagonist, dies, but the author changes his life, as Tolstoy accepted Russian Orthodox religion at the end of writing Anna Karenina , as Dickens left his wife after writing David Copperfield , as Kafka laughed aloud while reading “The Metamorphosis” to his friend Max Brod. Does this mean that no character can have a tragic ending? Nineteenth-century novelists such as Eliot, Flaubert, and James were much interested in bringing the grandeur and artistic respectability of tragedy to the novel but, as I shall argue later, it turned out to be more difficult than they thought.

有时，作者本人会率先回应小说本身蕴含的希望。小说中的人物，甚至是主人公，会死去，但作者会改变自己的人生，正如托尔斯泰在创作《安娜·卡列尼娜》的结尾皈依了俄罗斯东正教，狄更斯在写完《大卫·科波菲尔》后离开了妻子，卡夫卡在给朋友马克斯·布罗德朗读《变形记》时开怀大笑。这是否意味着所有人物都不能拥有悲剧的结局？十九世纪的小说家，如艾略特、福楼拜和詹姆斯，都热衷于将悲剧的宏伟和艺术价值融入小说，但正如我稍后将要论述的，这远比他们想象的要困难得多。

For the novelist even more, perhaps, than for the reader, the novel is a game. He enters into a state of mind that is akin to the states of mind of players of other games, a state of flow or presence that feels playful to him even as he is writing of terrible horrors. The experience of composition, which is inherently joyful and detached, offsets the contemplation of horror. For some authors, the game aspect of novel-writing is the most inspiring, and the author becomes enamored of the tricks, puns, figures of speech, references to other works, abstract patterns, or insights from other endeavors he has used to structure his novel. In The Awkward Age , for example, Henry James tried an unusual playlike structure that contrasts with his more straightforwardly narrated novels such as The Portrait of a Lady and The Ambassadors. The plot is simple: two young women need to be married off, but none of the eligible young men is quite suitable for reasons of either attractiveness or sensibility. The novel is divided into ten discrete parts, taking place as if on a stage among the same group of characters in a limited number of settings. Each section is told from a different point of view, and James suppresses his usual intrusive narrator's voice, telling the story mostly through action and dialogue. What James gets from this game is immediacy and intensity, and, as in a play, the efficient passage of time. He requires the reader to pay attention or get confused. Although James wrote The Awkward Age in the 1890s , before movies were invented, the novel anticipates movies such as the Japanese film Rashomon because it uses point of view rather like a camera to select features James wants to emphasize in the ongoing narrative in a way that would not be possible with a drama, and thereby reveal more about each character, perhaps, than would be possible with a more conventional narrator. By his own testimony, James was thrilled with his inventiveness in The Awkward Age , but it was and still is one of his more obscure novels because the form has an artificial quality that interferes with the reader's sympathetic identification with the characters.

对小说家而言，或许比对读者而言，小说更像是一场游戏。他进入一种类似于其他游戏玩家的心境，一种心流或专注的状态，即便描写的是可怕的恐怖，这种状态也让他感到轻松愉悦。创作本身就充满乐趣和超脱，这种体验抵消了对恐怖的沉思。对一些作家来说，小说创作的游戏性是最具启发性的，他们会沉迷于自己用来构建小说的各种技巧、双关语、修辞手法、对其他作品的引用、抽象模式，或是来自其他创作的洞见。例如，在《尴尬的年纪》中，亨利·詹姆斯尝试了一种不同寻常的戏剧化结构，这与他叙事更为直白的小说，如《贵妇画像》和《大使们》形成了鲜明对比。故事情节很简单：两位年轻女子需要出嫁，但所有适婚的年轻男子都因为外貌或性格上的缺陷而显得不够合适。这部小说分为十个独立的部分，仿佛在舞台上，由同一群人物在有限的场景中展开。每个部分都以不同的视角叙述，詹姆斯摒弃了他惯用的旁白式叙述方式，主要通过动作和对话来讲述故事。这种叙事手法赋予了小说一种即时性和强烈的感染力，并且如同戏剧一般，有效地展现了时间的流逝。他要求读者集中注意力，否则就会感到困惑。尽管詹姆斯在19世纪90年代创作了《尴尬的年代》，当时电影尚未发明，但这部小说却预示了诸如日本电影《罗生门》之类的电影，因为它运用视角如同摄影机一般，在叙事中选取詹姆斯想要强调的特征，而这在戏剧中是无法实现的，从而或许比传统的旁白方式更能揭示每个人物的内心世界。据詹姆斯本人所述，他对《尴尬的时代》中的创造力感到非常兴奋，但这部小说过去是、现在仍然是他比较晦涩难懂的作品之一，因为其形式具有一种人为的特质，妨碍了读者对人物产生同情和认同。

The author, like the reader, is given a social dispensation as part of his participation in the game—what his characters do is not held against him personally. Many authors make careers of depicting brutality, horror, cruelty, vice, and graphic violence; others make careers of depicting vast wealth and social status, perfect marriages, romantic fervor, and happy-ever-after endings. These writers are not required to be realists because they are not professing to play a realist game. Nor are they “writing what they know.” No one expects Stephen King to have performed all the mayhem his characters perform, and they would in fact be shocked if he had. A novelist's life is allowed to be different from the games he plays. In fact, for novelists who write with particular skill about evil (Dickens, Bram Stoker, Stephen King), it is required to be different.

作者和读者一样，作为参与这场游戏的一部分，被赋予了一种社会特权——他笔下人物的所作所为不会追究他个人的责任。许多作家以描绘残暴、恐怖、残酷、罪恶和血腥暴力为生；另一些作家则以描绘巨额财富和社会地位、完美的婚姻、浪漫的激情和幸福美满的结局为生。这些作家无需成为现实主义者，因为他们并没有声称自己在玩一场现实主义的游戏。他们也不是在“写自己所知”。没有人会期望斯蒂芬·金亲身经历过他笔下人物所犯下的所有暴行，事实上，如果他真的这么做了，人们反而会感到震惊。小说家的生活可以与他所参与的游戏有所不同。事实上，对于那些擅长描写邪恶的小说家（狄更斯、布拉姆·斯托克、斯蒂芬·金）来说，这种不同是必然的。

The fact that a novel is a book also shapes its psychology in several ways. In the first place, the novel itself, the unfolding narrative, has no independent identity as an object, as other forms of art such as paintings, sculptures, and pieces of music do; nor can it be recited or performed from the stage—even when, as sometimes happens, a novel is commemorated by a full reading, as Ulysses was commemorated in Dublin on the hundredth anniversary of Bloomsday, no one expects listeners to sit quietly in a room listening attentively for the entire duration of the reading. If a novel finds no eager readers, it does not even exist. As a result, every novel has to be helped to find readers. A novel does not have the cachet of rarity—a novel from an edition that sells a thousand copies is not intrinsically more valuable than a novel from an edition that sells a million copies. When both editions first go on sale, they sell for the same twenty-five dollars. Because there are no one-of-a-kind novels, rarity and fashionability never combine to drive up the price of a book. In fact, the more fashionable a novel becomes, the more copies of it are printed, and the higher the residual profit for the author and the publisher—a novel is more like a tomato than it is like a diamond necklace. Every novel, no matter how abstract, wants to sell a million copies, and so every novelist has to offer some reason that his novel might appeal to lots and lots of readers.

小说作为一种书籍，其本质也从多个方面塑造了它的心理。首先，小说本身，即展开的叙事，并不像绘画、雕塑和音乐等其他艺术形式那样，拥有独立的客体身份；它既不能被朗诵，也不能在舞台上表演——即便有时会举办小说朗读会来纪念某部作品，例如在布鲁姆日一百周年之际，都柏林举办了《尤利西斯》的朗读会，也没有人会期望听众全程安静地坐在房间里，全神贯注地聆听。如果一部小说找不到热切的读者，它就如同不存在一般。因此，每一部小说都需要被帮助才能找到读者。小说并不具备稀有性带来的光环——销量一千册的版本并不比销量一百万册的版本更有价值。这两个版本最初上市时，售价都是二十五美元。因为世上没有独一无二的小说，所以稀有性和流行度并不会推高一本书的价格。事实上，小说越流行，印刷量就越大，作者和出版商的剩余利润也就越高——小说更像是西红柿，而不是钻石项链。每一部小说，无论多么抽象，都想卖出百万册，因此，每一位小说家都必须拿出某种理由，证明自己的小说能够吸引大量的读者。

Like all purveyors of commodities as opposed to luxuries, novelists are usually perfectly willing to advertise (which is another reason the novel fits in with modern life). Jane Austen's novels were not published under her name, but as “written by a lady.” This was not as bland then as it seems now—a lady was a specific being, genteel, well-bred, and respectable. In the disagreements of the period about whether young women should be allowed to read novels (rather than sermons), “by a lady” was like a Good Housekeeping Seal of Approval— these novels were harmless (but, of course, they were not, because they gave voice to the aims and desires of young girls, as if those aims and desires were worth considering). Advertising for the novel, especially when done by the novelist himself or herself, is just like any other form of advertising—it doesn't hurt, and it can be educational; it may work, and it may not—but third-party endorsements and great word of mouth work better than anything else.

与所有商品（而非奢侈品）的供应商一样，小说家通常非常乐意做广告（这也是小说能够融入现代生活的另一个原因）。简·奥斯汀的小说并非以她的名字出版，而是署名“一位女士所著”。这在当时并不像现在看来那么平淡无奇——“女士”指的是特定的人，举止优雅、教养良好、受人尊敬。在那个关于年轻女性是否应该被允许阅读小说（而不是布道）的争论中，“一位女士所著”就像是《好管家》杂志的认可印章——这些小说无害（但实际上并非如此，因为它们表达了年轻女孩的愿望和渴望，仿佛这些愿望和渴望值得重视似的）。小说的广告，尤其是由小说家本人进行的广告，与其他任何形式的广告并无二致——它无伤大雅，而且可能具有教育意义；它可能有效，也可能无效——但第三方推荐和良好的口碑传播效果远胜于其他任何方式。

In fact, though some novelists are more uncomfortable with it than others, the psychology of the novel must include some form of authorial self-justification. How else do ordinary citizens of the modern world justify drawing attention to themselves and their ideas for hours and hours on end? At the base of every novel, then, is an argument the author is making about why a novel is worth writing, selling, and reading. Defoe, who always demonstrates the way the novel fits into commercial culture, knew from his work writing criminal confessions that there was already a market for descriptions of crimes combined with acts of repentance. Harriet Beecher Stowe knew that the evils of slavery she was hearing about in Cincinnati from escaped slaves were unknown to many Americans. Louisa May Alcott knew that adolescent girls needed to realize that there were alternatives to the conventional idea of dependency and marriage current in her day. Rohinton Mistry knew that the lives of poor people in Bombay were almost unimaginable to middle- and upper-class citizens in India and elsewhere. Aphra Behn knew that her experience in South America was unique, and that she had seen things that other English men and women would never see. Zora Neale Hurston knew that the inner lives of poor black people were hidden from mainstream culture. When an author has the conviction that his novel is a timely social and historical document, it seems to justify itself and to carry the author along.

事实上，尽管有些小说家对此感到不自在，但小说的心理必然包含某种形式的作者自我辩解。否则，现代世界的普通公民如何才能为自己连续数小时吸引人们关注自身及其思想的行为找到正当理由呢？因此，每部小说的核心都是作者提出的一个论点，即为什么这部小说值得创作、出版和阅读。笛福总是展现小说如何融入商业文化，他从撰写罪犯自白录的工作中了解到，对犯罪行为的描述与忏悔行为相结合的作品早已存在市场。哈里特·比彻·斯托知道，她在辛辛那提从逃亡奴隶那里听到的奴隶制的罪恶，对许多美国人来说是闻所未闻的。路易莎·梅·奥尔科特知道，青春期女孩需要意识到，除了她那个时代盛行的依附和婚姻观念之外，还有其他选择。罗欣顿·米斯特里知道，孟买穷人的生活对于印度和其他地方的中上层阶级公民来说几乎是难以想象的。阿芙拉·贝恩深知她在南美的经历独一无二，她目睹了其他英国男女永远无法看到的景象。佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿也明白，贫苦黑人的内心世界被主流文化所掩盖。当一位作家坚信自己的小说是一部具有时代意义的社会和历史文献时，它似乎便能自圆其说，并引领作者一路前行。

To write about the inner life of a slacker, of someone whose claim to existence is only that his capacity for pleasure is vaster and more refined than anyone else's in the history of the world, might be harder to justify, but Marcel Proust manages to do it—not by asserting his importance but by demonstrating his talents. The opening section of Swann's Way , before the tasting of the madeleine, is about falling asleep, humankind's most routine and least regarded activity. As M. carries the reader through these ruminations, he demonstrates that the reader can trust him to deal with all the other more usual and more interesting things that civilized people do as well. To write about the inner life of a child-molester is even more unjustifiable, but in Lolita , Vladimir Nabokov has a conviction, too—the assertion of absolute artistic freedom by an author; the story justifies itself by means of the beauty and intricacy of the telling. And to tell the story of an ordinary family, as Anne Tyler does in Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant , may be the hardest of all to justify. The Tulls have no pretensions to distinction, other than the normal distinctions of ordinary life; they live at a certain address and have experienced certain events, that is all. Tyler is such a retiring and self-effacing writer that she makes no overt claims for her subject—like Proust, she relies on the telling itself to give it a reason. But in the end, the history of the novel is what justifies the story of the Tulls: the tales of all those other ordinary folks have given both writers and readers the conviction that everyday existence is something to be observed and learned from.

要描写一个游手好闲之徒的内心世界，一个存在的唯一理由就是他享受快乐的能力比世界历史上任何人都更广博、更精致的人的内心世界，或许更难令人信服，但马塞尔·普鲁斯特做到了——并非通过强调他的重要性，而是通过展现他的才华。《斯万之路》的开篇，在品尝玛德琳蛋糕之前，描写的是入睡，这是人类最平凡、最容易被忽视的活动。普鲁斯特带领读者进入这些沉思，也证明了读者可以信任他，让他也能处理文明人所做的其他更寻常、更有趣的事情。描写一个恋童癖者的内心世界就更加难以令人信服了，但在《洛丽塔》中，弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫同样抱有信念——作者对绝对艺术自由的坚持；故事本身通过叙述的优美和精妙来证明其合理性。讲述一个普通家庭的故事，就像安妮·泰勒在《思乡餐厅的晚餐》中所做的那样，或许是最难找到理由的。图尔一家除了平凡生活中常见的那些寻常事之外，并无任何标新立异之处；他们住在某个特定的地址，经历过某些特定的事情，仅此而已。泰勒是一位如此内敛谦逊的作家，她对自己的故事主题没有做出任何公开的标榜——就像普鲁斯特一样，她依靠叙述本身来赋予故事意义。但最终，正是这部小说的历史赋予了图尔一家的故事以意义：所有其他普通人的故事都让作家和读者确信，日常生活本身就值得观察和学习。

# ↩

6. Morality and the Novel

6. 道德与小说

A ll novels, because they move repeatedly between action and reflection, are simultaneously about private experience and public events. For this reason, morality is a perennial gray area in the novel—characters are always doing things in private that challenge the reader's sense of what is appropriate. The Decameron and The Heptameron took up topics of sexuality and virtue that were natural to their simultaneously public and private “gossip” structure: ten friends sitting around telling compelling stories, and these topics remained perennial concerns of lengthy written prose narratives with protagonists. The ambiguous public/private nature of the novel makes it ideally suited to portray immoral acts, especially sexually explicit ones, and the history of the novel is marked by books that were burned and banned but gained immortality and widespread distribution anyway.

所有小说，由于其在行动与反思之间反复转换，同时又涉及私人体验和公共事件。因此，道德在小说中始终是一个模糊不清的灰色地带——人物私下里总有一些行为挑战着读者对何为得体的认知。《十日谈》和《七日谈》探讨了性和美德等话题，这与它们兼具公共性和私人性的“闲聊”结构相得益彰：十个朋友围坐在一起，讲述引人入胜的故事，而这些话题也一直是长篇散文叙事作品中主人公们永恒关注的主题。小说这种模糊的公私界限使其非常适合描绘不道德的行为，尤其是露骨的性行为，而小说史也见证了许多书籍被焚毁、被禁，却最终获得永生和广泛传播的悲剧。

The very fact that the novel exists in that gray area that is both public and private encourages both sides of any controversy over morality. To begin with, the author's sense of privacy while he is writing permits him to take up subjects and compose scenes he might hesitate to address in company. The book's subsequent entrance into the public arena is generally unaccompanied by the person of the author, but happens piecemeal. Gossip about the novel then builds its desirability. After the first copies are distributed, it is virtually impossible for any authorities to stop their spread, and if a controversy enters the public mind, the desirability of the novel grows—it becomes less like a tomato and more like a diamond necklace as threats to limit or stop its distribution seem about to be realized. The supporters of the novel then may act quite disingenuously sincere, and challenge the very idea that the novel has a public life, because it is always experienced in private and the decision to read such a novel is always an individual one. The usual defense of a controversial novel is that if people are offended, they don't have to read the book (and people who are offended often have not read the book, but are acting on rumor). Because of the practical impossibility of stopping the spread of banned novels, every controversy that becomes widespread reinforces the idea that the zone of the novel is a free zone, a play zone, a zone of privacy, and a zone where the individual's relationship to the group is under active contemplation—in other words, immoral novels reinforce the very idea of the novel, usually making a reader (like a protagonist) more determined to make up her own mind because it is both moral and identity-confirming to do so.

小说游走于公私交界的灰色地带，这一事实本身就助长了任何道德争议的双方。首先，作者在写作时的私密性使他能够探讨一些在公共场合可能难以启齿的主题和场景。其次，小说进入公众视野的过程通常并非作者本人参与，而是零星地发生。围绕小说的流言蜚语逐渐提升了它的吸引力。首批样书发行后，任何权威机构几乎都无法阻止其传播。一旦争议进入公众视野，小说的吸引力便会与日俱增——随着限制或停止发行的威胁似乎即将成为现实，它不再像一颗番茄，而更像是一条钻石项链。此时，小说的支持者可能会表现得虚伪而真诚，质疑小说是否具有公共性，因为阅读小说始终是私人的，是否阅读这类小说也始终是个人的选择。对于一部引发争议的小说，人们通常的辩护理由是：如果有人感到冒犯，他们可以选择不读这本书（而那些感到冒犯的人往往并没有读过这本书，只是道听途说）。由于几乎不可能阻止禁书的传播，每一次引发广泛争议的事件都会强化这样一种观念：小说的世界是一个自由的领域、一个游戏的领域、一个私密的领域，也是一个个人积极思考自身与群体关系的领域——换句话说，不道德的小说反而强化了小说本身的意义，通常会让读者（如同小说中的主人公）更加坚定地做出自己的判断，因为这样做既符合道德规范，又能确认自身的身份认同。

One of the first banned novels was the anonymous Lazarillo de Tormes , which was published during the reign of the very controlling and conservative Philip II of Spain, who is also notorious for the Spanish Inquisition and the Spanish Armada. Lazarillo is a child narrator, who happens to observe the hypocrisy, brutality, and lechery of the adults in authority around him. Philip's efforts to ban the novel were absolutely unavailing. It went through many editions and spawned the coarse and comic genre of the picaresque, but the story does not follow Lazarillo as he goes upon a journey—in fact, much of the action is domestic. Lazarillo reports that the priest he serves hoards the bread and the nobleman he is later employed by absconds without paying his rent. Lazarillo's main freedom seems to be expressing an independent opinion about people he should pay respect to. Lazarillo de Tormes demonstrates what should be evident, and is in part the subject of The Decameron and The Heptameron —respectable people often have embarrassing secrets. It is not a very subtle or ambitious work—but its importance was enhanced by the fact of banning. Every banned novel makes the world in which it is banned more and more like itself—a place where individuals have inner lives that they protect and points of view that they value; a place where people of like minds connect through reading the novel, even when it is difficult to do so; a place where prohibited types of connections, often sexual ones, are actively pursued as gestures of resistance, where pressure from the outside reinforces the zone of privacy; and where moral rules are seen to be questions of taste, mores, and custom.

最早被禁的小说之一是匿名小说《托尔梅斯的拉扎里洛》，它出版于专制保守的西班牙国王腓力二世统治时期，腓力二世还因西班牙宗教裁判所和西班牙无敌舰队而臭名昭著。小说以孩童拉扎里洛的视角叙述，他目睹了周围掌权成年人的虚伪、残暴和好色。腓力二世试图禁掉这部小说，但最终徒劳无功。它多次再版，并催生了粗俗滑稽的流浪汉小说这一体裁。然而，故事并非围绕拉扎里洛的旅程展开——事实上，大部分情节都发生在他的日常生活中。拉扎里洛写道，他侍奉的牧师囤积面包，而他后来雇佣的贵族则拖欠房租后潜逃。拉扎里洛最大的自由似乎在于，他可以自由地表达自己对应该尊重的人的看法。 《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》展现了一个显而易见的事实，而这恰恰也是《十日谈》和《七日谈》的部分主题——体面的人往往也有难以启齿的秘密。这部作品并不精妙或雄心勃勃，但禁书事件反而提升了它的重要性。每一部被禁的小说都会让被禁的世界变得越来越像它本身——一个人们珍视内心世界和观点、并加以保护的世界；一个志同道合的人通过阅读小说建立联系的世界，即便这种联系有时十分艰难；一个被禁止的、往往是性关系的联系被积极追求以示反抗的世界；一个外部压力反而强化了隐私空间的世界；以及一个道德准则被视为品味、风俗和习惯问题的世界。

Early novels wrestled with these issues over and over, and their authors had to commit themselves to one side or the other. Though Cervantes seems to have been familiar with and influenced by Lazarillo de Tormes , and certainly The Heptameron , he decided that sexuality and manly virtue could not be reconciled. It is no coincidence that Quixote and Sancho leave Quixote's estate and pass most of the plot in the out-of-doors, a public world, where they are subject to the observation and opinions of a multitude of other characters. Part of the comedy of the plot is that Quixote has been misled by the romances he loves to read, and at one point his housekeeper and his servants decide to wall up his library so that not only can he not get at it, he is also supposed to wonder whether it ever existed. Books—romances, in fact, about love—are dangerous. Is Cervantes agreeing with this idea or making fun of it? At this point it is impossible to say, but the effect of Don Quixote on the subsequent history of the novel was to shift respectability away from depictions of sex, even as a component of love (private drama), and toward depictions of violence (public drama).

早期小说反复探讨这些问题，作者们不得不选择站在其中一方。尽管塞万提斯似乎熟悉并受到《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》以及《七日谈》的影响，但他最终认为性欲与男子气概无法调和。堂吉诃德和桑丘离开堂吉诃德的庄园，并将大部分情节发生在户外——一个公共世界——这绝非偶然，他们在那里要接受众多其他人物的观察和评判。情节的喜剧效果之一在于，堂吉诃德被他喜爱的浪漫小说所误导，甚至一度他的管家和仆人决定将他的藏书封起来，这样他不仅无法接触到这些书，还要怀疑它们是否真的存在过。书籍——尤其是关于爱情的浪漫小说——是危险的。塞万提斯是在认同这种观点，还是在嘲讽它呢？目前还无法断言，但《堂吉诃德》对小说后续发展的影响是，它使人们对性描写（即使是作为爱情的一部分，即私人戏剧）的尊重程度，转向了对暴力描写（公共戏剧）。

Nevertheless, throughout the eighteenth century, issues of sexuality were the ones that powered the rise of the novel, and authors tried various methods to put them over, including anonymity (Defoe); wit (Fielding); endless, and perhaps numbing, detail (Richardson); a cautionary tone (Susanna Rowson in Charlotte Temple , the best-selling novel in the United States at the end of the eighteenth century and the beginning of the nineteenth); and sheer brazen excess (de Sade). On the surface, it may be that the subject of romance seemed simple as well as appealing to eighteenth-century authors—what could be easier than to bring the attractive young woman and the manly fellow to the altar after a few exciting adventures? It is the standard plot of a multitude of plays. But in fact, the use of actors and the public nature of the stage circumscribed what the authors could portray (as did, of course, laws against lasciviousness and public nakedness). As soon as a character is alone in her chamber, though, writing a letter, like Pamela, or hiding out, like Roxana, the pressure on propriety intensifies. The character may set out only to report his or her adventures, but because the novel always moves between action and reflection, soon enough he or she is bringing to bear his or her intentions, desires, regrets, fears, self-justifications, and other, more secret thoughts. If the character tries to merely report actions, they quickly become confusing because without feelings, actions don't carry enough emotional weight to remain clear in the reader's mind. But as soon as the character begins to develop a rationale for his or her actions, the narrative moves toward a confession. And what good is a confession if the character has nothing to confess—that is, no moral dilemma, no temptation to be delivered from? Without drama, a novel ceases to be entertaining and therefore loses its reason to exist.

然而，在整个十八世纪，性问题正是推动小说兴起的动力，作家们尝试了各种方法来展现这些主题，包括匿名（笛福）；机智（菲尔丁）；无休止甚至令人麻木的细节描写（理查森）；警世的语气（苏珊娜·罗森在《夏洛特·坦普尔》中的表现，这部小说在十八世纪末十九世纪初成为美国最畅销的小说）；以及肆无忌惮的放纵（萨德）。表面上看，爱情题材对十八世纪的作家来说似乎既简单又吸引人——还有什么比让一位迷人的年轻女子和一位英俊的男子在经历几段刺激的冒险后步入婚姻殿堂更容易的呢？这几乎是所有戏剧的标准情节。但事实上，演员的使用以及舞台的公开性限制了作家们可以描绘的内容（当然，禁止淫荡和公共场合裸露的法律也起到了限制作用）。然而，一旦人物独自待在房间里，像帕梅拉那样写信，或者像罗克珊娜那样躲藏起来，体面的压力就会加剧。人物最初可能只是想记录自己的冒险经历，但由于小说总是在行动和反思之间切换，很快，他或她就会将自己的意图、欲望、悔恨、恐惧、自我辩解以及其他更隐秘的想法融入其中。如果人物只是试图叙述行动，这些行动很快就会变得混乱，因为没有情感，行动就缺乏足够的情感分量，难以在读者心中留下清晰的印象。但一旦人物开始为自己的行为寻找理由，叙事就会朝着坦白的方向发展。如果人物没有什么可坦白的——也就是说，没有道德困境，没有需要克服的诱惑——那么坦白又有什么意义呢？没有戏剧冲突，小说就失去了娱乐性，也失去了存在的意义。

In addition, of course, eighteenth-century novelists, like novelists before and after them, were eager to depict the world they lived in, and in the world they lived in seduction, sexual predation, rape, sexual slavery, marriages of convenience, marriages based solely on property considerations, prostitution, child abandonment, the sale of children into servitude of all kinds, and, of course, disease, suffering, and early death were commonplace. To raise the simple moral issue of whether a girl should be allowed to fall in love with the man of her own choice or be required to marry the man of her parents’ choice was to enter into a train of logic that could lead to all sorts of much more complex and difficult moral questions.

当然，十八世纪的小说家们，如同他们之前和之后的小说家一样，都热衷于描绘他们所生活的世界。在他们所生活的世界里，诱惑、性侵犯、强奸、性奴役、权宜婚姻、纯粹基于财产考量的婚姻、卖淫、遗弃儿童、贩卖儿童从事各种奴役活动，以及疾病、苦难和早逝，都司空见惯。仅仅提出一个女孩是否应该被允许爱上自己选择的男人，还是应该被迫嫁给父母选择的男人这样简单的道德问题，就会引发一系列逻辑推演，最终引出各种各样更为复杂和棘手的道德问题。

One way to deal with these issues was to address their moral content directly, which is what Voltaire does in Candide ( 1759 ) when he has Dr. Pangloss propose that “everything is for the best in this best of all possible worlds.” Candide himself, his beloved Cunegonde, and Dr. Pangloss then set out upon a whirlwind tour of the known world to test this hypothesis. The answer they come up with is considerably different and more brutal than the answer Quixote comes up with. Whereas Quixote is beaten from time to time, and tricked, and disillusioned, Candide finds wars, famines, epidemics, slavery, gratuitous brutality, and destruction of every kind—political, personal, environmental, social. No person and no place (except for El Dorado, far from Europe, entirely surrounded by impassable mountains, and rich beyond compare) is immune from the wholesale Hobbesian conflict of all against all, and no character, even the beautiful Cunegonde, is safe from the effects of the world. Evil is everywhere. Candide succeeds as a polemic, but it doesn't succeed as a novel, precisely because Voltaire sets out his program too clearly and hardly bothers with his novelistic duties of character and plot development. Surprisingly, it is the disreputable Justine , by the disreputable marquis de Sade, that makes the point Voltaire hoped to make with the impact Voltaire intended.

处理这些问题的一种方法是直接探讨其道德内涵，伏尔泰在《老实人》（1759）中正是如此。他让庞格洛斯医生提出“在这个所有可能世界中最好的世界里，一切都是最好的安排”。随后，老实人、他心爱的库内贡德和庞格洛斯医生踏上了一段旋风般的环球之旅，以验证这一假设。他们得出的答案与堂吉诃德的答案截然不同，也更加残酷。堂吉诃德时常遭受殴打、欺骗和幻灭，而老实人则目睹了战争、饥荒、瘟疫、奴隶制、无端的暴行以及各种形式的破坏——政治的、个人的、环境的、社会的。除了远离欧洲、四周群山环绕、富饶无比的黄金国埃尔多拉多之外，世间没有任何人或地方能够免受霍布斯式的全面冲突——所有人与所有人为敌——的影响，即使是美丽的库内贡德也无法逃脱世俗的侵蚀。邪恶无处不在。《老实人》作为一部论战作品是成功的，但作为一部小说却并不成功，原因恰恰在于伏尔泰过于直白地阐述了他的意图，而几乎没有顾及小说家应尽的人物塑造和情节发展。令人惊讶的是，正是声名狼藉的萨德侯爵笔下声名狼藉的朱斯蒂娜，以伏尔泰预期的震撼力，阐明了他想要表达的观点。

Justine was published in 1791 , during the French Revolution, and the novel's theme, you might say, is the right of every man of rank to do whatever he wants with any woman he can gain access to, preferably by force. The catalog of brutalized and exploited women in Justine runs the gamut from legitimately married wives and daughters of great families to nameless girls from the streets and includes examples of every rank and type in between. According to de Sade, being sold into marriage is the least of it. Women are also sold into slavery, thievery, and prostitution; they are turned over by their guardians to torturers and necrophiliacs if their guardians themselves don't care to torture and rape them. Young girls are routinely betrayed by both women and men, by those who like them and by those who hate them. The only true and lasting motives of anyone in de Sade's world are greed first and lust second (those who are less lusty gain more profit), though expounding various theories is also a pastime of libertines of every class. It is the explosion of theory that differentiates de Sade from Marguerite de Navarre's Hircan. For Hircan, the right to exploit women is a matter of honor—it bolsters the God-given social order. For a woman to rebel against it is a form of treason, or even blasphemy. In Justine , the goal is not to reinforce the social order but to maximize the exploitation of female flesh. If the women rebel or object, so much the better in terms of excitement, because the more desirable goal for the sadist is to inflict punishment since, as one of the men Justine meets early in the novel tells her, regular sex with women is boring and also damages the monetary value of the woman in question, especially if she is young and can be sold into marriage for a large sum. What real men really want is to be buggered by their servants.

《朱斯蒂娜》出版于1791年，正值法国大革命时期。可以说，这部小说的主题是：任何有身份的男人都有权随意处置任何他能接触到的女人，最好是用武力。小说中被虐待和剥削的女性形形色色，从名门望族的合法妻子和女儿，到街头无名少女，涵盖了所有阶层和类型的女性。在萨德看来，被卖为妻只是其中最轻微的。女性还会被卖为奴隶、从事盗窃和卖淫；如果监护人自己不愿折磨和强奸她们，就会把她们交给施虐者和恋尸癖者。年轻女孩经常遭到背叛，背叛者既有喜欢她们的人，也有憎恨她们的人。在萨德的世界里，所有人的真正且持久的动机首先是贪婪，其次是欲望（欲望越淡，获利越多），尽管阐述各种理论也是各个阶层浪荡子的消遣。正是这种理论的爆炸式增长，使萨德与玛格丽特·德·纳瓦尔笔下的希尔坎区别开来。对希尔坎而言，剥削女性的权利是一种荣誉——它巩固了上帝赋予的社会秩序。女性反抗这种秩序是一种叛国行为，甚至是亵渎神明。而在《朱斯蒂娜》中，目标并非维护社会秩序，而是最大限度地剥削女性的肉体。如果女性反抗或反对，那对施虐者来说反而更刺激，因为对施虐者而言，更理想的目标是施加惩罚。正如朱斯蒂娜在小说开头遇到的一位男子告诉她的那样，与女性进行常规性行为既乏味，也会损害女性的经济价值，尤其是当她们年轻貌美，可以被高价卖给别人时。真正的男人真正想要的，是被自己的仆人肛交。

When the men and women Justine meets on her journey around France are not violating her, they are trying to convince her that even if what they are doing to her is not right according to conventional morality, then at least it's natural and inevitable. Many of the sexual scenes are shockingly graphic, but many are politically shocking, too. At one point Justine is standing in the shade of a tree, and she sees a large, wealthy, and scenic monastery in the valley below her. She goes there for refuge and is taken into a torture ring run by powerful monks and church elders, who not only cruelly exploit and torture succeeding populations of girls and women, but also murder them for pleasure and dispose of the bodies on the grounds of the monastery. She and another girl attempt to escape; she succeeds, the other girl doesn't. Justine's journey shows her the secret life of all of France— every chteau, every wood, every house in town, every church, every seat of secular or religious power hides one or more libertines, who constitute a vast, informal conspiracy, or, you might say, a vast, corrupt governing class unfettered by law or morality.

在朱斯蒂娜游历法国的旅途中，她遇到的男男女女虽然没有侵犯她，但他们试图说服她，即使他们对她所做的一切不符合传统道德，至少也是自然而然、不可避免的。许多性爱场景都令人震惊地露骨，同时也触及了许多政治敏感话题。有一次，朱斯蒂娜站在树荫下，看到山谷下方有一座规模宏大、富丽堂皇、风景如画的修道院。她前往那里寻求庇护，却落入了一个由权势显赫的僧侣和教会长老掌控的酷刑团伙。这些人不仅残忍地剥削和折磨一批又一批的女孩和妇女，还为了取乐而杀害她们，并将尸体丢弃在修道院内。她和另一个女孩试图逃跑；她成功了，另一个女孩却没能逃脱。朱斯蒂娜的旅程向她展示了整个法国的秘密生活——每座城堡、每片树林、城镇里的每一栋房子、每座教堂、每一个世俗或宗教权力中心都隐藏着一个或多个放荡不羁之徒，他们构成了一个庞大的非正式阴谋集团，或者，你可以说，是一个庞大的、腐败的统治阶级，不受法律或道德的约束。

I don't think a modern reader can read Justine , even in the context of other eighteenth-century novels, without wondering if even a portion of what de Sade portrayed was true, or if it was all a projection on his part. It seems obvious that de Sade wrote Justine for pornographic reasons—that is, the plot and the protagonist are there to serve the author's and the reader's shared desire to fetishize sex and cruelty and to use images for lascivious excitement. De Sade himself asserted that Justine was “capable of corrupting the devil” (possibly an example of authorial wishful thinking). Even so, while most eighteenth-century novels that portray rape, intended rape, or rape through false marriage more or less treat the issue as a personal one—a particular man attempting the virtue of a particular woman (only Defoe has a larger view of the structural disadvantages of womanhood), de Sade makes rape part of the apparatus of state control as expressed by individual members of the ruling class (most of whom possess formal authority; they are not renegades or rogues). He is also the only one who asserts that there is no virtue anywhere in the society—no one person who is not lustful, greedy, ready to kill for the slightest advantage. How does the author really feel about this state of affairs? On the one hand, various mouthpieces for his views make the case that nature is red in tooth and claw, so such cruel relations between people are natural and not to be resisted or regretted. On the other hand, he allows Justine to be unconvinced. In the end she wins, insofar as she is able; she never gives up her attachment to autonomy, and she is spared further suffering through sudden death. Justine is a true heroine; she never betrays herself, always tries to understand and survive, never loses her moral compass. Surely she speaks for the author as much as the men do.

我认为，即使将《朱斯蒂娜》置于其他十八世纪小说的语境中，现代读者在阅读时也难免会怀疑，萨德笔下描绘的究竟有多少是真实发生的，还是仅仅是他个人的臆想。萨德创作《朱斯蒂娜》的动机显然是出于色情目的——也就是说，故事情节和主人公的存在，是为了满足作者和读者共同的欲望：将性和残忍物化，并利用图像来激发淫欲。萨德本人甚至断言，朱斯蒂娜“能够腐蚀魔鬼”（这或许只是作者的一厢情愿）。即便如此，尽管大多数十八世纪小说中描写强奸、意图强奸或通过虚假婚姻进行的强奸，或多或少都将其视为个人问题——某个男人试图玷污某个女人的贞洁（只有笛福对女性所处的结构性劣势有着更宏观的视角），但萨德却将强奸视为国家控制机制的一部分，并由统治阶级的成员（他们大多拥有正式权力；他们并非叛逆者或恶棍）来执行。他也是唯一一个断言社会中不存在任何美德的人——没有一个人不贪婪、不淫荡，不为任何微不足道的利益而杀人。作者对这种现状究竟作何感想？一方面，他的观点被各种代言人用来论证自然界弱肉强食，因此人与人之间这种残酷的关系是自然的，无需反抗或后悔。另一方面，他又允许朱斯蒂娜对此持怀疑态度。最终，她取得了胜利，尽管她力所能及。她始终坚持自主，最终因猝死而免于进一步的痛苦。朱斯蒂娜是一位真正的女英雄；她从未背叛自己，始终努力理解和生存，从未迷失道德准则。毫无疑问，她和那些男性角色一样，都代表了作者的心声。

Perhaps the political cast of Justine is accidental to the simple requirement of a novel to have a protagonist. If de Sade's purpose is to portray a world of tortures and temptations merely as a pornographic catalog, then Justine makes a good protagonist—in part a tour guide to this world, in part a foil for it—by striving for virtue. She does what protagonists do, for while it cannot be said that she is transformed by her journey, she is revealed as even more resolute than she appeared to be at the beginning. Perhaps de Sade is simply creating a logical scheme upon which he can hang his inhumane fantasies, but he does give Justine an articulate point of view. Though for the purposes of the plot, she must go on in a way that becomes almost purely existential, since she loses everything but her dignity and her identity and never has reason to hope for anything better than more torture, and is never convinced by the evidence of her own senses or by the arguments of the parade of libertines, she knows what she wants, and she continues to want it. However many times she is violated physically, she is never violated psychologically—she is as virtuous as Pamela at the end. And the reader never betrays Justine, either, by sympathizing with her exploiters, no matter how eloquent they are in their arguments. When at the end she opens a window and is struck by lightning, de Sade's ploy to get himself out of the novel has the effect of an apotheosis—the singularity of Justine's death suits her singular ability to endure and becomes a type of anointing. Justine shows that whatever an author's motives for depicting horror, the form of the novel itself molds the depiction. Ostensibly shocking and immoral, Justine actually promotes a certain moral point of view—that integrity and virtue can be retained and recognized in the face of relentless suffering. In addition, to expose secret corruption is to challenge its existence because of the nature of the novel as a common and available commodity.

或许，朱斯蒂娜的政治色彩仅仅是小说必须有主角这一基本要求的偶然产物。如果萨德的目的仅仅是将一个充满酷刑和诱惑的世界描绘成一部色情作品，那么朱斯蒂娜通过追求美德，成为了一个优秀的主角——她既是这个世界的向导，也是这个世界的反面。她做了所有主角都会做的事，虽然不能说她的旅程改变了她，但她展现出的决心比故事开始时更加坚定。或许萨德只是在构建一个逻辑框架，以此来支撑他那些非人道的幻想，但他确实赋予了朱斯蒂娜一个清晰的视角。尽管为了情节需要，她必须继续走下去，而这种走下去几乎完全是存在主义式的，因为她除了尊严和身份之外失去了一切，也从未有过任何希望，除了更多的折磨之外别无他物。她既不相信自己的感官体验，也不相信那些放荡不羁之徒的辩解，但她始终清楚自己想要什么，并且执着地想要着。无论她遭受多少次肉体上的侵犯，她的精神却从未受到摧残——最终，她和帕梅拉一样纯洁无瑕。读者也从未背叛朱斯蒂娜，不会同情那些剥削她的人，无论他们的辩解多么雄辩滔滔。当最后她打开窗户被闪电击中时，萨德为了摆脱小说而耍的伎俩却产生了一种神化的效果——朱斯蒂娜之死的独特性与她独特的忍耐力相得益彰，成为一种加冕仪式。 《朱斯蒂娜》表明，无论作者描绘恐怖的动机是什么，小说的形式本身都会影响这种描绘。表面上看似令人震惊且不道德，《朱斯蒂娜》实际上却宣扬了一种道德观点——即使面对无情的苦难，正直和美德依然可以保持并得到认可。此外，由于小说作为一种大众化的、易于获取的商品，揭露隐秘的腐败本身就是对腐败存在的挑战。

The degree to which we comfortably read novels that were once banned, proscribed, or denounced is the degree to which we are trained by the novel to accept the ambiguous public/private nature of novels as a whole. If the private side of the novel promotes depictions of sex, then the public side promotes depictions of violence, which we also read in private. Because all lengthy written prose narratives with protagonists concern tension or conflict between the protagonist and the group, the moral implications of social conflict have always been a subject of the novel. One way of noting how this works is to look at the Icelandic sagas, which seem to have been invented entirely to explore this issue. Violence is as tempting to the writer, of course, as sex, because it raises the stakes of the plot to a high and dramatic level, which is enhanced further by the facility with which the author can move between the blows delivered and the thoughts of those delivering them. Scenes of violence in a novel, for example, don't have to be burdened by exclamations and asides, like sword fights on the stage; the reader gets the dual suspense of the progress of the fight combined with the hidden and usually different progress in the intentions and reactions of the fighters. As with sexual issues, though, the author always finds himself wrestling with extra moral questions that an apparently simple fight poses.

我们能够自在地阅读那些曾经被禁、被禁止或被谴责的小说，其程度取决于小说本身对我们接受公共/私人性质模糊性的程度。如果说小说的私人层面鼓励对性的描写，那么公共层面则鼓励对暴力的描写，而这些暴力描写我们也同样会在私人场合阅读。由于所有以主人公为中心的长篇散文叙事都涉及主人公与群体之间的紧张关系或冲突，因此社会冲突的道德内涵一直是小说的主题。了解这一点的一个方法是考察冰岛萨迦，这些萨迦似乎完全是为了探讨这个问题而创作的。当然，暴力对作家来说和性一样具有诱惑力，因为它能将情节的紧张程度提升到一个高且戏剧性的水平，而作者能够自如地在暴力行为和施暴者的内心世界之间切换，更增强了这种戏剧效果。例如，小说中的暴力场景不必像舞台上的剑术对决那样充斥着惊叹和旁白；读者既能感受到战斗进程带来的紧张感，又能体会到战斗双方意图和反应中隐藏的、通常截然不同的变化。然而，就像性问题一样，作者总是会发现自己不得不面对看似简单的战斗背后所隐藏的道德困境。

A saga begins with a misfit who gets into a conflict with those around him. He may be a fairly decent or respected man whose conflict is almost accidental, such as Gisli, in Gislasaga , or he might be a naturally aggressive and pugnacious individual, such as Egil, in Egils-saga , but he always has some quality that sets him apart to begin with (women characters may have these qualities also). In the course of the narrative, a combination of personality and circumstances or luck or fate expands the conflict until it becomes an unresolvable feud. At each stage of the rising action, men of importance attempt to resolve the issues by assigning blame and penalties of outlawry or forfeiture of property or money, and, at every stage of the conflict, some example of graphic violence is included in the narrative—heads are hacked off, men are cut in two from neck to crotch, a man continues to fight while holding his intestines together with his shirt, a family is burned alive in their house. In some cases, as with Gisli and Egil, the misfit is simply too strong a personality to accept his punishment. In other cases, as in Njalssaga , the two sides continue to inflame the situation by provoking one another in spite of the penalties. As the conflict spreads through the district—or, indeed, the whole country—the violence gets more graphic. The saga ends either when the misfit is killed, as with Gisli, or when the group can no longer tolerate the violence the feud has sparked, as in Njalssaga.

传奇故事通常以一个格格不入的人与周围的人发生冲突开篇。他或许是位相当体面或受人尊敬的人，冲突几乎是偶然发生的，例如《吉斯拉传奇》中的吉斯利；又或许是位天性好斗好斗的人，例如《埃吉尔传奇》中的埃吉尔。但无论如何，他总有一些特质使他与众不同（女性角色也可能具备这些特质）。随着故事的推进，性格、环境、运气或命运的共同作用使冲突不断扩大，最终演变成一场无法化解的世仇。在冲突升级的每个阶段，一些重要人物都会试图通过追究责任和施以惩罚（例如驱逐出境或没收财产或金钱）来解决问题。而在冲突的每个阶段，叙事中都会穿插一些血腥暴力的场景——人头被砍下，男人被从脖子到下体拦腰斩断，有人用衬衫捂着肠子继续战斗，一家人被活活烧死在房子里。在某些情况下，例如吉斯利和埃吉尔，格格不入者个性过于强势，无法接受惩罚。而在另一些情况下，例如尼亚尔萨加，尽管受到惩罚，双方仍继续互相挑衅，激化局势。随着冲突蔓延至整个地区乃至全国，暴力事件也愈演愈烈。故事的结局要么是格格不入者被杀（如吉斯利），要么是群体再也无法容忍这场仇杀引发的暴力（如尼亚尔萨加）。

The thirteenth and fourteenth centuries in Iceland were marked by violence and lawlessness all over the island. The probable author of Egilssaga , Snorri Sturluson, was himself killed by political rivals. The situation became so desperate in the middle of the fourteenth century that the Icelanders gave up their independence and asked the Norwegian king to resume control of the island (control of Iceland from Europe continued then for six hundred years, until after the Second World War, when the Danes, who succeeded the Norwegians, gave Iceland independence). The history of the sagas shows that Icelanders of the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries wrestled constantly with the nature of social unrest, sometimes locating its origin in personalities, sometimes in circumstances, but testifying always to its ubiquity. In every saga, ever-present weapons and volatile personalities combine to injure the group. But the sagas also show that freedom and intransigence have an appeal—the saga authors can't help admiring the strength of such personalities as Egil, who is not attractive in any way, being churlish, beetle-browed, and short-tempered. He represents some essential Icelandic quality of irreducible independence opposed to the effete courtiers of the Norwegian king. Even so, while the sagas were deeply indebted to the epic tradition and existed side by side with Icelandic epic poems, they were closer to novels than epics. The essential purpose of sagas was not to glorify the regrettable necessity of slaughter—gods like Zeus and Krishna do not enter into the action and try to influence or advise the characters—but to measure the social costs of individualism and its corollary, freedom.

13至14世纪的冰岛，暴力和混乱席卷全岛。埃吉尔萨迦的作者斯诺里·斯图鲁松本人也被政治对手杀害。14世纪中叶，局势恶化到冰岛人放弃独立，请求挪威国王重新统治该岛（此后，冰岛一直处于欧洲列强的统治之下，长达六百年之久，直到二战后，接替挪威统治冰岛的丹麦人才给予冰岛独立）。萨迦的历史表明，13至14世纪的冰岛人不断与社会动荡的本质作斗争，他们有时将动荡的根源归咎于个人，有时归咎于环境，但都无一例外地证明了动荡的普遍性。在每部萨迦中，随处可见的武器和易怒的人物共同造成了群体的伤害。但萨迦也表明，自由和不妥协具有吸引力——萨迦作者不禁钦佩埃吉尔这类人物的坚强意志，尽管他外表粗鲁、眉头紧锁、脾气暴躁，毫无魅力可言。他代表了冰岛人某种不可动摇的独立精神，与挪威国王那些软弱无能的朝臣形成鲜明对比。即便如此，尽管萨迦深受史诗传统的影响，并与冰岛史诗并存，但它们更接近小说而非史诗。萨迦的根本目的并非歌颂杀戮这种令人遗憾的必要性——宙斯和克里希纳等神祇并未介入剧情，试图影响或劝诫人物——而是为了衡量个人主义及其必然结果——自由——所带来的社会代价。

After the Icelanders turned over their government to the king of Norway, the saga, one of the greatest forms of literature in the history of civilization, went out of fashion, replaced by tales and poems that are more like folklore than novels. Without the social struggles that marked the saga era, and the dilemmas of freedom that are so like those that Europeans and their descendants have faced in the past three hundred years, the Icelandic form of the lengthy written prose narrative with a protagonist had no reason to exist.

冰岛人将政权移交给挪威国王后，萨迦——文明史上最伟大的文学形式之一——逐渐式微，取而代之的是更接近民间传说而非小说的故事和诗歌。萨迦时代所经历的社会斗争，以及与过去三百年来欧洲人及其后裔所面临的自由困境极为相似的种种抉择，使得冰岛那种以主人公为中心的长篇散文叙事形式失去了存在的意义。

Novelists gradually became more adept at analyzing what has turned out to be one of the novel's most fertile subjects, the morality of personal relationships, which seems, on the surface, to avoid both the pitfalls of sex and the pitfalls of violence. Perhaps the works of Jane Austen are our paradigm. Her six novels are deemed entirely safe for consumption by the most innocent of readers; “evil” hardly enters her world, except in the form of insensitivity or rudeness. Of course, the smooth acceptability of Austen's work turns out to be an illusion— underneath her proper sentiments and her perfectly modulated tone of ironic reserve there is a sharp, irreverent, and even revolutionary spirit. But in her explorations of personal relationships, she showed that it was possible to write serious, astute, and sophisticated “domestic” novels, and these sorts of novels, largely avoiding both sex and violence, became the staple of the nineteenth century.

小说家们逐渐擅长分析人际关系中的道德问题，而这已成为小说中最具启发性的主题之一。表面上看，人际关系似乎既避开了性的陷阱，也避开了暴力的陷阱。简·奥斯汀的作品或许就是我们的典范。她的六部小说被认为完全适合最纯真的读者阅读；“邪恶”几乎不会出现在她的世界里，除非是以冷漠或粗鲁的形式出现。当然，奥斯汀作品的这种平易近人最终被证明是一种假象——在她恰当的情感和恰到好处的讽刺语调之下，蕴藏着一种尖锐、不敬，甚至是革命性的精神。但她对人际关系的探索表明，严肃、敏锐、老练的“家庭”小说也是可以创作的，而这类小说，由于大多避免了性和暴力，成为了十九世纪的主流文学。

Even in these novels, though, potential moral issues abound, along with the power to shock the reader, and far more shockingly cruel, in its way, than Justine is that staple of middle school, Wuthering Heights. No one has ever considered Wuthering Heights to be unsuitable for young girls; most women read it for the first time when they are thirteen or fourteen. There are no sex scenes in Wuthering Heights , and many readers doubt whether the lovers, Cathy and Heathcliff, ever have sex. She is a young girl when he runs away; there is no suggestion that she has been unchaste. She is a married woman when he returns; there is no suggestion that she betrays her husband. Whether Heath-cliff has ever made love to another woman by the time he returns is moot—he is obsessed with Cathy and appears to have thought of nothing else in his time away. No doubt part of the reason girls love Wuthering Heights is that it may (only the author knows for sure) portray the most passionate love as asexual and entirely spiritualized, rather like standing on a high promontory and feeling the wind blowing off the moors. At the same time, there are no beatings or shootings in Wuthering Heights. The only blood shed is by a ghost in a dream.

即便在这些小说中，也充斥着潜在的道德问题，以及震撼读者的力量。而比《朱斯汀》更令人震惊的，莫过于中学经典读物《呼啸山庄》。从来没有人认为《呼啸山庄》不适合年轻女孩阅读；大多数女性第一次读这本书时，年龄都在十三四岁。书中没有性爱描写，许多读者甚至怀疑凯茜和希斯克利夫这对恋人是否真的发生过性关系。希斯克利夫离家出走时，凯茜还是个年轻女孩；书中没有任何暗示表明她不贞。希斯克利夫回来时，凯茜已为人妻；书中也没有任何暗示表明她背叛了丈夫。至于希斯克利夫回来之前是否与其他女人有过性关系，也无关紧要——他痴迷于凯茜，似乎在离家期间，他的脑海里只有她。毫无疑问，女孩们喜爱《呼啸山庄》的部分原因在于，它或许（只有作者才知道确切答案）将最炽烈的爱情描绘成无性且完全精神化的，如同站在高高的岬角上，感受着荒原上吹来的风。同时，《呼啸山庄》中没有殴打或枪击的场景。唯一流血的，是梦中的鬼魂。

Nevertheless, the theme of Wuthering Heights is that any betrayal, any cruelty, any indifference to others, including spouses and children, is, if not justifiable, then understandable, in the context of sufficient passion. A woman who returns to Wuthering Heights as an adult most likely feels more uncomfortable with Heathcliff, in particular, than she did as a girl. For one thing, and this is not unimportant, Heathcliff is rude by choice. Since charm is one of the qualities that keeps readers reading, Heathcliff's rudeness has to be compensated for, and it never is. For another, Heathcliff is wantonly cruel to young Catherine and Hareton (whom he has betrayed as a father figure by failing to educate him in any way), because he means to avenge himself upon their dead parents through them, moment by moment and day by day. He oppresses, neglects, and abuses them because they are who they are. In other words, his only redeeming quality grows increasingly abstract as the novel progresses, and he doesn't develop any new ones. The Heathcliff of the novel is not played by Laurence Olivier. He is played by your scary Uncle Hugo, who never liked you for a moment.

然而，《呼啸山庄》的主题是，任何背叛、任何残忍、任何对他人（包括配偶和子女）的冷漠，即便不能被合理化，至少在强烈的激情之下也是可以理解的。一个成年后重返呼啸山庄的女人，很可能比少女时代更难以忍受希斯克利夫，尤其是他这个人。首先，这一点至关重要，希斯克利夫的粗鲁是他有意为之。魅力是吸引读者继续阅读的关键因素之一，因此希斯克利夫的粗鲁必须得到某种补偿，而这种补偿却从未出现。其次，希斯克利夫肆意虐待年幼的凯瑟琳和哈里顿（他没有尽到父亲的责任，没有给予哈里顿任何教育），因为他想通过他们，日复一日、时时刻刻地，向他们死去的父母复仇。他压迫、忽视、虐待他们，仅仅因为他们是他们自己。换句话说，随着小说的推进，他唯一的优点变得越来越抽象，而且他也没有发展出任何新的优点。小说中的希斯克利夫并非由劳伦斯·奥利弗扮演，而是由你那可怕的雨果叔叔扮演，他从来就没喜欢过你。

None of the characters of Wuthering Heights is a model of goodness, and all of their crimes are interpersonal ones. The older Cathy is capricious and selfish; her daughter is cross and petty (though kind, in the end, to Hareton). Hindley is a mean drunk, Edgar is long-suffering but weak, and Edgar's sister is spoiled and impetuous. Young Linton is, as Heathcliff truthfully observes, the worst of the bunch, though that amounts only to being whiny, imperious, and irritating. That nearly everyone comes to a bad end is not the satisfaction that it might be, though, because the reader's experience of the general bad nature of the whole crew is prolonged. Do the characters of Wuthering Heights perpetrate even a grain of the harm that the characters of Justine do? No. Does Wuthering Heights seem in the end to be a nastier novel than Justine does? Yes. They are similar in that both are unrelieved and both have endings that are happy relative to the rest of the novel. But it is more disheartening to read about Heathcliff's domestic sins than it is to see the crimes of the ruling class exposed, because the exposure of political crimes seems like a step toward ameliorating them, while Heathcliff's cruelties are specifically directed at those he should be nurturing, and only chance intervenes between him and his victims— exposure only reminds us of how pervasive domestic abuse is. The paradox is that novelists ended up exploring the rich subject of the morality of interpersonal relationships only to discover that while, on the one hand, this subject was safe from the dangers of sex and violence, on the other hand, achieving in such plots the satisfying feeling of redress is difficult if not impossible.

《呼啸山庄》中的人物没有一个是善良的典范，他们犯下的罪行也都是人际关系上的。年长的凯茜任性自私；她的女儿脾气暴躁、斤斤计较（尽管最终对哈里顿很友善）。辛德利是个刻薄的酒鬼，埃德加忍耐力强但意志薄弱，埃德加的妹妹则娇生惯养、冲动鲁莽。正如希斯克利夫所言，小林顿是这群人中最糟糕的，但这也仅仅意味着他爱抱怨、专横跋扈、令人厌烦。然而，几乎每个人都落得悲惨的下场，这并没有给读者带来应有的满足感，因为读者会长时间地感受到这群人普遍的恶劣本性。《呼啸山庄》中的人物所犯下的恶行，哪怕只有《贾斯汀》中人物所犯下的一点点吗？没有。《呼啸山庄》最终看起来比《贾斯汀》更令人厌恶吗？是的。它们的相似之处在于，两者都未曾缓解，而且结局相对于小说其他部分而言都算是圆满的。但读到希斯克利夫的家庭罪行比看到统治阶级的罪行被揭露更令人沮丧，因为揭露政治罪行似乎是朝着改善现状迈出的一步，而希斯克利夫的残忍行为却专门针对他本应关爱的人，他与受害者之间只有偶然的联系——揭露只会让我们更加意识到家庭虐待的普遍性。悖论在于，小说家们最终探索了人际关系道德这一丰富的主题，却发现一方面，这个主题可以避开性和暴力的危险；另一方面，在这样的情节中，要达到令人满意的补偿感却难上加难，甚至是不可能的。

One of the particular vocations of the novel from the beginning has been the portrayal of brutes, criminals, and psychopaths. The first story of The Decameron takes as its protagonist the wickedest man in the world, who likes to lie and steal, who is sexually deviant, who even lies when he is giving his last confession. What we know about his crimes, though, is narrated, because every time he speaks, he lies. The reader accepts him as the paradigm of evil because the other characters of the tale report that he is and Boccaccio's cast of listeners accept their judgment. The story works only if his evil nature is a premise rather than subject to discussion or proof. Boccaccio gives this tale a lot of space, but he doesn't develop his evil character's state of mind in any way. The evil characters in The Heptameron are presented in a similarly cut-and-dried way, but Marguerite and her fellow critics speculate about the motives of some of the more egregious perpetrators more than Boccaccio's listeners do. Most eighteenth-century novelists were much interested in motives and rationales for evil actions (Henry Fielding, for example, who seems ebullient and earthy in Tom Jones , explored darker themes in Jonathan Wild and Amelia) , and eighteenth-century novels are full of immorality and crime (perhaps the lengthiest depiction of the mind of a heartless seducer is Lovelace, in Samuel Richardson's Clarissa). Eighteenth-century libertines and murderers want to communicate. Authors couch their characters’ self-revelations as confessions, letters, diaries, and testaments (for example, the memoir of James Hogg's “Justified Sinner”). Even in the Romantic period, as with Lermontov's A Hero of Our Time and Julien Sorel in The Red and the Black , the psychopath readily enters into the world of communication.

从一开始，小说的一个独特之处在于刻画恶棍、罪犯和精神变态者。《十日谈》的第一个故事以世上最邪恶的人为主角，他喜欢撒谎和偷窃，性变态，甚至在临终忏悔时也撒谎。然而，我们对他的罪行的了解都来自叙述，因为他每次开口说话都在撒谎。读者之所以接受他为邪恶的化身，是因为故事中的其他人物都这样描述他，而薄伽丘笔下的听众也接受了他们的判断。这个故事只有在他的邪恶本性仅仅是前提，而非需要讨论或证明的对象时才成立。薄伽丘在这个故事中用了大量的篇幅，但他并没有以任何方式去刻画这个邪恶人物的内心世界。 《七日谈》中的反派角色也以类似的直白方式呈现，但玛格丽特和她的评论家同伴们对一些罪大恶极的罪犯的动机进行了比薄伽丘的听众更深入的探讨。大多数十八世纪的小说家都对邪恶行为的动机和理由非常感兴趣（例如，亨利·菲尔丁在《汤姆·琼斯》中显得热情奔放、质朴自然，但在《乔纳森·怀尔德》和《阿米莉亚》中则探索了更为阴暗的主题），十八世纪的小说充斥着不道德和犯罪（塞缪尔·理查森的《克拉丽莎》中对冷酷无情的诱惑者洛夫莱斯的描写或许最为详尽）。十八世纪的浪荡子和杀人犯渴望交流。作家们将笔下人物的自我剖析包装成忏悔、书信、日记和遗嘱（例如，詹姆斯·霍格的回忆录《正义的罪人》）。即使在浪漫主义时期，就像莱蒙托夫的《当代英雄》和《红与黑》中的于连·索雷尔一样，精神病患者也很容易进入交流的世界。

All the way up through the beginning of the nineteenth century, evil was viewed by novelists (as well as other writers and thinkers) as a constant of human nature. A typical example of how evil was depicted is to be found in the work of Sir Walter Scott, not much read now but wildly popular in its own day. Scott's novels regularly took up large social issues. In several novels, he concerned himself with the Scottish religious wars of the seventeenth century, which were bitterly contested ideological conflicts with lingering doctrinal, social, and political ramifications. In Scott's novels, villainy (opportunism, rudeness, snobbishness, unkindness, narrow-mindedness, willingness to do violence) occurs randomly, and membership in certain groups does not automatically translate into venality—some clergymen are decent, others are fanatical; some aristocrats are kind, others are brutal; some ideologues are honorable, others are self-serving. Scott subtly shows how, in times of ideological ferment, virtuous acts and evil acts grow out of the shifting combination in every individual of temperament, circumstances, beliefs, and desires. Events and character interact in a classically tragic way—outcomes have a fated quality. The painful effect of dramatic irony is muted by distance from the period of the narrative—Scott is careful to include images of the peaceful graves of his characters that remind the reader that the passions that motivated the conflicts have vanished as thoroughly as the conflicts themselves— and there is no sense that things could have turned out, or could turn out, differently. Even in a novel as passionately dramatic as Scott's The Bride of Lammermoor , in which, as a result of being forced to marry against her will, a young girl kills her new husband and then herself goes mad, a sense of peace and resignation result from the traditional idea that the combination of character and circumstances will always result in what we realize in retrospect was inevitable. One of Scott's innovations, artistically, was to take traditional tragic patterns and apply them, not just to kings and princes, but also to a whole society of characters, high and low, male and female, victorious or defeated. Another was to pay close attention, even in the context of the Gothic-seeming plot The Bride of Lammermoor , to the intricacies of psychological and sociological cause and effect. Gothic tales such as The Mysteries of Udolpho , by Ann Radcliffe, were all the rage in Scott's day, and he puts plenty of uncanny incidents into his novel, which is set in a gloomy castle in the Highlands where superstitions are the norm, but he links his heroine's fate not to these, but to the stress of her difficult position as a pawn in her mother's quest for power, and the effects upon her own sensitive and uncomprehending nature of the conflicting strong personalities around her. Mysterious events, such as the ominous disappearance of a portrait, have an effect, but only heighten the sense of fear and anxiety already created by concrete conflicts and events. Scott's ability to lucidly synthesize threads of cause and effect much inspired Charles Dickens, who read his works avidly as a young man, but Dickens wasn't interested in the past. He was interested in the present.

直到十九世纪初，小说家（以及其他作家和思想家）都将邪恶视为人性的固有属性。沃尔特·斯科特爵士的作品便是邪恶描绘的典型例证，尽管如今鲜有人问津，但在当时却风靡一时。斯科特的小说经常探讨重大的社会议题。在几部小说中，他着重描写了十七世纪苏格兰的宗教战争，这场战争是激烈的意识形态冲突，其教义、社会和政治影响至今仍挥之不去。在斯科特的小说中，邪恶（机会主义、粗鲁、势利、冷酷无情、心胸狭隘、暴力倾向）的出现是随机的，加入某些群体并不意味着必然是贪婪的——有些神职人员品行端正，有些则狂热不堪；有些贵族仁慈和蔼，有些则残暴无情；有些思想家正直高尚，有些则自私自利。斯科特巧妙地展现了在意识形态动荡的时代，善行与恶行是如何在每个人的性情、境遇、信仰和欲望不断变化的组合中滋生的。事件与人物以一种经典的悲剧方式相互作用——结局带有宿命的意味。戏剧性讽刺的痛苦效果因与叙事时代的距离而减弱——斯科特精心安排了人物安详的坟墓意象，提醒读者，那些驱动冲突的激情早已如同冲突本身一样彻底消逝——因此，人们不会觉得事情原本可以有不同的结局，或者说，事情将来可能会有不同的结局。即使在像斯科特的《拉默穆尔的新娘》这样充满激情戏剧性的小说中，一位年轻女子因被迫违背意愿结婚而杀死了她的新婚丈夫，随后自己也精神失常，一种平静和顺从的情绪仍然源于一种传统的观念：性格与境遇的结合总是会导致我们事后意识到不可避免的结局。斯科特在艺术上的创新之一，是将传统的悲剧模式应用于各个阶层的人物，无论地位高低、男女老少、成败得失，而不仅仅局限于国王和王子。另一项创新是，即便是在看似哥特式的《拉默穆尔的新娘》这样的故事中，他也十分关注心理和社会因果关系的复杂性。安·拉德克利夫的《乌多尔夫的秘密》等哥特式小说在斯科特的时代风靡一时，因此他在小说中也融入了许多离奇的事件。故事发生在苏格兰高地一座阴森的城堡里，迷信盛行。然而，斯科特并没有将女主人公的命运与这些迷信联系起来，而是将其归因于她作为母亲权力斗争中的一枚棋子所承受的困境，以及周围那些性格冲突的强势人物对她敏感而懵懂的性格所产生的影响。神秘事件，例如画像的离奇失踪，固然会产生影响，但只会加剧由具体冲突和事件所造成的恐惧和焦虑。斯科特清晰地梳理因果关系的能力深深启发了查尔斯·狄更斯，狄更斯年轻时曾如饥似渴地阅读他的作品，但狄更斯对过去并不感兴趣，他关注的是当下。

In the nineteenth century the theory of evil changed, which changed the nature of morality in the novel, and therefore the portrayal of brutes, criminals, and psychopaths. What was really at the heart of the nature of good and evil, novelists realized, was secrecy and, indeed, silence.

十九世纪，邪恶理论发生了转变，这改变了小说中道德的本质，也因此改变了对残暴者、罪犯和精神病患者的刻画。小说家们意识到，善恶本质的核心在于秘密，更确切地说是沉默。

It seems that Charles Dickens, the most influential English author of the nineteenth century, was genuinely drawn to criminals and psychopaths. From the time of Oliver Twist (written when Dickens was in his midtwenties), all the way until the end of his career, he excelled at depicting nasty brutes: Sikes, who beats his girlfriend to death in a rage (Oliver Twist); Quilp, a choleric, garrulous thief and bully (The Old Curiosity Shop); Murdstone, a cold and socially respected tyrant (David Copperfield); and Carker, the smiling and Iago-like betrayer (Dombey and Son). Every Dickens novel has a different variety—sometimes lascivious, sometimes greedy, sometimes power-mad, sometimes vengeful (Madame Defarge), sometimes merely small and mean (Uriah Heep), but always richly, and even gleefully, realized. Dickens was superbly inventive, but never more so than in his exploration of the psychology of evil. What is important, technically, is that, with each new novel, his way of portraying his perpetrators becomes less and less dramatic and more and more internal. Sikes vents his inner rage when he beats Nancy. He is eloquent as well as cruel, and that's all we need to know about him. Ten years later, in Dombey and Son , Dickens portrays Carker the Manager, who plans to steal both Dombey's wife and his fortune. The way in which Dickens's prose slips easily into Carker's mind, revealing to the reader his secret thoughts and plans, especially how the world appears and feels to him, is so effortless that it doesn't seem like anything new, but it is. Carker's inner life is known only to him and to the reader, and his schemes excel in seductive psychological plausibility, drawing the reader into their logic as if Carker were the protagonist, not the villain. The growing internalization of the psychology of all of his characters was a feature of Dickens's work as he matured—in Dombey and Son , for example, his characters convincingly and movingly coexist inside the novel, physically together but cut off from one another by differing and often mutually exclusive perceptions of the world that are overcome only through enormous effort. Such insights into the nature of human isolation and subjectivity constitute a large part of Dickens's gift to his readers, but the application of this idea and of Dickens's gift for empathy with sociopathic personalities constitutes a philosophy that has had enormous effect on how modern people understand evil as a form of logic, and even of madness that is internally consistent, unrecognized as evil by the perpetrator, and compelling. By the end of his career, Dickens was as good as anyone who has ever lived at clarifying the motivations of those who harm others.

十九世纪最具影响力的英国作家查尔斯·狄更斯似乎对罪犯和精神病患者情有独钟。从他二十五六岁时创作的《雾都孤儿》开始，直到他创作生涯的尾声，他都擅长刻画那些令人憎恶的恶棍：比如《雾都孤儿》中怒气冲冲地将女友活活打死的赛克斯；《老古玩店》中脾气暴躁、喋喋不休的窃贼兼恶霸奎尔普；《大卫·科波菲尔》中冷酷无情却受人尊敬的暴君默德斯通；以及《董贝父子》中面带微笑、如同伊阿古一般的叛徒卡克。狄更斯的每一部小说都塑造了形形色色的罪犯——有时好色，有时贪婪，有时权力欲熏心，有时充满复仇之心（德法奇夫人），有时只是卑鄙无耻（尤赖亚·希普），但这些人物形象总是栩栩如生，甚至令人捧腹大笑。狄更斯极富创造力，尤其在探索邪恶心理方面更是如此。从技巧上讲，重要的是，随着每一部新小说的出版，他对作恶者的刻画方式变得越来越内敛，戏剧性也越来越弱。赛克斯殴打南希，是在宣泄他内心的愤怒。他既能言善辩又残忍无情，而我们对他的了解也就仅限于此了。十年后，在《董贝父子》中，狄更斯塑造了经理卡克，他计划窃取董贝的妻子和财产。狄更斯的文字行云流水般地展现了卡克的内心世界，将他隐秘的想法和计划，尤其是他眼中的世界，都娓娓道来，如此自然流畅，以至于读者感觉不到任何新意，但实际上却别具匠心。卡克尔的内心世界只有他自己和读者知晓，他的阴谋诡计极具诱惑力，在心理层面极具说服力，让读者仿佛置身其中，接受他的逻辑，如同卡克尔是主角而非反派一般。随着狄更斯创作的日臻成熟，他笔下所有人物心理的内化程度也日益加深，这成为他作品的一大特色——例如在《董贝父子》中，人物在小说中真实而动人地共存，他们身处同一空间，却因对世界截然不同甚至相互排斥的认知而彼此隔绝，而这种隔阂唯有通过巨大的努力才能克服。这种对人类孤独和主观性的深刻洞察，构成了狄更斯留给读者的重要遗产。而他对这一理念的运用，以及他对反社会人格的共情能力，构成了一种哲学，这种哲学对现代人理解邪恶（将其视为一种逻辑）乃至疯狂（将其视为一种内在逻辑自洽、施害者自身不自知且令人信服的行为）产生了深远的影响。狄更斯在其职业生涯后期，对伤害他人者的动机的刻画，堪称史上最杰出的作家之一。

To each novelistic psychopath of the Dickensian sort, his crimes make perfect sense, and as the reader comes to understand the logic, she is tempted to understand the sense, to become, in some way, less horrified at what has been done and more accepting of violent personalities in general. One effect of this technique is that old questions of sin, evil, and transgression of social norms become, with empathy (which is, remember, not “feeling with” but “perceiving with”), new questions of sanity and mental illness. When the novelist makes the reader understand a logic based on horrific premises, is the malefactor distanced from his humanity, or is humanity enlarged to encompass his logical facility? The novel explores this question repeatedly and offers no convincing conclusion.

对于狄更斯笔下那种小说式的精神变态者来说，他们的罪行似乎合情合理。当读者逐渐理解了这种逻辑，便会不由自主地想要理解其中的意义，从而在某种程度上减少对罪行的恐惧，并更加包容暴力人格。这种手法的一个效果是，在共情（记住，共情并非“感同身受”，而是“感同身受”）的作用下，原本关于罪恶、邪恶和违背社会规范的问题，会转化为关于理智和精神疾病的新问题。当小说家让读者理解一种基于骇人前提的逻辑时，作恶者是因此而丧失了人性，还是人性反而被扩展，从而涵盖了他逻辑上的敏锐？小说反复探讨了这个问题，却始终没有给出令人信服的结论。

At the same time, like Scott, Dickens explored cause and effect— what has made Ralph Nickleby, Scrooge, Jasper, and Headstone the way they are? Some of his explanations are more convincing than others. For example, John Jasper, in The Mystery of Edwin Drood , smokes opium, which may explain the extreme degree of his calculating isolation; Scrooge not only has had an impoverished childhood, but also went into business with a partner who encouraged his miserly proclivities. In his most insightful portrayal, that of Bradley Headstone, the stalker in Our Mutual Friend , Dickens shows how Brad-ley's shame at his class origins has combined with his temperamental proclivities (envy and self-repression) to engender an uncontrollable murderous paranoia and obsession. Even when Dickens's specific psychological theories don't hold water, the idea of cause and effect, the idea that there can be a theory of evil (and goodness), does. As early as Oliver Twist , Dickens is laying out a how-to manual for making criminals—first you deny them porridge and all sense of self-respect, then you give them criminal associates and teach them a few skills, such as picking pockets and engaging in prostitution. It is a very short step from this sort of causal logic to the advocacy of political and social solutions for what had always been considered individual moral failings, and Dickens readily made it.

与此同时，狄更斯也像斯科特一样，探讨了因果关系——是什么造就了拉尔夫·尼克尔贝、斯克鲁奇、贾斯珀和赫德斯通这几个人物？他的一些解释比其他解释更具说服力。例如，《艾德温·德鲁德之谜》中的约翰·贾斯珀吸食鸦片，这或许可以解释他为何如此精于算计、孤僻冷漠；斯克鲁奇不仅童年贫困，还与一位助长他吝啬倾向的合伙人合伙做生意。在狄更斯最深刻的刻画中，他塑造了《我们共同的朋友》中的跟踪狂布拉德利·赫德斯通，展现了布拉德利如何因出身阶级而感到羞耻，这种羞耻感与他与生俱来的性格倾向（嫉妒和自我压抑）相结合，最终滋生出一种无法控制的杀人妄想和执念。即使狄更斯的具体心理学理论站不住脚，但因果关系的概念，以及善恶理论的存在，却是站得住脚的。早在《雾都孤儿》中，狄更斯就描绘了一套制造罪犯的“操作指南”——首先剥夺他们的粥和自尊，然后让他们结交犯罪同伙，并教他们一些技能，比如扒窃和卖淫。从这种因果逻辑到倡导用政治和社会手段来解决一直以来被认为是个人道德缺陷的问题，其实只有一步之遥，而狄更斯也欣然接受了这一转变。

But the novel that had the most sensational effect on the moral life of its times was Uncle Tom's Cabin , the best-selling novel of the nineteenth century in the United States, and a big seller in England and in Europe, too (both Dickens and Tolstoy read it). Stowe began with a polemical purpose—to promote the abolition of slavery by disseminating stories of life on southern plantations that she heard from escapees passing through Cincinnati (where she lived) on the Underground Railroad. She couched her argument in starkly moral terms, invoking Christian principles and ideals as a matter of course, and depicting fairly openly for the period both the physical violence and the sexual license that slavery produced. Stowe, who lost a young child to illness, was especially moved by the plight of mothers and children who were separated by traffic in slaves and as a result of slave-breeding establishments—two of her most memorable characters are Cassy, whose children have been sold away from her, and Topsy, bred in a slave-breeding establishment and allowed to grow up without any nurture whatsoever. But the main protagonist and antagonist are Tom and Simon Legree, who represent good and evil, respectively. What distinguishes them from characters of melodrama (at least in the novel, which engendered any number of stage melodramas throughout the nineteenth century) is Stowe's analysis of, on the one hand, Tom's choices in the course of his martyrdom, and on the other, Legree's origins, motives, and psychology. Tom makes virtuous choices for logical and believable reasons. At the beginning, he allows himself to be sold south because he knows enough to fear that if the plantation he lives on goes bankrupt, his whole family is in jeopardy. Once in New Orleans, he continues to hope that his kindly but feckless master will free him, as he promises. Once on Legree's plantation, Tom knows that he is so lost in the bayous of southern Louisiana that escape is a long shot, and though a slave rebellion is conceivable, a positive outcome is not likely. In addition, Tom is a man of faith who truly believes that this world is passing, and his real home is with his Savior—why jeopardize his salvation when very little good is likely to come of it?

但对当时的道德生活产生最轰动影响的小说当属《汤姆叔叔的小屋》。这部小说是十九世纪美国最畅销的小说，在英国和欧洲也广受欢迎（狄更斯和托尔斯泰都读过）。斯托夫人创作这部小说的初衷是带有论战色彩——她希望通过传播从逃亡奴隶那里听来的南方种植园生活故事来推动废除奴隶制。这些逃亡奴隶通过“地下铁路”途经辛辛那提（她居住的地方）。她以鲜明的道德语言来阐述自己的观点，自然而然地援引基督教的原则和理想，并相当坦率地描绘了奴隶制带来的暴力和性放纵。斯托夫人因幼子病逝而痛失爱子，因此她对因奴隶贩卖和奴隶繁殖场而被迫分离的母子悲惨境遇尤为感同身受。她笔下最令人难忘的两个人物分别是卡西（她的孩子被卖给了奴隶）和托普西（在奴隶繁殖场长大，缺乏任何关爱）。但小说的主人公和反派分别是汤姆和西蒙·莱格里，他们分别代表着善与恶。与通俗剧中的人物（至少在小说中是如此，尽管这部小说在整个十九世纪催生了无数舞台剧）不同，斯托夫人对汤姆在殉道过程中所做的选择，以及莱格里的出身、动机和心理进行了深入的分析。汤姆的善行选择合乎逻辑且令人信服。起初，他甘愿被卖到南方，因为他深知，如果他居住的种植园破产，他的全家都将面临危险。到了新奥尔良，他仍然抱有一丝希望，希望他那善良却不负责任的主人会像承诺的那样释放他。到了莱格里的种植园后，汤姆意识到自己已经迷失在路易斯安那州南部的沼泽地带，逃跑的希望渺茫，虽然奴隶起义并非不可能，但成功的可能性微乎其微。此外，汤姆是个虔诚的信徒，他坚信这个世界终将过去，他真正的归宿是他的救世主那里——既然起义几乎不会带来任何好处，又何必冒险去冒险呢？

Legree has no faith but is supremely superstitious. A hard and greedy northerner originally, he has no personal or spiritual resources, no friends, and no sense of order or aesthetic pleasure. His only recreation is drinking, but drinking renders him violent and paranoid. At no point does Stowe cause the reader to feel sympathy for Legree, but she does provide a believable analysis for his absolute lack of fellow feeling not only toward his slaves but also toward everyone else, and she links this analysis to her analysis of slavery in the United States— the southerners may own the slaves, but northern banks provide the money, earn much of the profit, and turn a blind eye to the injustice of the system.

莱格里没有信仰，却极度迷信。他原本是北方人，性格冷酷贪婪，既没有个人财富，也没有精神寄托，没有朋友，更没有秩序感和审美趣味。他唯一的消遣就是喝酒，但喝酒却让他变得暴力和偏执。斯托夫人从未让读者对莱格里产生同情，但她对莱格里冷酷无情的性格给出了令人信服的分析，这种冷酷不仅体现在他对奴隶的冷漠上，也体现在他对所有人的冷漠上。她将这种分析与她对美国奴隶制的分析联系起来——南方人或许拥有奴隶，但北方的银行却提供了资金，赚取了大部分利润，并对这种制度的不公正视而不见。

Stowe's ideas were not original, but the sharp delineation of character required by a novel as opposed to a sermon or an essay aided Stowe's moral crusade because she was able to systematically set up and demolish every argument for slavery by inserting into the reader's head vivid, dramatic set pieces that engaged the reader's emotions while undercutting each proslavery rationale. Uncle Tom's Cabin brilliantly employs the natural rhetorical tools of the novel form. It eavesdrops on the private conversations of black characters, and lo and behold, they are intelligent, brave, virtuous, funny, charming—in short, they irradicably demonstrate that slaves are human. It promotes freedom by vividly depicting tyranny. It puts characters such as Miss Ophelia (from New England) and Augustine St. Claire (from New Orleans) in situations where they have to discuss their options and make choices, and because they are sympathetic characters, the reader wants them to make sympathetic choices.
