As Tom travels from his natal plantation in Kentucky down the river to New Orleans and then into the swamps of Louisiana, he is repeatedly discussed, by slave owners and slave dealers and other slaves—his journey toward martyrdom is Stowe's beautifully disguised catalog of arguments for and against slavery. In the early 1850s , when she was writing, catalogs of arguments for and against slavery were rife, but only the novel form, and Stowe's adept handling of it, could change the terms of the discussion and renew the issues in a way that galvanized millions of people and caused President Lincoln to greet her, some years later, with the remark “So this is the little lady who made this big war.” Repeatedly, in Uncle Tom's Cabin , Stowe asks the reader to consider and decide the larger and smaller emotional and moral questions of slavery. In the many months that the novel ran serially in the National Era , Stowe gave her readers steady practice in deciding against slavery, and in understanding causal relationships between the system of slavery and its moral effects.

斯托夫人的思想并非原创，但小说（而非布道或散文）对人物刻画的精准把握，恰恰助力了她的道德运动。她能够系统地构建并驳斥奴隶制的每一个论点，通过在读者脑海中植入生动而富有戏剧性的场景，调动读者的情感，同时瓦解每一种支持奴隶制的理由。《汤姆叔叔的小屋》巧妙地运用了小说这种文体固有的修辞手法。它偷听黑人角色的私下对话，展现出他们聪明、勇敢、善良、风趣、迷人——简而言之，他们无可辩驳地证明了奴隶也是人。这部小说通过生动地描绘暴政，宣扬了自由。小说将奥菲莉娅小姐（来自新英格兰）和奥古斯丁·圣克莱尔（来自新奥尔良）等人物置于必须讨论各种选择并做出抉择的境地。由于这些人物令人同情，读者希望他们做出令人同情的选择。汤姆从肯塔基州的故乡种植园出发，沿河而下前往新奥尔良，最终进入路易斯安那州的沼泽地。他的旅程不断被奴隶主、奴隶贩子和其他奴隶所议论——他走向殉道的旅程，实际上是斯托夫人精心伪装的关于奴隶制正反两方论点的罗列。在19世纪50年代初斯托夫人写作的年代，关于奴隶制正反两方论点的罗列比比皆是，但只有小说这种形式，以及斯托夫人对这种形式的巧妙运用，才能改变讨论的语境，并以一种能够激励数百万人的方式重新唤起人们对奴隶制问题的关注，以至于几年后，林肯总统在接见她时说道：“原来这就是引发这场大战的小妇人啊。”在《汤姆叔叔的小屋》中，斯托夫人反复引导读者思考并抉择奴隶制所涉及的各种情感和道德问题。这部小说在《国家时代》杂志连载的几个月里，斯托夫人不断地引导读者做出反对奴隶制的决定，并理解奴隶制制度及其道德后果之间的因果关系。

What nineteenth-century novelists discovered was that the exploration of cause and effect that is natural to the novel mitigates the idea that evil is random, and that the requirement of the novel form that the protagonist be in a continuously depicted relationship with his society has the effect of placing responsibility. As soon as responsibility is apportioned, both author and reader start to feel that evil can be fixed, and fixed by amateurs, since the novel is always an amateur production. The effect of novels by Dickens, Stowe, and their contemporaries (which were, in some sense, the cultural phenomena of their day similar to Star Wars or Sex and the City in our day) was to make morality a political question—a discussion of good and bad individual actions and their effects, as always, but also of wealth, power, and influence. The novel has certain inherent characteristics—it is naturally democratic; it promotes individuality and freedom; it is intimate and sociable and connective; it elevates inner life over appearance; it is, often in spite of itself, hopeful; and it is naturally popular. These qualities fit into and exemplify the idea of the modern liberal society and in the course of the nineteenth century came to be seen as moral issues (though they can as easily contradict another sort of society's system of morality as uphold it).

十九世纪的小说家们发现，小说中固有的对因果关系的探索，削弱了邪恶随机发生的观点；而小说形式要求主人公与社会保持持续的互动关系，则起到了赋予责任的作用。一旦责任被分配，作者和读者都会开始觉得邪恶是可以被解决的，而且是由非专业人士来解决，因为小说本身就是一种非专业人士的创作。狄更斯、斯托夫人及其同时代作家的小说（在某种程度上，它们是当时的文化现象，类似于我们今天的《星球大战》或《欲望都市》）将道德问题政治化——讨论的是个人善恶行为及其后果，一如既往，但同时也涉及财富、权力和影响力。小说具有某些内在特征：它天然具有民主性；它提倡个性与自由；它亲切、社交且具有联结性；它重视内在生活而非外在表现；它常常不经意间流露出希望；而且它天然具有大众性。这些特质符合现代自由社会的理念，并体现了这一理念，在十九世纪逐渐被视为道德问题（尽管它们既可以轻易地与另一种社会的道德体系相矛盾，也可以轻易地维护它）。

The great conflict of the twentieth century concerned whether morality was made up of a set of personal choices having to do with right and wrong behavior, as described by, say, the Ten Commandments, or whether it was made up of a set of political choices having to do with the inequitable distribution and abuse of power and wealth. All sorts of social and economic institutions that had once been considered more or less the natural order of things became moral dilemmas (and zones of ideological conflict)—slavery, marriage and domestic abuse, child labor, the rewards of capital versus the rewards of labor, genocide in war or as an act of conquest, exploitation and destruction of natural resources, the impoverishment of the human spirit as an effect of labyrinthine and secretive bureaucracy. The novel promoted this moral shift. The novel as a form is usually seen to be moral if its readers consider freedom, individuality, democracy, privacy, social connection, tolerance, and hope to be morally good, but it is not considered moral if the highest values of a society are adherence to rules and traditional mores, the maintenance of hierarchical relationships, and absolute ideas of right and wrong. Any society based on the latter will find novels inherently immoral and subversive.

二十世纪最大的冲突在于，道德究竟是由一系列关乎对错行为的个人选择构成，例如十诫所描述的那样；还是由一系列关乎权力与财富分配不均及滥用的政治选择构成？各种曾经被视为自然秩序的社会和经济制度，都变成了道德困境（以及意识形态冲突的领域）——奴隶制、婚姻和家庭暴力、童工、资本回报与劳动回报的冲突、战争或征服中的种族灭绝、自然资源的剥削和破坏，以及错综复杂、秘密重重的官僚机构对人类精神的摧残。小说推动了这种道德观念的转变。如果读者认为自由、个性、民主、隐私、社会联系、宽容和希望在道德上是好的，那么小说这种文体通常被认为是道德的。但如果一个社会的最高价值观是遵守规则和传统习俗、维护等级关系以及绝对的善恶观念，那么小说就不被认为是道德的。任何基于后一种价值观的社会都会认为小说本质上是不道德的，甚至是颠覆性的。

All through the nineteenth century, novelists explored and exposed social abuses, thereby constantly forcing the moral and the political, the personal and the public, to interpenetrate. Dickens and Stowe had plenty of company—Eliot, Dostoevsky, Hawthorne, Tolstoy, Balzac, Zola, and countless others. Machiavelli would have been appalled. But Machiavelli did not have to contend with a citizenry that was entertaining itself on long train journeys with novels—that is, with routine contemplation of political and moral questions about social and economic arrangements.

整个十九世纪，小说家们不断探索和揭露社会弊端，从而持续地迫使道德与政治、个人与公共领域相互交织。狄更斯和斯托夫人并非孤例——艾略特、陀思妥耶夫斯基、霍桑、托尔斯泰、巴尔扎克、左拉以及无数其他作家都与他并肩前行。马基雅维利若在世，定会感到震惊。然而，马基雅维利所面对的民众，却不必在漫长的火车旅途中以小说消遣——也就是说，不必像他那样，将对社会经济安排的政治和道德问题的日常思考融入到日常生活中。

If reading a novel is an act that underscores the reader's feelings of agency in a way that audience-based forms of art do not have to, and if novel-readers have no other experience of choice, just this one may indeed politicize them. The novel always promotes moral questions as capable of being understood and decided by individuals. This is part and parcel of the novel's natural allegiance to the notion that things are not as they appear. If things are not as they appear, then the individual (author or character or reader) is required to divine how they really are and to understand the contrast between how they appear to others and how they appear to him. But the protagonist, as he comes to understand the difference between reality and appearance, also is required to sacrifice something. Typically, the equation works as follows: If he sacrifices his own sense of truth, then he is dishonored. If he sacrifices love, life, wealth, position, or any other commonly accepted good in favor of his own sense of truth, then he is damaged or destroyed but not dishonored. If he can mesh inner truth and outer truth with only the sacrifice of illusions or foolish expectations, then he is a character in a comic novel. But in any case, the novel is absolutely wedded to point of view and therefore must train its readers to see that things are not as they appear even if, perhaps, they are; it also trains its readers to make the honorable choice—that is, one's own truth over accepted truths.

如果阅读小说能够以其他面向观众的艺术形式所不具备的方式，凸显读者的主体性，并且如果小说读者别无选择，那么仅凭小说本身就可能使他们具有政治意识。小说总是将道德问题视为个人可以理解和决定的问题。这源于小说对“事物并非如表面所见”这一观念的天然认同。如果事物并非如表面所见，那么个人（作者、角色或读者）就必须探寻事物的真相，并理解事物在他人眼中的呈现与自身眼中的呈现之间的差异。但是，主人公在理解现实与表象之间的差异的同时，也必须做出牺牲。通常，这种等式是这样的：如果他牺牲了自己的真理观，那么他便蒙受耻辱。如果他为了追求真理而牺牲爱情、生命、财富、地位或任何其他公认的价值，那么他虽会受到伤害或毁灭，但不会蒙受耻辱。如果他能仅凭牺牲幻想或愚蠢的期望就能将内在真理与外在真理融合在一起，那么他就是喜剧小说中的人物。但无论如何，小说都与叙事视角密不可分，因此必须引导读者认识到事物并非表面看起来那样，即便它们或许确实如此；它也引导读者做出高尚的选择——即选择自己的真理而非公认的真理。

Nineteenth-century novelists explored all sorts of moral and political ideas, but the one they kept returning to, the one most central to the novel, was the question of female virtue, which is simultaneously the most apparently personal, the most socially and politically explosive, and the most inflammatory. Just as Dickens and Stowe recast issues of stealing, killing, coveting, pride, avarice, sloth, lust, and even gluttony, anger, and envy as social constructs and political questions, so Gustave Flaubert changed the traditional critique of how and why women exist. Madame Bovary is an especially good example of how, without even meaning to, a novelist may transform the world simply by observing it. Flaubert, who had none of the reformist ambitions of Dickens and Stowe, famously remarked, “Madame Bovary, c'est moi.”

十九世纪的小说家们探索了各种各样的道德和政治理念，但他们反复提及、贯穿小说始终的核心问题是女性美德。这个问题看似最为私人化，实则最具社会和政治爆发性，也最具煽动性。正如狄更斯和斯托夫人将偷窃、杀戮、贪婪、骄傲、贪婪、懒惰、色欲，甚至暴食、愤怒和嫉妒等问题重新定义为社会建构和政治议题一样，古斯塔夫·福楼拜也改变了关于女性存在方式和原因的传统批判。《包法利夫人》尤其能说明，小说家如何在无意间通过观察世界而改变世界。福楼拜不像狄更斯和斯托夫人那样怀有改革者的野心，他曾说过一句名言：“包法利夫人，就是我。”

On the surface, this makes no sense. Flaubert is careful to describe Emma in a very particular way—a pretty young woman of peasant background who is not well educated, who marries a man she doesn't care for, and then gets involved in several affairs with other men who treat her badly. She finally commits suicide, leaving behind her a very confused husband and an uncomprehending daughter. Flaubert shows that Emma has no real taste or discrimination and is incapable of any sort of higher mental life. She is out of the ordinary in the stubbornness of her aspirations for some sort of relief from French provincial existence, but entirely ordinary in all of her talents and capacities. Flaubert depicts her minutely but mercilessly and coldly—there is no sense, as in, say, Moll Flanders or Vanity Fair , that the author has respect or grudging fondness for his heroine. Nor do Emma's problems seem to be caused by the society in which she lives—although many of those around her cheat and betray her, the tone of the novel suggests that everyone is doing the best he can do given his circumstances, and that the circumstances of French provincial life are not amenable to change (unlike the public health system in London, for example, or the existence of Negro slavery in the United States).

表面上看，这完全说不通。福楼拜对爱玛的刻画非常细致入微——她是一位出身农家、家貌美的年轻女子，受教育程度不高，嫁给了一个自己并不喜欢的男人，之后又与几个对她不好的男人发生婚外情。最终，她选择了自杀，留下了一个困惑不已的丈夫和一个懵懂无知的女儿。福楼拜指出，爱玛缺乏真正的品味和鉴赏力，也无法拥有任何更高层次的精神生活。她固执地渴望摆脱法国乡村生活的束缚，这或许是她与众不同的地方，但她的才华和能力却又平庸无奇。福楼拜对她的描写细致入微，却又冷酷无情——不像《莫尔·弗兰德斯》或《名利场》那样，作者对女主人公丝毫没有敬意或勉强的喜爱之情。艾玛的问题似乎也不是由她所处的社会造成的——尽管她周围的许多人欺骗和背叛了她，但小说的基调表明，每个人都在尽力而为，而法国乡村的生活环境是无法改变的（例如，与伦敦的公共卫生系统或美国存在的黑奴制度不同）。

What Flaubert adds to Emma is his own experience of the sensuousness of things. When Emma and Rodolphe are walking or driving, for example, the movement of the leaves in the trees or the passage of the carriage down the road is ravishing—to Emma and to the author, and therefore to the reader. To motivate Emma's fall, Flaubert infuses her inner life with exceptional richness, with what must have been his own sensitivity to sensation and to feeling. Madame Bovary was an instant and lasting success. Flaubert's embrace of Emma's way of experiencing things imparted to the novel a new degree of psychological insight and refinement and complicated the reader's experience of her lack of traditional virtue. This is not on the surface political, especially since “character is fate” for Emma as much as for the hero of any tragic play. Emma's road to her destiny is a train track downhill, and there is no sense that she can get off the train.

福楼拜在《爱玛》中融入了他自身对感官体验的感悟。例如，当爱玛和鲁道夫散步或驾车时，树叶的摇曳或马车驶过道路的景象都令人陶醉——对爱玛、对作者，乃至对读者而言皆是如此。为了推动爱玛的堕落，福楼拜赋予了她极其丰富的内心世界，这其中必然蕴含着他自身对感官和情感的敏锐感知。《包法利夫人》一经问世便获得了持久的成功。福楼拜对爱玛体验事物方式的把握，赋予了小说一种全新的心理洞察力和细腻的笔触，也使读者对她缺乏传统美德的感受更加复杂。这表面上并非出于政治目的，尤其因为“性格即命运”对爱玛而言，正如对任何悲剧英雄一样。爱玛通往命运的道路如同一条下坡的铁轨，而她似乎再也无法摆脱这列火车。

But it is evident that there is something wrong with Emma, and pretty soon the reader begins to wonder about cause and effect. Is her persistent inability to fit into and accept her life her own fault or the fault of the provincial existence that the author clearly disdains? And if the problem lies within, is it something inborn, like looks or temperament, or does it have its origins in some life circumstance— motherlessness, perhaps? While Flaubert follows Emma's ups and downs seemingly moment by moment, he makes no suggestions about the reasons for her lack of fit. How she experiences her discomfort and dissatisfaction is how he represents it. He is more observant than she is, but as an artist, he clearly understands that if he were to subject her to some sort of analysis based on superior understanding, her fall would seem less inevitable and less dramatic. She would go back to being a typical young woman with no strength of character, whom the reader could easily judge and dismiss. The immediacy of his depiction, though, only strengthens the reader's tendency to wonder about the causes and effects that Flaubert ignores. As a result of Flaubert's technique and his identification with Emma, the astute reader can't help wondering whether, if the causes and effects of Emma's mental condition were understood more clearly (better than by the author or the narrator, let's say), perhaps an answer (or a cure) would present itself. And this response is a private one. The reader is not influenced by public conventions, such as those of the stage or the opera, to view the character's fate as a form of spectacle, but rather to view it as very akin to her own fate or the fate of a friend (and gossips always believe that they know what's best for the subject of the gossip, if only she would listen to them).

但显而易见，艾玛身上存在着某种问题，读者很快便开始思考其中的因果关系。她始终无法融入并接受自己的生活，究竟是她自身的问题，还是作者明显鄙夷的那种乡野生活的错？如果问题出在她自身，那究竟是与生俱来的，比如容貌或性情，还是源于某种生活境遇——或许是失去母亲？福楼拜细致入微地描绘了艾玛的起伏跌宕，却并未对她格格不入的原因做出任何解释。他只是如实地展现了她内心的不适和不满。他比艾玛更善于观察，但作为一名艺术家，他显然明白，如果他基于某种高深的理解对她进行分析，她的堕落就会显得不那么必然，也不那么戏剧化。她会重新变成一个缺乏个性的典型年轻女性，读者可以轻易地对她做出评判和否定。然而，他笔下人物的直接描写反而加剧了读者对福楼拜所忽略的因果关系的思考。由于福楼拜的写作技巧以及他对爱玛的认同，敏锐的读者不禁会想，如果爱玛精神状况的成因和后果能够被更清晰地理解（比如说，比作者或叙述者理解得更透彻），或许就能找到答案（或治愈方法）。而且，这种思考是私人的。读者不会受到舞台或歌剧等公共惯例的影响，将人物的命运视为一种奇观，而是会将其与自身或朋友的命运联系起来（而爱嚼舌根的人总是自以为知道什么对被议论者最好，只要她听他们的就行）。

Obviously, the rise of psychoanalysis (Freud was born a year before Madame Bovary was published), both as a theory and as a consumer good, grows out of this idea that causes can be traced and effects modified, and that a prolonged effort to do so is possible and even justified for the most average, Emma-like, readerlike person. Whether or not Freud ever read Madame Bovary , we can't help but think that Emma would present a tempting case for him, that he would diagnose her as hysterical, and that he would guide her into talking her way into fitting with the life she cannot abide (in our day, we would be tempted to diagnose her, too, maybe as bipolar or depressed, and to treat her with drugs). By giving Emma his own sensibility in such careful detail, Flaubert succeeds not only in writing a great novel but also in authoring the first, but by no means the last, case history. Just as an overtly political novel such as Uncle Tom's Cabin sparks a political response— the nation can be changed to fix injustice—a profoundly psychological novel sparks a response based in psychology—a person can be changed to fit her circumstances (especially if they are defined as all human circumstances). A traditionally moral issue, that of lust (and Emma lusts for all sorts of pleasures, not just sexual ones), becomes a medical one.

显然，精神分析的兴起（弗洛伊德出生于《包法利夫人》出版前一年），无论作为一种理论还是一种消费品，都源于这样一种理念：原因可以追溯，结果可以改变，而且即使对于最普通、像爱玛一样、喜欢阅读的人来说，长期努力也是可能且合理的。无论弗洛伊德是否读过《包法利夫人》，我们都忍不住会想，爱玛会给他提供一个极具吸引力的案例，他会诊断她患有癔症，并引导她用花言巧语去适应她无法忍受的生活（在今天，我们也会忍不住给她诊断，也许是双相情感障碍或抑郁症，并用药物治疗她）。福楼拜通过如此细致地赋予爱玛他独特的感性，不仅成功地创作了一部伟大的小说，而且还撰写了第一个，但绝非最后一个，案例分析。正如《汤姆叔叔的小屋》这样一部政治色彩浓厚的长篇小说会引发政治反应——国家可以因此而改变，以纠正不公——一部深刻的心理小说也会引发基于心理学的反应——人可以被改变以适应其所处的环境（尤其当这些环境被定义为所有人类环境时）。一个传统的道德问题，即欲望（艾玛渴望各种各样的快乐，而不仅仅是性欲），变成了一个医学问题。

And just as the social nature of the novel as a form requires injustice to be redressed, it also requires that personal suffering be relieved.

小说作为一种艺术形式的社会性质，既要求纠正不公正现象，也要求减轻个人痛苦。

We cannot imagine the characters of The Decameron or The Hep-tameron , with all their troubles, saying “What's wrong with me?” Like Roxana or Robinson Crusoe, they might say “How have I sinned and what am I going to do about it?” After centuries of education by novels, though, the average person has come to be routinely introspective, and to substitute therapeutic dilemmas and political questions for moral rules. All of the ways that morality and politics are tangled together in the novel come together in Marcel Proust's la recherche du temps perdu (In Search of Lost Time). M., the protagonist and narrator of Proust's seven volumes, has one primary rhetorical task—to maintain the reader's willingness to keep reading until he really gets to the essential points of his argument in volume seven, nearly four thousand pages into the novel; he must make himself attractive, or at least fascinating. He does so by characterizing himself in great detail, and these are some of his characteristics: he is tolerant and accepting of differences in lifestyles, opinions, and ways of doing things; he never demeans groups such as servants, homosexuals, or Jews that are routinely demeaned by others; he has good manners and acts in a generally kind way; he is a supporter of Dreyfus, the Jewish officer in the French army who was slandered and wrongfully imprisoned in the 1890s ; he is skeptical of those who claim or seek power and influence; he is good at detecting hypocrisy, self-aggrandizement, social cruelty, and subtle rudeness in those around him, and he shows these qualities to be ridiculous and demeaning; he accepts that humans are complex, with both good and bad characteristics, and he also accepts that good and bad characteristics have little or no relation to success and failure. He is, in other words, the ideal liberal protagonist who speaks even of his own passions judiciously and analytically. He is, also, perhaps, unique in the history of the novel in his ability to hold a reader's interest at length. But M. has what most people would consider immoral proclivities with regard to young women of a Lolita age. He likes to exploit such girls and from time to time reports on his exploits. He shares several characteristics with the men in Justine —his most dramatic and in many ways significant accomplishment is to keep his young girlfriend, Albertine, imprisoned in his family home, restricting her movements and enforcing what amounts to solitude for some months, until she finally flees. He is as cruel and narcissistic in his imprisonment of Albertine as Humbert Humbert is in his imprisonment of Lolita, and exhibits far less shame. And yet Humbert, because he is disdainful and snobbish in his expressions, rather nasty in his treatment of others, and always unsociable (in comparison with M.'s ever-flowing sociability), is a model villain, while M. generally gets a pass on the villainy front because he is adept at arousing in the reader both sympathy and empathy. A significant feature of his success in obtaining the reader's forgiveness for his immoral acts is that the whole subject of his seven-volume novel is cause and effect; throughout the narrative, he continuously traces threads of psychological and sociological connection. He often considers the question of what might be wrong with him, and in the end his very ability to consider it so thoroughly persuades the reader either to accept what is wrong with him, or decide that whatever is wrong with him is worth the result. It is a great rhetorical accomplishment.

我们无法想象《十日谈》或《七日谈》中的人物，在经历了种种磨难之后，会问自己“我到底怎么了？”。就像罗克珊娜或鲁滨逊·克鲁索一样，他们或许会问“我犯了什么罪？我该如何弥补？”。然而，经过几个世纪的小说熏陶，普通人已经习惯于内省，并用心理困境和政治问题来代替道德准则。小说中道德与政治交织的所有方式，都在马塞尔·普鲁斯特的《追忆似水年华》中得到了淋漓尽致的展现。普鲁斯特这部七卷本巨著的主人公兼叙述者M，肩负着一项主要的修辞任务——保持读者的阅读兴趣，直到第七卷——小说近四千页之后，他才真正触及到论证的核心要点；他必须让自己具有吸引力，或者至少引人入胜。他通过详细描述自己的性格特征来做到这一点，以下是他的一些性格特征：他宽容并接受生活方式、观点和做事方式的差异；他从不贬低那些经常被他人贬低的群体，例如仆人、同性恋者或犹太人；他举止得体，待人友善；他是德雷福斯的支持者，德雷福斯是法国军队中的一名犹太军官，在19世纪90年代遭到诽谤和冤狱；他对那些声称或追求权力和影响力的人持怀疑态度；他善于发现周围人的虚伪、自大、社会残酷和隐晦的粗鲁，并指出这些品质是可笑和卑劣的；他承认人性复杂，既有优点也有缺点，他也承认优点和缺点与成功和失败几乎没有关系。换句话说，他是一位理想的自由主义主人公，甚至能以审慎而理性的态度谈论自己的激情。或许，在小说史上，他也是独一无二的，能够长时间牢牢抓住读者的注意力。然而，M. 对像洛丽塔那样年轻的女性有着大多数人认为是不道德的癖好。他喜欢利用这些女孩，并且不时地炫耀自己的“战绩”。他与《朱斯蒂娜》中的男性角色有诸多相似之处——他最引人注目、在许多方面也意义重大的“成就”是将年轻的女友阿尔贝蒂娜囚禁在家中，限制她的行动，并强迫她与世隔绝数月之久，直到她最终逃离。他对阿尔贝蒂娜的囚禁，如同亨伯特·亨伯特囚禁洛丽塔一样残酷自恋，而且他表现出的羞耻心要少得多。然而，亨伯特因为其傲慢自大的言辞、对他人刻薄无礼的态度，以及始终不善交际（与M.热情奔放的社交能力形成鲜明对比），而成为一个典型的反派角色。M.之所以通常能被读者原谅，是因为他善于唤起读者的同情和共鸣。他之所以能成功获得读者对其不道德行为的宽恕，一个重要的原因在于，他这部七卷本小说的主题是因果关系；在叙事过程中，他不断地追溯心理和社会层面的关联。他经常思考自己究竟出了什么问题，而最终，正是他这种深入思考的能力，说服了读者要么接受他自身的问题，要么认为无论他有什么问题，最终的结果都是值得的。这是一种高超的修辞技巧。

Inevitably, as prefigured by Justine , the novel must amalgamate politics and sex, and, as with Justine , many readers denounce the amalgamation on moral grounds when the real offense is political. A case in point is Lady Chatterley's Lover. Though Lady Chatterley's Lover was banned in England and in America because of its explicit scenes of lovemaking, it has come to seem merely bracing in its frankness about sexuality, while it still offers a fairly aggressive critique of early twentieth-century English society. The premise is simple, and similar to the premise of any number of French novels—the wife of a wealthy and landed gentleman, unsatisfied with her marriage, takes up with another man, in this case the gamekeeper on the Chatterley estate. The novel takes place in the wake of the First World War, and, significantly, both men have served in the war and been changed by it—Chatterley is paralyzed and confined to a wheelchair, while Mellors, the gamekeeper, has used the opportunity to become more sophisticated in his thinking and less subservient in his manner. Chatterley is no long-suffering hero who has transcended his bodily injuries and found a higher purpose. He is a querulous, whiny, dog-in-the-manger sort who enjoys exerting the power he has, including his power over his wife, Connie, just for the sake of seeing others acknowledge it. Lawrence explicitly renders him as the representative of his class and his nation in terms of both his economic power and his emasculation. In spite of Chatterley's suffering, Lawrence isn't nice to him at all, and that remains probably the only shocking element of the novel (though there is one scene where, over dinner, Mellors and Connie's father discuss her sexual behavior in a way that seems more than crude, as well as politically incorrect, of course). Lawrence wrote in a traditional realistic style that makes his critique all the more straightforward and his sex scenes all the more confrontational. Part of the reason that Lady Chatterley's Lover has ceased to shock, however, is that it doesn't really challenge Connie's subordinate position. For the sake of sexual pleasure, she shifts “owners,” from Chatterley to Mellors, but Mellors is gruff and rude and promises Connie only motherhood, not power or even agency. Nevertheless, the banning of Lady Chatterley's Lover had the characteristic effect of making the novel desirable and, in this case, eventually bringing the portrayal of sex on the page so much more into the literary mainstream that what once seemed shocking on the page (when the novel was printed in Italy and Lawrence's friend told him that it was a good thing the compositor couldn't read English or he might have refused to set the type) now seems quaint and sentimental. Twentieth-century novelists were not able to return to the pre-Dickensian idea of evil as randomly distributed, causeless, and incorrigible, but it was not for lack of trying. Many twentieth-century novelists explicitly rejected the nineteenth-century project of social improvement, but the novel itself defied them. The best some novelists were able to do was return to a Jane Austen–like setting of manners and personal relationships, but all plots require conflict; once the nineteenth-century novelists had broadened the representable world and deepened the representable inner life, had applied complexity to both, and come up with ever more refined and intelligent logical connections, the novel's inherent political (and ideological) nature was revealed, and morality and politics in the novel could never be separated again.

正如《朱斯蒂娜》所预示的那样，小说必然要将政治与性融合在一起。而如同《朱斯蒂娜》一样，许多读者出于道德原因谴责这种融合，却忽略了其真正的冒犯之处——政治。以《查泰莱夫人的情人》为例。尽管《查泰莱夫人的情人》因其露骨的性爱描写而在英国和美国遭到禁售，但如今人们似乎只是觉得它对性的坦率令人耳目一新，同时它仍然对二十世纪初的英国社会进行了相当尖锐的批判。小说的前提很简单，与许多法国小说的前提类似——一位富裕地主的妻子，对自己的婚姻感到不满，于是与另一个男人发生了关系，在这个故事中，这个男人是查泰莱庄园的猎场看守。小说以第一次世界大战为背景，值得注意的是，两位主人公都曾参战并深受战争影响——查特莱瘫痪，终生只能依靠轮椅行动；而猎场看守梅勒斯则利用这段经历，在思想上变得更加成熟，举止也更加不拘小节。查特莱并非那种饱经磨难、超越身体创伤、找到更高人生意义的英雄。他是一个爱抱怨、爱发牢骚、占着茅坑不拉屎的人，乐于炫耀自己的权力，包括对妻子康妮的权力，仅仅是为了博取他人的认可。劳伦斯明确地将他塑造成其阶级和国家的缩影，既体现在他的经济实力上，也体现在他被剥夺了男子气概的程度上。尽管查泰莱夫人饱受折磨，劳伦斯对他却毫不留情，这或许是这部小说唯一令人震惊之处（当然，其中有一幕是，在晚餐时，梅勒斯和康妮的父亲谈论她的性行为，其方式粗俗不堪，而且显然也不符合政治正确）。劳伦斯采用传统的现实主义风格进行写作，这使得他的批判更加直白，性爱描写也更具冲击力。然而，《查泰莱夫人的情人》之所以不再令人震惊，部分原因在于它并没有真正挑战康妮的从属地位。为了获得性快感，她将“主人”从查泰莱转移到了梅勒斯，但梅勒斯粗鲁无礼，只给予康妮母爱，而非权力或自主权。然而，《查泰莱夫人的情人》的禁售却产生了意想不到的效果，反而使这部小说更受欢迎，并最终将性描写带入了文学主流，以至于曾经在纸面上显得惊世骇俗的内容（当这部小说在意大利印刷时，劳伦斯的朋友告诉他，幸好排字工不懂英文，否则他可能会拒绝排版）如今看来却显得古怪而感伤。二十世纪的小说家们未能回归狄更斯之前的那种将邪恶视为随机分布、无缘无故且不可救药的观念，但这并非因为他们缺乏尝试。许多二十世纪的小说家明确地拒绝了十九世纪的社会改良计划，但小说本身却挑战了他们的固有观念。一些小说家所能做的，最多也就是回归简·奥斯汀式的礼仪和人际关系背景，但所有情节都需要冲突；十九世纪的小说家们拓展了可表现的世界，深化了可表现的内心世界，并将复杂性应用于两者，并提出了越来越精细和巧妙的逻辑联系，小说的内在政治（和意识形态）性质就此显露出来，小说中的道德和政治再也无法分离。

# ↩

7. The Art of the Novel

7. 小说的艺术

F or many generations, the novel had no pretensions to art. The novel was not rooted in classical rhetorical and imaginative forms, nor taught in schools and universities. Because novels were read for pleasure rather than “improvement,” novelists were from the beginning autodidacts, reading their own, idiosyncratic “courses” of novels, picking and choosing what to emulate and imitate, often writing in secret and pleasing themselves first of all rather than teachers or scholars. Numerous novelists published anonymously or under pseudonyms—Madame de La Fayette, Daniel Defoe, Jane Austen, the Brontës, George Eliot—doing so because they had something to lose by claiming their work, usually respectability. Novelists who published under their own names were often those who were not socially prominent or who, like Samuel Richardson and Henry Fielding, already had literary lives before they began to write novels. Artistically, novelists were do-it-yourselfers, and what they knew about “the novel” they gleaned from their favorite authors. We know from their own testimony that Forster read James, James read Dickens, Dickens read Smollett, Smollett read Cervantes, Cervantes read Marguerite of Navarre, Marguerite read Boccaccio (and, of course, Forster read Cervantes, Dickens read Scott, Scott read Boccaccio, Scott read Cervantes, Fielding read Cervantes, Dickens read Cervantes, Woolf read Austen, Dickens, and James, Stendhal read Marguerite, Balzac read Stendhal, James read Balzac, Turgenev read Stendhal, Stendhal read Madame de La Fayette, Madame de La Fayette read Marguerite de Navarre, Dostoevsky read Turgenev, Tolstoy read Turgenev, Gogol read Turgenev, Turgenev read Lermontov, Lermontov read Scott, Tanizaki read Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, and Lady Murasaki, and so forth). Though some novelists have had classical educations, many, such as Defoe, Dickens, and almost every woman, had a Shakespeare-type education, “small Latin and less Greek.” Many novelists’ innovative and lively attachment to vernacular speech and up-to-the-minute forms of expression remained uncontaminated by the early drudgery of translating long passages of Latin and Greek. There was nothing “correct” about the novel to begin with (akin to, for example, the classical unities of the drama), and so every author was free to experiment with what might be incorrect but satisfying. When their own compositions became famous and popular, each novelist's techniques entered into both the narrative and the technical lexicon of the novel.

在很长一段时间里，小说并不标榜自己是艺术。小说并非植根于古典的修辞和想象形式，也未被纳入学校和大学的教学大纲。由于人们阅读小说是为了消遣而非“提升”，小说家从一开始就是自学成才，他们阅读自己独特的“小说课程”，从中挑选并模仿，常常秘密写作，首先取悦的是自己，而非老师或学者。许多小说家匿名或使用笔名发表作品——例如拉法耶特夫人、丹尼尔·笛福、简·奥斯汀、勃朗特姐妹、乔治·艾略特——这样做是因为如果署名，他们可能会失去一些东西，通常是名誉。而那些以真名发表作品的小说家，往往是社会地位不高的人，或者像塞缪尔·理查森和亨利·菲尔丁那样，在开始创作小说之前就已经拥有了一定的文学成就。在艺术上，小说家们都是自己动手创作的，他们对“小说”的了解都是从他们最喜欢的作家那里汲取的。我们从他们自己的证词中得知，福斯特读过詹姆斯，詹姆斯读过狄更斯，狄更斯读过斯莫利特，斯莫利特读过塞万提斯，塞万提斯读过纳瓦拉的玛格丽特，玛格丽特读过薄伽丘（当然，福斯特读过塞万提斯，狄更斯读过斯科特，斯科特读过薄伽丘，斯科特读过塞万提斯，菲尔丁读过塞万提斯，狄更斯读过塞万提斯，伍尔夫读过奥斯汀、狄更斯和詹姆斯，司汤达读过玛格丽特，巴尔扎克读过司汤达，詹姆斯读过巴尔扎克，屠格涅夫读过司汤达，司汤达读过拉法耶特夫人，拉法耶特夫人读过纳瓦拉的玛格丽特，陀思妥耶夫斯基读过屠格涅夫，托尔斯泰读过屠格涅夫，果戈理读过屠格涅夫，屠格涅夫读过莱蒙托夫，莱蒙托夫读过斯科特，谷崎润一郎读过托尔斯泰、陀思妥耶夫斯基和紫式部，等等）。尽管有些小说家接受过古典教育，但许多人，例如笛福、狄更斯以及几乎所有女性小说家，都接受过莎士比亚式的教育——“略懂拉丁语，希腊语更少”。许多小说家对白话文和现代表达方式的创新和生动运用，并未受到早期翻译大量拉丁语和希腊语的枯燥乏味的影响。小说本身并没有什么“正确”的标准（类似于古典戏剧的三一律），因此每位作家都可以自由地尝试那些可能并不正确但却令人满意的表达方式。当他们的作品声名鹊起、广受欢迎时，每位小说家的技巧都融入了小说的叙事和术语体系之中。

Seminal novelists and others made a technical contribution to the art of writing novels along with a contribution to the treasury of stories, settings, and characters—later novelists testified to their influence. Cervantes showed not only that a long narrative of an innocent man traveling about the countryside had virtually unlimited plot possibilities, but also that a narrative voice talking about such adventures in a chatty way was both agreeable and reassuring. Madame de La Fayette showed not only that all three participants in a love triangle could be equally sympathetic, but also that a narrator could efface herself sufficiently to seem to enter transparently into the thoughts of each of the participants, thereby raising the story above the level of gossipy speculation into the realm of philosophy. When Daniel Defoe wrote in the different voices of Robinson Crusoe, Moll Flanders, H. F, Roxana, and the others, he showed that an author could do two things at one time—observe his protagonist and embody him—giving the reader a rich empathetic experience while maintaining control of the themes that the life of the protagonist represented. When Fielding combined the conventions of stage comedy with the peripatetic adventures of an apparent reprobate, he showed that the juxtaposition of high and low was stimulating as well as broadening. When Lermontov placed his Byronic protagonist in the precisely and lyrically rendered landscape of the Caucasus, he showed how the Russian novel could be made both grand and irreducibly Russian in spite of imported ideas. When Balzac expanded his canvas by having major characters in one novel turn up as minor characters in others, he began to capture the kaleidoscopic variety of France and especially of Paris, but he also showed that while plots are good organizing devices and lenses for viewing particular lives and incidents, they do not need to dictate the roles particular characters, and, by extension, readers, play.

一些开创性的小说家和其他作家不仅在技巧上为小说写作艺术做出了贡献，也丰富了故事、场景和人物的宝库——后世小说家都见证了他们的影响。塞万提斯不仅证明了讲述一个天真无邪的男子在乡间游历的长篇叙事拥有几乎无限的情节可能性，而且还证明了以闲聊式的叙述口吻讲述这些冒险经历既令人愉悦又令人安心。拉法耶特夫人不仅证明了三角恋中的三个角色都可以同样令人同情，而且还证明了叙述者可以充分地隐去自身，仿佛透明地进入每个角色的内心世界，从而将故事从闲言碎语的层面提升到哲学的境界。丹尼尔·笛福以鲁滨逊·克鲁索、莫尔·弗兰德斯、H·F、罗克珊娜等人的不同视角进行写作，展现了作家如何同时做到两件事——观察主人公并融入其内心世界——从而赋予读者丰富的共情体验，同时又能掌控主人公人生所代表的主题。菲尔丁将舞台喜剧的惯例与一个看似浪荡不羁之人的浪荡冒险经历相结合，表明高雅与庸俗的并置既能激发灵感，又能拓展视野。莱蒙托夫将他笔下拜伦式的主人公置于高加索地区精准而抒情的风景之中，展现了俄罗斯小说如何在吸收外来思想的同时，依然保持其宏大而又不可磨灭的俄罗斯特色。当巴尔扎克通过让一部小说中的主要人物在其他小说中作为次要人物出现来拓展他的视野时，他开始捕捉法国，尤其是巴黎的万花筒般的多样性，但他也表明，虽然情节是很好的组织工具和观察特定生活和事件的视角，但它们并不需要决定特定人物（以及延伸开来，读者）所扮演的角色。

Each specific contribution was not necessarily invented by each seminal novelist. Every period was full of inventors and novelists who are now lost in general obscurity but who were nevertheless read by their contemporaries, whose new ideas were noticed and made use of. Technical ideas about the craft of novel-writing are not intellectual property except insofar as they are wedded to particular words written in particular sequences. Rather, techniques are subtle expansions of perception that stimulate a reader's thoughts about his own ideas and perceptions in new ways. The novel, in fact, requires technical innovation, because there is simply no way to make the time pass and the characters exist within a particular setting without being inventive. Even if I set out to rewrite Don Quixote incident by incident with the merest detail changed (let's say, the action happens ten years after the action of the real Don Quixote) , I will be presented with some challenge or other that requires a technical solution—perhaps the reign of one king has given way to that of another and two or three laws governing travel from town to town have changed, or deforestation has altered part of Quixote's landscape. If a handful of details about Quixote's journey are no longer plausible, then those details ramify into other scenes, and pretty soon I have a different novel altogether, as, indeed, Cervantes himself had a different novel altogether in the second volume of Don Quixote from the novel he had in the first. Great seminal novelists may or may not be more rawly original than their contemporaries; what they do is manage to wed originality of technique with depth of insight or breadth of knowledge or charm or some other quality that demonstrates the value of that technical innovation and makes it memorable to future novelists.

每项具体的贡献并非一定是每一位开创性小说家的独创。每个时代都涌现出许多发明家和小说家，他们如今或许已湮没在历史长河中，但他们的作品却被同时代的人阅读，他们的新思想被人们发现并加以运用。关于小说写作技巧的构思并非知识产权，除非它们与特定的文字和特定的顺序紧密相连。相反，技巧是对感知的微妙拓展，它以全新的方式激发读者对自身观念和感知的思考。事实上，小说需要技巧创新，因为若不进行创造性的创作，就无法使时间流逝，也无法使人物在特定的环境中生存。即使我着手逐一改写《堂吉诃德》，哪怕只改动最细微的细节（比如说，故事发生在真实堂吉诃德事件发生十年之后），我也会遇到这样那样的挑战，需要用技术手段来解决——或许是君主更迭，两三条城镇间的交通法规发生了变化，又或许是森林砍伐改变了堂吉诃德所处地貌的一部分。如果堂吉诃德旅程中的某些细节不再合情合理，那么这些细节就会延伸到其他场景，很快我就会得到一部截然不同的小说，正如塞万提斯本人在《堂吉诃德》第二卷中写出了与第一卷截然不同的故事一样。伟大的开创性小说家或许并不比同时代的人更具原创性；他们真正擅长的是将技巧上的独创性与深刻的洞察力、广博的知识、独特的魅力或其他特质相结合，从而展现出这种技巧创新的价值，并使其为后世小说家所铭记。

∗ Sometimes the reader doesn't know how stimulated she has been. In retrospect, for example, I can see how much my novel Moo owes to David Lodge's novel Small World , but at the time, I perceived only that I loved Lodge's novel and that it gave me permission to loosely corral many characters into one capacious narrative rather than to focus on the adventures of a single protagonist. While I was reading Small World , I was focusing on the jokes and the Arthurian references. While I was writing Moo , I was thinking about coordinating the action of the plot to the period of the school year and working out the ecological theme and structure. Small World existed in my mind as a template I was semi-aware of (I had read it once) and remembered with fondness.

* 有时读者并不知道自己受到了多大的启发。例如，现在回想起来，我才意识到我的小说《哞哞》深受大卫·洛奇的小说《小世界》的影响，但当时我只觉得我喜欢洛奇的小说，它让我可以自由地将众多人物松散地纳入一个包罗万象的叙事框架，而不是仅仅关注单一主人公的冒险经历。读《小世界》时，我关注的是其中的笑料和亚瑟王传说的典故。而创作《哞哞》时，我则在思考如何将故事情节与学年周期相契合，并构思生态主题和结构。《小世界》在我脑海中就像一个模板，我虽然半知半解（我读过一遍），却依然对它怀有美好的回忆。

An author's technique grows out of his temperament, his intentions, and his ideas, but it also grows out of his circumstances. A good example is Laurence Sterne. Sterne was classically educated, at Cambridge University, and he became a clergyman in Yorkshire, but he had no money apart from his living and the fees he sometimes received for giving sermons in York Minster. Like Defoe, he plied his pen for some twenty years in service of partisan politics, at least in part as repayment for clerical preferments he received from powerful friends and relatives in and around York. The first two volumes of The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy , however, were conceived as explicitly nonpolitical, a reaction to having incurred the wrath of the Church of England in 1759 with a satire on church politics called “A Political Romance.”

作者的写作技巧源于其性情、意图和思想，但也受其所处环境的影响。劳伦斯·斯特恩就是一个很好的例子。斯特恩在剑桥大学接受过古典教育，后来成为约克郡的一名牧师，但他除了生活费和偶尔在约克大教堂布道所得的收入外，几乎没有其他收入。与笛福一样，他笔耕不辍近二十年，为党派政治服务，至少部分原因是为了回报他在约克及其周边地区有权势的朋友和亲戚给予他的教职晋升。然而，《项狄传》的前两卷却明确地以非政治性为创作初衷，这源于他在1759年创作了一部名为《政治传奇》的讽刺教会政治的作品，触怒了英国国教。

Sterne was surprised by Tristram Shandy ‘s wild success, but he reveled in it, even in the negative attention (Dr. Johnson was certain its popularity was a passing fad), and was soon a famous man, consorting with David Garrick, meeting the king, and having his portrait painted by Joshua Reynolds. As usual with best sellers, though, it quickly became apparent that the author had to keep writing to maintain the income stream. Sterne was more than willing to do whatever he could to sustain his popularity—one of the first ideas he had was to publish a volume of his own sermons under the name “Parson Yorick,” a character in Tristram Shandy , implying an autobiographical link between the racy novel (which, of course, frankly discusses all sorts of bodily functions in addition to sex) and his career as a clergyman. Next, he composed two more volumes about Tristram, emphasizing what he considered to be its strongest selling point: eccentricity. Ultimately he published nine volumes in the 1760s , never changing his tone or his method, though gradually shifting his story away from Tristram and his parents toward the mild and mysterious eccentric Uncle Toby. In his embrace of his signature techniques—bawdy jokes, odd ideas and observations, digressions, thought association—in a ten-year effort to sustain sales, Sterne is almost a parody of novelists in general. And he was right. Though he tried another book—a travel narrative about a journey through France and Italy—it was not successful because it did not have that precise combination of subject and sensibility that seemed so original, and turned out to be so lasting, in Tristram Shandy.

《项狄传》的巨大成功令斯特恩始料未及，但他却乐在其中，即便面对负面评价（约翰逊博士断言这股热潮不过是昙花一现），他也欣然接受。斯特恩很快声名鹊起，与大卫·加里克交往甚密，觐见国王，甚至请约书亚·雷诺兹为他画像。然而，正如所有畅销书一样，作者很快就意识到必须不断写作才能维持收入来源。斯特恩非常乐意竭尽所能地维持自己的名气——他最先想到的办法之一，就是以《项狄传》中的人物“约里克牧师”的名义出版一本自己的布道集，暗示这部充满争议的小说（当然，除了性之外，小说还坦率地探讨了各种生理功能）与他作为牧师的生涯之间存在某种自传式的联系。接下来，他又创作了两卷关于项狄传的小说，着重强调他认为这部小说最大的卖点：古怪的性格。最终，他在18世纪60年代出版了九卷《项狄传》，始终未变其文风和写作手法，只是逐渐将故事的重心从特里斯特拉姆和他的父母转移到了温和而神秘的古怪叔叔托比身上。为了维持销量，斯特恩在长达十年的时间里，坚持运用其标志性的写作技巧——粗俗的笑话、奇特的想法和观察、离题的叙述以及联想——这几乎是对当时所有小说家的一种讽刺。而他的做法是正确的。尽管他尝试创作了另一部作品——一部关于法国和意大利之旅的游记——但这部作品并不成功，因为它缺乏《项狄传》中那种独树一帜、经久不衰的题材和情感的完美结合。

With repeated employment, a certain technique ceases to be technical and comes to characterize an author's entire oeuvre and to constitute his original vision. Jane Austen claimed that her works were like miniatures painted on ivory—she was ambitious not for breadth, or even depth, but for precision. She not only knew what she wanted to do and could do (given her secluded life), she also knew how she was distinct from other novelists, and she liked to exploit her distinction. Her technique did not seem to limit her ability to grow, though—each successive heroine is different from the others, each new family is set into a somewhat larger context than earlier families. Austen's miniatures expand and deepen without bursting off the ivory.

反复运用某种技巧，它便不再仅仅是技巧，而是成为作家全部作品的特征，并构成其独特的创作理念。简·奥斯汀曾说，她的作品如同象牙上的微型画——她追求的并非广度，甚至也不是深度，而是精准。她不仅清楚自己想做什么、能做什么（鉴于她隐居的生活），也清楚自己与其他小说家的区别，并且乐于发挥这种独特性。然而，她的技巧似乎并未限制她的创作能力——每一位女主人公都与前一位截然不同，每一个新的家庭都置于比之前家庭更为宏大的背景之中。奥斯汀的微型画作在象牙之上不断扩展和深化，却始终保持着精准的构图。

Anthony Trollope, more worldly and more ambitious than Austen but possessed of a similar judicious, ironic style, wrote forty-seven novels by employing a rigorous system of composition that on the surface does not even look like a technique as much as a lifestyle—when he was planning The Way We Live Now , he scheduled himself to write some ten thousand words per week and to complete the two-volume, 950 -page (in the Oxford edition) novel in thirty-two weeks. He finished in twenty-nine weeks. For most of his writing career (from age twenty until fifty-two) he worked as a civil servant in the post office— he wrote his weekly ten thousand words beginning at about five-thirty every morning. Trollope was no dull boy—he loved fox hunting, socializing, traveling, eating, and drinking, and made time for a good measure of each. In addition, Trollope, who, like Sterne, was sensitive about the hardships of an impoverished childhood, cared a great deal about “pecuniary emolument,” as Jane Austen would have called it. In Trollope's autobiography (begun when he was about sixty and published after his death) he related as many details about deals he had made and the relative success or failure of each book as about more personal aspects of his life or more artful aspects of his career. The effect of his autobiography was to diminish his posthumous reputation as a novelist, but the systematic approach he espoused as a way of succeeding professionally worked also as a narrative technique, a way of exploring in great detail certain aspects of the inner life and of the many facets of English bourgeois existence that he is famous for anatomizing.

安东尼·特罗洛普比简·奥斯汀更世故、更有抱负，但同样拥有睿智而讽刺的文风。他一生创作了四十七部小说，采用的是一种严谨的写作方法，乍看之下与其说是一种技巧，不如说是一种生活方式——在构思《我们现在的生活方式》时，他给自己制定了每周写作约一万字的计划，目标是在三十二周内完成这部两卷本、牛津版共950页的小说。最终，他只用了二十九周就完成了。在他写作生涯的大部分时间里（从二十岁到五十二岁），他都在邮局担任公务员——他每天早上五点半左右开始写作，完成每周一万字的写作目标。特罗洛普绝非一个乏味的人——他热爱猎狐、社交、旅行、美食和美酒，并且每样都乐在其中。此外，特罗洛普和斯特恩一样，对贫困童年的艰辛感同身受，因此也十分看重“金钱报酬”（正如简·奥斯汀所言）。在他的自传（大约六十岁时开始撰写，死后出版）中，他详尽地描述了自己达成的交易以及每本书的成败，其篇幅与他个人生活的方方面面以及职业生涯中更具艺术性的技巧一样多。自传的出版削弱了他作为小说家的身后声誉，但他所倡导的系统性方法，既是他事业成功的途径，也是一种叙事技巧，使他能够深入细致地探索内心世界以及他所擅长剖析的英国资产阶级生活的方方面面。

It is, of course, impossible to encapsulate Trollope's accomplishments in a few paragraphs, but a passage from The Eustace Diamonds might convey something of his technique:

当然，要用寥寥数语概括特罗洛普的成就是不可能的，但《尤斯塔斯钻石》中的一段文字或许能展现他的一些写作技巧：

Lady Linlithgow, upon whom Lizzie's beauty could have no effect of that kind, had nevertheless declared her to be very beautiful. And this loveliness was of a nature that was altogether pleasing, if once the beholder of it could get over the idea of falseness which certainly Lizzie's eye was apt to convey to the beholder. [p. 358 ]

林利斯戈夫人虽然不认为莉齐的美貌对她有那种影响，但她还是称赞莉齐非常漂亮。这种美是完全令人愉悦的，只要观赏者能够克服莉齐的眼神中那种虚假的印象。[p. 358]

A few lines later, Trollope turns his attention to Lizzie's lover:

几行之后，特罗洛普将注意力转向了莉齐的情人：

All this had been tendered to Frank—and with it that worldly wealth which was so absolutely necessary to his career. For though Greystock would not have said to any man or woman that nature had intended him to be a spender of much money and a consumer of many good things, he did undoubtedly so think of himself.

这一切都已赐予弗兰克——包括对他事业至关重要的世俗财富。虽然格雷斯托克不会对任何人说他天生就该挥金如土、享受各种美好事物，但他无疑就是这样看待自己的。

Trollope's methodical habits are evident in both these passages. In the midst of love, there is calculation—Lizzie's beauty against her false nature; Frank's desires and ambitions against his instinctive recognition of Lizzie's nature; and, in both cases, external appearance against internal truth. His style works the same way, though to more poignant effect, in The Last Chronicle of Barset , where the calculation is about a minor crime: Does the poor, charitable, passionate, but irritable and stiff-necked curate actually pass a bad check? And who of his associates is ready to believe such a thing, and who is unconvinced? Trollope is a genius of measurement—yes, in his autobiography, he counts up the money and totes up his success, but in his novels he weighs and balances and measures the ramifications of countless decisions, impulses, and feelings, recognizing always that in a tightly interconnected culture, the smallest wrong step can have dire consequences, but also that it is possible to think too much and thereby destroy happiness that impulse might have gained. Trollope was a great analyst of marriage as a series of decisions that turn into a relationship and then, as time goes by and the children grow up, into history and architecture; simultaneously, he was the great analyst of politics as it devolves into feelings and their effects on the nation. If we say that Trollope is the ultimate realist, we are recognizing that his work as well as his life recognized more points of view, more endeavors, more sensations, more things to think about and reasons to think about them than almost any other novelist; that the technique he developed for balancing the attractions of these sensations—in sentences, paragraphs, chapters, characters, and entire books—beautifully mimics the way many people construct their identities moment by moment. Since no novel can simply exist, like a painting or a sculpture, but must communicate something intelligible, the ways in which it can be well crafted are numerous, and since the twin challenges of time and space are always present, novelists never lose sight of technical questions, and technical questions are always rhetorical ones as well.

特罗洛普的写作习惯在这两段文字中都显而易见。在爱情之中，也暗藏着算计——莉齐的美貌与她虚伪的本性之间的冲突；弗兰克的欲望和野心与他对莉齐本性的直觉认知之间的矛盾；而且，在这两个例子中，外表都与内在的真实相悖。在《巴塞特郡的最后编年史》中，他的写作风格同样运用了这种手法，但效果更为深刻。在这部作品中，算计的焦点在于一起轻微的犯罪：这位贫穷、慈善、热情，却又易怒固执的牧师真的会开空头支票吗？他的同伴中，谁会相信这种事，谁又会对此深信不疑？特罗洛普是一位衡量天才——没错，在他的自传中，他细数着财富，记录着自己的成就；但在他的小说中，他权衡、平衡、衡量着无数决定、冲动和情感的后果，始终意识到在一个紧密相连的文化中，哪怕是最微小的错误都可能造成可怕的后果；但他也明白，过度思考反而会扼杀冲动可能带来的幸福。特罗洛普是一位伟大的婚姻分析家，他将婚姻视为一系列决定如何演变成一段关系，并随着时间的流逝和子女的成长，最终成为历史和建筑；与此同时，他也是一位伟大的政治分析家，他将政治演化为情感及其对国家的影响。如果我们说特罗洛普是终极现实主义者，那就意味着我们承认，他的作品和人生都比几乎任何其他小说家都更能捕捉到更多视角、更多尝试、更多感受、更多值得思考的事物以及思考它们的理由。他发展出的平衡这些感官吸引力的技巧——无论是在句子、段落、章节、人物还是整部作品中——都巧妙地模仿了许多人逐时构建自身身份的方式。小说不能像绘画或雕塑那样仅仅存在，而必须传达某种可理解的信息，因此，小说的创作手法多种多样。同时，由于时间和空间的双重挑战始终存在，小说家们也从未忽视技术问题，而技术问题本身也总是与修辞问题息息相关。

At the beginning of the twentieth century, though, novelists began making a case not only that novels were art, but also that certain qualities of certain novels were more artistic than others. Whether a novel should be, or could be, art was not, of course, entirely an aesthetic question, given both the novel's history as morally suspect and its wide appeal. The questions were still to some extent framed in terms of technique, but the ideal was no longer just to promote the novel's ability to communicate more and more details about more and more things, but also to have an aesthetic shape or effect that would be intended by the author and felt by the reader as consciously graceful, beautiful, or “right.” The foremost proponent of these sorts of ideas was Henry James, both implicitly in the way he wrote his novels and explicitly in what he wrote about them. As a young man, James reviewed both Dickens and Trollope, and not kindly. Of one of Trol-lope's novels he wrote, “Life is vulgar, but we know not how vulgar it is until we see it set down in his pages” (review of Can You Forgive Her? , quoted in Oxford Reader's Companion to Trollope). With Our Mutual Friend he was not impressed, declaring it “the poorest of Mr. Dickens's works” (quoted in Oxford Reader's Companion to Dickens). And even though James seems to have admired George Eliot and attempted to get to know her and her companion George Henry Lewes, he still considered Middlemarch “an indifferent whole.” We can tell by his subsequent writings, his own novels, and his essays on the nature of the novel as a form that he aspired to produce something simultaneously less vulgar and less formless than the novels of the great Victorians, and that he wished his work to elevate the novel to the status of art.

然而，在二十世纪初，小说家们开始论证小说不仅是艺术，而且某些小说的某些特质比其他小说更具艺术性。当然，鉴于小说历史上曾饱受道德质疑，以及其广泛的受众群体，小说是否应该或能够成为艺术，并非完全是一个美学问题。这些问题在某种程度上仍然以技巧为框架，但理想不再仅仅是提升小说传达越来越多细节的能力，而是要使其拥有一种美学形态或效果，这种形态或效果是作者有意为之，并被读者自觉地感受到的优雅、优美或“恰当”。亨利·詹姆斯是这类理念最主要的倡导者，这体现在他小说的写作方式中，也体现在他对这些小说的评论中。年轻时，詹姆斯曾评论过狄更斯和特罗洛普的作品，而且措辞并不友好。他曾这样评价特罗洛普的一部小说：“生活是庸俗的，但只有当他把生活描绘出来时，我们才知道它究竟有多么庸俗”（《你能原谅她吗？》书评，引自《牛津特罗洛普读者指南》）。他对《我们共同的朋友》并不感冒，称其为“狄更斯先生最差的作品”（引自《牛津狄更斯读者指南》）。尽管詹姆斯似乎很欣赏乔治·艾略特，并试图结识她和她的伴侣乔治·亨利·刘易斯，但他仍然认为《米德尔马契》“平庸至极”。从他后来的作品、他自己的小说以及他关于小说这种文体本质的论文中，我们可以看出，他渴望创作出比维多利亚时代伟大作家的小说更不庸俗、更严谨的作品，并且他希望自己的作品能将小说提升到艺术的地位。

James's first successful novel was The Portrait of a Lady , published in 1881 , when James was thirty-eight. His “lady” is Isabel Archer, an American young woman who is brought to Europe by her aunt, to give her a year abroad before she gets married. Isabel is an appealing, independent-minded young woman who isn't ready to yield to the charms, such as they are, of her American suitor. Soon enough, in England, she attracts the attention of two more men—her invalid cousin Ralph and an attractive aristocrat who doesn't seem to attract Isabel. Giving up the protections of engagement and marriage, though, proves more dangerous than Isabel foresees. Her aunt is blind to the possibility that Isabel might be duped, but when Isabel is left a large inheritance, her fate is decided. She falls into the clutches of the elegant but penniless Madame Merle, who introduces her to Gilbert Osmond, an American in Florence with no visible means of support and an expensive habit of connoisseurship. By the end of the novel it is clear to Isabel that she is trapped—her marriage is an evil, loveless sham (Osmond is portrayed as being a vaguely satanic combination of calculation and vengeful selfishness), her child has died, and she has lost access to Osmond's daughter, of whom she is fond. Everything that Isabel has learned about love and marriage growing up in the United States turns out to be wrong—in Europe, marriage is a pure commodity relationship, and it is the fate of girls (including Osmond's daughter) to be bought, sold, and dominated. Their only choices are to accept their fate knowingly or to undergo it without understanding it. That Isabel would suffer disillusionment is only a measure of her former illusions.

詹姆斯的第一部成功小说是《贵妇画像》，出版于1881年，当时詹姆斯38岁。小说中的“贵妇”是伊莎贝尔·阿切尔，一位美国年轻女子，被她的姑妈带到欧洲，让她在结婚前体验一年的异国生活。伊莎贝尔是一位迷人而独立自主的年轻女子，她并不甘于被美国追求者的魅力所迷惑。很快，在英国，她又吸引了另外两位男士的注意——一位是她体弱多病的表兄拉尔夫，另一位是一位英俊的贵族，但这位贵族似乎对伊莎贝尔并不感兴趣。然而，放弃订婚和婚姻的庇护，比伊莎贝尔预想的要危险得多。她的姑妈对伊莎贝尔可能受骗的可能性浑然不觉，但当伊莎贝尔继承了一大笔遗产时，她的命运就此注定。她落入了优雅却一贫如洗的梅尔夫人手中，梅尔夫人将她介绍给了吉尔伯特·奥斯蒙德，一个在佛罗伦萨的美国人，他没有明显的经济来源，却有着挥金如土的鉴赏癖。小说结尾，伊莎贝尔清楚地意识到自己身陷囹圄——她的婚姻是一场邪恶的、毫无爱情的骗局（奥斯蒙德被描绘成一个阴险狡诈、充满报复心的自私自利的化身），她的孩子夭折了，她也失去了与奥斯蒙德女儿的联系，而她一直很喜欢这个女儿。伊莎贝尔在美国成长过程中所学到的关于爱情和婚姻的一切都被证明是错误的——在欧洲，婚姻纯粹是一种商品关系，女孩们（包括奥斯蒙德的女儿）的命运就是被买卖、被支配。她们唯一的选择要么是心甘情愿地接受命运，要么是在不知情的情况下默默承受。伊莎贝尔的幻灭，恰恰反映了她过去那些不切实际的幻想。

In The Portrait of a Lady , James does what he had intended to do— he excludes the vulgar by focusing on a few wealthy and well-educated Europeans and Americans, and he uses intense psychological analysis and careful depiction of settings to fill the spots where the vulgar might have been. The plot of James's novel, so similar to myriad earlier plots about what is to be done with women and what they could conceivably do with themselves, unfolds with great deliberateness as Isabel's friends and the narrator contemplate her fate. Isabel herself is something of a cipher—perhaps she is reserved, perhaps she is independent, perhaps she is unusually innocent, but she seems to recede as the novel progresses. Not knowing what she wants, she turns down many things that are offered. When she does choose something (to take a tour), James does not follow her and show the reader how it affects her. When we rejoin her after the tour, we are supposed to understand how she now contrasts to who she had been before the tour, but the contrasts are hazy because Isabel retains her reserve. For compelling dynamism in her character James substitutes analysis of her in his narrative voice. This has the effect of circumscribing her even further. The narrator expresses his admiration of her, but the reader can't help feeling intuitively that she is as trapped by his reportorial voice as she is by the expectations of those around her. Nevertheless, Isabel's fate is affecting, particularly so because she is very young and Osmond is not especially old, either. The trap she seems destined to inhabit is going to last a long time.

在《一位女士的画像》中，詹姆斯实现了他的预期——他通过聚焦于少数富有且受过良好教育的欧洲人和美国人，排除了庸俗的元素，并运用深刻的心理分析和细致的环境描写，填补了庸俗可能出现的空白。詹姆斯的这部小说情节与之前无数关于女性命运以及她们可能如何抉择的小说情节极为相似，随着伊莎贝尔的朋友和叙述者对她命运的思考，故事以一种极其谨慎的方式展开。伊莎贝尔本人则像个谜——或许她矜持，或许她独立，或许她天真无邪，但随着小说的推进，她似乎逐渐淡出人们的视线。由于不清楚自己想要什么，她拒绝了许多别人提供的选择。即使她最终做出了选择（比如参加旅行团），詹姆斯也没有跟随她的视角，向读者展现这一选择对她的影响。巡演结束后，我们再次见到她时，理应能感受到她与巡演前截然不同的性格，但由于伊莎贝尔依然保持着矜持，这种对比显得模糊不清。詹姆斯用叙述的口吻分析她，而非展现她性格中引人入胜的活力。这反而进一步限制了她的发挥。叙述者表达了对她的钦佩，但读者却不由自主地感到，她不仅被周围人的期望所束缚，也被叙述者的叙述口吻所困。尽管如此，伊莎贝尔的命运依然令人动容，尤其考虑到她还很年轻，而奥斯蒙德也并不算老。她似乎注定要陷入的困境，将会持续很久。

James and his friend Edith Wharton were ambitious Americans. They recognized that, as vital and satisfying as the tradition of the English novel was, English novels were missing something that French novels possessed—psychological refinement and depth. They wanted to get that depth into their own novels, but to avoid the sordid subjects that were the meat and potatoes of the French novel.

詹姆斯和他的朋友伊迪丝·华顿都是雄心勃勃的美国人。他们意识到，尽管英国小说的传统至关重要且令人满足，但它却缺少法国小说所拥有的某种东西——心理描写上的细腻和深度。他们希望将这种深度融入自己的小说中，但又不想触及法国小说中那些低俗不堪的主题。

James reveals his basic principle, and basic fear, in his introduction to Roderick Hudson , in the uniform edition of his novels that was published as the “New York Edition” in 1907 . James is explicit about the fact that as soon as he began to write this first novel (in 1874 ), he began to worry: “I recall again the quite uplifted sense with which my idea, such as it was, permitted me at last to put quite out to sea…. Yet it must even then have begun for me, too, the ache of fear, that was to become so familiar, of being unduly tempted and led on by ‘developments’” (The Art of the Novel , p. 4 ). He goes on, somewhat later, in a typically elaborate but telling Jamesian simile: “A young embroiderer of the canvas of life [James himself, of course] soon began to work in terror, fairly, of the vast expanse of that surface, of the boundless number of its distinct perforations for the needle, and of the tendency inherent in his many-coloured flowers and figures to cover and consume as many as possible of the little holes” (p. 5 ). Throughout the introductions of the New York Edition, James recalls how ideas for novels came to him through a single chance remark made to him at a party or a detail relayed to him over dinner. As soon as a particular “seed’ struck him, he would make strenuous efforts not to hear any more of the details surrounding the actual incident or character being related because in his own mind, details and connections were already burgeoning. Prominent Victorian authors, of course, specialized in “developments”—as a result, much of the action in their books had to be a bit melodramatic, if only to have definition.

詹姆斯在1907年出版的“纽约版”小说全集（统一版本）中，为罗德里克·哈德逊所作的序言揭示了他的基本原则和根本恐惧。詹姆斯明确指出，他从1874年开始创作第一部小说时，就开始感到担忧：“我再次想起，我的想法，尽管如此，最终还是让我扬帆起航，那种感觉是多么令人振奋……然而，即便在那时，我也一定开始感受到那种恐惧的煎熬，这种恐惧后来变得如此熟悉，害怕被‘发展’过度诱惑和牵着鼻子走”（《小说的艺术》，第4页）。他稍后又用一个典型的詹姆斯式精妙而又意味深长的比喻继续说道：“一位年轻的刺绣师（当然指詹姆斯本人）在人生的画布上刺绣，很快就开始感到恐惧，确切地说，是恐惧那广袤无垠的画布，恐惧那无数针眼，也恐惧他那些五彩缤纷的花朵和人物图案会尽可能地覆盖和吞噬那些小孔”（第5页）。在纽约版的导言中，詹姆斯回忆起他的小说灵感是如何从聚会上偶然听到的一句话或晚餐时听到的某个细节中涌现出来的。一旦某个“种子”在他心中萌芽，他就会竭力避免听到关于事件或人物的更多细节，因为在他的脑海中，各种细节和联系已经开始萌芽。当然，维多利亚时代的著名作家都擅长“情节发展”——因此，他们作品中的许多情节都必须略带戏剧性，即便只是为了让故事更加清晰。

Henry James, though, wanted to write important novels in which the action was less melodramatic—books not about murders and suicides and virtue beset, but about the progress of the inner life, in which the climax might be only a silent recognition by the protagonist that she has made a commitment fatal to her happiness. Readers had to be educated to understand the weight of such subterranean drama, and so in the course of the three decades after The Portrait of a Lady , James disciplined the novel in several ways. He rarely wrote in the first person, but almost always in the third-person limited point of view, and he often located that point of view in one or two characters present in the action of the novel but peripheral to it, as he relates the bad behavior of Maisie's parents in What Maisie Knew through Maisie's uncomprehending eyes, or as he relates The Ambassadors through the consciousness of Lambert Strether. The effect of this was to get two for one—the events unfold, those centrally implicated act out their drama, and the effects of their drama on those around them are evident, too. In the case of The Ambassadors , the drama has a more significant effect on Strether, who decides in late middle age not to let life pass him by, than it does on the lovers he has come to Europe to break up, and James gets to simultaneously explore the hidden drama of Strether's inner life and the overt drama of Chad and Madame de Vionnet's mildly shocking affair. In his introduction to The Golden Bowl , James refers to something he disapproves of— “the mere muffled majesty of irresponsible ‘authorship’” that results from not locating clearly both the events of the story and the perspective from which it is to be viewed. Even when the filtering narrative consciousness is all but indistinguishable from James himself, the discipline of naming and characterizing the filtering consciousness organizes the way in which James the author can talk about the plot and the protagonist. The protagonist is also always set into a specific and carefully rendered social milieu, which becomes part of the story, on the one hand, and defines how intimate the novel may get, on the other. James often writes about subjects that in other hands would be considered immoral (in The Wings of the Dove , a couple concocts a plan in which the man will seduce and marry a wealthy but dying American heiress to get her fortune; in the course of the novel, the focus of the young man's passions shifts from one girl to the other), but the strict arrangement of the material and the effect of James's elaborate style in rendering all feelings and passions analyzable and characterizable enables him to raise their level of respectability, their level of complexity, and their level of aesthetic satisfaction. James's work gains a great deal of intensity through the contrast of the inner life of a passionate or idealistic character with the ironclad proprieties of his or her world, and is quite successful at portraying the pain of compromise, self-knowledge, and endurance.

然而，亨利·詹姆斯想要创作一些情节不那么戏剧化的重要小说——这些小说并非讲述谋杀、自杀和道德沦丧，而是着重刻画人物内心世界的成长，其高潮或许仅仅是主人公默默地意识到自己做出了一个会让她失去幸福的承诺。读者需要接受一定的教育才能理解这种潜藏的戏剧张力，因此在《一位女士的画像》之后的三十年里，詹姆斯从多个方面对小说创作进行了革新。他很少使用第一人称，几乎总是采用第三人称有限视角，并且常常将视角设定在小说情节中出现但又处于边缘地位的一两个人物身上，例如在《梅西的世界》中，他通过梅西懵懂的视角来叙述她父母的恶劣行径；又如在《大使》中，他通过兰伯特·斯特雷瑟的意识来讲述故事。这样做可谓一举两得——事件展开，核心人物上演各自的戏剧，而这些戏剧对周围人的影响也显而易见。以《大使》为例，这场戏剧对斯特雷瑟的影响远大于对他来到欧洲拆散的那对恋人的影响。斯特雷瑟在中年晚期决定不再虚度光阴，因此詹姆斯得以同时探索斯特雷瑟内心世界的隐秘戏剧，以及查德和德·维奥内夫人那段略显惊世骇俗的婚外情。在《金碗》的引言中，詹姆斯提到了他所不赞同的某种现象——“不负责任的‘作者’所展现的那种含糊不清的威严”，这种威严源于未能清晰地定位故事的事件和叙述视角。即使叙事意识的过滤作用几乎与詹姆斯本人难以区分，命名和刻画这种过滤意识的规范也组织了詹姆斯作为作者谈论情节和主人公的方式。主人公总是被置于一个精心描绘的特定社会环境中，这既成为故事的一部分，又决定了小说可以深入到何种程度。詹姆斯经常描写在其他人笔下会被认为是不道德的主题（例如在《鸽之翼》中，一对情侣密谋让男方引诱并娶一位富有但即将离世的美国女继承人以夺取她的财产；在小说中，这位年轻男子的激情在两个女孩之间摇摆不定），但詹姆斯对素材的严格安排以及他精雕细琢的文风，使得所有情感和激情都变得可分析、可刻画，从而提升了这些情感和激情的体面性、复杂性和审美满足感。詹姆斯的作品通过充满激情或理想主义的人物内心世界与他/她所处世界的铁腕礼仪之间的对比，获得了极大的强度，并且非常成功地描绘了妥协、自我认知和忍耐的痛苦。

∗ The Turn of the Screw is in the first person.

《螺丝在拧紧》采用第一人称叙述。

Significantly, James was also much afraid of having to go too far afield. He comments on this in the preface to Daisy Miller when he recalls a visit to New York that he made in the 1870s . He found himself stuck “at the very moderate altitude of Twenty-fifth Street… alone… with the music-masters and French pastry-cooks, the ladies and children—immensely present and immensely numerous these, but testifying with a collective voice to the extraordinary absence… of a serious male interest.” Prohibited (he implies by financial considerations) from investigating what was going on on Wall Street, “and New York was, for force and accent, nothing else worth speaking of,” James chose a different milieu to explore in his novels, not a milieu of work but one of leisure. Obviously James was not suited by talent or temperament to make a case for expansiveness as a virtue in the novel, so he made the case for form, a form based, as in classical painting, on perspective. Just as in great Renaissance and Baroque paintings the arrangement of the figures depends for effect on where the painter positions the viewer, so what the reader learns about the story James is telling is carefully controlled by the character (or consciousness) assigned by the author to tell the story. Underscoring this effect is the care and detail with which James depicts settings; many James novels read like a series of tableaux vivants , where the American characters are dwarfed by their European surroundings, which embody history and tradition as well as art and beauty. Wherever they come from in America, what the characters do is not about who they are and cannot truly be understood apart from the particular buildings, streets, towns, and landscapes in which they find themselves in Europe. When James fails to follow Isabel Archer on her tour, for example, he indicates that who she is and the context of her decisions about her life are not to be understood as a result of what she does, but as the product of the social context in which she finds herself at the time she is making the decision.

值得注意的是，詹姆斯也十分害怕远走他乡。他在《黛西·米勒》的序言中回忆起19世纪70年代的一次纽约之行时，对此有所提及。他发现自己被困在“第二十五街那平淡无奇的地段……独自一人……与音乐教师、法国糕点师、女士和孩子们为伴——这些人数量众多，熙熙攘攘，却共同诉说着……男性严肃兴趣的罕见缺失。”由于经济原因（他暗示如此），詹姆斯无力探究华尔街的种种，而“纽约，就其气势和氛围而言，也并无其他值得一提之处”，因此，他选择在小说中探索另一种环境——并非工作环境，而是休闲环境。显然，詹姆斯的才华和性情都不适合在小说中将宏大作为一种美德来论证，所以他转而强调形式，一种如同古典绘画般基于透视的形式。正如文艺复兴和巴洛克时期的伟大绘画中，人物的排列方式取决于画家如何安排观者的位置，詹姆斯笔下故事的叙述也受到作者赋予叙述者的角色（或意识）的精心控制。詹姆斯对场景的细致描绘更强化了这种效果；他的许多小说读起来就像一系列活人画，美国人物在他们所处的欧洲环境中显得渺小，这些环境不仅体现了历史和传统，也蕴含了艺术和美。无论人物来自美国的哪个地方，他们的行为都与他们的身份无关，也无法脱离他们身处的欧洲特定建筑、街道、城镇和风景而真正理解。例如，当詹姆斯没有跟随伊莎贝尔·阿切尔游览时，他暗示我们不应仅仅从她的行为本身来理解她的身份以及她人生抉择的背景，而应将其视为她做出抉择时所处社会环境的产物。

James's argument about what was better and what was best (the depiction of moral dilemmas being better and the ever more refined parsing of motive and character being best, with the hand of the author always masterful but hidden) was not directed at the traditional audience of the novel—let's say the Defoe/Dickens audience, who thought the novel was fine and plenty artful; it was directed at the sort of audience who would have the taste to read and the money to buy the elaborate New York Edition of his works, some twenty-three volumes, and, also, to himself as a celebration and perhaps justification of his lifelong devotion (with a short hiatus in the 1890s , when he wrote unsuccessfully for the London stage) to a suspect form.

詹姆斯关于什么更好、什么最好（对道德困境的描绘更好，对动机和人物的日益精细的剖析最好，作者的手法总是精湛但隐蔽的）的论点，并非针对小说的传统读者——比如笛福/狄更斯的读者，他们认为小说很好，也很有艺术性；而是针对那些有品味阅读，并且有钱购买他作品的精美纽约版（约二十三卷）的读者，同时也是对他自己的一种庆祝，或许也是对他终生（在19世纪90年代曾短暂中断，当时他为伦敦舞台创作剧本，但并不成功）对这种可疑形式的奉献的一种辩解。

James was not a popular writer—he often lamented the poor sales of his novels—but he had a powerful effect on novelists who came after him, and on the very idea of what a novel should be, especially in England and the United States. But other novelists had opinions, too, and one of these was Leo Tolstoy, who in 1898 published his own manifesto, “What Is Art?” Tolstoy, like James, seems to be reacting to the nineteenth-century novelistic social project, but his reaction is diametrically opposed to James's. Tolstoy begins his argument not with the novel but with other commonly accepted forms of art—music, ballet, and drama—and describes the ill-paid and difficult labor that goes into producing such art. He focuses especially on the disparities of social class that these (and other forms) promote and confirm—art is an economic product like any other in that those who work the hardest to produce it have the least wherewithal to understand it or to consume it (the workers can't afford the fruits of their labor). The wrinkle in Tolstoy's analysis is that, unlike James, he considers exclusiveness a bad thing; the problem is not in the uneducated taste of one class of potential consumers, but in the perverted taste of the other class of confirmed consumers (and producers). True art, Tolstoy asserts, would appeal to universal human thoughts, desires, and needs, would be simple to understand, would be inclusive rather than exclusive.

詹姆斯并非一位畅销作家——他常常感叹自己小说销量惨淡——但他对后世小说家，以及小说本身的理念，尤其是在英国和美国，产生了深远的影响。然而，其他小说家也有自己的见解，其中一位便是列夫·托尔斯泰。1898年，托尔斯泰发表了自己的宣言《何谓艺术？》。与詹姆斯一样，托尔斯泰似乎也在对19世纪小说的社会建构做出回应，但他的回应与詹姆斯截然相反。托尔斯泰的论证并非从小说入手，而是从其他公认的艺术形式——音乐、芭蕾和戏剧——入手，描述了创作这些艺术作品所付出的艰辛而又报酬微薄的劳动。他尤其关注这些艺术形式（以及其他艺术形式）所加剧和强化的社会阶级差异——艺术和其他经济产品一样，是一种经济产品，因为那些辛勤创作的人往往最缺乏理解或欣赏它的能力（劳动者买不起自己劳动的成果）。托尔斯泰分析的难点在于，与詹姆斯不同，他认为排他性是件坏事；问题不在于一部分潜在消费者缺乏教养，而在于另一部分既定消费者（和生产者）的扭曲品味。托尔斯泰断言，真正的艺术应该诉诸人类普遍的思想、欲望和需求，应该通俗易懂，应该包容而非排他。

Tolstoy was particularly offended by the erotic content of the art he surveyed, and he contends that much of the purpose of art in his day was to inflame the passions of the jaded upper class; he also attacks notions of beauty and pleasure as class-based and empty. He angrily throws Shakespeare, Dante, and even himself into the trash bin. To us, Tolstoy seems to be purveying a belief in the sort of utopianism that ended up producing the nightmares of the twentieth century, but his polemic is a natural extension of the methods of the nineteenth-century novel—should enough material be organized and clearly arranged according to sometimes subtle but ultimately understandable principles of not only cause and effect but sympathy and empathy, then the wholesale transformation of society into something more like a novel—something organized and connected, something if not happier, then smarter—could follow. The proper art could “fix” society, but improper art (and this is the source of Tolstoy's anger—he is surrounded by improper art) can only damage society. His experience of the peasantry on his estate, to begin with, and other “true Russians” not of the upper class has convinced him that erotic passion in particular, but other forms of greed, selfishness, and brutality as well, have their source not in changeless human nature but in social arrangements and contaminating images and ideas—an extension of the ideas of many nineteenth-century novelists, including Dickens and Stowe, but seen through a point of view more religious and less pragmatic than either of theirs.

托尔斯泰尤其反感他所考察的艺术作品中的情色内容，他认为当时艺术的很大一部分目的在于煽动厌世的上层阶级的欲望；他还抨击美和快乐的观念，认为它们基于阶级且空洞无物。他愤怒地将莎士比亚、但丁，甚至他自己都扔进了垃圾桶。在我们看来，托尔斯泰似乎在兜售一种最终酿成二十世纪噩梦的乌托邦主义，但他的论战实际上是十九世纪小说手法的自然延伸——如果足够多的素材能够按照有时微妙但最终可以理解的原则（不仅包括因果关系，还包括同情和共情）进行组织和清晰的安排，那么社会就可以被彻底改造，变得更像一部小说——一个有组织、有联系、即使不更幸福，也更智慧的社会。恰当的艺术可以“修复”社会，而不当的艺术（这正是托尔斯泰愤怒的根源——他被不当的艺术所包围）只会损害社会。首先，他在庄园里与农民的接触，以及其他非上层阶级的“真正的俄罗斯人”的经历，使他确信，情欲，尤其是其他形式的贪婪、自私和残暴，其根源并非在于不变的人性，而在于社会制度和有害的观念——这与狄更斯和斯托夫人等许多十九世纪小说家的观点一脉相承，但托尔斯泰的视角比他们更偏向宗教，也更少实用主义。

Novelists after James and Tolstoy were shaped by their influence in several ways. In England, the next generation of novelists reacted strongly against James in a formal sense, constructing the modernist novel in contrast to the “traditional realist novel” (which was really more or less the novels of Henry James and his English contemporaries such as Arnold Bennett, since James had excluded the stranger characteristics of the novel represented by Dickens, Stowe, Melville, and the Brontës from the realm of true art), but they accepted his basic idea that the novel was, or could be, exclusive rather than inclusive, and that a novel without much popular appeal could do things artistically that a novel with popular appeal could not. They accepted his idea that the audience for a quality novel might not be large enough to support the author by means of commerce; this idea is a truism today, but it was new, and even revolutionary, for Virginia Woolf, James Joyce, and many of their contemporaries.

詹姆斯和托尔斯泰之后的作家在多个方面都受到了他们的影响。在英国，下一代小说家在形式上强烈反对詹姆斯，他们构建了现代主义小说，以此与“传统现实主义小说”（实际上，这或多或少指的是亨利·詹姆斯及其英国同时代作家，如阿诺德·贝内特的作品，因为詹姆斯将狄更斯、斯托夫人、梅尔维尔和勃朗特姐妹所代表的那些更奇特的小说特征排除在了真正艺术的范畴之外）形成对比。但他们接受了詹姆斯的基本观点，即小说是（或可以）具有排他性而非包容性，一部缺乏大众吸引力的小说在艺术上可以做到一部大众小说无法做到的事情。他们接受了詹姆斯的观点，即一部高质量小说的读者群可能不足以支撑作者的创作；这一观点在今天看来是老生常谈，但对于弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫、詹姆斯·乔伊斯以及他们的许多同时代作家来说，却是新颖的，甚至是革命性的。

The Bloomsbury group, which consisted of Virginia Woolf, her husband, Leonard; her sister, Vanessa, a painter; and several other essayists and intellectuals, was bohemian in a sense, but it was never low-class; Virginia's (and Leonard's) novel-writing was never considered less artistically innovative or respectable than the painting, criticism, and essay-writing of the others. The men of Bloomsbury were university-educated in the most socially accepted way; two generations earlier, they would have become clergymen. Thanks in part to the fact that Henry James set up and promoted a socially respectable form of the novel, they could now become intellectuals and artists. In addition, Virginia Woolf looked to her friends and relatives for inspiration. She observed and depicted them, as novelists have always done, but James's precepts gave her an added justification—she was creating art, something new and valuable that had never been thought of before and would be true in a way that previous novels had not been true. She was explicit about this in many essays, in particular “Mr. Bennett and Mrs. Brown,” which she revised several times. Her complaint against Arnold Bennett and his contemporaries, realist novelists all, was that they lose the sense of “life” and “human nature” by focusing too much on the materials of the set, on the “upholstery of the carriage”—in other words, that in the always restricted linear discipline of unfolding prose, they have devoted too many words to furniture and not enough to capturing sensations, especially momentary ones. She defends some of the techniques and effects of her contemporaries by claiming that awkwardness and discomfort are necessary corollaries to breaking free from old strictures. Of Ulysses , she points out, it “seems to me the conscious and calculated indecency of a desperate man who feels that in order to breathe he must break the windows.” But Woolf's attack in 1934 on Arnold Bennett was class-based, also. When he died, she encapsulated his life in her diary: “a shop keeper's view of literature; yet with the rudiments, covered over with fat and prosperity and the desire for hideous Empire furniture, of sensibility … I remember his determination to write 1000 words daily; and how he trotted off to do it that night.”

布卢姆斯伯里团体由弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫、她的丈夫伦纳德、她的妹妹瓦妮莎（一位画家）以及其他几位散文家和知识分子组成，从某种意义上说，他们是波西米亚式的，但绝非低俗之辈；弗吉尼亚（以及伦纳德）的小说创作从未被认为在艺术创新或体面程度上逊于其他成员的绘画、评论和散文创作。布卢姆斯伯里的成员都接受过当时社会认可的大学教育；如果放在两代人之前，他们很可能成为牧师。部分要归功于亨利·詹姆斯创立并推广了一种社会认可的小说形式，他们如今才能成为知识分子和艺术家。此外，弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫从她的朋友和亲戚身上汲取灵感。她观察并描绘他们，正如小说家们一直以来所做的那样，但詹姆斯的理念为她提供了额外的理由——她正在创作艺术，一种前所未有的、有价值的新事物，一种以以往小说所不具备的方式呈现的真实。她在许多文章中都明确表达了这一点，尤其是在她多次修改的《贝内特先生和布朗太太》一文中。她对阿诺德·贝内特及其同时代现实主义小说家的批评是，他们过于关注场景的物质性，关注“马车的内饰”，从而失去了对“生活”和“人性”的感知——换句话说，在叙事展开的线性结构中，他们用了太多的笔墨来描写家具，而忽略了捕捉感受，尤其是瞬间的感受。她为同时代作家的一些技巧和效果辩护，认为笨拙和不适是挣脱旧有束缚的必然结果。她指出，《尤利西斯》“在我看来，是一个绝望之人为了呼吸而不得不打破窗户的自觉而刻意的猥亵行为”。但伍尔夫在1934年对阿诺德·贝内特的抨击也带有阶级色彩。他去世后，她在日记中概括了他的一生：“他对文学的看法就像一个店主；然而，他身上却有着敏锐的感知力，只是被肥胖、富裕和对丑陋的帝国风格家具的渴望所掩盖……我记得他决心每天写 1000 字；以及那天晚上他是如何小跑着去写作的。”

For Woolf and her contemporaries, James's imprimatur of “art” and the privacy and status of uncommerciality allowed them to explore what the middle class—the great audience of Dickens and many other Victorian novelists—considered to be uninteresting but also immoral topics. Of course, it is every novelist's claim, standard at least from the days of Marguerite de Navarre, that what is “novel” in his or her work is also important to the true understanding of human nature; it worked in the 1920s to allow a new class of writers with a different set of values and interests into the hitherto popular realm of the novel, and it also worked to promote the artificial bifurcation of the novel into more prestigious “critical successes” and less prestigious “popular successes.” It worked, in fact, just the same way for novelists from the educated classes as it always had for other excluded groups, expanding the subject matter, the style, the tone, and the audience for the novel as a form.

对于伍尔夫和她的同时代作家而言，詹姆斯对“艺术”的认可，以及非商业性的私密性和地位，使他们得以探索中产阶级——狄更斯和许多其他维多利亚时代小说家的主要读者群——认为既乏味又不道德的话题。当然，至少从玛格丽特·德·纳瓦尔时代起，每位小说家都声称，作品中的“新颖”之处对于真正理解人性也至关重要；这种说法在20世纪20年代奏效，它使得一批拥有不同价值观和兴趣的新兴作家得以进入此前以大众为主的小说领域，同时也促成了小说人为的二元划分：更具声望的“评论界成功之作”和声望较低的“大众成功之作”。事实上，这种做法对于受过教育阶层的小说家来说，与以往对其他被排斥群体一样有效，它拓展了小说这一文体的主题、风格、基调和读者群体。

For the rest of the twentieth century, novelists, readers, and critics continued to argue about what was artful in the novel, but they accepted James's premise that some novels were art, and other, more commercial ones, were not. E. M. Forster, who was a contemporary of Woolf and Joyce, wrote a book called Aspects of the Novel that takes up the issue of “What Is Art?” and addresses James specifically on the subject of form. Forster's witty, benign style is especially generous in some ways— Aspects of the Novel has held up over the years because it doesn't seem like merely an advertisement for Forster's own work— but his criticism of James is pointed. After a lengthy appreciation of James's own favorite novel, The Ambassadors , Forster remarks, “The beauty that suffuses The Ambassadors is the reward due to a fine artist for hard work…. Success to the full extent of his possibilities has crowned him. The pattern has woven itself with modulation and reservations Anatole France will never attain. Woven itself wonderfully. But at what a sacrifice!” (p. 159 ). What most readers object to, according to Forster, is not the difficulty of the prose, but the fact that “they cannot grant his premise, which is that most of human life has to disappear before he can do us a novel” (p. 160 ). What Forster objects to is the subjection of the novel's natural profusion to the rigors of a structure that is evident to the reader's sensibility, to what is required so the reader will stop thinking of a novel as life (which is disorganized and chock-full of uncontrollable developments) and start thinking of it as art, which is conscious of itself at all times. Forster proposes that the novelist in search of artfulness substitute the model of music for the model of painting, and that he attempt to attain a kind of internal pattern analogous to rhythm. He uses In Search of Lost Time as his example. When Proust repeats certain ideas and themes in his four-thousand-page novel, they constitute a “lovely waxing and waning” whose effect is “to fill us with surprise and freshness and hope.” The huge French novel is not asked to limit itself and fix itself inside a structure, “and yet it hangs together because it is stitched internally” (p. 165 ). Unfortunately for his argument, Forster does not point out in contrasting The Ambassadors with In Search of Lost Time that the former is written in James's customary third-person limited point of view, while the latter is written in an absolutely unashamed first-person point of view, which allows Proust the freedom to digress and yet remain within the consistent voice of a single consciousness. Consistency is Proust's default setting (as it is the default setting of every first-person narrator), so “developments” enliven the narrative but never disrupt it. Whether artistic “rhythm” can be achieved in a novel written in the third person is a question Forster's own novel A Passage to India sheds light upon (see below). Needless to say, though, from the perspective of Tolstoy's argument, In Search of Lost Time only compounds the problems of art as both immoral and exclusive.

在二十世纪余下的时间里，小说家、读者和评论家们继续争论小说中何为艺术，但他们接受了詹姆斯的前提：有些小说是艺术，而另一些更偏商业化的小说则不是。与伍尔夫和乔伊斯同时代的E·M·福斯特写了一本书，名为《小说面面观》，探讨了“何为艺术？”这一问题，并专门就形式问题与詹姆斯展开了辩论。福斯特诙谐而温和的文风在某些方面尤其慷慨——《小说面面观》之所以经久不衰，正是因为它并非仅仅是对福斯特自身作品的宣传——但他对詹姆斯的批评却十分尖锐。在对詹姆斯最喜爱的长篇小说《大使们》进行了一番详尽的赏析之后，福斯特评论道：“《大使们》中弥漫的美，是一位优秀艺术家辛勤耕耘应得的回报……他已臻于完美，达到了他所能达到的巅峰。这部作品的格局精妙绝伦，韵味悠长，连阿纳托尔·法朗士都难以企及。它如此精妙绝伦，但代价又是多么巨大啊！”（第159页）。福斯特认为，大多数读者反对的并非其晦涩难懂的文风，而是“他们无法接受他的前提，即在创作小说之前，人类生活的大部分必须消失”（第160页）。福斯特反对的是将小说自然而然的丰富性屈从于读者感官所能感知的严苛结构，屈从于某种要求，以使读者不再将小说视为生活（生活杂乱无章，充满不可控的发展），而是将其视为艺术——一种始终具有自我意识的艺术。福斯特提出，追求艺术性的小说家应以音乐模式取代绘画模式，并尝试获得一种类似于节奏的内在模式。他以《追忆似水年华》为例。普鲁斯特在其四千页的巨著中反复出现某些思想和主题，构成了一种“优美的起伏变化”，其效果是“让我们充满惊喜、新鲜感和希望”。这部鸿篇巨制的法国小说无需限制自身，也无需拘泥于某种结构，“然而它却能浑然一体，因为它内部结构严密”（第165页）。不幸的是，福斯特在对比《大使》和《追忆似水年华》时，并未指出前者采用的是詹姆斯惯用的第三人称有限视角，而后者则完全采用第一人称视角，这使得普鲁斯特可以自由地展开叙述，同时又能保持单一意识的连贯性。连贯性是普鲁斯特的默认设置（也是所有第一人称叙述者的默认设置），因此“发展”能够丰富叙事，却不会破坏叙事的连贯性。至于第三人称小说是否也能达到艺术的“节奏”，福斯特自己的小说《印度之行》对此有所阐述（见下文）。然而，毋庸置疑，从托尔斯泰的论点来看，《追忆似水年华》只会加剧艺术既不道德又排他性的困境。

Fortunately for us, all four of our theorists of art in the novel put their theories to the test by writing novels as they thought novels should be written. What we have to learn from looking at their works is not that one or the other had a better or worse theory, but that the form of the novel was in many ways too powerful or too intransigent to be subdued by a mere theory. If we consider A Passage to India in light of Forster's admiration of Proust, we see that the novel is Proustian in the sense that all relationships depicted in the novel are personal, and all betrayals are personal, too, as in Proust. When the scene of these relationships and betrayals is transposed from France to India, though, and the characters must relate across highly charged boundaries of race and class, Forster's political insights into Anglo India become profound, and the novel almost unbearably poignant. The primary “rhythmical” feature is the enigmatic Professor Godbole, who appears in several of the scenes, sometimes as a friendly figure, who is always kindly and well-disposed, but sometimes as an unfriendly figure, who hampers the plans of the protagonists; in the end, he is neutral, as if divine. Nevertheless, the “rhythm” of In Search of Lost Time and of A Passage to India is not what makes each novel memorable—it is rather the intelligence and insight of each narrative consciousness. Proust could employ all sorts of subtle patterning devices, but if his remarks were not regularly arresting and his metaphors not original and apt, the novel would just seem gassy and pretentious. If Forster were not truly interested in the inner life of Aziz, were not authentically empathetic with him and the other characters, A Passage to India would be just another example of colonial novelizing. Furthermore, Forster accepts, at least implicitly, the nature of the novel as a social document—he doesn't shrink at all from depicting particular customs among particular people at a particular historic juncture—he doesn't find them fleeting or peripheral, he finds them interesting and worth carefully describing. The effect, in 2005 , is to give A Passage to India currency. By acknowledging its own specificity and depicting, without overt political theories, a plethora of personal relationships—that is, because it beautifully exploits characteristics natural to the novel as a form— A Passage to India seems less dated and more insightful than many other novels of its day.

幸运的是，这四位小说艺术理论家都以自己的方式实践了他们的理论，创作出了他们心目中理想的小说。我们从他们的作品中学到的并非谁的理论更好或更差，而是小说这种形式在很多方面都过于强大或难以驾驭，以至于任何理论都无法将其征服。如果我们从福斯特对普鲁斯特的推崇角度来解读《印度之行》，就会发现这部小说具有普鲁斯特式的特质：小说中描绘的所有关系都是私人的，所有的背叛也都是私人的，正如普鲁斯特的作品一样。然而，当这些关系和背叛的场景从法国转移到印度，当人物必须跨越种族和阶级的重重界限时，福斯特对英属印度的政治洞察便变得深刻起来，这部小说也变得几乎令人难以承受地凄美动人。主要的“节奏”特征是神秘的戈德博勒教授，他在多个场景中出现，有时以友善的形象示人，总是和蔼可亲；有时又以不友善的形象出现，阻挠主人公们的计划；最终，他保持中立，仿佛神明一般。然而，《追忆似水年华》和《印度之行》之所以令人难忘，并非在于它们的“节奏”，而是各自叙事意识的智慧和洞察力。普鲁斯特可以运用各种精妙的叙事手法，但如果他的论述不够引人入胜，比喻不够新颖贴切，那么这部小说就会显得空洞浮夸、矫揉造作。如果福斯特没有真正关注阿齐兹的内心世界，没有真正理解他和其他人物的感受，《印度之行》就只不过是又一部殖民主义小说而已。此外，福斯特至少在潜意识里接受了小说作为社会文献的本质——他毫不避讳地描绘特定历史时期特定人群的特定习俗——他并不认为这些习俗转瞬即逝或无关紧要，而是认为它们引人入胜，值得细致刻画。在2005年，这使得《印度之行》焕发了新的生命力。它承认自身的特殊性，并在不涉及明显政治理论的情况下，描绘了丰富的人际关系——也就是说，因为它巧妙地运用了小说这种形式固有的特征——《印度之行》比同时期的许多其他小说更不显过时，也更具洞察力。

∗ For plot synopses of A Passage to India and Anna Karenina , readers unfamiliar with those works may consult the section “A Hundred Novels” in the latter part of this book.

* 对于《印度之行》和《安娜·卡列尼娜》的情节概要，不熟悉这两部作品的读者可以参考本书后半部分的“一百部小说”章节。

To the Lighthouse , written three years after A Passage to India , offers an interesting paradox. Woolf divides the novel into three sections.
