There are intermediate steps between Lazarillo de Tormes and Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant , too. Let's say they are Don Quixote (in which the opinions of a peasant, Sancho, are given as much space as the opinions of his master), Roxana (in which practical methods of daily economic survival are detailed), Humphry Clinker (in which the points of view of servants are depicted along with those of masters, in the different styles natural to each character), and Jane Eyre (in which the impoverished working woman gets to observe and judge everyone around her), Thrse Raquin (in which the inner lives of entirely ordinary and venal characters are anatomized because they are ordinary, not in spite of it), Main Street (in which the geographic diversity of the novel is expanded to include characters outside the cultural center), and Ulysses (in which the most grand and elegant narrative methods are applied to an ordinary day). After Ulysses , we have The Man Who Loved Children (in which high drama is made of an ordinary family) and The Moonflower Vine (in which the inner lives of characters who not only think of themselves as ordinary, but are proud to be ordinary, are juxtaposed in a manner that reveals how dramatic each character really considers his fate to be). Just as the line of descent from The Decameron to Lovely Green Eyes has altered the social and psychological nature of women, the line from Lazarillo to Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant has transformed the identity of average citizens, women and men.

在《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》和《思乡餐厅的晚餐》之间，也存在一些中间阶段的作品。例如，《堂吉诃德》（其中农民桑丘的观点与他主人的观点一样占据了同等的篇幅）、《罗克萨娜》（其中详细描述了日常生活中实用的经济生存方法）、《汉弗莱·克林克》（其中仆人和主人的观点以各自独特的风格并置描绘）、《简·爱》（其中贫困的劳动妇女得以观察和评判她周围的每一个人）、《特蕾莎·拉金》（其中对完全平凡且贪婪的人物的内心世界进行了剖析，正是因为他们平凡，而不是尽管平凡）、《大街》（其中小说的地理范围扩大到包括文化中心以外的人物）以及《尤利西斯》（其中将最宏大、最优雅的叙事手法应用于一个普通的一天）。在《尤利西斯》之后，我们有了《爱孩子的男人》（这部作品将一个普通家庭的悲剧演绎得淋漓尽致）和《月光花藤》（这部作品将那些不仅自认为平凡，而且以平凡为荣的角色的内心世界进行对比，揭示了每个角色对自己命运的真实感受）。正如从《十日谈》到《美丽的绿眼睛》的传承改变了女性的社会和心理特征一样，从《拉撒路》到《思乡餐厅的晚餐》的传承也改变了普通民众，无论男女的身份认同。

But identity—Who am I?—is a political as well as a personal question, and as the form of the novel spread around the world in the twentieth century, successive generations of novelists answered it in more and more complex and dramatic political terms: at first I am English, but later I am Russian, I am Austro-Hungarian, I am American, I am Irish (but a speaker of English), but later, I am an Italian speaker in Trieste; I am bilingual (standard English/Mississippi English, Russian/ English, English/French, Farsi/English), I am Vietnamese and French, I am Korean-Japanese-American, I am Mexican-American—the novel takes as its very premise that identity is point of view and language functioning together, simultaneously.

但身份——我是谁？——既是一个政治问题，也是一个个人问题。随着小说这种形式在二十世纪传播到世界各地，一代又一代的小说家以越来越复杂和戏剧化的政治术语来回答这个问题：起初我是英国人，但后来我是俄罗斯人，我是奥匈帝国人，我是美国人，我是爱尔兰人（但说英语），但后来我又成了的里雅斯特的意大利语使用者；我是双语者（标准英语/密西西比英语、俄语/英语、英语/法语、波斯语/英语），我是越南人和法国人，我是韩裔日裔美国人，我是墨西哥裔美国人——小说的根本前提是，身份是视角和语言同时发挥作用的体现。

As each national literature has appropriated the form of the novel, it has taken up different concerns—worries about ill-conceived marriages crossing boundaries of social class, for example, are not as prominent a part of nineteenth-century Russian novels as of nineteenth-century English novels, but exactly who is English and who isn't is not as central a theme in English novels as exactly who is Russian is a theme of Russian novels. The ubiquity of state authority is not as much a concern of American novels as of German ones, but the attractions of outlawry are not as much a feature of German novels as of American ones. The conflicts between romance and marriage are not of such overriding importance in Scandinavian novels as they are in French novels; in Scandinavian novels everyone works, every day, no matter what his or her status, while in English and French novels, members of certain classes have too much time on their hands. But even though national literatures have their common dramatic characteristics, at the same time that a novelist appears to readers to be declaring, for example, “I am Russian,” to himself he is saying, “I may be Russian, but…” He cannot help distinguishing himself from the Russians around him. A feature of this sense of distinctiveness that the novel cultivates in both readers and writers is that many authors have been quite self-conscious about importing the form of the novel as a way of either revealing their own cultures to the world or of improving their own cultures by making them more cosmopolitan. Naguib Mahfouz, for example, experimented with using traditional Middle Eastern tale-telling forms in The Harafish , but wrote his most famous work, The Cairo Trilogy , in the realistic mode of some of the European novelists he admired, such as Balzac. Junichiro Tanizaki was influenced by the great nineteenth-century Russian novelists, as is evident in the realistic style and epic scope of The Makioka Sisters; he also translated The Picture of Dorian Gray into Japanese and wrote a short story on a similar theme, about a woman who is transformed by a mysterious tattoo. Inspired by The Tale of Genji after moving from Tokyo to Osaka, though, he wrote a historical novel about the sixteenth century, The Secret History of the Lord of Musashi.

各国文学对小说形式的运用各有不同，关注的主题也各有侧重——例如，对于跨越社会阶层的不明智婚姻的担忧，在十九世纪的俄国小说中远不如在十九世纪的英国小说中那样突出；但究竟谁是英国人、谁不是英国人，在英国小说中也并非像究竟谁是俄国人那样是核心主题。国家权威的无处不在在美国小说中不如在德国小说中那样受关注，但亡命之徒的诱惑力在德国小说中也远不如在美国小说中那么显著。爱情与婚姻之间的冲突在斯堪的纳维亚小说中远不如在法国小说中那样重要；在斯堪的纳维亚小说中，无论社会地位如何，每个人都每天工作，而在英国和法国小说中，某些阶层的人却拥有过多的空闲时间。尽管民族文学具有共同的戏剧特征，但当小说家在读者面前宣称“我是俄罗斯人”时，他内心却在说“我或许是俄罗斯人，但是……”他无法避免将自己与周围的俄罗斯人区分开来。小说在读者和作家心中培养的这种独特性，体现在许多作家都非常自觉地借鉴小说形式，以此向世界展现自身文化，或通过使其更具国际化来提升自身文化。例如，纳吉布·马哈福兹在《哈拉菲什》中尝试运用传统的中东叙事形式，但他最著名的作品《开罗三部曲》却采用了他所敬仰的欧洲小说家（如巴尔扎克）的现实主义风格。谷崎润一郎也深受十九世纪俄罗斯伟大小说家的影响，这一点在其作品《细冈姐妹》的现实主义风格和史诗般的格局中显而易见。他还把《道林·格雷的画像》翻译成日语，并创作了一篇题材相似的短篇小说，讲述一位女子因神秘纹身而发生改变的故事。然而，在从东京搬到大阪后，他受到《源氏物语》的启发，创作了一部以十六世纪为背景的历史小说《宫本武藏秘史》。

Every national literature grows through an accumulation of specific individualities that coexist within the general impression the reader infers from different novels. The readiness of the novel to take up issues of identity has helped spread the form around the world, because readers and writers of novels are always asking, “Who are you? Are you like me? Are you different from me?” Both of these latter questions are to be answered with a yes, which, of course, like all equivocal answers, leads readers and writers to seek more and more evidence. And just as the novel has encouraged readers to think they can contemplate their own marriages and decide whether to do something about them, and has thereby changed the place of marriage in many cultures, it also encourages readers to think they can identify themselves on their own, to explore and know their own natures. It encourages them to think that such an exploration at length—even, say, at the length of Marcel Proust's In Search of Lost Time —is a possible as well as a worthy endeavor. Robinson Crusoe's and Roxana's justification for speaking of themselves, that they have sins on their consciences, ceased to be necessary after two hundred years of novels. M.'s four thousand pages of introspection need no preliminary excuse, only the ongoing justification of being intelligent and well-written enough to reward the act of reading. As we look around the world at the beginning of the twenty-first century, we can see that questions of identity dominate political discourse in the same way that questions about marriage (and about whether women are agents or objects) dominate personal discourse.

每一种民族文学的成长都源于特定个性的积累，这些个性与读者从不同小说中推断出的整体印象并存。小说乐于探讨身份认同问题，这促进了其在全球的传播，因为小说读者和作者总是会问自己：“你是谁？你像我吗？你与我不同吗？”后两个问题的答案都是肯定的，而这当然像所有模棱两可的答案一样，会促使读者和作者寻求更多的证据。正如小说鼓励读者思考自己的婚姻，并决定是否采取行动，从而改变了婚姻在许多文化中的地位一样，它也鼓励读者思考如何独立地认识自我，探索和了解自己的本性。它鼓励读者认为，这种深入的探索——即使像马塞尔·普鲁斯特的《追忆似水年华》那样详尽——也是可能且值得的。鲁滨逊·克鲁索和罗克珊娜为自己辩解的理由——他们良心有愧——在两百年的小说发展之后已不再必要。M.四千页的内省之作无需任何先入为主的解释，只需不断地证明其文笔精湛、思想深刻，足以令人读来回味无穷。当我们环顾二十一世纪初的世界，便会发现，身份认同问题主导着政治话语，正如婚姻问题（以及女性是主体还是客体）主导着个人话语一样。

The novel in the twentieth century contradicted the separate reductionisms of both science and social conformity. That Proust should have considered himself worthy of so many words is in some sense less surprising than that he should have considered so detailed an introspection possible. Science, in the persons of Freud or Heisenberg (whose principle it was that the introduction of the measuring instrument itself changes the nature of the thing to be measured), would have discounted the value of Proust's efforts had he consulted them. But the novelist and his protagonist are never simply part of a statistical sample, small or large. Every word in its expression of the act of choice and in its distinctiveness from every word that other novelists have chosen to depict similar situations resists any attempt to dissolve the novelist, his protagonist, and his ideas into a larger context. At the same time, the tendency of the novel to expand and of all its parts to proliferate tends to emphasize the particular, leaving the general to be implied. Novelists and their protagonists may act according to general patterns as commonly as fruit flies do, but the burgeoning particulars of every novel dazzle the senses, mask the general patterns, and train the reader to pay attention to differences. What scientists and politicians (and religious leaders) promulgated throughout the twentieth century—that most people are more or less alike, that citizens should conform to certain roles, that certain beliefs are essential to a virtuous life or ultimate salvation—the novel itself could not go along with, whatever the professed beliefs of the novelist as citizen. And the novel requires no license or certification, only desire. The novel asserts that an ordinary person, with steady application, can become an expert upon who he himself really is simply by writing it down in his own unique style. At the end of Zeno's Conscience , for example, Zeno explicitly rejects psychoanalysis in favor of what he has learned in the course of writing his memoirs about being himself. His quirks are his identity; he doesn't wish to be cured of them.

二十世纪的小说反驳了科学和社会规范各自独立的还原论。普鲁斯特认为自己配得上如此多的文字，这在某种意义上并不令人惊讶，更令人惊讶的是他竟然认为如此细致的内省是可能的。如果普鲁斯特咨询弗洛伊德或海森堡（他们的原则是，测量工具的引入本身就改变了被测量对象的性质），科学界肯定会轻视他的努力。但小说家及其主人公绝非仅仅是统计样本的一部分，无论样本大小。每一个字，无论其表达的是选择的行为，还是与其他小说家用来描绘类似情境的词语截然不同，都抵制着将小说家、他的主人公及其思想融入更大语境的任何尝试。与此同时，小说不断扩展的趋势以及其各个组成部分不断增殖的特性，往往强调特殊性，而将普遍性留给隐喻。小说家及其主人公的行为或许像果蝇一样遵循着普遍的模式，但每部小说中不断涌现的细节却能令人眼花缭乱，掩盖普遍模式，并训练读者关注差异。二十世纪科学家、政治家（以及宗教领袖）所宣扬的——大多数人或多或少都相似，公民应该遵守某些角色，某些信仰对于美德生活或最终救赎至关重要——无论小说家作为公民所宣称的信仰如何，小说本身都无法与之相符。小说不需要任何执照或认证，只需要渴望。小说断言，一个普通人，只要持之以恒地练习，就能通过用自己独特的风格将自己写下来，成为真正了解自己的专家。例如，在《芝诺的良心》结尾，芝诺明确地拒绝了精神分析，转而支持他在撰写关于自我的回忆录过程中所学到的东西。他的怪癖就是他的身份；他不想治愈这些疾病。

In the twentieth century, the pressure to conform came from all sides. If the government was a theocracy, as in Azar Nafisi's Iran, for example, then it was a revolutionary act to read Pride and Prejudice If the government is a corporatocracy, as the U.S. government is now, then reading Edward Abbey's novel about a gang of violent saboteurs, The Monkey Wrench Gang , is an act of resistance. If the government was a workers’ republic, such as China in the 1960s , then reading any Western novel was dangerous. If entrenched power rests upon notions of the inherent inferiority of a single group, as in Hurston's American South, then Their Eyes Were Watching God is insurrectionary. But for the novel, the insurrection in all cases does not lie with the idea that a different ruling group will be substituted for the old one; it lies with the idea that individuals will be freed from the most onerous impositions of rule itself and allowed to identify themselves and act on their own identities. This tension exists between the protagonist and any group. The protagonist of a novel makes up his own mind about every norm, situates himself in relationship to every group. The history of the twentieth century, a century of constant movement and change, of shifting boundaries of all sorts, including but not limited to racial, ethnic, geographical, moral, political, economic, and religious, placed a burden upon every thinking person to define and situate himself or herself, if only to attain what every protagonist desires, a sense of oneself as an actor in the plot, with a defined, logical, and justified moral position, a sense that the action of the plot has a meaning, and a sense that the outcome of the plot is understandable. The popularity of the novel was a response to this burden.

在二十世纪，来自四面八方的压力迫使人们顺从。如果政府是神权政治，例如阿扎尔·纳菲西笔下的伊朗，那么阅读《傲慢与偏见》就是一种革命行为。如果政府是企业政治，例如如今的美国政府，那么阅读爱德华·艾比关于一群暴力破坏分子的小说《猴子扳手帮》就是一种抵抗行为。如果政府是工人共和国，例如20世纪60年代的中国，那么阅读任何西方小说都是危险的。如果根深蒂固的权力建立在对某个群体固有劣等性的观念之上，例如赫斯顿笔下的美国南方，那么阅读《他们的眼睛望着上帝》就是一种起义。但就这部小说而言，起义在所有情况下都不在于用另一个统治集团取代旧的统治集团；它的核心在于，个人将摆脱最繁重的规则束缚，得以认同自我，并依循自身身份行事。这种张力存在于主人公与任何群体之间。小说主人公对每一种规范都有自己的判断，并将自身置于与每个群体的关系之中。二十世纪的历史，一个不断运动和变革的世纪，各种界限不断变化，包括但不限于种族、民族、地理、道德、政治、经济和宗教界限，这给每一个有思想的人都带来了一种负担：定义和定位自身，哪怕仅仅是为了达到每个主人公所渴望的境界——一种作为情节参与者的自我意识，拥有明确、合乎逻辑且合理的道德立场，一种情节行动具有意义的感知，以及一种情节结局可以理解的感知。小说的流行正是对这种负担的回应。

∗ See Azar Nafisi, Reading Lolita in Tehran (New York: Random House, 2003 ) p. 347 .

* 参见 Azar Nafisi，《在德黑兰阅读洛丽塔》（纽约：兰登书屋，2003 年）第 347 页。

Some twentieth-century novels did challenge the idea of freedom and personal agency, but the only way the novel can do so is by showing that a point of view is determined by outside forces. Such is the thrust of Kafka's The Trial and other Kafka works. Part of the shock of reading Kafka after reading other novels is the profound sense his protagonists have of being restricted and trapped, unable to reach a conclusion about who they are and what is meaningful. Sometimes the trap is literal—in “The Burrow,” the burrowing creature is always occupied in repairing and improving the burrow that protects but also constricts him. In “The Metamorphosis,” the mind of a man is trapped in the body of a bug. In The Trial , Josef K.'s trap may be real and bureaucratic or it may be self-imposed by obsessive anxieties. In each case the simplicity of Kafka's use of the tale form reinforces the sense of restriction—the sequence of events is all. It is arbitrary and may have no meaning but it is inexorable, and the protagonist's point of view is there only to register and record it. In some sense, he is too disoriented by events to have an opinion about them and so he can't learn from them and his feelings about them have an automatic and rather animal quality. His point of view is reduced to a series of reactions. Hermann Broch, in The Sleepwalkers , is as suspicious as Kafka of freedom, but the problem his characters have is not that they have no freedom, rather that a sense of freedom is pathological and inevitably leads to cruelty. But Kafka was born in 1883 and Broch in 1886 ; they were not twentieth-century men in some sense. Paradoxically, the effect of their work upon the twentieth century was, like that of The Good Soldier , to demonstrate that sense could be made of senseless events. At the end of the twentieth century, Kafka's and Broch's heirs, novelists who write about the horrors of history, such as Arnost Lustig (the Holocaust), Chang-rae Lee (Japanese use of torture in World War II), and Kate Atkinson (combat in both world wars), tend to demonstrate faith in logic and meaning in spite of the scenes depicted. These writers are much more likely than Kafka to construct plots in which freedom can be felt, understood, accepted, and controlled as long as the protagonist can ponder his identity and understand the nature of his connection to the group. The underlying assertion of almost every novel is that meaning exists and can be understood because it can be arranged in a sequence that then takes on some sort of logic. As a result, late twentieth-century novelists seem to find meaning in even the most meaningless and brutal circumstances in part because the early twentieth-century modernists had shown them how to do so—Josef K.'s experiences may be meaningless or at least inscrutable, but at the end of Guided Tours of Hell and Three Pigs in Five Days , Francine Prose's protagonists, who share a third-person limited point of view with Josef K., as well as his sense of smallness, restriction, and self-absorption, do not have to suffer terminal meaninglessness. Their perplexity might be but an intermediate step to future understanding. As long as they don't die, narrative itself holds out the hope that they will figure things out and learn something.

二十世纪的一些小说确实挑战了自由和个人能动性的概念，但小说能够做到这一点的唯一途径是展现视角是由外力决定的。卡夫卡的《审判》和其他作品正是如此。读过其他小说之后再读卡夫卡，部分原因在于他笔下的主人公深刻感受到被束缚和困住，无法对自身身份和意义做出判断。有时，这种束缚是字面意义上的——在《地洞》中，掘地生物总是忙于修缮和完善既保护自己又限制自己的地洞；在《变形记》中，人的思想被困在昆虫的身体里；在《审判》中，约瑟夫·K的困境可能是真实存在的官僚主义陷阱，也可能是他因执念而自我设限。在每一种情况下，卡夫卡对故事形式的简洁运用都强化了这种束缚感——事件的顺序就是一切。它是任意的，或许毫无意义，但却不可阻挡，主人公的视角仅仅是为了记录和呈现它。某种程度上，他被事件搞得晕头转向，以至于无法对它们发表意见，因此他无法从中吸取教训，他对事件的感受也带有一种自动的、近乎动物性的特质。他的视角被简化为一系列反应。赫尔曼·布洛赫在《梦游者》中，像卡夫卡一样对自由抱有怀疑，但他笔下人物的问题不在于他们缺乏自由，而在于自由感本身就是一种病态，并且必然导致残酷。然而，卡夫卡生于1883年，布洛赫生于1886年；从某种意义上说，他们并非二十世纪的人。矛盾的是，他们的作品对二十世纪的影响，如同《好兵》一样，在于证明了人们可以从看似毫无意义的事件中解读出意义。在二十世纪末，卡夫卡和布洛赫的继承者们，如描写历史恐怖的小说家，如阿诺斯特·卢斯蒂格（描写大屠杀）、李昌来（描写二战期间日军的酷刑）和凯特·阿特金森（描写两次世界大战的战斗），尽管描绘的场景令人触目惊心，却往往展现出对逻辑和意义的信仰。与卡夫卡相比，这些作家更倾向于构建这样的情节：只要主人公能够思考自身的身份，理解自身与群体之间的联系，自由便能够被感知、理解、接受和掌控。几乎每一部小说的潜在论断是：意义之所以存在且可以被理解，是因为它可以被排列成某种逻辑序列。因此，二十世纪后期的小说家似乎总能在最无意义、最残酷的境遇中找到意义，部分原因在于二十世纪早期的现代主义者已经向他们展示了如何做到这一点——约瑟夫·K的经历或许毫无意义，或者至少令人费解，但在《地狱导览》和《五日三猪》的结尾，弗朗辛·普罗斯笔下的主人公们，与约瑟夫·K一样拥有第三人称有限视角，也同样感受到自身的渺小、受限和自我沉溺，却不必承受最终的虚无。他们的困惑或许只是通往未来理解的中间步骤。只要他们不死去，叙事本身就蕴含着希望，他们终将解开谜团，有所领悟。

At the beginning of the twenty-first century, issues of identity are combining with mass communications, high-speed travel, and accelerated resource consumption to engender what seems to be a new phase of history, but questions raised in my hundred novels remain intractably current. In the summer of 2003 I happened to go to Scotland at about the time a Scottish newspaper did a survey of the Scottish novels Scotsmen considered great. At the top of the list was James Hogg's The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner , which I had never heard of. Sir Walter Scott, whose statue was on Prince's Street, was not on the list at all. Hogg's book was almost two hundred years old, but it had an uncanny currency in a time when the U.S. president was saying that he had invaded a foreign country because God told him to do so. I learned from the novel that in certain seventeenth-century Scottish evangelical sects, the inner assurance that one had received God's grace was thought to lead to all sorts of destructive actions. I learned that this feature of “antinomianism” has dogged certain branches of Protestantism from the beginning. As I read about Hogg's “memoirist” Robert Wringham and his familiar tempter, I could not stop thinking about George Bush and Dick Cheney. I saw that the deadly seriousness of religious controversy in the United States perhaps owes more to our Scottish heritage than to our English heritage.

二十一世纪初，身份认同问题与大众传播、高速旅行和资源消耗的加速交织在一起，似乎催生了一个全新的历史阶段，但我一百部小说中提出的问题却依然具有难以回避的现实意义。2003年夏天，我恰巧去了一趟苏格兰，当时一家苏格兰报纸做了一项调查，评选苏格兰人心目中的伟大苏格兰小说。榜首是詹姆斯·霍格的《一个正义罪人的私人回忆录与忏悔录》，我之前从未听说过这本书。沃尔特·斯科特爵士的雕像矗立在王子街上，却完全不在榜单之列。霍格的这本书出版至今已有近两百年，但在美国总统声称他入侵他国是因为上帝指示他这么做的那个时代，它却有着一种不可思议的现实意义。我从小说中了解到，在十七世纪苏格兰某些福音派教派中，人们认为内心确信自己已蒙受上帝恩典会导致各种破坏性行为。我还了解到，这种“反律主义”的特征从一开始就困扰着某些新教分支。读到霍格笔下的“回忆录作者”罗伯特·林厄姆和他熟悉的诱惑者时，我不禁想起乔治·布什和迪克·切尼。我意识到，美国宗教争论的严重性或许更多地源于我们的苏格兰传统，而非英格兰传统。

A few months later, I read Garrison Keillor's WLT: A Radio Romance , about a fictional Minneapolis radio station on which the homely, wholesome programs broadcast are belied by the backbiting, greed, lust, hypocrisy, and shamelessness that are the constants of life at the station. I recognized Keillor's theme—that the media reduce every idea and pleasure to an advertising gimmick and a lie and prosper by doing so. The darkness of Keillor's vision, which was surprising and a little off-putting when the novel first came out in 1992 , seemed prescient and all the more current during the election season of 2004 , when lies and spin were the order of the day. I found it difficult but compelling to read Rohinton Mistry's A Fine Balance , about the 1975 state of emergency in India, when, according to the novel, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi cheated in the elections, threw the opposition in jail, and retroactively changed election laws. Mistry's very clear and eloquent evocation of the lives of his four obscure and representative characters seemed both lively and hopeless in some way—their individual ambitions and desires are so paltry in the face of not only habit, culture, and oppression, but also population pressure, economic realities, and disorganization. I was fascinated and a little bit horrified by Jennifer Egan's 2001 novel Look at Me , which not only straightforwardly addresses the nature of identity in a world dominated by big money, big media, good intentions, mind-altering substances, and the Internet, but also peers into the inner life of a believable terrorist hiding in Rockford, Illinois. I thought of Justine when I read in The Guardian about a French serial killer who said he went hunting for virgins twice a year. And when I read about the banning of religious symbols, especially the head scarf, in French public schools, and about honor killings of Muslim women living in Europe, I thought of The Heptameron , which is a catalog of honor dilemmas in which many women are killed.

几个月后，我读了加里森·凯勒的《WLT：广播罗曼史》。小说讲述了一个虚构的明尼阿波利斯广播电台的故事。电台里播放的节目看似温馨健康，实则充斥着背后议论、贪婪、色欲、虚伪和无耻，这些都是电台生活的常态。我认出了凯勒的主题——媒体将一切想法和乐趣都简化成广告噱头和谎言，并以此牟利。凯勒笔下阴暗的景象，在1992年小说初版时，着实令人惊讶，甚至有些反感。但在2004年的选举季，谎言和舆论操纵盛行之时，这种阴暗的景象显得格外具有预见性，也更具现实意义。罗欣顿·米斯特里的《微妙的平衡》讲述了1975年印度的紧急状态，小说中，总理英迪拉·甘地在选举中作弊，将反对派投入监狱，并追溯性地修改了选举法。阅读这本书的过程既艰难又引人入胜。米斯特里对四个默默无闻却又极具代表性的人物的刻画清晰而富有感染力，既生动又令人感到某种程度上的绝望——面对习俗、文化和压迫，以及人口压力、经济现实和混乱的社会，他们的个人抱负和愿望显得如此渺小。詹妮弗·伊根2001年的小说《看看我》让我既着迷又有些恐惧。这部小说不仅直白地探讨了在一个被巨额资金、大型媒体、善意、精神药物和互联网主导的世界中身份认同的本质，还深入剖析了一个藏身于伊利诺伊州罗克福德的、令人信服的恐怖分子的内心世界。我在《卫报》上读到一篇关于一位法国连环杀手的文章，他声称自己每年两次猎杀处女，这让我想到了贾斯汀。当我读到法国公立学校禁止宗教标志（尤其是头巾）以及欧洲穆斯林妇女因荣誉谋杀而丧命的新闻时，我想起了《七日谈》，这是一部记录荣誉困境的著作，其中许多妇女因此丧命。

In the course of 650 years, Boccaccio and his successors have helped to create a certain kind of world. It is a world not unlike the novel, a world that seems to many people transparent and automatic but isn't.

在650年的时间里，薄伽丘和他的后继者们共同创造了一种独特的世界。这个世界与小说中的世界颇为相似，在许多人看来，这个世界似乎透明而自动，但事实并非如此。

In this world, everyone, male and female, could become, might be, his or her own protagonist—that is, could develop a rich inner life based on the competing demands of conscience and ambition, selfishness and social connection. In this world each person feels a tension between himself or herself and the group, and also wishes to learn how to negotiate that tension. In this world individual existence has the potential for meaning—it can be understood and possibly changed or at least learned from. Cause and effect can be disentangled and observed. Events don't simply follow one another, as coordinate clauses do in a medieval narrative; they shape one another and grow out of one another, as subordinate clauses do in a modern narrative. In this world the ordinary person can step back, observe both the world and himself or herself, make a judgment, and then make a choice. This world is an agglomeration of individuals who relate to others as individuals. It is a world where “point of view” is a well-developed and important concept, the Western liberal ideal, and a paradox: if you look at a novel or a democracy one way, it is the tale of one person; if you look at it another way, it is a tale of a group. Neither the person nor the group ever gains permanent ascendancy; the two coexist. When, during the 2000 U.S. presidential election, Al Gore was asked to name his favorite book, he named The Red and the Black. Part of the reason I put it on my list was his recommendation. After I read it, I couldn't really understand what he liked about it—Julien Sorel seemed quite unlike Mr. Gore would want to seem, a cold, ambitious opportunist who uses and betrays women, then gets into trouble with the law and is executed in the end. But at least Gore's choice was a long and serious novel. The man in charge of the Western world had chosen a children's book, The Very Hungry Caterpillar , by Eric Carle. Let's not remark that this book is a tale of gluttony; let's just observe that it isn't a novel, that its choice as George W. Bush's favorite book perhaps reflects the fact that he doesn't read, or hasn't read, any serious novels. After a hundred and more novels of all kinds and degrees of seriousness, I was well aware that the habit of reading novels molds the mind in several significant ways, ways that other forms of literature do not. I wish that my president was reading Pride and Prejudice. Or As I Lay Dying. Or The Harafish. Or A Journal of the Plague Year.

在这个世界里，每个人，无论男女，都有可能成为自己的主角——也就是说，每个人都可以在良知与抱负、自私与社会联系等相互冲突的需求基础上，发展出丰富多彩的内心世界。在这个世界里，每个人都能感受到自身与群体之间的张力，并渴望学习如何化解这种张力。在这个世界里，个体的存在蕴含着意义——它可以被理解，甚至被改变，或者至少可以从中汲取经验。因果关系可以被厘清和观察。事件并非像中世纪叙事中的并列从句那样简单地依次发生；它们彼此塑造，相互发展，如同现代叙事中的从句那样。在这个世界里，普通人可以退后一步，观察世界和自身，做出判断，然后做出选择。这个世界是由众多个体组成的集合体，而这些个体彼此之间也存在着个体关系。这是一个“观点”概念发展成熟且至关重要的世界，它是西方自由主义的理想，同时也是一个悖论：如果你从某种角度看待一部小说或一个民主制度，它讲述的是一个人的故事；如果你从另一个角度看待它，它讲述的是一个群体的故事。无论是个人还是群体，都无法获得永久的主导地位；二者共存。2000年美国总统大选期间，当被问及最喜欢的书是什么时，阿尔·戈尔提到了《红与黑》。我把它列入书单的部分原因正是因为他的推荐。读完之后，我实在无法理解他喜欢这本书的理由——朱利安·索雷尔似乎与戈尔先生想要塑造的形象截然不同，他是一个冷酷无情、野心勃勃的机会主义者，利用并背叛女性，最终触犯法律并被处决。但至少戈尔的选择是一部篇幅较长且严肃的小说。这位掌控西方世界的人选择了一本儿童读物——埃里克·卡尔的《好饿的毛毛虫》。我们暂且不谈这本书讲述的是贪吃的故事；我们只需注意到它并非小说，它之所以成为乔治·W·布什最喜欢的书，或许反映出他不读，或者说从未读过任何严肃的小说。在读过一百多部各种类型、不同程度严肃程度的小说之后，我深知阅读小说的习惯会以多种重要方式塑造人的思维，而其他文学形式则无法做到这一点。我真希望我的总统正在读《傲慢与偏见》，或者《我弥留之际》，或者《哈拉菲什》，或者《瘟疫年代日记》。

After more than a hundred novels and two and a half years of history, I saw that the world I thought was established and secure, at least in the West, is more fragile than I thought, because it is newer than I realized. That a woman could be an agent rather than an object or a possession, that a marriage can be chosen, then rejected, that an identity can be constructed by an ordinary person—these are difficult ideas, strange to many, and dangerous to some. The tension between the individual and the group that the novel depicts is often intolerable to the group, and for some groups, an individual does not have a right to a point of view. The routine quality of the novel, the way that novels seem ubiquitous and benign, pleasurable, or fun, or even tedious to schoolchildren, masks their subversiveness and helps us forget how they have remade the world. I saw, with some surprise, that my world is fragile not only because of forces from the East, but also because of forces from within the West, forces from Texas, forces from Wyoming, forces from the evangelical right, forces from the corporate world, forces from the world of think tanks and political institutes. We seem to live in a world now where all thoughts are focused on the idea of prevailing, of imposing one's beliefs on others, and no thoughts, no thoughts are given to the costs of prevailing, or even what it means. Have these people never read Moby-Dick ? Well, no, they haven't.

读了一百多部小说，经历了两年半的历史学习之后，我意识到，我曾经以为稳固可靠的世界——至少在西方是如此——其实比我想象的更加脆弱，因为它比我意识到的要新得多。女性可以成为行动者而非客体或所有物，婚姻可以被选择，也可以被解除，普通人可以构建身份——这些都是难以接受的观念，对许多人来说很陌生，对某些人来说甚至很危险。小说所描绘的个体与群体之间的张力，对群体而言往往是难以容忍的，对某些群体来说，个体甚至没有表达观点的权利。小说的日常性，小说看似无处不在、无害、令人愉悦、有趣，甚至对小学生来说枯燥乏味，掩盖了它们的颠覆性，也让我们忘记了它们是如何重塑世界的。我颇感意外地发现，我的世界之所以脆弱，不仅是因为来自东方的势力，也因为来自西方内部的势力，来自德克萨斯的势力，来自怀俄明的势力，来自福音派右翼的势力，来自企业界的势力，来自智库和政治机构的势力。我们似乎生活在一个所有思想都聚焦于如何取胜、如何将自己的信仰强加于人的世界里，却丝毫不会去思考取胜的代价，甚至连取胜的意义都不愿提及。这些人难道没读过《白鲸》吗？不，他们确实没读过。

These are current concerns that perhaps someday will seem momentary in retrospect, but they remind me that those who don't read novels are condemned to repeat the oldest mistakes in literature—the mistake of hubris, a Greek mistake, and the mistake of attributing one's own emotions to God, a Judeo-Christian-Islamic mistake. Pride, arrogance, moral blindness, and narcissism are endemic among humans, especially humans who occupy positions of power, either in society or in the family. But when I have read a long novel, when I have entered systematically into a sensibility that is alien to mine, the author's or a character's, when I have become interested in another person because he is interesting, not because he is privileged or great, there is a possibility that at the end I will be a degree less self-centered than I was at the beginning, that I will be a degree more able to see the world as another sees it. And there is the possibility that I will be able to reason about my own emotions. In the end I will be more empathetic (I will understand through the logical connection made in the novel and my experience of the author's sensibility as expressed in his style) and I will be more sympathetic (I will feel along with the characters and perhaps the author).

这些都是当下的担忧，或许将来回首往事时会显得微不足道，但它们提醒我，不读小说的人注定要重蹈文学中最古老的覆辙——傲慢的错误（源自古希腊）和将自身情感归于上帝的错误（源自犹太教、基督教和伊斯兰教）。骄傲、自大、道德盲目和自恋在人类中普遍存在，尤其是在那些身居要职的人身上，无论是在社会还是家庭中。但是，当我读完一部长篇小说，当我系统地进入一种与我、作者或书中人物截然不同的感性世界，当我因为某人本身有趣而非因为他的特权或伟大而对他产生兴趣时，我或许会在读完之后比读完时少一些自我中心，更能从他人的视角看待世界。而且，我或许能够理性地看待自己的情感。最终我会更加感同身受（我会通过小说中建立的逻辑联系以及我对作者风格所表达的感性的体验来理解），我会更加同情（我会与角色甚至作者感同身受）。

When I've read lots of long novels, I will be trained in thinking about the world in many sometimes conflicting ways. One of the great pleasures of the forty-five thousand pages and more that I read in three years was something outside of the authors’ plot making and character drawing and theme organizing—it was the pleasure I gained from the authors’ passing observations and remarks. I came to see these passing phrases as not only the authors’ unique fingerprints all over what in many cases were familiar story lines, but also precious artifacts of what a man—say, Walter Scott—happened to see one day while he was walking down the street in 1810 ; or what a woman, Elizabeth Bowen, happened to feel one evening while dancing the fox-trot in 1925 ; or what another man, Nikolai Gogol, happened to smell and hear by the banks of the Dnieper River one morning in 1820 . To hold all of these moments in my mind, to have access to them, is to have a broad sense of the world—not only of these particular sensations, but also of the feelings about them that the authors have transmitted simultaneously with the sensation. The inhumane mercilessness Scott sees in a certain bald head and the potential embarrassment of dancing poorly Bowen senses in a certain movement and the primitive energy Gogol feels as the birds sing in the grass certainly do not coexist in my experience, but they do coexist in my memory, thanks to The Tale of Old Mortality, The Death of the Heart , and Taras Bulba. In a world where weapons of mass destruction are permanent features of the landscape, I cannot help believing that a lively sense of the reality of other consciousnesses on the part of those whose fingers are on the trigger is essential to human survival. The novel has made a world in which people are fairly adept at both feeling and thinking, and at thinking about feeling. The way in which novels are created—someone is seized by inspiration and then works out his inspiration methodically by writing, observing, writing, observing, thinking through, and writing again—is by nature deliberate, dominated neither by reason nor by emotion. Perched on the cusp between the particular and the general, between expertise and common sense, the novel promotes compromise, and especially promotes the idea that lessons can be learned, if not by the characters, then by the author and the reader. The world of the novel is a rational world; even while the author and the characters are lamenting its irrationality, cause-and-effect relationships can be teased out of events and recognized, if only after the fact.

当我读过很多长篇小说后，我的思维方式就会变得多种多样，有时甚至相互矛盾。三年间，我读了四万五千多页，其中最大的乐趣之一并非在于作者的情节构思、人物塑造和主题组织——而是作者不经意间的观察和评论。我逐渐意识到，这些不经意的语句不仅是作者在看似熟悉的故事情节中留下的独特印记，更是珍贵的记录，展现了沃尔特·斯科特在1810年某天漫步街头时的所见所闻；或是伊丽莎白·鲍恩在1925年某晚跳狐步舞时的所感所悟。或者，又或者，是另一位作家尼古拉·果戈理在1820年的一个清晨，在第聂伯河畔闻到和听到的景象。将所有这些瞬间铭记于心，能够触及它们，便能让我拥有对世界的广阔认知——不仅是对这些特定感受的认知，更是对作者们在感知的同时所传递的情感的认知。斯科特在某个秃头中看到的非人般的冷酷无情，鲍文在某个动作中感受到的笨拙舞姿可能带来的尴尬，以及果戈理在鸟儿于草地上歌唱时感受到的原始能量，这些在我的经历中当然无法共存，但它们却在我的记忆中并存，这要归功于《旧日死亡的故事》、《心之死》和《塔拉斯·布尔巴》。在一个大规模杀伤性武器已成为常态的世界里，我不得不相信，对于那些掌握着武器扳机的人来说，对其他意识的真实存在保持敏锐的感知，对于人类的生存至关重要。这部小说构建了一个世界，在这个世界里，人们相当擅长感受和思考，也擅长思考感受本身。小说的创作方式——灵感乍现，然后通过写作、观察、写作、观察、思考、再写作，有条不紊地将灵感付诸实践——本质上是深思熟虑的，既不受理性支配，也不受情感左右。小说游走于特殊与普遍、专业知识与常识之间，提倡妥协，尤其强调了即使小说中的人物无法从中汲取教训，作者和读者也能从中有所收获。小说的世界是一个理性的世界；即使作者和人物都在哀叹它的非理性，因果关系仍然可以从事件中梳理出来并被识别出来，即便只能事后才能发现。

When we talk about the death of the novel, what we are really talking about is the possibility that empathy, however minimal, would no longer be attainable by those for whom the novel has died. If the novel has died for the bureaucrats who run our country, then they are more likely not to pause before engaging in arrogant, narcissistic, and foolish policies. If the novel has died for men (and some publishers and critics say that men read fewer novels than they used to), then the inner lives of their friends and family members are a degree more closed to them than before. If the novel dies, or never lives, for children and teenagers who spend their time watching TV or playing video games, then they will always be somewhat mystified by others, and by themselves as well. If the novel should die, what is to replace it?

当我们谈论小说的消亡时，我们真正讨论的是，对于那些小说已死的人来说，哪怕是最微弱的同理心，也可能不再能够获得。如果小说对那些掌控我们国家的官僚来说已经消亡，那么他们就更有可能在推行傲慢、自恋和愚蠢的政策之前毫不犹豫。如果小说对男性来说已经消亡（一些出版商和评论家认为，男性阅读小说的数量比以前少了），那么他们与亲朋好友的内心世界之间的联系就比以往更加疏远。如果小说对那些把时间花在看电视或玩电子游戏上的儿童和青少年来说已经消亡，或者从未真正存在过，那么他们将永远对他人，甚至对自己，感到困惑不解。如果小说真的消亡了，那么什么又将取代它呢？

My guess is that mere technology will not kill the novel. It is too different from movies and other forms of visual entertainment to be replaced by them. Nor do I believe that novels are bannable. Too many of them reside in private hands; they would be as hard to get rid of as guns and bullets. But novels can be sidelined—dismissed to the seraglio, where they are read by women and children and have no effect on those in power. When that happens, our society will be brutalized and coarsened by people who speak rather like us and look rather like us but who have no way of understanding us or each other.

我的猜测是，仅仅是科技发展并不会扼杀小说。小说与电影和其他视觉娱乐形式截然不同，无法被它们取代。我也不认为小说应该被禁。太多小说藏于私人手中，想要彻底清除它们就像清除枪支弹药一样困难。但小说可能会被边缘化——被束之高阁，沦为妇女儿童的读物，对当权者毫无影响。当这种情况发生时，我们的社会将被那些言谈举止与我们相似，却无法理解我们或彼此的人所摧残和腐蚀。

# ↩

9. The Circle of the Novel

9. 小说的循环

The modern novel should be largely a work of reference. Most authors spend their time saying what has been said before—usually said much better. A wealth of references to existing works would acquaint the reader instantaneously with the nature of each character, would obviate tiresome explanations and would effectively preclude mountebanks, upstarts, thimble-riggers and persons of inferior education from an understanding of contemporary literature. Conclusion of explanation.
That is all my bum, said Brinsley.

现代小说应该主要以参考书的形式呈现。大多数作者都在重复别人已经说过的话——而且通常别人说得更好。大量引用现有作品可以让读者立刻了解每个角色的性格，避免冗长的解释，并有效地阻止江湖骗子、暴发户、投机取巧之徒和教育程度低下的人理解当代文学。解释结束。“那都是我的胡言乱语，”布林斯利说道。

— FLANN O‘brien , At Swim-Two-Birds

——弗兰·奥布莱恩，《双鸟游泳》

T here is, of course, still another way to consider the novel, apart from who wrote it and why, apart from how it feels to read it. All novels exist discretely as items in the catalog of novels, and every one is like and unlike every other one. We can't really understand any one novel without comparing it to others—not necessarily to decide whether it is great, greater, or greatest, but just to see how in any particular novel all the potential ingredients are chosen and assembled. In addition, all novels happen to be related to many other forms of discourse—the “art” of the novel always has to contend with the fact that the novel is an essentially compromised form. The novel as we know it grew out of earlier types of literature and can't be understood except by reference to them. In addition, the impulse to write a novel grows out of related impulses to communicate and tell stories, and the novel can't be understood apart from that apparently universal human urge.

当然，除了作者是谁、创作缘由以及阅读感受之外，还有另一种看待小说的方式。所有小说都独立存在于小说的目录中，每一部小说都与其他小说既相似又不同。如果不与其他小说进行比较，我们就无法真正理解任何一部小说——这并非是为了评判它是伟大、更伟大还是最伟大，而是为了了解在一部特定的小说中，所有潜在的元素是如何被选择和组合的。此外，所有小说都与许多其他话语形式相关——小说的“艺术”始终必须面对这样一个事实：小说本质上是一种妥协的形式。我们所知的小说源于早期的文学类型，只有参照这些早期文学类型才能理解它。此外，创作小说的冲动源于交流和讲述故事的冲动，而小说也无法脱离这种看似普遍的人类需求而被理解。

The easiest way, I think, to conceptualize this aspect of the novel is to imagine an analog clock face with the novel in the middle and the forms of discourse it is related to arranged around the circumference. If we then plot some of our novels around the clock, how the catalog of novels arranges itself is easier to understand, and how novels succeed or fail is also easier to understand. Most authors do not, of course, consciously position their novels in relation to all the others, but inevitably, after the novel is out of the author's hands, it takes up its position in the bookcase, in the reader's mental library, and, for the sake of argument, on the face of our clock.

我认为，理解小说这一方面最简单的方法是想象一个模拟钟面，小说位于中心，与之相关的各种话语形式则围绕着钟面排列。如果我们把一些小说按照这个钟面的顺序排列，就能更容易理解小说目录的构成，以及小说成败的原因。当然，大多数作者并不会刻意地将自己的小说与其他作品联系起来，但不可避免地，当小说离开作者之手后，它会在书架上、在读者的脑海中占据一席之地，而且，为了便于讨论，也在我们的“钟面”上占据一席之地。

The clock has twelve stations, of course. Each station represents a specific type of discourse. Each type has essential characteristics and offers the reader a particular form of pleasure. If the reader does not gain the sort of pleasure she expects from that type of discourse, she will be disappointed no matter what other pleasures she does gain (if, for example, she is listening to a joke and it isn't funny, it doesn't matter much whether it is informative or eloquent). Much of a reader's willingness to suspend disbelief grows out of whether she and the author agree on what category or categories of discourse a text falls into.

当然，时钟有十二个站点。每个站点代表一种特定的话语类型。每种类型都有其本质特征，并为读者带来特定的愉悦感。如果读者没有从该类型的话语中获得她所期望的愉悦感，那么无论她获得了什么其他的愉悦感，她都会感到失望（例如，如果她在听一个笑话，但这个笑话并不好笑，那么它是否具有信息量或文笔优美都无关紧要）。读者是否愿意暂时放下怀疑，很大程度上取决于她和作者是否对文本所属的话语类别达成共识。

THE CLOCK

时钟

The first five forms exist to allow an author and a reader to communicate systematically about specific types of information:

前五种形式的存在是为了让作者和读者能够系统地交流特定类型的信息：

  1. Travel narrative , simple in a way, offers a series of adventures and descriptions organized around a journey. The travel narrative is always about something exotic or unknown. The travel involved may be literal—to distant places—or it may be figurative—into the mind of another creature—but if the reader gets no sense of being transported out of her own mundane existence, then the travel narrative has not delivered on its promise.

    旅行叙事，简单来说，就是围绕一段旅程展开一系列冒险和描述。旅行叙事总是与异域风情或未知事物有关。这种旅行可以是字面意义上的——前往遥远的地方——也可以是比喻意义上的——进入另一种生物的内心世界——但如果读者没有感受到被带离自身平凡生活的体验，那么这段旅行叙事就辜负了它的承诺。

  2. History relates a series of past events in a way that will enable the reader to make sense of them systematically, and to relate them to her own experience. Essential to history is the idea that time has passed and that the past is different from the present. The reader is asked to reason and understand; her pleasure arises from a sense that perspective has been achieved upon events that previously seemed chaotic or meaningless.

    历史以一种能够帮助读者系统理解并联系自身经验的方式，叙述一系列过去发生的事件。历史的核心在于认识到时间的流逝以及过去与现在的差异。读者需要进行推理和理解；阅读的乐趣源于对先前看似混乱或毫无意义的事件有了更清晰的认识。

  3. Biography is the portrayal and analysis of a single person. The reader wants to feel that she has come to know that person well, perhaps better than the person knows himself, and she also wants to contemplate the nature of humanity. It doesn't matter if the subject of the biography is very like the reader or very unlike her; it is enough that the subject and the reader exist simultaneously in the reader's mind.

    传记是对某个人物的刻画和分析。读者希望感觉自己对传记中的人物有了深入的了解，甚至比人物本人更了解他/她自己，同时也希望从中思考人性的本质。传记的主人公与读者本人是否非常相似或截然不同并不重要；重要的是，传记主人公和读者能够同时存在于读者的脑海中。

  4. Tale may partake of all the previous forms—it can be about a place, a person, or a former time—but it is always fictional and always entertaining. It can therefore include any entertaining element—magic, trickery, deception, dread, implausible plot twists, happy endings, unrealistic circumstances, and nonhuman consciousnesses—but it must induce pleasure or it doesn't qualify as a tale.

    故事可以包含所有先前的形式——它可以讲述某个地方、某个人物或某个过去的故事——但它始终是虚构的，也始终具有娱乐性。因此，它可以包含任何娱乐元素——魔法、诡计、欺骗、恐惧、匪夷所思的情节转折、大团圆结局、不切实际的情境，以及非人类的意识——但它必须能带来愉悦感，否则就不能称之为故事。

  5. Joke is a mini-tale, but whereas a tale may arouse feelings of awe, fear, or wonder, a joke only has to arouse a laugh.

    笑话是一个小故事，但故事可能会引起敬畏、恐惧或惊奇之感，而笑话只需要引起笑声即可。

    Three forms depend on and acknowledge privacy and secrecy:

    三种形式都依赖于隐私和保密，并承认隐私和保密的重要性：

  6. Gossip is public speculation about private matters. It uses disconnection and secrecy even while using the tools of communication.

    流言蜚语是对私人事务的公开猜测。即使使用通讯工具，它也仍然采用疏离和保密的方式。

    Gossip is an inherently popular form, like jokes and tales, and it promotes the idea of common sense over erudition. The pleasure for the reader is that gossip not only reveals secrets, it also interprets and assimilates them.

    八卦本身就是一种很受欢迎的文体，就像笑话和故事一样，它推崇的是常识而非学识。八卦的乐趣在于，它不仅揭露秘密，还能解读和吸收这些秘密。

  7. Diary/letter is the most intimate form of discourse. In diaries and letters, private matters are recalled and analyzed. The pleasure comes from the sense that the diarist or letter writer is as honest as he can consciously be, and that his revelations are private ones. The reader feels that the whole of the narrator's mind is open to her, that she is as intimate with him as he is with himself, but that, as with the biography, she may come to understand him better than he understands himself.

    日记/书信是最私密的交流形式。在日记和书信中，私人事件被回忆和分析。阅读的乐趣在于，读者会感到日记作者或书信作者尽可能地坦诚，并且他的倾诉是私密的。读者会觉得叙述者的整个内心世界都向自己敞开，自己与他之间的亲密程度如同他与自己的内心世界一样，但就像阅读传记一样，读者或许会比他自己更了解他。

  8. Confession is the diary as a self-conscious form of rhetoric— intimacy overheard gives way to an intentional persuasion of the reader that the confessor's interpretation of events has meaning and weight. The confession is different from the diary/letter in that the events being discussed are finished and therefore seen as a whole sequence rather than unfolding while the narrator is writing. For the reader, the pleasure of the confession is its self-contradiction—intimacy used rhetorically is likely to be combined with either deception or self-deception.

    忏悔录是一种自觉的修辞形式，它类似于日记——偷听到的私密对话逐渐演变为一种有意说服读者的策略，即忏悔者对事件的解读具有意义和分量。忏悔录与日记/信件的不同之处在于，它所讨论的事件已经发生，因此被视为一个完整的序列，而不是在叙述者写作过程中逐渐展开的。对读者而言，忏悔录的乐趣在于其自相矛盾——修辞性地运用亲密感往往伴随着欺骗或自欺。

    The next two forms are essentially rhetorical rather than, like travel, history, and biography, narrative:

    接下来的两种形式本质上是修辞性的，而不是像游记、历史和传记那样的叙事性：

  9. Polemic uses emotion, as narrative does, but presents it as argument, marshaling events, characters, and insights in service to a rhetorical point. The pleasure, for the reader, is eloquence intensified by feeling and the sense that the writer is pushing the bounds of propriety.

    论战作品如同叙事作品一样运用情感，但它将情感表达为论证，巧妙地运用事件、人物和洞见来服务于某个修辞观点。对读者而言，其乐趣在于情感的渲染增强了雄辩的表达，以及作者挑战传统礼仪界限的意识。

  10. Essay , like polemic, uses logic and example to make an argument, but gets rid of the emotional fervor, adopting instead a reasoned and objective tone. The pleasure for the reader is always, as in biography and history, in the sense that the arguments are complete, well reasoned, thoroughly worked out, and demonstrated.

    散文与论战一样，运用逻辑和例证来论证观点，但它摒弃了情绪化的激情，转而采用理性客观的语气。读者阅读散文的乐趣，如同阅读传记和历史一样，在于其论证完整、逻辑严密、论证充分且有理有据。

    The stations at the top of the clock are the two main narrative precursors of the novel, always understood to be fiction, but more formal, significant, and complex than the tale:

    时钟顶部的车站是小说的两个主要叙事先驱，它们始终被认为是虚构的，但比故事本身更正式、更有意义、更复杂：

  11. Epic. The goal of this form (at least among Indo-Europeans) was to solidify a warrior nation's sense of its own identity and the battle prowess of its warriors. The epic was essentially tragic, since, as Krishna remarks to Arjuna at the beginning of the Bhagavad Gita , there is no avoiding either death or killing in this world. The reader's pleasure in the epic comes from a sharpened sense of what makes up a particular national character.

    史诗。这种形式（至少在印欧语系民族中）的目的是巩固尚武民族的自我认同感及其战士的战斗力。史诗本质上是悲剧性的，因为正如克里希那在《薄伽梵歌》开篇对阿朱那所说，在这个世界上，死亡和杀戮都是无法避免的。读者从史诗中获得的愉悦感来自于对特定民族性格构成要素的深刻理解。

  12. Romance , of course, is about love, sex, and relationships. The pleasure of romance comes when the reader recognizes and sympathizes with the idea that a particular connection between two characters is interesting, worthy, believable, and involving.

    当然，浪漫小说讲述的是爱情、性和人际关系。浪漫小说的乐趣在于，读者能够理解并认同两个角色之间某种特定的联系是有趣、有价值、可信且引人入胜的。

The novel uses all of these forms. Some novels use many of them, others use only a few, but it is impossible to have a novel that uses none of them. If we take some novels and plot them around the clock, we can get insight both into how these novels work and why some of them seem “great.”

小说运用了所有这些形式。有些小说运用了多种形式，有些小说只运用了几种，但不可能出现一部小说完全不使用任何一种形式。如果我们选取一些小说，并逐日分析它们的情节，就能深入了解这些小说的运作方式，以及为什么有些小说会显得“伟大”。

We can try out our clock by considering a paradigmatic great realist novel, Middlemarch , the most novelish of novels. In Middlemarch (which uses history, biography, joke, gossip, essay, travel, and romance) Eliot adopts a tone that is too reasonable for polemic and too objective for a tale. She excludes diary/letter and confession by remaining in the third-person point of view. And Middlemarch is not an epic—its characters are influenced by history and are characteristic of a certain time and place, but they do not shape and define Englishness. The biographical subjects are Dorothea, Casaubon, Rosamond, Lydgate, Mary, and Fred. Eliot characterizes each in detail—looks, clothing, domicile, family, social class, aspirations, motivations, actions, reflections—and also locates them carefully in their separate contexts, not only that of the town and environs of Middlemarch, but also in what it means to be a man, a woman, and a human being. She uses their habits and choices to develop and reveal their moral natures. At the end she tells what happened to them after the close of the plot, reinforcing the idea that they have whole lives, as biographical subjects do. But she is no less interested in the history of Middlemarch. The novel is set in a specific time and place—the rural Midlands of England, before the parliamentary reform of 1832 and before the full onset of the industrial revolution, some thirty-five years before the composition of the novel. Middlemarch is meant to reliably evoke the earlier era and to reflect upon the changes, for better and worse, between the two periods. Eliot is also aware of how the town functions, and she uses the gossip form in a very sophisticated manner to communicate character and plot information to the reader as well as to build up a picture of the town as a network of social relationships.

我们可以通过分析一部堪称典范的伟大现实主义小说——《米德尔马契》来检验我们的时间观念。这部小说堪称小说中的小说。在《米德尔马契》（融合了历史、传记、笑话、闲聊、散文、游记和爱情等元素）中，艾略特采用了一种过于理性而缺乏论战色彩，又过于客观而缺乏叙事性的语调。她坚持采用第三人称视角，避免了日记/书信和忏悔式的叙述。《米德尔马契》并非史诗——书中的人物受历史影响，具有特定时代和地域的特征，但他们并未塑造或定义英国性。传记式的人物包括多萝西娅、卡索邦、罗莎蒙德、利德盖特、玛丽和弗雷德。艾略特细致地刻画了每个人——外貌、衣着、住所、家庭、社会阶层、抱负、动机、行为和思考——并将他们置于各自的语境之中，不仅是米德尔马契小镇及其周边地区，也包括作为男人、女人和人的意义。她通过人物的习惯和选择来塑造和揭示他们的道德本质。在故事结尾，她讲述了他们在故事结束后的遭遇，强化了他们拥有完整人生的理念，正如传记人物一样。但她对米德尔马契的历史同样充满兴趣。小说设定在特定的时间和地点——英格兰中部乡村，时间设定在1832年议会改革之前，工业革命全面爆发之前，也就是小说创作的三十五年前。米德尔马契旨在真实地展现那个时代的风貌，并反思两个时期之间发生的种种变化，无论好坏。艾略特也深谙小镇的运作方式，她巧妙地运用闲聊的形式，向读者传递人物和情节信息，同时构建出小镇错综复杂的社会关系网络。

The organization of the novel sets it up as an analytical argument and therefore essaylike. Although Dorothea is an appealing protagonist, the reader is not allowed to focus upon her. After the first long section (“Miss Brooke”), the novel shifts to the concerns of other characters, who are delineated as carefully as Dorothea has been. She never quite comes to the fore again as she does in the beginning. Even though she is probably Eliot's favorite character, and maybe a representation of the author herself, the novel focuses on Dorothea's relationships and asks the reader to observe the drama of her inner development rather than to become emotionally involved with it. Restraining the reader's sympathies is perhaps Eliot's motive for depicting Will Ladislaw, who comes to town to edit a newspaper and whom Dorothea eventually marries after her first husband, Casaubon, dies, as not quite worthy of Dorothea—he is no Mr. Darcy. Eliot is making an argument about what a moral life is and how to lead one, and she is interested in the mistakes the characters make as representative mistakes rather than as personal catharses. As beautifully drawn as these six characters are, and as many of the other characters are, the pattern and meaning of their choices are what really interest the author.

小说的结构使其呈现出分析论证的风格，因此也更像一篇散文。尽管多萝西娅是一位引人入胜的主人公，但读者却无法将注意力完全集中在她身上。在第一篇幅较长的章节（“布鲁克小姐”）之后，小说便将笔触转向其他人物，这些人物的刻画与多萝西娅一样细致入微。她再也没有像开头那样成为故事的焦点。尽管她可能是艾略特最喜欢的角色，甚至可能是作者自身的化身，但小说的重点却放在多萝西娅的人际关系上，并引导读者观察她内心世界的演变，而不是让她产生情感上的共鸣。或许正是出于克制读者同情心的目的，艾略特才将威尔·拉迪斯劳——这位来到小镇担任报社编辑，并在多萝西娅的第一任丈夫卡索邦去世后最终嫁给她的男子——描绘得配不上多萝西娅，他远非达西先生。艾略特探讨的是何为道德生活以及如何践行道德，她关注的是人物所犯的错误，并将之视为具有代表性的错误，而非个人情感宣泄。尽管这六个人物以及其他许多人物都刻画得栩栩如生，但真正令作者感兴趣的是他们选择的模式和意义。

Romance, of course, can be presented realistically, almost as if it weren't romance, but no character that Eliot really cares about goes unrewarded in Middlemarch; the marriages that are made according to Eliot's prescriptions—Mary's with Fred, Dorothea's with Will Ladislaw—get to be happy. Lydgate, of course, receives no reward—neither professional satisfaction nor conjugal happiness—because in spite of his intelligence and good intentions, he is as undeserving as his shallow wife. He not only cannot understand Rosamond, he also is barred by male arrogance from even trying to understand her until it is too late. The reader can't help infer that the author thinks he should have chosen a plainer, more genuine girl, and that if he didn't have the sense to do so, his fate is deserved.

当然，爱情也可以写得非常写实，几乎不像是爱情故事，但在《米德尔马契》中，艾略特真正关心的人物没有一个得不到回报；那些按照艾略特的安排缔结的婚姻——玛丽和弗雷德的结合，多萝西娅和威尔·拉迪斯劳的结合——最终都获得了幸福。而利德盖特自然没有得到任何回报——既没有事业上的满足，也没有婚姻的幸福——因为尽管他聪明且心地善良，但他和他肤浅的妻子一样不配拥有这一切。他不仅无法理解罗莎蒙德，而且由于男性的傲慢，他甚至在为时已晚之前都无法尝试去理解她。读者不禁会推断，作者认为他应该选择一个更朴素、更真诚的女孩，如果他没有这样的明智之举，那么他的命运也是咎由自取。

And that is part of the joke, but only part. Pictures of George Eliot (Mary Ann Evans) always show her unsmiling and sober, a moralist to the core, but Middlemarch is full of smart, subtle, and very funny ideas and turns of phrase. She is much slyer than those overt satirists Dickens and Thackeray, for example. Although always aware of life's potential for grief and tragedy, she pokes much ironic fun at Mr. Brooke, Dorothea's uncle, at Mr. Casaubon, at Fred Vincy, and many of the lesser denizens of Middlemarch. Her favorite characters are those, like Mary Garth and Mr. Farebrother, whose views are leavened with irreverence. Middlemarch is a serious but not a somber novel. Eliot puts wit and irony to work as antidotes to sentimentality, recognizing that the piquancy of wit makes the hard work of distinguishing between right and wrong much easier. Middlemarch shows that Eliot believed that virtue and pleasure, good nature and right thinking are intrinsically connected in a healthy mind.

这固然是幽默的一部分，但仅仅是一部分。乔治·艾略特（玛丽·安·埃文斯饰）的画像总是面无表情、一本正经，骨子里是个道德家，但《米德尔马契》却充满了机智、微妙而又妙趣横生的想法和措辞。她比狄更斯和萨克雷等直白的讽刺作家要狡黠得多。尽管她始终意识到生活中可能存在的悲伤和悲剧，但她仍然对多萝西娅的叔叔布鲁克先生、卡索邦先生、弗雷德·文西以及米德尔马契的许多其他次要居民进行了大量的讽刺挖苦。她最喜欢的角色是像玛丽·加思和费尔布拉泽先生那样，观点中带有几分不敬的人。《米德尔马契》是一部严肃但不沉闷的小说。艾略特运用机智和讽刺来对抗感伤主义，她深知机智的辛辣使辨别是非变得容易得多。 《米德尔马契》表明艾略特认为，在一个健康的心灵中，美德与快乐、善良的本性和正确的思想是内在联系的。

Middlemarch shows us that a novel that partakes of at least four or five of our categories seems rich and various, and that a debt to either romance or epic is essential, because these are the “long story” forms (though it is not possible to have a novel that is a pure epic, a pure romance, or a pure combination of the two, because the objective tone of travel narratives, histories, biographies, essays, and, in some sense, polemics, becomes the realistic tone of the novel). If we look at another great artifact of the Victorian period, Vanity Fair (travel, history, biography, joke, polemic, epic), we can see that two authors can use five of the same “public” categories but come up with an entirely different type of novel if one of them shifts from the objective tone of the essay category to the angry tone of the polemic category. Vanity Fair was intended by Thackeray to be a grand portrait of the England he knew, canvassing the rulers and the ruled, men and women, the middle class, the aristocracy, the landed gentry, the colonialists, the military. But because of its satiric, polemical tone, it becomes an antiepic (the English hero dies anonymously at Waterloo), an antiromance (Amelia Sedley, Dobbin's beloved, turns out to be a disappointment in the end), an antitravel narrative (there is nothing exotic in France, much less India), an antihistory (Waterloo and everything subsequent turn out to be much like the present day of the novel), and even an antibiography in some sense, since Amelia and Dobbin are not portrayed as being especially striking individuals, and Becky disappears from the novel as if she had not dominated it from the beginning. The modern reader might not understand what Thackeray is satirizing, since his polemic is not about any recognizable ideology in the way Dickens's is or Stowe's is. Thackeray was explicitly worried about the decline of the gentleman as an English type—a brave, responsible, mature man of good breeding and good manners, honest, dutiful, and courteous. Most of his satire is directed against men who have the power and pedigree to be gentlemen, such as the Crawleys (landed gentry) and Lord Steyne (wealth, power, and influence). In some sense his views did not disagree with those of Charles Dickens—both felt that the English ruling class was ruling irresponsibly and selfishly. But while Dickens felt that middle-class virtues of domesticity, hard work, feelings of connection to both those at the top and those at the bottom, inventiveness, and wealth creation were a possible solution, Thackeray didn't see a solution. He was thus conservative in his political inclinations— Vanity Fair describes loss and deterioration, and stymies notions of change or improvement. Becky, who seems to be Thackeray's protagonist at the beginning of the novel, is enterprising, imaginative, energetic, and accomplished, but her motives are usually of the narrowest and most selfish kind (the one time she takes pity on someone and extends herself to please her is one of the most moving moments in the novel). Dobbin, who seems to be Thackeray's protagonist at the end of the novel, is unselfish, but he is slow and stolid. Becky's friend Amelia is virtuous but unimaginative and silly. No adult has a responsible relationship with any child and is therefore capable of nurturing good values in the next generation. Some of those who have been disappointed nurse their grievances to the grave (such as Mr. Sedley, Amelia's father) or are too foolish to resist further injury (such as Jos Sedley, Amelia's brother). Vanity Fair is overtly political, but like all conservative novels, it seems to be satirizing human nature itself rather than human nature as constituted in a particular way by particular social, economic, and cultural arrangements. Unlike Middlemarch , it offers no alternative model through the mechanism of a happy ending, a wholly positive character, a charming narrative voice, or an example of spiritual redemption. The absence of such an alternative reinforces the polemical aspect and removes the potential for analysis—cause and effect show only how history has made both society and personal relationships what they are. There is no indication that they could be different, nor could they be redeemed.

《米德尔马契》向我们展示了，一部小说如果至少涵盖了我们列出的四五个类别，就会显得丰富多彩；而借鉴浪漫小说或史诗小说是必不可少的，因为这些都是“长篇故事”的形式（尽管不可能存在纯粹的史诗小说、纯粹的浪漫小说，或者两者纯粹的结合体，因为游记、历史、传记、散文，以及某种意义上的论战文章的客观语调，最终会成为小说的现实主义语调）。如果我们考察维多利亚时代的另一部杰作《名利场》（游记、历史、传记、笑话、论战、史诗），就会发现，两位作者即使使用相同的五个“公共”类别，如果其中一位的语调从散文的客观语调转向论战的激烈语调，最终也会创作出截然不同的小说。 《名利场》原本是萨克雷意图描绘他所熟知的英国的一幅宏大画卷，囊括统治者和被统治者、男人和女人、中产阶级、贵族、乡绅、殖民者和军人。但由于其讽刺和论战的基调，它最终变成了一部反史诗（英国英雄在滑铁卢战役中默默无闻地死去）、一部反浪漫小说（多宾的爱人阿米莉亚·塞德利最终令人失望）、一部反游记（法国毫无异域风情，更遑论印度）、一部反历史小说（滑铁卢战役及其后的一切都与小说中的现代社会极为相似），甚至在某种意义上是一部反传记，因为阿米莉亚和多宾并没有被刻画成特别引人注目的人物，而贝基则仿佛从未从一开始就占据主导地位一般，从小说中消失了。现代读者或许难以理解萨克雷的讽刺对象，因为他的论战并非像狄更斯或斯托夫人那样，围绕着某种可辨识的意识形态展开。萨克雷明确担忧的是英国绅士形象的衰落——这种形象通常指勇敢、负责、成熟、举止得体、诚实、尽职、彬彬有礼的绅士。他的大部分讽刺都针对那些拥有绅士地位和显赫家世的人，例如克劳利家族（乡绅地主）和斯泰恩勋爵（拥有财富、权力和影响力）。在某种程度上，他的观点与查尔斯·狄更斯的观点并无冲突——两人都认为英国统治阶级的统治不负责任且自私自利。但狄更斯认为，中产阶级的美德，如顾家、勤奋、与社会各阶层保持联系、创造力和创造财富，或许是解决之道，而萨克雷却看不到任何出路。因此，他的政治倾向是保守的——《名利场》描绘的是衰败和恶化，扼杀了变革或进步的理念。贝基似乎是小说开头萨克雷笔下的主人公，她进取、富有想象力、精力充沛且才华横溢，但她的动机通常极其狭隘和自私（她唯一一次心生怜悯，竭尽全力取悦他人，是小说中最感人的时刻之一）。多宾似乎是小说结尾萨克雷笔下的主人公，他无私奉献，但却迟钝而沉闷。贝基的朋友阿米莉亚品德高尚，但缺乏想象力且愚蠢。没有哪个成年人与孩子之间建立起负责任的关系，因此也无法在下一代身上培养良好的价值观。一些失望之人将怨恨带入坟墓（例如阿米莉亚的父亲塞德利先生），或愚蠢到无法抵挡进一步的伤害（例如阿米莉亚的哥哥乔斯·塞德利）。《名利场》的政治色彩浓厚，但如同所有保守主义小说一样，它似乎讽刺的是人性本身，而非特定社会、经济和文化安排所塑造的人性。与《米德尔马契》不同，它没有通过圆满结局、完美无瑕的人物、迷人的叙述视角或精神救赎的例子来提供任何替代模式。这种替代方案的缺失强化了其论战性质，并剥夺了分析的可能性——因果关系仅仅展现了历史如何塑造了社会和人际关系的现状。没有任何迹象表明它们可以有所不同，或者可以被救赎。

Touches of history, biography, essay, and polemic are the marks of the realistic novel, the ways in which the novelist introduces gravity into his story. Each of the realistic novels on our list uses one or the other. But others do, too. Dracula (travel, history, biography, tale, gossip, diary/letter, confession, essay, epic, romance) is especially clever in borrowing the objective, fact-piling style of both history and biography to enhance the eerie weight of what is essentially a tale. In fact, of all the novels on the list, Dracula is one of the ones that use the most forms. All mysteries and thrillers are really tales. Dracula uses the information-gathering form of the case history to imply analysis and an objective tone to make the tale more plausible and more sinis-terly a part of the modern world. In addition, Dracula's five pursuers are heroic; Dracula himself represents good and bad aspects of his Transylvanian history. Mina Harker, the romantic heroine, must be and is saved by her husband and his friends, while other female characters are not. Characters travel not only to Transylvania but also to Yorkshire. Several of the characters write privately of their experiences, and many of the interlocking narratives are in the first person, like confessions. Indeed, Mina's husband has to confess to witnessing Mina, in a scene reminiscent of the marquis de Sade, drinking Count Dracula's blood. Dracula is considered one of the best and most perennial examples of the horror genre, and surely this is the reason— Stoker makes very intelligent use of many authenticating novelistic forms to bolster his otherwise unbelievable tale and to reward the reader for continuing to read. But unlike Eliot and Thackeray, Stoker isn't out to analyze or prove a social theory, only to make his tale as exciting as possible, so Dracula stays slotted in its genre and doesn't break out into the mainstream of the ambitious literary novel.

历史、传记、散文和论辩的元素是现实主义小说的标志，也是小说家赋予故事以严肃性的方式。我们榜单上的每一部现实主义小说都运用了其中一种或几种手法。但其他小说也同样如此。《德古拉》（融合了游记、历史、传记、故事、八卦、日记/书信、忏悔录、散文、史诗和爱情等多种文体）尤其巧妙地借鉴了历史和传记客观、罗列事实的风格，增强了这部本质上是故事的作品的诡异氛围。事实上，在所有上榜小说中，《德古拉》是运用文体最多的作品之一。所有悬疑和惊悚小说本质上都是故事。《德古拉》运用案例史的信息收集形式来暗示分析和客观的语气，使故事更具可信度，也更阴森地融入现代世界。此外，德古拉的五位追捕者都是英雄；德古拉本人则代表了他特兰西瓦尼亚历史中善与恶的两面。浪漫小说的女主角米娜·哈克必须也确实得到了丈夫和他的朋友们的拯救，而其他女性角色则没有这样的幸运。故事中的人物不仅前往特兰西瓦尼亚，还去了约克郡。一些角色私下记录了自己的经历，许多交织的叙事都以第一人称叙述，如同忏悔录一般。事实上，米娜的丈夫不得不承认，他目睹了米娜在一个令人联想起萨德侯爵的场景中，饮下了德古拉伯爵的血。德古拉被认为是恐怖小说中最优秀、最经久不衰的作品之一，这无疑是原因所在——斯托克巧妙地运用了许多使小说更具真实感的叙事手法，以此来强化他那原本略显荒诞的故事，并激励读者继续阅读。但与艾略特和萨克雷不同，斯托克并非意在分析或论证某种社会理论，而只是为了让他的故事尽可能地引人入胜，因此，《德古拉》始终停留在其类型小说的范畴内，未能跻身于雄心勃勃的文学小说的主流之列。

Another novel that uses many categories, though with more serious overtones, is T H. White's modern recasting of the Arthurian legends, The Once and Future King (travel, history, biography, tale, joke, gossip, polemic, essay, epic, romance). Although White's novel (actually four related novels written over two decades) is advertised as a children's fantasy novel, it is hard to know what children might make of some of White's crueler scenes and more serious themes concerning power, destiny, maternal seductiveness, and neglect, not to mention betrayal and adultery. White not only weds tale (the Arthurian material), history (extensive details from twelfth- and thirteenth-century English life), epic, romance, and joke, he also jumps suddenly and with sharp changes of tone from one to another. Some characters appear as comic figures, such as King Pellinore and Merlyn, others as realistic characters of considerable psychological complexity, such as Arthur, Guenever, Lancelot, Gawaine, and his brothers. Gawaine's mother, Morgause, has the witchlike features of a character in a tale, but the underlying nature of a seductive, neglectful mother in a Freudian novel. She is too complex to be simply evil, but her effect on her children is damaging and haunting; through them she affects the whole kingdom.

另一部融合多种元素的小说是T·H·怀特对亚瑟王传说的现代改编之作《永恒之王》（旅行、历史、传记、故事、笑话、八卦、论战、散文、史诗、爱情）。尽管怀特的这部小说（实际上是历时二十年创作的四部相关小说）被宣传为儿童奇幻小说，但很难预料孩子们会如何看待怀特笔下一些较为残酷的场景以及关于权力、命运、母性诱惑和忽视等更为严肃的主题，更不用说背叛和通奸了。怀特不仅将故事（亚瑟王传说）、历史（大量十二、十三世纪英国生活细节）、史诗、爱情和笑话融为一体，而且还在不同元素之间突然切换，语气也随之剧烈变化。有些角色以喜剧形象出现，例如佩利诺尔国王和梅林；另一些角色则以心理复杂、写实的形象出现，例如亚瑟王、格温娜维尔、兰斯洛特、高文和他的兄弟们。高文的母亲摩高斯有着童话故事中女巫般的外貌，但其内在本质却如同弗洛伊德小说中那个充满诱惑却又疏于管教的母亲。她过于复杂，无法简单地用邪恶来概括，但她对子女的影响却是毁灭性的、挥之不去的；通过他们，她影响了整个王国。

In addition, White had a strong interest in all forms of hunting and hawking, as well as in agriculture and natural history; much of the depiction of his English countryside is in objective, almost scientific, detail (fifty years after its publication, it is a catalog of a way of life lost and an ecosystem denuded by population growth and industrialization, one of White's themes). The Once and Future King is also a meditation upon conflict and war, upon the psychological links between childhood and adulthood, and upon the interactions of hatred, betrayal, courage, spiritual deprivation, and Fate. It uses every station on the clock except diary/letter and confession (it even explores, through the Lancelot and Guenever material, the pernicious but inevitable effects of gossip). It takes advantage of both the lighter and the darker ironies implicit in the contrast of romance and epic, on the one hand, with the realistic inconveniences of everyday life on the other. As befits a novel written at the nadir of the modern period, though, The Once and Future King expresses no faith in innocence or holy foolishness or the worth of good intentions. It shows that varied use of the different forms related to the novel makes a novel richer and more powerful. If a novelist can use them unapologetically and knowingly, giving the reader funny jokes and real information and a worthy romance and a true sense of the broader national concerns he is getting at, the reader will be willing to suspend disbelief and accept what on the surface might seem to be jarring tonal discontinuities.

此外，怀特对各种形式的狩猎和猎鹰活动，以及农业和自然史都抱有浓厚的兴趣；他对英国乡村的描绘大多客观细致，近乎科学（出版五十年后，这部作品已成为一部记录逝去生活方式和因人口增长和工业化而遭到破坏的生态系统的目录，这也是怀特的主题之一）。《永恒之王》也是一部关于冲突与战争、童年与成年之间的心理联系，以及仇恨、背叛、勇气、精神匮乏和命运之间相互作用的沉思录。它几乎运用了所有叙事手法，唯独日记/书信和忏悔除外（它甚至通过兰斯洛特和格温娜维尔的故事，探讨了流言蜚语的有害却又不可避免的影响）。它巧妙地运用了浪漫史诗与日常生活现实困境之间对比的讽刺意味，既有轻松的，也有阴暗的。然而，正如一部创作于现代文学低谷时期的小说所应有的那样，《永恒之王》对天真无邪、愚昧无知或善意的价值都毫无信仰。它表明，对小说各种形式的灵活运用能使小说更加丰富有力。如果一位小说家能够毫不掩饰、心领神会地运用这些形式，为读者呈现幽默的笑话、真实的信息、动人的爱情故事以及他所探讨的更广泛的国家议题，那么读者便愿意暂时放下怀疑，接受那些表面上看似突兀的语调断裂。

A tale is something that tellers and listeners agree, for the sake of entertainment, might have happened, but it always contains the possibility of impossibility—this is the charming hook upon which White hangs his novel, and also the reason it became an animated Disney feature, but the greatest example of an author using the tale form on this list is Franz Kafka's The Trial. Everything about Josef K.'s experience is mysterious and problematic. Who are the officials? Who sent them? What are the laws they are enforcing? Why do they act as they do? What is the meaning of their existence, or, indeed, of Josef's existence? Where does the action take place—a particular town (Prague, for example), a mythic town, or Josef K.'s mind? Josef's story is told in an objective and realistic way, as if this were not a tale but an example of a realistic novel, but the names and dates that would anchor it in the way that Middlemarch is anchored in the 1830s in the English Midlands are missing. The Trial also exploits the promise of the tale to be entertaining—it seems until the end to be a joke. Tricks are constantly being played on Josef K, and many of those around him think his situation is funny as well as worrisome. His dilemma is, indeed, intended to rouse a laugh, only not in Josef K., since he is the butt of the joke. The reader is not encouraged to be entirely sympathetic to him—as Josef addresses his dilemma, he sometimes acts unwisely or oddly, and the reader is allowed to think that she might have acted more intelligently or less neurotically in similar circumstances and thereby achieved a different outcome. Nor is Josef an epic hero. He does not typify his nation—we don't even know what his nation is; he never even tries to act courageously; all he wants is to do the proper thing and survive—he is too eager to subordinate himself to be the protagonist of an epic. Only insofar as the reader identifies with his helplessness is he allowed any tragic dimension at all. The important thing to remember about The Trial emerges as we look at our clock— without romance, without travel, without polemical anger, without analytical perspective, without even the introspection of a diary or a confession, Josef K. is a hapless modern man, bereft of all the resources the novel has to offer against the meaningless workings of mechanical modernity.

故事是讲述者和听众为了娱乐而共同认可的、可能发生过的事情，但它总是包含着不可能的可能性——这正是怀特的小说引人入胜之处，也是它被改编成迪士尼动画长片的原因。不过，这份榜单上运用故事形式的最佳范例当属弗朗茨·卡夫卡的《审判》。约瑟夫·K的经历充满了神秘和疑点。官员是谁？是谁派他们来的？他们执行的是什么法律？他们为何如此行事？他们的存在意义何在？约瑟夫的存在意义又是什么？故事发生在何处——某个具体的城市（例如布拉格）、一个虚构的城镇，还是约瑟夫·K的内心世界？约瑟夫的故事以客观写实的方式讲述，仿佛这不是一个故事，而是一部现实主义小说。然而，书中缺少了那些能将故事与19世纪30年代的英格兰中部地区联系起来的人名和日期，就像《米德尔马契》那样将故事牢牢地锚定在了那里。 《审判》也巧妙地利用了故事本身的娱乐性——直到结尾，它似乎都是一个笑话。约瑟夫·K不断遭遇各种诡计，他周围的许多人都觉得他的处境既滑稽又令人担忧。他的困境的确意在博人一笑，只不过笑点不在约瑟夫·K身上，因为他才是被嘲笑的对象。读者并非被引导去完全同情他——在约瑟夫应对困境的过程中，他有时会做出不明智或怪异的举动，这让读者不禁思考，如果自己身处类似的境地，或许会采取更明智或更少神经质的行动，从而得到不同的结果。约瑟夫也不是史诗英雄。他并不代表他的国家——我们甚至不知道他属于哪个国家；他从未尝试过勇敢行事；他只想做正确的事，活下去——他太渴望屈从于他人，以至于无法成为史诗的主角。只有当读者认同他的无助时，他才被赋予了悲剧色彩。当我们审视时钟时，《审判》这部作品最关键的一点便显露出来——没有浪漫，没有旅行，没有激烈的争论，没有分析的视角，甚至没有日记或忏悔式的内省，约瑟夫·K只是一个不幸的现代人，他失去了小说所能提供的所有资源，来对抗机械现代性毫无意义的运作。

∗ In the second volume of Don Quixote , Quixote is the object of an elaborate and cruel practical joke that puts him in a situation similar to that of Josef K. Nothing Quixote can think of or do seems to untangle the confusion, and his humiliation has a ready audience in the duke, the duchess, and their retainers. Quixote, though, is an epic hero with a firm set of beliefs in medieval romantic ideals of chastity, generosity, courage, and faith. He attempts to adhere to his ideals throughout his ordeal, and the reader is a witness to both sides of the equation—the elaboration and enjoyment of the ruse by the duke and the duchess and the growing confusion, and then, it seems, despair, on the part of Quixote. He has what Josef K. does not have— a worldview to fall back upon—and it has been learned from literature. Even when this worldview does not work as a formula for fruitful action or as a picture of the world Quixote lives in, it does sustain Quixote's sense of who he is. He does not die meaninglessly and alone, as Josef K. does, but in his own bed, in the company of well-wishers. Don Quixote partakes of many of the contributory narrative forms—tale, joke, confession, and even essaylike discourses on various subjects are folded into a travel narrative, a history, a biography, an epic, and a romance. The two volumes of the novel seem to encompass the world of the late sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries partly because they encompass nine of our twelve narrative forms.

在《堂吉诃德》第二卷中，堂吉诃德成了精心策划的残酷恶作剧的对象，陷入了与约瑟夫·K类似的困境。堂吉诃德绞尽脑汁，却始终无法摆脱困境，而他的屈辱也得到了公爵、公爵夫人及其随从的围观。然而，堂吉诃德是一位史诗英雄，他坚定地信奉中世纪浪漫主义的理想，例如贞洁、慷慨、勇气和信仰。在整个磨难中，他都努力坚守这些理想。读者得以见证事情的两面：公爵和公爵夫人精心策划并享受着这场骗局，而堂吉诃德则逐渐陷入困惑，最终似乎走向绝望。他拥有约瑟夫·K所不具备的东西——一个可以依靠的世界观——而这世界观正是从文学中习得的。即使这种世界观并非行之有效的行动指南，也无法描绘堂吉诃德所处世界的全貌，它却维系着堂吉诃德的自我认知。他不像约瑟夫·K那样孤独无助地死去，而是安详地躺在自己的床上，在亲友的陪伴下离世。《堂吉诃德》融合了多种叙事形式——故事、笑话、忏悔，甚至散文式的论述，巧妙地融入了游记、历史、传记、史诗和浪漫故事之中。这部小说的两卷似乎囊括了十六世纪末至十七世纪初的世界，部分原因在于它包含了我们所知的十二种叙事形式中的九种。

That A Tale of Two Cities (travel, history, tale, joke, polemic, epic, romance) is meant as a tale is evident by the use of the word “tale” in the title rather than, say, “history” or “story.” A tale is meant to be entertaining, and Dickens's tale is—it is full of adventure and excitement—but a tale also can always be cautionary in a way that a story or a history cannot be because a tale is traditionally used as an exemplum or parable. Dickens intended his fellow Englishmen to understand that they could still be forced to learn the lesson of the French Revolution if the bureaucracy (the Circumlocution Office in Bleak House) and the aristocracy (Lord and Lady Dedlock, also in Bleak House) did not mend their methods of governing. All of Dickens's writing during and for many years after the Crimean War ( 1853 – 56 ) partook of the disgust and contempt he felt for the English Parliament, English bureaucracy, and the English class system. In one letter he wrote during that war, he seemed to think that even his eloquence (which he himself considered “inimitable”) could not express the depths of incompetence and venality to which the government had sunk. The tale form enabled him to wed polemic and entertainment and excused him from the realistic requirements of detailed, plausible cause and effect (which can give the reader a chance to disagree with the author's arguments and make up her own mind). Dickens was no advocate of revolution; in A Tale of Two Cities he sets forth his nonrevolutionary critique of European society. But he does not use analysis. Instead, he weds techniques typical of the tale—the way, for example, that characters such as Madame De-farge, Dr. Manette, and The Vengeance act in a repetitive, dreamlike manner—to the impassioned eloquence characteristic of the polemic.

《双城记》（游记、历史、故事、笑话、论战、史诗、爱情）显然是以故事的形式呈现，这一点从标题中使用“故事”（tale）而非“历史”（history）或“故事”（story）等词语便可见一斑。故事旨在娱乐大众，狄更斯的这部作品也不例外——它充满了冒险和刺激——但故事也总能起到警示作用，这是历史或故事所无法做到的，因为故事传统上被用作典范或寓言。狄更斯意在让他的英国同胞明白，如果官僚机构（如《荒凉山庄》中的迂回办公室）和贵族阶层（如同样出自《荒凉山庄》的戴德洛克勋爵和夫人）不改进他们的治理方式，他们仍然可能被迫吸取法国大革命的教训。狄更斯在克里米亚战争（1853-1856）期间及战后多年创作的所有作品，都体现了他对英国议会、官僚机构和阶级制度的厌恶和蔑视。在他战争期间写的一封信中，他似乎认为，即便他自认为“无人能及”的雄辩，也无法表达政府堕落到何种程度的无能和贪婪。小说这种形式使他能够将论战与娱乐结合起来，也使他不必拘泥于详尽、合情合理的因果关系（这会让读者有机会质疑作者的观点，并形成自己的判断）。狄更斯并非革命的拥护者；在《双城记》中，他阐述了自己对欧洲社会的非革命性批判。但他并没有运用分析。相反，他将故事中典型的技巧——例如，德法日夫人、马内特医生和复仇女神等人物以重复的、梦幻般的方式行事——与论战中特有的热情雄辩结合起来。

In the Evrmonde brothers, the father and uncle of Charles Darnay, he gives us a pair of rapists, murderers, and thieves who are callous, cruel, and scheming, but he gives their crimes a folktalelike atmosphere (late at night in the castle, the young girl dies). When Darnay's uncle is murdered, he even turns into a monster, through the association of his death mask with the castle gargoyles. That Madame Defarge, the sister of the raped girl, and her husband should not only hate the brothers but also desire to torture and kill them is the most natural thing in the world, but gradually Madame Defarge, too, becomes a monster. By contrast, we have the tale of Sydney Carton, who begins as a realistic English type of idle young man of good education and bad habits. Through his love for Lucie he is transformed into a saint, and his execution in place of Darnay is explicitly narrated as a reenactment of the Crucifixion.

在查尔斯·达内（Charles Darnay）的父亲和叔叔埃弗蒙德兄弟身上，作者塑造了一对冷酷无情、阴险狡诈的强奸犯、杀人犯和窃贼，但他却赋予他们的罪行一种民间故事般的氛围（深夜，在城堡里，年轻的女孩死去）。当达内的叔叔被谋杀后，他甚至变成了一个怪物，因为他的死亡面具与城堡里的石像鬼产生了联系。被强奸女孩的姐姐德法奇夫人和她的丈夫不仅憎恨这对兄弟，而且渴望折磨并杀死他们，这在世上是最自然不过的事情，但德法奇夫人也逐渐变成了一个怪物。与之形成鲜明对比的是西德尼·卡顿（Sydney Carton）的故事，他最初是一个典型的英国式游手好闲、受过良好教育却生活不良的年轻人。他对露西（Lucie）的爱使他蜕变为圣人，他代替达内被处决的情节被明确地描述为耶稣受难的重现。

Polemics must be eloquent, and it is through an eloquence that is almost incantatory that Dickens addresses the challenge of depicting collective emotions and class warfare. Every novel about class conflict or mass movement is at a disadvantage, because a scene that a film, for example, could effectively put on the screen for a few moments—a rioting crowd or an attacking army—the novelist must string out word by word. To handle this challenge, Dickens uses metaphorical language energized by anger. When he introduces the depredations of the aristocracy, he portrays “Monseigneur,” who requires numberless servants merely to serve him his chocolate. “Monseigneur” represents, by synecdoche, the corrupt luxury of the ruling class. When, in the next chapter, Monseigneur goes to his country estate, Dickens describes the landscape: “A beautiful landscape, with the corn bright in it, but not abundant. Patches of poor rye where corn should have been, patches of poor peas and beans, patches of most coarse vegetable substitutes for wheat. On inanimate nature, as on the men and women who cultivated it, a prevalent tendency towards an appearance of vegetating unwillingly—a dejected disposition to give up, and wither away” (p. 103 ). Toward the end, when Lucie is living in Paris, she watches some women dance the carmagnole. Dickens's description conveys his views about the revolutionaries:

论战必须雄辩有力，而狄更斯正是凭借着近乎吟诵般的雄辩，应对了描绘集体情感和阶级斗争的挑战。每一部描写阶级冲突或群众运动的小说都处于劣势，因为电影只需几分钟就能有效地呈现的场景——例如暴乱的人群或进攻的军队——小说家却必须逐字逐句地细细描绘。为了应对这一挑战，狄更斯运用了充满愤怒的隐喻语言。当他揭露贵族的暴行时，他塑造了“先生”这一形象，这位先生需要无数仆人伺候他，仅仅是为了给他端上巧克力。“先生”通过提喻手法，象征着统治阶级腐败奢靡的生活方式。在下一章中，当蒙塞尼厄前往他的乡间庄园时，狄更斯这样描述那里的景色：“风景优美，玉米长势喜人，但并不丰收。本该是玉米的地方却长着稀疏的黑麦，豌豆和豆角也长得稀疏，小麦则被各种粗糙的蔬菜所取代。无论是自然界还是耕耘它的人们，都普遍呈现出一种不情愿地萎靡不振的姿态——一种沮丧的、想要放弃、想要枯萎的心态”（第103页）。临近结尾，露西住在巴黎时，她看到一些女人跳卡马尼奥舞。狄更斯的这段描写传达了他对革命者的看法：

They danced to the popular Revolution song, keeping a ferocious time that was like a gnashing of teeth in unison. Men and women danced together, women danced together, men danced together, as hazard had brought them together. At first, they were a mere storm of coarse red caps and coarse woollen rags; but, as they filled the place, and stopped to dance about Lucie, some ghastly apparition of a dance-figure gone raving mad arose among them. They advanced, retreated, struck at one another's hands, clutched at one another's heads, spun round alone, caught one another and spun round in pairs, until many of them dropped. While those were down, the rest linked hand in hand, and all spun round together: then the ring broke, and in separate rings of two and four they turned and turned until they all stopped at once, began again, struck, clutched, and tore, and then reversed the spin, and all spun round another way. Suddenly they stopped again, paused, struck out the time afresh, formed into lines the width of the public way, and, with their heads low down and their hands high up, swooped screaming off. No fight could have been half so terrible as this dance. It was so emphatically a fallen sport— a something, once innocent, delivered over to all devilry—a healthy pastime changed into a means of angering the blood, bewildering the senses, and steeling the heart. [Book 3 , chapter 5 ]

他们伴着那首流行的革命歌曲翩翩起舞，节奏狂野而齐齐，如同咬牙切齿。男男女女一起跳舞，女人一起跳舞，男人一起跳舞，仿佛命运将他们聚集到了一起。起初，他们只是一团粗糙的红帽子和破烂的羊毛衣衫；但当他们挤满了场地，停下来围绕着露西跳舞时，人群中出现了一个可怕的、疯狂的舞者幻影。他们前进，后退，互相击打对方的手，抓住对方的头，独自旋转，互相抓住对方，两人一组旋转，直到许多人倒下。倒下的人，其余的人手拉手，一起旋转：然后圆圈散开，他们分成两人一组、四人一组，不停地旋转，直到所有人同时停下，然后又重新开始，击打、抓住、撕扯，然后反向旋转，所有人又以另一种方式旋转起来。他们突然又停了下来，停顿片刻，重新划出节奏，排成与人行道一样宽的队伍，低着头，高举着双手，尖叫着冲了出去。任何战斗都比不上这场舞蹈的恐怖。这完全是一种堕落的运动——曾经纯洁无瑕，如今却沦为魔鬼的玩意儿——一种健康的消遣变成了激怒血液、迷惑感官、磨砺意志的手段。[第三卷，第五章]

The requirements of the polemic demand emotional intensity, and emotional intensity can be achieved with highly figurative language. Dickens had an analysis—he got it from Thomas Carlyle's history of the French Revolution. But the success of A Tale of Two Cities as a depiction of the nature of revolutions depends on the narrative tools he gained from the use of the tale and the polemic and how he meshed them with his more typical use of joke, romance, epic, travel, and history.

论战需要强烈的情感，而强烈的情感可以通过高度比喻性的语言来实现。狄更斯对此有所分析——他从托马斯·卡莱尔的法国大革命史中汲取了灵感。但《双城记》作为对革命本质的刻画之所以成功，取决于他从故事和论战中汲取的叙事技巧，以及他如何将这些技巧与他更常用的幽默、浪漫、史诗、游记和历史等元素融合在一起。

An author with a different, nonpolemical temperament, such as Ivan Turgenev, may write a political novel that has a polemical story but not a polemical effect. Turgenev's Fathers and Sons (biography, tale, gossip, essay, romance) takes up political issues that were current in Russia and Europe in the 1850s , while he was writing the novel— scientific objectivity versus Romanticism. He views them through the lens of the generation gap, but the effect of Fathers and Sons is not so much to press an agenda as to weigh the advantages and disadvantages of several agendas and then leave the question open.

像伊万·屠格涅夫这样性情迥异、不喜争论的作家，或许会创作一部情节充满争议却不具争议性的政治小说。屠格涅夫的《父与子》（一部融合了传记、故事、闲谈、散文和爱情元素的小说）探讨了19世纪50年代俄国和欧洲的政治热点问题——科学客观性与浪漫主义的冲突。他从代沟的角度审视这些问题，但《父与子》的最终目的并非强加某种政治观点，而是权衡各种观点的利弊，最终留下一个开放式的答案。

Turgenev pretends at the beginning that his story is a simple one; indeed, it has the light, self-contained tone of a tale, never the ponderous, exhaustive air of a history. A young man leaves the university and returns to the family estate. He brings with him his best friend. The first young man is an easygoing, good-looking, and rather immature fellow, but much beloved by his father and his uncle. The second is what we might call “a brain.” He has been a brilliant student and he holds the newest German theories, but one of his theories is that all allegiances, and even affections, are suspect. No one of the older generation quite knows what to make of this second young man. When he visits his own parents, they are affectionate, but nevertheless he is estranged from them—he seems to be cold by nature. Ultimately he offends his friend's uncle (an aging exponent of European Romanticism), and the uncle challenges him to a duel, which they fight. The uncle is injured, but more than that, embarrassed.

屠格涅夫在故事开头假装故事很简单；的确，它有着轻松自在的叙事风格，而非历史著作那种沉重冗长的笔调。一个年轻人离开大学，回到家族庄园。他带回了自己的挚友。第一个年轻人性格随和，相貌英俊，略显稚嫩，却深受父亲和叔叔的喜爱。第二个年轻人则堪称“才子”。他曾是一位才华横溢的学生，掌握着最新的德国理论，但他的理论之一是：一切忠诚，甚至情感，都值得怀疑。老一辈人对这个年轻人感到困惑不解。当他回娘家探望父母时，父母对他很亲切，但他却与他们疏远——他似乎天性冷漠。最终，他得罪了朋友的叔叔（一位年迈的欧洲浪漫主义拥护者），叔叔向他发起决斗，两人应战。叔叔受伤了，但更重要的是，他感到很尴尬。

There are also sisters and mothers in the novel. The two young men are intrigued by a beautiful woman, an example of an independent “new” woman, so the novel takes up the concerns of romance, but the beautiful woman proves more than either of them can handle. The brilliant young man falls for her, but his affections are unrequited, because she is not interested in giving up her freedom. The brilliant young man dies. The first young man falls in love with the younger sister of the “new woman,” and the last scene of the novel is their marriage feast, which takes place on the estate where the father has also married his mistress, a local girl who had borne him a son. The last scene presents a pastoral vision of integrated family happiness and strong but courteous affections.
