All of the characters still living at the end are the feckless ones, the ones motivated primarily by attachment to each other, to the estate, and to doing things more or less as they have always been done, and they are happy enough. They miss the stricter and more ideological characters, but only in an abstract way—their comfort isn't much mitigated by the events of the novel, sad as those might be.

小说中也有姐妹和母亲的形象。两位年轻男子被一位美丽的女子所吸引，她是一位独立自主的“新女性”的典范，因此小说探讨了爱情的主题，但这位美丽的女子却让他们难以招架。才华横溢的年轻人爱上了她，但他的爱慕却得不到回应，因为她不愿放弃自己的自由。这位才华横溢的年轻人最终去世。另一位年轻人爱上了这位“新女性”的妹妹，小说的最后一幕是他们的婚宴，宴会在父亲娶了情妇——一位为他生了儿子的当地女子——的庄园举行。最后一幕展现了一幅田园牧歌般的景象：家庭和睦幸福，彼此间深厚而又彬彬有礼的感情。所有活到最后的角色都是些不思进取的人，他们的主要动力是彼此的依恋、对庄园的眷恋以及墨守成规，但他们也过得相当幸福。他们怀念那些更严厉、更有意识形态的人物，但只是在抽象意义上的怀念——小说中的事件，尽管令人悲伤，并不会大大减轻他们的这种感受。

Fathers and Sons is more analytical than any of our other political novels. Each advocate of an ideological position is unsympathetic in some way. The brilliant young man seems to have only the coldest of feelings—any sort of connection is anathema to him, even the connection he feels toward the beautiful, self-possessed woman. The Romantic uncle is clearly old, prissy, and outdated. He may represent passion, but it is the passion of resentment rather than desire. In the end, simple family feeling papers over the differences, which are not resolved, either between the characters or in the author's analysis. To a more ideological writer, such as Dostoevsky, who disliked Turgenev, it must have seemed as if Turgenev came to no conclusion at all. But to modern readers, used to the brutal effects of competing ideologies, Turgenev's conclusion may seem to have the charm of perennial verity—even though the problems of the nation cannot be solved, with a little bit of luck, families can live, reproduce, and enjoy one another. Fathers and Sons uses the methods of realism, but its talelike qualities rob it of any sort of bombast; it offers entertainment first and enlightenment only if the reader can understand the subtler implications of the characters’ thoughts, actions, and relationships. It is a political novel with tact, content to offer observations rather than a program.

《父与子》比我们其他任何政治小说都更具分析性。每一种意识形态的拥护者都以某种方式令人难以产生共鸣。那位才华横溢的年轻人似乎只有最冷漠的情感——任何形式的联系对他来说都是令人厌恶的，即使是他对那位美丽而沉稳的女性产生的感情也不例外。那位浪漫的叔叔显然老态龙钟、古板守旧。他或许代表着激情，但那是一种怨恨而非欲望的激情。最终，简单的亲情掩盖了人物之间以及作者分析中始终未解决的分歧。对于像陀思妥耶夫斯基这样更倾向于意识形态的作家（他不喜欢屠格涅夫）来说，屠格涅夫似乎根本没有得出任何结论。但对于习惯了意识形态冲突带来的残酷后果的现代读者来说，屠格涅夫的结论或许具有一种永恒真理的魅力——即使国家问题无法解决，只要稍加幸运，家庭就能生存、繁衍并享受彼此的陪伴。 《父与子》运用了现实主义手法，但其叙事风格却使其摒弃了任何浮夸之感；它首先提供的是娱乐，只有当读者能够理解人物思想、行为和关系中更为微妙的含义时，才能从中获得启迪。这是一部手法巧妙的政治小说，它满足于提出观察而非纲领。

Some novels use the private stations of our clock as models, and one of my favorite early ones is The Expedition of Humphry Clinker , Tobias Smollett's 1771 epistolary novel (travel, joke, gossip, diary/letter, polemic, confession, romance). Diaries and letters share the quality of immediacy—as the action is unfolding, the narrator writes what is happening without knowing how it is going to turn out. This can seem artificial, which is probably one reason that the epistolary novel has more or less died out—modern readers are likely to suspend disbelief in many volumes of Proustian introspection without needing the added frame of letters or entries with dates and reasons for writing. Even so, Humphry Clinker is well worth reading. It relies on the perfectly natural combination of travel narrative and diary/letter. Five characters—a middle-aged man who is ailing; his sister, with whom he does not get along; their nephew, who has just finished university; their niece, who is just finishing her schooling, too; and the sister's maidservant—embark upon a tour of the spas of England. Each has a correspondent back home, so the sights and adventures of the journey are reported variously by the five letter writers, each of whom characterizes himself or herself, gossips about the others, and sees what the others don't see. Like Sterne and Fielding, Smollett had an earthy sense of humor and a full complement of pet peeves. The polemical edge comes in the letters of Matthew Bramble, the squire who is financing the tour for the sake of his health—Matthew doesn't like much of what he sees on his journey. Even so, the conceit of having five disparate letter writers allows the novel to add up analytically to a less grumpy and polemical whole. Uncle Matthew may be right about many things, but the more exuberant voices of the other characters, and the action (three weddings in the end, and a healthy acceptance of the joys of sexuality) contradict his dark view. Humphry himself, a manservant Matthew hires early in the journey, turns out not to be a character as much as a catalyst for Matthew's redemption. The Expedition of Humphry Clinker is a rare example of an author using the forms of diary/letter, polemic, joke, and gossip to generate, in effect, travel narrative, analysis, history, and biography (with some good romance thrown in), and it has the charm of novelty.

有些小说以我们日常生活的点滴为蓝本，我最喜欢的早期作品之一是托比亚斯·斯莫利特1771年的书信体小说《汉弗莱·克林克的远征》（融合了旅行、笑话、闲聊、日记/书信、论战、忏悔和浪漫元素）。日记和书信都具有一种即时性——随着事件的展开，叙述者记录下正在发生的事情，却并不知道最终的结局。这种手法有时会显得刻意，这或许也是书信体小说逐渐式微的原因之一——现代读者往往能够接受普鲁斯特式的长篇内省，而无需借助书信或带有日期和写作原因的条目作为框架。即便如此，《汉弗莱·克林克的远征》仍然值得一读。它巧妙地结合了旅行叙事和日记/书信，浑然天成。小说的五个主要人物分别是：一位体弱多病的中年男子；与他关系不睦的妹妹；他们的侄子刚从大学毕业，侄女也即将毕业，还有姐姐的女仆——三人踏上了英格兰温泉之旅。他们各自在家乡都有一位通讯员，因此，旅途中的所见所闻和奇遇便由这五位写信人以不同的视角呈现。每个人都刻画了自己的性格，议论着其他人，并看到了其他人看不到的东西。和斯特恩、菲尔丁一样，斯莫利特也拥有朴实的幽默感和一连串令人恼火的小癖好。马修·布兰布尔的信件则更具争议性，这位乡绅为了健康而资助了这次旅行——马修对旅途中所见的很多东西都不太满意。即便如此，五位性格迥异的写信人这一设定，使得整部小说在分析层面上呈现出一种不那么愤世嫉俗和充满争议的整体效果。马修叔叔或许在很多方面都说得对，但其他角色更加热情洋溢的言辞，以及故事的情节发展（最后三场婚礼，以及对性爱乐趣的健康接纳）都与他阴郁的观点相悖。汉弗莱本人，马修在旅途初期雇佣的男仆，与其说是一个人物，不如说是马修救赎的催化剂。《汉弗莱·克林克的探险》是一部罕见的佳作，作者巧妙地运用日记/书信、论战、笑话和闲聊等多种形式，创作出一部集旅行叙事、分析、历史和传记于一体的作品（其中还穿插了一些浪漫爱情故事），并因此散发出一种新颖的魅力。

At first glance, John Updike's stories about Henry Bech, his literary alter ego, seem like a polemical joke—that is, a satire. Bech's motives are always selfish and fearful. He is lusty but has no taste for reciprocal relationships; he uses literary contacts only to advance his own status; his work is precious to him, but only insofar as it once raised his status or lowered it—he doesn't have much attachment to what he has written or the act of writing it because it doesn't express any ideas or feelings he is committed to. He is full of envy, resentment, self-pity, and a sort of craven awareness of his needs that passes for self-knowledge. In his view, no one on the literary scene is any different. The literary world is divided into fools and knaves—silly women who respect him because they don't know any better are marginally less interesting than smart women who have his number but sleep with him anyway. Men in general are mostly uninteresting or vaguely threatening (until the end, when he decides to revenge himself upon reviewers who have failed to appreciate him over the years). Literary accomplishment is a farce—when Bech becomes president of a famous literary organization he had once respected, he sees all the members as eccentric has-beens and disbands the organization in order to sell the expensive real estate it owns.

乍看之下，约翰·厄普代克笔下以亨利·贝克（他的文学化身）为主角的故事，似乎是一个带有讽刺意味的玩笑。贝克的动机总是自私而恐惧的。他好色，却对互惠互利的关系毫无兴趣；他利用文坛人脉只是为了提升自己的地位；他的作品对他而言弥足珍贵，但这种珍贵仅仅体现在作品曾经提升或降低过他的地位——他对自己写的东西，或者写作本身，并没有多少感情，因为这些作品并没有表达他所认同的任何思想或情感。他充满了嫉妒、怨恨、自怜，以及一种卑鄙的、自以为是的自我认知。在他看来，文坛上的人都一样。文坛分为傻瓜和骗子——那些因为不懂事而尊敬他的愚蠢女人，远不如那些明知他底细却依然与他上床的聪明女人有趣。总的来说，男性角色大多乏味无趣，或者隐隐透着威胁感（直到最后，他决定报复那些多年来未能赏识他的评论家）。文学成就不过是一场闹剧——当贝克成为他曾经尊敬的一个著名文学组织的会长时，他却把所有成员都视为古怪的过气人物，最终解散了该组织，以便出售其名下价值不菲的房产。

And yet Updike's Bech stories are much more fun than Vanity Fair , no doubt because Updike's own narrative presence offers an alternative to Bech—because we are aware of Updike observing Bech, the stories become a kind of confession. Bech is Updike's alter ego, but so is Updike Bech's alter ego. Bech is sour, but on the evidence of Updike's style in writing about Bech (pointed but good-natured), Updike is not sour. Bech thinks of no one but himself, but Updike's detailed observations and clear, smooth style show that he thinks not only of Bech, but also of all the women and men Bech meets. Bech's life is one humiliation after another (since even success is some form of humiliation), but Updike makes it clear that it is Bech's own perception that is seeing humiliation where it doesn't exist. For Bech, everything is a personal insult. For Updike, the literary world is large and impersonal. Forces that seem directed at Bech are just the natural ebb and flow of age, time, and circumstance. In one early story, Bech goes to a women's college in the Virginia countryside (travel narrative). He can't take the natural fertility of the campus, and he suffers existential vertigo at not being the center of the universe. Updike beautifully renders the flowers, trees, weather, and lawns that torment Bech, in all their normal, impersonal beauty. They do not torment Updike. He feels comfortable with them, and yet he is no less precise in describing Bech's discomfort.

然而，厄普代克的贝克故事远比《名利场》有趣得多，这无疑是因为厄普代克自身的叙述视角为贝克提供了一种替代——因为我们意识到厄普代克在观察贝克，这些故事便成了一种忏悔。贝克是厄普代克的另一个自我，而厄普代克也是贝克的另一个自我。贝克性格阴郁，但从厄普代克描写贝克的风格（尖锐却不失善意）来看，厄普代克本人却并不阴郁。贝克眼里只有自己，但厄普代克细致入微的观察和清晰流畅的文风表明，他不仅关注贝克，也关注贝克遇到的所有男男女女。贝克的一生充满了屈辱（因为即使是成功也是一种屈辱），但厄普代克明确指出，是贝克自身的感知让他看到了并不存在的屈辱。对贝克来说，一切都是对他个人的侮辱。对厄普代克而言，文学世界广阔而冷漠。那些看似针对贝克的种种力量，不过是岁月、时光和境遇的自然潮起潮落。在他早期的一篇小说中，贝克前往弗吉尼亚乡村的一所女子学院（游记）。他无法适应校园里自然的丰饶，并因不再是宇宙的中心而感到一种存在主义式的眩晕。厄普代克以细腻的笔触描绘了那些令贝克备受煎熬的花草树木、天气和草坪，展现了它们平凡而冷漠的美。这些景物本身并不令厄普代克感到痛苦。他与它们相处融洽，却依然精准地刻画了贝克的不安。

The disjuncture between Updike and Bech is funny (making use of the joke category) and stays funny from the beginning to the end of The Complete Henry Bech. As Bech becomes more outrageous, Updike becomes more daring, and this daring is thrilling, an example of authorial virtuosity that the reader can't help finding enlivening. For Updike, the Bech stories are a mock history, a mock biography, and a mock confession—how would he render so well all of Bech's craven feelings and impulses if he had never experienced them? But they are an essay, too, on how the literary life works, and this analytical component comes from the witty separation between author and character. And they are gossip—the reader can't help being aware that what Updike knows about being a Jewish writer he learned from talking to and about Jewish writers. And then, in the end, when it seems almost too late, Bech gets to have a romance—though not, as might have been expected, with a wife or a lover (he is too jaded and selfish for that). He disdains women too habitually to reform, but he has a baby girl at last, and his final appearance (in front of the Nobel committee, of course) is not about self, lust, or prizes, it is about the little girl speaking and Bech's honest pleasure, after seventy years, in someone other than himself.

厄普代克和贝克之间的这种脱节本身就很有趣（此处运用了“笑话”一词），而且从《亨利·贝克全集》的开头到结尾都贯穿着这种趣味。随着贝克变得越来越离经叛道，厄普代克也变得越来越大胆，而这种大胆令人兴奋，展现了作者精湛的技艺，让读者不禁感到振奋。对厄普代克而言，贝克的故事既是一部戏仿的历史，又是一部戏仿的传记，还是一份戏仿的忏悔录——如果他从未亲身经历过贝克那些卑劣的情感和冲动，又怎能如此精准地描绘出来呢？但这些故事同时也是一篇关于文学生活运作方式的随笔，而这种分析性的成分正是源于作者与人物之间巧妙的分离。此外，它们也带有八卦色彩——读者不禁会意识到，厄普代克对犹太作家身份的了解，正是通过与犹太作家们的交流以及谈论他们而获得的。最后，就在一切似乎都为时已晚的时候，贝克终于迎来了一段恋情——尽管并非如人们所料，是与妻子或情人（他太过愤世嫉俗和自私，无法接受那样的爱情）。他根深蒂固地鄙视女性，难以改变，但他最终还是有了一个女儿。他最后一次露面（当然是在诺贝尔奖委员会面前）并非为了自我、欲望或奖项，而是为了小女孩的讲述，以及贝克在七十年后，终于从他人身上感受到的真挚喜悦。

Italo Svevo's Zeno's Conscience (history, joke, gossip, confession, essay, epic, romance) shows, like the Bech stories, that confession requires a light touch. Zeno's Conscience is, ostensibly, the psychoanalytic notes of a prominent businesssman from Trieste, which have been gathered and are being published as an act of revenge by his analyst, who writes an introduction. The reader quickly forgets this conceit because Zeno's voice is more charming and more arresting than the voice of the vengeful psychoanalyst. When, at the end of the novel, Zeno decides that he does not want to be cured, the reader can only agree. Nevertheless, the use of psychoanalysis as a conceit sets up Zeno's confessions as an organized contemplation not only of who he is and what he has done, but also of his wife and her family, his business, and the way life works (or worked before the First World War) in Trieste, which is not quite Italian but not quite central European, either. Zeno does not order his confession chronologically, but in terms of the importance of his problems. Ironically, his least important problem, trying to quit smoking, is also his most difficult. His greatest problem (he says) is that he was cajoled, or maybe tricked, into marrying his wife, who was exactly the one sister of four he did not want to marry. But his confessions prove to him that his marriage is satisfying in a lot of ways, and that if his life had worked out as he originally planned, it would have been much worse.

伊塔洛·斯韦沃的《泽诺的良心》（历史、笑话、八卦、忏悔录、散文、史诗、爱情小说）与贝克的故事一样，都表明忏悔需要轻描淡写。表面上，《泽诺的良心》是一位来自的里雅斯特的著名商人的精神分析笔记，这些笔记被他的心理分析师收集起来并出版，作为报复之举。这位分析师还为本书撰写了序言。然而，读者很快就会忘记这种故弄玄虚，因为泽诺的声音比那位心怀复仇的心理分析师的声音更迷人、更引人入胜。当小说结尾泽诺决定不接受治疗时，读者也只能表示赞同。然而，运用精神分析这一概念，使得泽诺的忏悔录成为他对自身身份和所作所为的系统性思考，不仅包括对自身身份和所作所为的反思，还包括对妻子及其家庭、事业以及的里雅斯特（这座城市既非纯粹的意大利，也非纯粹的中欧）生活方式的反思。泽诺的忏悔录并非按时间顺序排列，而是按照问题的重要性排序。讽刺的是，他最不重要的问题——戒烟——却也是他最难解决的问题。他自称最大的问题是，他被哄骗，或许是被欺骗，娶了妻子——而她恰好是他最不想娶的四个姐妹中唯一的一个。但他的忏悔录也让他意识到，他的婚姻在很多方面都令他感到满意，而且如果他的人生真的按照最初的计划发展，情况会糟糕得多。

Not many of our novels are confessions, because confession is the hardest form to pull off. Most authors choose to examine the consciences of others, and, given the pleasures of gossip, most readers are content to collude in this idea. This is the formal bargain of the usual type of novel—author and reader will stand a bit to the side of the characters and observe them, inwardly and outwardly, and will agree to pretend that the characters are not the author and his friends. Successful observation requires detachment, and the reward of successful observation is new knowledge. Overt confession places a rhetorical burden on the author not to embarrass himself and a social burden on the reader not to be aroused to disgust, dislike, or boredom. Both Updike and Svevo show that the author can preempt the reader's possibly negative reaction to the confession mode by exercising detachment right at the beginning, by showing that the confession is above all an exercise in analysis and history, forms that require detachment and an objective tone. Updike, of course, exercises detachment by naming his negativity “Bech.” Svevo exercises his detachment by confessing his most trivial but besetting sin first, and only then going on to concerns that have greater moral complexity.

我们的小说中很少有忏悔录，因为忏悔是最难驾驭的文体。大多数作者选择审视他人的良知，而鉴于八卦的乐趣，大多数读者也乐于接受这种做法。这是通常小说形式的约定——作者和读者都与人物保持一定的距离，观察他们的内心世界和外在表现，并同意假装这些人物并非作者及其朋友。成功的观察需要超脱，而成功观察的回报则是新的认知。公开的忏悔给作者带来了修辞上的负担，以免让自己难堪；也给读者带来了社会上的负担，以免引起厌恶、反感或厌倦。厄普代克和斯韦沃都表明，作者可以通过在故事伊始就保持超脱来预先消除读者对忏悔模式可能产生的负面反应，即表明忏悔首先是一种分析和历史的练习，而这两种形式都需要超脱和客观的语气。当然，厄普代克通过把自己的消极情绪命名为“贝克”来展现超脱。斯韦沃则通过先坦白自己最微不足道但却困扰着他的罪过，然后再去探讨那些具有更复杂道德意义的问题，来展现他的超脱。

Now, obviously, both of these confessions are conceits. They are not the actual confessions of John Updike and Ettore Schmitz (Svevo's real name), but the conceit is useful for smuggling in real contemplation of real feelings and events. For the novelist's purposes, the form of the confession is as difficult as real confession—he still has to make his confessing character attractive enough to beguile the reader into continuing to read. Zeno persuades us of his sincerity by telling tales upon himself in which his faults are displayed, by lamenting his faults, and by showing his loving relationship with his wife. In the course of his confession—that is, of portraying himself and his relationships—he also constructs a social history of his place (Trieste) and his class (wealthy merchants) in the pre–World War I era.

显然，这两段忏悔都是虚构的。它们并非约翰·厄普代克和埃托雷·施密茨（斯韦沃的真名）的真实忏悔，但这种虚构手法巧妙地将对真实情感和事件的思考融入其中。对小说家而言，忏悔的形式与真实的忏悔一样困难——他仍然需要让忏悔者足够吸引人，才能让读者继续阅读下去。泽诺通过讲述自己的故事来展现他的缺点，通过哀叹自己的缺点，并通过展现他与妻子的恩爱关系，来使我们相信他的真诚。在他的忏悔过程中——也就是在描绘自己和人际关系的过程中——他还构建了第一次世界大战前他所在的城市（的里雅斯特）和阶层（富商）的社会历史。

An added feature of the confession is illustrated by Nicholson Baker's 1992 novel Vox (tale, joke, gossip, confession, essay, romance). In this case, confession is combined with tale in a lengthy but self-contained episode of phone sex. There is no framing device—the reader is not told anything and must infer whatever information she can from the conversation. What seems to be going on is that a man from the West Coast and a woman from the East Coast hook up over the phone. They end up talking for several hours and, possibly, revealing a lot about themselves, but always anonymously. The apparent purpose of the call is mutual arousal, and there is some phone sex, but there is also mere conversation, and some of it is boring. It is never clear whether the callers are being honest or deceptive at any stage of the conversation, but nevertheless, two characters, and a novel, are constructed. Reading Vox requires a certain amount of patience, but Baker is full of tricks. He asks us to accept the idea that a novel can be interesting even when it is stripped of all the usual novelistic furniture—not only plot and individualized characters, but also the assurance that what we are reading is significant or pivotal in the lives of the characters. Maybe it is, maybe it isn't. The strict frame of the novel, which begins with the beginning of the call and ends when the callers hang up, means that we never know, and this is part of Baker's joke. Since a tale and a confession (and a joke) may always be untrue without contradicting the premises of these forms or forestalling the payoff, the reader is never uncomfortable doubting Vox —she can believe it or not. A tale has to be entertaining (which Vox is), and a confession has to seem intimate (which Vox does). The pleasure is in the acceptance of the conceit, as in a joke, not in the assertion of truth. If the partners to the call were actual potential romantic partners, not separated by so much distance, then the possible lies would give rise to more tension, but no real romance is likely to eventuate, so the two confessors and taletellers are free to elaborate at will.

尼克尔森·贝克1992年的小说《Vox》（故事、笑话、八卦、自白、散文、爱情）展现了自白的一个独特之处。在这部小说中，自白与故事结合，构成了一段冗长却又自成一体的电话性爱片段。小说没有框架结构——读者什么也得不到，只能从对话中自行推断。故事讲述的是一位来自西海岸的男子和一位来自东海岸的女子通过电话相识。他们聊了几个小时，或许还透露了很多关于自己的信息，但始终保持匿名。通话的目的似乎是为了彼此挑逗，其中确实包含一些电话性爱，但也穿插着一些普通的对话，而有些部分略显乏味。在对话的任何阶段，我们都无法确定通话者是真心实意还是有所隐瞒，但即便如此，两个人物和一个完整的故事还是被塑造了出来。阅读《Vox》需要一定的耐心，但贝克巧妙地运用了许多技巧。他要求我们接受这样一个观点：即使小说剥离了所有常见的叙事元素——不仅是情节和个性鲜明的角色，也包括我们所读的内容对人物生活具有重要意义或关键性的保证——它依然可以引人入胜。也许是，也许不是。小说严格的框架——从通话开始到挂断结束——意味着我们永远无法得知真相，而这正是贝克玩笑的一部分。由于故事、忏悔（以及玩笑）都可以是虚构的，却不会违背这些形式的前提或阻碍最终的结局，读者永远不会对沃克斯产生怀疑——她可以相信，也可以不相信。故事必须引人入胜（沃克斯的故事正是如此），忏悔必须显得私密（沃克斯的故事也确实如此）。乐趣在于接受这种虚构，就像玩笑一样，而不是断言真相。如果通话双方是真正的潜在恋人，而且彼此之间没有那么大的距离，那么可能的谎言会引起更大的紧张气氛，但不太可能发展出真正的恋情，所以两位倾诉者和讲故事的人可以随意发挥。

Some of these same issues come up in Wuthering Heights , which in form is a tale nested in a confession nested in gossip, along with elements of travel narrative, history, epic, and romance. At the beginning of the novel, Lockwood, a renter from southern England, shows up to take possession of a neglected property in Yorkshire. He happens to go to his landlord's house to pay his respects (and perhaps to snoop a bit). He runs into some misadventures that result in an injury that confines him to his bed. To entertain him, his housekeeper, Nelly Dean, who has known the family of his landlord all her life, tells him their story, and her own, since she was implicated in the events. The degree to which she has been implicated, in fact, is one of the facets of the novel most disputed by critics, some of whom see her as a Machiavellian figure manipulating all of the other characters for her own purposes.

这些问题在《呼啸山庄》中也有所体现。这部小说形式复杂，故事嵌套在忏悔之中，忏悔又嵌套在闲言碎语之中，同时还融合了游记、历史、史诗和爱情等元素。小说开篇，来自英格兰南部的租客洛克伍德来到约克郡，接管一处年久失修的房产。他顺道拜访了房东，或许也想窥探一下。然而，他却遭遇了一些意外，导致受伤卧床不起。为了打发时间，他的管家内莉·迪恩——她从小就认识房东一家——便向他讲述了他们的故事，以及她自己的经历，因为她也牵涉其中。事实上，她究竟牵涉到何种程度，正是这部小说中最具争议的方面之一，一些评论家认为她是一个权谋家，为了自己的利益操纵着其他所有角色。

Unlike Svevo and Updike, Nelly Dean is thoughtless in her confession. She tells it straightforwardly, perhaps not realizing that the form of confession requires addressing the issue of responsibility. A confessing character is not allowed to be merely a witness, nor can she fudge her own motives for taking certain actions or making certain decisions. For Emily Brontë, using Nelly to tell the story poses several insoluble problems that demonstrate the rhetorical difficulties of confession. The primary one of these is that if Nelly spends too much time discussing her own motives, she shifts attention away from the real story—that of the two generations of Lintons and Earnshaws and their interactions with Heathcliff. A confessing character almost can't help being the main character of his or her own story, but Nelly's story is not the most interesting or dramatic, and if she were to spend more time on herself, she would seem self-involved and misguided. In Emily Brontë's time, the modernism of Svevo and Proust, which could be defined as an intense experience and revelation of the self no matter whether the self has much to offer, was still eighty years in the future—the inherent drama of a situation still largely dictated whether the situation was worthy of a novel. Brontë did the best she could with the compromise of Nelly, no doubt deciding that the tale form she chose (with listener, teller, and tale all portrayed in the novel) would work best for the uncanny and violent material she had to work with, and for the complex time scheme of the story, which combines past and present in the first part, and develops further in the second part, when Lockwood returns to give up the house and gather his belongings.

与斯维沃和厄普代克不同，内莉·迪恩的忏悔显得漫不经心。她直截了当地讲述，或许并未意识到忏悔的形式要求她正视责任问题。忏悔者不能仅仅作为证人，也不能掩盖自己采取某些行动或做出某些决定的动机。对艾米莉·勃朗特而言，让内莉讲述故事会带来几个无法解决的问题，这些问题也体现了忏悔修辞的难点。其中最主要的一点是，如果内莉花费太多时间讨论自己的动机，就会使读者的注意力从真正的故事——林顿家族和恩肖家族两代人与希斯克利夫的互动——上转移开来。忏悔者几乎不可避免地会成为自己故事的主角，但内莉的故事并非最引人入胜或最扣人心弦，如果她把更多时间花在自己身上，就会显得自恋且误入歧途。在艾米莉·勃朗特生活的年代，斯韦沃和普鲁斯特的现代主义——无论自我是否能提供多少价值，都可将其定义为一种强烈的自我体验和揭示——还要八十年后才会出现。当时，情境本身的戏剧性在很大程度上决定了它是否值得写成一部小说。勃朗特在《内莉》这部作品中做出了她所能做到的最好妥协，毫无疑问，她认为她选择的叙事形式（小说中同时刻画了听者、讲述者和故事本身）最适合她所面对的怪诞而暴力的素材，也最适合故事复杂的时间结构。故事的第一部分融合了过去和现在，并在第二部分进一步展开，洛克伍德返回放弃房子并收拾行李。

Indeed, Brontë's material was so shocking and violent that even her sister Charlotte declared to her biographer that she didn't understand how Emily came up with it, or what it meant about her sister's nature, though they lived and wrote together for thirty years. Cathy's capri-ciousness, Heathcliff's vengefulness, their passion for one another, the elemental brutality of the setting—all of these features of the novel required some sort of remoteness from the everyday Victorian world of the 1840s . By making it all gossip, Brontë could get her novel written and published. The public (those few who read the novel, which was not popular in its day) was given permission to think of it all as hearsay, and, more important, to feel its power at a distance and, if need be, dismiss it, which many readers did. Is Nelly implicated in the fates of her charges? I don't think this question can be answered with reference to the text, but, rather, arises from the way the needs of the material and the forms Brontë employed jostle against one another in the final product.

事实上，勃朗特的素材如此令人震惊和暴力，以至于连她的妹妹夏洛蒂都向传记作者坦言，她无法理解艾米莉是如何构思出这些情节的，也无法理解这些情节揭示了她姐姐的性格，尽管她们共同生活和写作了三十年。凯茜的任性、希斯克利夫的复仇心、他们彼此间的激情、以及故事背景中原始的残酷——小说的所有这些特征都要求与19世纪40年代维多利亚时代的日常生活保持某种距离。通过把这一切都描绘成流言蜚语，勃朗特得以完成并出版了这部小说。公众（当时这部小说并不流行，读者寥寥无几）被允许将这一切都视为道听途说，更重要的是，被允许与小说的力量保持距离，并在必要时将其抛诸脑后，而许多读者也确实这样做了。内莉是否与她所照料的那些人的命运有关？我认为这个问题不能通过参考文本来回答，而是源于勃朗特在最终作品中运用的材料和形式之间的相互冲突。

A. S. Byatt's Possession (travel, history, biography, joke, gossip, diary/letter, confession, essay, epic, romance) is a good example of how far an author can extend the forms the novel partakes of and still maintain the sense of forward motion. Possession consists of two parallel romance narratives that take place 130 years apart. In the 1980s a young scholar discovers a draft of a love letter written to a mysterious woman by a famous male Victorian poet who is thought to have been uxoriously and faithfully married. He then contacts another young scholar, and between them they ascertain the identity of the letter's recipient, an obscure female Victorian poet whose reputation has been resurrected by modern feminist scholarship. In the course of their scholarly investigation the two academics are drawn to one another, and they finally get together in the modern happy ending. But they uncover a passionate and ill-fated love affair between their two poets that resulted in grief, anger, and, of course, lots of poetry—not a happy ending at all (until the last minute).

A·S·拜厄特的《占有》（融合了游记、历史、传记、笑话、八卦、日记/书信、忏悔录、散文、史诗和爱情等多种文体）堪称典范，展现了作者如何拓展小说的各种形式，同时又能保持叙事的连贯性。《占有》由两条相隔130年的平行爱情故事构成。在20世纪80年代，一位年轻学者发现了一封维多利亚时代著名男诗人写给一位神秘女子的情书草稿。这位诗人被认为婚姻美满，忠贞不渝。随后，他联系了另一位年轻学者，两人共同探寻信件的收信人——一位鲜为人知的维多利亚时代女诗人，她的声誉因现代女性主义研究而重获关注。在学术研究的过程中，两位学者彼此吸引，最终走到了一起，迎来了现代式的幸福结局。但他们却发现两位诗人之间有一段充满激情却又不幸的恋情，这段恋情导致了悲伤、愤怒，当然还有大量的诗歌——根本没有一个幸福的结局（直到最后一刻）。

Possession is, above all, a tour de force. However the reader feels about the characters and the story, she cannot help being astonished and impressed by Byatt's array of literary skills. She simply creates two, three, four entire worlds—the world of modern scholarship is the least of them, a slightly comic depiction of the nature of academic life, with its rivalries and jealousies and grant-earning necessities. Inside this frame she sets the lives and works of her two poets—Randolph Ash and Christabel La Motte. He represents the masculine—he is a famous and aggressive man of his time, prolific upon all sorts of manly themes such as Norse mythology and natural history. She represents the feminine. She is not prolific at all, and her work is in a Celtic, folk-loric tradition of spells and lyrics. Byatt uses and composes in all of the forms her scholars and poets would be familiar with—poetry of many types, academic prose, letters, diary entries, tales, even gossip (since some of what the modern characters learn is in the form of speculation). In the course of intertwining her two narratives and bringing each of them to a satisfactory conclusion (which involves, for the Victorian narrative, revealing everything that happened and what it meant, and for the modern narrative bringing the two protagonists together in the end), Byatt has much to say about the methods and goals of scholarship, about the nature of literature, about the differences between the Victorian period and ours, and about the relationship of the intellect to love and passion. The way in which Byatt structures her novel is a beautiful lesson in arrangement as a simple and effective method of making an argument (the ghost of George Eliot appears fleetingly at the beginning of the novel—clearly Byatt learned a great deal from Eliot's careful architecture). As Byatt presents her narrative portion by portion, she piques the reader's interest in forms that might otherwise not appeal—each poem or bit of biography serves to solve a portion of the mystery and forward the plot, and as a result it is dangerous to skip anything. Byatt is not an especially funny writer, but she subtly recognizes the operation of irony, especially in the modern story, so she is witty in the same way Eliot is—as a form of intelligent recognition of the differences between ideals (foolish or not) and reality. She uses just about every station on our novel-clock (not polemic, perhaps, athough a minor character expresses a good deal of anger in one section) and then some. Part of the display of Byatt's virtuosity is that she uses the different forms but does not dissolve them together into one mix, as some other novelists do—she juxtaposes their different literary styles and intentions, and uses plot suspense to move the reader forward, as Bram Stoker does in Dracula. In fact, one of the pleasurable uses of our novel-clock is to note connections between novels that on the surface seem unrelated. Possession seems far more serious and literary than Dracula , but both require the suspense and mystery of the tale (which is highly plotted) to energize the form (which could otherwise seem chaotic). If we were to analyze Anna Karenina by means of our clock, we would see that it is a lot like Middlemarch in overall tone and intention, but since Tolstoy did not employ the wit of George Eliot to add both liveliness and perspective to his long novel, he had to use something else, and he used the features of the epic. The epic qualities of Anna Karenina redeem the potential sordidness of the adultery story and also give the novel as a whole scope and importance.

《占有》这部作品，首先，堪称一部杰作。无论读者对书中的人物和故事有何感想，都无法不被拜厄特精湛的文学技巧所折服。她仅凭一己之力便构建了两、三、四个完整的世界——现代学术界只是其中最微不足道的一个，它以略带喜剧色彩的笔触描绘了学术生活的本质，包括其中的竞争、嫉妒以及为获得资助而不得不面对的种种困境。在这个框架之内，她将两位诗人——兰道夫·阿什和克里斯特贝尔·拉莫特——的生活和作品置于其中。阿什代表男性——他是当时一位声名显赫、作风强硬的诗人，创作了大量以北欧神话和自然史等男性主题为题材的作品。拉莫特则代表女性。她的作品并不多产，而且她的作品属于凯尔特民间传说传统，以咒语和抒情诗为主。拜厄特运用并创作了她笔下学者和诗人所熟悉的各种文体——多种类型的诗歌、学术散文、书信、日记、故事，甚至八卦（因为现代人物所了解到的某些信息是以推测的形式呈现的）。在将两条叙事线索交织在一起并各自走向令人满意的结局的过程中（维多利亚时代的叙事线索揭示了所有发生的事情及其意义，而现代叙事线索则让两位主人公最终走到了一起），拜厄特对学术研究的方法和目标、文学的本质、维多利亚时代与我们当今时代的差异，以及理智与爱欲之间的关系，都有着深刻的见解。拜厄特构建小说的方式堪称典范，它展现了布局作为一种简洁有效的论证方法的魅力（乔治·艾略特的影子在小说开头短暂出现——显然，拜厄特从艾略特精心构建的叙事结构中获益良多）。拜厄特以分段叙事的方式呈现故事，巧妙地激发了读者对原本可能并不感兴趣的文学形式的兴趣——每一首诗或每一段传记都服务于解开部分谜团、推进情节发展，因此，跳过任何部分都可能带来危险。拜厄特并非一位特别幽默的作家，但她对反讽的运用却十分精妙，尤其是在现代故事中，因此她的机智与艾略特如出一辙——是对理想（无论是否愚蠢）与现实之间差异的深刻洞察。她几乎运用了小说叙事的所有要素（或许并非论战性的，尽管某个次要角色在某一章节中表达了相当多的愤怒），甚至更多。拜厄特技艺精湛之处在于，她运用不同的文学形式，却不像某些小说家那样将它们混杂在一起——她将它们不同的文学风格和意图并置，并像布拉姆·斯托克在《德古拉》中那样，运用情节悬念来推动读者的阅读。事实上，我们运用小说时钟的一大乐趣在于发现那些表面上看似毫不相干的小说之间的联系。《占有》似乎比《德古拉》更严肃、更具文学性，但两者都需要故事本身（情节紧凑）的悬念和神秘感来赋予其活力（否则可能会显得杂乱无章）。如果我们用小说时钟来分析《安娜·卡列尼娜》，就会发现它在整体基调和意图上与《米德尔马契》颇为相似，但由于托尔斯泰没有像乔治·艾略特那样运用机智来为他的长篇小说增添活力和视角，他不得不另辟蹊径，运用了史诗的特征。《安娜·卡列尼娜》的史诗特质不仅弥补了通奸故事可能存在的低俗之处，也赋予了整部小说更广阔的视野和更重要的意义。

And so, where does greatness lie? The clock suggests some ideas. Four of our novels are generally considered great: Middlemarch, The Trial, Vanity Fair , and Wuthering Heights. Three of them (The Complete Henry Bech, Vox , and Possession) are too new to be judged great, but they are certainly profoundly respected contemporary works. Six of them (Dracula, Humphry Clinker, The Once and Future King, Fathers and Sons, A Tale of Two Cities , and Zeno's Conscience) have adherents, but each is in some way eccentric or perhaps limited. Maybe the proper word to describe their effect is not “great” but “striking.”

那么，伟大究竟体现在哪里呢？时钟或许能提供一些线索。我们收藏的小说中，有四部被普遍认为是伟大的：《米德尔马契》、《审判》、《名利场》和《呼啸山庄》。其中三部（《亨利·贝克全集》、《声音》和《占有》）出版时间尚短，尚不能断言其伟大，但它们无疑是备受推崇的当代佳作。还有六部（《德古拉》、《汉弗莱·克林克》、《永恒之王》、《父与子》、《双城记》和《芝诺的良心》）拥有各自的拥趸，但每一部都或多或少有些古怪，或者说存在局限性。或许，用“引人注目”来形容它们的影响更为恰当。

There is no single quality that the “great” novels share other than the biographical quality—the sense that the reader comes to understand a character completely, better than the character understands himself or herself. Becky, Josef K., Dorothea, Lydgate, Heathcliff, and Cathy are all bodied forth as more knowable and logical than it is humanly possible to be. The only quality that all of the novels are without is the intimate form of the diary/letter, which might be a coincidence, but also, in relationship to the biographical quality, might mean that greatness in a novel entails perspective upon the protagonist that the diarist or letter-writer can't achieve even when the diary form is a conceit. Three of our great novels have a romantic element. Freud maintained that the two great human endeavors are love and work. Perhaps a great novel can run for only two hundred pages or less without romance, as The Trial does, though, as Wuthering Heights ( 340 pages) makes clear, work is more expendable. In many novels work exists more as furniture than motivation, though part of the genius of several of these novels is serious attention to the meaning of a life work—Lydgate's medical vocation, Becky's struggle for survival (since by gender she is excluded from a vocation—this is one of the great themes of the nineteenth-century novel). Josef K. has a job, but it is not treated like a vocation—his vocation is trying to figure out what is happening, what is imposed upon him. Vanity Fair is explicitly epic, and so is Wuthering Heights if we consider the Yorkshire moors a separate country from England, as Emily Brontë seems to have. Wuthering Heights may be seen as an epic of the moors.

除了传记性——即读者对人物的理解甚至超越人物自身——之外，“伟大”小说并无其他共同之处。贝基、约瑟夫·K、多萝西娅、利德盖特、希斯克利夫和凯茜都被塑造得比人类所能达到的更加可知、更加合乎逻辑。所有这些小说唯一共同缺乏的特质是日记/书信这种私密的叙述形式，这或许只是巧合，但结合传记性来看，也可能意味着伟大小说的精髓在于它能提供一种视角，让读者对主人公有更深刻的理解，而这种视角是日记或书信作者即便采用日记形式也无法企及的。我们所知的三部伟大小说都包含浪漫元素。弗洛伊德认为，人类的两大追求是爱情和工作。或许像《审判》那样，一部伟大的小说可以篇幅只有两百页甚至更少，而无需爱情元素；然而，正如《呼啸山庄》（340页）所清晰展现的那样，工作在小说中显得更为可有可无。在许多小说中，工作更像是装饰品而非动力，尽管其中一些小说的精妙之处在于对毕生事业意义的严肃探讨——例如莱德盖特的医生职业，贝基为生存而奋斗（由于性别原因，她被排除在任何职业之外——这是十九世纪小说的一大主题）。约瑟夫·K有一份工作，但这份工作并不被视为一种职业——他的职业是努力弄清正在发生的事情，弄清强加在他身上的是什么。《名利场》显然是一部史诗，如果我们像艾米莉·勃朗特那样，将约克郡荒原视为一个独立于英格兰的国度，那么《呼啸山庄》也同样如此。《呼啸山庄》或许可以被视为一部荒原史诗。

What is perhaps more significant is that only The Trial does not use many of the forms. Middlemarch uses seven—romance, history, biography, joke, gossip, essay, and travel; thus it offers the payoffs of relationship understanding, historical understanding, biographical understanding, shared laughter (and perspective, through irony), community wisdom (through gossip), objective analysis, and finally a sense that the mundane English Midlands are actually exotic

或许更重要的是，只有《审判》这部作品没有运用多种叙事形式。《米德尔马契》运用了七种——爱情、历史、传记、笑话、闲聊、散文和游记；因此，它能够带来诸多益处，例如：对人物关系的理解、对历史的理解、对人物传记的理解、共同的欢笑（以及通过反讽获得的视角）、社群智慧（通过闲聊获得）、客观的分析，最终，还能让人感受到平凡的英格兰中部地区其实充满异域风情。

∗ Don Quixote uses almost every form but the diary and the polemic in one section or another— even a sense of history is employed when the second volume reflects on the effects of the first and when Quixote comments upon the supposed decline in civilization that has intervened between the time of his knightly heroes and the present time of the novel. So perhaps the straightest path for a novelist seeking greatness is variety and capaciousness: the novel promises to encompass all things as an effect of its almost infinite expandability; when the author piles word upon word, sentence upon sentence, and incident upon incident, he signals this ambition and is also expected to make good on his promise. In eight hundred pages, ambitions are usually realized or not.

*《堂吉诃德》几乎运用了除日记和论战之外的所有文体——甚至在第二卷中，当堂吉诃德反思第一卷的影响，以及当堂吉诃德评论他笔下骑士英雄的时代与小说所处的时代之间文明的衰落时，也融入了历史感。因此，对于一位追求伟大的小说家而言，或许最直接的途径是多样性和包容性：小说几乎无限的延展性使其能够包罗万象；当作者堆砌文字、句子和事件时，他既展现了这种雄心壮志，也期待着他能够兑现这一承诺。在八百页的篇幅中，雄心壮志要么得以实现，要么未能实现。

Obviously, though, what we take away from any of these great novels is more than a sense of broad inclusiveness. Each one has a distinct type of greatness. The voice of George Eliot seems uniquely wise and thoughtful; the voice of William Makepeace Thackeray seems uniquely serious, sharp, and worldly; the voice of Emily Brontë seems uniquely passionate. It is tempting to divorce these types of uniqueness from the general quality and breadth that are natural to the novel and that so many novels have. What seems to be happening is that the author's voice and his or her protagonist's potential fit one another and illuminate one another in a unique way. But in fact, capaciousness works for the novelist in several ways. When he includes many components in his novel, he stimulates his own thinking as he tries to get the parts to mesh—dilemmas of narrative as simple as time sequence and cause and effect require the author to think about the complex connections between his parts and to express these complexities in his style, which becomes more probing and more idiosyncratic. A person of natural wit, such as George Eliot, ends up bringing her wit to bear upon more interesting ideas and relationships between and among ideas and thereby expands the power of her wit. The ultimate feeling we get from each of these great novels, that of knowing the protagonists abundantly, grows naturally out of all the forms around the clock they are required to inhabit. Sometimes the parts don't mesh—Becky Sharp does not sit comfortably in her novel the way Dorothea Brooke sits comfortably in hers, because Thackeray's tone is polemical—his anger is directed both at Becky and at the world she lives in—but the greatness of Becky is that she is morally suspect and yet strangely admirable, stronger, more alive, and yet more vulnerable than the conventional characters who have none of the self-knowledge Becky has. The jostling of Thackeray's polemical tone with the epic, romantic, geographical, and historical elements of the novel produce Becky. The greatness of these capacious novels grows out of how the integration of the parts stretches and stimulates their authors at every level—the level of style; the level of structure; the level of characterization; and the level of thought about ideas, feelings, and sensations. Part of the author's genius was that he (or she) rose to the occasion provided by the materials of the novel, but another part of his genius was that he created the occasion by conceiving the materials of the novel to begin with.

显然，我们从这些伟大的小说中得到的远不止是包罗万象的包容性。每一部小说都有其独特的伟大之处。乔治·艾略特的文笔似乎独具智慧与深思；威廉·梅克比斯·萨克雷的文笔似乎独具严肃、犀利与世故；艾米莉·勃朗特的文笔似乎独具热情。人们很容易将这些独特性与小说本身固有的、许多小说都具备的普遍品质和广度割裂开来。表面上看，作者的文笔和主人公的潜能似乎彼此契合，并以一种独特的方式相互映衬。但实际上，这种包容性对小说家来说有诸多益处。当小说中包含众多元素时，作者会激发自身的思考，努力使各个部分相互融合——即使是像时间顺序和因果关系这样简单的叙事难题，也要求作者思考各个部分之间错综复杂的联系，并用自己的风格来表达这些复杂性，从而使其风格更加深入、更加独特。像乔治·艾略特这样天生机智的人，最终会将她的机智运用到更有趣的思想以及思想之间的关联上，从而拓展了她机智的力量。我们从每一部伟大的小说中获得的最终感受——对主人公的深入了解——自然而然地源于他们必须全天候栖身的各种境遇。有时，各个部分并不协调——贝基·夏普在小说中的地位并不像多萝西娅·布鲁克那样自在，因为萨克雷的语气是论战式的——他的愤怒既指向贝基，也指向她所生活的世界——但贝基的伟大之处在于，她道德上令人怀疑，却又奇特地令人钦佩；她比那些缺乏自我认知的传统人物更坚强、更鲜活，却也更脆弱。萨克雷论战式的语气与小说中史诗般的、浪漫的、地理的和历史的元素相互碰撞，最终造就了贝基这个人物。这些鸿篇巨制的伟大之处在于，各个部分的完美融合从各个层面——风格层面、结构层面、人物刻画层面以及对思想、情感和感受的思考层面——都极大地拓展和激发了作者的创作潜能。作者的才华一部分在于他（或她）能够充分利用小说提供的素材，另一部分则在于他从一开始就构思出了小说的素材，从而创造了创作的契机。

The Trial , though, shows that radical simplicity and focus, resulting in an intensity of intimacy that is thoroughly original, is another path to greatness. What Kafka understands better than anyone is the simple power of narration—a story is constructed one image and one incident at a time. Once the images and incidents are expressed clearly, they exist powerfully and in some sense ineradicably in the reader's mind. If they are sufficiently compelling, the reader cannot help contemplating them. To qualify them in any way, even by relating them to other ideas, is to muddy them. The Trial is an effective answer to E. M. For-ster's lament that attention to “What happens next?” inevitably renders a narrative too common or pedestrian to be truly profound. “What happens next?” can be a far more interesting question than those Forster preferred—“Who does it happen to?” “What does it feel or seem like?” “What does it mean?”—but only if, like Kafka, the author doesn't acknowledge those questions at all. Kafka's form of greatness is, perhaps, more original and difficult to conceive of than the other, more capacious form. I think this is because since the novel is naturally sociable and it encourages readers and authors to think in sociable ways, Josef K.'s isolation even when he is talking to someone is exceptional. Whatever is sociable around Josef K. is strange and maybe untrustworthy (this is true of the main character of “The Burrow” and ”The Metamorphosis” as well as “In the Penal Colony”). Kafka dispenses with the natural sociability of the novel and comes up with an entirely new and compelling vision. But like the other authors of great novels, he also has a genius for conceiving ideas that are both important per se and capable of stimulating his own most characteristic and insightful thinking. Greatness in a novel does not depend upon perfection of the object; perfection of the object is merely an added dimension to the greatness of certain novels. But every great novel offers incomprehensible abundance in some form—even The Trial , only a couple of hundred pages long, is abundantly meticulous, abundantly intimate, abundantly strange, and abundantly original.

然而，《审判》表明，极致的简洁和专注，最终成就了一种独树一帜的亲密感，这也是通往伟大的另一条道路。卡夫卡比任何人都更懂得叙事的简单力量——故事是由一个个意象、一个个事件构建而成的。一旦这些意象和事件被清晰地表达出来，它们便会在读者的脑海中留下深刻而持久的印记。如果它们足够引人入胜，读者便会不由自主地去思考它们。任何形式的限定，哪怕是将它们与其他概念联系起来，都会使它们变得模糊不清。《审判》有力地回应了E·M·福斯特的感叹：对“接下来会发生什么？”的过度关注，必然会使叙事变得平庸乏味，难以达到真正的深刻。“接下来会发生什么？”这个问题本身或许比福斯特更青睐的那些问题——“发生在谁身上？”“感觉如何？”“意义何在？”——更有趣，但这只有在作者像卡夫卡一样，完全忽略这些问题的情况下才成立。卡夫卡的伟大之处或许比其他更包容的形式更独特、更难以理解。我认为这是因为小说本身具有社交性，它鼓励读者和作者以社交的方式思考，因此，约瑟夫·K即使在与人交谈时也显得格外孤僻。在约瑟夫·K周围，任何具有社交性的事物都显得怪异，甚至可能不可信（《地洞》、《变形记》以及《在流放地》的主人公都是如此）。卡夫卡摒弃了小说固有的社交性，创造出一种全新且引人入胜的视角。但与其他伟大作家一样，他也拥有构思思想的天赋，这些思想本身就意义非凡，并且能够激发他自身最具特色和洞察力的思考。小说的伟大并不取决于对象本身的完美；对象的完美仅仅是某些小说伟大之处的附加维度。但每一部伟大的小说都以某种形式提供了难以理解的丰富性——即使是只有几百页的《审判》，也充满了细致入微的描写、细腻的情感、奇特的情节和原创性。

# ↩

10. A Novel of Your Own (I)

10. 你自己的小说（一）

N ow that you have decided to begin your novel, you may congratulate yourself. You have not been asked or groomed to N write a novel. You have not gone to novel-writing school, nor taken a standard curriculum of preparatory courses. Chances are, no one wants you to write your novel—if they say they do, they are just meaning that you should get it over with or get on with it. The people you know actually dread reading the novel you are about to write— they don't want to read about themselves, they don't want to be bored, and they fear embarrassment for everyone. You are, therefore, free.

既然你已经决定开始写小说，不妨好好祝贺自己。你既没有被要求也没有被培养去写小说。你既没有上过小说写作学校，也没有参加过任何标准的预备课程。很有可能，根本没人希望你写小说——如果他们说希望，那也只是希望你赶紧写完。你认识的人其实很害怕读你即将写的小说——他们不想读到关于自己的故事，不想感到无聊，也害怕让大家都尴尬。因此，你是自由的。

As you write the first word, you are embracing the novel's greatest tradition, that of obscure beginnings. No other art is so simple or so cheap to engage in as literature. A lifetime's reading may be borrowed from the library; a pencil and some sheets of paper may be purloined without much trouble. You can sit at the kitchen table. You can sit on the stool in the bathroom and put a board across your knees. There is no outlay for paints or clay. And since you are writing a novel, you aren't going to need actors or film or a stage. You aren't going to need a reader for companionship (a difference between you and poets—your characters can serve as your companions if you want them to). Perhaps the nicest thing about beginning your novel is that you don't have to begin anything again for a very long time if you don't care to, because after you set down the first thought, every time you come back to that first thought is a rewrite. Of course, the first thought must be followed by a second one, and so on, but if you abjure fear, it will be—it is in the nature of thoughts to follow upon one another.

当你写下第一个字时，你就拥抱了小说最伟大的传统——晦涩的开篇。没有哪一种艺术形式像文学这样简单易行，成本又如此低廉。你可以从图书馆借阅一生的书籍；一支铅笔和几张纸也唾手可得。你可以坐在厨房的餐桌旁，也可以坐在浴室的凳子上，膝盖上放一块木板。你无需花费任何颜料或黏土。既然你在写小说，你就不需要演员、电影或舞台。你也不需要读者陪伴（这与诗人不同——如果你愿意，你的角色可以成为你的伙伴）。或许，开始写小说最美妙的地方在于，如果你不想，很长一段时间内都不用再重新开始，因为一旦你写下第一个想法，每一次回到最初的想法都是一次重写。当然，第一个念头之后必然会产生第二个念头，以此类推，但如果你摒弃恐惧，它就会——念头本来就是环环相扣的。

What you are aiming for is willing suspension of disbelief, and the first person who must suspend disbelief is yourself. Some beginning novelists have more disbelief to suspend than others, but even if your burden of disbelief is heavy, the only way to suspend it is to keep adding sentences to the ones you have already written. Sheer length persuades, at least to some degree, because it builds an object in the mind. In Within a Budding Grove , Marcel Proust's installment of In Search of Lost Time about his adolescence, there is a short passage concerning the author's first attempts at writing. Inspired by the conversation of a favorite author, whom he meets at the home of his beloved, M. resolves to begin his own career by setting aside in advance whole days in which he will commence (“it was better not to start on an evening when I felt ill-prepared” [p. 210 ]). It seems like a good plan, except that he doesn't ever commence, instead finding more and more excuses to put off what he has been planning. Within days he becomes so discouraged that he snaps at his grandmother when she inquires after his “work.” The irony that you should note is that what will be his work is already evident—one of his modes of procrastinating is to visit the house where he had met his favorite author. Each night when he comes home from socializing, his mind is filled with the conversations he has heard, which inspire imaginary conversations in which he takes all the roles. All he would need do is write a few of these conversations down, and he would find his work creating itself, as, indeed, it did in subsequent years. What I see in this anecdote is not only that the young Proust wasn't ready to begin, but also that one of the strongest features of his talent, his preternatural ability to observe the social world around him, was announcing itself loudly and clearly when he was still very young. So it is with you.

你的目标是让读者心甘情愿地暂时放下怀疑，而首先要放下怀疑的人正是你自己。有些初出茅庐的小说家需要放下的怀疑比其他人更多，但即便你的怀疑负担沉重，唯一能放下它的方法就是不断地在已有的文字基础上添加新的句子。篇幅本身就能起到说服作用，至少在某种程度上，因为它能在读者的脑海中构建出一个对象。在马塞尔·普鲁斯特的《追忆似水年华》中，《花丛中》是他关于自己少年时代的一章，其中有一段关于作者最初写作尝试的短文。在爱人家中偶遇一位他最喜欢的作家后，普鲁斯特深受启发，决定开始自己的写作生涯，为此他提前安排好整天的时间进行写作（“最好不要在晚上开始，因为那时我感觉准备不足”[第210页]）。这计划看似不错，但他却始终没有着手，反而找了越来越多的借口拖延。几天后，他变得十分沮丧，以至于祖母询问他的“作品”进展时，他竟然冲祖母发火。讽刺的是，他未来的作品其实早已显现——他拖延的其中一种方式就是去拜访他最喜欢的作家的故居。每天晚上，他从社交聚会回家后，脑海中都会浮现出他听到的对话，这些对话激发了他进行想象，让他扮演各种角色。他只需要把其中的一些对话记录下来，他的作品就会自然而然地形成，正如后来几年里发生的那样。我从这个轶事中看到的不仅是年轻的普鲁斯特还没有准备好开始写作，而且还表明他天赋中最强大的特质之一——他超乎寻常的观察周围社会的能力——在他很年轻的时候就已经清晰地展现出来了。你也是如此。

My favorite anecdote about the ease and pleasure of writing a book comes from Ilene Beckerman, who in 1995 published her memoir Love, Loss, and What I Wore. Her initial impulse had been to jot down some memories from the early days of her marriage for her children, herself, and her best friend, so she kept paper and pencils at hand, and every time she remembered something, she wrote it out. Sometimes it was a few pages long, sometimes only a page. She did not write about the memories in any particular order, only when they occurred to her. She filed each page with the others in a manila folder, and after a year she pulled out the folder, read over the pages, organized them chono-logically, and had them typed. She made five copies—one for herself and each of her three children, and one for her best friend. Some months after she was finished, the phone rang. It was her best friend, who asked her whether she would mind talking to a publisher about publishing her memoir. Though she was totally taken by surprise, she agreed. Her friend said, “Now, Ilene, be nice.” She was nice. The publisher was nice, too, and made such a success of the book that Becker-man went on to write another and to have an enjoyable experience as an author and celebrity.

我最喜欢的关于写作的轻松与乐趣的轶事来自伊琳·贝克曼。1995年，她出版了回忆录《爱、失去与我的衣着》。最初，她只是想为孩子们、自己和最好的朋友记录下婚姻初期的一些回忆，所以她随身带着纸笔，每当想起什么，就写下来。有时写好几页，有时只有一页。她并没有按照任何特定的顺序来写，只是想到什么就写什么。她把每一页都放进一个牛皮纸文件夹里，一年后，她拿出文件夹，通读了一遍，按时间顺序整理好，然后打印出来。她打印了五份——一份给自己，一份给三个孩子，一份给最好的朋友。几个月后，电话响了。是她最好的朋友打来的，问她是否愿意和出版社谈谈出版回忆录的事。她完全没想到，但还是答应了。她的朋友说：“伊琳，要友善。”她很友善。出版商也很友善，这本书大获成功，贝克曼又写了另一本书，并享受了作为作家和名人的美好经历。

One thing to understand about this anecdote is that she wasn't merely lucky. She believed in what she was writing—she found it valuable, interesting, and worthwhile, if only as a private record, and she considered herself capable of achieving her goal. Because of the circumstances of her effort, she had no self-doubts. She knew her audience would be pleased with her gift. Because she was ready to write when she had a memory, but didn't force herself to write when she did not, her writing didn't seem first and foremost an obligation, and so she was able to get into the habit without much trouble. Perhaps her smartest idea was to keep the folder and the paper and pencils at hand. A book, and especially a novel, must be a habit. Almost all novelists cultivate more discipline than Ilene Beckerman did, but what this anecdote reveals is that the absolutely minimal, simplest, easiest way of writing can accumulate a book as well as the most dedicated, self-conscious, ascetic way. Some novelists write by obligation, others by desire. These are questions of temperament. There is no intrinsically better way, since the only standard of achievement to begin with (and for quite a long time) is the accumulation of pages. Another thing both Beckerman and Proust should show you is that writing is writing, not planning. The sooner you put words on paper, the happier you will be.

理解这个轶事的关键在于，她并非仅仅是幸运。她相信自己所写的内容——她认为它有价值、有趣且有意义，即便只是作为一份私人记录，而且她相信自己能够实现目标。正因为如此，她对自己毫无怀疑。她知道读者会欣赏她的这份礼物。她会在有灵感时随时动笔，而不会在没有灵感时强迫自己写作，因此写作对她而言并非首要的义务，所以她能够毫不费力地养成写作的习惯。或许她最明智的做法就是随身携带文件夹、纸笔。一本书，尤其是一部小说，必须成为一种习惯。几乎所有小说家都比伊琳·贝克曼更有自律性，但这个轶事揭示的是，最极简、最简单、最轻松的写作方式，也能像最专注、最自省、最苦行僧式的写作方式一样，最终成就一部作品。有些小说家写作是出于义务，有些则是出于渴望。这些都是性情的问题。没有绝对更好的方法，因为衡量成就的唯一标准（而且在很长一段时间内）就是作品数量的积累。贝克曼和普鲁斯特都向你表明，写作就是写作，而不是计划。你越早把文字写在纸上，就会越快乐。

As with any discipline, from playing hockey to baking a souffl to playing the violin, there are certain requisite skills that a novelist must be comfortable with, but they are only skills to be learned, not inherent talents. If you are comfortable punctuating, spelling, and using understandable grammar (which may or may not be standard grammar), you will enjoy writing more and better believe that you can do it. Language is a tool the limbic system uses to write the novel in the same way that a hammer is a tool a carpenter uses or a bat is a tool a baseball player uses. The more automatic your use of the tool is, the less friction there is between you and the page. Just as throughout your life you have taken the time to learn to use many tools, so you must take the time to learn to use the tool of written language. Your eloquence in speaking is entirely separate from your potential eloquence in writing. Eventually the two will merge, but to begin with, fluency in the one has only the remotest relationship with fluency in the other. If you were not lucky enough to learn the mechanics of prose style in school, you can learn them as a protonovelist. They are merely rules and habits. Learning how to write conventional sentences is much easier than quitting smoking, learning to ride a horse, or taking up carpentry in middle age.

就像任何技能一样，从打冰球到烤舒芙蕾再到拉小提琴，小说家也必须掌握一些必要的技能，但这些技能只能学习，并非与生俱来。如果你能熟练地使用标点符号、拼写和语法（无论是否符合标准），你就会更享受写作，而且你完全可以做到。语言是大脑边缘系统用来写作的工具，就像锤子是木匠的工具，球棒是棒球运动员的工具一样。你使用工具越熟练，你与文字之间的摩擦就越小。正如你一生中花时间学习使用各种工具一样，你也必须花时间学习如何使用书面语言这一工具。你的口语表达能力与你潜在的写作能力完全不同。最终两者会融合，但一开始，口语的流畅与写作的流畅之间只有微乎其微的联系。如果你在学校里没能学到散文写作的技巧，你可以作为一名原型小说家来学习。它们不过是一些规则和习惯。学习如何写出规范的句子远比戒烟、学习骑马或中年学习木工容易得多。

Every aspect of novel-writing, from knowing the difference between a comma and a semicolon to being able to conceive a multivol-ume historical saga of French cosmopolitan life, is as likely to be a skill as a talent. No theory of the workings of the brain has revealed a specific novel-writing center in either the right brain or the left brain. For your purposes, this means that there is no definable end to the process of developing your tools—you will not hit a novel-writing glass ceiling in the way that you might hit a piano-playing glass ceiling or a pitching-speed glass ceiling. Let's imagine a novel-writing pyramid of skills. The bottom layer of punctuation, grammar, and spelling is knowledge you will use in every sentence you write. This, the layer that needs to be mastered first, is the most artificial one. There are several reasons for this. One is that because it is artificial, it requires a good deal of practice—repetition resulting in unconscious employment of the necessary tool. Until spelling, grammar, and punctuation work independently of the conscious mind, their operation will interfere with the operation of the other layers. But, more importantly, the most artificial layer is also the one that defines the activity we are engaged upon—the employment of prose to entertain and enlighten, the making of the repository of our art, which is a written book, the drawing of a distinction between this system and other systems of words. It is through the employment of grammar, punctuation, and spelling that we signal ourselves and the reader to prepare for a certain experience.

从区分逗号和分号到构思一部展现法国都市生活的多卷本历史巨著，小说写作的方方面面都既是技能也是天赋。目前没有任何关于大脑运作的理论揭示出大脑左右脑中存在专门负责小说写作的中心。就你而言，这意味着提升写作技巧的过程没有终点——你不会像弹钢琴或投球速度那样，在小说写作方面遇到瓶颈。让我们想象一个小说写作技能金字塔。最底层是标点符号、语法和拼写，这些知识是你写的每个句子都会用到的。这一层需要首先掌握，也是最需要人工练习的。原因有很多。其中之一是，正因为它是人工练习，所以需要大量的练习——重复练习最终会形成对必要工具的无意识运用。在拼写、语法和标点符号能够独立于意识运作之前，它们的运行必然会干扰其他层面的运作。但更重要的是，最人为的层面也恰恰定义了我们正在进行的活动——运用散文来娱乐和启迪，创造我们艺术的宝库（即书籍），以及将这套文字系统与其他文字系统区分开来。正是通过语法、标点和拼写的运用，我们向自己和读者发出信号，让他们为某种特定的体验做好准备。

Above this bottom layer is a layer of diction, which is familiarity with words and expressions. Sensory data and ideas conceived in the mind go in and out of words and are at the same time incarnated and energized by words. We can imagine it to be a variety of quantum and wave theory of light. The words are the quanta, the mental process is the waves. As the writer composes, waves of thought precipitate into quanta of words, which stimulate waves of thought. Each transformation expends energy but also creates it, because though choosing the right words is an effort, the right words are inspiring. Some writers, such as Vladimir Nabokov, have a particular sort of erudition—a wide-ranging and precise knowledge of all the words available to express a certain idea, which comes from a knowledge of many languages and wide reading in many different fields. Other writers, such as Charles Dickens, excel in reproducing the demotic (the language of the people) because they have sharp hearing and good memories. Their own style is remarkably various—influenced and colored by the general human talent for coming up with sharp and colorful phrases, sayings, slang expressions, and shaping intonations. Other writers, such as Zora Neale Hurston, choose to specialize in a particular dialect because it is expressive and also characteristic of the group she wants to portray. All writers, though, begin with some sort of diction and then develop it. Dickens, for example, began with a remarkable ability to mimic the speech of voluble lower-class characters, shady con men, and politicians, among other types. In the course of his career, he developed a diction for talking about the emotional lives of characters such as Paul Dombey, in Dombey and Son; Lady Dedlock, in Bleak House; Bradley Headstone, in Our Mutual Friend; and John Jasper, in The Mystery of Edwin Drood. Even Dickens, perhaps the most inherently gifted user of words ever to write an English novel, didn't have all dictions at his command from the beginning. Any diction is good enough for writing some novel, though. The question is, is it good enough (that is, does it have enough words and do you know how the words are properly used) for writing the novel you want to write? If it is not good enough, the best way to improve it is to learn more about the subject of your novel. One of the ways to learn something is to simply pick up the jargon of your subject. And at the beginning, when you are learning words and writing at the same time, it doesn't matter whether you simply regurgitate the words and phrases and ideas you learn; it matters only that you learn them.

在底层之上是措辞层，即对词语和表达方式的熟悉程度。感官数据和脑海中构思的想法在词语中进出，同时又被词语所具象化和赋予能量。我们可以将其想象成光的量子和波动理论的一种变体。词语是量子，思维过程是波。当作家创作时，思想的波滴落成词语的量子，这些词语又激发出新的思想波。每一次转化都会消耗能量，但也创造能量，因为尽管选择合适的词语需要付出努力，但合适的词语却能激发灵感。有些作家，例如弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫，拥有一种特殊的博学——对表达特定思想的所有可用词语都有广泛而精准的了解，这源于他对多种语言的掌握以及在不同领域的广泛阅读。另一些作家，例如查尔斯·狄更斯，则擅长再现通俗语言（民众的语言），因为他们拥有敏锐的听觉和良好的记忆力。他们的写作风格千差万别——这得益于人类普遍拥有的创造精辟生动的词句、谚语、俚语和塑造语调的天赋。有些作家，例如佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿，则选择专注于某种特定的方言，因为这种方言既富有表现力，又能体现她想要描绘的群体特征。然而，所有作家都是从某种语言风格起步，然后逐步发展完善的。例如，狄更斯一开始就展现出惊人的模仿能力，能够模仿滔滔不绝的底层人物、阴险的骗子和政客等各种人物的言谈。在他的创作生涯中，他逐渐形成了一套独特的语言风格，用来描绘《董贝父子》中的保罗·董贝、《荒凉山庄》中的戴德洛克夫人、《我们共同的朋友》中的布拉德利·海德斯通以及《艾德温·德鲁德之谜》中的约翰·贾斯珀等人物的情感生活。即使是狄更斯，这位或许是英语小说史上最具语言天赋的作家，也并非一开始就精通所有词汇。不过，任何词汇量都足以写出一部小说。问题在于，它是否足够好（也就是说，词汇量是否足够，以及你是否懂得如何正确使用这些词汇），足以写出你想要的小说？如果不够好，提升词汇量的最佳方法就是深入了解你的小说主题。学习新事物的方法之一就是掌握该主题的术语。在写作初期，当你边学边写的时候，是否只是机械地复述所学的词汇、短语和概念并不重要；重要的是你真正学会了它们。

Some writers are afraid of research, thinking perhaps it will contaminate their ideas, but the strangest fact about the novel (“novel” means “new or original”) is that novelty and originality are automatic. What is difficult is not to write something new but to write something interesting and true. As any piece becomes interesting and true, it becomes original. On the other hand, many original pieces of writing never find readers because they are solipsistic, tedious, tendentious, or self-indulgent. To pursue truth and interest is much more productive than to pursue originality, which will happen in any case. As evidence, I offer my experience teaching beginning undergraduate students. In the course of some fourteen semesters, with at least twenty-five students per semester, I never mixed up students or forgot their names after I had read their first stories. No two stories were ever alike, even if the students had never written before in their lives, even if, no doubt, some of the students were recycling ideas from stories they had read. The student could not help remaking his material in his own image. But not every story was interesting. The ways that the students made the stories interesting invariably made them more original, but they could get more original without getting more interesting. So from the standpoint of enlarging your diction, do not be afraid of any sort of contamination of your linguistic purity by the research you pursue.

有些作家害怕研究，认为研究可能会污染他们的创作思路，但小说（“小说”意为“新的”或“原创的”）最奇特之处在于，新颖性和原创性是自然而然产生的。难的不是写出新的东西，而是写出有趣且真实的东西。任何作品一旦变得有趣且真实，它就具有了原创性。另一方面，许多原创作品却无人问津，因为它们过于自恋、枯燥乏味、带有偏见或自我放纵。追求真理和趣味远比追求原创性更有成效，因为原创性无论如何都会出现。作为佐证，我以自己教授本科新生的经历为例。在大约十四个学期里，每个学期至少有二十五个学生，我从未弄混过学生，也从未在读过他们的第一篇故事后忘记他们的名字。没有两个故事是相同的，即使这些学生以前从未写过东西，即使毫无疑问，有些学生会借鉴他们读过的故事中的创意。学生们总是会不由自主地用自己的方式重塑素材。但并非每个故事都引人入胜。学生们使故事引人入胜的方式总是能让故事更具原创性，但原创性并不一定意味着故事本身也更有趣。因此，从拓展词汇量的角度来看，不要害怕你的研究会对你的语言纯粹性造成任何形式的“污染”。

The layer above diction is that of story and character, or plot and protagonist. The special appeal of the novel is the alternation of action and reflection—something happens, it is given meaning by either the narrator or the charactors, then something else happens that grows out of the meaning given the first event, which is then given meaning, and so on, until the climax—the largest action, and the denouement, the final meaning. The balance between story and character is unique to every novel, and the balance between action and meaning is different for every author, but every novel has both. Characters confronted by events must make choices, which reveal and develop their characters. Events are shaped by the choices of those involved in them. Events naturally possess energy that manifests itself as suspense, but mere events can jade the reader if they are too meaningless. Beginning novelists are often naturally event types or meaning types. As you accumulate paragraphs and pages, observe what intrigues you more—setting a scene and making something happen, or considering how the event is to be understood or felt. You will fall into one camp or the other. The side that does not come easily to you is the side you should develop by intelligently broadening your reading and learning how other authors negotiate the pitfalls of each. Fiction is not so much about what happens as about how it happens; how it happens is intimately bound up with who does it.

在措辞之上，是故事和人物，或者说情节和主人公。小说的独特魅力在于行动与反思的交替——某件事发生，叙述者或人物赋予它意义；接着又发生另一件事，它从前一件事的意义中衍生而来，然后又被赋予新的意义，如此循环往复，直至高潮——最宏大的行动，以及结局——最终的意义。故事与人物之间的平衡对每部小说而言都是独一无二的，行动与意义之间的平衡对每位作者而言也各不相同，但每部小说都包含这两者。面对事件的人物必须做出选择，这些选择揭示并塑造了他们的性格。事件的发生受到相关人员选择的影响。事件本身蕴含着能量，这种能量会以悬念的形式展现出来，但如果事件本身过于空洞，就会令读者感到厌倦。初学者往往自然而然地分为两种类型：一种是事件型，另一种是意义型。随着你积累段落和篇幅，观察一下什么更能吸引你——是营造场景、推动情节发展，还是思考如何理解或感受事件。你最终会归入其中一派。你应该努力培养的，正是那些你觉得难以驾驭的阵营。你需要通过理性地拓展阅读，学习其他作家如何巧妙地应对各种写作陷阱，才能真正掌握它们。小说与其说是关于发生了什么，不如说是关于事情是如何发生的；而事情是如何发生的，又与叙述者是谁息息相关。

The primary failure of event and therefore of plot is that what happens is not understandable to the reader. This can be a problem of organization—the sequence of events is not understandable or cannot be visualized very clearly because there is too little material or too much. But even when the events are understandable, they may be implausible, not interesting, or not compelling. The solution for such problems is in character and meaning. Henry James was a great advocate of placing the narrative point of view firmly in the mind of one or two minor characters present at the action of the novel who happened to be good-quality witnesses. Their predilections would dictate organization, visualization, and emotional involvement in the action and also would attest to its significance and interest. A risk of James's method is that all events and their emotional impact would be secondhand—the danger for the reader is that she might be lost in the intricacies of the story without enough emotional motivation to keep going. But even a novelist who doesn't adopt as rigid a system for solving these particular plot problems as James did must use his characters to organize the plot and give it significance. If we take Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White as an example of a novel (a mystery) in which the plot must work, Collins's method, of entering the viewpoints of various characters (all of whom are a bit clichd), works admirably—each diary document pictures the somewhat ridiculous action vividly, implies that there is more here than meets the eye, and hits the special emotional note that character is there to supply. The variety enlivens the proceedings, and the reader is carried along perhaps in spite of herself. The same is true of Dracula —if we had to see Count Dracula from a single point of view over and over again, he would lose his dangerous powers by becoming too familiar to us; but seeing him intermittently, combined with witnessing each character's speculations and dreads, gives the count power without overtaxing the author's inventiveness.

事件（进而情节）失败的主要原因在于读者无法理解所发生的事情。这可能是组织结构的问题——事件的顺序难以理解，或者由于素材过少或过多而无法清晰地呈现出来。但即便事件本身可以理解，它们也可能显得不合情理、缺乏趣味或缺乏吸引力。解决这类问题的关键在于人物塑造和意义构建。亨利·詹姆斯大力提倡将叙事视角牢牢地置于小说事件发生时在场的一两个次要人物的脑海中，而这些人物恰好是优秀的见证者。他们的偏好将决定事件的组织结构、形象呈现和情感投入，同时也将印证事件的意义和趣味性。詹姆斯这种方法的风险在于，所有事件及其情感影响都将是间接的——读者可能会迷失在错综复杂的故事情节中，却缺乏足够的情感动力继续读下去。但即便小说家不像詹姆斯那样采用如此严谨的体系来解决这些特定的情节问题，他们也必须运用人物来组织情节并赋予其意义。以威尔基·柯林斯的《白衣女人》为例，这部小说（一部悬疑小说）的情节必须引人入胜。柯林斯采用的叙事手法——从不同角色（尽管都有些老套）的视角切入——堪称妙笔生花。每篇日记都生动地描绘了略显荒诞的情节，暗示着事情远不止表面那么简单，并精准地触及了角色所应有的情感。这种多样性使故事更加生动，读者或许会在不知不觉中被卷入其中。同样的道理也适用于《德古拉》——如果我们总是从同一个视角来看待德古拉伯爵，他就会因为过于熟悉而失去其危险的力量；但通过间歇性的视角转换，结合对每个角色的猜测和恐惧的观察，既赋予了伯爵强大的力量，又不会过度消耗作者的创造力。

For many authors, the best combination of clear observation and immediacy is a first-person narrator narrating his or her “unfolding.” A wonderful example of this technique is Jamaica Kincaid's Annie John , a short novel about the inner life of an adolescent girl on the Caribbean island of Antigua. Kincaid's style, which is very controlled but rich, works to finesse the two most serious pitfalls of first-person narration—the temptation of digressiveness and the temptation of self-dramatization. The proper balance between action and self-revelation is hard to find. If the world of the novel gets too complex to efficiently portray, the first-person narrator can lose himself in the mix and comes off as paler and less interesting than the other characters, but if the narrator seems interested in himself to the exclusion of all the other characters that seem potentially interesting to the reader, he can seem solipsistic and dull. But views on this vary, and an author can make a case for anything—the contemporary novelist William T Vollmann's argument for writing only in the first person, including in theoretical and nonfiction works, is that to write in the first person is to acknowledge that all ideas and opinions are subjective and to take responsibility for them.

对许多作家而言，清晰的观察和身临其境的感受的最佳结合，莫过于第一人称叙述者讲述其内心世界的“展开”。牙买加·金凯德的小说《安妮·约翰》便是这一技巧的绝佳范例。这部短篇小说讲述了加勒比海安提瓜岛上一位少女的内心世界。金凯德的文风克制而丰富，巧妙地避开了第一人称叙述的两大陷阱——离题和自我戏剧化。在情节推进和自我剖析之间找到恰当的平衡点并非易事。如果小说世界过于复杂，难以有效展现，第一人称叙述者便会迷失其中，显得黯然失色，不如其他角色那样引人入胜；但如果叙述者只关注自身，而忽略了其他可能吸引读者的角色，则会显得自恋而乏味。但对此的看法各不相同，作者可以为任何事情辩护——当代小说家威廉·T·沃尔曼认为，包括理论和非虚构作品在内，写作都应该只用第一人称，因为用第一人称写作意味着承认所有想法和观点都是主观的，并对其负责。

Nevertheless, all narrative voices are equally conceits, and as long as you understand that the alternating rhythm of action and reflection, plot and character must feed one another, you can choose any manner of going back and forth that is comfortable to you, the author, and suitable to the subject.

然而，所有叙述声音都同样是虚构的，只要你明白行动与反思、情节与人物的交替节奏必须相互促进，你就可以选择任何你（作者）觉得舒服且适合主题的来回切换方式。

One layer higher on the pyramid, requiring more thought and adding a more sophisticated dimension to your work, are the complementary concepts of setting and theme—or, you might say, the specific and the general. When Captain Ahab sets out on the Pequod in search of a particular white whale, he is not the same person as the unnamed captain of the Bachelor , a “glad ship of good luck” the Pequod meets on the Japanese cruising ground. Melville shows by name and description that first and foremost we are to consider a particular man whose ship is also particular in all its features. The March sisters, in Little Women , do not live in California. As I Lay Dying does not take place in Paris. Persuasion takes place in Bath and Tristram Shandy takes place in Yorkshire. Prince Myshkin is not from Trieste and Zeno never visits St. Petersburg. Arnost Lustig's Lovely Green Eyes is not about Mississippi. The Bride of Lammermoor lives in a particular Scottish landscape because the loyalties of her mother, father, and lover are dictated in large part by territorial conflicts that are also religious conflicts, and her fate is partly determined by local superstitions. The originating impulse for many novels is an author's belief that a particular locality is interesting and worthy of entrance into cultural commerce—that Dickens's London is worth looking at, but so is Egdon Heath (Thomas Hardy) or Cairo (Naguib Mahfouz). The paradox is that not only is each of these places equally in the world, each of these places equally is the world. The nature of the novel itself asserts this, by contrast to almost all the rest of conventional human wisdom, which states that there are “centers” and “peripheries.” In the Earth's Big Bookstore, all novels, no matter where they are set, fall silent and disappear when the covers are closed. When the covers of one of them are opened, the world of that book becomes the center of the world, and the rest of the world and the rest of the books revolve around it. The particular becomes general, and the relationship between setting (which includes all of the characters’ circumstances) and theme (which are conclusions to be drawn about the characters’ humanity) becomes manifest.

在金字塔的更高一层，需要更多思考，也为你的作品增添更精妙的维度的是互补的概念——背景与主题，或者说，具体与普遍。当亚哈船长驾驶“裴廓德号”去寻找一头特定的白鲸时，他并非“裴廓德号”在日本海域遇到的那艘“幸运之船”——“单身汉号”上那位不知名的船长。梅尔维尔通过姓名和描述表明，我们首先要关注的是一个具体的人，他的船也同样具有独特的特征。《小妇人》中的马奇姐妹并不住在加利福尼亚。《我弥留之际》的故事并非发生在巴黎。《劝导》的故事发生在巴斯，《项狄传》的故事发生在约克郡。梅什金王子并非来自的里雅斯特，芝诺也从未到访过圣彼得堡。阿诺斯特·卢斯蒂格的《美丽的绿眼睛》并非以密西西比河为背景。 《拉默穆尔的新娘》之所以发生在苏格兰的某个特定地域，是因为她的母亲、父亲和爱人的忠诚在很大程度上受制于领土冲突，而这些冲突也包含宗教冲突；她的命运也部分由当地的迷信所决定。许多小说的创作动力源于作者对某个特定地域的喜爱，认为它值得被纳入文化交流——狄更斯笔下的伦敦值得一看，埃格登荒原（托马斯·哈代）或开罗（纳吉布·马哈福兹）也同样如此。悖论在于，这些地方不仅同样存在于世界之中，它们本身也同样是世界的一部分。小说的本质本身就印证了这一点，这与几乎所有其他关于“中心”和“边缘”的传统人类智慧形成鲜明对比。在地球的大书店里，所有小说，无论其背景设定在哪里，一旦合上书页，便会归于沉寂，消失无踪。当其中一本书的书页被翻开，这本书的世界便成为世界的中心，其余的世界和其余的书籍都围绕着它运转。特殊之处转化为普遍现象，背景（包括所有角色的境遇）与主题（即对角色人性的探讨）之间的关系也随之显现。

As with character and action, setting and theme feed one another. If your themes are too general, then investigate your setting more closely, and anchor your characters more deeply within their circumstances. If your story seems too trivial, then ask yourself about the connections between these circumstances and the larger human condition. This implies that both setting and theme are equally prone to problems, but this is not true—readers are so likely, either by instinct or training, to extrapolate from the particular to the general, that while they always need help visualizing and understanding specifics, they rarely need help connecting them to a larger concept of humanity. As with action, organization is the key—the real danger with particulars is that they will get confusing and hard to follow, like forest undergrowth that hides the path, or that they will proliferate in a way that suggests that the author is communicating primarily with himself—details piled upon details that are only partially depicted tax the reader's patience. In some ways this presents itself as a feature of style—is the author capable of density and lucidity at the same time? For me, Musil's The Man without Qualities rewards patience and attention with special depth and clarity, but many readers find the narrative dry and hard to follow. Likewise, the world is full of readers for whom every detail of Ulysses is worth keeping track of, but there are other readers who find this a thankless and tiresome task. Style, though, is the evidence of how the author's mind works. How he selects, arranges, and presents his particulars is the closest we get to who he is. As you write your story, you will inevitably reveal yourself.

如同人物与情节一样，背景与主题也相辅相成。如果你的主题过于宽泛，那就更深入地探究你的背景，并将你的人物更深刻地融入到他们的境遇之中。如果你的故事显得过于琐碎，那就思考这些境遇与更宏大的人性之间的联系。这似乎暗示着背景和主题都同样容易出现问题，但事实并非如此——读者出于本能或训练，往往会从具体细节推断出普遍意义，因此，尽管他们总是需要帮助来想象和理解具体细节，但他们很少需要帮助来将这些细节与更宏大的人性概念联系起来。如同情节一样，组织结构是关键——细节的真正危险在于它们会变得混乱难懂，就像森林中的灌木丛遮蔽了道路一样；或者它们会以一种让人感觉作者主要是在自言自语的方式泛滥——堆砌起来却只描绘了一部分的细节会耗尽读者的耐心。在某种程度上，这本身就是一种风格特征——作者能否同时做到内容丰富且清晰易懂？对我而言，穆齐尔的《没有个性的人》以其独特的深度和清晰度，值得耐心和专注的读者细细品读，但许多读者却觉得它的叙述枯燥乏味，难以理解。同样，世上有很多读者认为《尤利西斯》的每一个细节都值得细细品味，但也有一些读者觉得这是一项吃力不讨好且令人疲惫的任务。然而，文风恰恰体现了作者的思维方式。他如何选择、安排和呈现细节，是我们最接近他本人的方式。当你书写自己的故事时，你也必然会流露出自己的内心。

Every novel has themes. Most serious authors devote considerable thought to their themes, and, indeed, for many authors, the desire to explore or express certain ideas is the originating impulse for writing a novel. For some authors, the desire to write and the interest in character come first, and the product is some short stories; after a while, understanding the implications of a larger picture—a longer time frame or a larger group of characters—is inspiring, and a novel is begun. This may happen at about the time the writer is thirty, a good age for integrating what you have learned in childhood and youth. If we look at our list of authors, we can see that those who were writing in their twenties, whether successful or unsuccessful, often recon-ceived their work at about age thirty. Dickens was hugely popular and successful with The Pickwick Papers, Oliver Twist , and other episodic novels of his twenties, but when he began Martin Chuzzlewit at thirty, he took up his first overarching theme, that of selfishness, to give unity to both his writing and his social theories. Zola, who also wrote and published in his twenties, began his cycle of novels, Les Rougon-Macquart , when he was thirty. Henry Fielding's satirical ambitions got him censored for theatrical pieces he staged when he was thirty, so he turned to the novel, publishing Joseph Andrews when he was thirty-five. Herman Melville wrote several popular romances in his twenties; he was thirty-two when he published Moby-Dick. Henry James wrote Roderick Hudson , his first novel, when he was thirty-two. Thirty-two hardly seems young; it is more or less the age when the first stage of maturity is complete, when a marriage is contracted, and when children are born. It seems a culminating age to many people (though from the perspective of twenty-five years on, it seems to have been more like a commencement). At any rate, for an author in his thirties, theories and themes abound, and often, as for Fyodor Dostoevsky, who was arrested, nearly executed, and sent to a Siberian work camp when he was thirty, they consolidate or contradict ideas the author imbibed in his late teens and twenties. It is the sense of whole things coming together, of the flowering of reason and understanding, and of the connections between particulars that had hitherto seemed discrete that give rise to a novel. We may see in this the joy of an author voluntarily revealing himself or herself.

每部小说都有主题。大多数严肃作家都会对主题进行深入思考，事实上，对许多作家而言，探索或表达某些想法的渴望正是他们创作小说的最初动力。对一些作家来说，写作的欲望和对人物的兴趣先于主题，他们最初创作的是一些短篇小说；一段时间后，他们开始理解更宏大的图景——更长的时间跨度或更多的人物群体——所带来的启发，于是便着手创作小说。这种情况通常发生在作家三十岁左右，这个年龄段非常适合整合童年和青年时期所学到的东西。如果我们回顾一下作家名单，就会发现那些在二十多岁时开始写作的作家，无论成功与否，往往都会在三十岁左右重新构思他们的作品。狄更斯凭借《匹克威克外传》、《雾都孤儿》等二十多岁时创作的连载小说而广受欢迎，并取得了巨大成功。但当他三十岁开始创作《马丁·丘泽尔维特》时，他确立了第一个贯穿其作品的主题——自私，以此来统一他的作品和社会理论。左拉同样在二十多岁时开始写作和出版作品，他在三十岁时开始创作他的系列小说《鲁贡-马卡尔家族》。亨利·菲尔丁三十岁时，因其讽刺作品而遭到戏剧审查，于是他转而创作小说，并在三十五岁时出版了《约瑟夫·安德鲁斯》。赫尔曼·梅尔维尔在二十多岁时创作了几部广受欢迎的浪漫小说；他在三十二岁时出版了《白鲸》。亨利·詹姆斯在三十二岁时创作了他的第一部小说《罗德里克·哈德逊》。三十二岁似乎并不算年轻；三十多岁大致是成熟第一阶段完成、缔结婚姻、生育子女的年纪。对许多人来说，这似乎是一个巅峰的年纪（尽管从二十五年后的视角来看，它更像是一个开始）。无论如何，对于一位三十多岁的作家来说，各种理论和主题层出不穷，而且往往像陀思妥耶夫斯基那样——他在三十岁时被捕，险些被处决，并被送往西伯利亚劳改营——这些理论和主题会巩固或反驳他在十几岁末和二十几岁时吸收的思想。正是这种整体融合的感觉，理性与理解的绽放，以及此前看似独立的细节之间相互联系的觉醒，催生了一部小说。我们或许可以从中看到作家自愿袒露心扉的喜悦。

For every novelist, and therefore for you, wherever the larger ideas come from, they must seem at the time you employ them to be illuminating and bringing together intensely perceived particulars, expediting a work that could only be about these characters who are performing just these actions.

对于每一位小说家来说，也包括你，无论更宏大的思想源自何处，它们在被运用时都必须显得具有启发性，并将深刻感知到的细节联系起来，从而推动一部只能讲述这些角色所做这些行为的作品的创作。

At the apex of the pyramid is the element most general and yet most difficult to attain: complexity. Life itself is complex, and every subset of life (marriage, any professional enterprise, reproduction, owning and maintaining a home, any recreational activity) is equally complex. The brain is complex. Any individual activity contains as much complexity as the brain contemplating it is capable of. Complexity is like infinity—within the infinite set of numbers is an infinite subset of real numbers and another of whole numbers. Infinity makes all sets and subsets the same size, even though that is impossible. Thus it is with life and all its parts, including the novel.

金字塔的顶端是最普遍却也最难企及的要素：复杂性。生活本身就是复杂的，而生活的每一个组成部分（婚姻、任何职业活动、生育、拥有和维护房屋、任何休闲活动）都同样复杂。大脑也是复杂的。任何个体活动所包含的复杂性，取决于思考该活动的大脑所能承受的程度。复杂性如同无穷——在无限的数字集合中，存在着一个无限的实数子集和一个无限的整数子集。无穷使得所有集合和子集的大小相同，尽管这是不可能的。生活及其所有组成部分，包括小说，亦是如此。

More complexity is more fun as well as more true. One thing novelists habitually do is return to the same themes over and over. Since the energy of the novel and of the novelist's career is supplied by the limbic system of the brain, no doubt the conventional view is true, that the novelist can't help revisiting and worrying patterns of meaning and emotion that are important to his sense of who he is, or to his very notions of survival. Even so, when he returns to them each time, he brings new ideas and skills to them and attempts to illuminate them again to make better sense of them.

越复杂越有趣，也越真实。小说家们常常会反复探讨相同的主题。小说创作和小说家职业生涯的能量都源自大脑的边缘系统，因此，人们普遍认为，小说家无法避免地会反复审视和思考那些对其自我认知或生存意义至关重要的意义和情感模式，这种观点无疑是正确的。即便如此，每次重拾这些主题时，他都会带来新的想法和技巧，并试图再次阐明它们，使其更易于理解。

Any aspect of a novel may be made more complex, but not every aspect. Ulysses , for example, is probably the most complex novel in the English language, but the underlying story is not complex at all—two men set out on a particular day to do several fairly routine things. Toward the end of the day, they meet, connect, and then go home, possibly somewhat transformed by the events of the day and their meeting. Ulysses's complexity of psychology and style is imposed upon this simple structure as a theory about the true nature of literature and of life—even the most routine day is a culmination of all that has gone before it; even the most modern novel contains within itself all of the literature the author knows. By contrast, Wilkie Collins's The Woman in White has a highly complex plot and structure (different narrators tell different parts as the story unfolds) but a simple and clear style and a conventional theory of psychology (though the sociology of the characters is more interesting). It is an easier read than Ulysses but not so highly esteemed by critics. Emotional complexity is a feature of the modern novel, achieved through the general post-Flaubert recognition that characters often harbor conflicting and contradictory feelings about themselves and their situations.

小说的任何方面都可以变得更加复杂，但并非所有方面都如此。例如，《尤利西斯》可能是英语世界中最复杂的小说，但其故事内核却并不复杂——两个男人在某一天出发，去做一些相当例行的事情。临近傍晚，他们相遇、交流，然后各自回家，或许在这一天的经历和相遇中，他们都发生了一些改变。《尤利西斯》将复杂的心理描写和风格强加于这种简单的结构之上，以此来阐释文学和人生的真谛——即使是最平凡的一天，也是之前所有经历的累积；即使是最现代的小说，也包含了作者所知的全部文学知识。相比之下，威尔基·柯林斯的《白衣女人》情节和结构极其复杂（随着故事的展开，不同的叙述者讲述不同的部分），但风格简洁明了，心理学理论也较为传统（尽管对人物社会学的刻画更为有趣）。它比《尤利西斯》更容易阅读，但评论界对其评价却不高。情感复杂性是现代小说的一个特点，这是后福楼拜时代人们普遍认识到人物常常对自己和自己的处境抱有矛盾和冲突的情感而实现的。

Emotional complexity is easy to communicate—it can be exhaustively explored in a realistic manner, as Robert Musil explores the emotional lives of the main characters of The Man without Qualities , using a deliberate style rich in metaphor and figurative language that likens the mysterious emotional lives of the characters to known objects and ideas, as in the following passage, which efficiently details three types of relationships in the first sentence—Ulrich's perception of Diotima's relationship to him, Diotima's imitation of her husband, and her husband's care in his professional relationships—and then pinpoints the nature of Ulrich's ambivalence about Diotima in the next two sentences.

情感的复杂性很容易表达——它可以被以现实的方式详尽地探讨，就像罗伯特·穆齐尔在《没有个性的人》中探讨主人公的情感生活一样，他运用了一种刻意的、充满隐喻和比喻的语言风格，将人物神秘的情感生活比作已知的物体和概念，如下面的段落所示，它在第一句中有效地详细描述了三种关系——乌尔里希对迪奥蒂玛与他之间关系的感知、迪奥蒂玛对她丈夫的模仿以及她丈夫在职业关系中的关心——然后在接下来的两句话中准确地指出了乌尔里希对迪奥蒂玛的矛盾心理的本质。

In his first minutes of withdrawal, Diotima treated him with the bland courtesy—carefully and pointedly overdone—that she had copied from her husband, who made use of it in dealing with young aristocrats who happened to be his subordinates but
who might someday be his ministers…. When he was once more holding her mild, weightless hand in his, they looked into each other's eyes. Ulrich had the definite impression that they were destined to be a great nuisance to each other through love. [pp. 107 – 8 ]

在他最初离开的几分钟里，迪奥蒂玛用一种淡淡的礼貌——刻意而又过分——对待他，这种礼貌是她从丈夫那里学来的，她丈夫用这种方式对待那些年轻的贵族，他们碰巧是他的下属，但将来可能会成为他的大臣……当他再次握住她那轻柔的手时，他们彼此凝视着。乌尔里希确信，他们注定会因为爱情而彼此成为极大的麻烦。[第107-108页]

Or emotional complexity can be allusively explored through the radical simplification of story and style, as Kafka explores the emotional life of Josef K. by depicting it and relying on the inherently referential nature of language to supply ambiguity and larger significance. Emotional complexity is the sine qua non of the serious literary novel. Often linked to emotional complexity is moral complexity, which explores the relationship between feeling on the one hand and good and evil on the other, but moral complexity alone can energize a novel—Yukio Mishima's novel The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea , about some boys who murder the stepfather of one of their number, has few attractive characters and a very cool tone, but the author successfully engages the reader in the dilemmas of his characters’ moral lives and the larger exploration of what the existence of these characters at this time in history means about Japanese culture and morality.
