运气好的话，你会找到一个好方法来组织你需要完成的工作。我写《复制钥匙》（Duplicate Keys）的时候，这是一部推理小说，我做了一套卡片，每个场景一张。每张卡片上我列出了出场的角色、他们应该做什么、他们应该做什么但没做什么，以及此时此刻谁应该知道什么。因为悬疑小说只有通过精心揭示信息才能成立，所以我必须清楚地了解哪些信息已经揭示，哪些信息尚未揭示。我的卡片在《复制钥匙》中效果很好，但当我开始重写我的下一部中篇小说《善意》（Good Will）时，卡片的方法就完全不适用了。写《哞》（Moo）时，我制作了一个图表，顶部是章节编号，侧边是角色名称。每当一个角色出现在一个章节中，我就在章节和角色交叉的方框里画一个点。我可以一眼看出哪些角色被忽略了；当我完成初稿时，我的目标是让图表上的点分布均匀，代表整部小说。开始重写时，我发现许多人物都有各自的故事线，而且每条线索都必须逻辑清晰、环环相扣，即便它们最终交织成一个更大的情节。我首先将手稿拆分成各个独立的故事线，按篇幅由长到短排列，然后通读每一条故事线。接着，我修改了每条故事线，并将它们重新编织在一起。之后，我又通读了一遍全文，着重处理情节的连贯性和过渡衔接。

You have plenty of ingenuity. If you are receptive to your rough draft but detached from it, you will come up with some sort of method that will make your novel palpable to you and spur your inspiration with a sense of progress. Thinking about your novel and grasping it as a whole without going through it over and over will prevent you from making mistakes and falling into difficulties that arise simply from habit.

你极富创造力。如果你能以开放的心态审视自己的初稿，但又保持一定的距离，你就能找到一种方法，让你的小说在你心中鲜活起来，并激发你的创作灵感，让你感受到创作的进展。思考你的小说，从整体上把握它，而不是反复阅读，这将帮助你避免犯错，并防止你陷入因习惯而产生的困境。

Now it is time to start through it. You should want to go through it. Fear, shame, confusion, and ignorance can deter you as you do your rewrite, just as they may have in the rough draft; the antidotes are the same. This time, though, the momentum is on your side. What you have already written is pushing you forward. What you need to accomplish is smaller than what you have already achieved. For inspiration, keep reading novels. As you aim for perfection, don't forget that there is no perfect novel, that because every novel is built out of specifics, every novel offers some pleasures but does not offer some others, and while you can try to achieve as many pleasures as possible, some cancel out others. For example, it is very hard to achieve both broad and deep. The prime example of deep is, of course, Madame Bovary. At the time of its publication, no previous author had ever gone so deeply into the psychology of a single character, especially a female character with all sorts of female weaknesses. Madame Bovary was a revelation to its readers and changed the history of the novel, in part because it showed that the reader could make a connection even to an unsympathetic character, even to a woman who was not virtuous. Once Flaubert showed the way, many subsequent novelists used his method to extend the embrace of the novel to many protagonists who might have seemed unlikely in earlier times.

现在是时候开始修改了。你应该渴望完成它。恐惧、羞愧、困惑和无知可能会像在初稿阶段一样，阻碍你进行修改；但应对之法也是一样的。不过这一次，势头在你这边。你已经写好的内容正在推动你前进。你需要完成的目标比你已经取得的成就要小得多。为了获得灵感，可以继续阅读小说。当你追求完美时，不要忘记世上没有完美的小说，因为每部小说都是由具体细节构成的，所以每部小说都会提供一些乐趣，也会缺少另一些乐趣。虽然你可以努力追求尽可能多的乐趣，但有些乐趣会相互抵消。例如，很难同时做到既广博又深刻。深刻的典范当然是《包法利夫人》。在它出版的时候，没有任何一位作家像她那样深入地刻画过一个人物的心理，尤其是一个拥有各种女性弱点的女性角色。 《包法利夫人》对读者而言是一次启示，它改变了小说的历史，部分原因在于它表明，读者甚至可以与一个不讨喜的角色，甚至一个不贞洁的女性，建立情感联系。福楼拜开创了先河之后，许多后来的小说家都效仿他的方法，将小说的包容性扩展到许多在以前看来不太可能出现的主人公身上。

The novels of Henry James also serve as examples of deep. When E. M. Forster says of James in Aspects of the Novel , “Most of human life has to disappear before he can do us a novel” (p. 160 ), he attributes this to James's desire to make of every novel an artistic whole, and certainly this was one of James's preoccupations, but he also wanted to explore particular human feelings and impulses patiently and exhaustively, with intense and careful focus. When we enjoy The Portrait of a Lady or The Ambassadors , we are according James the privilege of saying a lot about a fairly small thing. James takes very seriously the idea that the unexamined life is not worth living. I may feel as strongly that the unlived life is not worth examining, but when I am reading Henry James, I am learning how to examine in greater detail, with more refinement of sensibility. A modern example of deep would be Jamaica Kincaid's Annie John , which is short but so evocatively written that we feel we have visited an island, and a consciousness, in the Caribbean in a way not otherwise possible than through this novel. Annie's problem is her vexed feelings for her mother, out of which grow all of her other feelings about Antigua, her father, herself, and the world. If the novel were broader , her feelings would be put into context and lose intensity. In the cases of Annie and Emma Bovary, the important thing is not what their feelings mean, but what they are, and whether the reader empathizes with them.

亨利·詹姆斯的小说也是深刻的典范。E·M·福斯特在《小说面面观》中谈到詹姆斯时说：“在他能为我们写出一部小说之前，大部分的人生经历都必须消失”（第160页），他认为这是因为詹姆斯渴望将每一部小说都打造成一个完整的艺术作品。这当然是詹姆斯关注的重点之一，但他同时也希望以专注而细致的笔触，耐心而透彻地探索特定的人类情感和冲动。当我们欣赏《贵妇画像》或《大使》时，我们实际上是在赋予詹姆斯一项特权，让他得以就一件看似微不足道的小事进行深刻的探讨。詹姆斯非常认真地看待“未经审视的人生不值得过”这一观点。我或许也同样强烈地认为，未经审视的人生不值得审视，但当我阅读亨利·詹姆斯的作品时，我正在学习如何以更细致、更敏锐的视角去审视人生。现代作品中深刻的一个例子是牙买加·金凯德的《安妮·约翰》。这部小说篇幅虽短，但文笔却极富感染力，仿佛带领读者亲身游历了加勒比海的一座岛屿，并深入体验了那里的某种精神世界，这种体验唯有通过这部小说才能实现。安妮的困境在于她对母亲复杂而矛盾的情感，而她对安提瓜岛、父亲、自身以及整个世界的所有其他感受都源于此。如果小说的篇幅更长，她的情感就会被置于特定的语境中，从而失去其强烈的感染力。对于安妮和艾玛·包法利而言，重要的不是她们的情感意味着什么，而是她们的情感本身是什么，以及读者是否能够感同身受。

Novelists of the nineteenth century tried over and over to get both broad and deep. That is one reason their novels ran eight hundred to nine hundred pages. Some nearly succeeded— Middlemarch nearly succeeds because after the first section about Dorothea, we retain a strong sense of kinship with her. The scenes of her marriage with Casaubon are affecting as well as brilliantly insightful. But in her effort to depict a whole place at an important time (the town of Middlemarch just before the parliamentary Reform Bill of 1832 ), Eliot is forced to drop Dorothea and apply her intensity of focus to other characters, like Lydgate and Rosamond Vincy and Fred Vincy and Mary Garth. The result is that although we end up wishing them well, they do fall into an authorial pattern, which is abstract and therefore distancing. Many readers would say that Ulysses achieves both broad and deep , and truly, Joyce enters the mind of Leopold Bloom as thoroughly as maybe it is possible to do, but the idleness of Bloom's concerns in the course of his day and the fact that he doesn't in the end act upon anything he learns, but instead goes to bed with his wife to all intents and purposes unchanged (he will, after all, get up the next morning and have a similar day, except that it won't be recorded for posterity), rob the novel of emotional impact for many readers. In the end, novelists who want both broad and deep are constrained by the form of the novel—prose elaborating and elaborating—to go on into multiple volumes, as Proust did. And as length increases, readers get intimidated and works become the property of specialists rather than of the reading public as a whole. Even Tolstoy had to make a choice in Anna Karenina —he had to limit himself to two couples, Anna and Vronsky and Levin and Kitty. To explore only four consciousnesses (along with a little exploration of Karenin), he allowed himself almost a thousand pages.

十九世纪的小说家们不断尝试兼顾广度和深度。这正是他们的小说篇幅动辄八九百页的原因之一。有些小说几乎成功了——《米德尔马契》几乎成功了，因为在描写多萝西娅的第一部分之后，我们仍然对她抱有强烈的亲近感。她与卡索邦的婚姻场景既感人至深，又极具洞察力。然而，为了描绘一个重要时期（1832年议会改革法案颁布前的米德尔马契镇）的整个地方，艾略特不得不放弃多萝西娅，转而将她全部的笔力集中于其他人物身上，例如利德盖特、罗莎蒙德·文西、弗雷德·文西和玛丽·加思。结果是，尽管我们最终都希望他们一切顺利，但他们仍然落入了作者的惯用模式，这种模式抽象而疏离。许多读者会说《尤利西斯》兼具广度和深度，的确，乔伊斯对利奥波德·布卢姆的内心世界刻画得淋漓尽致，但布卢姆终日无所事事，最终却并未将所学付诸行动，而是与妻子入睡，一切似乎都未曾改变（毕竟，第二天早上醒来，他依然会经历类似的一天，只不过这一天不会被后世记录下来），这使得这部小说在许多读者心中缺乏情感冲击力。最终，那些力求兼具广度和深度的作家，都会受到小说形式的限制——散文的不断展开——不得不像普鲁斯特那样，写成多卷本。而随着篇幅的增加，读者会感到畏惧，作品也逐渐沦为专家的专属，而非广大读者的阅读对象。即使是托尔斯泰，在《安娜·卡列尼娜》中也不得不做出选择——他只能将笔触限制在两对情侣身上：安娜和伏龙斯基，以及列文和基蒂。为了探索四种意识（以及对卡列宁的少量探索），他给自己写了将近一千页。

You may prefer broad. If so, you have plenty of company. Many comic novels, such as David Lodge's Small World and my own Moo , are broad. So is Naguib Mahfouz's The Harafish. But your critics are going to complain that your characters are stereotyped, thinly realized, or not very engaging. Some readers are happy to give up depth for pattern and breadth, for the sparkle of the author's vision, wit, and intelligence; others will tar you with the Dickensian brush—your works are not quite refined enough to be truly great, your psychological insights aren't very astute, you deal in types rather than real people, and finally they don't care as much about your characters as they do about the deep ones. But broad necessarily makes a pattern and so is intellectual and abstract. Deep necessarily hides the author's theories about psychological causes and effects beneath an illusion of unfolding humanity, and so is more emotionally appealing but perhaps not very interesting. Your job is to understand which you want to emphasize and to make the best of the possibilities of that alternative.

你或许偏爱宏大的叙事风格。如果是这样，你并不孤单。许多喜剧小说，例如大卫·洛奇的《小世界》和我自己的《哞》，都属于宏大的叙事风格。纳吉布·马哈福兹的《哈拉菲什》也是如此。但你的批评者会抱怨你的人物形象刻板、单薄，或者缺乏吸引力。有些读者乐于为了模式和广度而放弃深度，为了作者的远见卓识、机智和智慧而放弃深度；而另一些读者则会用狄更斯式的笔触来评判你——你的作品不够精炼，称不上真正伟大；你的心理洞察不够敏锐；你笔下的人物类型化，而非真实鲜活；最后，他们更关注那些深刻的人物，而不是你笔下的人物。但宏大的叙事必然会形成某种模式，因此也必然带有理性和抽象的色彩。而深刻的叙事则必然会将作者关于心理因果关系的理论隐藏在逐渐展开的人性幻象之下，因此它更具情感吸引力，但或许也缺乏趣味性。你的任务是理解你想强调哪一种，并充分利用这两种选择所带来的可能性。

Over the centuries, more authors have probably placed their bets on the realistic novel than on any other type. After all, one of the reasons the novel exists is to explore the dilemmas of the author and his contemporaries: Marguerite de Navarre was interested in the love problems that her circle knew firsthand or at one remove; Miguel de Cervantes confronted his knight and squire with typical travelers’ adventures at inns and along roadsides in a recognizable Spain. Henry Fielding was careful to set Tom Jones during a particular month of a particular military campaign—he used an almanac to be sure he even got the phases of the moon right. Realism is naturally interesting because most people can relate to realistic characters and problems, and realism is natural to the novel because of the mundane—let's say, prosaic—nature of prose. But realism, too, makes compromises. It goes in and out of fashion, and when it is out of fashion it is usually because readers feel that “realism” doesn't quite reproduce the surreal quality of life as they experience it. Realism is no less subjective than fabulism or surrealism, but realists and their readers agree that there is a generally accepted form that reality takes; that it can be depicted, read about, and agreed upon; and that its boundaries are fairly clear and separate it recognizably from unrealities such as insanity, fantasy, wishful thinking, heightened states of consciousness, and dreams. Realism can seem pedestrian and unoriginal, appealing only to readers without any sense of adventure. Realism is dogged by the need for plausibility and accountability. The problem is that plausible events are often not very much fun, while implausible events have to be depicted in detail and accounted for, and these requirements may take more time in the telling than the event is worth. Most literary best sellers are examples of realism, because realism has the widest audience, but most realistic novels get disdained by sophisticated critics as “middlebrow”—not innovative enough to be of interest to the most sophisticated readers. Some critics feel that the possibilities of realism have been fully explored, at least in America and Europe, in the dominant literary cultures. They might wonder if it is really necessary to redo Madame Bovary. The realistic novel, though, accepts the importance of the novel as a social document and the need for successive generations to depict the world as it appears to them. The realistic novel expresses the idea that normal life is intrinsically interesting, and that if the novelist is sufficiently insightful and observant, new wine can be poured into old bottles. And anyway, it's nice to have a large readership and maybe get your book made into a movie.

几个世纪以来，或许有更多作家将目光投向了现实主义小说，而非其他任何类型。毕竟，小说存在的意义之一，就是探索作者及其同时代人的困境：玛格丽特·德·纳瓦尔关注的是她身边的人亲身经历或间接感受到的爱情问题；米格尔·德·塞万提斯笔下的骑士和侍从，在西班牙的客栈和路边，上演着典型的旅行者奇遇。亨利·菲尔丁甚至煞费苦心地将《汤姆·琼斯》的故事设定在某个特定战役的某个特定月份——他甚至查阅了年鉴，以确保连月相都准确无误。现实主义之所以引人入胜，是因为大多数人都能与现实生活中的人物和问题产生共鸣；而现实主义也与小说本身相得益彰，因为散文本身就具有平凡——或者说，朴实——的特点。但现实主义也并非完美无缺，它也需要做出妥协。现实主义时而流行，时而过时，通常是因为读者觉得“现实主义”无法完全再现他们所体验到的超现实生活特质。现实主义与寓言或超现实主义一样具有主观性，但现实主义者及其读者都认同现实存在一种普遍接受的形式；现实可以被描绘、阅读和认可；而且现实的边界相当清晰，能够将其与诸如精神错乱、幻想、一厢情愿、高度意识状态和梦境等非现实事物明显区分开来。现实主义有时会显得平庸乏味，只对那些缺乏冒险精神的读者有吸引力。现实主义受制于对合理性和可解释性的追求。问题在于，合情合理的事件往往缺乏趣味性，而不合理的事件则需要详细描述和解释，而这些要求可能会使叙述的时间超过事件本身的价值。大多数文学畅销书都是现实主义作品，因为现实主义拥有最广泛的读者群，但大多数现实主义小说却被一些眼光挑剔的评论家斥为“平庸之作”——缺乏创新，无法吸引最资深的读者。一些评论家认为，至少在欧美主流文学文化中，现实主义的可能性已被充分挖掘。他们或许会质疑，是否真的有必要重写《包法利夫人》。然而，现实主义小说承认小说作为社会文献的重要性，以及后代需要描绘他们眼中的世界。现实主义小说表达了这样一种理念：平凡的生活本身就充满趣味，如果小说家足够敏锐，观察力足够强，就能赋予旧瓶装新酒。而且，拥有庞大的读者群，甚至有机会将自己的作品改编成电影，总是令人欣喜的。

If you are writing a comic novel, chances are it will have limited appeal no matter how funny it is, unless you are writing comforting nonsatirical books like those of P. G. Wodehouse. Every comic effort has a narrower potential audience than every realistic effort, because individual readers differ in their acceptance of the irreverence and disrespect inherent in the comic sensibility. What is scathing and off-putting to some is just right to others. What is mirthful and light to some is flat to others. If writing comic novels weren't wonderfully enjoyable, I doubt that anyone would make the effort, because the rewards are few—no prizes, no respect, and not many sales, only the satisfaction (considerable though it is) of a joke well told. Fortunately, if you are writing a comic novel, it is because you have a certain verbal gift, you can't be stopped anyway, and you understand already that phrase-turning is its own reward.

如果你写的是喜剧小说，无论它多么滑稽，受众都可能有限，除非你写的是像P·G·伍德豪斯那样轻松愉悦的非讽刺作品。所有喜剧作品的潜在读者群都比现实主义作品要窄，因为每个读者对喜剧中固有的不敬和轻蔑的接受程度各不相同。对某些人来说尖刻刺耳、令人反感的东西，对另一些人来说却恰到好处。对某些人来说轻松愉快的东西，对另一些人来说却索然无味。如果写喜剧小说不是件乐事，我怀疑会有人愿意尝试，因为回报寥寥——没有奖项，没有尊重，销量也不高，只有讲好笑话带来的满足感（尽管这种满足感也相当可观）。幸运的是，如果你正在写喜剧小说，那是因为你拥有某种语言天赋，反正你也停不下来，而且你已经明白，妙语连珠本身就是一种乐趣。

A comic novel has two aspects, and they are strongly distinguished by the author's political sensibility. Both aspects have to be funny, which is a stylistic requirement. Every witticism is like a small bubble that pops in the text, brightening it and giving it a small push forward, but every witticism sets up the need for another, and most readers want the text to be popping with regularity. Beyond this, though, is the conservative/liberal issue. A traditional comic play, which is the paradigm of comedy, promises several marriages at the end of the fifth act, and these marriages represent social integration and the resolution of conflict. The liberal comic novel offers the same sort of social resolution—it is a funny novel with a comic plot structure, where conflicts are resolved and antagonistic feelings are shown to be illusory. Thus the liberal comic novel at bottom expresses a worldview that is a bit at odds with other types of novels. If, in the realistic novel, the protagonist normally sacrifices something for the sake of knowledge—he ends up not happier, but smarter—in the liberal comic novel he ends up happier and smarter. This movement contradicts what many serious readers consider the norm, so if you are writing a liberal comic novel, you have to understand the possibilities of your material in a way that makes happier and smarter plausible rather than implausible. One of my favorite examples of a liberal comic novel is Nancy Mitford's Love in a Cold Climate , in which a young girl insists on marrying a confirmed bachelor who is also one of her mother's old lovers, the heir to the enormous family estate turns out to be a penniless young gay man living by his wits in Paris, and all the characters are rejuvenated and redeemed by a large infusion of French style.

喜剧小说包含两个方面，而作者的政治敏感性是区分这两个方面的重要因素。这两个方面都必须幽默，这是其文体上的要求。每一个妙语都像一个气泡，在文本中破裂，为其增添光彩，推动情节向前发展；但每一个妙语都引出了下一个妙语的出现，大多数读者都希望文本能够定期地迸发出这些妙语。然而，除此之外，还存在保守主义/自由主义的问题。作为喜剧典范的传统喜剧，通常会在第五幕结尾促成几桩婚姻，这些婚姻象征着社会融合和冲突的化解。自由主义喜剧小说也提供了类似的社会解决方案——它是一部情节结构滑稽的幽默小说，其中冲突得以化解，敌对情绪被揭示为虚幻。因此，自由主义喜剧小说本质上表达了一种与其他类型小说略有不同的世界观。如果说在现实主义小说中，主人公通常会为了求知而牺牲一些东西——最终他不会更快乐，但会更聪明——那么在自由主义喜剧小说中，他最终既快乐又聪明。这种趋势与许多严肃读者所认为的常态相悖，因此，如果你要创作一部自由主义喜剧小说，你必须理解你的素材所蕴含的可能性，使主人公的快乐和聪明成为合情合理的情节，而不是不合情理的情节。我最喜欢的自由主义喜剧小说之一是南希·米特福德的《寒冷气候下的爱情》。小说中，一位年轻女孩坚持要嫁给一位坚定的单身汉，而这位单身汉恰好是她母亲的旧情人之一；庞大家族遗产的继承人原来是一位在巴黎靠机智谋生的穷困潦倒的年轻同性恋男子；所有角色都因浓郁的法式风情而焕发新生，获得救赎。

The conservative comic novel, which doesn't propose that happiness is a possible outcome, has its own difficulties, because a dark world-view combined with lots of jokes almost inevitably carries a tone of contempt and can be quite distancing for the reader, who enjoys the jokes for a while but can be offended by what she perceives as cruelty. The conservative comic novelist, or satirist, almost inevitably adopts a superior tone that challenges the reader's “navet.” The jokes have to be especially good and the satire especially smart to sustain the reader's commitment (the novels of Kingsley Amis such as Lucky Jim and The Old Devils qualify as conservative comic novels).

保守派喜剧小说并不认为幸福是一种可能的结果，因此它自身也存在一些问题。因为阴暗的世界观加上大量的笑话，几乎不可避免地会带有轻蔑的意味，这会让读者感到疏离。读者或许会觉得这些笑话很有趣，但很快就会被其中看似残酷的内容所冒犯。保守派喜剧小说家或讽刺作家几乎总是会采取一种高人一等的语气，挑战读者的“天真”。为了维持读者的兴趣，笑话必须特别精彩，讽刺必须特别精妙（金斯利·艾米斯的《幸运的吉姆》和《老魔鬼》等小说就属于保守派喜剧小说）。

And while you, the author, are exerting yourself to achieve the impossible, since comic novels are perhaps the most difficult form, you must understand that your effort itself is not appreciated. What could be more honorable and worthy than trying to raise a laugh? And yet, readers and reviewers seem to react with special venom to comic or satiric novels they don't like. I am not sure why this is, but as a result, it's a good thing that writing a comic novel is its own reward.

而作为作者的你，正竭尽全力去完成看似不可能的任务——毕竟喜剧小说或许是最难创作的体裁——你必须明白，你的努力本身并不会得到赏识。还有什么比逗人发笑更值得称道的呢？然而，读者和评论家似乎对他们不喜欢的喜剧或讽刺小说格外苛刻。我不确定这是为什么，但正因如此，创作喜剧小说本身就是一种莫大的乐趣。

Experimental fiction can take any form, but essentially it is more or less nonrealistic—you are playing with the narrator/character/novelist relationship and in the process dispensing with the realist illusion that the reader is watching the characters go about their business as if they were fellow citizens, only with special access to their inner lives. You undoubtedly wrote an experimental rough draft because you are smart and inventive and not content to do again what has been done before. You are very aware that a novel is “novel,” so you want your novel to live up to the promise of the form. Congratulations. But the special burden of the experimental novel is that you have to continue to be smart, and then get smarter. An intriguing concept will carry you a long way, but not all the way. You have to exploit your material from beginning to end—like jokes, inventiveness begets the need for more inventiveness. At the same time, your inventiveness, I am sorry to say, must have a point that the reader finds enlightening. The promise of any theme-oriented novel, especially one that flouts convention, is that you have a reason and purpose in flouting convention, and that if the reader wades into the unfamiliar stream that is your novel, she will get something out of it besides an unpleasant experience. As with comic fiction, some readers have a smaller capacity to tolerate the unknown, and your audience may turn out to be limited, but if you were interested in writing a standard realistic novel, that's what you would be doing. Remember above all that readers outside of graduate school really do not care what is good for them. It may be that reading your novel (or Henry Miller's novels) will set them straight forever, but they do not care about that in the slightest. Even you, as smart as you are, have no powers over the reader except the usual seductive ones. Experimental novelists are in some ways the most frustrated, because they are visionary. Every experimental novel is a dose of medicine in the form of unpalatable truths or a radical shift in perspective. If you are an experimental novelist, you are probably some sort of malcontent anyway, and your experience writing, selling, and publishing your novel could sour, or further sour, your relationship to society. As a result of all these considerations, your task in rewriting your rough draft is never to compromise, because no reward will compensate you for the feeling that you gave in to weakness, whatever its source. It is easier to do it your way, to polish the jewel until it is just how you want it, and maybe never find a publisher or a readership, than it is to take advice you disdain and end up with a product you cannot in good conscience claim as your own.

实验小说可以采取任何形式，但其本质或多或少是非现实的——你是在玩味叙述者/角色/小说家之间的关系，并在这一过程中打破现实主义的幻觉，即读者并非像普通公民一样旁观角色的日常生活，只是拥有了窥探他们内心世界的特殊权限。毫无疑问，你之所以写出实验性的初稿，是因为你聪明且富有创造力，并且不满足于重复前人做过的事情。你非常清楚小说的“新颖性”，所以你希望你的小说能够不负其形式之名。恭喜你。但实验小说的特殊之处在于，你必须保持聪明，并且不断超越自我。一个引人入胜的概念可以让你走得很远，但并非万能。你必须从头到尾充分利用你的素材——就像笑话一样，创造力会催生出更多创造力的需求。同时，恕我直言，你的创造力必须具有能够启发读者的意义。任何主题小说，尤其是那些打破常规的小说，其价值在于你打破常规是有理由和目的的，而且如果读者涉足你小说这片陌生的领域，除了不愉快的阅读体验之外，还能有所收获。就像喜剧小说一样，有些读者对未知事物的容忍度较低，你的读者群可能也会比较有限，但如果你只想写一部标准的现实主义小说，那你最终会做的就是写一部现实主义小说。记住，研究生以外的读者其实并不关心什么对他们有益。也许读了你的小说（或者亨利·米勒的小说）会让他们幡然醒悟，但他们对此毫不在意。即使是你，再聪明，除了惯用的诱惑手段之外，也无法左右读者。实验小说家在某种程度上是最沮丧的，因为他们富有远见。每一部实验小说都是一剂良药，以令人难以接受的真相或视角上的根本性转变的形式呈现。如果你是一位实验小说家，你或许本身就有些愤世嫉俗，而写作、推销和出版小说的经历可能会恶化你与社会的关系。正因如此，你在修改初稿时绝不能妥协，因为任何回报都无法弥补你屈服于软弱所带来的痛苦，无论这种软弱源于何处。与其听从你鄙夷的建议，最终得到一部你无法昧着良心称之为自己作品的作品，不如按自己的方式创作，精雕细琢，直到它完全符合你的心意，即便可能永远找不到出版商或读者。

Attempt to do your first rewrite as you did your rough draft, as continuously as possible and without consulting anyone. Inevitably you possess the several intelligences that go into writing a novel in varying degrees, and these differences will manifest themselves as you work. If your sharper intelligences are psychological and verbal, you will round out your characters and improve your style, but perhaps your logical/structural intelligence is a bit lacking, so you will not understand how to make the larger structure work—possibly you won't even notice that the balance is off. An interesting novel with structural weaknesses is George Eliot's The Mill on the Floss , a book Eliot felt to be autobiographical, even though she gave Maggie Tulliver a quite different life and death from her own. The Mill on the Floss is meant to have a plot, with a dramatic climax in which Maggie is lured away by her cousin's fianc, returns in disgrace, and then dies trying to save her estranged brother in a flood. Really, though, the climax, as dramatic as it is, seems tacked onto the interesting and complex portrait of the drama of Maggie's search for some way to use her intelligence, her passions, and her idealism. The novel purports to be about the conflict, much of it covert, between Maggie and her disapproving older brother, but Eliot never successfully portrays Tom's appeal. Maggie ends up seeming too good for him in a way the author doesn't understand. The structure of the novel gives nearly equal weight to all the parts of Maggie's life—childhood, family, her father's ruin, her relationship with Tom, the love plot. Only Maggie's intensity endures throughout, so a story meant to build dramatically by the accretion of incident ends up seeming arbitrary. A real climax has to seem to solve the problem the exposition poses. The climax of The Mill on the Floss merely ends the problem of Maggie's inability to fit into the world and the family into which she was born.

尝试像写初稿那样进行第一次修改，尽可能连续地修改，并且不要咨询任何人。你必然具备创作小说所需的各种智能，只是程度不同，这些差异会在你的写作过程中显现出来。如果你的智能更偏向心理智能和语言智能，你就能更好地塑造人物，提升写作风格，但你的逻辑/结构智能可能略显不足，因此你可能无法理解如何构建整体结构——甚至可能根本察觉不到这种失衡。乔治·艾略特的《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》就是一部结构上存在缺陷的有趣小说。艾略特认为这部小说带有自传性质，尽管她赋予玛吉·图利弗的人生经历与她本人截然不同。《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》原本应该有一个情节，并在高潮部分展现了玛吉被表妹的未婚夫引诱而去，最终落得狼狈不堪的下场，并在洪水中为救她疏远的哥哥而牺牲。然而，尽管高潮部分扣人心弦，却显得像是生硬地附加在玛吉寻找运用自身智慧、热情和理想的方式这一引人入胜且错综复杂的人生轨迹之上。小说声称要讲述玛吉与她那不赞同她的哥哥汤姆之间的冲突（其中许多冲突是隐晦的），但艾略特始终未能成功地刻画出汤姆的魅力。最终，玛吉似乎配不上他，而作者对此却浑然不觉。小说的结构几乎平等地展现了玛吉人生的各个方面——童年、家庭、父亲的破产、她与汤姆的关系以及爱情线。唯有玛吉的强烈情感贯穿始终，因此，原本旨在通过事件的累积来构建戏剧性高潮的故事，最终却显得随意而突兀。一个真正的高潮必须能够解决前文提出的问题。《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》的高潮仅仅是结束了玛吉无法融入她出生的世界和家庭这一难题。

Maybe, like Henry James, you have a genius for structure, even though your style is flat and unevocative. Into that category I would put Dracula. Bram Stoker succeeds in achieving his uncanny effects because the mystery they represent contrasts with the pedestrian voices of his narrators, who never pretend to be anything other than average late Victorian folks with some special knowledge, but conventional attitudes, toward love and morality.

或许，你像亨利·詹姆斯一样，拥有结构上的天赋，尽管你的文风平淡乏味。我会把《德古拉》归入这一类。布拉姆·斯托克之所以能营造出那种诡异的氛围，是因为他笔下神秘的事物与叙述者平凡的嗓音形成了鲜明的对比。这些叙述者从不伪装成什么特别的人，他们只是拥有一些特殊知识的普通维多利亚时代晚期居民，但在爱情和道德方面却秉持着传统的观念。

The key to the first rewrite is to fix it all the best you can, working through it until you are fairly satisfied not only with the effort you've made but also with the product you've come up with. You might say it is not perfect, but you are reasonably satisfied with it. This means that you and it have more or less parted ways—it more or less stands on its own, setting out its terms and fulfilling them without tempting you to justify it or make excuses for it or, indeed, to sit with a reader and anxiously oversee her reading of it!

第一次修改的关键在于尽你所能地修改，反复推敲，直到你不仅对自己的努力感到满意，也对最终成果感到满意为止。你或许会说它并不完美，但你对它已经相当满意了。这意味着你和它已经或多或少地分道扬镳——它或多或少地独立存在，设定并履行着自己的规则，而不会让你忍不住去为它辩解或找借口，更不会让你坐在读者旁边，焦虑地监督她阅读！

As you come to the end of the first rewrite you will have to deal with the denouement, which you have been avoiding. The problem of the denouement is that you have to seem to the reader to know what you have been doing, but not to be imposing any final thoughts about the meaning of the novel, or having last-minute ideas. You also have to get your narrative voice and your characters gracefully off the stage, and you have to stay within the tone you have set up. You cannot betray impatience, even though you are probably relieved to be approaching the end of a lengthy task. The key to a good denouement is not thought, though, but intuition. If you solve all the problems of your novel in successive drafts, if you become throughly familiar with your novel so everything about it, but especially some feeling it gives you, is present in your mind, your limbic brain will provide you with the denouement. You may be dissatisfied with the denouement until the very end because it is literally beyond your understanding but know it is right anyway. The most famous denouement in English literature are the last words of Molly Bloom at the end of Ulysses , “and yes I said yes I will Yes.” It is famous because it is both appropriate and full of pleasure and hope. It sums up all the ironies of Leopold Bloom's marriage, but also all the good will in Bloom himself.

当你完成第一次修改时，你将不得不面对你一直回避的结局。结局的难点在于，你必须让读者觉得你明白自己一直在做什么，但又不能强加任何关于小说意义的最终想法，或者临时抱佛脚。你还要巧妙地让叙述者和人物退出舞台，并保持你设定的基调。即使你可能因为即将完成这项漫长的任务而感到如释重负，你也不能流露出急躁。然而，好的结局的关键不在于思考，而在于直觉。如果你在连续的修改中解决了小说的所有问题，如果你对小说了如指掌，以至于关于它的一切，尤其是它带给你的某些感受，都清晰地印在你的脑海中，那么你的大脑边缘系统就会为你提供结局。你或许会在最后一刻对结局感到不满，因为它确实超出了你的理解范围，但你知道它是正确的。英国文学中最著名的结局莫过于《尤利西斯》结尾处莫莉·布卢姆的遗言：“是的，我说过，我愿意。” 这句话之所以闻名，是因为它既贴切又充满喜悦与希望。它概括了利奥波德·布卢姆婚姻中的所有讽刺之处，同时也展现了布卢姆本人所有的美好愿望。

Now you are ready to show your novel to someone.

现在你可以把你的小说拿给别人看了。

Ideally, your first reader will have an editorial sensibility, which may be defined as being interested in the novel as a form, knowledgeable, somewhat detached from you and your life, and without a strong investment of his or her own in what a novel should be (that is, that it should be like something your reader would write). As noted above, relatives, friends, and other novelists do not make the best first readers because they inevitably feel conflicts of interest. However, editorial sensibilities are not as available as they might be, and you may have to show it to someone who is less than ideal. If so, an educated novelreader would be your best choice, possibly a novelist who teaches creative writing in a summer program.

理想情况下，你的第一位读者应该具备编辑的敏锐度，这种敏锐度可以定义为：对小说这种文体感兴趣，知识渊博，与你和你的生活保持一定的距离，并且不会对小说应该是什么样子（也就是说，它应该像你的读者自己写的东西）抱有强烈的个人偏好。如上所述，亲戚、朋友和其他小说家并非最佳的第一位读者，因为他们不可避免地会感到利益冲突。然而，具备编辑敏锐度的人并非唾手可得，你可能不得不把书稿交给一些并非理想人选的人。如果真是这样，一位受过良好教育的小说读者或许是你的最佳选择，比如一位在暑期创意写作课程中教授小说的作家。

When you have your conversation about the novel you have written, once again (because this is very difficult) try to direct it toward analysis rather than judgment. Inevitably and unfortunately, the conversation will open with some summary judgment of the novel. You must let this opening go by and pay attention to the subsequent analysis, even if your reader asserts that your novel is a literary abomination typical of your sort of crude and unredeemed sensibility. “Yes, but,” is your response—Yes, but what about the exposition? Did you understand who was who and what the problem was? Yes, but what about the rising action? Did it move too abruptly? Was there anything missing in the logic of the sequence of events? Was it repetitive or overlong? Did you understand the themes, and did they become more complex and interesting as you read? Yes, but was the climax both expected and unexpected, surprisingly right after you thought about it? Yes, but did the felicities of style make you want to read on? You should be committed enough by this time to what you have done that the fires of judgment raging all around you cannot deter you from questioning the dragon. This means that your material still fascinates you, draws you to it, enables you to pick out helpful nuggets from whatever else your reader says and ignore the rest.

当你和别人谈论你写的小说时，再次强调（因为这很难），尽量引导他们进行分析而非评判。不可避免地，对话往往会以对小说的概括性评价开场。你必须忽略这种开场白，专注于接下来的分析，即便你的读者断言你的小说是文学上的败类，体现了你那种粗俗不堪、毫无底线的审美趣味。“是的，但是……”你应该这样回应——是的，但是开篇部分呢？你是否理解了人物关系和问题的症结所在？是的，但是情节发展呢？它是否过于突兀？事件顺序的逻辑是否存在缺陷？是否重复冗长？你是否理解了主题，并且随着阅读的深入，这些主题是否变得更加复杂有趣？是的，但是高潮是否既在意料之中又出乎意料，在你思考之后才突然出现？是的，但是文风的精妙之处是否让你想要继续读下去？到了这个时候，你应该已经对自己所做的事足够投入，以至于周围熊熊燃烧的评判之火都无法阻止你质疑那些阻碍你前进的因素。这意味着你的素材依然让你着迷，吸引着你，使你能够从读者的其他评论中提炼出有用的精华，而忽略其余部分。

If your reader is good at his editorial job, he may be able to suggest improvements. If you know your weaknesses—psychology, structure, style, understanding what the larger themes are—you will be better able to listen to these suggestions and learn from them. You don't want to slavishly do what he says—you want to be able to consider a suggestion in the light of not only what you already know about the book, but also of your intentions. I, for example, might have made a strong case to George Eliot for cutting the first two-thirds of The Mill on the Floss by 25 percent, leaving a more shapely novel, but she might have decided that in the end, the plot wasn't as important as the texture of rural English life that she wanted to achieve by including those parts I wanted to cut. My cuts, she might have decided, would make a shapelier but less innovative novel, and at her level of experience, she wasn't yet ready, as she would be a few years later, to conceive of a structure that would fully exploit the potential of her material. Or, I might have told her, Maggie's adventure with her cousin's fianc is too pale and timid to truly warrant her subsequent disgrace. Then she and I might have had a spirited discussion about female virtue in the provinces in the 1830s , about gossip, respectability, and appearances versus reality. Once again the solution to the problem would depend on Eliot's own judgment about what is plausible, what was allowable in the novel of her day, and what she feels comfortable with as a single, self-supporting, female author. In your discussion with your reader, you have the last word, but the more educated and less defensive you are about your novel, the more likely you are to come up with a solution to its problems. Solutions come from the free operation of invention. If, in the face of judgment and analysis, you can retain your ability to play with your material—and, indeed, your playful mood—you are more likely to be able to invent your way to a higher form of your novel.

如果你的读者是一位优秀的编辑，他或许能够提出改进建议。如果你了解自己的不足——例如对人物心理、结构、风格以及对主题的理解——你就能更好地倾听这些建议并从中学习。你当然不想盲目地照搬他的建议——你应该能够结合自己对作品的已有认知以及创作意图来考虑这些建议。例如，我或许会极力劝说乔治·艾略特将《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》的前三分之二删减25%，使小说更加精炼。但她最终可能认为，情节远不如她想要通过保留那些我建议删减的部分来展现的英国乡村生活质感重要。她或许会觉得，我的删减会让小说更加精炼，但却缺乏创新性。而且，以她当时的经验水平，她还无法像几年后那样，构思出一种能够充分发挥素材潜力的结构。或者，我可能会告诉她，玛吉和她表哥未婚夫的那段风流韵事太过苍白无力，不足以让她遭受后来的羞辱。然后，我和她或许会就19世纪30年代英国乡村的女性品德、流言蜚语、体面以及表象与现实的对比展开一番热烈的讨论。问题的解决方案最终取决于艾略特本人对何为合理、在她所处的时代小说中何为可接受的判断，以及作为一名独立自主的女作家，她自身对何为自在的把握。在与读者的讨论中，你拥有最终的发言权，但你对自己的小说了解得越多、越不设防，就越有可能找到解决问题的办法。解决方案源于自由的创作。如果在面对评判和分析时，你仍能保持对素材的驾驭能力——以及你那份玩味的心态——你就更有可能通过创作，将你的小说推向更高的境界。

All the time you are working on your rewrite, be careful to correct spelling errors, grammatical errors, errors of diction, typos, errors of fact, and other small mistakes. To do so bolsters your sense of progress and your sense of professionalism. To fail to do so makes your manuscript look worse than it is and interferes with your ability to contemplate it.

在修改过程中，务必仔细核对拼写错误、语法错误、用词错误、错别字、事实错误以及其他细小错误。这样做能增强你的成就感和专业感。反之，如果疏忽大意，你的稿件看起来会比实际情况更糟糕，也会影响你认真思考和修改。

How do you know if you are finished? The first step here is to know yourself. Are you a dissatisfied perfectionist who tends to overdo everything? Or are you a careless sort who loses interest after the first rush of energy? Novels are long projects, and are more difficult to write if you go about it unsystematically. The reader wants both the finished surface and the energy simultaneously, all through the book. Your rewriting should promote both.

如何判断自己是否完成了写作？首先要了解自己。你是那种不满足于现状、追求完美、凡事都力求过火的人吗？还是那种热情过后便失去兴趣、漫不经心的人？小说创作是一项漫长的工程，如果缺乏条理，写作难度会更大。读者希望在阅读过程中，既能感受到作品的完整性，又能体会到其中的激情。你的修改应该兼顾这两方面。

One danger of doing too many drafts, especially if you are rearranging events and sequences of action or materially changing characters, is that you can get very confused about what happens when and what you have put in, taken out, and added to. There is no solution to this problem, because the more times you read the drafts through, the more information about the drafts you have to keep straight. If you are getting confused about what is happening, stop, take a long break, give the novel to your astute, editorial-type reader, and ask her explicitly to keep track of the action or the characters or the other things that confuse you. There are two types of confusion. In the first type, you don't know what is going on because you haven't figured it out yet. In the second type, you don't know what is going on because all the things you've written have become disordered in your mind. For this reason, three good drafts, done thoughtfully and thoroughly, are better than ten drafts without a plan. Your novel doesn't have to be perfect to find a publisher; it only has to be promising and engaging. An editor will inevitably have suggestions, and if you feel that you have perfected the novel before the editor buys it, you will be less open to what are probably good suggestions. The job of the editor is to help you—to be able to diagnose both what the novel needs and how to get you to supply it— and one thing a good editor will really help you do is keep track of events, action, and characters.

修改太多稿件的一个危险在于，尤其是在你重新安排事件和情节顺序，或者大幅修改人物角色时，你可能会对事件发生的先后顺序以及你添加、删除和修改的内容感到非常困惑。这个问题没有解决办法，因为你阅读稿件的次数越多，需要理清的信息就越多。如果你对故事情节感到困惑，那就停下来，休息一段时间，把小说交给一位眼光敏锐、像编辑一样的读者，并明确地请她帮你梳理情节、人物或其他让你感到困惑的地方。困惑有两种类型。第一种是你还没理清思路，所以不知道发生了什么。第二种是你写的东西在你脑子里变得混乱，所以你不知道发生了什么。因此，三份精心构思、认真细致的稿件胜过十份漫无目的的稿件。你的小说不必完美才能找到出版商；它只需要有潜力且引人入胜即可。编辑必然会提出建议，如果你在编辑购买之前就觉得自己已经把小说完善到了极致，那么你可能就不太愿意接受那些原本可能很好的建议。编辑的职责是帮助你——能够诊断出小说需要什么，以及如何让你提供这些——而一位优秀的编辑真正能帮你做到的一件事，就是梳理事件、情节和人物关系。

In the preceding paragraph, I am assuming, of course, that you tend to the perfectionist side. If you are a slob, though, pay no attention to the previous remarks. If your manuscript has coffee stains, crossings out, grease spots, spelling errors, sentences that run off the bottom of the page and around to the back, typos, and if it shows evidence of having been dropped into the bathwater, keep rewriting it until it is neat, sequential, polished, and, as far as you are concerned, perfect. Your standards are low. Try to exceed them.

当然，在前一段中，我假设你倾向于完美主义。但如果你是个邋遢鬼，那就别理会前面的话。如果你的稿子上有咖啡渍、涂改痕迹、油渍、拼写错误、句子写到页底甚至背面、错别字，甚至像是被扔进过洗澡水里一样，那就继续修改，直到它整洁、条理清晰、润色得当，在你看来完美无瑕。你的标准很低，那就努力超越它。

The feeling you are looking for as you decide whether you are finished is exhaustion. I do not mean literal physical fatigue as much as the sense that you have used up your inventiveness, your intelligence, and your ideas with regard to this story and these characters. While you are still interested in them, you have thought every thought you are capable of about them. Chances are your novel is not perfect, and someone else will have a good idea of how it can be improved or at least be done differently the first time he reads it, but you have come to the end of your relationship with it. Print it out; go to a bookstore and buy a book about publishing, which is a whole subject in itself

当你决定是否完成写作时，你要寻找的感觉是精疲力竭。我指的并非字面意义上的身体疲惫，而是指你感觉自己已经耗尽了所有关于这个故事和这些人物的创造力、智慧和想法。虽然你仍然对他们感兴趣，但你已经把所有能想到的都想过了。你的小说很可能并不完美，别人第一次读到它时或许就能提出改进建议，或者至少可以尝试不同的写法，但你已经和它走到了尽头。把它打印出来；去书店买一本关于出版的书，出版本身就是一个庞大的课题。

∗ Some incidents that take place at the 90 percent mark:

* 一些发生在90%分界点的事件：

Orlando: pp. 280 – 81 —Orlando gets the poem she has been working on for hundreds of years published.

奥兰多：第 280-281 页——奥兰多发表了她创作了数百年的诗歌。

Justine: pp. 260 – 61 —Justine is recaptured by her old tormentor, Dubois.

贾斯汀：第 260-261 页——贾斯汀被她以前的折磨者杜波依斯再次抓获。

Three Pigs in Five Days: pp. 153 – 54 —Nina in the conciergerie (holding pen for the guillotine during the French Revolution) is betrayed by her lover.

五天三头猪：第 153-154 页——妮娜在法国大革命期间的监狱（关押断头台的牢房）中被她的情人出卖。

To Kill a Mockingbird: p. 250 —The beginning of the Halloween pageant that ends in the children's being terrorized on the way home.

《杀死一只知更鸟》：第 250 页——万圣节游行的开始，以孩子们在回家的路上遭受惊吓而告终。

The Idiot: p. 584 —Myshkin has his climactic epilectic attack at the big party.

白痴：第 584 页——梅什金在盛大的派对上突发癫痫。

Lady Chatterley's Lover: p. 324 —Mellors writes his manifesto to Connie, who is pregnant by him and expecting in the spring.

《查泰莱夫人的情人》：第 324 页——梅勒斯向康妮写下他的宣言，康妮怀了他的孩子，预产期在春天。

Madame Bovary: p. 230 —Emma poisons herself.

包法利夫人：第 230 页——爱玛服毒自杀。

# ↩

12. Good Faith: A Case History

12. 诚信：一个案例

I read the article while forcing myself to imagine that it had been written by someone else. Then all my images, all my reflexions, all my epithets taken in themselves, unvarnished by the failure which they represented in relation to my aims, charmed me by their brilliance, their unexpectedness, their profundity.

我读这篇文章时，强迫自己想象它是别人写的。然后，我所有的画面、所有的思考、所有的形容词，都褪去了它们与我的目标不符的失败痕迹，以其光彩、出人意料和深刻的内涵令我着迷。

— MARCEL PROUST , The Fugitive

——马塞尔·普鲁斯特，《亡命天涯》

W hen I closed the file of my rough draft of Good Faith , I was on what became page 286 in the published novel. The immediate reason I lost heart was that I had impulsively introduced a heart attack into the narrative (the protagonist's fundamentalist father) and then realized that the death of the father would complicate the protagonist's emotional life and add many pages to a novel that was supposed to begin accelerating toward the climax. Page 286 was about 70 percent of the way into the novel.

当我合上《善意》的初稿时，我写到了最终出版的小说第286页。我感到沮丧的直接原因是，我一时冲动在故事中加入了心脏病发作的情节（主人公的原教旨主义父亲），后来我意识到父亲的去世会使主人公的情感生活变得复杂，并给这部原本应该开始加速走向高潮的小说增加许多篇幅。第286页大约是小说的70%。

For those who haven't read Good Faith , its premise is fairly easy to summarize. Joe, about forty, is a small-town real-estate agent in a scenic region; he is newly divorced but generally happy and not filled with high aspirations. At the beginning of the novel, two things happen, apparently independently of one another—a stranger (Marcus) comes to town full of big plans; and an old friend of Joe's (Felicity), the daughter of his partner and married, entices him into having a clandestine affair. It is 1982 , the beginning of the Reagan era, when mores are beginning to loosen in the more conservative regions of the United States, and though he is cautious by nature and suspicious of both Marcus and Felicity, Joe allows himself to be seduced by both of them, with consequences that are, to say the least, surprising to him, if not, with the perspective of twenty years, equally surprising to the reader.

对于没读过《善意》的人来说，它的情节梗概很容易概括。乔，四十岁左右，是风景秀丽的小镇上的一名房地产经纪人；他刚刚离婚，但总体来说生活幸福，并没有什么远大的抱负。小说开篇，两件看似毫不相干的事情同时发生：一个陌生人（马库斯）带着宏大的计划来到小镇；乔的老朋友（费利西蒂），他合伙人的女儿，已婚，引诱他开始了一段秘密恋情。故事发生在1982年，里根时代初期，美国一些较为保守的地区开始逐渐放松道德规范。尽管乔生性谨慎，对马库斯和费利西蒂都抱有戒心，但他最终还是被两人诱惑，其后果至少对他自己来说十分意外，即便以二十年后的视角来看，对读者而言也同样令人惊讶。

The “seed” of Good Faith was an anecdote related to me by a friend about his own experiences as a real-estate agent in the 1980s . Since I had written two books about the eighties already (A Thousand Acres and Moo) , I was always interested in how other tales of the eighties fit in with my theories about that regrettable period of American history, and my friend's anecdote fit in perfectly. The anecdote was self-contained and seemed as though it would be easy to expand into a good novel. Not long before I closed my file, I had, at the 62 percent mark (page 255 in this novel, or equivalent to the beginning of the fourth act in a five-act play), consolidated and reoriented the narrative, in a scene where Marcus assumes greater control over the partnership and Joe closes his own real-estate office, losing his independence and taking a decisive step toward becoming completely vulnerable to Marcus. I did not do this knowingly, but I wasn't surprised later that I had done it—almost every novel gathers itself at the 62 percent mark, changes strategy, and freshens. In To Kill a Mockingbird , Bob Ewell lies on the stand about seeing Tom and his daughter having sex. In The Trial , Josef K. meets Titorelli the painter; the “process” Josef K. is undergoing expands into new realms of confusion. In Justine , Justine arrives at a large chteau and meets the count, who, while he is violating her, explains to her exactly how sex and marriage work among the French aristocracy. In Madame Bovary , Emma begins to give up her attempts at domestic conformity and then goes to see her first opera, Lucia di Lammermoor , which quickens her romantic yearnings. In adding a heart attack on page 278 , I was adding drama to keep myself entertained, but I also changed the pacing of the novel without getting closer to the point. I cut out the heart attack (no more than a page or two), but this made me feel as though I had lost the thread of the novel entirely and was bored, to boot.

《善意》的“种子”源于一位朋友讲述的他在上世纪八十年代做房地产经纪人的经历。由于我已经写过两本关于八十年代的书（《一千英亩》和《哞哞》），我一直很想知道其他关于八十年代的故事如何与我对美国历史上那段令人遗憾的时期的理论相契合，而我朋友的轶事恰好完美地契合了我的思路。这个轶事本身就很完整，似乎很容易扩展成一部精彩的小说。在我即将完成这部小说时，我写到了62%的位置（小说第255页，相当于五幕剧的第四幕开头），对叙事进行了整合和重新调整。在其中一个场景中，马库斯逐渐掌控了合伙关系，而乔关闭了自己的房地产公司，失去了独立性，并朝着完全受制于马库斯的方向迈出了决定性的一步。我并非有意为之，但事后我并不感到意外——几乎每部小说都会在62%左右重新调整策略，焕然一新。在《杀死一只知更鸟》中，鲍勃·尤厄尔在证人席上撒谎，否认亲眼目睹汤姆和他的女儿发生性关系。在《审判》中，约瑟夫·K遇到了画家蒂托雷利；约瑟夫·K正在经历的“过程”也随之扩展，陷入了新的混乱。在《朱斯蒂娜》中，朱斯蒂娜来到一座大城堡，遇到了伯爵，伯爵在侵犯她的同时，向她详细解释了法国贵族中性与婚姻的运作方式。在《包法利夫人》中，爱玛开始放弃对家庭规范的追求，然后去看了她的第一部歌剧《拉美莫尔的露琪亚》，这加剧了她对浪漫的渴望。我在第278页添加了一场心脏病发作的情节，是为了增加戏剧性，让自己保持阅读兴趣，但也改变了小说的节奏，却并没有更接近主题。我删掉了心脏病发作那段（只有一两页），但这让我感觉完全失去了对小说的理解，而且还觉得很无聊。

∗ A few more particulars of Good Faith: the novel takes place over the course of about two years and involves the attempt, by Joe and his associates, to develop a dream property, the pristine and luxurious estate of a wealthy local couple who want to divest themselves and move to another property they own in Florida. The cast of characters includes several from the local savings and loan who are attempting to forward financial schemes of their own. In addition to Joe, Marcus, and Felicity, the main characters are Felicity's parents, Gordon and Betty, whose background is a bit mysterious; Joe's parents, who are very strict fundamentalists; two enterprising gay guys who like to buy property and fix it up; and Marcus's sister, who colludes with Marcus, but also warns Joe about him.

* 关于《善意》的更多细节：小说的故事发生在两年左右的时间里，讲述了乔和他的同伙试图开发一处梦寐以求的房产——一对当地富裕夫妇的豪华庄园。这对夫妇想出售这处房产，搬到他们在佛罗里达州的另一处房产居住。小说中的人物包括几位来自当地储蓄贷款机构的人，他们也都在试图推进各自的金融计划。除了乔、马库斯和费利西蒂之外，主要人物还有费利西蒂的父母戈登和贝蒂，他们的背景有些神秘；乔的父母，他们是极其严格的原教旨主义者；两个喜欢买房翻新的精明的同性恋男子；以及马库斯的妹妹，她与马库斯勾结，但也警告乔提防他。

I diagnosed my boredom as fear, but I wasn't sure what I was afraid of. Most of the parts of my plot were already in place and I understood them. I knew enough to go on and was fairly clear how I should go on. As I noted in the introduction, I felt considerable underlying fear as a result of the World Trade Center attacks and their aftermath; performance fears rested on top of that, in particular the fear that if the plot wasn't building enough to quicken my pulse, then most likely it wasn't building enough to quicken anyone else's pulse. This is what the boredom felt like. I recoiled at what Henry James would have called “the developments,” the very proliferation of dialogue, narration, characters doing this and that, scenes piling upon scenes. Not only did I recoil at what I still had to produce, I also recoiled at what I had already produced. The whole thing presented itself to me as a dusty, sunburned road, and I was trudging down it. As it petered out in the few days after I added and removed the heart attack, I wrote a few things I liked, including a bit of dialogue where Joe runs into a gay couple at the hardware store. These two guys were always witty, so I enjoyed their wit all over again. But it was as if their wit used up my own, and when I read the scene the next day, it did not stimulate any more thoughts.

我把自己的无聊感诊断为恐惧，但我并不确定自己究竟在害怕什么。我的大部分情节已经构思完毕，而且我理解它们。我知道的足够多，可以继续下去，也相当清楚自己应该如何继续。正如我在引言中提到的，由于世贸中心袭击事件及其后续影响，我内心深处感到相当恐惧；而表演上的恐惧则叠加在这种恐惧之上，尤其是害怕如果情节发展不足以让我心跳加速，那么很可能也无法让其他人心跳加速。这就是我感到无聊的原因。我厌恶亨利·詹姆斯所说的“情节发展”，厌恶对话、旁白、人物的各种行为以及场景的堆积。我不仅厌恶自己尚未完成的部分，也厌恶自己已经完成的部分。这一切在我眼中就像一条尘土飞扬、烈日炙烤的道路，而我正艰难地跋涉其上。在增删了心脏病发作那段情节后的几天里，灵感逐渐消退。期间我写了一些自己喜欢的内容，包括乔在五金店偶遇一对同性恋伴侣的一段对话。这两个家伙一向风趣幽默，所以我再次欣赏到了他们的机智。但仿佛他们的机智耗尽了我的灵感，第二天我重读这段时，却再也提不起任何兴致。

By contrast, at the 70 percent mark in Horse Heaven , I so loved my small sets of characters that I relished each visit with them—each group (say Rosalind, Al, and Limitless, or Deirdre, Tiffany, and Audrey) was a refreshing change from the other groups. Though I dreaded the moment when I would finish Horse Heaven , I enjoyed getting there. That novel presented itself to me not as a dusty road but as a collection of bright stages I was privileged to visit. At the 70 percent point in A Thousand Acres , which I had not enjoyed writing but which I had found intellectually stimulating, the conflicts among the characters were intensifying, and Ginny's disagreements with her husband, in particular, were emerging into the open. The novel seemed to me to be building steam. I felt myself moving with the characters toward something horrible but alluring and exciting—a nasty, adrenaline-fueled revelation that couldn't be avoided.

相比之下，在《马之天堂》写到70%的时候，我深深地爱上了书中那些小角色，以至于每次与他们相遇都让我无比享受——每一组人物（比如罗莎琳德、阿尔和利米特莱斯，或者迪尔德丽、蒂芙尼和奥黛丽）都与其他人物组截然不同，令人耳目一新。虽然我害怕《马之天堂》的结局，但我却很享受创作的过程。这部小说在我眼中并非一条尘土飞扬的道路，而是一系列光彩夺目的舞台，我有幸得以一一探访。而在《千亩地》的70%处，虽然我并不享受写作的过程，但却从中获得了许多智力上的启发。书中人物之间的冲突愈演愈烈，尤其是金妮与丈夫之间的矛盾，更是逐渐浮出水面。在我看来，这部小说似乎正在积蓄力量。我感觉自己正与书中的人物一同走向某种可怕却又充满诱惑和刺激的结局——一个令人不快、肾上腺素飙升、无法回避的真相。

In Good Faith , I was required by the nature of the plot to be careful and calculating so that the reader, like Joe, would be seduced and beguiled. This was a feature of a betrayal plot that I hadn't reckoned with when I began the novel. All plots are about what happens, and then what happens after that, and so on; usually as events approach the climax, the things that happen next pile on one another more and more energetically. But this plot was about a scheme, and just as Marcus had to think through his scheme ever more carefully, so I had to think through the various aspects of the scheme ever more carefully—it could not lose plausibility, it could not be too exposed, Joe could not appear too foolish, Marcus could not appear to be too insincere, decoy elements had to be supplied that would eventually fit in with the main plot but seem gratuitously lifelike. I had to resist the energy of the plot if it made me careless and yet sustain it for the sake of the reader. And there was no relief, no jumping to other characters and plots, as I had done in Horse Heaven.

在《善意》这部小说中，情节的性质要求我谨慎周密，精心策划，以便让读者像乔一样被诱惑和蒙蔽。这是我在开始创作这部小说时没有预料到的背叛情节的特点。所有情节都围绕着发生了什么，以及之后发生了什么，如此循环往复；通常，随着事件接近高潮，接下来发生的事情会越来越密集地叠加在一起。但这部小说的情节是关于一个阴谋，正如马库斯必须更加仔细地思考他的计划一样，我也必须更加仔细地思考计划的各个方面——它不能失去合理性，不能过于暴露，乔不能显得太愚蠢，马库斯不能显得太虚伪，必须加入一些诱饵元素，这些元素最终会融入主线情节，但又显得格外真实。我必须克制情节的推进，以免它让我疏忽大意，但同时又要为了读者而保持这种推进力。而且，没有喘息之机，也不能像在《马的天堂》中那样，跳到其他角色和情节中去。

Perhaps the lesson here was that plotting is hard work—harder than style (which is at least in part natural), harder than character-drawing (which is more or less complete early on, because once the characters are standing up and talking, they operate largely on their own internal logic). Another lesson may be that plotting is a bit airless by nature—the more involved the plot, the more mechanical it is, and the more careful the novelist must be to hide the mechanics. And yet I love to read cleverly plotted novels. They have the extra pleasure of contrivance—if we look at a beautifully made box or listen to a Mozart piano sonata masterfully played, we love to say, “How do they do that?” When I read a P. G. Wodehouse novel, I also say, “How did he do that?”

或许，这里要传达的教训是：构思情节是一项艰巨的工作——比文风（至少在某种程度上是自然而然的）更难，比人物塑造（人物塑造在故事早期就基本完成，因为一旦人物站起来说话，他们就主要依靠自身的内在逻辑行事）更难。另一个教训可能是，构思情节本身就有些生硬——情节越复杂，就越机械化，小说家就越需要小心翼翼地掩盖其中的机械性。然而，我却很喜欢读情节巧妙的小说。它们有一种额外的乐趣，那就是精巧的设计——当我们欣赏一个制作精美的盒子，或者聆听一首演奏精湛的莫扎特钢琴奏鸣曲时，我们总会忍不住问：“他们是怎么做到的？”当我读P·G·伍德豪斯的小说时，我也会问：“他是怎么做到的？”

When I was teaching writing, I would sometimes come across gaps in student stories or spots where the student had stopped writing altogether. When I asked the students why, they would say that they had fallen asleep, or had had to go to work. Almost invariably, outside circumstances had intervened to prevent the completion of the story. But no. When the other students and I read those stories, we quickly saw that whatever the writers themselves thought, it was apparent to us that the story had failed just at that point—if it had not, the writer would have gone on with it in spite of outside circumstances. And so Good Faith , too, in spite of the World Trade Center attacks, had failed just at that point, in the late summer of 1983 , when Joe had nothing to do but work on the project and no place to go but the office.

我教写作的时候，有时会发现学生的故事里有空白，或者学生完全停笔的地方。我问学生原因，他们会说自己睡着了，或者不得不去上班。几乎无一例外，都是外部因素阻碍了故事的完成。但事实并非如此。我和其他学生一起阅读这些故事时，很快就发现，无论作者自己怎么想，在我们看来，故事的失败就发生在这一点上——如果不是这样，作者即使面临外部环境的阻碍也会继续写下去。同样，《善意》这部作品，尽管发生了世贸中心袭击事件，也恰恰在1983年夏末，乔除了埋头写作之外别无他事，除了办公室也无处可去的时候，在那个地方戛然而止。

When I resumed writing the novel in the second half of October 2001 (after writing the introduction to this book and reading The Tale of Genji) , the first thing I did was bring on my most energetic character, Marcus Burns. Although I don't like Marcus and am not like Marcus, and in some ways revile Marcus, “Marcus Burns, c'est moi,” as Flaubert would say. In Good Faith , it is Marcus's desire that initiates the action of the story. He is the one with the appetite and the intention. So I began chapter 21 . Joe and Marcus are driving out to the expensive farm they plan to develop. Joe is bored and disgruntled (“the scenery looked tired and uninteresting, the dusty end of summer”— there was my attitude, right there). Marcus doesn't say much at first, but then he begins persuading Joe to do yet another thing that Joe hasn't thought of—find a woman and get married. Marcus, of course, has a plan and a theory. He has picked a particular woman as a suitable mate for Joe—someone good-looking, cosmopolitan, and short; although he is married to a tall woman himself, he has a theory that favors shortness in the wives of powerful men.

2001年10月下旬，我重新开始创作这部小说（此前我刚写完本书的引言，并读完了《源氏物语》）。我做的第一件事就是塑造我笔下最有活力的角色——马库斯·伯恩斯。虽然我不喜欢马库斯，也和他截然不同，甚至在某些方面厌恶他，但正如福楼拜所说，“马库斯·伯恩斯，那就是我”。在《善意》这部小说中，正是马库斯的欲望推动了故事的发展。他才是那个充满欲望和意图的人。于是，我开始了第二十一章的写作。乔和马库斯正驱车前往他们计划开发的那座昂贵的农场。乔感到百无聊赖，闷闷不乐（“景色看起来疲惫不堪，毫无生气，夏末的尘土飞扬”——这正是我当时的感受）。马库斯起初沉默寡言，但随后他开始劝说乔去做一件乔从未想过的事情——找个女人结婚。当然，马库斯对此早有计划和理论。他为乔挑选了一位合适的伴侣——一位外貌出众、见多识广、身材娇小的女性；虽然他自己娶了一位身材高挑的妻子，但他却认为有权势的男人的妻子身材娇小更受欢迎。

In some sense, I was required simply to pass the time for about eighty pages. My job was to accelerate and intensify the rising action without seeming to be going anywhere—the climax had to surprise Joe to work. Any interaction he had with Marcus had two goals—to entangle him inextricably in Marcus's scheme and to lull the reader's suspicions of Marcus. (The reader had to be suspicious of Marcus— without the reader's suspicions, there would be no suspense, but unless the reader's suspicions were lulled, the climax would come on too fast and seem obvious.) For me, the payoff for focusing on Marcus was one I liked. If there is any sort of character I enjoy writing about, it is one who is full of bull, who talks compulsively, and who has plenty of theories that are partially correct but are always manipulative. Jess, in A Thousand Acres; Gift, in Moo; Leo the compulsive bettor in Horse Heaven; and the satanic veterinarian Curtis Doheny, also in Horse Heaven. Since I, too, am a compulsive theorizer, I often give these characters some of my own theories. It energizes the characters and energizes me, too, and it prevents me from letting such characters, who have no integrity, get too far outside my sympathies.

某种程度上，我的任务仅仅是打发时间，写完这八十页左右。我的工作是在不显得毫无进展的情况下，加快并强化情节的推进——高潮必须让乔感到意外才能奏效。他与马库斯的任何互动都有两个目的：一是让他无可避免地卷入马库斯的阴谋，二是消除读者对马库斯的怀疑。（读者必须对马库斯抱有怀疑——如果没有读者的怀疑，就不会有悬念；但如果读者的怀疑没有被消除，高潮就会来得太快，显得过于显而易见。）对我来说，专注于马库斯这个角色所带来的回报是我喜欢的。如果说我最喜欢写哪种类型的角色，那就是那种满嘴跑火车、喋喋不休、满脑子都是半真半假却又总是充满操控性的理论的人。比如《一千英亩》里的杰西；《哞》里的吉夫特；《马天堂》里那个赌徒利奥；还有《马的天堂》里的那个邪恶兽医柯蒂斯·多赫尼。因为我也是个喜欢钻研理论的人，所以我经常会把自己的一些理论强加给这些角色。这既能激发角色的活力，也能激励我自己，而且还能防止我彻底失去对这些毫无原则的角色的同情。

And so Good Faith resumed, and I almost made my deadline. I had intended to be finished with the rough draft on December 31 . I was finished on January 17 . I sent it to my editor with some anxiety, because I didn't expect her to like it.

于是，《诚信》一书重新开始，我几乎赶上了截稿日期。我原本计划在12月31日完成初稿，结果1月17日就完成了。我有些忐忑地把稿子发给了编辑，因为我并不指望她会喜欢。

When she did like it, I saw some things about the novel as a form that I had always known about but never experienced, and the first was that it had its own energy and forward motion. The sense of this as it came back to me from my editor's reading was especially strong with Good Faith because I felt detached from it. When I sent the first draft of Horse Heaven in, my attitude had been much different. I loved the novel so much that I assumed everyone who read it would feel the same. I loved it the way you love a horse or a child—I delighted in it. When the publisher did not respond with a similar love, I hardly noticed because my delight was so intense. That the publisher repeatedly referred to the first draft of Horse Heaven as “the material” rather than “the draft” or “the novel” seemed funny to me rather than ominous, partly because I loved “the material” so much that I knew I could rummage around in it and extract from its richness any sort of novel. With Good Faith , I was surprised but gratified—I had set up the machine and my editor's response indicated that it ran pretty well, if not perfectly. Since she liked it better than I did, it was my task in the second draft to make it more to my taste. I figured that when we both came to like it, it would be satisfactory and publishable, but the experience of composing the rough draft had been so taxing that I never expected to cherish it.

当她喜欢这部小说时，我才意识到小说这种文体的一些特质，这些特质我一直有所耳闻，却从未真正体验过。首先，小说本身就蕴含着一种独特的能量和前进的动力。这种感觉在编辑阅读后尤为强烈，因为我当时感觉自己与《善意》这部作品保持着一定的距离。当我把《马的天堂》的初稿寄过去时，我的态度截然不同。我如此热爱这部小说，以至于我理所当然地认为每个读者都会有同样的感受。我对它的喜爱就像对一匹马或一个孩子那样——我沉浸其中，欣喜不已。当出版社没有给予我同样的喜爱时，我几乎没注意到，因为我的喜悦如此强烈。出版社反复将《马的天堂》的初稿称为“素材”，而不是“草稿”或“小说”，这在我看来与其说是预兆，不如说是滑稽可笑。部分原因是，我如此热爱“素材”，以至于我知道我可以随意挖掘，从中提炼出任何类型的小说。我对《诚意》一书的成果感到既惊讶又欣慰——我搭建好了机器，编辑的反馈表明它运行得相当不错，即便并非完美无瑕。由于她比我更喜欢这本书，因此在第二稿中，我的任务是使其更符合我的口味。我当时的想法是，当我们都满意的时候，它就应该可以出版了，但撰写初稿的过程实在太耗费精力，我从未想过自己会如此珍视它。

When I received the manuscript back from my editor and read it myself, I once again liked it better than I had thought I would. Marcus wasn't my friend, but he had a way about him as a character of organizing the action and the themes. Felicity and the gay couple kept both Joe and me in a good mood. Felicity's sense of freedom and the gay couple's sense of irony contrasted refreshingly with Joe's plodding quality. Of course, Joe has to be a plodder, just as David Copperfield has to be a plodder—narrating a novel in the first person is a thankless and arduous task. The most annoying thing, of course, is the constant employment of the word “I.” “I did this,” “I thought that,” “then I did this,” “then he said to me”—it is a repetitive and debilitating form of discourse, tied tightly to the action (because digressiveness is usually even more tedious).

当我收到编辑退还的稿件并亲自阅读后，我再次发现它比我预想的还要好。马库斯并非我的朋友，但他作为人物，在组织情节和主题方面确实独具魅力。费利西蒂和那对同性恋伴侣让我和乔都心情愉悦。费利西蒂的自由奔放和那对同性恋伴侣的讽刺幽默与乔的沉稳沉闷形成了鲜明的对比，令人耳目一新。当然，乔必须是个沉稳的人，就像大卫·科波菲尔必须是个沉稳的人一样——用第一人称叙述小说是一项吃力不讨好且艰巨的任务。最令人恼火的当然是“我”这个字的频繁使用。“我做了这件事”、“我想了那件事”、“然后我做了这件事”、“然后他对我说”——这种重复乏味的叙述方式令人疲惫不堪，而且与情节紧密相连（因为离题的叙述通常更加枯燥乏味）。

There were two things about the rough draft that were quite wrong, though. One was Joe's garrulousness. Joe did tend to babble on, but not in the same way Marcus did. As a person who bullshits for a living, Marcus can indeed numb the listener with theories and ideas; in fact that is his trump card, psychologically. His strategy is to divine in his listeners just what will make them happy, and then weave theories about it without seeming to be actually offering anything. He lulls their doubts partly by seeming to know what he is talking about but also partly by putting them into a half sleep. Perhaps instinctively, Marcus knows that the prey might run if the adrenaline begins to pump. But Joe's garrulousness that annoyed me in the rough draft came from something other than strategy—it came from ignorance, both his and mine. He had a habit of continuing to talk even after he stopped having anything to say, like a bad date. I had the tools I needed to fix this problem once I recognized it—in the first place, I knew much more at the end of the rough draft about every aspect of the novel, so I was no longer as ignorant as I had been when I was composing the rough draft. Where Joe kept talking, knowing vaguely that there was more to say but not knowing what it was, was where I had known as the author that there was more to a particular moment than I could think of at the time. Now I could fill in those blanks. Also, I could just cut him off. I noticed that he had a habit of letting his remarks dribble to a close. As I read through the rough draft, every time I felt myself getting irritated with him, I cut that part—I unsaid it, exactly the way you cannot do on a bad date! By the time I had been through the second draft with these two things in mind, I liked Joe much better and felt that his good qualities were no longer lost in the verbal underbrush.

不过，初稿里有两点确实不太对劲。一是乔的喋喋不休。乔的确有点爱唠叨，但跟马库斯的唠叨方式完全不同。马库斯靠胡扯为生，他确实能用各种理论和想法麻痹听众；事实上，这在心理层面上是他的王牌。他的策略是揣摩听众的心思，找出什么能让他们开心，然后围绕这些理论编造故事，却又让人感觉他好像什么都没提供。他之所以能消除听众的疑虑，一部分是因为他看起来好像很懂行，另一部分则是因为他让他们昏昏欲睡。或许是出于本能，马库斯知道如果肾上腺素飙升，猎物就会逃跑。但初稿里让我恼火的乔的喋喋不休并非出于策略——而是源于无知，既有他的无知，也有我的无知。他有个习惯，即使没什么可说的了，也还继续说下去，就像一次糟糕的约会。一旦我意识到这个问题，我就有了解决问题的工具——首先，在初稿完成后，我对小说的各个方面都了解得更多了，不再像写初稿时那样一无所知。乔滔滔不绝地说着，隐约觉得还有话要说，却又说不清具体是什么，而作为作者的我却知道，某些特定时刻还有更深层次的含义，只是当时我无法完全表达出来。现在我可以填补这些空白了。而且，我还可以打断他。我注意到他有个习惯，就是说话总是拖拖拉拉，没说完。在阅读初稿的过程中，每当我感觉自己被他惹恼时，我就删掉那部分——就像在糟糕的约会中不能那样，把话说完！当我带着这两点想法完成二稿时，我对乔的印象好多了，觉得他的优点不再被他那些含糊不清的话语所掩盖。

The last two chapters were a bigger problem and actually required a good deal of thought. The rule of thumb, of course, is that when the climax doesn't work, the problem is in the exposition, but I didn't feel that the rule of thumb fit in this case. Something else was preventing the climax from working, but for quite a long time I couldn't figure out what it was. I finally realized, though, that a book about a scam and a betrayal has two climaxes—the climax of the action, when big things are happening and the narrator doesn't know what they mean, and the climax of the interpretation, when the narrator extracts the real meaning of not only the climax but also of the whole train of events. The problem with my last two chapters was that these two climaxes were mixed together, so the interpretation stole the suspense from the action. As eager as I was to get to the end, I had to continue to be patient in detailing the action, and I had to treat what would normally be the denouement as action—Joe's thought process as he works through what has happened to him needed to be well organized and to progress through time in the same way as any other type of action.

最后两章的问题更大，确实需要仔细思考。当然，通常来说，如果高潮部分不尽如人意，问题就出在铺垫上，但我感觉这条经验法则并不适用于我的情况。肯定还有其他因素阻碍了高潮的发挥，但我琢磨了很久也没弄明白究竟是什么。最终我意识到，一本关于骗局和背叛的书应该有两个高潮——一个是行动的高潮，此时发生了很多大事，但叙述者却一头雾水；另一个是解读的高潮，此时叙述者不仅理解了高潮本身，也理解了整个事件脉络的真正含义。我最后两章的问题就在于，这两个高潮混杂在一起，导致解读部分喧宾夺主，削弱了行动部分的悬念。尽管我急于看到结局，但我必须继续耐心细致地描写情节，并且必须把通常的结局当作情节来处理——乔在处理发生在他身上的事情时的思考过程需要组织良好，并且像任何其他类型的情节一样随着时间的推移而发展。

The prose I had already written led me astray and hid the real problems and their solutions from me. I would read along and read along, and on the surface it all looked okay to me. I was falling in the most common way for my own fluency—I was reading as a reader when I should have been reading as a writer. The only way to overcome this problem was to do something that felt drastic as a way of making a break from the dream of the existing text, and that was to rip apart the last two chapters and rewrite them almost completely. The understanding of the problem came after the ripping apart because the ripping apart was the only way I could remove myself from a state of receptivity.

我之前写好的文字误导了我，让我看不到真正的问题和解决方法。我一遍又一遍地读，表面上看起来一切都很好。我陷入了最常见的误区——我本应该像个作家一样阅读，却用读者的视角去阅读。克服这个问题的唯一方法是采取一种看似极端的做法，打破现有文本的束缚，那就是把最后两章推翻重写。对问题的理解是在推翻之后才出现的，因为只有推翻才能让我摆脱被动接受的状态。

Every form of the novel contains some basic implausibility. The confessional novel, which is retrospective and in the first person, is implausible in the way the narrator has to appear not to know what he surely must know so the plot can unfold in a suspenseful and orderly fashion. Any intrusion of subsequent knowledge into the unfolding plot either confuses the issues or shifts the reader's attention to other questions. My intention was to put what happened to Joe in the foreground because Joe had been betrayed, and when someone feels betrayed, he or she is likely to go over the sequence of events carefully and even obsessively to work out how or where a relationship went wrong. My real interest was in the emotional experience of betrayal— that was where the drama lay and how the themes gained weight. The author, of course, has to address whatever questions he chooses in a consistent, logical, and orderly manner. He can't unknowingly shift the terms of the discussion in the middle of the narrative or both the themes and the plot will go awry. When I began to bring order to the last chapters—when I began to be patient and not hurry to the end— then the climax sorted itself out. The author feels pulled toward the end, as the reader does, but the author must resist the pull in order to put in all the information the reader needs to understand the ending, and through that the themes of the novel. When I wrote the second draft of the last two chapters of Good Faith , I knew the section needed more work, but felt it was no longer a blight upon the whole enterprise.

每种小说形式都包含一些基本的不合理之处。自白式小说采用回顾式的第一人称叙述，其不合理之处在于叙述者必须假装不知道自己必然知道的事情，这样情节才能以悬念迭起、条理清晰的方式展开。任何事后补充的信息都会使情节发展变得混乱，或者将读者的注意力转移到其他问题上。我的目的是将乔的遭遇放在首位，因为乔遭到了背叛。当一个人感到被背叛时，他或她很可能会仔细地、甚至执着地回顾事件经过，以弄清这段关系是如何或在哪里出了问题。我真正感兴趣的是背叛带来的情感体验——这才是戏剧冲突的根源，也是主题得以凸显的关键所在。当然，作者必须以连贯、合乎逻辑且有条理的方式来探讨他所选择提出的任何问题。他不能在叙述过程中无意间改变讨论的语境，否则主题和情节都会偏离轨道。当我开始整理最后几章的内容——当我开始耐心写作，不再急于求成——高潮自然而然地就出现了。作者和读者一样，都会被一种想要走向结局的冲动所牵引，但作者必须克制这种冲动，才能提供读者理解结局所需的所有信息，进而理解小说的主题。当我写完《善意》最后两章的第二稿时，我知道这部分还需要进一步修改，但感觉它不再是整部作品的瑕疵了。

∗ The author can choose to address any questions he wishes, and “what happened” might not be the first choice of many confessional authors—for example, in Lolita we know from the beginning that Humbert Humbert is in jail; the story is thereby shifted from “what happened?” to “how did he get here and how are we to account for his attitude and tone?”

* 作者可以选择回答他想回答的任何问题，“发生了什么事”可能不是许多自白式作者的首选——例如，在《洛丽塔》中，我们从一开始就知道亨伯特·亨伯特在监狱里；故事因此从“发生了什么事？”转变为“他是如何走到这一步的，以及我们如何解释他的态度和语气？”

Another necessary aid to revision was a map of Joe's geographical region, with all the houses and towns and roads and neighborhoods depicted. I went through the rough draft and wrote down every geographical fact, made a list, and drew a map. I fixed inconsistencies and bits of confusion, not because I expected a reader to be able to orient Joe in his world but because I expected myself to. When I was in seventh grade, I remember, my mother gave me The Annotated Sherlock Holmes , by William S. Baring-Gould. I thought it would be an authoritatively expanded edition of the detective's adventures, full of pictures and notes that would intensify my pleasure in Holmes's adventures, but Baring-Gould spent a fair amount of space pointing out inconsistencies in the stories, and the inconsistencies made me uncomfortable because they challenged my willing suspension of disbelief, just as, when I was six years old and comparing The Bobbsey Twins to The Bobbsey Twins at School , I was quite disturbed by the fact that in the first volume Nan and Bert were eight and Freddie and Flossie were four, while in the later volume, Nan and Bert were twelve and Freddie and Flossie were six. I didn't want readers of Good Faith to worry about such things.

另一个必要的修改工具是乔所在地区的地图，上面标出了所有的房屋、城镇、道路和街区。我仔细阅读了初稿，记下了每一个地理信息，列了个清单，然后画了一张地图。我修正了前后矛盾和容易混淆的地方，这并非因为我期望读者能够理解乔所处的世界，而是因为我期望自己能够做到这一点。我记得，在我七年级的时候，母亲送给我威廉·S·巴林-古尔德的《注释版福尔摩斯探案集》。我原以为这会是一部权威的、内容更丰富的侦探冒险故事集，图文并茂，注释详尽，能让我更尽情地享受福尔摩斯探案的乐趣。然而，巴林-古尔德却花了相当多的篇幅指出故事中的矛盾之处。这些矛盾之处让我感到不适，因为它们挑战了我原本就乐于接受的“不信感”。就像我六岁时，将《鲍勃西双胞胎》和《鲍勃西双胞胎上学记》进行比较，发现第一册里南和伯特八岁，弗雷迪和弗洛西四岁，而第二册里南和伯特十二岁，弗雷迪和弗洛西却六岁，这让我非常困惑。我不希望《善意》的读者也为此烦恼。

∗ This is not to say that my novels are as perfectly consistent as I would like them to be. At a reading, someone once pointed out that in Horse Heaven I have eight horses running in a race, and I say that they have sixty-four legs. Apologies to all!

* 这并不是说我的小说像我希望的那样完美无瑕。有一次朗读会上，有人指出在《马的天堂》里，我写了八匹马赛跑，但我却说它们有六十四条腿。在此向大家致歉！

What I noticed and liked about the rough draft of Good Faith was something I had not expected—it went down easy. I attributed this in part to Joe's voice, which was casual and undemanding. I had noticed this in other first-person narratives I had written, and it is the signal virtue of writing in the first person—the conceit of the human voice telling a story is readily accepted by the reader. It is comfortable and familiar and sociable, especially if the voice makes no pretensions to being special, but just seems to be telling the story because something interesting or dramatic happened that needs to be told. Defoe's novels are perfect examples of this—each of his protagonists asserts from the beginning that he or she is just an average person who did something or saw something that ought to be recorded, so the voice is friendly and so the reader reciprocates that friendliness. I had intended Joe to be friendly for narrative reasons—he is a real-estate agent, after all, and of course he has to be at least relatively friendly in order to be betrayed. His natural style is colloquial American English, which is a friendly style. He is more or less a self-effacing guy. Somehow all of this added up, for me as a reader, to a smooth passage of the narrative, a smooth passage of time, really, where events and seasons melt into one another rather undramatically (by contrast to A Thousand Acres , which is based on a drama).

在阅读《善意》的初稿时，我注意到并喜欢上了它，这出乎我的意料——它读起来非常轻松。我认为这部分要归功于乔的叙述语气，它随意而亲切。我在自己写的其他第一人称叙事作品中也注意到了这一点，而这正是第一人称写作的显著优点——由人声讲述故事的设定很容易被读者接受。这种叙述方式让人感到舒适、熟悉且亲切，尤其当叙述者不刻意标榜自己与众不同，而只是因为发生了一些有趣或戏剧性的事情需要被记录下来时。笛福的小说就是绝佳的例子——他笔下的每个主人公从一开始就表明自己只是一个普通人，做了或看到了一些应该被记录下来的事情，因此叙述语气亲切友好，读者也会以同样的友好回应。我之所以想让乔保持友好，是出于叙事上的考虑——毕竟他是一名房地产经纪人，当然，他至少要相对友好，才有可能被背叛。他自然的写作风格是口语化的美式英语，这种风格很友好。他本人也比较谦逊。不知何故，所有这些因素加在一起，对我这个读者来说，使得叙事流畅自然，时间也流畅地流逝，事件和季节的更迭显得自然而然（与根据戏剧改编的《一千英亩》形成鲜明对比）。

It was this way that Good Faith had of slipping down easily that remained my inspiration and talisman as I worked through the second, third, and fourth drafts. It seemed to be the most essential quality of the novel and it seemed to be pretty much there, already present. My job was to elaborate on this quality, to make it slip down more and more easily with each rewriting—to perform, in fact, what Marcus was doing to Joe, a seduction. This meant that the sense of Joe's innocence, and the sense of everyone's innocence, even Marcus's, had to remain with the reader almost to the end. As political and cultural events followed one another through 2002 and 2003 , this quiet appearance of innocence I felt was part of the novel and essential to it meant that it came to represent my own feelings about the themes of the novel less and less. Jane Smiley the citizen was growing increasingly alarmed and angry while Jane Smiley the author of Good Faith was simply pointing out and suggesting a few political ideas and thoughts. In particular, I felt that the deregulation fashion of the eighties was exceptionally wrongheaded and had done all sorts of harm to all sorts of sectors of American life—the environment, consumer protection, the media, and now the financial and business sectors. As a citizen I was humming with ill-suppressed indignation and Cassandra-like predictions of future economic and social collapse, but Good Faith could not be wrenched from the tone Joe gave it. His betrayal plot required that he not know what was going on and not foresee what could happen, and the first-person narrative required that I not interfere with his telling the story. In one sense it was good that the novel went down easy; in another sense I couldn't stand how easy the novel went down because the polemicist in me wanted to make sure the reader saw what I saw and understood it as I understood it. However, it was not in me to burst out of my narrative form—either I didn't yet have the conviction or I didn't have the imagination. The novel remained as it had been conceived in 2000 , before current events began to accelerate. I could not reconceive it or break up its narrative integrity. I am sure it would have been different if it had been conceived a year, or even six months, later. The only solution to its failures as a polemic was to conceive another novel.

正是《善意》中那种自然流露的特质，在我修改第二稿、第三稿和第四稿的过程中，始终激励着我，成为我的精神支柱。这似乎是这部小说最本质的特质，而且它似乎早已存在，浑然天成。我的任务是进一步强化这种特质，让它在每一次修改中都更加自然地流露——实际上，就是像马库斯对乔所做的那样，进行一种诱惑。这意味着，乔的纯真，以及所有人的纯真，甚至包括马库斯的纯真，都必须在读者心中保持到接近结尾。随着2002年和2003年政治和文化事件的接踵而至，这种我曾认为是小说一部分且至关重要的纯真表象，却越来越少地代表了我对小说主题的个人感受。作为普通公民的简·斯迈利变得越来越惊恐和愤怒，而作为《善意》作者的简·斯迈利，则只是在提出一些政治观点和想法。尤其是我觉得八十年代的放松管制风潮极其错误，对美国生活的方方面面都造成了损害——环境、消费者保护、媒体，以及现在的金融和商业领域。作为一名公民，我内心充满了难以抑制的愤慨，并像卡桑德拉一样预言着未来的经济和社会崩溃，但《善意》这本书的基调却始终无法从乔的叙述中剥离。他的背叛情节要求他对此一无所知，也无法预见未来可能发生的事情，而第一人称叙述又要求我不能干预他讲述故事。从某种意义上说，小说读起来轻松易懂是件好事；但从另一个角度来看，我又无法忍受它如此轻松易懂，因为我内心深处的辩论家渴望确保读者能够看到我所看到的，并理解我所理解的一切。然而，我却无法突破这种叙述模式——或许我当时还没有足够的信念，或许我缺乏足够的想象力。这部小说保持了2000年构思时的样子，那时时事还没有加速发展。我无法重新构思，也无法破坏其叙事的完整性。我确信，如果晚一年，甚至晚六个月构思，结果肯定会不一样。它作为论战作品的失败，唯一的解决办法就是创作另一部小说。

∗ I see Good Faith as confession and history, with some romance, some essay, a good deal of gossip, a few jokes, some local travel, and even a touch of epic smuggled ironically in, but no letters, no polemic, no tales, and no biography, since Marcus's fate is unknown—ambitious, according to “The Circle of the Novel,” but fairly self-effacing because of Joe.

我认为《善意》是一部忏悔录和历史，其中夹杂着一些浪漫故事、一些散文、大量的八卦、一些笑话、一些当地游记，甚至还讽刺地融入了一丝史诗般的元素，但没有信件、没有论战、没有故事，也没有传记，因为马库斯的命运未知——根据《小说的圈子》的说法，他雄心勃勃，但因为乔的缘故，他相当谦逊。

I finished the final draft and turned it in in August 2002 . It felt unfinished and unrealized to me all the way to the end of the process. I worried at the last chapter over and over, mostly sorting out the sequence of events, breaking them down, and organizing them for clarity, but I also felt there was some emotional capstone missing. It was small—less a capstone than a tiny bean balancing on the top of a pile of other beans—but essential. I knew that if I left it out, I would know that the novel was unfinished, unintegrated somehow, but that maybe a reader would not know. Maybe the thing I wanted was almost too much, and the novel really didn't need it. Maybe it was a matter of taste. At any rate, I read the novel over one more time, and I did end up adding one last thing, the second-to-last phrase, which is, “for once I recognized something my parents had talked about all my life, and that was the operation of grace in the material world.” I added this with an intense sense of satisfaction. It brought several things together—Joe and his parents, Joe's secular view of life and his parents’ faith-based view of life, the legal and religious connotations of the novel's title, and the two halves of Felicity (the female protagonist)—her exuberance and her physical grace. At the same time, the word “grace” set up unfortunate verbal and thematic echoes with the name of one of the characters, Marcus's sister Grace. Her name had to be changed, and I thought about this for about a day, trying out typical Catholic names of Grace's generation. I read over some of her lines, and they didn't work with a two-syllable name. I also felt I had to use a name with a long “a” sound, which left few names—not Amy, not Elaine, not any one I could think of other than Jane, my own name.

2002年8月，我完成了最终稿并提交。直到写作过程结束，我都感觉它不够完整，不够理想。我反复琢磨最后一章，主要是梳理事件顺序，将它们拆解重组，力求清晰明了。但我总觉得缺少某种情感上的点睛之笔。它很小——与其说是点睛之笔，不如说是一颗小小的豆子稳稳地立在一堆豆子顶上——但却至关重要。我知道，如果我删掉它，我会觉得小说不够完整，有些地方不够连贯，但读者或许不会察觉。也许我想要的东西有点过头了，小说其实并不需要它。也许这只是个人喜好问题。总之，我又通读了一遍小说，最终还是加上了倒数第二句话：“我终于明白了父母一直以来跟我谈论的一件事，那就是恩典在物质世界中的运作。” 加上这句话时，我感到无比的满足。它将几个元素融合在一起——乔和他的父母，乔世俗的生活观和他父母基于信仰的生活观，小说标题的法律和宗教内涵，以及女主人公费利西蒂的两面性——她的热情奔放和优雅的身姿。与此同时，“优雅”这个词与小说中一个角色的名字——马库斯的妹妹格蕾丝——在语言和主题上产生了不愉快的共鸣。她的名字必须改掉，我为此思考了大约一天，尝试了格蕾丝那一代典型的天主教名字。我重读了她的一些台词，发现它们与双音节的名字并不相符。我还觉得我必须使用一个带有长“a”音的名字，这使得选择余地很小——艾米不行，伊莱恩不行，除了简（我自己的名字）之外，我想不出其他名字。

Naming Grace “Jane” seemed daring in a minor way, simply because of the coincidence with my name, but then I remembered that Jane Austen had named Jane Bennet after herself, and I figured if she could do it, I could, too. I used my “find and replace” utility to change the name (what a fabulous tool that is for a novelist!) and sent the finished manuscript in.

给格蕾丝取名“简”似乎有点大胆，仅仅是因为和我的名字巧合。但后来我想起来简·奥斯汀也用自己的名字给简·班纳特取名，我想既然她能做到，我也能。我用“查找替换”功能改了名字（这对小说家来说真是个好工具！），然后把完成的稿件寄了出去。

The novel now entered the publication process. Most authors do not have much say over the packaging of the novel because the publishing house considers packaging—how the novel looks but also how it is presented to the public—its domain. I think it is fruitful to think of novels as passing through levels of decreasing privacy—first a notion hardly even realized by the novelist, then a draft understandable mostly by the novelist, then subsequent drafts, each of which has a more public aspect than the last one, then one or more edited drafts, aiming more and more specifically for public existence. The last of these is the copyedited draft, in which an expert in grammar, spelling, and other details of language and continuity makes the novel more or less standard (let's say she ties its shoelaces and buttons its buttons properly). This last draft is then printed and furnished with packaging meant to demonstrate a few things about it and to put the prospective reader into a mood. This mood may be different from the mood of the writer. For example, my mood when I wrote Good Faith was green, humid, and breezy—I always had a background sense of the landscape Joe was driving through on his way from open house to open house. When I contemplate the book in retrospect, I mostly picture weather—it is a sensuous book for me and for Joe; never can he separate what happened and what was said from what sort of day it was when that event took place. The mood of the novel package in hardcover, though, is washed-out red, white, and blue, because the publisher chose to highlight the themes of the novel to sell it as important as well as readable. The cover of the novel looks like outmoded advertising of the sort we used to see in the fifties, when a company, by advertising its integrity, made that very integrity seem suspect. The design is witty and smart, and, indeed, when the book designer came up with it, everyone liked it. When publication date rolled around and I received a box of twelve copies, I found opening the box a pleasure. The books looked pink, welcoming, almost benign. Their matte finish was cool and asked, somehow more than the glossy finish of Horse Heaven , to be picked up and held in the hand, a dry book against a dry palm. The title page, too, was designed to carry a double message—it looked vaguely like both a stock certificate and a carnival advertisement.

小说现在进入出版流程。大多数作者对小说的包装没有太多发言权，因为出版社认为包装——包括小说的外观以及它如何呈现给公众——是他们的职责。我认为，将小说的创作过程想象成经历一系列隐私程度递减的阶段是有益的：首先，小说家几乎从未意识到隐私的存在；然后，形成一个主要由小说家自己理解的草稿；接着是后续的草稿，每一稿都比前一稿更具公共性；之后是一稿或多稿的编辑稿，越来越明确地以公开出版为目标。最后一个阶段是经过校对的稿件，由语法、拼写和其他语言细节以及连贯性的专家对小说进行校对，使其更加规范（比如说，她把鞋带系好，扣好纽扣）。最终稿件会被印刷出来，并配上相应的包装，旨在展示小说的一些特点，并营造一种氛围。这种氛围可能与作者当时的心情截然不同。例如，我写《善意》时，脑海中浮现的是一片绿意盎然、潮湿微风的景象——乔开车穿梭于各个开放参观的房屋之间，沿途的风景始终萦绕在我的脑海里。回想这本书，我脑海中浮现的也大多是天气——对我而言，对乔来说，这是一本充满感官体验的书；他永远无法将发生的事情和说过的话与事件发生时的天气状况割裂开来。然而，精装版小说的包装却采用了褪色的红、白、蓝三色，因为出版商选择突出小说的主题，以使其既重要又易读。小说的封面看起来像是上世纪五十年代那种过时的广告，当时公司通过宣传自身的诚信，反而使这种诚信本身显得可疑。设计诙谐巧妙，事实上，当书籍设计师提出这个设计时，每个人都很喜欢。出版日期到来，我收到一箱十二本时，打开箱子的那一刻让我感到无比愉悦。书看起来粉嫩可爱，几乎令人感到亲切。它们的哑光表面清冷而别致，比起《马天堂》的光面，更让人忍不住拿起来捧在手里，感受一本干燥的书贴在干燥的手掌上。扉页的设计也别具匠心，既像股票证书，又像嘉年华广告。

If I sound cynical here, I don't mean to. Since every novel is various and rich with incidents, characters, and themes, its package has to be simplified somehow and made representative. The reader has to be reminded that reading is a pleasure of some sort—perhaps sensual and happy and funny, or perhaps austere and difficult, but I can't imagine that a row of texts differentiated merely by titles and authors would induce large-scale purchases. Once, maybe they did, but we are used to both facets of the object now—the feel and look of the book and the promise of the novel within. My book was to be matte, bright, graphic; the novel within was to be smart and sly, with perhaps a few hidden attractions (good-natured but detailed sex scenes). It took a few commercial risks—there was no telling, for example, if anyone cared about real-estate agents or real estate, no matter how much money was at stake, or if anyone cared about the 1980s . My name on the front was meant to work as a recommendation; compliments gleaned from the publication of previous novels, listed on the back, were to bolster that recommendation, tastefully reminding the reader of my claims to her attention. My job and the publisher's job were related but distinct. The publisher's job was to get the reader to buy; my job was to get the reader to begin reading and keep reading.

如果我的话听起来有些愤世嫉俗，那并非我的本意。因为每部小说都各具特色，情节丰富，人物众多，主题深刻，所以其包装必须有所简化，才能具有代表性。读者需要被提醒，阅读本身就是一种乐趣——或许是感官上的愉悦和轻松的，或许是严肃而艰涩的，但我无法想象仅仅用书名和作者来区分的书籍会引发大规模的购买。或许曾经如此，但如今我们已经习惯了书籍的两个方面——书的质感和外观，以及其中小说内容的吸引力。我的书封面是哑光的，色彩鲜艳，画面生动；书中的小说则要睿智而巧妙，或许还隐藏着一些诱人的元素（比如一些轻松但细致的性爱描写）。这其中也存在一些商业风险——例如，无论投入多少资金，谁也无法预料是否有人会关心房地产经纪人或房地产，或者是否有人会对20世纪80年代感兴趣。封面上我的名字本身就是一种推荐；封底列出的之前出版的小说所获得的赞誉，是为了进一步强化这种推荐，巧妙地提醒读者我的作品值得关注。我的工作和出版社的工作相关但又截然不同。出版社的工作是让读者购买书籍；我的工作是让读者开始阅读并持续阅读。
