The author seems to be putting together a complex portrait of a historical figure who is exceptionally manly in the most basic sense—he cannot be taken advantage of even by kings. His pride is not a tragic flaw—he does not suffer a tragic end, but dies in his bed, a very old man, subject to the same indignities as all old men (once, when he pushes himself up to the fire, one of his serving women reprimands him and tells him to get back to bed and stay out of the way).

埃吉尔的诗歌在整部传奇中被大量引用，展现了他的自我认知（尽管由于这些诗歌运用了大量程式化的修辞手法，现代读者或许会觉得它们难以揭示其本质）。他晚年经历的几件事——爱子的去世、与女儿的一段往事——也使他成为传奇中最复杂、心理最细腻的英雄之一。他并非像终结者那样冷酷无情（尽管据说他拥有那种力量），也并非愚钝迟钝（他与那些野蛮无情的角色形成鲜明对比），更不是冷酷无情（他深爱着妻子、家人以及众多朋友）。作者似乎在刻画一个复杂而深刻的历史人物形象，他拥有最基本的男子气概——即使是君王也无法占他便宜。他的骄傲并非悲剧性的缺陷——他没有遭遇悲惨的结局，而是在床上去世，成了一个非常年老的人，遭受了所有老人同样的屈辱（有一次，当他挣扎着走到火堆旁时，他的一个女仆斥责了他，让他回到床上，别碍事）。

Egil Skallagrimsson was a historical figure and an ancestor of Snorri Sturluson's. There is no way of knowing how accurate Snorri was in depicting Egil's adventures, but by focusing on him and making each incident of his life logical, Snorri manages to avoid some of the problems that writers of other sagas run into, in particular the sense that a character's actions are against his own interests, that plausibility is being sacrificed to plots, and that what is going on is really not understandable. The reader may not agree with Egil's every action and opinion, but Egil himself is vivid and believable.

埃吉尔·斯卡拉格里姆松是一位历史人物，也是斯诺里·斯图鲁松的祖先。我们无从得知斯诺里对埃吉尔冒险经历的描写究竟有多准确，但他通过聚焦埃吉尔，并使他人生中的每一个事件都合乎逻辑，成功地避免了其他萨迦作家常遇到的一些问题，尤其是避免了人物行为违背自身利益、情节发展牺牲真实性以及故事本身令人费解等问题。读者或许不会认同埃吉尔的每一个行为和观点，但埃吉尔这个人物本身却栩栩如生，令人信服。

Egilssaga demonstrates one of the most effective novelistic techniques—that of simply telling the action and the dialogue in detail without commenting much upon them. As the story accumulates interesting detail (and it does have to be interesting), the reader's unwillingness to suspend disbelief is overcome by the simple effect of imagining what is going on. Then the reader begins supplying cause and effect and meaning as a way of knitting together actions that at first may have seemed random or unbelievable. The anomalous takes shape and becomes simply unusual and therefore worthy of note. Snorri never intrudes, and yet his knowledge, confidence, and absolutely clean and beautifully paced manner of telling the story indicate an author with a great deal of experience—and, indeed, Snorri was a powerful Icelander of the mid-thirteenth century who also compiled and edited a collection of myths and legends known as Snorri's Edda.

《埃吉尔萨迦》展现了一种最有效的叙事技巧——即详细叙述情节和对话，而不加过多评论。随着故事中趣味细节的积累（而故事本身必须引人入胜），读者最初难以接受的怀疑会被想象所克服。随后，读者开始赋予因果关系和意义，将起初看似随机或难以置信的事件串联起来。异常之处逐渐成形，变得非同寻常，因而值得关注。斯诺里从未干预，但他渊博的知识、自信的笔触以及流畅优美的叙述节奏，都表明他是一位经验丰富的作家——事实上，斯诺里是十三世纪中期一位颇具影响力的冰岛人，他还编纂了神话传说集《斯诺里埃达》。

3. The Saga of the People of Laxardal

3. 拉萨达尔人民的传奇

TRANS., KENEVA KUNZ, IN THE SAGAS OF ICELANDERS , ED. ROBERT KELLOGG (1250-70; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 2000), PP. 271-421.

译者：KENEVA KUNZ，《冰岛人传奇》，罗伯特·凯洛格编（1250-70；纽约：企鹅出版社，2000 年重印），第 271-421 页。

The prose narrative, novel-like tradition of the Icelandic saga flowered in medieval Iceland between the first half of the thirteenth century and the middle of the fourteenth century. Several writers of Icelandic literature are known—Ari Thorgilsson, who wrote the history of Iceland at the beginning of the twelfth century, and Snorri Sturluson, who compiled the legends and myths of the prose Edda in the middle of the thirteenth century. Some believe that The Saga of the People of Laxardal was written by a woman.

冰岛萨迦的散文叙事传统，如同小说一般，在中世纪的冰岛蓬勃发展，时间大约在十三世纪上半叶至十四世纪中叶。冰岛文学中涌现出几位知名作家，例如十二世纪初撰写冰岛历史的阿里·索吉尔松，以及十三世纪中叶编纂散文体埃达的斯诺里·斯图鲁松。有人认为《拉克萨尔达尔人萨迦》的作者是一位女性。

The action of the saga takes place at the end of the tenth century, at about the time Scandinavia was converting from worship of Norse gods to Christianity. After a preliminary explanation of why the original settlers left Norway and how they settled the valley of the Lax (Salmon) River, the story focuses on two families—that of Hoskuld, a prominent farmer with several sons, and that of Gudrun, the most beautiful woman ever to be born in Iceland. As a young woman, Gudrun has four dreams that predict the fate of her four marriages. Hoskuld has several sons, of whom two, Kjartan and Bolli, are the most beautiful and promising. Gudrun is a strong-minded woman— she gets rid of husband number one in favor of husband number two, but husband number two is drowned. She then falls in love with Kjartan, and when he decides to go to Norway to seek his fortune, she asks to go along, but he refuses to take her. While he is gone, Bolli asks to marry her, telling her that Kjartan has lost interest in her in favor of the Norwegian king's daughter. When Kjartan returns, wealthy and more handsome than ever, Bolli and Gudrun are already married. Jealousy, envy, spite, conflict, and killings ensue. The feud spreads around the valley, with betrayal and trickery the order of the day, until at last all family representatives are satisfied with their compensation and Gudrun devotes herself to religion. One of the most famous exchanges in all of Icelandic literature happens at the very end, when Gudrun's son asks her which of her husbands she preferred. She says, “Him I treated worst was the one I loved the best.” She means Kjartan, whom she had goaded her husband Bolli to kill.

这部传奇故事发生在十世纪末，大约在斯堪的纳维亚半岛从北欧诸神信仰转向基督教的时期。故事首先简要介绍了最初的定居者为何离开挪威，以及他们如何在拉克斯河（鲑鱼河）谷定居。随后，故事聚焦于两个家庭：一个是拥有数个儿子的显赫农场主霍斯库尔德的家庭，另一个是冰岛有史以来最美丽的女子古德伦的家庭。年轻时的古德伦做了四个梦，预示着她四段婚姻的命运。霍斯库尔德有几个儿子，其中两个，基亚尔坦和博利，最为英俊潇洒，前途无量。古德伦意志坚定——她抛弃了第一任丈夫，迎娶了第二任丈夫，但第二任丈夫却不幸溺水身亡。之后，她爱上了基亚尔坦。当基亚尔坦决定前往挪威谋生时，她请求同行，但遭到了拒绝。在他离开期间，博利向她求婚，告诉她基亚尔坦已经对她失去了兴趣，转而爱上了挪威国王的女儿。当基亚尔坦回来时，他比以往任何时候都更加富有英俊，而博利和古德伦已经结为夫妻。嫉妒、羡慕、怨恨、冲突和杀戮接踵而至。这场世仇蔓延到整个山谷，背叛和欺骗成了家常便饭，直到最后所有家族代表都对各自的补偿感到满意，古德伦也皈依了宗教。冰岛文学中最著名的对话之一发生在故事的结尾，古德伦的儿子问她更喜欢哪个丈夫。她回答说：“我最不待见的那个人，却是我最爱的。”她指的是基亚尔坦，她曾怂恿丈夫博利杀死他。

The writers of the Icelandic sagas were a good deal more cryptic than Murasaki Shikibu. They specialized in the economically rendered but telling detail, and the reader has to be alert to pick up the undercurrents of the story. The contemporary audiences of the sagas were interested not only in what happened, but also who was who and who their thirteenth-century descendants were—the sagas worked as genealogy and geography, not only as stories. And all the saga writers were aware of what the other saga writers were writing about—the sagas had many characters in common and many formal effects in common. For example, it often happens in a saga that a character wants to do something that others think is unwise. When he proposes this course of action, the standard reply is, “You will do as you wish in any case.” There is also a customary use of understatement—toward the end of the present saga, men surround the sheep-tending hut of one of the characters. When he injures one of them with a spear thrust through a window, the other members of the ambush remark “that there must be men inside.”

冰岛萨迦的作者比紫式部晦涩得多。他们擅长以简洁的笔触描绘却又意味深长的细节，读者必须保持警觉才能领会故事的弦外之音。萨迦的当代读者不仅关注故事情节，也关心人物关系以及他们十三世纪的后裔——萨迦不仅是故事，更是家谱和地理志。而且，所有萨迦作者都了解其他作者的创作内容——萨迦中有许多共同的人物和形式特征。例如，萨迦中经常出现这样的情节：某个人物想要做某件别人认为不明智的事情。当他提出这个建议时，人们通常会回答：“无论如何，你都得按自己的想法去做。”此外，萨迦中还惯用含蓄的表达方式——在萨迦的结尾，一群人包围了其中一个人物的牧羊小屋。当他用长矛穿过窗户刺伤其中一人时，其他伏击者说道：“里面一定有人。”

The Icelandic sagas were written about an armed society full of hotheaded citizens with strong propensities toward violence. The characters often make choices we might find difficult to understand. At the beginning of the Laxardal saga, one man cheats another out of his half of a catch of fish. A few days later, the cheated man comes up behind him and cuts off his head. He is in turn pursued by the first man's relatives. In spite of her third dream, which predicts the death of her third husband through killing, Gudrun goads and belittles him and promotes conflict. In part, the strangeness of the Icelandic sagas comes from their focus—most were written in a time of widespread fighting about the temptation and curse of widespread fighting (in fact, the society the sagas depict was probably more peaceful than the sagas make it seem). The sagas relate a sequence of events without delving into the psychology of the participants—characters rarely reveal their motivation, except by an ironic sentence or two. The sagas, therefore, add up to a theory of human behavior, but neither the characters nor the narrators discourse about that theory. The theory is simple and brutal—people do what they are fated to do, actions are quite often foolish, only the wisest manage to avoid disaster, and the best attitude is one of stoic irony.

冰岛萨迦描绘的是一个武装社会，那里的公民性情暴躁，暴力倾向强烈。故事中的人物常常做出一些我们难以理解的选择。在《拉克萨尔达尔萨迦》的开头，一个人骗走了另一个人一半的渔获。几天后，被骗的人从背后砍下了他的头颅。随后，他遭到第一个人的亲属的追杀。尽管古德伦做了第三个梦，预示着她的第三任丈夫会死于杀戮，但她仍然挑衅、贬低他，并煽动冲突。冰岛萨迦的奇特之处部分源于其主题——大多数萨迦写于战乱频仍的年代，探讨的是战争的诱惑与诅咒（事实上，萨迦所描绘的社会可能比萨迦中展现的要和平得多）。萨迦叙述了一系列事件，却很少深入探讨人物的心理——人物很少透露自己的动机，除非是通过一两句讽刺的话语。因此，这些传奇故事构成了一种关于人类行为的理论，但无论是故事中的人物还是叙述者，都没有对这一理论进行过深入探讨。这个理论简单而残酷——人们会做他们命中注定要做的事，他们的行为往往是愚蠢的，只有最睿智的人才能避免灾难，而最好的态度是坚忍的反讽。

The result is an ambience of impending doom and mischance, and the absence of free will and a sense of spiritual redemption. The characters are enslaved by their impetuosity and pride, benumbed by the repeated destruction of relationships. When they foresee evil outcomes, their expressions of regret are muted and rueful. Not for the Norse men and women those floods of tears that Murasaki Shikibu's characters indulge in. For these Norse, life is so fleeting that they don't even have the luxury to reflect upon how fleeting it is.

其结果营造出一种厄运将至、厄运难耐的氛围，以及自由意志的缺失和精神救赎的缺失。人物被冲动和骄傲所奴役，被一次又一次的人际关系破坏所麻木。当他们预见到不祥的结局时，他们的悔恨之情也显得低沉而哀伤。北欧男女不会像紫式部笔下的人物那样痛哭流涕。对这些北欧人来说，生命如此短暂，他们甚至没有余力去思考生命的短暂。

For the modern reader, though, the Norse characters share with the Japanese characters unfamiliar moral standards. Gudrun is frequently called the greatest heroine of the sagas, but she does not have the moral characteristics of appealing modern heroines. She is powerful, greedy, angry, envious, treacherous, and unloving, but she is never judged for these qualities. Her beauty and the grandness of her story are what elevate her to greatness. Like Genji, she can commit what we would call “sins” or “crimes” because she exists outside of subsequent Christian moral precepts and outside of the ordinary—that is her claim to being a worthy protagonist.

然而，对于现代读者来说，北欧神话中的人物与日本神话中的人物一样，都拥有着陌生的道德标准。古德伦常被誉为萨迦中最伟大的女英雄，但她并不具备现代人眼中魅力十足的女英雄所应有的道德品质。她强大、贪婪、愤怒、嫉妒、背信弃义、冷酷无情，但她从未因此受到评判。她的美貌和她故事的宏大格局才是她被奉为伟大的原因。如同源氏一样，她可以犯下我们今天所谓的“罪孽”或“罪行”，因为她游离于后世基督教的道德准则之外，也游离于寻常之外——这正是她作为一位杰出主角的资格所在。

4. Giovanni Boccaccio. The Decameron

4.乔瓦尼·薄伽丘。十日谈

TRANS. G. H. MCWILLIAM (1352; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1995), 909 PP.

译者：G. H. MCWILLIAM (1352；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1995 年)，909 页。

The Decameron is a compendium of tales and stories compiled, translated, composed, and arranged by Florentine man of letters Giovanni Boccaccio during the time of the Black Death ( 1347 – 49 ). Ten young people of means—seven women and three men, and each with one servant—elect to leave Florence, the scene of much illness, death, and social chaos, and go into the countryside for fourteen days. There they find and make use of three beautiful and abundant locations (think of them as perfect resort compounds) to rest and recuperate their spirits before returning to the city. They decide to pass the time singing, dancing, feasting, enjoying nature, and telling stories with various themes, many of them comic or satiric, a few of them macabre or gruesome, several tragic. Some are only a page or two long, some are as simple as jokes, and some are long and complex, exploring social, philosophical, and spiritual themes.

《十日谈》是佛罗伦萨文人乔万尼·薄伽丘在黑死病肆虐时期（1347-1349年）编纂、翻译、创作和整理的一部故事集。十位家境优渥的年轻人——七位女性和三位男性，每人各带一名仆人——决定离开疾病肆虐、死亡横行、社会动荡不安的佛罗伦萨，前往乡下度过十四天。他们在那里找到了三处风景优美、物产丰饶的地方（可以将其视为完美的度假胜地），休养生息，恢复精神，然后再返回城市。他们决定以歌唱、舞蹈、宴饮、欣赏自然风光和讲述各种主题的故事来消磨时光，其中许多故事滑稽或讽刺，少数故事阴森恐怖，还有一些故事悲惨。有些故事只有一两页，有些故事简单得像笑话，有些故事则篇幅很长、情节复杂，探讨了社会、哲学和精神等主题。

It is hard to convey the richness of Boccaccio's accomplishment, which is surely one of the great prose masterpieces of all time. Boccaccio makes full use of the possibilities of his form. He begins with a graphic and detailed picture of life in Florence during the Black Death. It is not only that the population has been decimated, it is also that the people have been brought to a state of coarse numbness and brutality in their relations with one another, leaving their loved ones to die alone and be buried alone, while they are rioting and carousing, giving up all forms of decorum and prudence.

薄伽丘的成就之丰富难以言表，这无疑是散文史上最伟大的杰作之一。薄伽丘充分发挥了散文体裁的优势。他以生动细致的笔触描绘了黑死病肆虐期间佛罗伦萨的景象。不仅人口锐减，人们彼此之间的关系也变得麻木而残暴，他们任由亲人孤独死去、孤苦伶仃地埋葬，自己却纵情享乐、寻欢作乐，抛弃了一切礼仪和谨慎。

Boccaccio was a great lover of Dante and The Divine Comedy , and later in his life became a friend of the poet Petrarch. Boccaccio was a convivial, influential, and well-connected man in Florence, and The Decameron was famous from the beginning of its circulation among the literate classes. One thing that is especially interesting about it is Boccaccio's evident awareness of himself as a target of criticism in the literary rather than the social or political sense. At the beginning of the fourth day, he breaks the frame and addresses some of the criticisms— that some of the stories aren't accurately translated, but also that their subject matter (often of a sexual or erotic nature) is inappropriate or unworthy of literary art. He defends himself from the first charge by challenging his critics to produce originals different from his, and from the second two charges by noting that sexual desire is as natural as hunger. To deny sexual desire, “one has to have exceptional powers, which often turn out to have been used, not only in vain, but to the serious harm of those who employ them.”

薄伽丘酷爱但丁及其《神曲》，晚年又与诗人彼特拉克结为挚友。薄伽丘在佛罗伦萨是一位风趣幽默、颇具影响力且人脉广泛的人物，《十日谈》自问世以来便在文人雅士中广为流传。这部作品最引人入胜之处在于，薄伽丘显然意识到自己会受到文学而非社会或政治意义上的批评。在第四日开篇，他打破了故事框架，回应了一些批评——有人认为部分故事翻译不准确，也有人认为其题材（通常涉及性或情色）不合时宜，有损文学艺术。对于第一个批评，他挑战批评者创作出与他不同的原创作品；对于后两个批评，他则指出性欲与饥饿一样自然。要抑制性欲，“一个人必须拥有非凡的能力，而这种能力往往被证明不仅徒劳无功，而且对使用者造成了严重的伤害。”

The tragic and gruesome stories notwithstanding, The Decameron is essentially a comic work, and Boccaccio's choice to write it in prose enhances its comic qualities. Most of the stories are about connections successfully achieved, often through guile, but often, also, through love and fidelity. Although several of the stories, especially the last, have a misogynistic cast, the desirability of male-female relations is never in question. Women and men are not perfect, but they are better off in one another's arms having “delight and joy of one another, causing the nightingale to sing at frequent intervals” (p. 396 ) than not. The ten young people form a perfect comic society, surrounded by beauty and abundance that they can fully appreciate (Boccaccio includes a scene in which the women go away and find a small valley where they swim naked in a clear lake to cool themselves); they have differing opinions but no conflict. They treat one another with courtesy and respect, but for the fourteen days of the taletelling, they do not couple up—their relations remain ones of friendship; the balance among all the participants is maintained.

尽管《十日谈》中不乏悲剧和骇人的故事，但它本质上是一部喜剧作品，薄伽丘选择用散文体来创作更增强了其喜剧特质。大多数故事都讲述了人与人之间成功建立的联系，这种联系往往是通过计谋，但也常常源于爱与忠贞。虽然其中一些故事，尤其是最后一个故事，带有厌女色彩，但男女关系的合理性从未受到质疑。男女并非完美，但他们彼此相爱，享受着“彼此的喜悦和快乐，令夜莺不时歌唱”（第396页），总比分离要好。这十位年轻人构成了一个完美的喜剧社会，他们被美丽富饶的环境所环绕，并能充分欣赏这一切（薄伽丘描写了这样一个场景：女人们离开家，找到一个小山谷，在清澈的湖水中裸泳消暑）；他们意见不一，却没有冲突。他们彼此以礼相待，互相尊重，但在为期十四天的讲故事活动中，他们不会结成伴侣——他们的关系始终是友谊；所有参与者之间的平衡得以维持。

Though many of the tales are based on traditional material, Boccaccio locates quite a few of them in the Florence of his day, or in other parts of Italy that his readers were familiar with. He uses well-known names—sometimes, he uses a famous family name, such as Cavalcanti, but introduces a fictional member. Like Lady Murasaki and the Icelandic saga writers, Boccaccio is interested in the particularities of his time and place—he is well aware, for example, of the power of the Florentine mercantile class and of the vagaries of the bourgeois life. Many of his characters gain sudden wealth and then lose it through money-lending or trade. He also depicts the increasing fluidity of social and economic class as well as some of the problems of what we would call the professions—doctors and scholars. In other words, while Boccaccio's structure and material are medieval in many ways, the sense of change and possibility, the irreverence toward traditional figures of authority (especially the church), and the individuality of the scores and scores of characters he creates are modern and “prosaic.” Prose is for exploring what is unique about situations and characters—we might say that prose is “Aristotelian.” Poetry is for exploring what incidents and persons typify—it is “Platonic.” Like many prose writers, Boccaccio adopts a rather self-effacing narrative voice—his statement, above, that he does not have the power to defy nature, extends beyond the realm of sexuality and desire to the realm of art and philosophy. The accumulation of telling detail—that is, of psychological truth—is what he is after.

尽管许多故事取材于传统，但薄伽丘将其中不少故事的背景设定在他所处的时代的佛罗伦萨，或是读者熟悉的意大利其他地区。他使用一些耳熟能详的名字——有时，他会使用像卡瓦尔坎蒂这样的著名姓氏，但会引入一个虚构的人物。与紫式部夫人和冰岛萨迦作家一样，薄伽丘对他所处的时代和地域的特殊性很感兴趣——例如，他非常清楚佛罗伦萨商人阶层的权力以及资产阶级生活的变幻莫测。他笔下的许多人物都曾一夜暴富，又因放贷或经商而失去财富。他还描绘了社会和经济阶层日益流动化的趋势，以及我们今天所说的专业人士——医生和学者——所面临的一些问题。换句话说，尽管薄伽丘的结构和素材在许多方面都带有中世纪的印记，但他作品中展现的变革与可能性、对传统权威人物（尤其是教会）的不敬，以及他笔下众多人物鲜明的个性，却都体现出现代性和“散文式”的特征。散文旨在探索情境和人物的独特之处——我们可以说散文是“亚里士多德式的”。诗歌则旨在探索事件和人物的典型特征——它是“柏拉图式的”。如同许多散文作家一样，薄伽丘采用了一种相当谦逊的叙述口吻——他上面所说的自己无力违背自然规律，其含义超越了性欲的范畴，延伸到了艺术和哲学的领域。他所追求的是积累富有表现力的细节——也就是心理层面的真相。

If narrative is about how something happens, and its meaning grows out of specific, and often very tiny, turns of events, then it cannot help but explore the differences between individuals, because events impose choices on the characters, and choices reveal intentions and predispositions that are always made on an individual basis. Quite often the choices contradict conventional rules or standards, and then the narrator and the character must defend or illustrate the rationale for a particular choice. While The Decameron does not have the structure of a novel, in that it is not about a single set of characters who are engaged in working out a single plot, it does have the piling on of character and incident that is typical of a novel and that seems to reveal (like The Tale of Genji) life as it is being lived around the author. In fact, the verisimilitude of The Decameron is so marked that scholars have been at pains to point out that Boccaccio's portrait of the plague in Florence is not taken from the author's experience, but from a depiction of the plague in Florence of the ninth century that Boccaccio had read.

如果叙事讲述的是事情如何发生，其意义源于具体且往往非常细微的事件转折，那么它必然会探讨个体之间的差异，因为事件会迫使人物做出选择，而选择则揭示了人物的意图和倾向，这些意图和倾向总是因人而异的。很多时候，这些选择与传统的规则或标准相悖，这时叙述者和人物就必须为特定选择辩护或阐明其理由。《十日谈》虽然不具备小说的结构，因为它并非围绕单一人物展开单一情节，但它确实具备小说典型的人物和事件堆砌，并且似乎（如同《源氏物语》一样）揭示了作者周围的生活。事实上，《十日谈》的真实性非常显著，以至于学者们不遗余力地指出，薄伽丘对佛罗伦萨瘟疫的描述并非取材于作者的亲身经历，而是取材于薄伽丘读过的关于九世纪佛罗伦萨瘟疫的描述。

As in many great novels, the treasury of detail in The Decameron defies analysis, or even sufficient appreciation. The reader (and it is a reader— The Decameron is too long to be recited, too detailed to be filmed except in an abbreviated form, too various to be dramatized, too huge to be painted) can only appreciate each brilliant turn of phrase or each exquisite irony or each perfect set piece and then move on to the next, allowing them, afterward, to coexist imperfectly but delightfully in the memory, until her enjoyment is renewed with another reading.

如同许多伟大的小说一样，《十日谈》中丰富的细节令人难以分析，甚至难以充分领略。读者（的确是读者——《十日谈》篇幅太长，无法朗诵；细节太丰富，除了删节版之外无法搬上银幕；内容太繁杂，无法戏剧化；规模太宏大，无法绘画）只能欣赏每一个精彩的措辞、每一个精妙的讽刺、每一个完美的场景，然后继续阅读下一个，让它们在记忆中以一种不完美却令人愉悦的方式并存，直到再次阅读时，才能重拾这份乐趣。

5. Lazari 11 o de Tormes

5. 拉撒路 11 o de Tormes

TRANS. STANLEY APPELBAUM (1554; REPR., NEW YORK: DOVER, 2001), 103 PP.

斯坦利·阿佩尔鲍姆译（1554 年；纽约：多佛出版社，2001 年重印），103 页。

While The Heptameron (see below) marked, perhaps, the end of something (a medieval way of looking at things, from the point of view of the master class), Lazarillo de Tormes perhaps marked the beginning of something—the modern way of looking at things, from the point of view of an average, or less than average, citizen who was interested not in romance or chivalric prowess, but survival. Not quite a novel, more like a story or a fragment, Lazarillo de Tormes was an unsuppressible Spanish narrative of the sixteenth century. Published in 1554 , it was enormously popular, and continued to be so for the next couple of centuries, however energetically the authorities tried to ban it. It was widely read and imitated, the first, or perhaps the proto, picaresque novel, about the adventures of a lower-class and in many ways disreputable young man, often a petty criminal (though Lazarillo himself is simply impoverished).

《七日谈》（见下文）或许标志着某种时代的终结（一种中世纪的、从统治阶级视角出发的看待事物的方式），而《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》或许标志着某种时代的开端——一种现代的、从普通民众（甚至低于普通民众）视角出发的看待事物的方式。这些普通民众对浪漫情怀和骑士精神并不感兴趣，他们只关心生存。与其说是一部小说，不如说更像是一个故事或片段，《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》是十六世纪西班牙一部无法被压制的叙事作品。该书出版于1554年，风靡一时，并在接下来的几个世纪里持续流行，尽管当局竭力试图查禁它。它被广泛阅读和模仿，是第一部，或许是第一部原型流浪汉小说，讲述了一个出身低微、在许多方面都声名狼藉的年轻人的冒险故事，他常常犯些小罪（尽管拉撒路本人只是贫困潦倒）。

The author gives Lzaro (who narrates in his own voice) three or four adventures in finding himself a master and a livelihood, and then seems to lose interest and marries him off to a woman who may or may not be cuckolding him. Lzaro's voice is charming, and the details he relates of the tricks played upon him and others are interesting enough, but the novella seems primitive in comparison with some of the other works discussed on our list. In addition to being of considerable literary-critical and historical interest, though, Lazarillo de Tormes shows plenty of the characteristics intrinsic to prose narrative—it is a lively social document concerned with daily life as the author is living it. Apart from Lzaro, the characters he meets are types, but they are in no way ideals—a blind man who mistreats him and whom he tricks, a friar who hoards all his bread, and an impoverished nobleman who absconds without paying his rent, leaving Lzaro to fend for himself. Lzaro, though a child and a servant, is perfectly willing to express his opinion of these characters, and his opinion is not respectful. Though short almost to the point of being fragmentary, Lazarillo de Tormes was subversive in giving a voice to the hitherto voiceless, and demonstrates that the novel is indeed a naturally democratic form—promising not “every man a king” but rather “every man a protagonist.”

作者让拉扎罗（以第一人称叙述）经历了三四次寻找主人和谋生的冒险，之后似乎失去了兴趣，便安排他娶了一个可能对他不忠的女人。拉扎罗的叙述声音迷人，他讲述的自己和他人遭遇的种种诡计也颇为有趣，但与我们榜单上讨论的其他作品相比，这部中篇小说显得略显稚嫩。然而，除了具有相当的文学批评和历史价值外，《托尔梅斯的拉扎里洛》也展现了散文叙事的诸多特征——它是一部生动的社会纪实，关注作者的日常生活。除了拉扎罗之外，他遇到的其他人物都是典型人物，但绝非理想化的形象——一个虐待他、又被他戏弄的盲人，一个囤积面包的修士，以及一个拖欠房租后逃之夭夭、留下拉扎罗自谋生路的穷贵族。拉扎罗虽然只是个孩子，又是个仆人，却毫不掩饰地表达了自己对这些人物的看法，而且他的看法并不恭敬。尽管《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》篇幅很短，几乎近乎残缺，但它却具有颠覆性，因为它赋予了以往被剥夺话语权的人们以声音，并证明了小说本身就是一种天然的民主形式——它承诺的不是“人人皆可为王”，而是“人人皆可为主角”。

6. Marguerite de Navarre The Heptameron

6. 玛格丽特·德·纳瓦拉 《七梅龙》

TRANS. PAUL A. CHILTON (1557-58; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1984), 543 PP.

保罗·A·奇尔顿译（1557-58 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1984 年），543 页。

The Heptameron was compiled (or composed) in conscious imitation of The Decameron at the court, and probably under the direct supervision of Marguerite, the queen of Navarre and the sister of Franois I, king of France. It was published after Marguerite's death, so it is impossible to say with certainty that she wrote it, but she did write poetry and did sponsor much literary activity at court, including the work of Rabelais. Marguerite died in 1549 , at age fifty-seven. A version of The Heptameron was published in 1557 , and an edition giving credit to Marguerite the following year.

《七日谈》是在宫廷中有意模仿《十日谈》编纂而成，很可能是在纳瓦拉王后玛格丽特（法国国王弗朗索瓦一世的妹妹）的直接监督下完成的。该书出版于玛格丽特去世之后，因此无法确定她是否是作者，但她确实创作诗歌，并在宫廷中资助了许多文学活动，包括拉伯雷的作品。玛格丽特于1549年去世，享年57岁。《七日谈》的一个版本于1557年出版，次年出版了一个署名为玛格丽特的版本。

The construction of the story cycle is similar to that of The Decameron —a group of men and women are confined to an out-of-the-way spot and decide to tell ten stories every day until a hundred have been told, but the frame, and the mood, of the later French work is decidedly different from that of the earlier Italian work. Whereas Boccaccio's young people leave plague-ridden Florence in search of a happy land where they can refresh themselves, and Boccaccio devotes considerable effort to describing the paradises they find, the storytellers of The Heptameron , who are older and married or widowed, come together by chance in the wilds of the Pyrenees after several frightening misadventures in which the husband of one of the ladies, Longarine, is killed. They take refuge in a monastery while a bridge is being built that will permit their departure. Little space is given to describing the setting, but more space is given to the group commentary at the end of each story. Additionally, they adopt the rule that the stories are to be true rather than from books. It seems that most if not all of the stories were taken from the lives of actual contemporaries of the tellers, who are also largely identifiable—Parlamente seems to be Marguerite herself, and Hircan seems to be Henri of Navarre. The others seem to be noble friends or relatives of theirs. Thus, though many of the stories are artfully told, they occupy a middle ground between gossip and fiction, and they are used by the group for a prolonged discussion of love, faith, virtue, and the true natures of men and women. The argument is unresolved because the manuscript breaks off at the beginning of the eighth day.

故事的结构与《十日谈》相似——一群男女被限制在一个偏僻的地方，决定每天讲述十个故事，直到讲完一百个为止。然而，这部法国后期作品的框架和氛围与早期的意大利作品截然不同。薄伽丘笔下的年轻人离开瘟疫肆虐的佛罗伦萨，寻找一片可以休憩的乐土，薄伽丘也花费大量笔墨描绘他们找到的天堂；而《七日谈》中的说书人年纪较大，已婚或丧偶，在经历了一系列惊险的冒险之后，偶然在比利牛斯山脉的荒野中相遇。其中一位女士隆加琳的丈夫在冒险中丧生。他们躲进一座修道院，等待一座桥梁建成，以便离开。书中对场景的描写篇幅不多，但对每个故事结尾的集体评论却着墨颇多。此外，他们还遵循一条规则：故事必须取材于真实事件，而非书籍。这些故事似乎大多取材于讲述者同时代人的真实生活，而且这些人大多身份可辨——帕拉门特似乎就是玛格丽特本人，希尔坎似乎是纳瓦拉的亨利。其他人则像是他们的贵族朋友或亲戚。因此，尽管许多故事讲述得颇具技巧，但它们介于闲谈和虚构之间，被这个群体用来展开关于爱情、信仰、美德以及男女本性的漫长讨论。这场争论最终未能解决，因为手稿在第八天的开头戛然而止。

The Heptameron has neither the charm nor the comic exuberance of The Decameron , but it has a dark, obsessive, compelling quality of its own that carries the reader through many stories that seem in some ways to be about the same thing—how to work out the inequities between men and women, and, if they can't be worked out, how to justify them by appealing to Scripture or natural law. If a hallmark of the tales in The Decameron is the lively coupling of all sorts of lovers in spite of all sorts of obstacles, and whose pleasures are approved of by the author, a hallmark of The Heptameron is quite the opposite—love and sex are dangerous but unavoidable, and the consequences of passion are almost always dishonor, illness, or death. Hircan is the spokesman for the extreme male position—if a man falls in love with a woman, his love is demonstrated only by his determination to bed her by any means; if seduction doesn't work, then rape is not only justified, but also required. If she resists, then for the sake of his honor he may kill her (at the same time, since Parlamente is his wife and she is present, Hircan often protests that these are abstract rules that apply to others and not to him, since he is entirely satisfied in his marriage). The women use their stories to demonstrate how love and virtue can coexist in certain women, but the terms of women's lives are so circumscribed that the group never agrees about what love is for a woman. They all agree, however, that women's lives are dangerous, especially those of beautiful women, and that there is no real protection if a woman attracts the notice of a passionate lover. In one story, a young man enlists the aid of a serving girl to carry letters to the well-born woman he loves. The father of his beloved (a duke) discovers the activities of the serving woman and threatens her. She pleads with the duchess to send her off to a convent to avoid the duke's wrath, and she does so, but the duke persuades his wife that he doesn't mean to harm the girl. She promises the girl safety on her life and honor, so the girl comes back, whereupon the duke has her imprisoned and hanged, even though the duchess begs him not to. Though this story shocks most of the listeners, the duke has his defenders, who assert that he has the right to treat his servants as he pleases. In this regard, it is important to remember that The Heptameron was the work of the actual ruling class—a king, his queen, and their friends. Part of its rhetorical purpose is to maintain status quo power relationships in French society. Although the storytellers lament sometimes that life is the way it is, none of them suggests that it be arranged differently.

《七日谈》既没有《十日谈》的魅力，也没有其滑稽的活力，但它却有一种独特的阴郁、执着而又引人入胜的特质，引领读者阅读许多看似主题相同的故事——如何解决男女之间的不平等，以及如果无法解决，如何诉诸圣经或自然法则来为其辩护。如果说《十日谈》的标志性特征是形形色色的恋人克服重重阻碍最终结合，并且他们的欢愉得到作者的认可，那么《七日谈》的标志性特征则截然相反——爱情和性是危险的，却又无法避免，激情带来的后果几乎总是耻辱、疾病或死亡。希尔坎是极端男性立场的代言人——如果一个男人爱上了一个女人，他表达爱的方式就是不惜一切代价与她发生关系；如果诱惑无效，那么强奸不仅是正当的，而且是必要的。如果她反抗，为了维护他的荣誉，他可能会杀了她（与此同时，由于帕拉门特是他的妻子，而且她就在场，希尔坎经常辩解说，这些规则是抽象的，只适用于别人，不适用于他，因为他对自己的婚姻非常满意）。女人们用她们的故事来说明爱情和美德在某些女性身上是如何共存的，但女性的生活条件如此受限，以至于她们对女性的爱情究竟是什么始终无法达成共识。然而，她们一致认为，女性的生活充满危险，尤其是美貌的女性，如果一个女人引起了一位热情爱人的注意，她就没有任何真正的保护。在一个故事里，一个年轻人雇佣了一位女仆，让她帮忙给心爱的出身高贵的女子送信。他心上人的父亲（一位公爵）发现了女仆的所作所为，并威胁她。她恳求公爵夫人将她送往修道院，以躲避公爵的怒火，公爵夫人照做了。但公爵却说服妻子，他无意伤害这个女孩。她以自己的生命和名誉担保女孩的安全，于是女孩回来了。公爵不顾公爵夫人的苦苦哀求，将她囚禁并处以绞刑。尽管这个故事令大多数听众震惊，但公爵也有拥护者，他们声称他有权随意对待自己的仆人。从这个角度来看，重要的是要记住，《七日谈》是当时统治阶级——国王、王后及其朋友——的作品。它的修辞目的之一就是维护法国社会现有的权力关系。尽管故事讲述者有时会感叹生活就是如此，但他们中没有人提出过改变现状的建议。

The only recourse—and a problematic one it is—is faith and the direct experience of God's love. Several of the storytellers relate stories that they consider show true devotion to religion and virtue, and much of the framing material is taken up with the religious observances of the ten men and women. The leader of the group, an older, very devout woman named Oiselle, conducts lessons from Scripture at the start of every day. The subtext of The Heptameron is the Reformation and Counter-Reformation, which unsettled sixteenth-century Europe with anticlerical and evangelical ideas. But while everyone in the group seems to agree with these new ideas in principle, many of them doubt whether they can work in reality, given the importance of position and appearance. The seventy-two stories repeatedly demonstrate that no happiness can be found in the world the characters inhabit— no theory or technique or belief or degree of caution, no amount of power, and no social institution, whether marriage or law, offers protection from the passions of relatives and associates, most of which begin with love and attraction but end with hatred and resentment. The final effect of The Heptameron is very dark, and much in contrast to The Decameron.

唯一的出路——尽管这本身也是个难题——便是信仰以及对上帝之爱的直接体验。几位讲述者讲述了他们认为展现了对宗教和美德的真正虔诚的故事，而故事的大部分篇幅都用来描写这十位男女的宗教仪式。这群人的领袖是一位名叫奥伊塞尔的年长虔诚的女性，她每天清晨都会带领大家学习圣经。《七日谈》的潜台词是宗教改革和反宗教改革，这两场运动以其反教权主义和福音派思想撼动了十六世纪的欧洲。虽然这群人似乎在原则上都认同这些新思想，但考虑到地位和外表的重要性，许多人怀疑这些思想在现实中是否行得通。这七十二个故事反复表明，在人物所处的世界里，幸福无处可寻——任何理论、技巧、信仰或谨慎程度，无论权力大小，无论婚姻还是法律等社会制度，都无法保护他们免受亲友的情感伤害。这些情感大多始于爱慕，最终却以仇恨和怨恨收场。《七日谈》的最终效果十分阴郁，与《十日谈》截然不同。

In the face of the Black Death, Boccaccio is able to construct an opposing picture of beauty, virtue, friendship, and forgiveness, where fear and tragedy are more than counterbalanced by honest pleasure and real connection. Two hundred years later, under less obviously trying conditions, Marguerite and her friends depict a cruel and senseless world where treachery is standard and people's lives and reputations are always at stake. Does this reflect the changes brought about by religious ferment? The impasse that feudal notions of power and class had come to? Other cultural and economic uncertainties? Whatever the source, the sense of a culture in conflict is marked. And neither is there any countervailing sense of peace and beauty in the natural landscape—the storytellers are lost in the wilds; at most, they can refresh themselves in a meadow of grass that is hardly described. The impression that The Decameron leaves of being an inexhaustible treasure of life's variety gives way to the sense in The Heptameron of returning over and over to the same few dilemmas without hope of resolving them. And yet, The Heptameron seems a sincere and in some ways innocent work in which the storytellers survey their world as straightforwardly as they can, themselves unaware of the overall effect of their efforts. Out of its contradictions grow some of the most interesting and fertile questions in all of subsequent European prose literature.

面对黑死病，薄伽丘构建了一幅截然不同的图景：美、德、友谊和宽恕，恐惧和悲剧被真诚的快乐和人与人之间的真挚情感所抵消。两百年后，在看似不那么严峻的环境下，玛格丽特和她的朋友们描绘了一个残酷无情的世界，背叛司空见惯，人们的生命和名誉时刻岌岌可危。这是否反映了宗教动荡带来的变革？封建权力与阶级观念的僵局？还是其他文化和经济上的不确定性？无论根源何在，冲突的文化氛围都清晰可见。自然景观中也丝毫没有与之抗衡的宁静与美好——故事讲述者迷失在荒野之中；他们最多只能在一片几乎没有描述的草地上稍作休憩。《十日谈》给人留下的取之不尽、用之不竭的生活百态印象，在《七日谈》中却被一种感觉所取代：故事一遍又一遍地回到那几个看似无解的困境，却始终没有找到解决之道。然而，《七日谈》似乎是一部真诚且在某种程度上天真的作品，叙述者们尽可能直白地审视着他们的世界，却并未意识到其行为的整体影响。正是从这部作品的矛盾之处，孕育出了后世欧洲散文文学中最有趣、最富启发性的问题。

7. Miguel de Cervantes Don Quijote

7. 米格尔·德·塞万提斯 堂吉诃德

VOL. 1., TRANS. BURTON RAFFEL (1605; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1999), 335 PP.

第 1 卷，伯顿·拉斐尔译（1605 年；纽约：W. W. 诺顿，1999 年重印），335 页。

The first volume of Don Quixote was published in 1605 , about fifty years after The Heptameron, Gargantua and Pantagruel ( 1532 - 64 ), and Lazarillo de Tormes. It is a truism of modern criticism that Don Quixote is the first modern novel, but the first volume seems to me more of a piece with the works of the mid-sixteenth century than is generally acknowledged. The premise of Don Quixote is that a certain genteelly impoverished gentleman, deluded by reading too many cheap chival-ric romances, takes up sword, shield, and cardboard helmet and leaves home on his aged steed, Rocinante, to live as a knight-errant. He employs a squire, Sancho Panza, and devotes himself to a local maiden (to whom he has never spoken), naming her Dulcinea. He then gets into a series of misadventures with mule drivers, goatherds, innkeepers, tragic lovers, clerics, policemen, and other passersby, always asserting against the evidence of his (and everyone else's) senses that his realistic world of Spain under the reign of Philip III is actually a storybook world of queens and castles and knights and enchantments.

《堂吉诃德》第一卷出版于1605年，比《七日谈》、《巨人传》（1532-1564）和《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》晚了大约五十年。现代批评界普遍认为《堂吉诃德》是第一部现代小说，但在我看来，第一卷与十六世纪中期的作品更为契合，而非人们通常认为的那样。《堂吉诃德》的故事梗概是：一位家境贫寒的绅士，因沉迷于廉价的骑士传奇故事而误入歧途，拿起剑、盾和纸板头盔，骑着他那匹老马罗西南特离家，开始了游侠骑士的生活。他雇佣了侍从桑丘·潘萨，并一心爱上了一位素未谋面的当地少女，给她取名为杜尔西内娅。然后，他与骡夫、牧羊人、旅店老板、悲剧恋人、神职人员、警察和其他路人发生了一系列不幸的遭遇，他总是违背自己（以及其他人）的感官体验，坚称他所处的菲利普三世统治下的西班牙的现实世界实际上是一个充满女王、城堡、骑士和魔法的童话世界。

Cervantes uses Don Quixote's delusions in several ways, and some of the best parts of the novel are his conversations with Sancho Panza, in which Sancho attempts to disabuse Quixote of his illusions and Quixote attempts to convince Sancho of their superior reality. Nevertheless, more often than not, Don Quixote earns injuries as well as ridicule in his “chivalric” endeavors. He is unhorsed and beaten up more than once, and several times gets into battles that his companions see as sources of entertainment. In the end, he more or less wins Sancho to his side—not because Sancho believes in Quixote's romantic world, but because Sancho loves his master and chooses to defend him against the doubts of others. When the two finally return to their village, and Sancho encounters his wife, he quells her doubts (partly with a subtle threat of marital force after they get home) and makes the same promises to her that Don Quixote has made to him (and that have come to nothing).

塞万提斯以多种方式运用了堂吉诃德的妄想，小说中最精彩的部分莫过于他与桑丘·潘萨的对话。在这些对话中，桑丘试图让堂吉诃德认清自己的幻想，而堂吉诃德则试图说服桑丘相信他们所描绘的现实远比幻想更加美好。然而，堂吉诃德的“骑士精神”往往伴随着伤痛和嘲笑。他不止一次被人从马上摔下来，遭到殴打，还多次卷入被同伴们视为娱乐消遣的战斗。最终，他或多或少地赢得了桑丘的信任——并非因为桑丘相信堂吉诃德的浪漫世界，而是因为桑丘爱他的主人，并选择不顾他人的质疑，维护他的尊严。当两人最终回到村庄，桑丘遇到妻子时，他打消了妻子的疑虑（部分原因是回家后以婚姻的威慑力相威胁），并向她做出了唐吉诃德对他做出的同样承诺（但这些承诺最终都落空了）。

The story of Don Quixote and Sancho Panza's travels also serves as a frame for several other stories, told them by travelers they meet upon the road, and these stories bear a striking resemblance to stories in The Decameron and The Heptameron. Don Quixote , volume i , is not a modern novel in the sense that it describes a distinct and significant transformation in the mental state of its hero. He goes out deluded and he returns home deluded; what is perhaps different is the reader's interest in and sympathy with him. Cervantes is careful to balance Quixote's comic, pathetic, and noble qualities and (rather like the two earlier works) to provide frequent commentary on his protagonist through the dialogue of the other characters.

唐吉诃德和桑丘·潘萨的游历故事也构成了一个框架，串联起他们在旅途中遇到的其他旅人讲述的几个故事，这些故事与《十日谈》和《七日谈》中的故事有着惊人的相似之处。《唐吉诃德》第一卷并非一部现代小说，因为它并没有描述主人公精神状态的显著转变。他出发时满怀幻想，回来时依然满怀幻想；或许不同之处在于读者对他的兴趣和同情。塞万提斯巧妙地平衡了唐吉诃德的滑稽、悲悯和高尚的特质，并且（与前两部作品类似）通过其他人物的对话，频繁地对主人公进行评述。

Four of the interpolated tales—Marcela's Tale; the Tale of Carde-nio, Don Fernando, and Dorotea; the Tale of Anselmo, Lothario, and Camila; and the Tale of the Veiled Woman—deal with many of the same themes and some of the same plot ideas as tales in Marguerite de Navarre's collection. As in The Heptameron , all are concerned with how a beautiful woman is supposed to negotiate her rights and obligations in a world of rapists and seducers. Marcela sets the tone when she declares that the death of her lover, Grisstomo, whom she had never encouraged, is his own fault, and that she is not to be blamed for heart-lessness or lack of mercy, since she had openly declared her financial and emotional independence from the world of men, and her beauty, which has lured him to her, is not her fault but God's gift. Soon after Marcela, Don Quixote and Sancho meet Cardenio, another disheartened lover (and fellow madman), who has been betrayed, as far as he knows, by his betrothed, Luscinda, and his best friend, Don Fernando. Not long after Cardenio tells his story, Don Quixote and Sancho meet a woman disguised as a man (when she takes off her cap, her blond hair falls to the ground), who tells the story of her betrayal. She turns out to be the seduced and abandoned betrothed of Don Fernando, Dorotea, and not long after that, the group of friends encounters Don Fernando himself and the grief-stricken Luscinda, who has only just been prevented from killing herself. Luscinda and Cardenio are reunited, Don Fernando repents and is reunited with Dorotea, and the whole group then hears the story of Anselmo, who is married to Camila, but who persuades his best friend, Lothario, to put her love and virtue to the test (somewhat similar to the last tale of The Decameron , in which Gualtieri puts his wife, Griselda, to several cruel tests to make her prove the truth of her marital vows, and very much an elaboration of Tale 47 in The Heptameron , in which friends from childhood are sundered by the husband's mortal certainty that his new wife and old friend have become lovers). The Tale of the Veiled Woman, in which the daughter of a wealthy Moor, Hadji Murad, engineers her own abduction so she can go to Spain and become a Christian, is also reminiscent of the pan-Mediterranean feel of several of Boccaccio's tales in which Christians and Muslims travel between Europe and the Islamic world because of war, piracy, or trade.

四个穿插的故事——《马塞拉的故事》、《卡德尼奥、唐·费尔南多和多萝西娅的故事》、《安塞尔莫、洛塔里奥和卡米拉的故事》以及《蒙面女子的故事》——与玛格丽特·德·纳瓦尔的短篇小说集中的故事有着许多相同的主题和部分相同的情节构思。如同《七日谈》一样，所有这些故事都关注于一位美丽的女子如何在充斥着强奸犯和诱惑者的世界里权衡自己的权利和义务。马塞拉在故事中奠定了基调，她宣称，她从未鼓励过的情人格里斯托莫的死是他咎由自取，她不应为自己的冷酷无情或缺乏怜悯而受到指责，因为她曾公开宣称自己在经济和情感上独立于男人的世界，而她吸引格里斯托莫的美貌并非她的过错，而是上帝的恩赐。马塞拉之后不久，唐吉诃德和桑丘遇到了卡德尼奥，他也是一位心灰意冷的恋人（也是个疯子），据他所知，他被未婚妻卢辛达和最好的朋友唐·费尔南多背叛了。卡德尼奥讲述完自己的遭遇后不久，唐吉诃德和桑丘又遇到了一位女扮男装的女子（她摘下帽子时，金色的长发垂落一地），她讲述了自己被背叛的经历。原来，她正是被唐·费尔南多诱骗后抛弃的未婚妻多萝西娅。不久之后，这群朋友又遇到了唐·费尔南多本人，以及悲痛欲绝的卢辛达，她刚刚被阻止自杀。卢辛达和卡德尼奥重逢，唐·费尔南多忏悔并与多萝西娅重聚，然后大家听了安塞尔莫的故事。安塞尔莫已与卡米拉结婚，但他劝说他最好的朋友洛塔里奥考验卡米拉的爱情和贞洁（这与《十日谈》的最后一个故事有些相似，在那个故事中，瓜尔蒂耶里让他的妻子格里塞尔达经历几个残酷的考验，以证明她婚姻誓言的真实性；这与《七日谈》中的第47个故事非常相似，在那个故事中，儿时的朋友因为丈夫坚信他的新婚妻子和老朋友成了情人而分道扬镳）。 《蒙面女人的故事》讲述了富有的摩尔人哈吉·穆拉德的女儿策划自己被绑架，以便前往西班牙皈依基督教的故事，也让人想起薄伽丘的几部故事中泛地中海的氛围，在这些故事中，基督徒和穆斯林因为战争、海盗或贸易而在欧洲和伊斯兰世界之间旅行。

Cervantes's frame doesn't serve him quite as well in introducing these tales, so he puts Don Quixote to sleep and lets the other characters take over for a while—neither Quixote nor Sancho have much to offer in analyzing these love themes, since Sancho is a peasant and Quixote apparently has never had relations with a woman. The tales themselves show that issues raised in the French stories are no more resolved fifty years later in the Spanish ones, though times have changed since Boccaccio—there is a moment in the story of Anselmo and Lothario where the reader can imagine Boccaccio ending the tale with a laugh, right when both Anselmo and Lothario are enjoying Camila. Boccaccio would consider cuckolding a just punishment for Anselmo's compulsive failure of trust and an attentive lover a just reward for Camila's initial resistance. And when, in the earlier tale, Don Fernando comes to his senses and accepts Dorotea as his wife, the reader can almost hear the commentary Marguerite's friends might have supplied for and against Don Fernando's rights and obligations as a lusty nobleman, for and against Dorotea's course of action after the loss of her virtue, for and against Luscinda's failure to complete the suicide she had vowed, for and against Cardenio's failure to revenge himself upon his friend. In particular, the psychology of Don Fernando's redemption would have been far more believable to Marguerite's panel of critics than to us. He does not undergo a character shift, but is merely recalled by the group to the rules and obligations of his social class (after which he can serve as the benefactor of several other characters who need pecuniary assistance, including Don Quixote, who refuses to pay his bill at the inn because no knights in books are ever required to pay bills).

塞万提斯的叙事框架在引出这些故事时并不十分有效，所以他让堂吉诃德暂时“沉睡”，让其他角色接管故事——堂吉诃德和桑丘在分析这些爱情主题方面都无能为力，因为桑丘是个农民，而堂吉诃德显然从未与女性有过任何关系。故事本身表明，法国故事中提出的问题在五十年后的西班牙故事中依然没有得到解决，尽管时代已经发生了变化——在安塞尔莫和洛塔里奥的故事中，有一个场景读者可以想象，当安塞尔莫和洛塔里奥正享受着卡米拉的欢愉时，薄伽丘会以一声笑声结束这个故事。薄伽丘会认为，戴绿帽是对安塞尔莫屡次背信弃义的惩罚，而一个体贴的情人则是对卡米拉最初抗拒的奖赏。在之前的故事中，当唐·费尔南多幡然醒悟，接受多萝西娅为妻时，读者几乎可以听到玛格丽特的朋友们对唐·费尔南多作为一位好色贵族的权利和义务、多萝西娅失贞后的行为、卢辛达未能完成自杀誓言、卡德尼奥未能向朋友复仇等问题的评论。尤其值得一提的是，唐·费尔南多的“救赎”在玛格丽特的评论家圈子里远比在我们看来更可信。他并没有经历性格上的转变，只是被这群人提醒要遵守他所属社会阶层的规则和义务（之后他便可以成为其他几个需要经济援助的角色的恩人，包括唐吉诃德——唐吉诃德拒绝支付旅店的账单，因为书中的骑士从来不需要付账）。

It is hard to say what is notably “modern” in the first volume of Don Quixote , unless it is Cervantes's own literary views, which pit the destructive lies of the popular chivalric romances against the more enlightening works of serious contemporary authors that he champions in a discussion between two priests who accompany Quixote back to his home village. But Cervantes's premise, the idea of a man trying to live a knight-errant's life in the Spain of Cervantes's day, is a simple and brilliant comic idea that reveals how different Cervantes himself considered his time to be from the medieval period. In addition, Don Quixote is a good example of the best way to write a novel—Cervantes takes a rather simple premise and follows it through its train of logic. Many brilliant works illustrate the value of intelligently pursuing a simple concept—for example, Franz Kafka's “The Metamorphosis” (man turns into a bug), Charles Dickens's A Christmas Carol (man is visited by dreams of his past, present, and future). Some concepts are so easily grasped and yet so pregnant with possibilities that they almost unfold themselves, giving the writer a visible structure within which he is free to explore ideas, character, themes, and even styles, as Cervantes does with his interpolated tales.

很难说《堂吉诃德》第一卷中哪些地方真正体现了“现代性”，除非指的是塞万提斯自身的文学观点。在两位陪同堂吉诃德返回故乡的牧师的对话中，他将当时流行的骑士传奇故事中那些具有破坏性的谎言与他所推崇的严肃当代作家的更具启迪意义的作品进行了对比。但塞万提斯的创作前提——一个男人试图在塞万提斯时代的西班牙过上游侠骑士的生活——本身就是一个简单而巧妙的喜剧构思，它揭示了塞万提斯本人对所处时代与中世纪截然不同的看法。此外，《堂吉诃德》也是小说创作的典范——塞万提斯选取了一个相对简单的前提，并沿着其逻辑脉络将其展开。许多杰出的作品都展现了巧妙地探究简单概念的价值——例如，弗朗茨·卡夫卡的《变形记》（人变成虫子）、查尔斯·狄更斯的《圣诞颂歌》（人梦见自己的过去、现在和未来）。有些概念如此易于理解，却又蕴含着如此丰富的可能性，它们几乎无需思考便能自行展开，为作家提供了一个清晰的框架，使他能够自由地探索各种想法、人物、主题乃至风格，正如塞万提斯在其穿插的故事中所做的那样。

Miguel de Cervantes Don Quijote

米格尔·德·塞万提斯 堂吉诃德

VOL 2., TRANS. BURTON RAFFEL (1615; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1999), 396 PP.

第 2 卷，伯顿·拉斐尔译（1615 年；纽约：W. W. 诺顿，1999 年重印），396 页。

Cervantes published the second volume of Don Quixote in 1615 , ten years after the first, and it is important to understand that it is a sequel, not a part of the original conception. For novelists, a novel is an experience as well as a product, and part of the experience is the post-publication fate of the novel as well as the novelist's further thoughts and feelings about the characters and the situation. After publication, the world speaks back to the novelist about what had once been his private thoughts, and in Cervantes's case, he was clearly inspired in several ways by Don Quixotes reception. Modern critics seem especially to appreciate the brilliance of Cervantes's “metafiction”—his incorporation of Quixote's response to volume i , allegedly written about him by Sidi Hamid Benengeli, into his further adventures, as well as his response to the false volume 2 , written by a literary pirate and published in the interim. These layers upon layers of embedded fictionalizing prefigure Italo Calvino or Robert Coover. When Milan Kundera says that “Don Quixote is the novel all future novels answer to,” perhaps it is this, in part, that he is referring to. And it does seem very postmodern (very post–E. M. Forster, let's say) for the novel to be so simultaneously self-referential and playful. Once again, though, I think Cervantes's accomplishment is more on the order of conceiving a simple and brilliant premise—that the reader of books has become the hero of a book—and following it out. To call Don Quixote the first modern novel misrepresents how it appeared to the author himself, which was as a book among books, part of a flourishing and much-discussed literary culture that Cervantes had opinions about, not as a precursor to books that Cervantes would never see. When an author seems to predict the future in an uncanny way, it is not because he looks forward to us as we look backward to him, but because he intuits the structure of some or many aspects of the world he is living in, and is adept at extrapolating from it.

塞万提斯于1615年出版了《堂吉诃德》第二卷，距离第一卷出版已有十年之久。重要的是要明白，它是续篇，而非最初构思的一部分。对小说家而言，小说既是一种体验，也是一种作品。这种体验的一部分，既包括小说出版后的命运，也包括小说家对书中人物和情境的进一步思考和感受。出版之后，世界会回应小说家曾经的私密想法。就塞万提斯而言，他显然从《堂吉诃德》的反响中汲取了多方面的灵感。现代评论家似乎尤其欣赏塞万提斯“元小说”的精妙之处——他将堂吉诃德对第一卷的回应（据称是西迪·哈米德·贝南杰利所写）融入到他接下来的冒险故事中，同时，他也回应了由一位文学盗版者撰写并在此期间出版的伪作《堂吉诃德》第二卷。这些层层叠叠的虚构元素预示了伊塔洛·卡尔维诺或罗伯特·库弗的风格。米兰·昆德拉曾说“《堂吉诃德》是所有后世小说的标杆”，或许他指的正是这一点。这部小说如此兼具自指性和趣味性，确实显得非常后现代（或者说，非常后E·M·福斯特式）。不过，我认为塞万提斯的成就更多地在于构思了一个简单而精妙的前提——读者已成为书中的英雄——并将其付诸实践。称《堂吉诃德》为第一部现代小说，是对作者本人理解的误解。在他眼中，《堂吉诃德》只是众多书籍中的一本，是当时蓬勃发展、备受关注的文学文化的一部分，而塞万提斯本人也对这种文化持有自己的观点。他并非预示着某些他从未见过的书籍的出现。当一位作家似乎以一种不可思议的方式预测未来时，这并不是因为他像我们回顾过去一样展望未来，而是因为他直觉地理解了他所生活的世界的某些或许多方面的结构，并且擅长从中推断。

The second volume of Don Quixote begins about a month after the first ends, when Quixote, recovered from his wounds, decides to embark upon a third tour of knight-errantry, and persuades Sancho, somewhat against his better judgment, to go with him. Cervantes introduces several significant new characters, the most important being Samson Carrasco, a local villager who is a graduate of the University of Salamanca, an educated young man. It is he who tells Quixote about the knight's new fame, but he also, more secretively, decides to cure Quixote of his madness. How to think of Don Quixote's madness and therefore how to treat him is the consistent theme of the novel, and supplies a firmer and more sophisticated story line than the adventures of the first volume.

《堂吉诃德》第二卷的故事发生在第一卷结束大约一个月后。堂吉诃德伤愈后，决定开始他的第三次游侠之旅，并说服了桑丘——尽管桑丘内心并不情愿——与他同行。塞万提斯引入了几个重要的新角色，其中最重要的是萨姆森·卡拉斯科，一位毕业于萨拉曼卡大学的当地村民，一位受过良好教育的年轻人。正是他告诉堂吉诃德这位骑士的新名声，同时，他也暗中决定治愈堂吉诃德的疯狂。如何看待堂吉诃德的疯狂，以及因此而如何治疗他，是贯穿整部小说的主题，也为这部小说构建了一个比第一卷冒险故事更加严谨、更加复杂的故事情节。

Don Quixote and Sancho get farther from home than in the first volume, and their adventures have a metaphysical flavor. At one point Quixote sends Sancho to report his lovesickness to Dulcinea. Sancho goes to her village but can't find her, so when he returns, he lies, and says he did see her. Later, when the two of them go to her village to find her, Sancho, covering for the fact that he doesn't know what she looks like (and Don Quixote doesn't know, either), identifies her as one of three peasant girls they encounter as they near the village. Don Quixote is disappointed and upset at the girl's coarseness. He decides she's been enchanted, and for the duration of the novel eagerly seeks the means of her disenchantment. The longest section of the second volume concerns Don Quixote's tormenting at the hands of a duke and duchess he and Sancho encounter hunting in a woodland. The noble pair are familiar with the first volume of Don Quixote's story, and after they realize who he is, they contrive to make him and Sancho the butts of a series of elaborate theatrical jokes. At the end of the episode of the duke and duchess, both Quixote and Sancho have changed. Sancho is no longer interested in the perquisites of governing, but is eager to get back to his village and his family; Don Quixote has lost a measure of his energy. Not long afterward, he is unhorsed by another knight and forced to acknowledge the beauty of that knight's lady, which he finds fatally disheartening.

唐吉诃德和桑丘在第二卷中比第一卷走得更远，他们的冒险也带上了几分玄妙的色彩。有一次，唐吉诃德让桑丘去向杜尔西内娅诉说他的相思之苦。桑丘去了杜尔西内娅的村子，却没找到她。回来后，他撒谎说自己见过她。后来，两人再次前往杜尔西内娅的村子寻找她时，桑丘为了掩饰自己不知道她长什么样（唐吉诃德也不知道），谎称她是他们在村子附近遇到的三个农家女孩之一。唐吉诃德对女孩的粗俗感到失望和恼火。他认定女孩中了邪，并在整部小说中竭力寻找解除她魔法的方法。第二卷中最长的篇幅讲述了唐吉诃德和桑丘在林中狩猎时，被一对公爵夫妇折磨的故事。这对贵族夫妇熟知《堂吉诃德》的第一卷，在认出他的身份后，便精心策划了一系列戏谑的闹剧，让堂吉诃德和桑丘成为笑柄。在公爵和公爵夫人的故事结束后，堂吉诃德和桑丘都发生了变化。桑丘不再对统治的特权感兴趣，而是渴望回到自己的村庄和家人身边；堂吉诃德则失去了往日的活力。不久之后，他被另一位骑士从马上摔了下来，被迫承认那位骑士夫人的美貌，这令他心灰意冷，痛苦不堪。

Quixote does return home, and with another plan, but he soon falls ill, and just as he regains his sanity long enough to repudiate knighthood and his books of chivalry once and for all, he makes his will and dies.

堂吉诃德回到了家，并制定了另一个计划，但他很快就病倒了，正当他恢复了理智，准备彻底放弃骑士精神和骑士小说时，他立下了遗嘱，然后去世了。

In the first volume, Quixote's adventures are pure expressions of his delusions—he mistakes windmills for giants and an inn for a castle, for example. Those he meets have simple reactions to his delusional actions—they defend themselves against him with greater or lesser vigor. The narrator relates and the reader witnesses his adventures. The interpenetration of points of view is far more complex in the second volume. In the first place, Sancho and Quixote are made self-conscious by the knowledge that not one but two books have been written about them, one false and one true, so they become alert not only to what they are doing but also to whether those they meet have heard of them. Frequently those they meet have heard of them, which adds another layer of consciousness to the narrative. Some of those they meet—not only the duke and duchess—want to manipulate them so they can further witness the revelation of their characters (which, in both cases, are drawn from literary sources—Don Quixote makes constant reference to his books about knights, and Sancho is constantly spouting proverbs, that is, constantly setting his actions and thoughts into a traditional, commonsense frame of reference). The adventures of the second volume are more numerous and less broad, and most of them take place among a better class of people than the mule drivers and innkeepers of the first volume. As a result, there is a greater emphasis on interpretation and a smaller emphasis on action. The second volume is vastly more literary than the first.

在第一卷中，堂吉诃德的冒险经历纯粹是他妄想的体现——例如，他把风车错认成巨人，把客栈错认成城堡。他遇到的人们对他的妄想行为的反应也很简单——他们或多或少地奋力反抗。叙述者讲述着他的冒险经历，而读者则亲眼目睹。到了第二卷，视角交织的叙述方式则复杂得多。首先，桑丘和堂吉诃德意识到，关于他们的事迹已被写成两本书，一本是虚构的，一本是真实的，这让他们变得格外警觉，不仅注意自己的一举一动，也留意遇到的人是否听说过他们。他们遇到的人往往都听说过他们，这又为叙事增添了一层意识层面。他们遇到的一些人——不仅仅是公爵和公爵夫人——都想利用他们，以便更深入地了解他们的性格（这两种性格都取材于文学作品——堂吉诃德不断提及他的骑士小说，桑丘则不断引用谚语，也就是说，他不断地将自己的行为和思想置于传统的、常识性的框架之中）。第二卷的冒险故事更多，但规模更小，而且大多数故事都发生在比第一卷中的骡夫和客栈老板阶层更高的人群中。因此，第二卷更注重诠释，而较少关注情节发展。第二卷的文学性远胜于第一卷。

In addition, Cervantes is more sophisticated in the manner in which he interpolates his tales. He is still interested, for example, in seduction, in the position of girls and women in contemporary Spain, and in the Moors, but instead of putting Don Quixote to sleep so tales can be told, he incorporates them into Don Quixote's adventures or into the tricks played upon him—he knows his protagonist better and is more able to depict his reactions. And his protagonist is more complex. Don Quixote and Sancho have a great deal of discussion in volume two. This cannot help but enrich both the reader's and the author's sense of what Don Quixote and Sancho are like, and equip the author with greater and greater insight into his characters—one of the miracles of the novel is the way characters are developed and revealed at the same time. That is the illusion of roundness—that a sequence of words/ images is pointing out what is already present in a character, when in fact those things seemingly being pointed out are really ideas that, possibly, the author has never thought of before. If Cervantes's first volume is a sometimes awkward step away from The Heptameron and Lazarillo de Tormes toward the second volume, the second volume is a more assured step away from the first toward the modern novel, wherein every episode fills in the psychology of the characters until the reader comes to feel what Forster talks about in Aspects of the Novel , that she knows these beings far better and more intimately than she knows any real person.

此外，塞万提斯在穿插故事的方式上也更加老练。例如，他仍然对诱惑、当代西班牙女性的地位以及摩尔人感兴趣，但他不再让堂吉诃德沉睡以便讲述故事，而是将这些元素融入堂吉诃德的冒险经历或他所遭遇的诡计之中——他对笔下的主人公更加了解，也更能刻画他的反应。而且，他的主人公也更加复杂。在第二卷中，堂吉诃德和桑丘进行了大量的对话。这无疑丰富了读者和作者对堂吉诃德和桑丘的理解，也使作者对笔下的人物有了更深刻的洞察——这部小说的奇妙之处之一就在于人物的塑造和展现。这就是圆满的错觉——一系列文字/意象似乎在指出人物身上已有的特质，而实际上，这些看似被指出的特质，或许是作者从未想过的想法。如果说塞万提斯的第一卷是从《七日谈》和《托尔梅斯的拉撒路》向第二卷略显生涩的过渡，那么第二卷则是从第一卷向现代小说更为自信的转变。在现代小说中，每一章都细致地刻画着人物的心理，直到读者最终感受到福斯特在《小说面面观》中所描述的那种感觉：她对这些人物的了解，远胜于对任何真实人物的了解。

Don Quixote and Sancho are beloved characters because they are not perfect. It is never to be decided whether Quixote is wise or mad, whether Sancho is intelligent or foolish. Their looks and talents and states of mind are secondary to their moral qualities—they are kind, upright, chaste, and affectionate toward one another. They have moods and intentions and desires. In the second volume, they achieve depth of character in both the literary sense—complexity—and in the common usage of the term—integrity. They are tested by events, they are tested by people they meet, they are tested by one another. A more integrated, less episodic plot would involve Quixote and Sancho in a world quite removed from the reader's. As it is, we come to feel close to them, in part because we are the only witnesses to everything that happens to them.

堂吉诃德和桑丘之所以深受喜爱，正是因为他们并不完美。我们永远无法断定堂吉诃德是智者还是疯子，桑丘是聪明还是愚笨。他们的外貌、才华和心境都远不及他们的道德品质重要——他们善良、正直、贞洁，彼此深爱。他们有自己的情绪、意图和欲望。在第二卷中，他们的性格得到了充分的展现，既体现在文学意义上的复杂性，也体现在日常用语中的正直。他们经受着各种事件的考验，经受着所遇之人的考验，也经受着彼此的考验。如果情节更加连贯，减少片段式的叙述，堂吉诃德和桑丘的世界就会与读者的世界截然不同。但正因为如此，我们才能与他们产生亲近感，部分原因在于我们是他们所有经历的唯一见证者。

8. Madame de La Fayette The Princess of Cléves

8. 克莱夫王妃拉斐特夫人

TRANS. WALTER J. COBB, ED. NANCY K. MILLER
沃尔特·J·科布译，南希·K·米勒编辑
(1678; REPR., NEW YORK: NEW AMERICAN LIBRARY, MERIDIAN, 1989), 162 PP.
(1678；重印，纽约：新美国图书馆，子午线，1989 年)，162 页。

The ten storytellers and critics of The Heptameron propose themselves a riddle that after seventy stories they cannot answer. It is stated by Parlamente (probably Marguerite herself) as follows: “Just suppose that I were able to name a lady who had been truly in love, who had been desired, pursued and wooed, and yet had remained an honest woman, victorious over her body, victorious over her love and victorious over her would be lover. Would you admit that such a thing were possible?” (p. 120 ). She then tells the story of Amador and Florida (Story 10 ), in which a faithful young man eventually attempts the rape of the woman he loves out of sheer force of desire; she resists and maintains her virtue, denying him all future access to her, but not ceasing to love him.

《七日谈》的十位故事讲述者和评论家给自己出了个谜，讲完七十个故事后，他们仍然无法解答。这个谜题由帕拉门特（很可能就是玛格丽特本人）提出如下：“假设我能说出一位真正坠入爱河的女士的名字，她曾被渴望、追求和求爱，却始终保持贞洁，战胜了自己的肉体，战胜了爱情，也战胜了那些想要追求她的人。你们会承认这种事有可能发生吗？”（第120页）。随后，她讲述了阿马多尔和弗洛里达的故事（第十个故事），故事中，一位忠诚的年轻人最终因为强烈的欲望而试图强奸他心爱的女子；她奋力抵抗，坚守贞洁，拒绝了他日后任何接近她的机会，但她对他的爱却从未停止。

Her nine listeners do not all accept her interpretation. Hircan insists that since Florida only screams, she isn't really resisting, while Oisille takes the attempted rape as evidence that Amador's love is false. All seventy stories more or less unsatisfactorily work over the same dilemma—can true love be honorable and still be satisfied? A hundred and twenty years later, Madame de La Fayette takes up the same riddle in her most famous novel and answers it more successfully, by drawing a more intricate and insightful psychological portrait of a husband and wife, Monsieur de Cléves, Madame de Cléves, and her lover, the duc de Nemours. Madame de La Fayette sets her novel in the court of Henri II, son of Franois I and nephew of Marguerite, and she also makes allusion to Marguerite's work, as a book of tales. Florida's tale becomes the tale of The Princess of Cléves. It is the first entirely successful use of the novel form.

她的九位听众并非都接受她的解读。希尔坎坚持认为，佛罗里达只是尖叫，并非真正反抗；而奥西尔则将这起未遂强奸事件视为阿马多尔的爱是虚假的证据。这七十个故事或多或少都未能令人满意地探讨了同一个难题——真爱能否既高尚又圆满？一百二十年后，拉法耶特夫人在她最著名的小说中再次探讨了同样的谜题，并通过对克莱夫夫妇及其情人内穆尔公爵更为细腻深刻的心理刻画，给出了更为成功的答案。拉法耶特夫人将小说的背景设定在弗朗索瓦一世之子、玛格丽特的侄子亨利二世的宫廷，并提及玛格丽特的作品——一本故事集。佛罗里达的故事由此演变成了《克莱夫公主》的故事。这是小说体裁首次得到完全成功的运用。

Madame de La Fayette did several things with her material that previous novelists had not done. First, she deployed her characters in order of their importance and interest, and she stuck to her deployment. She devotes most of her text to Madame de Cléves (who is about eighteen years old during the novel—the whole novel concerns the emotional lives of teenage girls and their somewhat older mates), who has the most unusual dilemma. She concentrates second upon Monsieur de Cléves, who has the second most unusual dilemma, and third upon the duc de Nemours, whose dilemma is straightforward. Around these three are ranged their relatives and patrons, who serve to promote and complicate the action and to witness and comment upon it. Their relatives and patrons are the king of France, his mistress, the queen of France, the dauphin, and the queen dauphine, Mary of Scots (Madame de La Fayette was a countess herself, so this is a ruling-class production like The Heptameron). Once she has arranged her characters according to how interesting they are, she maintains her focus upon them, not letting herself get distracted by other interesting material—as Cervantes did, for example.

拉法耶特夫人对她的素材运用有几项前人未曾尝试过的做法。首先，她按照人物的重要性和趣味性安排他们的出场顺序，并且始终坚持这一安排。她将大部分篇幅用于描写克莱夫夫人（小说中她大约十八岁——整部小说都围绕着少女及其年长同伴的情感生活展开），她面临着最为特殊的困境。其次，她着重描写克莱夫先生，他面临着第二特殊的困境；再次，她则聚焦于内穆尔公爵，他的困境则相对简单明了。围绕着这三位人物的是他们的亲戚和赞助人，这些人推动着情节的发展，使故事更加复杂，并见证和评论着这一切。他们的亲戚和赞助人包括法国国王、他的情妇、法国王后、王太子以及王后玛丽·斯图亚特（拉法耶特夫人本人也是一位伯爵夫人，因此这部小说如同《七日谈》一样，是一部统治阶级的作品）。她根据人物的趣味性对他们进行排序后，就会专注于他们，不会像塞万提斯那样被其他有趣的素材分散注意力。

Most important, she always maintains at the forefront of the narrative the questions of how the characters are experiencing their feelings and why they feel and act as they do. Consciously or unconsciously, Madame de La Fayette discovered that all actions and feelings are representable, even ones that seem unbelievable, if the novelist shows their progress step by step and makes the short connections between each step plausible. In other words, she was able to incorporate uniqueness into the context of the conventional and to do it smoothly and naturally—this is an essential function of the novel as a form. In short, The Princess of Cléves works because the author is especially good at organizing, focusing, and thinking through her material—and all of these efforts work together to propel the plot.

最重要的是，她始终将人物如何体验自身情感以及他们为何如此感受和行动的问题置于叙事的核心。无论是有意识还是无意识，拉法耶特夫人都发现，只要小说家循序渐进地展现人物的情感发展，并使各步骤之间的联系合情合理，那么所有行为和情感，即使是那些看似不可思议的，也都能被呈现出来。换句话说，她能够将独特性融入传统框架，并且做到流畅自然——这正是小说作为一种文体的重要功能。简而言之，《克莱沃公主》之所以成功，是因为作者尤其擅长组织、聚焦和深思熟虑地构思素材——而所有这些努力共同推动了情节的发展。

The Princess of Cléves beautifully illustrates the relationship between novels and gossip. The novel's setting, the French court, is a dangerously gossipy place. Power, love, influence, politics, status, war, peace, and national alliances all depend upon intrigue and shifting loyalties. Everyone at the court is alert to the body language of everyone else, and ready to infer carefully hidden feelings and then broadcast their surmises. Intimate information is a form of capital to be used in the continuous exchange of power and influence, and women play as resolutely as men. The stakes are high, as is illustrated by the death of King Henri—within hours of his death, former favorites are out, new ones have gained offices and influence, and the entire balance of power has shifted. As the ten storytellers of The Heptameron well knew, there is little room for innocence or virtue, and yet sin is a risky game. Madame de Cléves's greatest act of courage is to go among the courtiers seething with passions she can't afford to disclose in any way, and her only relief is the opportunity to leave the court in the normal course of her duties without drawing attention to herself. But the novel illustrates its debt to gossip in a couple of other ways, too. For one thing, the author interpolates several cautionary or illustrative tales, as Cervantes does, but she interpolates them with brilliant grace as gossip. They not only fit, constituting significant interaction between the characters, they also develop the themes and the plot without derailing the action. In particular, though, Madame de La Fayette's focus on her heroine's state of mind and her deft investigation of it reveal a sensibility for whom human motivation is of natural and compelling interest, both in general and in particular. Only an accomplished and astute (and compassionate) gossip could have entered into her characters as fully as she does.

《克莱沃公主》精妙地展现了小说与流言蜚语之间的关联。小说的背景设定在法国宫廷，这是一个充满危险的流言蜚语之地。权力、爱情、影响力、政治、地位、战争、和平以及国家联盟，都依赖于阴谋诡计和摇摆不定的忠诚。宫廷中的每个人都对彼此的肢体语言保持警惕，随时准备揣测他人精心隐藏的情感，并将自己的猜测公之于众。私密信息是一种资本，用于持续不断的权力与影响力交换，而女性也像男性一样积极参与其中。正如亨利国王的驾崩所揭示的那样，风险极高——在他去世后的几个小时内，昔日的宠臣纷纷落马，新的人物获得了官职和影响力，整个权力平衡发生了翻天覆地的变化。正如《七日谈》中的十位说书人所熟知的那样，天真和美德在这里几乎没有容身之地，然而罪恶却是一场充满风险的游戏。克莱夫夫人最大的勇气在于她敢于深入那些内心充满激情却又无法轻易表露的朝臣之中，而她唯一的慰藉便是能够按部就班地离开宫廷，不引起任何人的注意。但这部小说对八卦的借鉴还体现在其他几个方面。首先，作者像塞万提斯一样，穿插了一些警世或寓意深刻的故事，但她巧妙地将它们融入八卦之中，展现出一种精妙绝伦的笔触。这些故事不仅与情节契合，构成了人物之间重要的互动，而且还推动了主题和情节的发展，而没有偏离故事主线。尤其值得一提的是，拉法耶特夫人对女主人公内心世界的关注以及她对这种状态的精妙探究，展现出一种对人性动机的敏锐洞察力，无论从普遍层面还是具体层面来看，这都具有天然的吸引力。只有一位技艺精湛、洞察力敏锐（且富有同情心）的八卦高手，才能像她那样将人物刻画得如此淋漓尽致。

Madame de La Fayette was proud of her depiction of life as it had been lived 120 years before her time. She was proud that she got her facts and her history straight while seamlessly introducing her fictional couple, and no one has seriously questioned that she did so. Nevertheless, a comparison of The Princess of Cléves and The Heptameron shows that something changed in those 120 years that enabled the author to see both her characters and her form in a more modern way. Marguerite and her friends cannot quite make sense of the true stories they tell—they don't quite understand what love and virtue are, and even though they go over the same material time and again, they cannot make the two fit. There are no happy endings. Rapes, deaths, imprisonments, and other cruelties abound, and explicit religious practice does little to console the characters or brighten their depiction of the world around them. What Madame de Cléves dares to do both times she is in a crisis (when she confesses to her husband that she loves someone else, and when she confesses to the duc de Nemours that she loves him but cannot marry him) is to be honest and, against her better judgment and that of everyone she knows, to trust the men who say they love her. In other words, she expresses true love and faith—and her inner life—in a way that contradicts notions of love and faith that are conventions of the period (passion, ardor, physical attraction). The two men are astounded at how much more they love her even though she has not given them what they want, but she has given them something far more rare (as they know instinctively) and asked them to give her something equally rare—the right to her own feelings. While the characters of The Princess of Cléves do not deem themselves happy at the end of the novel, each of them achieves peace—the Princess through the active pursuit of higher thoughts, Nemours through the passage of time, and Monsieur de Cléves through learning the truth about his wife's virtue. The reader, though, has a very happy ending when the princess anatomizes the idea of courtly love and lays it to rest forever.

拉法耶特夫人对她笔下描绘的120年前的生活感到自豪。她为自己既能准确把握史实，又能巧妙地将虚构的人物自然地融入故事而感到骄傲，也从未有人质疑过她是否做到了这一点。然而，对比《克莱沃公主》和《七日谈》便可知，这120年间发生了一些变化，使得作者能够以更为现代的视角审视笔下的人物和作品形式。玛格丽特和她的朋友们无法完全理解他们讲述的真实故事——他们并不真正理解爱与美德的本质，即便反复探讨相同的主题，也无法将二者融为一体。故事中没有圆满的结局。强奸、死亡、监禁和其他种种暴行比比皆是，而宗教仪式也丝毫未能抚慰人物的心灵，更无法改变他们对周遭世界的认知。克莱夫夫人两次身处危机（一次是向丈夫坦白自己爱上了别人，另一次是向内穆尔公爵坦白自己爱他却无法嫁给他）都敢于坦诚，并且违背自己和所有认识她的人的意愿，选择相信那些声称爱她的男人。换句话说，她以一种与当时传统爱情观念（激情、热恋、肉体吸引）截然不同的方式，表达了真爱、信仰以及她内心的世界。两位男士惊讶于她并没有满足他们的愿望，反而给予了他们更为珍贵的东西（他们凭直觉就能感受到），并请求他们给予她同样珍贵的东西——她拥有自己情感的权利。尽管《克莱沃公主》中的人物在小说结尾都不认为自己幸福，但他们最终都获得了内心的平静——公主通过积极追求更高层次的思想而获得，内穆尔通过时间的流逝而获得，克莱沃先生则通过了解妻子贞洁的真相而获得。然而，当公主彻底剖析宫廷爱情的本质并将其永远埋葬时，读者却迎来了一个非常美好的结局。

The modern reader looks for a novel that is irresistibly involving. Though perhaps not the novel's greatest virtue, this is its greatest appeal, a bonus that detaches, calms, and relaxes the reader's mind, no matter how agitating the subject matter—thus the paradox that very disturbing material can be “loved” by millions of readers. The early works we have read so far, while worthy and sometimes great, have not been consistently involving. What Madame de La Fayette succeeded in doing was to take traditional material and use the natural tools of the novel to make something new of it. She had an inherently interesting story; she ably depicted both the individual characters and their social milieu; she organized her material so it progresses relentlessly but not predictably; she thought through her themes, researched her setting, had compassion for her characters. Best of all, though, she successfully negotiated the most important aspect of the novel form— the manner in which an individual character distinguishes herself or himself from his world while acknowledging the pressure to conform. As a result, The Princess of Cléves is not only worthy, or even great, it is a page-turner, and a modern novel, too.

现代读者追求的是引人入胜的小说。虽然这或许并非小说的最大优点，却是其最大的魅力所在，它能让读者超脱尘世，平静下来，放松身心，无论题材多么令人不安——因此，即便题材令人不安，也能被数百万读者“喜爱”，这便构成了一种悖论。我们迄今为止读过的早期作品，虽然不乏佳作，有时甚至堪称伟大，但却并非始终引人入胜。拉法耶特夫人的成功之处在于，她运用传统题材，并巧妙地运用小说的固有技巧，将其转化为全新的作品。她构思了一个引人入胜的故事；她出色地刻画了人物及其所处的社会环境；她巧妙地组织情节，使其推进紧凑却又出人意料；她深思熟虑地构思主题，研究背景，并对笔下的人物充满同情。然而，最重要的是，她成功地驾驭了小说形式中最重要的一环——如何在承认自身所处环境的压力的同时，又能将自身与世界区分开来。因此，《克莱夫公主》不仅值得一读，甚至堪称伟大，而且引人入胜，也是一部现代小说。

9. Aphra Behn. Oroonoko and “The Fair Jilt”

9. 阿芙拉·贝恩。《奥鲁诺科》和《美丽的弃儿》

ED. PAUL SALZMAN (1688; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1994), 45 PP.

保罗·萨尔兹曼 (1688 年；纽约：牛津大学出版社，1994 年重印)，45 页。

The novel, of course, owes equally to the romance and the history, and Don Quixote , especially the second volume, can be seen as the history of a man who took romances too much to heart. Many early novels, to distinguish themselves from romances and to stake their claim to truthfulness, present themselves as histories (and in several languages, notably French and Icelandic, the words for “history” and “story” are the same [histoire and saga , respectively]). Aphra Behn, the first woman to make a successful career as a writer in England ( 1640 – 89 ), placed her short novel Oroonoko squarely in the category of a history by attesting that she herself had known Prince Oroonoko during her stay in Surinam, and that he had related the facts of his earlier life to her himself. Various commentators over the years have used her assertions against her (there is more evidence supporting them than contradicting them) either to claim that she lied or to deny her skills as a literary artist, but claiming to be merely reporting a true story is a standard novelist's assertion, usually employed to bolster the moral and ethical claims of novels in general and for certain novels in particular. Behn had a specific polemical purpose in telling her story, which was to expose the slave trade between Africa and the New World. She could only make a splash by asserting the truthfulness of her account (many of the same issues were to come up 170 years later, with Uncle Tom's Cabin). She was well aware that her material was controversial, and it remains so, even though her novel is short, obscure, and entirely the province of academic specialists.

当然，小说既受浪漫故事的影响，也受历史的影响。《堂吉诃德》，尤其是第二卷，可以被视为一个沉迷于浪漫故事的人的自传。许多早期小说为了与浪漫故事区分开来，并标榜自身的真实性，都以历史的面目出现（在一些语言中，特别是法语和冰岛语中，“历史”和“故事”是同一个词，分别是histoire和saga）。阿芙拉·贝恩是第一位在英国获得成功写作生涯的女性（1640-1689），她将自己的短篇小说《奥鲁诺科》明确地归类为历史小说，因为她声称自己在苏里南逗留期间认识了奥鲁诺科王子，并且王子亲自向她讲述了自己早年的经历。多年来，许多评论家都曾利用贝恩的言论来攻击她（事实上，支持她言论的证据远多于反驳的证据），要么指责她撒谎，要么否定她的文学才华。然而，声称自己只是在叙述一个真实的故事，是小说家常用的说辞，通常用来强化小说整体乃至某些特定小说的道德和伦理主张。贝恩讲述这个故事有着明确的论战目的，那就是揭露非洲与新大陆之间的奴隶贸易。她只有坚持自己叙述的真实性才能引起轰动（许多类似的问题在170年后随着《汤姆叔叔的小屋》的出版而再次出现）。她很清楚自己的作品具有争议性，即便她的小说篇幅短小、晦涩难懂，且完全是学术专家的研究领域，时至今日，争议依然存在。

The history of Oroonoko is rather simple. The prince of a populous and prosperous but warlike tribe in West Africa, he falls in love with a beautiful maiden of the same tribe, Imoinda, who also is desired by his grandfather, the king, who designates her as his partner, though he is impotent. For customary reasons, Imoinda cannot thereafter become the wife of Oroonoko, but they don't forget each other, and during a ceremonial dance, she stumbles into his arms, arousing the suspicions of the grandfather, who later that evening discovers the two having a tryst. Imoinda is sold into slavery. Not long after, Oroonoko, too, ends up on a slave ship heading for the New World, as a result of the treachery of the English captain of the ship (who had invited Oroonoko onto the ship as his guest, then put him in chains). Oroonoko ends up at Aphra Behn's plantation in Surinam, where he meets up with Imoinda. Behn takes an active interest in his story and his fate. He and Imoinda are married and she becomes pregnant. They now want to buy their way out of slavery before their child is born a slave, and the English slave owners agree to allow this, but repeatedly betray their word and refuse to free the two. Oroonoko (renamed Caesar) leads a slave revolt. Thinking that he will surely die, he kills Imoinda (with her full cooperation) and then is captured. The uprising is put down; he is tortured, killed, and dismembered, stoic to the last.

奥罗诺科的故事很简单。他是西非一个人口众多、富裕但好战的部落的王子，爱上了同部落的美丽少女伊莫因达。伊莫因达也受到奥罗诺科祖父——国王的喜爱，尽管国王阳痿，仍指定她为自己的伴侣。由于习俗的原因，伊莫因达无法成为奥罗诺科的妻子，但他们彼此思念。在一次仪式舞蹈中，伊莫因达不慎跌入奥罗诺科的怀抱，引起了祖父的怀疑。当晚，祖父发现了两人幽会的情景，伊莫因达被卖为奴隶。不久之后，奥罗诺科也因为英国船长的背信弃义，登上了一艘驶往新大陆的奴隶船。船长邀请奥罗诺科上船，称他是自己的客人，却将他囚禁起来。奥罗诺科最终来到苏里南的阿芙拉·贝恩的种植园，在那里他遇到了伊莫因达。贝恩对他的故事和命运非常感兴趣。他和伊莫因达结为夫妻，伊莫因达怀了孕。他们想在孩子出生前赎身，摆脱奴隶身份。英国奴隶主同意了，但却屡次背信弃义，拒绝释放他们。奥罗诺科（改名为凯撒）领导了一场奴隶起义。他认为自己必死无疑，便杀死了伊莫因达（伊莫因达完全配合），然后被俘。起义被镇压；他遭受酷刑，被杀害并肢解，至死都保持着坚忍不拔的精神。

In fact, Oroonoko owes quite a bit to the romance. Behn clearly imagines conditions in Africa, which she has never seen, to be somewhat like conditions at an elaborate European court, where power, convention, taboo, and intrigue dictate the tragic outcome of romantic personal attachments, and the most worthwhile characters are the best looking and the highest born. Imoinda and Oroonoko conform to standard European ideas of male and female virtue—she is beautiful, loving, and submissive, and he is doughty, handsome, and virtuous. Conditions in Surinam Behn depicts with a greater sense of authenticity, and she spends some of her short narrative describing the Indian population as well as the landscape, flora, and fauna. She also alludes to the cession of Surinam to the Dutch—Oroonoko's story takes place entirely within a recognizable historical context—but Oroonoko remains a romantic hero—his uniqueness is too great and his fate too dramatic for the reader to feel that she comes to know or understand him. Behn does not use dialogue—every scene is narrated—and so Oroonoko's and Imoinda's voices are absent from the narrative (as are the voices of the English slave traders and slave owners). Behn was a dramatist and her other narratives make use of dialogue, but her technique wasn't sophisticated enough (and perhaps her polemical purpose was too great) to risk allowing Oroonoko to speak for himself (though she testifies that he speaks several languages as a result of exposure to Europeans in Africa). Undeniably, though, the tale she tells is a horrifying one; the reader doesn't have to feel a thing for Oroonoko and Imoinda as individuals to recoil at their fate. What happens to them gains power insofar as it is shown to be representative of the way slaves are treated by their English masters in Surinam (and elsewhere, of course). The treacheries and brutalities of the English have a believable idiosyncratic cast that makes the reader nod and believe.

事实上，《奥鲁诺科》很大程度上得益于浪漫主义。贝恩显然将她从未亲眼见过的非洲景象想象成类似欧洲宫廷的繁华景象：权力、习俗、禁忌和阴谋决定着浪漫爱情的悲剧结局，而最有价值的人物往往是外貌出众、出身高贵之人。伊莫因达和奥鲁诺科符合欧洲传统的男女美德观念——她美丽、温柔、顺从；他勇敢、英俊、正直。贝恩对苏里南的描写则更具真实感，她在短篇小说中用了不少篇幅来描述当地的印第安人以及风景、动植物。她还暗示了苏里南割让给荷兰的历史——奥鲁诺科的故事完全发生在一个可辨识的历史背景下——但奥鲁诺科仍然是一个浪漫的英雄——他的独特性和命运的悲剧性太过突出，以至于读者难以真正了解或理解他。贝恩没有使用对话——每个场景都是叙述性的——因此，奥鲁诺科和伊莫因达的声音在叙事中缺席（英国奴隶贩子和奴隶主的声音也同样缺席）。贝恩是一位剧作家，她的其他叙事作品都运用了对话，但她的技巧还不够娴熟（或许是因为她论战的目的过于强烈），不敢冒险让奥鲁诺科自己发声（尽管她证实，由于在非洲接触过欧洲人，他会说几种语言）。然而，不可否认的是，她讲述的故事令人毛骨悚然；读者无需对奥鲁诺科和伊莫因达这两个个体产生任何同情，也会对他们的命运感到震惊。他们的遭遇之所以如此震撼人心，是因为它展现了奴隶在苏里南（当然也包括其他地方）遭受英国主人虐待的普遍方式。英国人的背信弃义和残暴行径具有令人信服的独特色彩，让读者不禁点头称是。

“The Fair Jilt” is a more traditional tale, and is in fact reminiscent of some of the darker tales of The Decameron. Miranda, a wealthy young woman who has lost her parents, is beautiful but secretly promiscuous. Her first victim is a young man who has gone into the Franciscan order because his brother has stolen his beloved and married her. Miranda throws herself at him, then accuses him of rape when he rejects her advances. He is put in prison. She then falls for Tarquin, who may or may not be the wealthy pretender to the throne of the Roman Empire. He truly loves her, in spite of her evil nature, and they collude to rob her younger sister of her half of the family fortune by twice attempting to kill her so the money will revert to Miranda. Tarquin is tried and set to be beheaded, but the executioner misses his aim, and Tarquin is saved, only to demonstrate when he revives that he still loves Miranda, evil though she may be. Through various legal maneuvers they are preserved from execution (though now impoverished) and they learn their lesson, going off to live peacefully together until they die of old age. Miranda's first victim is redeemed and released triumphantly from prison as well. Behn doesn't fully explore the moral implications of this outcome or Miranda's transformation. Like Boccaccio, Behn accepts the existence of evil people. She is less interested in their moral improvement than she is in their adventures and their effect on those around them. She is not a psychological novelist as her near-contemporary Madame de La Fayette is, because Behn is more interested in actions than in reasons, or even in plausibility. That people act and how these actions affect others are as far as she goes. But Behn's work is worth reading not only for historical interest but also because she had an eye for what you might call the wonders of life. She was drawn to strong drama and didn't shrink from depicting violence and treachery, nor from expressing “feminine” feelings and thoughts about it. Her work is unusually bold and sometimes startlingly frank.

《美貌的荡妇》是一个较为传统的故事，实际上与《十日谈》中一些较为阴暗的故事颇为相似。米兰达是一位家境富裕的年轻女子，父母双亡，她容貌姣好，却暗地里放荡不羁。她的第一个受害者是一位年轻男子，他因为哥哥抢走了心爱的女子并娶了她而加入了方济各会。米兰达主动接近他，却在他拒绝后诬告他强奸。他因此锒铛入狱。之后，她又爱上了塔奎因，此人或许是罗马帝国的王位觊觎者，也或许不是。尽管她本性邪恶，塔奎因依然深爱着她。两人合谋，两次试图谋害米兰达的妹妹，企图夺取她应得的一半家产，以便将钱财归米兰达所有。塔奎因受审并被判处斩首，但刽子手失手，塔奎因侥幸生还。复活后，他再次证明自己依然深爱着米兰达，即便她邪恶至极。通过各种法律手段，他们免于死刑（尽管如今已家道中落），并吸取了教训，从此过上了平静的生活，直至寿终正寝。米兰达的第一个受害者也得到了救赎，并凯旋出狱。贝恩并没有深入探讨这一结局的道德意义，也没有深入探讨米兰达的转变。与薄伽丘一样，贝恩也承认恶人的存在。她更关注的是恶人的冒险经历及其对周围人的影响，而不是他们的道德转变。她不像同时代的拉法耶特夫人那样是一位心理小说家，因为贝恩更关注行为本身，而非动机，甚至也并非出于合情合理。她笔下的人物行为以及这些行为如何影响他人，仅止于此。但贝恩的作品值得一读，不仅因为其历史价值，更因为她敏锐地捕捉到了生活中的种种奇妙之处。她钟情于扣人心弦的戏剧，从不回避描绘暴力和背叛，也从不回避表达女性对此的感受和思考。她的作品风格异常大胆，有时甚至坦率得令人震惊。

10. Daniel Defoe. Robinson Crusoe

10. 丹尼尔·笛福，《鲁滨逊漂流记》

(1719; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, MODERN LIBRARY, 2001), 282 PP.

（1719 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，现代文库，2001 年），282 页。

Daniel Defoe was the son of Nonconformists, a merchant, and an active writer and pamphleteer—possibly the most prolific English writer ever. His father was a tallow chandler and his mother was from a family with some connections to the gentry. He lived a very active life—he was briefly the captive of pirates, he went bankrupt several times, he served in the army of William of Orange, he was pilloried and repeatedly arrested for subversive pamphleteering, and he saw his work become both famous and notorious. He started writing novels at fifty-nine, and after his major novels, he published The Complete English Tradesman, An Essay on the History and Reality of Apparitions, A New Family Instructor , and The Complete English Gentleman , among other titles. In other words, Defoe was a certain type of active, hardheaded English Protestant businessman, and his novels consistently reflect his interest in survival, money, trade, and enterprise in general. His protagonists must make their way in the world, often against very difficult conditions, and all the while they are doing so, they reflect on the moral, religious, and personal meaning of their efforts.

丹尼尔·笛福出生于一个非国教徒家庭，父亲是商人，他本人则是一位活跃的作家和小册子作家——或许是英国历史上最多产的作家。他的父亲是蜡烛商，母亲则出身于一个与乡绅阶层略有联系的家庭。他的一生可谓丰富多彩：曾短暂被海盗俘虏，数次破产，在奥兰治亲王威廉的军队中服役，因发表颠覆性小册子而被示众并多次被捕，他的作品也因此声名鹊起，但也饱受争议。他五十九岁开始创作小说，在主要小说之后，他还出版了《英国商人全书》、《论幻象的历史与现实》、《新家庭指南》和《英国绅士全书》等作品。换句话说，笛福是一位典型的活跃、精明的英国新教商人，他的小说也始终反映出他对生存、金钱、贸易和商业等主题的关注。他的主人公必须在世上闯出一片天地，常常要面对非常艰难的条件，而在此过程中，他们一直在思考自己努力的道德、宗教和个人意义。

Robinson Crusoe has enormous appeal, in part because it is so simple a story (it was based on the actual experiences of a man named Alexander Selkirk, who published a book in 1712 about his experiences living alone for more than four years on an island off the coast of Chile). A young man goes off to sea against the wishes of his family. After several adventures, he is cast away on a deserted island near South America. Between the provisions he gets from the wrecked ship and the natural resources of the island, he puts together what might even be called a prosperous and satisfying life for nearly thirty years, at which point he is discovered and given passage back to civilization.
