《鲁滨逊漂流记》之所以如此吸引人，部分原因在于它的故事非常简单（它取材于亚历山大·塞尔柯克的真实经历，塞尔柯克于1712年出版了一本书，讲述了他独自在智利海岸附近的一个岛屿上生活四年多的经历）。一个年轻人不顾家人的反对，出海远航。经历了一系列冒险之后，他被困在南美洲附近的一个荒岛上。凭借从沉船上获得的补给和岛上的自然资源，他在那里过上了近三十年堪称富足而充实的生活，直到他被发现并被送回文明世界。

The evidence of Defoe's writings both before and after his novels is that he was interested above all in practical matters—how to conduct trade, how to raise a family, how to be a gentleman—and Robinson Crusoe is only a single step away from these volumes—and how to survive. How-to manuals are good models for novels. They exemplify completeness, for one thing. One of the signal charms of Robinson Crusoe is this very sense—that Defoe has anticipated any ideas that the reader might have about Crusoe's geographical, ecological, social, spiritual, physical, and mental situation—and answered the reader's questions before they are formed. Crusoe seems to live in a natural, tangible, physical world, exotic but knowable. Out of necessity, Crusoe approaches his world with investigative openness, and as a result of his investigations, his island becomes real, not at all phantasmagorical. In addition, “how-to” in a novel always yields “who”—the manner in which a character goes about his task reveals his uniqueness. This is the most essential mark of narrative for a very simple reason: the story must progress. Each idiosyncratic action progresses the story but at the same time distinguishes the protagonist not only from those around him (or her) but also from the reader and other individuals the reader knows or has read about. A novel cannot tarry too long with the meaning of events, because meaning is usually experienced as either revelation or instruction. Revelation is by nature momentary, and instruction is by nature not very entertaining. Beads of meaning, therefore, tend to be strung along a wire of actions. Thus individuality, meaning, and action (which may coalesce more formally into plot) are inextricably mixed in the form of the novel and dissolved in the further idiosyncrasy of the narrative voice.

笛福在创作小说之前和之后的作品都表明，他最感兴趣的是实际问题——如何经商、如何养家糊口、如何做一个绅士——而《鲁滨逊漂流记》与这些作品仅一步之遥——以及如何生存。实用指南是小说的绝佳范例。首先，它们体现了完整性。《鲁滨逊漂流记》最引人入胜之处就在于此——笛福似乎早已预料到读者可能对鲁滨逊的地理、生态、社会、精神、身体和心理状况产生的任何想法——并在读者产生疑问之前就解答了这些疑问。鲁滨逊似乎生活在一个自然、真实、物质的世界中，既充满异域风情又触手可及。出于生存的需要，鲁滨逊以探索的开放心态去了解他的世界，而正是通过他的探索，他的岛屿变得真实可信，而非虚幻缥缈。此外，小说中的“如何做”总是会引出“谁”——人物完成任务的方式揭示了他的独特性。这是叙事最本质的特征，原因很简单：故事必须推进。每一个独特的行动都推动着故事发展，同时也使主人公不仅与周围的人（或她）区分开来，也与读者以及读者认识或读过的其他人物区分开来。小说不能在事件的意义上停留太久，因为意义通常以启示或教诲的形式呈现。启示本质上是短暂的，而教诲本质上并不引人入胜。因此，意义的珠子往往串在一系列行动的线索上。由此，个性、意义和行动（它们可能更正式地融合为情节）在小说的形式中密不可分地交织在一起，并最终消融于叙述声音的独特性之中。

Crusoe, like other Defoe narrators, has a very winning voice: he is practical, concrete, self-effacing, honest. He seems to address the reader both respectfully and modestly. He offers no excuses for bad judgment or misbehavior; he questions his own motives; he both reflects about events and gets on with his tale. More important, there is nothing odd about him. By contrast to narrators with a more vivid style, he does not seem to be using eloquence to make a case for neurosis, obsession, or any other strange mental condition. He is an average guy, trying to get by, to maintain a good conscience, to do the right thing, to observe himself. He is telling his tale because it is interesting in itself, not because he is remarkable—when it turns out that he is remarkable, that is the reader's observation, not Crusoe's.

克鲁索和其他笛福笔下的叙述者一样，有着极具感染力的叙述风格：他务实、具体、谦逊、诚实。他似乎以既尊重又谦逊的态度与读者交流。他从不为自己的判断失误或不当行为辩解；他会反思自己的动机；他既会反思过往的事件，也会继续讲述自己的故事。更重要的是，他身上没有任何怪异之处。与那些文风更为生动的叙述者不同，他似乎并没有用雄辩的言辞来证明自己患有神经症、强迫症或其他任何奇怪的精神疾病。他只是一个普通人，努力生活，努力保持良心，努力做正确的事，努力反省自己。他讲述自己的故事，是因为故事本身就引人入胜，而不是因为他有什么非凡之处——当读者最终发现他确实非凡时，那是读者的观察，而不是克鲁索的。

Like Aphra Behn, Defoe takes up the theme of European colonialism. He is somewhat more comfortable with its cruelties than Behn was, perhaps because he is a practical man. The most telling incident with regard to this is when the young Crusoe is captured and enslaved off the coast of Africa. He sees enslavement as a universal risk—to be captured in a strange land is to be enslaved, whether the captive is white, black, or brown. Escape is necessary and natural, though dangerous. Likewise, when he first sees the cannibals on his island, Crusoe observes that the men the cannibals eat have only one common characteristic: they are captives. Those who get eaten could just as well be the eaters, had the battle gone the other way. When Crusoe rescues and educates Friday, he observes that Friday has a taste for human flesh that he should overcome, but he doesn't condemn him for having that taste, he communicates to him that such a taste is anathema to both himself—Crusoe, Friday's rescuer—and to God, whom Crusoe sincerely professes. At the same time, Crusoe worries about whether he should attempt to kill or harm the cannibals, because even though their habits are repulsive to him, they have done him no harm and are acting only in accordance with their own beliefs. For years before he actually attacks the cannibals, he worries about his moral relationship to them—always in the terms that God made them as they are, and who is he to interfere? In the end, he and Friday do attack the cannibals and rout them, but only because Friday recognizes one of the victims as his own father and Crusoe recognizes the other victim as a European. The conclusion seems to be rather modern—they may do what they do inside their own culture, but not hurt others who don't share their beliefs.

与阿芙拉·贝恩一样，笛福也探讨了欧洲殖民主义的主题。他或许比贝恩更能坦然面对殖民主义的残酷，这可能是因为他更为务实。最能说明这一点的事件莫过于年轻的克鲁索在非洲海岸被俘虏并沦为奴隶。他认为奴役是一种普遍存在的风险——无论白人、黑人还是棕色人种，在异国他乡被俘就意味着沦为奴隶。逃跑是必要且自然的，尽管充满危险。同样，当克鲁索第一次在岛上见到食人族时，他注意到食人族吃掉的人只有一个共同点：他们都是俘虏。如果战局反过来，那些被吃掉的人也可能成为吃人的人。当克鲁索救起并教导星期五时，他注意到星期五嗜食人肉，他应该克服这种嗜好。但他并没有因此谴责星期五，而是告诉他，这种嗜好不仅令他自己——救了星期五的克鲁索——深恶痛绝，也令他所信仰的上帝深恶痛绝。与此同时，克鲁索也在纠结是否应该杀死或伤害那些食人族，因为尽管他们的习俗令他作呕，但他们并没有伤害他，只是按照自己的信仰行事。在真正攻击食人族之前的几年里，他一直在思考自己与他们的道德关系——他始终认为，上帝创造了他们，他又有什么资格干涉呢？最终，他和星期五确实攻击了食人族并击溃了他们，但这仅仅是因为星期五认出其中一名受害者是自己的父亲，而克鲁索认出另一名受害者是欧洲人。结论似乎相当现代——他们或许会在自己的文化内部做他们想做的事，但不会伤害那些不认同他们信仰的人。

Robinson Crusoe is a seminal work, simple on the surface but embodying many of the complexities and contradictions of the modern world. It is hard to dislike and impossible to dismiss, yet 286 years later, after intervening centuries of genocide, exploitation, and war, it can't help making us uneasy.

《鲁滨逊漂流记》是一部开创性的作品，表面看似简单，实则蕴含着现代世界的诸多复杂性和矛盾之处。它令人难以反感，也无法被忽视，然而，286年后的今天，经历了几个世纪的种族灭绝、剥削和战争，它仍然让我们感到不安。

Daniel Defoe Roxana

丹尼尔·笛福 罗克萨娜

(1724; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1996), 330 PP.

（1724；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1996 年），330 页。

If novel-writing (and romance-writing) in France was a diversion of the aristocracy, Defoe made English novel-writing an activity of the entrepreneurial middle class, which was largely made up of Nonconformists, whose religious beliefs encouraged continual investigations of conscience. It was fine for, and even required of, Nonconformists that they work hard, live simply, and grow rich, but only in good conscience, and all of Defoe's major novels show the uneasy relationship between doing well and doing good. It is certainly no coincidence, given the preoccupation of European novelists with the condition of women's lives, that through Roxana, Defoe analyzes the relationship of womanhood to money and sex.

如果说法国的小说创作（以及浪漫小说创作）是贵族阶层的消遣，那么笛福则将英国的小说创作变成了中产阶级的一项活动。这个中产阶级大多由非国教徒组成，他们的宗教信仰促使他们不断反思自己的良知。对于非国教徒来说，努力工作、生活简朴、致富是理所当然的，甚至是必须的，但前提是必须心安理得。笛福的所有主要小说都展现了致富与行善之间令人不安的关系。考虑到欧洲小说家对女性生活状况的关注，笛福通过罗克珊娜这个人物来分析女性与金钱和性之间的关系，这绝非偶然。

The first time Roxana makes an illicit liaison, she has the best possible excuse—her husband has left her and her five starving children. In desperation, she foists her children upon the husband's wealthier relatives (the husband's sister would rather the parish take care of them, but Defoe is explicit about the hardships of the eighteenth-century welfare state). Soon afterward, Roxana's wealthy landlord begins to court her, and manages to win her by means of tact, kindness, and, of course, the goading spur of her degree of want. She is probably in her mid- to late twenties at this point, and very beautiful and desirable. Her lover, a jeweler, takes her to France, where they live in luxury for a time, until he is murdered by robbers while delivering some jewels to a princely client. The client pays a condolence visit to Roxana and falls in love with her. She is attracted by his kindness, generosity, and princely rank, and becomes his mistress for several years. He has other mistresses, but she begins to believe that she is the favorite. All along, she is having both babies and second thoughts, but she is also accumulating money, living frugally, and adding to her principal. It is this lack of sentimentality and this focus on the ways and means of prospering that supply the novel's essential charm and originality. If every novel is about how characters live and act—that is, the manner in which they do things reveals who they are—then Roxana is about how a representative beautiful woman does what most of the people in the world have to do every day of their lives—how she makes a living, how she manipulates the opportunities and accidents that life and the social system present her, how she employs intelligence, stratagem, and all other available means (looks and charm among them) to make her fortune as a courtesan, but also about what both her methods and her results mean to her, how it feels to be a woman in such circumstances. In this, Roxana is different from almost every female protagonist before her, because her survival is something she makes for herself out of mundane materials such as “bills” (the forerunner of the bank draft), interest-bearing notes, presents, china, household furnishings, and other things bought new and sold at a profit. Throughout the novel, she balances independence and feeling—after experiencing the effects of marital property laws in her first, disastrous marriage, she resists marriage for a long time in spite of her consciousness of sin.

罗克珊娜第一次出轨时，她有了一个天大的借口——丈夫抛弃了她和五个饿得奄奄一息的孩子。走投无路之下，她把孩子们托付给了丈夫家境富裕的亲戚（丈夫的妹妹更希望由教区来照顾他们，但笛福毫不掩饰地描写了十八世纪福利制度的艰辛）。不久之后，罗克珊娜富有的房东开始追求她，并凭借机智、温柔，当然还有她极度贫困的诱惑，最终赢得了她的芳心。此时她大概二十五六岁，容貌姣好，魅力十足。她的情人是一位珠宝商，他带她去了法国，两人在那里过着奢华的生活，直到他在给一位王子客户送珠宝时被劫匪杀害。这位王子前来吊唁，并爱上了罗克珊娜。她被他的善良、慷慨和王子身份所吸引，成为了他的情妇，长达数年之久。他还有其他情妇，但她开始觉得自己才是他最宠爱的。在此期间，她既生育子女，也经历着内心的挣扎，但她同时也在积攒财富，过着节俭的生活，不断增加自己的本金。正是这种不带感伤色彩的描写，以及对致富之道的关注，赋予了这部小说独特的魅力和原创性。如果说每一部小说都讲述人物如何生活和行动——也就是说，他们的行事方式揭示了他们的本质——那么《罗克珊娜》讲述的是一位典型的美丽女性如何做着世界上大多数人每天都必须做的事情：如何谋生，如何利用生活和社会制度给予她的机遇和偶然事件，如何运用智慧、计谋以及一切可用的手段（包括美貌和魅力）作为一名交际花发家致富。但小说也探讨了她的方法和结果对她而言意味着什么，以及在这种环境下作为一名女性的感受。在这一点上，罗克珊娜与她之前几乎所有的女性主人公都不同，因为她的生存完全是靠自己利用诸如“汇票”（银行汇票的前身）、计息票据、礼物、瓷器、家具以及其他新购入后转手获利的物品而实现的。在整部小说中，她都在独立和情感之间寻求平衡——在她第一次不幸的婚姻中体验了婚姻财产法的影响后，尽管她意识到自己有罪，但她仍然长期抗拒婚姻。

Eventually, though, her conscience catches up with her. Back in London, she at first continues her successes, but then, as she gets older, now possessed of some means, she decides to live even more discreetly than she had been doing, with the help of her longtime maidservant and confidante, Amy. She moves to an obscure end of town, into the house of a Quaker lady. Many years have passed since Roxana gave up her children, and her oldest daughter now reappears, threatening to expose Roxana, but also, in some way, threatening to get close to her. The daughter is done away with by the maid (there is some ambiguity here about Roxana's role in the murder), and subsequently both Roxana and the maid lose everything, though this part of the story is not detailed. The novel turns out to be Roxana's confession.

然而，最终她的良心还是谴责了她。回到伦敦后，她起初继续着她的成功，但随着年龄增长，手头也宽裕了一些，她决定比以往更加低调地生活，并得到了她多年的女仆兼知己艾米的帮助。她搬到了城里一个偏僻的角落，住进了一位贵格会教徒的家中。罗克珊娜放弃孩子已经很多年了，她的大女儿突然出现，威胁要揭露罗克珊娜的秘密，但同时，似乎也想接近她。女儿被女仆杀害（罗克珊娜在谋杀案中的角色在这里有些模糊不清），随后罗克珊娜和女仆都失去了一切，尽管故事的这一部分并没有详细描述。这部小说最终揭示了罗克珊娜的自白。

Modern readers have admired the darkness of Roxana and its psychological, sociological, and economic astuteness, but it is by no means easy to understand exactly what Defoe is getting at. On the one hand, Roxana commits sins she regrets, but her downfall is not depicted in any detail, and her pleasure in her growing knowledge of the world and its ways is depicted with substantial satisfaction. Until the arrival of her grown daughter upon the scene, it does not appear that she will suffer—she is as prudent in her personal choices as she has been in her investments. Her daughter poses a dilemma that the ruthless maidservant solves for her—Roxana is passive rather than active in the murder. I think the best interpretation of the novel is that the part of it that would interest an author of, say, 1900 —the dreadful psychological and phantasmagorical possibilities of the daughter's pursuit of her mother and the mother's guilty conscience—was not what interested the author of Robinson Crusoe, Moll Flanders , and The Complete English Tradesman. While he may have known he had a great idea, the novel itself hadn't progressed far enough for him to be able to exploit it. But nor had the theory and practice of women leading independent lives and having independent thoughts. In some sense, Roxana and Amy are good examples of characters getting out of the author's control and leading him into themes he is not prepared to fully explore. Defoe was once pilloried for his political writings. In Roxana , he is still taking risks.

现代读者赞赏罗克珊娜身上那种阴郁的气质，以及她对心理、社会和经济的敏锐洞察，但要真正理解笛福的意图绝非易事。一方面，罗克珊娜犯下了令她后悔的罪行，但她的堕落过程却鲜有细节描写，而她对世事变迁的认知不断加深所带来的愉悦感，却被描绘得淋漓尽致。直到她成年的女儿出现之前，她似乎都不会遭受任何苦难——她在个人选择上如同在投资上一样谨慎。女儿给她出了个难题，而冷酷无情的女仆替她解决了——罗克珊娜在谋杀案中是被动的，而非主动的。我认为对这部小说的最佳解读是，其中那些在1900年左右的作家会感兴趣的部分——女儿追寻母亲过程中可怕的心理创伤和幻象，以及母亲的愧疚感——并非《鲁滨逊漂流记》、《莫尔·弗兰德斯》和《英国商人全集》的作者所关注的。尽管他可能意识到自己有一个绝妙的想法，但小说本身的发展还不足以让他充分发挥。女性独立生活和独立思考的理论和实践也同样如此。从某种意义上说，罗克珊娜和艾米这两个人物很好地诠释了作者是如何摆脱控制，将他引向他尚未准备好深入探讨的主题的。笛福曾因其政治作品而饱受诟病。在《罗克珊娜》中，他依然在冒险。

# ↩

11. Samuel Richardson. Pamela; or, Virtue Rewarded

11. 塞缪尔·理查森。《帕梅拉；或，美德的回报》

(1740; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1985), 538 PP.

（1740；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1985 年），538 页。

Pamela illustrates several important features of the novel as a form as well as several turning points in the history of the English novel. Published in 1740 , it was a sensation, went into several editions, and was rewritten for the stage in the way novels are sold to Hollywood today. Richardson, who had been a printer and stationer since 1720 , published it under his own name, and writers all over London realized that they could earn money as novelists. Richardson not only followed Pamela with Clarissa , which was also a great success, and several other works, he also continued to revise and perfect Pamela until his death in 1761 at age seventy-three. The accepted modern edition is taken from the 1810 edition published by his daughters, including all of the emendations and corrections Richardson made in his lifetime.

《帕梅拉》展现了小说这一体裁的几个重要特征，以及英国小说发展史上的几个转折点。该书于1740年出版，引起轰动，多次再版，并被改编成舞台剧，就像如今小说被卖到好莱坞一样。理查森自1720年起便从事印刷和文具生意，他以自己的名字出版了这部小说，伦敦各地的作家们由此意识到，他们也可以靠写小说赚钱。理查森不仅在《帕梅拉》之后创作了同样大获成功的《克拉丽莎》和其他几部作品，而且还不断修订和完善《帕梅拉》，直至1761年去世，享年73岁。如今公认的版本取材于他女儿们于1810年出版的版本，包含了理查森生前所做的所有修订和更正。

Novels always reveal the traces of their original conception, and Pamela is a particularly good example of this. Richardson began to write a handbook of model letters in 1739 , and a sequence he wrote for this book, letters from a servant girl to her father, grew into the plot we have—a fifteen-year-old waiting maid whose employer dies. She is then pursued and preyed upon by the son, who is a wealthy and powerful member of the landed gentry. She energetically preserves her virtue even to the last extremity—after he abducts her, imprisons her, and attempts to bribe her. He attacks her in her bed while his co-conspirator, a housekeeper he has employed, holds her hands. Pamela falls into a fit, Mr. B. feels remorse, and the rest of the novel is about his reformation. He eventually marries her, and then manages to reconcile his sister and neighbors to the marriage. Depicting models was clearly on Richardson's mind, and in the end he produced not model letters but model characters engaged in model behavior— Richardson wrote for money but he also wrote to educate, and in so doing helped elevate the form of the novel to respectable status in English literature in spite of the risqu nature of the subjects he chose (Clarissa , much longer, explores abduction and rape in even greater detail).

小说总会留下最初构思的痕迹，《帕梅拉》便是最好的例证。理查森于1739年开始撰写一本范文集，他为这本书创作的一系列女仆写给父亲的信件，逐渐发展成了我们现在看到的这部小说——一位十五岁的女仆，她的雇主去世后，她遭到雇主的儿子——一位富有权势的乡绅——的追求和骚扰。她始终坚守贞洁，直至最后一刻——在她被绑架、囚禁并试图贿赂之后。他趁着同谋——一位他雇佣的女管家——抓住她的手——在床上对她施暴。帕梅拉惊恐万分，B先生感到悔恨，小说的其余部分讲述了他的悔改过程。最终，他娶了她，并设法让他的妹妹和邻居们接受了这桩婚事。理查森显然想描绘模范人物，最终他创作的不是模范信件，而是从事模范行为的模范人物——理查森写作是为了赚钱，但也是为了教育，这样做有助于提升小说在英国文学中的地位，尽管他选择的主题具有冒险性质（《克拉丽莎》篇幅更长，对绑架和强奸的描写更加详细）。

It is hard to like Pamela, because she is so obviously a Goody Two-shoes, but the reader simply cannot help getting used to her, and in the end all but the most obdurate are likely to come around, at least to accepting the principle that she deserves to get the guy, the money, and the estates, if not the adulation of everyone she meets. The reason the reader is won over is that she keeps reading, and the more she reads, the more familiar she becomes with the ins and outs of Pamela's reasoning, and in spite of all Pamela's self-praise, her reasoning is astute and complex and the reader can hardly get ahead of her. In addition, her dilemma is a significant one—Mr. B.'s attempts upon her virtue are wholehearted and unrelenting, and they are vividly portrayed. After an interval the reader may find tedious, during which he reforms himself, and Pamela's discourse is reduced to various forms of gratitude for his goodness and condescension, Mr. B.'s sister comes upon the scene and stages what is surely one of the most violent tantrums ever to grace classic literature. And then it turns out that the spoiled, willful manners of the upper classes are part of Richardson's subject matter, and the novel becomes a rather subversive piece of work. The desperation of Pamela's situation and the detail with which it is told work upon the reader's love of suspense, drawing the reader onward in spite of distaste for the tone or the characters, but then the experience itself of reading overcomes that distaste. Richardson's greatest risk—putting the novel in Pamela's voice—becomes the source of its success, because we end up feeling intimate with her in a way that third-person narration would not allow.

帕梅拉很难让人喜欢，因为她显然是个循规蹈矩的乖乖女，但读者却不由自主地习惯了她。最终，除了最顽固的读者之外，几乎所有人都可能会转变观念，至少会接受她理应得到那个男人、金钱和庄园，即便无法赢得所有人的赞美。读者之所以会被她打动，是因为她坚持读下去，读得越多，就越熟悉帕梅拉的逻辑。尽管帕梅拉自恋不已，但她的推理却精明而复杂，读者几乎无法预料她的下一步行动。此外，她面临的困境也十分重大——B先生对她贞洁的追求是全心全意、毫不留情的，而且被描绘得栩栩如生。在一段读者或许会觉得乏味的过渡期之后——在此期间，男主角改过自新，帕梅拉的话语也逐渐简化为对他的善意和居高临下的感激之情——B先生的妹妹登场，上演了一场堪称经典文学史上最激烈的暴怒之一。随后，读者会发现，上流社会被宠坏的任性举止正是理查森笔下的主题之一，小说也因此变成了一部颇具颠覆性的作品。帕梅拉的绝望处境以及对细节的详尽描写，巧妙地利用了读者对悬念的喜爱，即便读者对小说的基调或人物感到反感，也会被吸引着继续读下去。然而，阅读本身的体验最终会克服这种反感。理查森最大的冒险——采用帕梅拉的视角叙述——反而成就了小说的成功，因为我们最终与她产生了一种亲密感，这是第三人称叙述所无法实现的。

Richardson, like Defoe, was born into the artisan class, and he had the same respect as Defoe for hard work, enterprising spirit, self-worth grounded in religious belief, and independent thought. Like Defoe, he was not classically educated, and he had an outsider's view of the gentry. In the last quarter of the novel, when Mr. B. explains why he had never wanted to get married, Richardson shows a good understanding of developmental psychology, marital relations, and class consciousness. The way marriage is supposed to be—the wife obedient, the husband responsible, duties shared, and respect evident on both sides—is contrasted with the way marriage usually is: “the yawning husband, and the vapourish wife, are truly insupportable to one another; but separate, have freer spirits, and can be tolerable company” (p. 464 ). Richardson also believed in economic self-improvement— doing good and doing well. Like Defoe, he had a taste for psychology that grew out of the requirement that Nonconformists search their souls, and lives, for evidence of God's grace—right thinking and right acting would be rewarded by prosperity as well as ease of conscience. This is not the only way for an author to develop psychological understanding, but it does cause him to ruminate upon trains of cause and effect—how actions and psychology work together through time to create a character's fate (and build a plot). It is not that character is destiny, but that choices are destiny. Both Pamela and Roxana reflect constantly upon the consequences of wrong and right choices, in this world and in the hereafter. They do not consider Fate, for example, and so instead of illustrating, let's say, the workings of a tragic flaw, they model how to get through the day or the week. There is no tragic flaw—each choice that comes up offers the renewed chance of either salvation or damnation. This religion of the middle class, the self-made protagonist, stands in strong contrast to the pattern of aristocratic literature (notably the epic) that preceded it, in which the hero is the dupe of circumstances, and his only choice is the manner in which he meets his fate.

理查森和笛福一样，出身于工匠阶层，他们同样敬重勤劳、进取精神、根植于宗教信仰的自我价值感以及独立思考。和笛福一样，理查森也没有接受过正规教育，他对上流社会抱有局外人的视角。在小说的最后四分之一，当B先生解释他为何从未想过结婚时，理查森展现了他对发展心理学、婚姻关系和阶级意识的深刻理解。他笔下理想的婚姻——妻子顺从，丈夫负责，夫妻双方共同承担责任，彼此尊重——与现实婚姻形成了鲜明的对比：“打哈欠的丈夫和精神萎靡的妻子，彼此实在难以忍受；但如果分开，他们就能拥有更自由的精神，也能成为彼此可以相处的伴侣”（第464页）。理查森也相信经济上的自我提升——既要行善，也要有所成就。和笛福一样，他对心理学的兴趣源于非国教徒必须审视自己的灵魂和生活，寻找上帝恩典的证据——正确的思想和行为会得到丰厚的回报，以及良心的安宁。这并非作家发展心理学理解的唯一途径，但它确实促使他思考因果关系——行动和心理如何随着时间的推移相互作用，塑造人物的命运（并构建情节）。并非性格决定命运，而是选择决定命运。帕梅拉和罗克珊娜都在不断反思错误选择和正确选择在今世和来世的后果。例如，她们不考虑命运，因此，她们没有去描绘某种悲剧缺陷的运作方式，而是示范如何度过每一天或每一周。这里没有所谓的悲剧缺陷——每一个选择都提供了救赎或毁灭的全新机会。这种中产阶级的宗教，这种白手起家的主人公，与之前的贵族文学（尤其是史诗）的模式形成了鲜明的对比。在贵族文学中，英雄是环境的受害者，他唯一的选择就是如何面对自己的命运。

Novels grow, as Pamela so clearly illustrates. Richardson rewrote the novel so many times because his plot opened important and interesting themes that he continued to think about, and his thoughts (and perhaps criticisms from friends and fans) reminded him of bits of the story that could be made more plausible or smoother or funnier or clearer. This is a common event in novel-writing, though in our day and age, editors and publishers try to make sure that the novel finishes growing before it is printed. Perhaps it was not part of the author's original intention, for example, to discuss the proper education of gentlemen, and in fact for the first two-thirds of the novel, Mr. B. is an unsympathetic stick figure. It becomes clear, though, that for the sake of plausibility, he has to justify his decision to marry Pamela, and in so doing, he becomes more like her—willing to go on at length about his actions and motivations. Ostensibly he reveals himself, but in fact he is developing new facets of character as Richardson has to account for what he does.

正如帕梅拉的故事所清晰展现的那样，小说会不断发展完善。理查森反复修改这部小说，是因为他的情节引出了许多重要而有趣的主题，他不断地思考这些主题，而他的想法（或许还有来自朋友和读者的批评）让他意识到故事中某些部分可以更加合理、流畅、有趣或清晰。这在小说创作中很常见，尽管在当今时代，编辑和出版商会尽力确保小说在付印前完成所有修改。例如，探讨绅士的正确教育或许并非作者最初的意图，事实上，在小说的前三分之二，B先生只是一个令人反感的单薄人物。然而，很明显，为了使故事合理，他必须为自己娶帕梅拉的决定辩解，而在这个过程中，他变得越来越像帕梅拉——愿意详细地解释自己的行为和动机。表面上他展现了真实的自我，但实际上，随着理查森不得不为自己的所作所为负责，他正在发展出新的性格层面。

Pamela , in spite of the tradition of abduction and rape in European literature, is implausible. What is the most implausible thing changes as the plot develops. Is it more implausible that Pamela would save herself? More implausible that Mr. B. would be so unrelenting? More implausible that he would want to marry her? More implausible that she would come to love him? More implausible that she would accept his love child from an earlier liaison? Every turn of the plot is implausible, but the detailed narration of how each event takes place lays to rest the issue of implausibility. The reader wants to find out what happens, so the reader accepts and goes on. Richardson reasons, persuades, almost numbs the reader, but the evidence of Pamela's classic status shows that he does gain the reader's willing suspension of disbelief.

尽管欧洲文学中不乏绑架和强奸的题材，但《帕梅拉》这部作品本身却显得不合情理。随着情节发展，最不合情理之处也在不断变化。是帕梅拉能够自救更不合情理？是B先生如此执迷不悟更不合情理？是他想要娶她更不合情理？是她爱上他更不合情理？还是她接受他与前任所生的私生子更不合情理？情节的每一个转折都显得不合情理，但对每个事件发生过程的细致叙述却最终消除了这种不合情理的疑虑。读者渴望知道接下来会发生什么，于是接受了这种不合情理的设定，并继续读下去。理查森运用逻辑推理、说服技巧，几乎让读者麻木，但《帕梅拉》的经典地位表明，他确实赢得了读者心甘情愿的“暂停怀疑”。

12. Henry Fielding The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling

12. 亨利·菲尔丁《弃儿汤姆·琼斯的故事》

ED. FREDSON BOWERS (1749; REPR., NEW YORK
RANDOM HOUSE, MODERN LIBRARY, 1994), 982 PP.

弗雷德森·鲍尔斯 (1749 年；纽约兰登书屋现代文库，1994 年再版)，982 页。

Henry Fielding had been a playwright, but his theater was closed in 1737 by an act of Parliament in retaliation for his satirical attacks on the government of Prime Minister Robert Walpole. It was Pamela that inspired Fielding to try fiction. He thought Richardson's novel was so ridiculous that he lampooned it in Shamela , then expanded his parody in Joseph Andrews , which purported to be the history of Pamela's virtuous brother and Lady Booby, the sister of Mr. B. After the death of his beloved wife, Charlotte, though, Fielding decided to try his hand at something larger and more original with a central character, Sophia Western, inspired by Charlotte. His friend and patron, Ralph Allen, served as the inspiration for the virtuous Squire Allworthy.

亨利·菲尔丁曾是一位剧作家，但他的剧院于1737年被议会勒令关闭，以报复他讽刺首相罗伯特·沃波尔政府的剧作。正是《帕梅拉》这部小说激发了菲尔丁尝试创作小说的灵感。他认为理查森的小说荒诞不经，于是创作了《沙梅拉》对其进行讽刺，之后又在《约瑟夫·安德鲁斯》中扩展了这种戏仿，这部小说讲述的是帕梅拉品德高尚的哥哥和B先生的妹妹布比夫人的故事。然而，在他挚爱的妻子夏洛特去世后，菲尔丁决定尝试创作一部规模更大、更具原创性的作品，并以夏洛特为原型塑造了索菲娅·韦斯特恩这一中心人物。他的朋友兼赞助人拉尔夫·艾伦则成为了品德高尚的奥尔沃西乡绅的原型。

Although Fielding was a famous and esteemed writer, Tom Jones exhibits complexity and generosity of character portrayal that is unprecedented in his other work, and it justly became a great English classic. We think of it as epitomizing the bawdy, bright energy of eighteenth-century England, contrasting strongly with the darker and more repressed passions of the Victorian period, and while Tom Jones is certainly exuberant, it, too, has its shadows and its subversive elements.

尽管菲尔丁是一位声名显赫、备受推崇的作家，《汤姆·琼斯》却展现出他其他作品中前所未有的复杂而丰富的人物刻画，并因此当之无愧地成为英国文学的经典之作。我们认为它完美地体现了十八世纪英国那种喧闹而明媚的活力，与维多利亚时代更为阴暗压抑的情感形成了鲜明的对比。《汤姆·琼斯》固然热情奔放，但也同样蕴含着阴暗面和颠覆性的元素。

Two babies are born to the family of Squire Allworthy. One of these, Tom, is a foundling, apparently the abandoned child of a local girl, Jenny Jones, and the schoolmaster, Mr. Partridge. The other is the son of Mr. Allworthy's sister, Bridget, and her opportunist ne'er-do-well husband, Captain Blifil. Tom grows up good-natured and handsome, but impetuous and lusty. Blifil is far more careful, and it is made apparent to the reader, though not to Mr. Allworthy, that Blifil is a cold, opportunistic hypocrite, just like his father. As the boys near manhood, Tom falls for Sophia Western, the daughter of the neighboring landowner, and she for him, but their relations are complicated by his illegitimacy and by his prior attachment to Molly Seagrim, the daughter of Allworthy's gamekeeper. Tom is hated by Blifil and also by the tutors Allworthy has hired for the boys, Square (the philosopher) and Thwackum (the prelate), who agree on nothing else. Sophia's father, Squire Western, becomes convinced that Sophia is in love with Blifil, and sets his heart on the two of them marrying, which would allow him to join his estate with Allworthy's. When Sophia reveals that she hates Blifil, he confines her to her room and swears he will force the marriage. She escapes and flees to London. In the meantime, Blifil, Square, and Thwackum have engineered Tom's disinheritance, and Tom, too, is on the road.

奥尔沃西乡绅家添了两个孩子。其中一个叫汤姆，是个弃婴，显然是当地女孩珍妮·琼斯和学校老师帕特里奇先生遗弃的孩子。另一个是奥尔沃西先生的妹妹布里奇特和她那投机取巧、游手好闲的丈夫布利菲尔船长的儿子。汤姆长大后性情温和，相貌英俊，但却性情冲动，好色。布利菲尔则谨慎得多，读者（尽管奥尔沃西先生并不知情）可以明显看出，布利菲尔和他父亲一样，是个冷酷无情、投机取巧的伪君子。随着两个男孩逐渐长大成人，汤姆爱上了邻近地主的女儿索菲娅·韦斯特恩，索菲娅也爱上了他，但由于汤姆是私生子，而且他之前还和奥尔沃西家猎场看守的女儿莫莉·西格林有过一段情，他们的关系变得复杂起来。汤姆不仅被布利菲尔憎恨，也被奥尔沃西为孩子们聘请的两位家庭教师——哲学家斯奎尔和教士斯瓦克姆——所厌恶，这两位教师除了汤姆之外，在其他方面都意见相左。索菲娅的父亲韦斯特恩乡绅认定索菲娅爱上了布利菲尔，一心想让他们结婚，这样他就能将自己的庄园并入奥尔沃西的产业。当索菲娅透露自己憎恨布利菲尔时，布利菲尔将她囚禁在房间里，并扬言要强迫他们结婚。索菲娅逃了出来，前往伦敦。与此同时，布利菲尔、斯奎尔和斯瓦克姆密谋剥夺了汤姆的继承权，汤姆也踏上了逃亡之路。

Fielding is possibly the most intrusive (or second most, after Laurence Sterne) narrator in the history of the English novel. At the beginning of each book and frequently in the course of the rest of the novel, he breaks off the action to comment on artistic or philosophical or political questions, and many readers find this at least a little annoying. But much of Fielding's greatness lies in the qualities he displays in these sections, and to love Tom Jones , a reader has to accept and love the voice of the author/narrator (Fielding doesn't differentiate between the two). Tom himself is rather a shadowy character—a good, handsome protagonist and not much else; his dialogue is much more conventional and flowery than that of his author. His appeal is bolstered by Fielding's partisanship and affection, and by his open warmth in comparison to Blifil's sneakiness, but he has few endearing idiosyncrasies. Other characters—Squire Western, his sister, and even Sophia herself—are more vividly drawn, but Tom and Fielding partake of each other in the reader's mind, and I think it is fair to consider Fielding an older and more worldly version of the hero without imputing too much autobiography to the novel.

菲尔丁或许是英国小说史上最爱插话的叙述者（或者说，仅次于劳伦斯·斯特恩，位列第二）。在每本书的开头，以及之后的情节中，他都会频繁地中断故事发展，对艺术、哲学或政治问题进行评述，这让许多读者感到些许恼火。但菲尔丁的伟大之处很大程度上恰恰在于他在这些章节中所展现的特质。要想真正喜爱《汤姆·琼斯》，读者就必须接受并喜爱作者/叙述者的声音（菲尔丁并未区分二者）。汤姆本人则是一个颇为神秘的角色——一个善良英俊的主人公，仅此而已；他的对话远比作者的文风更加程式化、华丽辞藻。菲尔丁的偏袒和深情，以及他坦率的热情（与布利菲尔的阴险狡诈形成鲜明对比），都增强了汤姆的魅力，但他却鲜有令人喜爱的个性特征。其他角色——韦斯特恩乡绅、他的妹妹，甚至索菲亚本人——都刻画得更加生动，但汤姆和菲尔丁在读者心中是相互影响的，我认为可以公平地将菲尔丁视为主人公的年长世故版本，而无需在小说中赋予过多的自传色彩。

Tom's journey is what Sterne would have called “Cervantick.” In the course of his adventures, he gets into farcical imbroglios at inns, meets various characters who tell him enlightening tales, and becomes temporarily entangled with the army, which happens to have been called up to pursue the ongoing eighteenth-century skirmishes between the Jacobite Catholics and the Hanoverian Protestants (the Battle of Culloden, in which the forces of the Stuart pretender were defeated at Inverness by the duke of Cumberland, a son of George II, took place in April 1746 ). Fielding is so careful to place the action of the novel in contemporary times that it is likely he used an almanac to make sure he was accurate about the phases of the moon during the action of the novel.

汤姆的旅程正是斯特恩所说的“塞万提斯式”的。在他的冒险经历中，他辗转于各大客栈，陷入一系列滑稽的困境，结识形形色色的人物，聆听他们讲述的启迪人心的故事，并一度与军队纠缠在一起。这支军队恰好被征召来平息18世纪詹姆斯党天主教徒和汉诺威新教徒之间的冲突（卡洛登战役发生在1746年4月，斯图亚特王朝的僭位者在因弗内斯被乔治二世之子坎伯兰公爵击败）。菲尔丁如此细致地将小说的背景设定在当代，以至于他很可能使用了年鉴来确保小说故事发生期间月相的准确性。

Sophia's journey is the more compelling because it raises the more interesting questions. The reader knows absolutely that Sophia cannot and must not be forced to marry Blifil, because not only does she hate him, the author despises him as well. Nevertheless, her course of action is a moral minefield, because she has to assert herself, but cannot appear to be unfeminine or unvirtuous. The novel is peopled with women who are unable to achieve the proper balance—Miss Western, Sophia's aunt, is portrayed as a good-hearted and strong-willed but laughable spinster whose ignorance is dressed up in military analogies that she gets from her preferred reading of political and military subjects. Lady Bellaston, who seduces Tom when he gets to London, is a hardened courtesan. Sophia's cousin, Mrs. Fitzpatrick, has made the mistake of marrying unhappily and against the wishes of her family, and is destined to end up like Lady Bellaston, if she is lucky. Jenny Jones (Mrs. Waters, whom Tom meets on the road) is kind-hearted and intelligent, but also of low repute, since she lives with men she is not married to. There are only two possible choices for Sophia—to live with her father as a spinster and tend to his needs, or to marry the man she loves, with her father's consent. For most of the novel, both of these choices are impossible. Once Sophia is discovered in London, too, Lady Bellaston and Miss Western collude to force her to marry Lord Fellamar, who attempts to rape her upon the advice of Lady Bellaston—if he does rape her, she will have to marry him, should he be willing to marry his own whore, which he is.

索菲娅的经历之所以更引人入胜，是因为它提出了更多耐人寻味的问题。读者完全清楚，索菲娅不能也不应该被迫嫁给布利菲尔，因为她不仅恨他，作者也同样厌恶他。然而，她的选择却处处充满道德困境，因为她必须坚持自己的立场，却又不能显得不够女性化或不贞洁。小说中的女性角色都难以找到合适的平衡点——索菲娅的姑妈韦斯特恩小姐被描绘成一个心地善良、意志坚强却又滑稽可笑的老处女，她用自己从政治军事书籍中汲取的军事比喻来掩盖自己的无知。贝拉斯顿夫人，在汤姆抵达伦敦后引诱他，则是一位老练的交际花。索菲娅的表妹菲茨帕特里克夫人犯了一个错误，违背家人的意愿嫁给了一个不幸的人，如果她足够幸运的话，最终的结局或许也会像贝拉斯顿夫人一样。珍妮·琼斯（汤姆在路上遇到的沃特斯太太）心地善良，聪明伶俐，但名声不佳，因为她与一些未婚男子同居。索菲娅只有两个选择：要么像个老处女一样与父亲同住，服侍他；要么在父亲的同意下，嫁给自己心爱的男人。在小说的大部分篇幅里，这两个选择都行不通。索菲娅在伦敦的身份被发现后，贝拉斯顿夫人和韦斯特恩小姐合谋逼迫她嫁给费拉马尔勋爵。费拉马尔勋爵在贝拉斯顿夫人的唆使下企图强奸她——如果他强奸了她，她就不得不嫁给他，前提是他愿意娶自己的娼妓，而他确实愿意。

Sophia's own notions of love are considered naive and even dangerous by all of the female characters because, though Fielding does not say so, should they become universal, they would subvert the property arrangements that English marriage is founded upon. As with most other English novels, the only comic solution is the merger of love and money. Of course, Fielding solves the puzzle—his robust, ironic style foreshadows that he will.

索菲娅对爱情的看法被所有女性角色都认为天真甚至危险，因为尽管菲尔丁没有明说，但如果这种观念普遍化，就会颠覆英国婚姻赖以建立的财产制度。如同大多数其他英国小说一样，唯一的喜剧式解决方案就是将爱情与金钱结合起来。当然，菲尔丁最终解开了这个谜题——他那犀利而讽刺的文风早已预示了这一点。

Much of the plot of Tom Jones is designed to solve the riddle of Sophia's affections and to make Tom worthy of her hand, both as a man and as a property-holder, but Sophia must save herself without losing her feminine nature, and she does so by being the immovable object rather than the irresistable force—her cousin, Mrs. Fitzpatrick, demonstrates the dangers of acting on her own wishes as opposed to simply resisting the untoward wishes of others. Nightingale, whom Tom meets in London, is Mrs. Fitzpatrick's male counterpart—a young man who seduces a poor young woman and then must be cajoled into marrying her by Tom in the teeth of the resistance of his relatives, and even of his own resistence; he can't imagine what he is going to do to earn a living if his father disinherits him. Ultimately his father is persuaded not to disinherit him.

《汤姆·琼斯》的大部分情节都是为了解开索菲娅的爱情之谜，并使汤姆无论作为一个男人还是一个财产所有者，都配得上她的芳心。但索菲娅必须在不丧失女性特质的前提下拯救自己，而她做到这一点的方式是成为一股不可撼动的力量，而非一股不可抗拒的力量——她的表妹菲茨帕特里克太太就展现了顺从自身意愿的危险，而仅仅抵制他人的不良意愿则不然。汤姆在伦敦遇到的奈廷格尔，正是菲茨帕特里克太太的男性翻版——一个引诱了一位贫穷年轻女子，然后汤姆不顾亲戚们的反对，甚至连他自己的抗拒，最终劝说他娶了她；他无法想象如果父亲剥夺他的继承权，他该如何谋生。最终，他的父亲被说服，没有剥夺他的继承权。

The Fielding question—how can the young people be married off according to their affections?—turns out to have a rather revolutionary answer: the property-owning parental class must go along with the inclinations of their offspring, even if the result is mixing of classes and dilution of assets. The real aristocracy is of the heart and the mind— much the same conclusion Richardson comes to in Pamela. Such is the gist of Tom Jones , the story. As a social document, though, The History of Tom Jones, a Foundling , details the contingent nature of this solution compared with the vast inequities and immoralities surrounding the exceptional and blessed central characters. Fielding's narrative tone is generous, comic, and evenhanded, but his depiction implicitly suggests that the main difficulties do not reside in human nature but in social arrangements. Charles Dickens, a more explicitly revolutionary novelist, loved this eighteenth-century predecessor, and no doubt partly for this reason—Fielding was alive to the idea that social circumstances could be changed, though he wasn't prepared to suggest wholesale solutions.

菲尔丁提出的问题——如何让年轻人按照自己的意愿结婚？——最终得到了一个颇具革命性的答案：拥有财产的父母阶层必须顺从子女的意愿，即便这会导致阶级混杂和财产稀释。真正的贵族在于心灵和智慧——这与理查森在《帕梅拉》中得出的结论大同小异。这就是《汤姆·琼斯》故事的精髓。然而，作为一部社会文献，《弃儿汤姆·琼斯的故事》详细阐述了这一解决方案的偶然性，并将其与围绕着这些杰出而幸运的主人公的巨大不公和不道德现象进行了对比。菲尔丁的叙述语气宽容、幽默且公正，但他的描写却含蓄地暗示，主要问题并非出在人性，而是出在社会制度上。更具革命性的小说家查尔斯·狄更斯非常喜爱这位十八世纪的前辈，无疑部分原因就在于此——菲尔丁意识到社会环境是可以改变的，尽管他并不准备提出彻底的解决方案。

13. Charlotte Lennox. The Female Quixote

13. 夏洛特·伦诺克斯，《女堂吉诃德》

(1752; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1998), 383 PP.

（1752；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1998 年），383 页。

The Female Quixote is not about a woman who sets out on a series of adventures with her faithful companion, but about a young girl of aristocratic English parentage who grows up on a secluded estate reading romances, and who takes all her ideas of romance and valor from them. When she comes into contact with mid-eighteenth-century society, her misapprehensions and predilections are startling and disturbing to those she meets, and inconvenient, and even dangerous, to herself, but she persists in them until she is disabused through a lengthy discussion with a learned doctor (possibly modeled on Samuel Johnson).

《女堂吉诃德》讲述的并非一位女性与忠实伙伴踏上一系列冒险之旅，而是一位出身英国贵族家庭的年轻女孩，她在与世隔绝的庄园里阅读浪漫小说，并将所有浪漫和英勇的观念都源于此。当她接触到十八世纪中期的社会时，她的误解和偏好令她遇到的人感到震惊和不安，也给她自己带来了不便，甚至危险。但她却固执己见，直到与一位博学的医生（可能是以塞缪尔·约翰逊为原型）进行了一番长谈后才幡然醒悟。

The Female Quixote , not nearly as famous as Tom Jones or Pamela , and not, indeed, part of the eighteenth-century canon, except to specialists, is both entertaining and instructive as a work and as a historical document. Charlotte Lennox was a contemporary of Johnson and Samuel Richardson's, who collaborated to help her both write and publish this novel before she was, according to Richardson, yet twenty-four years old. At that point she was already married, widely traveled, and the author of another novel, The Life of Harriot Stuart. She went on to write several more novels, but none as popular as The Female Quixote.

《女堂吉诃德》远不如《汤姆·琼斯》或《帕梅拉》那样闻名，事实上，除了专家之外，它也并非十八世纪经典作品的一部分。然而，作为一部作品和历史文献，它既引人入胜又富有教育意义。夏洛特·伦诺克斯与约翰逊和塞缪尔·理查森是同时代的人，理查森曾帮助她创作并出版了这部小说，据理查森所说，当时她还不到24岁。那时她已经结婚，游历甚广，并且著有另一部小说《哈里奥特·斯图尔特传》。她后来又创作了几部小说，但没有一部能像《女堂吉诃德》那样广受欢迎。

Like the Cervantes original, the Lennox novel is intended to be comic—to portray the ludicrous effects of an improper education upon a susceptible mind, and like Don Quixote, Arabella, Lennox's protagonist, is entirely estimable apart from her fixation on stories of passion, romance, and war (not the same stories as Quixote enjoyed, but French romances ostensibly set in ancient times though written in the seventeenth century by de Scudry and La Calprende).

与塞万提斯的原著一样，伦诺克斯的小说旨在喜剧化——描绘不当教育对易受影响的心灵造成的荒谬影响，而且与堂吉诃德一样，伦诺克斯的主人公阿拉贝拉除了痴迷于激情、浪漫和战争的故事之外，其他方面都非常值得尊敬（与堂吉诃德喜欢的故事不同，而是德·斯库德里和拉·卡尔普朗德在十七世纪创作的，表面上以古代为背景的法国浪漫小说）。

As with Don Quixote , as the story grows, its comic aspects darken and soften, the natural result of prolonged acquaintance with the protagonist. The author's effort to sustain the ridiculous aspects of Arabella's psyche while not losing the reader's sympathy inevitably presents some challenges, but Lennox approaches them cleverly. The first of these is that Arabella, like Quixote, is rude, disputatious, and occasionally aggressive. The novel is a social form—the reader relates to characters as she would to acquaintances—and one of the paradoxes of the novel is that social faults can be more off-putting to readers than moral faults, at least at first. But as in life, the reader takes her cue from others around the protagonist, and in this case, the fact that the sensible Mr. Glanville, Arabella's cousin, finds her appealing and genuine (though he is frequently, and most plausibly, irritated and upset by her ideas) excuses her enough for the reader to go on with her. In addition, Lennox contrasts Arabella with her much more typical cousin, Charlotte, who is more realistic, but also small-minded and shallow. Also, Lennox never allows Arabella to seem entirely in the wrong. Sometimes she comes up with a reasonable rationale for her actions; at other times it is she who is most harmed by her actions, and at still other times we see that at least her actions stem from honorable and generous motives. Her variety keeps her interesting (though I have to admit that the balance isn't perfectly maintained, and Arabella gets tedious from time to time). Lennox is also careful to locate the comedy in the characters around her—a very sophisticated choice for so youthful an artist. Arabella voices absurdities, but the reader doesn't laugh until her relatives and friends react to them. This device is frequently used in movies, when, for example, one character does something and another does a double take, thereby opening up the distance between the action and its meaning that comic perspective requires.

如同《堂吉诃德》一样，随着故事的展开，其喜剧元素逐渐变得阴暗而柔和，这是读者与主人公长期相处后自然而然的结果。作者试图在保持阿拉贝拉荒诞心理的同时，又不失去读者的同情，这无疑带来了一些挑战，但伦诺克斯巧妙地应对了这些挑战。首先，阿拉贝拉和堂吉诃德一样，粗鲁、好争辩，有时甚至具有攻击性。小说是一种社会文学体裁——读者与书中人物的关系如同与熟人相处——而小说的一个悖论在于，至少在最初阶段，社会缺陷可能比道德缺陷更令读者反感。但正如现实生活一样，读者会从主人公周围的人身上寻找线索。在这个故事里，理智的格兰维尔先生——阿拉贝拉的表兄——觉得她既讨人喜欢又真诚（尽管他经常，而且很可能，会被她的想法惹恼和沮丧），这足以让读者原谅她，并继续读下去。此外，伦诺克斯将阿拉贝拉与她更典型的表妹夏洛特进行了对比。夏洛特更现实，但也心胸狭隘、肤浅。而且，伦诺克斯从未让阿拉贝拉显得完全错误。有时她会为自己的行为找到合理的理由；有时她会因为自己的行为而受到最大的伤害；还有些时候，我们会看到她的行为至少是出于高尚和慷慨的动机。她的多样性使她始终引人入胜（尽管我不得不承认，这种平衡并非完美，阿拉贝拉有时也会让人感到乏味）。伦诺克斯还巧妙地在她周围的人物身上寻找喜剧元素——对于一位如此年轻的艺术家来说，这无疑是一个非常精妙的选择。阿拉贝拉说着一些荒诞的话，但读者直到看到她的亲朋好友的反应才会发笑。这种手法在电影中很常见，例如，一个角色做了某件事，另一个角色反应过度，从而拉开了动作与其意义之间的距离，这正是喜剧效果所需要的。

The perennial problem of a novel in which a character is deluded is how to believably undelude him or her, and what comes after that. This is a problem natural to the novel, since the novel is always about whether and how particular individuals fit into their social milieu. Cervantes offers one solution to this problem: Don Quixote is defeated and then falls ill. He wakes up sane but then dies, having no reason to live anymore. Arabella, too, suffers physically (she nearly drowns), but upon recovery, she has a long discussion with the Samuel Johnson–like figure, who appeals to her intelligence with reasoned arguments. She repudiates her former reading, marries Glanville, and lives happily ever after, because, really, all along, her motives were of the best. Some readers accept this ending and some don't, but appealing to her reason makes sense partly because she is always using logical arguments, though based on false authorities and strange premises, and also because it is a tack that none of the other characters has tried. The doctor appeals to her intelligence, where the others have appealed only to her sense of propriety or self-love.

小说中，当一个角色陷入妄想时，一个永恒的难题是如何令人信服地让他/她醒悟过来，以及之后会发生什么。这是小说固有的问题，因为小说的核心始终在于探讨特定个体如何融入其社会环境。塞万提斯提供了一种解决方案：堂吉诃德战败后病倒了。他醒来后恢复了理智，但最终死去，因为他失去了活下去的理由。阿拉贝拉也经历了身体上的痛苦（她差点溺水），但康复后，她与一位类似塞缪尔·约翰逊的人物进行了一次长谈，这位人物用理性的论证打动了她的智慧。她摒弃了之前的阅读，嫁给了格兰维尔，从此过上了幸福的生活，因为，实际上，她一直以来的动机都是美好的。有些读者接受这个结局，有些则不接受，但诉诸理性是合理的，部分原因是她始终运用逻辑论证，尽管这些论证建立在虚假的权威和奇怪的前提之上，也因为这是其他角色从未尝试过的方法。医生诉诸于她的智慧，而其他人只是诉诸于她的礼仪或自尊。

Arabella's delusions are interesting, also, as part of the continuing novelistic discussion of the status and rights of women. To her contemporaries, her fears of being made love to, or raped and kidnapped, make no sense. Charlotte and the other female characters like being made love to, and don't fear being “carried away;” their greater concern is to appear more innocent than they are. This is certainly because they live in a safer world than the world of The Heptameron. The underground river of the French romance has carried medieval conflicts between love and virtue, honor and power into the mundane modern world of eighteenth-century England, where they still have enough ambiguity to compel a great deal of interest. Arabella's dilemma (will she marry as the dictates of her father and property demand, or will she pursue her own course?) is the same old dilemma, though benignly rendered in this case. What to do with the girls is the perennial dilemma of the novel, sometimes given first place, sometimes given second place, but clearly a preoccupation of European life in every country and in every era. Where do Lennox's own sympathies lie? The ending to The Female Quixote is not well developed (evidence is that she had too much material for two volumes but not enough for three and decided to wind things up as quickly as she could), but it does give a clue that the enterprising Lennox, who had sufficient talent and wit to interest the greatest literary men of her day, thought that including women in the discussion of their own lives and fates was at the very least an excellent place to start.

阿拉贝拉的妄想也颇为有趣，因为它延续了小说中关于女性地位和权利的探讨。在她同时代的人们看来，她害怕被强迫、被强奸或被绑架的想法毫无道理。夏洛特和其他女性角色都乐于享受性爱，并不害怕被“带走”；她们更在意的是让自己看起来比实际更天真无邪。这当然是因为她们生活在一个比《七日谈》的世界更安全的世界里。法国浪漫小说的地下河流将中世纪爱情与美德、荣誉与权力之间的冲突带入了十八世纪英国平凡的现代世界，这些冲突依然具有足够的暧昧性，足以吸引人们的浓厚兴趣。阿拉贝拉的困境（她会按照父亲和财产的要求结婚，还是会坚持自己的道路？）与以往的困境并无二致，只是在这个例子中，她的困境被赋予了温和的色彩。如何处置女性角色是小说中永恒的难题，有时被放在首位，有时被放在次要位置，但显然是欧洲各国、各个时代人们普遍关注的问题。伦诺克斯本人又倾向于何方呢？《女堂吉诃德》的结尾并不完整（证据是她素材太多，两卷不够，三卷又不够，于是决定尽快收尾），但这确实透露出一个线索：这位才华横溢、机智过人，足以吸引当时最杰出的文坛巨匠的伦诺克斯认为，至少让女性参与到对自身生活和命运的讨论中，是一个绝佳的开端。

14. Laurence Sterne. The Life and Opinions of Tristram Shandy, Gentleman

14. 劳伦斯·斯特恩。《绅士特里斯特拉姆·香迪的生平与见解》

ED. MELVYN NEW AND JOAN NEW
编辑：梅尔文·纽和琼·纽
(1759-67; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN BOOKS, 1997), 543 PP.
(1759-67；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1997 年)，543 页。

Tristram Shandy may be the most masculine novel ever written. Sterne was a middle-aged, long unhappily married clergyman when he began his novel, and he seems to have had no interest in the marriage dilemmas of young people. His novel is comic, or at least funny, but dispenses entirely with comic structure as borrowed from plays—there is no happy ending, symbolized by a series of weddings, and what is really of interest is not marriage and money but the interplay of the individual mind with its circumstances. The novel's sources are in sermons, scientific and philosophical treatises, military histories, anecdotes, and conversation. It was conceived and carried out as a serial work, rather like a set of sermons, and was, from first publication, a sensation that Sterne strove hard for the rest of his life to keep alive. It was highly esteemed by twentieth-century critics and writers, who much appreciated the novel's complexity and self-consciousness.

《项狄传》或许是史上最具男性气质的小说。斯特恩开始创作这部小说时，已是一位中年牧师，婚姻不幸多年，他对年轻人的婚姻困境似乎毫无兴趣。他的小说诙谐幽默，或者至少令人捧腹，但却完全摒弃了从戏剧中借鉴的喜剧结构——没有以一系列婚礼象征的皆大欢喜的结局，真正引人入胜的并非婚姻和金钱，而是个人心灵与环境的互动。小说的素材来源于布道、科学和哲学论著、军事史、轶事以及对话。它以连载的形式构思和创作，如同布道集一般，自出版以来便引起轰动，斯特恩终其一生都在努力延续这部作品的热度。二十世纪的评论家和作家们对这部小说推崇备至，他们非常欣赏小说的复杂性和自省意识。

Explanatory notes in the Penguin edition run to 130 pages of small type, and even so are not enough. The reader may be forgiven for not fully understanding the novel, because it is not only replete with obscure references and written in a highly and even aggressively nonlinear style, it also takes shame as its theme, and explores it by means of blank pages, unclear allusions, and information implied but stated only through series of asterisks.

企鹅版的注释长达130页，字号也很小，即便如此也远远不够。读者或许可以原谅自己无法完全理解这部小说，因为它不仅充斥着晦涩的典故，而且写作风格高度非线性，甚至可以说是突兀，更以羞耻为主题，通过空白页、含糊不清的暗示以及一系列星号所隐含的信息来探讨这一主题。

The novel opens with the conception of Tristram, and the joke/ tragedy is that just as Tristram's father, Walter, is climaxing, Tristram's mother asks him if he has remembered to wind the clock, thus distracting him and scattering “the animal spirits, whose business it was to have escorted and gone hand-in-hand with the HOMUNCULUS, and conducted him safe to the place destined for his reception.” Walter, his brother Toby, and Toby's man, Trim, are the main characters of the novel. Walter is a philosopher and autodidact with many cherished and eccentric notions. Toby is a veteran of campaigns of the early eighteenth century on the European continent and has suffered a mysterious and debilitating wound in his groin. Trim, too, is a wounded veteran. The two brothers live near one another, and Toby and Trim occupy themselves by reproducing in miniature, on the bowling green of Toby's estate, the battles and sieges they read about in the newspapers. Although all three men and the other male characters (Dr. Slop and Yorick the curate) consider themselves worldly and up to date, all are, in fact, figures of radical and irredeemable innocence, especially in contrast to the female characters, Mrs. Shandy, Susannah, the midwife, and the widow Wadman, who ignore ideas in favor of practicalities and represent the workings of ignorant, or perhaps natural, chance in the formation of Tristram.

小说以特里斯特拉姆的受孕开篇，而其中的笑点/悲剧在于，就在特里斯特拉姆的父亲沃尔特达到高潮之际，特里斯特拉姆的母亲问他是否记得给钟上弦，这分散了他的注意力，也惊散了“那些本应护送小矮人（托比）并肩而行，将其安全送达预定地点的动物精灵”。沃尔特、他的兄弟托比以及托比的仆人特里姆是小说的主要人物。沃尔特是一位哲学家兼自学者，拥有许多珍视的、古怪的想法。托比是十八世纪初欧洲大陆战役的老兵，腹股沟处受过一次神秘而严重的伤。特里姆也是一位受伤的老兵。两兄弟住得很近，托比和特里姆经常在托比庄园的保龄球场上，用微缩模型重现他们在报纸上读到的战役和围攻。虽然这三兄弟以及其他男性角色（斯洛普医生和牧师约里克）都自认为见多识广、与时俱进，但实际上，他们都天真得近乎原始，尤其与女性角色——珊迪太太、助产士苏珊娜和寡妇沃德曼——形成鲜明对比。这些女性角色摒弃思想，注重实际，她们的成长体现了无知，或许也体现了自然的偶然性。

Tristram is undone by four events: his mother's inopportune question, the crushing of his nose at birth, Susannah's failure to remember the proper name (“Trismegistus”) at the christening, and Susannah's suggestion that instead of peeing in the chamber pot, the young boy simply pee out the window. Unfortunately, the window sash falls just at that moment, causing an unexpected circumcision. But it may also be that Tristram is undone, not by the events themselves, but by Walter's convictions that such details are formative for the character and the fate of the child, and so the novel repeatedly poses this dilemma: is it the events themselves or the interpretation of them that dictates their outcome?

特里斯特拉姆的悲剧由四件事引发：母亲不合时宜的问题、出生时鼻子被压碎、苏珊娜在洗礼仪式上忘记了他的正确名字（“特里斯墨吉斯忒斯”），以及苏珊娜建议小男孩不要在便壶里小便，而是直接从窗户往外撒尿。不幸的是，窗扇恰好在那一刻掉落，导致他意外地接受了割礼。但或许，特里斯特拉姆的悲剧并非源于这些事件本身，而是源于沃尔特坚信这些细节对孩子的性格和命运至关重要。因此，小说反复提出这个两难困境：究竟是事件本身决定了事件的结局，还是人们对事件的解读决定了事件的结局？

As the novel progresses, Uncle Toby becomes more and more the central character, and the last volume depicts his wooing by a neighbor, widow Wadman. Widow Wadman loves Toby and is not herself unattractive, but before she accepts his proposal, she very much wants to know the nature and effects of the wound in his groin. Toby has had so little to do with women that he seems not to understand the facts of life. When Trim reveals to him what the widow wants to know and why, he is overwhelmed, though delicately so, by a sense of shame that is fatal to his continued affections, and that is that for the widow Wadman.

随着小说的推进，托比叔叔逐渐成为中心人物，最后一卷描写了邻居寡妇沃德曼追求他的故事。沃德曼寡妇爱慕托比，她自己也颇具魅力，但在接受他的求婚之前，她非常想知道他腹股沟伤口的性质和后果。托比与女性鲜有接触，似乎对女性的生理需求一无所知。当特里姆向他揭示寡妇想知道什么以及原因时，他虽然内心柔软，却也感到一阵难以言喻的羞耻，这最终断送了他对沃德曼寡妇的爱意，沃德曼寡妇也因此失去了他。

Sterne's theme of shame is strongly linked to the overt display of masculinity. Toby and Trim are hobbyists of war, embracing the very activity that injured them. At a gathering where clergymen are debating a point of doctrine, another entirely masculine activity, a hot roast chestnut drops into the open fly of one of them, who attributes his injury to Yorick's malice. Later, when Trim is disporting himself with widow Wadman's cook on one of Toby's model bridges, the bridge collapses and reinjures Trim's knee. In other words, all of Sterne's men live in a world where male activities present a constant and immediate danger of injury or embarrassment to masculinity itself. Women either do not notice or haven't the intellect to appreciate this. The efforts of Walter, in particular, to forestall these dangers are unavailing: he suffers the death of his elder son, Bobby, and the strange fate (not entirely disclosed) of his younger son, Tristram, in spite of his carefully thought-out system, which includes the composition of “Tristra-paedia,” his work on educating his son, which so distracts him from Tristram himself that the boy is left too long in the hands of the women.

斯特恩笔下的羞耻主题与男性气概的外露紧密相连。托比和特里姆都是战争爱好者，他们沉迷于这项曾让他们受伤的活动。在一次牧师们辩论教义的聚会上——这又是另一项完全属于男性的活动——一颗滚烫的烤栗子掉进了其中一位牧师敞开的裤子拉链里，他把受伤归咎于约里克的恶意。后来，当特里姆在托比的模型桥上与沃德曼寡妇的厨娘嬉戏时，桥塌了，特里姆的膝盖再次受伤。换句话说，斯特恩笔下的所有男性都生活在一个男性活动随时可能造成伤害或羞辱的世界里，这种危险威胁着男性气概本身。女性要么对此视而不见，要么缺乏理解这种危险的能力。沃尔特为阻止这些危险所做的努力尤其徒劳无功：尽管他精心设计了一套体系，包括编写《特里斯特拉姆教育手册》，但他的长子鲍比还是去世了，而他的幼子特里斯特拉姆也遭遇了奇怪的命运（并未完全揭示）。然而，这套体系分散了他对特里斯特拉姆的注意力，导致这个男孩被留在妇女手中太久。

Bawdiness is the inevitable accompaniment of Sterne's theme of manly shame, but it is the bawdiness of privacy and innuendo rather than the openly tawdry, realistic, cultural bawdiness of Fielding, Defoe, and Richardson. Each of these great eighteenth-century writers takes up the overt sexuality of the period and addresses it in a different way—for Defoe the issue is guilt; for Fielding, social decay; for Richardson, individual worth as against social power; and for Sterne, the unavoidable and unrelieved experience of shame, thus his appeal to the twentieth century, which also was interested in and sensitive to the workings of shame.

斯特恩作品中男性羞耻感的主题必然伴随着粗俗，但这种粗俗是私密的、含蓄的暗示，而非菲尔丁、笛福和理查森作品中那种公开的、庸俗的、现实的、文化意义上的粗俗。这三位伟大的十八世纪作家都触及了那个时代公开的性观念，并以不同的方式加以探讨——笛福关注的是罪恶感；菲尔丁关注的是社会衰败；理查森关注的是个人价值与社会权力的冲突；而斯特恩关注的是无法避免且无法摆脱的羞耻感，因此他的作品对二十世纪具有吸引力，因为二十世纪的人们同样对羞耻感的运作机制感兴趣且十分敏感。

Tristram Shandy also reminds us that the novel was not invented as a page-turner—in some sense this novel was not even invented as a novel, since Sterne wrote later volumes that were outside the original plan as a way of prolonging his success—plot is minimal here, and style is the organizing principle. But suspense is only a contingent virtue of the novel, not a necessary one; Tristram Shandy is often charming and even profound, and while reading it, if she is in the mood, the reader may not care at all that it is not compellingly told as a story. Reading Tristram Shandy feels like eavesdropping on a truly unique sensibility in a truly intimate way.

《项狄传》也提醒我们，小说并非为了引人入胜而创作——某种意义上，这部小说甚至并非一开始就被当作小说来创作的，因为斯特恩后来创作的几卷都偏离了最初的计划，以此来延续他的成功——这里的情节极简，风格才是其核心。但悬念只是这部小说的一个附带优点，而非必要条件；《项狄传》常常充满魅力，甚至意味深长，读者在阅读时，如果心情合适，或许根本不会在意它的故事叙述是否引人入胜。阅读《项狄传》就像是以一种极其私密的方式，偷听一种极其独特的感性之声。

15. Voltaire Candide

15. 伏尔泰的《老实人》

(1759; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1991, 1966), 60 PP.

（1759 年；重印，纽约：W. W. NORTON，1991 年，1966 年），60 页。

Every novel is a social document in prose with something wrong with it, but not every social document in prose with something wrong with it is a novel. Candide , in some ways a profound and influential piece of philosophical fiction, is not a novel, but illustrates by contrast some characteristic features of the real novel. Maybe the closest relative to Candide that we have already discussed is Lazarillo de Tormes. The one we haven't discussed is Rabelais's Gargantua and Pantagruel ( 1542 ), a piece of work so masculine and French that I find it unreadable. Like Lazarillo and Pantagruel, Candide is forced to go out into the world. Like the previous two, the requirement suits him because he is interested to discover the nature of the world. In this he differs from Don Quixote, who thinks that he already knows the nature of the world and plans to redeem it by doing knightly deeds. The world Candide finds is Uncle Toby's world, strangely darkened, a world of endless wars and battles, less the scene of military pattern and strategy than the scene of pointless destruction and torment. In this world, though, there is no Shandy Hall, a safe haven where theories are spun out of predilections and affections. There is only chaos and accident. The goal of the characters is to make sense of the world; the goal of the author is to show that sense cannot be made of it.

每部小说都是一部用散文写成的社会文献，其中都存在一些缺陷，但并非所有存在缺陷的社会文献都是小说。《老实人》在某种程度上是一部深刻而富有影响力的哲学小说，它并非小说，而是通过对比展现了真正小说的一些特征。或许我们之前讨论过的与《老实人》最接近的作品是《拉撒路》。我们尚未讨论的是拉伯雷的《巨人传》（1542），这部作品充满了浓厚的男性气息和法国特色，以至于我难以卒读。与《拉撒路》和《巨人传》一样，《老实人》中的老实人也被迫踏入社会。与前两位一样，这种要求对他来说正合适，因为他渴望探索世界的本质。这一点上，他与堂吉诃德不同，堂吉诃德自认为已经洞悉世界的本质，并计划通过骑士精神来救赎世界。坎迪德发现的世界，正是托比叔叔的世界，一个奇异阴暗的世界，一个无休止的战争与战斗的世界，与其说是军事模式和战略的舞台，不如说是毫无意义的破坏和折磨的场所。然而，在这个世界里，没有香迪厅——一个可以让人基于喜好和情感编织理论的避风港。这里只有混乱和意外。书中人物的目标是理解这个世界；而作者的目标则是表明，这个世界根本无法被理解。

In this regard, it is interesting to contrast Voltaire with English novelists writing at the same time. Voltaire was a wealthy and influential man who created and lived upon a great estate just inside France, near the Swiss border (when he got into political trouble with the king of France, he could cross into Switzerland). He lived to a great age, surrounded by friends and relatives, apparently in good health (owing to an abstemious diet). Yet his view of life is far darker than that of Fielding, Sterne, and Smollett (see below), who were plagued by financial troubles and ill health, who died young, and yet give us worlds of great beauty that are shadowed by darker events but not dominated by them.

在这方面，将伏尔泰与同时期的英国小说家进行对比颇为有趣。伏尔泰是一位富有且颇具影响力的人物，他在法国境内靠近瑞士边境的地方建造并居住着一座庞大的庄园（当他与法国国王发生政治冲突时，他可以越境进入瑞士）。他长寿，身边亲朋好友环绕，身体也似乎很健康（这得益于他节制的饮食）。然而，他对人生的看法远比菲尔丁、斯特恩和斯莫利特（见下文）更为阴郁。菲尔丁、斯特恩和斯莫利特饱受经济困境和疾病的折磨，英年早逝，但他们仍然为我们留下了充满美感的世界，这些世界虽被黑暗的事件所笼罩，却并未被其所主宰。

A novel starts with an action or an event; Candide begins with a premise—that all things are for the best in this best of all possible worlds. It is the raison d'tre of the characters Candide, Pangloss (Can-dide's tutor), Cungonde (Candide's beloved), and their friends to test this premise, and it is immediately found wanting—in the first few pages of the book, Candide is kicked out of his home, the castle is invaded by enemies, Cungonde is raped and killed, and Dr. Pangloss contracts a venereal disease that maims and disfigures him. No effort is made to render these events with any texture; the reader is not asked to empathize with the characters (that is, imagine their experience of things), only to observe and marvel. The characters themselves hardly suffer. Even though they lose parts of themselves, are bereft of loved ones, watch the sufferings of others, are injured, robbed, endangered, betrayed, enslaved, and isolated from all they know, they are always resilient enough to survive, to tell their stories, and to speculate about how their stories fit into the larger scheme of things. The world Candide travels through is a world of godless chaos and suffering. It is, in many ways, suddenly the modern secular world of huge energies wasted in pointless conflict. Voltaire's essential point is that the world is not the result of intelligent design, and certainly not the object of care and scrutiny by a higher power (Voltaire was famous for his atheism and anticlerical views). His quick pace and broad scope depersonalize every incident, and the narrative achieves a vertiginous effect—the point of view is so distant from the characters that every feeling they have, from hope to despair, from love to vengefulness, is simply evidence of folly. In sixty pages Voltaire does not take the time to develop scenes, characters, or even conversations; he is far more interested in giving the illusion of great distances traveled and great events witnessed. But in the end, the very resilience of the characters goes to support Pangloss's contention rather than contradict it—even though things have not turned out as Candide expected them to when he still lived in the castle of Thunder-ten-Tronckh, he is married to Cungonde and he lives in comfort with his friends at his estate near Constantinople, where he tends his own garden. The necessities of a story (that we end with the same characters we begin with) undermine the philosophical assertion that the torrent of incidents seems to illustrate.

小说通常以某个动作或事件开篇；而《老实人》则以一个前提开篇——在这个所有可能世界中最好的世界里，一切都是最好的安排。小说中的人物，包括老实人、他的家庭教师潘格洛斯、老实人心爱的孔贡德以及他们的朋友们，存在的意义就在于检验这个前提，而这个前提很快就被证明是站不住脚的——在书的开头几页，老实人就被赶出了家门，城堡遭到敌人入侵，孔贡德被强奸并杀害，潘格洛斯医生也染上了性病，导致残疾和毁容。作者并没有努力去描绘这些事件的细节；读者无需与人物产生共鸣（也就是说，无需设身处地地想象他们的感受），只需观察和惊叹即可。人物本身几乎没有遭受任何痛苦。即使他们失去了部分自我，失去了挚爱，目睹了他人的苦难，遭受了伤害、抢劫、危险、背叛、奴役，并与所有熟悉的事物隔绝，他们始终坚韧不拔，得以生存，讲述自己的故事，并思考这些故事如何融入更宏大的宇宙图景。坎迪德游历的世界是一个无神论的混乱和苦难的世界。在许多方面，它突然变成了现代世俗世界，巨大的能量被浪费在毫无意义的冲突中。伏尔泰的核心观点是，世界并非智能设计的产物，当然也不是更高力量关注和审视的对象（伏尔泰以其无神论和反教权主义观点而闻名）。他快速的节奏和广阔的视野使每一个事件都失去了人性，叙事达到了一种令人眩晕的效果——视角与人物如此遥远，以至于他们所经历的每一种情感，从希望到绝望，从爱到复仇，都仅仅被视为愚蠢的证据。在短短六十页中，伏尔泰并未花时间去展开场景、人物，甚至对话；他更感兴趣的是营造一种长途跋涉、目睹重大事件的错觉。然而，最终，人物的坚韧恰恰印证了庞格罗斯的论断，而非与之相悖——尽管事态的发展并非如康迪德当年居住在雷霆城时所预期的那样，如今他已与孔贡德结为连理，与朋友们在君士坦丁堡附近的庄园里过着舒适的生活，并亲自照料着自己的花园。故事的必然性（即故事的结尾与开头的人物相同）削弱了这一系列事件似乎想要阐明的哲学论断。

In fact, prose narratives of a certain length with something wrong with them do not lend themselves to being used as philosophical proofs. They are too transparent; it is too easy for the reader to see that the writer is setting up the story to demonstrate what he already supposes rather than to investigate some significant unknown question. Because it is a narrative, the novel is inescapably subjective. Every word that the writer chooses, every manner in which he constructs a sentence bears witness to the subjectivity of his argument. The power a novelist brings to his argument is never objective information or the power of reason (though intelligence illuminates lots of novels), it is always the power of emotion—the reader feels what the characters are feeling, so she accepts their point of view as true. Every fictive argument must be circular, because all its attempts at objectivity are false.

事实上，篇幅达到一定程度且存在缺陷的散文叙事并不适合用作哲学论证。它们过于直白；读者很容易看出，作者构建故事是为了证明他已有的假设，而不是为了探究某个重要的未知问题。由于小说是一种叙事作品，它不可避免地带有主观性。作者选择的每一个词，他构建句子的每一个方式，都见证了他论证的主观性。小说家赋予其论证的力量从来不是客观信息或理性（尽管智慧在许多小说中都发挥了作用），而是情感的力量——读者感同身受地体会着人物的感受，因此会接受他们的观点。任何虚构的论证都必然是循环论证，因为它所有试图追求客观性的努力都是徒劳的。

Candide is an eloquent social document testifying to the spiritual and humanitarian failures of European colonial exploration and settlement. It is as harsh in its representation of Europe's export of its own troubled culture as any twentieth-century revolutionary tract could be. It represents the world as polluted and destroyed by greed, cruelty, social inequity, and blindness. Everywhere Candide goes, Europeans have already been there and wrecked it, or else the natives (as in El Dorado) have taken precautions to protect themselves. Much of Candide has the ring of truth. In addition, of course, it is representative of its period—the eighteenth-century French Enlightenment—in its anticlerical and in many ways humanistic ideas, as well as in its cynicism. I read it first as an assignment in ninth grade and didn't understand a word of it, though many of the images of suffering and disfigurement shocked me and stuck in my mind. Perhaps schools assign it because it is short and full of action, but it is not a novel because the “agon” is missing from the “protagonist”—Candide acts but he has no inner life that invites us to empathize or sympathize with him. Candide exists alongside the novel as a separate form of discourse, succeeding in making its philosophical arguments only to the degree that it gives up being a novel.

《老实人》是一部雄辩的社会文献，它揭露了欧洲殖民探索和定居在精神和人道主义方面的失败。它对欧洲输出自身饱受摧残的文化的描写，其尖锐程度丝毫不亚于任何二十世纪的革命檄文。书中描绘的世界被贪婪、残忍、社会不公和盲目所污染和摧毁。无论老实人走到哪里，欧洲人都已到过那里，并对其进行了破坏；或者，当地居民（如埃尔多拉多）采取了预防措施来保护自己。《老实人》中的许多内容都带有真理的意味。此外，它当然也代表了其所处的时代——十八世纪法国启蒙运动——其反教权主义和在许多方面体现的人文主义思想，以及其愤世嫉俗的一面。我第一次读这本书是在九年级，当时是作为一项作业，我一个字都没看懂，但书中许多关于苦难和残缺的描写却让我震惊不已，并深深地印在了我的脑海里。或许学校之所以布置阅读这本书，是因为它篇幅短小，情节紧凑，但它并非小说，因为“主人公”缺乏“斗争”——康迪德行动迅速，但他缺乏能引发读者共鸣或同情的内心世界。康迪德与小说并存，成为一种独立的论述形式，它之所以能够成功地阐述其哲学论点，恰恰是因为它放弃了小说的身份。

16. Tobias Smollett. The Expedition of Humphry Clinker

16. 托比亚斯·斯莫利特，《汉弗莱·克林克探险队》

(1771; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1983), 336 PP.

（1771 年；重印，纽约：W. W. NORTON，1983 年），336 页。

Now mostly unread, Tobias Smollett was a famous writer in his day, the author of five well-received novels and many volumes of historical and political commentary. Like Defoe and Fielding, he was first a polemicist and only later a novelist. Unlike Defoe and Fielding, Smollett was born in Scotland and trained at the University of Edinburgh to be a doctor. He was regularly referred to by his contemporaries as “Dr. Smollett.” In the eighteenth century, Scotland and the University of Glasgow were the home of what was known as “Scottish Empiricism”—a philosophical and scientific school of thought that has been highly influential in shaping the modern world around objectivity, pragmatism, and systematic observation. Its most famous product, of course, was Adam Smith, author of The Wealth of Nations. Dr. Smollett was well known for being crusty and Scottish and skeptical, and one thing that differentiates Humphry Clinker from most comic English novels is that it doesn't make the resolution of the gentle young lovers’ romance the sole end of the plot, but accords it a rather small proportion of the narrative, setting it into the context of the differing concerns of other characters, who all have their own intentions, plans, and learning tasks. It therefore has considerable crusty and skeptical mature appeal.

托比亚斯·斯莫利特的作品如今鲜为人知，但他在当时却是一位名家，著有五部广受好评的小说以及多卷历史和政治评论。与笛福和菲尔丁一样，他最初是一位论战家，后来才成为小说家。与笛福和菲尔丁不同的是，斯莫利特出生于苏格兰，并在爱丁堡大学接受医学训练。他的同时代人常常称他为“斯莫利特博士”。十八世纪，苏格兰和格拉斯哥大学是“苏格兰经验主义”的中心——这一哲学和科学思想流派对现代世界的塑造产生了深远的影响，它强调客观性、实用主义和系统观察。当然，其最著名的代表人物是《国富论》的作者亚当·斯密。斯莫利特博士以其古怪的性格、苏格兰式的特质和怀疑精神而闻名。与大多数英国喜剧小说不同的是，《汉弗莱·克林克》并没有将这对年轻恋人的爱情结局作为故事的唯一终点，而是将其置于叙事的一小部分，并将其置于其他角色的不同关注点之中。这些角色都有各自的意图、计划和学习任务。因此，这部小说具有相当成熟的、略带古怪和怀疑精神的吸引力。

A family sets out upon a long journey. The principals are Matthew Bramble, a country squire in Wales; his sister Tabitha, a spinster of about forty-five; their nephew, Jery, who has just left Oxford and is considering his career; their niece, Lydia, who has left her school and is in love with an unsuitable young man; and Tabitha's maid, Win, somewhat older than Lydia, along to take care of Tabitha. The ostensible purpose of the journey is to take the waters of various spas in an effort to relieve Matthew's ills, which seem to be digestive. Their longest sojourns are in Bath, London, Yorkshire, and Edinburgh, but there are plenty of stops in between. Each of the five writes letters to someone at home, and these letters constitute the text of the novel. Humphry is a character they encounter on the way, who links up with their family in a surprising plot twist.

一家人踏上了漫长的旅程。主人公是威尔士乡绅马修·布兰布尔；他四十五岁左右的妹妹塔比莎，一位未婚女子；刚从牛津大学毕业、正在考虑未来职业的侄子杰里；辍学后爱上一个不合适的年轻人的侄女莉迪亚；以及塔比莎的女仆温，她比莉迪亚年长一些，负责照顾塔比莎。此行的表面目的是前往各个温泉疗养，以缓解马修的消化系统疾病。他们停留时间最长的地方是巴斯、伦敦、约克郡和爱丁堡，但沿途还有许多其他停留点。五人各自给家里的亲人写信，这些信件构成了小说的主体。汉弗莱是他们在旅途中遇到的一个人物，他与这个家庭有着意想不到的联系。

The greatness of Smollett's novel is in the simplicity of his formal idea. Each writer has his or her own concerns, his or her own style, and his or her own observations. The five sets of letters work together to progress the strands of the plot and to comment upon the various scenes the travelers encounter. Most of the adventures are told from more than a single point of view, and the effect is to reduce the dominance of the narrator and create the illusion of a more inclusive and various world through which all travel together, no one's opinions taking precedence over those of the others. This, of course, is in striking contrast to both Fielding and Sterne. Smollett is no less than they a man of strong opinions and partisan feelings, but his polemical purpose is forwarded indirectly, by his molding of the plot and his depiction of what his narrators see and do, rather than by assertions of a strong narrator. The result is wonderfully sophisticated and almost modern—and as an exponent of a school of thought that has come to dominate the way we see the world, Smollett seems less dated to us than his contemporaries.

斯莫列特小说的伟大之处在于其形式构思的简洁。每位作者都有各自的关注点、风格和观察视角。五组信件相互交织，推动情节发展，并对旅行者们遇到的各种场景进行评述。大部分冒险故事都采用多视角叙述，这种手法削弱了叙述者的主导地位，营造出一个更加包容多元的世界，所有人共同穿梭其中，彼此观点平等。这与菲尔丁和斯特恩的风格截然不同。斯莫列特同样是一位观点鲜明、立场鲜明的作家，但他并非通过强有力的叙述者来表达自己的观点，而是通过对情节的巧妙构思和对叙述者所见所闻的细致刻画，间接地展现其论辩目的。其结果精妙绝伦，几乎达到了现代的水平——作为主导我们看待世界方式的一种思想流派的代表人物，斯莫利特在我们看来似乎比他的同时代人更不落伍。

Humphry Clinkers complexity works by seeming simple; its profundity works by seeming mundane. The characters tell their stories and express their opinions, while the author constructs the relationships between the themes and the motifs in the background, there to be understood by the astute reader but not forced upon her. The novel seems to be an entertaining story or a typical eighteenth-century travel narrative, but really it is, among other things, a story of spiritual redemption and reconciliation, a story of the re-creation of the pastoral order and of the right order of society. It takes up the same question as Candide —how can we understand the world and how can we live in it?—and it gives a similar but better worked-out answer: cultivate the estates we are given, avoid ambition and luxury, and enter into relationships with those who are given us to love, even if they are not very appealing. Smollett successfully solves the paradox of the novel form—how can the specific lives of ordinary characters represent the commonality of human life, both as it's lived in society and as it's lived subjectively? The adventures the characters have on their expedition add up to maps of the inner world and of the outer world—every episode is both plausible and meaningful. But by contrast to Candide , many of the episodes are routine—at one point, Matthew's rest is disturbed by some men who are playing musical instruments on the staircase of his boardinghouse. At another, he is mistakenly saved from drowning by Humphry, who interprets Matthew's gasp at the frigidity of the sea as a cry for help. At another point, Humphry catches sight of Win's bare buttocks as she is climbing down a ladder, escaping a fire, and falls in love with her. Every incident is plausible and funny and realistic, which is no doubt why some readers thought Smollett was the funniest writer of his day. But his jokes are subtle, inviting laughter rather than demanding it.

汉弗莱·克林克的复杂性在于其看似简单的表象；其深刻性则在于其看似平凡的表象。人物讲述着各自的故事，表达着各自的观点，而作者则在背景中构建着主题与意象之间的关联，这些关联等待着敏锐的读者去领悟，而非强加于人。这部小说看似一部引人入胜的故事，或是一部典型的十八世纪游记，但实际上，它讲述的不仅仅是精神的救赎与和解，更是一个关于田园秩序与社会秩序重建的故事。它探讨了与《老实人》相同的问题——我们如何理解这个世界，又如何在其中生存？——并给出了一个相似但更为完善的答案：耕耘我们所拥有的土地，摒弃野心和奢侈，与那些命中注定要爱的人建立关系，即便他们并不那么讨人喜欢。斯莫利特成功地解决了小说形式的悖论——普通人物的具体生活如何才能代表人类生活的共通性，既包括社会层面的生活，也包括主观层面的生活？人物在探险途中的种种经历，构成了一幅幅内心世界和外部世界的地图——每一个片段都既合情合理又意义深远。但与《老实人》不同的是，许多情节都显得平淡无奇——比如，马修的休息被几个在他寄宿公寓楼梯上演奏乐器的男人打扰；又比如，汉弗莱误将马修因海水冰冷而发出的喘息声当成了求救信号，救了他一命；再比如，温从梯子上爬下来逃离火灾时，汉弗莱瞥见了她裸露的臀部，便爱上了她。每个情节都合情合理、滑稽可笑、贴近现实，这无疑也是一些读者认为斯莫利特是当时最幽默的作家的原因。但他的笑话很含蓄，是引导读者发笑，而不是强迫读者笑。

Humphry Clinker was Smollett's last novel, and like all mature work, it was written with the instinctive knowledge that the author no longer had to force it—that his style naturally expressed his views, and that it could do so with artless subtlety. It is not so much that the writer now trusts the reader to be alert to every word and intention, more that he now truly knows what he wants to say and how to say it—he no longer has to say it twice for it to be clear to himself. Additionally, Smollett's novel is forgiving and open-hearted. The ridiculous figures have their say and their achievement of self-knowledge just as the attractive figures do. Baser human motivations are forgiven—when Matthew's sister, Tabby, finds a man to marry her, the fact that both are marrying for practical as well as romantic reasons is acknowledged. After the triple wedding, in a moment possibly unique in English fiction, Smollett remarks (in the voice of Jery) upon the physical evidence that each character has enjoyed the sexual connection with his or her new spouse—the gentle lovers with their eyes, the middle-aged couple through attentive and exuberant behavior, and Humphry (illegitimate) and Win (a maid), through words (Humphry says, “For what we have received, Lord make us thankful”). Such an acknowledgment of the joys—and godliness—of sexuality combines with the usual English sentiment at the end of a comic novel that at last the money and the love are brought together to add an unusually humane strand to the history of English narrative.

《汉弗莱·克林克》是斯莫利特的最后一部小说，如同所有成熟作品一样，它源于作者的本能认知：他不再需要刻意雕琢，他的文风自然而然地表达了他的观点，而且表达得毫不矫揉造作。这并非意味着作者现在相信读者能够敏锐地捕捉到每一个字句和意图，而是因为他现在真正明白自己想要表达什么以及如何表达——他不再需要反复赘述才能让自己完全理解。此外，斯莫利特的小说宽容而真挚。书中那些滑稽可笑的人物和那些魅力四射的人物一样，都有自己的表达方式，也都有自己对自我的认知。小说对人性的卑劣动机也予以宽容——当马修的妹妹塔比找到结婚对象时，小说承认两人结婚既有现实因素，也有浪漫情怀。在三方婚礼之后，斯莫利特（借杰瑞之口）以一种或许在英国小说中独一无二的方式，评论了每个角色与新婚伴侣享受性爱的种种迹象——温柔的情侣用眼神交流，中年夫妇用体贴而热情的举止，以及汉弗莱（私生子）和温（女仆）用言语表达（汉弗莱说：“主啊，愿我们因所拥有的一切而感恩”）。这种对性爱之乐——以及神圣性——的认可，与英国喜剧小说结尾常见的感伤情怀相得益彰：金钱与爱情最终交织在一起，为英国叙事史增添了一抹难得的人文情怀。

Another feature of Humphry Clinker worth remarking upon is that it really does work as a reliable social document. Because Bramble and Jery (and, of course, the author) are interested in the world they travel through and are observant (at the University of Edinburgh, Dr. Smollett would have been trained to be particular and systematic in his observations), there is a great deal in the novel about how people lived in eighteenth-century Britain. Matthew discourses on architecture, medicine, politics, society, customs, modes of travel, and much else. To an American it is particularly interesting to note that while you could read Fielding, Richardson, and Sterne and never know that the North American colonies existed, Smollett makes one of his most interesting characters a man who has been to America, has been captured and scalped by the Indians, and is planning to return there.

《汉弗莱·克林克》的另一个值得一提的特点是，它确实是一部可靠的社会文献。由于布兰布尔和杰里（当然还有作者本人）对他们游历的世界充满兴趣，并且观察入微（斯莫利特博士在爱丁堡大学接受的训练使他能够细致而系统地观察），小说中大量描写了十八世纪英国人的生活。马修探讨了建筑、医学、政治、社会、习俗、交通方式等等诸多方面。对美国人来说，尤其值得注意的是，尽管你可能读过菲尔丁、理查森和斯特恩的作品，却从未意识到北美殖民地的存在，而斯莫利特笔下最引人入胜的角色之一，却是一位去过美洲、被印第安人俘虏并剥去头皮，且正计划重返美洲的男子。

17. Choderlos de Laclos Les Liaisons dangereuses

17. Choderlos de Laclos，《危险关系》

TRANS. P. W. K. STONE (1781; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1961), 393 PP.

P. W. K. STONE 译（1781 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1961 年），393 页。

When Laclos conceived Les Liaisons dangereuses , he wanted to create a sensation, and when he published it, he succeeded. It was a great succs du scandale and sold many copies. Some twenty years after Laclos himself died in the Napoleonic Wars ( 1802 ), the novel was tried in a criminal court, condemned, and burned. Laclos, by the way, married at forty-six and later became known for his life of conventional family happiness.

拉克洛创作《危险关系》时，意在引起轰动，而当他出版这部小说时，他的确做到了。这部小说引起了巨大的轰动，销量极佳。在拉克洛本人于拿破仑战争中阵亡约二十年后（1802年），这部小说被送上刑事法庭，最终被判有罪并焚毁。顺便一提，拉克洛在四十六岁时结婚，后来以他传统的家庭幸福生活而闻名。

The premise of the novel is that two experienced libertines, the vicomte de Valmont and the marquise de Merteuil, set out to manipulate the relationships of several of their associates, both for fun and for revenge. The marquise wishes to get back at a former lover by compromising his intended bride, and Valmont wishes to seduce a legen-darily virtuous woman merely to exercise his powers. The tangle of intrigue and deception that ensues leaves two dead, one in a convent, one disgraced, and one in exile. That Valmont and Merteuil will succeed in their seductions is never really in doubt, so one problem of the novel is lack of suspense, but the compensation is the intricacy of the arguments each character puts forth to support his or her position and the complex psychology of each of the intersecting relationships.

小说的前提是，两位经验丰富的浪荡子爵瓦尔蒙和梅特伊侯爵夫人，为了取乐和复仇，开始操纵几位同伴的感情关系。侯爵夫人想通过破坏前情人的未婚妻来报复他，而瓦尔蒙则想勾引一位传说中贞洁的女子，仅仅是为了炫耀自己的权势。随之而来的阴谋和欺骗交织在一起，导致两人死亡，一人被送进修道院，一人身败名裂，一人流亡他乡。瓦尔蒙和梅特伊的勾引最终能否成功几乎毫无悬念，因此小说的一个问题是缺乏悬念，但其优点在于每个角色为支持自身立场而提出的论证都十分精妙，以及错综复杂的人际关系所展现出的心理描写。

Like Humphry Clinker, Les Liaisons dangereuses is composed of letters written during several months by different characters, though the recipients of these letters are also these characters (the recipients of the Smollett letters do not figure in the plot of that novel). The letters therefore not only report events and comment on them, they also precipitate events. The characters’ secret intentions and the forms of polite discourse of the era dictate that much of what the letters communicate is insincere or exaggerated, but Laclos is superb at juxtaposing letters to reveal layers of deception and imply the deeper story (or not—the true feelings, especially, of Valmont are enticingly mysterious; perhaps he is the heartless libertine that he purports to be in his letters to the marquise, perhaps he truly loves the prsidente de Tourvel beyond his expectations and is ashamed of how he has treated her and is glad to die in the end). The reader has only clues to any interpretation. The mysteries surrounding the marquise are fewer and less interesting, but the main ones are: Does she really love the vicomte from the beginning? Is the whole plot simply a way to win him back? Is her cool manner simply a coquettish cover?

与《汉弗莱·克林克》一样，《危险关系》也是由不同人物在几个月内写成的信件组成，但收信人也正是这些人物（斯莫列特信件的收信人并未出现在该小说的情节中）。因此，这些信件不仅记录和评论事件，还推动了事件的发生。人物的隐秘意图以及当时的礼仪规范决定了信件中许多内容并非真心实意或有所夸张，但拉克洛巧妙地将信件并置，揭示出层层欺骗，暗示着更深层次的故事（或者并非如此——尤其是瓦尔蒙的真实感受，充满神秘感，引人入胜；或许他真如在写给侯爵夫人的信中所说的那样冷酷无情，或许他真的爱着图尔维尔夫人，远超预期，并为自己对待她的方式感到羞愧，最终欣然赴死）。读者只能从线索中寻找解读的契机。围绕侯爵夫人的谜团不多，也无趣得多，但主要的谜团是：她从一开始就真的爱着子爵吗？整个故事是否只是为了赢回他的心？她冷淡的态度是否只是故作妩媚的伪装？

Both Valmont and the marquise seem to be respected members of society, and they live in accordance with the self-contradictory principles laid down in The Heptameron. Indeed, Valmont might be quoting the assembled party of the earlier work when he writes, “I know a hundred, a thousand ways of robbing a woman of her reputation; but whenever I have tried to think how she might save herself, I have never been able to think of a single possibility.” Then he adds, “You yourself… whose strategy is masterly, have triumphed a hundred times… more through good luck than good judgment.” The marquise sets out her ideas and strategies in another long letter that also may be considered a response to the untenable position of women in a society where men feel obliged to prey upon their bodies and feelings in every way they can and then to humiliate them. Her method is to set up scenarios where any sort of subsequent gossip by the man is so implausible in the context of the woman's reputation for virtue that he dare not say anything. She has trained herself to hide every feeling and manipulate every circumstance—she demonstrates her methods with a man Valmont meets in society and dislikes. As a result of her plot, he is thrown in prison and socially destroyed.

瓦尔蒙和侯爵夫人似乎都是受人尊敬的社会成员，他们奉行着《七日谈》中自相矛盾的原则。事实上，瓦尔蒙在信中写道：“我知道一百种、一千种败坏女人名誉的方法；但每当我试图思考她如何自保时，却从未想到任何办法。”他或许正是引用了前作中众人的话语。随后他又补充道：“你本人……你的策略炉火纯青，已经百般得逞……与其说是出于智慧，不如说是运气。”侯爵夫人在另一封长信中阐述了她的想法和策略，这封信也可以被视为对女性在社会中处境艰难的回应——在这个社会里，男性觉得有义务想方设法地掠夺女性的身体和情感，然后羞辱她们。她的方法是精心设计一些情境，让男人在女性的贞洁名声面前，任何流言蜚语都显得如此荒谬，以至于他们不敢妄加评论。她训练自己隐藏所有情感，操控一切局面——她用瓦尔蒙在社交场合遇到的一个他很讨厌的男人来展示自己的手段。结果，这个男人被投入监狱，社会地位也彻底崩塌了。

Valmont and the marquise are certainly unsympathetic characters, but through the reader's continuous exposure to how they think, they achieve a certain appeal. They are not, perhaps, the most intelligent people in their circle, but they are the most rational in that they discount all emotions even as they are feeling them, and they recognize that the society they live in is merciless but also the only one they value. The portrait their letters paint is convincing (especially in light of what else we have read of the pre-Revolutionary French aristocracy). Additionally, the world they live in is not unrecognizable. French literature from The Heptameron through Zola is continuous—nasty people motivated by greed, selfishness, lust, and schadenfreude doing nasty things with wit but no good nature, corrosively honest except in personal relationships, where secrecy and deceit rule. It is hard to know whether Laclos's avowed intention to create a stir is the intention of all French novelists, but while English novels, especially eighteenth- and nineteenth-century ones, depict an England that is perhaps more appealing than England truly was, French novels depict a nation of vipers. One can only hope that for all that French novelists present themselves as social documentarians, they were actually just trying to make money.
