瓦尔蒙和侯爵夫人无疑是令人难以同情的角色，但读者通过不断了解他们的思维方式，却能感受到他们身上某种独特的魅力。他们或许并非同辈中最聪明的人，但却是最理性的，因为他们即便身处情感之中，也能将其抛诸脑后；他们也明白自己所处的社会残酷无情，却也是他们唯一珍视的社会。他们的书信描绘出的形象令人信服（尤其是在结合我们对法国大革命前贵族阶层的其他了解之后）。此外，他们所处的世界并非完全陌生。从《七日谈》到左拉，法国文学一直延续着这样的主题——一群被贪婪、自私、欲望和幸灾乐祸所驱使的卑劣之徒，他们用机智而非善意行恶，除了在人际关系中，他们诚实得如同腐蚀剂，而在人际关系中，秘密和欺骗才是王道。很难说拉克洛公开宣称的制造轰动的意图是否代表了所有法国小说家的意图，但英国小说，尤其是十八、十九世纪的小说，所描绘的英国或许比真实的英国更具吸引力，而法国小说则描绘了一个充满毒蛇的国家。人们只能希望，尽管法国小说家标榜自己是社会纪实作家，但他们实际上只是想赚钱而已。

18. The Marquis de Sade. Justine

18.萨德侯爵。贾斯汀

(1791; REPR., NEW YORK: GROVE PRESS, 1965), 290 PP.

（1791 年；重印，纽约：格罗夫出版社，1965 年），290 页。

In the context of Pamela, Tom Jones , and Candide, Justine is eminently recognizable. A young girl is left without protectors in the world. She embarks upon a forced journey, seeking asylum and some means to support herself. Like Pamela, Cunegonde, and Sophia Western, she is betrayed by those she trusts and whose job is to protect her. She is raped or threatened with rape. Many of those she meets are happy to sell her to the rich and powerful. Her task is to preserve her virtue and her life, or, if she can't, to develop some sort of worldview that accounts for her choice to accept what has happened to her or not to accept it and die. To the question of whether a woman is to be allowed to be an agent and live freely, de Sade answers, “Only if she is willing to abide by the chaotic system of exploit or be exploited that is the rule of modern life.” His answer is not different from the answers of the other authors, only more extreme. Several women characters do manage to prosper, at least temporarily, but to do so, they not only give up their sexual virtue, they also commit arson, infanticide, and murder; they steal, betray, and destroy out of necessity and gratuitously. The men characters generally not only survive but get wealthier and more powerful—the young count who murders his aunt for the inheritance becomes wealthy beyond his dreams; the doctor who dissects his living daughter after raping her repeatedly becomes a respected government official; the monk who is the torturer and murderer of uncounted abducted girls is made head of the entire Benedictine order. Justine, whose only desires are to keep her virtue and find something useful to do, is condemned to go from one enslavement to another, until, at last having disburdened herself of her story, she is killed by a bolt of lightning.

在《帕梅拉》、《汤姆·琼斯》和《老实人》的语境下，朱斯蒂娜的形象显而易见。一个年轻女孩在世上孤立无援，被迫踏上旅程，寻求庇护和谋生之道。如同帕梅拉、库内贡德和索菲娅·韦斯特恩一样，她被自己信任、本应保护她的人背叛。她遭到强奸或被强奸的威胁。她遇到的许多人都乐于将她卖给权贵。她的任务是保全贞洁和性命，或者，如果无法做到，就必须建立某种世界观，以解释她为何选择接受或拒绝这一切，最终走向死亡。对于女性是否应该被允许成为自主者并自由生活的问题，萨德的回答是：“只有当她愿意遵守现代生活那套剥削或被剥削的混乱体系时，才有可能。”他的答案与其他作家的答案并无二致，只是更加极端。一些女性角色确实设法获得了成功，至少是暂时的，但为了做到这一点，她们不仅放弃了贞洁，还犯下了纵火、杀婴和谋杀的罪行；她们出于无奈或无缘无故地偷窃、背叛和破坏。男性角色通常不仅活了下来，而且还变得更加富有和强大——为了继承遗产而谋杀姑姑的年轻伯爵变得富可敌国；在多次强奸女儿后解剖其尸体的医生成为了受人尊敬的政府官员；折磨并杀害了无数被绑架女孩的僧侣成为了整个本笃会的首领。而朱斯蒂娜，她唯一的愿望就是保持贞洁并找到一些有用的事情做，却注定要从一个奴役之地沦落到另一个奴役之地，直到最后，在她终于倾诉了自己的故事之后，被一道闪电击中身亡。

De Sade relates all of Justine's torments in a tone of excited, sentimental relish, as, for example, when Justine witnesses the torture of a younger girl at the monastery: “Rodin contemplates… his inflamed eye roves, his hands dare profane the flowers his cruelties are about to wither; it all takes place directly before us, not a detail can escape us: now the libertine opens and peers into, now he closes up again those dainty features which enchant him” (p. 537 ). Such incidents alternate with cool discussions about her fate that Justine has with almost all of her tormentors—for example, the count of a remote chteau. His particular fetish is bloodletting. Justine's job becomes taking care of his fourth young wife as he prepares to murder her. He remarks to Justine (who is traveling under the name Thérèse), “How are you justified, pray tell me, Thérèse, in asserting that a husband lies under the obligation to make his wife happy? and what titles dares this woman cite in order to extort this happiness from her husband?” (p. 645 ).

德·萨德以一种激动而感伤的口吻叙述了朱斯蒂娜所遭受的一切折磨，例如，当朱斯蒂娜目睹修道院里一个年轻女孩遭受酷刑时：“罗丹凝视着……他那充满怒火的目光四处游移，他的双手竟敢亵渎那些即将被他残暴折磨而枯萎的花朵；这一切都发生在我们眼前，没有一个细节能逃过我们的眼睛：一会儿，这个放荡不羁的浪荡子睁开双眼窥视，一会儿，他又合上双眼，那张令他着迷的精致脸庞”（第537页）。这类场景与朱斯蒂娜和几乎所有折磨她的人——例如，一位偏僻城堡的伯爵——之间关于她命运的冷静讨论交替出现。这位伯爵尤其痴迷于放血。朱斯蒂娜的任务变成了照顾他的第四任年轻妻子，因为他正准备谋杀她。他对朱斯蒂娜（化名特蕾丝）说：“请告诉我，特蕾丝，你凭什么断言丈夫有义务让妻子幸福？这个女人又凭什么敢引用什么理由来从丈夫那里勒索幸福呢？”（第645页）。

Nevertheless, Justine (Rousseau declared that any girl who read a single page of the novel would be lost) is not nihilistic. The key to the novel is that since Justine's world is entirely without fellow feeling, what happens to her is impersonal. People do not betray her and torture her out of personal enmity or malignity, they do so because they feel no connection to her or to anyone else. Justine becomes a little ridiculous because she is always throwing herself upon the mercy of men who have tortured her in the past, but she does so because her psychology is the virtuous mirror of their vice—she cannot unlearn the sense of common humanity that they cannot learn. It can hardly be said that virtue triumphs at the end of Justine , or even that Justine attains a Voltairean truce with the world. But one character does point out that given the world they both inhabit, the fact that she is still alive, vigorous, and virtuous (as opposed to virginal) is something to be grateful for, almost a sign of having been among the elect. Justine and some of the other destroyed women characters retain their sense of who they are and what they believe to the end of their lives—examples of the inability of Sadist culture to annihilate all humanity in spite of its enormous power. Justine never betrays herself; her mind is never changed; the sympathy of the reader is never lost.

然而，朱斯蒂娜（卢梭曾断言，任何女孩只要读过这本小说一页就会迷失）并非虚无主义者。这部小说的关键在于，由于朱斯蒂娜的世界完全缺乏同情心，发生在她身上的事都是非个人的。人们背叛她、折磨她并非出于个人恩怨或恶意，而是因为他们与她或任何人之间都没有任何联系。朱斯蒂娜总是乞求那些曾经折磨过她的人的怜悯，这让她显得有些滑稽可笑，但她之所以这样做，是因为她的心理是他们罪恶的一面美德的镜子——她无法忘记他们无法学会的那种人性共通的感受。很难说在《朱斯蒂娜》的结尾，美德取得了胜利，甚至朱斯蒂娜与世界达成了伏尔泰式的和解。但其中一个角色指出，鉴于她们所处的世界，她依然活着、精力充沛、品德高尚（而非贞洁），这本身就值得庆幸，几乎是天选之人的标志。贾斯汀和其他一些饱受摧残的女性角色，至死都保持着自我认知和信仰——这正体现了虐待狂文化即便拥有强大的力量，也无法彻底毁灭全人类。贾斯汀从未背叛自己；她的思想从未改变；读者也始终对她抱有同情。

It is indeed true that Justine's adventures are told very graphically, but what is more shocking about them than the acts committed is that they offer repeated and insistent evidence of the absence of any feeling of shared humanity in the world of pre-Revolutionary France. Justine's torturers (a gang of thieves, a young count, a group of monks, a counterfeiter, a doctor, a financier, and others) constitute a catalog of the French ruling class and of masculine power. Everyone Justine meets is more than without pity—is, rather, actively cruel, vicious, deceitful, selfish, and cold. When they exercise their intelligence and imagination, they do so only to invent more perfect methods of torture, that either cause more pain or cause pain to more women. Men are not shown as being capable of feeling pain or of empathizing with the pain of women. Had Justine been written by a woman, it could well have functioned as a revolutionary political document, a real man-hating polemic, but the context of de Sade's other writings casts ambiguity over his intentions for what seems to have been his favorite novel.

诚然，朱斯蒂娜的遭遇描写得十分生动，但比这些暴行本身更令人震惊的是，它们反复且有力地证明了法国大革命前夕社会中人性的缺失。折磨朱斯蒂娜的施虐者（一伙盗贼、一位年轻的伯爵、一群僧侣、一个伪钞制造者、一位医生、一位金融家等等）构成了法国统治阶级和男性权力的缩影。朱斯蒂娜遇到的每个人都冷酷无情——他们不仅没有怜悯之心，反而残忍、恶毒、狡诈、自私、冷酷。他们运用智慧和想象力，只是为了发明更完美的酷刑手段，要么造成更大的痛苦，要么让更多的女性遭受痛苦。男性似乎完全没有感受到痛苦，也无法体会女性的痛苦。如果《朱斯蒂娜》是由一位女性创作的，它很可能成为一部革命性的政治文献，一部真正仇恨男性的论战作品，但萨德的其他作品的背景使人们对他创作这部似乎是他最喜欢的小说的意图产生了疑问。

As a social document, Justine perhaps helps explain the chaotic violence of the French Revolution and is thus an important book for students of European history. It portrays as a given the absolute selfish corruption of an entire society and foretells certain attitudes that have become features of modern life—the idea that destructive acts are part of the natural order, the idea that the winnowing out of the weak is positive (the free market, anyone?), the idea that certain populations are expendable because they produce nothing the society wants, the idea that because customs differ from country to country, all virtues and vices are relative. Justine is as full of argument as graphic violence. In fact, one of the charms Justine has for her tormentors is her persistent desire to convince them of the error of their ways. There is an odd psychological truth to this—they not only want to exercise power, they also want to view themselves as right. Justine's many debates with her captors give the novel much of its formal sophistication, because through their voices and arguments, Justine's tormentors become characters rather than figures.

作为一部社会文献，《朱斯蒂娜》或许有助于解释法国大革命的混乱暴力，因此对欧洲历史研究者而言是一部重要的著作。它将整个社会的绝对自私腐败描绘成理所当然，并预言了某些已成为现代生活特征的态度——破坏性行为是自然秩序的一部分，淘汰弱者是积极的（自由市场就是个例子），某些群体因为无法生产社会所需而被视为可有可无，以及由于各国风俗不同，所有美德与恶习都是相对的。《朱斯蒂娜》既充满了论证，也充满了血腥暴力。事实上，朱斯蒂娜对折磨她的人的魅力之一，就在于她坚持不懈地想要说服他们认识到自己的错误。这其中蕴含着一种奇特的心理真相——他们不仅渴望行使权力，也渴望认为自己是正确的。贾斯汀与绑架者的多次辩论赋予了这部小说形式上的精妙之处，因为通过他们的声音和争论，贾斯汀的折磨者变成了角色，而不是人物。

The marquis de Sade was a contradictory man, as most authors are. He was not as isolated or powerful or wealthy as the male characters of Justine. Nor does he seem to have been as impervious to the claims of virtue, since the woman to whom he dedicated Justine seems to have been a long-term companion with a reputation for virtue that de Sade acknowledged in several letters as well as in his dedication. Authors often fail to live up to their narrative personae—de Sade seems to have aspired to a purity of viciousness as others have aspired to wit or charm or benevolence.

萨德侯爵是个矛盾体，就像大多数作家一样。他不像《朱斯蒂娜》中的男性角色那样孤僻、权势滔天或富甲一方。他似乎也并非对美德的标榜无动于衷，因为他将《朱斯蒂娜》献给的那位女性，似乎是一位与他相伴多年的伴侣，且以品德高尚著称，萨德在多封信件以及献词中都对此表示认可。作家往往无法完全符合他们笔下的人物形象——萨德似乎追求的是一种纯粹的邪恶，正如其他人追求的是机智、魅力或仁慈一样。

19. Sir Walter Scott. The Tale of Old Mortality

19. 沃尔特·斯科特爵士，《老莫塔利的故事》

(1816; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1999), 353 PP.

（1816 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1999 年），353 页。

The night before he fights the climactic duel in A Hero of Our Time (see below), Pechorin, Lermontov's protagonist, picks up a novel to while away the time. He writes, “It was Walter Scott's Old Mortality. At first it was an effort to read, but I was soon carried away by the magic of the tale. The Scottish bard must surely be rewarded in heaven for every moment of pleasure given by his book.” This excellent review is the least ironic and most wholehearted remark the embittered Romantic Pechorin makes.

在《当代英雄》（见下文）中，主人公佩乔林在决斗前夜（也就是他即将面对的那场高潮决斗的前夜），为了消磨时间，拿起了一本小说。他写道：“是沃尔特·斯科特的《老莫塔利蒂》。起初读起来有些吃力，但很快我就被故事的魔力所吸引。这位苏格兰吟游诗人一定能因他的作品带给我的每一刻愉悦而在天堂得到奖赏。” 这篇精彩的书评，是愤世嫉俗的浪漫主义者佩乔林所作的最不带讽刺意味、也最真挚的一番话。

The Tale of Old Mortality is part of Scott's tetralogy of novels about the history of Scotland in the seventeenth century, one for each of the four regions of the country—the Borders, the Highlands, the West, and Fife. The Tale of Old Mortality , the second of the four, concerns the 1679 insurrection of the Presbyterian Scottish Calvinists against King Charles II of England and Scotland. The first three-quarters of the book follows the fates of several characters caught up in the conflict— Henry Morton, a young moderate Protestant; the woman he loves (Edith), who is the daughter of royalist aristocrats; Henry's rival Lord Evandale, also a royalist; a career soldier, Claverhouse, who commands the regular troops; and a career rebel, Balfour, who initiates the action by murdering the archbishop of St. Andrews. Although the historical event is of minor importance, and the love story a bit perfunctory, Old Mortality is insistently compelling for the depth and complexity of Scott's understanding of the personal and political implications of the rebellion and for the psychological astuteness with which he draws the characters. It also resonates with events at the beginning of the twenty-first century in a way that at first seems almost uncanny.

《老莫塔利蒂的故事》是斯科特以十七世纪苏格兰历史为背景的四部曲小说之一，每部小说分别讲述了苏格兰的四个地区——边境地区、高地、西部和法夫——的故事。《老莫塔利蒂的故事》是四部曲中的第二部，讲述了1679年苏格兰长老会加尔文教徒反抗英格兰和苏格兰国王查理二世的起义。本书的前四分之三篇幅围绕着几位卷入这场冲突的人物展开：年轻的温和派新教徒亨利·莫顿；他所爱的女人伊迪丝，一位保皇派贵族的女儿；亨利的对手，同样是保皇派的埃文代尔勋爵；指挥正规军的职业军人克拉弗豪斯；以及刺杀圣安德鲁斯大主教、挑起这场起义的职业叛乱分子贝尔福。尽管历史事件本身并不重要，爱情故事也略显敷衍，《旧日死亡》却凭借斯科特对这场叛乱的个人和政治意义的深刻而复杂的理解，以及他对人物心理刻画的敏锐洞察力，而引人入胜。此外，它与二十一世纪初发生的事件之间也存在着一种起初看似不可思议的共鸣。

Scott was born in 1771 and was thoroughly a member of the revolutionary generation. The great news of his youth and early adulthood, when he was writing his famous poems and beginning his novels, was the French Revolution and the career of Napoleon, who was finally defeated by the British just before Scott began writing his tetralogy on factional strife in seventeenth-century Scotland. “What is a revolution for?” and “How far is it permissible to go?” are the questions that Scott addresses in The Tale of Old Mortality.

斯科特生于1771年，是革命一代的典型代表。在他青年和成年早期，也就是他创作著名诗歌和开始小说创作的时期，最重大的消息莫过于法国大革命和拿破仑的崛起。就在斯科特开始创作以十七世纪苏格兰派系斗争为背景的四部曲之前，拿破仑最终被英国击败。“革命的目的是什么？”以及“革命的底线在哪里？”是斯科特在《旧日死亡的故事》中探讨的问题。

Scott's literary style is both limpid and nimble. He effortlessly moves among all the required dialects—the thick Scottish of the peasant characters, which almost requires formal translation (there are extensive notes), the elevated formal English of the royalist characters, and the various colorful mixes of the two. He is especially remarkable at reproducing the biblically influenced testifying and preaching of the more extreme members of the rebel party. The narrative style that binds it all together is witty, intelligent, and fast-paced. All in all, there is nothing at all tiresome or even old-fashioned in Old Mortality. Scott has caught just the right tone of organized conversational intimacy— not unlike the tone of his contemporary Jane Austen.

斯科特的文风既流畅又灵动。他驾驭各种方言游刃有余——从农民角色浓重的苏格兰口音（几乎需要正式翻译，书中附有大量注释），到保皇党角色高雅的正式英语，以及两者之间丰富多彩的混合。他尤其擅长刻画叛军中极端分子受圣经影响的证词和布道。贯穿全书的叙事风格诙谐、睿智且节奏明快。总而言之，《老莫里蒂利》丝毫没有令人厌倦或老套之处。斯科特精准地捕捉到了那种条理清晰、亲切自然的对话氛围——与他同时代的简·奥斯汀的风格颇为相似。

For the modern reader, the history known to Scott and his contemporaries is largely unknown, so the plot has an added dimension of suspense, but there is a kind of gloomy familiarity to it—a band of “criminals” or “revolutionaries” (depending upon your point of view) happen upon a “rightful” or “miscreant” religious leader late one night and kill him. The government sends in troops, who go house to house looking for the killers and sweeping into their nets all sorts and shades of dissenting citizens. Soon two camps have formed—the progovern-ment camp and the pro-insurrectionary camp—and they are required to do battle, but in fact most of the people involved do not believe wholeheartedly in one side or the other, in particular Henry Morton, a young gentleman of modest education and modest ambition whose father had been a leader in an earlier antiroyalist rebellion. Henry finally sides with the rebels because he believes in freedom of religion and opposes the cruel methods of the government, but he continues to argue for forbearance and moderation as the war progresses. One of Scott's signal achievements is that he depicts the more fanatical evangelical elements of the rebel party with insight—they lose partly because they do not understand how the world works, and they don't understand partly because they don't care. When they are finally beaten and executed, they go to their deaths with bravery because they truly do expect a glorious reward—Scott understands both the strangeness and the strength of mystical religious conviction without ridiculing it or sharing in it.

对于现代读者而言，斯科特及其同时代人所知的历史大多鲜为人知，因此，故事情节增添了一份悬念，但同时也带有一种阴郁的熟悉感——一群“罪犯”或“革命者”（取决于你的立场）在一个深夜偶遇一位“正直”或“邪恶”的宗教领袖并将其杀害。政府派出军队，挨家挨户搜捕凶手，并将形形色色的异议人士一网打尽。很快，两大阵营形成——亲政府阵营和支持起义的阵营——他们被迫交战，但事实上，大多数卷入其中的人并非全心全意地支持任何一方，尤其是亨利·莫顿，一位受过普通教育、志向平凡的年轻绅士，他的父亲曾是早年反君主制叛乱的领袖之一。亨利最终站在了叛军一边，因为他信仰宗教自由，反对政府的残酷手段，但随着战争的进行，他始终主张保持克制和温和。斯科特的一项杰出成就，在于他深刻地刻画了叛军中那些狂热的福音派分子——他们失败的部分原因是他们不了解世界的运行规律，而他们不了解的部分原因则是他们漠不关心。当他们最终战败被处决时，他们勇敢地走向死亡，因为他们真心期待着荣耀的奖赏——斯科特既理解神秘宗教信仰的怪诞之处，也理解其强大的力量，但他既没有嘲讽它，也没有认同它。

Scott is equally clear and evenhanded about the military aspects of conflict. He depicts the battles in a natural and organized way, so the most neophyte modern female reader can see how and why they turn out as they do and what that means. He also understands how soldiers’ minds work. The cool, elegant, ruthless Claverhouse is fascinating, and so is the ruthless, crude, and fanatical Balfour. The telling sign of a great novelist of rich imaginative gifts is the ability to draw beautiful minor characters and to allow them to remain minor. Scott is such a novelist.

斯科特对战争的军事层面同样清晰客观。他以自然而有条理的方式描绘战役，即使是初涉此道的现代女性读者也能明白战役的来龙去脉及其意义。他对士兵的心理也了如指掌。冷静、优雅、冷酷的克拉弗豪斯令人着迷，而冷酷、粗犷、狂热的贝尔福也同样如此。一位才华横溢、想象力丰富的伟大作家，其标志之一便是能够塑造出鲜活生动的配角，并让他们保持配角的身份。斯科特正是这样一位作家。

What Scott is awkward at is changing the scene. He must follow the battle, the propaganda campaign, and the love story, and this requires more than a few “meantime, back at the ranch” sorts of transitions. The modern novel has discovered some techniques that weave disparate sections together more seamlessly and naturally than Scott was able to do, but his own voice is the compensation for this awkwardness—it is a frank but artful voice, reasonable but evocative, and both reassuring and enlightening. Modern readers generally avoid Scott as outdated and potentially tedious, but issues and dilemmas that interested him are still with us, and his desire, as a novelist, to imagine an enlightened and humane outcome deserves revival.

斯科特的不足之处在于场景转换。他必须兼顾战争、宣传运动和爱情故事，这就需要频繁地使用“与此同时，回到农场”之类的过渡方式。现代小说已经发展出一些技巧，能够比斯科特更流畅自然地将不同的章节衔接起来，但他独特的叙述风格弥补了这一不足——坦率而又不失艺术性，理性而又引人入胜，既令人安心又发人深省。现代读者通常认为斯科特的作品过时且可能枯燥乏味，因此避而远之，但他所关注的问题和困境至今仍然存在，而他作为小说家，渴望构想一个充满启迪和人道的结局，这种愿望也值得我们重新审视。

Sir Walter Scott. The Bride of Lammermoor

沃尔特·斯科特爵士，《拉默穆尔的新娘》

(1819; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1998), 349 PP.

（1819 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1998 年），349 页。

The Bride of Lammermoor is the fourth of Scott's tetralogy of Scottish novels of the seventeenth century but is utterly unlike Old Mortality and, according to most critics, utterly unlike anything else Scott wrote. He was suffering from extremely painful gallstones while composing the novel (which he dictated), and according to one of his secretaries, when he read the published version “he did not recollect one single incident, character, or conversation it contained!” Perhaps this is evidence that the id, or the limbic brain, or the muse can compose without the faculty of reason, because The Bride of Lammermoor is never confused or disorganized. It is especially rich in themes and motifs that remain consistent throughout the novel and that give it a pleasing sense of completeness.

《拉默穆尔的新娘》是斯科特十七世纪苏格兰小说四部曲中的第四部，但它与《老莫塔利蒂》截然不同，而且据大多数评论家所说，也与斯科特的其他任何作品都截然不同。他在创作这部小说（由他口述）时正饱受胆结石的折磨，痛苦不堪。据他的一位秘书说，当他读到出版的版本时，“他竟然记不起小说中的任何情节、人物或对话！”或许这证明，本我、边缘系统或缪斯女神可以在缺乏理性的情况下进行创作，因为《拉默穆尔的新娘》的结构清晰，条理分明。小说中贯穿始终的主题和意象尤为丰富，赋予了它一种令人愉悦的完整性。

The plot is simple: an ancient aristocratic family, the Ravenswoods, lose their estate through bad management, political upheaval, and legal wrangling to another family, the Ashtons. Sir William Ashton is a talented and wealthy but base-born lawyer; his wife, Lady Ashton, is a member of a very powerful family. Edgar Ravenswood is bent upon revenge, but an accident intervenes through which he is introduced to Lucy Ashton while her mother is away in England for some months. Sir William allows the acquaintance, partly through oversight and partly as a political maneuver, and Lucy and Edgar fall in love and betroth themselves. When Lady Ashton returns, she is unalterably opposed to the marriage, and forces Lucy instead to marry another suitor, who is wealthy and has similar political and religious loyalties to those of the Ashtons. Even though Lucy shows obvious signs of mental stress, the marriage goes forward. On the wedding night, Lucy attempts to kill her new husband with a dagger she has stolen. She then succumbs to madness and dies. The novel became a famous opera by Donizetti, Lucia di Lammermoor , and obviously has many romantic and operatic elements. But it is also a technically interesting novel because even though its elements don't seem as though they are going to mesh in an affecting and illuminating way, Scott manages to make it work.

故事梗概很简单：古老的贵族雷文斯伍德家族因经营不善、政治动荡和法律纠纷而失去了庄园，拱手让给了阿什顿家族。威廉·阿什顿爵士是一位才华横溢、家财万贯的律师，但出身卑微；他的妻子阿什顿夫人则出身于一个权势显赫的家族。埃德加·雷文斯伍德一心复仇，却因一场意外结识了露西·阿什顿，当时露西的母亲正在英国逗留数月。威廉爵士出于疏忽和政治考量，默许了两人的相识，露西和埃德加坠入爱河并订婚。阿什顿夫人回来后，坚决反对这桩婚事，强迫露西嫁给另一位求婚者，此人家财万贯，政治和宗教信仰也与阿什顿家族相似。尽管露西精神状态明显不佳，但婚礼还是如期举行了。新婚之夜，露西试图用偷来的匕首杀死她的新婚丈夫。随后她精神崩溃，死去。这部小说后来被多尼采蒂谱写成著名的歌剧《拉美莫尔的露琪亚》，显然融合了许多浪漫和歌剧元素。但它在技巧上也颇具趣味，因为尽管小说中的各种元素看似难以巧妙融合，斯科特却成功地将它们融为一体，令人动容。

One striking characteristic of the novel is that Scott uses the forms and tones of realism to depict his romantic and folkloric elements. He explores the psychology of the Ashtons’ family life very carefully, delineating the ways in which Lady Ashton dominates her husband, the ways in which the cleverness that has made him successful also makes him vulnerable to manipulation, and the ways in which the dysfunctional family romance among husband, wife, and daughter make everyone vulnerable to destruction. Edgar Ravenswood is no less carefully analyzed. His nurture as the son of an irascible, traditional, and probably not very intelligent aristocrat is contrasted nicely with his gentler nature as a man who understands that the world is changing and would like to live on the new terms, and also as a strong man who feels tenderness for a weak and apparently vulnerable woman in spite of his intuition that someone with more vitality and enterprise would suit him better.

这部小说的一大特色在于，斯科特运用现实主义的形式和笔触来描绘其浪漫和民间传说的元素。他细致入微地探索了阿什顿一家的心理生活，刻画了阿什顿夫人如何支配她的丈夫，他赖以成功的才智如何也使他容易受人摆布，以及夫妻与女儿之间功能失调的家庭关系如何使每个人都面临毁灭的危险。埃德加·雷文斯伍德的形象也同样被细致地剖析。他出身于一个脾气暴躁、思想保守、或许并不聪明的贵族家庭，这种成长经历与他温和的性格形成了鲜明的对比。他明白世界正在改变，并渴望适应新的生活；同时，他也是一个坚强的男人，尽管直觉告诉他，一个更有活力、更有魄力的女人更适合他，但他仍然对一个柔弱、看似脆弱的女人心生怜悯。

Scott is clear that all the power relationships in this world are out of whack and in flux, from political ones (as represented by the marquis of Atholl) to familial ones (as represented by the parents’ relationships to their offspring) to master/servant ones (as represented by Balder-stone and Ravenswood, but also those of minor characters) to gender ones (Lady Ashton has openly usurped her husband's power, but the relationship between Ravenswood and Lucy is equally unbalanced). The polity is out of joint, and there is nothing romantic love can do to redeem it.

斯科特明确指出，这个世界上的所有权力关系都处于失衡和动荡之中，从政治关系（以阿索尔侯爵为代表）到家庭关系（以父母与子女的关系为代表），再到主仆关系（以巴尔德斯通和雷文斯伍德为代表，但也包括一些次要角色），以及性别关系（阿什顿夫人公然篡夺了丈夫的权力，但雷文斯伍德和露西之间的关系同样失衡）。整个社会秩序混乱，任何浪漫的爱情都无法挽救它。

The novel is full of supernatural elements, such as three old hags who are reminiscent of the three witches in Macbeth , and omens, signs, legends, and prophecies. Many of these are accounted for or debunked by the narrator. For example, the sudden exchange of one portrait for another at the marriage feast is traced to the agency of one of the malevolent old women. Her malevolence is not of mysterious origin— she is envious, full of class resentment, and angry at the way Lady Ash-ton has treated her in the past. Nevertheless, the exchange of paintings serves to forward the prophecy that disaster will ensue if the master of Ravenswood returns to his old castle to seek a wife. Scott, in fact, has a quite sophisticated view of the way stories and gossip sometimes dictate events, not because prophecies have innate power, but because they gain social power through agreement.

这部小说充满了超自然元素，例如三个老巫婆，她们让人联想起《麦克白》中的三个女巫，还有各种预兆、征兆、传说和预言。叙述者对其中许多都进行了解释或驳斥。例如，婚宴上画像的突然互换，被追溯到其中一位心怀恶意的老妇人所为。她的恶意并非源于神秘——她心怀嫉妒，充满阶级怨恨，并且对阿什顿夫人过去对待她的方式感到愤怒。然而，画像的互换确实印证了预言：如果拉文斯伍德的主人回到他以前的城堡寻找妻子，灾难将会降临。事实上，斯科特对故事和流言蜚语有时如何影响事件走向有着相当深刻的见解，这并非因为预言本身具有内在的力量，而是因为它们通过社会共识获得了影响力。

Scott was a natural novelist because he understood and portrayed ambiguities and complexities with seeming effortlessness, in prose that even in the twenty-first century seems accessible and clear. His narrators always tell the story with an automatic tone of reasonableness that keeps the narrative anchored in the world, yet they do not discount any potential source of motivation or action. He is a natural psychologist, too, who can convincingly motivate characters of all social classes and temperaments, both minor and major. He hasn't fared as well in the modern world as Jane Austen, but he is somewhat like her—one of a long line of liberal British writers for whom human individuality is a source of inspiration as well as psychological, social, political, spiritual, and philosophical speculation.

斯科特是一位天生的小说家，因为他能以近乎毫不费力的方式理解并描绘出各种暧昧和复杂性，其散文即使在二十一世纪也依然通俗易懂、清晰明了。他笔下的叙述者总是以一种自然而然的理性口吻讲述故事，使叙事扎根于现实世界，同时又不忽略任何潜在的动机或行为来源。他也是一位天生的心理学家，能够令人信服地刻画各个社会阶层、各种性格的人物，无论其地位高低。他在现代社会的成就不及简·奥斯汀，但他与奥斯汀有几分相似——他们都是众多英国自由主义作家中的一员，这些人从人类的个性以及心理、社会、政治、精神和哲学思考中汲取灵感。

20. Mary Shelley. Frankenstein

20. 玛丽·雪莱，《弗兰肯斯坦》

(1818; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN PUTNAM, SIGNET, 2000), 198 PP.

（1818 年；重印，纽约：企鹅普特南出版社，2000 年），198 页。

Mary Shelley was the wife of Percy Bysshe Shelley, the great Romantic poet, and the daughter of Mary Wollstonecraft (author of A Vindication of the Rights of Women , who died a few days after Mary's birth) and William Godwin (a radical polemicist and author). Frankenstein was conceived and written when Mary was nineteen years old and much under the influence of her husband and Lord Byron, when they were all living on the shores of Lake Geneva. The two poets and Mary, along with Byron's companion, Dr. Polidori, had been reading ghost stories, and decided to try writing some. The poets quickly got bored with their humdrum and, you might say, prosaic task, but Polidori and Mary each produced pieces. Mary's novel was published anonymously, and most readers assumed that Percy had written it. It was not until 1831 , after Percy's death and Mary's return to England, that she published an edition under her own name with her own explanation of the circumstances of authorship.

玛丽·雪莱是伟大的浪漫主义诗人珀西·比希·雪莱的妻子，也是玛丽·沃斯通克拉夫特（《女权辩护》的作者，在玛丽出生几天后去世）和威廉·戈德温（一位激进的辩论家和作家）的女儿。玛丽十九岁时，深受丈夫和拜伦勋爵的影响，创作了《弗兰肯斯坦》。当时他们都住在日内瓦湖畔。两位诗人、玛丽以及拜伦的同伴波利多里医生都喜欢读鬼故事，于是决定尝试自己写一些。诗人很快就对这种单调乏味的工作感到厌倦，但波利多里和玛丽各自都完成了一部分。玛丽的小说以匿名形式出版，大多数读者都认为是珀西写的。直到1831年，珀西去世，玛丽回到英国后，她才以自己的名义出版了小说，并解释了作者身份的由来。

Frankenstein poses a challenge to the modern reader's willingness to suspend disbelief because Mary does not detail how Frankenstein actually creates the monster. She is far more interested in feelings and reactions than she is in processes and events, but by eliding over the mechanics, she tempts the modern reader to dismiss the actuality of the monster—we all know how long it takes a multitude of inventors to do something as relatively simple as creating a robot that can walk up stairs. That it takes Victor two years of solitary work (imagine a graduate student robbing graves) to make a thinking and growing creature is simply ridiculous. But the implausibility of the science isn't the only difficulty; Victor's own reactions are also implausible—or, perhaps, not rendered carefully enough so the reader is drawn into empathizing with them. The author has not found a prosaic style that gives objective context to the feelings of the characters—their sentiments are high, low, exalted, tender, grand, unmixed. In other words, they are poetic sentiments spoken by poetically conceived characters— the wise father, the perfect friend, the beautiful and virtuous young woman. Much of the narrative is dialogue, but it is ideal rather than vernacular dialogue.

《弗兰肯斯坦》对现代读者能否接受书中情节提出了挑战，因为玛丽并没有详细描述弗兰肯斯坦是如何创造怪物的。她更关注人物的感受和反应，而非过程和事件本身，但她对具体机制的忽略，却诱使现代读者忽视怪物的真实存在——我们都知道，即使是制造一个能上楼梯的机器人这样相对简单的任务，也需要众多发明家花费大量时间才能完成。而维克多竟然花了两年时间独自钻研（想象一下一个研究生去盗墓）才创造出一个会思考、会成长的生物，这简直荒谬至极。然而，科学上的不合理并非唯一的难题；维克多自身的反应也同样不合情理——或者说，作者的描写不够细致，无法让读者产生共鸣。作者似乎没有找到一种客观的散文风格来展现人物的情感——他们的情绪或高尚或卑微，或崇高或温柔，或宏大或纯粹，或纯粹无差别。换句话说，这些诗意的情感出自于诗意塑造的人物之口——睿智的父亲、完美的挚友、美丽贤淑的年轻女子。叙事的大部分是对话，但这些对话是理想化的，而非日常口语化的。

For the modern reader, the novel fails in its intention to depict and evoke horror. In part this is a failure of style, and in part it is a failure of technique—the author dwells too little on grisly details. We have to take the horror too much secondhand. Though objectively the events of the novel are horrifying—three murders, a wrongful execution, another death—the author, for whatever reasons of sensibility or youth, chooses not to make a spectacle of them. Since the novel was a popular sensation at publication, it is possible that we are simply inured to the ideas, and require visuals to elicit a reaction—most horror stories from the period don't seem horrible to us (this is not true of plays— Shakespeare's Titus Andronicus , John Webster's The White Devil , and Percy Bysshe Shelley's The Cenci can produce revulsion). Nevertheless, Frankenstein is an advance on Justine in the sense that Shelley (and other Romantics) were looking for a way to successfully depict horror that the reader would feel as well as observe. Nineteenth-century realist novelists subsequently built on Mary Shelley and the writings of other Romantics to render these states of mind in greater detail and set them into a more mundane context that would make them more believable and produce a bigger thrill.

对现代读者而言，这部小说未能达到其描绘和唤起恐怖氛围的预期效果。部分原因是文风上的缺陷，部分原因是技巧上的不足——作者对血腥细节的描写过于简略。我们只能间接地感受到其中的恐怖。尽管客观来说，小说中的事件令人毛骨悚然——三起谋杀案、一起冤案、另一起死亡——但作者出于某种敏感或年轻的原因，选择不将这些事件渲染得淋漓尽致。由于这部小说出版时曾引起轰动，或许我们已经对这些概念习以为常，需要视觉上的冲击才能产生反应——那个时期的大多数恐怖故事在我们看来并不恐怖（戏剧则不然——莎士比亚的《泰特斯·安德洛尼克斯》、约翰·韦伯斯特的《白魔鬼》和珀西·比希·雪莱的《钦奇家族》都能令人感到反感）。然而，《弗兰肯斯坦》在某种意义上比《朱斯蒂娜》更胜一筹，因为雪莱（以及其他浪漫主义作家）一直在寻求一种能够成功描绘恐怖的方式，让读者既能感受到又能观察到恐怖的景象。十九世纪的现实主义小说家们在玛丽·雪莱和其他浪漫主义作家的作品基础上，更加细致地刻画了这些心理状态，并将它们置于更为平凡的语境中，使其更具可信度，也更能营造惊悚氛围。

Where Frankenstein succeeds is as a novel about an idea—once again, as with many great novels, the idea is simple. A man creates a humanlike creature, a train of events is set into motion, and the narrative follows them. Frankenstein was the first “high concept” idea of the modern era; the idea was actually new, and Mary and her friends did receive it as a revelation. That didn't mean that it had no sources. Mary and her whole group were moved and impressed by Coleridge's long poem “The Rime of the Ancient Mariner,” about the terrors of an outcast, and they were also much influenced by the portrayal of the relations among God, Adam, and Satan in Milton's Paradise Lost. Byron and Shelley both professed sympathy for the Devil in their writings, and explored the Promethean ideas that Milton had, possibly inadvertently, hinted at. Mary, though, stays firmly on the side of Frankenstein and his family—although she allows the monster to state his point of view, his desires never prevail, and he, unlike Frankenstein, remains unredeemed in the end. Though Frankenstein looks forward to reunion with his loved ones beyond the grave, the monster's only future is nonbeing. Because he is an unnatural creation, his outcast state cannot be relieved; both of his creators, Frankenstein and Mary Shelley, are merciless toward him.

《弗兰肯斯坦》的成功之处在于它作为一部关于理念的小说——和许多伟大的小说一样，这个理念很简单：一个人创造了一个类人生物，一系列事件由此展开，故事也随之展开。《弗兰肯斯坦》是现代第一个“高概念”作品；这个理念确实是全新的，玛丽和她的朋友们也将其视为一种启示。但这并不意味着它没有渊源。玛丽和她的朋友们深受柯勒律治的长诗《古舟子咏》的感动和启发，这首诗描绘了一个被放逐者的恐惧；他们也深受弥尔顿《失乐园》中上帝、亚当和撒旦之间关系的刻画的影响。拜伦和雪莱都在他们的作品中表达了对魔鬼的同情，并探讨了弥尔顿可能无意中暗示过的普罗米修斯式的思想。然而，玛丽始终坚定地站在弗兰肯斯坦及其家人一边——尽管她允许怪物表达自己的观点，但他的愿望最终未能实现，而且与弗兰肯斯坦不同，他最终也未能得到救赎。弗兰肯斯坦期盼着死后与亲人重聚，而怪物的未来却只有虚无。因为他是一个非自然的造物，他被放逐的命运无法改变；他的两位创造者，弗兰肯斯坦和玛丽·雪莱，都对他毫不留情。

The novel does not easily take up the subject of horror, and most ghost stories and narratives of horror date fairly quickly. Frankenstein worked in its day. Though it has since become a model of what not to do if you really want to frighten the reader, it is an excellent social document that combines the drama of Mary Shelley's life with several of the ideas and modes of expression current when she was writing. In addition, Frankenstein shows the capacity of the popular novel to change the way society looks at things. One of the truisms of human existence that the monster comments upon, and that seems also to dictate the plot of the novel, is the idea that “the human senses are insurmountable barriers to our union”—in other words, that the monster's ugly strangeness cannot be overcome in his relations to humans, and he can live only in isolation. Frankenstein is possibly the first novel to have explored this assumption, and in doing so, undermines it without challenging it. The reader cannot help empathizing with the monster's isolated state and feeling at least some sympathy for him. One is tempted to ally herself with him against his creator. By portraying the inner life, the novel as a form contradicts the importance of appearance in a way that drama and film do not. Frankenstein set in motion the processes that created the world we live in, where ugliness and strangeness do not dictate a person's isolation and where intolerance of an unorthodox appearance is viewed as a primitive attitude that education can remove. The 1931 movie Frankenstein demonstrates a related effect—when it first came out, Boris Karloff as the monster was frightening, but familiarity bred affection. Now audiences hardly see his threatening qualities at all; it has been a long time since Hollywood tried to use human deformity as intrinsically scary. Scary humans in movies these days are often quite beautiful; what is scary about them is that appearances are deceiving, not revealing. In part, it is the empathy that is essential to the success of a good novel that has changed the way we respond to appearances.

这部小说并没有轻易触及恐怖的主题，而且大多数鬼故事和恐怖叙事很快就会过时。《弗兰肯斯坦》在当时是成功的。尽管它后来成为了一个反面教材，告诫人们如果真的想吓唬读者应该避免什么，但它仍然是一部优秀的社会文献，将玛丽·雪莱的人生经历与她写作时期流行的多种思想和表达方式巧妙地融合在一起。此外，《弗兰肯斯坦》也展现了通俗小说改变社会看待事物方式的能力。小说中，怪物评论的一条关于人类生存的真理，似乎也主导了整个情节，那就是“人类的感官是我们结合的不可逾越的障碍”——换句话说，怪物丑陋的怪异之处无法在与人类的关系中得到克服，他只能孤独地生存。《弗兰肯斯坦》可能是第一部探讨这一假设的小说，并且在探讨的过程中，它既没有挑战这一假设，又对其进行了削弱。读者不禁会对怪物的孤立状态产生共鸣，并对他产生至少一些同情。人们很容易想要与他结盟，对抗他的创造者。小说这种艺术形式通过描绘人物的内心世界，以一种戏剧和电影无法企及的方式，反驳了外表的重要性。弗兰肯斯坦开启了塑造我们如今世界的进程：在这个世界里，丑陋和怪异不再决定一个人的孤立，对非正统外貌的偏见被视为一种原始的、可以通过教育消除的观念。1931年的电影《弗兰肯斯坦》展现了类似的效果——影片上映之初，鲍里斯·卡洛夫饰演的怪物令人恐惧，但随着熟悉感的加深，观众对他产生了喜爱之情。如今，观众几乎不再感受到他身上的威胁；好莱坞早已不再试图将人类的畸形作为恐怖的元素。如今电影中那些令人恐惧的人物往往非常俊美；真正令人恐惧的是，外表具有欺骗性，而非揭示本质。在某种程度上，正是小说成功所必需的同理心，改变了我们对外表的反应方式。

21. Jane Austen. Persuasion

21. 简·奥斯汀，《劝导》

(1818; REPR., NEW YORK: DOVER, 1997), 188 PP.

（1818 年；重印，纽约：多佛出版社，1997 年），188 页。

I have read Persuasion many times. When I first read it, I was younger than any of the characters, and now I am older than any of the characters, and also older than the author, who died at forty-two. I have read Pride and Prejudice as many times, and I have read Emma several times as well. The clarity of Jane Austen's literary style and the fineness of her sensibility are worth revisiting over and over. I could have indulged myself by including all of her novels on our list, because though the pleasures to be taken from her novels differ as one ages, they never lessen. I chose Persuasion because Austen gives her heroine not only the poignant Cinderella bonus of being chosen over all the more apparently appealing girls, but also because in her last novel, her insights into her social milieu are especially brisk and broad.

我读过《劝导》很多遍。第一次读的时候，我比书中任何一个人物都年轻；现在，我比书中任何一个人物都年长，也比作者本人年长——她四十二岁就去世了。《傲慢与偏见》我也读过很多遍，《爱玛》也读过好几遍。简·奥斯汀清晰的文风和细腻的情感值得反复品读。我本可以把她所有的小说都列入书单，因为虽然随着年龄的增长，从她的作品中获得的乐趣有所不同，但这些乐趣却从未减少。我选择《劝导》是因为奥斯汀不仅赋予了她的女主人公灰姑娘式的悲惨结局——在众多看似更迷人的女孩中脱颖而出，而且在她最后一部小说中，她对当时社会环境的洞察尤为敏锐和深刻。

Anne Elliot is twenty-seven years old. She has lost her looks and is very much on the verge of becoming a spinster. In addition, her father and sister, vain of their own looks and social position, have been extravagant, and the family must now retrench. Rather than simply economizing, they decide to rent out the family estate and move to Bath. The couple who take the estate turn out to be the sister and brother-in-law of Anne's former suitor, a career naval officer, whom she hasn't seen in the eight years since his proposal was turned down by her family as not sufficiently prestigious. Captain Wentworth, however, has changed his circumstances, and, now both rich and respected, is looking for a wife.

安妮·艾略特二十七岁，容颜不再，眼看就要成为老处女了。此外，她的父亲和姐姐都自负于自己的容貌和社会地位，挥霍无度，如今家里不得不节衣缩食。他们没有选择简单的节约，而是决定出租家族庄园，搬到巴斯去住。接手庄园的夫妇竟然是安妮以前追求者的妹妹和妹夫。这位海军军官自八年前求婚时被安妮的家人以不够体面为由拒绝后，安妮就再也没见过他。然而，温特沃斯上校如今境况大变，既富有又受人尊敬，正在寻找妻子。

Austen was a revolutionary novelist in several particulars that are somewhat hidden by her clever and charming writing style. First among these is that she focused on the emotional lives of women at a time when virtuous women were not allowed to have emotional lives. In Tom Jones , for example, Fielding allows Sophia to decline to marry Blifil, whom she abhors, but she is not allowed to express, or even feel, a preference for Tom. Female virtue in the eighteenth century (and into the Victorian period, as in the novels of Anthony Trollope) required that young women be entirely ignorant of love and choice until they were solicited. But all of Austen's novels pay close attention to the desires of female characters—in Pride and Prejudice , the fact that Jane Bennet cares for Mr. Bingley and wishes for a proposal from him without knowing whether he cares for her is fully explored. With utter naturalness, Austen gives her female protagonists both ambition and the intelligence to realize it without impugning their virtue. Austen was also alive to the position of women who had no alternative to marriage or continued submission to parents. Anne Elliot, who is constantly at the beck and call of her married sister and yet is repeatedly demeaned by her relatives, can claim nothing for herself in the way of privileges, independence, or money.

奥斯汀是一位具有革命性意义的小说家，这一点在她机智迷人的文笔下往往被掩盖。首先，她关注女性的情感生活，而当时的贞洁女性却被禁止拥有情感生活。例如，在《汤姆·琼斯》中，菲尔丁允许索菲娅拒绝嫁给她厌恶的布利菲尔，但她却不能表达，甚至不能感受到对汤姆的爱慕。十八世纪（以及维多利亚时代，如安东尼·特罗洛普的小说）的女性贞洁要求年轻女性在被追求之前对爱情和选择一无所知。但奥斯汀的所有小说都细致入微地刻画了女性角色的欲望——在《傲慢与偏见》中，简·班纳特对宾利先生的爱慕以及渴望得到他的求婚，在她不确定宾利先生是否也爱她的情况下，得到了充分的展现。奥斯汀以极其自然的方式，赋予笔下的女性主人公抱负和实现抱负的智慧，而丝毫不损害她们的贞洁。奥斯汀也敏锐地意识到那些除了结婚或继续顺从父母之外别无选择的女性的处境。安妮·艾略特总是听命于已婚的姐姐，却又屡遭亲戚的羞辱，她无法为自己争取任何特权、独立或金钱。

By the time Austen wrote Persuasion , she had become something of an egalitarian. The powerless Anne is surrounded by vanity, selfishness, and social climbing. Those who follow standard social norms, such as Anne's father and sister, are portrayed as silly and venal. The naval officers Anne meets who have risen through merit are portrayed as worthy of respect and affection because they have traveled and learned interesting things. And they have the perspicacity to appreciate her. The core of the novel is Austen's record of Anne's private thoughts about Frederick Wentworth. After many readings, the satisfaction of her wishes is pleasurable but hardly suspenseful. What remains interesting and new about them, however, is the intimacy of Austen's relationship to her heroine. Anne is attentive to every nuance of the social intercourse around her; she is almost, in some sense, a spy among her relations, calculating the meanings of their actions and moods and gauging how they will affect her.

奥斯汀创作《劝导》时，已逐渐成为一位平等主义者。无助的安妮被虚荣、自私和攀附权贵的风气所包围。那些遵循传统社会规范的人，例如安妮的父亲和姐姐，被描绘成愚蠢而贪婪。安妮遇到的那些凭借自身功绩晋升的海军军官，则因其阅历丰富、见多识广而值得尊敬和爱戴。他们也拥有欣赏安妮的敏锐洞察力。小说的核心是奥斯汀对安妮关于弗雷德里克·温特沃斯的内心独白的记录。反复阅读之后，安妮愿望的实现固然令人愉悦，却缺乏悬念。然而，真正引人入胜、耳目一新的是奥斯汀与女主人公之间亲密无间的关系。安妮对周围社交互动的每一个细微之处都十分关注；在某种意义上，她几乎就像是亲戚中的一名间谍，揣摩着他们的言行举止和情绪变化，并预判它们将如何影响自己。

The larger aspect of Anne's quietly observing habit is Austen's depiction of the social codes of the English gentry early in the nineteenth century. No doubt it is impossible for a modern reader to understand all of the refinements of gesture and implication that Austen catalogs, but the gist remains—almost every social signal is codified. Knowing the code is a sign of proper breeding and education, and is the key to social acceptance, and yet following only the code without true feeling is equally a sign of moral emptiness. Anne (and Austen) recognizes that the code is as much a device of oppression as a set of manners, and the novel's good characters are those who have inner lives—cultivated through private systems of belief—that reveal themselves not only in proper behavior, but also in proper motives. In all her novels, Austen satirizes individual selfishness, irresponsibility, foolishness, and egotism. In Persuasion she enlarges her critique and shows that personal failings grow out of social distortions. She is neither as lighthearted as in Pride and Prejudice , nor as forgiving as in Emma. But the passion at the heart of Anne's unchanging love for Captain Went-worth softens the novel. It is a haunting, appealing, and yet disquieting example of Jane Austen's almost perfect sense of character, style, and pace, an example of the way a true master novelist (and lover of novels—Austen often defended novel-reading and in this novel gently pokes fun at too much poetry-reading) employs all of her tools to their best advantage.

安妮默默观察的习惯，其更深层的含义在于奥斯汀对十九世纪初英国绅士阶层社会规范的刻画。毫无疑问，现代读者不可能完全理解奥斯汀笔下描绘的种种姿态和言外之意，但其核心要义依然清晰——几乎所有社交信号都被编纂成册。了解这些规范是良好教养和受过良好教育的标志，也是获得社会认可的关键；然而，仅仅遵循规范而缺乏真情实感，同样是道德空虚的体现。安妮（以及奥斯汀本人）意识到，这些规范既是一套礼仪，也是一种压迫的工具。小说中那些优秀的人物，都拥有丰富的内心世界——通过个人的信仰体系得以培养——这些内心世界不仅体现在得体的行为举止中，也体现在正确的动机之中。在奥斯汀的所有小说中，她都讽刺了个人的自私、不负责任、愚蠢和利己主义。在《劝导》中，她进一步拓展了批判的范围，指出个人的缺陷源于社会的扭曲。她既不像《傲慢与偏见》中那样轻松愉快，也不像《爱玛》中那样宽容大度。但安妮对温特沃斯上校那份始终如一的爱，却为这部小说增添了几分柔和。它既令人难以忘怀，又引人入胜，同时又令人不安，堪称简·奥斯汀近乎完美的人物刻画、文风和节奏把控的典范。这部小说展现了一位真正的文学大师（同时也是一位小说爱好者——奥斯汀经常为阅读小说辩护，并在小说中巧妙地讽刺了过度阅读诗歌的现象）如何将她所有的写作技巧发挥到极致。

22. James Hogg. The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner

22. 詹姆斯·霍格，《一个义愤填膺的罪人的私人回忆录和忏悔录》

(1824; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1987), 242 PP.

（1824 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1987 年），242 页。

James Hogg was a self-taught literary man, a shepherd by birth who wrote and farmed for much of his life. He knew Scott and wrote a book about him. Depending upon your point of view, The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner is either a political novel about faith and doctrine, or a religious tale with political overtones, but it is very much about how controversies over religion express themselves both psychologically and sociologically. It begins, appropriately to our study, with a forced marriage. A wealthy young woman is married for property considerations to an older man whose religious beliefs she does not share. She avoids consummating the alliance on the wedding night, but her husband then locks her up and rapes her repeatedly until she flees to her father, who beats her and sends her back to her husband. This episode, very much in the spirit of The Hep-tameron , only stiffens her resistance. She and her husband live in separate parts of the castle for some years thereafter, and she produces two sons. The elder shares his father's beliefs, which are Church of Scotland, and the younger his mother's, which are Calvinist.

詹姆斯·霍格是一位自学成才的文学家，他生于牧羊人家庭，一生大部分时间都在写作和务农。他认识斯科特，并写了一本关于斯科特的书。从不同的角度来看，《一个正义罪人的私人回忆录和忏悔录》既可以是一部关于信仰和教义的政治小说，也可以是一部带有政治色彩的宗教故事，但它的核心在于探讨宗教争议如何在心理和社会层面上呈现出来。正如我们研究的主题，故事以一场强迫婚姻开篇。一位富有的年轻女子为了财产利益嫁给了一位年长的男子，而她并不认同他的宗教信仰。新婚之夜，她拒绝与丈夫圆房，但她的丈夫却将她囚禁起来，并反复强奸她，直到她逃到父亲那里。父亲殴打了她，然后把她送回丈夫身边。这一情节与《七君子传》颇为相似，反而更加坚定了她的反抗。此后几年，她和丈夫分别住在城堡的不同区域，她生下了两个儿子。哥哥的信仰和父亲一样，是苏格兰教会的信徒；弟弟的信仰和母亲一样，是加尔文教的信徒。

These unfortunate preliminaries pave the way for a sibling rivalry from hell. The elder son, raised by the liberal father, is inexplicably harassed by his brother, who appears to be a sanctimonious prig and mischief-maker, egged on by the resentful mother and her religious mentor. After he is imprisoned for murder, however, the younger son leaves a memoir explaining his actions in terms of what the reader readily identifies as satanic possession (though the Devil does not enter into him, rather becomes his unshakable companion). Like The Tale of Old Mortality , Hogg's novel is set in the late seventeenth century, when religious controversies raged in Scotland, partly defining and partly defined by class conflicts and regional antagonisms, and also when, as in The Bride of Lammermoor , visions, ghosts, supernatural figures, and superstitions were typical beliefs among members of all classes.

这些不幸的开端为一场残酷的兄弟阋墙埋下了伏笔。长子由开明的父亲抚养长大，却莫名其妙地受到弟弟的欺凌。弟弟看似道貌岸然、顽劣不堪，而心怀怨恨的母亲和她的宗教导师则在一旁怂恿。然而，在因谋杀罪入狱后，次子留下了一部回忆录，用读者很容易理解的“撒旦附身”来解释自己的行为（尽管魔鬼并未进入他的体内，而是成为了他不可动摇的伙伴）。与《古老的死亡故事》一样，霍格的小说也以十七世纪末为背景，当时苏格兰宗教纷争激烈，这些纷争部分源于阶级冲突和地域对抗，部分又源于此。同时，正如《拉默穆尔的新娘》中所描述的那样，幻象、鬼魂、超自然人物和迷信是各个阶层人士普遍的信仰。

The two brothers, George and Robert, contrast in temperament, religion, and politics. George is a hale fellow, a lover of games and society, openhearted and well meaning. He is also the heir to the family lands and wealth. Robert's legitimacy is questionable, though he is acknowledged by the father as his son. Robert is annoying from the beginning—he first introduces himself to George, and to the reader, by interfering in a tennis match, standing in the middle of the play until he is knocked down and injured. He acts churlish and resentful toward George and the other boys and soon is hounding George unmercifully, but with a condescending, sanctimonious air. According to the narrator, he has been convinced by his foster father, his mother's spiritual adviser, that he is a particular type of privileged believer, a “justified sinner”—that is, a member of God's elect, a person already awarded “grace,” so that no act he might perform on Earth could endanger his election (salvation). This notion is a logical extension of the Calvinist idea of grace—if no human act of goodness, generosity, or penance could influence or limit the power of God and His capacity to anoint His privileged few, then no evil act could influence Him, either, so there exists a class of believers who can do no wrong—whatever they do is right, no matter how harmful it might be.

乔治和罗伯特两兄弟性格、宗教信仰和政治观点截然不同。乔治身体健壮，热爱游戏和社交，为人热情友善。他也是家族土地和财富的继承人。罗伯特的身世却存疑，尽管父亲承认他是自己的儿子。罗伯特从一开始就令人讨厌——他第一次出现在乔治面前，也是在读者面前，就是在一场网球比赛中插队，站在场中央，直到被击倒受伤。他对乔治和其他男孩粗鲁无礼，充满怨恨，很快就开始无情地纠缠乔治，而且态度傲慢自大，道貌岸然。据叙述者所述，他的养父，也就是他母亲的属灵导师，让他相信自己是特殊的特权信徒，一个“蒙恩的罪人”——也就是说，他是上帝的选民，已经蒙受了“恩典”，因此他在世上所做的任何事都不会危及他的蒙拣选（救赎）。这种观念是加尔文主义恩典观的逻辑延伸——如果任何人的善行、慷慨或忏悔都无法影响或限制上帝的能力以及祂膏立少数特权者的能力，那么任何恶行也无法影响祂，因此存在着这样一类永远不会犯错的信徒——无论他们做什么都是正确的，无论这做什么有多么有害。

Satan, of course, is drawn to Robert's pride, and befriends him almost immediately after his parents declare that they have seen a valid sign that he is among the elect. Robert wonders about his new companion but finally decides that he must be a prince, and possibly he is Peter the Great of Russia, who was rumored to be traveling about at the end of the seventeenth century, educating himself. Robert is not happy with his new companion, though. Even while he is listening to the prince's flattery and using his powers to pay back old scores, he realizes that much about their relationship is inexplicable, especially the fact that he himself feels no pleasure and considerable uneasiness in the prince's company. Soon, it seems, there is evidence that Robert has committed crimes he has no memory of—either the prince is committing them disguised as Robert, or Robert is committing them himself in some sort of oblivious state.

当然，撒旦被罗伯特的骄傲所吸引，在他父母宣称看到了他已蒙拣选的迹象后不久，便与他结为朋友。罗伯特对这位新伙伴感到疑惑，最终认定他必定是一位王子，或许就是传闻中在十七世纪末游历四方、自学成才的俄罗斯彼得大帝。然而，罗伯特对这位新伙伴并不满意。即便他一边听着王子的奉承，一边用自己的力量报复旧怨，他仍然意识到他们之间的关系有很多难以解释之处，尤其是他自己与王子相处时，不仅没有感到任何愉悦，反而感到十分不安。很快，似乎出现了罗伯特犯下自己毫无记忆的罪行的迹象——要么是王子伪装成罗伯特犯下的罪行，要么是罗伯特本人在某种无意识的状态下犯下的罪行。

The suspense of the novel is not in who Robert's mysterious companion is, but in whether Robert will ever understand and acknowledge his mistaken view of himself as a “justified sinner.” The Private Memoirs and Confessions of a Justified Sinner is very much a tale—the third-person narrator never commits himself as to the verifiability of the strange events he relates, and the novel is supposed to raise a thrill of gothic dread in the reader. Even so, Hogg places every incident and character within the realistic confines of known Scottish history, including a destructive riot that ensues in Edinburgh after the first contretemps between George and Robert, which Hogg analyzes sociologically as a function of party loyalties in a period of heightened partisanship. Hogg, though himself the son of Calvinists, sees how extreme religious beliefs are apt to destroy all sense of common humanity and infuse political life with inflexible passion—this, he is saying, is where Satan finds an entry, and mayhem ensues.

这部小说的悬念不在于罗伯特神秘同伴的身份，而在于罗伯特是否终将理解并承认他自认为“罪有应得”的错误观念。《一个罪有应得者的私人回忆录与忏悔录》本质上是一部故事——第三人称叙述者从未明确表示他所讲述的奇异事件是否属实，而这部小说旨在唤起读者哥特式的恐惧感。即便如此，霍格仍将每一个事件和人物都置于已知的苏格兰历史的现实框架之内，包括乔治和罗伯特首次冲突后在爱丁堡爆发的破坏性骚乱。霍格从社会学的角度分析了这场骚乱，认为它是在党派斗争日益激烈的时期，党派忠诚所致。霍格虽然是加尔文教徒的儿子，但他看到极端的宗教信仰很容易摧毁人类的共同意识，并使政治生活充满僵化的激情——他认为，这就是撒旦进入社会的地方，混乱随之而来。

Hogg's novel may have seemed eerie or unearthly at the time it was written. These aspects of the narrative have faded and the horror is no longer so horrible. But the psychological and sociological observations he makes have not faded. Robert's feelings about his devilish mentor sound very much like addiction; rigid religious self-righteousness still has the same effect on civil society as it did hundreds of years ago; unhappy, violent marriages produce unhappy, violent children. Ideological passions in novels do not enter American literature from the English novel, but perhaps from the Scottish tradition, along with Scots-Irish Calvinist religious traditions that have shaped much of our culture.

霍格的小说在创作之时或许显得诡异或超凡脱俗。如今，这些叙事元素已然褪色，恐怖感也不再那么强烈。但他所作的心理和社会学观察却依然历历在目。罗伯特对他那魔鬼般的导师的感受，听起来很像一种瘾；僵化的宗教自以为是，对公民社会的影响与数百年前并无二致；不幸的暴力婚姻会滋生不幸的暴力子女。小说中的意识形态激情并非源自英国小说，而是可能来自苏格兰传统，以及塑造了我们文化诸多方面的苏格兰-爱尔兰加尔文主义宗教传统。

23. Stendhal. The Red and the Black

23. 司汤达，《红与黑》

TRANS. MARGARET R. B. SHAW (1830; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 2002), 509 PP.

玛格丽特·R·B·肖译（1830 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，2002 年），509 页。

Stendhal (n Henri Beyle) was forty-five when he began to write his first novel, and it was published at about the time of the Revolution of 1830 , in France, which ratified and regularized the changes in French life and politics begun by the French Revolution. It is thus a social document of a high order as well as a wonderful novel. Stendhal did what many novelists have done—he took a story he found in a newspaper and fashioned it into a work of the imagination by inferring the feelings and thoughts of the principal characters. The novel was meant to be current and socially engaged—Stendhal was a liberal and a freethinker, and he intended to portray French politics, French provincial life, and Parisian life. He had specific political views—that the royalists and the Catholic Church were in collusion against the interests of the rest of the population and that they planned to aid Charles X in reinstituting absolute monarchy. But the novel doesn't only display these views; it also stands on its own as a psychological portrait and as a depiction of the causes and effects of sexual passion.

司汤达（原名亨利·贝勒）四十五岁时开始创作他的第一部小说，这部小说大约在1830年法国大革命时期出版。这场革命巩固并规范了法国大革命开启的法国社会和政治变革。因此，它既是一部杰出的社会文献，也是一部精彩的小说。司汤达的做法与许多小说家类似——他从报纸上找到一个故事，通过推断主要人物的感受和思想，将其改编成一部充满想象力的作品。这部小说旨在反映当时的社会现实——司汤达是一位自由主义者和思想家，他意在描绘法国政治、法国地方生活和巴黎生活。他持有特定的政治观点——保皇党和天主教会勾结起来损害其他民众的利益，并计划帮助查理十世恢复君主专制。但这部小说展现的远不止这些观点；它本身也是一幅心理肖像，描绘了性激情的起因和后果。

Julien Sorel is a good-looking peasant boy with ambitions and aptitudes above his station in life. Looks are important, because they allow him to gain access to places and groups that would otherwise be closed to him, and they encourage others to attribute noble qualities, such as pride and fineness of feeling, to him even before he has learned enough to actually possess such qualities. In part, The Red and the Black is a study of the social effects of manner—Julien ends as he does because others have expected great things of him, and he has come to expect them, too. It is not clear whether he has great talents or only certain facilities—part of Stendhal's point is that Julien's development is public rather than private, and that he acts out the expectations of others. But perhaps as an effect of the resentful pride he has developed as a result of the antipathy of his father and brothers, he is always willing to take a dare. From beginning to end, whenever there is a choice between caution and boldness, Julien cannot allow himself to choose caution. He thus has the predispositions of a Romantic hero, if not the talent, passion, or singularity.

于连·索雷尔是一位相貌英俊的农家少年，他胸怀大志，才华横溢，远超其出身。外貌对他至关重要，因为它使他得以进入原本对他封闭的场所和群体，也使他人在他尚未真正具备这些品质之前，就将诸如骄傲和细腻情感之类的高尚品格赋予他。在某种程度上，《红与黑》是对举止的社会影响的探讨——于连最终的结局，是因为他人对他寄予厚望，而他也逐渐接受了这种期望。他究竟是天赋异禀还是仅仅具备某些特质，这一点并不明确——司汤达的观点之一是，于连的成长是公开的而非私密的，他的行为也迎合了他人的期望。或许正是由于父亲和兄弟的冷漠，他心中滋生了怨恨的骄傲，因此他总是乐于冒险。从始至终，每当面临谨慎与大胆的选择时，于连都无法让自己选择谨慎。因此，他具备浪漫主义英雄的特质，尽管缺乏天赋、激情或独特性。

Missing by a generation the occasion for great military prowess, Julien enters the church, thinking that he can realize his ambitions there, but the church is split along partisan lines and he casts his lot with the wrong side (the Jansenists as opposed to the Jesuits). It is women who save him.

朱利安错过了展现卓越军事才能的时代，他进入教会，以为可以在那里实现自己的抱负。然而，教会内部派系林立，他却误入歧途（加入了詹森派，而非耶稣会）。最终，是女性拯救了他。

His first love affair is with the wife of the mayor of his small town, who hires him to tutor her three sons. Madame de Rnal is as interesting as Julien—a retiring, innocent product of a strict upbringing, with no real friends or position in society, she has never even read a novel. She is entirely unprepared for the surge of passion she feels for Julien. At first Julien doesn't respond to her feelings, but the excitement of the liaison eventually arouses him, too, until the gossip of the town and the suspicions of M. de Rnal force the two of them to part.

他的初恋对象是小镇镇长的妻子，她聘请他担任自己三个儿子的家庭教师。德·拉纳尔夫人和于连一样有趣——她性格内向，天真无邪，家教甚严，没有真正的朋友，也没有社会地位，甚至从未读过小说。她完全没有预料到自己会对于连产生如此强烈的爱意。起初，于连对她的感情毫无回应，但这段恋情的刺激最终也唤醒了他，直到镇上的流言蜚语和德·拉纳尔先生的猜疑迫使两人分道扬镳。

Church politics bring Julien to Paris, to a position as secretary to a wealthy aristocrat and government minister, M. de La Mole, who has a son and a daughter about Julien's age. Julien quickly realizes that he has more on the ball than the son or the other young aristocrats who hang around. In the meantime, his employer begins to treat him with kindness and familiarity, and the daughter, Mathilde, a great beauty, begins to involve him in her self-created drama of grand, doomed passion. Julien is not precisely reluctant to go along, but his motives grow more out of pride and daring than out of actual love for Mathilde. The climax is precipitated by her discovery that she is pregnant.

教会政治将于连带到了巴黎，让他担任富有的贵族兼政府大臣德拉莫尔先生的秘书。德拉莫尔先生有一儿一女，年龄与于连相仿。于连很快意识到，自己比德拉莫尔先生的儿子和其他在德拉莫尔先生身边闲逛的年轻贵族们更有头脑。与此同时，他的雇主开始对他亲切友好，而德拉莫尔先生的女儿玛蒂尔德，一位绝世美人，也开始将他卷入自己精心编造的、注定悲剧的爱情故事中。于连并非完全不情愿，但他的动机更多是出于骄傲和冒险，而非对玛蒂尔德的真爱。故事的高潮是玛蒂尔德发现自己怀孕了。

Stendhal is matter-of-fact about the passions of his female characters, neither prudish nor sentimental. For Madame de Rnal, love only just overwhelms her religious scruples, but it does overwhelm them. For Mathilde, virtue is a social necessity, but neither a moral nor a religious imperative. Almost to the end, her goal is to be married to Julien on any terms, even the most compromising. It is Julien who repeatedly attempts to figure out how to reinsert her into society with as little damage to her reputation and her fate as possible. At the same time, Stendhal pays minute attention to the progress of each character's feelings—they are not defined as being “in love,” but rather the interplay of desire, pride, resentment, fear, second thoughts, prudence, and gamesmanship is carefully depicted, making Julien's love affairs seem rather cold by contrast to, say, the love of Tom Jones and Sophia Western, but infinitely more interesting. For Julien and his mistresses, the growth of love is political rather than natural, and, indeed, love has no goal except moment-by-moment sensation. Julien is not courting either woman, so a happy ending is not to be expected. Rather, the means justify the end: the passions of the characters set them so completely outside the normal run of mercenary, mean, and empty French society that they must die or go insane—Julien is executed, Madame de Rnal dies of a broken heart, and Mathilde acts out her mad ideal of a medieval queen (by coincidence, Marguerite de Navarre), burying her lover's head with her own hands, then building a shrine to it. The ending is neither comic nor tragic but ironic, made so by the carefully detailed social portrait of contemporary provincial and Parisian France that Stendhal never loses sight of.

司汤达对笔下女性角色的情感描写冷静客观，既不矫揉造作，也不多愁善感。对于德·拉纳尔夫人而言，爱情勉强压倒了她的宗教顾虑，但最终还是战胜了它们。对玛蒂尔德来说，美德是社会的必需品，但并非道德或宗教的强制要求。几乎直到故事的结尾，她的目标都是无论如何都要嫁给于连，哪怕是最妥协的条件。于连则反复尝试，想方设法让她重新融入社会，同时尽可能减少对她名誉和命运的损害。与此同时，司汤达细致入微地刻画了每个角色情感的演变——他们并非被简单地定义为“恋爱”，而是被细致地描绘了欲望、骄傲、怨恨、恐惧、犹豫、谨慎和权谋之间的微妙交织，这使得于连的爱情与汤姆·琼斯和索菲娅·韦斯特恩的爱情相比显得有些冷漠，却也更加引人入胜。对于连和他的情妇们来说，爱情的萌生并非自然而然，而是政治性的；事实上，爱情除了当下的感官体验之外，别无其他目的。于连并没有追求任何一位女子，因此，幸福的结局并不在意。相反，手段本身就足以证明结局的正当性：人物的激情将他们彻底置于唯利是图、卑鄙空虚的法国社会之外，以至于他们要么走向死亡，要么陷入疯狂——于连被处决，德·雷纳尔夫人因心碎而死，玛蒂尔德则活出了她疯狂的中世纪女王形象（巧合的是，她就是纳瓦拉的玛格丽特），亲手埋葬了爱人的头颅，并为他建造了一座神龛。结局既非喜剧也非悲剧，而是充满讽刺意味，这得益于司汤达对当时法国外省和巴黎社会细致入微的刻画，而他始终没有忽略这一点。

Julien, Mathilde, and Madame de Rnal are complex and fascinating characters, but the character of the narrator is at least as fascinating, and acts as a countervailing realistic consciousness in which their Romanticism is always submerged. He never fails to have a wide perspective, never fails to set their actions and feelings into social context, never fails to analyze the steps by which they arrive at decisions and actions. His France is never a transcendent or sentimentalized place—it is a place where greed, ambition, envy, and hatred are always at work, appearances are deceiving, and prudence is an essential virtue but no guarantee of safety. His voice is entirely ironic—he neither respects nor denigrates Julien's aspirations; he merely observes them with a degree of sympathy. He seems to like Madame de Rnal for the innocent profundity of her love and to respect the intensity of Mathilde's determination, but he recognizes that the three characters lose as well as gain by their actions. He doesn't offer them as models; there is an absurd quality to their choices that surely comes from the fact that Stendhal found the story and made himself its primary observer, but did not generate the story out of his own experience.

朱利安、玛蒂尔德和德·雷纳尔夫人都是复杂而迷人的角色，但叙述者的角色同样引人入胜，他扮演着一种与之抗衡的现实主义意识的角色，始终将他们的浪漫主义情怀置于其中。他始终保持着广阔的视野，始终将他们的行为和情感置于社会背景之中，始终分析他们做出决定和采取行动的步骤。他笔下的法国绝非一个超脱尘世或充满感伤的地方——这是一个贪婪、野心、嫉妒和仇恨始终交织的地方，表象具有欺骗性，谨慎虽是必要的品德，却无法保证安全。他的叙述语气完全是反讽式的——他既不尊重也不贬低朱利安的抱负；他只是带着某种程度的同情观察着它们。他似乎欣赏德·雷纳尔夫人纯真而深刻的爱，也敬佩玛蒂尔德坚定的决心，但他明白这三个角色在行动中既有得也有失。他并没有将他们作为榜样；他们的选择具有一种荒谬的特质，这无疑源于司汤达发现了这个故事，并让自己成为故事的主要观察者，但他并没有根据自己的经验创作这个故事。

The Red and the Black is not formally perfect. It seems to ramble, and the parts don't quite fit together. The shooting and the trial and the execution at the end go too quickly, and the novel has to cover more territory than it can handle with the degree of leisurely detail it employs in the first half. Julien is not entirely sympathetic. At times he is too scheming and at other times too proud. The case is made that he is extraordinary, but maybe he is really only something of a misfit. His psychology seems complete but not appealing. All the same, this is an incredibly rich novel, much more straightforwardly bold than the nineteenth-century novel is conventionally credited with being.

《红与黑》在形式上并非完美无瑕。它似乎有些散漫，各个部分衔接得不够流畅。枪击、审判和最后的处决都进行得太快，小说需要涵盖的内容远超其前半部分悠闲的描写所能驾驭的范围。朱利安这个角色并非完全讨喜。他有时过于阴险狡诈，有时又过于骄傲自大。作者试图证明他非同凡响，但或许他实际上只是个格格不入的人。他的心理刻画看似完整，却并不讨喜。尽管如此，这仍然是一部极其丰富的作品，其大胆直白的风格远超人们对十九世纪小说的传统认知。

# ↩

24. Nikolai Gogol Taras Bulba

24. 尼古拉·果戈理 塔拉斯·布尔巴

TRANS. BERNARD FARBAR (1835; REPR., PRESTIGE BOOKS, 1962), 125 PP.

转运。伯纳德·法巴尔（1835 年；出版，名誉图书，1962 年），125 页。

On the back of this out-of-print edition is a blurb from Ernest Hemingway, “One of the ten greatest books of all time!” Well, maybe yes. If not one of the ten greatest, certainly one of the greatest, if by great we mean that much of the time a reader is reading Taras Bulba , she experiences a conscious and pressing feeling of pleasure and admiration, or if by great we mean that some of the feelings one experiences are simultaneously strange and profound, as if the author's take on things is not merely original, but uprecedented.

在这本绝版书的封底，印着欧内斯特·海明威的推荐语：“史上十大最伟大的书籍之一！” 嗯，也许是吧。即便不是十大最伟大的书籍之一，也绝对是最伟大的书籍之一。如果我们所说的“伟大”是指读者在阅读《塔拉斯·布尔巴》时，大部分时间都能感受到一种清晰而强烈的愉悦和钦佩之情；或者如果我们所说的“伟大”是指读者所体验到的某些感受既奇特又深刻，仿佛作者对事物的见解不仅是原创的，而且是前所未有地。

Taras Bulba is brisk and refreshing and constantly communicates a sense that is more than authenticity and more than intelligence and more, even, than love. It is as if by thinking so continuously and with such concentration about his subject, Gogol (who was in his twenties when he wrote Taras Bulba) arrived at truth. This, of course, is the illusion of supreme art. The time is the sixteenth century. The place is the Ukrainian steppe, which is nominally controlled by Poland but subject to the depredations of the Tatars and the Turks. Taras and his family and friends are Cossacks, Slavic warrior bands who follow the Russian Orthodox religion and have been constantly at war for about two hundred years. Taras is a vigorous man of middle age with two sons just returning from school in Kiev. He takes them to the “Setch,” which is a townlike permanent encampment of Cossacks. Because treaties prevent the sort of raiding Taras would like for the training of his sons, he begins to instigate mischief by appealing to the pride of the warriors. Soon, though, a band shows up reporting that Jews have taken over churches and are charging Russians money to hold services and that Roman priests have harnessed Orthodox Christians to carriages. The Cossacks set out to avenge these insults and eventually lay siege to a walled Polish town.

《塔拉斯·布尔巴》节奏明快，令人耳目一新，它不断传递着一种超越真实、超越智慧，甚至超越爱的意味。仿佛果戈理（创作《塔拉斯·布尔巴》时年仅二十多岁）通过对主题的持续思考和专注，最终抵达了真理。当然，这只是至高艺术的幻象。故事发生在十六世纪的乌克兰草原，名义上由波兰统治，实则饱受鞑靼人和土耳其人的蹂躏。塔拉斯和他的家人朋友都是哥萨克人，他们是信奉俄罗斯东正教的斯拉夫武士，两百多年来一直处于战乱之中。塔拉斯是一位精力充沛的中年男子，他的两个儿子刚从基辅的学校毕业回家。他带着孩子们来到“塞奇”，那是哥萨克人一个类似城镇的永久营地。由于条约限制了塔拉斯为训练儿子们而希望进行的劫掠活动，他开始煽动战士们的骄傲，挑起事端。不久，一群人前来报告说，犹太人占领了教堂，并向俄罗斯人收取举行宗教仪式的费用；罗马教廷的牧师还强迫东正教徒骑在马车上。哥萨克人决心报复这些侮辱，最终围攻了一座波兰城墙环绕的城镇。

It is impossible to read this novella without looking through the lens of the 175 years that have intervened between Gogol's time and ours. Russians, Poles, Jews, and Muslims lived in proximity, all on fire with orthodoxy, all tempted and enraged by rumors and prejudices, and all armed. Gogol felt great admiration and kinship for the Cossacks (he was from Ukraine), and his admiration encompassed both the cruelty and the stoicism that were the terms of sixteenth-century existence.

如果不透过果戈理时代与我们时代之间相隔的175年这面镜子来解读这篇中篇小说，是不可能理解的。俄罗斯人、波兰人、犹太人和穆斯林比邻而居，他们都笃信东正教，都深受谣言和偏见的诱惑和激怒，也都拥有武器。果戈理对哥萨克人怀有深深的敬佩和亲近之情（他来自乌克兰），这种敬佩既包含了十六世纪生活的残酷，也包含了他们坚韧不拔的精神。

Out of this admiration, he forged a literary style that is intensely modern in the way it depicts paradoxes of feeling and sensation. At one point early in the novel, Gogol evokes a peace that truly passeth understanding:

出于这种钦佩，他创造了一种极具现代感的文学风格，这种风格描绘了情感和感觉的悖论。在小说的早期，果戈理曾描绘出一种真正超越理解的宁静：

Meanwhile the beauty of the July night had acquired a magnificent and awesome quality. It was the glare of the neighboring districts that had not yet burned to the ground. In one place the flame spread slowly and majestically over the heaven. In another, meeting with something inflammable and bursting into a whirlwind, it hissed and flew upwards to the very stars, and its severed tongues died in the highest regions of the sky. Here stood the charred, black monastery, like a stern Carthusian monk, displaying its gloomy grandeur at every new outburst of flame; there blazed the monastery garden. One could almost hear the trees hissing as they were wrapped up in smoke; and as the fire broke through, it suddenly lighted up clusters of ripe plums with a hot, phosphorescent, violet gleam or turned the yellow pears here and there to pure gold; and in the midst of this, hanging against the wall of the building or from a bough, would be seen the black figure of some poor Jew or monk whom the fire was devouring together with the building.

与此同时，七月的夜色更添了几分壮丽和震撼。那是邻近地区尚未被大火吞噬的火光。一处，火焰缓缓而庄严地蔓延至天际；另一处，火焰遇上易燃物，瞬间化作旋风，嘶嘶作响地直冲云霄，最终在天际最高处熄灭。焦黑的修道院矗立于此，宛如一位肃穆的卡尔特教派修士，在每一次新的火焰爆发中，都展现出它阴郁的威严；修道院的花园也燃起了熊熊烈火。人们仿佛能听到树木在浓烟中嘶嘶作响；当火焰突破防线时，一簇簇成熟的李子突然被炽热的磷光紫罗兰色光芒点亮，或将零星的黄梨染成纯金。在这片火海之中，人们会看到一些可怜的犹太人或僧侣的黑色身影，他们正和建筑物一起被大火吞噬，挂在建筑物的墙上或树枝上。

Taras's intentions for his sons, which amount to some enjoyable raiding and plunder, do not work out as planned. Taras, like most Cossacks, is disdainful of the softer attractions of women—the boys are meant to be warriors. But during the siege of the walled Polish town, his younger son, Andrei, betrays the Cossacks and his father, for the sake of the love of a seductive Polish beauty. Taras must kill him, which he does without remorse. The older boy, Ostap, less romantic, is brave and tough, but when the Cossacks are defeated, Ostap is captured and taken to Warsaw. Taras himself is wounded, but when he recovers, he persuades a Jewish merchant to sneak him into the Polish city, where he witnesses Ostap's dramatic torture and execution. The Cossacks’ subsequent revenge is violent and unmerciful, and Taras's last words call for war, not peace. Gogol's Cossacks are as unremitting and matter-of-fact as the Vikings of Egilssaga (and probably related to them, since Scandinavians under Rurik settled the north–south-flowing rivers of Russia in the Middle Ages).

塔拉斯对儿子们的期望不过是让他们享受劫掠的乐趣，但事与愿违。和大多数哥萨克一样，塔拉斯对女性的柔情蜜意不屑一顾——在他眼里，儿子们注定要成为战士。然而，在围攻波兰城墙环绕的城镇时，他的小儿子安德烈为了爱上一个妩媚的波兰女子，背叛了哥萨克和父亲。塔拉斯不得不杀了他，而且毫不留情。大儿子奥斯塔普则少了几分浪漫情怀，他勇敢坚韧，但哥萨克战败后，奥斯塔普被俘，押往华沙。塔拉斯本人也身负重伤，但康复后，他劝说一位犹太商人带他偷偷潜入波兰城，亲眼目睹了奥斯塔普遭受酷刑和处决的惨状。哥萨克随后展开了残酷无情的复仇，塔拉斯临终前呼吁战争，而非和平。果戈理笔下的哥萨克人像埃吉尔萨加的维京人一样不屈不挠、务实无华（而且可能与他们有关，因为在中世纪，留里克率领的斯堪的纳维亚人定居在俄罗斯南北流淌的河流沿岸）。

But the medieval Icelandic writers did not display a refined sense of the beauty of the landscape or a complex sense of the characteristic psychology of the Norsemen as Gogol does of the Cossacks. Taras and his sons are always shown in the context of Cossack culture, on the broad and beautiful stage of the central Asian grasslands. Like many Russian writers, Gogol employed his gifts in trying to discern the nature of Russianness and in forging a literary identity for Russia that would somehow help to engender a road to the future. Gogol's ideas were deeply conservative—true Russianness is defined, in Taras Bulba , as bold, muscular, nationalistic, and backward-looking. Each life is dictated by Fate and must be endured and challenged rather than thought through or arranged. National characteristics persist: Poles are Catholic, gaudy, effete, and treacherous; Tatars are unknowable; Jews are well connected (the novella's anti-Semitism is one of its more uncomfortable features); Cossacks are real men. But these national characteristics do not necessarily lead to salvation or redemption—in the context of sixteenth-century Ukraine, they only lead to more and more complex dilemmas and more grueling challenges that must be endured.

但中世纪冰岛作家对风景之美的细腻感知，以及对北欧人复杂心理的深刻洞察，远不及果戈理对哥萨克人的刻画。塔拉斯和他的儿子们总是被置于哥萨克文化的背景下，在中亚草原这片广袤美丽的舞台上展开。如同许多俄罗斯作家一样，果戈理运用他的才华，试图探寻俄罗斯性的本质，并为俄罗斯塑造一种文学身份，以期找到一条通往未来的道路。果戈理的思想根深蒂固地保守——在《塔拉斯·布尔巴》中，真正的俄罗斯性被定义为大胆、强健、民族主义和怀旧。每个人的人生都由命运主宰，必须忍受和挑战，而非深思熟虑或精心安排。民族特性依然存在：波兰人信奉天主教，衣着华丽，软弱无能，且奸诈狡诈；鞑靼人难以捉摸；犹太人关系密切（这部中篇小说中的反犹主义是其最令人不安的特征之一）。哥萨克人是真正的男子汉。但这些民族特性并不一定能带来救赎或解脱——在十六世纪的乌克兰，它们只会导致越来越复杂的困境和越来越严峻的挑战，而这些困境和挑战必须忍受。

Gogol's most famous novel is Dead Souls , which he partially destroyed before he died, and his most famous stories are “The Overcoat” and “The Nose.” He wrote several plays; the production of his satiric play The Inspector General resulted in his departure from Russia for Western Europe when it seemed to offend the czar, who left the theater during the first act. Gogol was and continues to be an immortal but controversial Russian writer whose works are difficult to categorize. Later, more ideological Russian authors often tried to enlist his works as evidence for his belief in one program or another, but Gogol's forms are so various and his tone so idiosyncratic that it is impossible to come up with a consistent set of beliefs that can be attributed to him. When he burned the final manuscipt of Dead Souls , it may have been because of a conversion to fanatical Russian Orthodox belief, or it may not have been for that reason at all—scholars don't agree. But individual completed works make perfect sense and are wonderfully enjoyable because Gogol is so inventive that the reader cannot resist suspending disbelief. He is the perfect example of a writer who cannot help but express the idea of artistic freedom even if, perhaps, it isn't in his best interest (as when he offended the czar and felt he had to exile himself) or something he wants to do (as when he completed Dead Souls in a way he himself rejected).

果戈理最著名的小说是《死魂灵》，他在去世前部分销毁了这部作品；他最著名的短篇小说是《外套》和《鼻子》。他创作了多部戏剧；他的讽刺剧《钦差大臣》的演出似乎冒犯了沙皇，导致他离开俄国前往西欧，沙皇在第一幕演出期间离场。果戈理是一位不朽的、但又充满争议的俄罗斯作家，他的作品难以归类。后来，一些意识形态色彩浓厚的俄罗斯作家常常试图引用他的作品来佐证他对某种理念的信仰，但果戈理的写作形式如此多样，他的文风又如此独特，以至于我们无法找到一套可以归于他的统一的信仰体系。他焚毁《死魂灵》的最终手稿，或许是因为他皈依了狂热的俄罗斯东正教信仰，或许并非如此——学者们对此莫衷一是。但果戈理的个别作品本身就合情合理，而且妙趣横生，因为果戈理的想象力如此丰富，以至于读者无法抗拒地沉浸其中。他完美地诠释了这样一位作家：他无法抑制地表达着艺术自由的理念，即便这或许并非出于他的最佳利益（例如，他触怒了沙皇，被迫自我流放），或者并非他所愿（例如，他以一种自己都否定的方式完成了《死魂灵》）。

25. Mikhail Lermontov A Hero of Our Time

25. 米哈伊尔·莱蒙托夫：我们时代的英雄

TRANS. PAUL FOOTE (1840; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1966), 185 PP.

保罗·富特译（1840 年；纽约：企鹅出版社，1966 年重印），185 页。

Lermontov wrote one novel, many poems, and some dramas and critical essays. He was born in 1814 , and became an acclaimed literary figure, the heir to Pushkin, before he turned twenty-four. He was exiled twice to the Caucasus, first for an inflammatory essay about Pushkin's death, and later for dueling. He fought three duels, and died in the third one at age twenty-eight. A Hero of Our Time , though it is short and in some sense fragmentary, and though all of its themes are outdated and it depicts an era that passed quickly and had few ramifications for the modern world, is truly a fascinating novel—for me, perhaps one of the most fascinating ever written.

莱蒙托夫一生创作了一部长篇小说、多首诗歌、一些戏剧和评论文章。他生于1814年，不到24岁就成为备受赞誉的文学人物，被誉为普希金的继承人。他曾两次被流放到高加索，第一次是因为一篇关于普希金之死的煽动性文章，第二次是因为决斗。他参与了三次决斗，并在第三次决斗中丧生，年仅28岁。《当代英雄》虽然篇幅短小，在某种程度上也略显零散，其主题也已过时，所描绘的时代转瞬即逝，对现代世界的影响微乎其微，但它仍然是一部引人入胜的小说——对我而言，它或许是有史以来最引人入胜的小说之一。

Lermontov's protagonist, Pechorin, was modeled on the eponymous hero of Pushkin's famous narrative poem Evgeny Onegin ( 1831 ). Part of the fascination of A Hero of Our Time is in the efficient and evocative way in which Lermontov constructs his narrative. Pechorin appears in five self-contained stories, the first two written by an unnamed narrator who is traveling in the Caucasus, meets up with an old soldier named Maxim Maximych, and elicits from him a tale of horse-stealing and abduction as an example of local color. He is intrigued by Pechorin, who has figured in that story, and becomes more intrigued when the two of them happen to run into Pechorin sometime later. When, in the second story, Pechorin refuses to take possession of his own journals, which Maxim Maximych has saved for him, the narrator asks to have them, and then “publishes” them. The last three stories are in Pechorin's voice. Of these, the longest, and the centerpiece of the novel, is “Princess Mary,” in which Pechorin coolly seduces and then disdains a girl he does not care for in full view of her cousin, Vera, a married woman who is the love of Pechorin's life, and also in full view of an old associate of his, Grushnitsky, who is himself in love with Mary. The intrigue leads to the death in a duel of Grushnitsky, a nervous breakdown for the girl, and ruin for Vera when her husband realizes he has been cuckolded. The last story is a meditation upon Fate, and ends just before Pechorin meets Maxim Maximych for the first time. The sequence of stories makes a narrative circle—“Bela” comes after “Princess Mary” chronologically, but before it in the novel; enigmas of Pechorin's character as it appears in “Bela” are explained in “Princess Mary” and “The Fatalist.” All five of the stories resonate with one another, as does the third-person narrative by “Lermontov” juxtaposed with the first-person narrative by Pechorin. At the end, the reader feels she has become remarkably intimate with Pechorin and, given his pleasure in manipulating people and wrecking lives, such intimacy carries a measure of discomfort. But only a measure. Pechorin's voice is so simultaneously confiding, honest, clear, and reasonable that he does seem remarkable in the end—the reader is seduced as the women had been. Is he exceptional? Is he one of a kind or just a glib example of a type? What are the wellsprings of his character? Is his life an example of social and political waste, an example of the workings of Fate, the inevitable result of poor upbringing and education? Do we like him? Does his honesty make up for his selfishness? Is he cold or despairing?

莱蒙托夫笔下的主人公佩乔林是以普希金著名叙事诗《叶甫根尼·奥涅金》（1831）中的同名主人公为原型创作的。《当代英雄》的魅力之一在于莱蒙托夫简洁而富有感染力的叙事结构。佩乔林出现在五个独立的故事中，前两个故事由一位在高加索旅行的匿名叙述者撰写。这位叙述者遇到了一位名叫马克西姆·马克西米奇的老兵，并从他那里听来了一个关于偷马和绑架的故事，以此作为当地风土人情的例证。他对故事中的人物佩乔林很感兴趣，后来两人再次偶遇佩乔林时，这种兴趣更加浓厚。在第二个故事中，佩乔林拒绝接受马克西姆·马克西米奇为他保存的日记，叙述者便要求得到这些日记，然后将其“出版”。最后三个故事均以佩乔林的视角叙述。其中最长、也是小说的核心篇章是《玛丽公主》。在这个故事中，佩乔林当着玛丽公主的表妹薇拉——一位已婚女子，也是佩乔林一生挚爱——以及他的老相识格鲁什尼茨基的面，冷酷地引诱并轻蔑地抛弃了自己并不在意的女孩。格鲁什尼茨基本人也深爱着玛丽。这场阴谋最终导致格鲁什尼茨基在决斗中丧命，玛丽公主精神崩溃，而薇拉则因丈夫发现自己被戴了绿帽子而家道中落。最后一个故事是对命运的沉思，结尾恰好在佩乔林与马克西姆·马克西米奇初次相遇之前。这些故事构成了一个叙事上的循环——《贝拉》在时间顺序上位于《玛丽公主》之后，但在小说中却位于《玛丽公主》之前；《贝拉》中展现的佩乔林性格的谜团在《玛丽公主》和《宿命论者》中得到了解答。这五个故事彼此呼应，莱蒙托夫的第三人称叙述与佩乔林的第一人称叙述交相辉映。故事结尾，读者会感到自己与佩乔林之间建立了一种非同寻常的亲密关系。鉴于他乐于操纵他人、毁掉他人的人生，这种亲密关系难免令人感到一丝不安。但仅仅是一丝不安而已。佩乔林的声音既坦诚、真诚、清晰又合情合理，以至于最终他显得格外引人注目——读者如同那些女性一样，被他深深吸引。他是否真的与众不同？他是独一无二的，还是仅仅是某种类型人物的拙劣模仿？他性格的根源是什么？他的人生是社会和政治的浪费，是命运的捉弄，还是糟糕的成长环境和教育的必然结果？我们喜欢他吗？他的坦诚能否弥补他的自私？他是冷漠无情还是绝望绝望？

The key to Pechorin's success as a narrator of his own adventures is his impeccable manners. He details the action clearly and reports on his own feelings and doubts about what he is doing calmly, without any sort of undue emotion. He even reports on his emotions (such as his fear and despair after the fatal duel) without undue emotion. Nothing is so seductive in a narrator as self-knowledge, and Pechorin seems to have some. He doesn't know why he is as he is, and he doesn't know how or why he might change, but he does seem to know who he is, and in the end, that is enough.

佩乔林之所以能成功地讲述自己的冒险经历，关键在于他无可挑剔的举止。他能清晰地描述事件经过，并冷静地叙述自己的感受和疑虑，不带任何过激的情绪。即使是描述自己的情绪（例如决斗后内心的恐惧和绝望），他也同样保持着克制。对于叙述者而言，最吸引人的莫过于对自身的了解，而佩乔林似乎就具备这种能力。他不知道自己为何如此，也不知道自己会如何改变，更不知道为何会改变，但他似乎清楚自己是谁，而最终，这就足够了。

The narrator's ostensible reason for writing is that he is keeping travel notes, and in the first two stories in particular the mountain scenes of the Caucasus region of central Asia—high, snow-covered peaks, rough roads, native families in huts and tents, Cossacks in forts—are beautifully evoked. To the modern reader, the references to the Chechen rebels and the Muslim villagers are eerie and striking. We understand the plight Bela is in once she has been kidnapped and seduced by Pechorin because we have seen Afghan women in veils in the news. At the beginning of the twenty-first century, A Hero of Our Time turns out to be a compelling historical document in a way that it might not have been in 1975 , and this is a testament to Lermontov's powers of observation and his sense that descriptions of the exotic regions he passed through were appropriate to the form of the novel.

叙述者写作的表面理由是记录旅行见闻，尤其是在前两个故事中，他对中亚高加索地区的山景——高耸入云、白雪皑皑的山峰、崎岖不平的道路、居住在茅屋和帐篷里的当地居民、驻守堡垒的哥萨克骑兵——描绘得栩栩如生。对于现代读者而言，文中提及的车臣叛军和穆斯林村民令人毛骨悚然，也极具冲击力。我们之所以能够理解贝拉被佩乔林绑架和诱骗后的困境，是因为我们在新闻中见过戴着面纱的阿富汗妇女。在二十一世纪初，《当代英雄》展现出一种引人入胜的历史文献价值，这在1975年或许难以想象，也证明了莱蒙托夫敏锐的观察力以及他对所到之处异域风情的描写与小说形式的契合。

Pushkin was the younger Lermontov's friend and model, but for our purposes, a key difference between each author's work is that one is poetry and the other is prose. Pushkin's lovers and their story typify certain Russian qualities that are lovingly described in his poetry—this is how lyricism in poetry works. Images are coordinated by poetic forms so they will coalesce into a larger meaning that makes something general of their particular qualities. Prose makes no such promises. The mountains in the distance may mean something, but they may not—they may only be a majestic backdrop, their exotic appearance sufficient reason for them to be described, especially when the novel explicitly presents itself as a travel narrative. The very ambiguity that defines Pechorin comes from the contingent elements of the narrative about him. The structure of the novel shows that certain events took place; materials narrating those events were gathered together by means of a separate sequence of events; the book we have in our hands represents still another sequence of events—an interpretive sequence. The conceit is that all of these sequences came about by chance. Do they add up to something? This is the novel as casual and natural, as almost not a novel, as having only a fortuitous existence, not an intentional one. It is conceit that might not have worked except that the idle confiding coolness of Pechorin's tone makes it work.

普希金是小莱蒙托夫的朋友和榜样，但就我们的目的而言，两位作家作品的关键区别在于，一位是诗歌，另一位是散文。普希金笔下的恋人及其故事体现了某些俄罗斯特质，这些特质在他的诗歌中得到了深情的描绘——这就是诗歌抒情性的运作方式。诗歌形式协调意象，使它们凝聚成更宏大的意义，从而将各自的特质概括为某种普遍意义。散文则没有这样的承诺。远处的群山或许具有某种意义，或许没有——它们可能仅仅是雄伟的背景，其异域风情足以成为描述它们的理由，尤其是在小说明确以游记形式呈现的情况下。定义佩乔林的正是这种模糊性，它源于围绕他展开的叙事中那些偶然的元素。小说的结构表明某些事件确实发生过；叙述这些事件的素材是通过另一套事件序列收集起来的；而我们手中的这本书则代表了另一套事件序列——一套诠释序列。这种构思的奇特之处在于，所有这些情节都是偶然发生的。它们最终是否指向某种意义？这部小说如此随意自然，几乎不像是一部小说，它的存在仅仅是偶然，而非刻意为之。这种构思原本可能并不奏效，但佩乔林那种漫不经心、坦诚而又冷静的语气却让它得以成立。

A Hero of Our Time demonstrates that flawless judgment and technical genius of an author can go a long way to overcome being passed over by history. A novel need not fall entirely into the historical document category, as so many, once thought great, have done. If a narrator, either third-person or first-person, strikes up a comfortable and interesting relationship with the reader, the reader is happy to read about almost anything.

《当代英雄》证明，作者卓越的判断力和精湛的写作技巧足以弥补被历史遗忘的遗憾。小说不必完全沦为历史文献，尽管许多曾经被奉为经典的作品最终都落入了历史文献的窠臼。如果叙述者——无论是第三人称还是第一人称——能够与读者建立起一种轻松有趣的关系，读者便会乐于阅读几乎任何题材的作品。

26. Honor de Balzac

26. 奥诺·德·巴尔扎克

Cousin Pons

表哥庞斯

TRANS. HERBERT J. HUNT

译者：赫伯特·J·亨特

(1846-47; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1965, 1968), 334 PP.

（1846-47 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1965 年、1968 年），334 页。

Cousin Bette

表妹贝蒂

TRANS. MARION AY TON CRAWFORD
TRANS. MARION AY TON CRAWFORD

(1846-47; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1965, 1968), 448 PP.

（1846-47 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1965 年、1968 年），448 页。

Balzac's greatest work is a cycle of novels called La Comdie hu-maine , in which he attempts to capture the vastness and variety of life in Paris in the middle of the nineteenth century. Each novel and story is different, and meant to stand alone, but many characters recur in different capacities. The result is a dense fictional kaleidoscope of materialism, envy, spite, worldliness, and occasional virtue—characters of all ages and types and social positions encounter one another, act in one another's dramas, and then go on, in many cases, to something completely different. Two important novels in the larger project are Cousin Bette and Cousin Pons , which were written as a pair on the theme of “poor relations.”
