巴尔扎克最伟大的作品是名为《人间喜剧》的系列小说，他试图捕捉十九世纪中期巴黎生活的广阔与多样性。每部小说和故事都各不相同，原本可以独立成篇，但许多人物以不同的身份反复出现。最终呈现出一幅纷繁复杂的虚构万花筒，其中充斥着物质主义、嫉妒、怨恨、世故和偶尔闪现的美德——各个年龄段、各种类型、不同社会地位的人物彼此相遇，在彼此的人生戏剧中扮演着重要角色，然后，在很多情况下，走向截然不同的人生道路。在这一宏大的创作计划中，两部重要的小说是《贝蒂表妹》和《庞斯表哥》，这两部小说以“穷亲戚”为主题，共同创作而成。

Balzac was a great materialist. His novels always discuss money, and most of his characters are motivated largely by greed, though occasionally by lust. How much income each has, the expenses of each, what each wants to earn by gaining some sort of position, how much it costs to live in Paris or to marry a daughter to a desirable husband are all central concerns in Balzac's world. In this sense he is the quintessential realistic novelist, since nothing drives sentimentality out of a novel like exact sums of money, and monetary anxiety is a common feature of novel plots, both because the opposing temptations of greed and true feeling offer efficient moral choices for characters and because authors themselves are often writing for a living and pressed for money, and so monetary questions are interesting to them.

巴尔扎克是一位伟大的唯物主义者。他的小说总是围绕金钱展开，他笔下的大多数人物都受贪婪驱使，偶尔也会受到欲望的影响。每个人的收入、支出、渴望通过某种地位获得什么、在巴黎生活需要多少钱，或者把女儿嫁给一个理想的丈夫需要多少钱，这些都是巴尔扎克世界的核心问题。从这个意义上讲，他是典型的现实主义小说家，因为没有什么比精确的金钱数字更能驱散小说中的感伤主义，而金钱焦虑也是小说情节的常见特征。这既是因为贪婪和真情之间的对立诱惑为人物提供了有效的道德选择，也是因为作家本身常常为了谋生而写作，面临经济压力，因此金钱问题对他们来说也颇具吸引力。

For Cousin Bette and Cousin Pons, considerations of poverty and dependence on wealthy relatives are central to their characters. Bette is the plain cousin; her pretty benefactor has been married long ago to a dedicated libertine whom she loves very much. This woman, Baroness Hulot, who is exceptionally religious, has tried to help Bette, but Bette has secretly cultivated her resentments. She attempts to harm the family in every way possible while all the time pretending to be grateful and affectionate. Cousin Pons is a small-time musician and big-time collector of objets d'art. Because he is devoted to and jealous of his collection, he lives in poverty—his only pleasure is gastronomy. He is in the habit of dining with his wealthy friends and benefactors, but over the years he gets less and less welcome at their tables, and eventually he is insulted and dismissed by his cousins, who have no idea he owns an enviable treasure. He has one friend, Schmcke, who is, indeed, a schmuck—an utter innocent who loves Pons but can hardly help him against the vultures who gather once the news of his wealth emerges. Most of the novel describes Pons's decline toward death as everyone but Schmcke and a couple of people from the theater where he works scheme to steal, defraud, and murder.

对于贝蒂表妹和庞斯表哥来说，贫困和对富裕亲戚的依赖是他们性格的核心。贝蒂相貌平平；她那位漂亮的恩人很久以前就嫁给了一个放荡不羁的浪荡子，而她非常爱这个男人。这位名叫于洛男爵夫人的女子极其虔诚，曾试图帮助贝蒂，但贝蒂却暗自怀恨在心。她想方设法地伤害这个家庭，同时又假装感激涕零、亲切友好。庞斯表哥是个名不见经传的小音乐家，却是一位狂热的艺术品收藏家。由于他痴迷于自己的收藏，并且对它们极度珍视，他的生活十分贫困——他唯一的乐趣就是美食。他习惯于与富有的朋友和恩人共进晚餐，但随着时间的推移，他越来越不受待见，最终被他的表兄弟们羞辱和疏远，而他们却丝毫不知他拥有令人艳羡的珍宝。他只有一个朋友，名叫施姆克，这人确实是个傻瓜——一个彻头彻尾的傻瓜，他爱着庞斯，却无力阻止那些在他财富消息传开后蜂拥而至的觊觎者。小说的大部分篇幅都在描写庞斯走向死亡的过程，除了施姆克和他工作的剧院里的几个人之外，所有人都密谋着偷窃、诈骗和谋杀。

Both novels have several gruesome fascinations. In Cousin Bette , Bette's protge, a young woman she sponsors as a seductress, contracts a fatal and disfiguring venereal disease, which Balzac describes in some detail. In Cousin Pons , Pons is tormented by his concierge, whose attempts to bully him to death by haranguing and contradicting him are portrayed at length. In both novels the sordid habitations of the poor or low characters are described with relish. It is also true, though, that Pons's cherished collection is carefully depicted—Balzac himself was a knowledgeable and ambitious collector who perhaps awarded to Pons pieces he himself might have wished to own.

两部小说都包含一些令人毛骨悚然的引人入胜之处。《贝蒂表妹》中，贝蒂的门徒——一个她资助的、被她培养成诱惑者的年轻女子——染上了一种致命且毁容的性病，巴尔扎克对此进行了细致的描写。《庞斯表兄》中，庞斯饱受门房的折磨，门房不断对他进行谩骂和反驳，试图将他逼死，这一情节也被详尽地刻画出来。两部小说都饶有兴致地描写了穷人或底层人物肮脏不堪的住所。不过，庞斯珍爱的收藏品也得到了细致的描绘——巴尔扎克本人是一位博学而雄心勃勃的收藏家，他或许将一些自己梦寐以求的藏品赠予了庞斯。

Many novelists of the mid-nineteenth century had social theories, and Balzac's narratives are regularly interspersed with expository asides on such things as the course of Pons's illness or the reasons certain dying people have visions and others don't. Balzac was not as careful of his authorial voice and narrative position as certain more artful authors such as George Eliot and Henry James were later, but he was writing very quickly—the cycle of novels (projected to be 115 volumes, with 85 completed) was organized and written in about ten years (some of the volumes were already written when Balzac decided how he was going to shape his larger project). The author had to devise a natural and eloquent storytelling method that enabled him to deliver both information and drama easily and quickly. His stories are sus-penseful and his intrusions seem automatic, as if the conversational voice is right there beside the composing voice, ready to offer additional insights at any time. Balzac seems almost uniquely unself-conscious as an author, as if, in the rush of events and analysis, he simply doesn't have time to ponder and cultivate his narrative presentation.

十九世纪中期许多小说家都持有社会理论，巴尔扎克的叙事中也经常穿插着对庞斯病情发展或某些临终者为何能看到幻象而另一些人却看不到幻象等问题的旁白。巴尔扎克不像后来的乔治·艾略特和亨利·詹姆斯等一些技艺更为精湛的作家那样注重作者的声音和叙事立场，但他写作速度极快——这部计划创作115卷的小说系列（已完成85卷）在大约十年内就完成了编排和写作（巴尔扎克在决定如何构建他的宏大计划时，部分卷册已经写好）。作者必须设计出一种自然流畅、引人入胜的叙事方法，使他能够轻松快捷地传递信息和戏剧冲突。他的故事悬念迭起，旁白的插入显得自然流畅，仿佛对话的声音就与叙述的声音并肩而立，随时准备提供新的见解。巴尔扎克作为作家似乎有着一种近乎独一无二的不拘泥于自我意识的态度，仿佛在事件和分析的洪流中，他根本没有时间去思考和精心构思他的叙事表达方式。

Nor does Balzac seem to have a larger political theory. Many of his characters are vile—inhumanly greedy, callous, cruel, and almost too cold even to be called sadistic. Bette is one of these—on her deathbed “quite wretched at the good fortune that was shining on her family,” her only comfort is that they have no idea how she hates them and are, therefore, “mourning her as the good angel of the family” (p. 458 ). Her cousin-in-law, Baron Hulot, who seems in the last chapters to have been redeemed by the suffering of his wife and family, ends up in the bed of the kitchen maid; his saintly and devoted wife overhears him say to the girl, “My wife hasn't long to live, and if you like you can be a baroness” (p. 461 ). Balzac accounts for their natures by depicting Paris, France, and Frenchness in ever more detail, leaving the reader to conclude that the characters are horrible because they are French, and perhaps even more horrible because they live in Paris (although the narrow-minded greed of some of the provincial characters, like Bette and like the father in the opening chapters of Lost Illusions , is perhaps more brutishly automatic than that of socially calculating Parisians). In Cousin Pons , innocence is reserved for Schmcke, who is German, and kindliness is reserved for some of the hardworking theater people, who seem to actually have fun from time to time, but at any rate to be relatively free of the status anxiety that motivates the others. In Cousin Bette Madame Hulot plays the same role, though her innocence is a result of faith rather than nationality. These characters do not figure in the plots as models to be emulated, though. Rather they end up as consenting dupes for the others, simply because they do not have the energy or the perspicacity to counteract the endless plots against them. Balzac, therefore, expresses a version of novelistic conservatism— humans are unredeemed and apparently unredeemable; France is a Boschian landscape of iniquity, Paris its sewer. Even so, Balzac's novels have a comic liveliness, as if the author's fascination with the social scene were unbounded and its very energy compensated for its repellent inhabitants.

巴尔扎克似乎也没有什么宏大的政治理论。他笔下的许多人物都十分卑劣——贪婪得毫无人性，冷酷无情，残忍至极，甚至冷血到几乎称不上虐待狂。贝蒂就是其中之一——在她临终之际，“对家族所享有的好运感到无比痛苦”，她唯一的慰藉是，家人并不知道她有多么憎恨他们，因此“把她当作家族的守护天使来哀悼”（第458页）。她的表兄于洛男爵，在最后几章中似乎因妻子和家人的苦难而得到救赎，最终却与厨房女仆同床共枕；他那圣洁而忠诚的妻子无意中听到他对女仆说：“我的妻子时日不多了，如果你愿意，你可以成为女男爵”（第461页）。巴尔扎克通过对巴黎、法国以及法国文化的细致描绘来解释人物的性格，让读者得出这样的结论：这些人物之所以可怕，是因为他们是法国人；或许更可怕的是他们生活在巴黎（尽管像贝蒂和《幻灭》开篇几章中的父亲那样的某些外省人物的狭隘贪婪，可能比那些精于算计的巴黎人的贪婪更加粗暴无情）。在《表兄庞斯》中，天真无邪的特质属于德国人施姆克，而善良则属于一些辛勤工作的戏剧界人士，他们似乎偶尔也能享受生活，但至少相对而言，他们不像其他人那样受制于身份焦虑。在《表兄贝蒂》中，于洛夫人扮演着类似的角色，尽管她的天真源于信仰而非国籍。然而，这些人物在故事情节中并非作为值得效仿的榜样出现。相反，他们最终沦为他人的傀儡，仅仅因为他们既无力也无洞察力去对抗针对他们的无休止的阴谋。因此，巴尔扎克表达了一种小说式的保守主义——人性无可救药，而且似乎也无法被救赎；法国是一幅博斯笔下罪恶横行的景象，巴黎则是其罪恶的污水沟。即便如此，巴尔扎克的小说仍然充满喜剧般的活力，仿佛作者对社会景象的迷恋永无止境，而这种活力本身就足以弥补其中令人厌恶的人物。

27. Charlotte Brontë Jane Eyre

27. 夏洛蒂·勃朗特《简·爱》

(1847; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 2000), 397 PP.

（1847 年；重印，纽约：W. W. NORTON，2000 年），397 页。

If many, or most, European novels take up the question of what is to be done about, or with, girls, Jane Eyre is one of the first to most steadily and resolutely address the question of “What do girls (or women) want?” Jane's great characteristic, from the moment we meet her, is to be immovably certain about what she wants. She is not influenced by the opinions of those in authority about what she should want or must not want, and punishment only reinforces her sense of self. She is never deluded, like the heroine of The Female Quixote , for example, and never unsure of her feelings, like Pamela. She recognizes that she might not fit into the world as it is constituted, that she might have to settle for less than she knows is available, but, romantic as she is, she is an intransigent realist about herself. Her journey of self-knowledge is never about discovering true feeling; it is always about making connections between appearances and realities, about separating truths from lies.

如果说许多（或大多数）欧洲小说都在探讨如何对待女孩，那么《简·爱》则是最早以最坚定、最果断的方式探讨“女孩（或女人）想要什么？”这一问题的作品之一。从我们认识简的那一刻起，她最大的特点就是对自己想要的东西无比确定。她不受权威人士关于她应该想要什么或不应该想要什么的意见影响，惩罚反而强化了她的自我认知。她不像《女堂吉诃德》中的女主人公那样自欺欺人，也不像帕梅拉那样对自己的感情犹豫不决。她意识到自己或许无法融入这个世界，或许不得不接受低于她所知的现实，但尽管她充满浪漫情怀，她对自己却是一个毫不妥协的现实主义者。她的自我认知之旅并非在于发现真情实感，而在于将表象与现实联系起来，在于辨别真假。

Jane's is the archetypal orphan tale. A plain girl, reviled by her relatives, sets out on her lonely life journey. She must use the tools she has. In her case, these are intelligence and a passion to minutely observe everyone around her. Given the chance, she can love and respect those worthy of her love and respect—the nurse Bessie, her friend Helen Burns, her teacher Miss Temple—but she offers neither love nor respect to those who treat her badly or are in themselves unworthy. In a hierarchical society she refuses categorically to be servile or even to show the normal forms of respect. As a result, she is profoundly lonely, but she has no idea, except through work, of how to assuage her loneliness. She encounters the Beast—in this case Mr. Rochester, the unhappy and intimidating lord of the manor—and she readily understands that he is more bluff than bite. He, for his part, recognizes something in her—honesty in every sense—that he finds intriguing and then seductive. He decides that he must have her, and engineers that very thing that Pamela was so afraid of, a false marriage (full of true feeling, but illegal). Jane escapes, becomes destitute, and is rescued by kind strangers who turn out to be long-lost relatives. She gains a fortune through the death of a distant uncle, shares it with her relatives, and escapes, at the last moment, another false marriage—this one legal but without feeling. She returns to Rochester, discovers that he has been maimed, blinded, and widowed all in one unlucky (lucky) accident, and, Reader, she marries him.

简的故事是典型的孤儿故事。一个相貌平平的女孩，被亲戚们厌恶，踏上了孤独的人生旅程。她必须利用自己所拥有的资源。对她而言，这些资源是智慧和敏锐的观察力。如果有机会，她可以爱和尊重那些值得她爱和尊重的人——保姆贝西、朋友海伦·伯恩斯、老师坦普尔小姐——但她对那些虐待她或本身就不值得她爱和尊重的人，既不爱也不尊重。在一个等级森严的社会里，她断然拒绝卑躬屈膝，甚至拒绝表现出通常的尊重。结果，她感到无比孤独，但除了工作之外，她不知道该如何排解这种孤独。她遇到了“野兽”——在这个故事里，这个“野兽”指的是罗切斯特先生，那位郁郁寡欢、令人畏惧的庄园主——她很快就明白，他只是虚张声势，并没有真正的攻击性。他却在她身上看到了某种特质——一种全方位的真诚——这让他着迷，并最终被她深深吸引。他决定一定要得到她，于是精心策划了帕梅拉一直害怕的事情：一场虚假的婚姻（充满真情实感，却不合法）。简逃离了这段婚姻，变得一贫如洗，幸得几位好心的陌生人相救，而这些人竟然是她失散多年的亲戚。她从一位远房叔叔的去世中继承了一笔遗产，与亲戚们分享，并在最后一刻逃脱了另一场虚假的婚姻——这次的婚姻合法却毫无感情。她回到罗切斯特，发现他因一场不幸（却也幸运）的意外而致残、失明并成了鳏夫，读者朋友们，她嫁给了他。

Jane Eyre is as satisfying as it is unsatisfying. The material is as powerful as the strongest wish—that the fascinating man is yielding and loving within, that the plain girl appeals, that a connection can be so powerful as to express itself telepathically across a hundred miles, that the chastened groom and the vindicated bride can live happily (and in good conscience) forever after, that good can grow out of evil. However, realism keeps inserting itself. At the highest moments of the drama—particularly when Jane hears Rochester calling her and when she discovers his newly reduced condition—the reader is tempted to back away, sensing that this is not how life works, and Jane's unique journey is atypical and therefore unlikely and implausible.

《简·爱》既令人满足又令人失望。故事的素材如同最强烈的愿望一般强大——希望那位迷人的男子内心温柔体贴，希望那位相貌平平的女子心生爱慕，希望彼此间的联系能够跨越百里，心灵感应般地传递，希望悔改的新郎和洗清冤屈的新娘从此过上幸福美满（且心安理得）的生活，希望善能够从恶中诞生。然而，现实的残酷却不断袭来。在剧情最扣人心弦的时刻——尤其是当简听到罗切斯特的呼唤，以及发现他日渐衰弱的境况时——读者不禁会想要退缩，因为他们意识到生活并非如此，简的独特经历非同寻常，因而显得不太可能，也难以令人信服。

Now we are at the heart of the dilemma of the novel. Are the stories the novel relates typical or unique? Do we expect the novel to reconfirm our beliefs about the world or to challenge them? Is the point of the novel the revelation of the ideal or the depiction of the real? In fact, no individual novelist can decide which side of this dilemma to adopt. Realism or idealism is native to his or her temperament and intrinsic to his or her vision of the world. But Jane Eyre reveals something about the dilemma—compelling idealistic novels, novels that grow from wishes—are beloved. Compelling realistic novels, novels that grow from astute observation of likely outcomes, are respected. A diet of too many idealistic novels comes to seem shallow. A diet of too many realistic novels comes to seem sordid.

现在我们触及了小说困境的核心。小说讲述的故事是典型的还是独特的？我们期待小说印证我们对世界的认知，还是挑战它们？小说的目的是揭示理想，还是描绘现实？事实上，没有哪个小说家能够决定自己应该选择哪一边。现实主义还是理想主义，取决于他或她的性情，也取决于他或她的世界观。但《简·爱》揭示了这一困境的某些方面——引人入胜的理想主义小说，那些源于愿望的小说，备受喜爱；引人入胜的现实主义小说，那些源于对可能结果的敏锐观察的小说，则受到尊重。过多的理想主义小说会显得肤浅，过多的现实主义小说则会显得庸俗。

For some readers, the idea that Jane and Rochester communicate telepathically at the moment when both are experiencing their greatest distress is perfectly plausible. The two of them have demonstrated in several ways before this point that even though their intentions and social positions are different, their spirits are joined. Jane, especially, believes in the tangible expression of spiritual qualities. Brontë has prepared the ground rather carefully, with her depiction of Jane's school friend Helen Burns and Jane's discovery of her cousins. In fact, the whole novel demonstrates the power of projection. The orphan girl of unique mental strength summons up both her trials and their rewards. All the scenes she passes through are vivid, dramatic, and essentially solitary, as if displayed for the education of herself alone. The novel seems to be, and only works as, a document of subjectivity. For some readers this subjectivity coincides with their own experience of the world and is right. For others it is ridiculous.

对某些读者而言，简和罗切斯特在各自最痛苦的时刻进行心灵感应的想法完全合情合理。此前，两人已多次表明，尽管他们的意图和社会地位不同，但他们的精神却紧密相连。尤其是简，她相信精神特质可以具象化。勃朗特精心铺垫，通过对简的同学海伦·伯恩斯以及简发现表亲的描写，为这一情节埋下了伏笔。事实上，整部小说都展现了投射的力量。这位拥有非凡精神力量的孤女，将她经历的磨难和收获都娓娓道来。她所经历的一切场景都生动鲜明、扣人心弦，且本质上是孤独的，仿佛是为了自我启迪而呈现。这部小说似乎，也只有作为一部主观性记录才能成立。对某些读者而言，这种主观性与他们自身的体验相吻合，是正确的。而对另一些读者而言，它则显得荒谬可笑。

Nevertheless, it takes a novel of unique subjectivity and stubbornness to even ask the question “What do women themselves want?” as opposed to the question “What should be done with women?” Jane's answer is, women want independent, equal, and loving connection at whatever social cost. The vitality of Jane Eyre in the 158 years since publication and its niche in the lives of adolescent girls have given it political as well as artistic power. Many girls have come to know, through Jane Eyre , what it is possible to want, even if, as they grow up, they back away from the cost.

然而，只有一部小说拥有独特的视角和不屈不挠的精神，才会提出“女性自身想要什么？”这个问题，而不是“应该如何对待女性？”。简·爱的答案是：女性渴望独立、平等和充满爱的关系，无论付出怎样的社会代价。自出版以来的158年间，《简·爱》的生命力以及它在少女生活中占据的重要地位，赋予了它政治和艺术的双重力量。许多女孩通过《简·爱》了解到，她们可以渴望什么，即使长大后，她们会因为害怕付出代价而退缩。

28. Emily Brontë. Wuthering Heights

28. 艾米莉·勃朗特。《呼啸山庄》

(1847; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1995), 338 PP.

（1847 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1995 年），338 页。

Whereas Jane Eyre is a recognizable young woman, uncompromising but not terrifically unusual, who makes the case that governesses, though quiet and plain, have full inner lives and deserve consideration, the characters of Wuthering Heights are hardly recognizable at all, and most readers encounter them with fascinated amazement. I would suggest that they come to seem stranger and more inhumane as the reader gets older—their absolutism and passion seem more normal to a girl in her early teens, caught in the tangle of junior high school, than they do to someone who has married, had children, and gotten in the habit of conforming to social expectations.

简·爱是一位形象鲜明的年轻女性，她固执己见，但并非特立独行，她证明了家庭教师虽然安静朴素，却拥有丰富多彩的内心世界，值得被尊重。而《呼啸山庄》中的人物则截然不同，他们几乎完全陌生，大多数读者在阅读时都感到既着迷又惊奇。我认为，随着读者年龄的增长，这些人物会显得更加怪异，甚至更加不近人情——他们的专断和激情对于一个十几岁、正处于初中生活困境的女孩来说或许更为正常，但对于一个已经结婚生子、习惯于循规蹈矩的人来说，却显得格格不入。

Emily Brontë was only thirty when she died, and although Charlotte lived with her and had known her all her life, she did not profess to understand her, or even to understand her novel, which was published in the same year as Jane Eyre. Charlotte seemed wild and intransigent to her biographer Elizabeth Gaskell, but Emily seemed “stronger than a man, simpler than a child” to Charlotte. She likened Emily's novel to a mountain crag become human. It had not so much been written by Emily as come through her, fully formed. Additionally, Emily didn't have much to say—she left no letters and few diary entries. There are no reported conversations. Heathcliff, Catherine, Linton, and their children seem real: it is Emily who seems ghostly.

艾米莉·勃朗特去世时年仅三十岁。尽管夏洛蒂与她同住，相识一生，但她并不声称自己理解艾米莉，甚至不理解她那部与《简·爱》同年出版的小说。在传记作者伊丽莎白·盖斯凯尔眼中，夏洛蒂显得狂野不羁，而艾米莉在夏洛蒂眼中却“比男人更坚强，比孩子更纯真”。她将艾米莉的小说比作一座具人性的山峰。与其说是艾米莉写成的，不如说是透过她，完整地呈现出来。此外，艾米莉很少说话——她没有留下任何信件，日记也寥寥无几。没有任何关于她与夏洛蒂对话的记载。希斯克利夫、凯瑟琳、林顿以及他们的孩子们都栩栩如生：反倒是艾米莉仿佛幽灵一般。

Reviewers at the time didn't know quite what to make of Wuthering Heights —it was almost as if it arrived from another country, where the customs and the national character were much different, and not even really English; and indeed, it did. The Yorkshire moors were settled in the tenth and eleventh centuries by Vikings, who brought both language and culture with them. Even in the nineteenth century, the Yorkshire dialect owed a lot to Norse, and by the evidence of the novel, Yorkshire character owed a lot to the bitter passions, hatreds, and feuds of the sort frequently detailed in the Icelandic sagas.

当时的评论家们对《呼啸山庄》感到困惑——它仿佛来自另一个国度，那里风俗和民族性格截然不同，甚至算不上真正的英国小说；而事实也的确如此。约克郡的荒原在十至十一世纪由维京人定居，他们带来了语言和文化。即使到了十九世纪，约克郡方言仍然深受北欧语的影响，而从小说来看，约克郡人的性格也深受冰岛萨迦中经常描绘的那种激烈的情感、仇恨和世仇的影响。

The outline of the story is simple. Two families live near one another, one on the mountain, a rougher, harsher family, the Earn-shaws, the other in the valley, a better-educated, more sociable family, the Lintons. Mr. Earnshaw walks to Liverpool one day to do some trading and brings home Heathcliff, a wild child, whom he comes to favor over his own two offspring, Catherine and Hindley. The three children grow up in relative isolation until two of them, Heathcliff and Catherine, try spying on the children in the valley, Edgar and Isabella. Catherine is bitten by a dog and ends up staying with the Lintons. When she returns home, her horizons have widened to include the books and dresses and social attainments that the Lintons care about. Catherine, a passionate girl, then attempts to balance and reconcile the wilder and the more domesticated forms of existence, but various bits of bad luck foil her attempts, and Heathcliff runs away, only to return several years later, a wealthy man, even stronger and also more sinister than before. He intrudes upon Catherine's marriage to Edgar. After she dies, he ensnares Catherine's older brother through drink and gambling, then systematically wreaks revenge upon the Lintons until eventually he is the only member of the older generation still alive. All of the offspring are in his power—Cathy (daughter of Catherine and Linton, beautiful, affectionate, and plucky), Hareton (son of Hindley and his wife, rude and uneducated but good at heart), and Linton (son of Heathcliff and Isabella, sickly and mean). The children, now in their late teens, are living with Heathcliff at the estate on the moor when the novel opens. The story is related by two narrators: Lock-wood, a visitor from London who is the tenant of the valley estate, and Nelly, housekeeper and childhood companion of the older generation. While the story is startling and even shocking, the narrative frame is brilliant. Lockwood is a conventionally educated, pompous, and rather stupid man. His flat-footed sensibility lends authenticity to his part in the narrative, since he is clearly too dull to make this sort of thing up. Nelly Dean, while more intelligent than Lockwood, is as conventional in a moral sense. She is observant, orderly, and enduring without being passionate or imaginative. Many critics dislike her, and blame her for balking the passions of her employers, as if the plot of Wuthering Heights could possibly go some other way than it does, but the novel resides in the Norse tradition of fated action. Once Heathcliff is introduced, his alien nature and heritage must cause conflict until it is removed (through his death and that of Linton, his son). Nelly does her best to ensure the survival of the body of the family until it is cured of the infection. Nelly serves the important function of forgiving Heathcliff all his sins, even as she witnesses them. It is her commentary that renders him human, because it is to her, a lifelong and not judgmental companion, that Heathcliff can reveal the workings of his own mind. Without this dimension, he would simply be a villain or a devil, since his actions are relentlessly calculated to destroy others (also see the discussion of Nelly in chapter 9 , “The Circle of the Novel”).

故事梗概很简单。两家人住在附近，一家住在山上，性格粗犷，脾气暴躁，名叫恩肖家；另一家住在山谷里，受过良好教育，更善于交际，名叫林顿家。一天，恩肖先生步行去利物浦做生意，带回了一个名叫希斯克利夫的野孩子。他后来对希斯克利夫格外宠爱，甚至超过了自己的两个孩子凯瑟琳和辛德利。三个孩子在相对封闭的环境中长大，直到有一天，希斯克利夫和凯瑟琳试图偷窥山谷里的孩子埃德加和伊莎贝拉。凯瑟琳被狗咬伤后，只好留在林顿家。当她回到家时，她的视野已经开阔，开始关注林顿家所珍视的书籍、服饰和社交礼仪。热情奔放的凯瑟琳试图平衡并调和她狂野与温顺的生活方式，但种种厄运却屡屡挫败她的努力。希斯克利夫离家出走，几年后却以富翁的身份归来，比以往更加强大，也更加阴险。他介入了凯瑟琳与埃德加的婚姻。凯瑟琳死后，他利用酗酒和赌博引诱凯瑟琳的哥哥，然后有条不紊地对林顿家族展开报复，最终成为老一辈中唯一在世的人。所有的孩子都落入了他的掌控——凯茜（凯瑟琳和林顿的女儿，美丽、温柔、勇敢）、哈里顿（辛德利和妻子的儿子，粗鲁无知但心地善良）以及林顿（希斯克利夫和伊莎贝拉的儿子，体弱多病、心肠歹毒）。小说开篇时，孩子们都已接近二十岁，与希斯克利夫一起住在荒原上的庄园里。故事由两位叙述者讲述：一位是来自伦敦的访客洛克伍德，他是山谷庄园的佃户；另一位是管家内莉，也是老一辈的儿时玩伴。故事本身令人震惊，甚至匪夷所思，但其叙事结构却十分精妙。洛克伍德受过传统教育，傲慢自大，而且相当愚钝。他迟钝的感知力反而赋予了他在叙事中的角色以真实感，因为他显然太过迟钝，不可能编造出这种事。内莉·迪恩虽然比洛克伍德更聪明，但在道德层面上却同样循规蹈矩。她观察力敏锐，做事井井有条，坚韧不拔，却缺乏激情和想象力。许多评论家不喜欢她，指责她阻碍了雇主的激情，仿佛《呼啸山庄》的情节还能有其他发展方向似的。但这部小说根植于北欧神话的宿命论传统。希斯克利夫一出场，他与周围环境格格不入的特质和出身必然会引发冲突，直到冲突最终消散（通过他和他的儿子林顿的死亡）。内莉竭尽全力确保家人的身体能够存活，直到他们摆脱感染。内莉扮演着重要的角色，她宽恕了希斯克利夫的所有罪过，即便她亲眼目睹了这一切。正是她的评价使他变得有人性，因为只有对她——这位终生相伴且不加评判的伴侣——希斯克利夫才能袒露心扉。如果没有这一层面，他只会是一个恶棍或魔鬼，因为他的行为都是蓄意毁灭他人的（另见第九章“小说的循环”中对内莉的讨论）。

Lockwood tells the story in three parts: part one is his own story of being trapped at the Heights by a storm and seeing what may be Cathy's ghost; part two is the background related to him by Nelly while he is recovering from the illness he contracted escaping from the Heights to the Grange; and part three is what Nelly relates some six months later, when he returns to give up his lease and retrieve his possessions. His story echoes Heathcliff ‘s in part—his intrusion unbalances the isolation of Heathcliff's power over the three children, and he unwittingly sets in motion the release from bondage of young Catherine and Hareton.

洛克伍德将故事分为三部分：第一部分是他自己被困在高地庄园，遭遇暴风雨，并看到了疑似凯茜鬼魂的经历；第二部分是内莉在他从高地庄园逃到格兰奇庄园途中染病康复期间向他讲述的背景故事；第三部分是内莉大约六个月后讲述的故事，当时他返回庄园退租并取回自己的物品。他的故事在某种程度上与希斯克利夫的故事相呼应——他的介入打破了希斯克利夫对三个孩子绝对的控制，并无意中促成了年轻的凯瑟琳和哈里顿摆脱束缚的进程。

The greatness of Wuthering Heights arises from the fact that it unfolds with absolute conviction. Not only does each scene follow the previous one with superb narrative economy, the author also offers very little interpretation of the events or the characters. Wuthering Heights is possibly the only English novel that ignores the reader so thoroughly, in such a European, and even Kafkaesque, way. The characters do what they do, events take place, enough said. Such novels have an undeniability about them that renders them vivid and concrete, as if they were mere artifacts of existence than of minds. The reader may, and in fact must, make of them what she will. Intransigence is the root charm of Wuthering Heights —characters in other novels live by passion, as Cathy and Heathcliff do, but these characters are unapologetic about it—they don't seem to understand that there is any other way to live. Their intransigence is a significant factor in the reader's willingness to suspend disbelief—every character in the novel, major and minor, might in some way be off-putting (selfish or feckless or petty or unkind), but they persist in being who they are, as the wild moors persist in being wild. And when the reader is in the mood, most other novels seem all too civilized by comparison.

《呼啸山庄》的伟大之处在于它以绝对的信念展开叙述。不仅每一幕都以精炼的叙事手法与前一幕衔接得天衣无缝，作者对事件和人物的解读也寥寥无几。《呼啸山庄》或许是唯一一部如此彻底地忽略读者的英国小说，其手法颇具欧洲特色，甚至带有卡夫卡式的怪诞。人物做着他们该做的事，事件发生着，仅此而已。这类小说有一种不容置疑的特质，使其生动而具体，仿佛它们是存在的遗迹而非思想的产物。读者可以，而且实际上必须，按照自己的方式去解读它们。《呼啸山庄》的魅力根源在于它的不妥协——其他小说中的人物也像凯茜和希斯克利夫一样，因激情而活，但这些人物对此毫不掩饰——他们似乎根本不明白还有其他的生活方式。他们的固执己见是读者愿意暂时放下怀疑的重要因素——小说中的每个角色，无论主角还是配角，都可能在某些方面令人反感（自私、不负责任、斤斤计较或冷酷无情），但他们始终保持着自己的本性，就像荒野始终保持着荒野的本性一样。而当读者有此兴致时，相比之下，大多数其他小说都显得过于文明了。

29. William Makepeace Thackeray Vanity Fair

29. 威廉·梅克比斯·萨克雷，《名利场》

(1848; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 2003), 809 PP.

（1848 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，2003 年），809 页。

At the beginning of Vanity Fair , two girls leave school. One is the sweet-natured daughter of a prosperous commercial family, Amelia Sedley. The other is her friend Becky Sharp, whose background is far more suspect (her mother was French, for one thing). Becky is smart and pretty, but never for a moment sweet-natured; she knows that she will have to use her wits to survive, and she intends to do so. The period is the Napoleonic Wars. Amelia is soon engaged and then married to an officer in the British army, and in one of the great set pieces of the novel, she accompanies him to Belgium, where he is killed in the Battle of Waterloo, leaving her with a son and a sentimental attachment to his memory. In the meantime, Becky flirts with Amelia's foolish brother, home from India, and then marries the rakish younger son of a wealthy country family, Rawdon Crawley. Rawdon lives in hopes of a large inheritance from his aunt, whom Becky attends to and flatters unceasingly. One by one, the plans and dreams of each character (and there are many besides these) come to nothing, wrecked by history but also by greed, selfishness, shortsightedness, and sentimentality.

在《名利场》的开篇，两个女孩离开了学校。一个是性格温柔善良的富裕商贾家千金艾米莉亚·塞德利，另一个是她的朋友贝基·夏普，贝基的身世却可疑得多（比如，她的母亲是法国人）。贝基聪明漂亮，但绝非温柔善良；她深知自己必须运用智慧才能生存下去，并且她也决心这样做。故事发生在拿破仑战争时期。艾米莉亚很快与一位英国军官订婚并结婚。在小说的一大亮点中，她随丈夫前往比利时，丈夫在滑铁卢战役中阵亡，留下她和儿子，以及对他深深的思念。与此同时，贝基与艾米莉亚刚从印度回来的愚蠢弟弟调情，之后嫁给了富裕乡绅家庭风流成性的幼子罗顿·克劳利。罗顿一心想从他姑妈那里继承一大笔遗产，而贝基则对姑妈百般讨好、阿谀奉承。每个人物的计划和梦想（除了罗顿之外还有很多）都一个接一个地破灭，它们不仅被历史所摧毁，也被贪婪、自私、短视和感伤所摧毁。

I don't think it is possible to understand Vanity Fair without acknowledging Thackeray's extensive familiarity with French literature, because this huge novel takes up a Balzacian purpose—to depict English life over a period of twenty years, with an array of characters of all classes (at least all classes middling and above), and to depict it with the cool detachment implied equally by the title Vanity Fair as by Balzac's title La Comdie humaine. At the beginning and the end of the novel Thackeray explicitly likens his characters to puppets on a stage whose actions reveal general truths about human nature. Thackeray's purpose is essaylike (to demonstrate and argue) rather than poemlike (to evoke) or dramalike (to move). Becky is skilled in ways similar to characters in French novels—she dresses beautifully, she is smoothly hypocritical and coquettish, she has almost professional-level talents in music, she is unmotherly (she sends her child to a wet nurse, for one thing), and she is without any apparent profound emotions. She is greedy and always aware of where her self-interest lies. The plot of the novel can be understood in accordance with this French/English contrast—the typical English plot brings the love and the money together at the altar, and the typical French plot explores the ramifications of passion after the marriage has taken place. In Vanity Fair the characters marry for love and suffer the consequences—the novel explores what happens when those who have the money cannot be reconciled to the romantic aspirations of their children, and in fact never forgive the children for their acts of independence.

我认为，如果不了解萨克雷对法国文学的广泛了解，就无法理解《名利场》。因为这部鸿篇巨制有着巴尔扎克式的创作意图——描绘英国二十年间形形色色的人物（至少涵盖了中上阶层），并以一种冷静超脱的笔触来展现这一切，这种笔触既体现在《名利场》的标题中，也体现在巴尔扎克的《人间喜剧》的标题中。在小说的开头和结尾，萨克雷明确地将笔下的人物比作舞台上的木偶，他们的行为揭示了人性的普遍真理。萨克雷的创作目的更像是散文（旨在论证和阐述），而非诗歌（旨在唤起情感）或戏剧（旨在打动人心）。贝基的种种特质与法国小说中的人物颇为相似——她衣着华丽，虚伪做作，风情万种；她拥有近乎专业水准的音乐天赋；她缺乏母性（比如，她把孩子送到奶妈家）；她似乎没有任何深刻的情感。她贪婪成性，时刻清楚自己的利益所在。小说的情节可以从这种法式/英式对比来理解——典型的英式情节将爱情与金钱在婚礼上完美结合，而典型的法式情节则探讨婚后激情带来的种种后果。在《名利场》中，人物因爱而婚，并承受着相应的后果——小说探讨了当那些拥有财富的人无法接受子女的浪漫情怀，甚至永远无法原谅子女的独立行为时，将会发生什么。

Unlike most of the other great Victorian novelists, Thackeray was born a gentleman and educated at a public school and at Cambridge. His allegiances were not with energetic upstarts, such as Dickens, or Nonconformists and women, such as Eliot, or sui generis provincials, such as the Brontës. His vision was conservative; it was colored by the fact that he lost his property as a young man through speculation and high living. The darkness he saw in human nature was thus a general sinfulness and vanity. He was not a liberal, like Dickens, who felt that social and economic circumstances accounted for most if not all of mankind's propensity to transgress. For Thackeray it is in human nature itself, even in the nature of virtuous characters, to be selfish and dissatisfied. As he says, “Which of us is happy in this world? Which of us has his desire? or, having it, is satisfied?” This is much more a French view than an English one, since many great English characters are happy in the possession of their desires—Tom Jones in the possession of Sophia, Darcy and Elizabeth in the possession of one another, as are even Cathy and Hareton, even Jane and Rochester, while many French characters, such as Julien Sorel, not to mention the more extreme characters in Justine and Les Liaisons dangereuses , are never happy in possession of anything they act to achieve.

与其他大多数维多利亚时代伟大的小说家不同，萨克雷出身绅士，就读于公学，后进入剑桥大学深造。他并不认同狄更斯那样充满活力的后起之秀，也不认同艾略特那样的非国教徒和女性，更不认同勃朗特姐妹那样特立独行的乡野作家。他的思想较为保守，这源于他年轻时因投机和奢靡生活而失去财产的经历。因此，他认为人性中的阴暗面是一种普遍的罪恶感和虚荣心。他不像狄更斯那样是自由主义者，认为社会和经济环境是造成人类大部分甚至全部越轨倾向的原因。在萨克雷看来，自私和不满是人性本身的一部分，即使是品德高尚的人也难免如此。正如他所说：“我们当中谁在这世上是幸福的？我们当中谁能如愿以偿？或者，即便拥有了，又有谁能真正满足？”这更多的是一种法国式的观点，而不是英国式的观点，因为许多伟大的英国人物都乐于拥有自己的欲望——汤姆·琼斯拥有索菲娅，达西和伊丽莎白彼此拥有，甚至凯茜和哈里顿，甚至简和罗切斯特也是如此，而许多法国人物，例如朱利安·索雷尔，更不用说《朱斯蒂娜》和《危险关系》中那些更极端的人物，他们永远不会因为拥有自己努力追求的东西而感到快乐。

The liberal satiric vision promotes specific reforms to get rid of specific evils and thereby enable people to gain their desires, but the conservative satiric vision is a wholesale one, asserting that nothing works and life must only be endured. Is either one truer or more profound? The answer for most readers is a matter of temperament as much as reason.

自由主义的讽刺视角提倡具体的改革以消除具体的弊端，从而使人们能够实现愿望；而保守主义的讽刺视角则是一种整体性的批判，它断言一切都无济于事，生活只能忍受。究竟哪一种更真实、更深刻？对大多数读者而言，答案既取决于理性，也取决于性情。

Thackeray's exploration of Becky's nature and her circumstances is detailed and profound, and says much about women that continues to be convincing. For one thing, Becky is smart. She understands her situation and knows that she must act to better it or sink into some sort of degradation. She gambles, using her charm and her wits to gain access to the money belonging to others, and she occasionally wins, but at several junctures her reading of the characters of those around her is mistaken—they turn out to be more selfish and more irrational than she had expected. Aunt Crawley, for example, cannot be reconciled to Rawdon's marriage to Becky in spite of the fact that she rather likes Becky, who attends to her and flatters her. Pitt Crawley, who benefits from Aunt Crawley's peevishness, can never be brought to make reparations for what he knows are his ill-gotten gains. Becky expects each of them to put sentiment or right ahead of greed, and her errors of judgment mean that she never has a respite from her plotting and scheming. Her husband, Rawdon, has no useful skills other than gambling and card playing, and Thackeray leaves it unclear whether Becky actually markets her attractiveness the way French women characters on the make tend to do. Becky's plotting finally destroys her when she and the powerful Lord Steyne have Rawdon arrested for debt and thrown in the sponging house so they can perhaps manage a tryst. The result is that Rawdon leaves her, Steyne is humiliated and does likewise, and Becky must shift for herself. Since her reputation is famously and fatally tainted by this incident, her situation deteriorates until she manages at the very end to hook the hapless Jos Sedley and inherit his insurance.

萨克雷对贝基的性格和处境的刻画细致入微、发人深省，对女性的描写至今仍令人信服。首先，贝基很聪明。她明白自己的处境，也知道必须采取行动改善现状，否则就会堕落。她靠赌博为生，利用自己的魅力和智慧获取他人的钱财，偶尔也能赢钱，但她对周围人的判断却屡屡出错——他们比她预想的更加自私、更加不理智。例如，克劳利姨妈虽然很喜欢贝基，贝基也对她百般讨好，但她始终无法接受罗顿娶贝基。而皮特·克劳利则从克劳利姨妈的怨气中获利，他明知自己的所得不义之财，却始终不愿做出任何补偿。贝基期望每个人都能把情感或正义置于贪婪之上，而她判断失误，让她永远无法摆脱阴谋诡计。她的丈夫罗顿除了赌博和打牌之外一无是处，而萨克雷并没有明确交代贝基是否像那些一心想出人头地的法国女性那样，利用自己的魅力来谋取私利。最终，贝基的阴谋诡计毁了她自己：她和权势滔天的斯泰恩勋爵合谋，以债务为由逮捕了罗顿，并将他关进了收容所，以便他们能有机会幽会。结果，罗顿离开了她，斯泰恩勋爵颜面尽失，也离她而去，贝基不得不独自谋生。由于此事令她声名狼藉，处境每况愈下，直到最后，她才设法勾搭上了倒霉的乔斯·塞德利，继承了他的保险金。

Although her decline is not edifying, Becky, of all the characters in the novel, is the only one capable of giving unalloyed pleasure to others. She is selfish and self-interested but observant. Every other character is blinded by his or her own desires. Becky alone sees what others want and occasionally acts to give it to them. She is remorseless but sometimes compassionate. My favorite moment in the novel comes when Becky at last gets to dine at the home of Lord Steyne. While the men are present, the women are marginally polite to her, but once the ladies leave the dining room and go to the drawing room, they ignore Becky completely. Finally Lady Steyne speaks to her out of pity, and, grateful, Becky plays and sings Mozart for her. Thackeray writes of Lady Steyne, whose life is one of almost Sicilian submission to the power of her husband, “She was a girl once more, and the brief period of her happiness bloomed out again for an hour” (p. 573 ). Toward the end of the novel it is Becky who understands that Amelia's illusions about her dead husband are dangerous for her, and it is Becky who acts to disabuse her of them.

尽管贝基的衰落令人不齿，但在小说的所有人物中，她却是唯一一个能给他人带来纯粹快乐的人。她自私自利，却又观察入微。其他人物都被各自的欲望蒙蔽了双眼。只有贝基能看透他人的需求，并偶尔付诸行动。她冷酷无情，但有时也流露出怜悯之心。小说中我最喜欢的一幕是贝基终于有机会在斯泰恩勋爵的家中用餐。男人们在场时，女人们勉强对她客气些，但当她们离开餐厅前往客厅后，便完全无视了贝基。最终，斯泰恩夫人出于怜悯与她交谈，贝基感激不尽，为她演奏并演唱了莫扎特的乐曲。萨克雷这样描写斯泰恩夫人，她的生活几乎如同西西里人一般，对丈夫的权力百依百顺：“她仿佛又回到了少女时代，短暂的幸福再次绽放，持续了一个小时”（第573页）。小说临近结尾时，是贝基意识到阿米莉亚对已故丈夫的幻想对她来说很危险，也是贝基采取行动让她醒悟过来。

My guess is that Thackeray was fonder of Becky than he let on, and that the narrator's steady abuse of her was a way of distancing himself from her. If the narrator judges her for her failures of virtue before the reader has a chance to, and the author succeeds in thoroughly punishing her, then her story is not shocking and disreputable but just, and the author can delineate her virtues and vices in their fascinating combination without suffering harm to his own reputation for respectability.

我猜想，萨克雷对贝基的喜爱远比他表现出来的要深，而叙述者对她的持续贬低，其实是一种与她保持距离的方式。如果叙述者在读者有机会评判她品德败坏之前就对她进行评判，并且作者成功地对她进行了彻底的惩罚，那么她的故事就不是令人震惊和不光彩的，而是公正的，作者就可以在不损害自身体面声誉的情况下，细致地描绘她身上那些引人入胜的善恶交织。

Vanity Fair is ruthlessly satiric. Some readers consider it the greatest English novel because of its sweep and sophistication. Other readers find it heavy going—interesting but not innovative enough (like David Copperfield and Madame Bovary) to make the effort worthwhile. The good stuff, I would say, is at the end rather than the beginning. In the latter half, the style, the characters, and the plot mesh more smoothly, and the author's wisdom grows somewhat less angry and more resigned. And in the end, the love and the money do come together, thanks to Becky.

《名利场》是一部辛辣讽刺的作品。一些读者认为它是最伟大的英国小说，因为它气势恢宏、构思精巧。另一些读者则觉得它晦涩难懂——虽然有趣，但缺乏足够的创新性（例如《大卫·科波菲尔》和《包法利夫人》），不足以让人觉得费力。我认为，这部小说的精华在于结尾而非开头。在后半部分，文风、人物和情节融合得更加流畅，作者的智慧也从愤怒转向了无奈。最终，在贝基的帮助下，爱情与金钱也得以圆满。

30 Harriet Beecher Stowe Uncle Tom's Cabin

30 哈里特·比彻·斯托《汤姆叔叔的小屋》

(1851; REPR., NEW YORK: MODERN LIBRARY, 2001), 662 PP.

（1851 年；重印，纽约：现代图书馆，2001 年），662 页。

Uncle Tom's Cabin was the most famous American novel of the nineteenth century, and Stowe the most famous American author. In the twentieth century, as critical standards and social norms shifted, the novel lost stature, especially in comparison to Moby-Dick and The Scarlet Letter , two contemporary novels that were not as popular in their day. Nevertheless, Uncle Tom's Cabin is essential reading both as a novel and as a social document. It is compelling and dramatic, full of vividly wrought characters, wonderful and intelligent dialogue, and ideas that were sophisticated in their time and remain so today.

《汤姆叔叔的小屋》是十九世纪最著名的美国小说，斯托夫人也是当时最著名的美国作家。到了二十世纪，随着评论标准和社会规范的转变，这部小说的地位有所下降，尤其与《白鲸》和《红字》这两部同时期的小说相比，尽管它们在当时并不像《汤姆叔叔的小屋》那样流行。然而，《汤姆叔叔的小屋》无论作为小说还是作为社会文献，都是必读之作。它引人入胜、扣人心弦，人物形象栩栩如生，对话精彩睿智，其思想在当时颇具前瞻性，即使在今天看来也依然深刻。

Stowe's story begins simply—a Kentucky plantation owner gets into financial difficulties, and to save the farm, he decides to sell two slaves—his farm manager, Tom, and the child of his wife's favorite house slave, Eliza. The scenes that ensue were as familiar to Americans of the nineteenth century as, let's say, scenes from the movie Star Wars are to modern Americans. Eliza escapes with her son by leaping from ice floe to ice floe across the frozen Ohio River. Tom is taken on a riverboat down the Mississippi; he is sold to a benevolent but indecisive owner and goes to live in New Orleans. After the famous death of his owner's daughter, the saintly Eva, and the death of his owner in a bar fight, he is then sold to Simon Legree, whose plantation is a sort of agricultural concentration camp lost in the bayous of Louisiana. At Legree's plantation, Tom meets Legree's bitterly angry slave concubine Cassy, and advises her to escape. When she does so, using a clever ruse, Legree beats Tom to death for not betraying her plans. Cassy, Eliza, her son, and Eliza's husband, George, are reunited in Canada at the end of the novel.

斯托夫人的故事开篇很简单：一位肯塔基州的种植园主陷入了财政困境，为了保住农场，他决定卖掉两个奴隶——他的农场管家汤姆，以及他妻子最宠爱的女奴伊莱扎的孩子。接下来的场景对于十九世纪的美国人来说，就像电影《星球大战》的场景对于现代美国人来说一样熟悉。伊莱扎带着儿子，从冰封的俄亥俄河上的浮冰跳到另一块浮冰上，成功逃脱。汤姆被带上一艘沿密西西比河而下的船，卖给了一位仁慈但优柔寡断的主人，并前往新奥尔良生活。在他主人的女儿，圣洁的伊娃去世，以及他的主人在酒吧斗殴中丧命之后，汤姆又被卖给了西蒙·莱格里，莱格里的种植园就像一个隐匿在路易斯安那州沼泽地带的农业集中营。在莱格里的种植园里，汤姆遇到了莱格里怒气冲冲的奴隶妾卡西，并劝她逃跑。卡西用巧妙的计谋逃走后，莱格里却因为汤姆没有告发她的计划而将他活活打死。小说结尾，卡西、伊丽莎、她的儿子以及伊丽莎的丈夫乔治在加拿大团聚。

Stowe's plot is inherently suspenseful, full of heroic action, dangerous encounters, and threatening situations; it is made more so by the fact that she is an astute psychologist, capable of drawing a variety of interesting characters who play off against one another while also serving Stowe's larger purpose of exploring how the institution of slavery fit into and corrupted American life in the antebellum era. Stowe took up the two most controversial subjects in America, black-white relations and religion, and addressed them directly, and it is impossible, even at the beginning of the twenty-first century, to read Uncle Tom's Cabin without being impressed, moved, or offended. I attribute the continued currency of her novel to the continued unresolved dilemmas surrounding her subjects, but also to the author's own unshrinking and passionate convictions.

斯托夫人的小说情节本身就充满悬念，充满了英雄般的行动、危险的遭遇和危机四伏的局面；更妙的是，她还是一位敏锐的心理学家，能够塑造出形形色色、引人入胜的角色，他们彼此之间相互交织，同时也服务于斯托夫人更宏大的主题：探讨奴隶制在南北战争前夕如何融入并腐蚀了美国社会。斯托夫人直面美国历史上最具争议的两个主题——黑白关系和宗教，并对其进行了直接的探讨。即使在二十一世纪初，读过《汤姆叔叔的小屋》的人，也难免会感到震撼、感动，甚至愤慨。我认为，这部小说经久不衰的原因不仅在于围绕着她笔下主题的那些悬而未决的难题，更在于作者本人毫不妥协、充满激情的信念。

In style and tone, Uncle Tom's Cabin owes something to Dickens novels such as The Old Curiosity Shop and to nineteenth-century conventions of melodrama—the author intends to arouse pity, horror, and anger in the reader in order to move her to action. At the same time, some of the best parts of Uncle Tom's Cabin are discussions between such characters as Ophelia and Augustine and Cassy and Tom, or between the Shelbys, discussions that develop Stowe's argument against slavery while also developing complexity in her characters. Stowe has a sophisticated sense of humor, too. Early in the novel, two of Shelby's slaves are sent to help the slave trader catch Eliza. They foil the capture partly by knowingly playing the typical musical-hall roles of stupid “niggers” that the slave trader expects. They defeat him, laugh at him, and avoid punishment all at the same time. Toward the end of the novel, when Cassy and her charge escape Legree, they perform a similar jujitsu—Cassy plays upon Legree's superstitions, and Stowe makes knowing use of the conventions of gothic horror. The reader is tempted to laugh at the fool Legree until he avenges himself by beating Tom to death.

在风格和基调上，《汤姆叔叔的小屋》借鉴了狄更斯的小说，例如《老古玩店》，以及十九世纪通俗剧的惯例——作者意在唤起读者的怜悯、恐惧和愤怒，从而促使他们采取行动。同时，《汤姆叔叔的小屋》中最精彩的部分是奥菲莉娅和奥古斯丁、卡西和汤姆，以及谢尔比一家之间的对话。这些对话不仅阐述了斯托夫人反对奴隶制的论点，也丰富了人物的复杂性。斯托夫人还拥有精妙的幽默感。小说开篇不久，谢尔比家的两个奴隶被派去帮助奴隶贩子抓捕伊丽莎。他们故意扮演奴隶贩子预料中的“黑鬼”这种典型的滑稽角色，从而挫败了抓捕行动。他们既打败了奴隶贩子，又嘲笑了他，最终逃脱了惩罚。小说临近结尾，卡西和她照顾的汤姆逃离勒格里的魔爪时，他们施展了类似的柔术——卡西利用了勒格里的迷信，而斯托夫人则巧妙地运用了哥特式恐怖小说的惯用手法。读者起初可能会嘲笑愚蠢的勒格里，直到他最终将汤姆活活打死，为自己报了仇。

The modern reader has been warned away from Uncle Tom's Cabin by several generations of scholars who prefer the nineteenth-century male sensibility (Moby-Dick, The Scarlet Letter) and by several generations of black writers who prefer to tell their own history. Stowe's reputation has also suffered from the fact that Christian belief has become a taboo point of view in any modern novel worthy of critical consideration. But no one interested in American history, or in the history of the novel, or in the work of women writers should miss Uncle Tom's Cabin. This novel is one of the most important, and one of the most intriguing and readable, too.

现代读者曾被几代学者劝阻不要阅读《汤姆叔叔的小屋》，因为他们更偏爱十九世纪男性视角的作品（如《白鲸》和《红字》）；也曾被几代黑人作家劝阻不要阅读，因为他们更倾向于讲述自己的历史。斯托夫人的声誉也因基督教信仰在任何值得评论的现代小说中都成为禁忌观点而受到影响。但是，任何对美国历史、小说史或女性作家作品感兴趣的人都不应该错过《汤姆叔叔的小屋》。这部小说不仅是最重要的作品之一，也是最引人入胜、最易读的作品之一。

31. Herman Melville. Moby-Dick; or, The Whale

31. 赫尔曼·梅尔维尔。《白鲸》

(1851; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1992), 625 PP.

（1851 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1992 年），625 页。

The Hungarian critic Gyrgy Lukcs maintained that the difference between the novel and the drama is that while the drama works by precipitating and then accelerating the action, the novel works by retarding the action. The requirement that the author put off the climax is both his boon and his bane. On the one hand, while he is digressing, the author can expand his focus, deepen his psychological and sociological analysis, and engage in speculation. On the other hand, he must do all of this subtly, without either losing track of the plot (and therefore the suspense that carries the reader forward) or by telegraphing too quickly what is going to happen, which shuts down the plot entirely. Moby-Dick demonstrates the pleasures and profundities of digression and is an excellent example of how a novelist can excel at what he perhaps should not have tried in the first place.

匈牙利评论家吉尔吉·卢克奇认为，小说与戏剧的区别在于，戏剧通过先抛出情节再加速推进，而小说则通过延缓情节发展来达到效果。作者必须推迟高潮，这既是他的优势也是他的劣势。一方面，在离题写作的过程中，作者可以拓展视野，深化心理和社会分析，并进行推测。另一方面，他必须巧妙地完成这一切，既不能偏离情节（从而失去推动读者前进的悬念），也不能过早地揭示即将发生的事情，导致情节完全停滞。《白鲸》展现了离题写作的乐趣和深刻之处，堪称小说家如何从原本不该尝试的事情中脱颖而出的绝佳范例。

In spite of the fact that the first line of the novel is “Call me Ish-mael,” Ishmael's own personality and fate are very little explored in Moby-Dick; the novel is not about character transformation. Ishmael takes up with Queequeg and goes to sea with him, but their relationship is not developed, nor are any other relationships on the Pequod. It is Ahab, in his obsession (he intends to find and kill the white whale), who becomes the main focus of the narrative, but his character is no more transformed than Ishmael's, though some of the ship captain's doubts and complexities are revealed from time to time. The Pequod looks for the white whale for hundreds of pages; the encounter itself takes thirty pages, or less than 5 percent of the novel. There is never any doubt about whether the whale will be found or pursued. At no juncture in the novel is there even the illusion of choice by Ahab, nor are there intervening circumstances. And so the novel is not about whether or even why the climactic event is to take place. The reader is simply asked to wait until it takes place and to contemplate it.

尽管小说开篇第一句是“叫我以实玛利”，但《白鲸》对以实玛利的性格和命运着墨甚少；这部小说并非着重描写人物转变。以实玛利与奎奎格结伴出海，但他们的关系并未得到充分发展，裴廓德号上的其他人物关系也同样如此。叙事的焦点在于亚哈船长，他执迷于寻找并猎杀白鲸，但他的性格转变并不比以实玛利更大，尽管偶尔也会展现出这位船长的一些疑虑和复杂情感。裴廓德号花了数百页篇幅寻找白鲸；而最终的遭遇却只占了三十页，不到全书的5%。白鲸是否最终被找到或追捕，始终毫无悬念。小说中从未出现过亚哈船长做出选择的假象，也没有任何变数。因此，这部小说并非探讨高潮事件是否会发生，甚至也不是探讨其为何会发生。读者只需静待其发生，并对此进行思考。

Moby-Dick relies on two things to maintain the reader's interest: the inherent strangeness of whaling, and the author's quest (expressed in his varieties of style) to exhaust the spiritual meanings of obsession (or “monomania,” as it was called then). Melville excels at picturing what the reader may not have ever previously imagined—“the peeled white body of the beheaded whale flashes like a marble sepulchre; though changed in hue, it has not perceptibly lost anything in bulk” (p. 336 ), or the sensation of losing oneself in staring over the calm sea, or the appearance of the ship on a dark night, with all the furnaces stoked, rendering the blubber into oil. Some readers skip some of Melville's more essayistic, informative passages about types of whales and so forth, but the true lover of this novel—its ideal reader—savors even those passages that are outdated, as more examples of the variety of thoughts Melville brings to his theme; maybe a good analogy for this novel in another artistic medium is Bach's “Goldberg Variations.” Much of the pleasure for the reader has to be witnessing the endless but systematic variety of the author's technique. Moby-Dick must be long because it takes a while for the author to impart to the reader enough information to enable the reader to make sense of everything the author wishes to communicate, just as it takes Bach a while to accustom the listener's ear and the listener's mind to his musical ideas. Part of every artist's job is to train his audience, though the artist may fail in his training and the audience may decline to be trained. But the reader willing to be trained to read and appreciate Moby-Dick gains a rare and steady pleasure—a prolonged experience of rightness and felicity of style and a vision of something entirely unknown suddenly made known. Othello is said by Shakespeare to woo Desdemona by telling her strange tales. So Melville, and all novelists who deal in the exotic, woo their readers. Those who love Moby-Dick , those who think it the best novel ever written in English, are those who relish the double strangeness of Melville's vision—the exotic locale and the visionary ideas—above every other joy that novels can afford.

《白鲸》依靠两点来维持读者的兴趣：一是捕鲸本身固有的怪诞性，二是作者（通过其多样的文风表达出来）对痴迷（当时被称为“单恋”）精神意义的探索。梅尔维尔擅长描绘读者可能从未想象过的景象——“被斩首的鲸鱼剥皮后的白色躯体像一座大理石墓穴般闪烁；虽然颜色变了，但体积却丝毫未减”（第336页），或是凝视平静海面时迷失自我的感觉，或是漆黑的夜晚，船上的炉火熊熊，将鲸脂炼成油的景象。有些读者会跳过梅尔维尔一些关于鲸鱼种类等更具散文风格、信息丰富的段落，但这部小说的真正爱好者——它的理想读者——会细细品味那些略显过时的段落，因为它们更能体现梅尔维尔对这一主题的丰富思考。或许用巴赫的《哥德堡变奏曲》来类比这部小说，在其他艺术媒介中会很贴切。读者的乐趣很大程度上来自于欣赏作者无穷无尽却又系统有序的写作技巧。《白鲸》篇幅很长，是因为作者需要时间才能向读者传递足够的信息，使读者能够理解作者想要表达的一切，正如巴赫需要时间让听众的耳朵和心灵适应他的音乐理念一样。每位艺术家的职责之一就是引导他们的读者，尽管艺术家可能在引导上失败，而读者也可能拒绝接受引导。但是，愿意接受引导去阅读和欣赏《白鲸》的读者，会获得一种罕见而持久的愉悦——一种对风格恰当与精妙的持久体验，以及对某种完全未知的事物突然显现的洞察。莎士比亚笔下的奥赛罗通过讲述奇闻异事来赢得苔丝狄蒙娜的芳心。同样，梅尔维尔以及所有描写异域风情的作家，都在用同样的方式来吸引他们的读者。那些喜爱《白鲸》的人，那些认为它是英语世界有史以来最伟大的小说的人，他们所享受的，是梅尔维尔的异域风情和富有远见的思想所带来的双重奇异感，胜过小说所能带来的任何其他乐趣。

Note added later:

后加注释：

I read Moby-Dick in the winter of 2003 , and wrote this entry within a couple of days. When I came back to rethink and rewrite the entry in the winter of 2005 , I found that I could hardly remember the novel, and certainly could not remember enough of it to expand my entry to include themes that other readers find compelling in Melville's vision. In some ways I consider this failure on my part odd. I have strong memories of most of the other works, including those I read before Moby-Dick , such as The Princess of Cléves and Scott's The Tale of Old Mortality , not to mention The Red and the Black , where, after two and a half years, I can remember how certain words looked on certain pages and where those pages were in the text. The interesting thing to me is that while Moby-Dick is possibly the greatest American novel and is beloved by many readers and scholars, it clearly didn't make much of an impression on me even though I was reading it attentively and not idly. The question, I think, is, can a reader read a book intentionally— that is, can she decide to be impressed by it, decide to take it in, decide to have a relationship with it? Some of the books on this list were difficult for me to relate to—I had internal arguments with the author all the way through; Ian McEwan's Atonement is a good example. These arguments helped fix those books in my mind even when I was not conscious of enjoying them. Other novels, of course, I liked very much and I remember them fondly every day or two in the ongoing flow of mental images that constitutes my inner life. But even though I had no argument with Moby-Dick and felt as though I was enjoying it and appreciating it without truly loving it, very little lingers, and I rarely think about it. Is this only because the concerns of the novel are extremely masculine and I don't really care about them? Is it because the style seemed heavy and ornate to me and didn't really communicate much about the psychology of the characters even though I wanted it to? Is it because the characters don't relate to one another in a way that I intuitively comprehend? More important, do I need to read it again and try to get more out of it? That strikes me as possible but not likely, rather like going out on another date with someone who was okay but not compelling the first time. On the other hand, even though the world is full of tempting new novels one can always go on to (I would like to go on to Michael Chabon's The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay and Marguerite Yourcenar's Memoirs of Hadrian , for example), the novel that one didn't connect with is always there on the shelf, waiting to be reexperienced by the different person you are going to be when you notice it again and are moved to pick it up.

我在2003年冬天读了《白鲸》，并在几天内写下了这篇书评。到了2005年冬天，当我重新思考并修改这篇书评时，我发现自己几乎记不起这部小说的内容，更别提记住足够多的细节来扩展我的书评，包括其他读者认为梅尔维尔的这部作品引人入胜的主题。在某种程度上，我认为自己的这种失败很奇怪。我对其他大部分作品都记忆犹新，包括我在读《白鲸》之前读过的作品，比如《克莱夫公主》和斯科特的《老莫塔利蒂的故事》，更不用说《红与黑》了——两年半之后，我仍然记得某些文字在特定页面上的样子，以及这些页面在文本中的位置。令我感到有趣的是，尽管《白鲸》可能是最伟大的美国小说，并且深受许多读者和学者的喜爱，但它显然没有给我留下深刻的印象，即使我是认真阅读的，而不是漫不经心地读。我认为问题在于，读者能否有意识地阅读一本书——也就是说，她能否决定是否被一本书打动，是否决定是否接受它，是否决定是否与它建立某种联系？这份书单上的一些书让我难以产生共鸣——我全程都在与作者进行内心的辩论；伊恩·麦克尤恩的《赎罪》就是一个很好的例子。这些辩论帮助我牢牢记住了这些书，即使我并没有意识到自己喜欢它们。当然，我也很喜欢其他一些小说，我几乎每天都会在脑海中浮现出它们，它们构成了我内心世界的一部分。但是，尽管我与《白鲸》之间没有产生任何冲突，也感觉自己在欣赏它，而不是真正地爱上它，但它却很少在我心中留下深刻的印象，我也很少想起它。这仅仅是因为这部小说的主题极其男性化，而我并不真正关心这些吗？还是因为它的文风在我看来沉重而华丽，并没有真正传达出人物的心理，尽管我很想了解？是因为书中的人物关系我无法凭直觉理解吗？更重要的是，我需要重读一遍，尝试从中获得更多感悟吗？我觉得这有可能，但可能性不大，就像和第一次约会时感觉还不错但并不吸引人的人再去约会一样。另一方面，尽管世上充满了诱人的新小说，我们总能找到新的阅读对象（比如我很想读迈克尔·夏邦的《卡瓦利埃与克雷的神奇冒险》和玛格丽特·尤瑟纳尔的《哈德良回忆录》），但那本我们没能产生共鸣的小说始终静静地躺在书架上，等待着我们以不同的视角重新审视它，直到我们再次看到它，并被它打动，拿起它。

32. Nathaniel Hawthorne. The House of the Seven Gables

32. 纳撒尼尔·霍桑，《七个尖角阁的房子》

(1851; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, MODERN LIBRARY, 2001), 227 PP.

（1851 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，现代文库，2001 年），227 页。

The House of the Seven Gables begins with what amounts to a prologue tracing the history of the house and the Pyncheon family, who own it. The first Colonel Pyncheon, in the time of the Salem witch trials, had coveted a property owned by another man, named Maule. He engineered an accusation of witchcraft against Maule, then confiscated Maule's land and built a house on it. Subsequently Colonel Pyncheon died, fulfilling the curse Maule had laid upon him prior to being executed. At the time of the narrative, the Pyncheon family is represented by two branches—the branch that lives frugally in the house, consisting of the middle-aged spinster Hepzibah and her brother Clifford, recently released from jail, and the branch that still has wealth and influence around the town, consisting of Judge Pyncheon. The way the novel is structured foreshadows that the two-hundred-year-old curse upon the family and the property will be realized and that justice will finally be done. The agent of this retribution/redemption is a distant cousin, Phoebe (“light”), who comes from the country to help Hepzibah in the tiny shop she establishes to support herself and Clifford. Eventually a boarder moves in, Holgrave, who seems to be the perfect new American man—enterprising, energetic, and interested in new technology (he is a daguerreotypist)—and he turns out to be a descendant of the Maule family. He and Phoebe come together at the end.

《七个尖角屋》以一段序言开篇，追溯了这座房子及其主人平钦家族的历史。第一代平钦上校在塞勒姆审巫案时期觊觎另一位名叫莫尔的男子的房产。他捏造了莫尔的巫术指控，没收了莫尔的土地并在上面建造了一座房子。后来，平钦上校去世，应验了莫尔在他被处决前对他下的诅咒。在故事发生的时期，平钦家族分为两个分支——一个是过着节俭生活的分支，由中年老处女赫普齐巴和她刚出狱的弟弟克利福德组成；另一个分支则在镇上仍然拥有财富和影响力，由平钦法官领导。小说的结构预示着，笼罩在这个家族和房产上的两百年诅咒终将应验，正义也终将得到伸张。促成这场复仇/救赎的使者是一位远房表妹菲比（意为“光”），她从乡下来到赫普齐巴家，帮她打理那家小店，赫普齐巴靠这家店养活自己和克利福德。后来，一位名叫霍尔格雷夫的房客搬了进来，他似乎是完美的美国新贵——进取、精力充沛，对新技术充满热情（他是一位银版摄影师）——而他竟然是莫尔家族的后裔。故事的结尾，他和菲比走到了一起。

The House of the Seven Gables is not especially appealing. It bears comparison with The Bride of Lammermoor because it makes use of similar materials—old curses, fated outcomes, and family histories. But whereas Scott is careful to make the psychology of the characters and their interactions mesh with the omens and predictions, so that by acting within character the characters seem to work out their destinies as predicted, Hawthorne is less of a psychologist and more of a moralist. His few characters are not so much agents of the plot as objects of the narrator's observations and victims of circumstances. It is, in particular, the manner in which Hawthorne toys with ideas of spirits and ghosts that robs the novel of both supernatural operations and realistic motivation. Rather, each character seems to be a manifestation of a certain type of atmosphere. What prevails instead of logic and action is aesthetic. Phoebe and Holgrave are attractive—she represents forgiveness and innocence, he represents reason. Judge Pyncheon is unattractive—he represents hypocrisy and is motivated principally by greed. Each character rather mechanically acts out what he or she represents, and eventually, through the agency of the ancient curse (and the author), Judge Pyncheon dies suddenly and then is held up by the narrator as an example of the suddenness of death in the midst of life (and egomania). At the same time, the family curse is revealed as not a curse but a natural process—Holgrave theorizes that the judge has died of natural causes (perhaps a heart attack or a stroke, the reader thinks) and that predisposition to such a death is inherited and also accounts for the earlier sudden death of Colonel Pyncheon. At the climax, the author does not take the opportunity to intensify his drama but rather to ratchet up his eloquence— The House of the Seven Gables turns out to be a sermon. The contrast with The Bride of Lammermoor is apparent in terms of style, too. Whereas Scott uses a clear, more or less objective style that naturally weighs the curses and superstitions against the more mundane forces shaping the lives of his characters, Hawthorne uses a highly charged and floridly ironic style that continuously reminds the reader what to think of the characters and the events.

《七个尖角屋》并不特别吸引人。它与《拉默穆尔的新娘》有相似之处，因为它们都运用了类似的素材——古老的诅咒、命中注定的结局和家族史。但斯科特巧妙地将人物的心理及其互动与预兆和预言融合在一起，使人物的行为符合其性格，仿佛最终实现了预言中的命运；而霍桑则更像是一位道德家，而非心理学家。他笔下的人物与其说是情节的推动者，不如说是叙述者观察的对象和环境的受害者。尤其值得一提的是，霍桑对鬼魂和幽灵概念的玩弄，使得这部小说既缺乏超自然的力量，也缺乏现实的动机。相反，每个人物似乎都只是某种氛围的化身。主导一切的不是逻辑和行动，而是审美。菲比和霍尔格雷夫很有魅力——她代表着宽恕和纯真，他代表着理性。平钦法官令人厌恶——他代表着虚伪，其行为主要受贪婪驱使。每个角色都机械地扮演着各自的角色，最终，在古老诅咒（以及作者的安排）的影响下，平钦法官猝然离世，叙述者以此为例，说明生命（以及自大）的猝死有多么突然。与此同时，家族诅咒被揭示为一种自然过程而非诅咒——霍尔格雷夫推测法官死于自然原因（读者可能会想到心脏病或中风），这种死亡倾向是遗传的，也解释了平钦上校早前的猝死。在故事的高潮，作者并没有借此机会增强戏剧张力，而是提升了其雄辩的表达——《七个尖角屋》最终变成了一篇布道。与《拉默穆尔的新娘》在风格上也形成了鲜明的对比。斯科特采用清晰、相对客观的风格，自然地将诅咒和迷信与塑造人物生活的更世俗的力量进行权衡；而霍桑则采用充满强烈情感和华丽讽刺的风格，不断提醒读者应该如何看待人物和事件。

All of Hawthorne's characters have psychological possibilities, but the plot hardly develops them. Hepzibah, a loving but unattractive old maid, gains neither grace nor self-knowledge. The narrator repeats over and over that her brother Clifford's losses can never be redeemed and are without a larger purpose. Holgrave and Phoebe's love is barely developed, and the judge is simply an emblem. Since the characters cannot, by the author's definition, change, the pages of the novel have to be used for something other than character development, so they are used for description (my favorite is of the chickens in the yard) that is often quite lyrical and that gives the novel its romantic air. But the reader has to wonder—well, this reader has to wonder—what Hawthorne was getting at to begin with. Is there some political purpose here? If so, is the original sin that has cursed the Pyncheon family really so simple as the fact that the first Pyncheon stole a small lot from a neighbor? Or is there a larger uneasiness?

霍桑笔下的所有人物都具有心理发展的可能性，但情节却几乎没有展开。赫普齐巴，一个善良却相貌平平的老处女，既没有获得优雅，也没有获得自我认知。叙述者反复强调，她哥哥克利福德的损失永远无法弥补，也没有任何更深远的意义。霍尔格雷夫和菲比的爱情几乎没有得到发展，而法官则仅仅是一个象征。既然按照作者的定义，人物无法改变，那么小说的篇幅就只能用于人物塑造之外的其他用途，于是便用来描写（我最喜欢的是对院子里鸡的描写），这些描写往往颇具诗意，赋予了小说浪漫的气息。但读者不禁要问——至少我本人不禁要问——霍桑最初究竟想要表达什么？这其中是否蕴含着某种政治目的？如果是的话，那么诅咒平钦家族的原罪真的仅仅是老平钦从邻居那里偷了一小块地吗？或者，是否存在更大的不安？

The House of the Seven Gables was written in 1850 , when Americans were broadly conscious of both the moral compromises of slavery and of the eradication of Native Americans but had not decided how to act upon their misgivings. It is possible, I think, to read the static and heavily moralistic qualities of Hawthorne's novel as a resistance to considering larger questions of injustice and guilt in favor of contemplating minor ones. The novel is attempting to interpret history as entirely personal, through the lens of a family curse, but the characters cannot as yet imagine how to solve even their minor dilemmas—they are stuck in a state of unhappiness and moral unease until something happens that is outside their control, and miraculously, that thing brings prosperity. Hawthorne pays very little attention to the social context of the family—the history of the town, for example, or what the town is like at the time of the novel; as a result, the family can be redeemed solely through the original terms of the curse, which makes the plot (for example, that Holgrave turns out to be a Maule) too predictable. This sort of talelike wishful thinking works in some novels, but Hawthorne doesn't deliver on the promise of the tale—that the story will be entertaining. The novel turns out to be sober but not realistic, mysterious but not entertaining, and so doesn't succeed as either a romance or a realistic novel. The Bride of Lammermoor , by contrast, does face up to history and acknowledge its moral complexities; characters act and react to the consequences of their actions, but Scott also makes canny use of folkloric elements, so the novel gives the pleasures of both realism and romance. Scott has a political philosophy that encompasses injustice, hatred, revenge, and the passage of time that leads to reconciliation. Hawthorne (in my opinion as a reaction to the charged issues of his time) is unsure of the meaning of the history he wants to depict. The result is strange and flat—if the reader cannot respond to his style, there is little else to respond to.

《七个尖角屋》写于1850年，当时美国人普遍意识到奴隶制的道德妥协以及对美洲原住民的灭绝，但尚未决定如何应对这些疑虑。我认为，霍桑这部小说中那种静态且浓重的道德说教意味，或许可以解读为一种对更宏大的不公正和罪恶问题的回避，而更倾向于关注一些细枝末节的问题。小说试图通过家族诅咒的视角，将历史完全解读为个人层面的，但小说中的人物甚至连解决这些小困境都无能为力——他们深陷于不幸和道德不安之中，直到发生了一件他们无法掌控的事情，而奇迹般地，这件事带来了繁荣。霍桑对这个家庭的社会背景——例如小镇的历史，或者小说时代小镇的状况——几乎不予关注。因此，只有按照诅咒的原意才能救赎这个家族，这使得情节（例如，霍尔格雷夫最终被证实是莫尔家族的人）过于可预测。这种故事式的幻想在某些小说中或许行得通，但霍桑并没有兑现故事的承诺——让故事引人入胜。这部小说最终显得冷静却不现实，神秘却不有趣，因此无论作为爱情小说还是现实主义小说，都未能取得成功。相比之下，《拉默穆尔的新娘》正视历史，承认其道德的复杂性；人物的行动及其后果都由他们自己承担，而斯科特也巧妙地运用了民间传说元素，因此这部小说兼具现实主义和爱情小说的魅力。斯科特的政治哲学涵盖了不公正、仇恨、复仇以及最终带来和解的时间流逝。霍桑（在我看来，这是他对当时社会敏感问题的回应）对自己想要描绘的历史的意义感到迷茫。结果很奇怪也很平淡——如果读者无法对他的风格产生共鸣，那么就没有什么其他东西值得共鸣了。

33. Gustave Flaubert. Madame Bovary

33. 古斯塔夫·福楼拜。《包法利夫人》

ED. PAUL DE MAN (1857; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1965), 255 PP.

保罗·德曼 (1857 年) 编辑；纽约：W. W. 诺顿，1965 年重印，255 页。

Everything about Madame Bovary has been passionately discussed since publication: is it good, is it great, is it a novel, is it a “realist” novel, is it true, is it worthy, who is Emma, how did the author feel about her, about the rest of the characters and the setting, about himself, about literature, about the form of the novel? It is Flaubert's single greatest achievement that he systematically excluded the answers to these questions from the text itself by focusing intently on his subjects, only once, at the very beginning, allowing the narrator to speak in his own voice, to introduce Charles Bovary in school. Thereafter, Flaubert insistently presents his story as an objective reality, giving clues to its meaning only through tone. When Charles dies, the story ends. No overt lessons are drawn from it. If Flaubert's letters are to be believed, this was an exceptionally difficult technique—it takes the novelist's inherent and necessary subjectivity and pretends it doesn't exist. The result is to introduce the author's subjectivity into the reader's mind, unapologeti-cally and successfully taking over her mind.

自《包法利夫人》出版以来，关于它的一切都引发了热烈的讨论：它好吗？它伟大吗？它是小说吗？它是“现实主义”小说吗？它是真实的吗？它值得一读吗？爱玛是谁？作者对她、对其他人物和故事背景、对作者本人、对文学、对小说形式有何感受？福楼拜最伟大的成就莫过于他系统性地将这些问题的答案排除在文本之外，而是专注于他笔下的人物，仅在开篇让叙述者以第一人称视角讲述查尔斯·包法利在学校的故事。此后，福楼拜坚持将故事呈现为客观现实，仅通过语气暗示其意义。查尔斯死后，故事结束。它没有给出任何明确的教训。如果福楼拜的信件属实，那么这是一种极其高超的技巧——它抹去了小说家固有的、必要的主观性，并假装它不存在。其结果是将作者的主观性引入读者的思想中，毫不掩饰地成功地控制了读者的思想。

Flaubert famously remarked, “Emma Bovary, c'est moi” (several versions of the remark survive). The context of the remark is sometimes reported as Flaubert's exasperated answer to repeated questions about whether the portrait of Emma was based upon a real person. We can interpret Flaubert's identification with Emma in different ways— as a simple rejection of questions that he felt impugned his imagination, as a recognition that every character depicted in the work of every author is a product of that author's inner life, or as a closer, conscious identification between Flaubert and Emma, pointing up his “feminine qualities,” or his “romantic nature,” or whatever. My own inclination is to see his remark as the answer to what I would call “the French paradox.” What is striking about Madame Bovary? It is not the plot. A hasty marriage to a boring husband, followed by several love affairs and ending in the destruction of everyone is the staple plot of French fiction. That the protagonist alone, or the lovers together, are surrounded by stupid, boring, unimaginative associates is the further ingredient of most such plots (in The Princess of Cléves , even the highest, most elegant court is by definition cruder than the princess and the duc de Nemours). These auxiliary characters are routinely portrayed as greedy, selfish, libertine, and nasty—Cousin Bette is the paradigm, and not a very extreme one at that. The French paradox is, how can a world as beautiful and delightful as France produce a literature universally peopled by vipers and fools?

福楼拜曾说过一句名言：“艾玛·包法利，就是我”（这句话有好几个版本流传至今）。有时人们认为，这句话是福楼拜对反复被问及艾玛的形象是否以真人为原型时，恼怒地作出的回应。我们可以从不同的角度解读福楼拜对艾玛的认同——一种解读是他对那些他认为质疑自己想象力的问题的简单拒绝；一种解读是他意识到每位作家笔下的每个人物都是其内心世界的产物；又或者，这是一种更紧密、更自觉的福楼拜与艾玛之间的认同，凸显了他自身的“女性特质”或“浪漫天性”等等。我个人倾向于将这句话视为对所谓“法国悖论”的解答。《包法利夫人》最引人注目之处究竟在哪里？并非情节。仓促嫁给一个乏味的丈夫，随后经历数段婚外情，最终走向毁灭，这几乎是法国小说的经典套路。大多数此类故事的共同点在于，主人公或恋人身边往往围绕着愚蠢、乏味、缺乏想象力的同伴（在《克莱沃公主》中，即使是最高贵、最优雅的宫廷，也比公主和内穆尔公爵粗俗得多）。这些配角通常被描绘成贪婪、自私、放荡不羁、令人厌恶——贝蒂表妹就是个典型，而且还算不上极端。法国的悖论在于：像法国这样美丽迷人的世界，怎么会孕育出一个充斥着毒蛇和傻瓜的文学世界呢？

It is Madame Bovary that resolves the paradox in a new and profound way—and like all paradoxes, it is easier to apprehend than to analyze. Emma's singular characteristic, which the style of the novel asks us to identify also as Flaubert's singular characteristic, is that she is repeatedly and perennially seduced by appearances. She is not merely sensuous. Rather, in how things look and feel, how patterns are created into images and scenes, Emma finds meaning that she then feels compelled to act upon. New drapes are as important to her as a new lover; having champagne at a hotel in Rouen tells her who she is, and who she is is entirely different from who she had thought she was not long before. She has a strong sense of taste—a striking image of this occurs early in the novel, when she is looking at a keepsake (a book of sentimental poems and pictures), and she is moved by the way the paper film that covers the pictures folds over itself. But such images abound—all of Emma's existence is permeated by such moments. It is as if she can never detach herself long enough to get her thoughts together (and, indeed, she has no method of objectification, being poorly educated, having no friends, and lacking any feeling of kinship with her husband). If Emma is Flaubert, then she is Flaubert without his resources of companionship, money, and purpose, but her stylistic aspirations are the same as his—to have things right and suitable. She thus is strangely similar to Balzac's and Laclos's, and even de Sade's selfish characters, but she is more sympathetic, because we see the world as she sees it, everything heightened by her passionate intensity.

《包法利夫人》以一种新颖而深刻的方式解决了这个悖论——而且如同所有悖论一样，理解它比分析它更容易。爱玛的独特之处，也是小说风格要求我们辨识的福楼拜的独特之处，在于她反复且永恒地被表象所诱惑。她并非仅仅是感官上的。相反，在事物的视觉和触觉上，在各种模式如何构成图像和场景中，爱玛找到了意义，并感到自己必须付诸行动。对她而言，新窗帘与新情人同样重要；在鲁昂的酒店里喝香槟让她认清了自己，而这个她与不久前自以为的自己截然不同。她拥有敏锐的品味——小说开篇不久便有一个令人印象深刻的描写：当她看着一本珍藏的画册（一本充满感伤的诗歌和图画集）时，她被覆盖在画册上的纸膜折叠的方式所打动。但这样的意象比比皆是——艾玛的整个人生都充斥着这样的瞬间。仿佛她永远无法抽离出来，整理思绪（事实上，她也根本没有客观思考的能力，因为她受教育程度低，没有朋友，与丈夫之间也缺乏任何亲情）。如果说艾玛是福楼拜，那么她就是没有福楼拜的陪伴、金钱和目标的福楼拜，但她的风格追求却与他如出一辙——追求完美和合宜。因此，她与巴尔扎克、拉克洛，甚至萨德笔下那些自私的角色有着奇特的相似之处，但她更令人同情，因为我们得以透过她的视角看待世界，而她那炽热的情感更将一切放大。

The fact that Flaubert reserves his judgment of Emma guarantees that she will be a revolutionary figure in French literature. She can be contemptible, and what she does to Charles can be reprehensible and frightening, but Flaubert never gives the reader permission to feel contempt for her (contrast this to Balzac's repeated condemnations of his characters—first he judges, only then does he offer mitigations of his judgments). Perhaps this very thing was the temptation of Gustave Flaubert that he found so arduous—the temptation to let himself judge rather than to suspend judgment. But as with Pamela , a personal, apparently artistic choice had a political effect once the novel was published. Flaubert's acceptance of Emma's kinship with him guaranteed that others would be able to feel a kinship with her in spite of her lack of virtue, kindness, intelligence, compassion, or true faith. As her inner life becomes the reader's, the reader can empathize with her, and perhaps even sympathize with her, without needing a traditional excuse (in The Red and the Black , for example, Madame de Rnal is not unlike Emma, but Stendhal gives us permission to sympathize with her by making her a well-meaning woman and a good mother).

福楼拜对爱玛保留评判的态度，注定了她将成为法国文学中一个革命性的人物。她或许令人鄙夷，她对查尔斯所做的一切也令人发指、触目惊心，但福楼拜从未允许读者对她产生鄙夷之情（这与巴尔扎克反复谴责笔下人物形成鲜明对比——巴尔扎克先是评判，之后才试图为自己的评判开脱）。或许，这正是古斯塔夫·福楼拜难以抗拒的诱惑——他难以抑制地想要评判他人，而不是选择保持中立。但正如帕梅拉的故事一样，这种看似出于个人艺术考量的选择，在小说出版后却产生了政治影响。福楼拜承认爱玛与他之间存在某种联系，这使得其他人即便爱玛缺乏美德、善良、智慧、同情心或真正的信仰，也能与她产生共鸣。当她的内心世界成为读者的内心世界时，读者可以与她产生共鸣，甚至可能同情她，而无需传统的借口（例如，在《红与黑》中，德·罗纳尔夫人与爱玛并无二致，但司汤达通过把她塑造成一个善良的女人和一位好母亲，让我们得以同情她）。

The other important thing about Madame Bovary is that there is something wrong with Emma. She does not fit into the world she was born into. Flaubert himself offers no theory of what the problem is— either with regard to origins or to any possible solution. One critic suggests it is simple bad luck, another that her education is wanting. There are plenty of characters in the history of prose fiction who have something wrong with them, but Flaubert's relentless depiction of Emma's life and death makes her seem comprehensible, like a case history. Because he depicts her in such detail, she ceases to be merely a person among others; in spite of her mediocrity, her life has been found dramatic, she has been found worthy of analysis. Her “case” predates Freud and the other literary theorists of psychology, but it sets them up—it prefigures that facet of the modern world, the minute analysis of the average man or woman.

《包法利夫人》的另一个重要之处在于，爱玛本身就存在某种缺陷。她无法融入她所出生的世界。福楼拜本人并未就此问题给出任何理论解释——无论是其根源还是任何可能的解决之道。一位评论家认为这仅仅是运气不好，另一位则认为她缺乏教育。散文小说史上不乏存在缺陷的人物，但福楼拜对爱玛生与死的细致描绘，使她显得合情合理，如同一个案例。正因为他如此细致地刻画她，她才不再仅仅是芸芸众生中的一个；尽管她平庸无奇，但她的人生却被赋予了戏剧性，她也因此被赋予了分析的价值。她的“案例”早于弗洛伊德和其他文学心理学家，却为他们奠定了基础——它预示了现代世界的这一层面：对普通男女进行细致入微的分析。

34. Charles Dickens. A Tale of Two Cities

34. 查尔斯·狄更斯，《双城记》

(1859; REPR., NEW YORK: BANTAM, 1989), 352 PP.

（1859 年；重印，纽约：BANTAM，1989 年），352 页。

In the 1840s and ‘ 50s , Dickens wrote a series of deeply serious political novels that explored the inequities and the suffering that grew out of the rise of urban capitalism in England. The last of these, Little Dorrit , contains some of Dickens's most insightful writing and harshest criticism of the world he lived in, but the plot became so tangled over the course of eighteen lengthy installments that Dickens had to include a note at the end explaining what happened. He then turned to what surely must have seemed like an even vaster and more confusing theme—the French Revolution. But the novel he came up with has an elegant and simple plot, while at the same time it is perhaps the most astute portrayal of the psychology and sociology of violent social change ever written.

在19世纪40年代和50年代，狄更斯创作了一系列深刻的政治小说，探讨了英国城市资本主义兴起所带来的不公和苦难。其中最后一部《小多丽》包含了狄更斯最具洞察力的文字，以及对他所处世界的最为尖锐的批判。然而，由于这部小说长达十八卷，情节错综复杂，狄更斯不得不在结尾处附上注释来解释故事背景。之后，他转向了一个对他而言无疑更加宏大、更加复杂的主题——法国大革命。但他最终创作出的这部小说情节简洁精炼，同时又可能是对剧烈社会变革的心理和社会学刻画最为精辟的著作。

Dickens's guide and mentor for A Tale of Two Cities was the historian Thomas Carlyle, whose work on the French Revolution Dickens had read more than once and much admired. His plan was to dramatize Carlyle's ideas, not to improve upon them. Nevertheless, Dickens's novel remains current while his friend's history does not. The reason is surely that Dickens is able to vividly embody the ambiguities of the Revolutionary period as well as to cogently characterize the social forces at work. Carlyle may have supplied the analysis, but Dickens understood the human truths at the source.

狄更斯创作《双城记》的指导者和导师是历史学家托马斯·卡莱尔，他曾多次阅读卡莱尔关于法国大革命的著作，并对其推崇备至。狄更斯的计划是将卡莱尔的观点戏剧化，而非对其进行改进。然而，狄更斯的小说至今仍具有现实意义，而他朋友的历史著作却已过时。原因无疑在于，狄更斯能够生动地展现革命时期的种种复杂矛盾，并清晰地刻画当时的社会力量。卡莱尔或许提供了分析，但狄更斯却洞悉了其中蕴含的人性真谛。

The characters of Dr. Manette, Lucie, Charles Darnay, Miss Pross, the Defarges, and even Sydney Carton are less complex, psychologically, than is usual for Dickens, signaling that his novel is, indeed, a “tale”—Lucie and Charles, in particular, are a simple and virtuous couple with almost no characteristics apart from their virtues. Dr. Manette is his imprisonment. Madame Defarge is relentlessness personified. The only characters with the usual Dickensian flourishes and idiosyncrasies are Jerry Cruncher, Miss Pross, and Mr. Lorry, but they hardly ever get out of hand, as quirky characters such as Mr. Micawber do in other Dickens novels. The plot is all, and it is a cinematic plot. Dickens was passionately interested in theater, and was an accomplished amateur actor. He wrote or collaborated on several plays over the years, and A Tale of Two Cities has the tightness of a play—it is full of coincidences, twins, doubles, and repetitions. But because of the spaciousness and grandness of Dickens's themes—the differences between France and England, the nature of mass movements, and social violence—it does as a novel what a play can't quite do—it moves through time and space, panning over crowds, capturing the surge of large groups in flux. The narrator's voice, which is particularly rich and insightful in this novel, works like a camera, pointing out what is important and focusing the reader's attention on particulars that make sense of the chaos.

马内特医生、露西、查尔斯·达内、普罗斯小姐、德法奇夫妇，甚至西德尼·卡顿这些人物，在心理层面上都比狄更斯通常笔下的人物要简单得多，这表明他的小说的确是一部“故事”——尤其是露西和查尔斯，他们是一对单纯善良的夫妇，除了美德之外几乎没有其他性格特征。马内特医生是查尔斯的囚笼。德法奇夫人则是冷酷无情的化身。只有杰瑞·克朗彻、普罗斯小姐和洛里先生这几个人物带有狄更斯惯用的夸张和怪癖，但他们几乎从未像狄更斯其他小说中那些古怪的人物（比如米考伯先生）那样失控。情节才是最重要的，而且是一个电影般的情节。狄更斯对戏剧充满热情，他本人也是一位技艺精湛的业余演员。多年来，他创作或参与创作了多部戏剧，《双城记》也具备戏剧的紧凑性——充满了巧合、孪生、双重身份和重复。但由于狄更斯主题的广阔和宏大——法英之间的差异、群众运动的本质以及社会暴力——它作为一部小说做到了戏剧难以企及的事情：它穿越时空，俯瞰人群，捕捉到大批人群涌动的动态。小说中叙述者的声音尤为丰富而深刻，如同镜头一般，指出关键所在，引导读者关注那些能够解释混乱局面的细节。

As a rule, the novel and the cinema don't work in similar ways, and as a rule the novel has not been good at depicting wars and revolutions, but in the sections where Dickens wants to give a sense of what groups are doing, he uses powerful and archaic images of fire, flood, and wild dancing. When he wants to depict the significance of a murder, he uses metaphors of stone gargoyles. He is communicating figuratively that the forces at work are elemental and morally natural—there is, after all, nothing so logical or implacable as the consequences of tyranny.

通常来说，小说和电影的运作方式并不相同，小说也通常不擅长描绘战争和革命。但在狄更斯想要展现群体行为的章节中，他运用了火、洪水和狂舞等充满力量且古老的意象。当他想描绘谋杀的意义时，他则使用石像鬼的隐喻。他以象征手法传达出，起作用的力量是原始的、符合道德自然规律的——毕竟，没有什么比暴政的后果更合乎逻辑、更无情的了。

But revenge, the basic motive of the republican characters, works like a machine, inhumanly mirroring and reproducing the tyranny that gave rise to it. As the Revolution progresses, Dickens's insights into the republican mind are no less unsentimental than his earlier insights into the aristocratic mind. Through Sydney Carton and Mr. Lorry, Dickens depicts what it is to remain human in the midst of fear and rage—it is to keep order, to maintain attachments and affections, to make plans with a cool head, to sustain a sense of compassion, to endure, and to accept defeat knowing that the body is not the only manifestation of life. A Tale of Two Cities is Dickens's most openly faithful novel, but his faith is simple—merely a faith in redemption through sacrifice and kindness.

但复仇，作为共和派人物的基本动机，如同机器一般运转，冷酷无情地映照并复制着催生它的暴政。随着革命的推进，狄更斯对共和派思想的洞察，丝毫不逊于他早期对贵族思想的洞察。通过悉尼·卡顿和洛里先生这两个人物，狄更斯描绘了在恐惧和愤怒之中如何保持人性——维持秩序，维系情感与羁绊，冷静地制定计划，保持同情心，忍耐，并坦然接受失败，因为他明白肉体并非生命的唯一体现。《双城记》是狄更斯最直白地忠于原著的小说，但他的信仰却十分简单——仅仅是一种通过牺牲和仁慈获得救赎的信仰。

Dickens always strove to depict the web of connections he saw between all individuals, no matter how far apart they appeared to be.

狄更斯总是努力描绘他所看到的所有人之间的联系网络，无论他们看起来多么遥远。

The connections in A Tale of Two Cities are very tight—defying plausibility for some readers. But I see the novel as a discourse on that very theme—the responsibilities and the pleasures of the connections to all around us that we barely see or feel and sometimes are reluctant to acknowledge, but exist anyway, whether we can sense them or not.

《双城记》中人物之间的联系非常紧密——对一些读者来说甚至难以置信。但我认为这部小说正是对这一主题的探讨——我们与周围一切事物之间联系的责任与乐趣，这些联系我们几乎看不到也感觉不到，有时甚至不愿承认，但它们确实存在，无论我们能否感知到。

35. Wilkie Collins. The Woman in White

35. 威尔基·柯林斯，《白衣女人》

(1860; REPR., NEW YORK: BANTAM, 1985), 564 PP.

（1860 年；重印，纽约：BANTAM，1985 年），564 页。

The Woman in White was one of the first, if not the first, great novels of detection, though the “detective” is not a private eye or a police official, but merely an interested party, Walter Hartright, an artist and drawing master. The crime is fraud rather than murder, and Collins depicts nothing grisly or violent, but nevertheless The Woman in White is a page-turner, showing that a good riddle, an intelligent style, and compelling characters are plenty sufficient for a thriller, and that questions of good and evil do not require large effusions of gore.

《白衣女人》即便不是第一部伟大的侦探小说，也是最早的侦探小说之一。尽管小说中的“侦探”并非私家侦探或警官，而仅仅是一位与案件相关的艺术家兼绘画教师沃尔特·哈特赖特。案件并非谋杀，而是诈骗，柯林斯也没有描绘任何血腥或暴力的场景，但《白衣女人》依然引人入胜，它证明了一个好的谜题、精妙的文风和鲜活的人物足以成就一部惊悚小说，而善恶的探讨也无需大量血腥暴力的描写。

Like many English novels, the story begins with a rich young woman and a poor young man, who fall in love but are separated by difficulties of class and wealth. Laura Fairlie has already been betrothed for two years at the novel's outset, to a man of large property from a distant part of England, in accordance with her father's last wishes. Walter and Laura fall in love, but are properly circumspect, and renounce one another within the first hundred pages. The stage is thus set for the typical English outcome, but Collins chooses a new way to get there.

如同许多英国小说一样，故事以一位富有的年轻女子和一位贫穷的青年男子相爱开篇，却因阶级和财富的差异而被迫分离。小说开篇时，劳拉·费尔利已按照父亲的遗愿，与一位来自英格兰远方、拥有巨额财产的男子订婚两年。沃尔特和劳拉坠入爱河，但两人都保持着应有的谨慎，在小说的前一百页就分道扬镳。故事的开端似乎预示着典型的英国式爱情结局，但柯林斯却选择了一条全新的叙事方式。

There is nothing apparently wrong with the prospective bridegroom, Sir Percival Glyde (except his sinister name), but Laura's beloved half-sister, Marian, and her dog are both suspicious of him. Nevertheless, the marriage goes forward even as symptoms of a coming disaster begin to accumulate. The pleasure of The Woman in White is not that it avoids damsel-in-distress clichs, but that it embraces them and converts them into actual complexities. Collins owes a lot to the tradition of Pamela and other virtue-beset novels, as well as gothic novels such as Mrs. Radcliffe's The Mysteries of Udolpho ( 1794 ), but he locates every scene and event in a specific, modern, and prosaic landscape. The characters meet on Hampstead Heath, in Cumberland, Hampshire, and in St. John's Wood in London. They ride in trains and cabs and speak in typical dialects. Most importantly, Col-lins's style is solid, objective, and reassuring (though he adopts several different points of view and styles of composition). He seems to be asking, can the old bogey of false marriage, of kidnapping and even rape happen right here, in England, in the sunshine of every day? And he seems to be answering yes.

准新郎珀西瓦尔·格莱德爵士表面上看起来并无不妥（除了他那不祥的名字），但劳拉挚爱的同父异母妹妹玛丽安和她的狗都对他心存疑虑。尽管如此，婚礼还是如期举行，而灾难的征兆也开始显现。《白衣女人》的魅力不在于它避开了“落难少女”的陈词滥调，而在于它拥抱了这些套路，并将它们转化为真正复杂的故事。柯林斯深受《帕梅拉》等其他美德至上的小说传统以及拉德克利夫夫人的《乌多尔夫的秘密》（1794）等哥特式小说的影响，但他将每一个场景和事件都置于一个具体、现代且平淡无奇的背景之中。人物在汉普郡的汉普斯特德荒原、坎伯兰郡、汉普郡以及伦敦的圣约翰伍德相遇。他们乘坐火车和出租车，说着典型的方言。最重要的是，柯林斯的文风稳健、客观且令人安心（尽管他采用了多种不同的视角和构图风格）。他似乎在问：虚假婚姻、绑架甚至强奸这些老生常谈的罪恶，是否真的会在英国，在每一天的阳光下发生？而他的答案似乎是肯定的。

And yet the end is never really in doubt, because Laura and Walter's love is true. The compelling quality of the narrative comes from the ambiguity of Collins's characters—in several situations, certain characters could make dangerous or harmful choices; other, more sympathetic characters are at their mercy.
