The momentum of the plot argues for the happier choice, but the complexity of the characters seduces the reader into imagining things going differently. Thus Collins fully exploits the paradox of the thriller. The thriller is essentially a tragicomic form. Maybe a paradigmatic model is Shakespeare's Measure for Measure , in which a false marriage is threatened; one character appears to die but revives; and a powerful, high-ranking character must sort out the difficulties and bring about the happy ending. “The danger but not the death” is simultaneously suspenseful and reassuring—the perfect entertainment for a reading public that lives in basically secure circumstances, as the literate middle class was beginning to do in the high Victorian period, when Collins's novels were published with great success.

然而，结局其实从未真正悬念过，因为劳拉和沃尔特的爱情是真挚的。故事引人入胜之处在于柯林斯笔下人物的复杂性——在很多情况下，某些角色可能会做出危险或有害的选择；而另一些更令人同情的角色则受制于他们。情节的推进似乎倾向于更美好的选择，但人物的复杂性又诱使读者去想象事情朝着不同的方向发展。因此，柯林斯充分利用了惊悚小说的悖论。惊悚小说本质上是一种悲喜剧形式。莎士比亚的《一报还一报》或许是一个典范：一段虚假的婚姻岌岌可危；一个角色看似死去却又复活；而一位权势显赫的人物必须化解重重危机，最终促成圆满结局。 “危险却无死亡”既令人紧张又令人安心——对于生活在基本安全环境中的读者来说，这是完美的娱乐，就像维多利亚时代盛期中受过教育的中产阶级开始过着这样的生活一样，而柯林斯的小说正是在那时出版的，并取得了巨大的成功。

A necessary requirement of Collins's sort of ungruesome thriller was that he create complex characters who could or might do anything, rather than mechanical types who were certain to act predictably. In The Woman in White , Count Fosco, his wife, Sir Percival, and Laura's half-sister Marian have a suspenseful richness. Following the workings of their minds and the ramifications of their relations with one another is enough—no need for bloodier shocks. And yet, in the end, the novel is less satisfying because of its suspenseful form—the wonderful prose, the fabulous characters, the astutely depicted settings have failed to reveal anything larger than the plot. The plot has taken over the author's point of view, and the critique or vision he might have offered has been sacrificed. This is the further paradox of the thriller, which subsequent authors have continued to wrestle with. The thriller posits various forms of evil and goodness that come into conflict. The next step, of course, is some sort of philosophical program that reflects upon the nature and sources of good and evil, but plot complexity prohibits discussion that is productive, and anyway, the demands of the plot beg the question—evil exists in the last analysis so that the author can write a thriller. While the thriller form addresses the classic concern of literature—the nature of and the interplay of good and evil—it addresses it tautologically, and proposes the discussion of good and evil as essentially an entertainment. Thriller writers after Collins tried to solve this ontological problem by depicting more gore and destruction (more danger and more death for less important characters), but still they cannot escape its paradoxes.

柯林斯那种不血腥的惊悚小说，其必要条件在于塑造复杂多变的人物，而非机械刻板、行为可预测的角色。在《白衣女人》中，福斯科伯爵、他的妻子珀西瓦尔爵士以及劳拉的同父异母妹妹玛丽安，都充满了悬念。仅仅关注他们的内心活动以及彼此关系的复杂影响就足以引人入胜——无需更血腥的冲击。然而，最终，这部小说却因其悬疑的形式而略显逊色——优美的文笔、精彩的人物、精妙的场景描写，都未能揭示出超越情节本身的更深层次的东西。情节占据了作者的视角，他本可以提出的批判或见解也被牺牲了。这正是惊悚小说的另一个悖论，也是后世作家不断探讨的课题。惊悚小说假定存在着各种形式的善与恶，而这些善与恶的冲突也由此展开。当然，下一步应该是某种哲学纲领，反思善恶的本质和根源，但情节的复杂性阻碍了富有成效的讨论。而且，情节本身的要求就回避了这个问题——归根结底，恶的存在只是为了让作者能够写出一部惊悚小说。虽然惊悚小说形式触及了文学的经典主题——善恶的本质及其相互作用——但它以一种同义反复的方式探讨了这个问题，并将对善恶的讨论本质上视为一种娱乐。柯林斯之后的惊悚小说作家试图通过描绘更多的血腥和破坏（更多的危险和次要角色的死亡）来解决这一本体论问题，但他们仍然无法摆脱其中的悖论。

One of the interesting features of cultural history since Collins's time is that the entertaining, tautological, and tragicomic form of the thriller has almost entirely taken over cultural considerations of good and evil, through best sellers and movies, and these have accustomed us to the evils in our world, reassured us that escape is possible for a few main characters (and we are all the main characters of our own stories), and so inured us to the existence of evil that it causes no outrage or even disquiet.

自柯林斯时代以来，文化史的一个有趣特点是，惊悚小说这种娱乐性强、同义反复、悲喜剧式的作品，通过畅销书和电影，几乎完全取代了人们对善恶的文化思考，使我们习惯了世界上的邪恶，让我们相信少数主角（我们都是自己故事的主角）是可以逃脱的，并且使我们对邪恶的存在麻木不仁，以至于它不会引起任何愤怒甚至不安。

# ↩

Wilkie Collins The Moonstone

威尔基·柯林斯《月亮宝石》

(1868; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1999), 466 PP.

（1868 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1999 年），466 页。

In narrative form, The Moonstone uses the same device of multiple tellers as The Woman in White. It also has a similar charming liveliness of style and similar typical English characters—the beautiful young heiress, the attractive scapegrace lover, the kindly faithful servants, and the villain who is virtuous on the surface and corrupt underneath. It is a novel designed to be reassuring, in which the temporarily cursed characters (cursed by the Moonstone, a jewel) are exiled from the beautiful country estate, and then restored to it by truth, love, and money.

在叙事形式上，《月亮宝石》与《白衣女人》一样采用了多视角叙述的手法。它也同样拥有迷人而生动的文风，塑造了类似的典型英国人物形象——美丽的年轻女继承人、英俊潇洒的浪荡情人、善良忠诚的仆人，以及表面正直、内心腐败的恶棍。这部小说旨在抚慰人心，讲述了暂时被诅咒（被月亮宝石诅咒）的角色们被逐出美丽的乡间庄园，最终又凭借真理、爱情和金钱重返故土的故事。

What The Moonstone has to offer is delightful ingenuity of plot. The premise is simple—a jewel is bequeathed to a young girl coming of age, and then stolen. A detective is called in. Some danger and some death (which I won't reveal the nature of) intervene before the fate of the jewel is discovered. The author uses a fairly elementary deduction strategy (which the modern reader may be a little too astute for) to mislead the characters and to tempt the reader to skip forward to discover the solution (the novel was originally published in thirty weekly parts, so skipping forward wasn't possible for its first readers). What the novel also has is something modern scholars like very much—the beginnings of a critique (or at least a consideration) of British colonial activities in India. The novel begins with British soldiers plundering an Indian town and stealing a holy jewel. It does not overtly analyze who has the right to possess the jewel, but it does, in the end, return the jewel to its original location. There are several Indian characters, a character of mixed race, and some discussion of opium-eating (Collins took laudanum, a form of opium, for a painful illness that modern scholars have not diagnosed). The morality of the opium trade was a topic of public debate while Collins was writing the novel, and to modern thinkers is a prime example of the callousness and corruption of British imperialist capitalism.

《月亮宝石》的魅力在于其巧妙的情节构思。故事的设定很简单：一颗宝石被遗赠给一位即将成年的少女，随后却被盗。一位侦探受命调查。在宝石的下落最终揭晓之前，期间发生了一些危险和死亡事件（具体内容恕我隐瞒）。作者运用了一种相当基础的推理策略（现代读者或许对此过于精明），误导了书中的人物，并诱使读者跳读以探寻真相（这部小说最初以三十个连载章节的形式每周更新，因此早期读者无法跳读）。此外，这部小说还包含着现代学者非常欣赏的一点——对英国在印度的殖民活动进行批判（或至少是思考）的雏形。小说以英国士兵洗劫印度小镇并盗走一颗圣物开篇。小说并未直接分析谁有权拥有这颗宝石，但最终还是将宝石归还给了它原本所在的地方。小说中出现了几个印度裔角色、一个混血角色，以及一些关于吸食鸦片的描写（柯林斯本人曾服用鸦片酊，一种鸦片制剂，用于治疗一种现代学者尚未确诊的痛苦疾病）。在柯林斯创作这部小说时，鸦片贸易的道德问题正处于公众辩论的焦点，而这部小说在现代思想家看来，正是英国帝国主义资本主义冷酷无情和腐败堕落的典型例证。

Collins is a perfect candidate for literary rehabilitation, because it is tempting to see a great deal that is subversive encoded in his novels, and so they are novels that seem to argue against their own affirmation of rational and traditional English life. Collins himself was a complex man, not nearly as respectable, or eager to appear respectable, as most English novelists, and he was a great protg of Dickens's, who upheld respectability in his writings but not in the last thirteen or fourteen years of his life. But is The Moonstone really subversive? As I pointed out in the entry on The Woman in White , the detective novel is a conservative form—the purpose of detection is to ferret out evil and dispose of it, temporarily righting the imbalance in the world created by criminal activity. In neither of these novels does Collins show any propensity to argue that the imbalance in the world can be righted in the sense that the pervasiveness of evil can be mitigated in general—the lesson the characters learn is to be more careful and perhaps take refuge behind large gates.

柯林斯是文学复兴的理想人选，因为人们很容易在他的小说中发现大量颠覆性元素，这些小说似乎都在反驳自身对理性与传统英国生活的肯定。柯林斯本人是个复杂的人，远不如大多数英国小说家那样受人尊敬，或者说并不热衷于展现体面。他是狄更斯的得意门生，狄更斯在其作品中维护着体面，但在他生命的最后十三四年里却并非如此。但《月亮宝石》真的具有颠覆性吗？正如我在《白衣女人》的条目中所指出的，侦探小说是一种保守的体裁——侦破的目的是揭露邪恶并将其清除，暂时纠正犯罪活动造成的社会失衡。在这两部小说中，柯林斯都没有表现出任何倾向去论证世界上的不平衡是可以纠正的，或者说邪恶的普遍性是可以减轻的——人物们学到的教训是要更加小心，或许还要躲在大门后面。

Collins's style is attractive, objective, and accessible. It is felicitous, like Scott's style. It does not open out into an irrational, visionary world as Dickens's style does. Collins the writer seems like a versatile but basically sanguine fellow for whom happiness is made up of normal forms of human love, comfort, stability, and companionship. Collins's emotional state never seems to drive his works—Dickens was often sentimental, or outraged, or awed, or overjoyed, or transported, and his characters and plots existed as embodiments of these intense states. Collins, by contrast, writes like a member of a society into which he fits fairly well and whose norms he feels comfortable with.

柯林斯的文风引人入胜、客观冷静且平易近人。它流畅自然，如同斯科特的文风一般。与狄更斯的风格不同，柯林斯的文风并不展现一个非理性的、充满幻想的世界。作为作家的柯林斯似乎是一位多才多艺但本质上乐观的人，他认为幸福是由人类正常的爱、舒适、稳定和陪伴构成的。柯林斯的情感状态似乎从未驱动过他的作品——狄更斯常常多愁善感、义愤填膺、敬畏不已、欣喜若狂或心潮澎湃，他笔下的人物和情节正是这些强烈情感的化身。相比之下，柯林斯的写作风格更像是融入一个他相当适应的社会，并认同该社会规范的一份子。

Collins's works give pleasure rather than pity, terror, or transcendence, like those of Dickens, the Brontës, or Shakespeare. Whether it was Collins's temperament, or the form of the detective novel itself, or Collins's ambitions for popular success that made these novels “encoded” or self-contradictory is not, I think, susceptible to critical understanding. Best to just enjoy.

柯林斯的作品带给人的是愉悦，而非像狄更斯、勃朗特姐妹或莎士比亚的作品那样，引发怜悯、恐惧或超脱之感。至于这些小说之所以显得“晦涩难懂”或自相矛盾，究竟是柯林斯的性情使然，还是侦探小说本身的文体，抑或是他对大众成功的渴望，我认为并非批判性分析所能解释的。最好的办法就是尽情享受。

36. Ivan Turgenev. Fathers and Sons

36. 伊万·屠格涅夫，《父与子》

TRANS. RICHARD FREEBORN

译者：理查德·弗里伯恩

(1862; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1998), 201 PP.

（1862 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1998 年），201 页。

Fathers and Sons is the transitional work between Russian novels of the Romantic period and the great Russian novels of the realist period. It even has an aged and attenuated Romantic character, Pavel Petrovich, who has sacrificed his life to unavailing passion and in the course of the novel fights a duel of his own instigation, even though duels are sadly out of date. Mostly, though, it has the ineffable charm and brevity of the Russian fiction that grew out of “Eugene Onegin,” Pushkin's great and much-beloved narrative poem of the 1830s . The style of Tur-genev's language and the way in which the narrative develops are suggestive and lyrical rather than dense. Detail seems to accumulate almost incidentally (though, of course, that sense of casualness is carefully contrived by the author).

《父与子》是俄国浪漫主义时期小说向现实主义时期伟大小说过渡的代表作。小说中甚至塑造了一个年迈而颓废的浪漫主义人物——帕维尔·彼得罗维奇，他为徒劳的激情献出了生命，并在小说中自导自演了一场决斗，尽管决斗在当时已然过时。然而，这部小说最主要的特质是它那难以言喻的魅力和简洁，这种魅力和简洁源于普希金19世纪30年代的伟大叙事长诗《叶甫根尼·奥涅金》。屠格涅夫的语言风格和叙事手法都充满暗示性和抒情性，而非晦涩难懂。细节的积累似乎近乎偶然（当然，这种随意感是作者精心设计的）。

Turgenev's central character is Bazarov, a “new man,” whose intellectual inspirations are German and scientific rather than French and Romantic. He is openly contemptuous of every received idea, including ideas of love or morality. The paradox of Bazarov's character and his social position is that he seems, both to himself and to those around him, to be Russia's only chance to save herself, but he has no belief in Russia's saving herself. Bazarov's friend Arkady is made of kinder, more conventional stuff. When the two men meet two sisters and fall in love, the reader can't help desiring a happy ending for Arkady, and that happy ending is achieved. But there is no happy ending for Bazarov, and in fact he rejects all ideas that would lead to a happy ending. A conventional happy ending would so betray Bazarov's principles that it would be more horrifying than the ending he achieves.

屠格涅夫笔下的中心人物是巴扎罗夫，一个“新人”，他的思想启蒙来自德国的科学思想，而非法国的浪漫主义思想。他公开蔑视一切既定观念，包括爱情和道德观念。巴扎罗夫的性格及其社会地位的悖论在于，无论在他自己还是在周围的人眼中，他似乎都是俄罗斯自救的唯一希望，但他却不相信俄罗斯能够自救。巴扎罗夫的朋友阿尔卡季则更为善良，也更循规蹈矩。当两人邂逅一对姐妹并坠入爱河时，读者不禁希望阿尔卡季能有一个幸福的结局，而这个结局也确实实现了。但巴扎罗夫却没有幸福的结局，事实上，他拒绝一切可能带来幸福结局的想法。一个循规蹈矩的幸福结局会彻底背离巴扎罗夫的原则，其恐怖程度甚至超过了他最终获得的结局。

Turgenev addresses Bazarov's nihilism, but because of the lightness of his technique he does not judge it. He is a realist in the sense that he holds up five characters for the reader's consideration—Bazarov, his father, Arkady, his father, and Arkady's uncle—and he follows their progress over the course of about a year, almost without comment. He doesn't weigh their fates morally; rather he observes them with a muted but natural generosity of spirit and then parts from them once their fates are decided. It may come as a surprise to the reader that the other characters seem to have such respect for Bazarov, since he is brusque and churlish and has none of their charm and feels none of the attachments they revel in. But he looks forward to Dostoevsky and is, in some sense, a true Russian type, a man who is resolutely searching for a way into a new and different era, a way to solve social, economic, and political problems that didn't exist in England or France. In this sense he is a modern, ideological man and thoroughly recognizable to modern readers, who have seen youthful nihilists with no manners come and go again and again.

屠格涅夫探讨了巴扎罗夫的虚无主义，但由于其笔法轻盈，他并未对此进行评判。从某种意义上说，他是一位现实主义者，他为读者呈现了五个人物——巴扎罗夫、他的父亲、阿尔卡季、他的父亲以及阿尔卡季的叔叔——并在大约一年的时间里，几乎不加评论地记录了他们的命运。他没有从道德层面去衡量他们的命运；相反，他以一种内敛而自然的宽容之心观察着他们，然后在他们的命运尘埃落定之后，与他们告别。巴扎罗夫性格粗鲁无礼，既没有他们的魅力，也没有他们所沉浸其中的情感，因此，其他人物似乎对他如此敬重，这或许会让读者感到惊讶。但他对陀思妥耶夫斯基充满期待，在某种意义上，他是一个典型的俄罗斯人，一个坚定地寻求进入一个崭新时代之路，寻求解决在英法两国都不存在的社会、经济和政治问题的方法的人。从这个意义上讲，他是一个现代的、有思想的人，对于一次又一次目睹没有教养的年轻虚无主义者来来去去的现代读者来说，他完全可以理解。

Like A Hero of Our Time, Fathers and Sons is a bit enigmatic— beautifully even in tone, suggesting more than it states, modest, never didactic, and yet true and important because of rather than in spite of its brevity. It is the sort of book a reader returns to, not because there is so much material there that she has to read it over and over to excavate it all, but because what is there is ephemeral, easily lost, and yet seductive.

如同《当代英雄》一般，《父与子》也略带神秘感——语调优美而平衡，言简意赅，谦逊低调，从不说教，却因其篇幅短小而显得真实而重要。这是一本值得读者反复品读的书，并非因为书中内容浩瀚如海，需要反复阅读才能挖掘全貌，而是因为书中的文字转瞬即逝，容易遗失，却又如此引人入胜。

37. Émile Zola, Thérèse Raquin

37. 埃米尔·佐拉，泰蕾兹·拉奎因

TRANS. AND ED. LEONARD TANCOCK (1867; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1981), 255 PP.

LEONARD TANCOK 翻译和编辑（1867 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1981 年），255 页。

Thérèse Raquin was Zola's first success, but initially it was a succs du scandale , since Zola was accused of writing pornography—there was such a critical outcry that he felt he had to defend himself in his preface to the second edition of the novel. Zola also wrote a stage version of the novel, which was popular at the time and more lasting than any other of his plays.

《泰蕾丝·拉甘》是左拉的首部成功之作，但最初却是一部丑闻式的成功，因为左拉被指责创作色情作品——评论界的强烈抗议迫使他不得不在小说第二版的序言中为自己辩护。左拉还创作了这部小说的舞台剧版本，该剧在当时广受欢迎，并且比他的任何其他戏剧作品都更加经久不衰。

The plot is focused and dramatic: two children are reared together, a boy and his cousin, by the boy's mother, a woman of some means who lives in a small French town. When the cousins reach marriageable age, they do what the mother wishes, which is to marry one another, because they have lived such a circumscribed life that they don't have any idea what else to do. Thérèse, the girl, is quiet and submissive, but secretly passionate. Camille, the boy, is sickly and spoiled. Though the three members of the small family live and work together, they have no intimacy with one another, and the inner life of each develops entirely in isolation from the inner life of the others. The mother eventually decides to take the money she has saved and open a small shop in Paris. Camille finds himself an office job, and the family gains a circle of friends, one of whom, Laurent, is about Camille's age and is strongly drawn to Thérèse, who reciprocates his lust.

故事情节紧凑而扣人心弦：男孩和他的表兄妹由男孩的母亲抚养长大，这位母亲家境殷实，住在法国的一个小镇上。当表兄妹到了适婚年龄，他们遵从母亲的意愿，结为夫妻，因为他们的生活过于封闭，不知何去何从。女孩泰蕾丝性格安静顺从，但内心却充满激情。男孩卡米尔体弱多病，娇生惯养。虽然这三个人生活在一起，共同工作，但彼此之间却缺乏亲密感，每个人的内心世界都与他人隔绝。最终，母亲决定用积蓄在巴黎开一家小店。卡米尔找到了一份办公室工作，一家人也结识了新朋友，其中一位名叫洛朗，与卡米尔年龄相仿，他深深地爱慕着泰蕾丝，而泰蕾丝也对他抱有爱慕之情。

Laurent and Thérèse plot to kill Camille and successfully make his death look like an accident, but while the scheme works and they end up marrying, their relationship is entirely contaminated by their secret, and their once-passionate attachment becomes a daily exercise in repulsion and panic. They live with Camille's mother, who eventually has a stroke, and they care for her with all apparent tenderness (her friends marvel at how considerately they treat her), but once again, each one puts his or her faith in arduously maintained secrecy, and each lives a hellish existence right beside the others, never comforted but always tormented by their presence (and by the growing presence of Camille, who obsesses each of them differently).

洛朗和泰蕾丝密谋杀害卡米尔，并成功地将他的死伪装成意外。虽然计划成功，他们最终也结了婚，但他们的关系却被这个秘密彻底玷污，曾经炽热的爱恋变成了每日的厌恶和恐慌。他们与卡米尔的母亲同住，母亲后来中风，他们表面上对她关怀备至（她的朋友们都惊叹于他们的体贴），但再一次，他们各自将希望寄托于苦苦保守的秘密之上，彼此之间如同身处炼狱，从未得到慰藉，反而饱受彼此的折磨（以及卡米尔日益增长的存在感，她以不同的方式令他们着迷）。

Thérèse Raquin demonstrates that a carefully worked-out psychological theory can be dramatic and compelling, even when the characters are not appealing or sympathetic. Zola himself, as both author and narrator, embraced the idea that characters without charm, education, or even notably human qualities were entirely worthy of literary depiction as examples of behavior patterns. In fact, the fewer special qualities his characters (you might call them, not protagonists or antagonists, but simply “agonists”—beings with feelings but requiring no partisanship by the reader) had, the more valuable they were as objective examples. Zola wanted to write fiction in the scientific mold—he called his style “naturalism.”

特蕾丝·拉坎证明，精心构建的心理学理论即便人物并不讨喜或令人同情，也能引人入胜、扣人心弦。左拉本人，既是作者又是叙述者，他认同这样的观点：那些缺乏魅力、教养，甚至缺乏显著人性特质的人物，完全值得被文学化地描绘，作为行为模式的例证。事实上，他笔下的人物（你或许可以称他们为“行动者”，而非主角或反派——他们有情感，但读者无需对他们抱有任何偏袒）越是缺乏特殊品质，他们作为客观例证的价值就越高。左拉希望以科学的模式创作小说——他称自己的风格为“自然主义”。

The melodrama of the story of Thérèse and Laurent is suspenseful, but it barely hides the theory supporting the action of the plot, which can be outlined as follows: the failure of Madame Raquin to reckon with Thérèse's nascent sexual feelings when she reared Thérèse and Camille together through childhood and adolescence made the young woman immune to Camille but susceptible to Laurent. The feelings these two had for one another were solely physical and depended heavily on the exciting secrecy of their initial relations. After the murder, the simultaneous presence of guilt and lust eventually destroyed the lust, and neither Laurent nor Thérèse were capable of any other form of connection to another human being. Guilt is all-consuming and works by a process of association, overwhelming, bit by bit, every aspect of the lives of the guilty. It cannot be expiated or relieved, but in the last scene, when Laurent and Thérèse drink poison with Madame Raquin as their silent and immobile witness (she has suffered a stroke), they achieve a single ambiguous moment of oneness.

泰蕾丝和洛朗的故事充满悬念，但其情节背后却隐藏着一个理论，可以概括如下：拉坎夫人未能察觉泰蕾丝萌生的性意识，导致她与卡米尔一同长大成人，使得泰蕾丝对卡米尔免疫，却对洛朗动了心。两人之间的感情仅限于肉体，且很大程度上依赖于最初关系的刺激和隐秘。谋杀案发生后，罪恶感与欲望的交织最终摧毁了欲望，洛朗和泰蕾丝都无法再与他人建立任何其他形式的联系。罪恶感如同毒药般吞噬一切，它通过联想作用，一点一点地侵蚀着罪人生活的方方面面。虽然无法赎罪或缓解，但在最后一幕中，当洛朗和泰蕾丝在拉金夫人（她中风了）的沉默和一动不动的见证下喝下毒药时，他们达到了一个暧昧的合一瞬间。

This is both a psychological and a spiritual theory—it asserts the inescapable solitude of the individual and the irredeemable natural selfishness of human nature. Zola's theory is a train of logic backed up by shrewdly chosen details of setting, action, and revealed thought. The premises, however, require the same leap of faith that any theory requires—his story demonstrates his theory because it was designed to do so.

这既是一种心理学理论，也是一种精神理论——它断言个体无法逃避的孤独以及人性中无可救药的自私。左拉的理论逻辑严密，并以精心挑选的场景、情节和思想细节加以支撑。然而，其前提也需要像任何理论一样，需要一定的信任——他的故事之所以能印证他的理论，正是因为它本身就是为此而设计的。

This self-referential quality does not disqualify Thérèse Raquin from being a good novel—I happen to like it—only from being a good scientific experiment. In fact, every novel requires the author to have a psychological theory—every train of logic (which in a novel is made up of actions, dialogue, and expressed thoughts) requires theory to progress from one step (one plot point) to the next. Some theories are more conventional than others, some are more profound than others, some date more quickly than others, but an author with a theory, even a theory that dates very quickly, is in general more humane and large-spirited than an author with no theory or no interest in theory. The very attempt to come up with a theory expresses a broader humanity and a wider perspective. In Zola's case it was as though he were saying, “Even these sorts of persons are interesting to me, and I can make them interesting to you.”

这种自指性并不妨碍《泰蕾丝·拉坎》成为一部优秀的小说——我恰好很喜欢它——它只是妨碍了它成为一项优秀的科学实验。事实上，每一部小说都需要作者拥有一套心理学理论——每一连串的逻辑（在小说中，逻辑由行动、对话和表达的思想构成）都需要理论支撑才能从一个情节点推进到下一个情节点。有些理论比其他理论更传统，有些比其他理论更深刻，有些比其他理论更容易过时，但一个拥有理论的作者，即使是一个很快就会过时的理论，通常也比一个没有理论或对理论不感兴趣的作者更具人文情怀和胸怀。试图提出理论本身就体现了一种更广阔的人性和更广阔的视野。就左拉而言，他仿佛在说：“即使是这类人也让我感兴趣，而且我也可以让你们对他们感兴趣。”

38. Anthony Trollope. The Last Chronicle of Barset

38. 安东尼·特罗洛普，《巴塞特的最后编年史》

(1867; REPR., NEW YORK: ALFRED A. KNOPF, EVERYMAN'S LIBRARY, 1993), 768 PP.

（1867 年；重印，纽约：阿尔弗雷德·A·克诺夫，Everyman's Library，1993 年），768 页。

Marcel Proust was only the most famous novelist to try out the virtues of what might be called the meganovel. In the 1830s and 1840s Balzac wrote his eighty-five novels that were loosely linked as La Comdie humaine , and Trollope wrote six novels of the fictional cathedral town of Barchester in the 1850s and 1860s , as well as a series of linked novels about English political life known as the Palliser novels. Many of these novels worked somewhat like Balzac's Comdie , with characters who appear as major in one and reappear as minor in others. The mega-novel allows the author to explore a milieu in depth and to follow his characters as they age and develop. The Last Chronicle of Barset is Trol-lope's last novel about Barchester, but the reader need not have read any of the others to enjoy it thoroughly.

马塞尔·普鲁斯特只是尝试过所谓“巨著”这一体裁的最著名小说家之一。19世纪30年代和40年代，巴尔扎克创作了85部松散关联的小说，统称为《人间喜剧》（La Comdie humaine）；19世纪50年代和60年代，特罗洛普以虚构的大教堂小镇巴切斯特为背景，创作了六部小说，此外他还创作了一系列以英国政治生活为主题的关联小说，即帕利泽系列小说。这些小说大多与巴尔扎克的《人间喜剧》有几分相似，人物在一部小说中是主要角色，而在另一部小说中则沦为次要角色。巨著使作者能够深入探索特定环境，并跟随人物的成长和变化。《巴切斯特的最后编年史》是特罗洛普关于巴切斯特的最后一部小说，但读者无需读过他之前的作品也能充分享受这部作品。

The premise of the novel is that an impoverished country curate, Mr. Crawley, passes a check for twenty pounds (maybe the equivalent of seven hundred dollars in modern money) in payment of a past due bill. When the check goes to the bank, it turns out that it is a check that had been lost by the estate agent of the signer of the check, Lord Lufton. Mr. Crawley gives two stories about where he got the check, but in fact he can't remember the origin of the check because of his perennially confused mental state. He is thus in danger of either being proved a thief or proved a madman. Neither will be to his benefit in demonstrating his competence to retain his curacy and continue to support his family.

小说的情节是这样的：一位贫困的乡村牧师克劳利先生为了偿还一笔逾期账款，开了一张二十英镑的支票（按现在的币值计算，大约相当于七百美元）。支票送到银行后，银行发现这张支票竟然是支票签署人卢夫顿勋爵的房产经纪人弄丢的。克劳利先生编造了两个关于支票来源的故事，但实际上，由于他长期精神恍惚，根本记不起支票的来历。因此，他面临着被认定为窃贼或疯子的危险。无论哪种情况，都无助于他证明自己有能力保住牧师职位，继续养家糊口。

The depiction of Crawley is a marvelously detailed and insightful portrait of a very antisocial, proud, and meticulous man, a domestic tyrant, a brilliant scholar, a flawed but compassionate human being. The analysis of his marriage and family life is no less compelling: his wife loves him but fears him, and never knows from one day to the next how to deal with him—she is always in danger of offending his pride with her concern, and yet she doubts whether he is competent to act on his own behalf (he isn't—for example, when he must go to court to be indicted on the charge of theft, he is too proud to get a lawyer, and he is indicted even though the justices are looking for some way, any way, to let him off).

对克劳利的刻画细致入微，极具洞察力，他既是一个极度反社会、骄傲自大、一丝不苟的男人，又是一个家庭暴君，同时也是一位才华横溢的学者，一个有缺陷却又充满同情心的人。对他的婚姻和家庭生活的分析同样引人入胜：他的妻子爱他，却又畏惧他，每天都不知道该如何与他相处——她的关心总是让她担心会触怒他的自尊心，但她又怀疑他是否有能力为自己辩护（他的确没有——例如，当他因盗窃罪被起诉时，他傲慢地拒绝聘请律师，尽管法官们想方设法要让他脱罪，他最终还是被起诉了）。

Crawley's difficulty works as an instrument to expose a cross section of the entire town. His guilt or innocence is a matter of wide discussion, and his impending trial serves to put a kink in the marital plans of a local squire, Major Grantly, who loves Crawley's nineteen-year-old daughter, but whose family is appalled at the thought of being allied through marriage with the daughter of a thief. And when Crawley's daughter, Grace, goes to stay with a friend, because he and his wife can no longer afford to keep her, she meets another young woman to whose hand her cousin aspires. Trollope is the master who orchestrates this social symphony, who engages the reader's sentiments and loyalties over these less than life-and-death issues, and who then very neatly and yet plausibly brings them to a graceful conclusion.

克劳利的困境犹如一把利器，将整个小镇的形形色色的人物展现了出来。他的罪与罚引发了广泛的讨论，即将到来的审判也打乱了当地乡绅格兰特利少校的婚事。格兰特利少校爱慕着克劳利十九岁的女儿，但他的家人却对与一个窃贼的女儿联姻感到震惊。克劳利的女儿格蕾丝因为父母无力继续供养，只好去朋友家暂住。在那里，她结识了另一位年轻女子，而她的表兄正对这位女子心生爱慕。特罗洛普是一位大师，他巧妙地谱写了这首社会交响曲，在这些并非生死攸关的大事上，牵动着读者的情感和忠诚，最终又以一种既精巧又合情合理的方式，将故事引向了一个优雅的结局。

Trollope has many virtues as a novelist. He is organized and efficient; he has a good sense of pace and of proportion, too. His characters are more than believable—they seem perfectly familiar, both as types and as individuals. Trollope's wisdom about the workings of marriage seems almost modern, and contrasts strongly with that of almost every other Victorian writer—he seems actually familiar with intimacy as most people know it, especially the way marriages have two manifestations—the one presented to the outside world, and the one the spouses themselves know. But the best thing about Trollope is that he is always one step ahead of the reader, who comes to feel that there is nothing in the world that the author doesn't know everything about. And Trollope's style, which is objective, understated, detailed, and eloquent, is perfectly suited for his sort of sociological and psychological expertise.

作为小说家，特罗洛普有很多优点。他结构严谨，写作高效；他对节奏和比例的把握也十分出色。他笔下的人物栩栩如生，令人信服——无论是作为类型还是作为个体，都让人感觉无比熟悉。特罗洛普对婚姻运作的洞察几乎达到了现代的水平，这与几乎所有其他维多利亚时代作家的观点都形成了鲜明的对比——他似乎真正了解大多数人所理解的亲密关系，尤其是婚姻的两种表现形式：一种是呈现在外人面前的，另一种则是夫妻彼此了解的。但特罗洛普最令人称道之处在于，他总是能先读者一步，让读者感觉世间万物，他都了如指掌。而特罗洛普客观、含蓄、细致、雄辩的文风，与他所拥有的社会学和心理学方面的专业知识完美契合。

Trollope was a worldly man—his mother was a popular novelist and travel writer who supported the family while he was growing up. He made his way in the British civil service and traveled extensively. Dickens, for example, went to America, France, and Italy. Trollope lived in Ireland, traveled to the United States and Europe more than once, and also to Australia, New Zealand, and South Africa. For purposes of his writings, he was perfectly familiar with how the English ruling class worked, both socially and politically. Judging by his composing style, he went about all things with care and deliberation—in fact, the sympathetic young men in his novels are often beset by indeci-siveness about romantic versus monetary concerns; young men in other Victorian novels usually disdain such practical considerations.

特罗洛普是个见多识广的人——他的母亲是一位颇受欢迎的小说家和旅行作家，在他成长过程中一直支撑着整个家庭。他凭借自身努力在英国公务员系统内谋得职位，并游历甚广。例如，狄更斯曾到访美国、法国和意大利。而特罗洛普则居住在爱尔兰，多次前往美国和欧洲，还到访过澳大利亚、新西兰和南非。为了更好地进行写作，他对英国统治阶级的社会和政治运作方式了如指掌。从他的写作风格来看，他做事谨慎周全——事实上，他小说中那些令人同情的年轻男子常常在爱情与金钱之间摇摆不定；而其他维多利亚时代小说中的年轻男子通常对这种实际考量不屑一顾。

Trollope is a master at entering the minds of a variety of characters and showing how their thoughts progress, and also at showing how they are often deluding themselves or how their views of themselves contrast with the way others see them. Each vivid character is fully enmeshed in a social network, and this enmeshment has consequences—Major Grantly and his father, for example, get into a very entertaining tug-of-war about his prospective engagement that involves anger, resentment, stubbornness, and empty threats on both sides that could easily result in the disinheritance of a beloved son by a beloved father, and which is almost entirely carried out through a discussion about foxes on the family estate. Truly odd characters, such as Crawley, are explored as astutely as more normal ones, but Trollope is unusual in that he can individualize normality and make it compelling—he can give the reader a picture of lives not so unlike her own, and concerns not so different from those she herself has. Trollope is not a sensualist like Flaubert, or a visionary like Dickens, or even a strict moralist like George Eliot. In the Barchester novels Trollope's view is essentially benign, and his endings comic in the red-blooded-Englishman tradition of Fielding and Scott. Trollope writes as if his reason is in charge, but also as if his reason is entirely cognizant of the irrational, the romantic, and the unscrupulous. In fact, he makes all those other Victorians seem a little overheated and melodramatic. This is a lovely and delicious novel.

特罗洛普是一位大师，他善于深入各种人物的内心世界，展现他们思想的演变，也擅长揭示他们常常如何自欺欺人，以及他们对自己的认知与他人眼中的自己之间的巨大反差。每个鲜活的人物都深深地卷入了社交网络，而这种卷入必然会带来后果——例如，格兰特利少校和他的父亲就他即将订婚一事展开了一场妙趣横生的拉锯战，双方都充满了愤怒、怨恨、固执和空洞的威胁，这场争斗很容易导致一位慈爱的父亲剥夺他心爱的儿子的继承权，而这场争斗几乎完全是通过一场关于家族庄园里狐狸的讨论展开的。像克劳利这样真正古怪的人物，与那些更正常的人物一样，都得到了特罗洛普敏锐的刻画。但特罗洛普的独特之处在于，他能够将看似平凡的事物赋予个性，并使其引人入胜——他能让读者看到与自己生活颇为相似的人生，以及与自己所关心的种种忧虑。特罗洛普并非像福楼拜那样的感官主义者，也非像狄更斯那样的空想家，甚至也不是像乔治·艾略特那样的严苛道德主义者。在巴切斯特系列小说中，特罗洛普的观点本质上是仁慈的，其结局也带有菲尔丁和斯科特笔下那种热血英国绅士的喜剧色彩。特罗洛普的写作仿佛理性主导一切，但同时又完全意识到非理性、浪漫和不择手段的一面。事实上，相比之下，其他维多利亚时代的作家都显得有些过火和矫揉造作。这是一部优美动人的小说。

Anthony Trollope The Eustace Diamonds

安东尼·特罗洛普《尤斯塔斯钻石》

(1873; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN BOOKS, 1986), 770 PP.

（1873 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1986 年），770 页。

The Eustace Diamonds was one of Trollope's later novels—he wrote it at fifty-eight, long after he had completed the Barchester novels, which gained him his reputation and his status, and at about the same time as The Way We Live Now , which was his darkest satire of contemporary English life. He acknowledged that his ideas for the novel were influenced both by The Moonstone , with its jewel theft, and by the character of Becky, in Vanity Fair.

《尤斯塔斯钻石》是特罗洛普晚期的小说之一——他五十八岁时创作了这部作品，此时距离他完成巴切斯特系列小说（该系列小说为他赢得了声誉和地位）已过去很久，而《我们现在的生活方式》的创作时间也大致相同，后者是他对当代英国生活最辛辣的讽刺作品。他承认，这部小说的构思受到了《月亮宝石》（其中的珠宝盗窃案）和《名利场》中贝基这个角色的影响。

The possession of the necklace in question is subject to dispute— Lizzie Eustace, the twenty-year-old widow of Sir Florian Eustace and the mother of the heir to the Eustace fortune, claims that her husband gave it to her free and clear before his death. The Eustace family solicitor, Mr. Camperdown, claims that she cannot possess it because it is an heirloom belonging to the estate and tries to insist upon its return, but Lizzie is not a young woman with whom insistence is possible. She is akin, in a way, to Melville's Bartleby the Scrivener—she carries stubbornness to a level previously unknown to her friends (a level quite irritating and even frustrating to the reader, whom Trollope does not allow to feel sympathy for Lizzie). Lizzie is selfish, stubborn, beautiful, manipulative, and almost successful, a girl no one likes but few can resist. Eventually her success is thoroughly compromised by her flaws of character, and those she had hoped to ensnare escape her, but it is not without cost to them. If most novels depict some positive or negative transformation of character by the protagonist, The Eustace Diamonds does not. The fact that Lizzie cannot learn from her experience, or even comprehend the differences between herself and others with more integrity, is the essence of her nature and is, actually, the great genius of Trollope's portrayal. What he is interested in is only secondarily Lizzie herself. Her place in society and her effect upon others are his real subjects, which he anatomizes minutely and in a cool, eloquent style. The result is that the reader nods and nods in agreement— Lizzie leaps from the page, unfamiliar in literature but utterly familiar in life, a portrait of a sister or a cousin or a friend whose behavior one is always trying to account for and failing.

这条项链的归属权存在争议——二十岁的莉齐·尤斯塔斯是弗洛里安·尤斯塔斯爵士的遗孀，也是尤斯塔斯家族继承人的母亲。她声称丈夫生前已将项链无偿赠予她。尤斯塔斯家族的律师坎珀当先生则认为项链属于家族传家宝，因此莉齐无权拥有，并试图要求她归还。然而，莉齐并非一个容易被说服的年轻女子。某种程度上，她与梅尔维尔笔下的抄写员巴特比颇为相似——她的固执程度远超她的朋友们（这种固执令读者感到恼火甚至沮丧，因为特罗洛普并没有让读者对莉齐产生任何同情）。莉齐自私、固执、美丽、善于操纵人心，而且几乎取得了成功，她是一个无人喜欢却又难以抗拒的女孩。最终，她的成功完全被她性格上的缺陷所损害，那些她原本希望诱捕的人也逃脱了她的掌控，但他们也为此付出了代价。大多数小说都会描绘主人公性格的某种正面或负面转变，《尤斯塔斯钻石》却并非如此。莉齐无法从自己的经历中吸取教训，甚至无法更坦诚地理解自己与他人之间的差异，这正是她性格的本质，也是特罗洛普刻画莉齐的精妙之处。他真正感兴趣的并非莉齐本人，而是她在社会中的地位以及她对他人的影响，他以冷静而雄辩的笔触，细致入微地剖析了这些。其结果是，读者频频点头表示赞同——莉齐跃然纸上，在文学作品中或许陌生，但在生活中却无比熟悉，她就像一个姐妹、一个表亲或一个朋友，她的行为总是让人费解，却又无从解释。

Lizzie isn't the only one—Frank, her cousin; Lucy, Frank's beloved; Lord George—almost every major character of the novel is alive, true, not clichd. Trollope is as insightful about the minor characters as he is about the major ones, and in that sense totally throws off what the English novel owes to the theater—no plot elements and no characters are coasting on theatrical conventions. All are depicted with the attention to detail and to the inner life that only the novel can accomplish.

莉齐并非唯一如此——她的表兄弗兰克、弗兰克的爱人露西、乔治勋爵——小说中几乎所有主要人物都栩栩如生、真实可信，而非老套陈腐。特罗洛普对次要人物的刻画与对主要人物的刻画同样深刻，从这个意义上说，他彻底颠覆了英国小说对戏剧的固有认知——没有任何情节或人物是依附于戏剧惯例而存在的。所有人物都以小说独有的细致入微和对内心世界的刻画而著称。

Trollope is often criticized for being habitually digressive, and in fact The Eustace Diamonds could have been shortened by about 15 percent if an authoritative editor had controlled Trollope's tendency to repeat himself. Nevertheless, Trollope's method is one of incremental accumulation of detail. He reminds us of what we know, then adds to it, always bringing in the new material in the context of the familiar. The result is an unparalleled sense that the reader understands everything about the situation and the characters (and, over the course of Trollope's entire oeuvre, the class society of Victorian England). He does not have Proust's sensibility—Trollope is cerebral and ironic rather than lyrical and evocative—but his works add up to a similar compendious exploration of a certain place and a certain time. Trollope is not overtly comic or satiric, like Dickens or Thackeray, but is generously ironic. His typical view of his characters is honest and astute but forgiving. The virtuous ones are not so very virtuous as to be unbelievable, and the villainous ones are not so much evil as ignorant and small. Trollope gives them plenty of opportunity to grow wise, and some of them take it while others do not.

特罗洛普常因惯于离题而受诟病，事实上，如果一位权威的编辑能够控制住他重复的倾向，《尤斯塔斯钻石》的篇幅或许可以缩短约15%。然而，特罗洛普的写作手法是循序渐进地积累细节。他先唤起我们已知的知识，然后在此基础上增添新的内容，始终将新材料置于熟悉的语境之中。其结果是，读者能够以一种无与伦比的方式理解故事背景和人物（以及，纵观特罗洛普的全部作品，维多利亚时代英国的阶级社会）。他没有普鲁斯特那样细腻的情感——特罗洛普的风格更偏向理性与讽刺，而非抒情与感性——但他的作品同样是对特定地点和特定时代的全面探索。特罗洛普不像狄更斯或萨克雷那样直白地运用喜剧或讽刺，但他的讽刺手法却十分巧妙。他笔下的人物通常诚实睿智，却又宽容大度。那些品德高尚的人并非完美得令人难以置信，而那些作恶的人与其说是邪恶，不如说是愚昧狭隘。特罗洛普给了他们许多成长的机会，有些人把握住了，有些人则错失良机。

A few years after The Eustace Diamonds Trollope wrote an autobiography in which he portrayed his novelistic enterprise not as a quest for high art but as a daily task not unlike other professional work. He also outlived his own popularity by a few years. Trollope didn't advertise his gifts very well, and his reputation suffered in consequence, but the entertainment value of his works, and their value as social documents, has grown. His characters have a familiarity and an immediacy that those of writers with a more distinct style do not, and the friendly density of his style has worn well, too. He is not as weird as Dickens, nor as jaded as Thackeray. Trollope doesn't mind a little sin, and he knows that lives go on after the plot ends (Lizzie Eustace turns up again in The Prime Minister , unimproved morally but believably older and more knowledgeable). He is a novelist for adults.

在《尤斯塔斯钻石》出版几年后，特罗洛普写了一部自传，书中他将自己的小说创作描绘成一项日常工作，而非追求高雅艺术。他的名气也比他本人大几年。特罗洛普并不善于宣传自己的才华，因此声誉受损，但他的作品的娱乐价值和作为社会文献的价值却与日俱增。他笔下的人物有一种亲切感和鲜活感，这是那些风格更为鲜明的作家所不具备的，而他亲切而浓郁的文风也经久不衰。他不像狄更斯那样怪诞，也不像萨克雷那样愤世嫉俗。特罗洛普并不介意一些小瑕疵，他也明白故事结束后，生活仍在继续（莉齐·尤斯塔斯在《首相》中再次出现，道德上并无改观，但显然更加成熟睿智）。他是一位为成年人创作的小说家。

39. Fyodor Dostoevsky The Idiot

39. 费奥多尔·陀思妥耶夫斯基《白痴》

TRANS. ALAN MYERS (1868; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1998), 652 PP.

译者：艾伦·迈尔斯（1868 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1998 年），652 页。

The “idiot” is Prince Myshkin, a young man who returns to Russia from years at a Swiss clinic, where he has been treated for epilepsy. In addition to his illness, and perhaps because of it, Myshkin is (and was intended to be by Dostoevsky) a representation of pure goodness. “Pure goodness,” as embodied by the prince, is made up of a cluster of characteristics—he is solitary, poor (at first), innocent and naive, honest, intuitive, generous, easily imposed upon, forgiving, “democratic” (in the sense that he cares little about social status), socially awkward, passive, afflicted by a magical disease, and susceptible to visions of love and brotherhood. He is also both strangely attractive and strangely repellent to those he meets. At least some of these characteristics Myshkin shared with his creator—epilepsy is the most obvious. It is fair to say, I think, that Dostoevsky built his protagonist around some image he had of himself. But the “idiot” is an idea trying to be a character. At times in the novel he almost achieves fullness, but he never throws off his origins in the author's ideas rather than in the author's world—he contrasts strongly, for example, to Raskolnikov, the main character of Crime and Punishment , who was based on a real murderer Dostoevsky read about in the newspaper (rather as Stendhal read about the man upon whom he based Julien Sorel). The problem with Prince Myshkin is that Dostoevsky has to give him a story, and the story Dostoevsky gives him is jumbled and overly dramatic.

这个“白痴”指的是梅什金王子，一位在瑞士诊所接受多年癫痫治疗后返回俄罗斯的年轻人。除了疾病之外，或许也正因为如此，梅什金（陀思妥耶夫斯基的本意）象征着纯粹的善良。“纯粹的善良”在王子身上体现得淋漓尽致，它由一系列特质构成：他孤僻、贫穷（起初）、天真无邪、诚实、直觉敏锐、慷慨大方、容易受人摆布、宽容大度、“民主”（因为他不太在意社会地位）、不善交际、性格被动、身患一种神秘的疾病，并且容易被爱与兄弟情谊所吸引。他对遇到的每个人来说，既有一种奇特的吸引力，又有一种奇特的排斥感。梅什金至少与他的创造者拥有某些共同的特质——癫痫是最明显的例子。我认为，可以说陀思妥耶夫斯基塑造这个主人公时，借鉴了他自身的一些形象。但“白痴”这个角色，其实是一个试图塑造人物的理念。小说中，他有时几乎达到了丰满的程度，但他始终无法摆脱其源于作者理念而非作者世界的本质——例如，他与《罪与罚》的主人公拉斯科尔尼科夫形成了鲜明的对比，拉斯科尔尼科夫的原型是陀思妥耶夫斯基在报纸上读到的一个真实杀人犯（就像司汤达读到他笔下于连·索雷尔的原型人物一样）。梅什金王子的问题在于，陀思妥耶夫斯基必须为他编造一个故事，而陀思妥耶夫斯基编造的故事却杂乱无章，过于戏剧化。

Almost as soon as the prince arrives in St. Petersburg, he encounters two beautiful women. One is the former mistress of a wealthy old man, a young woman who had been taken up as an orphan by the owner of the estate her family lived upon, and both educated and raped by him for several years. Her attempts to free herself of this man are the talk of the city. She arouses both pity and desire on the part of those who know her, and she seems to court the dangers of her position. The other woman is the spoiled youngest daughter of the prince's only living relative. The prince is drawn to both of these women, but he is too naive to understand, or perhaps feel, the difference between eros and agape. And perhaps Dostoevsky is pointing out that in a truly good man, especially one who is a virgin, as Myshkin certainly is, there is no difference. At any rate, he is the passive recipient of the passions of both women. But while both are strongly drawn to him, neither is capable of feeling or acting in a consistent manner, or even a kind manner. The prince is unable to choose between them, and unable to really understand the intentions of either of them. The reader may be forgiven for having the same problem.

王子刚到圣彼得堡不久，就邂逅了两位美人。一位是富翁的旧情妇，她幼时被家族庄园的主人收养，并在那里接受了多年的教育和凌辱。她试图摆脱这个男人的故事成了城中热议的话题。认识她的人既怜悯她，又渴望得到她，而她似乎也在挑战自己的处境。另一位是王子唯一在世亲属的娇生惯养的小女儿。王子被这两位女子深深吸引，但他天真得无法理解，或许也无法感受到爱欲（eros）与博爱（agape）之间的区别。也许陀思妥耶夫斯基想要表达的是，对于一个真正善良的男人，尤其是像梅什金这样纯洁无瑕的处男而言，这两者并无本质区别。无论如何，他只是被动地接受着两位女子的激情。虽然两人都深深地被他吸引，但他们都无法始终如一地表达情感或采取行动，甚至连善意都做不到。王子无法在他们之间做出选择，也无法真正理解他们各自的意图。读者或许也会有同样的困惑，这情有可原。

Dostoevsky may be exploring the age-old European problem of, on the one hand, whether a virtuous woman can truly love a man and retain her virtue and, on the other hand, how young women are to be disposed of in opposition to their own wishes. Toward the end of the novel, the father of the second young woman attributes the whole fiasco to the fact that the prince had been interested in “the woman question.” His real focus, though, seems to be the array of Russian characters the prince encounters after his sojourn in Switzerland, and whether he can handle them. He cannot. It's possible that the average reader can't handle them either, since they seem to be a bunch of drunks, hysterics, liars, madmen, and manic-depressives.

陀思妥耶夫斯基或许是在探讨一个由来已久的欧洲难题：一方面，贞洁的女子能否真心爱上一个男人并保持贞洁；另一方面，年轻女子又该如何违背她们的意愿而被处置。小说临近结尾时，第二位年轻女子的父亲将整件事归咎于王子对“女人问题”的关注。然而，他真正的关注点似乎在于王子在瑞士逗留后遇到的形形色色的俄罗斯人，以及他能否与他们相处。他显然无法做到。或许普通读者也无法应对这些人，因为他们看起来就像一群醉汉、歇斯底里者、骗子、疯子和躁郁症患者。

∗ The nineteenth-century precursor to feminism.

* 十九世纪女权主义的先驱。

The novel, as I suggested with regard to Flaubert, was one of the immediate sources of psychoanalytic theory, and Dostoevsky, like Dickens (whose work he loved), had a strong interest in mental illnesses—addictions, mood disorders, character disorders, personality disorders. All of the characters of The Idiot show symptoms of these. They do almost everything on impulse—marry, betray, attempt extortion, go into the country, forgive, commit murder, make assignations. Their reactions to these impulses, in themselves and in others, are distorted, and everyone's distorted reactions reinforce the distorted reactions of the others. For example, when an elderly and rather crazy man dies, even those characters who hadn't liked him grieve vociferously, but when a character is murdered, the two characters most involved hardly show any reaction at all. One thing that almost every character does at one point or another is discourse at length in a manner that is totally inappropriate to his or her social situation at the moment, about himself or herself. Histrionic display and disorder are the norms of their lives; giving vent to momentary feelings, their most natural form of expression. In such a society, mere perfect goodness must inevitably fail, simply because the success of passivity, honesty, and generosity depend on at least a degree of self-knowledge and consistency by those who are being benefited, or upon the acceptance of social norms about what is good. Fielding is able to depict Squire All-worthy as perfectly good because Squire Allworthy has a social function that gives his goodness a responsible and powerful outlet. His aims correspond to the creation and maintenance of social order in a cultivated and fertile landscape. The characters of The Idiot are constantly at loggerheads about every aspect of their inner lives and their outer lives, and this conflict is only just veiled by manners. Myshkin is conceived as a character without any power at all—with even less power than those around him. Powerlessness is an essential part of his goodness, so he is doomed.

正如我之前在谈到福楼拜时所指出的，这部小说是精神分析理论的直接来源之一。陀思妥耶夫斯基和狄更斯（他非常喜爱狄更斯的作品）一样，对精神疾病——成瘾、情绪障碍、性格障碍、人格障碍——有着浓厚的兴趣。《白痴》中的所有人物都表现出这些疾病的症状。他们几乎所有行为都出于冲动——结婚、背叛、敲诈勒索、去乡下、宽恕、谋杀、幽会。他们对这些冲动的反应，无论是在自身还是在他人身上，都是扭曲的，而且每个人扭曲的反应都会强化其他人的扭曲反应。例如，当一个年老且精神有些失常的男人去世时，即使是那些不喜欢他的人也悲痛欲绝；但当一个角色被谋杀时，两个最直接相关的角色却几乎没有任何反应。几乎每个角色都会在某个时刻，以一种与自身所处社会环境完全不符的方式，滔滔不绝地谈论自己。戏剧化的表演和混乱是他们生活的常态；他们任由瞬间的情感流露，这是他们最自然的表达方式。在这样的社会里，纯粹的善良注定会失败，因为被动、诚实和慷慨的成功至少依赖于受益者一定程度的自我认知和言行一致，或者依赖于对社会规范中“何为善”的接受。菲尔丁之所以能将奥尔沃西乡绅描绘成完美的善良，是因为奥尔沃西乡绅的社会功能赋予了他的善良以负责任且强有力的表达方式。他的目标与在耕耘肥沃的土地上创造和维护社会秩序相契合。《白痴》中的人物在内心世界和外在生活的方方面面都争执不休，这种冲突仅仅被礼仪所掩盖。梅什金被塑造成一个毫无权力的角色——甚至比他周围的人还要无权。无权是他善良的本质组成部分，因此他注定要走向毁灭。

Would both the female characters be ruined, each in her separate way, if Myshkin had not entered the scene? Dostoevsky seems to me to be saying that they would not, but to me, each of the women is so dedicated to contrary and perverse actions that each would have eventually enlisted someone or other in her self-destructive psychodrama. And yet if Myshkin doesn't precipitate the tragedies, the plot of the novel falls apart and Myshkin himself remains a man without a story. This, in fact, is the source of the failure that Dostoevsky felt in the finished novel. There is no inevitability to it—Myshkin has qualities but no intentions. It is not only that this makes him not tragic, it also makes him not a believable character. While Dostoevsky readily portrays characters who manifest extreme psychological states, he is not very good, at least in this translation, at finding a language that mimics their thought processes, except when they are spouting off to one another. He often has astute things to say about the characters—he can analyze, for example, what effect they have on others, or their motives for acting—but he cannot demonstrate how their trains of thought progress, as Trollope does, or how things seem to them, as Dickens does. Thus he cannot enable the reader to empathize with them. Such a language would be essential to making Myshkin's perfect goodness convincing, on the one hand, and to organizing the novel, on the other.

如果没有梅什金的出现，这两个女性角色是否也会以各自的方式走向毁灭？在我看来，陀思妥耶夫斯基似乎在暗示她们不会，但她们都如此执着于反常和扭曲的行为，以至于最终都会有人卷入她们自我毁灭的心理剧中。然而，如果没有梅什金的介入，小说的情节就会崩溃，梅什金本人也会沦为一个没有故事的人。事实上，这正是陀思妥耶夫斯基在完成这部小说后感到失败的原因。这一切并非必然——梅什金有特质，却没有意图。这不仅使他缺乏悲剧色彩，也使他成为一个不可信的角色。尽管陀思妥耶夫斯基擅长刻画那些展现极端心理状态的人物，但他并不擅长（至少在这个译本中）找到一种能够反映他们思维过程的语言，除非是他们彼此倾诉的时候。他常常对人物有精辟的见解——例如，他能分析人物对他人的影响，或是他们的行为动机——但他无法像特罗洛普那样展现人物的思维过程，也无法像狄更斯那样描绘人物的视角。因此，他无法让读者与人物产生共鸣。这种语言一方面对于使米什金的完美善良令人信服至关重要，另一方面对于构建整部小说也同样重要。

Of Dostoevsky's major works, The Idiot is the only one that takes up the typical English and French subject of marital alliance. There are moments when the novel seems to be moving toward a French or English comedy of manners—the ideas and especially the speeches of some of the characters are full of absurdities that could easily show up in Thackeray, Dickens, or Balzac as idiosyncrasies of the human condition. The marital alliance project itself is plenty absurd in this novel, but the prince is too good to have a sense of humor, and none of the other characters has the detachment required of wit.

在陀思妥耶夫斯基的主要作品中，《白痴》是唯一一部以英法两国常见的婚姻联盟为主题的作品。小说中某些片段似乎朝着法式或英式风俗喜剧的方向发展——某些人物的思想，尤其是他们的言谈，充满了荒诞不经的元素，这些荒诞之处很容易出现在萨克雷、狄更斯或巴尔扎克的作品中，成为对人性特质的刻画。小说中婚姻联盟本身就十分荒谬，但王子过于完美，缺乏幽默感，而其他人物也都缺乏机智所需的超脱。

It is perfectly all right to read Dostoevsky and wish you were reading Trollope. The extremity of the Dostoevskian world is a good reminder that the prolonged exposure to a novelist's sensibility required by a lengthy novel is akin to a long train ride with a stranger, sometimes more demanding and uncongenial than the reader is prepared for. In that sense, every novel is, in the end, a social experience as well as an experience of solitude. Even so, a dip into Dostoevsky's world is stimulating; Dostoevsky's boldness as a thinker and an artist set many of the terms for art, philosophy, and psychology that shaped the twentieth century and that are still influential in the twenty-first.

读陀思妥耶夫斯基，却又渴望读特罗洛普，这完全没问题。陀思妥耶夫斯基笔下世界的极端性提醒我们，阅读长篇小说需要长时间沉浸在小说家的感性之中，这就像与陌生人一起乘坐漫长的火车，有时比读者预想的更加苛刻和令人不适。从这个意义上讲，每一部小说最终都既是社交体验，也是孤独体验。即便如此，浅尝辄止地探索陀思妥耶夫斯基的世界仍然令人振奋；作为思想家和艺术家，陀思妥耶夫斯基的胆识为艺术、哲学和心理学奠定了许多基础，这些基础塑造了二十世纪，并且至今仍然影响着二十一世纪。

40. Louisa May Alcott Little Women

40. 路易莎·梅·奥尔科特《小妇人》

(1868-69; REPR., NEW YORK: SCHOLASTIC, APPLE, 1995), 562 PP.

（1868-69 年；重印，纽约：SCHOLASTIC，APPLE，1995 年），562 页。

Little Women is a hugely famous perennial best seller that is in some ways less interesting than Louisa May Alcott herself, who based the novel on her adolescence in Concord, Massachusetts, as the daughter of Bronson Alcott, a crony of Emerson, Thoreau, and Hawthorne. It was written in two volumes. The first ends with Meg's betrothal. The second begins three years later, with Meg's wedding, and follows the differing ways in which the four daughters and their ambitions are disposed of.

《小妇人》是一部经久不衰的畅销巨著，但在某些方面，它却不如路易莎·梅·奥尔科特本人那样引人入胜。奥尔科特以自己在马萨诸塞州康科德的青少年时期为蓝本创作了这部小说。她的父亲布朗森·奥尔科特是爱默生、梭罗和霍桑的密友。小说分为两卷。第一卷以梅格的订婚告终。第二卷则从三年后的梅格婚礼开始，讲述了四个女儿各自不同的人生道路和抱负。

Alcott wrote the novel for young women at the behest of a publisher she knew. It was instantly successful, and it has an openly didactic purpose—to teach moral lessons about proper values and attitudes. In the first chapter, for example, the sisters give their meager Christmas breakfast to a poor family who has no breakfast at all. As a result, they are given a treat by a wealthy neighbor, Mr. Laurence, at suppertime. Somewhat later in the novel, Amy vengefully burns some of Jo's writings. Jo is unforgiving, in spite of her mother's admonishments, and then suffers terrible remorse when Amy nearly drowns as a result of a skating accident. Adults reading the novel for the first time since childhood may be put off by such obvious lessons, but young readers are so accustomed to taking a dose of moralizing with their stories that to them Alcott's style seems perfectly natural. In fact, most girls, if they like Little Women , tend to prefer the first volume, when all the sisters are living cozily at home together, making do with what they have and relating mostly to one another.

奥尔科特应一位熟识的出版商之邀，为年轻女性创作了这部小说。小说一经出版便大获成功，其目的也十分明确——旨在传授正确的价值观和态度等道德教训。例如，在第一章中，姐妹俩将自己简陋的圣诞早餐分给了一个连早餐都没有的贫困家庭。作为回报，富有的邻居劳伦斯先生在晚餐时款待了她们。小说后半部分，艾米出于报复烧毁了乔的一些作品。尽管母亲百般劝诫，乔依然不肯原谅，后来艾米因滑冰事故险些溺水身亡，乔为此深感懊悔。成年读者如果自童年之后第一次重读这部小说，可能会对如此直白的说教感到反感，但年轻读者早已习惯于在故事中接受道德教诲，因此对他们来说，奥尔科特的这种风格显得自然而然。事实上，大多数女孩如果喜欢《小妇人》，往往会更喜欢第一卷，因为在第一卷中，所有的姐妹都和睦地生活在一起，依靠她们所拥有的东西，并且主要彼此交往。

It is in the second volume, though, that Alcott puts her mind to solving the long-standing question of how girls are to be dealt with, of whether and how money and love are to come together, and what is to be the goal and purpose of women's lives. Her answers are both bolder and more naive than those of some of her more respected contemporaries, such as George Eliot and Henry James. Four girls, four temperaments, four sets of desires mean four plausible outcomes, all linked together by the example of Marmee, whose principal ambition for her daughters is that they “be well and wisely married, and… lead useful, pleasant lives, with as little care and sorrow to try them as God sees fit to send.” She expressly disapproves of seeking high-status marriages, and aims to equip the girls mentally and spiritually for future challenges.

然而，在第二卷中，奥尔科特开始着手解决一个由来已久的问题：如何对待女孩，金钱与爱情是否以及如何结合，以及女性人生的目标和意义究竟是什么。她的答案比她一些更受尊敬的同代作家，如乔治·艾略特和亨利·詹姆斯，既大胆又天真。四个女孩，四种不同的性情，四种不同的欲望，意味着四种可能的结局，而这一切都与马奇太太的例子联系在一起。马奇太太对女儿们最大的期望是她们“嫁得好，婚姻美满，……过上充实而快乐的生活，尽量少受上帝的苦难和磨难”。她明确反对追求高地位的婚姻，并致力于在精神和心灵上为女孩们未来的挑战做好准备。

No activity is proscribed—in fact, from rather early in the novel, Jo earns money by selling sensational stories to tabloid newspapers (as Alcott herself did). The family cautions her, but welcomes the money and lets her find her own way to her real voice and subject. Alcott rather neatly avoids the trap Eliot falls into in her autobiographical novel The Mill on the Floss , of endowing her heroine with many of her own characteristics and dilemmas but none of her options. When Amy marries Laurie, the wealthy boy next door, after he has proposed to and been rejected by Jo, Alcott is careful to bring the two together slowly. In fact, her portrait of Amy, a rather unpleasant little girl in the first volume, is one of the most satisfying aspects of the second volume. Jo manages to find both publication and romance with Professor Bhaer; there could be no Prince Charming less appealing in the eyes of an eleven-year-old reader. To an older reader, he is far more attractive—intelligent, kind, comfortable, and well educated, in every way more suitable for the volatile Jo than Laurie.

书中没有任何活动被禁止——事实上，从小说一开始，乔就通过向小报出售耸人听闻的故事来赚钱（就像奥尔科特本人那样）。家人告诫她，但欢迎这笔钱，并让她自己去寻找真正属于自己的声音和主题。奥尔科特巧妙地避免了艾略特在其自传体小说《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》中犯下的陷阱：赋予女主人公许多她自己的性格特征和困境，却没有赋予她任何选择。当隔壁的富家子弟劳里向乔求婚被拒后，艾米嫁给了他，奥尔科特小心翼翼地让两人慢慢走到一起。事实上，她对艾米的刻画——在第一卷中她是一个相当令人讨厌的小女孩——是第二卷中最令人满意的部分之一。乔最终既获得了发表作品的机会，又与贝尔教授坠入爱河；在一位十一岁的读者眼中，恐怕没有比这更不讨喜的白马王子了。对于年纪稍长的读者来说，他更有魅力——聪明、善良、平易近人、受过良好教育，在各方面都比劳里更适合性情多变的乔。

Little Women may have lost its appeal for young adults simply because Jo and her three sisters aren't recognizable teenagers anymore, so the novel's concerns are no longer current enough to fit into our culture as timely lessons. Freed of its former purpose, though, the novel can take its place among other nineteenth-century novels whose preoccupying subject was the problematic status of women. Because Alcott wants to supply four happy endings, she works through and weighs not only what is to be achieved but also how to get there, while the necessity of having a moral lesson to teach forces her to be explicit about issues that many other novelists discuss but cannot solve. Having posed the question of what an intelligent mother might want for her daughters, she can then systematically demonstrate different ways by which the laudable goal might be achieved. She reminds us in doing so that all novels (not only novels for young people) are stories but also models—they demonstrate how a small thing might be done, such as stealing a valuable jewel, and also how a large thing might be done, such as pursuing a white whale or escaping from slavery.

《小妇人》或许对年轻读者失去了吸引力，原因很简单：乔和她的三个姐妹不再是人们印象中的少女，因此小说的主题不再具有时代意义，无法作为切合时宜的教诲融入我们的文化。然而，摆脱了原有的创作目的后，这部小说可以与其他十九世纪探讨女性地位困境的小说并列。由于奥尔科特想要呈现四个圆满的结局，她不仅思考并权衡了最终的目标，还思考了实现目标的途径。同时，她也必须传递某种道德教训，这迫使她直面许多其他小说家探讨过却无法解决的问题。在提出一位睿智的母亲会希望女儿们拥有怎样的未来之后，她便可以系统地展示实现这一美好目标的各种途径。她这样做提醒我们，所有小说（不仅仅是青少年小说）都是故事，也是榜样——它们展示了如何做一件小事，比如偷一件贵重的珠宝，以及如何做一件大事，比如追逐一头白鲸或逃离奴役。

41. George Eliot Middlemarch

41. 乔治·艾略特《米德尔马契》

(1872; REPR., NEW YORK: NEW AMERICAN LIBRARY, SIGNET, 1992), 811 PP.

（1872 年；重印，纽约：新美国图书馆，SIGNET，1992 年），811 页。

In Middlemarch , George Eliot's conception is so intricate and yet spacious, so detailed and yet broad, that it seems impossible to summarize. The subject is the town—Middlemarch—and its immediate environs in the 1830s , at the time of the Parliamentary Reform Bill in Britain, and yet the subject is several families of that town, the Brookes and their neighbors, who are wealthy gentry, the Garths and their relatives the Vincys, who are prominent tradespeople, and the Farebrothers, who live at the vicarage (Mr. Farebrother holds the living). And then there is Lydgate, the new doctor who comes to town. The subject of Middlemarch is all the relations among all these friends and relatives, young and old, and yet the subject is really how Dorothea Brooke, Mary Garth, Fred and Rosamond Vincy, and Tertius Lydgate pair up and marry. But that is not the real subject either, since every character has far more on his or her mind, and much more to learn, than traditional questions of romance. But we begin with Miss Brooke, who marries Mr. Casaubon, who is far too old for her. Mr. Casaubon calls in Dr. Lydgate, who is falling for Rosamond Vincy in spite of his better judgment. The plot, like all plots, develops from there, but because of the richness of Eliot's conception it seems to develop in all directions, less a story than a network of stories.

在乔治·艾略特的《米德尔马契》中，他的构思既错综复杂又包罗万象，既细致入微又恢弘壮阔，以至于难以概括。故事的背景是19世纪30年代英国议会改革法案颁布之际的米德尔马契小镇及其周边地区，但故事的焦点却集中在镇上的几个家庭：富裕的乡绅布鲁克一家及其邻居，颇具名望的商人加思一家及其亲戚文西一家，以及住在牧师住宅的费尔布拉泽一家（费尔布拉泽先生是现任牧师）。此外，还有新来的医生利德盖特。小说的主题是所有这些亲朋好友之间错综复杂的关系，无论老幼，但其核心却是多萝西娅·布鲁克、玛丽·加思、弗雷德和罗莎蒙德·文西以及特提乌斯·利德盖特的爱情故事。但这并非故事的真正主题，因为每个角色心中都萦绕着远比传统爱情问题复杂得多的想法，也需要学习的东西也更多。故事从布鲁克小姐开始，她嫁给了比她年长许多的卡索邦先生。卡索邦先生请来了利德盖特医生，尽管他明知不该，却还是爱上了罗莎蒙德·文西。情节如同所有情节一样，由此展开，但由于艾略特构思的丰富性，它似乎向各个方向发展，与其说是一个故事，不如说是一个故事网络。

I always think of Middlemarch , which I love and have read many times, as an example of the principle that a novel may not be perfect, may, in fact, be too grand to be perfect. Surely George Eliot (the pen name of Mary Ann Evans) brought as much intelligence, insight, wit, learning, evenhandedness, and native talent to the writing of her greatest novel as any novelist ever. She peopled it with an extraordinary range of characters whose actions and words seem to arise out of wholeness and complexity, even though some of them appear only briefly. Each character seems to live within a fully realized network of relationships that are simultaneously social, economic, personal, and intimate. Every scene is fully realized; the structure of the novel is spacious and satisfying, the pace deliberate but not slow—very much the pace of a rational mind contemplating one thing and then another, but dwelling unduly on none. Most important, perhaps, every sentence is so smart that the reader cannot help but feel little jolts of pleasure, one right after another, on every page. Eliot is often considered to be a Victorian moralist who could have lightened up a bit and lost nothing by it, but in fact her style is higly ironic and often dryly funny. For example, early in the novel, the doctor, Lydgate, follows an actress for whom he has a passion, to her new town. In the midst of shocking revelations about how her husband had come to be killed, Eliot has the woman speak: “‘You have come all the way from Paris to find me?’ she said to him the next day, sitting before him with folded arms and looking at him with eyes that seemed to wonder as an untamed ruminating animal wonders. ‘Are all Englishmen like that?’” Lydgate subsequently swears off romance and considers himself safe from Rosamond Vincy, since she contrasts so strongly with Laure, “the divine cow.” Elsewhere Mr. Brooke, Dorothea's shallow uncle, is suggesting to Casaubon, Dorothea's pedantic husband, that she divert herself with some eighteenth-century novels:

我总是想起我非常喜爱并反复阅读的《米德尔马契》，它完美地诠释了小说未必完美，甚至可能因为过于宏大而无法达到完美。乔治·艾略特（笔名，真名玛丽·安·埃文斯）在创作这部她最伟大的小说时，倾注的智慧、洞察力、机智、学识、公正和天赋，丝毫不逊于任何一位小说家。她塑造了一系列非凡的人物，他们的言行举止都显得完整而复杂，即便有些人物只是短暂出现。每个人物都仿佛生活在一个完整而复杂的关系网络中，这些关系同时涵盖了社会、经济、个人和亲密层面。每一个场景都栩栩如生；小说的结构开阔而引人入胜，节奏沉稳而不拖沓——恰如一个理性的头脑思考一件事又思考另一件事，却又不会在任何一件事上过度停留。或许最重要的是，每一句话都如此精妙，以至于读者在阅读每一页时，都会不由自主地感受到一丝丝的愉悦，这种愉悦感接踵而至。人们常认为艾略特是一位维多利亚时代的道德家，她本可以稍微轻松一些，而这并不会损失什么。但事实上，她的文风极具讽刺意味，且常常带有冷幽默。例如，在小说开篇，医生利德盖特追随一位他深爱的女演员来到她的新城镇。在她丈夫惨死的真相逐渐浮出水面之际，艾略特借她之口说道：“‘你大老远从巴黎来找我？’第二天，她坐在他面前，双臂交叉抱在胸前，用一种仿佛未经驯服的反刍动物般充满好奇的眼神看着他，问道：‘所有英国男人都这样吗？’”此后，利德盖特发誓不再谈恋爱，并认为自己可以远离罗莎蒙德·文西，因为她与“神圣的母牛”劳拉形成了鲜明的对比。在另一处，多萝西娅肤浅的叔叔布鲁克先生建议多萝西娅迂腐的丈夫卡索邦，让她读一些十八世纪的小说来消遣：

‘Smollett—Roderick Random, Humphry Clinker. They are a little broad, but she may read anything now that she's married,
you know. I remember they made me laugh uncommonly— there's a droll bit about a postilion's breeches. We have no such humor now. I have gone through all these things, but they might be rather new to you.’
‘As new as eating thistles,’ would have been an answer to represent Mr. Casaubon's feelings. [p. 280 ]

“斯莫利特——罗德里克·兰登，汉弗莱·克林克。他们的作品有点粗俗，但她现在结婚了，什么都看，你知道的。我记得他们的作品让我开怀大笑——其中有一段关于邮递员马裤的滑稽描写。我们现在可没有这种幽默感了。这些我都看过，但对你来说可能相当新鲜。”“就像吃蓟一样新鲜，”这大概就是卡索邦先生当时的感受。[第280页]

Virginia Woolf famously said that Middlemarch was “one of the only English novels written for grown-up people,” and other critics have declared it the greatest English novel, or even the greatest novel. And it certainly follows the natural inclination of the novel to expand and grow more various. The other candidates for greatest novel ever— Anna Karenina, Our Mutual Friend, Moby-Dick, Don Quixote , even the seven volumes of The Past Recaptured —hardly contain more. And everything that Middlemarch does contain is exquisitely considered and beautifully rendered.

弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫曾说过，《米德尔马契》是“为成年人而写的为数不多的英国小说之一”，其他评论家也称其为最伟大的英国小说，甚至是史上最伟大的小说。它的确符合小说不断发展和丰富多彩的自然规律。其他堪称史上最伟大小说的候选作品——《安娜·卡列尼娜》、《我们共同的朋友》、《白鲸》、《堂吉诃德》，甚至七卷本的《追忆似水年华》——也都难以超越它。《米德尔马契》的每一处细节都经过精心构思，笔触优美。

But a novel is less and less likely to be perfect as it grows because as it fills out and expands, the connections between the exquisitely rendered smaller parts grow more and more attenuated—they grow beyond the capacity of both the writer and the reader to keep track of them and thus remain compelled by them. Some novelists are able, sometimes, to overcome this tendency by using the reader's emotional investment in the characters to bolster suspense. An example of a novel that succeeds in hanging together, though very long, is Anna Karenina. Another is Our Mutual Friend , into which Dickens slips a chase sequence of almost unbearable suspense right at the moment when he might be beginning to exhaust the reader's powers of attention. Middlemarch doesn't have much suspense. The tales of three couples at the core of the novel (Dorothea and Will Ladislaw, Lydgate and Rosamond, Fred Vincy and Mary Garth) are told with such wisdom and measure that it is easy to imagine what will happen. What Eliot is after is analysis of their relationships rather than emotional investment in them. Characters whose fates might be suspenseful—Bulstrode and his wife—are unsympathetic. Suspense is not dependent on the reader's not knowing what is about to happen—a reader can read Pride and Prejudice half a dozen times and still feel a quickening of delight when Elizabeth and Darcy get together. But the pleasures of Middlemarch are more in the intellect and less in the emotions—the narrator stands at a greater distance from her characters, moving into their consciousnesses and then out again, making them the objects of her marvelous phrases rather than the originators of them, looking at how their senses of themselves fit into the sense other people have of them. As a result, it is not only that in the end, the reader feels more edified than gratified by the outcome of the novel, it is also that the dynamic energy of the novel is somewhat dissipated by the requirement of detailed understanding.

但随着小说篇幅的增加，它越来越难以保持完美，因为随着内容的丰富和扩展，那些精心刻画的小部分之间的联系会变得越来越松散——它们的发展超出了作者和读者追踪其脉络的能力，也因此难以继续吸引读者。有些小说家有时能够克服这种倾向，利用读者对人物的情感投入来增强悬念。《安娜·卡列尼娜》就是一部篇幅很长却结构紧凑的小说。另一个例子是《我们共同的朋友》，狄更斯在书中巧妙地插入了一段令人窒息的追逐戏，恰好发生在读者注意力开始分散的时候。《米德尔马契》则缺乏悬念。小说的核心是三对夫妇（多萝西娅和威尔·拉迪斯劳、利德盖特和罗莎蒙德、弗雷德·文西和玛丽·加思）的故事，作者以如此睿智和克制的笔触讲述，以至于读者很容易就能猜到接下来会发生什么。艾略特追求的是分析人物关系，而非让读者投入情感。那些命运本可能充满悬念的角色——比如布尔斯特罗德和他的妻子——却并不讨喜。悬念并非取决于读者对即将发生的事情一无所知——读者可以反复阅读《傲慢与偏见》六遍，每次看到伊丽莎白和达西重逢时，依然会感到欣喜若狂。然而，《米德尔马契》的乐趣更多地在于理性而非情感——叙述者与笔下的人物保持着一定的距离，他们时而进入人物的意识，时而抽离，成为她那些精彩语句的对象，而非语句的创造者，她探究的是人物的自我认知如何与他人对他们的认知相契合。因此，最终，读者不仅从小说的结局中感受到更多的是启迪而非满足，而且小说原本的活力也因对细节理解的要求而有所减弱。

Nevertheless, the three central relationships, which are surrounded by several smaller ones, are uniquely penetrating analyses of marriage unmatched in the work of any other author. The depiction of Lydgate and Rosamond, his limited but resolute wife, could serve as a whole course in the nature of marriage based on presuppositions and appearances (and with no possibility of divorce). Eliot's portrait of Dorothea and her dried-up scholar, Casaubon, is no less insightful, only less generally applicable. These marriages do not seem any more true of their place and time than they seem generally true—there are always well-meaning but ignorant men who marry beautiful but shallow women, always idealistic women who completely misapprehend male psychology. Of special note in this regard is the richness of what Eliot adds to literature about the natures and powers of women. By contrast, the writings of her male contemporaries about women (except possibly Anthony Trollope) seem deluded and sentimental or simply vague.

然而，围绕着这三段核心关系，以及其中几段较小的关系，对婚姻的剖析可谓独树一帜，其他任何作家都无法比拟。她对利德盖特和他那虽性格局限却意志坚定的妻子罗莎蒙德的刻画，足以构成一门完整的课程，探讨基于预设和表象的婚姻本质（而且没有离婚的可能性）。艾略特笔下多萝西娅和她那枯燥乏味的学者丈夫卡索邦的形象同样深刻，只是适用范围略窄。这些婚姻似乎并不比它们所处的时代更贴近现实——世上总有一些心地善良却无知的男人娶了美丽却肤浅的女人，也总有一些理想主义的女人完全误解了男性的心理。尤其值得一提的是，艾略特为文学中关于女性的本质和力量的描写增添了丰富的内涵。相比之下，她同时代男性作家（或许安东尼·特罗洛普除外）笔下的女性形象要么显得自欺欺人、矫揉造作，要么干脆含糊不清。

Middlemarch is also a wonderful social document, because Eliot was much interested in the intellectual and scientific issues of her time and embraced the power of her novel to depict such issues. Her characters have aspirations beyond money and happiness—Lydgate wants to add to the stock of scientific knowledge, Casaubon wants to discover the ancient roots of myth, Dorothea wants to benefit others. Among the three of them, they mark specific moments in the history of ideas. In fact, nineteenth-century philologists and folklorists did succeed in linking modern languages and modern literature with each other and with earlier roots, as Casaubon aspires to do. Philosophers of religion and ethics did take up the question of how an individual is to live a virtuous life, which Dorothea thinks about. Biologists, chemists, and others eventually found the key to the nesting layers of matter and energy that make up the world as we understand it. The specific hypotheses of the Middlemarch characters may be outmoded (and were in Eliot's day—she was writing in 1870 about the 1830s ), but Eliot has a good deal to say about the psychology of intellectual endeavor. She gracefully incorporates into her novel aspects of human life that had never found novelistic expression before she brought to bear her unique combination of gifts—wit, sensitivity to language, intelligence and learning, psychological insight, ambition, reasonableness, and courage, too, since much of what Mary Ann Evans learned, she taught herself.

《米德尔马契》也是一部精彩的社会文献，因为艾略特对她所处时代的思想和科学问题非常感兴趣，并充分利用小说的力量来描绘这些问题。她笔下的人物追求的远不止金钱和幸福——利德盖特渴望丰富科学知识，卡索邦想要探寻神话的古老根源，多萝西娅则希望造福他人。他们三人分别代表了思想史上的特定时刻。事实上，正如卡索邦所渴望的那样，十九世纪的语言学家和民俗学家确实成功地将现代语言和现代文学彼此联系起来，并与更早的根源联系起来。宗教和伦理哲学家也探讨了个人如何才能过上美德的生活，这也是多萝西娅所思考的问题。生物学家、化学家和其他领域的科学家最终找到了构成我们所理解的世界的物质和能量层层嵌套的关键。 《米德尔马契》中人物的具体假设或许已经过时（在艾略特生活的年代也是如此——她于1870年创作，描写的是19世纪30年代），但艾略特对知识探索的心理学却有着深刻的见解。她巧妙地将此前从未在小说中展现过的人类生活层面融入到她的小说创作中，这得益于她独特的才华组合——机智、对语言的敏锐、智慧和学识、心理洞察力、抱负、理性以及勇气，因为玛丽·安·埃文斯所学到的很多东西都是她自学的。

Perhaps Virginia Woolf considered Middlemarch the only English novel written for adults because Eliot keeps her characters working and striving past the denouement of the novel. Lydgate eventually earns money with his medical practice, but only at the cost of all his aspirations. More interestingly, and perhaps echoing Eliot's own life with writer George Lewes in a distant way, Fred Vincy and Mary Garth both write books and both contribute to the family income as tenants upon an estate that Fred had once hoped to inherit. Eliot's romantic ideal is not landed companionate marriage, but common work, equal contribution to the household, and vital intellectual development for both spouses.

或许弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫认为《米德尔马契》是唯一一部专为成年人创作的英国小说，因为艾略特笔下的人物在小说结局之后依然努力奋斗。利德盖特最终靠行医赚到了钱，但这却是以牺牲他所有的理想为代价的。更有趣的是，或许在某种程度上呼应了艾略特与作家乔治·刘易斯的婚姻生活，弗雷德·文西和玛丽·加思都著书立说，并且都作为佃户为家庭收入做出贡献，而这处庄园正是弗雷德曾经希望继承的。艾略特的浪漫理想并非拥有土地的伴侣式婚姻，而是共同劳动、对家庭贡献均等，以及夫妻双方都拥有重要的智力发展。

42. Leo Tolstoy. Anna Karenina

42. 列夫·托尔斯泰，《安娜·卡列尼娜》

TRANS. CONSTANCE GARNETT, REV. LEONARD J. KENT, AND NINA BERBEROVA
TRANS. CONSTANCE GARNETT, REV. LEONARD J. KENT, AND NINA BERBEROVA
(1877; REPR., NEW YORK: MODERN LIBRARY, 2000), 923 PP.
(1877; REPR., NEW YORK: MODERN LIBRARY, 2000), 923 PP.

The premise of Anna Karenina is simple and even basic—a wealthy Moscow family, the Oblonskys, are hoping to marry their younger daughter, Kitty, to a desirable aristocrat, Vronsky, even though another young man, Levin, a rather somber and countrified landowner, is in love with her. When Vronsky accompanies Oblonsky to the train station—Vronsky to pick up his mother, and Oblonsky to pick up his sister, Anna, who is married to an important government official— Vronsky meets the woman who really moves him. He begins to court Anna almost immediately, abandoning his suit of Kitty and his future in respectable Russian society. While Anna's marriage is breaking apart under the weight of this passion, Levin begins to find his purpose, first in the improvement of his estate and the condition of his workers, and later in his renewed and ultimately successful pursuit of Kitty.

《安娜·卡列尼娜》的故事梗概简单明了——莫斯科富裕的奥布隆斯基一家希望将小女儿基蒂嫁给一位英俊的贵族弗龙斯基，然而另一位名叫列文的年轻地主，一位略显阴郁、略带乡土气息的男子，却也深爱着她。一天，弗龙斯基陪同奥布隆斯基去火车站——弗龙斯基去接母亲，奥布隆斯基去接嫁给一位重要政府官员的姐姐安娜——弗龙斯基在那里遇到了真正打动他的女子。他几乎立刻开始追求安娜，放弃了对基蒂的追求以及在体面的俄罗斯社会中的未来。当安娜的婚姻在这段激情的重压下走向破裂时，列文开始找到自己的人生目标，先是致力于改善自己的庄园和工人的生活条件，后来又重新追求基蒂，并最终取得了成功。

The great nineteenth-century novelists all aimed at comprehensiveness. George Eliot's portraits of Casaubon, who is writing a key to all mythologies, and Lydgate, who is trying to find the unifying principle in disparate forms of living tissue in Middlemarch , are portraits of herself, and Dickens and Trollope and Balzac, as much as they are of scholars and scientists. Tolstoy, in Anna Karenina , seems to have felt that he could portray two marriages (the novel was originally called Two Marriages) in sufficient detail that they could stand as models for how marriage works in general, with Anna's marriage and adultery standing for one form (based on property, social status, lust, and a failure to grasp the spiritual life, what you might call the French form) and Levin's marriage to Kitty (based on love, common goals, usefulness, and spiritual redemption, a Russian version of what you might call the English form) standing for the other. There is a third marriage, too—the one that begins the novel, between Kitty's sister, Dolly, and Anna's brother, Stepan, which is based on the principle of getting along as best they can and having lots of children, but no real relationship between the spouses.

十九世纪伟大的小说家们都力求全面。乔治·艾略特笔下的卡索邦（他试图为所有神话找到一把钥匙）和利德盖特（他试图在《米德尔马契》中不同生命组织形态中寻找统一的原则）的形象，与其说是学者和科学家的写照，不如说是她自己、狄更斯、特罗洛普和巴尔扎克的写照。托尔斯泰在《安娜·卡列尼娜》中似乎认为，他可以足够细致地描绘两段婚姻（这部小说最初名为《两段婚姻》），使它们成为婚姻运作方式的典范：安娜的婚姻和婚外情代表了一种模式（基于财产、社会地位、欲望以及对精神生活的缺失，你可以称之为“法式婚姻”），而列文与基蒂的婚姻（基于爱情、共同目标、实用性和精神救赎，你可以称之为“英式婚姻”的俄式版本）则代表另一种模式。小说中还有第三段婚姻——凯蒂的妹妹多莉和安娜的哥哥斯捷潘的婚姻，这段婚姻的原则是尽可能地和睦相处，生很多孩子，但夫妻之间并没有真正的感情。

Tolstoy's method of comprehensiveness is the key to the novel's greatness—a close, realistically rendered attention to sensory details and details of emotional states. Each of his main characters—Karenin, Anna, Vronsky, Levin, and, to a lesser extent, Kitty—has chapters in which the narrator depicts in vivid detail the progress of a certain mood. For example, Anna falls ill with childbed fever when her illegitimate child is born. She writes Karenin, who has resolved to hate her and to ruin her by divorcing her, and asks him to forgive her on her deathbed. Karenin arrives in a state of deep rage and antipathy, but the scene at her bedside brings him to such a state of exalted forgiveness that he can never return again to precisely how he felt before he forgave her. His inner journey must and does progress, in his case to a weird form of fraudulent spiritualism. The reader is made to see Karenin's point of view in every detail and then to understand his transformation and to sympathize with it—the sympathy grows out of the empathy. The same method works with Levin, who is an irritable and irritating character. By the end of the novel, the reader is more or less in sympathy with Levin's ideas because she has experienced the events and emotions that gave rise to them along with Levin. As the novel progresses, it takes more and more mental effort to resist Levin (Tolstoy's stand-in) and disagree with him. It becomes almost overwhelmingly tempting, given Tolstoy's method, to yield to both the experiental details and the ideas and declare, with nineteenth-century critic Matthew Arnold, “We are not to take Anna Karenina as a work of art; we are to take it as a piece of life.” But it is not a piece of life— that it could be a piece of life is an illusion imparted by the passion, intensity, and technique that Tolstoy brings to his story. Tolstoy's method of composition was arduous—he wrote and threw out hundreds of pages—but as a result, he thought through all of his ideas until he had exhausted all of their possibilities, thereby staying one step ahead of the reader at every turn. It is this willingness to work everything out that gives Tolstoy's work its characteristic sense of authority.

托尔斯泰的全面性是这部小说伟大之处的关键——他对感官细节和情感状态的细致刻画，细致入微，写实生动。他笔下的每个主要人物——卡列宁、安娜、伏龙斯基、列文，以及在较小程度上，基蒂——都有专门的章节，叙述者在这些章节中生动地描绘了某种情绪的演变过程。例如，安娜在生下私生子后患上了产褥热。她写信给决心恨她、要通过离婚毁掉她的卡列宁，在临终前请求他的原谅。卡列宁带着深深的愤怒和厌恶赶来，但安娜床边的景象让他达到了一种超然的宽恕境界，以至于他再也无法回到原谅她之前的状态。他的内心之旅必然会继续，而且也确实如此，就他而言，最终走向了一种怪诞的、虚假的唯灵论。读者被引导去了解卡列宁的每一个细节，进而理解他的转变，并对他产生同情——这种同情源于共情。同样的方法也适用于列文，他是一个易怒且令人厌烦的角色。到了小说结尾，读者或多或少地认同了列文的观点，因为她与列文一同经历了那些引发这些观点的事件和情感。随着小说的推进，读者越来越难以抗拒列文（托尔斯泰的化身）的感受，也越来越难以反驳他。鉴于托尔斯泰的写作手法，读者几乎很容易被这些体验性的细节和思想所吸引，并像十九世纪评论家马修·阿诺德那样宣称：“我们不应该把《安娜·卡列尼娜》当作一件艺术品来欣赏；我们应该把它当作一段生活片段来欣赏。”但这并非生活片段——它之所以能被视为生活片段，只是托尔斯泰赋予故事的热情、强度和技巧所造成的错觉。托尔斯泰的创作方法十分艰辛——他写了数百页，又删掉了数百页——但正因如此，他才能将所有想法反复推敲，直至穷尽所有可能性，从而始终领先读者一步。正是这种精益求精的态度，赋予了托尔斯泰的作品一种独特的权威感。

But Tolstoy's desire for comprehensiveness presents him with the essential novelist's paradox and difficulty. Because mental states that are felt and understood in an instant take much longer than an instant to describe, he must pick and choose the ones he wishes to focus upon—that is, he has to make the time pass in some consistent way. The way he chooses inevitably imposes meaning on the text; although his choice is “technical,” it limits the universality of the story and it opens the author to “mistakes.” In the case of Anna Karenina , Tolstoy chooses to show how each relationship develops over the course of several years. Therefore he must pick the most dramatic moments in the plot and show how the characters are changed by them (a novel with a briefer time span or a tighter plot can unfold through both high drama and routine activity, thereby depicting the interplay of the two in creating character). The incidents that Tolstoy does pick are beautifully and truthfully portrayed (not in the sense that Tolstoy is telling the truth, but in the sense that the reader recognizes the action to be true to her experience), but, especially early in the novel, they are grand and therefore distancing.

但托尔斯泰对全面性的追求给他带来了小说家普遍面临的悖论和难题。因为瞬间就能感受到和理解的心理状态，描述起来却远比瞬间要花费更多时间，所以他必须有所选择，挑选出他想要着重描写的那些——也就是说，他必须让时间以某种连贯的方式流逝。他的选择不可避免地会赋予文本意义；尽管他的选择是“技术性的”，但它限制了故事的普适性，也使作者更容易犯错。以《安娜·卡列尼娜》为例，托尔斯泰选择展现每段关系在数年间的发展。因此，他必须选取情节中最具戏剧性的时刻，并展现人物如何因此而改变（一部时间跨度较短或情节紧凑的小说，可以通过高潮迭起的戏剧冲突和日常琐事来展开，从而描绘两者在塑造人物性格中的相互作用）。托尔斯泰所选择的事件被描绘得优美而真实（并非指托尔斯泰在讲述真相，而是指读者能够感受到这些事件与自身经历相符），但尤其是在小说的早期，这些事件显得宏大，因而令人感到疏离。

For me, the central difficulty of Anna Karenina is whether the reader believes in Vronsky and Anna's love or merely accepts it on faith. How they act and what they say demonstrate that something dramatic is going on between them, but the author offers no quiet and apparently routine scenes that show why him, why her (in this, of course, Tolstoy is also hampered by nineteenth-century reticence about intimate matters). In part two, chapters 9 and 10 , Karenin confronts Anna and attempts to get her to admit to and recant her feelings for Vronsky. At this point she and Vronsky have not had sexual relations. Chapter 11 begins with a postcoital confrontation between Anna and Vronsky—she is humiliated and ashamed at giving herself to him, and he is desperate. According to the narrator, it has been almost a year since they first met each other. The author has chosen not to depict the private aspects of their courtship—the moments, for example, that Stendhal depicts in The Red and the Black between Julien and Madame de Rnal, moments that would show the stages by which Anna has been brought to shame and Vronsky to satisfaction of his desires. So dramatic is her reaction to their union, in fact, that the reader has to ask how she let this happen—by what process has she been lulled and persuaded to give up her virtue? When Tolstoy skips over this process, he chooses not to give the reader essential access to Anna's psychology, but to let some sort of typical female psychology stand for her individual female psychology. The author begins to make up for this omission only after Anna's mental state begins to disintegrate. Still, she is less interesting and less true than she could have been if she had been more sharply individuated. This specific flaw is echoed over the course of the entire novel by the fact that while the reader may be observing the characters in some detail, she doesn't often feel especially intimate with them. The primary reason for this choice—the choice of dramatic moments over routine moments or over a mixture of dramatic moments and routine moments—is Tolstoy's technical need to have time pass as efficiently as possible, to show the process of development that constitutes his rhetorical point.

对我而言，《安娜·卡列尼娜》的核心难点在于读者究竟是相信弗龙斯基和安娜之间的爱情，还是仅仅出于信任而接受它。他们的言行举止表明两人之间存在着某种戏剧性的情感纠葛，但作者并没有提供任何平静而看似平常的场景来解释他为何如此，她为何如此（当然，托尔斯泰在这方面也受到十九世纪社会对私密话题讳莫如深的限制）。在第二部分第九章和第十章中，卡列宁质问安娜，试图让她承认并收回对弗龙斯基的感情。此时，她和弗龙斯基尚未发生性关系。第十一章以安娜和弗龙斯基性交后的对峙开篇——她因将自己交付于他而感到羞辱和耻辱，而他则感到绝望。据叙述者所述，他们相识至今已近一年。作者选择不去描绘他们恋爱过程中的私密时刻——例如，司汤达在《红与黑》中描绘的于连和德·罗纳尔夫人之间的那些场景，这些场景本可以展现安娜如何一步步走向羞耻，以及弗龙斯基如何最终满足了自己的欲望。事实上，安娜对他们结合的反应如此强烈，以至于读者不禁要问，她究竟是如何让这一切发生的？她究竟是被怎样的麻痹和说服，最终放弃了贞洁？托尔斯泰跳过了这一过程，他选择不让读者深入了解安娜的内心世界，而是用某种典型的女性心理来代表她独特的女性心理。直到安娜的精神状态开始崩溃，作者才开始弥补这一缺失。然而，即便如此，如果安娜的个性更加鲜明，她或许会更加引人入胜，也更加真实可信。这一缺陷贯穿整部小说，读者虽然能细致地观察人物，却往往难以与他们建立起亲密感。之所以选择戏剧性的情节而非日常琐事，或是两者兼而有之，托尔斯泰的根本原因在于他需要尽可能高效地推进时间流逝，以展现构成其修辞论点的事件发展过程。

There is no satisfactory solution to the requirement that time in the novel must pass in some way. If it passes in a routine, intimate way, the reader may wonder why she is bothering to read such a dull novel, and if it passes in a consistently dramatic way, the reader may wonder what relevance this has to her own rather routine life. (Some feminists might say, also, that Tolstoy did not imagine a female audience for his novel; for example, Kitty, Tolstoy's primary virtuous woman, feels terrific unease, which her husband supports, in having anything to do with Anna. It's hard to imagine that Tolstoy considered the depiction of Anna's sin and disintegration an appropriate subject for Kitty-like young girls reading in their bedrooms.)

对于小说中时间必须以某种方式流逝这一要求，并没有令人满意的解决方案。如果时间以一种日常的、私密的方式流逝，读者可能会疑惑自己为何要费心阅读这样一部乏味的小说；如果时间以一种持续戏剧化的方式流逝，读者可能会质疑这与自己平淡的生活有何关联。（一些女权主义者或许还会指出，托尔斯泰并没有为他的小说设想女性读者；例如，托尔斯泰笔下最贤良淑德的女性角色基蒂，在与安娜有任何瓜葛时都感到极度不安，而她的丈夫也支持这种不安。很难想象托尔斯泰会认为描写安娜的罪恶和堕落是适合像基蒂一样在卧室里阅读的年轻女孩的主题。）

Many novelists solve the time difficulty with a vivid and idiosyncratic literary style, which serves as an incentive to the reader to keep reading in spite of the dullness or the irrelevance of the events, and also makes the events seem more or less subjective, which has the effect of begging the question of how the time passes. But realistic novelists such as Tolstoy have also chosen not to do that—they don't want to suffer the fate of Dickens or the Brontës, the fate of having their ideas dismissed as too out of the mainstream to be accepted as universally true.

许多小说家用生动而独特的文学风格来解决时间流逝的难题，这种风格能激励读者即便面对枯燥乏味或无关紧要的情节也继续读下去，同时也使事件显得或多或少带有主观色彩，从而引发人们对时间如何流逝的思考。但像托尔斯泰这样的现实主义小说家却选择了不这样做——他们不想重蹈狄更斯或勃朗特姐妹的覆辙，不想让自己的思想因为过于离经叛道而被视为不被普遍接受的真理。

The realist novel does offer the reader the illusion of a certain sort of freedom, though. The style, felicitous but not intrusive, seems to ask the reader to make up her own mind as to the themes and intentions of the work as a whole, seems to allow her to divorce herself from the narrator's direction and look at the scenes as if they were real. On that score we can wonder if Tolstoy himself realized that one of the persistent themes of his novel is how females in general and women in particular pay for the pleasures of men, or if such observations came together in the work without his conscious intention. Vronsky's English mare is killed when Vronsky wants to ride her in a race himself and makes a mistake. Anna, of course, never recovers from Vronsky's successful seduction of her. Stepan sells off pieces of his wife's estate to pay for his pleasures. Levin is assailed by self-doubt when he sees Kitty in the pain of childbirth.
