Even so small a detail as the sex of Levin's hunting dog, Laska, implies foolish male appetite contrasted with submissive but knowing female effort. Tolstoy doesn't offer a solution for this unfairness, but it is so evident that the reader herself may begin contemplating political solutions.

现实主义小说确实能给读者带来某种自由的幻觉。其文风流畅而不突兀，似乎在引导读者自行判断作品的整体主题和意图，仿佛允许读者摆脱叙述者的引导，以身临其境的视角审视书中的场景。由此，我们不禁要问：托尔斯泰本人是否意识到，小说中反复出现的主题之一是女性（尤其是女人）如何为取悦男人付出代价？或者，这些观察是否并非出于他的本意，而是自然而然地融入了作品之中？弗龙斯基的英国母马因他想亲自骑乘参赛而失足丧命。安娜当然也从此无法从弗龙斯基的诱惑中恢复过来。斯捷潘变卖妻子的部分遗产来满足自己的享乐。列文目睹基蒂分娩的痛苦，陷入了深深的自我怀疑之中。即使是列文的猎犬拉斯卡的性别这样微小的细节，也暗示了男性愚蠢的欲望与女性顺从却又充满智慧的努力之间的对比。托尔斯泰并没有为这种不公提供解决方案，但它如此显而易见，以至于读者自己也可能开始思考政治上的解决之道。

Is Anna Karenina the greatest novel by the greatest novelist? Let us compare apples and grapefruits and peas and dogs, not to mention oranges and dreams. Anna Karenina has nothing in common with Tristram Shandy , so how can they be on a scale together? Indeed, Anna Karenina has nothing in common with Taras Bulba. I might feel, as I do, that Taras Bulba offers a unique stylistic experience—words brought together in a manner unmatched before or since, simultaneously original and right, operating instantly—let's call that “revelation.” Anna Karenina works upon me rhetorically, convincing me with insight after insight to share or at least accept the author's contentions. Let's call that “wisdom.” But the pleasures of each are not comparable with the other. Tolstoy had read Gogol and knew his work quite well. He had even learned from Gogol, but still he could not possibly be like Gogol because the novel itself promotes difference rather than similarity. For that reason the quest for “the greatest” is particularly futile with novels and novelists.

安娜·卡列尼娜是这位最伟大的小说家最伟大的小说吗？让我们把苹果、葡萄柚、豌豆、狗，甚至橘子和梦想放在一起比较。安娜·卡列尼娜与《项狄传》毫无共同之处，它们又怎能相提并论呢？事实上，安娜·卡列尼娜与《塔拉斯·布尔巴》也截然不同。我或许会觉得，《塔拉斯·布尔巴》提供了一种独特的文体体验——文字的组合方式前无古人，后无来者，既原创又恰当，瞬间就能产生效果——我们不妨称之为“启示”。安娜·卡列尼娜则以修辞手法打动我，用一个个洞见说服我认同，或者至少接受作者的观点。我们不妨称之为“智慧”。但两者带来的愉悦感却无法相提并论。托尔斯泰读过果戈理，对他的作品非常了解。他甚至从果戈理那里汲取了灵感，但他仍然不可能成为果戈理，因为小说本身强调的是差异而非相似。因此，对于小说和小说家而言，追求“最伟大”尤其徒劳。

43. Henry James. The Portrait of a Lady

43. 亨利·詹姆斯，《一位女士的画像》

(1881; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1986), 641 PP.

（1881 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1986 年），641 页。

Although The Portrait of a Lady was James's fifth novel, it was the first in which he developed all of his talents as well as all of his interests. He was thirty-seven when he began it, and he had high hopes. James had met and dined with George Eliot, and he admired her version of the realistic novel; Isabel Archer directly inherits the earlier dilemmas of Maggie Tulliver and Dorothea Brooke. But even though James was writing only a few years after Eliot wrote Middlemarch , he was a generation younger than she, and the novel has a much more modern feel. Still, what is to be done with the young woman? James disposes of the traditional English answer within the first hundred pages. Isabel appears on the scene, an attractive and moneyed aristocrat presents himself and proposes to her, and she instinctively turns him down, to the amazement of everyone around her. Then an old suitor appears, an American named Caspar Goodwood, and she very explicitly turns him down, also, though he is more importunate than the English lord. The problem of what to do with the young woman is not to be solved in the traditional way. James gives her money of her own, and the rest of the novel asks a new question: what is a young woman to do with herself?

尽管《贵妇画像》是詹姆斯的第五部小说，却是他第一部充分展现其才华和兴趣的作品。他开始创作这部小说时三十七岁，并寄予厚望。詹姆斯曾与乔治·艾略特会面并共进晚餐，他非常欣赏她对现实主义小说的诠释；伊莎贝尔·阿切尔直接继承了玛吉·图利弗和多萝西娅·布鲁克早期小说中的困境。尽管詹姆斯写作的时间仅比艾略特创作《米德尔马契》晚几年，但他比艾略特年轻一代，因此这部小说更具现代感。然而，这位年轻女子该如何处置呢？詹姆斯在开篇一百页就摒弃了传统的英国式答案。伊莎贝尔出现，一位英俊富有的贵族向她求婚，而她本能地拒绝了他，令周围所有人都感到惊讶。这时，一位名叫卡斯帕·古德伍德的美国人出现了，他曾是她的追求者。尽管古德伍德比那位英国勋爵更加纠缠不休，但她还是断然拒绝了他。如何处置这位年轻女子的问题，无法用传统的方式解决。詹姆斯给了她自己的钱，而小说的其余部分则提出了一个新的问题：年轻女子该如何安排自己的生活？

European society, and the Old World in general, do not have an answer. The course Isabel chooses, to marry Gilbert Osmond, an expatriate aesthete, is famously wrong. All of the characters in the novel and the author himself hint that Gilbert is meant to be diabolical. The couple have a child who dies, and by the time of that death there is such a breach between husband and wife that the option of motherhood has been foreclosed for Isabel. Several other models are supplied—Mrs. Touchett, who, though married, lives as if she were single; Madame Merle, who is entirely charming but without her own establishment and who whiles away her life congenially living off others; Countess Gemini, who is trapped in a loveless marriage of a coarser sort than the Osmonds; and Henrietta Stackpole, an employed journalist, distinctly new and American, a little attractive and a little silly. But after a brief separation, Isabel returns to her marriage, almost for lack of anything better to do. In 1881 James could not answer the old question except by supplying Isabel with the conviction that she has to adhere to the old form, empty as it has become.

欧洲社会，乃至整个旧世界，都对此束手无策。伊莎贝尔选择嫁给流亡海外的唯美主义者吉尔伯特·奥斯蒙德，这无疑是个错误的决定。小说中的所有人物，包括作者本人，都暗示吉尔伯特是个邪恶之人。这对夫妇育有一子，却不幸夭折。孩子去世时，夫妻二人已形同陌路，伊莎贝尔再也无法为人母。小说还塑造了其他几个典型人物：图切特夫人，她虽已婚，却过着如同单身女性般的生活；梅尔夫人，她魅力四射，却一无所有，终日靠他人养活度日；杰米尼伯爵夫人，她深陷一段比奥斯蒙德夫妇更为粗俗、毫无爱情可言的婚姻；还有亨丽埃塔·斯塔克波尔，一位职业记者，她身上散发着浓浓的美国气息，既有些许魅力，又有些许愚钝。然而，短暂的分居之后，伊莎贝尔几乎是出于无所事事的缘故，最终还是回到了婚姻之中。 1881 年，詹姆斯无法回答这个古老的问题，只能让伊莎贝尔相信她必须坚持旧的形式，尽管这种形式已经变得空洞无物。

The Portrait of a Lady , paragraph by paragraph, page by page, is exceptionally satisfying. James writes in a highly metaphorical style that continuously invites the reader to impute refined and yet dramatic meanings to the actions and feelings of his characters. If Dickens's characters move in a landscape of inner visions projected outward as monsters and innocents, James's characters live in an apparently real world, but only by analogy. James is always pausing to brilliantly characterize, not their feelings, but the feel of their situation. For example, discussing the character Edward Rosier, a childhood acquaintance of Isabel's, James writes, “His father was dead and his bonne was dismissed, but the young man still conformed to the spirit of their teaching—he never went to the edge of the lake.” This is typically Jamesian in tone and is very much extremely elevated and advanced gossip. His great analogies and intelligent analyses are attempts to characterize small psychological states and shifts rather than endeavors to depict the world (which for James is made up of estates and ruins and buildings as backdrops). James builds on the Victorian novelists by developing a theory of human psychology that deepens and complicates their insights, but much of what he says about his characters is not and cannot be known to themselves—they do not have the larger perspective that he, the master analyst, has. His purpose is to find commonalities in human nature and the inner life that his characters represent, and his tool for doing this is his style.

《贵妇画像》一章一章、一页一页地读来，令人无比满足。詹姆斯运用高度隐喻的写作风格，不断引导读者去赋予笔下人物的言行举止以精妙而又戏剧化的意义。如果说狄更斯笔下的人物生活在一个由内心世界投射而成的怪诞与纯真交织的世界中，那么詹姆斯笔下的人物则生活在一个看似真实的世界里，但这仅仅是通过类比实现的。詹姆斯总是巧妙地刻画人物，并非他们的感受，而是他们所处境遇的氛围。例如，在描写伊莎贝尔儿时的熟人爱德华·罗西尔时，詹姆斯写道：“他的父亲去世了，他的教父也被解雇了，但这个年轻人仍然恪守着他们的教诲——他从不去湖边。” 这段文字极具詹姆斯式的风格，堪称高雅而又高深的闲聊。他精妙的比喻和深刻的分析旨在刻画细微的心理状态和转变，而非描绘世界（在詹姆斯看来，世界不过是由庄园、废墟和建筑等背景构成）。詹姆斯在维多利亚时代小说家的基础上发展出一套人类心理学理论，深化并丰富了他们的洞见。然而，他对笔下人物的诸多描述，他们自身却无法知晓——他们并不具备他这位分析大师所拥有的宏大视角。他的目的是探寻人性的共通之处，以及他笔下人物所代表的内心世界，而他实现这一目标的工具便是他独特的写作风格。

The Portrait of a Lady , as a whole, therefore, can be irritating, especially, perhaps, to a female reader, because there is no satisfaction in Isabel's fate; though the question is asked, the answer is wanting, and the author seems not to know this. He seems to think that by supplying Isabel and her fellows with vast amounts of detailed motivation he can give their actions a tragic dimension, but in fact their paralysis seems self-imposed and very youthful, as if they simply aren't experienced enough to think of an alternative. The greatest insight of the novel occurs near the end, when it is suggested to Isabel that she will get over what has happened to her and become young again, but James doesn't linger over the idea—no doubt because to do so is to diminish the drama of the previous six hundred pages.

因此，《一位女士的画像》整体而言可能会令人恼火，尤其对女性读者而言，因为伊莎贝尔的命运令人难以释怀；尽管提出了这个问题，却没有得到解答，而作者似乎对此浑然不觉。他似乎认为，通过为伊莎贝尔及其同伴提供大量细致的动机描写，就能赋予他们的行为以悲剧色彩，但事实上，他们的麻木不仁似乎是自我设限，而且显得非常幼稚，仿佛他们只是缺乏足够的阅历去思考其他出路。小说中最深刻的洞察出现在临近结尾处，有人建议伊莎贝尔她会走出困境，重返青春，但詹姆斯并没有过多着墨于此——无疑是因为这样做会削弱前六百页所营造的戏剧张力。

For me, Isabel's dilemma is not in her character but in her world. She has three suitors plus a cousin who loves her without hope. All four are seriously flawed marital prospects—Lord Warburton is attractive and well-meaning, but like Darcy in his first proposal (in Pride and Prejudice) , he doesn't bother to court her, only to present himself.

对我而言，伊莎贝尔的困境不在于她的性格，而在于她所处的环境。她有三个追求者，外加一个爱她却毫无希望的表兄。这四个人都是有严重缺陷的结婚对象——沃伯顿勋爵英俊潇洒，心地善良，但就像达西在《傲慢与偏见》中的第一次求婚一样，他根本懒得追求她，只是为了露面而来。

Caspar Goodwood, Isabel's last hope at the end of the novel, is so aggressive as to strike the modern reader as akin to a stalker or a rapist, and in fact he does force a kiss on Isabel that she responds to, but then she does the most sensible thing, which is to flee—Goodwood's love expresses itself no less hatefully than Osmond's hate. Osmond is sly, weak, and insidious, but finally less dangerous than Goodwood. Cousin Ralph is well-meaning but fatally ill. There are no matches; the marriage market offers no attractive prospects. And then, as if to reiterate his point, James introduces Pansy, Osmond's daughter, who has been raised, unlike Isabel, to be perfectly submissive. She cannot be satisfied in the marriage market either, because Rosier, whom she loves, is too weak to claim her, and Warburton finally doesn't want her. She ends up immured in a convent, being further trained to submit, as if Osmond's will to efface her simply cannot be satisfied. Only Henrietta comes up with a companion, and her ability to do so comes from her willingness to live unconventionally with her friend Mr. Bantling, until she knows him well enough to marry him. Hers is an unorthodox and singular solution not generally applicable in James's world (though pretty workable from the perspective of the twenty-first century).

小说结尾，伊莎贝尔最后的希望——卡斯帕·古德伍德——咄咄逼人，在现代读者看来，他简直像个跟踪狂或强奸犯。事实上，他确实强吻了伊莎贝尔，而她也回应了。但之后，她做出了最明智的选择——逃离。古德伍德的爱与奥斯蒙德的恨一样令人憎恶。奥斯蒙德狡猾、软弱、阴险，但最终比古德伍德更不危险。表兄拉尔夫心地善良，却身患绝症。没有合适的人选；婚姻市场没有吸引人的前景。詹姆斯仿佛为了再次强调这一点，引入了奥斯蒙德的女儿潘西。与伊莎贝尔不同，潘西从小就被培养成绝对顺从的人。她在婚姻市场上也无法获得满足，因为她深爱的罗西尔软弱无能，无法拥有她，而沃伯顿最终也对她不感兴趣。她最终被囚禁在修道院，接受进一步的顺从训练，仿佛奥斯蒙德抹去她的意志永远无法得到满足。只有亨丽埃塔找到了伴侣，而她之所以能做到这一点，是因为她愿意与朋友班特林先生过着非同寻常的生活，直到她对他足够了解，可以嫁给他。她的这种解决办法非同寻常，在詹姆斯的世界中并不普遍适用（尽管从二十一世纪的角度来看，这相当可行）。

What motivates Isabel is not, in the end, as interesting as what motivates Gilbert Osmond to hate her once she has become his wife. James makes it clear that her independence of mind combined with her independent means arouse his resentment, but given his attitude toward Madame Merle, whom he also hates in spite of their long intimacy, what really seems to be the case is that he has an abiding resentment of women that he attempts to assuage by insisting upon their submission. There is the sense at the end of the novel that he is immuring Pansy because he is coming to hate her, too. Isabel's provisional tragedy is that she has wedded herself to his misogynism, but the relationships between the women are still in flux at the close of the novel. Osmond is a paper tiger—his power derives from the concessions of his sister, wife, and daughter. The potential for alliance among them remains at the end, when Isabel returns to Rome rather than save herself.

最终，伊莎贝尔的动机远不如吉尔伯特·奥斯蒙德在她成为妻子后对她产生憎恨的动机那样引人入胜。詹姆斯明确指出，伊莎贝尔的独立思想和经济独立激起了他的怨恨，但考虑到他对梅尔夫人的态度——尽管两人关系亲密，他仍然憎恨她——真正的原因似乎是他对女性根深蒂固的怨恨，他试图通过要求她们顺从来缓解这种怨恨。小说结尾处，我们能感受到他囚禁潘西是因为他开始憎恨她。伊莎贝尔暂时的悲剧在于她把自己嫁给了他的厌女症，但小说结尾时，这些女性之间的关系仍然处于变化之中。奥斯蒙德不过是纸老虎——他的权力来源于他的妹妹、妻子和女儿的妥协。当伊莎贝尔最终选择返回罗马而不是自救时，她们之间结盟的可能性依然存在。

It is tempting for the modern reader to make up her mind that changes in divorce laws have solved Isabel's problem. She has made a false marriage—the thing that preoccupied European authors from Boccaccio to Charlotte Brontë. Fifty or a hundred years later, she would have divorced and started over. Tragedy would have been transformed into error, and Isabel's life would not have been wasted.

现代读者很容易认定，离婚法的改变已经解决了伊莎贝尔的问题。她缔结了一段虚假的婚姻——这正是从薄伽丘到夏洛蒂·勃朗特等欧洲作家们一直关注的主题。五十年或一百年后，她或许会离婚，重新开始。悲剧或许会转化为错误，伊莎贝尔的一生也不会白白浪费。

Isabel's dilemma traces straight back to The Heptameron —is it allowed for women to live freely? In the 1550s , the answer was no—women without protectors were in danger of rape and murder. In the 1880s the answer was still no, but in spite of Caspar Goodwood, the strictures are more self-imposed than they had been.

伊莎贝尔的困境可以追溯到《七日谈》——女性是否可以自由生活？在16世纪50年代，答案是否定的——没有保护者的女性面临着被强奸和谋杀的危险。到了19世纪80年代，答案依然是否定的，但尽管有卡斯帕·古德伍德的推动，这些限制更多地是出于女性自身的意愿。

James was a sly and comic novelist. He pretended to treat his characters and their fates seriously and in great detail, but in fact every character, including Isabel and Osmond, verges on the absurd because the author is so interested in observing them that he detaches himself from them. They are all amusing—that is implicit in the gossipy style, though some, such as the countess and Henrietta, are more openly amusing than others. He can wring from the reader a sense of disquiet as the characters realize and lament their fates, but in the end they are limited by the very thing James offers in such abundance—the knowledge he has of them that is vaster than the knowledge they have of themselves. James liked to be known as “the Master,” as Dickens liked to be known as “the Inimitable,” but the epithet contains James's limitation as well as his genius—he couldn't cede a larger unexpected humanity to his creations and thereby touch his readers’ deepest feelings.

詹姆斯是一位狡黠而又滑稽的小说家。他假装认真细致地刻画笔下的人物及其命运，但实际上，包括伊莎贝尔和奥斯蒙德在内的每一个人物都近乎荒诞，因为作者过于沉迷于观察他们，以至于与他们产生了疏离感。他们都很有趣——这隐含在那种八卦式的写作风格中，尽管有些人物，比如伯爵夫人和亨丽埃塔，比其他人更直白地展现了他们的滑稽。当人物意识到并哀叹自己的命运时，他能让读者感到不安，但最终，他们却被詹姆斯笔下如此丰富的素材所限制——他对人物的了解远胜于他们对自己了解的程度。詹姆斯喜欢被称为“大师”，就像狄更斯喜欢被称为“无与伦比”一样，但这个称号既体现了詹姆斯的才华，也体现了他的局限——他无法赋予笔下的人物更广阔、更出人意料的人性，从而触动读者内心深处的情感。

Henry James. The Awkward Age

亨利·詹姆斯，《尴尬的时代》

(1899; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD WORLD'S CLASSICS, 1999), 321 PP.

（1899 年；重印，纽约：牛津世界经典出版社，1999 年），321 页。

In addition to writing many novels, Henry James wrote plays that were not, on the whole, popular or successful. When he finally gave up the drama and turned his attention back to the novel, he wrote a succession of mature, complex, and profoundly “Jamesian” novels in which his style was exactly as he wished it—particular, calculated, and highly modulated (as he got older, he stopped writing and dictated his work; Ford Madox Ford once remarked that if the reader were to read late James aloud, with much expression, the prose would make a lot more sense). His first novel after giving up the drama was The Awkward Age , which concerns marital arrangements of a group of upper-class Londoners at the end of the nineteenth century. The thematic premise is the contrast between two eighteen-year-old girls who are just becoming marriageable. One, Aggie, has been raised in a sequestered Italian fashion by her aunt; the other, Nanda, has been allowed more freedom by her mother and father (in part because the parents, who have aristocratic obligations but no money, want to farm their older children out at least some of the time so they can save money on their upkeep while possibly finding them wealthy mates). If there was ever a novel about marriage as a system of covert but acknowledged dealmaking, this is it.

除了创作大量小说外，亨利·詹姆斯还创作了一些戏剧，但总体而言并不受欢迎或成功。当他最终放弃戏剧创作，重新专注于小说创作时，他创作了一系列成熟、复杂且极具“詹姆斯式”风格的小说，其风格完全符合他的预期——独特、精雕细琢且变化多端（随着年龄的增长，他停止了手写，改为口述；福特·马多克斯·福特曾评论说，如果读者朗读詹姆斯晚期的作品，并赋予其丰富的情感，那么这些散文会更容易理解）。他放弃戏剧创作后的第一部小说是《尴尬的年纪》，讲述了十九世纪末一群伦敦上流社会人士的婚姻安排。小说的主题是两个即将出嫁的十八岁女孩之间的对比。其中一个女孩艾吉由她的姑妈以意大利式的隐居方式抚养长大；另一个女儿南达则得到了父母更多的自由（部分原因是这对父母身负贵族义务却囊中羞涩，他们想把年长的孩子至少暂时寄养在外，这样既能节省抚养费，又能为他们找到富有的伴侣）。如果说有哪部小说将婚姻描绘成一种隐秘却公开的交易，那非这部莫属。

As mentioned above, The Awkward Age was an experiment for James, who attempted to use some of the techniques he used in his plays. He communicates all the narrative information through scenes in which two or more of the characters are gathered together for a social occasion, and all the action of the novel is reported through the conversation of the characters, conversation that is complex, allusive, sometimes witty or playful, and always discreet. Part of the pleasure (or difficulty) of the novel, for the reader, is inferring what is going on through what amounts to eavesdropping. James uses several dramatic devices to maintain order. The characters are clearly distinguished from one another and identified, most of them in contrasting pairs. Nanda and Aggie are contrasted through their innocence (or navet); Aggie's aunt, the duchess, and Nanda's mother, Mrs. Brookenham, through their opinions and social positions. Of the two primary young men, Vanderbank is handsome, charming, and poor, while Mitchett is ugly, charming, and rich. The character who precipitates the action is Mr. Longdon, an old admirer of Nanda's grandmother who suddenly reappears from deepest Suffolk, after, it appears, pining for forty years. Mr. Longdon has also been the unsuccessful suitor of Vander-bank's mother.

正如前文所述，《尴尬的年纪》是詹姆斯的一次实验，他试图运用一些他在戏剧创作中使用的技巧。他通过两个或多个角色因社交场合而聚集的场景来传达所有叙事信息，小说中的所有情节都通过角色间的对话来展现——这些对话复杂、含蓄，有时诙谐或俏皮，但始终保持着谨慎。对读者而言，阅读这部小说的乐趣（或难点）之一，就在于通过这种近乎偷听的方式推断出正在发生的事情。詹姆斯运用了多种戏剧手法来维持叙事秩序。小说中的人物特征鲜明，彼此区分清晰，而且大多数人物都是成对出现的对比角色。南达和艾吉的对比在于她们的天真无邪（或称天真烂漫）；艾吉的姑妈，公爵夫人，以及南达的母亲，布鲁肯汉姆夫人，则对比在于她们的观点和社会地位。两位主要的年轻男子中，范德班克英俊迷人，家境贫寒；而米切特相貌丑陋，却魅力十足，家境富裕。引发这场事件的人物是朗顿先生，他是南达祖母的老相好，在苦苦思念了四十年后，突然从萨福克郡的偏远地区出现。朗顿先生也曾追求过范德班克的母亲，但未能成功。

The characters consider their own London society generally dangerous, because it is full of sexual intrigue among the married. The reader can easily see that it is also dangerous because the inequitable distribution of money, social power, and approval makes everyone sneaky and manipulative. One sign of the general danger of this social group (and by extension, the rest of London society) is that they are careful to praise and show affection to one another at all times, rather like denizens of Hollywood or the members of a large group of chimps who perform submissive behaviors so as not to alienate one another. The unwary reader might think they actually like one another, but their relations are based much more upon intrigue and having nice places to congregate than a sense of real connection. Nanda, whose “contamination” by her mother's free and easy ways comes up for a lot of discussion, is a natural innocent, so it is no surprise that she and Mr. Longdon, another innocent, end up together, even though Nanda is very much in love with Vanderbank, who likes her, but can't bring himself to propose, in spite of the fact that Longdon (without Nanda's knowledge) has promised to settle a large property on her. Vanderbank himself is having a serious flirtation with Nanda's mother (though several of the characters testify that the two haven't actually become lovers by the time the question of proposing to Nanda comes up).

书中人物认为他们所处的伦敦社交圈总体上很危险，因为已婚人士之间充斥着性丑闻。读者很容易看出，这种危险的另一个原因是金钱、社会权力和认可分配的不均，使得每个人都变得阴险狡诈、善于操纵。这个社交群体（以及由此延伸出的整个伦敦社交圈）普遍存在的危险的一个迹象是，他们时刻小心翼翼地互相赞美、表达爱意，就像好莱坞明星或一群为了避免彼此疏远而表现得顺从的黑猩猩一样。不加警惕的读者可能会误以为他们彼此之间真的喜欢对方，但他们的关系更多地建立在阴谋诡计和拥有舒适的聚会场所之上，而非真正的情感联结。南达天真无邪，她的母亲放荡不羁的生活方式“玷污”了她，这一点经常被人们讨论。因此，她和同样天真的朗顿先生最终走到一起也就不足为奇了。尽管南达深爱着范德班克，而范德班克也喜欢她，却始终无法开口求婚，即便朗顿先生（在南达不知情的情况下）已经承诺要给她一大笔遗产。范德班克本人正与南达的母亲暧昧不清（尽管有好几个角色作证说，在范德班克向南达求婚这件事被提上日程时，两人实际上还没有发展成恋人关系）。

James was proud of the way he structured the novel—entirely through dramatic scenes using for each the point of view of a different character. These points of view work as vantage points from which to both convey and interpret the progress of the plot. James was pleased with the subtlety of using arrangement and inference as substitutes for a strong narrative voice. He willingly gave up one of narrative's best devices, which is access to the inner life, no doubt to emphasize human nature as a social construct. Nonetheless, having given that up, he forces his conversations to carry a great deal of weight and ends up forbidding the reader the sense of intimacy that many readers look for in a novel first and foremost—it is hard to feel genuine intimacy with characters on whom you seem to be eavesdropping. The convention of the stage—that a play is going on and people are watching—turns into a kind of voyeurism in The Awkward Age. And it is hard to relax with this novel, or to feel oneself carried forward, because it is so easy to lose the thread of the narrative. Nevertheless, suspense does build as the reader grows more familiar with the characters.

詹姆斯对小说的结构方式引以为豪——完全通过戏剧化的场景，每个场景都以不同角色的视角展开。这些视角如同有利位置，既传达又诠释了情节的发展。詹姆斯对运用安排和推断来代替强有力的叙述声音的巧妙手法感到满意。他心甘情愿地放弃了叙事中最有效的技巧之一——展现人物的内心世界，无疑是为了强调人性作为一种社会建构的本质。然而，正是因为放弃了这一点，他才使得对话承载了过多的分量，最终剥夺了读者在小说中最渴望的那种亲密感——你很难与那些你似乎在偷听的角色产生真正的亲密感。舞台剧的惯例——戏剧正在上演，人们正在观看——在《尴尬的年龄》中变成了一种窥视。而且，很难在阅读这部小说时感到放松，或者被它牵着鼻子走，因为叙事线索太容易丢失了。然而，随着读者对角色越来越熟悉，悬念也会随之增强。

James's style always poses a problem that Ford Madox Ford's suggestion somewhat alleviates. James is as highly metaphorical a writer as Dickens, and rather like him in some respects. Both use metaphor not as ornamentation but as the primary method of communicating mental states, and both are interested in the interplay of fictional characters as a group of subjectivities communicating with one another and at the same time contrasting to one another. But whereas Dick-ens's metaphorical language is fully expressed and easy to understand, James's is partially submerged. The reader is repeatedly asked to infer the larger metaphor from a few words. Early in the novel, for example, Longdon is described: “He had at all events, conclusively, doubled the Cape of the years—he would never again see fifty-five: to the warning light of that bleak headland he presented a back sufficiently conscious. Yet, though, to Vanderbank, he could not look young, he came near— strikingly and amusingly—looking new…” (p. 20 ). The overt metaphorical language of the sentence is separated by modifiers and adverbs that imply the consciousness of the perceiver almost as tone of voice would—the perceiver (Vanderbank, but really James) wants to go beyond the precision of nouns and verbs into a quality of intensification or deintensification that can be supplied only through other parts of grammar or the rhythm of the sentences. If you take a paragraph of James and strip it of all adverbs, nothing is lost but the fussi-ness; and yet the fussiness is James's consciousness at work, which is why his style is unique.

詹姆斯的写作风格总是带来一个问题，而福特·马多克斯·福特的建议在一定程度上缓解了这个问题。詹姆斯和狄更斯一样，都是极富隐喻的作家，在某些方面甚至与狄更斯颇为相似。他们都运用隐喻，并非为了修饰，而是将其作为传达心理状态的主要手段；他们都关注虚构人物之间的互动，将他们视为一群相互交流又彼此对比的主观个体。然而，狄更斯的隐喻语言表达得淋漓尽致，易于理解，而詹姆斯的隐喻则被部分地隐藏起来。读者需要反复从寥寥数语中推断出更深层次的隐喻。例如，在小说的开头，对朗顿的描写是这样的：“无论如何，他已经彻底翻了一倍的岁月——他再也活不到五十五岁了：面对那荒凉海岬的警示灯，他展现出一个足够清醒的背影。然而，尽管在范德班克看来，他已不再年轻，但他却——令人惊讶地——显得焕然一新……”（第20页）。句子中显露的隐喻语言被修饰语和副词分隔开来，这些修饰语和副词暗示着感知者的意识，几乎就像语气一样——感知者（范德班克，但实际上是詹姆斯）想要超越名词和动词的精确性，达到一种强化或弱化的境界，而这种境界只能通过语法的其他部分或句子的节奏来实现。如果你从詹姆斯的一段文字中去掉所有副词，除了繁复的修辞之外，什么也不会失去；然而，这种繁复正是詹姆斯意识的体现，也正是他风格独特的原因。

James was an insightful observer of English society—Harold, Nanda's brother, is given the task of speaking unpleasant truths. A profligate young man always borrowing five-pound notes from anyone he can, he understands the marital bazaar and is willing to talk about it. About two-thirds of the way through the novel he says, “London, upon my honor, is quite too awful for girls, and any big house in the country is as much worse—with the promiscuities and opportunities and all that—as you know for yourselves. I know some places… where, if I had any girls, I'd see ‘em shot before I'd take ‘em.” He goes on to discuss the interest of Mr. Longdon in Nanda: “Oh yes, dear man, but what do you give us for her…. I'll be hanged … if he shall have her for nothing!” Nanda agrees to marry Mr. Longdon (who has perhaps successfully, in his own mind, scared Vanderbank off by offering to pay him to take her). The Awkward Age is officially, then, comic. But once again, the outcome is a little disconcerting. After all, Longdon is more than forty years older than Nanda, and though kindly and innocent, not much of a man that the reader can tell. But then neither is Vanderbank, who is indecisive, or Mitchett, who is unattractive (and whom Nanda doesn't like). James does some characteristic special pleading to match up the couples morally, but their relations seem reserved and too much manipulated. The pattern of their relationship is formal, almost ritualistic, like a minuet—they come into contiguity with one another, they act with some kindness and tenderness, but there is no sense of passion springing from the inner life of one character into the consciousness of another and galvanizing the two of them. James was a great parser of social connections, but the energy comes from the parsing rather than the connections.

詹姆斯对英国社会有着敏锐的洞察力——小说中，南达的哥哥哈罗德被赋予了揭露真相的任务。哈罗德是个挥霍无度的年轻人，总是四处借钱，他深谙婚姻市场，也乐于谈论其中的种种内幕。小说大约三分之二处，他说道：“我以我的名誉发誓，伦敦对女孩子来说实在太糟糕了，乡下的任何大宅子都一样糟糕——到处都是淫乱、机会等等——你们自己也知道。我知道一些地方……如果我有女孩子，我宁愿看到她们被枪毙，也不会娶她们。” 他接着谈到朗顿先生对南达的兴趣：“哦，是的，亲爱的先生，但是你打算给我们什么……如果他白白得到她，我宁愿被绞死！” 南达最终同意嫁给朗顿先生（朗顿先生或许自认为成功地吓跑了范德班克，因为他提出要付钱让他娶南达）。所以，《尴尬的年纪》这部作品的喜剧性质可以断定。但结局却再次令人有些不安。毕竟，朗顿比南达年长四十多岁，虽然他善良天真，但读者却看不出他是个多么有男子气概的人。而优柔寡断的范德班克，以及相貌平平（南达也不喜欢他）的米切特，也同样如此。詹姆斯运用了他惯有的特殊辩解，试图在道德上将这两对情侣拉近关系，但他们的关系显得拘谨而刻意。他们的关系模式程式化，近乎仪式化，如同小步舞曲——他们彼此靠近，彼此表现得友善温柔，但却感受不到激情从一方内心深处涌现，传递到另一方意识，并最终将两人紧紧联系在一起。詹姆斯擅长剖析人际关系，但这部作品的魅力却来自于对人际关系的剖析，而非人际关系本身。

44. Oscar Wilde. The Picture of Dorian Gray

44. 奥斯卡·王尔德，《道林·格雷的画像》。

(1891; REPR., NEW YORK: OXFORD UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1998), 184 PP.

（1891 年；重印，纽约：牛津大学出版社，1998 年），184 页。

The Picture of Dorian Gray was reviled as scandalous and wicked when it was published, which seems to have pleased its author. From the distance of more than a hundred years, though, it is possible to see that the outline of the plot is hardly scandalous—a young man makes a thoughtless pact with the Devil and suffers for it almost unremittingly until he finally kills himself. Perhaps the only new twist that Wilde brings to this ancient idea is that both the young man and the Devil exist entirely in the world. There is no implication that Lord Henry (Lord Harry, a common nickname for Satan) retains Dorian's soul into eternity or that there is an eternity.

《道林·格雷的画像》出版之初被斥为伤风败俗、邪恶至极，这似乎令作者颇为得意。然而，时隔百余载，我们或许会发现，其情节梗概其实并无伤风败俗之处——一个年轻人轻率地与魔鬼订立契约，并因此遭受近乎无情的折磨，直至最终自杀。或许王尔德对这一古老主题的唯一创新之处在于，小说中的年轻人和魔鬼都完全存在于现实世界之中。小说并未暗示亨利勋爵（哈里勋爵，撒旦的常用别称）将道林的灵魂囚禁于永恒，也并未暗示永恒的存在。

What may have been more scandalous was Wilde's scathing critique of English hypocrisy combined with his overt depiction of homosexual and bisexual affections carried out within the social structures of marriage and conventional property alliances. The standard resolution of English plots is shown thereby to be impossible because no true affection exists and the real purpose of money is to purchase ever more exotic sensual pleasures.

更令人震惊的或许是王尔德对英国虚伪的辛辣讽刺，以及他对同性恋和双性恋情感在婚姻和传统财产联盟等社会结构下的直白描写。由此可见，英国传统故事的结局是行不通的，因为真爱并不存在，金钱的真正目的在于购买越来越奇特的感官享乐。

The reader may or may not care for Wilde's epigrammatic style. Many of his paradoxes seem both arresting and true—“Nowadays people know the price of everything and the value of nothing,” for example—but epigram piled upon epigram seems more like a thoughtless habit or a form of neurosis than art. What is more appealing is Wilde's catalog of sensual pleasures. Dorian, who has plenty of money and has prayed for eternal youth and the appearance of innocence so he might experience as wide an array of pleasures as possible, goes far beyond mere sexual passion. He collects perfumes and jewels and embroideries and enjoys them as much as romantic affairs. He collects all sharp sensations—including the experience of having someone die for love of him, the experience of murder, and the experience of escape from being murdered. He takes opium and lures others to addiction. What he can't do—and his inability is the source of his torment—is to detach himself from his feelings and become a spectator of his own torments and those of others. In this, his highest aspiration, he can but intermittently emulate his mentor, Lord Henry.

读者或许会喜欢王尔德的警句风格，或许不会。他的许多悖论看似既引人注目又切中要害——例如“如今人们知道一切事物的价格，却不知道任何事物的价值”——但警句堆砌在一起，与其说是艺术，不如说更像是一种不假思索的习惯或某种神经症。王尔德对感官享乐的描绘则更具吸引力。道林拥有巨额财富，他祈求永葆青春，保持纯真无邪的外表，以便体验尽可能多的享乐，但他所追求的远不止于性欲。他收集香水、珠宝和刺绣，并像享受浪漫情事一样享受它们。他收集所有强烈的感官体验——包括有人为他而死、谋杀以及死里逃生。他吸食鸦片，并引诱他人染上毒瘾。他做不到的——而这正是他痛苦的根源——就是让自己脱离情感，成为自己和他人痛苦的旁观者。在这方面，他最大的愿望，他只能偶尔效仿他的导师亨利勋爵。

Lord Henry, the Satan figure, cannot remain young, as Dorian seems to, but has perfected his artistic distance. All developments in the social life around him arouse his interest, but none arouses his sympathy. He is no less cold toward Dorian, his protg, than he is toward his wife or his other associates. He is entirely solitary and untroubled by his condition. Epigrams about hypocrisy are his greatest pleasure. Since Lord Henry shares his author's verbal style, he was widely considered to be speaking for Wilde, which was part of the scandal. But as with de Sade, the fictional creation is colder and more inhuman than the creator was. Like de Sade, Wilde could, and in fact was required to, inhabit the victim, Dorian, as fully as he inhabited the torturer. There is a third character, Basil Hallward, an artist, the man who discovers Dorian and paints the magic portrait. Through him, the novel reflects on some aspects of art. Both Basil and Lord Henry understand that Dorian and Basil have transgressed a boundary through the making of the painting—Basil has been more than ordinarily inspired and has in turn inspired Dorian with love of himself as an object (in some sense, Basil has allowed Dorian to fetishize his own beauty), but Basil remains secure in the knowledge of what is art and what is life. He, too, represents Wilde, of course. When Dorian reveals to Basil that the portrait has magical powers, the artist urges the younger man to pray for salvation. Dorian, inspired indirectly by Lord Henry, has lost his sense of the difference between art and life and promptly tries out the sensation of murder. But he is ambivalent. It is only Lord Henry who can sustain the artist's technically inspired remoteness from life, always appreciating and critiquing but never feeling.

亨利勋爵，这个撒旦般的人物，不像道林那样似乎永远年轻，但他却将自己的艺术距离发挥到了极致。他周围的社交生活的一切发展都引起了他的兴趣，却无法激起他的同情。他对自己的门徒道林的冷漠，丝毫不亚于他对妻子或其他同僚的冷漠。他完全孤僻，对自己的处境毫不在意。讽刺虚伪的警句是他最大的乐趣。由于亨利勋爵的语言风格与作者如出一辙，人们普遍认为他是在代表王尔德发声，这本身就是丑闻的一部分。但正如萨德一样，虚构的人物比创造者本人更加冷酷无情。和萨德一样，王尔德能够，而且实际上也必须，像他扮演施虐者一样，完全地扮演受害者道林。小说中还有第三个人物，巴兹尔·霍尔沃德，一位艺术家，正是他发现了道林，并为他画下了那幅神奇的肖像。通过他，小说反思了艺术的某些方面。巴兹尔和亨利勋爵都明白，多里安和巴兹尔通过创作这幅画越过了某种界限——巴兹尔的灵感远超常人，反过来又激发了多里安对自身美貌的迷恋（某种程度上，巴兹尔允许多里安将自己的美貌奉为偶像），但巴兹尔始终坚守着艺术与生活的界限。当然，他也代表着王尔德。当多里安向巴兹尔透露这幅肖像画拥有魔力时，这位艺术家劝告年轻人祈求救赎。多里安间接受到亨利勋爵的影响，失去了对艺术与生活的区分，并立即尝试了杀戮的快感。但他内心充满矛盾。只有亨利勋爵才能维持艺术家那种技法精湛却又与生活疏离的状态，他总是欣赏和评论，却从未真正感受过生活。

The Picture of Dorian Gray was written almost exactly a hundred years after the far more brutal and cruel Justine and there are some similarities, especially in the argument that morality is “against nature,” or that moralists are essentially exercising caution rather than manifesting a real allegiance to goodness. And the narrator of Justine inveighs against religion, while the narrator of Dorian Gray mostly ignores it. Perhaps the outrage that greeted the later novel was more than anything an index of how much less jaded Victorian sensibilities were than those of the ancien rgime in France. Justine still can shock; Dorian Gray does not. In some ways the later novel seems more dated than the earlier one—a testament to psychological theories then current that Wilde was using to motivate the plot and the characters. For example, the premise of Dorian's ability to escape the results of his iniquities is that he looks youthful and unmarked in spite of them. Conventional wisdom in our day is that illness, poor nutrition, and sun damage change one's looks more than sin does.

《道林·格雷的画像》的创作时间几乎正好是《朱斯蒂娜》之后一百年，而《朱斯蒂娜》的残酷和暴力程度远超前者。两部作品之间存在一些相似之处，尤其是在道德“违背自然”的论点上，或者说道德家本质上是在谨慎行事，而非真正忠于善。此外，《朱斯蒂娜》的叙述者抨击宗教，而《道林·格雷的画像》的叙述者则大多忽略了宗教。或许，后一部小说引发的轩然大波，与其说是原因，不如说是维多利亚时代人们的审美趣味远比法国旧制度时期人们更加开放和包容的体现。《朱斯蒂娜》至今仍能令人震惊，《道林·格雷的画像》却不再如此。在某些方面，后一部小说似乎比前一部更具时代感——这证明了王尔德当时运用心理学理论来推动情节发展和塑造人物。例如，道林能够逃脱罪恶的惩罚，其前提是他尽管犯下罪行，却依然保持年轻容颜，毫发无损。如今人们普遍认为，疾病、营养不良和日晒损伤比罪恶更能改变人的容貌。

What remains after more than a hundred years is not the novel of ideas that Wilde once wrote, but a novel of sensuous surfaces that still beguile and give the pleasure that Wilde so clearly found ambiguous.

一百多年过去了，留存下来的不再是王尔德曾经写的思想小说，而是一部充满感官刺激的小说，它依然能给人带来愉悦，而王尔德显然认为这种愉悦是模棱两可的。

45. Bram Stoker Dracula

45. 布拉姆·斯托克《德古拉》

(1897; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, MODERN LIBRARY, 2001), 365 PP.

（1897 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，现代文库，2001 年），365 页。

The idea for Dracula came to Bram Stoker in a dream. The novel was a great sensation at the time of its publication and, like Frankenstein (also the fruit of a dream), quickly became part of popular culture. Because it was one of the first novels to be sold to the movies, and the movie was an even greater success than the novel, it is probably impossible for a twenty-first-century reader to come to the material fresh and capable of being horrified by the count. It is easy, instead, to feel knowing and Freudian about what must have really been going on in the minds of the characters and the mind of the author (all about repressed sexual feelings) as well as jaded about what constitutes true horror.

布拉姆·斯托克在梦中获得了创作《德古拉》的灵感。这部小说出版后引起了巨大轰动，并像《弗兰肯斯坦》（同样源于梦境）一样，迅速成为流行文化的一部分。由于它是最早被改编成电影的小说之一，而且电影的成功甚至超过了小说本身，因此，对于21世纪的读者来说，恐怕很难再像以前那样对德古拉伯爵感到新鲜和恐惧。相反，读者很容易对书中人物和作者的内心世界（一切都与压抑的性欲有关）产生一种既了解又带有弗洛伊德式解读的认知，同时也对何为真正的恐怖感到麻木。

Stoker's novel remains in print as a horror classic, though, because he plotted the rise and fall of Count Dracula with great care. He then adopted the strategy of multiple narrators, as Wilkie Collins had done with much success thirty years previously, making good use of the variety of effect such a strategy offers. And such a strategy enhances the suspense, because what each character, including the count himself, has at stake comes into play as the plot progresses.

斯托克的这部小说至今仍被奉为恐怖经典，因为他精心构思了德古拉伯爵的兴衰。他借鉴了威尔基·柯林斯三十年前的成功经验，采用了多视角叙述的策略，并充分利用了这种策略带来的丰富效果。随着情节的推进，每个角色（包括伯爵本人）的命运都逐渐明朗，这种策略也增强了悬念。

The novel begins when an English solicitor goes to Transylvania, in the Carpathian Mountains, to transact a bit of business, and finds himself trapped in a mysterious castle with a courtly but sinister aristocratic host, Count Dracula. Count Dracula, it turns out, is much feared by his own people as the principal representative of the undead, a soulless folk who achieve a form of immortality by drinking the blood of others. The count's country has become rather depopulated (possibly as a result of his depredations), and he is planning to move to the much more busy and accessible city of London. His existence is entirely circumscribed by rituals and rules, but when the count has surprise and ignorance on his side, he can find victims and drink their blood.

小说开篇，一位英国律师前往喀尔巴阡山脉的特兰西瓦尼亚处理一些事务，却意外被困在一座神秘的城堡中，城堡的主人是一位举止优雅却阴险狡诈的贵族——德古拉伯爵。原来，德古拉伯爵是亡灵的代表，这些没有灵魂的生物通过吸食他人的鲜血来获得某种形式的永生，因此令他的人民闻风丧胆。伯爵的领地人口锐减（或许是他肆意掠夺的结果），他正计划迁往更加繁华便利的伦敦城。他的生活完全被繁文缛节和规矩所束缚，但只要有人对他不知情，他就能找到猎物，吸食他们的鲜血。

The characters in Dracula are drawn from the same categories as James's and Wharton's characters—two marriageable young women, an American fellow, an English lord, and a young lawyer, plus a sinister European and a benign European. And Dracula in part asks the same questions as James and Wharton do: What is the role of the women? Can they be agents of their own salvation or destruction? What constitutes virtue, and what are the social implications of the definition? Especially interesting is the new notion Stoker brings to the idea of feminine purity. Dracula has two women characters, Lucy and Mina. Both are engaged to be married, but Lucy is restless and likes to walk in her sleep. One night, Mina follows her, and she finds her friend sitting on a bench by the sea, her head thrown back and two tiny wounds in her neck. The reader knows by this time that the count has claimed her as his source of sustenance. Lucy is eventually transformed into one of the undead. To save her soul, one of her friends must cut off her head and drive a stake through her heart, grisly work that is eased by the knowledge that she is damned otherwise (and not all that different from the fate of an unvirtuous woman in earlier centuries—it may not have been her fault, but she's tainted and must be destroyed).

《德古拉》中的人物与詹姆斯和沃顿笔下的人物属于同一类型——两位待嫁的年轻女子、一位美国小伙、一位英国贵族、一位年轻律师，外加一位阴险的欧洲人和一位和蔼的欧洲人。《德古拉》在某种程度上也提出了与詹姆斯和沃顿相同的问题：女性的角色是什么？她们能否成为自身救赎或毁灭的推动者？何为美德？其定义又蕴含着怎样的社会意义？斯托克对女性纯洁这一概念的全新诠释尤其引人注目。《德古拉》中有两位女性角色，露西和米娜。她们都已订婚，但露西生性不安，喜欢梦游。一天晚上，米娜跟踪她，发现她的朋友坐在海边的长椅上，头向后仰着，脖子上有两个细小的伤口。此时读者已经知道，伯爵已经将她当作自己的生命之源。露西最终变成了不死生物。为了拯救她的灵魂，她的一个朋友必须砍下她的头颅，并将木桩钉入她的心脏。这是一项极其残忍的工作，但想到否则她将遭受永世诅咒，也就减轻了这种痛苦（这与几个世纪前不贞女人的命运并没有太大区别——这可能不是她的错，但她已被玷污，必须被毁灭）。

Mina marries her fianc and helps the men look for the count, but through the unwitting agency of an inhabitant of the house where she is staying, Mina, too, falls victim to the count in a scene that can only be interpreted as sexual—he holds her by the neck and forces her to drink blood spurting from a vein he has opened in his chest. The author is clear that Mina, like Lucy, has been polluted, and her virtue has been stained. But she insists upon coming to her own aid, going with the men to Castle Dracula, guiding them by means of hypnotic visions of the count. She transcribes notes, keeps a journal, and helps to plan the attack upon the vampire. In fact, it is when the men treat Mina in the Victorian style, keeping things from her and trying to protect her for her own good, that she is most vulnerable and falls victim to her destroyer. Mina is one of the first female characters in Western literature who redeems herself. In a tradition that holds women suspect even if they are raped, Mina thoroughly “cleanses” her honor by acting against her defiler.

米娜嫁给了未婚夫，并帮助男人们寻找德古拉伯爵。然而，由于她所寄宿的一位住户无意间的帮助，米娜也落入了伯爵的魔爪。在一个只能被解读为性侵的场景中，伯爵掐住她的脖子，强迫她喝下从他胸口血管里喷涌而出的鲜血。作者明确指出，米娜和露西一样，都受到了玷污，她的贞洁被玷污了。但她坚持要自救，与男人们一同前往德古拉城堡，通过催眠般的幻象引导他们找到伯爵。她记录笔记，写日记，并协助策划对付吸血鬼的行动。事实上，当男人们以维多利亚时代的方式对待米娜，对她有所隐瞒，并试图为了她好而保护她时，她反而最脆弱，最终落入了毁灭者的魔掌。米娜是西方文学中最早实现自我救赎的女性角色之一。在即使被强奸也会受到怀疑的传统观念中，米娜通过反抗强奸者来彻底“洗清”自己的名誉。

Stoker gains this enlightened vision as a side benefit of thinking through his plot. We can think of his novel as requiring two things above all—putting something precious and vulnerable in jeopardy, and bringing the love and the money together in the end. Clearly, a woman had to be the victim, but a woman, the same woman, had to be redeemed. The count had to have some sort of uncanny power over his victim (and hypnosis and mind reading were popular ideas at the end of the nineteenth century). The clever part was making the mind-reading a two-way street—giving Mina her power over the count. Another of Mina's powers grows out of the multinarrator format for the novel. It is Mina, from time to time, who types and collates all the parts, thus affording herself an overview of the whole adventure. The structural and mechanical requirements of the novel pave the way for a new mode of looking at the characters.

斯托克在构思情节的过程中，意外地获得了这种富有洞见的视角。我们可以认为，他的小说最需要两点：一是将珍贵而脆弱的事物置于危险之中；二是最终将爱情与金钱结合起来。显然，受害者必须是一位女性，但最终也必须是一位女性，同一个女性，得到救赎。伯爵必须对他的受害者拥有某种不可思议的力量（在十九世纪末，催眠和读心术都是很流行的概念）。巧妙之处在于，他让读心术成为一种双向的力量——赋予米娜对伯爵的控制权。米娜的另一种能力源于小说的多叙述视角。正是米娜时不时地将所有部分整理归档，从而让她对整个故事有一个整体的把握。小说的结构和叙事机制为我们提供了一种全新的视角来审视这些角色。

Stoker did not have a string of solid, respectable successes, like some of his contemporaries. He was a smart popular novelist rather than a great literary novelist, and some of his horror material seems laughable today, but Dracula is well worth both reading and emulating, if only as a lesson in the thoroughness and seriousness Bram Stoker brought to his potentially silly material.

斯托克不像他的一些同时代作家那样，拥有一系列扎实而受人尊敬的成功作品。他是一位精明的通俗小说家，而非伟大的文学小说家，他的一些恐怖题材作品在今天看来或许有些滑稽可笑，但《德古拉》仍然非常值得一读，也值得效仿，即便仅仅是为了学习布拉姆·斯托克如何以严谨认真的态度对待那些看似荒诞的题材。

46. Kate Chopin. The Awakening

46. 凯特·肖邦。《觉醒》

(1899; REPR., NEW YORK: AVON BOOKS, 1972), 190 PP.

（1899 年；重印，纽约：AVON BOOKS，1972 年），190 页。

Possibly Kate Chopin read Henry James. Probably Henry James did not read Kate Chopin, though The Awakening was considered so scandalous when it was published that it was banned in the author's hometown library, and she herself was barred from the Fine Arts Club in the same city, so maybe he did. If he had, he might have enjoyed her boldness and been scandalized by her choice not to judge her protagonist, Edna Pontellier. What The Awakening has to offer, among other things, is honesty. To the eternal question of how women are to be disposed of as both objects and agents, Chopin offers an antecedent question: why is there a problem? And she also asks: what if society cannot provide the answer?

凯特·肖邦或许读过亨利·詹姆斯的作品。亨利·詹姆斯可能并没有读过凯特·肖邦的作品，尽管《觉醒》出版时被认为惊世骇俗，以至于在作者家乡的图书馆被禁，她本人也被同一城市的艺术俱乐部拒之门外，所以他或许读过。如果他读过，他或许会欣赏她的大胆，并对她选择不评判笔下主人公埃德娜·庞特利尔的做法感到震惊。《觉醒》的精髓之一在于坦诚。对于女性作为客体和主体应如何被对待这一永恒的问题，肖邦提出了一个先验问题：为什么会有这个问题？她还追问：如果社会无法提供答案，那又该怎么办？

As the novel opens, Edna, age twenty-eight, and her husband and two children are ensconced for the summer at a lake retreat north of New Orleans, where they are a prosperous, socially prominent family. Edna is just beginning to realize that she is different from the other women around her—not so consumed by husband and family, more susceptible to outside influences. As the summer progresses, Edna finds herself periodically ravished by sensual experiences—she learns to swim, she responds with a kind of swoon to an evening performance of piano pieces by Frdric Chopin (no relation). Eventually she falls in love with the son of the woman who runs the guesthouse and finds evidence that her affections are returned. When the family moves back to New Orleans for the winter, Edna must resume her bourgeois life, which includes much entertaining and formal visiting. Edna refuses, and begins to wander about the city, discovering places and ways of life she had never before been aware of. She takes instruction in painting and begins to sell her pictures through a dealer. Her actions only feed her dissatisfaction. She decides to utterly change the terms of her existence by moving out of the large mansion she shares with her family into a smaller house nearby.

小说开篇，28岁的埃德娜和丈夫以及两个孩子在位于新奥尔良北部的一处湖畔度假胜地度过暑假。他们家境殷实，在当地社会也颇有名望。埃德娜开始意识到自己与周围的女性不同——她不像她们那样被丈夫和家庭所束缚，更容易受到外界的影响。随着夏日的流逝，埃德娜时不时地沉浸在感官的愉悦之中——她学会了游泳，在欣赏弗雷德里克·肖邦（与她并无亲属关系）的钢琴曲时，她如痴如醉。最终，她爱上了旅馆老板娘的儿子，并且发现他也同样爱着自己。冬天，一家人搬回新奥尔良，埃德娜不得不重新回到她原本的资产阶级生活，这意味着要参加许多社交活动和正式的拜访。埃德娜拒绝了这一切，开始在城市里四处游荡，探索她从未了解过的地方和生活方式。她学习绘画，并通过画商出售自己的作品。她的行为只会加剧她的不满。她决定彻底改变自己的生活，搬出与家人共同居住的大宅，住进附近的一栋小房子里。

Toward the end of the novel, Edna suffers a couple of disappointments that lead her to realize that even the terms of her new life cannot be borne. Her newly awakened sensuality must have a worthy object, but it does not—there is to be no outlet for her passions. In addition, she can't, in the end, betray the honor of her children. Instinctively making a kind of death-before-dishonor decision, she swims out into the ocean and drowns, but not with a sense of fear, more with a sense of discovery and liberation.

小说临近结尾，艾德娜遭遇了一系列挫折，最终意识到即使是新生活的条件也令她难以忍受。她新生的感官欲望需要一个合适的对象，但却没有——她的激情无处释放。此外，她最终也无法背叛孩子的荣誉。出于本能，她做出了一个宁死不屈的决定，游向大海，溺水而亡。但她并非出于恐惧，而更多的是出于一种发现和解脱的感受。

It is very interesting to read The Awakening along with James, Wharton, and the other novelists of the turn of the twentieth century, because they all had the same thing on their minds, but James and Wharton weren't straightforward about the sexuality implicit in their protagonists’ dilemmas. Chopin, on the other hand, makes wonderful use of her exotic setting, evoking the heat, beauty, and physicality of not only her southern Louisiana landscape, but also of the Creole society she lives in, where men and women are much more open about all matters of sexuality and reproduction, even though virtue and the appearance of virtue are as important to them as to those in James's and Wharton's milieu. Chopin is no less definite than the others about the effects of such an awakening, though Edna does not die in defeat, as Lily Bart (Edith Wharton, The House of Mirth) seems to. Rather Edna recognizes that once she has awakened, it is better to sacrifice her life than to sacrifice her new sense of herself. When she swims out, her suicide is far from despairing, and quite unlike Lily's overdose of sleeping pills in a dingy room in New York City.

将《觉醒》与詹姆斯、沃顿以及其他二十世纪初的小说家们的作品放在一起阅读非常有趣，因为他们都关注着同一个主题，但詹姆斯和沃顿并没有直白地表达主人公困境中隐含的性欲。而肖邦则巧妙地运用了异域风情，不仅描绘了路易斯安那州南部的炎热、美丽和肉体之美，也生动地刻画了她所生活的克里奥尔社会。在那个社会里，男女对性和生育问题更加开放，尽管美德和美德的外在形象对他们来说与詹姆斯和沃顿笔下的人物一样重要。肖邦对这种觉醒的影响的描写与其他作家一样明确，尽管埃德娜并没有像莉莉·巴特（伊迪丝·沃顿，《欢乐之家》）那样死于失败。埃德娜意识到，一旦她觉醒，牺牲生命总比牺牲她新生的自我认知要好。当她游向远方时，她的自杀远非绝望，也与莉莉在纽约一间昏暗的房间里服用过量安眠药自杀截然不同。

The Awakening was Chopin's only novel—she died about five years after its publication—but it is well worth reading, not as much for the plot (though I think she makes a pretty good argument for Edna) as for the depiction of the gradual change of Edna's way of seeing the world and for the sympathy she shows her. Flaubert may have stated “Madame Bovary, c'est moi,” but his empathy was not quite sympathy. Not so Kate Chopin. Edna is a woman throughout The Awakening , and her quest for a sense of authenticity is never demeaned.

《觉醒》是肖邦唯一的小说——她在小说出版约五年后去世——但它非常值得一读，其亮点不在于情节（尽管我认为她为埃德娜辩护得相当有力），而在于对埃德娜世界观逐渐转变的刻画，以及她对埃德娜的同情。福楼拜或许说过“包法利夫人，就是我”，但他的同情并不完全等同于真正的同情。凯特·肖邦则不然。《觉醒》始终将埃德娜视为一个真正的女人，她对真实自我的追求从未被贬低。

# ↩

47. Sir Arthur Conan Doyle The Hound of the Baskervilles

47. 阿瑟·柯南·道尔爵士《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》

(1901; REPR., NEW YORK: NEW AMERICAN LIBRARY, SIGNET, 2001), 240 PP.

（1901 年；重印，纽约：新美国图书馆，SIGNET，2001 年），240 页。

∗ I learn from Michael Chabon's piece in The New York Review of Books that Conan Doyle and Oscar Wilde were once invited to lunch by the editor of Lippincott's Magazine , and asked to write long stories for the publication. The resulting works were The Sign of Four and The Picture of Dorian Gray. (Michael Chabon, “Inventing Sherlock Holmes,” The New York Review of Books , vol. 52 , no. 2 , Feb. 10 , 2005 .)

我从迈克尔·查邦发表在《纽约书评》上的文章中了解到，柯南·道尔和奥斯卡·王尔德曾受邀与《利平科特杂志》的编辑共进午餐，并被邀请为该杂志撰写长篇故事。最终的作品分别是《四签名》和《道林·格雷的画像》。（迈克尔·查邦，《福尔摩斯的诞生》，《纽约书评》，第52卷，第2期，2005年2月10日。）

Compared with Bram Stoker and the thriller writers who have come after him, Conan Doyle seems unusually, even boringly, squeamish. While purporting to delve into evil and danger, he keeps away from anything distasteful. Dickens was more graphic and horrible in parts of his sunniest works than Conan Doyle ever is. If The Hound of the Baskervilles is meant to impart a shudder, then the British reading public was more susceptible to shuddering at the turn of the twentieth century than they had ever been before. Many eighteenth- and nineteenth-century novels are more gruesome and uncanny than this one. But even so, we have to reckon with Sherlock Holmes, and in him, Conan Doyle created a unique figure who has served modern culture as an intriguing and reassuring model of civilized man. Holmes is a man of his time, but with a difference—what appeared in contemporary characters as anomie and isolation appear in Holmes as savoir faire. What appeared in others as coldness and suspect scientific rationality appear in Holmes as coolness and practical intelligence. What appeared in others as sensuality appears in Holmes as taste (in music and art). And what appeared in others as misogynism appears in Holmes as a mysterious and perhaps romantic choice. Holmes is the quintessential man of the British Empire—self-confident and self-reliant, athletic and active, intelligent and moral, a Tory in values but free of snobbery and political cant. And he likes to solve puzzles. And he is discreet, important, and famous. He ought to get tedious and even ridiculous, but he doesn't.

与布拉姆·斯托克以及后来的惊悚小说作家相比，柯南·道尔显得异常胆怯，甚至有些乏味。尽管他声称要深入探讨邪恶与危险，却对任何令人反感的内容避而不谈。狄更斯在他那些最轻松的作品中，某些情节的描写都比柯南·道尔更加生动恐怖。如果《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》意在让人不寒而栗，那么在二十世纪之交，英国的读者比以往任何时候都更容易受到这种恐惧的侵扰。许多十八、十九世纪的小说都比这部作品更加骇人听闻、匪夷所思。即便如此，我们也不能忽视夏洛克·福尔摩斯的存在。柯南·道尔塑造的福尔摩斯是一个独特的人物，他作为文明人的典范，在现代文化中扮演着引人入胜、令人安心的角色。福尔摩斯是时代的产物，但又有所不同——在当时的人物身上体现出的疏离和孤僻，在福尔摩斯身上却化作了老练世故；在其他人身上体现出的冷漠和可疑的科学理性，在福尔摩斯身上却体现为冷静和务实的智慧；在其他人身上体现出的感官享受，在福尔摩斯身上却体现为品味（对音乐和艺术的鉴赏）；在其他人身上体现出的厌女倾向，在福尔摩斯身上却体现为一种神秘而或许浪漫的选择。福尔摩斯是典型的英帝国人物——自信自立、身手矫健、精力充沛、智慧过人、品德高尚，价值观上虽是保守党人，却不带丝毫势利和政治虚伪。他喜欢解谜。他行事谨慎，举足轻重，名声显赫。他本应变得乏味甚至可笑，但他却始终保持着这种特质。

The premise of The Hound of the Baskervilles is that a certain wealthy family from a rather wild part of Devonshire is subject to a family curse involving a large infernal hound. One heir has died of mysterious causes before the novel opens, and another has just come to England to take up his inheritance. Can Holmes save the new heir and solve the mystery surrounding the death of the former one? Of course he can. The pleasure is in how Conan Doyle sets up the mechanics of the plot so that the reader, and Watson, don't figure it out before Holmes reveals what he knows. The trick is that Conan Doyle withholds no information from the reader, but turns it into misinformation through Watson's interpretation of it. The reader, used to Watson, knows he's wrong, but follows him pleasantly on various wild goose chases without reinterpreting the information until Holmes makes his revelations.

《巴斯克维尔的猎犬》的故事背景设定在德文郡一个偏僻地区的富裕家族，这个家族被一条凶猛的猎犬诅咒。小说开篇前，一位继承人已离奇死亡，另一位继承人刚刚来到英国继承遗产。福尔摩斯能否拯救这位新继承人，并解开前一位继承人死亡之谜？答案是肯定的。故事的妙处在于柯南·道尔如何巧妙地设置情节，让读者和华生在福尔摩斯揭晓真相之前都无法猜到结局。柯南·道尔并没有对读者隐瞒任何信息，而是通过华生的解读将其转化为错误信息。读者习惯了华生的判断，知道他错了，但仍然乐于跟随他进行各种徒劳的追查，直到福尔摩斯最终揭晓真相。

Conan Doyle tried to get rid of Holmes at least once, and apparently detested writing about him, but Holmes is as popular at the beginning of the twenty-first century as he was at the beginning of the twentieth (maybe more so). My view is that the reason for this is that somehow he truly predates the First World War, and that reading Holmes stories is endlessly reassuring—when Conan Doyle was writing most of the Holmes stories, the horrors of the war and the twentieth century could not be imagined, and while she is reading them, the reader can hardly imagine them, either. Many readers read them over and over, perhaps as escape, but perhaps as a way of imagining the world we live in as a manageable place, where all we need to orient ourselves is a little systematic brainpower. Holmes and Watson, with some help from Hollywood, have endured while other, more graphic thriller writers have not. But the intriguing thing about the Holmes stories is that the Hollywood versions have dated, while the originals have remained perennial. Holmes is the model all other detectives wrestle with because he is the coolest puzzle solver. Perhaps the lesson is that it is not the brutality or shock of the crime that invites willing suspension of disbelief, but the intrigue of the puzzle.

柯南·道尔至少有一次试图摆脱福尔摩斯这个角色，而且显然他本人也厌恶描写福尔摩斯，但福尔摩斯在二十一世纪初的人气却丝毫不减当年（甚至可能更胜一筹）。我认为原因在于，福尔摩斯的故事似乎真的早于第一次世界大战，而且阅读福尔摩斯的故事总能给人带来莫大的慰藉——在柯南·道尔创作福尔摩斯故事的年代，战争和二十世纪的种种恐怖景象还难以想象，而读者在阅读这些故事时，也很难去想象这些。许多读者反复阅读福尔摩斯的故事，或许是为了逃避现实，或许是为了将我们所生活的世界想象成一个可以掌控的地方，在那里，我们只需要一点系统性的思维就能找到方向。福尔摩斯和华生，在好莱坞的助力下，得以流传至今，而其他一些描写更为写实的惊悚小说作家却未能做到这一点。但福尔摩斯故事最引人入胜之处在于，好莱坞的改编版本早已过时，而原著却经久不衰。福尔摩斯是所有其他侦探效仿的榜样，因为他是最冷静的解谜高手。或许，这告诉我们，真正让观众心甘情愿地放下怀疑的，并非犯罪的残忍或骇人，而是谜题本身的悬念。

48. Joseph Conrad. Heart of Darkness

48. 约瑟夫·康拉德，《黑暗之心》

(1902; REPR., NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1971), 89 PP.

（1902 年；重印，纽约：W. W. NORTON，1971 年），89 页。

Heart of Darkness is a good example of how even the best-intentioned, most respected piece of fiction can devolve into a social document when attitudes change and history overtakes the thematic material of a given work of art. A hundred years after publication, Conrad's repeated images of the Africans Marlow meets in his journey up the Congo River seem racist and inhumane. Even when they are dying from the cruel treatment they receive at the hands of the Belgians (treatment that Conrad protested), they die as a group of pitiful creatures, not as individuals who have been exploited and handled unjustly and unmercifully. Conrad's habit of individualizing whites and generalizing blacks, arrogating consciousness and intellect solely to Europeans, no longer rates the respect it once received—for many years Heart of Darkness was considered a great novella, one of the half dozen great short novels in the European tradition.

《黑暗之心》很好地诠释了，即使是初衷最佳、备受推崇的小说，一旦社会风气转变，历史的进程超越了作品的主题，也会沦为社会文献。一百年后，康拉德笔下马洛在刚果河上遇到的非洲人的形象，在人们看来，既带有种族主义色彩，又缺乏人性。即便他们死于比利时人的残酷虐待（康拉德曾对此提出抗议），他们也只是一群可怜的生物，而非被剥削、被不公正、被无情对待的个体。康拉德惯于将白人个体化、将黑人概括化，并将意识和智慧强加于欧洲人身上，这种做法如今已不再像过去那样受人尊敬——多年来，《黑暗之心》一直被视为伟大的中篇小说，是欧洲文学传统中六部伟大短篇小说之一。

But the problem of Heart of Darkness is not merely a historical one— that attitudes changed—or a psychological one—that Conrad himself overlooked or avoided seeing evidence of vital African cultures when he visited the Congo in 1890 (as some scholars assert). The problem with Heart of Darkness is artistic, too, and it is a good lesson in how technical choices shape artistic vision. The symptom is that from beginning to end, the author and the narrator are victims of a thoroughgoing imperialist sentimentality that persistently substitutes false feeling for true observation. The first hint of this is when Marlow says of his aunt, “It's queer how out of touch with truth women are. They live in a world of their own, and there had never been anything like it, and never can be.” Such a remark could be made only by a man who had never actually listened to a woman or observed any of the women around him on any street in any city of Europe. Or, perhaps, read a novel by a woman. Or, perhaps, cared about women's lives. At any rate, Conrad's tendency to generalize from these sorts of feelings rather than to actually observe what is around him is clear from this point forward. Sentimentality is often defined as fake or exaggerated feeling, but it also may be seen as feeling that has no basis in the sentimentalist's actual experience—he does not truly observe or perceive the object, but rather projects fears or wishes onto the object and then reacts to them as if they were real.

但《黑暗之心》的问题并非仅仅在于历史层面——观念的转变——也并非仅仅在于心理层面——康拉德本人在1890年访问刚果时（正如一些学者所言）忽视或刻意回避了非洲文化的活力。《黑暗之心》的问题也在于艺术层面，它很好地诠释了技术选择如何塑造艺术视野。其表现是，从始至终，作者和叙述者都深受一种彻底的帝国主义感伤主义的毒害，这种感伤主义不断地用虚假的情感取代真实的观察。这一点在马洛谈到他的姑妈时就已初露端倪：“女人真是与现实脱节，这真奇怪。她们生活在自己的世界里，以前从未有过，以后也不会有。”只有从未真正倾听过女性的声音，从未观察过欧洲任何城市街头女性的人，才会说出这样的话。或许，他们从未读过女性作家的作品，或许，他们从未关心过女性的生活。总之，从这一点开始，康拉德倾向于从这类感受出发进行概括，而不是真正观察周围的事物，这一点就显而易见了。感伤主义通常被定义为虚假或夸大的情感，但它也可以被视为一种没有感伤主义者实际经验基础的情感——他并没有真正观察或感知对象，而是将恐惧或愿望投射到对象上，然后像对待真实事物一样做出反应。

Marlow's reaction to the coast of Africa is similar to Crusoe's two centuries earlier—the jungle seems impenetrable and fierce. When he enters at the mouth of the Congo River, however, his perception doesn't change—the vegetation along the river continues to hide something or someone whom Marlow hardly dares to look at or imagine. He is the opposite of an explorer, if an explorer is someone who actually looks for what is present in the new landscape, as Crusoe does. And then there is Kurtz. The reverse side of his fear-induced sentimentality is his impulse to worship Kurtz. Even before meeting him, after no more than hearing his name and a bit of his reputation, Mar-low is ready to attribute all sorts of greatness to Kurtz. He is thus enthralled. After he picks up Kurtz and returns him downriver, he spends lots of time listening to Kurtz and pondering his meaning, but he doesn't actually hear anything Kurtz says clearly enough to remember it or communicate it to his listeners. He is far more interested in his own feelings about Kurtz—what Kurtz symbolizes in his emotional life. When he subsequently visits Kurtz's fiance at the end of the novella, the two of them collude in memorializing Kurtz by sentimentalizing him. It is clear from how they converse that each wants to claim Kurtz's “greatness,” but neither one actually remembers any specifics about it.

马洛对非洲海岸的反应与两个世纪前的鲁滨逊相似——丛林似乎难以穿越，危机四伏。然而，当他进入刚果河口时，他的感知并没有改变——河岸边的植被依然隐藏着某种东西或某个人，马洛几乎不敢直视，也不敢想象。如果探险家的定义是像鲁滨逊那样，真正去探索新环境中的事物，那么马洛与探险家截然相反。然后，还有库尔茨。他恐惧引发的感伤的另一面，是他对库尔茨的崇拜。甚至在见到库尔茨之前，仅仅听过他的名字和一些名声之后，马洛就迫不及待地将各种伟大的事迹赋予库尔茨。他被库尔茨深深吸引。在把库尔茨带回下游之后，马洛花了大量时间倾听库尔茨的讲话，并思考他话中的含义，但他实际上并没有听清库尔茨说的任何话，以至于无法记住或传达给听众。他更关心的是自己对库尔茨的感受——库尔茨在他情感生活中所象征的意义。在小说结尾，当他拜访库尔茨的未婚妻时，两人合谋以感伤的方式纪念库尔茨。从他们的对话中可以明显看出，两人都想占有库尔茨的“伟大”，但实际上，他们都记不起库尔茨的任何具体事迹。

The real problem with Heart of Darkness is that Conrad substitutes eloquence for details and incidents. Marlow makes a long journey— from Belgium to Africa, then months in Africa waiting to go upriver, then downriver and back to Belgium and England. Clearly there is a story here, full of adventures and particulars, but the particulars are not related—they are summarized and interpreted for a rhetorical purpose. The author is less interested in telling a story than in making a point, but the point he makes is unconvincing because there is no evidence in the form of a well-constructed narrative with believable characters to back it up. Marlow's fear (and Kurtz's and Conrad's) approaches terror. What they fear is so overwhelming that it is unspeakable. At the root of such fear is guilt, perhaps. The Africans in the novella work not like human characters but like ghosts, or like the undead in Dracula —they are meant to infuse the reader with a sense of uncontrollable forces at work in the world, of dread that the reader is supposed to accept and partake of.

《黑暗之心》真正的问题在于康拉德用华丽的辞藻取代了细节和事件。马洛踏上了一段漫长的旅程——从比利时到非洲，然后在非洲待了几个月等待溯流而上，再顺流而下，最终回到比利时和英国。显然，这里面蕴含着一个充满冒险和细节的故事，但这些细节之间缺乏关联——它们被概括和解读，仅仅是为了达到某种修辞目的。作者与其说是想讲述一个故事，不如说是想阐明一个观点，但他提出的观点缺乏说服力，因为没有结构严谨的叙事和可信的人物来支撑。马洛（以及库尔茨和康拉德）的恐惧近乎恐怖。他们所恐惧的事物如此强烈，以至于难以言喻。或许，这种恐惧的根源在于罪恶感。小说中的非洲人不像人类角色，而像鬼魂，或者像《德古拉》中的亡灵——他们的目的是让读者感受到世界上存在着不可控制的力量，让读者感到恐惧，而这种恐惧是读者应该接受并参与其中的。

Heart of Darkness asks us to consider the idea of greatness in the novel, because it was considered great until dissenting voices, such as that of the Nigerian writer Chinua Achebe (in his 1975 lecture “An Image of Africa: Racism in Conrad's Heart of Darkness”) , invited the literary establishment to reconsider it. The important thing to remember is that thematic material in any novel—that is, the author's ideas about the world he lives in—goes in and out of style. A novel always documents the period of its composition; sometimes the story it tells transcends the period and transcends the themes the author thought he was using it to express. Sometimes, indeed, the period of a novel's composition becomes so distant that the thematic material ceases to mean anything, while the story remains compelling, as with Boccaccio's stories of feuding Florentine parties. It's hard to see how Conrad's novella will come back into the general canon, given his penchant for talking about Africans and women in casually demeaning terms. Perhaps if it did come back, that would be a sign that such talk and such views had returned to respectability. Resurrection is always possible as long as a book remains in print and someone is around to champion it. My own view, however, is that because the novella is artistically flawed—because the balance between thematic material and narrative material is off— Heart of Darkness will remain an interesting historical document but a bad work of art.

《黑暗之心》促使我们思考小说中的“伟大”概念，因为在尼日利亚作家奇努阿·阿切贝（Chinua Achebe）等人的异议之声出现之前，它一直被认为是伟大的作品。阿切贝在其1975年的演讲《非洲的形象：康拉德<黑暗之心>中的种族主义》中呼吁文学界重新审视这部作品。我们需要记住的重要一点是，任何小说的主题素材——即作者对其所处世界的思考——都会随着时代而变化。小说总是会记录其创作的时代；有时，它讲述的故事会超越时代，超越作者最初想要表达的主题。的确，有时，小说的创作时代会变得如此遥远，以至于主题素材失去了意义，而故事本身却依然引人入胜，例如薄伽丘笔下佛罗伦萨各派纷争的故事。鉴于康拉德惯于用轻佻的语气谈论非洲人和女性，很难想象他的中篇小说《黑暗之心》会如何重回经典之列。或许，如果它真的重回经典，就意味着这种言论和观点又重新获得了认可。只要一本书还在印刷发行，只要有人为它辩护，它就总有机会重获新生。然而，我个人认为，由于这部中篇小说在艺术上存在缺陷——主题和叙事之间的平衡失调——《黑暗之心》最终只会是一份有趣的史料，而非一部糟糕的艺术作品。

49. Edith WhartonThe House of Mirth

49. 伊迪丝·华顿《欢乐之家》

ED. CYNTHIA GRIFFIN WOLF (1905; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1985), 329 PP.

ED. CYNTHIA GRIFFIN WOLF (1905 年；重印，纽约：企鹅出版社，1985 年)，329 页。

The House of Mirth begins with a minor indiscretion. An unmarried New York society woman, Lily Bart, who is twenty-nine years old, gives in to the temptation to visit the apartment of a man she knows, Lawrence Selden, and her departure is witnessed by an unsavory social-climbing character named Rosedale. Lily is awkward during the encounter with Rosedale and manages to alienate him, but since she is to all appearances firmly planted in the highest society, the very society that Rosedale would like to frequent, she shrugs off her sense of unease and pursues her already formed plan, which is to secure herself a wealthy and socially prominent husband, an unappealing mama's boy named Percy Gryce.

《欢乐之家》的故事始于一次小小的失态。29岁的纽约社交名媛莉莉·巴特（Lily Bart）未婚，她一时兴起，去了熟人劳伦斯·塞尔登（Lawrence Selden）的公寓。她的离开被一个名叫罗兹戴尔（Rosedale）的卑鄙无耻、一心想往上爬的家伙目睹。莉莉在与罗兹戴尔的会面中显得笨拙，甚至疏远了他。但由于她表面上稳居上流社会——正是罗兹戴尔梦寐以求的社交圈——她便抛开不安，继续执行自己早已制定的计划：嫁给一个富有且社会地位显赫的丈夫，一个名叫珀西·格莱斯（Percy Gryce）的、令人反感的妈宝男。

But Lily does not succeed. Though she brings Gryce to the point of a proposal, she ends up offending him and he goes off without making an offer. Lily is now in considerable financial and some social danger.

但莉莉并没有成功。尽管她成功地让格莱斯萌生了求婚的念头，但最终却冒犯了他，格莱斯没有答应就离开了。莉莉现在面临着巨大的经济风险，社交生活也岌岌可危。

Though beautiful and possessed of perfect manners and only the best connections, she has come to an age where she has to play her cards right to gain an establishment. For the rest of the novel, Lily plays her cards wrong every time. Finally, socially and financially ruined, in part by the malice of others and in part by her own circumspection, she dies of an overdose of a sleeping draft in a shabby room, her life a beautiful, dignified, and in some sense perplexing wreck.

尽管她容貌姣好，举止优雅，人脉广泛，但到了这个年纪，她必须谨慎行事才能立足。然而，在小说的剩余篇幅中，莉莉却屡屡失手。最终，她因他人的恶意和自身的谨慎，在社交和经济上都一落千丈，死于一间破旧房间的安眠药过量。她的一生美丽、尊严，却又在某种意义上令人费解地走向了毁灭。

Wharton's characters consistently act out of what may seem to the reader to be a self-destructive reserve. It is clear to everyone around Lily, including the reader, that to survive she must marry for money, but throughout the novel she toys with making a more companionable connection with Lawrence Selden, who appreciates her but does not have enough money to marry. He also lives a kind of aesthetically perfected life that he doesn't care (except briefly) to disrupt. He comes closest of all the characters to feeling love for Lily, but his real role in the narrative is to observe her fall with a finer sensibility than the others around her are capable of. However much the reader may deplore Lily's downward spiral (which Wharton depicts in graphic detail), and however much the reader may wish for Selden to rescue her, it is clear from the first time she enters his apartment that he is incapable of really connecting with Lily or with anyone else. Her circumspection finds its echo in his core selfishness.

沃顿笔下的人物始终表现出一种在读者看来近乎自我毁灭的内敛。莉莉身边的人，包括读者在内，都清楚她必须嫁给有钱人才能生存下去，但在整部小说中，她却始终在与劳伦斯·塞尔登建立一种更亲密的关系之间摇摆不定。塞尔登欣赏她，却无力娶她。他过着一种近乎完美的生活，除了短暂的例外，他并不想打破这种生活。在所有人物中，他最接近于对莉莉产生爱意，但他在叙事中的真正作用，却是以比周围其他人更敏锐的视角，观察着她的堕落。无论读者多么痛心莉莉的堕落（沃顿对此进行了细致入微的描写），无论读者多么希望塞尔登能够拯救她，从莉莉第一次踏入他的公寓起，就显而易见，他根本无法与莉莉，乃至任何人建立真正的联系。莉莉的谨慎与他骨子里的自私形成了鲜明的对比。

It says something about Wharton's milieu—the wealthiest and oldest New York families—that by contrast to everyone they know, Lily and Selden are the hero and heroine of The House of Mirth.

这说明了沃顿所处的环境——纽约最富有、最古老的家族——与他们所认识的所有人形成鲜明对比的是，莉莉和塞尔登是《欢乐之家》中的英雄和女主角。

Wharton writes with judicious self-assurance and detailed, deliberate observation. Like James, Wharton was intent upon raising the artistic claims of the novel to the heights of great poetry, drama, or painting, and like James, she considered a finished or perfected quality to be the sign of a truly artistic novel. Her models were French rather than English—Flaubert rather than Dickens—and she admired the French novelists for their psychological probing and for the care with which they shaped their material. Herself possessed of wealth, she had the leisure to perfect her work rather than rush it into print at so many cents per word, and The House of Mirth does have a polished and deliberate style that is frequently mesmerizing. Wharton lived and wrote with an equanimity that is unusual in a productive novelist—she had one passionate affair in the course of an otherwise unsatisfactory marriage, she seems to have been sensible and charitable in all of her relationships, to have been in general drawn to doing the right thing, both morally and socially, all her life. These characteristics certainly were reinforced by the fact that the great success of her work did not change her circumstances. She lived the life she had been destined by birth to live, but with the added advantage of intelligence and moral sensibility. She is an excellent role model not often emulated.

沃顿的文笔自信而审慎，观察细致入微。与詹姆斯一样，沃顿致力于将小说的艺术性提升到伟大诗歌、戏剧或绘画的高度；她也像詹姆斯一样，认为一部真正具有艺术性的小说必须具备精雕细琢的品质。她的创作榜样是法国人而非英国人——是福楼拜而非狄更斯——她欣赏法国小说家对人物心理的深入探究以及对素材的精心雕琢。沃顿本人家境富裕，因此有闲暇去完善作品，而不是为了赶稿而匆忙出版。《欢乐之家》的文风流畅而严谨，常常令人着迷。沃顿生活和写作的平静，在一位多产的小说家身上实属罕见——在一段并不幸福的婚姻中，她曾有过一段激情四溢的婚外情；她似乎在所有人际关系中都表现得理智而仁慈；她一生都倾向于在道德和社会层面都做正确的事。她作品的巨大成功并没有改变她的境遇，这无疑强化了她的这些特质。她过着命中注定的生活，却又拥有智慧和道德感悟。她是一位杰出的榜样，却鲜有人效仿。

The modern reader may find Lily Bart just on the verge of being a case study in a science, psychology, that was just on the verge of being invented. She is interesting in psychological terms as well as in social terms (the terms Wharton chooses). She can't commit herself to the life she seems to prefer to lead. At every critical juncture, she torpedoes the very plans she has worked assiduously to bring about, and yet she also can't accept the working world—when she gets a job she needs very much, making hats, she is too clumsy and inexperienced to do the work and gets fired. She has been raised and trained to make a rich, loveless marriage, but she can't bring herself to do it.

现代读者或许会觉得莉莉·巴特简直就是心理学这门学科的典型案例，而心理学当时也正处于萌芽阶段。无论从心理学角度还是社会学角度（沃顿选择的视角），她都引人入胜。她无法全身心投入到自己似乎更向往的生活中。每逢关键时刻，她都会亲手毁掉自己苦心筹划的计划，然而她也无法接受职场——当她找到一份急需的工作——制帽时，却因为笨手笨脚、缺乏经验而无法胜任，最终被解雇。她从小就被灌输要嫁给一个富有却没有爱情的人，但她始终无法下定决心。

Wharton does not condemn or satirize Lily's world, but neither does she glamorize it. She does not question Lily's preference for this world, but she does present the world coolly, inviting the reader to observe that while it is a world full of beautiful things and places, delightful treats and privileges, it is also cold and destructive, a world where it is easier to do damage than to do good, easier to exclude than to connect. Therefore the reader is left to question whether there was ever any hope for Lily, since her preferred environment is one in which her sensibility cannot be satisfied.

沃顿既不谴责也不讽刺莉莉的世界，但她也没有美化它。她没有质疑莉莉对这个世界的偏爱，而是冷静地呈现了它，引导读者去观察：尽管这是一个充满美好事物和场所、令人愉悦的享受和特权的世界，但它也冷酷无情、充满破坏性，在这个世界里，作恶比行善容易，排斥比联结容易。因此，读者不禁会问，莉莉是否还有希望，因为她所向往的环境却无法满足她的情感需求。

Lily's problem is not being disposed of against her wishes, but disposing of herself against her wishes. Wharton indicates that the problem is not solved by female freedom of choice, only complicated by it. Without parents to push her, Lily can't act. Having passed the age of ignorance and become an astute observer of those around her, she is too far gone—paradoxically, it is not she who is past being desirable, but her surroundings, mansions and privileges and all, that are past being desirable enough to compel the fatal choice among the various less than ideal mates.

莉莉的问题不在于被违背意愿地抛弃，而在于违背意愿地抛弃自己。沃顿指出，女性的自由选择并不能解决这个问题，反而会使问题更加复杂。没有父母的督促，莉莉无法采取行动。她已经过了懵懂无知的年纪，对周围的一切都变得异常敏锐，以至于无法挽回——矛盾的是，并非她本人不再具有吸引力，而是她所处的环境，豪宅、特权等等，都已不再足以迫使她在众多并不理想的伴侣中做出致命的选择。

The House of Mirth also raises an interesting formal question. Although Lily's fall is dramatic and compelling, it is not especially representative and therefore not especially meaningful. Her unique qualities of beauty and circumspection combined with the special nature of her milieu—great wealth and impeccable breeding—mean that her story is not susceptible to being generalized. Lily's interest for Wharton, and for Lawrence Selden, is that she is unique on the surface and unique underneath. It is only in her psychological profile—her nascent identity as a case study—that she becomes like others, like people who may be reading about her, for example. But a novel is different from a case study in that it looks past surface distinctions to the similarities underneath. Therefore, though Lily is interesting to witness, she is hard to learn from. Every novel of fatal decline has intrinsic dramatic excitement (la Thérèse Raquin) , but Lily's decline is so specialized that The House of Mirth falls just short of greatness.

《欢乐之家》也提出了一个有趣的结构性问题。莉莉的陨落虽然戏剧性且引人入胜，但并不具有代表性，因此也缺乏意义。她独特的美貌和谨慎，以及她所处环境的特殊性——巨额财富和无可挑剔的教养——意味着她的故事难以被普遍化。莉莉之所以吸引沃顿和劳伦斯·塞尔登，是因为她表面独特，内在也同样独特。只有在她的心理层面——她作为案例研究的雏形——她才变得像其他人一样，比如像那些可能正在阅读她故事的人一样。但小说与案例研究的不同之处在于，小说会超越表面差异，探究其内在的相似之处。因此，尽管莉莉的故事引人入胜，但我们很难从中汲取经验教训。每一部描写致命衰落的小说都蕴含着内在的戏剧张力（如《泰蕾丝·拉坎》），但莉莉的衰落如此特殊，以至于《欢乐之家》与伟大之作仅一步之遥。

50. Max Beerbohm. The Illustrated Zuleika Dobson, or an Oxford Love Story

50. 马克斯·比尔博姆。《插图版祖莱卡·多布森，或牛津爱情故事》

(NEW HAVEN, CONN.: YALE UNIVERSITY PRESS, 1911), 350 PP.

（康涅狄格州纽黑文：耶鲁大学出版社，1911 年），350 页。

Max Beerbohm was an artist, a reviewer, an essayist, a caricaturist, and a generally beloved fellow about town, and upon publication, Zuleika Dobson was greeted with a chorus of delight that perhaps no one alive in the twenty-first century quite understands. The author of the introduction to the Yale University Press edition wonders, if the novel is a satire, what is it satirizing?, and that is perhaps a fair question. My guess is that it is not satirizing as much as it is making fun out of irresistible women, manly men, and undergraduate callowness. For our purposes, Zuleika Dobson also pushes to its ridiculous extreme the old question of what women are for. Zuleika, who is by profession a magician but by avocation a siren, is clearly for nothing. She has no money and no life goals other than to captivate the hearts of undergraduate men. When she first arrives at Oxford during “Eights Week,” she meets the duke of Dorset and, certain of his indifference, falls in love with him. The next day at breakfast, however, he reveals that he has fallen in love with her. She is stung and betrayed. She has no use for a man who actually loves her, and at once recoils. The duke now vows to commit suicide for her, and tries to do so at once, but circumstances intervene, and he has to put off his plan for twenty-four hours. In the course of the next day, he, too, falls out of love, but nonetheless he is bound by honor and tradition to go through with his vow. He is more than a little disconcerted to discover that every other undergraduate in Oxford has made the same vow, thereby diluting the drama of his plan. Witty complications ensue.

马克斯·比尔博姆是一位艺术家、评论家、散文家、漫画家，也是城里人人都爱的风云人物。他的小说《祖莱卡·多布森》出版后，受到了热烈的追捧，这种喜悦之情或许只有生活在二十一世纪的人才能真正理解。耶鲁大学出版社版的序言作者提出了一个疑问：如果这部小说是一部讽刺作品，那么它究竟讽刺了什么？这或许是一个值得思考的问题。我的猜测是，与其说是讽刺，不如说是在嘲弄那些魅力四射的女性、男子气概十足的男性以及大学本科生的幼稚无知。就我们的目的而言，《祖莱卡·多布森》还将“女性存在的意义是什么”这个老生常谈的问题推向了荒谬的极致。祖莱卡，一个职业是魔术师，业余爱好是妖娆女郎的女人，显然毫无意义。她身无分文，人生目标也只有俘获大学男生的心。她初到牛津大学时正值“八年级周”，在那里遇到了多塞特公爵。她确信公爵对她漠不关心，却依然爱上了他。然而，第二天早餐时，公爵却坦白自己爱上了她。她感到既痛苦又背叛。她对一个真正爱她的男人毫无兴趣，立刻退缩了。公爵发誓要为她自杀，并立即尝试，但事与愿违，他不得不将计划推迟24小时。第二天，他也对她失去了爱意，但出于荣誉和传统的约束，他不得不履行自己的誓言。他惊讶地发现，牛津大学里其他所有本科生都发过同样的誓言，这让他原本充满戏剧性的计划显得苍白无力。接下来，一系列诙谐幽默的插曲接踵而至。

Zuleika Dobson is lighthearted to the core, exuberant to the end (when Zuleika looks up the train schedule to Cambridge). Like the works of P. G. Wodehouse, it is undarkened by the least hint of social commentary. But unlike the novels of Wodehouse, it uses romantic conventions only to turn them upside down, not to reaffirm them. It is a model comic novel in that it exploits the comedy inherent in logic. Everything Zuleika, the duke, and all the other characters do is logically perfect, given their assumptions about virtue, honor, and social class, but everything they do is also ridiculous. If Beerbohm had a satirical agenda, no one seems to have discovered it. He twitted or killed off all his characters, to the delight of all his readers. Zuleika Dobson was a success when it came out, in 1911 . Whether it had any larger purpose at the time is impossible to know now, because it quickly took on a different meaning. Bertrand Russell noted much later in the century, “I read Zuleika Dobson with pleasure. It represents the Oxford that the two World Wars have destroyed with a charm that is not likely to be reproduced anywhere in the world for the next thousand years.”

《祖莱卡·多布森》从头到尾都洋溢着轻松愉悦的气氛（直到祖莱卡查阅开往剑桥的火车时刻表）。与P·G·伍德豪斯的作品一样，它丝毫没有社会评论的阴暗色彩。但与伍德豪斯的小说不同的是，它运用浪漫主义的惯例只是为了颠覆它们，而不是为了重申它们。这是一部喜剧小说的典范，因为它充分利用了逻辑中固有的喜剧元素。祖莱卡、公爵以及所有其他角色的所作所为，在他们对美德、荣誉和社会阶级的认知框架下，都显得合情合理，但他们的所作所为也同样荒谬可笑。如果比尔博姆确实有讽刺的意图，似乎没有人发现。他让所有角色都经历着嘲讽或死亡，这让所有读者都感到欣喜。《祖莱卡·多布森》在1911年出版时取得了成功。至于它当时是否还有更深远的意义，现在已无从知晓，因为它很快就被赋予了新的内涵。伯特兰·罗素在本世纪晚些时候指出：“我读祖莱卡·多布森的作品时感到非常愉快。它展现了被两次世界大战摧毁的牛津大学，其魅力在未来一千年内恐怕在世界任何地方都难以复制。”

The Yale University Press edition is illustrated with Beerbohm's original drawings.

耶鲁大学出版社的版本配有比尔博姆的原版插图。

51. Ford Madox Ford The Good Soldier

51. 福特·马多克斯·福特，《好士兵》

(1915; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1989), 256 PP.

（1915 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1989 年），256 页。

The Good Soldier is an odd and maybe even unique book in that the fact that it is a masterpiece, almost a perfect novel, comes as a repeated surprise even to readers who have read it before. In a dedicatory letter to the second edition written some ten years after the publication of the novel, Ford depicts himself “taking down one of [his] ten-year-old books [and exclaiming] ‘Great Heavens, did I write as well as that then?’… And I will permit myself to say that I was astounded at the work I must have put into the construction of the book, at the intricate tangle of references and cross-references” (p. xx). Ford wrote other very good novels—his tetralogy Parade's End is moving and innovative—but he called The Good Soldier his “auk's egg” (“having reached the allotted, I had laid my one egg and might as well die”); it does have the quality of saying absolutely everything about both his story and his theme—not just everything he has to say, but everything there is to say.

《好兵》是一部奇特，或许甚至是独一无二的作品，因为它堪称杰作，近乎完美，即使是读过它的读者，也会一次又一次地感到惊喜。在小说出版约十年后，福特为第二版写的一封献词信中，他描述自己“拿起一本十年前的书，惊呼道：‘天哪，我当时写得真好！’……我得承认，我当时对自己在这本书的创作中所投入的心血感到震惊，对其中错综复杂的引用和交叉引用感到震惊”（第xx页）。福特还写过其他非常优秀的小说——他的四部曲《队列之末》感人至深且极具创新性——但他称《好兵》是他的“海雀蛋”（“既然已经完成了既定目标，我产下了唯一的蛋，不如就此死去吧”）。它的确具备这样的特质：它完全表达了他的故事和他的主题——不仅是他要表达的一切，而是所有要表达的一切。

The story seems simple. Two wealthy couples, one American and one English, meet at a spa in Germany and spend several years in comfortable friendship until it is revealed that the American wife and the English husband are carrying on an affair that the English wife knows about but the American husband does not. After the deaths of the adulterers, more and more is uncovered about both the conduct and the emotional meaning of the affair. The story is narrated by the American husband and is in some sense a detective story, but he is no investigator. The facts come to him unwillingly, since he would have preferred from the beginning not to know; the suspense depends not on what has happened, as dramatic as it turns out to be, but on the narrator's unfolding interpretation of the passionate emotions manifested in very small gestures or brief remarks.

故事看似简单。两对富裕的夫妇，一对美国人，一对英国人，在德国一家温泉疗养院相遇，并维持了数年的亲密友谊。直到后来，人们发现美国妻子和英国丈夫之间存在着一段婚外情，英国妻子知情，而美国丈夫却毫不知情。婚外情的双方相继去世后，这段婚外情的真相及其背后的情感意义也逐渐浮出水面。故事由美国丈夫叙述，某种程度上像是一部侦探小说，但他并非侦探。真相并非他自愿得知，因为他从一开始就希望对此一无所知；悬念并非源于已发生的事情（尽管最终的结局颇为戏剧性），而是源于叙述者对那些细微举动或简短言语中所蕴含的强烈情感的解读。

Ford's greatest gamble is in the navet of the narrator (Dowell), supposedly an idle but well-meaning wealthy man from an old Philadelphia family who readily accepts a sexless marriage with a woman (Florence) whose emotional life is a secret and a deception. Florence persuades Dowell at the commencement of their honeymoon that marital relations might so tax her weak heart that they are out of the question—she turns him into a servant who takes care of her every need while also leaving her lots of free time to carry on with at least two lovers of her choosing. Dowell's idiom and mode of thinking are not perfectly American, and Ford's insights into American ways are slightly off, but America is not his subject, England is, and Dowell is convincing enough. His real virtue is that he is disarming, and he does not pretend to reliability. He freely offers his own self-doubts about his competence, both as an actor in the drama and as an interpreter, and he manages not to seem either untruthful or self-serving. He paints four portraits—Edward Ashburnham, the owner of a large estate in England; his wife, Leonora, daughter of impoverished Irish gentry; Florence, heiress to a New England fortune; and Nancy Rufford, Leonora's ward, who has lived with Edward and Leonora from age thirteen.

福特最大的赌注在于叙述者（道威尔）的天真无邪。道威尔表面上是一位游手好闲但心地善良的费城老家富翁，他欣然接受了与一位名叫弗洛伦斯的女子的无性婚姻，而弗洛伦斯的感情生活却是一个秘密，充满了欺骗。蜜月伊始，弗洛伦斯便说服道威尔，婚姻关系可能会让她脆弱的心脏不堪重负，因此根本不可能——她把道威尔变成了一个仆人，照顾她的一切需求，同时又让她有大量的空闲时间与至少两位她选择的情人厮混。道威尔的语言和思维方式并不完全符合美国人的习惯，福特对美国风俗的洞察也略有偏差，但美国并非福特的主题，英国才是，而道威尔的表演也足够令人信服。他真正的优点在于他令人卸下防备，并且不故作可靠。他坦诚地表达了自己对自身能力的怀疑，无论是作为戏剧演员还是作为诠释者，但他却成功地做到了既不显得虚伪，也不显得自私。他画了四幅肖像——爱德华·阿什伯纳姆，英国一个大庄园的主人；他的妻子莱昂诺拉，一个贫困的爱尔兰乡绅的女儿；弗洛伦斯，新英格兰的一位富家女继承人；以及南希·拉福德，莱昂诺拉的养女，她从十三岁起就和爱德华和莱昂诺拉一起生活。

Edward and Leonora have every appearance of grace, character, and respectability. Edward, too, is suffering from a bad heart, but he has been in the army in India, and has also been an excellent landlord and magistrate back in England. His failures are failures of self-knowledge and intelligence more than morality—he is upright, generous, and responsible. But, fatally, he is “a sentimentalist,” which makes him susceptible to the appearance of suffering or weakness, and also makes him immune to his wife (theirs is an arranged marriage), whose virtues are those of strength and reserve. She is repeatedly termed “cold” by Dowell, but her coldness seems more in the nature of untapped warmth (for example, she wants children, which she and Edward can't seem to produce). The first startling fact about them that the reader learns is that they haven't spoken in private for thirteen years, though they are gracious to one another in public (surely this is possible only in an especially grand setting, with perfectly trained servants). Everything about Edward is plausible for, even typical of, a man of his position, but Ford takes a different approach from every previous English author to have contemplated the landed gentry, because he takes Edward's inner life, as empty as it is, seriously, anatomizing and sympathizing with its very emptiness.

爱德华和莱昂诺拉举止优雅，品格高尚，令人尊敬。爱德华也患有心脏病，但他曾在印度服役，回到英国后也是一位优秀的房东和治安法官。他的失败与其说是道德上的缺陷，不如说是缺乏自知之明和智慧——他为人正直、慷慨、负责。然而，致命的是，他是个“多愁善感的人”，这使他容易流露出痛苦或软弱的一面，也使他对妻子（他们的婚姻是包办的）漠不关心，而妻子的优点在于坚强和矜持。道威尔多次称她“冷漠”，但她的冷漠似乎更像是未被开发的温暖（例如，她想要孩子，但她和爱德华似乎一直无法生育）。读者了解到的第一个令人震惊的事实是，尽管他们在公共场合彬彬有礼，但他们已经十三年没有私下交谈过了（这当然只有在特别奢华的场合，有训练有素的仆人伺候的情况下才有可能）。爱德华的一切行为对于他这样的身份的人来说都是合情合理的，甚至是典型的，但福特采取了一种与以往所有描写乡绅的英国作家都不同的方法，因为他认真对待爱德华的内心世界，尽管它很空虚，但他剖析并同情这种空虚。
