It is clear as the novel proceeds that not only do Edward and Leonora have no idea what intimacy is, they also have no way of having found out: for one thing, they don't read novels, and for another, Leonora consults priests and nuns for marital advice, and what they have to offer are thirdhand clichs such as “men are like that.” Edward consults no one, and there seems to be no structure in his life that would permit such consultation. Other men of his social class tell dirty stories, perhaps as a form of sharing information, but these make Edward uncomfortable. Thus, when Edward begins to feel out of sympathy with Leonora some three or four years into their marriage, he is ripe for exploitation, and he ends up making a costly liaison and losing about 40 percent of the principal value of his estate. Over the next ten years Leonora takes over management of the estate and brings it back to its original value, but the balance of their relationship is fatally undermined by her control and his untrustworthiness.

随着小说的展开，我们逐渐明白，爱德华和莱昂诺拉不仅对亲密关系一无所知，而且也无从知晓：一方面，他们不读小说；另一方面，莱昂诺拉向神父和修女寻求婚姻建议，而他们提供的却是诸如“男人就是这样”之类的陈词滥调。爱德华不向任何人咨询，他的生活似乎也没有任何结构允许他这样做。他所在阶层的其他男人会讲述一些不堪入目的故事，或许是为了分享信息，但这却让爱德华感到不自在。因此，在结婚三四年后，当爱德华开始对莱昂诺拉失去同情心时，他很容易被利用，最终他陷入了一段代价高昂的婚外情，损失了大约40%的遗产本金。在接下来的十年里，莱昂诺拉接管了遗产的管理，使其恢复到原来的价值，但她的控制欲和爱德华的不可信赖彻底破坏了他们关系的平衡。

Both the American marriage and the English marriage suffer from the emasculation of the husbands, and Dowell criticizes Leonora and Florence, but Ford depicts the husbands more complexly. They have fully colluded in their emasculation by not knowing how to be men— the reason for Dowell's failure (symbolized by the fact that unlike other Americans, he has no interest in earning money) is unclear, but the reason for Edward's failure is that he has received no instruction in anything but duties and forms. He is also slightly stupid. Dowell is content in his emasculation, but Edward has unfulfilled yearnings for companionship and support that he finds in a series of women, with Leonora's tacit acceptance. Leonora holds out the hope that once their financial imbalance is righted, he will get interested in her again, and things seem to be moving in that direction when Florence entangles Edward in her much colder and less sentimental designs—Dowell says that she “annexes him.”

美国式婚姻和英国式婚姻都存在丈夫被阉割的问题，道威尔批评了莱昂诺拉和弗洛伦斯，但福特对丈夫的刻画更为复杂。他们完全是默许了这种阉割，因为他们不知道如何做个真正的男人——道威尔失败的原因（象征着他不像其他美国人那样对赚钱感兴趣）尚不明确，但爱德华失败的原因在于他除了职责和礼仪之外，没有接受过任何其他方面的教育。他还有些愚钝。道威尔安于这种被阉割的状态，但爱德华渴望陪伴和支持，他从一系列女性身上寻求慰藉，莱昂诺拉对此默许。莱昂诺拉抱有希望，一旦他们的经济状况恢复正常，他就会再次对她感兴趣，而当弗洛伦斯将爱德华卷入她冷酷无情、缺乏温情的计划时，事情似乎正朝着这个方向发展——道威尔说，她“吞噬了他”。

Dowell maintains that Florence is a woman of the most shallow possible motivations—she wants to look good, dress well, display herself to intellectual advantage, and be catered to. She is purely and discreetly a social climber. Until Florence comes along, Leonora has accepted Edward's liaisons as well-meaning and necessary, worthy of her respect and even her care, but when he links himself with Florence, whom Leonora despises, she loses all respect for and sympathy with him, though she still loves and desires him.

道威尔认为，弗洛伦斯是个动机极其肤浅的女人——她只想让自己看起来漂亮，穿得体面，展现自己的才智，并受人伺候。她纯粹是个向上爬的女人，而且行事低调。在弗洛伦斯出现之前，莱昂诺拉一直认为爱德华的风流韵事出于好意且必要，值得她尊重甚至关心。但当爱德华与她鄙视的弗洛伦斯在一起后，她对爱德华彻底失去了尊重和同情，尽管她仍然爱着他，渴望着他。

While I don't want to retell the entire novel—especially since it interprets itself quite well—I do want to comment on Ford's style, which makes great use of paradox. At one point, for example, while giving the history of Edward's military career, he says, “It would have done him a great deal of good to get killed.” There is something quite reckless about that sentence, and yet it is perfectly understandable in context—it comes late in the novel, when we know that not only is Edward's end to be tragic, but also that the downward path to it is painful and pathetic. How much better for the dumb animal to have died heroically, in accordance with the system by which he lived. There are those who believe that The Good Soldier is one of the few stylistically perfect novels in any language, and perhaps what Ford was alluding to in his remarks about references and cross-references is this sense that the contradictory and complementary meanings in every paradoxical sentence are entirely understandable because he has made such a clear explication of his fictional situation—the psychologies of his characters, the interweaving of character and event, intention and chance.

虽然我不想复述整部小说——尤其因为它本身就很有解读空间——但我确实想谈谈福特的写作风格，他巧妙地运用了悖论。例如，在讲述爱德华的军旅生涯时，他曾说过：“对他来说，死一死或许是件好事。”这句话听起来颇为鲁莽，但结合上下文却完全可以理解——它出现在小说后半段，那时我们已经知道，爱德华的结局不仅悲惨，而且他走向悲剧的道路也痛苦不堪、令人唏嘘。对于这个愚钝的家伙来说，按照他生前所信奉的规则，英勇地死去岂不更好？有人认为《好兵》是任何语言中为数不多的风格完美的小说之一，也许福特在谈到引用和交叉引用时所暗示的正是这种感觉：每个自相矛盾的句子中矛盾和互补的含义都是完全可以理解的，因为他对他的虚构情境——人物的心理、人物与事件、意图与偶然的交织——做出了如此清晰的解释。

Ford originally titled his novel The Saddest Story. After the outbreak of the First World War and his departure for the front, his editor changed the title to The Good Soldier , which Ford did not care for. But the editor was right—Ford's title is empty and meaningless. The Good Soldier subtly cues the reader to the larger social dimension of Ford's subject. Leonora and Edward, and to a lesser degree Dowell and Florence, are struggling with ignorance as much as moral failure. They are representatives of a system that fails them and fails in their failure. It is the subtler side of Dickens's Circumlocution Office, of Thackeray's Vanity Fair. In Dickens and Thackeray's day, the landed gentry could still be attacked. By Ford's time, all of the social and cultural arrangements of feudal Europe were imploding in the First World War. Ford was astute enough to depict both the inevitability of the implosion and its sadness—the world of Jane Austen a hundred years on, depopulated, lonely, and dark.

福特最初将他的小说命名为《最悲伤的故事》。第一次世界大战爆发后，他奔赴前线，编辑将书名改为《好兵》，福特并不喜欢这个新标题。但编辑是对的——福特的原标题空洞无物。《好兵》巧妙地引导读者关注福特笔下人物所处的更广泛的社会层面。莱昂诺拉和爱德华，以及在某种程度上道威尔和弗洛伦斯，他们不仅在道德沦丧中挣扎，也在与无知作斗争。他们代表着一个辜负了他们、也因他们的失败而走向毁灭的体制。这正是狄更斯《迂回办公室》和萨克雷《名利场》中更为微妙的一面。在狄更斯和萨克雷的时代，地主阶级仍可能遭受攻击。而到了福特的时代，封建欧洲的所有社会和文化秩序都在第一次世界大战中土崩瓦解。福特敏锐地描绘了崩溃的必然性和它的悲伤——简·奥斯汀笔下的世界在一百年后，人口稀少，孤独而黑暗。

52. Sinclair Lewis Main Street

52. 辛克莱·刘易斯大街

(1920; REPR., NEW YORK: NEW AMERICAN LIBRARY, SIGNET, 1998), 474 PP.

（1920 年；重印，纽约：新美国图书馆，SIGNET，1998 年），474 页。

Sinclair Lewis may be ripe for a revival; his books bring up several interesting issues of art and fashion. Main Street is his most famous book, though certain critics prefer Babbitt as a better novel. Main Street was a tremendous best seller, published when Lewis was thirty-five, and cited by the Nobel Prize committee as a major reason he was given the Nobel in 1930 . Main Street is the story of Carol Kennicott, who graduates from a small women's college in the first chapter of the novel with rather vague aspirations to achieve something or reform something. After a reasonably long (but not very enlightening) courtship she marries small-town doctor Will Kennicott and moves with him to Gopher Prairie, Minnesota (based on Lewis's hometown of Sauk Centre). She is immediately dissatisfied with the town and her life there, and the rather episodic novel traces the simultaneous evolution of her marriage, her life in Gopher Prairie, and the passing of her youth. The novel is rather like a bildungsroman in that it describes the education of a young person through a series of trials, but Carol's is a domestic education, and it is hard to decide whether she grows or is simply overcome. In the end, under some protest, she manages to agree to life in Gopher Prairie, but not quite to accept it.

辛克莱·刘易斯的作品或许正迎来复兴的契机；他的作品探讨了艺术和时尚领域的诸多有趣议题。《大街》是他最著名的作品，尽管一些评论家认为《巴比特》更胜一筹。《大街》出版时刘易斯已35岁，是一部畅销巨作，并被诺贝尔奖委员会列为他1930年荣获诺贝尔文学奖的重要原因之一。《大街》讲述了卡罗尔·肯尼科特的故事。小说第一章中，她从一所小型女子学院毕业，对未来抱有模糊的憧憬，希望有所成就或有所改变。经过一段漫长（但并不十分精彩）的恋爱后，她嫁给了小镇医生威尔·肯尼科特，并随他搬到了明尼苏达州的戈弗草原镇（原型是刘易斯的家乡索克中心）。她很快就对这座小镇和她在那里的生活感到不满，这部情节略显零散的小说描绘了她婚姻的变迁、她在戈弗草原镇的生活以及她青春的逝去。这部小说颇似成长小说，描写了一个年轻人经历一系列磨难后的成长历程，但卡罗尔的成长是在家庭环境中进行的，因此很难判断她究竟是成长了还是被生活击垮了。最终，尽管有所抗拒，她还是勉强同意了在戈弗草原的生活，但却并未完全接受。

Lewis is careful to present Carol as immature but well-meaning, an unreliable spokesperson for the valid idea that there is something more to life than bridge, something more to politics than voting the straight Republican ticket, and something more to human relationships than empty forms and eager gossip. He sets up her husband, Will, as her foil—he is steady and, on the surface, unimaginative. He defends the town and his friends there against her denigrating comments, though as the novel progresses, he softens in his insistence on having their marriage conform to a traditional model. Carol is ambivalent. She is moved by all forms of beauty, including that of the Minnesota landscape and that of a young man who comes to town as a tailor late in the novel and who courts her (she entertains his crush but doesn't concede her virtue). In fact, she has no consistent allies and no rational program, only feelings that sometimes offend her fellow citizens and sometimes are offended by them. She not only criticizes their aesthetic but also crosses social boundaries by maintaining a friendship with her housemaid and her housemaid's husband, a jack-of-all-trades who is a Communist sympathizer. Carol's fecklessness is believable and sometimes irritating, but the townspeople's general resistance to every form of nonconformity is also believable. Lewis perfectly renders the frequently nice and friendly narrow-minded prejudice of small-town America that is all the more difficult to combat because it is well-meaning and patriotic.

刘易斯刻意将卡罗尔塑造成一个不成熟但心地善良的女孩，她代表着一种不可靠的观点：生活不只有桥牌，政治不只有投共和党的票，人际关系也不只有空洞的形式和热衷的闲言碎语。他把卡罗尔的丈夫威尔塑造成她的反面——他稳重可靠，表面上却缺乏想象力。他维护小镇和朋友们，反驳卡罗尔的贬损之词，但随着小说的推进，他坚持让婚姻遵循传统模式的态度也逐渐软化。卡罗尔内心充满矛盾。她会被各种美所打动，包括明尼苏达州的风景，以及小说后半段来到镇上做裁缝的年轻男子的魅力（她接受了他的爱慕，但并未放弃贞洁）。事实上，她没有坚定的盟友，也没有理性的计划，只有一些情感，这些情感有时会冒犯她的同胞，有时又会被他们冒犯。她不仅批评他们的审美，还跨越了社会界限，与她的女佣及其丈夫——一个同情共产主义的杂工——保持着友谊。卡罗尔的轻浮不羁令人信服，有时甚至令人恼火，但镇民们对一切形式的异议的普遍抵制也同样合情合理。路易斯完美地刻画了美国小镇上那种看似和善却又狭隘的偏见，这种偏见往往出于好意和爱国情怀，因此更难与之抗争。

Lewis was a satirist, but his plots were realistic plots rather than fabulist ones, so an element of exuberance is missing in the novel, and the tone sometimes seems unclear. Satirists such as Swift often signal the reader that it is time to laugh at the characters by making them or their situations fantastic. Other satirists, such as Fielding, use a certain elevated language or comic tone to do the same thing, but Lewis was satiric without being overtly funny or comic, which means that the signals the reader is supposed to pick up are easily missed. He called himself a “scold,” and that was an appropriate characterization—his criticisms of American life are far from lighthearted. He manages to be intelligent and interesting and even hopeful; his characters are well drawn and lively. But his plots meander and his tone is unclear. His novels aren't well-made wholes, but nor are they shambling stylistic charmers. In their time they dealt with issues that Americans wanted to read about—small-town life, the mind of the businessman, revivalist religion—but when those issues seemed to fade in importance, so did Lewis's reputation.

刘易斯是一位讽刺作家，但他的情节是现实主义的而非寓言式的，因此小说中缺少一种欢快奔放的元素，语气有时也显得模糊不清。像斯威夫特这样的讽刺作家常常通过让人物或他们的处境变得奇幻来暗示读者该嘲笑他们了。其他一些讽刺作家，比如菲尔丁，则运用某种高雅的语言或喜剧化的语调来达到同样的效果，但刘易斯的讽刺并不刻意追求幽默或滑稽，这意味着读者很容易错过他想要传达的信号。他自称“爱唠叨的人”，这的确是一个贴切的形容——他对美国生活的批判绝非轻松诙谐。他笔下的人物睿智、有趣，甚至充满希望；他们形象鲜明生动。但他的情节略显散漫，语气也不够清晰。他的小说并非浑然一体，但也并非徒有其表的华丽辞藻。在他们生活的时代，他们关注的是美国人想读到的问题——小镇生活、商人的思想、复兴主义宗教——但当这些问题的重要性似乎逐渐减弱时，刘易斯的声誉也随之下降。

Lewis adhered to a strongly felt social theory that was basically leftist, and he wrote at a time when almost all writers were required to declare their allegiance to the right or the left, at least in America. In Main Street , Lewis's loyalties sometimes come across as simply a democratic sensibility, and therefore aesthetically acceptable, and sometimes as an outmoded and false-seeming program for building the utopia of the future. No novelist can quite escape the social theories of his time, and in fact must be drawn to them, because the novel is a social investigation. So to some extent the reputation of every novelist will rise and fall according to how his social theory holds up. For example, in the 1960s and ‘ 70s , the era of the new left, Dickens was considered well-meaning but naive; his “program” was thought to be poorly worked out and inconsistent—not Marxist enough (though Marx was a great fan of Dickens). After Marxism went out of fashion, Dickens's amorphous social critique came to seem more universally true because it was not programmatic but based on feelings of generosity and brotherhood combined with specific criticisms of practices common in England during his lifetime.

刘易斯坚持一种根深蒂固的左翼社会理论，而他写作的年代，几乎所有作家都被要求表明自己的政治立场，至少在美国是如此。在《大街》这部作品中，刘易斯的政治立场有时仅仅被视为一种民主情怀，因此在审美上是可以接受的；有时则被视为一种过时且看似虚假的未来乌托邦构想。任何小说家都无法完全摆脱时代的社会理论，事实上，他们必然会受到这些理论的影响，因为小说本身就是一种社会调查。因此，在某种程度上，每位小说家的声誉都会随着其社会理论的经受考验而起伏。例如，在20世纪60年代和70年代的新左翼时代，狄更斯被认为心地善良但天真；他的“纲领”被认为构思粗糙、前后矛盾——不够马克思主义（尽管马克思本人是狄更斯的忠实拥趸）。马克思主义过时之后，狄更斯模糊的社会批判似乎更具普遍性，因为它不是纲领性的，而是基于慷慨和博爱的情感，并结合了对他所处的时代英国常见做法的具体批判。

Novelists of a conservative or more purely aesthetic bent hold up better on the surface, but their novels go in and out of fashion according to relevance or irrelevance. Trollope, for example, in some eras seems interesting and in others trivial but not, like Dickens, right or wrong. Some novelists are luckier than others in the eras of their formative intellectual years, but all weltanschauungs return, which means that most novelists have at least a chance of a revival.

表面上看，倾向保守或更纯粹审美的作家往往更经得起时间的考验，但他们的作品会随着时代变迁而兴衰更替。例如，特罗洛普的作品在某些时代显得引人入胜，而在另一些时代则显得平庸乏味，但与狄更斯不同，他的作品并非非黑即白。有些作家在他们思想形成的关键时期比其他作家更幸运，但世界观终会轮回，这意味着大多数作家至少都有复兴的机会。

53. Sigrid Undset. Kristin Lavransdatter, vol. 1, The Wreath

53.西格丽德·温塞特。克里斯汀·拉夫兰斯达特，卷。 1、花环

TRANS. TIINA NUNNALLY (1920; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1997), 336 PP.

转运。 TIINA NUNNALLY（1920 年；纽约：企鹅出版社，1997 年），336 页。

Sigrid Undset, who won the Nobel Prize in literature in 1928 , went one way and modernism went another, but Kristin Lavransdatter holds up quite well in any number of ways, even compared with the more experimental works of Undset's contemporaries. Her portrait, in three volumes, of the whole life of a Norwegian woman of the fourteenth century could not have been written with such frankness before Undset's day, and probably would not have been written at all outside of Scandinavia. Undset's success in creating the illusion that we are reading about the Middle Ages as they actually were lived is striking. Her details are not only rich, they are also subtly presented rather than paraded ostentatiously before the reader; every bit of local color is worked into the plot or the character development or the thematic material. The Nunnally translation, too, is excellent—straightforward but also evocative, lyrical enough in places, but not, like earlier translations, overtly romantic or archaic.

1928年诺贝尔文学奖得主西格丽德·温塞特（Sigrid Undset）的创作方向与现代主义的发展方向截然不同，但《克里斯汀·拉夫兰斯多特》（Kristin Lavransdatter）这部作品在诸多方面都经得起时间的考验，即使与温塞特同时代更具实验性的作品相比也毫不逊色。这部三卷本的小说描绘了一位十四世纪挪威女性的一生，在温塞特之前，恐怕无人能如此坦诚地写出这样的故事，而在斯堪的纳维亚半岛以外的地方，这样的作品恐怕也根本不会出现。温塞特成功地营造了一种身临其境的中世纪生活体验，令人叹为观止。她笔下的细节不仅丰富，而且呈现得十分巧妙，而非刻意炫耀；每一丝地方色彩都巧妙地融入到情节、人物塑造和主题之中。 Nunnally 的译本也十分出色——直白易懂，又不失感染力，有些地方还颇具诗意，但又不像早期的译本那样过于浪漫或古旧。

Kristin is the beautiful daughter of an unlucky marriage between Lavrans Bjorgulfsson and his wife, Ragnfrid. For a long time she is their only surviving child. Three sons die in infancy, and Ragnfrid is a reserved and melancholy mother. The family lives on a prosperous estate in northern Norway, but there is some sense that Lavrans could have done more with his life, and that Ragnfrid is viewed with suspicion by the neighbors.

克里斯汀是拉夫兰斯·比约古尔夫松和妻子拉格弗里德不幸婚姻的结晶，她美丽动人。很长一段时间里，她是他们唯一的孩子。三个儿子夭折，拉格弗里德是一位性格内敛、忧郁的母亲。一家人住在挪威北部一处富裕的庄园里，但总觉得拉夫兰斯本可以成就一番事业，而拉格弗里德也受到邻居们的猜忌。

Two more daughters are born, but no sons. It appears that Kristin is destined to be married off in the usual fashion to a dull but good man of her own social class. But one evening she goes out to say farewell to a young man who has been her childhood friend, and on the way home, another local fellow attempts to rape her. The shame and disquiet that grow out of this episode (like every other episode, the subject of much gossip) lead Lavrans to send Kristin to a convent in Oslo as a student for a year, and there she falls passionately for a very well-born but unsuitable man. He seduces her, transforming her character and her social position and setting her at odds with everything she believes and everyone she loves.

又添了两个女儿，却没有儿子。克里斯汀似乎注定要像往常一样，嫁给一个平庸但品行端正、与她同阶层的男人。然而一天晚上，她外出与儿时好友告别，回家途中，却遭到当地男子的强奸未遂。这件事（如同其他所有事件一样，也成了人们茶余饭后的谈资）令她羞愧难当，心神不宁，拉夫兰斯只好将克里斯汀送到奥斯陆的一所修道院学习一年。在那里，她疯狂地爱上了一个出身高贵却与她格格不入的男人。他诱惑了她，彻底改变了她的性格和社会地位，使她与自己的一切信仰和所爱之人背道而驰。

So far, Kristin Lavransdatter is not unlike The House of Mirth or George Eliot's The Mill on the Floss except that Undset is more explicit about the workings of sexual passion than either Wharton or Eliot. Nor is Undset intimidated by the failure of Kristin's virtue, since she doesn't kill her off, as Wharton and Eliot kill off their protagonists. The shame is great, as Kristin herself knows, but to Undset, the hard work of redemption is more interesting than sacrifice, and she allows Kristin and her seducer, Erlend, to get married. Their marriage (they produce seven sons) is explored in volume 2 , The Wife , and Kristin's experiences as a widow during the Black Death are explored in volume 3 , The Cross.

到目前为止，《克里斯汀·拉夫兰斯达特》与《欢乐之家》或乔治·艾略特的《弗洛斯河上的磨坊》并无太大区别，只是温塞特对性欲的描写比沃顿和艾略特都更加直白。温塞特也并未因克里斯汀贞洁的丧失而退缩，她并没有像沃顿和艾略特那样让主人公死去。克里斯汀深知耻辱之深，但在温塞特看来，救赎的艰辛远比牺牲更有意思，因此她允许克里斯汀与诱惑她的厄兰结婚。他们的婚姻（他们育有七个儿子）在第二卷《妻子》中有所展现，而克里斯汀在黑死病肆虐期间作为寡妇的经历则在第三卷《十字架》中有所描绘。

Perhaps the biggest difference between Undset's protagonist and most other female protagonists is that she is never without work to do. Even though she is a member of the gentry and her father owns an estate, she spins and weaves and makes beer and sews and helps with the planting and the harvesting. In Norway, all hands work, so Kristin never wonders, as Lily Bart does, why she exists. The choices are two—marriage or the convent—and the obligations are many. Life is arduous in a way that is never true in novels about women of the middle and upper classes in France and England. Undset writes about work and weather and famine and accidents, illnesses, pregnancy, animals, and the natural world with immediacy and ease. Though Und-set, too, explores the classic conflict between female virtue and female desire, she sets it into the context of female usefulness. It is clear by the end of The Wreath that Erlend and his friends think Kristin is not only worth possessing as an object of beauty and property, they also think she is going to get things organized on his estate, and she thinks so, too, though she is barely seventeen years old. No heroine out of Trollope or James would ever aspire to such a life.

或许温塞特笔下的女主人公与其他大多数女性主人公最大的不同之处在于，她永远没有闲工可做。尽管她出身乡绅，父亲拥有庄园，她仍然纺纱织布、酿酒、缝纫，还要帮忙播种和收割。在挪威，人人都要劳动，所以克里斯汀不像莉莉·巴特那样会思考自己存在的意义。她的选择只有两条——结婚或进入修道院——而责任却有很多。生活艰辛，这与描写法国和英国中上层阶级女性的小说截然不同。温塞特以生动自然的笔触描写了工作、天气、饥荒、意外、疾病、怀孕、动物以及自然世界。虽然温塞特也探讨了女性美德与欲望之间的经典冲突，但她将其置于女性实用性的语境之中。在《花环》的结尾，很明显，厄兰和他的朋友们不仅认为克里斯汀是一位值得占有的美人和财产，他们还认为她会把他的庄园管理得井井有条，而克里斯汀自己也这么认为，尽管她才十七岁。特罗洛普或詹姆斯笔下的任何女主人公都不会渴望过这样的生活。

Undset was a great lover of the Icelandic sagas, and she learned more from them than just the details of the fourteenth-century lifestyle. An important convention of the Icelandic sagas is that small events have large ramifications. In Hrafnkels Saga , a servant's disobedience results, eventually, in a serious feud and the deaths of many men. Kristin Lavransdatter works in the same way. Lives are changed and fates are decided. The chain of cause and effect may go back to something as incidental as, in this novel, the escape of an imported panther from its cage and the subsequent panic that results in Kristin and her friend getting separated from their escort. This very tracing of cause and effect, this sense that one knowable thing leads to another, is where Undset parts from modernism (as exemplified by The Trial). Every detail of Kristin Lavransdatter is significant, because the author knows what every detail means and how they all fit together. This makes the novel a rich and satisfying read. What happens to Kristin is not happy, but it does have meaning that she is able to understand (and that reflects Undset's own belief system after her conversion to Catholicism). The world Undset creates for Kristin is full of senseless suffering, but those who suffer are given full instructions for how to endure their suffering and make something of it. Undset's world is frightening but coherent.

温塞特酷爱冰岛萨迦，她从中汲取的远不止十四世纪生活方式的细节。冰岛萨迦的一个重要特点是，小事往往能产生巨大的影响。在《赫拉夫克尔萨迦》中，一个仆人的不服从最终引发了一场严重的世仇，导致多人丧命。《克里斯汀·拉夫兰斯多特》也遵循着同样的规律。生活因此改变，命运也因此决定。因果链可以追溯到一些看似偶然的事件，比如小说中一只进口黑豹从笼中逃脱，引发恐慌，导致克里斯汀和她的朋友与护卫走散。正是这种对因果关系的追溯，这种“一个可知的事件会引发另一个事件”的感知，使温塞特与现代主义（如《审判》）分道扬镳。《克里斯汀·拉夫兰斯多特》中的每一个细节都至关重要，因为作者深谙每个细节的意义以及它们之间的联系。这使得这部小说引人入胜，令人回味无穷。克里斯汀的遭遇并不美好，但却蕴含着她能够理解的意义（这也反映了温塞特皈依天主教后的信仰体系）。温塞特为克里斯汀创造的世界充满了无意义的苦难，但那些受苦的人却被赋予了完整的指导，教他们如何忍受苦难并从中汲取力量。温塞特的世界令人恐惧，却又自洽。

Undset was a patient and painstaking novelist. In addition to the literary pleasures of her work, the reader finds as well an underlying sense of honor and a willingness to wrestle with moral questions as moral questions rather than as political questions or questions of perception. Her works are well worth reading and reviving.

温塞特是一位耐心而严谨的小说家。除了作品本身的文学魅力之外，读者还能感受到其中蕴含的荣誉感，以及她勇于直面道德问题的态度——她将道德问题视为真正的道德问题，而非政治问题或认知问题。她的作品非常值得阅读和重温。

54. James Joyce Ulysses

54. 詹姆斯·乔伊斯《尤利西斯》

(1921; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1990), 783 PP.

（1921 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1990 年），783 页。

Whether a reader enjoys or appreciates Ulysses or not, it is absolutely true that it is interesting because it demonstrates several things that happen when an author exploits to a logical extreme the possibilities inherent in every novel. Its story is fairly simple—two men, a young man of twenty-one named Stephen Dedalus (based on Joyce himself), and an older man of thirty-eight, named Leopold Bloom, pass a single day and night, June 16 , 1904 , in parallel, at first missing each other and later meeting up before Bloom returns to his home and the bed of his wife, Molly. Joyce bases his story loosely on The Odyssey , making Bloom an Odysseus (or Ulysses) figure, and Stephen a figure of Tele-machus, Odysseus’ son. A complicating factor in Bloom's day is that he knows that Molly is to be visited by a sexual rival, Blazes Boylan, while Bloom is away. A complicating factor in Stephen's day is that he is to be paid his monthly wages, and he will be tempted in a number of ways to dissipate his money, waste his time, and betray his talents.

无论读者是否喜欢或欣赏《尤利西斯》，不可否认的是，这部小说引人入胜之处在于它展现了当作者将小说中蕴含的各种可能性发挥到极致时会产生的种种效果。故事本身相当简单——两个男人，一个是21岁的年轻人斯蒂芬·迪达勒斯（原型是乔伊斯本人），另一个是38岁的老人利奥波德·布卢姆，在1904年6月16日这一天一夜里平行地生活着。起初两人互不相识，后来在布卢姆回到家，回到妻子莫莉的身边之前，他们终于相遇。乔伊斯的故事取材于《奥德赛》，布卢姆被塑造成奥德修斯（或尤利西斯）的化身，而斯蒂芬则被塑造成奥德修斯的儿子忒勒马科斯的化身。布卢姆这一天的复杂之处在于，他知道莫莉在他外出期间会受到情敌布莱兹·博伊兰的拜访。斯蒂芬一天中遇到的一个复杂因素是，他要领取每月工资，他会受到各种诱惑去挥霍金钱、浪费时间、辜负自己的才能。

The most obvious characteristic of Ulysses is its complex and, to some people (including me), forbidding variety of styles. Even the most straightforward chapters, such as chapters one and two, are not easy to follow the first time through, and several of the chapters require repeated rereadings and true dedication (as well as some sort of companion learning aid, such as a key or a set of taped lectures, which is what I chose). It is impossible to read Ulysses without paying attention to every word (some readers advocate not really paying attention at all, just sort of letting the prose wash over, but to me, at least, this method results quickly in boredom). Most devotees of Ulysses maintain that every word rewards attention and that the system thus created is uniquely rich (“life itself” is the common claim). Since every novel is, in fact, a system of words in which each could, in theory, relate to every other, a novel that forces the reader to pay attention word by word and to reread it until many or most of the possible connections emerge and stick in the memory, then the difficulty of Ulysses serves as gatekeeper, luring those with the capacity for full enjoyment, deterring those without it. Ulysses also requires the reader to judge for herself whether the tendency of prose to elaborate itself into an ever more complex linguistic system serves or detracts from other elements of the novel. For some readers, the difficulty of Ulysses’ style mitigates its emotional impacts; for others, the style enriches the emotional basis of the story. Because the style is so extreme, though, the novel can seem abstract and arid, or uniquely rich.

《尤利西斯》最显著的特点是其复杂多样的文风，对某些人（包括我）而言，这种文风甚至令人望而生畏。即使是最直白的章节，例如第一章和第二章，初读也并非易事，有好几章都需要反复阅读，并投入大量精力（还需要一些辅助学习资料，例如答案或录音讲座，而我正是选择了后者）。阅读《尤利西斯》时，必须逐字逐句地关注（有些读者主张完全不必关注，只需让文字自然流淌，但至少对我而言，这种方法很快就会让人感到厌倦）。大多数《尤利西斯》的拥趸都认为，每一个字都值得细细品味，由此构建的体系无比丰富（“人生本身”是他们普遍的赞誉）。事实上，每一部小说都是一个文字系统，理论上，其中的每一行文字都与其他文字有所关联。因此，如果一部小说迫使读者逐字逐句地阅读，并反复琢磨，直到大部分可能的关联浮现并铭记于心，那么《尤利西斯》的晦涩难懂便如同守门人一般，吸引那些能够充分领略其精髓的读者，同时又将那些能力不足的读者拒之门外。《尤利西斯》也要求读者自行判断，其散文不断演化成日益复杂的语言体系，究竟是提升还是削弱了小说的其他元素。对一些读者而言，《尤利西斯》风格的艰涩削弱了其情感冲击力；而对另一些读者而言，这种风格则丰富了故事的情感内涵。然而，正因为其风格如此极端，这部小说有时显得抽象枯燥，有时又显得独具魅力。

Joyce's main protagonist, Leopold Bloom, is not traditional. He does not do much in the course of the day except observe, and in fact one of the unusual things about him, in addition to the fact that he is a Jewish outsider in Dublin, is that he is an avowed voyeur. Joyce gives him lots of venial faults and also lots of excuses. On the one hand, he is portrayed as an ordinary man, with some talents but not many (not like Stephen, who is a literary genius in the making and a wonderful singer to boot), but then again, Bloom is not typical. He's kinder, more vulnerable, more knowledgeable, more long-suffering, more fastidious, and more self-doubting than the Dubliners around him. He is, in spite of his possibly unsavory sexual proclivities, a better person than those he meets, and he thereby raises the moral tone of those sexual proclivities.

乔伊斯笔下的主人公利奥波德·布卢姆并非传统意义上的人物。他终日无所事事，只是观察周围的一切。事实上，除了身为都柏林的犹太局外人之外，他最不寻常之处还在于他自称是个偷窥狂。乔伊斯赋予他诸多无关紧要的缺点，同时也为他提供了许多借口。一方面，他被描绘成一个普通人，拥有一些才能，但并不出众（不像斯蒂芬那样才华横溢，不仅是一位冉冉升起的文学天才，还是一位出色的歌手）；但另一方面，布卢姆又并非典型人物。他比周围的都柏林人更善良、更脆弱、更有学识、更能忍耐、更讲究，也更缺乏自信。尽管他可能有一些不太体面的性癖好，但他比他遇到的其他人都要高尚，因此，他提升了这些性癖好的道德意义。

Young Stephen is prickly, sensitive, and arrogant. He acts the part of a prodigal roysterer, and Bloom is moved, toward the end of the novel, to save him from himself, but in fact, Stephen seems too self-conscious to ever actually let himself go to the degree that Joyce seems to want the reader to accept. At least when he is sober, Stephen seems chary of being taken advantage of, or even of being denigrated in any way; it is not plausible that he would suffer a wastrel's fate. His view of himself is grandiose. He is convinced that his failure to kneel and pray at his mother's dying bedside is what killed her (even though she was dying of cancer). He recognizes the same lack of generosity in himself that the reader does, but he gives it a bigger name. The story seems to suggest that Bloom needs a son to care for and Stephen needs a father to care for him, at least on this one night in June 1904 , but the reader may have her own opinion about whether this emotional armature for this story is compelling. There is some sense that stylistic pyrotechnics hide what is essentially a sentimental yearning by Bloom that results in a sentimental gesture (he even suggests that Stephen marry his daughter Milly; Stephen declines).

年轻的斯蒂芬性格古怪、敏感又傲慢。他装出一副浪荡子的样子，小说临近结尾时，布鲁姆试图将他从自我放纵中拯救出来。但事实上，斯蒂芬似乎过于在意自己的形象，以至于永远无法像乔伊斯希望读者接受的那样彻底放纵自己。至少在清醒的时候，斯蒂芬似乎很在意被人占便宜，甚至害怕被人以任何方式贬低；他不太可能落得浪荡子的下场。他对自己的看法非常自大。他坚信，母亲临终前没有跪在床边祈祷是导致她死亡的原因（尽管母亲死于癌症）。他和读者一样，都意识到自己缺乏慷慨，但他却给这种缺乏慷慨赋予了更宏大的色彩。故事似乎暗示，布鲁姆需要一个儿子来照顾，而斯蒂芬需要一个父亲来照顾他，至少在1904年6月的那个夜晚是如此。但读者或许会对这种情感框架是否令人信服有自己的看法。某种程度上，华丽的文风掩盖了布鲁姆内心深处的感伤渴望，最终导致了他感伤的举动（他甚至建议斯蒂芬娶他的女儿米莉；斯蒂芬拒绝了）。

Molly Bloom, is, of course, famous as the woman with the very beautiful large breasts (according to Bloom's testimony) who says “yes.” We see her from a distance at the beginning of the novel, when Bloom prepares her breakfast for her, and then again at the end, when the novel winds up with her long, interior monologue. Bloom thinks about Molly all day. He buys her a few things, he recalls their first few times together, he meditates upon her with desire, fondness, and forgiveness. But there is no evidence that they actually relate in the sense that they share their thoughts, have ongoing discussions about anything, or are truly intimate. He remembers one time when she had expressed physical desire, and it was after looking out the window at a passing man. She is a figment of Bloom's imagination, a representative of many feelings he has, but she seems to be a stranger to him. She is thus an object of sentimentality as much as Stephen is, and the novel seems to have at its core Bloom's deep loneliness, a sadness so normal to him that Bloom himself doesn't recognize it, and, what's worse, it doesn't seem as though Joyce recognizes it, either. The stylistic fireworks come to seem like an elaborate surface distraction from what is missing at the core of the plot, that substitutes for the exploration of the dilemmas and crises of a real relationship (or two). When Molly engages in her own monologue, her view of their life together contradicts Bloom's in material ways. It is also significant that they are in the habit of lying to one another and suspecting one another. None of these issues is resolved by the end of the novel, no doubt because to resolve them in the course of a day when the members of the couple do not see one another would be implausible, so the novel ends up as a lengthy demonstration of the uncrossable (except by the author) abyss between men and women.

当然，莫莉·布鲁姆最出名的就是她那对男人说“我愿意”的美貌和丰满的胸部（据布鲁姆自己所说）。小说开头，我们远远地看到她，布鲁姆正在为她准备早餐；结尾，小说以她冗长的内心独白作结，我们再次见到她。布鲁姆整天都在想着莫莉。他给她买了一些东西，回忆起他们最初几次相处的情景，带着渴望、喜爱和宽恕的心情沉思着她。但没有任何证据表明他们之间有过真正的交流，比如分享彼此的想法，进行持续的讨论，或者真正亲密无间。他记得有一次她表达了生理上的渴望，那是在她望向窗外一个路过的男人之后。她是布鲁姆想象中的人物，代表了他内心诸多复杂的情感，但对他来说，她似乎是一个陌生人。因此，她和斯蒂芬一样，都是情感的寄托。小说的核心似乎在于布卢姆深深的孤独，这种悲伤对他来说如此习以为常，以至于他自己都意识不到，更糟糕的是，乔伊斯似乎也对此浑然不觉。华丽的文风最终沦为一种精心设计的表象，掩盖了情节核心的缺失，取代了对一段（或两段）真实关系中困境与危机的深入探讨。当莫莉进行独白时，她对他们共同生活的看法与布卢姆的看法在本质上截然相反。同样值得注意的是，他们习惯于互相欺骗和猜忌。小说结尾并没有解决这些问题，毫无疑问，因为要在夫妻俩一天之内解决这些问题是不现实的，所以小说最终变成了对男女之间（除了作者之外）无法跨越的鸿沟的冗长展示。

Molly's monologue is supposedly an interior one, but it demonstrates, I think, the limits of Joyce's conception of her. She uses many, many verbal expressions, such as “of course shes right,” “who did I get the last letter from,” and “its all very fine for them but as for being a woman.” If this is indeed meant to render her inner life, then she has completely internalized talking as a way of thinking. She reminds me of Flora Finching, a character in Dickens's Little Dorrit , who is well-meaning but pathologically garrulous, and whose inner life is continuously paraded in front of, and contrasted to, that of the more discreet and less comic characters. Supposedly Joyce's wife said that he did not understand women, and Molly's style is, I think, a rendition of a woman observed rather than seen into.

莫莉的独白本应是内心独白，但我认为它恰恰暴露了乔伊斯对她理解的局限性。她使用了大量的口头表达，比如“她当然是对的”、“我最后一封信是谁寄来的”、“对他们来说一切都很好，但身为女人就不好说了”。如果这真的是为了展现她的内心世界，那么她已经完全把说话内化成了一种思考方式。她让我想起了狄更斯《小多丽》中的弗洛拉·芬奇，一个心地善良却病态地喋喋不休的角色，她的内心世界不断地被展现出来，并与那些更谨慎、不那么滑稽的角色形成对比。据说乔伊斯的妻子曾说过他不了解女人，而我认为，莫莉的风格是对一个被观察的女性的刻画，而不是对她的深入理解。

Joyce befriended and helped Italo Svevo, who wrote Zeno's Conscience. Ulysses and Zeno's Conscience form an interesting contrast, because Zeno is nearly as self-involved as Stephen and nearly as neurotic as Bloom, but one of the satisfying aspects of Svevo's novel is the solid sense of the presence of Zeno's wife as an intelligence that meets and matches his own rather than as a symbolic location in his mind.

乔伊斯与伊塔洛·斯韦沃结为好友并给予他帮助，后者创作了《泽诺的良心》。《尤利西斯》和《泽诺的良心》形成了有趣的对比，因为泽诺几乎和斯蒂芬一样自我中心，几乎和布卢姆一样神经质，但斯韦沃的小说令人满意之处在于，它真实地展现了泽诺妻子的存在，她拥有与泽诺自身智慧相契合的智慧，而不仅仅是泽诺脑海中的一个象征性场所。

Since every novel is also a social and historical document, Joyce exploits this possibility to the full, too. Bloom and Stephen perambulate around Dublin, filming the life of the city, both close-up and wide-angle, for some twenty hours. June 16 , 1904 , is an ordinary day, a representative day in the life of the Irish, more or less peaceful, more or less prosperous, perfectly contemporary, and one of Joyce's points is that an epic portrayal of life in Ireland must capture the ordinary with the seriousness and detail that are possible only through the deployment of many styles and forms (one lengthy section is written as a play). The reader has to find the depiction of Dublin life appealing, I think, to find it worth the effort.

由于每部小说同时也是一份社会和历史文献，乔伊斯也充分利用了这种可能性。布卢姆和斯蒂芬在都柏林漫步，用近景和广角镜头拍摄了这座城市的生活，时长约二十小时。1904年6月16日是普通的一天，是爱尔兰人生活中具有代表性的一天，或多或少地和平，或多或少地繁荣，完全符合当时的时代特征。乔伊斯想要表达的观点之一是，对爱尔兰生活的史诗式描绘必须以严肃和细致的态度捕捉平凡的日常，而这只有通过运用多种风格和形式才能实现（其中有一大段是以戏剧的形式写成的）。我认为，读者必须觉得对都柏林生活的描绘引人入胜，才会觉得这部作品值得一读。

Is Ulysses the ultimate novel? Yes, in two or three ways mentioned above. It is also the ultimate novel in another way—it cannot be judged at all except by the individual reader. It is either to one's taste or not, and no amount of lobbying by readers with other tastes can change one's mind.

《尤利西斯》是终极小说吗？是的，从前面提到的两三个方面来看，的确如此。但它在另一个方面也是终极小说——它只能由读者个人来评判。它要么符合你的口味，要么不符合，其他读者的游说也无法改变你的想法。

55. Italo SvevoZeno's Conscience

55. 伊塔洛·斯韦沃·泽诺的良心

TRANS. WILLIAM WEAVER
(1923; REPR., NEW YORK: VINTAGE INTERNATIONAL, 2001), 437 PP.

威廉·韦弗译（1923 年；纽约：Vintage International，2001 年再版），437 页。

“Italo Svevo” was the pen name of Ettore Schmitz, a well-to-do businessman who was educated as an Austrian and a German but who lived in Trieste and wrote in Italian (even though he says that the dialect of Trieste was his native tongue and that “with our every Tuscan word, we lie… by predilection, we recount all the things for which we have the words at hand, and… avoid those things that would oblige us to turn to the dictionary!” (p. 404 ). Zeno's Conscience was published when Svevo was sixty-two years old, and to his delight, it became much celebrated. He remarked to a friend, “Until last year, I was the… least ambitious old man in the world. Now I am overcome by ambition. I have become eager for praise. I now live only to manage my own glory.”

“伊塔洛·斯韦沃”是埃托雷·施密茨的笔名，他是一位富裕的商人，接受过奥地利和德国的教育，但居住在的里雅斯特，并用意大利语写作（尽管他声称的里雅斯特方言才是他的母语，并且“我们说的每一个托斯卡纳语单词都是谎言……出于偏好，我们总是把所有我们手头有词汇可查的事情都写出来，而……则避开那些需要我们查字典的事情！”（第404页）。《芝诺的良心》出版时，斯韦沃已经六十二岁了，令他欣喜的是，这本书大获成功。他曾对一位朋友说：“直到去年，我还是……世界上最没野心的老人。现在我却被野心冲昏了头脑。我渴望赞扬。我现在活着只是为了成就自己的荣耀。”

∗ Quoted in the introduction of the Weaver translation, p. xxi.

* 引自 Weaver 译本的引言，第 xxi 页。

The novel purports to be the journal of a man undergoing psychoanalysis, written at the behest of the analyst, and then published by the analyst to embarrass his patient and avenge his termination of the analysis. Zeno tells five interrelated stories: the story of his last attempt to quit smoking cigarettes, the story of the death of his father, the story of his marriage, the story of his mistress, and the story of his doomed business partnership with the husband of his wife's sister. Zeno's narrative style is plain and even ingenuous. He tells each story straightforwardly. But as the novel progresses, its themes, along with Zeno's feelings, get complicated. Zeno acts—the complications do not paralyze him—but he becomes more and more unsure of the meaning and the rightness of his actions until the last chapter, where he contemplates his psychoanalysis and decides that his doctor's very attempt to cure him is wrongheaded and that the images and memories the doctor wants to do away with are the ones Zeno himself cherishes the most. At one point he remarks, “I believe that he is the only one in this world who, hearing I wanted to go to bed with two beautiful women, would ask himself: Now let's see why this man wants to go to bed with them” (p. 413 ).

这部小说表面上是一位接受精神分析治疗的男子的日记，由分析师授意撰写，后又由分析师出版，目的是为了羞辱病人，并报复他终止了治疗。泽诺讲述了五个相互关联的故事：他最后一次戒烟的尝试、父亲的去世、他的婚姻、他的情妇，以及他与妻子的姐夫那注定失败的商业合作。泽诺的叙述风格朴实无华，甚至有些天真。他直截了当地讲述了每个故事。但随着小说的推进，其主题以及泽诺的内心感受都变得复杂起来。泽诺仍在行动——这些复杂情况并没有让他动摇——但他越来越不确定自己行为的意义和正确性，直到最后一章，他反思了自己的精神分析，并最终意识到医生试图治愈他的做法是错误的，医生想要抹去的那些画面和记忆，恰恰是泽诺自己最珍视的。他曾说过：“我相信他是世界上唯一一个听到我想和两个漂亮女人上床后会问自己：现在让我们看看这个人为什么想和她们上床”的人。（第 413 页）

Confessions are difficult to pull off, because, as Zeno himself says, “A confession in writing is always a lie” (p. 404 ), but a novel that takes the form of a confession doesn't have to be true, it only has to be alluring or intriguing, and Zeno's voice is both. His avowed motives are simple: to tell what happened and why. His actions don't speak well of Zeno. He is deceitful, lustful, envious, impulsive, lazy, and easily distracted. But in fact, major sins like these are often acceptable to readers because they make for an interesting narrative. Zeno is honest and generous. He seems to be telling the truth, at least to himself and the reader, even if not to his wife and his friends. And even though he deceives his friends, he almost always speaks well of them. Such generosity in a narrator (who is simultaneously speaking ill of himself) is appealing.

坦白很难写得好，正如泽诺自己所说，“书面忏悔永远是谎言”（第404页），但以忏悔形式呈现的小说不必真实，只需引人入胜或耐人寻味即可，而泽诺的声音恰好兼具两者。他坦白的动机很简单：讲述发生了什么以及为什么。他的行为并不光彩。他狡诈、好色、嫉妒、冲动、懒惰且容易分心。但事实上，像这样的重罪往往能被读者接受，因为它们构成了一个引人入胜的故事。泽诺诚实而慷慨。他似乎在说真话，至少对自己和读者而言如此，即使对他的妻子和朋友并非如此。尽管他欺骗了朋友，但他几乎总是对他们赞不绝口。这种慷慨体现在一个（同时也在贬低自己的）叙述者身上，令人着迷。

The five stories have some surprising twists. The story of his marriage is the best one—he begins visiting the house of a businessman he is fond of and discovers four daughters, all of whose names begin with “A” and all of whom have reputations for beauty. He promises himself that he will marry one of the beautiful daughters, but one turns out to be too young; one has “a squint” (which I take to mean strabismus); one wants a career instead of a husband; and the fourth one, the eligible one with whom he falls in love, can't stand him. He ends up with the exact sister he had vowed never to take, and as soon as they are engaged, he is filled with unexpected happiness. They have a very satisfying marriage, at least in part because he tells her about everything (except the mistress) and she trusts him. Admittedly, by modern American standards this is an odd marriage, but in comparison with the other marriages in the novel, it is companionable and mutually loving, and the reader has the feeling that if Augusta, Zeno's wife, withholds judgment, then the reader might as well do so, too.

这五个故事都有一些出人意料的转折。其中最精彩的是关于他婚姻的故事——他开始拜访一位他心仪的商人的家，发现他家有四个女儿，名字都以字母“A”开头，而且个个都以美貌著称。他暗下决心要娶其中一个，但一个年纪太小；一个“有点斜视”（我理解为斜视）；一个只想着事业而不是结婚；而第四个，也就是他爱上的那个条件优越的女孩，却对他恨之入骨。最终，他娶到了他发誓绝不娶的那个女孩，两人订婚后，他感到无比幸福。他们的婚姻非常美满，至少部分原因是他什么都跟她说（除了情妇的事），而她也信任他。诚然，按照现代美国的标准来看，这是一段奇怪的婚姻，但与小说中的其他婚姻相比，这段婚姻充满伴侣情谊，彼此相爱。读者会觉得，如果泽诺的妻子奥古斯塔都不愿妄加评判，那么读者自己也最好不要妄加评判。

Another aspect of Zeno's charm is that while he is more than a little feckless, he is also quite observant. Above all, he observes the paradoxes of human behavior, both his own and that of others. At one point he is asked to help someone he knows cannot be helped because the man won't take responsibility for his own affairs. Zeno says, “If I had been calmer, I would have spoken to her of my inadequacy for the task she was assigning me, but I would have destroyed all the unforgettable emotion of that moment. In my case, I was so moved that I had no sense of my inadequacy. At that moment, I thought no inadequacies existed for anyone” (p. 345 ). Zeno is always doing something unreasonable, quixotic, even self-destructive just because he enjoys the largeness of the feelings involved.

芝诺魅力的另一面在于，他虽然有些不负责任，却也观察力敏锐。尤其擅长洞察人类行为的悖论，包括他自己的和他人的。有一次，有人请他去帮助一个他明知无力回天的人，因为那人不愿为自己的事情负责。芝诺说：“如果我当时更冷静些，我就会告诉她我能力不足，无法胜任她交给我的任务，但那样一来，我就会抹杀那一刻所有难忘的情感。当时我太激动了，完全没有意识到自己的不足。那一刻，我觉得任何人都没有不足之处。”（第345页）芝诺总是做一些不理智的、异想天开的，甚至是自毁式的事情，仅仅因为他享受那种强烈的情感体验。

Zeno's retrospection brings him to 1915 , in the First World War. He sends his family to Tuscany and waits out the dangers of the war by himself in Trieste. By this time he has told his story in detail and also has pondered the requirements of psychoanalysis. He considers introspection, war, memory, health, and sickness and comes up with a remarkable peroration that casts a lyrical and reflective light backward over the whole novel and makes something profound of its apparently simple materials. I think it is justly celebrated, and forms, with The Trial and Ulysses , a trio of orthodox modernism wherein the consciousness of the passage of time and the parsing of consciousness itself are more important than the story or the plot elements. Zeno's Conscience is the Italian version, with recognizably Boccaccio-like elements of wives, mistresses, business, speculation, trickery, and sex that Ulysses and The Trial have less of, or have in a less shameless way. Perhaps it was inevitable that Boccaccio would meet Freud and that Boccaccio would win.

泽诺的回溯将他带到了1915年，第一次世界大战期间。他将家人送往托斯卡纳，自己则独自一人在的里雅斯特躲避战争的危险。此时，他已详细地讲述了自己的故事，也认真思考了精神分析的要求。他审视了内省、战争、记忆、健康和疾病，并写出了一段非凡的结尾独白，这段独白以抒情而反思的笔触回溯了整部小说，将看似简单的素材升华为深刻的内涵。我认为它所受到的赞誉实至名归，它与《审判》和《尤利西斯》一起，构成了正统现代主义的三部曲，在这三部作品中，对时间流逝的意识和对意识本身的剖析比故事或情节元素更为重要。 《芝诺的良心》是意大利版本，其中包含许多博卡乔式的元素，例如妻子、情妇、商业、投机、诡计和性，而《尤利西斯》和《审判》中这些元素较少，或者说处理得不那么露骨。或许博卡乔与弗洛伊德相遇，并且博卡乔最终胜出，是命中注定的。

56. E. M. Forster A Passage to India

56. E·M·福斯特《印度之行》

(1924; REPR., SAN DIEGO, CALIF.: HARCOURT BRACE JOVANOVICH, 1965), 322 PP.

（1924 年；重印，加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥：哈考特·布雷斯·乔万诺维奇出版社，1965 年），322 页。

A Passage to India is a good example of a novel that, as a result of history, lost and then regained the potency of its ideas. In 2005 it is far less outmoded than it may have seemed in 1955 , only a few years after Indian independence and partition. The keys to the novel's persistent currency are partly to be found in it—Forster's consistently personal (as opposed to institutional) focus and his exceptionally graceful style—and partly to be found outside it. Can Westerners, Muslims, and Hindus communicate across religious, cultural, and political boundaries? With American and English soldiers and officials once again trying to shape Eastern cultures to their own specifications, Forster's insights into how members of each society misread and read into each other's statements and actions are both timely and depressing.

《印度之行》堪称一部因历史变迁而一度失去其思想力量，后又重获力量的小说典范。2005年，它远比1955年——印度独立和印巴分治仅仅几年后——时显得更有时代感。这部小说经久不衰的关键，一部分在于其自身——福斯特始终坚持以个人视角（而非制度视角）进行叙述，以及他格外优雅的文风——一部分则在于其外部。西方人、穆斯林和印度教徒能否跨越宗教、文化和政治的界限进行有效沟通？当美国和英国的士兵及官员再次试图按照自身意愿塑造东方文化时，福斯特对不同社会成员如何误解和曲解彼此言行的深刻洞察，既切合时宜，又令人沮丧。

Forster tells the story of Dr. Aziz, about forty, who works in a hospital in a part of India governed directly by the English. One evening, he is visiting his local mosque when he happens upon an elderly Englishwoman, Mrs. Moore, who has recently come out to India to visit her son, a low-level government official, and to bring his propective fiance, Miss Quested. Aziz is at first offended to find an Englishwoman in the mosque, but when he realizes that she has behaved respectfully, and when she is effortlessly friendly toward him, he warms up, and after some negotiations, he offers to take Mrs. Moore, Miss Quested, and some others to visit local caves. Something unaccountable happens at the Marabar caves, and Miss Quested flees, later to accuse Aziz of molesting her. The English colony is outraged, and the accusation and subsequent trial turn into a political scandal. Forster's sympathies lie with Aziz and with Fielding, a teacher who dislikes his fellow countrymen and tries to live a more cosmopolitan life than the other officials. Miss Quested, who is confused but well intentioned, goes along with the legal machinery of the trial, but she has her doubts about what actually happened. At the trial she recants her accusation, throwing both sides into confusion and incurring the enmity of everyone. Individual doubts and second thoughts result in further conflicts and bitterness, and by the end of the novel each of the characters has been thwarted in his or her attempts to connect genuinely with the others.

福斯特讲述了阿齐兹医生的故事，他大约四十岁，在英国直辖印度的一家医院工作。一天晚上，他去当地的清真寺做礼拜，偶然遇到一位年长的英国妇女，摩尔夫人。摩尔夫人最近来到印度探望她的儿子——一位低级政府官员，并带来了他未来的未婚妻奎斯特小姐。阿齐兹起初对在清真寺里见到一位英国妇女感到不悦，但当他意识到摩尔夫人举止得体，并且对他非常友好时，他的态度有所缓和。经过一番交谈，他提出带摩尔夫人、奎斯特小姐和其他一些人去参观当地的洞穴。在马拉巴尔洞穴，发生了一件无法解释的事情，奎斯特小姐逃走了，后来指控阿齐兹性骚扰了她。英国殖民地对此感到愤怒，这起指控和随后的审判演变成了一场政治丑闻。福斯特同情阿齐兹和菲尔丁，菲尔丁是一位教师，他厌恶自己的同胞，并试图过一种比其他官员更加国际化的生活。奎斯特小姐虽然心地善良，但内心却很困惑，她顺从了审判的法律程序，但她对事情的真相却心存疑虑。在审判中，她撤回了自己的指控，这让双方都陷入了混乱，也招致了所有人的敌意。个人的疑虑和反复思考导致了更多的冲突和怨恨，到了小说结尾，每个人物都因无法与他人建立真正的联系而受挫。

From the beginning of the novel Forster limits his portrait of India to personal relationships and subjective experiences. The narrator's voice draws back from the characters mostly to depict the natural world—the stars or the caves or the rains. Each character is both an individual and a self-conscious representative of his or her group, but only insofar as he or she experiences it. For all of the characters, this self-consciousness causes a greater or lesser degree of defensiveness, irritability, and shame, but no one can imagine a different set of circumstances—the English seem to be in India to stay, and whatever any one person does or feels is rendered false by that evident and apparently permanent fact. The “realists” at the officials’ compound are crude and philistine in their opinions, but the idealists, such as Miss Quested and Mrs. Moore, come to grief as well.

从小说伊始，福斯特便将他对印度的描绘局限于人际关系和主观体验。叙述者的视角大多远离人物，转而描绘自然世界——星辰、洞穴或雨水。每个人物既是独立的个体，也是其所属群体的自觉代表，但这种代表仅限于其自身的体验。对于所有人物而言，这种自觉性都导致他们或多或少地产生防御、易怒和羞耻感，但没有人能够想象另一种境况——英国人似乎注定要留在印度，任何人的所作所为或所感所受，都会被这一显而易见且看似永恒的事实所否定。官员们的“现实主义者”观点粗俗庸俗，而像奎斯特小姐和摩尔太太这样的理想主义者，最终也难逃厄运。

A Passage to India is simultaneously profound and narrow because Forster eschews as a narrator what might be called the authoritative voice. The voice he does use recognizes that for the time being, it is enough to pose the problem without even implying or hoping that the problem can be resolved. Instead of guiding the reader toward a solution—that is, subtly or not so subtly advocating one policy or another—both the plot and the narrator guide the reader away from a solution. Each time a solution, even a sense of relief, seems imminent, the possibility explodes. For example, when Mrs. Moore, now despairing and ill, persuades her son to send her back to England, and a cabin and an escort are miraculously produced at the last minute, she dies in transit and has to be buried at sea. When Fielding persuades Aziz not to accept the penalty Miss Quested is supposed to pay, Aziz becomes convinced that Fielding means to marry Miss Quested and keep the money for himself. Only at the end, at a Hindu festival that none of the characters really understands, do the principals begin to be reconciled, but even when they do begin, the moment is followed by the recognition that full reconciliation is impossible. Forster demonstrates that the imposition of tyranny, even for the best motives by decent people, unfailingly distorts true feelings and relationships and requires ambivalence and double-dealing.

《印度之行》既深刻又狭隘，因为福斯特作为叙述者，摒弃了所谓的权威语气。他所使用的语气表明，就目前而言，仅仅提出问题就足够了，甚至无需暗示或期待问题能够得到解决。情节和叙述者并没有引导读者走向解决方案——也就是说，没有委婉或直白地倡导某种政策——而是引导读者远离解决方案。每当解决方案，哪怕只是一丝解脱的曙光，这种可能性都会瞬间破灭。例如，当绝望且身患重病的摩尔太太说服儿子送她回英国，并在最后一刻奇迹般地安排好了船舱和护卫时，她却在途中去世，不得不海葬。当菲尔丁说服阿齐兹不要替奎斯特小姐支付罚款时，阿齐兹却认定菲尔丁打算娶奎斯特小姐，并将这笔钱据为己有。直到结尾，在一个所有角色都难以理解的印度教节日上，主人公们才开始和解。然而，即便如此，他们很快意识到，彻底和解已不可能。福斯特以此表明，即使是出于好意，由正直之人实施的暴政，也必然会扭曲真实的情感和关系，并导致矛盾和欺骗。

Nevertheless, Forster's style is so elegant and smooth and his tone so apparently light that the novel is far from tragic, but rather infused with the sensibility of Professor Godbole, an enigmatic Hindu Brahman to whom both Aziz and Fielding are drawn but can't make sense of. The final section of the novel takes place at a yearly festival of the rebirth of Krishna. This is the most extended scene in the novel, and Forster carefully describes the town, the temple, and the rituals. But he also makes sure that the Western reader knows that none of these add up in the way Christians and Muslims would expect them to, and indeed that their meaning contradicts all ideas of “adding up.” Just as Hindu folk religion has, earlier in the novel, taken up the name of Mrs. Moore as “Esmiss Esmoor” and made of her a minor deity, now the larger moral implications of friendship and subjection, good and evil, are muddied and lost in the variegated complexity of the whole picture. Most novels, of course, express the idea that nothing is as it seems, but this one offers the idea that “is” and “seems” are interchangeable terms.

然而，福斯特的文风如此优雅流畅，语调又如此轻松，以至于这部小说远非悲剧，反而弥漫着戈德博尔教授的特质——这位神秘的印度教婆罗门，阿齐兹和菲尔丁都被他吸引，却又无法理解。小说的最后一部分发生在一年一度的克里希纳重生节上。这是小说中篇幅最长的场景，福斯特细致地描绘了小镇、寺庙和各种仪式。但他同时也确保西方读者明白，这一切的逻辑并非基督教徒和穆斯林所预期的那样，事实上，它们的意义与所有“逻辑”的概念都背道而驰。正如小说前面提到的，印度民间宗教将摩尔夫人的名字称为“埃斯米斯·埃斯莫尔”，并将她奉为一位次要神祇一样，如今，友谊与臣服、善与恶等更深层次的道德含义，也淹没在整幅图景的纷繁复杂之中。当然，大多数小说都表达了“眼见未必为实”的观点，但这部小说却提出了“是”和“看起来”是可以互换的术语的观点。

And yet, because Forster's voice is so specific, clear, and conversational, the reader is never confused about the action or the characters. One of the main assertions of the novel as a form is that the personal is political (as with Pamela) , but few authors have quite the ability that Forster has of making every character's most idle action represent both his psychology and his sociology. My guess is that he focused on the psychology and let the sociology write itself out of the fraught political atmosphere he found when he went to India in the early 1920s . The result is that even though many of the larger political issues of Anglo India were “solved” after the Second World War, A Passage to India remains profound because the deeper issues surrounding Western power and colonialism and its aftermath simply shifted to other areas of conflict. The novel, as a form, is about connection. By focusing on that very thing, Forster in some sense defies history itself.

然而，由于福斯特的叙述风格如此鲜明、清晰且对话式，读者对情节和人物始终不会感到困惑。小说作为一种文体，其主要论点之一是个人即政治（如《帕梅拉》一书），但鲜有作家能像福斯特那样，将每个人物最不起眼的举动都巧妙地融入其心理和社会学层面。我猜测，他专注于心理层面，而让社会学层面自然而然地从他20世纪20年代初前往印度时所感受到的紧张政治氛围中流露出来。因此，尽管英属印度的许多重大政治问题在二战后得到了“解决”，《印度之行》依然意义深远，因为围绕西方强权、殖民主义及其后果的更深层次问题只是转移到了其他冲突领域。小说作为一种文体，其核心在于联结。通过聚焦于此，福斯特在某种意义上挑战了历史本身。

But any novel written by a white man about colonialized people is suspect to some readers, because the author can only more or less successfully infer thoughts, motives, ideas, and values from characters who are unlike him. The novelist's only tools in his portrayals are observation, ideas, and a reader's willing suspension of disbelief. Ideas, of course, are often suspect, since most historical periods generate ideas that later seem wrong. If those ideas are egregiously self-aggrandizing, as many English ideas about Indians were, they become highly unsympathetic as times change. Most ideas later seem silly, but some of them seem harmless, such as Balzac's ideas about physiology, and some of them seem harmful, such as Victorian ideas about the nature of women and Conrad's ideas about Africa as expressed in Heart of Darkness.

但任何由白人作家创作的关于被殖民者的长篇小说，都会让一些读者心生疑虑，因为作者只能或多或少地从与自己截然不同的角色身上推断出他们的思想、动机、观念和价值观。小说家在刻画人物时，唯一的工具就是观察、想象，以及读者愿意暂时放下怀疑。当然，思想本身也常常令人怀疑，因为大多数历史时期都会产生一些后来看来是错误的观念。如果这些观念带有极度的自我吹捧色彩，就像许多英国人对印度人的看法那样，那么随着时代的变迁，它们就会变得令人反感。大多数观念后来都显得荒谬可笑，但有些观念似乎无伤大雅，例如巴尔扎克关于生理学的观点；而有些观念则似乎有害，例如维多利亚时代关于女性本质的观点，以及康拉德在《黑暗之心》中对非洲的描绘。

It isn't enough to point out that “for his time” an author was enlightened (that is, like us); relative enlightenment is good enough for a social document but not for an enduring work of art. Forster, I think, comes pretty close to being actually enlightened, even though here and there the voice of the narrator makes some generalization about Indians that probably would not bear scrutiny. What Forster does quite skillfully is deploy the special qualities of the novel to bolster his depictions. The first of these is giving each character good and bad moral traits as well as attractive and unattractive personality traits. This makes the characters seem rounded, and readers instinctively believe that mixed characters are more true than vicious or virtuous ones. The second of these is giving each character a degree of agency so that he or she seems realistically responsible for what he or she does. Aziz is the victim of British injustice and prejudice, but his own vanities and insecurities feed into the events that lead to his arrest, and these events are evident to the reader. Forster's focus on small moments and social occasions serves him, too, because his objection to the British is not that they rule India, or are bad rulers, but that they are rude and unkind— the reader is hardly allowed to reflect to what degree these are characteristics of culture, personality, or political structure; it is enough that she is offended, and therefore agrees with Forster's basic premise of shared humanity, as expressed by Mrs. Moore. Since the novel is always a social occasion, a reader is always offended by social transgressions even though she might not be by other antisocial plot occasions, such as murder. Forster's fourth claim to immortality is the precision of his observations. A long sequence of small, precise, and convincing observations gracefully and clearly expressed gives the reader a habit of complicity with the author that is hard to break if some small observation offends—the next small and perfect observation might make up for it.

仅仅指出一位作家“在他所处的时代”思想开明（也就是说，像我们一样）是不够的；相对的开明对于社会文献来说足够了，但对于一部不朽的艺术作品来说则远远不够。我认为福斯特的作品非常接近于真正的开明，尽管叙述者偶尔会对印度人做出一些可能经不起推敲的概括性描述。福斯特的精妙之处在于，他巧妙地运用小说本身的特性来强化人物刻画。首先，他赋予每个角色善恶并存的道德品质，以及讨喜和不讨喜的性格特征。这使得人物形象更加丰满，读者也会本能地认为，性格复杂的人物比纯粹的恶人或美德之人更加真实可信。其次，他赋予每个角色一定程度的自主性，使他们能够为自己的行为承担起应有的责任。阿齐兹是英国不公正和偏见的受害者，但他自身的虚荣心和不安全感也促成了最终导致他被捕的事件，而这些事件对读者来说是显而易见的。福斯特对细微瞬间和社交场合的关注也为他自己所用，因为他反对英国人并非因为他们统治印度或他们是昏庸的统治者，而是因为他们粗鲁无礼——读者几乎无暇思考这些特质在多大程度上源于文化、人格或政治结构；读者只需感到被冒犯，便认同了福斯特关于人类共通性的基本前提，正如摩尔夫人所表达的那样。由于小说始终围绕着社交场合展开，读者总是会对社会越轨行为感到冒犯，即便她可能不会对其他反社会情节（例如谋杀）感到反感。福斯特不朽的第四个原因在于他观察的精准。一系列细致、精准且令人信服的观察，以优雅清晰的语言表达出来，使读者与作者之间形成了一种默契，即使某个细微的观察冒犯了读者，这种默契也很难打破——下一个细微而完美的观察或许就能弥补这一点。

This is not to say that every reader willingly suspends disbelief in A Passage to India , only that Forster makes excellent use of the peculiarities of the novel to prolong the life of its apparent historical truth. Other novels of the period, such as The Great Gatsby or Main Street , do not seem to illuminate our own time nearly as cogently.

这并非意味着每位读者都会心甘情愿地接受《印度之行》中的种种不实之处，而是说福斯特巧妙地运用小说的独特之处，延长了其表面上的历史真实性的生命力。同时期的其他小说，例如《了不起的盖茨比》或《大街》，似乎都无法如此有力地揭示我们当今的时代。

57. F. Scott Fitzgerald. The Great Gatsby

57. F·斯科特·菲茨杰拉德，《了不起的盖茨比》

(NEW YORK: CHARLES SCRIBNER'S SONS, 1925), 194 PP.

（纽约：查尔斯·斯克里布纳之子出版社，1925 年），194 页。

It is hard to read The Great Gatsby with a fresh eye, not only because it is a famous novel by a famous author, but also because, along with his characters, Fitzgerald's observations and phrases have become so much a part of the way Americans think of themselves. The novel is also a principal American entrant into the pantheon of world greatness, so it bears the burden of universal critical acclaim.

很难用全新的视角去阅读《了不起的盖茨比》，不仅因为它是著名作家创作的名著，更因为菲茨杰拉德的观察和语句，连同他笔下的人物，早已深深融入美国人的自我认知之中。这部小说也是美国跻身世界文学殿堂的重要作品，因此也背负着举世公认的赞誉。

Most Americans are familiar with the story. Jay Gatsby, a man of vast wealth, mysteriously appears in a fashionable town on Long Island and begins throwing fabulous parties to which everyone comes, not because they have been invited or know the host, but just because everyone else is there. As our narrator, Nick Carraway, comes to know Gatsby, however, he learns that Gatsby has two secrets—that he is in love with Nick's cousin, Daisy, who is married to an unpleasant man named Tom, and that Gatsby's apparent wealth comes from questionable investments and gangster connections. When Gatsby reveals himself to Daisy, she at first resumes their five-year-old romance, but Tom quickly reasserts his power over her. Then, during a drive from New York to Long Island, Gatsby's car is involved in a hit-and-run accident in which Tom's mistress, Myrtle, is coincidentally killed. Myrtle's husband then finds Gatsby and kills him, afterward shooting himself. Gatsby has told Nick that Daisy had been driving the car, but this crime is covered up and Tom and Daisy famously “retreat… back into their money or their vast carelessness, or whatever it was that kept them together, and let other people clean up the mess they had made…” (p. 188 ). In the meantime, Nick arranges Gatsby's funeral, to which no one comes. Sound implausible?

大多数美国人都熟悉这个故事。杰伊·盖茨比，一个拥有巨额财富的男人，神秘地出现在长岛一个时尚小镇，开始举办奢华的派对。每个人都来参加，并非因为他们受邀或认识主人，而是因为大家都来了。然而，随着叙述者尼克·卡拉威逐渐了解盖茨比，他发现盖茨比有两个秘密：他爱上了尼克的表妹黛西，而黛西嫁给了一个名叫汤姆的令人厌恶的男人；盖茨比的财富表面上来源于可疑的投资和黑帮关系。当盖茨比向黛西表明身份时，黛西起初重拾了他们五年前的恋情，但汤姆很快又重新掌控了她。之后，在从纽约开车前往长岛的途中，盖茨比的车发生了一起肇事逃逸事故，汤姆的情妇默特尔不幸遇难。默特尔的丈夫随后找到了盖茨比，杀死了他，然后开枪自杀。盖茨比告诉尼克，是黛西开的车，但这件事被掩盖了，汤姆和黛西最终“退回到他们的金钱或他们漫不经心的生活，或者其他什么维系着他们的东西里，让别人来收拾他们造成的烂摊子……”（第188页）。与此同时，尼克安排了盖茨比的葬礼，却无人前来。听起来难以置信？

I have to admit that I don't care as much for The Great Gatsby as many people do. I think it should have been a hundred pages longer and that Fitzgerald should have developed the characters and their relationships more meticulously and in more detail. As it is, each character has only a few scenes, and those are mostly short. Once the author elaborately introduces each character, they do not develop or change as a result of the action, they only reveal their true natures, and their true natures are shallow. This is especially true of Daisy. Even Gatsby is disappointed in her; when he finds her again, it takes him only an hour or two to realize she is not what he thought she was. Nick admits that he can't describe her particular charm—it is in her voice or her face, but he doesn't actually describe either one, he merely tries to capture in a couple of phrases the impression her face and her voice give. Tom's signal quality is that he is threatening; Gatsby's, that he is romantic; Nick's, that he is honest; Daisy's, that she is strangely desirable. But Fitzgerald doesn't build these personalities so that they are truly convincing, by showing them to us action by incremental action. For scenes and dialogue he substitutes his own aphoristic style (rendered by Nick Carraway). Some of it is apt and smart, but much of it is sentimental and even nonsensical. The problem is that the tone of the novel is bittersweet before the action has earned the right to be bittersweet. Nick is already elegiac before anything is lost. A good comparison can be made to Zeno. Zeno is straightforward and occasionally ironic until the reader comes to know what has been lost and what Zeno feels about it; only then does Svevo allow his narrator to wax lyrical. A good example of Fitzgerald's sort of mistake takes place in the first two pages. The novel opens with the line, “In my younger and more vulnerable years, my father gave me some advice that I've been turning over in my mind ever since.

我必须承认，我并不像许多人那样喜欢《了不起的盖茨比》。我认为它应该再长一百页，菲茨杰拉德应该更细致、更深入地刻画人物及其关系。现在，每个人物都只有寥寥几个场景，而且大多都很短。作者精心介绍每个人物之后，他们并没有因为情节发展而有所成长或改变，只是展现了他们肤浅的本性。黛西尤其如此。就连盖茨比也对她感到失望；当他再次见到她时，只过了一两个小时就意识到她并非他想象中的那样。尼克承认他无法描述她独特的魅力——或许在于她的声音或容貌，但他并没有真正描述它们，只是试图用寥寥数语捕捉她容貌和声音所给人的印象。汤姆的显著特征是他的威胁性；盖茨比的显著特征是他的浪漫；尼克的显著特征是他的诚实。黛西身上有一种奇特的魅力。但菲茨杰拉德并没有通过循序渐进的行动来塑造这些人物，使他们真正令人信服。他用自己独特的格言式风格（由尼克·卡拉威演绎）来代替场景和对话。其中一些格言恰如其分，颇具智慧，但大部分却矫揉造作，甚至荒谬可笑。问题在于，小说的基调在情节尚未发展到足以令人感到苦乐参半的地步之前就已经呈现出了。尼克在失去任何东西之前就已经陷入了哀悼之中。这可以与泽诺相提并论。泽诺的叙述直白坦率，偶尔带有讽刺意味，直到读者了解了失去的是什么以及泽诺对此的感受；只有到了那时，斯韦沃才允许他的叙述者抒情地表达情感。菲茨杰拉德的这种错误在小说的前两页就有所体现。小说以这样一句话开篇：“在我年轻而脆弱的岁月里，父亲给了我一些建议，我至今仍在反复思考。”

“‘Whenever you feel like criticizing anyone,’ he told me, ‘just remember that all the people in this world haven't had the advantages that you've had.’” On the next page Nick rephrases the advice: “I am still a little afraid of missing something if I forget that, as my father snobbishly suggested, and I snobbishly repeat, a sense of the fundamental decencies is parcelled out unequally at birth.” Whether these two ideas are related is unclear. They seem not to be. Fitzgerald should have been aware that they are not the same, and he should have developed his argument beyond these flashy phrases to make it clear. The same is true of his last observation: “So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past” (p. 197 ). The image is lyrical and paradoxical but it doesn't really make sense.

“‘每当你想要批评别人的时候，’他告诉我，‘记住，这世上并非所有人都拥有你所拥有的优势。’”在下一页，尼克重述了这条建议：“我仍然有点害怕，如果我忘记了这一点——正如我父亲势利地暗示过，我也势利地重复一遍——那么，对基本礼仪的感知在出生时就并非人人平等地分配，我会错过一些东西。”这两个观点是否相关尚不清楚。它们似乎无关。菲茨杰拉德应该意识到它们并不相同，他应该超越这些华丽的辞藻，进一步阐述他的论点，使其更加清晰。他的最后一段话也是如此：“于是我们奋力前行，逆流而上，却不断地被推回过去”（第197页）。这个意象充满诗意和悖论，但实际上却难以理解。

What is Fitzgerald arguing for? The only way in which Gatsby is great is that he has devoted himself to an illusion and given up every virtue except the virtue of style to attain it. The illusion is not precisely Daisy, but rather the class that Daisy seemed to embody, with its comfort and elegance. We know that he doesn't actually honor Daisy from a dropped remark about their earlier interlude—that he seduced her or, as Nick says, “took her” before they were married or even engaged, and then didn't contact her because he wasn't wealthy yet, and he didn't want her without the wealth. Nick is skeptical of the sort of illusion Gatsby is susceptible to from the beginning (because he went to college and also has known Tom for a while), but for some reason he respects Gatsby for not being as skeptical as he is. This is a vividly written novel of a very young man (Fitzgerald was twenty-nine when it was published). It is not the wisdom of the ages. All the qualities of youth are present in the novel—snap judgments about others, overblown emotions, sharp observations about surfaces, self-doubt, self-hatred, and a lack of insight into women—plus considerable promise, of course—but I don't think it is careful enough, wise enough, or well enough thought through to be a masterpiece.

菲茨杰拉德究竟想表达什么？盖茨比之所以伟大，唯一的原因在于他全身心投入到一个幻象之中，为了实现这个幻象，他放弃了除优雅之外的一切美德。这个幻象并非指黛西本人，而是指黛西所代表的那个阶层，以及那个阶层的舒适与优雅。我们从他无意间提及的两人早年的邂逅中得知，他其实并不尊重黛西——他引诱了她，或者如尼克所说，“占有了她”，那时他们甚至还没结婚或订婚，之后他便不再联系她，因为他当时还不富有，他不想在没有财富的情况下拥有她。尼克从一开始就对盖茨比容易陷入的那种幻象持怀疑态度（因为他上过大学，而且认识汤姆也有一段时间了），但不知为何，他敬佩盖茨比不像他那样充满怀疑。这是一部笔触生动的小说，出自一位非常年轻的作家之手（菲茨杰拉德出版此书时年仅29岁）。它并非什么经得起时间考验的智慧箴言。小说中展现了所有年轻人的特质——对他人妄下断言、情绪过激、对表面现象的敏锐观察、自我怀疑、自我厌恶以及对女性缺乏洞察力——当然，还有相当大的潜力——但我认为它不够谨慎、不够睿智、不够深思熟虑，不足以成为一部杰作。

58. Franz Kafka The Tria

58. 弗朗茨·卡夫卡《三部曲》

TRANS. BREON MITCHELL (NEW YORK: SCHOCKEN BOOKS, 1925), 231 PP.

转运。布伦·米切尔（纽约：SCHOCKEN BOOKS，1925 年），231 页。

The Trial was published after Kafka's death by his friend Max Brod, who defied Kafka's own expressed wish that all of his papers and manuscripts be burned. Although Brod was right to save and publish his friend's work, thereby furnishing the twentieth century with its most uncannily truthful voice, it is also easy to understand why Kafka might have wanted to keep his work private. What is new in Kafka's work is an astonishing degree of intimacy and honesty—what is utterly original in fiction is always more private than what is original in other forms, because it is uncircumscribed by conventions (like poetry) or the presence of other people (like drama and movies). What makes novels public are traditional themes and stories: Will the boy and the girl get together at last? Will the husband be cuckolded? Will the individuals be reconciled to their communities? But Kafka's works have no traditional stories and so possess a much smaller public dimension. Reading Kafka's work can seem like no less an intrusion upon him than reading his diaries. His protagonists, often full of shame, also seem shameless in their readiness to confess their shames.

《审判》是卡夫卡去世后由他的朋友马克斯·布罗德出版的。布罗德违背了卡夫卡生前希望焚毁所有手稿的遗愿。尽管布罗德保存并出版了好友的作品，为二十世纪贡献了最令人震惊的真诚之声，这固然是正确的，但我们也很容易理解卡夫卡为何希望将作品保密。卡夫卡作品的新颖之处在于其惊人的私密性和坦诚——小说中真正原创的东西总是比其他形式的原创更具私密性，因为它不受传统（如诗歌）或他人存在（如戏剧和电影）的束缚。小说之所以具有公共性，是因为它们包含传统的主题和故事：男孩和女孩最终会在一起吗？丈夫会被戴绿帽吗？个人最终会与他们的社群和解吗？但卡夫卡的作品没有这些传统的故事，因此其公共性也小得多。阅读卡夫卡的作品，似乎与阅读他的日记一样，都是对他的一种侵犯。他笔下的主人公，往往充满羞耻感，却又毫不掩饰地坦白自己的羞耻。

In the opening chapter of The Trial , Josef K., a bank manager in his twenties in some central European city, is arrested for an unknown crime by authorities whose jurisdiction he doesn't recognize. In the course of the novel, he solicits help and advice from all sorts of associates, but their advice is contradictory and untrustworthy, and everything he learns about the court and the law system he is attempting to deal with indicates to him that the court is strict, arbitrary, senseless, and merciless. Finally (and Kafka himself did not finish the manuscript—it was found after his death and published in a somewhat patched-together form) Josef K. is killed by the side of the road, anonymously and, to all appearances, meaninglessly. Most Kafka protagonists suffer a similar fate—Gregor Samsa, who is turned into a bug, dies and gets thrown on a dust heap. The hunger artist loses his commercial value, dies of starvation, and is replaced by a much more crowd-pleasing panther. For Josef K, and all the others, though, the “process” (Der Prozess is The Trial's German title) of affliction, judgment, and guilt takes place as much within the mind as it does between the protagonist and the authorities. Its primary effect is to make him painfully self-conscious, so that he second-guesses his every action and intention, trying to decide what will work and whether he can justify his life, trying to decide, in fact, what is true or real and what is guilty projection.

在《审判》的开篇，约瑟夫·K，一位二十多岁的银行经理，在中欧某座城市里，因莫须有的罪名被他并不认可的执法部门逮捕。在小说中，他向形形色色的伙伴寻求帮助和建议，但他们的建议却自相矛盾、不可信赖。他对法庭和法律体系的了解，都让他觉得法庭严苛、专断、荒谬且冷酷无情。最终（卡夫卡本人并未完成这部手稿——它是在他去世后才被发现，并以略显残缺的形式出版的），约瑟夫·K被无辜地、毫无意义地杀害在路边。卡夫卡笔下的大多数主人公都遭遇了类似的命运——格里高尔·萨姆沙变成了一只虫子，最终死去，被扔进了垃圾堆；饥饿艺术家失去了商业价值，死于饥饿，取而代之的是一只更受大众欢迎的黑豹。然而，对于约瑟夫·K以及所有其他人来说，痛苦、审判和罪责的“过程”（《审判》的德语标题为《Der Prozess》）不仅发生在主人公与当局之间，也同样发生在他们的内心。它的主要作用是让他痛苦地自我怀疑，以至于他会反复斟酌自己的每一个行动和意图，试图决定什么会奏效，能否证明自己的人生是正当的，实际上，他试图分辨什么是真相，什么是罪恶的投射。

With his characteristic brilliance, Kafka, who was from Prague, focuses completely on Josef K.'s experience of his ordeal, and, most important, he tells a lively tale. Every Kafka story is dynamic and entertaining—in fact, Kafka himself is said to have found his stories to be tremendous fun when he read them aloud. His ability to keep the action moving forward not only encourages the reader to suspend disbelief but also seduces the reader into taking the narrative on the author's terms. While telling his story, Kafka makes no allusion to whatever analogous situations the reader may perceive—to arbitrary governments, to the judgment of God or religion (Kafka was Jewish), to the operation of guilt itself, to neurosis. The tight narrative focus quickly begins to accumulate symbolic power that more casual narratives cannot achieve. Most novelists give both sides of an analogy, for example. George Eliot does it best—on the one hand we have a character or a feeling or an event—let's say Mr. Casaubon. On the other we have the groping animal that Mr. Casaubon is like, and thus Mr. Casaubon's character is illuminated. With Kafka we have only the groping animal. We may link it to whatever or whomever we like. The groping animal does not illuminate merely a single character; we are not invited to relate it to a single character's individual quirks. The animal illuminates life itself, the nature of groping itself, which, after we think about it, turns out to be universal.

卡夫卡是布拉格人，他以其特有的才华，将笔触完全聚焦于约瑟夫·K的磨难经历，更重要的是，他讲述了一个生动的故事。卡夫卡的每一篇故事都充满活力，引人入胜——事实上，据说卡夫卡本人在朗读自己的故事时也觉得妙趣横生。他推动情节发展的能力不仅促使读者暂时放下怀疑，也引导读者按照作者的视角来理解叙事。在讲述故事的过程中，卡夫卡没有提及读者可能感知到的任何类似情境——无论是专断的政府、上帝或宗教的审判（卡夫卡是犹太人）、罪恶感本身，还是神经症。这种紧凑的叙事焦点迅速积累起象征意义，这是其他更随意的叙事方式所无法企及的。例如，大多数小说家都会同时呈现类比的两面。乔治·艾略特在这方面做得最好——一方面，我们有一个人物、一种感觉或一个事件——比如说卡索邦先生。另一方面，卡索邦先生就像一只摸索的动物，卡索邦先生的形象由此得以展现。而在卡夫卡的作品中，我们只有这只摸索的动物。我们可以把它与任何事物或任何人联系起来。这只摸索的动物并非仅仅照亮某个人物；我们并非被引导去将它与某个人物的个人怪癖联系起来。这只动物照亮了生命本身，照亮了摸索的本质，而当我们思考之后，会发现这本质是普遍存在的。

It is common for readers to wonder if a particularly original novelist is sane or insane, and to look into his life for evidence one way or the other. Evidence of some sort of mental condition (for example, Dosto-evsky's epilepsy or Fitzgerald's alcoholism) can come to color a reader's attitude toward whether the work is genuninely profound or visionary. Sometimes this comes up with Kafka, but his perfect logic, the evenness of his tone, his exquisite German style, and his knack for keeping the action moving forward make him seem transcendentally sane, so the question is thereby cast back into the world—if Kafka's protagonist makes so much sense in the way he tells his story, then it must be the court, or the family, or the town that is insane, and in fact the twentieth century itself seemed to prove this to be true. At the beginning of the twenty-first century it's hard to remember that while Kafka may have intuited much of what was latent in the world he lived in (he died in 1924 ), he didn't actually foresee what was to come.

读者常常会怀疑一位极具原创性的小说家究竟是神智清醒还是精神失常，并试图探究其生平以寻找佐证。某种精神疾病的迹象（例如陀思妥耶夫斯基的癫痫或菲茨杰拉德的酗酒）会影响读者对作品是否真正深刻或富有远见的看法。有时，卡夫卡也会出现这种情况，但他完美的逻辑、平和的语调、精妙的德语文风以及推动情节发展的技巧，都使他显得超然物外，因此，这个问题又回到了现实世界——如果卡夫卡的主人公以如此合乎逻辑的方式讲述故事，那么一定是法庭、家庭或城镇出了问题。事实上，二十世纪似乎也印证了这一点。二十一世纪初，人们很难想起，虽然卡夫卡可能预见到了他所生活的世界中潜藏的许多事物（他于 1924 年去世），但他实际上并没有预见到未来会发生什么。

Nevertheless, Kafka is a good example of the astute way in which some novelists seem to see patterns and movements in the world that others do not see. Such insight contributes, of course, to the lasting fascination their work arouses in generations of readers. The Trial must be read not only through the lens of the Holocaust, but also that of all the show trials and oppressive, arbitrary legal systems that the nations of the world imposed upon their citizens throughout the twentieth century. The details were different but the experience is the same: What do I do? Do I laugh or cry? Do I remove myself or engage? Is the legal system ridiculous or cruel, inhumane or only too evidently human? Am I a fool to think there is any possible outcome other than execution? Can this really be the world I live in? Part of Kafka's genius was that in his willingness to throw off conventional subjects and narrative modes, he concentrated more clearly on his intuitions. As a result, his “private” experience of his world turned out to be not only uniquely intimate but also uniquely subtle, insightful, and fascinating.

然而，卡夫卡很好地展现了某些小说家敏锐的洞察力，他们似乎能洞察他人所忽略的世界模式和动向。这种洞察力无疑有助于他们的作品在几代读者心中激起持久的吸引力。《审判》不仅要从大屠杀的角度来解读，还要从二十世纪世界各国强加于其公民的种种作秀审判和压迫性、专断的法律体系的角度来解读。细节虽有不同，但体验却如出一辙：我该怎么办？我该笑还是该哭？我该置身事外还是该参与其中？这套法律体系是荒谬可笑还是残酷无情，是毫无人性还是仅仅是人性的一部分？我是否愚蠢地认为除了死刑之外还有其他可能的结果？这真的是我生活的世界吗？卡夫卡的天才之处在于，他勇于摆脱传统的题材和叙事模式，从而更加清晰地聚焦于自己的直觉。因此，他对世界的“私人”体验不仅独特而私密，而且独特而微妙、深刻、引人入胜。

59. Hermann Broch The Sleepwalkers

59. 赫尔曼·布洛赫《梦游者》

TRANS. WILLA AND EDWIN MUIR
(1926; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1996), 648 PP.

威拉和埃德温·缪尔译（1926 年；纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1996 年再版），648 页。

The Sleepwalkers is another monument of modernism, which in some ways can be defined as the reaction of ambitious novelists to the breakdown of European culture that seemed to result from the First World War. Broch, like Sholokhov, attempted to address the subject of the war directly (showing individuals taking sides, trying to figure things out, suffering, being destroyed, and surviving) rather than indirectly (depicting individuals outside of the war through the shared but unexplored lens of the war, such as Joyce and Svevo). Like the other modernists, Broch found that he had to break up and remake the traditional form of the realist novel to begin to communicate what he wanted to say about his world, and, as with other modernist novels, this very disintegration of form has become a historical artifact. The First World War and even the Second World War no longer mean what they once did. The much-heralded end of rationality, or end of civilization, or even of consciousness, of course did not arrive with the transmutation of Europe from several warlike, armed mini-empires into the postcolonial European Union.

《梦游者》是现代主义的又一里程碑，从某种意义上说，现代主义可以被定义为雄心勃勃的小说家们对第一次世界大战后欧洲文化崩溃的一种回应。布罗赫与肖洛霍夫一样，试图直接探讨战争主题（展现人物选边站队、努力理解局势、遭受苦难、被摧毁以及最终幸存），而不是像乔伊斯和斯韦沃那样，通过战争这一共同却未被深入探讨的视角来描绘战争之外的人物。与其他现代主义作家一样，布罗赫发现他必须打破并重塑现实主义小说的传统形式，才能开始传达他想要表达的关于他所处世界的信息。而与其他现代主义小说一样，这种形式的解构本身也成为了历史的遗迹。第一次世界大战乃至第二次世界大战的意义已不再如昔。当然，人们大肆宣扬的理性终结、文明终结，甚至是意识终结，并没有随着欧洲从几个好战的武装小帝国转变为后殖民时代的欧盟而到来。

The Sleepwalkers concerns the convergence of three men of different generations and classes. Von Pasenow is the first, a hereditary Prussian aristocrat and career soldier whose marital and social fates are set by the end of the first novel, when his father, who both frightens and repels him, marries him off to the daughter of wealthy neighbors, and the two estates are united (the old happy ending translated into an unsavory and calculating piece of business that in spite of Pasenow's sexual queasiness does result in offspring). The second is Esch, twenty years younger, who is an up-and-coming urban bookkeeper at the beginning of the twentieth century. Esch is impetuous and volatile. Like Pasenow, he suffers from sexual uneasiness, which in his case is a combination of attraction and repulsion to the older maternal proprietress of the cafeteria he frequents. He can't stay away from her, but he beats her and repeatedly rapes her (which she allows, or seems to expect, as if the properest form of intercourse requires the woman to become as passive as possible).

《梦游者》讲述了三个不同世代、不同阶层的男人相遇的故事。冯·帕塞诺夫是第一个，他是普鲁士的世袭贵族，也是一名职业军人。在第一部小说的结尾，他的婚姻和社会命运就已经注定：他的父亲——既令他恐惧又令他厌恶——将他嫁给了富裕邻居的女儿，两个庄园也因此合并（传统的幸福结局被扭曲成一场令人不齿、充满算计的交易，尽管帕塞诺夫内心充满性压抑，但最终还是有了孩子）。第二个是埃施，比帕塞诺夫小二十岁，是二十世纪初一位冉冉升起的城市簿记员。埃施性情急躁，喜怒无常。和帕塞诺夫一样，他也饱受性方面的困扰，只不过他对经常光顾的那家咖啡馆里年长的女老板既有吸引力又有排斥感。他无法远离她，但他殴打她并反复强奸她（她默许了，或者似乎期待着，仿佛最恰当的性交方式要求女性尽可能地被动）。

In fact, The Sleepwalkers is a perfect Freudian gallery of various sublimated erotic dysfunctions that seem to be imposed upon the protagonists by the rigidity of the society they live in. Broch is exceptional at characterizing how each of his protagonists and several minor characters experience themselves and project those sensations onto the world around them. Both Pasenow and Esch suffer from a streak of hysterical overreaction to small things, which grow disproportionately large and distorted. For example, during Pasenow's interview with his prospective bride, her face stops looking like a face and starts looking like a landscape, which frightens and repels him. Later, Esch becomes convinced that his old boss has committed a crime and should be reported to the authorities. This conviction continues to weigh upon him through most of his section of the novel, even though it is apparent to the reader that the root of Esch's conviction is simply resentment at being fired.

事实上，《梦游者》堪称弗洛伊德式情欲障碍的完美体现，书中展现了各种被压抑的性欲障碍，这些障碍似乎是主人公们所处社会僵化体制强加于他们的。布洛赫极其擅长刻画每个主人公以及一些次要角色如何体验自我，并将这些感受投射到周围的世界。帕塞诺和埃施都患有一种歇斯底里的过度反应，这种反应往往对小事过度放大，最终扭曲变形。例如，在帕塞诺与未婚妻面谈时，她的脸不再像一张脸，而变成了一幅风景，这让他感到恐惧和厌恶。后来，埃施坚信他的前老板犯了罪，应该被举报给当局。这种信念贯穿了小说的大部分篇幅，尽管读者很清楚，埃施信念的根源仅仅是对被解雇的怨恨。

As with Kafka and Robert Musil, the protagonists’ most essential relationships seem to be with the state rather than with other people. If we contrast the German novelists with, say, Anthony Trollope, who was the English novelist who wrote most directly about government (in the Palliser novels, whose characters actually do govern England), it is striking to note that the average German citizen (or rather, citizen of the Austro-Hungarian Empire) feels the impersonal state as a palpable personal presence he must think about and relate to as much as or more than he relates to wives or children (though mothers and particularly fathers are often overwhelming and oppressive when they occur in the narrative). In the German novel, government is a sense of inescapable authority present in every mind; in the English novel, even the prime minister hardly has a relationship to the state at all—his relationships are to particular allies or functionaries or social arbiters. Government, in Trollope, is reduced to a network of friendship and influence much like any other English social network.

与卡夫卡和罗伯特·穆齐尔一样，这些小说家笔下主人公最重要的关系似乎在于国家而非其他人。如果我们把这些德国小说家与安东尼·特罗洛普——这位英国小说家对政府的描写最为直接（例如在帕利泽系列小说中，人物实际上统治着英国）——进行对比，就会发现，普通的德国公民（或者更确切地说，是奥匈帝国的公民）会将冷漠的国家视为一种切实存在的、必须认真思考和与之相处的实体，其重要性甚至超过了对妻子或子女的关注（尽管在叙事中，母亲，尤其是父亲，往往是令人难以承受和压迫的）。在德国小说中，政府是一种存在于每个人心中、无法逃避的权威感；而在英国小说中，即使是首相也几乎与国家没有任何关系——他与特定的盟友、官员或社会仲裁者建立关系。在特罗洛普的笔下，政府被简化为一个由友谊和影响力构成的网络，就像任何其他英国社会网络一样。

The third volume of The Sleepwalkers brings Esch and Pasenow together and subjects them to Huguenau, who is twenty years younger than Esch (about thirty when the volume begins, in 1918 ). Huguenau is Alsatian and Catholic; he speaks French. He is represented by contrast to his elders as having few sexual feelings at all, and as being of a purely commercial and mercenary bent. Huguenau doesn't mind hurting others if he has the chance, whereas Pasenow is afraid to hurt others and Esch hurts others only for the sake of a higher good. Huguenau is the most competent of the three—he successfully deserts the army (breaking off his relationship to the government and to all moral authority) by watching for an opportunity and having a sharp sense of timing. After he arrives in Esch's town, he uses the same instincts to take over Esch's newspaper and make himself a prominent citizen. But even though he has severed his relationship with authority, he cannot resist soliciting the attention of the town commandant (Pasenow) and attempting to achieve some sort of father/son relationship with him. Pasenow, now representing the remnants of decency, is much put off and tries to avoid the younger man. After Huguenau rapes Frau Esch and murders Esch, he engineers his escape and goes back to his home city, where he becomes a prosperous entrepreneur, husband, father, and solid citizen who never gives another thought to his crimes or betrayals. He epitomizes the amoral modern man who buys low and sells high no matter what else is going on.

《梦游者》第三卷将埃施和帕塞诺夫联系在一起，并让他们与比埃施小二十岁的休格瑙接触（故事开始时，即1918年，休格瑙大约三十岁）。休格瑙是阿尔萨斯人，信奉天主教，讲法语。与两位前辈形成鲜明对比的是，他几乎没有性欲，而且完全出于商业和唯利是图的动机。休格瑙不介意有机会就伤害他人，而帕塞诺夫害怕伤害他人，埃施则只有在为了更高的利益时才会伤害他人。休格瑙是三人中最有能力的——他凭借敏锐的洞察力和对时机的把握，成功地从军队逃脱（切断了与政府和所有道德权威的联系）。来到埃施的小镇后，他利用同样的本能接管了埃施的报社，并让自己成为当地一位显赫的人物。尽管他已与权威决裂，却仍忍不住博取镇长（帕塞诺夫）的关注，试图与他建立某种父子般的关系。帕塞诺夫如今代表着残存的良知，对此十分反感，并尽量避开这个年轻人。在休格瑙强奸了埃施夫人并杀害了埃施之后，他精心策划逃脱，回到家乡，成为一名成功的企业家、丈夫、父亲和正直的公民，对自己的罪行和背叛毫不在意。他堪称现代社会中那种不择手段、低买高卖的典型代表，无论世事如何变迁，他都毫不在乎。

Broch was not a happy novelist. He preferred philosophy to fiction, and he interpolates a philosophical essay supposedly written by one of the minor characters into the novel. In the essay he makes explicit and universalizes the arguments that his characters are meant to demonstrate. At one point he also writes the narrative of the three men as a drama, and he sometimes uses poetry to communicate certain ideas that prose is not intense enough for. The philosophical sections of the novel now seem dated, but are made relevant in the novel by the narrative sections, which, because of Broch's skills in character drawing, psychology, dialogue, and even plotting, hardly seem dated at all. Broch is an incisive stylist, similar to Robert Musil but without his dry wit, though bolder in his willingness to grapple with the events of the war itself rather than to imply them.
