布罗赫并非一位快乐的小说家。他更偏爱哲学而非虚构，甚至在小说中插入了一篇据称由一位次要人物撰写的哲学论文。在这篇论文中，他明确阐述并普遍化了小说人物旨在论证的观点。他一度将这三位主人公的故事写成戏剧，有时还会运用诗歌来传达散文难以充分表达的某些思想。如今看来，小说中的哲学部分略显过时，但由于叙事部分的出色表现，这些哲学部分在小说中依然具有现实意义。而叙事部分则因其精湛的人物刻画、心理描写、对话以及情节安排技巧，几乎丝毫没有过时之感。布罗赫的文风犀利，与罗伯特·穆齐尔相似，但少了穆齐尔的冷幽默，不过他更敢于直面战争本身，而非仅仅暗示战争。

Pasenow and Esch have what we would probably call mental illnesses—Pasenow seems to be obsessive-compulsive, and Esch seems to suffer from hyperactivity and attention deficit disorder accompanied by oppositional-defiant disorder. Huguenau is recognizable, too— antisocial personality disorder—though even today, people are divided about whether this is a mental illness, a spiritual fault, or simply a form of evil. Does the end of European civilization produce or result from the widespread occurrence of such mental conditions? In his philosophical sections, Broch traces the sources of his characters’ mental dysfunctions to the Reformation and the rise of Protestant individualism—Huguenau represents a Max Weber sort of figure, who is good at business because he feels no human connections. But the reader is, of course, free to disagree with the philosopher, and to make other cause-and-effect connections, because Pasenow, Esch, Huguenau, and the minor figures live more vividly as characters than as representatives of a philosophical system.

帕塞诺和埃施患有我们通常所说的精神疾病——帕塞诺似乎有强迫症，而埃施则似乎患有多动症和注意力缺陷障碍，并伴有对立违抗性障碍。休格瑙的情况也很明显——反社会人格障碍——尽管即使在今天，人们对于这究竟是精神疾病、精神缺陷，还是仅仅是一种邪恶，仍然存在分歧。欧洲文明的终结是造成还是导致此类精神疾病普遍存在？在哲学部分，布罗赫将笔下人物的精神障碍根源追溯到宗教改革和新教个人主义的兴起——休格瑙代表了马克斯·韦伯式的人物，他之所以擅长经商，是因为他感受不到人际关系。但读者当然可以不同意这位哲学家的观点，并建立其他的因果联系，因为帕塞诺、埃施、休格瑙以及其他次要人物作为人物本身比作为某种哲学体系的代表更加鲜活生动。

60. Marcel Proust. In Search of Lost Time

60. 马塞尔·普鲁斯特，《追忆似水年华》

vol. 1, Swann's Way;

第 1 卷，《斯万之路》；

vol. 2, Within a Budding Grove;

第 2 卷，在萌芽的树林中；

vol. 3, The Guermantes Way;

第 3 卷，盖尔芒特之路；

vol. 4, Sodom and Gomorrah;

第 4 卷，所多玛和蛾摩拉；

vol. 5, The Captive;

第 5 卷，俘虏；

vol. 6, The Fugitive;

第 6 卷，《逃亡者》；

vol. 7, Time Regained

第7卷，《夺回的时间》

TRANS. C. K. SCOTT MONCRIEFF, TERENCE KILMARTIN, ANDREAS MAYOR, AND D. J. ENRIGHT
(NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, MODERN LIBRARY, 1913-27), 4,200 PP.

C. K. SCOTT MONCRIEFF、TERENCE KILMARTIN、ANDREAS MAYOR 和 D. J. ENRIGHT 译（纽约：兰登书屋，现代文库，1913-27 年），4,200 页。

In many ways, In Search of Lost Time is the most extreme example of what can be done with the novel form. It is almost six times the length of Ulysses , five times the length of Our Mutual Friend. It is as ambitious as The Man without Qualities and was essentially complete at the time of the author's death. It is truly a lengthy written prose narrative with a protagonist. In terms of theme, plot, characters, style, and time scheme, it is both cohesive and coherent; easy to read in the course of a summer or a winter; and, for some aficionados, worth rereading over and over.

在许多方面，《追忆似水年华》堪称小说形式的极致典范。它的篇幅几乎是《尤利西斯》的六倍，是《我们共同的朋友》的五倍。它与《没有个性的人》一样雄心勃勃，并且在作者去世时已基本完成。这是一部真正意义上的长篇散文叙事作品，以主人公为中心展开。无论从主题、情节、人物、风格还是时间框架来看，它都浑然一体，逻辑严密；无论是在夏日还是冬日，都易于阅读；而且，对于一些爱好者来说，它值得反复品读。

The most interesting thing about it is that while it is indeed a novel, it employs the conceit of a memoir. The narrator's subject, as with any memoir, is what he has done in the course of his life and what he has made of it; and, indeed, the plot of the novel concerns what he has made of his life, not what he has done. The climax of Proust's thousands of pages occurs in volume 7 , when he goes to one last party and realizes as he arrives both what is important about his life and how it may be represented as a work of literature. In this, of course, he sets his novel in contrast to most other novels, in which events coalesce to form the plot and the climax takes place in an action or series of actions between the protagonist and an antagonist. But Proust chooses a more private sort of plot in which the reader, like the reader of a memoir, is asked to ponder at length and in detail the relationship between the protagonist's activities on the one hand and his feelings, sensations, thoughts, and observations on the other. As with Kafka, when Proust throws out standard plot conventions, he gives the reader a sense of unprecedented intimacy with the narrator, who may be the author, and who once or twice refers to himself as “M.” or “Marcel” but is not the author. In Search of Lost Time is a novel that uses the conceit of the memoir, is in no way a memoir, and assumes simultaneously the authority of the novel and the authority of the memoir. It is perfectly convincing.

这部小说最有趣的地方在于，它虽是一部小说，却采用了回忆录的叙事手法。如同任何回忆录一样，叙述者的主题是他一生中的所作所为以及他如何看待自己的人生；事实上，小说的情节也围绕着他如何看待自己的人生展开，而非他做过什么。普鲁斯特这部数千页巨著的高潮出现在第七卷，他参加最后一次宴会，并在抵达时意识到自己人生的意义所在，以及如何将人生写成一部文学作品。当然，在这一点上，他将自己的小说与大多数其他小说区分开来——在大多数小说中，事件汇聚成情节，而高潮则发生在主人公与反派之间的一次或一系列行动中。但普鲁斯特选择了一种更为私密的叙事方式，在这种方式中，读者如同阅读回忆录一般，需要深入细致地思考主人公的行为与其感受、感觉、思想和观察之间的关系。与卡夫卡一样，当普鲁斯特摒弃传统的叙事手法时，他赋予读者一种前所未有的与叙述者之间的亲密感。这位叙述者或许就是作者本人，他曾一两次自称“M”或“马塞尔”，但并非作者。小说《追忆似水年华》借用了回忆录的构思，却绝非回忆录，它同时兼具小说和回忆录的权威性。这种双重身份令人信服。

Proust's protagonist, “M.,” is slightly younger than Proust himself and seems to have been born in 1878 (Proust was born in 1871 ). He is an only child (Proust had a younger brother), and grows up in Paris and the small town of Combray, southwest of Paris (the town, originally called Illiers, is now called Illiers-Combray). He is a sensuous, observant, sickly, and emotional child who is deeply attached to his mother and grandmother, for whom he is a somewhat perplexing darling. The central incident of the first section of the novel is little M.'s success in gaining his mother's company for a single night—she stays with him because he is upset, and during the night reads to him aloud from George Sand's novel Franois le Champi , thus setting in motion both his ultimate downfall (his connoisseurship of emotional suffering) and his ultimate triumph (his mastery of literature).

普鲁斯特笔下的主人公“M”比普鲁斯特本人略小，似乎出生于1878年（普鲁斯特生于1871年）。他是独生子（普鲁斯特有个弟弟），在巴黎和巴黎西南部的小镇孔布雷长大（该镇原名伊利耶，现称伊利耶-孔布雷）。他是一个感性、善于观察、体弱多病且情感丰富的孩子，与母亲和祖母关系亲密，对她们来说，他既是宠儿，又有些令人费解。小说第一部分的核心事件是小M成功地让母亲陪伴他一晚——母亲因为他心情不好而留宿，并在夜里给他朗读乔治·桑的小说《弗朗索瓦·勒尚皮》，由此开启了他最终的堕落（他对情感痛苦的敏锐洞察）和最终的胜利（他对文学的精通）。

As M. grows up, he cultivates numerous relationships, some with men and some with women, that recapitulate and expand his early attachments. As he remembers the earlier ones in light of the later ones and is reminded by the later ones of the earlier ones, he constructs a theoretical and sensual network of connections that comes to constitute a portrait of his inner life, which he presents as both uniquely his and as representative of the typical workings of the inner lives of men in general. Almost every idea Proust offers is both particular and general, which is the paradox of the novel as a form working in the most absolute possible way. It is the construction of this network rather than the idiosyncrasies or dramas of the people he knows that actually interests him; he goes out of his way to remind the reader over and over that his characters aren't especially worthy of his affections or his analysis. Those who appear most often in the narrative—Madame de Guer-mantes, Robert Saint-Loup, the baron de Charlus, Gilberte Swann, Franoise, M.'s servant, and even his great love, Albertine—are routinely found to be conventional, uninspiring, and shallow. Personal qualities that the reader might think M. would respond to positively—

随着M.的成长，他发展出许多关系，既有男性，也有女性，这些关系既重现又拓展了他早期的情感联结。他一边回忆着早期的关系，一边又从后期的关系中回想起早期的关系，由此构建起一个理论与感官交织的网络，最终构成了他内心世界的画像。他将这幅画像既视为他独有的，又视为男性内心世界普遍运作的典型代表。普鲁斯特提出的几乎每一个观点都兼具特殊性和普遍性，这正是小说这种以最绝对的方式运作的艺术形式的悖论所在。真正吸引他的并非他所认识之人的个性或戏剧性事件，而是这个网络的构建；他反复提醒读者，他笔下的人物并非特别值得他倾注情感或进行深入分析。那些在叙事中频繁出现的人物——盖尔芒特夫人、罗伯特·圣卢、夏吕男爵、吉尔贝特·斯旺、弗朗索瓦丝、先生的女仆，甚至他的挚爱阿尔贝蒂娜——都常常被认为平庸、乏味且肤浅。读者可能会认为先生会欣赏的个人品质——

Saint-Loup's kindness to and affection for M., for example, or Gilberte's long-standing loyalty to him, or Madame de Guermantes's friendliness—are systematically demeaned. Nevertheless, these characters do form the world that he lives inside of and obsessively contemplates. Only the baron de Charlus, who is almost always arrogant and rude, gains M.'s steady respect.

例如，圣卢对先生的友善和爱戴，吉尔贝特对他长久的忠诚，以及盖尔芒特夫人的和蔼可亲——这些都被系统性地贬低了。然而，正是这些人物构成了他生活和痴迷思考的世界。只有几乎总是傲慢无礼的夏吕男爵，赢得了先生始终如一的尊重。

Of course, the most difficult aspect of a first-person narrative, especially a lengthy one, is the adoption of a voice that allows the narrator to talk endlessly about himself without offending the reader, and Proust is careful to create a voice that is both appealing and worth paying attention to. Some of his devices are obvious ones—whenever he talks about himself in the act of relating to the others, he is self-effacing and makes jokes at his own expense. According to his story, he is generally cherished and loved, but at the same time he is modest and tries as much as possible to stay in the background. He implies that when others distinguish or value him, they might well be making a mistake—but he is careful to repeat the affectionate or respectful things they say to him. He is surrounded by social climbers, but he isn't one— his social rise is mysterious, rather like a natural phenomenon, and happens in spite of his expressed desires. He himself would rather focus on other desires, especially the desire to get to know girls of a certain age, particularly attractive girls of obscure background. Proust's second device is to analyze himself as coolly as he analyzes others. He is a master at observing himself from a distance—never swayed so much by his own emotions that he can't delve deeply into them (sometimes in more detail than the reader cares for). This painstaking objectivity serves not only to give him something to talk about, but also to reassure the reader that he is telling the truth, or at least being more honest than any memoirist ever.

当然，第一人称叙事，尤其是长篇叙事，最难之处在于如何塑造一种既能让叙述者滔滔不绝地讲述自己，又不冒犯读者的声音。普鲁斯特巧妙地创造了一种既引人入胜又值得细细品味的声音。他的一些手法显而易见——每当他与他人交往时，他都会谦逊地谈论自己，甚至自嘲。根据他的叙述，他通常备受喜爱，但同时又谦虚低调，尽可能地保持低调。他暗示，当别人对他另眼相看或给予重视时，他们或许是误解了——但他会小心翼翼地复述那些对他表达爱意或敬意的话语。他身边都是一心向上爬的人，但他自己却并非其中之一——他的社会地位提升充满神秘色彩，更像是一种自然现象，而且并非出于他自身的意愿。他更愿意专注于其他欲望，尤其是结识特定年龄段的女孩，特别是那些出身不明却魅力十足的女孩。普鲁斯特的第二个技巧是冷静地分析自己，就像他分析他人一样。他是一位从旁观者的角度审视自己的高手——从不被自身情绪左右，以至于无法深入探究（有时甚至比读者想要了解的细节还要详尽）。这种一丝不苟的客观性不仅为他提供了写作素材，也让读者确信他所言属实，或者至少比任何一位回忆录作家都更加坦诚。

But of course he is not—he is writing a novel, and not a word of it is honest.

但他当然不是——他是在写小说，而且小说里没有一个字是诚实的。

French literature offered Proust plenty of examples of prestigious and successful memoirs—the novel has not dominated French literature as it has English and American literature, and in fact to be a critic, a man of letters, a memoirist, or a theoretician of some sort is possibly more respectable for an ambitious Frenchman than to be a novelist. But like many novelists, Proust preferred the freedom of the novel form for several reasons. One of these was overt—the actual details of his life and loves were more complicated and less interesting than details that would illustrate his theme. In addition, the love of his life was not a woman but a man, not Albertine but Alfred Agostinelli, upon whom Albertine was based. And many of the other acquaintances he would transmute into characters were still living (possibly to take offense) when the novel began to be published.

法国文学为普鲁斯特提供了大量声名显赫、成就斐然的回忆录范例——小说在法国文学中的地位远不及英美文学，事实上，对于一位雄心勃勃的法国人来说，成为评论家、文人、回忆录作家或某种理论家或许比成为小说家更受人尊敬。但与许多小说家一样，普鲁斯特出于多种原因更偏爱小说形式的自由。其中一个原因显而易见——他生活和爱情的真实细节远比那些能够阐明主题的细节复杂得多，也远不如后者有趣。此外，他一生挚爱并非女性，而是男性；并非阿尔贝蒂娜，而是阿尔弗雷德·阿戈斯蒂内利，阿尔贝蒂娜的原型正是他。而且，当他将许多其他熟人转化成小说人物时，这些人在小说开始出版时仍然在世（或许会因此感到不满）。

Proust's real purpose, though, is one that he advertises in his title, la recherche du temps perdu —he doesn't want to simply recall and perhaps justify the past, as memoirists do, he wants to give it palpable existence, which is what novelists do. That this is his intention he makes clear repeatedly in the course of the novel. He is in search of emotions that are as strong as those he once felt, and the route to those emotions is through sensation—most famously the taste of the made-leine dipped in lime-flower tisane—but also through other sensations that he delineates in the final volume of the novel, Le Temps retrouv , or Time Regained. His power to make something of his life comes to him one evening as he is entering a party given by old friends. In the course of a few moments he has three madeleinelike sensations that fill him with feelings he thought lost forever. These in turn persuade him that other formerly cherished but forgotten (in a visceral way, though not unremembered) emotions are available to him if he uses certain techniques to evoke them. The implication is that on the day after the party, he intends to sequester himself from society and dedicate himself to recapturing what he can (though in fact, a few days of illness intervene between his plan and its execution). This party is reported to take place during the First World War. The first volume of In Search of Lost Time had already been published, in 1913 , and volume 2 had been ready for the printer at the outbreak of the war, so M.'s revelation of his powers is a fictional incident as it is written, but it forms a beautiful simultaneous prologue and recapitulation in volume 7 of everything that has gone before in volumes 1 through 6 . The seven volumes of the novel become a cycle—volume 7 predates the other six in composition, but they lead ineluctably to it in M.'s “life.”

然而，普鲁斯特的真正目的，正如他在书名《追忆似水年华》（La Recherche du temps Perdu）中所揭示的那样——他并不想像回忆录作家那样，仅仅回忆过去，或许还要为过去辩解一番；他想赋予过去一种触手可及的存在感，这正是小说家所做的。他在小说中反复强调了这一点。他渴望找回曾经感受过的强烈情感，而通往这些情感的途径是通过感官体验——最著名的莫过于品尝蘸着菩提花茶的玛德琳蛋糕——但也包括他在小说最后一卷《追忆似水年华》（Le Temps Retrouv）中描绘的其他感官体验。一天晚上，当他参加老朋友举办的聚会时，他突然获得了重拾人生意义的力量。短短几分钟内，他体验到了三种如同品尝玛德琳蛋糕般的感觉，这些感觉让他重新感受到了那些他以为早已失去的情感。这些反过来又让他相信，如果他运用某些技巧来唤起那些曾经珍视但已被遗忘（虽然并非完全不记得，而是发自内心地遗忘）的情感，它们依然会回到他身边。这意味着，在聚会后的第二天，他打算与世隔绝，全身心地去重拾那些他能找回的东西（尽管事实上，他的计划和实施之间因几天的疾病而中断）。据说，这场聚会发生在第一次世界大战期间。 《追忆似水年华》第一卷已于1913年出版，第二卷在战争爆发时已付印，因此，M.展现超能力的情节在小说中是虚构的，但它在第七卷中构成了一个优美的序幕，同时也是对前六卷内容的回顾。这部小说的七卷构成了一个循环——第七卷的创作早于其他六卷，但在M.的“人生”中，它们都不可避免地指向了第七卷。

It is just about impossible to read Proust's novel without wondering how close the incidents and characters are to Proust's life, but in fact in writing the novel, Proust owed as much to literature as he did to his life, and for all that he asserts that his inspiration is the moment-by-moment passage of inner and outer time, the novel conforms very closely to conventions of French literature, especially in the depiction of M.'s relationship with Albertine.

读普鲁斯特的小说，几乎不可能不去思考小说中的事件和人物与普鲁斯特的生活有多么接近，但事实上，普鲁斯特在创作这部小说时，既受到了文学的影响，也受到了他自身生活的影响。尽管他声称他的灵感来源于内心和外部时间的瞬息万变，但这部小说却非常符合法国文学的惯例，尤其是在描写M.与阿尔贝蒂娜的关系方面。

Even though the original of the relationship in Proust's life was a homosexual one, Proust is careful to portray Albertine convincingly as a woman and M.'s relationship with her convincingly as heterosexual (though he implies that sexual relations were not common between them). M.'s love for Albertine is developed over the course of five volumes. At first, when he is visiting a seaside resort in Normandy, M. sees Albertine laughing with a group of girlfriends. All of the girls are sporty and jovial, and M. enjoys being with them without especially distinguishing any one as the object of his affections. That he is a lusty young man, eager to fall in love and occasionally resorting to prostitutes, he leaves no doubt. Albertine wins him by being ambiguously available—she seems to have experience, which arouses him, but she is incensed when he assumes that she will give him what he wants, at least when he first approaches her. Her behavior and thought processes always to some extent mystify him, and this mystery intensifies his desire. He discovers that when he is satisfied that she loves him, he is bored, but when she is acting as if she has something to hide, he is intensely jealous and avid for her.

尽管普鲁斯特生活中的这段关系最初是同性恋情，但他仍然细致地将阿尔贝蒂娜刻画得栩栩如生，并将M.与她之间的关系描绘得异性恋（尽管他暗示两人之间并没有频繁的性关系）。M.对阿尔贝蒂娜的爱恋在五卷书中逐渐展开。起初，当他在诺曼底的海滨度假胜地游玩时，M.看到阿尔贝蒂娜正和一群闺蜜谈笑风生。这些女孩个个活泼开朗，M.很享受和她们在一起的时光，并没有特别偏爱哪一个。他是个好色的年轻人，渴望坠入爱河，偶尔还会光顾妓院，这一点毋庸置疑。阿尔贝蒂娜的魅力在于她暧昧的一面——她似乎经验丰富，这让他心生渴望；但当他以为她会满足他的欲望时，她却勃然大怒，至少在他最初接近她时是如此。她的行为和思维方式总是让他感到有些困惑，而这种困惑反而加剧了他的渴望。他发现，当他确信她爱他时，他会感到厌倦；但当她表现得好像有什么事瞒着他时，他就会嫉妒得发狂，对她更加渴望。

At the beginning of volume 5 , The Captive , Proust invites Albertine to return to Paris and live with him (his mother is going to the country to take care of a relative). Their living arrangement quickly turns into an imprisonment of the woman by the man. Albertine lives in accordance with myriad rules established by M., from the time when she can enter his room in the morning to where she is allowed to go and whom she is allowed to see. He is endlessly suspicious of her activities, both in the present and in the past, and he is repeatedly devastated by some thought that she might be acting in a certain way, or might have acted in a certain way. He questions her and assumes that her responses are lies; he questions others about her, and persuades her best friend to accompany her everywhere and report her activities to him, but in the end he doubts the testimony of the friend, too. In particular, he cannot tolerate the thought that she is a lesbian, or had been a lesbian before he came along. Nevertheless, he obsessively cultivates his suspicions as a way of keeping his emotional attachment to her in turmoil because he actually doesn't like her much and there is nothing she can do to satisfy him. In one striking, and you might even say necro-philiac passage, he admits that really he only loves her when she is sound asleep, quiet and still, on his bed. Otherwise she drives him crazy. Even when she is living with him, what he really enjoys is his own sensation of things such as the morning light through the curtains. In another telling passage, he invites a young girl he meets to come into the house and sit on his lap; he then gives the girl five hundred francs. He is later taken to the police station and investigated after this incident is interpreted by the girl's parents as suspicious. He is released but told to be careful. In fact, whether or not Proust ever read de Sade (he does refer to Choderlos de Laclos), volumes 5 and 6 explore many of the same themes as Justine. By turning the love of his life into a woman in his novel, Proust ends up addressing the most traditional and central question of the French novel, and, indeed, of the European novel: what's to be done with women?

在第五卷《囚徒》的开头，普鲁斯特邀请阿尔贝蒂娜回到巴黎与他同住（他的母亲要去乡下照顾一位亲戚）。然而，他们的同居生活很快演变成普鲁斯特对阿尔贝蒂娜的囚禁。阿尔贝蒂娜必须遵守普鲁斯特先生制定的种种规矩，从她早上何时可以进入他的房间，到她可以去哪里、可以见谁，无一例外。他对她的一举一动都充满怀疑，无论是现在还是过去，只要想到她可能做过或曾经做过某些事，他就会感到痛苦不堪。他盘问她，并认定她的回答都是谎言；他向其他人打听她的消息，甚至说服她最好的朋友全程陪伴她，并向他汇报她的行踪，但最终，连朋友的证词也让他产生了怀疑。尤其令他无法容忍的是，她可能是个同性恋，或者在他出现之前就曾是同性恋。然而，他却执着地滋生猜疑，以此来维持自己对她的情感纠葛，因为他其实并不怎么喜欢她，而她也无力让他满意。在一个令人震惊，甚至可以说是恋尸癖式的段落中，他坦言，只有当她安然入睡，静静地躺在他的床上时，他才会真正爱她。否则，她会让他抓狂。即使她与他同住，他真正享受的也只是自己对事物的感受，比如透过窗帘洒进来的晨光。在另一个耐人寻味的段落中，他邀请一位偶遇的年轻女孩进屋，坐在他的腿上；然后给了女孩五百法郎。女孩的父母认为此事可疑，于是将他带到警察局接受调查。他最终被释放，但被告知要小心。事实上，无论普鲁斯特是否读过萨德的作品（他确实提到过肖德洛·德·拉克洛），《朱斯蒂娜》的第五卷和第六卷都探讨了许多与《朱斯蒂娜》相同的主题。普鲁斯特将他一生挚爱的女子化身为小说中的女性，最终探讨了法国小说乃至欧洲小说中最传统、最核心的问题：该如何对待女性？

Even so, M. is a new sort of man. He does not feel himself to be powerful in relation to Albertine—even though she is imprisoned in his house and surrounded by his spies, her secretiveness and his conviction that she doesn't love him cause him to feel powerless, so he redoubles his efforts to control her, on the one hand, and bribe her, on the other. He thus probes the impossibility of actually treating a woman as a possession. In the end, he ruins himself financially (at one point he offers to buy her both a Rolls-Royce and a yacht) and she manages to escape. Because throughout volumes 4 , 5 , and 6 , he is narrating his feelings in ever finer detail, the reader has what she may consider to be an excessive and tedious exposure to them. Just behind M.'s feelings, though, are Albertine's reported actions and responses. From these it is easy to infer Albertine's point of view, if not her motives—she is attempting to please and placate M., she is restive in her captivity, and she is ambivalent. M. is clear that he will never marry her, so what is in it for her? M. doesn't know, the reader doesn't know, and Albertine doesn't know. Albertine eventually escapes and returns to her hometown, where she is killed in an equestrian accident (Proust's real lover was killed in an aviation accident—he also, unlike Albertine, had a wife and children, whom Proust attempted to aid after his death). M. expresses minimal regret at the end of the relationship—he grieves for a while and then it is over, convincing him that since his passionate feelings did not last, Albertine was not worthy of them and that passionate feelings themselves are dependent upon circumstances and upon keeping the relationship in a turmoil—true love is actually intense jealousy. A woman's job is to promote jealousy and a man's job is to feel it. When the jealousy dissipates, the love does, too, since no other form of companionship with a woman is satisfying. Proust cites numerous examples of this idea throughout the novel—it is his guiding theme, first expressed in Swann in Love. M. never loves again, even though subsequently he does imprison nameless and faceless girls in the family house in Paris so he can make idle use of their companionship. The implication of Proust's entire discussion of Albertine and the other girls he is drawn to is that while his nature as a weak, unhealthy, kindly, and generous man prevents him from true sexual predation la de Sade, in principle there is nothing wrong with it, and in fact it is the way of the world.

即便如此，M. 也算得上是位新式的男人。他并不觉得自己对阿尔贝蒂娜拥有绝对的权力——尽管她被囚禁在他的家中，身边也布满了他的眼线，但她的神秘莫测以及他坚信她并不爱他，都让他感到无力。于是，他一方面加倍努力地控制她，另一方面又想方设法贿赂她。他由此试探着，将女人视为所有物是否真的可行。最终，他倾家荡产（他甚至一度提出要给她买一辆劳斯莱斯和一艘游艇），而她也成功逃脱。由于在第四、五、六卷中，他不断地细致入微地叙述自己的感受，读者或许会觉得这些描写过于冗长乏味。然而，在M. 的情感背后，却是阿尔贝蒂娜的行动和反应。从这些情节中，我们很容易推断出阿尔贝蒂娜的观点，即便无法完全理解她的动机——她试图取悦和安抚M.，她在囚禁中焦躁不安，内心充满矛盾。M.明确表示他永远不会娶她，那么她这样做又能得到什么好处呢？M.不知道，读者不知道，阿尔贝蒂娜自己也不知道。阿尔贝蒂娜最终逃脱并回到了家乡，却在一场骑马事故中丧生（普鲁斯特的真正情人死于空难——与阿尔贝蒂娜不同的是，他有妻子和孩子，普鲁斯特在他死后曾试图帮助他们）。M.对这段关系的结束几乎没有表现出任何遗憾——他悲伤了一段时间，然后一切就结束了。他意识到，既然自己炽热的感情没有持续下去，阿尔贝蒂娜就不值得他付出，而炽热的感情本身也取决于环境，取决于让这段关系始终处于动荡之中——真正的爱情实际上是强烈的嫉妒。女人的职责是激发嫉妒，男人的职责是感受嫉妒。当嫉妒消散，爱情也随之消逝，因为与女人之间除了嫉妒之外，别无其他形式的陪伴能够满足爱情。普鲁斯特在整部小说中都列举了许多这样的例子——这是贯穿全书的主题，最早在《恋爱中的斯万》中有所体现。斯万先生此后再也没有爱过，尽管他后来将一些不知名、没有面孔的女孩囚禁在巴黎的家中，以便肆意享受她们的陪伴。普鲁斯特对阿尔贝蒂娜以及其他令他心动的女孩的种种论述，其隐含的意义在于：尽管他天性软弱、不健康、善良慷慨，这使他无法像萨德那样真正地进行性掠夺，但从原则上讲，这种行为本身并没有什么错，事实上，这正是世间常态。

And Proust does take up the subject of homosexuality, as de Sade does, through the characters of the baron de Charlus and Robert de Saint-Loup. These two characters are complementary—they belong to the same aristocratic family. The baron is effeminate, outrageously rude, cruel when he can be, and intelligent, while Saint-Loup is a sort of Adonis—manly, athletic, thoughtful, and kind, but not especially smart or insightful. The baron, whom M. witnesses, at the beginning of volume 4 , having sex with a tailor who lives in the same compound as Proust, is always homosexual, and becomes, in the novel, a model for how homosexuals exist in French society. Robert begins with a mistress, marries for love, and ends as a homosexual. Between them they suggest that the point de Sade makes in Justine , that women exist to facilitate the transfer of property but real Frenchmen prefer to be buggered by their servants, is still as valid in 1890 as in 1790 . The climax of the baron's juxtaposition to Saint-Loup takes place in the seventh volume, when, during the war, M. happens upon a strange hotel that turns out to be a male brothel, where he witnesses Saint-Loup leaving and the baron, tied to a chair, being whipped by a young man he thinks has committed several murders (when M. subsequently talks to the male prostitutes, it turns out that they have committed no murders and are actually using the brothel money to support their aged parents). This, of course, is the terror de Sade attempted to evoke turning up as farce, but the point is the same—this is how the world really works, behind the facade of bourgeois marriage and notions of heterosexual “love.”

普鲁斯特确实像萨德一样，通过夏吕男爵和罗伯特·德·圣卢这两个人物探讨了同性恋这一主题。这两个人物互为补充——他们出身于同一个贵族家庭。男爵举止阴柔，粗鲁无礼，有时甚至残忍，但却十分聪明；而圣卢则像阿多尼斯一般，英俊潇洒，体格健壮，心思细腻，心地善良，但并不特别聪明或富有洞察力。在第四卷的开头，M.亲眼目睹男爵与一位与普鲁斯特住在同一院落的裁缝发生性关系，男爵始终是同性恋者，并在小说中成为法国社会中同性恋者生存状态的典范。罗伯特则以情妇为始，最终因爱结婚，最终也成为了同性恋者。他们共同暗示，萨德在《朱斯蒂娜》中提出的观点——女性的存在是为了方便财产转移，而真正的法国男人更喜欢被仆人鸡奸——在1890年仍然像1790年一样有效。男爵与圣卢的对比在第七卷中达到高潮。战争期间，M.偶然发现一家奇怪的旅馆，结果发现那是一家男妓院。他亲眼目睹圣卢离开，男爵被绑在椅子上，被一个他认为犯下数起谋杀案的年轻人鞭打（后来M.与男妓们交谈后发现，他们并没有杀人，实际上是用妓院的收入来赡养年迈的父母）。当然，这正是萨德试图唤起的恐怖，只不过是以闹剧的形式呈现，但重点是一样的——这就是世界的真实运作方式，隐藏在资产阶级婚姻和异性恋“爱情”的表象之下。

It is not common for the average reader to make it all the way through the seven volumes; the reason for this, most people suppose, is that the seven volumes are tedious or difficult. In fact, they are neither. Once the reader has gotten familiar with Proust's voice and the rhythms of his style, his way of thinking about and discussing things is fascinating and full of substance. He is the number one do-it-yourself psychoanalyst. He believes that an individual can plumb the depths of his own mental life and experience and learn true, valuable things about himself and the world he lives in by doing so. No “subconscious” exists beyond his ken that can be explored only with the help of an analyst. In this sense, In Search of Lost Time is, in spite of itself, a hopeful novel, because the author's sense that his endeavors are rewarding and productive is apparent on every page, whether the reader actually likes M. or not. At the same time, Proust's morality doesn't conform to what most people, and, more particularly, most women might consider to be comfortable. His views are ultimately narcissistic; he not only doesn't understand Albertine's point of view very well, he also doesn't care about it and finds no potential satisfaction in making an effort to do so. Any sort of real connection with another person, based on actual interest in that person, is beyond him, so he gives no thought to whether his desires and actions hurt others. He is a kindly narcissist, but a narcissist all the same, and at great, almost persuasive length.

普通读者很少能一口气读完这七卷本；大多数人认为，原因在于这七卷书枯燥乏味或晦涩难懂。事实上，它们并非如此。一旦读者熟悉了普鲁斯特的文风和节奏，就会发现他思考和探讨事物的方式引人入胜，且内容丰富。他是首屈一指的自助式心理分析师。他相信，每个人都可以深入探索自己的精神世界和经验，并从中获得关于自身和所处世界的真正宝贵信息。在他看来，并不存在任何超出认知范围的“潜意识”，也并非只能借助分析师的帮助才能探索。从这个意义上讲，《追忆似水年华》尽管本身并非完美无瑕，却是一部充满希望的小说，因为作者对自己努力的肯定和收获的信念跃然纸上，无论读者是否喜欢普鲁斯特笔下的主人公M，这种信念都清晰可见。与此同时，普鲁斯特的道德观并不符合大多数人，尤其是大多数女性所认为的舒适标准。他的观点归根结底是自恋的；他不仅不太理解阿尔贝蒂娜的观点，而且也毫不在意，并且认为努力理解她的观点也毫无意义。任何基于对他人真正兴趣而建立的与他人之间的真诚联系对他来说都遥不可及，因此他从不考虑自己的欲望和行为是否会伤害他人。他是一个和善的自恋者，但终究是一个自恋者，而且这种自恋表现得淋漓尽致，几乎到了令人信服的地步。

# ↩

61. D. H. Lawrence. Lady Chatterley's Lover

61. D·H·劳伦斯，《查泰莱夫人的情人》

(1928; REPR., NEW YORK: BANTAM, 1983), 328 PP.

（1928 年；重印，纽约：BANTAM，1983 年），328 页。

Lady Chatterley's Lover is really the story of Lady Chatterley, Connie, with whom Lawrence is sympathetic and in whose consciousness Lawrence convincingly places his narrative center while employing the flexibility of third-person omniscient point of view to occasionally gain access to the inner lives of some of the other characters. Connie's dilemma is that she is not only trapped in a loveless, childless marriage to Chatterley, who has been paralyzed and emasculated in the First World War, she is also lonely, isolated by class and geography on an ugly estate in the English Midlands. Chatterley is dependent, physically, but he is also exacting and jealous of his authority. Lawrence thoroughly anatomizes all of his unattractive qualities and traces the downward progress of Connie's attempts to be a good if not loving wife, even after she meets and begins to be interested in the estate gamekeeper, Mellors, who has also, in a more subtle way, been changed by his experiences in the war. Like Chatterley, Mellors now knows with more certainty what he wants from life. It is not, to begin with, an affair with Connie, but rather independence from English class society. Mellors represents a new sort of working-class Englishman, worldly and self-possessed and no longer content to know his place; he is, therefore, a worthy title character for Lawrence's novel, but it is only with Connie that the reader is allowed to feel at all intimate or comfortable.

《查泰莱夫人的情人》实际上是关于查泰莱夫人康妮的故事。劳伦斯对康妮充满同情，并将叙事中心巧妙地置于她的意识之中，同时运用第三人称全知视角，偶尔也能窥见其他一些人物的内心世界。康妮的困境不仅在于她被困于一段没有爱情、没有孩子的婚姻中，她的丈夫查泰莱在一战中瘫痪，丧失了男子气概；还在于她感到孤独，阶级和地理位置的双重束缚使她与世隔绝，被困在英格兰中部一处破败的庄园里。查泰莱在生理上依赖着她，但他同时也是一个苛刻且嫉妒心极强的人。劳伦斯细致入微地剖析了他所有令人反感的特质，并描绘了康妮努力成为一个好妻子（即便并非深爱丈夫）的种种尝试是如何一步步走向失败的，即便在她遇到并开始对庄园的猎场看守梅勒斯产生兴趣之后也是如此。梅勒斯同样在战争中经历了更为微妙的改变。和查泰莱一样，梅勒斯现在更加明确了自己的人生目标。首先，他追求的并非与康妮的恋情，而是摆脱英国阶级社会的束缚。梅勒斯代表了一种新型的英国工人阶级男性，他们见多识广、自信从容，不再甘于安于现状；因此，他堪称劳伦斯小说中当之无愧的主人公，但只有与康妮相处，读者才能感受到一丝亲近和舒适。

This, Lawrence's last novel, was his most scandalous. After the author oversaw its printing in an Italian print shop, a friend suggested that if the printer had been able to read what he was printing, he would not have been able to concentrate well enough to arrange the type. In the twenty-first century, perhaps because we are less easily shocked by mere sex, we can more readily appreciate all of the ways in which Lawrence challenged his readers.

这是劳伦斯的最后一部小说，也是他最具争议的作品。在作者亲自监督意大利一家印刷厂的印刷工作后，一位朋友开玩笑说，如果印刷工能看懂他印的东西，恐怕就无法集中精力排版了。在二十一世纪，或许是因为我们对单纯的性描写不再那么容易感到震惊，所以我们更容易理解劳伦斯在哪些方面挑战了读者。

Of course there are the sex scenes. They are explicit but not graphic in a cruel way, and certainly not pornographic. The manner in which Connie and Mellors make love is revealing of their characters rather than simply titillating. Both characters have sexual histories that dictate how they approach each other and intercourse itself; their images of themselves and their sense of the world around them change as a result of their sexual relations.

当然，书中也有性爱场景。这些场景描写露骨，但并不残酷血腥，更谈不上色情。康妮和梅勒斯做爱的方式并非仅仅为了挑逗，而是揭示了他们的性格。两人都有各自的性经历，这些经历影响着他们彼此相处的方式以及性交本身；他们的自我认知和对周围世界的感知也因性关系而改变。

Lawrence possessed subversive views of all kinds, though, and in this novel he is utterly frank about them—that is its boldest element. Just because Chatterley, for example, has been paralyzed in the war doesn't mean Lawrence is going to give him any leeway—he is depicted as cold, selfish, hypersensitive, snobbish, and weak—and it is these very qualities that enable him to transform himself into an English captain of industry. Lawrence lavishes plenty of analysis on what he considers to be the essential faults of England, the English class system, and the essential English character. At one point, when Chatter-ley wants to be a writer and is successful, Lawrence portrays his work as empty and worthless—its very success in England is a sign of its emptiness and worthlessness.

劳伦斯虽然持有各种颠覆性的观点，但在这部小说中，他却毫不掩饰地表达了这些观点——这正是这部小说最大胆之处。例如，查泰莱在战争中瘫痪，但这并不意味着劳伦斯会对他宽容——他被描绘成冷漠、自私、过度敏感、势利且软弱——而正是这些特质使他得以蜕变为一位英国实业家。劳伦斯对英国的本质缺陷、英国的阶级制度以及英国人的性格进行了大量的分析。小说中，当查泰莱想要成为一名作家并取得成功时，劳伦斯却将他的作品描绘成空洞无物——它在英国的成功恰恰证明了它的空洞和无用。

For the modern reader, perhaps especially for the modern female reader, Connie presents something of a dilemma. Lawrence is far more sympathetic toward her and also toward the other women characters, Mrs. Bolton and Connie's sister, than toward the men. For one thing, he doesn't require them to betray one another, a requirement many male authors impose on their female characters. Connie's sister strongly disapproves of Connie's love for Mellors, but she remains loyal and sympathetic in a believable way. But Lawrence also makes Mellors's first lovemaking with Connie into more or less a rape, since she doesn't quite seem to know what is going on and gives no consent. There are two ways of looking at this. On the one hand, Mellors takes Connie, which makes her seem a bit foolish and him a bit brutal. On the other hand, though, Connie, like many English heroines before her, does not risk possibly losing the reader's sympathy by acting wanton. As a result, Lawrence gets to have it both ways: Connie enjoys sex with Mellors, but she doesn't foresee it.

对于现代读者，尤其是现代女性读者而言，康妮这个角色带来了一种两难的境地。劳伦斯对她以及其他女性角色，比如博尔顿夫人和康妮的妹妹，都比对男性角色抱有更深的同情。首先，他并没有要求她们互相背叛，而这正是许多男性作家强加给笔下女性角色的情节。康妮的妹妹强烈反对康妮爱上梅勒斯，但她依然保持着忠诚和同情，这种表现令人信服。然而，劳伦斯也将梅勒斯与康妮的初次性爱描写得近乎强奸，因为康妮似乎并不完全明白发生了什么，也没有给予任何同意。对此有两种解读。一方面，梅勒斯强行占有了康妮，这让她显得有些愚蠢，而梅勒斯则显得有些残暴。但另一方面，康妮和许多之前的英国女主人公一样，并没有因为放荡的行为而冒着失去读者同情的风险。因此，劳伦斯两全其美：康妮享受与梅勒斯的性爱，但她对此毫无预料。

Mellors is hardly kind, cordial, and spiritually enlightened. He has particular sexual requirements, and he has given up looking for a woman who can fulfill them until he discovers Connie. Part of his manly appeal is that he does acknowledge his appetites, but he's opinionated and not easy to like. If he weren't so outspoken about his opinions, he would be a kind of green-man-of-the-forest figure; in some ways, he is more reminiscent of an American cowboy type than he is of any English type (and Lawrence lived for a while in the American West). Mellors is not a dreamboat to begin with, however, and there is no sense at the end of the novel, as there is with, say, Mr. Darcy in Pride and Prejudice , that he is willing to give up either his pride or his prejudice, or that Connie and Mellors will necessarily live happily ever after. It seems as though they will, like most couples, love and adjust. The basis of their marriage will be a strong sexual bond, and given that, they will make concessions and find a way of getting along. The last few pages of the novel peter out into practicalities—Connie and Mellors are living apart so he can get his divorce, and they are hoping to find a farm somewhere, with Connie's inheritance to provide the capital (love and money coming together once again). Lawrence's disaffection with England is so strong that he can't imagine a happy ending taking place there, only plenty of hard work.

梅勒斯先生算不上和善、热情，更谈不上精神上的开明。他有着特殊的性需求，在遇到康妮之前，他已经放弃了寻找能够满足这些需求的女人。他之所以具有男子气概，部分原因在于他坦然承认自己的欲望，但他固执己见，并不容易让人喜欢。如果他不那么直言不讳，他或许会像个森林里的绿人；在某些方面，他更像是美国牛仔，而非任何英国绅士（劳伦斯曾在美国西部生活过一段时间）。然而，梅勒斯先生从一开始就不是个完美无缺的白马王子，而且在小说结尾，我们丝毫感觉不到他愿意放弃自己的傲慢或偏见，也看不到康妮和梅勒斯先生一定会从此过上幸福的生活，不像《傲慢与偏见》中的达西先生那样。他们似乎会像大多数情侣一样，彼此相爱，互相适应。他们婚姻的基础是牢固的性关系，正因如此，他们会做出让步，找到相处之道。小说的最后几页逐渐转向实际问题——康妮和梅勒斯分居，以便他办理离婚手续，他们希望找到一处农场，康妮的遗产将作为启动资金（爱情与金钱再次交织在一起）。劳伦斯对英国的厌恶如此强烈，以至于他无法想象在那里会有幸福的结局，只有无尽的辛劳。

What I like about Lady Chatterley's Lover is that in the midst of all these innovative and, for their time, astounding scenes, Lawrence managed to put together a traditionally well-made novel. The characters are compelling and complex, the scene is rendered vividly, the themes of sexuality and class antagonism and the motifs of nature versus industry are carefully developed and understandable. Lawrence uses the classic tools of realism in a way that does not subvert the form, but rather extends the discussion of ideas that already underlie the form: What is to be done with women? How do women negotiate their simultaneous identities as agents and as possessions? What is authentic love? How do pastoral scenes and industrial scenes, money and work fit together? Lawrence doesn't quite have the answers, as the ending shows, but he is especially daring in how he asks the questions.

我喜欢《查泰莱夫人的情人》的原因在于，在所有这些创新且在当时堪称惊世骇俗的场景之中，劳伦斯成功地构建了一部结构严谨的传统小说。人物形象鲜明而复杂，场景描绘生动逼真，性与阶级对抗以及自然与工业的对立等主题都得到了精心的刻画，清晰易懂。劳伦斯运用了现实主义的经典手法，但并未颠覆其形式，而是拓展了对既有思想的探讨：女性该何去何从？女性如何平衡她们作为主体和作为附属品的双重身份？什么是真爱？田园风光与工业场景、金钱与劳动如何交织？正如结尾所示，劳伦斯并没有给出确切的答案，但他提出这些问题的方式却格外大胆。

62. Virginia Woolf. Orlando

62. 弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫。《奥兰多》

(1928; REPR., SAN DIEGO, CALIF.: HARCOURT BRACE JOVANOVICH, HARVEST, 1956), 329 PP.

（1928 年；重印，加利福尼亚州圣地亚哥：哈考特·布雷斯·乔万诺维奇，哈维斯特，1956 年），329 页。

Orlando is a confection, light and airy in tone, undercutting even its most serious insights with a certain coyness that probably came from Woolf's desire to flatter Vita Sackville-West, the object of her affections and the inspiration for her protagonist, Orlando, who is born during the reign of Queen Elizabeth yet is only just over thirty years old in 1928 .

《奥兰多》是一部轻松愉快的作品，其基调轻快明快，甚至连最严肃的见解也带着某种娇羞的意味，这或许源于伍尔夫想要奉承她所爱慕的对象、也是她笔下主人公奥兰多的灵感来源——维塔·萨克维尔-韦斯特。奥兰多出生于伊丽莎白女王统治时期，但在 1928 年也才三十出头。

Orlando has several adventures in four hundred years and meets many noteworthy personages. As a boy, he is introduced to Queen Elizabeth, who is so pleased with his “innocence, simplicity” that she gives his family a large property (evidently based on the estate where Vita Sackville-West resided). Later Orlando spends a century or so in Constantinople, only to return to England as a woman in time for the London literary era of Pope, Dryden, and Swift. She lives through the high domesticity of the Victorian era, marries, produces a child, and emerges in the twenties shopping at a department store and driving a motorcar out of London on the old Kent Road. Throughout, Orlando has been composing a poem called “The Oak Tree,” which survives numerous literary fashions and is finally published and wins an award. Her enduring qualities are a habit of independence, a love of the English countryside, and a certain reserve about marriage.

在四百年的时间里，奥兰多经历了数次冒险，结识了许多名人。孩提时代，他觐见了伊丽莎白女王，女王对他的“天真无邪”十分喜爱，便赐予他家一大片庄园（显然是以维塔·萨克维尔-韦斯特的故居为原型）。后来，奥兰多在君士坦丁堡生活了一个世纪左右，之后以女性的身份回到英国，正值伦敦文坛的黄金时代，与蒲柏、德莱顿和斯威夫特等文坛巨匠齐名。她经历了维多利亚时代繁华的家庭生活，结婚生子，并在二十年代出现在百货商店，驾驶着汽车沿着古老的肯特路驶出伦敦。在此期间，奥兰多一直在创作一首名为《橡树》的诗，这首诗经受住了文学潮流的变迁，最终得以出版并获奖。她身上最持久的品质是独立自主的性格、对英国乡村的热爱以及对婚姻的某种矜持。

Orlando is full of famous and delightful passages and set pieces. In perhaps the most famous, the Thames freezes all the way to the bottom, and King James puts on a great winter festival, with feasts, skating, and fireworks. When Orlando returns to England as a woman, after the sojourn in Constantinople, she is struck by the differences in how she is treated, and also how she feels: “Which is the greater ecstasy? The man's or the woman's? And are they not perhaps the same? No, she thought, this is the most delicious (thanking the Captain but refusing) to refuse, and see him frown. Well, she would, if he wished it, have the very thinnest, smallest sliver in the world. This was the most delicious, to yield and see him smile” (p. 155 ). But it is the whole last section, where Orlando finds herself in the present, that is the heart of the novel:

《奥兰多》中充满了著名而令人愉悦的段落和场景。其中最著名的或许是泰晤士河完全冰封，詹姆斯国王举办了一场盛大的冬季庆典，宴饮、滑冰、烟火齐放。奥兰多在君士坦丁堡逗留后以女性的身份回到英国，她惊讶于自己受到的待遇和感受的差异：“哪种狂喜更甚？男人的还是女人的？或许它们不是一样的？不，”她想，“最美妙的莫过于（她感谢船长，但拒绝了）拒绝，看着他皱眉。嗯，如果他愿意，她愿意给他世界上最薄、最小的一小片。最美妙的莫过于屈服，看着他微笑”（第155页）。但真正构成小说核心的是最后一部分，奥兰多回到现实生活的那一部分：

And so for some seconds the light went on becoming brighter and brighter, and the clock ticked louder and louder until there
was a terrific explosion right in her ear. Orlando leaped as if she had been violently struck on the head. Ten times she was struck. In fact it was ten o'clock in the morning. It was the eleventh of October. It was 1928 . It was the present moment. [p. 298 ]

于是，灯光持续亮了几秒钟，越来越亮，时钟的滴答声也越来越响，直到她耳边突然传来一声巨响。奥兰多像被重重击中头部一样猛地跳了起来。她仿佛被击中了十次。事实上，当时是上午十点。那是10月11日。那是1928年。就是现在。[p. 298]

This is a remarkable example of Woolf's talent for folding perception into consciousness—moving quickly back and forth between what the character is perceiving and how she feels about it. Such passages even now have a kind of utter freshness that makes other forms of narrative, even those with more exciting plots, seem a little thick. Nonetheless, Orlando does not have the weight and perfection of To the Lighthouse and Mrs. Dalloway.

这是伍尔夫将感知融入意识的卓越才能的绝佳例证——她能在人物的感知和感受之间快速切换。即使在今天，这样的段落依然散发着一种清新脱俗的气息，令其他叙事形式，即便情节更为精彩的作品，都显得有些冗长乏味。然而，《奥兰多》却不及《到灯塔去》和《达洛维夫人》那样厚重完美。

Orlando lives through everything without really living through anything. What Woolf is best at in her other works is breaking down the passage of time so the reader experiences a single day or two days that are divided by several years as utterly significant, moment by moment. When Woolf focuses on the events of a single day and the interactions of several characters who don't consciously have much to do with one another, she shows that traditional narrative significance, made manifest by large events, is not real—reality is in tiny threads of connection, tiny shifts in perception. Woolf is after meaning rather than events, showing that events and their meaning do not necessarily coincide, and important actors in events do not necessarily understand them as well as peripheral witnesses do. Orlando , because it takes place over some four hundred years, has only a few representative moments from each era. Woolf can't afford to linger. And Orlando has no society to interact with. Every relationship, every activity is doomed to be transient and therefore not especially vivid, so Orlando him/herself is not very vivid. What is vivid are Woolf's reflections on the idea of Orlando.

奥兰多经历了一切，却又仿佛什么都没真正经历过。伍尔夫在其他作品中最擅长的，是将时间的流逝分解开来，让读者体验到被数年时间分割的某一天或两天，并将其视为意义非凡的瞬间。当伍尔夫聚焦于某一天发生的事件，以及几个彼此之间并无太多关联的人物之间的互动时，她揭示了由重大事件所体现的传统叙事意义并非真实存在——现实存在于细微的联系之中，存在于感知的细微变化之中。伍尔夫追求的是意义而非事件本身，她表明事件及其意义并非必然一致，事件中的重要人物也未必能像旁观者那样深刻地理解事件。由于《奥兰多》的故事跨越了四百年，每个时代都只有寥寥几个具有代表性的瞬间。伍尔夫无法在细节上过多着墨。而且，奥兰多没有社会可以与之互动。每段关系，每项活动都注定是短暂的，因此并不鲜活生动，奥兰多本人也同样如此。伍尔夫对奥兰多这个概念的思考生动而深刻。

In fact, Orlando , which was made into a movie in 1993 , is an ideal vehicle for film. Costumes, sets, new and intriguing ideas, lots of scene changes, and an androgynous actress are exactly what Orlando needs to fill in the narrative blanks that Woolf leaves where Vita and her house would be if the reader knew them as well as Woolf does. As a rule, a good novel can't be made into a movie—it is too rich in the reader's consciousness to be reduced to film. But many almost good novels can be enhanced by the color, movement, and actors that film has to offer. Orlando is one of these.

事实上，1993年被改编成电影的《奥兰多》堪称电影的理想载体。服装、布景、新颖有趣的构思、大量的场景转换，以及一位雌雄莫辨的女演员，这些元素恰好填补了伍尔夫在小说中留下的叙事空白——如果读者像伍尔夫一样了解维塔和她的家，这些空白本应存在。通常来说，一部优秀的小说很难被改编成电影——它在读者的意识中占据了太过丰富的空间，难以被简化成影像。但许多接近优秀的小说，却能借助电影的色彩、动感和演员，得到提升。《奥兰多》便是其中之一。

However, it is also true that a novel doesn't have to be a good example of the form to be important and influential. All women writers after Woolf owe her an unprecedented debt. I think it is safe to say that women writers of my generation could not have conceived of themselves as they did—conceived of themselves as writers with a right to compose their works—without two things that Woolf offered: in her fiction, a serious depiction of female and male consciousnesses as they exist in themselves and interact with one another, equal and equally detailed, and, in her criticism, a consideration of literature (in the Common Readers and A Room of One's Own) in which Woolf's rights as a critic and reader are quietly and authoritatively asserted. Orlando is more a part of this second body of work than it is part of her fictional oeuvre. What Orlando has that few women in fiction had before her is power—power not to have to consider, as Lily Bart and Isabel Archer do, whom to marry and whom to yield to. Her power is so thorough that the questions of marriage and childbirth come up only as choices, never necessities. Perhaps the operative fact is that she has no father, only a house—and money.

然而，小说的重要性和影响力并不一定非得是该形式的典范。伍尔夫之后的所有女性作家都对她怀有前所未有的感激之情。我认为，如果没有伍尔夫提供的两样东西，我这一代的女性作家不可能像她们那样看待自己——不可能将自己视为拥有创作权利的作家：在她的小说中，她严肃地描绘了女性和男性意识的内在存在及其相互互动，两者平等且细致；在她的评论中（如《共同读者》和《一间自己的房间》），她对文学的思考以一种平静而权威的方式确立了自己作为评论家和读者的权利。《奥兰多》与其说是她小说作品的一部分，不如说是她这第二部分作品的一部分。奥兰多拥有此前鲜有女性作家拥有的力量——一种不必像莉莉·巴特和伊莎贝尔·阿切尔那样考虑嫁给谁、顺从谁的力量。她的权力如此强大，以至于婚姻和生育问题对她而言只是选择，而非必需品。或许关键在于，她没有父亲，只有一栋房子——和金钱。

Orlando does not have the poignant undertone that Woolf's other works do. It was composed out of exuberance and love, not out of fear and loss. But even though beautiful style gets you only so far in a novel, the style of Orlando is indeed beautiful.

《奥兰多》不像伍尔夫的其他作品那样带有淡淡的哀伤。它的创作源于热情和爱，而非恐惧和失落。尽管优美的文风在小说中只能起到有限的作用，但《奥兰多》的文风的确优美。

63. William Faulkner. As I Lay Dying

63. 威廉·福克纳。《我弥留之际》

(1930; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1987), 242 PP.

（1930 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1987 年），242 页。

William Faulkner was working as a night watchman at a power plant in Mississippi when he wrote As I Lay Dying in about eight weeks in the autumn of 1929 (oddly enough, commencement of work on the novel almost exactly coincided with the great crash of Wall Street on October 29 ). The novel was one of the first he set in Yoknapatawpha County, Mississippi, a region based upon Faulkner's own home county. It made him famous and brought him to the attention of Hollywood, where he later spent some twenty years writing screenplays and doctoring scripts.

1929年秋天，威廉·福克纳在密西西比州一家发电厂做夜班保安时，用了大约八周时间写出了《我弥留之际》（巧合的是，这部小说的创作几乎与10月29日华尔街股市崩盘的时间完全吻合）。这部小说是他最早以密西西比州约克纳帕塔法县为背景的作品之一，该县的原型正是福克纳的家乡。这部小说使他声名鹊起，并引起了好莱坞的注意。之后，他在好莱坞从事剧本创作和修改工作长达二十年之久。

The simple plot of As I Lay Dying is easy to understand and therefore allows for considerable southern gothic embroidery. A woman, Addie Bundren, dies, mother of Cash, Darl, Jewel, Dewey Dell, and Vardaman, wife of Anse. In accordance with Addie's wishes, Anse resolves to take her remains, in a coffin built by Cash, back to her original home, some forty miles away, where she wishes to be buried with her own family. The journey is impractical and costly, ill-fated from the beginning. Like most fictional journeys, it is full of adventures (the first set of mules drowns trying to cross the river, a barn burns down, buzzards follow the coffin, etc.), but given the purpose of the journey, the adventures are macabre and horrifying, not at all exciting or enlivening. Anse is never deterred, even though each of his children is injured in one way or another. Addie is buried. Anse buys himself a set of false teeth and finds a new wife.

《我弥留之际》的情节简单易懂，因此得以充分展现南方哥特式的风格。故事的主人公艾迪·邦德伦去世了，她是卡什、达尔、朱厄尔、杜威·戴尔和瓦达曼的母亲，也是安斯的妻子。为了遵照艾迪的遗愿，安斯决定将她的遗体——装在卡什亲手制作的棺材里——送回她位于四十英里外的故乡，与家人合葬。这段旅程既不切实际又耗资巨大，从一开始就注定充满厄运。如同大多数虚构的旅程一样，这段旅程也充满了各种冒险（第一批骡子在过河时溺水身亡，谷仓被烧毁，秃鹫尾随棺材等等），但考虑到此行的目的，这些冒险显得阴森恐怖，丝毫没有令人兴奋或振奋人心之处。尽管安斯的每个孩子都以某种方式受到了伤害，但他始终没有放弃。最终，艾迪被安葬了。安斯给自己买了一副假牙，还娶了个新妻子。

As I Lay Dying is a powerful and moving novel, widely considered one of the greatest novels by a great American novelist, but it is not an easy novel to agree on. Some readers think the Bundren family's misadventures are meant to be humorous, or at least absurd; others see biblical echoes, Homeric echoes, or tragedy. Some critics focus on Faulkner's modernist innovations in point of view and variety of language and on his attempts to characterize the inner life of madness (Darl), youthful innocence (Vardaman), and death itself (Addie). The fact is, Faulkner's technique is similar to Kafka's—to present, without comment, the putative experience of a character in an extreme situation and to let the reader follow the logic of both the situation and the experience as best she can. For Kafka's single typical Central European citizen and clarity of style, though, Faulkner substitutes American eccentrics and a multitude of voices, some conversational and familiar, others unique and difficult to make out. The result is oddly similar to Kafka in effect, since the reader begins in a state of confusion and ends in a state of acceptance (or not—such a technique is relatively high risk in that a certain irreducible percentage of readers simply do not care for the challenge and stop reading).

《我弥留之际》是一部震撼人心、感人至深的小说，被广泛认为是美国伟大作家福克纳最伟大的作品之一，但人们对它的评价却褒贬不一。一些读者认为邦德伦一家遭遇的种种不幸是为了博君一笑，或者至少是荒诞不经；另一些读者则从中看到了圣经、荷马史诗或悲剧的影子。一些评论家则着重探讨福克纳在叙事视角和语言多样性方面的现代主义创新，以及他对疯狂（达尔）、青春的纯真（瓦尔达曼）和死亡本身（艾迪）等人物内心世界的刻画。事实上，福克纳的写作技巧与卡夫卡颇为相似——不加评论地呈现人物在极端情境下的假定体验，让读者自行领悟情境和体验背后的逻辑。然而，福克纳用美国怪人以及众多声音取代了卡夫卡笔下典型的中欧公民形象和清晰的文风，这些声音有的亲切自然，有的则独特难辨。其效果与卡夫卡的作品出奇地相似，因为读者起初会感到困惑，最终却会接受（或者不接受——这种手法风险相对较高，因为总会有一部分读者不愿接受挑战，从而放弃阅读）。

Faulkner was not the first novelist to use the technique of multiple points of view—Virginia Woolf explored the idea only a few years earlier in To the Lighthouse and Mrs. Dalloway —but Faulkner was more interested than Woolf in extremity of setting and situation. Anse Bundren perhaps qualifies as one of the voiceless ignorant masses that middle-class literature overlooks—he is poor and feckless. His sons and daughter seem to have no recourse against him—they, too, are uneducated country people who seem odd even to their neighbors, and their neighbors are by no means part of the American mainstream. The Bundren children are more than unlettered—they have had no moral education in how to understand themselves and make choices. The precise diagnosis of Darl's mental illness is hard to figure out, and Vardaman seems to be about ten but to have the consciousness of a three- or four-year-old. Dewey Dell at least knows she is pregnant and that she needs to purchase an abortifacient—she has been instructed that far by her seducer—but she doesn't know enough to protect herself when her instructions don't work out as hoped. When the mules drown, the Bundrens are unmoved—they are so used to such acts of God (or carelessness) that they are numb to suffering. When Vardaman drills holes into the coffin, damaging Addie's face, the holes are patched, but an appropriate reaction is beyond everyone in the family. Each has a single emotion that he or she can express—Anse, self-pity; Jewel, anger; Darl, a sort of wonder; Vardaman, dogged curiosity; Dewey Dell, patience; and Cash, stoic acceptance.

福克纳并非第一个运用多视角叙事技巧的小说家——弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫几年前就在《到灯塔去》和《达洛维夫人》中探索过这一手法——但福克纳比伍尔夫更关注极端的环境和情境。安斯·邦德伦或许可以算作中产阶级文学所忽视的无声无知的大众之一——他贫穷而无能。他的儿女似乎对他束手无策——他们也是未受过教育的乡下人，甚至在邻居眼中也显得古怪，而他们的邻居也绝非美国主流社会的一员。邦德伦家的孩子们不仅不识字——他们甚至没有接受过如何理解自己和做出选择的道德教育。达尔的精神疾病难以准确诊断，而瓦达曼看起来大约十岁，却只有三四岁孩子的意识。杜威·戴尔至少知道自己怀孕了，也知道自己需要购买堕胎药——这是她的诱惑者指示她的——但她却不知道该如何保护自己，因为当堕胎药没有按预期起作用时，她该如何应对。骡子溺水身亡时，邦德伦一家无动于衷——他们早已习惯了这种天灾（或疏忽），对痛苦麻木不仁。当瓦达曼在棺材上钻孔，伤及艾迪的脸时，孔洞被修补好，但家里的每个人都无法做出恰当的反应。每个人都只能表达一种情绪——安斯，自怜；朱厄尔，愤怒；达尔，一种惊奇；瓦达曼，执着的好奇；杜威·戴尔，耐心；卡什，默默的接受。

As Virginia Woolf does, William Faulkner radically democratizes the novel by rendering the voices of those whom earlier literature had ignored, but there are several facets to his technique. Everything depends, for one thing, on the reader's willingness to believe that the characters are authentically presented—that the boy is a boy and the girl is a girl and the setting and circumstances are plausible. Initial confusion and ignorance on the part of the reader can only afford the author a certain degree of leeway. Once she becomes familiar with the characters, they have to embody the same logic as characters in any other novel. Individual stories have to be surprising as they happen but perfectly understandable in retrospect, so Darl has to be capable of setting the barn afire before he does it, even if the reader doesn't realize before he does it that he is going to do it. Dewey Dell has to be capable of keeping the secret of her plan even while the reader doesn't know she has a secret. It is such capacities that bring the characters close to the reader even as their looks, behavior, and diction move them further away. Of crucial importance to this feel of authenticity are Faulkner's theories of psychology and sociology. His view of the characters and how they coordinate the plot and the themes can't undermine how they allegedly think of and present themselves, or else certain actions and expressions will pop awkwardly out of the text, destroying its effect of seamlessness. It is in just such a circumstance, when the themes and the theories are supposed to be artfully disappearing because the author's voice has been subsumed by the characters’ narrating voices, that the author runs the greatest risk of seeming overbearing or manipulative. A straightforward narrator, who tells the story in his own voice, runs less of a risk, because he isn't trying to hide his presence. Faulkner has gotten in some trouble for his presentations of women, which even male critics haven't found especially sympathetic or convincing, and also into a bit of what you might call political-correctness trouble: Are the Bundrens garish types or true portraits? Would they see themselves as Faulkner sees them? Is their story tragic with ridiculous overtones, or ridiculous with tragic overtones? Is he honoring their humanity, or poking fun at their strangeness? Of course these questions can't be answered objectively—much depends on a reader's intuitive apprehension of the novel. I find that in spite of Addie's and Dewey Dell's too-predictable lapses from female virtue, the pathos of how Dewey Dell is doubly cheated in the end is the real heart of the novel.

如同弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫一样，威廉·福克纳通过展现那些被早期文学忽略的人物的声音，彻底实现了小说的民主化。但他的技巧包含多个层面。首先，一切都取决于读者是否愿意相信人物的真实性——男孩就是男孩，女孩就是女孩，故事的背景和情节也合情合理。读者最初的困惑和无知只能给作者一定的创作空间。一旦作者熟悉了人物，他们就必须遵循与其他小说人物相同的逻辑。每个故事在发生时都必须出人意料，但事后回想起来却又完全可以理解。例如，达尔必须能够在放火烧谷仓之前就预感到自己会这么做，即使读者事先并不知道。杜威·戴尔必须能够保守住自己的计划秘密，即使读者并不知道她有秘密。正是这些特质，使得人物即便在外貌、行为和措辞上与读者保持距离，却依然能拉近读者与人物之间的距离。福克纳的心理学和社会学理论对于这种真实感至关重要。他对人物的理解，以及他们如何协调情节和主题，都不能违背人物对自身认知和呈现方式的设定，否则某些行为和表达就会显得突兀，破坏文本的流畅性。正是在这种情况下，当主题和理论本应巧妙地隐去，因为作者的声音已被人物的叙述声音所掩盖时，作者最容易显得专横跋扈或操纵读者。而一个直白的叙述者，用自己的声音讲述故事，则风险较小，因为他无需刻意隐藏自己的存在。福克纳对女性的刻画引发了一些争议，就连男性评论家也觉得这些女性形象不够讨喜或令人信服，而且还陷入了一些所谓的“政治正确”的困境：邦德伦一家究竟是浮夸的典型人物，还是真实的写照？他们会像福克纳那样看待自己吗？他们的故事是带有荒诞色彩的悲剧，还是带有悲剧色彩的荒诞？福克纳是在尊重他们的人性，还是在嘲讽他们的怪异？当然，这些问题无法客观回答——很大程度上取决于读者对小说的直觉理解。我认为，尽管艾迪和杜威·戴尔在违背女性美德方面表现得过于可预测，但杜威·戴尔最终遭受双重欺骗的悲惨遭遇才是这部小说的真正核心。

As I Lay Dying is both original and odd, and it points up the way in which American literature has decentralized respectability. The aim is not to bring outlyers into the mainstream, but to broaden the mainstream so it includes the outlyers without destroying their uniqueness. It is the countervailing force against the homogenization of American life, states’ rights versus federal power—the part undissolved in the whole, representing it and reproducing it.

《我弥留之际》既新颖又奇特，它揭示了美国文学中“体面”概念的去中心化。其目的并非将边缘群体纳入主流，而是拓展主流的范畴，使其能够包容边缘群体，同时又不抹杀他们的独特性。它对抗着美国生活的同质化，对抗着州权与联邦权力之间的冲突——它是整体中未被消解的部分，既是整体的代表，也是整体的再现。

64. Robert Musil. The Man without Qualities

64. 罗伯特·穆齐尔。《没有个性的人》

VOL. 1, TRANS. EITHNE WILKINS AND ERNEST KAISER
第 1 卷，译者：艾斯妮·威尔金斯和欧内斯特·凯泽

(1931; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN PUTNAM, PERIGEE, 1980), 365 PP.

（1931 年；重印，纽约：企鹅普特南出版社，PERIGEE，1980 年），365 页。

The Man without Qualities is one of the most prestigious novels of the twentieth century, the sort of book that no one has read but everyone has heard of. It is well worth reading, even though it is very long, very slow, and was unfinished at the time of Musil's death. This first volume runs 365 pages, and the dilemma of the protagonist, Ulrich, is presented only on about page 300 . Nevertheless, the writing is so precise and the argument Musil makes about Ulrich and his situation so intricate that it is intellectually and aesthetically involving even before it becomes emotionally involving.

《没有个性的人》是二十世纪最负盛名的长篇小说之一，属于那种无人读过却人人皆知的书。尽管篇幅很长，节奏缓慢，而且在穆齐尔去世时尚未完成，但它仍然非常值得一读。第一卷共365页，主人公乌尔里希的困境直到300页左右才正式展开。然而，穆齐尔的文笔如此精炼，他对乌尔里希及其处境的论述如此错综复杂，以至于在情感触动人心之前，它就已经在智识和美学上引人入胜。

Ulrich is an unmarried man in his early thirties who has recently returned to Vienna from several years abroad. He is ostensibly a mathematician, but although his mind still works like that of a scientist, he has ceased to be inspired by his vocation, and finds himself in the midst of an existential crisis. He is a habitual thinker whose most characteristic activity is to continually refine his analysis of himself and the people around him. He is not meditative or contemplative—that is, he seeks neither peace nor enlightenment. Earlier, once through love and the natural world, and later through mathematics, he had sought truth, but not long before the novel begins, he slacks off, no longer passionate enough about it to be disappointed. He finds and redecorates a house and then takes up the typical activities of Viennese gentlemen—he procures himself a mistress and falls in with bureaucratic projects. As an idle pastime, he gets to know the leading lights of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, who, somewhat like their counterparts in the American South of the 1850s , have no idea that they are passing into history.

乌尔里希是一位三十出头的单身男子，最近刚从国外回来。他表面上是一位数学家，虽然思维依然像科学家一样敏捷，但他已不再对自己的职业充满热情，并陷入了一场生存危机。他是一个习惯性思考的人，最显著的习惯就是不断地分析自己和周围的人。他既不冥想，也不沉思——也就是说，他既不追求平静，也不追求启迪。早年间，他曾通过爱情和自然，后来又通过数学来探寻真理，但在小说开篇不久，他便懈怠了，不再像以前那样充满热情，以至于无法承受失望。他找到一栋房子，重新装修，然后开始从事维也纳绅士的典型活动——找了个情妇，并投身于官僚机构的工作中。闲暇时，他结识了奥匈帝国的杰出人物，这些人有点像 19 世纪 50 年代美国南方的那些人，他们丝毫没有意识到自己正在成为历史。

The novel has eight principal characters: Ulrich; his cousin Diotima, a tall, robust, beautiful middle-class woman who epitomizes a certain type of self-satisfied German-speaking Austrian; Diotima's lover, Arnheim, a Prussian mogul and man of letters whom Ulrich detests; Bonadea, Ulrich's own mistress, whose promiscuity and spiritual corruption sometimes intrigue him; and Leinsdorf, a highly placed government official who is in charge of the celebrations for the jubilee of Emperor Franz Josef. A sixth character, Moosbrugger, is a murderer whose trial interests Ulrich and a friend of his, Clarisse, who is married to Ulrich's estranged childhood companion. All of these characters have plenty of leisure, including Moosbrugger, who is in prison for the murder of a young prostitute.

这部小说有八个主要人物：乌尔里希；他的表妹迪奥蒂玛，一位身材高挑、体态丰腴、容貌姣好的中产阶级女性，是某种自鸣得意、沾沾自喜的德语奥地利女性的典型代表；迪奥蒂玛的情人阿恩海姆，一位普鲁士富豪兼文人，乌尔里希对他深恶痛绝；乌尔里希的情妇博纳迪亚，她的放荡不羁和精神堕落有时令他感到好奇；以及莱因斯多夫，一位身居要职的政府官员，负责筹办弗朗茨·约瑟夫皇帝的登基庆典。第六个人物是莫斯布鲁格，他是一名杀人犯，乌尔里希和他的朋友克拉丽丝（嫁给了乌尔里希疏远的儿时玩伴）都对他的审判很感兴趣。所有这些人物都拥有大量的闲暇时间，包括因谋杀一名年轻妓女而身陷囹圄的莫斯布鲁格。

Like most modernist novels, The Man without Qualities is not tragic, but it is not comic, either, if we take comic to mean that at least some of the characters achieve authentic connections with one another by the end of the novel (of course, there is no ending, since the novel was unfinished). It is, however, quite funny, or at least witty, as a result of Musil's amazingly specific and complex figurative language. The reader is quite often struck by epigrams and remarks that gracefully offer images and insights that are utterly original and right. At one point, for example, he writes, “this non-plussed feeling refers to something that many people nowadays call intuition, whereas formerly it used to be called inspiration, and they think that they must see something suprapersonal in it; but it is only something nonpersonal, namely the affinity and kinship of the things themselves that meet inside one's head” (p. 129 ). And in a remark that must surely apply to many of the unacccountable things that rogue governments and rogue corporations still do, he writes, “for it is only criminals who presume to damage other people nowadays without the aid of philosophy” (p. 227 ). The chapters on Moosbrugger and Count Leinsdorf are contrasting masterpieces of empathy—on the one hand, with a murderer whose grasp of reality is utterly logical but scarily tenuous, and on the other, with an aristocrat who has no idea what is going on in the nation he is responsible for.

与大多数现代主义小说一样，《没有个性的人》并非悲剧，但也并非喜剧——如果我们把喜剧理解为至少部分人物在小说结尾处建立了真正的联系（当然，由于小说并未完成，所以并没有真正的结尾）。然而，由于穆齐尔极其具体而复杂的比喻语言，这部小说却颇具幽默感，或者至少称得上诙谐。读者常常会被他那些精妙绝伦的警句和评论所打动，这些警句和评论巧妙地展现了完全原创且精辟的意象和洞见。例如，他曾写道：“这种茫然的感觉指的是如今许多人称之为直觉的东西，而过去人们称之为灵感，他们认为其中必定蕴含着某种超个人的东西；但它仅仅是某种非个人的东西，即在人的头脑中相遇的事物本身之间的亲缘性和关联性”（第129页）。他写道：“如今，只有罪犯才会不借助哲学就妄图伤害他人”（第227页），这句话无疑也适用于许多流氓政府和流氓公司至今仍在做的那些无法解释的事情。书中关于莫斯布鲁格和莱因斯多夫伯爵的章节堪称同理心的杰作——一方面，他笔下的杀人犯逻辑严密，却又脆弱得令人胆寒；另一方面，他笔下的贵族却对国家正在发生的事情一无所知。

Some novelists excel at giving the reader the emotional feel of a character's mind (Dickens), others at the sensuous feel of a character's mind (Flaubert). Musil is wonderful at both of these—even though Ulrich isn't very emotional, a couple of the other characters are, and Musil enters into them quite smoothly. He is astonishing at characterizing the logical way in which the thoughts and perceptions of a thinking man progress, climax, and begin again with another subject. Musil uses the third-person omniscient point of view, and is perfectly at ease entering the minds of all his characters; he seems to get especially close to them, as if what he were saying about them is so concise that it must be absolutely true. Ulrich is both attracted to and disdainful of Diotima; for example, Musil writes, “What it really came to always was that Diotima began talking as though God had on the seventh day put man, like a pearl, into the shell of the world, and Ulrich then reminded her that mankind was a little heap of dots on the outermost crust of a midget globe” (p. 333 ). But as foolish as Diotima is, it grows apparent that Ulrich is even more foolish, because, just as his friends and relatives keep telling him, he is going nowhere. He is always right, but never productive, never happy, and never, except momentarily, engaged. The reader may enjoy his talents and his state of mind, but Ulrich himself is building to something that may not be pleasant.

有些小说家擅长让读者感受到人物内心的情感（狄更斯），有些则擅长让读者感受到人物内心的感官体验（福楼拜）。穆齐尔在这两方面都做得非常出色——尽管乌尔里希并不十分情绪化，但其他几个人物却情感丰富，而穆齐尔能够非常自然地融入他们的内心世界。他惊人地擅长刻画一个有思想的人的思维和感知是如何逻辑地发展、达到高潮，然后又围绕另一个主题重新开始的。穆齐尔采用第三人称全知视角，能够轻松地进入所有人物的内心世界；他似乎与他们格外亲近，仿佛他对他们所做的描述如此简洁明了，就一定是绝对真理。乌尔里希既被狄奥提玛吸引，又对她不屑一顾；例如，穆齐尔写道：“迪奥蒂玛总是说得好像上帝在第七天把人像珍珠一样放进了世界的壳里，而乌尔里希则提醒她，人类不过是小地球最外层壳上的一堆小点”（第333页）。但迪奥蒂玛固然愚蠢，乌尔里希显然更愚蠢，因为正如他的朋友和亲戚们不断告诫他的那样，他毫无建树。他总是对的，却从未有所作为，从未快乐，也从未真正投入其中，除了短暂的片刻。读者或许会欣赏他的才华和心境，但乌尔里希自身正在走向某种不愉快的结局。

The Man without Qualities requires and rewards patience. Like most modernist novels, it forgoes plot in favor of ideas, character, and, in this case, many very funny insights into modern life. Most novels come to seem, while one is reading Musil, rather coarse; most characters, too easily satisfied. The older editions and translations show that Musil is due for a revival in English. It can't come too soon.

《没有个性的人》需要耐心，也必将获得回报。如同大多数现代主义小说一样，它摒弃了情节，转而着重于思想、人物，以及——就本书而言——对现代生活的诸多妙趣横生的洞察。阅读穆齐尔的作品时，你会发现大多数小说都显得粗糙不堪；大多数人物都显得过于容易满足。早期版本和译本表明，穆齐尔的作品亟需在英语世界重获新生。这一天越早到来越好。

65. Mikhail Sholokhov. And Quiet Flows the Don

65. 米哈伊尔·肖洛霍夫。《静静流淌的顿河》

TRANS. STEPHEN GARRY
译者：斯蒂芬·加里

(1934; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1989), 554 PP.

（1934 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1989 年），554 页。

Although there was, of course, a radical breach in Russian culture and politics between the czarist era and the Soviet era, Sholokhov wrote his epic of war and revolution among the Cossacks in the most traditional epic and realistic style, and this remained the preferred style of Soviet literature until the demise of communism in Russia in 1991 . For that reason alone, it is interesting to analyze the differences between Sholokhov's novel and those of his Western contemporaries, but in fact And Quiet Flows the Don is a compelling novel in its own right, full of historical incident and human interest.

尽管沙皇时代与苏联时代之间，俄罗斯文化和政治发生了翻天覆地的变化，但肖洛霍夫仍然以最传统的史诗和现实主义风格创作了这部关于哥萨克战争与革命的史诗巨著。这种风格在1991年苏联解体之前一直是苏联文学的主流。仅凭这一点，分析肖洛霍夫的小说与西方同时代作家的作品之间的差异就颇为有趣。但事实上，《静静地流淌着顿河》本身就是一部引人入胜的小说，充满了历史事件和人文情怀。

Sholokhov's progenitors were Gogol, who wrote about the steppe and the Cossacks in many stories and in Taras Bulba , and Tolstoy, who wrote about the Cossacks and also the Napoleonic Wars, in War and Peace. Like Gogol, Sholokhov wanted to portray a Cossack nation within the Russian nation, and like Tolstoy, he wanted to show the sweep of Russian history through a, or perhaps the most, pivotal period. He begins in about 1910 , several years before the start of the First World War, and ends this volume during the civil war, after a defeat of the Red Army in Cossack territory, before the final resolution in favor of the Communists.

肖洛霍夫的先驱是果戈理和托尔斯泰。果戈理在许多故事和《塔拉斯·布尔巴》中描写了草原和哥萨克人；托尔斯泰则在《战争与和平》中描写了哥萨克人和拿破仑战争。与果戈理一样，肖洛霍夫也想在俄罗斯民族内部描绘一个哥萨克民族；与托尔斯泰一样，他想通过一个，或许是最重要的时期，展现俄罗斯历史的脉络。他的故事始于1910年左右，即第一次世界大战爆发前几年，并在内战期间结束，此时红军在哥萨克地区战败，最终共产党获胜。

The novel begins with the family of Melekhov. The patriarch, Pan-taleimon, is the half-Turkish son of Prokoffey and a woman he has brought back from the Turkish war, whom the women in the village consider to be a witch. She is attacked toward the end of her pregnancy and dies while giving birth to Pantaleimon. He grows into a prosperous member of the village, but he is hotheaded and has a difficult time getting along with his own sons, especially Gregor. Gregor is in his early twenties when the main action of the novel begins, and his first act is to commence a scandalous affair with the wife of a neighbor who is away training in the army.

小说以梅列霍夫一家为开篇。一家之主潘塔莱蒙是普罗科菲与一位从土耳其战场带回来的女子所生的混血儿子，村里的妇女都认为她是女巫。她在临产前遭到袭击，在生下潘塔莱蒙时去世。潘塔莱蒙长大后成为村里的富人，但他性情急躁，与自己的儿子们相处不融洽，尤其是与格里高尔。小说的主要情节开始时，格里高尔二十出头，他的第一个举动便是与一位正在外地服兵役的邻居的妻子开始了一段惊世骇俗的婚外情。

Gregor, his mistress, and his wife form an odd triangle. For many years Gregor spurns the wife, and at one point she attempts to kill herself, but after the death of his daughter with his mistress, he returns to his wife and impregnates her with twins. In the meantime, war, revolution, and civil war disrupt the life of the village and bring everyone abruptly into the modern age, where they discover that all of their presuppositions about how things work are outmoded and suspect. This is epitomized in the relationship between two subsidiary characters, Bunchuk and Anna. Bunchuk is a modern man—a specialist in Marxist theory and the machine gun. Anna is a Jew and a female comrade. They meet and fall in love without parental permission or oversight, thrown together by events. They try to resist their passion because it is inconvenient to the revolution, but they succumb. She becomes pregnant, but is then shot in a street battle.

格里高尔、他的情妇和妻子构成了一个奇特的三角关系。多年来，格里高尔一直冷落妻子，妻子一度试图自杀。然而，在他与情妇所生的女儿去世后，他回到妻子身边，并让她怀上了双胞胎。与此同时，战争、革命和内战扰乱了村庄的生活，将所有人骤然带入现代社会。他们发现，自己对事物运行规律的所有预设都已过时且令人怀疑。这一点在两个次要人物——邦丘克和安娜——的关系中体现得淋漓尽致。邦丘克是一个现代人——精通马克思主义理论，也擅长使用机枪。安娜是一位犹太人，也是一位女同志。他们未经父母许可或监督便相遇相爱，命运将他们推到了一起。他们试图克制自己的激情，因为这不利于革命，但最终还是屈服了。安娜怀孕了，却在一次街头战斗中被枪杀。

Sholokhov is careful to show the Marxists’ analysis of the Russian Revolution, blaming the agonies and the discontent resulting from the senseless cruelty of the First World War for the outbreak of class warfare. The Cossacks are fighters, but according to Sholokhov, they do not really understand why they are fighting the Hungarians and the Germans. As in Gogol's depiction of the sixteenth century, they are cavalrymen—Sholokhov is especially good on their feelings for their horses—but in a world of machine guns, bombs, poison gas, and trench warfare, cavalrymen are more vulnerable, not less, because of their skills. Once the Cossacks have become inured to fighting, injury, and death, though, and once they have lost their sense of connection to the czar, then it is only a matter of time before they bring their expertise as killers home (one character comments that the short Russo-Japanese War resulted in the Revolution of 1905 , and so the much longer and more brutal world war will certainly result in a much longer and more brutal revolution). Sholokhov organizes his narrative by vignettes, many of which are moving and surprising.

肖洛霍夫细致地展现了马克思主义者对俄国革命的分析，将第一次世界大战的残酷无情所造成的苦难和不满归咎于阶级战争的爆发。哥萨克人是战士，但肖洛霍夫认为，他们并不真正理解自己为何要与匈牙利人和德国人作战。正如果戈理笔下的十六世纪一样，他们是骑兵——肖洛霍夫对他们与战马之间的情感刻画尤为出色——但在一个充斥着机枪、炸弹、毒气和堑壕战的世界里，骑兵的技能非但没有让他们变得更强大，反而使他们更加脆弱。然而，一旦哥萨克人对战斗、伤亡习以为常，一旦他们与沙皇失去了联系，那么他们迟早会将杀戮的本领带回故土（书中一个人物评论道，短暂的日俄战争导致了1905年革命，因此，旷日持久、残酷无比的世界大战也必然会导致旷日持久、残酷无比的革命）。肖洛霍夫以一系列小故事来组织叙事，其中许多故事都感人至深、出人意料。

But Sholokhov was not as disciplined as either Gogol or Tolstoy in organizing his material and understanding how to use a few protagonists to illuminate all parts of the plot. No doubt he wanted to avoid “heroic” clichs. But the effect is that in the second half of the novel, forward motion dissipates into a catalog of events that don't have much more than historical meaning. The novel becomes an occasionally vivid history movie where many actors have cameos but none carries the action. At the same time, Sholokhov does avoid the abstractions of modernism, where the protagonist's state of mind and experience of consciousness are given more weight than events. The First World War seems to have challenged every European writer's ability to portray reality—some opted for narrow focus (Svevo), others for altered consciousness (Ford Madox Ford in his Parade's End) , some for lyricism (the “Time Passes” section of Virginia Woolf's To the Lighthouse). Others ignored the war altogether and began with a fresh consciousness in the twenties (The Man without Qualities, The Great Gatsby, Lady Chatterley's Lover). Inspired by the great nineteenth-century Russians, though, Sholokhov attempted to trace the path from one form of consciousness and one era of history to the next, doing so chronologically, never forgetting that the events happened to men and women and that men and women lived and died in the events, and also that they were mass events in a way that almost no European events had ever been before. Like Lawrence, Sholokhov attempted the realist solution to dilemmas that had rarely or never been portrayed before, and as with Lawrence, some of the outcomes now seem weak because there was no way to truly imagine the future when Sholokhov was writing.

但肖洛霍夫在组织素材和运用少数几个主人公来阐明情节各个方面，不如果戈理或托尔斯泰那样严谨。毫无疑问，他想避免落入“英雄”的俗套。但结果是，在小说的后半部分，情节推进逐渐消散，变成了一系列除了历史意义之外并无实质内容的事件罗列。小说变成了一部偶尔生动的历史电影，许多角色只是客串，却无人真正推动剧情发展。与此同时，肖洛霍夫也避免了现代主义的抽象化，在现代主义中，主人公的心理状态和意识体验比事件本身更为重要。第一次世界大战似乎挑战了每一位欧洲作家描绘现实的能力——有些人选择聚焦于狭隘的视角（如斯韦沃），有些人则追求意识的改变（如福特·马多克斯·福特的《游行结束》），还有些人则追求抒情（如弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的《到灯塔去》中的“时光流逝”一节）。另一些人则完全无视战争，在二十年代以全新的意识重新出发（《没有个性的人》、《了不起的盖茨比》、《查泰莱夫人的情人》）。然而，受十九世纪俄罗斯伟大作家的启发，肖洛霍夫试图追溯从一种意识状态和一个历史时期到下一个时期的路径，他按时间顺序进行叙述，始终不忘这些事件发生在男男女女身上，男男女女在这些事件中生老病死，而且这些事件的规模之大，几乎是欧洲历史上前所未有的。与劳伦斯一样，肖洛霍夫试图用现实主义的视角来解决那些鲜少甚至从未被描绘过的困境，而且也像劳伦斯一样，由于肖洛霍夫写作时人们无法真正预见未来，他笔下的一些结局如今看来略显苍白无力。

Nevertheless, the novel is not a good medium for portraying mass events—words and sentences are too sequential and linear to evoke the overwhelming without making it abstract by using figurative language (as Dickens did in A Tale of Two Cities). What movies can show in a couple of minutes the novel lumbers through in many pages. The novel can detail the inner experience of mass horror by slicing small events finer and finer, evoking their cruelty more and more exquisitely (often through the memories of the protagonist rather than his or her immediate experience). For various reasons, Sholokhov opted not to do this by not giving any of his Cossacks the capacity for introspection. It is only through Bunchuk and Anna, who appear late in the novel, that the reader even begins to see the personal gains and costs of modern life.

然而，小说并非描绘群体事件的理想媒介——文字和句子过于循序渐进，难以在不借助比喻等抽象手法（如狄更斯在《双城记》中所做的那样）的情况下，唤起那种震撼人心的氛围。电影几分钟就能展现的内容，小说却要用大量的篇幅才能勉强呈现。小说可以通过对细小事件的层层剖析，细致入微地刻画群体恐怖的内在体验，从而更加精妙地展现其残酷（通常是通过主人公的回忆，而非其直接经历）。出于种种原因，肖洛霍夫选择不采用这种方式，他笔下的哥萨克人没有展现出任何内省的能力。直到小说后半段出现的邦丘克和安娜，读者才开始感受到现代生活带来的个人得失。

This novel's sometimes pedestrian and sometimes lyrical and sometimes horrific realism give it the feel of authenticity even as it slips out of the mainstream of the twentieth-century novel. In particular, what was once set decoration—Sholokhov's evocation of the timeless beauty of the steppe—has become another entry in the catalog of the lost world. And Quiet Flows the Don has become a historical document— not a bad fate, I think, for a Marxist novel.

这部小说时而平淡，时而抒情，时而又令人毛骨悚然的现实主义，赋予了它一种真实感，即便它已脱离了二十世纪小说的主流。尤其值得一提的是，曾经只是场景装饰的——肖洛霍夫对草原永恒之美的描绘——如今已成为逝去世界名录中的又一条目。《静静流淌的顿河》也因此成为了一部历史文献——我认为，对于一部马克思主义小说而言，这并非坏事。

66. Zora Neale Hurston. Their Eyes Were Watching God

66. 佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿。《他们的眼睛望着上帝》

(NEW YORK: HARPER, 1937), 193 PP.

（纽约：哈珀出版社，1937 年），193 页。

Zora Neale Hurston was a trained anthropologist who produced two novels, several field studies, and an autobiography. At about the time of Their Eyes Were Watching God , she was celebrated and successful, but for ten years before her death in 1960 , she fell into deep obscurity—working as a maid, falling victim to illness, and finally dying in a welfare home, only to be buried in an unmarked grave. Her work and her reputation were resurrected in the late 1960s in black studies courses. In 1973 , novelist Alice Walker searched for and marked her grave in Eatonville, Florida. By the late 1970s , Hurston's novel had become a classic of American literature, and it has remained continuously in print since then.

佐拉·尼尔·赫斯顿是一位受过专业训练的人类学家，她创作了两部小说、数部田野调查报告和一部自传。在《他们的眼睛望着上帝》问世前后，她声名鹊起，事业有成。但在1960年去世前的十年里，她却默默无闻——做过女佣，饱受疾病折磨，最终在一家福利院去世，葬于一座无名墓穴。直到20世纪60年代末，随着黑人研究课程的开设，她的作品和声誉才得以重现。1973年，小说家爱丽丝·沃克在佛罗里达州伊顿维尔找到了她的墓地并立碑纪念。到了20世纪70年代末，赫斯顿的小说已成为美国文学的经典之作，并一直畅销至今。

Hurston's protagonist is Janie, who is married off by her grandmother at sixteen to a prosperous but authoritarian farmer who has land and a house but who intends that Janie will work, breed, and do what he says. Janie and her grandmother have different opinions about what constitutes a good life for a woman—the grandmother knows that a beautiful woman on her own is in considerable danger and is likely to fall into not only a state of unvirtue, but also a dangerous life of vice. Janie, though, is both sensitive and sensuous—she wants love and pleasure, and she is seduced away from her first husband by the ambitious Joe Starks, a city man passing through on his way to a new and entirely black town. Within days of their arrival in the new town, Joe makes himself the mayor, builds himself a store, and soon becomes the wealthiest and most influential citizen. Janie is married to him for some twenty years, but he, too, proves unsympathetic and tyrannical. She is not sorry to see him die, but she is more or less indifferent to the fact that he leaves her a wealthy woman— wealth and safety had never been her goals in the first place. Some months after Joe's death, she meets Tea Cake, who is much younger, but very lively and affectionate. Defying her cautious friends, Janie marries Tea Cake and goes with him to the Everglades, where they work on the farms during the winter planting and harvesting season. Tea Cake is no parent's idea of a good catch—he's a musician and a gambler who is nearly killed in several fights and is not above flirting with other women from time to time, but his love for Janie is sincere and he is manly, fun, and smart. His end is unusual and horrifying, making full use of the setting and milieu that Hurston has chosen for her novel.

赫斯顿笔下的主人公简妮十六岁时被祖母嫁给了一位富裕但专横跋扈的农场主。农场主拥有土地和房屋，却只希望简妮能干活、生儿育女，并对他言听计从。简妮和祖母对女性美好生活的看法截然不同——祖母深知，一个美丽的女子独自生活会面临极大的危险，不仅可能堕落，还可能沉沦于罪恶的深渊。然而，简妮既敏感又感性——她渴望爱情和快乐，最终被雄心勃勃的乔·斯塔克斯诱惑，离开了她的第一任丈夫。乔·斯塔克斯是一位途经此地前往一座新兴的、完全由黑人组成的城镇的城里人。他们抵达新城镇几天后，乔就当上了镇长，建了一家商店，很快便成为镇上最富有、最有影响力的居民。简妮与他结婚约二十年，但他同样冷酷无情，专横跋扈。她并不为他的死感到惋惜，但对于他给她留下一笔遗产，她也漠不关心——财富和安全从来都不是她最初的追求。乔去世几个月后，她遇到了茶饼，他比她年轻得多，却活泼热情。尽管朋友们都劝她不要嫁给茶饼，简妮还是嫁给了他，并随他去了大沼泽地，在那里过冬播种和收割的季节，他们在农场里工作。茶饼并非父母眼中的好伴侣——他是个音乐家，也是个赌徒，曾多次在斗殴中险些丧命，而且时不时会和其他女人调情，但他对简妮的爱是真挚的，他为人正直、风趣幽默、聪明睿智。他的结局非同寻常，令人毛骨悚然，充分展现了赫斯顿为小说选择的背景和氛围。

But while Their Eyes Were Watching God is illuminating and exciting, it does not fit into any political program. The point of Janie and Tea Cake is that they do not conform. They are not good or even wise, they are free, and the essence of their appeal to one another is this freedom. Their idea of a good time is laughing, talking, and teasing one another (and, of course, by implication, having terrific sex). How their good times are to be earned or paid for is another question. Two or three times, Tea Cake goes off unexpectedly and without saying a word. The first time is when he finds Janie's money and goes on a bender. He returns, though not in shame, exactly, having lost most of it. He then proposes to win it back playing dice and poker, and he does, though he gets cut in a fight while doing so. He is not a middle-class striver by any means. But the implication is that his pleasure- and freedom-oriented personality is valuable because he hasn't given up a sense of wider possibilities in favor of property and authority. Janie goes with him and lives the exciting but insecure life that he prefers because she loves him and also because that life is more fun than the alternatives.

尽管《他们的眼睛望着上帝》这部作品引人入胜、扣人心弦，但它并不符合任何政治纲领。简妮和茶饼的精髓在于他们的不循规蹈矩。他们既不善良，也不睿智，他们自由自在，而他们彼此吸引的本质正是这种自由。他们所谓的快乐时光就是欢笑、交谈、互相戏谑（当然，言下之意是，还有美妙的性爱）。至于他们的快乐时光是如何获得的，则是另一个问题。茶饼曾两三次不告而别。第一次是他捡到简妮的钱后，便挥霍一空。他回来时，虽然输光了大部分钱，但并不感到羞愧。之后，他提议通过玩骰子和扑克赢回这些钱，他也确实做到了，只是在打架中受了伤。他绝非那种一心追求中产阶级生活的人。但这暗示着，他追求享乐和自由的性格之所以有价值，是因为他没有为了财产和权力而放弃更广阔的可能性。简妮跟随他，过着他所向往的刺激却又充满不确定性的生活，因为她爱他，也因为这种生活比其他选择更有趣。

One aspect of Hurston's novel is her rendition of Florida black vernacular. While she narrates in standard English, the characters always speak in dialect, which simultaneously sets the scene, broadens both the subject and the audience of the novel, and gives Janie's and Tea Cake's choices a context. White people are peripheral in this novel, and generally to be avoided. The reader has the sense that she is being invited to witness a place and a life that are hidden, and, in the twenty-first century, largely lost. The same device is at work in Halldr Lax-ness's novel of rural Iceland Independent People —men sit around and gossip, producing an ad hoc cosmology that is simultaneously local and universal. Janie and Tea Cake overtly agree or disagree with the prevailing wisdom only once in a while, but it reveals them to the reader and to themselves. As an anthropologist who returned to her home territory to observe the local customs, Hurston put herself in an interesting intermediate position between writing from the place and writing of the place. A lesser novelist might have found the balance difficult, but Hurston is well aware that her allegiance must be to the integrity of her characters and that the other aspects of a novel will sort themselves out if the drama of the plot and the logic of the character development seem authentic.

赫斯顿的小说的一大亮点在于她对佛罗里达黑人方言的运用。虽然叙述采用标准英语，但人物始终使用方言，这既烘托了氛围，又拓宽了小说的主题和读者群，还为简妮和茶饼的选择赋予了语境。白人在这部小说中处于边缘地位，而且通常被刻意回避。读者仿佛被邀请去见证一个隐秘的地方和一种隐秘的生活，而这种生活，在二十一世纪已基本消逝。哈尔德·拉克斯内斯的小说《独立的人》也运用了同样的叙事手法——男人们围坐在一起闲聊，构建出一种既具有地域性又具有普世性的临时世界观。简妮和茶饼偶尔才会公开地赞同或反对这种主流观点，但这却让读者和他们自己都更加了解了他们。作为一位回到故土观察当地风俗的人类学家，赫斯顿巧妙地将自己置于一种有趣的中间位置：既是“从地方出发”的写作，又是“书写地方”的写作。水平稍逊的小说家或许难以把握这种平衡，但赫斯顿深知，她必须忠于笔下人物的完整性，而如果情节的戏剧性和人物发展的逻辑性显得真实可信，小说的其他方面自然会迎刃而解。

67. Elizabeth Bowen. The Death of the Heart

67. 伊丽莎白·鲍恩，《心之死》

(GARDEN CITY, N.Y.: DOUBLED AY, ANCHOR, 1938), 418 PP.

（纽约州花园城：DOOULED AY，ANCHOR，1938 年），418 页。

Americans, I think, may be forgiven if they don't quite understand what is going on in this novel, because almost all of its emotional dynamic takes place beneath the surface, and the characters, wealthy Londoners not long after the First World War, speak almost entirely in language codes that refer to behavior codes that are either now lost or were always understood by only a select few. On the surface, there are two stories that intersect: that of Anna Quayne, in her thirties, who, as a result of a failed early love affair, has married a rather boring but respectable man; and that of Portia Quayne, Anna's sixteen-year-old half sister-in-law, who comes to live with the Quaynes for a year when her mother dies, leaving her an orphan. Portia is not only young; she is also diffident and alienated, fully aware that her position in the family is compromised by the fact that the father she shares with Thomas Quayne had been kicked out of the family home by Thomas's mother when he confessed that he was having an affair with Portia's mother, who had become pregnant. Anna, though more aggressive and self-assured than Portia on the surface, also feels compromised. Unable to produce children, she lives an idle, superficial life of social contacts, fashion, and gossip. The action begins when Anna confesses to her friend St. Quentin that she has read Portia's diary, and that the diary is not terribly complimentary about Anna herself or about anyone Portia has come to know in her new life.
