我认为，如果美国读者不太理解这部小说的内容，也情有可原，因为几乎所有的情感张力都隐藏在表面之下。小说中的人物是第一次世界大战后不久的伦敦富裕阶层，他们几乎完全使用着一套暗语，这些暗语指向的行为准则要么已经失传，要么原本就只有极少数人才能理解。表面上看，小说讲述了两个交织的故事：一个是三十多岁的安娜·奎恩，她早年一段失败的恋情让她嫁给了一个略显乏味但体面的男人；另一个是安娜十六岁的同父异母小姑子波西亚·奎恩，她的母亲去世后，她成了孤儿，便来到奎恩家住了一年。波西亚不仅年轻；她也同样羞怯疏离，深知自己在家庭中的地位岌岌可危：她与托马斯·奎恩的生父曾因与波西亚的母亲有染而被托马斯的母亲赶出家门，而波西亚的母亲当时已经怀孕。安娜表面上比波西亚更加强势自信，但内心也同样感到不安。由于无法生育，她过着游手好闲、肤浅的生活，沉溺于社交、时尚和八卦。故事由此展开：安娜向好友圣昆廷坦白，她读过波西亚的日记，日记里对安娜本人以及波西亚在新生活中结识的任何人都颇有微词。

The principal action of the novel is that Portia falls in love with Eddie, an irresponsible young man who hangs around Anna and to whom Thomas has recently given a job. Eddie acts out a kind of romantic hysteria that Portia takes seriously as love and thinks will lead to marriage. Eddie at least understands that he is utterly incapable of commitment or even generosity. He is akin to the Oscar Wilde young men of a previous generation whose object is to parasitize as many people as possible for as long as possible before coming to a bad end.

小说的主要情节是波西亚爱上了埃迪，一个不负责任的年轻人，他总是和安娜厮混，托马斯最近还给他安排了一份工作。埃迪表现得像个歇斯底里的浪漫主义者，波西亚却当真，以为这就是爱情，并认为这会让他步入婚姻殿堂。埃迪至少明白自己完全没有能力承担责任，甚至连慷慨大方都做不到。他就像上一代奥斯卡·王尔德笔下的那些年轻人，他们的目标是在落得悲惨下场之前，尽可能长时间地寄生在尽可能多的人身上。

But none of Bowen's characters is appealing. Anna is heartless; Thomas is ineffectual; St. Quentin, a novelist, is a social troublemaker; and family friends of Anna's whom Portia visits are simply not respectable, whatever other insights or talents or vitality they might have. Only Major Brutt, an old friend of Anna's who turns up, is in the least bit kindly, but he cannot find a job and appears to be heading toward some sort of netherworld that Bowen leaves nameless. In other words, once again, what is to be done with the girl? Bowen's answer seems to be that first her heart is to be killed, as Anna's has been before the outset of the novel and as Portia's is by Eddie, and then she might be found some sort of husband who would not be worthy of her respect or her affections, and then they will live out their lives in a formal marital sham.

但鲍恩笔下的人物没有一个讨人喜欢。安娜冷酷无情；托马斯无能为力；小说家圣昆廷是个社交麻烦制造者；波西亚拜访的安娜的那些朋友，无论他们有什么其他见解、才华或活力，都实在令人不敢恭维。只有安娜的老朋友布鲁特少校偶尔出现，他稍微有点好心，但他找不到工作，似乎正走向鲍恩没有明确指明的某种冥界。换句话说，鲍恩又一次提出了一个问题：这个女孩该何去何从？鲍恩的答案似乎是，首先要扼杀她的心，就像安娜在小说开篇之前就已经被扼杀，就像波西亚的心被埃迪扼杀一样；然后，她或许会被安排嫁给一个配不上她尊重和爱慕的丈夫，然后他们就只能在形式上的婚姻中苟活下去。

This is not to say that The Death of the Heart isn't a fine novel. Bowen's style makes it work. She writes with precision and pungency. At one point she observes, “On that early March evening, Anna and Portia both, though not together, happened to be walking in Regent's Park. This was Portia's first spring in England: very young people are true but not resounding instruments. Their senses are tuned to the earth, like the senses of animals; they feel, but without conflict or pain. Portia was not like Anna, already halfway through a woman's checked, puzzled life, a life to which the intelligence only gives a further distorted pattern. With Anna, feeling was now unwilling, but she had more resonance” (p. 158 ). Elsewhere, she writes of Portia's friend Lilian, “She walked around with the rather fated expression you see in photographs of girls who have subsequently been murdered, but nothing had so far happened to her” (p. 61 ). Every page has some sharp, arresting observation. Bowen's voice is cool, specific, rarely asking larger emotional questions, but always alluding to them indirectly. Anna, for example, may be unsympathetic—all of her feelings have become selfish—but Bowen indicates that it is life itself, or at least respectable life as it is constructed around Regent's Park, that has formed her.

这并非说《心之死》不是一部优秀的小说。鲍恩的文风使它熠熠生辉。她的文字精准而犀利。她曾写道：“三月初的一个傍晚，安娜和波西亚碰巧都在摄政公园散步，虽然她们并非同行。这是波西亚在英国的第一个春天：年轻人真诚却缺乏感染力。他们的感官与大地相连，如同动物一般；他们有感觉，却没有冲突或痛苦。波西亚不像安娜，她已步入女人饱受困扰、迷茫困惑的人生中期，而理智只会让这种人生更加扭曲。安娜此时已不愿流露情感，但她的情感却更加强烈”（第158页）。在另一处，她写道，波西亚的朋友莉莲“她走路时带着一种宿命般的神情，就像你在那些后来被谋杀的女孩的照片里看到的那样，但到目前为止，她还没有遭遇任何不幸”（第61页）。每一页都蕴含着精辟而引人入胜的观察。鲍恩的笔触冷静而精准，很少直接提出宏大的情感问题，却总是以间接的方式加以暗示。例如，安娜或许令人难以同情——她所有的情感都变得自私——但鲍恩指出，正是生活本身，或者至少是摄政公园周围构建的那种体面生活，塑造了她。

Portia is not to be saved because there is no one to save her. Major Brutt would like to save her, but when she comes to him from Eddie at the end of the novel, the mere sight of her in his hotel goads him to recognize that he has nothing to offer her. Only Matchett, Anna's housekeeper, cares about Portia, but Matchett herself is hard and judgmental, fond but not welcoming. Bowen's London is a cold place, far from Austen's Hampshire, where the people may be hard to take, but at least there are plenty of them. Bowen's characters find some solace only in going to the movies; conversations (such as Anna's with St. Quentin) can easily lead to betrayal and intrusion, and parties, such as those Eddie goes to or the one Portia is taken to when she is away on her visit, lead only to embarrassment or sometimes debauchery. All the characters act toward all the other characters as if attempts at intimacy or even warmth are at the least embarrassing, certainly impossible, and always in very poor taste.

波西亚注定无法得救，因为无人能够拯救她。布鲁特少校本想救她，但小说结尾，当她从埃迪手中来到他面前时，仅仅是看到她出现在他的旅馆里，就让他意识到自己无能为力。只有安娜的管家马切特关心波西亚，但马切特本人冷漠而苛刻，虽然亲切却并不热情。鲍恩笔下的伦敦冷酷无情，与奥斯汀笔下的汉普郡截然不同。汉普郡的人们或许难以相处，但至少人多热闹。鲍恩笔下的人物只能在电影院里找到些许慰藉；谈话（例如安娜与圣昆廷的对话）很容易演变成背叛和侵犯，而聚会，比如埃迪参加的那些，或是波西亚外出探亲时被带去的那场，最终只会带来尴尬，有时甚至是放荡不羁。所有角色对待其他角色的方式，都仿佛在说，尝试建立亲密关系甚至表达温暖，至少是令人尴尬的，当然是不可能的，而且总是非常低俗的。

Bowen was a generation younger than Virginia Woolf and about the same age as Nancy Mitford. Bowen wrote at a time when women's lives were beginning to change under the pressure of modern urban life, which offered more freedom of every sort, but Anna and Portia, still suspicious of education and work, don't know what to do with their freedom. Only Matchett, the housekeeper, has a vocation, know-how, dedication. But even she has been exiled from her true home, the Quayne family estate in the country (Bowen grew up on family property in Ireland). There is some sense that all of the characters would be better off there than in the house next to Regent's Park, but as with The Good Soldier twenty years earlier, that traditional English paradise has shut down and there is nowhere else available.

鲍恩比弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫年轻一代，与南希·米特福德年龄相仿。鲍恩写作的年代，现代都市生活的压力开始改变女性的生活，赋予她们各种各样的自由。然而，安娜和波西亚仍然对教育和工作抱有怀疑，不知如何利用这份自由。只有管家玛切特拥有职业、技能和奉献精神。但即便如此，她也被放逐出了真正的家——位于乡下的奎恩家族庄园（鲍恩在爱尔兰的家族庄园长大）。某种程度上，所有人物都觉得，如果回到那里，生活会比住在摄政公园旁的房子里更好。但正如二十年前的《好兵》一样，那片传统的英式天堂已经崩塌，别无他处。

68. P. G. Wodehouse. The Return of Jeeves, Bertie Wooster Sees It Through, Spring Fever, The Butler Did It

68. P·G·伍德豪斯。《万能管家吉夫斯归来》、《伯蒂·伍斯特历险记》、《春热病》、《管家干的》。

(1953, 1955, 1948, 1956; REPR., NEW YORK: GRAMERCY BOOKS, 1983), 682 PP.

（1953、1955、1948、1956 年；重印，纽约：GRAMERCY BOOKS，1983 年），682 页。

To all appearances, P. G. Wodehouse is that rarest of comic novelists, a writer with no ax to grind. His novels are similar in feel but diverse in plot and point of view. They are like stock theatrical comedies or Hollywood romantic comedies of the 1930s —they seem simply to exist, more alike than different, and with no visible social analysis or intent. They are above all else well disposed. For some readers, this may seem naive or suspect. For others, it is a relief and a delight.

从表面上看，P·G·伍德豪斯是喜剧小说家中极为罕见的一位，他笔下的作品并无任何个人恩怨。他的小说风格相似，情节和视角却各不相同。它们就像是上世纪30年代的舞台喜剧或好莱坞浪漫喜剧——它们似乎只是自然而然地存在着，相似之处远多于不同之处，而且没有任何明显的社会分析或意图。最重要的是，它们都充满了善意。对一些读者来说，这或许显得天真或可疑；而对另一些读者来说，这却是一种解脱和愉悦。

In some ways, Wodehouse's plots are strictly traditional. More often than not, they involve bringing a charming and well-meaning but impecunious young person together with another charming and well-meaning and very pecunious young person. But the emphasis in Wodehouse is not on the young lovers—it is enough that she is beautiful and has a couple of other desirable traits (for example, the young woman in The Butler Did It has a melodious speaking voice and is an excellent cook). And it is enough that the young man is well spoken and honorable. In a Wodehouse novel, the emphasis shifts to the older, more knowing, and more idiosyncratic characters—Jeeves and other butlers, members of the House of Lords who have fallen on hard times, bachelor friends of the loving couple (Wodehouse wrote many books in the narrative voice of Bertie Wooster, who remarks, “Florence gave him the swift heave-ho and—much against my will, but she seemed to wish it—became betrothed to me”), or knaves of various ilks. He is more interested in the efforts of men of a certain age (earls, barons, retired butlers) to find some comfort and the opportunity to live out their quirks and crotchets in peace.

在某些方面，伍德豪斯的小说情节非常传统。通常情况下，故事讲述的是一位魅力十足、心地善良但家境贫寒的年轻人，与另一位魅力十足、心地善良且家境殷实的年轻人相遇。但伍德豪斯作品的重点并不在于这对年轻恋人本身——女主角只要美貌动人，并具备其他一些令人向往的特质（例如，《管家干的》中的年轻女子嗓音甜美，厨艺精湛），男主角只要谈吐得体、品行端正，就足以构成一段佳话。在伍德豪斯的小说中，重点转移到了那些年纪更大、见多识广、个性更鲜明的角色身上——吉夫斯和其他管家、落魄的上议院议员、爱侣的单身朋友（伍德豪斯以伯蒂·伍斯特的视角创作了许多小说，伯蒂曾写道：“弗洛伦斯迅速地把他赶走了，然后——虽然我极不情愿，但她似乎很希望如此——就和我订婚了”），或是形形色色的无赖。他更感兴趣的是，那些上了年纪的男人（伯爵、男爵、退休管家）如何努力寻找慰藉，并有机会平静地展现他们的怪癖和古怪之处。

Wodehouse's great genius is in his comic style, which works in part by paradox, like that of Oscar Wilde. Of Lord Shortlands's daughter and antagonist in Spring Fever he writes, “She was a girl who had an annoying habit of paying no attention to questions, being brisk and masterful and concentrated on her own affairs; the sort of girl, so familiar a feature of the English countryside, who goes about in brogue shoes and tweeds and meddles vigorously in the lives of the villagers, sprucing up their manners and morals until you wonder that something in the nature of a popular uprising does not take place” (p. 297 ). In Bertie Wooster Sees It Through , Bertie muses, “When you are trying to raise a thousand quid, the first essential, of course, is to go to someone who has got a thousand quid, and no doubt he had learned from Florence that I was stagnant with the stuff” (p. 152 ), illustrating another aspect of Wodehouse's charm—his way of inventing phrases that sound like slang but that are original to him. Bertie, in particular, has a distinct narrative rhythm that carries his novels and makes them seem especially jaunty. His style always contrasts with that of his butler, Jeeves, who is far more knowledgeable and cultured than Bertie. When Bertie asks him his opinion of a play Bertie is considering investing in, Jeeves remarks, “it seemed to me a somewhat immature production, lacking in significant form. My personal tastes lie more in the direction of Dostoevsky and the great Russians.” Jeeves's savoir faire combined with his loyalty to Bertie is very reassuring, implying that the English upper classes, while feckless, are also harmless, and easily used for a higher purpose by their much more enterprising servants.

伍德豪斯的伟大之处在于他的喜剧风格，这种风格部分是通过悖论来达到效果的，就像奥斯卡·王尔德的风格一样。在描写《春热》中肖特兰兹勋爵的女儿兼反派角色时，他写道：“她是个令人讨厌的女孩，对别人的问题漠不关心，做事干脆利落、精明强干，一心只想着自己的事情；这种女孩在英国乡村很常见，她们穿着布洛克鞋和粗花呢套装，热衷于干涉村民的生活，不断提升他们的礼仪和道德，以至于你会怀疑是否有什么民众起义之类的事情正在酝酿之中”（第297页）。在《伯蒂·伍斯特历险记》中，伯蒂沉思道：“当你想筹一千英镑的时候，首先当然是去找一个有一千英镑的人，毫无疑问，他从弗洛伦斯那里得知我在这方面一蹶不振”（第152页），这展现了伍德豪斯魅力的另一面——他创造的短语听起来像俚语，但却是他独创的。伯蒂尤其拥有独特的叙事节奏，贯穿他的小说，使之显得格外轻快活泼。他的风格总是与他的管家吉夫斯形成鲜明对比，吉夫斯比伯蒂博学多识，更有教养。当伯蒂询问吉夫斯对一部他正在考虑投资的戏剧的看法时，吉夫斯评论道：“在我看来，这出戏有点不成熟，缺乏实质内容。我个人更喜欢陀思妥耶夫斯基和伟大的俄罗斯作家。”吉夫斯的处事圆滑和他对伯蒂的忠诚令人非常放心，这表明英国上层阶级虽然不负责任，但也无害，很容易被他们更有进取心的仆人利用来实现更高的目标。

In his characters and plots, Wodehouse takes the tragic material of such earlier novels as The Good Soldier and reimagines it with grace and joy. Wodehouse, born in 1881 , was a near contemporary of Ford Madox Ford, but Wodehouse immigrated to America in 1909 and got to Hollywood soon thereafter. He quickly saw the absurdities of English-American relations—that the Americans had the money but the English had the class, and that much fun could be made of the exchange of money for class. The real repositories of tradition, for Wodehouse, are not the aristocrats themselves, but their servants, especially their butlers, whose job is to run the household and also to uphold forms of respect. Wodehouse's English society is not like Austen's or Ford's—it is far more permeable and various. Butlers turn out to have been safecrackers, lords turn out to be bookmakers. Everyone is in search of the same thing—a good meal, a comfortable establishment, and some time to pursue one's hobbies. The breakdown of the class system is not the occasion for regret, but the occasion for ingenuity (an ingenuity that mirrors Wodehouse's own).

伍德豪斯在其人物和情节中，借鉴了《好兵》等早期小说中的悲剧素材，并以优雅和欢快的笔触重新演绎。伍德豪斯生于1881年，与福特·马多克斯·福特几乎是同时代的人，但他于1909年移民美国，不久后便来到好莱坞。他很快便洞察到英美关系的荒谬之处——美国人拥有财富，而英国人则拥有阶级，而这种金钱与阶级的交换本身就充满了讽刺意味。在伍德豪斯看来，传统的真正传承者并非贵族本身，而是他们的仆人，尤其是管家，他们的职责不仅是管理家务，还要维护社会的尊严。伍德豪斯笔下的英国社会与奥斯汀或福特笔下的截然不同——它更加开放包容，也更加多元化。管家可能曾是窃贼，贵族也可能是赌博经纪人。每个人都在追求同样的东西——一顿美餐、一个舒适的场所，以及一些时间从事自己的爱好。阶级制度的瓦解并非令人遗憾的契机，而是激发创造力的契机（这种创造力与伍德豪斯本人如出一辙）。

Wodehouse wrote film scripts and plays, and his novels are all plotted in the same way, which eventually becomes tedious—the outcome of the action is never in suspense, and the compensatory motive for turning the pages is intended to be humorous or farcical plot twists, but these don't have anough substance to actually work. Enough Wodehouse is enough after a while, but some Wodehouse is essential to a happy literary life.

伍德豪斯写过电影剧本和戏剧，他的小说情节都千篇一律，读久了难免乏味——故事结局毫无悬念，而推动读者翻页的动力本应是幽默或滑稽的情节转折，但这些转折缺乏实质内容，难以真正奏效。读多了伍德豪斯的作品会感到厌倦，但适量阅读伍德豪斯的作品对于快乐的文学生活来说必不可少。

∗ For a balanced and detailed look at Wodehouse's controversial career during World War II please see Anthony Lane, “Beyond a Joke,” The New Yorker , vol. 80 , no. 9 , Apr. 19 , 26 , 2004 , pp. 19 – 26 .

* 有关伍德豪斯在二战期间备受争议的职业生涯的平衡而详细的介绍，请参阅 Anthony Lane 的文章“Beyond a Joke”，载于《纽约客》杂志，第 80 卷，第 9 期，2004 年 4 月 19 日、26 日，第 19-26 页。

69. T. H. White. The Once and Future King

69. T. H. 怀特，《永恒之王》

(1939; REPR., NEW YORK: PENGUIN PUTNAM, ACE, 1958), 639 PP.

（1939 年；重印，纽约：企鹅普特南出版社，ACE，1958 年），639 页。

The Once and Future King is steeped in learning and literature, and yet it is not quite literarily respectable in the way that the works of, say, Kingsley Amis or Virginia Woolf are. Maybe it has been contaminated in the minds of critics by popularity and Walt Disney animation. Nevertheless, it is a serious work, delightful and witty in many ways and yet very somber overall. The volume published as The Once and Future King is actually four works separately composed during about twenty years. The first, The Sword in the Stone , concerns the lost childhood of Arthur, future king of England, and his education by Merlyn. The second, The Queen of Air and Darkness , tells the story of adolescent sons of Orkney (Gawaine, Agravaine, Gaheris, and Gareth) and their mother, Morgause, who, unbeknownst to him, is Arthur's half sister. The third, The Ill-Made Knight , takes up the story of Sir Lancelot and his uneasy relationship with Queen Guenever and with Arthur. The fourth, briefest book, The Candle in the Wind , concerns the end of the Round Table and Arthur's death.

《永恒之王》博大精深，充满文学气息，却又不像金斯利·艾米斯或弗吉尼亚·伍尔夫的作品那样享有极高的文学地位。或许是受到了大众文化和迪士尼动画的影响，才让评论家们对它产生了偏见。尽管如此，它仍然是一部严肃的作品，妙趣横生，引人入胜，但整体基调却十分阴郁。这部名为《永恒之王》的合集实际上是由四部独立创作的作品组成，创作历时约二十年。第一部《石中剑》讲述了英格兰未来的国王亚瑟王失落的童年以及他接受梅林教导的故事。第二部《空与暗的女王》讲述了奥克尼群岛的少年王子们（高文、阿格拉文、加赫里斯和加雷斯）以及他们的母亲摩高斯的故事，摩高斯是亚瑟王的同父异母妹妹，而亚瑟王对此毫不知情。第三部《不完美的骑士》则讲述了兰斯洛特爵士与格温娜维尔王后以及亚瑟王之间复杂微妙的关系。第四卷《风中之烛》篇幅最短，讲述了圆桌骑士的终结和亚瑟王的死亡。

White, born in India in 1906 , was a brilliant student at Cambridge in the twenties, when he was already reading Malory's Morte d'Arthur. He clearly saw in Malory's cycle the British version of the Oresteia— an epic creation myth in which the violation, even the unintentional violation, of a cluster of taboos eventually leads to the disintegration of the nation created, even though, in White's work, almost everyone involved is reasonable, compassionate, and well intentioned. The outlines of the story are well known: the young Arthur, rushing to find a weapon for his foster brother, Kay, pulls a magic sword from a magic stone, revealing himself as the rightful king of England. He then engages in several wars, and during one of these he finds himself in Orkney, where he is seduced by means of a charm into sleeping with his half sister Morgause. The child of this union is Mordred. He then duly marries Guenever, but she subsequently falls in love with the greatest knight of the Round Table, Lancelot, who has come from France. The Orkney brothers, including Mordred, repeatedly use Guenever and Lancelot's adultery as an excuse for forwarding their own resentments, until finally all loves and all friendships have been sacrificed. Morgause is beheaded by her own sons. Lancelot mistakenly kills Gareth and Gaheris, Guenever is nearly burned at the stake. Lancelot kills Agravaine during a raid and Gawaine in a battle. Arthur is left bereft, only to die at the end, wondering if it is possible to govern at all.

怀特1906年出生于印度，二十年代在剑桥大学求学时才华横溢，当时他已经开始阅读马洛里的《亚瑟之死》。他显然从马洛里的这部作品中看到了英国版的《奥瑞斯忒亚》——一部史诗般的创世神话，其中一系列禁忌的违背，即便并非有意为之，最终也导致了所创造国家的瓦解。然而，在怀特的作品中，几乎所有相关人物都通情达理、富有同情心且心怀善意。故事梗概广为人知：年轻的亚瑟为了给养兄凯寻找武器，匆忙地从一块魔法石中拔出一把魔法剑，从而显露出自己作为英格兰合法国王的身份。之后，他卷入了数场战争，其中一场战争期间，他来到了奥克尼群岛，在那里，他被一种魔法诱惑，与他的同父异母妹妹摩高斯发生了关系。他们的孩子是莫德雷德。随后，他如约迎娶了格温娜维尔，但格温娜维尔却爱上了圆桌骑士中最伟大的骑士——来自法国的兰斯洛特。奥克尼兄弟，包括莫德雷德，屡次以格温娜维尔和兰斯洛特的通奸为借口，发泄各自的怨恨，最终所有的爱情和友谊都化为乌有。摩高斯被自己的儿子们斩首。兰斯洛特误杀了加雷斯和加赫里斯，格温娜维尔险些被绑在火刑柱上烧死。兰斯洛特在一次突袭中杀死了阿格拉文，又在战斗中杀死了高文。亚瑟王悲痛欲绝，最终在临终之际，仍在思考自己是否还能继续统治下去。

The Once and Future King is full of insights, scenes, and flourishes that are really quite astonishing. No doubt because of the material, for one thing, it is one of the few English novels that are utterly frank about the power of love and sex. Morgause is portrayed as a beautiful but trivial and silly woman, a witch like her sister Morgan le Fay, but not serious enough to do real spells. The harm she does is in the seductive and yet neglectful way she rears her sons, deforming their emotional lives so they are always subject to violent jealousies, outbursts, and hatreds. At one point they hear that she has gone with a couple of visiting knights to search for a unicorn but hasn't found it (not being a virgin, of course—and there is the implication that Agravaine has witnessed her seduction of one of the visiting knights that was the real purpose of the hunt). So the brothers persuade the kitchen maid, who is a virgin, to accompany them on a unicorn hunt of their own—they are intent upon winning their mother's attention by presenting her with a unicorn's head. The unicorn does indeed come to the kitchen maid and lay his head in her lap. Both moved and frenzied by the beauty of the unicorn, the four boys kill it and attempt to take the head as a trophy, creating only pain, grief, and mess with their efforts, and then getting in trouble when they return home.

《永恒之王》充满了令人惊叹的洞见、场景和精彩描写。毫无疑问，这得益于其题材，首先，它是为数不多的坦率描写爱情和性力量的英国小说之一。莫高斯被描绘成一个美丽却肤浅愚蠢的女人，像她的妹妹摩根勒菲一样是个女巫，但她不够厉害，无法施展真正的魔法。她造成的伤害在于她用诱人却又疏于管教的方式抚养儿子，扭曲了他们的情感生活，使他们总是饱受强烈的嫉妒、爆发和仇恨的折磨。有一次，他们听说她和几个来访的骑士一起去寻找独角兽，但一无所获（当然，她并非处女——而且暗示阿格拉文目睹了她勾引其中一位骑士，而这才是他们狩猎的真正目的）。于是，兄弟四人说服了还是处女的厨房女佣，陪他们一起去猎捕独角兽——他们一心想用独角兽的头颅来博得母亲的欢心。独角兽果然来到女佣面前，把头放在她的腿上。四个男孩被独角兽的美丽所感动，又被它的美貌冲昏了头脑，他们杀死了独角兽，试图把头颅当作战利品带走，结果却带来了痛苦、悲伤和混乱，回家后也因此惹上了麻烦。

White seems to know all there is to know about boys. Arthur and the knights of the Round Table are so many boys grown into manhood, seething with ambitions, conflicting desires, strong emotions, and barely recognized motives. At one point he writes of the Orkney brothers, “The idea which the children had was to hurt the donkeys. Nobody had told them it was cruel to hurt them, but then, nobody had told the donkeys, either. … So the small circus was a unity—the beast reluctant to move and the children vigorous to move them, the two parties bound together by a link of pain to which they both agreed without question. The pain itself was so much a matter of course that it had vanished out of the picture, as if by a process of cancellation” (p. 242 ). This is prose at its prosy finest, an observation made in a conversational tone with profoundly moving implications, that grows out of a simple scene, preceded and followed by many other equally apropos and yet simple observations.

怀特似乎对男孩的一切都了如指掌。亚瑟王和圆桌骑士们就像许多长大成人的男孩，他们野心勃勃，欲望交织，情感强烈，动机却难以捉摸。他曾这样描写奥克尼兄弟：“孩子们的想法是伤害驴子。没人告诉过他们伤害驴子很残忍，但驴子们也没告诉过他们……于是，这个小小的马戏团就成了一个整体——驴子不愿动弹，孩子们却使劲拉着它们，双方都被痛苦的纽带紧紧联系在一起，而他们都对此毫不质疑。痛苦本身如此理所当然，以至于它仿佛被某种机制抹去了一般，从画面中消失了”（第242页）。这是散文的极致之作，以对话般的语气，从一个简单的场景中引申出深刻动人的意味，而这一场景的前后又穿插着许多同样贴切却又简洁的观察。

White's novel is intense and rich. The first volume, which tells the story of Arthur's education (he is transformed into several animals and birds), is a treasury of English natural history and increasingly obscure forms of sport, such as falconry and boar hunting. The same is true in the third volume, which tells how Lancelot became the greatest knight. White writes, “Uncle Dap was the only one in the family who took Lancelot seriously, and Lancelot was the only one who was serious about Uncle Dap. It was easy not to be serious about the old fellow, for he was that peculiar creation which ignorant people laugh at—a genuine maestro. His branch of learning was chivalry.” And then White shows convincingly what a maestro of chivalry would know and how he would think (p. 324 ). White uses the inherent flexibility of prose to deliver a lot of information, not only background information that makes it easy for the modern reader to picture twelfth-and thirteenth-century England, but also good analogues to modern society—jousting as a form of cricket, for example—that work not only to clarify what might be confusing, but also to show the continuity of English life from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century.

怀特的这部小说内容丰富、引人入胜。第一卷讲述了亚瑟的成长故事（他曾化身为多种动物和鸟类），堪称英国自然史的宝库，其中还介绍了猎鹰术和野猪狩猎等日渐冷门的运动项目。第三卷同样精彩纷呈，讲述了兰斯洛特如何成为最伟大的骑士。怀特写道：“达普叔叔是家中唯一认真对待兰斯洛特的人，而兰斯洛特也是唯一认真对待达普叔叔的人。人们很容易对这位老先生不以为然，因为他是那种无知之人嘲笑的奇特人物——一位真正的骑士大师。他精通骑士学。” 随后，怀特令人信服地展现了一位骑士大师的知识储备和思维方式（第324页）。怀特利用散文固有的灵活性传递了大量信息，不仅提供了背景信息，使现代读者能够轻松地想象十二、十三世纪的英国，而且还提供了与现代社会的良好类比——例如，将马上比武比作板球——这不仅有助于澄清可能令人困惑的内容，而且还有助于展现英国生活从中世纪到二十世纪的延续性。

The Once and Future King is about male society, but White is not a misogynist. His portrait of Guenever is sympathetic and rich. Of particular note is the moment when Lancelot and Guenever first fall in love. They are out hawking, and Guenever makes a mistake in her task of helping Lancelot with his hawk. He rebukes her, and then, when her feelings are hurt, he suddenly recognizes that “she had been giving kindness, and he had returned it with unkindness. But the main thing was that she was a real person.” This recognition of common humanity is the source of their inconvenient and passionate love.

《永恒之王》讲述的是男性社会，但怀特并非厌女者。他对格温娜维尔的刻画既充满同情又细腻动人。尤其值得一提的是兰斯洛特和格温娜维尔初次坠入爱河的场景。他们外出放鹰，格温娜维尔在帮助兰斯洛特照看猎鹰时出了差错。兰斯洛特责备了她，但当她感到受伤时，他突然意识到“她一直善待我，而我却以冷漠回应。但最重要的是，她是一个真实的人。”正是这种对人性的共同认知，孕育了他们那段既充满波折又炽热的爱情。

The Once and Future King is full of comic scenes. One of the ways White deals with some of Malory's absurdities is to make them funny, as with King Pellinore and the Questing Beast or the visit of King Pellinore and Sir Palomides to Orkney. But he never forgets that underlying the good fellowship and prosperity that Arthur brings to “Gramarye,” or medieval England, are violence, rape, and incest. And there is human nature, too. In his efforts to substitute “right” for “might,” Arthur discovers that the human urge to win, to prevail, to gain status and revenge offers a constant challenge to any system of governing that hopes to promote cooperation rather than conflict.

《永恒之王》充满了滑稽的场景。怀特处理马洛里笔下某些荒诞情节的方式之一就是将其转化为笑料，例如佩里诺尔国王与寻兽，或是佩里诺尔国王与帕洛米德斯爵士访问奥克尼群岛。但他始终没有忘记，亚瑟王带给“格拉玛瑞”（即中世纪英格兰）的友好和繁荣背后，隐藏着暴力、强奸和乱伦。此外，人性也同样重要。亚瑟王试图以“正义”取代“强权”，但他最终发现，人类渴望胜利、渴望胜利、渴望地位和渴望复仇的本能，对任何旨在促进合作而非冲突的统治体系都构成了持续的挑战。

In the final volume, White does explicitly what is always tempting to the novelist—he analyzes the circles of relationships that begin with the most intimate and move toward the most impersonal and political. He is intent upon discovering the links between the personal and the political, between love and power, between the family and the nation. The promise of such an analysis is that the proper arrangement and resolution of personal relationships, with all their betrayals and disappointments and pleasures and satisfactions, will result in social peace and, conversely, proper laws and governance will result in healthy intimacies. The underlying premise of the novel as a form is that such rationalization and reconciliation is possible, because the novel always tries to set the individual into the social context. Merely making the links implies that a good fit is possible—if not for this protagonist, then for some other, less recalcitrant one. It is not that liberal social institutions have created the novel, it is that the novel is in its very organization liberal, because the individual always continues to exist and be compelling and the social group always continues to exist, also, containing in its very existence the idea that the individual can be reconciled to it. King Arthur recognizes before he dies that he has not succeeded in creating the kingdom he hoped for, owing, of course, to the effects of his own sins. But he is the once and future king. The novel ends with the implication that upon his return, he will try again, with better results.

在最后一卷中，怀特明确地做了小说家总是忍不住想做的事——他分析了人际关系的循环往复，从最亲密的关系开始，逐渐过渡到最疏离、最政治化的关系。他致力于探寻个人与政治、爱情与权力、家庭与国家之间的联系。这种分析的意义在于，妥善安排和解决人际关系，包括其中所有的背叛、失望、快乐和满足，将带来社会和平；反之，合理的法律和治理也将带来健康的亲密关系。小说作为一种文体，其根本前提是这种理性化和和解是可能的，因为小说总是试图将个体置于社会背景之中。仅仅建立这些联系就意味着一种良好的契合是可能的——即便对这位主人公而言并非如此，那么对其他一些不那么桀骜不驯的主人公而言也是如此。并非自由主义社会制度创造了小说，而是小说本身在其结构上就体现了自由主义精神，因为个体始终存在且具有吸引力，社会群体也始终存在，并且其存在本身就蕴含着个体可以与之和解的理念。亚瑟王在临终前意识到，他未能建立自己梦寐以求的王国，这当然是由于他自身罪孽的后果。但他既是昔日之王，也是未来之王。小说结尾暗示，他死后将再次尝试，并取得更好的结果。

70. Christina Stead. The Man Who Loved Children

70. 克里斯蒂娜·斯特德。《爱孩子的男人》

(1940; REPR., NEW YORK: PICADOR, 2001), 576 PP.

（1940 年；REPR.，纽约：PICADOR，2001 年），576 页。

The Man Who Loved Children is one of the few novels that come close to attaining the grandeur of tragedy, and the tragedy it most recalls, perhaps, is Medea. It is also a thoroughly modern novel and a fascinating social document. Stead's father was a Fabian socialist, and Stead was born in Australia. She lived for many years in the United States, was married to a prominent Marxist writer, and was up to date in her understanding of all the myriad subjects and ideas that come up in the course of this long and dense work of fiction. Most important, though, is that she actually does give her ordinary government bureaucrat and his unhappy wife that sense of unstoppable and fated intensity that literature usually reserves for kings and queens.

《爱孩子的男人》是少数几部接近悲剧宏大境界的小说之一，而它最令人联想起的悲剧或许是《美狄亚》。它同时也是一部彻头彻尾的现代小说，以及一部引人入胜的社会文献。斯特德的父亲是一位费边社会主义者，而斯特德本人出生于澳大利亚。她曾在美国生活多年，嫁给了一位著名的马克思主义作家，因此对这部篇幅宏大、内容丰富的虚构作品中涉及的众多主题和思想都有着深刻的理解。然而，最重要的是，她确实赋予了笔下这位普通的政府官员和他不幸的妻子一种不可阻挡、命中注定的强烈情感，而这种情感通常只有文学作品中的君王和王后才能体会。

Sam and Henny Pollit, husband and wife and parents of six and then seven children (the eldest, Louisa, Sam's child by his former wife, is the novel's protagonist), live in a large house in Washington, D.C. Henny is a former southern belle, one of twelve offspring of a wealthy and influential man, David Collyer. Sam is self-made, also from a big family, but a big family without money or status (one of his sisters is a schoolteacher). Sam is smart but impolitic, and Stead is masterful at communicating the maddening excesses of his demeanor. He is drunk on his own words, on his own elevated ideas, on his grandiose sense of himself and his mission. In a normal novel he would be a comic blowhard waiting for a comeuppance, something of a clown, but with the dark addition of unmitigated narcissism. Henny is dissatisfied and angry, disappointed in her marriage, and unsuited to her role (though more capable of performing it than Sam gives her credit for). She is maternal but not kind; toward Louisa she is often cruel and openly unloving. Toward the other children she is irascible and unpredictable. Sometimes she seems fond and indulges them, but at other times she is rejecting and impatient. At the outset of the novel she hasn't spoken to Sam in some years (they communicate by notes or through the children), and she has a lover named Bert, a large career bachelor she goes out with from time to time (Sam also has his flirtations). In the course of the novel, Sam and Henny enlarge. At first eccentric, they grow beyond dysfunctional, neurotic, and even psychotic, until they eventually become simply, irreducibly, hugely themselves, as beyond help or even diagnosis as King Lear or Prometheus.

萨姆和亨妮·波利特夫妇育有六个孩子，后来又生了七个（长女路易莎是萨姆与前妻所生，也是小说的主人公），他们住在华盛顿特区的一栋大房子里。亨妮曾是南方名媛，是富有且有权势的男人大卫·科利尔的十二个子女之一。萨姆白手起家，也出身于一个大家庭，但这个家庭既没有钱也没有地位（他的一个姐妹是位教师）。萨姆聪明却不善交际，斯特德精妙地刻画了他令人抓狂的种种过激行为。他沉醉于自己的言辞、高深的思想以及对自身和使命的夸大认知。在一般的小说里，他或许会是一个滑稽的自大狂，等待着自食恶果，有点像个小丑，但萨姆身上却多了几分肆无忌惮的自恋。亨妮心怀不满，怒火中烧，对婚姻感到失望，也觉得自己不适合自己的角色（尽管她比萨姆认为的更有能力胜任）。她有母性，但并不温柔；对待路易莎，她常常冷酷无情，毫不掩饰自己的冷漠。对待其他孩子，她则暴躁易怒，喜怒无常。有时她似乎很宠爱他们，纵容他们，但有时她又会冷漠疏离，缺乏耐心。小说开篇，她已经好几年没和萨姆说过话了（他们通过纸条或孩子们交流），她还有一个名叫伯特的情人，一个事业有成的单身汉，两人偶尔会约会（萨姆也有自己的风流韵事）。随着小说的展开，萨姆和亨妮的性格逐渐膨胀。起初他们只是古怪，后来发展到超越功能失调、神经质甚至精神错乱的地步，最终，他们彻底地、无可挽回地成为了他们自己，如同李尔王或普罗米修斯一般，无法被治愈，也无法被诊断。

Not every novel that wants to be a tragedy gets to be one. Usually novelists and readers have to be content with melodrama or somber realism, but Stead avoids both, and her techniques are very specific. Most commentators, including the poet Randall Jarrell (who resurrected The Man Who Loved Children twenty-five years after its first failed publication), complain of Sam's and Henny's excess—they have no sense of decorum, and they parade their disagreements openly in front of the children, their families, and the neighbors while all the time protesting that they prize discretion. For another thing, both are more than eloquent—Henny specializes in arias of invective, while Sam never shuts up about anything, but especially about his ideas and projects. He pries constantly into the private lives of his children and also, when he feels like it, holds children who don't please him up to the ridicule of the other children. He is a smiling tyrant, all-seeing, all-questioning, an atheist god in his own mind and in the minds of the younger children, who have no defense against either his crimes or his charms. Henny is the anarchist, or the nihilist, since no system, no government, no order, and, eventually, no life at all are preferable in her mind to the interminable presence of Sam. Sam and Henny are as dramatic as any stage characters, always demonstrating the progress of their inner lives to an audience. The excess is what saves their story from sober realism or Zolaesque naturalism. The only character who has an inner life is Louisa, the witness, and in many ways the consciousness through which the action is distilled.

并非所有想成为悲剧的小说都能如愿以偿。通常，小说家和读者只能接受情节剧或阴郁的现实主义，但斯特德却避开了这两者，她的写作技巧也十分独特。大多数评论家，包括诗人兰德尔·贾雷尔（他在《爱孩子的男人》首次出版失败二十五年后将其重新出版），都抱怨萨姆和亨妮的过激行为——他们毫无礼仪可言，在孩子、家人和邻居面前公开争吵，同时又不断标榜自己珍视谨慎。此外，两人都极其能言善辩——亨妮擅长滔滔不绝的谩骂，而萨姆则喋喋不休，尤其喜欢谈论自己的想法和计划。他不断窥探孩子的私生活，而且，只要他愿意，就会让那些不合他心意的孩子在其他孩子面前出卖自己。他是个面带微笑的暴君，无所不知，无所不问，在他自己和年幼的孩子们心中，他都是一个无神论的神。孩子们既无法抵挡他的罪行，也无法被他的魅力所迷惑。亨妮是个无政府主义者，或者说是虚无主义者，因为在她看来，任何制度、任何政府、任何秩序，最终甚至任何生命，都比不上萨姆无休止的存在。萨姆和亨妮的戏剧性堪比任何舞台剧角色，他们总是向观众展现自己内心世界的变迁。正是这种夸张的表达方式，使他们的故事免于落入冷静的现实主义或左拉式的自然主义窠臼。唯一拥有内心世界的角色是路易莎，她是见证者，在很多方面，她都是整个故事的意识源泉。

What saves the Pollits’ story from melodrama is the presence of the chorus, the five younger children, who respond with exquisite sensitivity and evenhanded affection to each parent. Ernie, the oldest boy, is especially fond of Henny, even though she betrays him repeatedly. Evie, who looks like Henny, is always being enlisted by Sam to do such things as come into his bed in the morning and scratch his head. He baby-talks her and woos her or criticizes and abuses her by turns, ensuring her future, according to both Louisa and Henny, as a wifely doormat or worse. Little Sam and Saul, twins, are no less transgressed upon and invaded, but they have solidarity with one another and serve mostly as an audience for the ridicule of the older children. Stead is wonderfully adept at individualizing the children and showing how each reacts to and is molded by each parent. The reader's constant sense of this chorus, of the damage the parents are doing both individually and together, is finally overwhelmed but never suppressed by excess and relentlessness. There is no sense by the end of the novel of cause and effect, no understanding of the specific costs the children will have to pay as adults for the storm of their childhoods. Stead wisely doesn't even address this question. It is enough to present the storm. The reader coexists with the children in the inescapable and enormous world that Sam and Henny have made, a family as horrible, irredeemable, and incurable as the family of Agamemnon or Atreus.

波利特一家故事之所以没有沦为煽情剧，全赖于五个年幼的孩子——这群孩子如同合唱队一般，他们对父母双方都展现出细腻的情感和均衡的爱。大儿子厄尼尤其喜欢亨妮，尽管她屡次背叛他。长相酷似亨妮的伊薇总是被山姆“指使”去做一些诸如早上爬到他床上挠头之类的事情。山姆一会儿用儿语哄她、讨好她，一会儿又批评她、虐待她，在路易莎和亨妮看来，这注定了她未来只能沦为妻子的垫脚石，甚至更糟。双胞胎小山姆和索尔也同样遭受着父母的侵犯和欺凌，但他们彼此之间却有着深厚的友谊，大多时候只是作为大孩子们嘲笑的对象。斯特德巧妙地刻画了每个孩子的个性，展现了他们如何与父母互动，又如何被父母塑造。读者始终能感受到这种合唱般的氛围，感受到父母各自以及共同造成的伤害，这种氛围最终被过度和无情所淹没，却从未被压制。小说结尾，读者无法理解因果关系，也无法理解孩子们成年后将要为童年风暴付出的具体代价。斯蒂德明智地没有触及这个问题。仅仅呈现这场风暴就足够了。读者与孩子们一同置身于萨姆和亨妮所创造的那个无法逃避的巨大世界中，这是一个如同阿伽门农或阿特柔斯家族般可怕、无可救药、无法治愈的家庭。

Nevertheless, Stead has a lively and informed political consciousness. What is at stake in the Pollit household is power, and even given all of Henny's failures as a parent, it is she who understands this. Sam Pollit is an absolutist who desires not only to invade his children's every thought, but also to have all their love and devotion. Big Brother in Orwell's 1984 is no more totalitarian than Sam Pollit. One of his more unsavory habits is to call himself “poor little Sam,” to make the children pity him as a victim, usually when he has just finished ordering them around or has just been challenged by Henny or Louisa. He is a constant fount of propaganda about himself, about the neighbors, about unnamed hostile strangers, about history, culture, science, geography, religion, and the proper way to live. At the end of the novel it appears as though he is going to have a radio show and become a media celebrity, thus unstoppably expanding his audience far beyond the family circle (Stead hardly seems to be a satirist in The Man Who Loved Children , but this is surely a quietly satirical moment). Stead clearly understands that the family is not sentimentally walled off from politics, but is the source of all political feeling and understanding. When Louisa runs away at the end of the novel, Stead explicitly shows that her sense of who she is, what the world is, and what her “home nation” is shifts as soon as she crosses the bridge that separates the house from the other side of the creek. For Stead the good news is that freedom of thought is possible—at least it is if Big Brother has had to live with an opposition, even an opposition that has been wrong-headed and unwise. The presence of the opposition allows at least some of the chorus (or audience) space for constructing notions of reality that are independent. At the same time, only Louisa escapes. She has to leave the other children to their fates, which is not a collective solution and reaffirms the underlying premise of tragedy that when kings and queens do battle, the general outcome for most of mankind is not a happy one.

然而，斯特德的政治意识活跃而敏锐。波利特家的核心在于权力，即便亨妮作为母亲屡屡失败，她也最清楚这一点。萨姆·波利特是个专制主义者，他不仅想侵入孩子们的每一个想法，还想得到他们所有的爱和忠诚。奥威尔《1984》中的老大哥并不比萨姆·波利特更专制。他最令人厌恶的习惯之一就是自称“可怜的小萨姆”，以此博取孩子们的同情，尤其是在他刚刚命令完孩子们，或者刚刚被亨妮或路易莎挑战之后。他不断地向孩子们灌输各种观念，从他自己，到邻居，再到那些不知名的敌对陌生人，以及历史、文化、科学、地理、宗教，甚至所谓的“正确”生活方式。小说结尾，他似乎即将拥有自己的广播节目，成为媒体名人，从而势不可挡地将受众群体扩展到家庭之外（在《爱孩子的男人》中，斯特德似乎并非讽刺作家，但这无疑是一个暗含讽刺意味的片段）。斯特德显然明白，家庭并非与政治情感隔绝，而是所有政治情感和理解的源泉。小说结尾，路易莎离家出走，斯特德明确地表明，她对自身、世界以及“祖国”的认知，在她跨过连接家和溪对岸的桥的那一刻就发生了转变。对斯特德而言，好消息是思想自由是可能的——至少，如果“老大哥”不得不面对反对派的存在，即便这种反对派是错误的、不明智的，那么思想自由就成为可能。反对派的存在至少为部分“合唱团”（或受众）提供了构建独立现实观念的空间。与此同时，只有路易莎逃脱了。她不得不留下其他孩子听天由命，这并非一个集体的解决方案，也再次印证了悲剧的根本前提：当国王和王后交战时，对大多数人来说，结局往往并不美好。

The Man Who Loved Children was a critical and commercial failure when it was first published, and it is easy to see why. In the first place, it was unprecedented in its seamless integration of politics, psychology, and tragedy. Stead was a true heir to Charles Dickens in her understanding of how personalities project themselves outward and create symbolic worlds that are limned by eloquence. Most of Dickens's heirs intuitively grasped the truth of his depictions of the power of mental universes, but only Stead was able to do what Dickens did routinely, which was to have two or more of these universes abut and challenge one another. But Stead the sociologist was colder and more honest than Dickens, whose sentimental attachment to a Victorian ideal of family comity was sometimes shaken but never destroyed. Stead seems never to have had such a thing. At the opening of her novel, Sam and Henny are way beyond the point where most people (including Dickens himself) would have sought separation or divorce.

《爱孩子的男人》初版时遭遇了评论界和商业上的双重失败，个中缘由不难理解。首先，它史无前例地将政治、心理学和悲剧完美融合。斯蒂德对人格如何向外投射并创造出雄辩勾勒出的象征世界有着深刻的理解，堪称狄更斯的真正继承者。狄更斯的大多数继承者都凭直觉领悟了他对精神世界力量的描绘，但只有斯蒂德能够像狄更斯那样，将两个或多个这样的精神世界并置、相互挑战。然而，作为社会学家的斯蒂德比狄更斯更加冷峻、更加坦诚。狄更斯对维多利亚时代家庭和谐理想的感伤情怀虽时有动摇，但从未消逝。斯蒂德似乎从未有过这种情怀。在小说开篇，萨姆和亨妮的关系早已远远超出了大多数人（包括狄更斯本人）会选择分居或离婚的地步。

This novel is not for everyone, nor for every mood. I have read it twice with great admiration. When I tried to read it a third time (when I had a young family myself), I couldn't stand it. If Hamlet runs four hours and Lear almost five, well, The Man Who Loved Children runs fourteen or fifteen hours, and though the plot is actually quite neat and progresses steadily, novel-readers are not used to fifteen-hour storms. The catharsis here, compared with any other tragedy, is a long time coming. Nevertheless, Stead's novel is like Ford Madox Ford's The Good Soldier in its power to astonish and compel with each reading. It is sui generis among novels, and Stead, too, never wrote anything else like it.

这部小说并非人人都能接受，也并非适合所有心情。我曾满怀敬意地读过两遍。当我尝试第三次阅读时（那时我自己也已为人父母），却无法忍受。如果说《哈姆雷特》长达四个小时，《李尔王》接近五个小时，那么《爱孩子的男人》则长达十四五个小时。尽管情节其实相当精巧，推进也十分稳健，但小说读者并不习惯长达十五个小时的“风暴”。与其他任何悲剧相比，这部小说的情感宣泄来得格外漫长。然而，斯特德的这部小说如同福特·马多克斯·福特的《好兵》一样，每次阅读都能给人带来震撼和共鸣。它在小说中独树一帜，而斯特德本人也从未写出过类似的作品。

Some commentators have wondered why this novel has not entered women's studies curricula or even twentieth-century literature curricula. I think it is because the novel is so anomalous that it can't easily be accommodated on a list with other novels. I would teach it along with some Greek tragedies or maybe a Russian novel or two written about Josef Stalin.

一些评论家不解为何这部小说没有被纳入女性研究课程，甚至没有被纳入二十世纪文学课程。我认为这是因为这部小说太过独特，难以与其他小说归为一类。我会把它和一些希腊悲剧，或者一两部描写约瑟夫·斯大林的俄国小说一起教授。

71. Junichiro Tanizaki. The Makioka Sisters

71.谷崎润一郎。牧冈姐妹

(NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1948), 529 PP.

（纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1948 年），529 页。

All novels eventually become historical documents, because they either chronicle everyday life taking place all around the author as he writes, or they chronicle his ideas of what is true or important, which are always strongly determined by his circumstances. But some novels are conceived as historical documents, and one of these is The Makioka Sisters. Tanizaki wrote many novels in a long career—he was born in 1886 , and continued publishing until he died in 1965 . The Makioka Sisters was written during the Second World War, largely, it would seem, to depict a traditional Japanese way of life that was fast disappearing. Even so, Tanizaki's treatment of the four Makioka sisters— Tsuruko, Sachiko, Yukiko, and Taeko—and the husbands of the older two—Tatsuo and Teinosuke—is evenhanded and has, on the surface, an idle tone. The family dilemma is a rather simple one: Yukiko, the third sister, is approaching age thirty unmarried. Taeko, several years younger, has a liaison, but can't marry until Yukiko does.

所有小说最终都会成为历史文献，因为它们要么记录了作者写作时周围发生的日常生活，要么记录了作者对真理或重要性的思考，而这些思考总是深受其所处环境的影响。但有些小说本身就是以历史文献的形式创作的，《卷冈姐妹》便是其中之一。谷崎润一郎一生创作了许多小说——他生于1886年，一直持续出版到1965年去世。《卷冈姐妹》创作于二战期间，其主要目的似乎是为了描绘一种正在迅速消逝的日本传统生活方式。即便如此，谷崎润一郎对卷冈四姐妹——鹤子、幸子、雪子和妙子——以及两位姐姐的丈夫——辰雄和贞之助——的描写却十分公正，表面上看似漫不经心。这个家庭的困境其实很简单：三姐雪子即将年满三十岁，却仍未婚。比她小几岁的妙子有婚外情，但只有雪子结婚后她才能结婚。

The fault, for Yukiko, may be in her stars and it may be in herself. She is small, retiring, and old-fashioned, but stubborn. Many proposals have come and gone over the years; always something has happened to obstruct each one—either the man has been found deficient at last, or Yukiko has been unable to commit herself. Though the Makiokas are no longer a wealthy and powerful family, they do have prestige— Sachiko, the protagonist, often wonders if family pride has forestalled marriages that would have been perfectly acceptable. Over the five years of the action of the novel, the breakdown of each marriage negotiation is an index to how the Makiokas think of themselves, how others think of them, and how the Makiokas attempt to divine how others think of them and what this means for how they are to estimate their own value and status. In the meantime, Taeko, in her twenties, acts like a Westernized, liberated woman—she wears Western clothes, smokes cigarettes, and supports herself, at first by making elaborate dolls and then by setting up as a dressmaker. She gets into more and more trouble, and with each incident there is the ever-increasing danger that Yukiko's prospective suitors will be put off by scandal.

对由纪子而言，或许是命运使然，或许是她自身的原因。她身材娇小，性格内向，思想守旧，却又十分固执。这些年来，求婚无数，却又都无疾而终；总有种种变故阻碍着她——要么是男方最终被发现不合格，要么是由纪子自己无法做出承诺。尽管真纪冈家族已不再是富裕显赫的家族，但他们依然享有一定的声望——主人公幸子常常思忖，是否正是家族的骄傲阻碍了那些原本完全合适的婚姻。在小说故事发生的五年间，每一次婚姻谈判的失败都折射出真纪冈家族成员如何看待自己，他人如何看待他们，以及真纪冈家族成员如何试图揣测他人对自己的看法，并以此来评估自身的价值和地位。与此同时，二十多岁的妙子举止像个西化、思想解放的女性——她穿着西式服装，抽烟，靠制作精美的娃娃维持生计，后来又开了一家裁缝店。她惹出的麻烦越来越多，每一次事件都加剧了雪子的潜在追求者们因丑闻而望而却步的风险。

Though Tanizaki's plotting seems casual, the novel builds considerable suspense with each change in the fortunes of the characters. It is similar in technique to a novel by Anthony Trollope, or perhaps to an Icelandic saga. Events move along at a steady pace. The author writes of dramatic moments in much the same way as he writes of insignificant moments, and pretty soon the reader understands that in the chain of cause and effect, what seems insignificant might be more important than what is dramatic—in fact, there is no way to know, so the characters are always going over incidents in their minds, trying to find the thread that will make the action work out.

尽管谷崎润一郎的叙事看似随意，但随着人物命运的每一次转变，小说都营造出相当的悬念。其技巧与安东尼·特罗洛普的小说，或者冰岛萨迦有异曲同工之妙。事件以稳定的节奏推进。作者对戏剧性时刻和无关紧要的瞬间都以几乎相同的笔触描写，读者很快就会明白，在因果链中，看似无关紧要的事件或许比戏剧性的事件更为重要——事实上，我们无从得知真相，因此人物总是反复思考过往的事件，试图找到最终促成事件解决的关键线索。

The Makioka Sisters has plenty of action: Taeko is nearly drowned in a huge flood; Sachiko finds herself in a typhoon; the Second World War begins, first in China and then in Europe; Taeko's boyfriend is disinherited for stealing from the family jewelry store; Sachiko's daughter contracts scarlet fever; Taeko's other boyfriend gets gangrene from an operation and must suffer an amputation before he dies; Taeko herself contracts dysentery. Even so, the style of the novel, which is to portray the dialectical progress of Sachiko's and to some extent Teinosuke's thoughts as they deal with the difficulties and problems of five years, never varies—whatever the event, and whatever the characters’ emotions, consideration is all, calculation is all. Each marriage negotiation is a microcosm of the characters’ lives in general— what information is going to get out and to whom? Can leaks (for example, through the maids) be controlled? Is confession the best strategy, and if so, how is it to be expressed? What must be put up with and what can be manipulated? For an American reader, who perhaps sees impulsiveness as more passionate and true than endless calculation, the Makiokas are saved, I think, by their evident fondness for one another and the desire to preserve one another from as much pain as possible—these characters are hardly ever selfish, and even Taeko, some of whose actions come to seem selfish to Sachiko, is given the benefit of the doubt—perhaps she is simply more like the sisters’ father in temperament, perhaps she has been poorly trained or poorly guided by the sisters themselves.

《牧冈姐妹》情节跌宕起伏：妙子险些被洪水淹死；幸子遭遇台风；第二次世界大战爆发，先在中国，后蔓延至欧洲；妙子的男友因盗窃家族珠宝店而被剥夺继承权；幸子的女儿患上猩红热；妙子的另一位男友手术后感染坏疽，不得不截肢后去世；妙子本人也染上了痢疾。尽管如此，小说的叙事风格始终如一，即刻画幸子（以及在某种程度上也包括贞之助）在五年间面对种种困境和问题时，其内心活动的辩证演变——无论发生什么，无论人物的情感如何，考虑和算计才是最重要的。每一次婚姻谈判都像是人物生活的缩影——哪些信息会泄露出去，又会泄露给谁？泄密（例如通过女佣）能否得到控制？坦白是最佳策略吗？如果是，又该如何表达？哪些必须忍受，哪些可以巧妙应对？对于美国读者而言，他们或许认为冲动比无休止的算计更真挚、更富激情，因此，我认为，真木冈姐妹之所以能幸免于难，是因为她们彼此间显而易见的深厚感情，以及竭力保护对方免受痛苦的愿望——这些人物几乎从不自私，即使是妙子，她的一些行为在幸子看来或许有些自私，但她们也给予了她信任——或许她的性情更像姐妹俩的父亲，或许她没有得到姐妹俩的正确引导或教导。

As the reader gets more comfortable with the novel and its milieu, Sachiko's perennial second thoughts and cautions come to have their attractions. As they ponder and discuss the ramifications of every step, Sachiko and Teinosuke are actually creating the continuity that is otherwise vanishing around them—part of Tanizaki's theme of the disappearance of the old ways. Sachiko's and Teinosuke's worries serve to link this year's cherry blossom viewing with last year's and that of many previous years. They make of the parade of Yukiko's suitors a train of logic—this is who we were then, this is who we are now, and this is how we have become what we are now. When Tatsuo declines to spend much money on the sixteenth anniversary of the father's death, it says something about everything having to do with the family—who the father was, what Tatsuo's estimation of himself is, what has changed in Japanese society. Impulsiveness, as represented by Taeko, comes to seem not pure and innocent as much as a way of dispensing with the past that must have the effect of turning the continuity of individual lives into a series of unrelated explosions. As a result of her contemplations, Sachiko is often anxious, but as a result of cultivating her awareness of her history and putting all new events into context, she is also often reassured.

随着读者逐渐熟悉小说及其背景，幸子始终如一的犹豫和谨慎也开始展现出其魅力。幸子和贞之助在思考和讨论每一步的后果时，实际上是在构建一种正在消逝的延续性——这正是谷崎润一郎“旧习消逝”主题的一部分。幸子和贞之助的担忧将今年的赏樱与去年以及以往许多年的赏樱联系起来。他们将雪子的追求者们像一列逻辑列车般推演——这就是我们过去的样子，这就是我们现在的样子，这就是我们变成现在的样子的原因。当辰雄在父亲逝世十六周年纪念日不愿花费太多时，这暗示着与家庭相关的一切——父亲是怎样的人，辰雄如何看待自己，以及日本社会发生了哪些变化。以妙子为代表的冲动，与其说是纯洁无辜，不如说是一种摆脱过去的方式，必然会将个人生活的连续性扭曲成一系列互不相干的爆炸。幸子常常因为沉思而焦虑，但她也常常因为培养对自身历史的认知，并将所有新事件置于特定的背景中而感到安心。

The Makioka Sisters is a good example of the notion that a novel does not so much need a plot as an organizing principle. Though Tanizaki was quite familiar with Western novels, the sense of an Aristotelian sort of plot, based on conflict and aiming toward a large climax, meant to be cathartic, was not second nature to him, as it is to most literate Westerners. The marriage finally contracted for Yukiko is not self-evidently the best marriage or the worst—it is the one everyone finally manages in the end, and the reader understands that it does not promise to be extra happy or extra unhappy—it promises to fit in with the marriages around it. The same goes, in large part, for Taeko's marriage—a bartender with entrepreneurial aspirations who will let her do her dressmaking is the best she can hope for, but he is a kindly, presentable fellow, and maybe it will all work out. Tanizaki's intent is neither to damn nor to redeem his characters. For the most part, they are distinct within their group, but not inherently in conflict with it. It is neither a defeat to be subsumed within it nor a victory against nature to find integration. It is simply a detailed example of how something happens, how things work.

《牧冈姐妹》很好地诠释了小说与其说需要情节，不如说需要组织原则这一观点。尽管谷崎润一郎对西方小说颇为熟悉，但那种基于冲突、旨在达到高潮、具有净化作用的亚里士多德式情节，对他而言并非像大多数受过教育的西方人那样自然而然。雪子最终缔结的婚姻并非显而易见的最好或最坏——它是所有人最终都能接受的婚姻，读者也明白它既不承诺格外幸福，也不承诺格外不幸——它承诺的是与周围的婚姻相协调。妙子的婚姻在很大程度上也是如此——一个有创业抱负、愿意让她做衣服的酒吧招待，这已经是她所能期望的最好结果了，但他为人友善、举止得体，或许一切都会好起来。谷崎润一郎的意图既非谴责也非救赎他笔下的人物。大多数情况下，它们在各自的群体中都独树一帜，但并非本质上与群体相冲突。融入群体既非失败，融入群体也非战胜自然。这仅仅是事物如何发生、如何运作的一个具体例证。

Tanizaki's novels are not all so based in ordinary life. He was strongly influenced by The Tale of Genji and other highly dramatic Japanese cultural traditions, and he disagreed with the increasing Westernization of Japanese culture, but in The Makioka Sisters he resisted both anger and polemic, relying instead upon what seems almost like mere gossip to create a novel of the highest art.

谷崎润一郎的小说并非全部取材于日常生活。他深受《源氏物语》和其他极具戏剧性的日本文化传统的影响，并且不认同日本文化日益西化的趋势。但在《卷冈姐妹》中，他摒弃了愤怒和论战，转而依靠看似普通的闲聊，创作出了一部艺术臻于完美的作品。

72. Vladimir Nabokov Lolita

72. 弗拉基米尔·纳博科夫《洛丽塔》

(NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1955), 317 PP.

（纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1955 年），317 页。

Most people know the basic plot of Lolita —for one thing, two movies have been made from it, one with James Mason and one with Jeremy Irons. Humbert Humbert, an educated European middle-aged man with a fetishistic attraction for twelve- to fourteen-year-old girls, inserts himself into the domestic arrangements of a woman with a twelve-year-old daughter. When the woman is fortuitously killed, HH, as he calls himself, takes the daughter on a prolonged crosscountry car trip, repeatedly raping, molesting, bribing, and imprisoning her as they travel from motel to motel. After she escapes, he pursues her and her “rescuer,” first discovering Lolita, now eighteen, married, and pregnant, but still not interested in HH, then shooting the rescuer (a playwright named Quilty). The novel purports to be HH's jailhouse confession.

大多数人都知道《洛丽塔》的基本情节——首先，这部小说已被改编成两部电影，一部由詹姆斯·梅森主演，另一部由杰瑞米·艾恩斯主演。亨伯特·亨伯特，一位受过良好教育的欧洲中年男子，对十二至十四岁的女孩有着强烈的迷恋。他闯入了一位带着十二岁女儿的女性的家庭。当这位女性意外身亡后，自称亨伯特的他带着女儿开始了漫长的横跨美国之旅，一路上不断强奸、猥亵、贿赂并囚禁她，辗转于各个汽车旅馆之间。女儿逃脱后，亨伯特继续追捕她和她的“救命恩人”，先是发现了十八岁的洛丽塔，她已婚并怀孕，但仍然对亨伯特不感兴趣。随后，亨伯特枪杀了救命恩人（一位名叫奎尔蒂的剧作家）。小说声称是亨伯特在狱中的自白。

Lolita is a controversial novel, of course. It has made it into the critical pantheon of great twentieth-century novels, but it is also notorious, and it does not seem possible that it will be dislodged from either category. Even more than Ulysses it stands as a kind of index of literary taste. If you don't like it, then you don't truly understand great art. On the other hand, if you do like it, then what kind of person are you? Nabokov himself was opinionated about the nature of art—working as hard as James or Tolstoy to promote a theory of art and of the novel that led straight to him and his sort of greatness. As a teacher and an essayist, he was a tireless self-promoter who relentlessly demeaned as philistine those who didn't share his perceptions and ideas. His particular whipping boy was Dostoevsky, whose reputation he attempted to puncture at every opportunity, possibly because he had read Dosto-evsky's books in his youth and didn't remember them very well (as recent translators of Dostoevsky have suggested), possibly because Dostoevsky was very popular in the United States (Nabokov promoted Gogol, for example, who was less well known to a general American audience), or possibly because the two were so philosophically at odds. At any rate, whereas Dostoevsky was always engaged with political and moral questions, Nabokov maintained that he disdained such things as being outside the realm of true art, and at first glimpse Lolita seems to bear out Nabokov's view.

《洛丽塔》当然是一部充满争议的小说。它已跻身二十世纪伟大小说的殿堂，但同时也臭名昭著，而且似乎不太可能从这两个类别中脱身。它甚至比《尤利西斯》更能代表一种文学品味的标杆。如果你不喜欢它，那就说明你并不真正理解伟大的艺术。另一方面，如果你喜欢它，那你又是什么人呢？纳博科夫本人对艺术的本质有着独到的见解——他像詹姆斯或托尔斯泰一样孜孜不倦地推广一种艺术理论和小说理论，而这种理论最终将他引向了他自己以及他所认为的伟大。作为一名教师和散文家，他不知疲倦地自我推销，毫不留情地将那些不认同他观点和想法的人贬低为庸俗之辈。他尤其喜欢抨击陀思妥耶夫斯基，并抓住一切机会诋毁他的名声。这或许是因为他年轻时读过陀思妥耶夫斯基的作品，但记忆模糊（正如一些陀思妥耶夫斯基作品的近期译者所指出的那样），或许是因为陀思妥耶夫斯基在美国非常受欢迎（例如，纳博科夫推崇果戈理，而果戈理在美国普通读者中知名度较低），又或许是因为两人在哲学思想上截然相反。无论如何，陀思妥耶夫斯基始终关注政治和道德问题，而纳博科夫则认为这些问题不属于真正的艺术范畴，对此他嗤之以鼻。乍看之下，《洛丽塔》似乎也印证了纳博科夫的观点。

Philosophically, Lolita is in the tradition of conservative novels by novelists who accept the innate evil of human nature, such as Thackeray. In conservative novels such as Vanity Fair, The Picture of Dorian Gray , and Lolita , redemption is as impossible to achieve as true connection, and the protagonist either remains isolated at the end or achieves a new degree of isolation as a result of the action of the novel. Conservative novelists are much more likely to reserve a special place for art (or at least aesthetics) as a (or the) pure moral category in a world where all other moral categories have failed. They are also more likely to disdain the social programs of more liberal and socially active novelists who see human nature as either inherently good, or at least neutral, and capable of positive moral change. Nabokov made a vigorous case against the novel as a social or biographical document. In particular, he ridiculed psychological ideas current in the midcentury, especially Freudian ideas, that attempted to make causal connections in the emotional and mental lives of both characters and authors. He does not explore how HH and Lolita became, respectively, a pedophile and a slut; he simply accepts that they are, and that most of the other characters in the novel have secret sins as well. The pleasure and the redemption in the face of human nature is to use the artistic materials at hand to create a beautiful and interesting pattern, preferably one that is as intricate and convoluted as possible, full of internal and external references, wordplay, and complexities that enhance the game aspect of the work of art (and thereby make it more exclusive).

从哲学角度来看，《洛丽塔》属于保守主义小说传统，这类小说家接受人性固有的邪恶，例如萨克雷。在《名利场》、《道林·格雷的画像》和《洛丽塔》等保守主义小说中，救赎和真正的联结一样遥不可及，主人公最终要么依然孤立，要么因为小说情节的推进而陷入更深的孤立。保守主义小说家更倾向于将艺术（或至少是美学）视为纯粹的道德范畴，认为它存在于一个其他所有道德范畴都失效的世界。他们也更倾向于鄙视那些更自由、更积极参与社会活动的作家的社会纲领，这些作家认为人性本质上是善的，或者至少是中性的，并且能够进行积极的道德转变。纳博科夫曾有力地论证过小说不应被视为社会或传记文献。他尤其嘲讽了20世纪中期流行的心理学观点，特别是弗洛伊德的观点，这些观点试图在人物和作者的情感和心理生活中建立因果联系。他没有探究HH和洛丽塔分别如何变成恋童癖和荡妇；他只是接受了他们就是如此的事实，并认为小说中的大多数其他人物也都有不可告人的罪恶。面对人性，乐趣和救赎在于运用手头的艺术素材，创造出美丽而有趣的图案，最好是尽可能复杂精妙、充满内外指涉、文字游戏和各种复杂元素的图案，从而增强艺术作品的游戏性（并使其更具独特性）。

Lolita is an American novel, but Nabokov was a Russian and a European novelist. He was, in some sense, the major heir to the nineteenth-century Russian novelists, and in spite of his own distaste for biographical connection, I think it is fair to observe how the pattern of Russian history produced his ideas. Nabokov's father was an enlightened liberal jurist in Russia who went into exile in 1919 and was assassinated in 1922 , when Nabokov was twenty-three. The assassins were czarists. The great Russian novels of the nineteenth century were energized by a single quest—to find a way for Russia to enter the modern world without losing its Russian identity. Nabokov's father's assassination represented the path that Russia did not take, the constitutional Western secular path, and the author never stopped disdaining the path Russia did take. He readily saw that the fervor of the nineteenth-century novelists had resulted in a cruel and irrational upending of Russian society. As far as Nabokov was concerned, that closed off the two traditional forms of redemption—social change and spiritual change. The only alternative was to make the best of the physical world, flawed though it is.

《洛丽塔》是一部美国小说，但纳博科夫是一位俄罗斯作家，也是一位欧洲小说家。从某种意义上说，他是十九世纪俄罗斯小说家的主要继承人。尽管他本人并不喜欢将自己的经历与传记联系起来，但我认为，考察俄罗斯历史的模式如何塑造了他的思想是合理的。纳博科夫的父亲是一位开明的自由主义法学家，1919年流亡海外，1922年遇刺身亡，当时纳博科夫23岁。刺客是沙皇。十九世纪伟大的俄罗斯小说都受到一个共同追求的驱动——找到一条俄罗斯融入现代世界而不丧失自身身份的道路。纳博科夫父亲的遇刺代表了俄罗斯没有选择的道路，即西方的宪政世俗道路，而这位作家始终对俄罗斯最终选择的道路抱有蔑视。他敏锐地意识到，十九世纪小说家的狂热导致了俄国社会的残酷而非理性的颠覆。在纳博科夫看来，这堵死了两种传统的救赎之路——社会变革和精神变革。唯一的出路就是尽力适应这个充满缺陷的物质世界。

Lolita has to be seen as the story of a man who is making the best of the world as he knows it—his only higher faculty is a particular aesthetic response to a certain sort of girl. He wants to manipulate her as if she were a set of artistic materials. Early on, in fact, before the death of Lolita's mother, Charlotte, when Lolita happens to sit on his lap and he happens to climax without her realizing it, HH says, “Lolita had been safely solipsized,” and then, “What I had madly possessed was not she, but my own creation, another, fanciful Lolita—perhaps more real than Lolita; overlapping, encasing her; floating between me and her, and having no will, no consciousness—indeed, no life of her own” (p. 62 ). Except that fate intervenes to tempt him with custody of the real Lolita, and his instincts are the worst possible guide to either fostering her or finding satisfaction himself. The result is that she escapes, he never stops loving her or regretting his treatment of her, he fails to expiate his sins in his own mind, and he discovers that their relationship has always been unpleasant and meaningless to Lolita.

《洛丽塔》必须被视为一个男人如何尽其所能地利用他所知的世界的故事——他唯一高尚的才能是对某种特定类型女孩的审美反应。他想把她当作一套艺术材料来操控。事实上，早在洛丽塔的母亲夏洛特去世之前，当洛丽塔偶然坐在他的腿上，而他恰巧在她毫无察觉的情况下达到了性高潮时，HH说道：“洛丽塔已经被安全地‘唯我论’了。”然后，他又说：“我疯狂拥有的并非她，而是我自己的创造，另一个虚构的洛丽塔——或许比洛丽塔更真实；她与洛丽塔重叠，将她包裹；漂浮在我与她之间，没有意志，没有意识——实际上，她没有自己的生命”（第62页）。然而，命运介入，让他有机会抚养真正的洛丽塔，而他的本能却成了最糟糕的指引，无论是抚养她，还是从中获得满足。结果是她逃走了，他却从未停止爱她或后悔自己对她的所作所为，他无法在内心深处赎清自己的罪孽，并且他发现，对于洛丽塔来说，他们的关系一直都是不愉快的，毫无意义的。

Nabokov was thoroughly familiar with French literature and certainly recognized that the physical trap that the imprisoned girl finds herself in is mirrored by the mental trap the libertine himself resides in—the more HH seeks satisfaction from Lolita, the less he can find it and the more obsessed with her he becomes. Her outer hell is his inner hell, and his inner hell drives him to reinforce her outer hell at every possible point. The difference between HH and other tormentors, even Proust's M., is that HH believes in love and they don't, but the practical methods they all use to imprison their victims are the same. More than that, Lolita is a classic European novel in its preoccupation with the classic European theme of the irreducibly ambiguous nature of women and girls. Nabokov's answer to the traditional question is muted but distinct—when HH finds Lolita married, pregnant, eighteen years old, and living in a shack with her husband, he respects her autonomy—not only her right to choose her life but also her right to judge her history for herself. He gives her money he owes her from her mother's estate and leaves, more or less getting his papers in order so he can finish his tasks. But this recognition doesn't resolve his frustration. He can't possess her, but he also can't leave the mental hell he has made for himself. Unfortunately for this autonomy theory, Lolita soon dies in childbirth, killed by the author, thereby rendering all of the action of the novel more or less meaningless except as an expression of HH's aesthetic.

纳博科夫对法国文学了如指掌，他当然明白，被囚禁的女孩所处的肉体困境，正是浪荡子自身所处精神困境的映射——HH越是试图从洛丽塔身上寻求满足，就越是无法得到，也越是为她着迷。她的外在地狱便是他的内在地狱，而他的内在地狱驱使他想方设法地强化她的外在地狱。HH与其他施虐者，甚至包括普鲁斯特笔下的M，不同之处在于HH相信爱情，而他们不相信，但他们用来囚禁受害者的实际手段却如出一辙。不仅如此，《洛丽塔》也是一部经典的欧洲小说，因为它关注的是欧洲文学中一个经典的主题：女性和女孩身上那不可化约的暧昧本质。纳博科夫对这个传统问题的回答含蓄而鲜明——当亨利·哈迪斯发现洛丽塔已婚、怀孕、十八岁，并与丈夫住在简陋的小屋里时，他尊重她的自主权——不仅是她选择自己人生的权利，也是她自己评判自己历史的权利。他从洛丽塔母亲的遗产中拿出欠她的钱给她，然后离开，大致整理好文件以便完成他的工作。但这种认可并没有消除他的挫败感。他无法占有她，也无法摆脱自己亲手打造的精神炼狱。不幸的是，洛丽塔很快死于难产，死于作者之手，这使得小说中的所有情节除了作为亨利·哈迪斯审美的一种表达之外，几乎失去了意义。

Is Lolita a great novel? How does it compare to Anna Karenina , a novel that Nabokov himself respected, or to Middlemarch or to Madame Bovary ? How does it compare to the monuments of modernism such as Ulysses or The Trial ? For one thing, in 315 pages, Lolita is much more limited and less capacious than the socially descriptive and expansive nineteenth-century novels; it is less stylistically ambitious than Ulysses , less profound and original than The Trial. It doesn't quite sustain each third of the narrative (before Charlotte's death, between Charlotte's death and Lolita's escape, the pursuit of Quilty)—the last third is sketchy and not very interesting, as if the author can't realize HH without Lolita, or as if the stalking and the murder aren't that important to him as a theme, but he has to follow out the plot anyway. The last third shows that his observation of the American landscape is pictorial rather than analytical, not very insightful and similar in this to his observation of Lolita herself (as HH points out toward the end of his narrative). It might be assumed that since both novels ran into censorship difficulties, Lolita is similar to Ulysses in the way Lolita challenges sexual taboos, but Joyce's hero, Leopold Bloom, is a social outcast, not a moral outcast—Joyce makes the case for him that he is kinder and more truly connected than the people around him. Nabokov makes no such case for HH, and in fact HH never defends his abuse of Lolita; rather he never stops expressing his remorse. Lolita is more similar to Madame Bovary , in which the reader is asked to experience the subjective life of a character conventionally considered immoral. But the precedent of Flaubert's technique was a hundred years old by Nabokov's time, so technically Lolita is an advance upon Justine but not upon Madame Bovary. Lolita is a compelling, complex, and intriguing novel, but the only value it expresses is the value of freedom, and freedom, as Nabokov explores it, is highly ambiguous. When HH and Lolita are driving around the country, doing whatever they wish, their freedom is a prison of idleness and fear. When Nabokov is asserting his artistic freedom from the political and moral traditions of the novel (and the Russian novel in particular), he finally has nowhere to take his plot—the action leads to no revelations that aren't already present in earlier sections of the book. He must fall back on reiteration of his original ideas to wind everything up. So no, I don't think Lolita is a great novel, but I also don't think, as an example of artistic experimentation, that it can be avoided by anyone truly interested in the history and nature of the novel.

《洛丽塔》是一部伟大的小说吗？它与纳博科夫本人也十分敬重的《安娜·卡列尼娜》、或者《米德尔马契》和《包法利夫人》相比如何？它又与《尤利西斯》或《审判》等现代主义巨著相比如何？首先，《洛丽塔》篇幅仅有315页，远不及那些社会描写丰富、格局宏大的十九世纪小说那样包罗万象；它的文风也不如《尤利西斯》那样雄心勃勃，也不如《审判》那样深刻和独创。小说未能完整地展开叙事的三个部分（夏洛蒂死前、夏洛蒂死后到洛丽塔逃亡之间、以及对奎尔蒂的追捕）——最后三分之一显得草率且乏味，仿佛作者没有洛丽塔就无法完成《爱的复仇》，又仿佛跟踪和谋杀对他而言并非重要的主题，但他仍然不得不按部就班地推进情节。最后三分之一表明，他对美国风景的观察是具象的而非分析性的，缺乏洞察力，这一点与他对洛丽塔本人的观察如出一辙（正如HH在叙述结尾处所指出的那样）。人们或许会认为，由于这两部小说都遭遇了审查困境，《洛丽塔》与《尤利西斯》在挑战性禁忌方面有相似之处，但乔伊斯的主人公利奥波德·布卢姆是社会弃儿，而非道德弃儿——乔伊斯为他辩护，证明他比周围的人更善良，与人之间的联系也更紧密。纳博科夫并没有为HH做这样的辩护，事实上，HH从未为自己虐待洛丽塔的行为辩解；相反，他始终在表达自己的悔恨。《洛丽塔》更类似于《包法利夫人》，在这两部小说中，读者都被要求体验一个通常被认为是不道德的角色的主观生活。但福楼拜的技法在纳博科夫时代已经存在了一百年之久，因此从技术层面来说，《洛丽塔》超越了《朱斯蒂娜》，却不及《包法利夫人》。《洛丽塔》是一部引人入胜、错综复杂、耐人寻味的小说，但它所表达的唯一价值是自由的价值，而纳博科夫对自由的探索却充满了歧义。当赫尔曼·霍夫曼和洛丽塔驾车环游全国，随心所欲时，他们的自由实际上是一座懒惰和恐惧的牢笼。当纳博科夫试图摆脱小说（尤其是俄国小说）的政治和道德传统，展现其艺术上的自由时，他最终却发现自己的情节无处可去——故事的发展并没有带来任何新的启示，一切都已在前文中出现。他只能依靠对最初想法的重复来勉强收尾。所以，不，我不认为《洛丽塔》是一部伟大的小说，但我也不认为，作为艺术实验的一个例子，任何真正对小说的历史和本质感兴趣的人都可以回避它。

73. Rebecca West. The Fountain Overflows

73. 丽贝卡·韦斯特。《喷泉溢流》

(NEW YORK: VIKING, 1956), 313 PP.

（纽约：维京出版社，1956 年），313 页。

Rebecca West is better known as a journalist than as a novelist—she wrote a monumental history and analysis of the Balkans, Black Lamb and Grey Falcon , in the 1940s , and had a long and illustrious career (she died in 1982 , at age ninety, and her output of books of all types numbers many volumes). She was especially famous for her clear and pointed writing style, and The Fountain Overflows , written when she was in her midsixties, is emphatically the work of someone for whom writing is as natural as breathing. Everything about the prose of the novel is subtle but lucid—diction and pacing, the voice that moves effortlessly between past and present, evocation and comment. By turns, the narrator writes as an opinionated and willful adolescent observer and with the cooler judgment of a mature woman. While the action of the novel is often painful, the style is never lugubrious, yet there is an undercurrent of muted sadness in the contrast between past and present that is very affecting. This novel has many emotional layers, but is so readable that its technical sophistication (not to mention its wisdom about family life, women, men, girls, and history) has been too much overlooked.

丽贝卡·韦斯特作为记者的名气远胜于小说家——她在20世纪40年代撰写了关于巴尔干半岛的鸿篇巨著《黑羊与灰鹰》，并拥有漫长而辉煌的职业生涯（她于1982年去世，享年90岁，著述颇丰，涵盖各类书籍）。她尤其以清晰犀利的写作风格著称，《喷泉涌流》写于她六十多岁时，这部作品充分展现了她写作的自然流畅，如同呼吸一般自然。小说的散文处处精妙而清晰——用词和节奏，在过去与现在之间游刃有余的叙述视角，以及对细节的描绘和评论。叙述者时而像一个固执己见、任性的青少年观察者，时而又像一位成熟女性冷静的评判者。尽管小说情节常常令人痛苦，但其风格却从不阴郁沉闷，过去与现在的对比中蕴含着一丝淡淡的哀伤，令人动容。这部小说有很多情感层次，但它又非常易读，以至于它的技术复杂性（更不用说它对家庭生活、女性、男性、女孩和历史的智慧）被严重忽视了。

The Fountain Overflows opens when Rose, the narrator, is about eight or nine. She is one of four children. The oldest sister, Cordelia, is twelve or thirteen, and Rose has a twin sister, Mary. The boy, Richard Quin, is not yet of school age. They are the offspring of a famous Anglo-Irish conservative theorist and journalist, who is under some sort of a cloud that the children don't understand, and a Scottish pianist, who has given up her concert career in favor of domestic life. Socially they occupy a particular niche—educated and influential but not prosperous, and not English, gentry. It is clear from the first page of the novel that Papa is a bounder—brilliant, untrustworthy, and profligate, though charming and idealistic—while Mamma is volatile and long-suffering, with a true artistic temperament (that is, focused, as she says, on the fact that “there is a great deal in life that is not affected by what happens to you” (p. 307 ). Mamma's attitude both ensures the survival of the family and makes for a good deal of eccentricity—the girls, for example, often shudder at the spectacle of their mother's appearance when she goes out, but they are passionately devoted to her and to their father. They are forgiving and understanding and strong in a way that would make any modern child psychologist shudder.

《喷泉涌流》开篇时，叙述者罗斯大约八九岁。她是家中四个孩子之一。大姐科迪莉亚十二三岁，罗斯还有一个双胞胎妹妹玛丽。弟弟理查德·奎因还没到上学的年纪。他们的父亲是一位著名的英爱保守派理论家兼记者，他身上笼罩着一层孩子们无法理解的阴云；母亲是一位苏格兰钢琴家，她放弃了音乐会演出生涯，回归家庭生活。在社会地位上，他们占据着一个特殊的位置——受过良好教育，有影响力，但并不富裕，也不是英国的绅士阶层。从小说第一页就能看出，爸爸是个无赖——才华横溢，却不可信赖，挥霍无度，尽管他魅力十足，充满理想——而妈妈则性情多变，忍耐力极强，具有真正的艺术家气质（正如她所说，她专注于“生活中有很多事情并不受你遭遇的影响”这一事实，第307页）。妈妈的态度既确保了家庭的维系，也造就了家庭中诸多古怪之处——例如，女儿们常常对母亲外出时的装扮感到不寒而栗，但她们却对母亲和父亲都无比忠诚。她们宽容、善解人意，坚强得足以让任何现代儿童心理学家感到震惊。

The novel opens just after Papa has taken an editorial job with a small suburban London newspaper—his first job in London—and the family moves into a house he had lived in as a boy. It ends when the three girls depart in some sense into their adult lives—Rose and Mary take musical scholarships, and Cordelia discovers a talent for clothing design. West chooses and develops her themes and weds them to her plot very slyly and smoothly. By using the form of the memoir, she seems merely to be retailing incidents and adventures, with many colorful characters along the way, but really she is exploring the nature of family life, emotional inheritance, and love between parents and children, siblings and friends.

小说开篇不久，爸爸在伦敦郊区一家小型报社找到了一份编辑工作——这是他在伦敦的第一份工作——一家人搬进了他儿时居住的房子。小说结尾，三个女儿以某种方式步入了各自的成年生活：罗斯和玛丽获得了音乐奖学金，科迪莉亚则发现了自己在服装设计方面的天赋。韦斯特巧妙地选择并发展了她的主题，并将它们与情节完美地融合在一起。通过回忆录的形式，她似乎只是在罗列各种事件和冒险经历，其中穿插着许多形形色色的人物，但实际上，她是在探讨家庭生活的本质、情感的传承，以及父母与子女、兄弟姐妹与朋友之间的爱。

Papa is a womanizer and a gambler. The children notice that their smooth, happy times are punctuated by troubled times, in which not only is there no money, but also people keep coming to the house angrily seeking payments on past due bills, and that these times are followed by sudden removal to new lodgings. Mamma is sensitive and impractical, not at all equipped to be the wife of such an unreliable man. One early crisis in the novel results from Papa's refusal to communicate with his family—on the date when Mamma is to take the children from one house to another, he hasn't bothered to tell her the address or to send her a key. Embarrassment is Mamma's frequent lot. But just as she doesn't allow the children to resent and demean their father, West doesn't allow the reader to judge him for his sins. She quite skillfully portrays him from Rose's point of view as a complex human being who is not exactly doing the best he can but is subject to many conflicting impulses. Not the least of these is that he is Irish by birth but conservative by temperament, not unlike Joyce's Buck Mulligan, a natural traitor to everyone, including himself.

爸爸是个花花公子，也是个赌徒。孩子们注意到，他们平静快乐的时光总是被困境打断，不仅没钱，还不断有人怒气冲冲地上门催讨拖欠的账单，而这些困境之后，他们又不得不匆匆搬到新的住处。妈妈敏感而又不切实际，根本无法胜任这样一个不靠谱男人的妻子。小说开篇不久，爸爸就因为拒绝与家人沟通而引发了一场危机——妈妈要带孩子们从一处住所搬到另一处，他却既没告诉她新家的地址，也没给她寄钥匙。妈妈常常因此感到尴尬。但正如她不允许孩子们怨恨和贬低他们的父亲一样，韦斯特也不允许读者因为父亲的过错而对他妄加评判。她巧妙地从罗斯的视角出发，将父亲刻画成一个复杂的人，他并非尽其所能，而是饱受各种矛盾冲动的折磨。其中最不重要的一点是，他虽然是爱尔兰人，但性格保守，这与乔伊斯笔下的巴克·穆里根颇为相似，他天生就是个叛徒，背叛了所有人，包括他自己。

West's subtlety is beautifully displayed in an incident late in the novel: Mamma's cousin Jock, Scottish by birth, is considered by Rose to be a cruel, selfish, and crude man who plays at being a stock comic Scotsman while refusing to provide for his wife and daughter, who live much of the time with Rose and her sisters. He has the family gift for music, and Rose is both puzzled at and disdainful of what he has done with his gift. One night he comes by after playing his flute in a rehearsal of Handel's Messiah. After behaving obnoxiously, he takes out his instrument and plays a solo from Gluck's Orpheus. When afterward the women confront him with his earlier behavior, he says, sincerely for the first time in the novel, “Life is so terrible. There is nothing to do with it but break it down into nonsense.” This is clearly how Papa feels, also—West's sense is that somehow the men they know are less resilient and more despairing than the women.

韦斯特的细腻笔触在小说后半段的一个事件中展现得淋漓尽致：妈妈的表弟乔克，苏格兰人，在罗斯眼中是个残忍、自私、粗俗的男人。他装出一副滑稽可笑的苏格兰人模样，却拒绝供养自己的妻子和女儿，她们大部分时间都和罗斯以及她的姐妹们住在一起。他继承了家族的音乐天赋，罗斯既不理解又鄙夷他如何利用这份天赋。一天晚上，他排练完亨德尔的《弥赛亚》后，吹完长笛来到罗斯家。他举止粗鲁无礼，随后拿出乐器，吹奏了格鲁克《奥菲欧》中的一段独奏。事后，当罗斯和她的姐妹们质问他之前的行为时，他第一次在小说中真诚地说：“生活太糟糕了。除了把它分解成无意义的东西，我们还能做什么呢？”显然，爸爸也是这么想的——韦斯特觉得，他们认识的男人似乎比女人更缺乏韧性，也更绝望。

Papa finally leaves the family. His motive is not quite clear, but the catalyst is a pamphlet that he had been writing for a fee about the future (this is set in about 1906 ). Papa is not sanguine, and the picture he paints is both horrifying and unbelievable to the man who has commissioned the pamphlet. Papa is a man whose despair is both personal and political, and when Mamma discusses his departure with the children, she tries to get them to understand how his complexity, her complexity, the complexity of family life, and the complexity of the rapidly changing world around them fit together. In retrospect, of course, from the point of view of 1956 , Papa is not wrong in his predictions, but West makes her point tactfully and then leaves it alone. It is a mark of her skill as a novelist and the richness with which she paints her world that when she makes comments in her narrator's voice they flow in along with the rest and do not disturb the artful illusion of her narrative.

爸爸最终离开了家。他的动机并不十分明朗，但导火索是他受雇撰写的一本关于未来的小册子（故事背景设定在1906年左右）。爸爸并不乐观，他描绘的未来图景对于委托他撰写小册子的人来说既恐怖又难以置信。爸爸的绝望既源于个人经历，也源于政治考量。当妈妈和孩子们谈论他的离开时，她试图让他们理解，爸爸的复杂性、妈妈自身的复杂性、家庭生活的复杂性以及他们周围瞬息万变的世界的复杂性是如何交织在一起的。当然，从1956年的视角来看，爸爸的预言并非全无道理，但韦斯特巧妙地表达了自己的观点，然后便不再赘述。这正是她作为小说家的功力所在，也是她笔下世界丰富多彩的体现。当她以叙述者的口吻发表评论时，这些评论自然流畅，与故事的其他部分浑然一体，丝毫不会破坏她精心构建的叙事幻象。

West is much interested in the nature of art, especially as represented by music, and one part of her plot has to do with Cordelia, the oldest sister, who does not play the piano and, according to the mother, Rose, and Mary, has no musical talent of any kind. She takes up the violin and then is befriended by a woman teacher of a certain age who also plays the violin and thinks Cordelia has talent. The give and take between Cordelia and Miss Beevor, as seen through the eyes of a judgmental (and talented) younger sister, is quite entertaining, and serves as an occasion for West to develop her argument about truth, talent, and the requirements of art. This thread of the novel is quite unusual and original as a way of laying out the protagonist's inner struggle to become the artist who has written the novel, and the climax of The Fountain Overflows proves to be both surprising and stimulating.

韦斯特对艺术的本质，尤其是音乐，有着浓厚的兴趣。小说情节的一部分围绕着大姐科迪莉亚展开。科迪莉亚不会弹钢琴，而且据她的母亲罗斯和玛丽所说，她没有任何音乐天赋。后来，她开始学习小提琴，并结识了一位上了年纪的女教师。这位女教师也拉小提琴，并认为科迪莉亚很有天赋。科迪莉亚和比弗小姐之间的互动，通过一个爱评判（但同样才华横溢）的妹妹的视角展现出来，颇为有趣，也为韦斯特展开关于真理、天赋和艺术要素的论述提供了契机。小说的这一线索相当独特新颖，它展现了主人公内心挣扎，最终成为小说作者的历程。《喷泉溢出》的高潮部分既出人意料又引人深思。

Of course, it is always difficult to end a memoir, because life goes on and the protagonist is still alive, so why stop now? West does so in a smart way, giving Mamma and Papa both their due, serving up a realistic but upbeat denouement, and working out the thematic material, too. It is quite an accomplishment, and all the greater for being written with such verve and smoothness that the novel was serialized in Ladies’ Home Journal before publication.

当然，写回忆录总是很难的，因为生活仍在继续，主人公也还活着，为什么要就此结束呢？韦斯特处理得非常巧妙，既给予了父母应有的评价，又呈现了一个既现实又乐观的结局，同时也对主题进行了深入的探讨。这的确是一项了不起的成就，更难能可贵的是，这部小说在出版前曾在《女士家庭杂志》上连载，其文笔生动流畅，充满活力。

The Fountain Overflows is a perfect example of a certain kind of woman's writing that is so smart it seems as though it must have been as easy to compose as it is to read, so smart that it doesn't seem important compared to more difficult and experimental novels. Lots of modernists of West's generation had so much trouble integrating theme and story that they let the story aspect (narrative, plot, the smooth buildup of incident to climax and denouement) break down, asserting that the realistic novel didn't have the capacity to communicate what had to be said. A novel such as West's shows that a flexible, subtle, and intelligent style can communicate almost anything if the novelist is willing to accord the reader respect. The breakdown of narrative happens when the author wishes to emphasize thematic points rather than integrate them and risk that the reader will remain unconvinced (or unaware) of the author's opinions. It is the didactic novelist who doesn't have patience for narrative structure. Modernism might be seen as an attempt to coerce the reader, or at least convince her, rather than let her make up her own mind. But West is so in control of the emotional dynamic of her narrative that no opinion she offers in her voice as Rose, the child, or as the mature narrator, or in the voice of Mamma ever goes unnoticed. The story is convincing because it is wise, graceful, and thoroughly thought through.

《喷泉溢出》完美地展现了某种女性写作风格，这种风格如此精妙，仿佛创作起来和阅读起来一样轻松自如；如此精妙，以至于与那些更晦涩难懂、更具实验性的小说相比，它似乎显得不那么重要了。许多与韦斯特同时代的现代主义作家都难以将主题与故事融合，以至于他们任由故事的各个方面（叙事、情节、事件到高潮和结局的流畅铺垫）崩塌，并断言现实主义小说无法传达所有想要表达的内容。像韦斯特这样的小说表明，如果小说家愿意尊重读者，灵活、微妙而睿智的文风几乎可以传达任何信息。叙事的崩塌发生在作者试图强调主题而非将其融入故事之中，从而冒着读者无法理解（或根本不理解）作者观点的风险时。正是那些说教式的作家缺乏耐心去构建叙事结构。现代主义或许会被视为一种试图强迫读者，或者至少说服读者，而不是让读者自己做出判断。但韦斯特对叙事的情感张力掌控得如此精准，以至于无论是她以孩童罗斯、成熟叙述者，还是以妈妈的口吻表达的观点，都清晰可辨，不容忽视。故事之所以引人入胜，是因为它充满智慧、文笔优美，且构思精巧。

74. Nancy Mitford. The Pursuit of Love, Love in a Cold Climate

74. 南希·米特福德。《追寻爱情，寒冷气候中的爱情》

(1945, 1949; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 2001)

（1945年，1949年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage出版社，2001年）

# ↩

Don't Tell Alfred

别告诉阿尔弗雷德

(1960; REPRINT, NEW YORK: CARROLL & GRAF, 1990), 698 PP.

（1960 年；重印，纽约：CARROLL & GRAF，1990 年），698 页。

While it's not necessary to read Nancy Mitford's three linked novels about the Radlett clan all at once, it is almost irresistible to do so, they are so humane, worldly, and hilarious. Mitford, of course, was the eldest daughter of the famous Mitford family, the subject of numerous biographies and memoirs (the most informative of which is sister Jessica's Hons and Rebels). From a purely theoretical point of view, reading Nancy's novels in conjunction with Jessica's memoir is enlightening as an example of how a novelist selects, changes, and enhances given material to make it appealing and to make it fit a given form. Nancy Mitford was a great comic novelist, and her novels necessarily ignore some of the darker threads of the Mitford story, and of midcentury history, in which she and all the rest of them were deeply involved. The astute reader becomes aware of shadows and echoes that give the novels depth, even though the novelist does not linger over them but fits them into the comic form and tone of her work.

虽然不必一次性读完南希·米特福德关于拉德利特家族的三部关联小说，但这样做几乎令人难以抗拒，因为它们如此充满人情味、贴近生活，又妙趣横生。米特福德本人是著名的米特福德家族的长女，这个家族曾被撰写过无数传记和回忆录（其中最有价值的是她妹妹杰西卡的《荣誉与叛逆者》）。从纯粹的理论角度来看，将南希的小说与杰西卡的回忆录结合起来阅读，可以很好地理解小说家如何选择、改编和润色素材，使其更具吸引力并符合特定的写作形式。南希·米特福德是一位杰出的喜剧小说家，她的小说必然会忽略米特福德家族故事以及她和家族其他成员都深陷其中的20世纪中期历史中一些较为阴暗的情节。敏锐的读者会注意到小说中那些赋予小说深度的阴影和回响，尽管小说家并没有过多着墨于它们，而是将它们融入到作品的喜剧形式和基调中。

The Pursuit of Love takes place in the 1930s and concerns the ultimately successful quest of Linda Radlett, the family beauty and the daughter of extremely eccentric parents, to find a satisfying romantic attachment. She is two generations younger than Isabel Archer or Lily Bart and fully ready to dispose of herself. And she does what Isabel and Lily do: she makes a mistake the first time. But two generations after Isabel and Lily, she is able to happily rectify her mistake by running off with another man, who also proves unsatisfactory, and then to rectify it again.

《追寻爱情》的故事发生在20世纪30年代，讲述了出身名门、父母性格古怪的琳达·拉德利特最终找到真爱的故事。她比伊莎贝尔·阿切尔和莉莉·巴特年轻两代，早已做好了恋爱的准备。她也像伊莎贝尔和莉莉一样，第一次犯了错。但比伊莎贝尔和莉莉晚两代，她却能通过与另一个男人私奔来弥补自己的错误，尽管这段感情最终也让她失望，但她最终还是找到了真爱。

Love in a Cold Climate is a “paraquel” to the first novel. Fanny, the narrator of The Pursuit of Love , returns to narrate another story of the thirties, this one about neighbors of the Radletts, Lord and Lady Montdore and their daughter, who are the last manifestation of a supremely ancient and wealthy aristocratic family. Once again the story turns on the daughter's search for love, and once again her first try is unsuccessful, but Mitford adds several wonderfully clever twists to the plot—the real protagonist is not the daughter but her imposing, selfish, middle-aged mother, who also seeks and finds love.

《寒冷气候下的爱情》是第一部小说的“续篇”。《追寻爱情》的叙述者范妮再次出现，讲述另一个发生在三十年代的故事，这次的主角是拉德利特家的邻居蒙多尔勋爵夫妇及其女儿。他们是极其古老而富有的贵族家族的最后传人。故事再次围绕女儿的寻爱展开，她的第一次尝试也再次以失败告终。但米特福德为情节增添了几个巧妙的转折——真正的主角并非女儿，而是她那位强势、自私的中年母亲，她也在寻找并最终找到了爱情。

By the time of Don't Tell Alfred it is the late 1950s , and Fanny and Alfred are parents and foster parents to the children who were born as a result of the unions in the first novel. Those children are now falling in love and beginning their own adult lives, but Fanny's (and the author's) attention has shifted slightly to Fanny's mishaps and adventures as the wife of the British ambassador to France; the children's pairings are secondary.

到了《别告诉阿尔弗雷德》的故事发生时，已是20世纪50年代末，范妮和阿尔弗雷德已为人父母，同时也是第一部小说中那些结合所生孩子的养父母。这些孩子如今也开始恋爱，步入各自的成年生活，但范妮（以及作者）的关注点略微转移到了范妮作为英国驻法大使夫人的种种遭遇和奇遇上；孩子们的感情生活则退居其次。

Of the three novels, Love in a Cold Climate is the most playful and makes the most unconventional use of the comic form. It is delightful from beginning to end, perfectly sustained in tone and style, always recognizing disappointment and even tragedy from a distance, but ever willing and able to make the most of whatever circumstances present themselves. The key is expressed by the Radlett “chorus,” Jassy and Victoria. At one point they come into Fanny's house after Lady Montdore has left. Whereas she had complained offensively about the tea, they exclaim, “Not digestives! Vict—look! Digestives! Isn't Fanny wonderful? You can always count on something heavenly—weeks since I've tasted digestives, my favorite food, too!” (p. 397 ).

在三部小说中，《寒冷气候下的爱情》最为轻松诙谐，对喜剧形式的运用也最为别出心裁。它从头到尾都令人愉悦，基调和风格始终保持完美，虽然对失望乃至悲剧始终保持着一定的距离感，但却总能巧妙地利用各种境遇。拉德利特家的“合唱队”——杰西和维多利亚——完美地诠释了这一点。有一次，蒙多尔夫人离开后，他们来到范妮家。范妮之前还对茶颇有微词，而他们却惊呼：“不是消化饼干！维克——你看！消化饼干！范妮真是太棒了！她总能带来人间美味——我已经好几个星期没吃到消化饼干了，那也是我最爱的食物！”（第397页）。
