The central figures in the “love plot,” Lady Montdore's only daughter, Polly, and Boy Dougdale, rumored to be a former admirer of Lady Montdore herself, could be the couple in a realistic novel, a tragedy, or a melodrama, since he has a habit of abusing little girls (established at the beginning), and their marriage (which Polly insists on) is a huge disappointment to everyone in the family and a scandal in the neighborhood. Likewise, the fact that upon the death of Lord Montdore the estate is to pass into the hands of a Canadian cousin who turns out to be homosexual could also function much differently in a different sort of novel, but Mitford works all of these connections exuberantly into the mix. In fact, the cousin turns out to be a fabulous deus ex machina who comes from his own rather compromised circumstances in France and exerts his charms and his skills to sort everyone out and make everyone happy.

这部“爱情故事”的核心人物是蒙多尔夫人的独生女波莉和博伊·道格代尔，后者据传曾是蒙多尔夫人的爱慕者。他们的故事完全可以出现在现实主义小说、悲剧或情节剧中，因为博伊有虐待幼女的恶习（这一点在故事开头就已交代），而他们的婚姻（波莉坚持要嫁）令全家人都大失所望，也成了邻里间的丑闻。同样，蒙多尔勋爵去世后，庄园将传给一位加拿大表亲，而这位表亲竟然是同性恋，这一情节在其他类型的小说中也可能产生截然不同的效果。但米特福德巧妙地将所有这些联系融合在一起，令人耳目一新。事实上，这位表亲最终成为了一个绝妙的“救世主”，他来自法国一个境遇颇为坎坷的地方，凭借自己的魅力和能力，最终化解了所有人的矛盾，让每个人都获得了幸福。

The bracing answer, for Mitford, to the dilemmas of passion, selfishness, and loneliness is generous worldliness, especially of the French sort. She doesn't hesitate to laugh at the contrasting foibles of the French and the English (at one point Lady Montdore hosts a French noblewoman for dinner, and is for the first time in her life brought to speechlessness by the marquise's unceasing and detailed questions about the estate's every practical and financial arrangement), but in the end the French have the answers—good clothes, good food, settled methods of dealing with love and passion, and in general a reasonable approach to life that protects from the emotional ups and downs that bedevil the English characters. At the same time, the English characters have a liveliness and energy that literally populates Fanny's world. Mitford would have been growing up with her parents on the family estate when Ford Madox Ford was writing The Good Soldier , but there is quite an opposite feel in her novels—the English aristocracy is not stupid and attenuated and on its last legs, good riddance, it is passionately making its way into the modern world, full of ideas, political disagreements, and jokes.

在米特福德看来，面对激情、自私和孤独的困境，最令人振奋的答案是宽容的世故，尤其是法式的世故。她毫不掩饰地嘲笑法国人和英国人截然不同的怪癖（蒙多尔夫人曾款待一位法国贵妇共进晚餐，侯爵夫人没完没了地详细询问庄园里的每一项实际安排和财务安排，让她生平第一次哑口无言），但最终，法国人找到了答案——华服、美食、处理爱情和激情的成熟方式，以及一种理性的生活态度，使他们免受困扰英国人的情感起伏之苦。与此同时，英国人身上也散发着一种鲜活的生命力和活力，真正地融入了范妮的世界。米特福德在福特·马多克斯·福特创作《好兵》时，应该正和父母一起在家族庄园长大，但她的小说却给人一种截然相反的感觉——英国贵族不再愚蠢、衰弱、奄奄一息，他们正充满热情地融入现代世界，充满了各种想法、政治分歧和玩笑。

The best thing about Nancy Mitford is that she's funny. The humor, like much of the humor of the English novel in general, grows out of appreciation of human idiosyncrasy. Lady Montdore and Cedric, the Canadian, in particular, are beautifully observed. Powerful and rich, Lady Montdore is also opinionated and selfish, but Mitford insightfully depicts the unhappiness that gives her narcissism poignancy. Cedric's former life in Paris is very lightly sketched in, but the details indicate that Cedric, too, has been saved by those he is saving, and knows it. The second best thing about Nancy Mitford is that she has been everywhere that the reader may not have been, and has kept her eyes open and her wits about her. Though her canvas is personal, like Jane Austen's, she is not at all blind to either political events or social movements; she just happens to filter her insights through characters that preexist them. For a politically astute and experienced midcentury novelist, that is an unusual choice. It may have made her seem frivolous at the time, but it makes her seem perspicacious now. Ideology changes, she might have said, but gossip lasts forever.

南希·米特福德最棒的地方在于她的幽默感。这种幽默，如同大多数英国小说中的幽默一样，源于对人性独特之处的欣赏。蒙多尔夫人和加拿大人塞德里克尤其被她刻画得栩栩如生。蒙多尔夫人权势显赫、家境富裕，却也固执己见、自私自利，但米特福德敏锐地描绘了她内心深处的不快乐，正是这种不快乐赋予了她的自恋以悲悯之情。塞德里克在巴黎的过往生活被她轻描淡写地勾勒出来，但细节表明，塞德里克也曾被他所拯救的人所拯救，并且他自己也明白这一点。南希·米特福德的第二大优点在于，她去过读者可能从未去过的地方，并且始终保持着敏锐的观察力和清醒的头脑。虽然她的作品如同简·奥斯汀的作品一样带有浓厚的个人色彩，但她对政治事件和社会运动并非视而不见；她只是巧妙地将自己的洞见融入到那些先于这些事件而存在的人物之中。对于一位政治敏锐、经验丰富的世纪中期小说家来说，这的确是一个不同寻常的选择。这在当时或许会让她显得轻浮，但如今看来却显得颇具洞察力。她或许会说，意识形态会改变，但流言蜚语却永存。

Research on the Web indicates that while the Mitford family is of continuing popular interest, Nancy's virtues as a novelist are somewhat overlooked. It should be the other way around. She is a wonderful novelist who added a distinct vision to the tradition of the English comic novel. There is much more to her work, technically and sub-stantively, than meets the eye, but only if the reader can stop wallowing in pleasure long enough to notice it. Reading Nancy Mitford makes me believe that writing comic novels is one of the most purely humanitarian endeavors civilization has ever come up with.

网络研究表明，尽管米特福德家族的故事一直备受大众关注，但南希作为小说家的才华却在某种程度上被忽视了。这本应是反过来的。她是一位杰出的小说家，为英国喜剧小说的传统注入了独特的视角。她的作品无论从技巧还是内涵上都远比表面看起来更加丰富，但前提是读者能够暂时放下对阅读的沉溺，去发现其中的奥妙。阅读南希·米特福德的作品让我相信，创作喜剧小说是人类文明所能创造的最纯粹的人道主义事业之一。

75. Harper Lee. To Kill a Mockingbird

75. 哈珀·李，《杀死一只知更鸟》

(1960; REPR., NEW YORK: WARNER, 1982), 281 PP.

（1960 年；重印，纽约：华纳，1982 年），281 页。

To Kill a Mockingbird is perhaps the Uncle Tom's Cabin of the twentieth century (and no doubt it is no coincidence that the man Atticus Finch defends from a charge of rape is named “Tom”). The instant and enduring popularity of To Kill a Mockingbird as a Pulitzer Prize-winning novel and, very shortly thereafter, an Academy Award-winning film (for adapted screen play) shows that liberal ideas about the sources, problems, and solutions to American racism have wide appeal and that Americans would like the challenge of racism overcome, but only as an extension of other liberal values of fairness and individualism. To Kill a Mockingbird is now frequently taught in high schools in the United States. It is in many ways a perfect high school text—the plot is understandable, the characters are appealing, the light tone masks a serious purpose, and the motivations of the children, Scout and Jem, are considered typical (at least by many adults) of real American children (children born before the era of pop culture at least). In addition, the lessons of the novel are clear and can hardly be contradicted in a moral society—every man deserves a fair trial, no matter what his skin color, and educated people, people with sense and honor, prefer the rule of law to the rule of prejudice and revenge.

《杀死一只知更鸟》或许是二十世纪的《汤姆叔叔的小屋》（毫无疑问，阿提克斯·芬奇为之辩护的强奸犯名叫“汤姆”绝非巧合）。这部小说一经问世便迅速走红，并荣获普利策奖，随后又被改编成电影，荣获奥斯卡最佳改编剧本奖。其经久不衰的流行表明，关于美国种族主义的根源、问题和解决方案的自由主义思想具有广泛的吸引力，美国人希望克服种族主义的挑战，但前提是将其作为公平和个人主义等其他自由主义价值观的延伸。《杀死一只知更鸟》如今已成为美国高中的常用教材。它在很多方面都是一部完美的高中教材——情节通俗易懂，人物形象生动，轻松的基调下蕴含着严肃的主题，而书中两个孩子斯库特和杰姆的动机，至少在许多成年人看来，是现实生活中美国儿童（至少是流行文化时代之前出生的儿童）的典型特征。此外，这部小说的教训很明确，在一个有道德的社会里很难被反驳——每个人都应该得到公平的审判，无论他的肤色如何，受过教育的人，有理智和荣誉感的人，更喜欢法治而不是偏见和复仇的统治。

Most Americans know the plot—Scout and Jem are growing up in Alabama in the 1930s . Their childhood is made up of the traditional amusements—staying out of trouble as much as possible, running around the neighborhood, tormenting the neighbors, engaging in make-believe and other imaginative games. They have a friend, Dill, who visits in the summer. The widowed father, Atticus, is assigned by a local judge to defend a black man who lives in the town against a charge of rape pressed by a girl and her father who are the town derelicts—dirty, drunken, and violent. Although Atticus defends Tom eloquently and everyone in the court knows that he has proved that Tom cannot have committed the rape, Tom is convicted anyway and sent away to prison, where in spite of the hope for a successful appeal, he tries to escape and is shot. The derelict father, humiliated by Atticus, attempts revenge and is killed in the act.

大多数美国人都知道这个故事——斯库特和杰姆在20世纪30年代的阿拉巴马州长大。他们的童年充满了传统的娱乐活动：尽可能避免惹麻烦，在街区里奔跑玩耍，捉弄邻居，玩角色扮演和其他充满想象力的游戏。他们有个朋友叫迪尔，夏天会来拜访他们。寡居的父亲阿蒂克斯受当地法官指派，为镇上的一名黑人男子辩护，该男子被指控强奸，而指控者是镇上的一对流浪汉——肮脏、酗酒、暴力。尽管阿蒂克斯为汤姆辩护得淋漓尽致，法庭上的每个人都知道他已经证明汤姆不可能犯下强奸罪，但汤姆最终还是被判有罪，被送进了监狱。尽管人们都希望他能上诉成功，但他还是试图越狱，结果被击毙。流浪汉的父亲被阿蒂克斯羞辱后，试图报复，结果在复仇过程中被击毙。

One of the chief appeals of the novel is Scout's voice. Only six but literal-minded, outspoken, and tomboyish, Scout offers a rough, innocent perspective on the pretensions and compromises of the adults around her. She is quick to judge and hot-tempered. The author relies for irony throughout the novel on the disparity between what the reader knows is happening and what Scout thinks is happening. Both Scout and her brother, Jem, are educated by the events of the years covered by the narrative (three or four), but they are educated in different ways because their temperaments are distinct. Scout learns to control her emotions and understand, at least to some degree, that adult society is complex and nuanced. Jem learns what bravery is—not taking dares as much as taking responsibility. There is some sense early in the novel that Jem is disappointed in Atticus's manliness, but by the end he has learned to respect him.

这部小说最吸引人的地方之一在于斯库特的叙述视角。她只有六岁，却思维直率、直言不讳，像个假小子，以一种粗犷而天真的视角审视着周围成年人的虚伪和妥协。她很容易妄下判断，而且脾气暴躁。作者在整部小说中都运用了反讽手法，即读者所了解的事件与斯库特所认为的事件之间的差异。斯库特和她的弟弟杰姆都在小说所涵盖的三年或四年间经历了种种事件，但由于性格迥异，他们的成长方式也截然不同。斯库特学会了控制自己的情绪，并在某种程度上理解了成人社会的复杂性和微妙之处。杰姆则明白了什么是勇敢——与其说是冒险，不如说是承担责任。小说开头，杰姆似乎对阿提克斯的男子气概感到失望，但到了结尾，他学会了尊重阿提克斯。

The lessons Atticus teaches all have to do with respect—he considers even the Ewells, father and daughter, worthy of courtesy. When provoked by interfering relatives or childish misbehavior, he chooses to exhibit respect rather than to correct or offend. Is he a rounded, vivid character? At this point it is hard to know, because it is impossible to imagine him outside of his portrayal by Gregory Peck in the film of the novel.

阿提克斯教导的一切道理都与尊重有关——他甚至认为尤厄尔父女也值得尊敬。当受到爱管闲事的亲戚或孩子顽劣行为的激怒时，他选择以尊重代替纠正或冒犯。他是一个性格丰满、栩栩如生的人物吗？这一点我们很难判断，因为我们很难想象他脱离格里高利·派克在电影中的演绎会是什么样子。

There is no sense as the novel progresses that structural change is possible in the world Scout lives in. Maycomb County is small—there have apparently been no immigrants since the first settlers took their land and their places in society. Just as the Ewells have always been bums, the Finches have always been eccentrics. Just as the whites inhabit the main part of town and occupy all the important economic and social positions, the blacks live south of town and keep to themselves. The death of Tom and the death of Ewell cancel each other out, and Scout observes that talk of the trial quickly subsides. She accepts, in some sense, that she and Jem may have been the only people in town to have learned something from the event—when the sheriff insists on keeping the circumstances surrounding the death of Ewell quiet, he, like everyone else, is accepting that trying to change the town is more trouble than it is worth.

随着小说的推进，斯库特所处的世界似乎没有丝毫结构性变革的可能。梅科姆县很小——自从第一批定居者占据了他们的土地和社会地位后，这里似乎就再也没有移民了。正如尤厄尔一家一直游手好闲，芬奇一家也一直古怪离奇。正如白人居住在镇子的主要区域，占据了所有重要的经济和社会地位，黑人则住在镇子南边，与世隔绝。汤姆的死和尤厄尔的死相互抵消，斯库特注意到，关于审判的讨论很快就平息了。在某种程度上，她接受了这样一个事实：她和杰姆可能是镇上唯一从这件事中有所感悟的人——当警长坚持对尤厄尔之死的真相保持沉默时，他和其他人一样，也承认试图改变这个小镇得不偿失。

When we look back to To Kill a Mockingbird through the lens of the intervening years, we can see why the civil rights movement in the United States had to be instigated and led by black people themselves—even the most well-meaning white people (Atticus Finch is the model) didn't have the understanding and the will to break up the status quo and reimagine American life as socially, culturally, and politically as well as legally egalitarian. The virtue that Atticus represents—respect, and especially respect for privacy and eccentricity—is a virtue that makes change more difficult because it fails to question social forms that, Lee shows, are a significant part of racism. Atticus and the children, for example, make no headway at all against racist gossip. The best they can do—and Scout is always admonished to do this—is not to pay any attention. Maintaining the surface appearance of propriety is too important for her to declare her allegiances.

当我们透过这些年来的视角回望《杀死一只知更鸟》时，就能明白为什么美国的民权运动必须由黑人自己发起和领导——即使是最善良的白人（阿提克斯·芬奇就是个例子）也缺乏打破现状、重塑美国社会、文化、政治乃至法律平等的理解和意愿。阿提克斯所代表的美德——尊重，尤其是对隐私和个性的尊重——反而使变革更加艰难，因为它未能质疑那些李所揭示的、构成种族主义重要组成部分的社会形式。例如，阿提克斯和孩子们在对抗种族主义流言蜚语方面毫无作为。他们所能做的——斯库特总是被告诫要这样做——就是置之不理。对她而言，维护表面上的得体太过重要，以至于她无法表明自己的立场。

Thus To Kill a Mockingbird is doubly a social document—it documents small-town southern life and attitudes in the 1930s (rigid and antediluvian) but also liberal attitudes in the 1950s (stuck in legalism and individualism, unable to actually effect change). At the same time, it is an essential American text because it is so readable and straightforward. Teachers enthusiastically teach it along with novels written by black writers about similar subjects, and it serves as a safe introduction to more challenging material.

因此，《杀死一只知更鸟》具有双重社会文献意义——它既记录了20世纪30年代美国南方小镇的生活和观念（僵化守旧），也反映了20世纪50年代自由主义的观念（固守律法主义和个人主义，无力真正带来改变）。同时，它也是一部重要的美国文学作品，因为它通俗易懂，语言简洁明了。教师们热情地将它与黑人作家创作的类似题材的小说一起教授，它也为学生进入更具挑战性的内容提供了一个安全的入门途径。

It is interesting to speculate what Harper Lee might have written if she had kept writing novels, but she has been exceptionally reclusive. When asked why she didn't write another novel, she replied that the Pulitzer and the Hollywood success spoiled her. Perhaps they did. But perhaps she simply had only one story to tell, and her telling of it carried her to the limits of mainstream white liberal possibilities for imagining the great American subject—relations between black and white. After To Kill a Mockingbird , the right to tell the story went to black writers, where it still resides at the start of the third millennium.

设想如果哈珀·李继续写小说，她会写出什么样的作品，这很有意思，但她一直过着极其隐居的生活。当被问及为何不再创作小说时，她回答说，普利策奖和好莱坞的成功让她变得骄纵。或许的确如此。但或许她只是只有一个故事要讲，而她讲述这个故事的方式，已经触及了主流白人自由主义者对美国宏大主题——黑白关系——的想象极限。在《杀死一只知更鸟》之后，讲述这个故事的权利落到了黑人作家手中，直到第三个千年之初，这一权利依然掌握在他们手中。

76 Jetta Carleton. The Moonflower Vine

76 杰塔·卡尔顿。月光花藤

(NEW YORK: SIMON & SCHUSTER, 1962), 318 PP.

（纽约：西蒙与舒斯特出版社，1962 年），318 页。

This novel may be the most obscure contemporary novel on our list, but those who have read it, if the customer reviews at Earth's Biggest Bookstore are any guide, are very loyal to it. Jetta Carleton wrote only this novel, which appears to be autobiographical, at least in part, but Carleton's style is so dense and precise and her method of imagining the inner lives of each character so daring that she seems to have been unconstrained by fears either of remembering things wrongly or of offending her relatives. Her subject is the romantic passions of five members of the Soames family—Matthew and Callie, the husband and wife, and Jessica, Leonie, and Mathy, the older three of the four daughters (Mary Jo, the youngest, is understood to be the narrator). These adventures are narrated out of sequence—the first to be told is how Jessica falls in love at eighteen with the hired hand and runs off with him to his family in the Ozarks, where she subsequently makes her home even after her husband dies of what appears to be tuberculosis. The novel then flashes back to the youth of the patriarch, Matthew, who is the somewhat remote but controlling and dominant presence in the family. Far from being the cold and sometimes frightening figure he appears to be to the women, he is inordinately susceptible to female charms, and over his years of employment as a teacher and superintendent of schools in his small Missouri town, he succumbs to the attractions of numerous young girls, some of whom he flirts with and even dallies with in spite of conscientious resolves not to. Carleton's attitude toward Matthew's peccadilloes is forgiving—in the context of twenty-first-century strictures on sexual harassment, maybe surprisingly forgiving; the girls are portrayed as not actually seductive, but in some sense responsive, using Matthew for their own romantic designs as much as he uses them. The result of one of these flirtations is Callie's assertion, late one night in the woods, of her marital rights, and the conception of Mathy, the third daughter, whom Matthew is a little afraid of, since she represents to him the wages of sin (he had been thinking of the girl he was infatuated with while making love to Callie). The next section is about Mathy, who grows up wayward, independent, and self-willed, and ends up running off with an attractive young man, Ed, whom Matthew knows from his school and doesn't like. The reader can see that Ed and Mathy are certain to come to a bad end—the question is what the family will make of it. After Mathy dies, Matthew uses the adoption of Mathy's son, Peter, who is much like his mother, as a way to make more of his second chance with her than he had of the first. Callie's reaction is more mysterious—to the girls she seems to go crazy with mourning but they decide that that is a mother's right, and anyway, she eventually comes out of it. After the other two girls run off, Leonie stays home with her parents, subjecting them to her various virtues until she realizes that they would prefer that she left them alone. She then goes to Kansas City, intending to throw off all restraint and have some fun. She ends up connecting with Ed himself, and eventually marrying him.

这本小说或许是我们榜单上最冷门的当代小说，但从“地球最大书店”的顾客评论来看，读过它的人都对它赞不绝口。杰塔·卡尔顿只创作了这一部小说，它似乎带有自传性质，至少部分如此。卡尔顿的文风浓郁而精准，她对每个角色内心世界的刻画也大胆无畏，仿佛她完全不受记忆出错或冒犯亲人的顾虑。小说的主题是索姆斯一家五口人的爱情故事——马修和卡莉，夫妻二人；杰西卡、莱奥妮和玛西，四个女儿中的三个姐姐（最小的女儿玛丽·乔被认为是叙述者）。这些冒险故事以非线性叙事的方式展开——首先讲述的是杰西卡十八岁时爱上了雇工，并与他私奔到他在奥扎克山区的家中。即使丈夫死于疑似肺结核，她也依然在那里安家。小说随后闪回到一家之主马修的青年时代。马修虽然有些疏离，但却是家中控制欲极强、占据主导地位的人物。与他在女性眼中冷酷无情、有时甚至令人畏惧的形象截然不同，他极易被女性的魅力所吸引。在他担任密苏里州小镇教师和学监的那些年里，他经不住众多年轻女孩的诱惑，甚至与其中一些女孩调情、调情，尽管他曾下定决心不这样做。卡尔顿对马修的这些小过错持宽容的态度——在21世纪对性骚扰的严格审查下，这种宽容或许令人惊讶。书中描绘的女孩们并非真的具有诱惑力，而是在某种程度上顺从，她们利用马修来实现自己的浪漫计划，正如马修利用她们一样。其中一次调情的结果，是卡莉在一个深夜于树林中宣示了她的婚姻权利，并怀上了第三个女儿玛茜。马修对玛茜有些害怕，因为她在他看来代表着罪孽的代价（在与卡莉做爱时，他一直在想着自己迷恋的那个女孩）。接下来的章节讲述了玛茜的故事。她长大后变得任性、独立、固执己见，最终与一个英俊的年轻男子艾德私奔。艾德是马修的同学，马修并不喜欢他。读者可以预见艾德和玛茜的结局注定悲惨——问题是，这个家庭会如何看待这件事。玛茜去世后，马修收养了玛茜的儿子彼得，彼得很像他的母亲，马修希望借此机会，比第一次与玛茜相处时更加珍惜这段感情。卡莉的反应更加难以捉摸——在女孩们看来，她似乎悲痛欲绝，但她们认为这是母亲应有的权利，而且无论如何，她最终还是走出了阴霾。另外两个女孩离家出走后，莱奥妮留在家里陪伴父母，尽其所能地讨好他们，直到她意识到父母更希望她别再打扰他们。于是，她去了堪萨斯城，打算彻底放松，尽情玩乐。结果，她遇到了艾德本人，并最终嫁给了他。

Carleton mostly avoids the perils of this material, which, baldly summarized, sounds scandalous and best-sellerish, a Peyton Place of the Midwest, by depicting the southern Missouri landscape of the family farm in exceptional detail. The farm is small but much beloved, full of fields and grasses, trees and shrubs, rocks and flowers that present a seasonal drama to the members of the family. All admire and appreciate their natural surroundings, sometimes in spite of themselves. Since most of the novel takes place in the summer, when the family is settled on the farm, the characters frequently suffer from the heat, which has the effect of making the scenery palpable and especially sensual.

卡尔顿巧妙地避开了这类题材的种种弊端——如果简单地概括，这类题材听起来像是耸人听闻、畅销书式的作品，堪称中西部版的《佩顿小镇》——而是以极其细腻的笔触描绘了密苏里州南部家庭农场的景色。农场虽小，却深受家人喜爱，田野草地、树木灌木、岩石花草遍布，四季更迭，为家庭成员们呈现出一幅幅生动的画卷。每个人都欣赏并珍惜着周围的自然环境，有时甚至不由自主地沉浸其中。由于小说的大部分情节都发生在夏季，也就是一家人定居农场的时候，人物们常常饱受酷暑的煎熬，这使得周围的景色更加鲜活生动，也更具感官上的享受。

The five characters are a convincing family in several ways. They resemble one another but are ill-assorted, as members of families often are. Their contrasts to one another are exaggerated by proximity. Matthew loves Callie and she is essential to his sense of his identity and self-confidence, but her lack of interest in intellectual things (she can't read, though she pretends sometimes she can) means that he can't share things with her that are important and satisfying to him. Callie is sexy but submissive, and hardly ever dares to challenge Matthew, or even ask anything of him. She recognizes, though, that he had been the best bet of all the young men she might have chosen, and in the end he is a good husband even though he hasn't shown her the tenderness she might have liked. Carleton excels at depicting the personalities of the girls, who often don't understand one another at all, and would never, they think, make the choices that the others have made, or even have similar relationships to their parents. And yet there is familial loyalty and attachment, mostly arising out of a shared sense of the enjoyment of the farm and each other.

这五个角色在很多方面都构成了一个令人信服的家庭。他们彼此相似，却又格格不入，正如家庭成员之间常常存在的情况一样。近距离的相处更加凸显了他们之间的差异。马修深爱着卡莉，她对他的自我认同和自信至关重要，但卡莉对知识性事物缺乏兴趣（她不识字，尽管她有时会假装识字），这意味着他无法与她分享那些对他而言重要且令人满足的事情。卡莉性感却又顺从，几乎从不敢挑战马修，甚至不敢向他提出任何要求。然而，她也意识到，在所有她可能选择的年轻男子中，马修是最佳人选，最终他成为了一个好丈夫，尽管他没有展现出她渴望的温柔。卡尔顿擅长刻画女孩们的性格，她们常常彼此不理解，而且她们认为自己永远不会做出其他人做出的选择，甚至不会与父母建立类似的关系。然而，家庭成员之间仍然存在着忠诚和依恋，这主要源于他们对农场和彼此的共同喜爱。

To my mind, this is a novel characteristic of its time, the 1950s , because it completely avoids all political themes. To read it you would never know that black people existed in southern Missouri, that the area was still a hotbed of post–Civil War resentments, that the Cold War was raging, and that World War II had taken place. The novel exists in a timeless world of seasons and of girls coming of age, love their greatest concern, with earning a living teaching school or giving music lessons a distant second. The Soames family thinks only of religion, love, nature, and sometimes music. They are American innocents in spite of their lustiness, quite untainted by the compromises of American history. The novel is neither liberal nor conservative— more, perhaps, tribal, in the sense that while the characters do make authentic connections, these connections are only within their own family rather than with anyone outside (except for Jessica, who moves away). In addition, the world is repeatedly redeemed, not by human action but by natural renewal, as symbolized by the nightly flowering of the moonflower vine (a relative of the morning glory). In the end, none of the characters comes to an understanding of Christianity or Christian precepts—doctrines of fundamentalist Protestant religion don't seem to fit what they have learned—nor do they embrace their sexuality (though they seem to learn that they can't get rid of it), but they do come to an understanding of the nature and purpose of forgiveness, and each character achieves a feeling that happiness, even fleeting happiness, is to be recognized and cherished.

在我看来，这部小说极具时代特色，因为它完全避开了所有政治主题。读完之后，你根本不会意识到密苏里州南部曾有黑人居住，那里仍然是内战后怨恨的温床，冷战正酣，第二次世界大战也已爆发。小说构建了一个超越时空的世界，四季更迭，少女们在青春期成长，爱情是她们最关心的事情，而教书或教音乐谋生则退居其次。索姆斯一家只关心宗教、爱情、自然，有时也关注音乐。尽管他们也充满欲望，但他们依然是纯真的美国人，完全没有受到美国历史妥协的玷污。这部小说既非自由主义也非保守主义——或许更偏向于部落主义，因为尽管人物之间确实存在真挚的情感联系，但这些联系仅限于他们的家庭内部，而非与外界任何人（除了搬走的杰西卡）。此外，世界并非通过人类行为，而是通过自然更新而不断得到救赎，正如月光花藤（牵牛花的近亲）夜间盛开的花朵所象征的那样。最终，剧中人物都没有真正理解基督教或基督教教义——原教旨主义新教的教义似乎与他们所学到的并不相符——他们也没有接受自己的性取向（尽管他们似乎明白自己无法摆脱它），但他们确实理解了宽恕的本质和意义，每个人都体会到，幸福，即使是转瞬即逝的幸福，也值得被认识和珍惜。

Several American novels on our list— The House of the Seven Gables, The Awakening, To Kill a Mockingbird , and The Moonflower Vine — gain considerable dramatic tension from secrets that the characters are required to keep to maintain respectability in the towns where they live. The conflict between who a character feels herself or himself to be and what is acceptable to friends and colleagues is as constant a theme in American novels as, say, a character's relationship to the state is in German novels. In exploring the romantic secrets of each member of a single family, Carleton offers something of a catalog of ideas on the subject of secret desires— The Moonflower Vine could have been a scandalous novel. But by presenting each character's desire as a moral dilemma for that character, and especially by consistently depicting the bonds of love that eventually hold the family together, she succeeds in arousing both empathy and sympathy in the reader. At the same time that she portrays the “normality” of her family, she demonstrates that “normality” is always more complex than it appears on the surface.

我们榜单上的几部美国小说——《七个尖角屋》、《觉醒》、《杀死一只知更鸟》和《月光花藤》——都因人物为了在居住地维护体面而不得不保守的秘密而获得了相当大的戏剧张力。人物自我认知与朋友和同事认可之间的冲突，如同人物与国家的关系在德国小说中一样，是美国小说中一个永恒的主题。卡尔顿通过探索一个家庭中每个成员的浪漫秘密，呈现了一系列关于秘密欲望的观点——《月光花藤》原本可能是一部惊世骇俗的小说。但她将每个人物的欲望都呈现为他们自身的道德困境，尤其着重描绘最终维系这个家庭的爱的纽带，成功地唤起了读者的同情和怜悯。在展现她家庭“正常”状态的同时，她也表明，“正常”总是比表面看起来要复杂得多。

77. Yukio Mishima. The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea

77. 三岛由纪夫，《海之堕落者》

TRANS. JOHN NATHAN
译者：约翰·内森

(1965; REPR., NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1994), 181 PP.

（1965 年；重印，纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1994 年），181 页。

Mishima is a good example of a novelist whose novels are more ambiguous and nuanced than his press releases. Philosophically, Mishima was very conservative in a specifically Japanese way—he adhered to traditional samurai ideals of warrior-based masculinity and felt that the modernization and Westernization of Japan following the Second World War was a catastrophe. He committed ritual suicide in 1970 , at age forty, after attempting to rouse the Japanese army with a small paramilitary band called The Shield Society, which he had founded.

三岛由纪夫的作品就是一个很好的例子，他的小说比他的新闻稿更加晦涩难懂、意味深长。在哲学上，三岛的保守主义非常具有日本特色——他恪守传统的武士道精神，认为二战后日本的现代化和西化是一场灾难。1970年，年仅四十岁的他切腹自尽。此前，他曾试图带领自己创立的小型准军事组织“盾会”来鼓舞日本军队的士气。

Mishima was almost unbelievably prolific. Between his years at the university and his death, he published 150 novels, plays, and short stories, many of which were made into movies. The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea was made into a movie set in England six years after Mishima's death.

三岛由纪夫的创作力惊人。从大学时期到去世，他出版了150部小说、戏剧和短篇故事，其中许多都被改编成了电影。《海之坠落》在他去世六年之后被改编成电影，故事背景设定在英国。

The novel is a tale with realistic trappings and, in our era of single parents, a familiarity that it did not have upon first publication. Noboru, thirteen, lives with his mother, Fusako, a widow who owns and manages a luxury shop specializing in Western clothing and gifts. Through Noboru's fascination with ships (they live in the port city of Yokohama), they meet Ryuji, a second mate on a large cargo ship, who falls for Fusako. Unbeknownst to the adults, Noboru has discovered a peephole between his room and his mother's room, which he is making frequent use of, and he is also involved with a group of boys who spend their time cultivating perfect dispassion—no attachments, no pity, etc. The unnamed head of the group uses humiliation, arrogance, logic, and the grievances the boys feel against their parents to establish power over the others and “train” them. Early in the book they eviscerate a kitten.

这部小说情节写实，在如今单亲家庭盛行的时代，它所展现的亲切感是初版时所不具备的。十三岁的升和寡妇母亲房子一起生活，房子经营着一家专营西式服装和礼品的奢侈品商店。升对船只着迷（他们住在港口城市横滨），因此结识了大型货轮上的二副龙二，龙二爱上了房子。大人们并不知道，升在自己房间和母亲房间之间发现了一个窥视孔，他经常使用这个孔。此外，他还加入了一个男孩团体，这个团体致力于培养一种完美的冷漠——不带任何情感，不流露怜悯等等。这个团体的首领没有透露姓名，他利用羞辱、傲慢、逻辑以及男孩们对父母的怨恨来控制其他人并“训练”他们。在小说的开头，他们就残忍地杀害了一只小猫。

Noboru is ambivalent about Ryuji—he is attracted to the romance of being a sailor and enjoys Ryuji's stories of his adventures, but he has an idea of pure heartless manliness that he feels Ryuji should adhere to; when Ryuji is kind or shows any sense of connection to either Noboru himself or Fusako, the boy is offended. The other boys, especially the Chief, nurture Noboru's feelings and encourage him to believe that Ryuji is transgressing some objective ideal of masculine purity. In the meantime, when he looks through the peephole, Noboru's own view of his world becomes estranged and fetishized. He watches his mother dress and undress, he watches the adults make love, he sometimes just watches the empty room, but each time he sees a dramatically artful scene that seems to him to have more meaning than what he sees without the peephole.

升对龙司的态度很矛盾——他被水手生活的浪漫情怀所吸引，也喜欢听龙司讲述他的冒险故事，但他心中却有一个纯粹冷酷的男子气概的刻板印象，认为龙司应该恪守这种形象；每当龙司对他本人或房子表现出任何善意或亲近之情时，升都会感到被冒犯。其他男孩，尤其是船长，都在助长升的这种情绪，并鼓励他相信龙司违背了某种客观的男性纯洁理想。与此同时，当他透过窥视孔向外看时，升对世界的感知变得疏离而又充满迷恋。他看着母亲穿衣脱衣，看着大人们做爱，有时只是凝视着空荡荡的房间，但每一次，他看到的都是一幅充满戏剧张力的画面，在他看来，这些画面比他透过窥视孔看到的景象更有意义。

As the romance between the adults progresses, the boys decide to exert their power before they turn fourteen (the Chief tells them there are no consequences if they commit violent acts before turning fourteen), so they lure Ryuji to a secluded spot and drug him. The implication at the end of the novel is that they eviscerate him as they had the kitten.

随着成年人之间的恋情发展，男孩们决定在十四岁生日前行使权力（首领告诉他们，十四岁前犯下暴力罪行不会受到惩罚），于是他们将龙二引诱到一个偏僻的地方，并给他下了药。小说结尾暗示，他们像对待小猫一样残忍地杀害了他。

Apart from plot suspense, the interest of the novel arises from the fact that Ryuji holds pretty much the same ideas that the boys do, he just happens to be twenty years older. An austere, solitary man, he had gone to sea in the first place because he sensed that he was destined for some perfect and unique transcendent moment that would give his life special meaning. But even though he has seen much of the world, been in danger, and lived his life according to his own rules, life on the ocean has turned out to be as mundane as life on land (for which he has habitual contempt). His relationship with Fusako appears at first to offer the sort of gratification he is looking for, too—he is very drawn to her—but when he gives up sailing and begins to prepare for married life and life in the shop, his ideals are disappointed. His murder at the hands of the boys may not be grand, but at least it is unique and strange. It preserves him from what he might discover to be a worse fate.

除了情节悬念之外，这部小说的趣味还在于，龙二与那几个男孩有着几乎相同的理念，只不过他比他们年长二十岁。他性格孤僻，不喜张扬，当初出海是因为他预感到自己注定会经历某种完美而独特的超凡时刻，从而赋予生命特殊的意义。然而，尽管他见识过世间百态，经历过无数危险，也一直按照自己的方式生活，但海上生活最终却和陆地生活一样平淡乏味（而他对陆地生活早已习以为常地不屑一顾）。起初，他与房子的恋情似乎也给了他所寻求的那种满足感——他深深地被她吸引——但当他放弃航海，开始为婚姻生活和店铺经营做准备时，他的理想却破灭了。他被那几个男孩杀害或许并不惊天动地，但至少是独特而奇特的。这使他免于遭受他可能发现的更糟糕的命运。

Mishima builds his novel by juxtaposing the perceptions of each of the three main characters and showing that none of them, but especially Ryuji, can communicate what he or she really feels. When Fusako comes to love Ryuji, she loves not what he means to say, but what he manages to say, which, according to the narrator, is always a misrepresentation of his true feelings, though not exactly a lie. Noboru's feelings, too, are more complex and various than the adults can understand, partly because he is secretive, partly because he is under the influence of the Chief, and partly because he doesn't know himself what he is feeling and thinking. There is the strong implication that without the Chief, stepfamily life would have proceeded in the standard manner—fine enough on the surface, dissatisfaction and resentment below the surface.

三岛由纪夫通过对比三个主要人物各自的感知来构建他的小说，并揭示了他们之中，尤其是龙二，都无法真正表达自己的感受。当房佐子爱上龙二时，她爱的并非他想要表达的内容，而是他最终能够表达出来的东西。根据叙述者的说法，这些表达总是对他真实感受的一种扭曲，尽管并非完全是谎言。升的感受也比成年人所能理解的更加复杂多样，部分原因是他的隐秘，部分原因是他受到首领的影响，还有部分原因是他自己也不清楚自己的感受和想法。小说强烈暗示，如果没有首领，重组家庭的生活将会按部就班地进行——表面上一切安好，暗流涌动，怨恨和不满弥漫。

Even though The Sailor Who Fell from Grace with the Sea fits well enough into the Western tradition of “wild child” novels such as Lord of the Flies , which was published at about the same time, it's important to remember that Mishima was a Japanese writer, and a conservative one at that, whose ideas were inspired by non-Western traditions of Zen Buddhism and warrior discipline. Structurally and stylistically he sets the novel up to explore questions of transience, aesthetic opposition, purity, and the workings of impersonal Fate. In some sense it doesn't matter what the boys’ motives are, or whether they are “evil”— their actions form part of a pattern. The origins of the pattern are within the other characters as well as within the boys. The reader is encouraged to focus on the pattern rather than on moral questions (perhaps this is why the tale ends before the consequences begin). All of the characters are more strongly motivated by “rightness” in an aesthetic sense than they are by “rightness” in a moral sense. Ryuji, for example, interprets his passion for Fusako as the perfect fleeting love for the perfect-looking woman (she is very slight and beautiful) he has been waiting for. As he relates to Noboru, he is self-consciously attempting to follow a picture he has in his mind of how fathers act and people on land relate to one another. Fusako is an arranger, too—when she sees Ryuji off a few days after they meet, she wears a particular type of kimono so he will remember a particular view of her as his ship departs. The Chief's ideals are especially ruthless, but they are no different in their sources than the ideals of the others—purity is all.

尽管《水手之死》与同期出版的《蝇王》等西方“叛逆少年”小说传统颇为契合，但我们必须记住，三岛由纪夫是一位日本作家，而且是一位思想较为保守的作家，他的创作灵感源于禅宗佛教和武士道等非西方传统。在结构和风格上，他将小说设定为探讨短暂、审美对立、纯洁以及非人格化的命运运作等问题。某种程度上，男孩们的动机是什么，或者他们是否“邪恶”，都无关紧要——他们的行为构成了一种模式。这种模式的根源不仅在于男孩们自身，也在于其他角色。读者被引导关注这种模式，而非道德问题（或许这就是故事在后果显现之前就结束的原因）。所有角色的动机更多地源于审美意义上的“正确”，而非道德意义上的“正确”。例如，龙二将他对房佐子的爱慕解读为对完美女子（她身材纤细，容貌绝美）的完美而短暂的爱情，而这正是他一直在等待的。当他与升相处时，他刻意地试图遵循自己脑海中关于父亲如何行事以及陆地上人们如何相处的画面。房佐子也是一位善于安排的人——在与龙二相遇几天后送他离开时，她特意穿了一件特定的和服，以便龙二在船只启航时能记住她特定的模样。首领的理想尤其残酷无情，但其根源与其他人的并无二致——纯洁至上。

But the novel is a tale, not a polemic. The Chief is hardly a respectable spokesman for nihilism—it is clear that he is being badly raised by his own parents, who are wealthy, shallow, and abusive. There is no sense that Ryuji's youthful view of his unique destiny was warranted by unique abilities—he is just a guy. Whatever Mishima's political views, he perfectly understands the resistance of the novel as a form to use as bald propaganda, and he opts instead for evocative, ambiguous subtlety, which is what gives this novel its staying power.

但这部小说是一部故事，而非论战之作。主人公并非虚无主义的合格代言人——显然，他受到了父母的糟糕教育，他的父母富有、肤浅且虐待成性。小说中丝毫没有暗示龙二年轻时对自己独特命运的认知源于其非凡的才能——他只是个普通人。无论三岛由纪夫的政治立场如何，他都深谙小说作为一种赤裸裸的宣传工具所面临的阻力，因此他选择了富有感染力、含蓄而微妙的表达方式，而这正是这部小说经久不衰的原因所在。

78. Jean Rhys. Wide Sargasso Sea

78. 制作里斯。广阔的萨加索海

(NEW YORK: W. W. NORTON, 1966), 190 PP.

（纽约：W. W. NORTON，1966 年），190 页。

In Jane Eyre , Charlotte Brontë's version of Beauty and the Beast , the beast turns out not to be the man, Mr. Rochester, but his first wife, Bertha Mason, the Creole madwoman he had been tricked into marrying for the sake of money as a young man. Ugly (her eyes are described as “red balls”), brutish, dangerous, and sexually dissolute, she is reviled by Jane as well as by Rochester, and everyone, including the reader, is expected to breathe a sigh of relief when she dies, because she doesn't deserve to live and to come between the soulmates Jane and Rochester. However it was that she struck the reader of 1847 , though, she strikes the modern reader as a failed depiction—our understanding of mental illness and its care has changed so completely that the way in which Bertha is treated seems cruel and her response to it natural—she is more sinned against than sinning. Added to that, a modern understanding of the cruelties of European colonialism makes Bertha an interesting figure in her own right, rather than just a figure in the lives of Jane and Rochester.

在夏洛蒂·勃朗特的《简·爱》中，这个改编自《美女与野兽》的故事，野兽并非罗切斯特先生，而是他的第一任妻子伯莎·梅森——一个克里奥尔疯女人，年轻时罗切斯特被骗娶，只因他贪图钱财。她丑陋（她的眼睛被形容为“红球”），粗野，危险，性放荡，简和罗切斯特都对她深恶痛绝。当她死去时，包括读者在内的所有人都会松一口气，因为她不配活在这个世上，更不配介入简和罗切斯特这对灵魂伴侣之间。然而，无论1847年的读者如何看待她，在现代读者眼中，她都是一个失败的刻画——我们对精神疾病及其治疗的理解已经发生了翻天覆地的变化，以至于伯莎所遭受的待遇显得残酷，而她的反应也显得合情合理——她更多的是受害者，而非加害者。此外，现代人对欧洲殖民主义残酷性的理解，使得伯莎本身成为一个有趣的人物，而不仅仅是简和罗切斯特生活中的一个人物。

Jean Rhys, who was born in Dominica, in the West Indies, excavated Bertha, renamed her, and gave her her own novel. In the process, she gives Jane Eyre a political and historical context that only enriches the ambiguities of that novel and of all English and European fiction. Bertha Rochester begins life as Antoinette Cosway (a much more appealing name), a Creole girl whose father has died and whose beautiful mother cannot handle either the plantation she owns or the servants who people it. She is saved by an English planter named Mason, who takes over a plantation nearby. He is well-meaning but completely misunderstands the colonial cultural mix, according to Antoinette and her mother, who live in considerable fear. As a result of a slave revolt, Antoinette's mysteriously afflicted brother is severely burned and her mother goes out of her mind. Antoinette herself goes to school, where she is happy for a while. Rochester enters the picture as a young man. His marriage with Antoinette and his removal to the plantation take place while he is ill and disoriented, and though he is at first well disposed toward her, he soon backs away as a result of the insinuations of a disgruntled local man, whose motives are suspect. Rochester then sleeps with one of the house servants, thereby offending and rejecting Antoinette. She grows increasingly jealous, fearful, and unstable, until at last he forces her to leave Jamaica and move to England, where her incarceration exacerbates her mental instability. The novel ends just as she is leaving her attic to set fire to the house.

出生于西印度群岛多米尼加的让·里斯挖掘出了伯莎这个人物，给她改了名字，并创作了一部以她为主角的小说。在此过程中，她为《简·爱》赋予了政治和历史背景，这不仅丰富了这部小说本身的复杂性，也丰富了所有英国和欧洲小说的复杂性。伯莎·罗切斯特最初名叫安托瓦内特·科斯韦（一个更悦耳的名字），是一位克里奥尔女孩，父亲去世后，她美丽的母亲既无力管理自己拥有的种植园，也无力管理园里的仆人。一位名叫梅森的英国种植园主接管了附近的一个种植园，救了她。据安托瓦内特和她的母亲说，梅森心地善良，但却完全不了解殖民地文化的融合，她们生活在极度的恐惧之中。一场奴隶起义导致安托瓦内特患有神秘疾病的弟弟严重烧伤，她的母亲也精神失常。安托瓦内特自己去上学，在那里她度过了一段快乐的时光。罗切斯特以年轻男子的形象出现在故事中。罗切斯特与安托瓦内特结婚并被迁往种植园时，他正处于病痛和精神恍惚之中。起初他对安托瓦内特颇有好感，但很快便因一个心怀不满的当地人的挑拨离间而疏远了她，而此人的动机令人怀疑。之后，罗切斯特与一位女仆发生了关系，这激怒并疏远了安托瓦内特。安托瓦内特的嫉妒、恐惧和精神状态日益恶化，最终，罗切斯特强迫她离开牙买加，前往英国。在英国的监禁加剧了她的精神不稳定。小说结尾，安托瓦内特正要离开阁楼放火烧毁房子。

A novel is a piece of logic, and Rhys's logical analysis of how Antoinette Cosway is transformed into Bertha Rochester is utterly convincing. The premises are cultural instability, pervasive mistrust, and childhood trauma. The logical steps are progressive misunderstanding and isolation, which eventually evolve into outright cruelty. The conclusion is Bertha's inner nightmare, which results in an objective inferno.

小说是一部逻辑作品，里斯对安托瓦内特·科斯韦如何蜕变为伯莎·罗切斯特的逻辑分析令人信服。其前提是文化不稳定、普遍存在的不信任以及童年创伤。逻辑步骤是逐步加深的误解和孤立，最终演变为赤裸裸的残忍。结局是伯莎内心的噩梦，最终酿成一场惨绝人寰的悲剧。

Since the novel thrives on subjectivity, any consciousness is sufficiently interesting to be made into one. Wide Sargasso Sea uses Brontë's own insight against her—she had asserted that even the inner life of a poor, plain, and overlooked governess could be compelling, but made a repulsive object of a madwoman. Rhys shows that the line between sanity and madness can't be drawn either, and that Bertha has a back story as worthy of sympathy as Jane's. What Rhys seems to be saying is that every female consciousness presents a problem that marriage as a property arrangement cannot solve and can only complicate.

由于小说以主观性为核心，任何意识都足以成为小说的主题。《藻海无边》利用勃朗特自身的洞察力反驳她——她曾断言，即使是贫穷、平凡、被人忽视的家庭教师的内心世界也引人入胜，却将疯女人描绘成令人厌恶的对象。里斯指出，理智与疯狂之间的界限同样难以划定，伯莎的过往经历与简的一样值得同情。里斯似乎想要表达的是，每个女性的意识都提出了婚姻作为一种财产安排无法解决的问题，而婚姻只会使问题更加复杂。

79. John Gardner. Grende

79. 约翰·加德纳。《格伦德》

(NEW YORK: ALFRED A. KNOPF, 1971), 174 PP.

（纽约：ALFRED A. KNOPF，1971 年），174 页。

Five years after Jean Rhys rewrote Jane Eyre and three years after Tom Stoppard rewrote Hamlet (in Rosencrantz and Guildenstern Are Dead) , John Gardner rewrote Beowulf. In general, I like the idea of recasting earlier works, but every recasting is an interpretation and therefore thematically based, and the resulting works are as much or more the products of their own times as the works that inspire them. Those of us who risk the extra measure of ephemerality that comes from rooting a novel overtly in another work take comfort in a couple of things. One is that reworking old material is a tradition as old as literature. Certainly Beowulf was the written culmination of an oral tradition that was at least several centuries old in Anglo-Saxon and that was itself based on narrative patterns that go back to the earliest Indo-European epics. Beowulf's and Hrothgar's concerns have a dark, cold, northern flavor, but they are not terribly different from Arjuna's concerns in the Bhagavad Gita and Agamemnon's concerns in The Iliad —glory and heroism versus death and mass murder. Likewise, Hamlet and King Lear (the source of my novel A Thousand Acres) are Elizabethan reworkings of earlier stories. Old stories have more than staying power; they force the reader and the writer to contemplate the most basic human concerns once again—the nature of love, death, art, and existence, of family, fear, injury, and hope. They also give the author a rare and precious treat, the chance to follow an earlier mind step by step into a knotty artistic dilemma, to test with each word and idea what has changed and what has remained the same about the story. In addition, every work of literature exhausts the inventiveness of its author and could use another rewrite. A work that evokes in a reader enough fascination so he or she will put in the hours to try to solve those last little problems of logic, continuity, or thematic contradiction is a work that speaks especially clearly out of the past.

在让·里斯重写《简·爱》五年后，以及汤姆·斯托帕德在《罗森克兰茨和吉尔登斯顿之死》中重写《哈姆雷特》三年后，约翰·加德纳重写了《贝奥武夫》。总的来说，我喜欢重写早期作品的想法，但每一次重写都是一种诠释，因此都基于主题，最终的作品与其灵感来源的作品一样，甚至更甚于其所处的时代。我们这些敢于冒险将小说直接植根于另一部作品，从而承担其短暂性风险的人，可以从两点中获得慰藉。首先，改编旧作是一种与文学本身一样古老的传统。《贝奥武夫》无疑是盎格鲁-撒克逊时期至少存在了几个世纪的口头传统的书面化成果，而这种口头传统本身又基于可以追溯到最早的印欧史诗的叙事模式。贝奥武夫和赫罗斯加的忧虑带有阴郁、冷峻的北方色彩，但与《薄伽梵歌》中阿周那的忧虑以及《伊利亚特》中阿伽门农的忧虑并无本质区别——荣耀与英雄主义与死亡与屠杀之间的冲突。同样，《哈姆雷特》和《李尔王》（我的小说《一千英亩》的灵感来源）也是伊丽莎白时代对早期故事的改编。古老的故事不仅经久不衰，更迫使读者和作者再次思考人类最基本的关切——爱、死亡、艺术和存在的本质，家庭、恐惧、伤害和希望的意义。它们也为作者提供了一种难得的宝贵机会：一步步追随前人的思想，深入探究错综复杂的艺术困境，逐字逐句地检验故事中哪些部分发生了改变，哪些部分保持不变。此外，每一部文学作品都会耗尽作者的创造力，因此也需要再次修改。一部作品如果能激起读者足够的兴趣，让他或她愿意花费时间去尝试解决逻辑、连贯性或主题矛盾方面的最后一些小问题，那么这部作品就特别清晰地反映了过去。

John Gardner was a motorcyle-riding medievalist in a black leather jacket, a true representative of his era. He was daring, he was dedicated to writing and teaching writing, and he believed in the tour de force, a novel so glittering and unusual that it would take the literary world by storm, and if it more or less bypassed the larger world of readers, that would be okay, too. He wrote eleven books before his death in 1982 at age forty-nine. Grendel was the one that made his reputation. Grendel is the memoir or meditation of Beowulf's monster enemy, who turns out, like Jean Rhys's rendition of the monstrous Mrs. Rochester, to have a logical, and even an appealing, point of view. Like Bertha, Grendel is a complete outsider, marked by isolation and loneliness and doomed to act out the fascination he feels for those who fear and reject him. He lives in a sordid cave with his mother, who has devolved in old age into a grumbling, suffocating, lumpish beast unable to offer Grendel, who is quite garrulous and inquisitive by contrast, any companionship. Grendel suspects that he is related in some way to humans, because he understands their speech, though they only intermittently understand his. His relationship to them is complex. He has a natural desire to eat them, which he often does, but he is moved by their poetry and by the beauty of the queen to a frustrated, lovelike state. Mostly, since they can't hurt him but are always boastful and fearful simultaneously, he feels contempt for them. He seeks wisdom from those he can talk to—the dragon in particular— but he is the only one of his kind, and no general theory applies to him. He is doomed to live out his avid alienation until the arrival in a long-ship of Beowulf and the Geats, a tribe of humans that seems, even to Grendel, to possess actual power.

约翰·加德纳是一位骑着摩托车、身穿黑色皮夹克的中世纪学者，是那个时代的真实写照。他胆识过人，致力于写作和写作教学，并且坚信“杰作”的存在——一部光芒四射、别具一格的小说，足以席卷文坛；即便它未能引起广大读者的共鸣，他也毫不在意。1982年，年仅49岁的他去世前，共创作了11部作品。《格伦德尔》是他成名作。这部小说以贝奥武夫的怪物敌人——格伦德尔的视角，既是回忆录，也是沉思录。格伦德尔，如同简·里斯笔下那位令人毛骨悚然的罗切斯特夫人，拥有合乎逻辑，甚至颇具魅力的观点。与伯莎一样，格伦德尔也是一个彻头彻尾的局外人，饱受孤立和孤独的折磨，注定要将他对那些恐惧和排斥他的人的迷恋付诸行动。他与年迈的母亲住在肮脏的山洞里。他的母亲已经退化成一头咕哝不断、令人窒息、臃肿不堪的野兽，无法陪伴格伦德尔。与她形成鲜明对比的是，格伦德尔却十分健谈且好奇。格伦德尔怀疑自己与人类有着某种联系，因为他能听懂人类的语言，而人类却只能偶尔听懂他的。他与人类的关系十分复杂。他天生渴望吞噬他们，而且也经常这么做，但他又会被他们的诗歌和女王的美貌所打动，陷入一种既沮丧又充满爱意的状态。大多数时候，由于人类无法伤害他，却总是既自负又恐惧，他对他们感到鄙夷。他向那些能够交谈的人——尤其是巨龙——寻求智慧，但他是独一无二的，没有任何普遍的理论适用于他。他注定要忍受这种强烈的疏离感，直到贝奥武夫和盖特人乘坐长船到来。盖特人是一个人类部落，即使对格伦德尔来说，他们似乎也拥有真正的力量。

Grendel, of course, is not Beowulf's only victim, and because he dies, the novel cannot follow the poem to the end, but anyone familiar with the poem can infer what happens after Beowulf, by means of a trick as well as his superhuman strength, manages to destroy the monster.

当然，格伦德尔并不是贝奥武夫唯一的受害者，而且由于他死了，小说无法完全按照诗歌的结尾发展，但任何熟悉这首诗的人都可以推断出贝奥武夫凭借计谋和超人的力量消灭怪物之后发生了什么。

Gardner's novel has the merit of extreme cleverness, which is the hallmark of a tour de force—with one simple idea it presents the reader with a whole new way of looking at something she thought she already knew all about. In Beowulf Grendel is all physical—a huge, hairy, dark beast who kills and eats Hrothgar's thanes in a senseless and erratic manner. In Grendel the monster is all talk—he says of himself, “Talking, talking. Spinning a web of words, pale walls of dreams, between myself and all I see.” He kills and eats the thanes, but that is mostly because they are such fools. Otherwise he is their witness. He watches their settlements, their tribal battles and wars, their attempts to gain themselves peace by waging war, and he can't understand how their minds work—their actions are too illogical and futile and their lives are too short. What they consider to be a long time is only a brief span in his much longer and more tedious existence. In addition, he has the wisdom of the dragon to go on, and the dragon is for all intents and purposes eternal—he can see the future and the past. To him, sitting on his hoard of jewels, all relationships are meaningless, and Grendel's longing for some sort of understanding or connection is as silly as the same sort of longings in the humans.

加德纳的小说最可贵之处在于其极富巧思，这正是杰作的标志——它仅用一个简单的构思，就为读者呈现了一种全新的视角，去审视那些她自以为早已熟知的事物。在《贝奥武夫》中，格伦德尔完全是肉体上的存在——一个巨大、毛茸茸的黑色野兽，以一种毫无意义且反复无常的方式杀害并吞食赫罗斯加的侍臣。而在《格伦德尔》中，这个怪物则只会空谈——他这样描述自己：“喋喋不休。编织一张文字之网，一道道苍白的梦境之墙，将我与我所见的一切隔开。”他杀害并吞食侍臣，但这主要是因为他们愚蠢至极。除此之外，他只是他们的见证者。他观察着他们的定居点、他们的部落战争、他们试图通过发动战争来换取和平的努力，但他无法理解他们的思维方式——他们的行为太过不合逻辑且徒劳，他们的生命也太过短暂。在他们看来漫长的岁月，在他漫长而乏味的生命中，不过是转瞬即逝的一瞬。此外，他拥有巨龙的智慧，而巨龙几乎是永恒的——他能预见未来，也能预见过去。对他而言，坐在珠宝宝库中，一切关系都毫无意义，格伦德尔渴望某种理解或联系，就像人类的类似渴望一样愚蠢。

Since there is no point in writing a tour de force without making a case for something, Gardner makes a case for the necessity of the dark side. Grendel comes to justify his existence, which he otherwise cannot understand, as the required antagonist who drives the humans to a height of bravery and philosophy they would not otherwise reach without his presence. In this he subtly shifts the balance of literature, especially plotted literature, away from the protagonist and toward the antagonist—it's all too easy to say that without Claudius, for example, Hamlet would have lived a decent and peaceful life—Grendel would say that without Claudius, Hamlet would be a nobody. But Grendel is not only interesting for the case he makes, he is also entertaining because, though the humans speak translated Anglo-Saxon, Grendel speaks like we do (as does the dragon, though he speaks more like a philosophy professor than an English professor). This is a technique that serves Gardner well, because it simultaneously diminishes the epic size of the humans, adds wit, makes the story a novel, and brings the novel into the modern era. The other good effect of this technique is that through his narration, as through a small lens, we can see medieval Denmark in the primitive period of the early Germanic tribes. Gardner does not paint these scenes grandly and in detail, as T H. White paints his medieval world, but he evokes it, especially with descriptions of animals, such as mountain goats, that have since vanished from Europe. His dark ages are dark, indeed, but the reader has to wonder after reading this novel of foolish, vainglorious, aggressive human folly how much has changed.

既然写出一部杰作却不提出论点毫无意义，加德纳便以此论证了黑暗势力存在的必要性。格伦德尔最终为自己的存在找到了理由——尽管他原本无法理解这种存在——因为他是不可或缺的反派，正是他驱使人类走向勇气和哲学的巅峰，而如果没有他的存在，人类根本无法达到这种境界。在此，他巧妙地改变了文学作品，尤其是情节文学作品的重心，使其从主角转向反派——例如，我们很容易说，如果没有克劳狄斯，哈姆雷特就能过上体面而平静的生活——而格伦德尔则会说，如果没有克劳狄斯，哈姆雷特将一事无成。但格伦德尔的魅力不仅在于他提出的论点，更在于他本身就极具娱乐性，因为尽管人类说的是翻译过来的盎格鲁-撒克逊语，格伦德尔却说着我们人类的语言（巨龙也是如此，尽管它的说话方式更像是哲学教授而非英语教授）。这种技巧对加德纳来说非常有效，因为它既削弱了人物的宏大形象，又增添了诙谐幽默，使故事更具小说性，并将小说带入了现代背景。这种技巧的另一个优点是，通过他的叙述，如同透过一扇小小的透镜，我们得以窥见中世纪丹麦早期日耳曼部落的原始状态。加德纳并没有像T·H·怀特那样，以宏大的笔触和细致的描写来描绘这些场景，而是通过对山羊等如今已在欧洲消失的动物的描写，生动地唤起了读者的记忆。他笔下的黑暗时代的确黑暗，但读者在读完这部描写人类愚蠢、虚荣和好斗的小说后，不禁会思考，究竟有多少改变已经发生。

But is Grendel profound as well as smart? The critical faculty, the faculty that takes such pleasure in analyzing literature that it wants to fix it, is sometimes impatient with the details and texture that give a novel staying power, and in the end the problem with Grendel is that it is long enough to explore its ideas but not dense enough to be a really good story. Gardner's idea itself limits his execution, because since Grendel must live in a solipsistic universe, his plot doesn't have much action. What he learns he must learn in the abstract because he is conceived to be without any other interests except his interest in those who can't interact with him. Gardner sticks close to the plot of Beowulf , and we admire his erudition and imagination in doing so, but his fidelity to his source prevents him from really fleshing out a world of his own.

但《格伦德尔》是否既深刻又睿智呢？评论家们热衷于分析文学作品，甚至想要对其进行修正，但他们有时会对赋予小说持久生命力的细节和层次感缺乏耐心。最终，《格伦德尔》的问题在于，它的篇幅足以探讨其思想，但又不够充实，无法成为一个真正精彩的故事。加德纳的构思本身就限制了他的创作，因为格伦德尔必须生活在一个唯我论的世界里，所以他的情节缺乏动作。他所学到的东西都必须是抽象的，因为他被设定为除了那些无法与他互动的人之外，没有任何其他兴趣。加德纳忠实于《贝奥武夫》的情节，我们欣赏他的博学和想象力，但他对原著的忠诚却阻碍了他真正构建一个属于他自己的世界。

80. Alice Munro. Lives of Girls and Women

80. 爱丽丝·门罗。《女孩和女人的生活》

(NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1971), 278 PP.

（纽约：企鹅出版社，1971 年），278 页。

Munro has a special genius for understanding the profound implications of incidents that most people, even most writers, notice and forget, or perhaps turn into anecdotes. She is truly, in Henry James's phrase, someone “upon whom nothing is lost.” The short-story form has showcased her talents because she has been able to transform it. Avoiding the tricks and surprises of earlier exponents, and writing with an unprecedented complexity of insight and precision of style, she has given her stories the weight of novels.

门罗拥有非凡的天赋，她能洞察大多数人（甚至大多数作家）都会注意到却遗忘，或者仅仅当作轶事提及的事件背后所蕴含的深刻意义。用亨利·詹姆斯的话来说，她真是一位“洞察一切”的人。短篇小说这一体裁充分展现了她的才华，因为她能够将其升华。她摒弃了前人惯用的技巧和故弄玄虚，以空前的洞察力和精准的文风进行写作，赋予了她的故事堪比长篇小说的分量。

But Munro did write one novel, Lives of Girls and Women. It is both a fine novel and a wonderful introduction to Munro's subsequent work. Like many first novels, Lives of Girls and Women is semiautobio-graphical—it takes place in rural Ontario; the protagonist is Del, who seems to be about the same age as the author would have been in the 1940s ; and it is told in the first person. But Munro's semiautobiograph-ical first novel already fully displays her characteristic gifts, in particular her ability to judiciously consider every aspect of a situation or a scene, to subtly highlight the details that make her argument, and to suggest more than she states.

但门罗确实写过一部长篇小说，《女孩与女人的生活》。这部小说既是一部优秀的作品，也是了解门罗后续作品的绝佳入门。和许多处女作一样，《女孩与女人的生活》带有半自传性质——故事发生在安大略省的乡村；主人公德尔的年龄似乎与作者在20世纪40年代的年龄相仿；而且小说采用第一人称叙述。但门罗这部半自传性质的处女作已经充分展现了她独特的才华，尤其体现在她能够审慎地审视情境或场景的方方面面，巧妙地突出论证细节，并暗示远超字面意思的深意。

Del's family is unorthodox, which Del understands from the beginning of the novel (which opens when Del is about ten). For one thing, her father is trying to earn a living raising silver foxes for fur coats, so they live in the country, on a road where her mother feels out of place and bored, and where Del, too, is mildly alienated. Already, at ten, Del is an observant and inquisitive child. She does what she is told, and passes no judgments upon the adults and their choices, but her inner life, both imaginative and moral, is full and convincing. Del's nuclear family is a small cell of both a larger community—the town where Del and her mother eventually move—and the extended family that Del visits and observes on her father's side. Both town and countryside are depressed—what had not been a very promising agricultural region to begin with has declined because of the Depression and has not revived because of the war. When Del's mother takes up selling encyclopedias to earn more money, Del goes along. The farms and families she visits are eccentric in the way that subspecies become eccentric when they lose contact with the rest of their fellows—they pursue old habits and make the best of things and accept that life is the way it is and there is no escape. As Del gets older and her horizons extend beyond her family, she makes a little tour of her region and samples what it has to offer.

德尔的家庭并不寻常，这一点从小说一开始（德尔大约十岁时）德尔就明白。首先，她的父亲为了生计饲养银狐制作皮大衣，所以他们住在乡下，住在一条她母亲感到格格不入、百无聊赖的路上，德尔也同样感到有些疏离。十岁的德尔已经是个观察力敏锐、求知欲强的孩子。她听话，从不评判大人及其选择，但她丰富的内心世界，无论是想象力还是道德观念，都饱满而令人信服。德尔的核心家庭既是更大社区（德尔和她母亲最终搬去的城镇）的一个小单元，也是德尔经常拜访和观察的父亲那边的大家庭的缩影。城镇和乡村都笼罩在萧条的氛围中——原本就不是什么很有发展前景的农业区，因为经济大萧条而衰落，又因为战争而未能复苏。为了补贴家用，黛尔的母亲开始卖百科全书，黛尔也跟着去了。她拜访的农场和家庭都有些古怪，就像某些亚种与同类失去联系后会变得古怪一样——他们固守旧习，尽力而为，接受生活本该如此，无处可逃。随着黛尔长大，她的视野也逐渐开阔，她开始在家乡附近游览，体验那里的一切。

Her maiden aunts and her history-buff uncle give way to ladies of the town that her mother tries to befriend, then her uncle and his American wife. After that, she begins going to church, not the family church, the one they know, but a smaller, poorer, and more ritual-filled Episcopal church on the other side of town. After that, her circle widens to include boys and other, more conventional girls. With each expansion, though, Munro never fails to keep track of the characters and scenes she has previously introduced. The maiden aunts not only grow older and more feeble, they also change in some ways but stay the same in other ways. Her mother tries one thing after another to lift the boredom of life in Wawanash County; nothing works, and she, too, subtly grows older and less hopeful. The parents’ marriage changes while at the same time Del comes to understand more about it. As she grows up, so does her brother. As she evolves to be more like her mother, so Owen evolves to be more like her father, who is also changing. The delicacy with which Munro portrays these characters is smoothly kaleidoscopic—one manifestation shades into another as Del herself matures and solidifies.

她的姑妈们和热爱历史的叔叔逐渐被她母亲试图结交的镇上女士们取代，然后是她的叔叔和他的美国妻子。之后，她开始去教堂，不是他们熟悉的家族教堂，而是镇子另一边一座规模较小、较为简陋、仪式繁复的圣公会教堂。再之后，她的社交圈扩大，开始与男孩和其他更传统的女孩交往。然而，随着她社交圈的不断扩展，门罗始终没有忽略之前引入的人物和场景。姑妈们不仅日渐衰老虚弱，她们在某些方面发生了变化，但在另一些方面却依然如故。她的母亲尝试了各种各样的方法来摆脱瓦瓦纳什县生活的单调乏味；但都无济于事，她自己也在不知不觉中老去，希望也日渐渺茫。父母的婚姻发生了变化，与此同时，德尔也开始对婚姻有了更深的理解。随着她的成长，她的哥哥也在成长。随着她越来越像她的母亲，欧文也越来越像她的父亲，而她的父亲也在发生变化。门罗对这些人物的刻画细腻入微，笔触如万花筒般流畅变幻——随着德尔自身的成长和成熟，一种形象逐渐过渡到另一种。

All of Munro's themes are subtle; the reader is hardly aware that she deploys them. A second time through the novel, though, shows her purpose. She is writing a bildungsroman, a story of how the writer became herself. It begins immediately: when Del can hardly read, she notices and is fascinated by tabloid newspapers that collect in the shack of the tenant:

门罗的所有主题都十分微妙；读者几乎察觉不到她的运用。然而，第二次阅读这部小说时，她的意图便显露出来。她写的是一部成长小说，讲述的是作家如何成为她自己的故事。故事开篇便已展开：当德尔几乎不识字时，她注意到并着迷于房客小屋里堆积如山的通俗小报。

I read faster and faster, all I could hold, then reeled into the sun, onto the path that led to our place, across the fields. I was bloated and giddy with revelations of evil, or its versatility and grand invention and horrific playfulness. But the nearer I got to our house, the more this vision faded. Why was it that the plain back wall of home, the pale, chipped brick, the cement platform outside the kitchen door, washtubs hanging on nails, the pump, the lilac bush with brown-spotted leaves, should make it seem so doubtful that a woman would really send her husband's torso, wrapped in Christmas paper, by mail to his girlfriend in South Carolina? [p. 6 ]

我越读越快，直到精疲力竭，然后踉跄着走向阳光，沿着田野间通往我们住处的小路走去。我感到一阵眩晕，脑海里浮现出各种关于邪恶的启示，或是它的多样性、惊人的创造力和可怕的玩味。但越靠近家，这种景象就越发模糊。为什么家那朴素的后墙、苍白斑驳的砖墙、厨房门外的水泥平台、挂在钉子上的洗衣盆、水泵、叶子上长着褐色斑点的丁香树，会让我如此怀疑一个女人真的会把她丈夫的躯干用圣诞包装纸包起来，寄给他在南卡罗来纳州的女友呢？[第6页]

This juxtaposition between the dramatic and the mundane, which sheds light on both, will be the essence of Munro's vision from then on. Equally, she writes as soon as she knows how. She is employed by the tenant to answer an ad in the newspaper seeking a position for a “Lady with one child.” Del, only in fourth grade, isn't content to serve as amanuensis—she has stylistic objections to his dictation: “‘You start with Dear and then the person's name,’ I said, ‘unless it's a business letter and then you start with Dear Sir or Dear Madam if it's a lady. Is it a business letter?’” (p. 13 ).

这种戏剧性与日常性的并置，既揭示了二者的本质，也成为了门罗此后作品的精髓。同样，她一学会写作就开始了。她受雇于房客，去回应报纸上刊登的一则招聘“一位育有一子的女士”的广告。当时只有四年级的德尔并不甘心做个抄写员——她对房客的口述有文体上的异议：“‘你应该以“亲爱的”开头，然后是对方的名字，’我说，‘除非是商务信函，那样的话，你就应该以“尊敬的先生”或“尊敬的女士”开头。这是商务信函吗？’” （第13页）

Each subsequent chapter offers her other models for how to think of writing—her uncle's life work, much cherished by her aunts, is a local history in which every small incident gets equal, even, thorough treatment:

接下来的每一章都为她提供了其他写作思路——她叔叔毕生的心血之作，深受她姑姑们的喜爱，是一部地方史，其中每一个小事件都得到了平等、均匀、详尽的描述：

“Nearly a thousand pages.”
“More pages than Gone with the Wind.”
”He typed it so beautifully, no mistakes.” [p. 67]

“将近一千页。”“比《飘》的页数还多。”“他打字打得真漂亮，没有一个错误。”[第67页]

At school, Del encounters art in the form of the yearly operetta, which the third-grade teacher, Miss Farris, and the organist from the church, Mr. Boyce, seem to mold the children into by sheer force of showbiz will. Del is alert to how children who had seemed to have no special qualities at all somehow blossom during the rehearsals and performances of The Pied Piper. When Miss Farris subsequently drowns (accident? suicide?), Del takes it in—it conforms to her sense of how the dramatic and the mundane mesh, and also reaffirms her sense that many things occur beneath the rather drab surface of the town that the adults won't, or don't know how to, talk about.

在学校里，黛尔接触到了艺术，那就是每年一度的轻歌剧。三年级老师法里斯小姐和教堂的管风琴师博伊斯先生似乎凭借着强大的表演天赋，将孩子们塑造成剧中人物。黛尔敏锐地注意到，那些原本看似毫无特质的孩子，在《花衣魔笛手》的排练和演出中，竟奇迹般地绽放出光彩。后来，法里斯小姐溺水身亡（意外？自杀？），黛尔深受触动——这印证了她对戏剧性与日常琐事交织的理解，也再次印证了她之前的感受：在这个略显沉闷的小镇表面之下，隐藏着许多不为人知的秘密，而大人们要么不愿提及，要么不知如何开口。

As Del gets older, her rather conveniently chosen and not very congenial best friend, Naomi, begins experimenting with clothes, makeup, men, and sex. Naomi seems sure of herself; Del is less so, on the surface, but more truly inquisitive, as she always has been, underneath. Naomi wants to find for herself what amounts to a good position in life, and she marshals all of her resources to do so. Del, whose position in life has always been anomalous, cares only about novel experiences—what they feel like and what they mean. Naomi wants to catch a husband. Del wants to feel passion, and she succeeds with the mysterious Jerry, whom she meets at a revival meeting and instantly recognizes in some visceral, sexual way. Jerry, far from Del's educational or social equal, works in the local lumberyard. Del can't get enough of him, and they engage in a frenzied relationship that distracts her from the university exams she has been preparing for all her life. But Munro is careful not to account for Del's choice in any clichd, Freudian way. Jerry speaks to her, he changes the course of her life; he is, though she doesn't quite realize it, the pivot between conventional success, as represented by examinations, university, professional life, and the alternative Del achieves, which is artistic vision. It is through Jerry that the odd layers of her childhood and youth, the foxes and her parents’ marriage and the bookishness and her aspirations to faith as well as passion, meld into a whole.

随着黛尔渐渐长大，她那位看似顺理成章却并不合拍的闺蜜娜奥米开始尝试各种服饰、化妆、男人和性。娜奥米似乎自信满满；黛尔表面上则不然，但内心深处却像她一贯那样充满好奇。娜奥米渴望找到一份体面的生活，为此她竭尽全力。而黛尔的生活境遇一直与众不同，她只在乎新鲜体验——感受它们，探究它们的意义。娜奥米想要找到丈夫，黛尔则渴望激情。她在一次复兴布道会上遇到了神秘的杰瑞，并立刻被他某种本能的、性方面的吸引力所吸引。杰瑞的学历和社会地位都远不及黛尔，他在当地的木材厂工作。黛尔对他欲罢不能，两人陷入了一段疯狂的恋情，让她无暇顾及自己毕生都在准备的大学考试。但门罗小心翼翼地避免用任何陈词滥调或弗洛伊德式的解释来阐释德尔的选择。杰瑞与她交谈，改变了她的人生轨迹；尽管她并未完全意识到，但杰瑞是她人生中两个关键的转折点：一个是传统的成功——以考试、大学、职业生涯为代表——另一个是德尔所追求的另一种人生——艺术视野。正是通过杰瑞，她童年和青年时期那些奇特的经历，狐狸、父母的婚姻、书卷气、对信仰和激情的渴望，最终融合为一个完整的整体。

81. Naguib Mahfouz The Harafish

81. 哈拉鱼纳吉布·马哈福兹

TRANS. CATHERINE COBHAM (GARDEN CITY, N.Y.: DOUBLEDAY, ANCHOR, 1977), 406 PP.

CATHERINE COBHAM 译（纽约州花园城：DOUBLEDAY，ANCHOR，1977 年），406 页。

Naguib Mahfouz was born in Egypt in 1911 , wrote dozens of books and novels, and won the Nobel Prize in 1988 . He was the great twentieth-century chronicler of the Arab world, and his most famous work is The Cairo Trilogy , written in the realist tradition about a neighborhood, called an alley, in Cairo, and following the lives of the inhabitants as they encounter the modern world. The Harafish dispenses with realism and tells a cycle of tales about a single family, also in a particular alley, over the course of ten generations, or hundreds of years. Of particular interest to Mahfouz are only a few concepts as they work in the lives of each successive generation—virtue (defined as both personal propriety and the correct uses of power and wealth), ambition, love, and the self-consciousness that comes from inheriting power and influence.

纳吉布·马哈福兹1911年出生于埃及，著有数十部书籍和小说，并于1988年荣获诺贝尔文学奖。他是二十世纪阿拉伯世界最伟大的编年史家，其最著名的作品是《开罗三部曲》。这部作品以现实主义传统为背景，讲述了开罗一条名为“巷子”的街区居民在面对现代世界时的生活。《哈拉菲什》则摒弃了现实主义，讲述了一个家族在同一条巷子里，跨越十代人（数百年）的一系列故事。马哈福兹尤其关注几个概念在每一代人生活中的作用——美德（既指个人礼仪，也指正确运用权力和财富）、抱负、爱情，以及继承权力和影响力所带来的自我意识。

The founder of the family is an abandoned infant, Ashur al-Nagi, discovered by a blind reciter of the Koran as he is making his way toward the mosque one evening. He takes the child home and raises him to be virtuous and strong, an able protector of the “harafish,” or working poor of the alley he lives in. Ashur's great adventure and piece of luck is that he has a dream that tells him to leave the alley during a bout of the plague. When he returns, all the wealthy families have died, and he assumes both their wealth and their power, but he devotes himself to the benefit of the neighborhood. His descendants are well aware of his example as the generations pass, but they dishonor it more than they honor it—most often the most powerful and ambitious man of each generation is either seduced by love into some sort of unwise marriage or sexual adventure, or is seduced by wealth into selfishness and dissipation. In each generation the great temptation is to become the clan chief, but when each man realizes his ambition, he discovers that the chieftaincy is also a test of courage, fighting skill, and character. In one case, the ambition falls to a woman— Zahira—who decides to use her beauty to gain wealth and power rather than love. She marries and divorces several times and causes quite a scandal. Eventually she is beaten to death by one of her betrayed husbands, and the sight of her bloodied face then haunts her child, Galal, who becomes possessed by either nihilistic despair, or madness, or the Devil, depending on who is interpreting his behavior.

这个家族的创始人是被遗弃的婴儿阿舒尔·纳吉。一天晚上，一位盲人诵经者在前往清真寺的路上发现了阿舒尔。他将孩子带回家，悉心抚养，使他成为一个品德高尚、意志坚强的人，能够保护他所居住的巷子里的“哈拉菲什”（harafish，即贫苦劳动者）。阿舒尔的奇遇和幸运之处在于，他做了一个梦，梦中指示他在瘟疫肆虐期间离开巷子。当他返回时，所有富裕的家庭都已去世，他继承了他们的财富和权力，但他却致力于造福邻里。他的后代虽然了解他的榜样，但随着时间的推移，他们却更多地是在亵渎而非效仿——每一代最有权势、最有野心的人，往往要么被爱情诱惑而陷入不明智的婚姻或风流韵事，要么被财富诱惑而变得自私自利、放荡不羁。每一代人最大的诱惑都是成为氏族首领，但当每个人都实现自己的野心时，他们才发现首领之位也是对勇气、战斗技巧和品格的考验。其中一位名叫扎希拉的女子，却怀揣着这样的野心。她决定利用自己的美貌来获取财富和权力，而非爱情。她多次结婚又离婚，引起了轩然大波。最终，她被其中一位背叛她的丈夫殴打致死。她血淋淋的面容从此萦绕在她的儿子加拉尔心头，加拉尔的行为也因此变得诡异莫测，有人认为是虚无主义的绝望，有人认为是疯狂，还有人认为是魔鬼附身，这取决于谁来解读他的行为。

For the Western reader, The Harafish is appealingly alien. Mahfouz strips the narrative of the usual indicators of the passage of time— there is no sense of progress, or even of how daily life takes shape. The characters have jobs and ideas and plans, names and looks, but the details are left out, as if they are too common and unchanging to be worth describing. They pass between the bar and the caf. They wander into the vicinity of the mosque, where they hear singing, but the door of the mosque never opens, and no one ever enters or emerges. The mosque shows no recognition of the people—even when they are starving, the mosque passes out no alms, and the people, no matter how virtuous or interested in the doings of the mosque, never participate in the joys of the mosque—God is present, but it is the job of the people to be attentive to Him, not His to be attentive to them.

对西方读者而言，《哈拉菲什》散发着一种异域风情，引人入胜。马哈福兹剥离了叙事中常见的时间流逝的痕迹——没有进步感，甚至没有日常生活的痕迹。人物有工作、有想法、有计划，有名字、有外貌，但细节都被省略了，仿佛它们太过寻常、一成不变，不值得描述。他们穿梭于酒吧和咖啡馆之间。他们漫步到清真寺附近，听到歌声，但清真寺的大门始终紧闭，无人进出。清真寺对民众漠不关心——即使他们饥寒交迫，清真寺也不会施舍；而民众，无论多么虔诚，多么关心清真寺的活动，也从未参与过清真寺的欢乐——真主存在，但敬拜真主是民众的责任，而非真主的职责。

The Harafish is a string of tales. Tales are often overt or covert parables, and if The Harafish eventually suggests causes and effects, they are not sociological but psychological, since the sociology of the alley never changes. The psychology of the characters is rooted in their temperaments and their social positions. Some protagonists are hot-blooded and pugnacious. Others are greedy, others selfish, others beneficent and self-effacing. The appearance of these characteristics is random to a certain degree—for example, the luck of a father's marriage choice may dictate whether the son is graceful and strong or self-indulgent and shortsighted. Or circumstances may intervene to cut off a promising career. There is a persistent sense of danger—in every generation, both men and women must be wary of crossing powerful enemies, or even relatives, who are full of hatred or resentment. The clan chief is the only person capable of giving the harafish protection, but he himself is always beset and insecure. By the last pages of the novel, the triumphs and defeats of all the characters, major and minor, come to seem futile (though Mahfouz is too skillful to make them repetitive). The long history of the al-Nagis doesn't add up to what they think it does—in fact, it doesn't add up at all. The return of Ashur in the tenth tale ends up being a respite rather than a climax.

《哈拉菲什》是一系列故事的集合。这些故事往往是或明或暗的寓言，即便《哈拉菲什》最终暗示了因果关系，也并非社会学意义上的，而是心理学意义上的，因为这条巷子的社会结构亘古不变。人物的心理根植于他们的性情和社会地位。有些主人公性情急躁好斗，有些贪婪自私，有些则仁慈谦逊。这些性格特征的出现在某种程度上是随机的——例如，父亲择偶的运气可能决定儿子是优雅强健还是放纵短视。或者，一些境遇可能会扼杀前途光明的事业。危险的气息始终萦绕在人们心头——每一代人，无论男女都必须提防强大的敌人，甚至是充满仇恨或怨恨的亲戚。氏族首领是唯一能够保护哈拉菲什的人，但他自己却总是四面楚歌，缺乏安全感。到了小说的最后几页，所有人物，无论大小，的成败都显得徒劳无功（尽管马哈福兹技艺高超，避免了情节重复）。纳吉斯家族漫长的历史并非他们所认为的那样完整——事实上，它根本就说不通。第十个故事中阿舒尔的回归最终只是一种喘息，而非高潮。

It is possible to utterly enjoy the stately drama of the history of the al-Nagis without being at all drawn to the violent and dangerous world they live in. Betrayal is commonplace and can occur between the closest relatives. Enmity is expected from most associates outside the family if they haven't been bought off or made into allies. Women are as unpredictable as men, and even the most helpful and faithful wife is likely to be displaced by a younger one. Family relationships depend entirely upon the character and circumstances of the patriarch, and he can devolve into a hashish-smoking drunk at any time. Mahfouz's tone is even throughout. Though he is skillful at engendering suspense, in the end even the most suspenseful adventure ends as gossip and then turns into a story or a legend. Whether the reader finds this reassuring or disheartening is in some sense beside the point—this is one of those novels that subordinates individual dramas to a larger pattern than comedy or tragedy. It is a good example, like The Makioka Sisters , of the adaptation of a European form to a non-European culture. The result shares some characteristics of all novels (in this case, readability and accessibility) but arrives at different meanings and makes a subtly different impression on the reader.

即使完全不被纳吉斯家族所处的暴力危险世界所吸引，读者依然可以尽情享受其庄严的历史剧。背叛司空见惯，甚至发生在至亲之间。除非被收买或拉拢，否则大多数外人都会与家族成员为敌。女性和男性一样难以捉摸，即使是最贤惠忠贞的妻子也可能被更年轻的女子取代。家庭关系完全取决于一家之主的性格和境遇，他随时都可能沦为吸食大麻的酒鬼。马哈福兹的笔调始终如一。尽管他擅长营造悬念，但最终，即使是最扣人心弦的冒险也沦为流言蜚语，最终演变成故事或传说。读者对此感到欣慰还是沮丧，在某种程度上并不重要——这是一部将个体悲剧置于更宏大叙事框架之下的小说，而非喜剧或悲剧。它和《牧冈姐妹》一样，是欧洲文学形式融入非欧洲文化的一个很好的例子。虽然它具备所有小说的一些共同特征（例如易读性和易理解性），但最终呈现出的意义却有所不同，给读者留下的印象也略有差异。

82. Iris Murdoch. The Sea, the Sea

82. 艾瑞斯·默多克。《大海，大海》

(NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1978), 495 PP.

（纽约：企鹅出版社，1978 年），495 页。

The Sea, the Sea is a disquieting novel, substantial and serious but puzzling in many ways. It is the self-told story of Charles Arrowby, a successful London theater director who decides to retire to the seaside and write something rather like a memoir. It turns out to be a confession and an account of how a man comes to terms with his own egoism, but it is also a demonstration of how difficult the confessional mode is, especially if the narrator is supposed to be morally transformed by his experiences. In The Sea, the Sea , Murdoch has given Charles Arrowby a rich sensual appreciation of nature and sharp observations of his friends, but she also has taken on the added challenge of writing from within his consciousness while portraying him as not merely foolish and heedless, as Flaubert, for example, portrays Emma Bovary, but boorish, contemptuous, and selfish—less forgivable traits in the social world of writer, reader, and protagonist. She then piles plot twist upon plot twist, taxing the reader in several ways. She achieves a high degree of suspense but also of implausibility, and resolves it all through the deus ex machina of Charles's cousin James, who acts as Charles's savior for unexplained reasons of his own and then passes on to a higher plane of existence, or so Charles is led to believe.

《大海，大海》是一部令人不安的小说，内容丰富而严肃，但在许多方面却令人费解。小说以查尔斯·阿罗比的自述形式展开，他是一位成功的伦敦戏剧导演，决定退休到海边，写一部类似回忆录的作品。最终，这部作品既是一部忏悔录，也是一个人如何克服自身利己主义的叙述，同时也展现了忏悔式写作的难度，尤其当叙述者需要通过自身经历实现道德上的转变时。在《大海，大海》中，默多克赋予查尔斯·阿罗比对自然丰富的感官享受和对朋友敏锐的观察力，但她也面临着更大的挑战：从阿罗比的内心世界出发进行写作，同时将他描绘成一个粗鲁、傲慢、自私的人，而不仅仅是像福楼拜笔下的艾玛·包法利那样愚蠢和鲁莽——这些特质在作家、读者和主人公所处的社交世界中都是难以容忍的。她随后接连抛出各种情节转折，从多方面考验着读者的理解力。她成功地营造了高度悬念，但也制造了许多不合情理之处，最终通过查尔斯的表弟詹姆斯的“天降神兵”式出现来解决所有问题。詹姆斯出于某种不明原因成为了查尔斯的救星，然后便升入了更高的存在层面——至少查尔斯是这么认为的。

At first Charles seems quite attractive. He is worldly, articulate, gossipy, witty in some ways, and full of information and stories. He seems forthcoming about his likes and dislikes, as if, by sixty-three, he has earned the right to live as he pleases. His most unattractive quality is that he gives in to the temptation to fiddle with the lives of others, especially the affections of an old girlfriend, Lizzie, who is at this point happy enough living in an unorthodox relationship with another old friend, Gilbert, who is homosexual. Charles is in the midst of breaking this relationship up when he realizes that his real first love, a girl he had known in youth, is living in his new town with her husband, who seems to be something of a bully. Charles immediately becomes romantically obsessed with this woman, Hartley, and attempts to rescue her from her marriage by kidnapping her and holding her hostage in his house while other houseguests party around them. A long section in the middle of the novel consists of Charles's obsessive self-justifications and hysterical fantasies about Hartley, who, it is clear to the reader, is both frightened of Charles and not worthy of his interest, even on the score of renewing first love. As if to compound his errors in judgment, Charles also conceives an infatuation with Hartley's adopted son, Titus. Charles is a heavy burden to his author because his best quality, his eloquence, is also his worst, since his habit of applying the full force of his eloquence to every idea, no matter how foolish or misguided, inures the reader to believing him, or even paying much attention to him.

查尔斯起初看起来颇具魅力。他见多识广，能言善辩，爱八卦，有时还颇具幽默感，而且博闻强识，故事也讲不完。他似乎毫不掩饰自己的喜好和厌恶，仿佛到了六十三岁，他已经有资格随心所欲地生活。他最令人反感的一点是，他总是忍不住去干涉别人的生活，尤其是他以前的女友莉齐的感情。莉齐此时正和另一位老朋友吉尔伯特——一位同性恋者——过着一段非传统的恋情，生活得十分幸福。查尔斯正打算拆散这段恋情时，却发现自己真正的初恋——一个他年轻时就认识的女孩——正和她的丈夫住在他的新城市里，而她的丈夫似乎是个恶霸。查尔斯立刻对这个名叫哈特利的女人产生了强烈的迷恋，他试图通过绑架哈特利并将她囚禁在自己家中，以此来“解救”她。当时，其他客人正在屋里聚会玩乐。小说中段有一大段篇幅描写了查尔斯对哈特利的执着辩解和歇斯底里的幻想。读者显然能看出，哈特利既害怕查尔斯，又不值得他关注，即便是在重燃初恋的意义上。仿佛为了加深自己的判断失误，查尔斯还迷恋上了哈特利的养子提图斯。查尔斯对作者来说是个沉重的负担，因为他最大的优点——雄辩——也是他最大的缺点。他习惯于用尽全力去阐述每一个观点，无论多么愚蠢或错误，这让读者麻木地相信他，甚至对他漠不关心。

Murdoch's Flaubertian gambit is to give Charles a profound and appealing talent for describing the natural landscape around him, especially the look of the sea as it changes moment by moment. This facet of his eloquence gives his voice the substance and attractiveness it has and in some sense works to make him seem more reliable as a narrator through most of the novel. No doubt this fineness of perception is a trait Charles shares with his author, and perhaps it is meant to stand at the beginning of the novel for disregarded and unexploited moral qualities that the action of the novel is meant to develop. However, the steady alternation of the narrative between precise description of the scene and precise description of Charles's unbelievable wishes, scenarios, and inferences works to give all of his thoughts a sameness—his finer thoughts and potentialities come to seem equally tainted by self-delusion, so it is hard for the reader to see the moral growth the author seems to have intended.

默多克效仿福楼拜，赋予查尔斯一种深刻而迷人的天赋，让他能够描绘周围的自然景观，尤其是变幻莫测的大海。这种雄辩的特质赋予了他的叙述声音以实质和魅力，并在某种程度上使他在小说的大部分篇幅中显得更加可靠。毫无疑问，这种敏锐的感知力是查尔斯与作者的共同特征，或许它象征着小说开篇那些被忽视和未被开发的道德品质，而小说的情节正是为了发展这些品质。然而，叙事中对场景的精确描述与对查尔斯那些匪夷所思的愿望、设想和推断的精确描述之间的不断交替，使得他的所有想法都显得千篇一律——他那些更美好的想法和潜能似乎也同样被自我欺骗所玷污，因此读者很难看到作者似乎想要表达的道德成长。

But what did she intend? The standard novel depicts moral transformation through the operation of the plot, which is made up of actions, reactions, and interactions among the characters. The pact between author and reader is that a particular sequence of events is being described because these events above all others are pivotal in the protagonist's life. Such a pact is easy to make with classic novels—in the English novel that ends in a marriage or two, the importance of the events as life-shaping is obvious, especially since marriages in classic times were lifelong. In the classic French novel of romance and adultery, too, events are pivotal, because usually death is the result of the action. In The Sea, the Sea , the only person to experience both the action of the novel and the moral transformation of Charles Arrowby is Charles himself. After the fatal weeks, the other characters either die or go about their business. At the most, they are relieved that Charles is less of an egomaniac. The drama throughout the novel takes place in Charles's own mind, without much reference at all to other people. The reader can thus see these five hundred pages as fairly trivial— Charles is an emotional loner who should never have solicited the attentions of the other characters in the first place, and by the end of the novel he is back where he started, only with a few more sentimental feelings about himself than he had at the beginning. The one aspect of the novel that gives it more seriousness than this is its eloquence— we want Charles's sensibility to be more worthy than it seems. Murdoch does her best to endow him with her own worthiness, but in my opinion it doesn't quite come off. She tries to objectify and subjectify his moral life at the same time, but her tool—his writing style— muddles her effort. Her ideas about how moral transformation works do not come across believably, either through the plot or through the telling of the story.

但她究竟意欲何为？传统小说通过情节的推进来展现道德转变，而情节则由人物之间的行动、反应和互动构成。作者与读者之间的约定是，之所以描述特定的事件顺序，是因为这些事件对主人公的人生至关重要。这种约定在经典小说中很容易达成——在以一两场婚姻结尾的英国小说中，这些事件对人生的塑造意义显而易见，尤其是在古典时代，婚姻往往是终身的。在经典的法国爱情小说和婚外情小说中，事件同样至关重要，因为死亡通常是行动的结果。在《大海，大海》中，唯一经历小说情节和查尔斯·阿罗比道德转变的人只有查尔斯本人。在致命的几周之后，其他人物要么死去，要么继续过着他们的生活。他们最多只是庆幸查尔斯不再那么自大。整部小说的戏剧冲突都发生在查尔斯的内心世界，几乎没有提及其他人。因此，读者可能会觉得这五百页的内容相当琐碎——查尔斯是个情感孤僻的人，他一开始就不该去招惹其他角色的注意。到了小说结尾，他又回到了原点，只是比开头多了几分感伤。这部小说唯一比这更严肃的地方在于它的文笔——我们希望查尔斯的感性比表面看起来更有价值。默多克竭力赋予他她自己的价值，但在我看来，她并没有完全做到。她试图同时客观化和主观化他的道德生活，但她的工具——他的写作风格——却使她的努力显得混乱。她关于道德转变如何运作的观点，无论是通过情节还是通过叙事，都难以令人信服。

The Sea, the Sea is a good example of the principle that no novel can transcend its conception. Iris Murdoch was certainly an important and ambitious novelist, with rich measures of intelligence, style, knowledge, and experience. In this novel she brought all of these gifts to bear upon her subject, but the more Charles partakes of Murdoch's talents, the less credible he becomes, so that at the emotional climax of the novel, when he is living in his cousin James's house and finally understanding the true emotional sources of his life, the reader feels no answering sympathy. The idea of redemption applies, but the reality of it does not.

《大海，大海》很好地诠释了“任何小说都无法超越其构思”这一原则。艾瑞斯·默多克无疑是一位重要且雄心勃勃的小说家，她才智过人、文笔优美、知识渊博、阅历丰富。在这部小说中，她将所有这些天赋都倾注于笔下，但查尔斯越是吸收了默多克的才华，就越显得缺乏可信度。以至于在小说的情感高潮——他住在表兄詹姆斯的家中，最终领悟到自己生命中真正的情感根源时——读者却无法产生任何共鸣。救赎的概念固然存在，但其现实意义却荡然无存。

83. David Lodge How Far Can You Go?

83. 大卫·洛奇 你能走多远？

∗ The American edition of the book is as follows: Souls and Bodies (New York: William Morrow, 1981 ), 243 pp.

* 该书的美国版如下：灵魂与肉体（纽约：威廉·莫罗出版社，1981 年），243 页。

(LONDON: PENGUIN LTD, 1981), 256 PP.

（伦敦：企鹅有限公司，1981 年），256 页。

One of the results of the competing fashions in academic criticism that seized English departments on college campuses in the 1970s and 1980s was that novelists came to understand and in many cases to embrace the political aspect of the novel. Art, especially art that advertised itself as universal or timeless, came to be seen as another area in which the dominant social, cultural, and economic groups could press their views and close off discussion of subversive or challenging subjects. One result of this critical ferment was the remaking of literary history, which meant the inclusion in the canon of authors previously excluded as well as the redefinition of standards of value. Another result was a sharper understanding of contradictory impulses in individual novels. David Lodge, who taught English literature at the University of Birmingham, has written both novels and critical works, usually alternating between the two. He was (and is) both quite astute and up to date in literary theory and quite entertaining and smart as a novelist. How Far Can You Go? shows pretty much how far you can go in turning a story into a historical inquiry if you have a lively intelligence; a clear, comic, and detailed style; and a humane sensibility.

20世纪70年代和80年代，大学校园的英语系掀起了学术批评领域相互竞争的风潮，其结果之一是，小说家们开始理解，并在许多情况下接受了小说的政治层面。艺术，尤其是那些标榜自身具有普世性或永恒性的艺术，被视为主流社会、文化和经济群体宣扬自身观点、压制颠覆性或挑战性话题讨论的又一领域。这场批评浪潮的后果之一是文学史的重塑，这意味着一些此前被排除在经典之外的作家被纳入其中，价值标准也被重新定义。另一个后果是对个别小说中矛盾冲动的理解更加深刻。曾在伯明翰大学教授英国文学的戴维·洛奇（David Lodge）既创作小说，也撰写评论作品，通常两者交替进行。他过去（现在也是）在文学理论方面颇具洞察力且与时俱进，同时作为小说家，他的作品也颇具趣味性和智慧。《你能走多远？》（How Far Can You Go?）这表明，如果你拥有活跃的思维、清晰、幽默、细致的文风以及人文情怀，你就能将一个故事发展成一场历史探究，并走得非常远。

There is possibly no more straightforward novel than How Far Can You Go? It opens in a cold, damp Catholic church in 1952 , during weekday Mass. Eight or nine characters are introduced, all English Catholic university students, along with the priest, who is a few years older. The five men and four women are set very particularly in time, given not only a specific historical moment but also a list of doctrines they have been taught and believe in. The novel then follows them as they study, fall in love, graduate, marry, have children, grow older, and find their faith tested in any number of ways. Lodge is always clear that they are based on people he knows; that they are representative of their time, place, and situation; and that he is ruthlessly summarizing their inner lives for the sake of his argument. Drama is subordinated to pattern, the characters’ experience of emotion to the narrator's ideas about what their pleasure and torments signify. And yet the novel is rigorous but not cold, objective in tone but compelling to read, no doubt thanks to Lodge's very crisp and insightful and funny style.
