或许没有比《你能走多远？》更直白的小说了。故事开篇于1952年一个阴冷潮湿的天主教堂，正值平日弥撒。小说引入了八九个人物，他们都是英国天主教大学的学生，还有一位比他们年长几岁的神父。这五男四女被设定在一个特定的时代背景中，不仅被赋予了特定的历史时刻，还被赋予了一系列他们所接受和信仰的教义。小说随后跟随他们的脚步，讲述他们学习、恋爱、毕业、结婚、生子、逐渐老去，并在各种考验中经历信仰的磨难。洛奇始终明确地指出，这些人物原型是他认识的人；他们代表了他们所处的时代、地点和境遇；而他为了论证自己的观点，对他们的内心世界进行了毫不留情的概括。戏剧性被置于模式之下，人物的情感体验服从于叙述者对他们的喜怒哀乐所代表的意义的解读。然而，这部小说严谨而不冷漠，客观却引人入胜，这无疑要归功于洛奇简洁明快、洞察力敏锐且幽默风趣的文风。

Lodge's characters have only first names, as befits examples. Dennis and Angela, already a couple at the beginning of the novel, become the most prosperous but encounter the greatest challenges—not only is their fourth child born with Down syndrome, their third child is killed in traffic. Michael is obsessed with sex. He and Miriam, who had converted to Catholicism to marry him, have the most companionable marriage, but he is most troubled by the pleasures of the flesh he thinks he has missed by adhering to doctrinal strictures. Edward is a doctor whose practice of medicine is troubled and distorted by the church's insistence on limiting birth control to the rhythm method, or “Vatican roulette,” as Michael calls it. Miles is a supercilious homosexual who finally accepts his sexual orientation, and Adrian is a revolutionary always agitating for liberal changes with pamphlets and meetings. Ruth, the plainest of the girls, becomes a nun. Her whole way of life is repeatedly modified by changes of doctrine. Polly, always the most experimental, marries a television producer and winds up wealthy, successful, divorced, and liberated. The novel ends arbitrarily, before the stories of the characters end, right about the time John Paul II is elected pope. The characters are now in their forties. Lodge gives each a small send-off, but there is no overall plot structure, meaning no climax and no denouement.

洛奇笔下的人物都只有名字，这很符合人物性格的特点。丹尼斯和安吉拉在小说开篇已是一对伴侣，他们生活最为富裕，但也遭遇了最大的挑战——他们的第四个孩子患有唐氏综合征，第三个孩子则在车祸中丧生。迈克尔沉迷于性。他和为了嫁给他而皈依天主教的米里亚姆拥有最和谐的婚姻，但他却因恪守教义的束缚而错失了肉体的欢愉，这令他备受煎熬。爱德华是一名医生，教会坚持将避孕方法限制在安全期避孕法，迈克尔称之为“梵蒂冈轮盘赌”，这让他的行医之路变得举步维艰，甚至扭曲了他的健康。迈尔斯是一个傲慢的同性恋者，最终接受了自己的性取向。阿德里安则是一位革命者，他始终通过散发传单和组织集会来推动自由主义的变革。露丝是这群女孩中最朴素的一个，后来成为了一名修女。她的整个生活方式都因教义的变迁而不断改变。波莉向来最爱尝试新鲜事物，她嫁给了一位电视制片人，最终变得富有、成功、离了婚，并且获得了自由。小说的结尾显得有些随意，人物的故事尚未完结，恰好在约翰·保罗二世当选教皇前后。此时，人物都已年过四十。洛奇为每个人安排了简短的告别，但小说没有整体的情节结构，既没有高潮也没有结局。

It is the author himself, as narrator (and his narrative voice seems to be identical with his personal voice), who makes How Far Can You Go? work. When he introduces his characters in the first chapter, he also introduces himself contemplating them. One lengthy early paragraph introduces all the outmoded beliefs they have been taught and still hold at eighteen but will soon abandon. At the end, he reintroduces himself in the first person, saying, “While I was writing this last chapter…” Thus Lodge signals his satirical but generous attitude—he doesn't blame them for anything they do, whether it is proscribed as sin by the church or is simply foolish or egotistical. They are, after all, his friends, and he worries about the same things they do. The novelist is not concerned with punishments and rewards (that is, with how they experience their lives) but with how what they do fits in with what they have been taught and what they learn once they are faced with the adventures and choices of adulthood.

真正让《你能走多远？》这部作品引人入胜的，是作者本人作为叙述者（而且他的叙述声音似乎与他个人的声音完全一致）。在第一章中，当他介绍笔下的人物时，他也同时介绍了自己，并对他们进行了一番思考。开篇一段篇幅较长的文字，讲述了他们从小被灌输的、十八岁时仍然坚持的过时观念，而这些观念他们很快就会放弃。在结尾，他再次以第一人称介绍自己，说道：“当我写完最后一章的时候……”由此，洛奇展现了他讽刺却又宽容的态度——他不会责怪他们所做的一切，无论这些行为是否被教会视为罪恶，或者仅仅是愚蠢或自私。毕竟，他们是他的朋友，他和他们一样为此担忧。小说家关注的并非惩罚和奖赏（即他们如何体验人生），而是他们的所作所为如何与他们从小被灌输的观念以及在面对成年生活的冒险和抉择时所学到的东西相契合。

Like Lodge's other novels, How Far Can You Go? is preoccupied with sexuality, and much of the poignancy of the characters’ stories comes from their ambivalence about sex and love. When they most want it—as young men and women—it is forbidden. Once they are married, there is the constant danger of pregnancy. The rhythm method of birth control introduces further disincentives, especially, as Edward comes to believe, because the failure of the rhythm method is more likely to lead to genetic anomalies. By the time all of the characters finally overcome their doubts and begin to take the Pill, marital sex has become routine. Each of the characters, but especially Michael, is beset by the feeling that he or she has missed something, a feeling that dogs their marriages and careers even as liberalism sets in and takes hold. They don't want to adhere to strict doctrines as earlier generations did, but once they give them up, a residual anxiety is accompanied by the feeling that adhering to them thus far has been a waste of time.

与洛奇的其他小说一样，《你能走多远？》也聚焦于性，书中人物故事的辛酸之处很大程度上源于他们对性和爱的矛盾心理。当他们最渴望性爱的时候——年轻男女时期——却被禁止。结婚后，怀孕的风险始终存在。安全期避孕法又带来了更多阻碍，尤其是爱德华逐渐意识到，安全期避孕法的失败更容易导致基因异常。当所有人物最终克服疑虑开始服用避孕药时，夫妻间的性生活已经变得司空见惯。每个人物，尤其是迈克尔，都感到自己错过了什么，这种感觉如影随形，即便在自由主义兴起并逐渐占据主导地位之后，也依然困扰着他们的婚姻和事业。他们不想像前几代人那样墨守成规，但一旦放弃，一种挥之不去的焦虑感便会伴随着一种感觉：之前坚持这些教条都是浪费时间。

I have read How Far Can You Go? several times, and I am always impressed by how satisfying it is. Its subject is not one I have any special interest in, and probably I wouldn't read a novel about English Catholicism that had a more internal sensibility. Lodge's influences— Joyce, Graham Greene, and Evelyn Waugh—are ones I am fairly indifferent to. Nevertheless, I admire Lodge's willingness to bring his entire mind to every novel he writes, and this means his good nature as well as his intellectual curiosity, his perplexity as well as his hopefulness, his sadness as well as his sharp narrative skills, and his pleasure in experiment as well as his vast knowledge of literary tradition. And he is very funny, too.

我读过《你能走多远？》好几遍，每次都为它带给我的满足感而印象深刻。我对它的主题并没有什么特别的兴趣，或许我也不会去读一本更注重内在情感的关于英国天主教的小说。洛奇的创作深受乔伊斯、格雷厄姆·格林和伊夫林·沃的影响，但我对他本人并无太大的感觉。尽管如此，我依然钦佩洛奇将全部心血倾注于每一部小说创作中的态度，这体现在他既有善良的本性，又有求知欲；既有困惑，又有希望；既有悲伤，又有精湛的叙事技巧；既有对实验的热情，又有渊博的文学传统知识。而且，他本人也十分幽默。

84. Muriel Spark. Loitering with Intent

84. 穆里尔·斯帕克。《有目的的徘徊》

(NEW YORK: NEW DIRECTIONS, 1981), 214 PP.

（纽约：新方向出版社，1981 年），214 页。

Muriel Spark is a true woman of letters who has written many novels and many volumes of poetry, as well as short stories, biographies, criticism, and other essays. She has been at work for fifty years or more, and her output has been consistently of high quality as well as consistently unlike the work of any other author. Loitering with Intent purports to be a memoir by an older woman of letters about the fate of her first novel, written exactly at the middle of the twentieth century, when the novelist was lingering on the fringes of London intellectual life and waiting for the onset of success. It is not actually autobiographical in the strictest sense, in that it does not relate events that appear in Spark's biography; it is rather a reflection on the strange condition of being a novelist and finding events of one's life beginning to echo and reflect the incidents in one's work. Spark has a thesis, but it may be that she is also enjoying a joke—pressing the plausibility of her thesis to extremes and daring her voice, her style, and the apparatus of the realistic novel to carry it off.

缪丽尔·斯帕克是一位真正的女作家，她创作了许多小说、诗集、短篇小说、传记、评论和其他散文。她从事写作已有五十余年，作品始终保持着极高的水准，并且风格独树一帜。《徘徊的意图》一书自称是一位年长的女作家所著的回忆录，讲述了她第一部小说的命运。这部小说写于二十世纪中叶，当时这位小说家正徘徊在伦敦知识分子生活的边缘，等待着成功的到来。严格来说，它并非自传，因为它并没有讲述斯帕克生平中的事件；它更像是对身为小说家的奇特境遇的一种反思，探讨了生活经历如何开始在作品中产生回响和共鸣。 Spark 有一个论点，但她可能也在享受一个玩笑——将她的论点的合理性推向极致，并挑战她的声音、风格和现实主义小说的结构来支撑它。

Fleur, Spark's protagonist, takes a job with Sir Quentin, who appears to be a wealthy, disinterested, though snobbish, man of letters. Sir Quentin runs a club of people whom he is encouraging to write, called the “Autobiographical Association.” His motives are unclear, but Fleur begins to suspect him of something unsavory, largely because he is such a snob and because he treats his mother as if she were senile when she does not appear to be so to Fleur. In the meantime, Fleur is working on and completing her novel. It is taken by a publisher, but then, after the proof stage, returned to her. The manuscript is stolen from Fleur's room and, to all appearances, destroyed.

弗勒是斯帕克笔下的主人公，她受雇于昆汀爵士。昆汀爵士表面上是一位富有、不爱读书，但略显势利的文人墨客。他经营着一个名为“自传协会”的俱乐部，鼓励人们写作。昆汀爵士的动机不明，但弗勒开始怀疑他另有所图，主要是因为他傲慢自大，而且对待母亲如同对待老态龙钟的老妇人一般，而弗勒却觉得她并非如此。与此同时，弗勒正在创作并完成她的小说。小说被出版社拿走，但在校对阶段之后又被退还给了她。之后，手稿从弗勒的房间里被盗，而且似乎已被销毁。

Loitering with Intent is set at a particular moment in English history, five years after the end of the Second World War, but it is strangely vague as a social document. Fleur is hardly interested in the world around her, or is interested in it only as it begins to behave like her novel. There is rationing, there are bombed-out craters, jobs are hard to find, characters have been demobilized from the armed forces, but these are so incidental to what is important to Fleur that they do not gel into any kind of depiction of a passing cultural or political moment. Fleur's world is as eternal to her as the conventional plots of novels or the insights of the authors of the books she likes. She has no theories, almost no interests other than her books and friends she likes because they are fun and kindly (including Quentin's mother, who is far less senile than she lets on).

《徘徊的意图》的故事背景设定在英国历史上的一个特定时期——二战结束五年后，但作为一部社会纪实作品，它却出奇地模糊不清。弗勒对周遭的世界几乎漠不关心，或者说，她对这个世界的兴趣仅限于它开始像她小说里描述的那样发展。那里有配给制，有被炸毁的弹坑，工作难找，有人从军队退役，但这些对弗勒来说都无关紧要，以至于无法构成对某个转瞬即逝的文化或政治时刻的任何描绘。对弗勒而言，她的世界如同小说的传统情节或她所喜爱的作家的洞见一样永恒。她没有理论，除了书本和她喜欢的那些有趣又善良的朋友（包括昆汀的母亲，她远没有她表现出来的那么老态龙钟）之外，几乎没有其他兴趣。

As in other Spark novels, the plot is elaborate, but at the same time Spark doesn't seem to particularly care about it, nor does she develop her characters in the conventional way, by giving them important tasks that simultaneously develop and reveal them. Rather, they have certain taglines (Quentin always querulously addresses his mother as “Mummy!,” for example, and Dottie, Fleur's friend, is repeatedly referred to as “an English Rose”), and their activities form a sort of background pattern or armature for Fleur's observations about herself, her world, and her work. The most important thing about Fleur is that she is happily and intently writing a novel. She enjoys everything about it and has great faith in it while she is writing it. As she discusses it in her “memoir,” it sounds juvenile and highly plotted, a run-of-the-mill English potboiler about strange goings-on among the upper crust, or at least among upper-crust wannabes. What stands out about it (even for Fleur, once she has gone on to her next novel) is her pleasure in writing it and her love of it as her production. She is never oppressed by self-doubts or doubts about the novel—even after she finishes it and falls out of love with it, she still honors it for what it is, the prologue to the rest; her novel, but just a novel.

如同斯帕克的其他小说一样，情节错综复杂，但斯帕克似乎并不特别在意，她也没有按照传统的方式塑造人物，赋予他们重要的任务，从而在塑造和揭示人物的同时，也让他们经历磨难。相反，每个人物都有一些标志性的口头禅（例如，昆汀总是抱怨地称呼他的母亲为“妈妈！”，而弗勒的朋友多蒂则被反复称为“英国玫瑰”），他们的活动构成了一种背景模式或框架，用来衬托弗勒对自身、世界和工作的观察。弗勒最重要的特质在于她正兴致勃勃、全神贯注地创作一部小说。她享受创作过程中的一切，并对这部小说充满信心。正如她在“回忆录”中所描述的那样，这部小说听起来幼稚且情节繁复，就像一部平庸的英国通俗小说，讲述的是上流社会，或者至少是那些渴望跻身上流社会的人之间发生的奇闻轶事。这部小说最突出的地方（即使对弗勒而言，在她开始创作下一部小说之后也是如此）在于她写作时的愉悦感以及她对这部作品的热爱。她从未被自我怀疑或对小说本身的怀疑所困扰——即使在完成之后，她不再喜欢这部小说，她仍然尊重它，视其为整部作品的序章；是她的小说，但仅仅是一部小说。

Loitering with Intent is an oddity, a bildungsroman that is a farce rather than an epic. Idiosyncratic charm is the hallmark of Spark's work; Loitering with Intent is a good introduction to her sensibility as well as her oeuvre.

《徘徊的意图》是一部奇特的作品，与其说是史诗，不如说是一部闹剧式的成长小说。斯帕克作品的标志是其独特的魅力；《徘徊的意图》是了解她个人风格及其全部作品的绝佳入门之作。

85. Anne Tyler. Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant

85. 安妮·泰勒。《在思乡餐厅的晚餐》

(NEW YORK: ALFRED A. KNOPF, 1982), 303 PP.

（纽约：ALFRED A. KNOPF，1982 年），303 页。

Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant is interesting in part because it doesn't seem to have a reason to exist. It does not seem to be autobiographical; it sets forth no political or social analysis—no ideas about anything except how the Tull children, Cody, Jenny, and Ezra, were shaped by their family life, especially by the sudden departure of their father, Beck, and the erratic, prickly behavior of their mother, Pearl. It is a serious though not overly sober narrative of the life of a particular family whose members consider themselves ordinary, and whom the author, too, seems to consider ordinary in a sociological sense—none of them has any claims to outstanding accomplishments or talents—but each is full of idiosyncrasies, though no more so than any other family. On the surface, Tyler seems to be engaging in a form of comic naturalism—like Zola, she details the ordinary and never proposes that a change in social conditions would change her characters’ lives. But unlike Zola's characters, hers do not come to grief, they come to understanding and accommodation. Things go on as they begin, and how they go on is satisfactory enough in the end.

《思乡餐厅的晚餐》之所以引人入胜，部分原因在于它似乎并无存在的理由。它并非自传体小说；它没有提出任何政治或社会分析——除了描写图尔家的三个孩子，科迪、珍妮和埃兹拉，如何被家庭生活塑造之外，没有其他任何想法，尤其是父亲贝克的突然离去以及母亲珀尔反复无常、难以相处的行为。这是一部严肃却又不失轻松的叙事作品，讲述了一个特定家庭的生活。这个家庭的成员自认为平凡，而作者似乎也从社会学的角度认为他们是平凡的——他们中没有人拥有任何杰出的成就或才能——但每个人都充满了个性，尽管这种个性与其他任何家庭并无二致。表面上看，泰勒似乎在运用一种喜剧自然主义手法——像左拉一样，她细致地描绘了平凡的日常，从未暗示社会环境的改变会改变她笔下人物的生活。但与左拉笔下的人物不同，她笔下的人物最终没有走向悲剧，而是走向了理解与包容。事情按部就班地进行着，最终的结果也令人满意。

The novel begins with Pearl on her deathbed, then moves quickly backward to her meeting, as a young girl turning into an old maid, with Beck Tull, who is good-looking and travels for a living and is not quite the mate Pearl had originally imagined for herself. Nor does she plan to have more than one child, but when Cody, the eldest, suffers a frightening childhood illness, Pearl persuades Beck to give her two more. Beck leaves the family when Cody is fourteen. Tyler's characterizations are especially sharp—the reader can see in the way Beck combs his hair and the style of his dialogue that he is a certain type of mid-twentieth-century man, flashy but unreliable, an employed drifter in a suit, not a bum but not quite committed to the middle class. Pearl is filled with resentment at her situation. She, too, is a mid-century type, a woman with social pretensions fallen on hard times, who is fanatical about keeping up appearances and incapable of friendships outside the family, fearful that someone might get the opportunity to look down on her as she looks down on most others. She is devoted to her three children but resentful of them, prone to hysterical rages in which she demeans and denounces them for not considering her desires in some way. She is a bad mother, something of a witch, but Tyler doesn't allow the children or the reader to come to a final judgment of her; rather she asks the reader to patiently consider Pearl and, at the very end, to empathize with her, as Ezra does.

小说以珀尔病危的姿态开篇，随后迅速倒叙，讲述了她少女时期与贝克·图尔的相遇。贝克英俊潇洒，四处漂泊谋生，但并非珀尔最初设想的理想伴侣。珀尔原本只打算生一个孩子，但当长子科迪患上可怕的儿童疾病后，她劝说贝克再给她生两个。科迪十四岁时，贝克离开了这个家庭。泰勒的人物刻画尤为犀利——读者从贝克梳头的姿势和说话方式就能看出，他是二十世纪中期某种典型男人的代表：浮夸却不可靠，西装革履的游手好闲之徒，虽非游手好闲之辈，却也对中产阶级缺乏归属感。珀尔对自己的处境充满了怨恨。她也是典型的世纪中期女性形象，一个曾经渴望上流社会地位，如今却落魄潦倒的女人。她极度注重维护体面，无法与家人以外的人建立友谊，生怕别人有机会像她瞧不起别人那样瞧不起她。她深爱着三个孩子，却又对他们充满怨恨，动辄歇斯底里地发怒，贬低和谴责他们没有顾及她的意愿。她是个糟糕的母亲，有点像个女巫，但泰勒并没有让孩子们或读者对她做出最终的评判；相反，她要求读者耐心地去思考珀尔，并在故事的结尾，像埃兹拉那样，对她产生同情。

Ezra is Pearl's favorite child and Cody's hated rival, an easygoing, almost oblivious caretaking sort whose only ambition in life is to cook good meals and see families (including his own) enjoy dining together. Ezra owns the Homesick Restaurant, which is a quirky establishment without a menu or a particular style of cooking. He has a knack for getting along with others that Cody, more observant and selfish, lacks and resents. The only girl, Jenny, is smart and pretty. She does well in college and becomes a doctor, but she is Pearl's opposite in her chaotic family life and her indifference to appearances.

埃兹拉是珀尔最宠爱的孩子，也是科迪最痛恨的对手。他性格随和，几乎有些迷糊，一心只想照顾别人，人生唯一的愿望就是烹饪美食，让家人（包括他自己的家人）享受一起用餐的乐趣。埃兹拉拥有一家名为“思乡餐厅”的特色小店，没有菜单，也没有固定的烹饪风格。他很擅长与人相处，而更善于观察、也更自私的科迪却缺乏这种能力，并因此心生怨恨。家中唯一的女孩珍妮聪明漂亮，大学成绩优异，后来成为了一名医生。但她与珀尔截然相反，她生活混乱，而且对外表毫不在意。

Tyler's novel covers some forty-five or fifty years, progressing by means of certain family incidents that are told through the different memories of each of the characters. There is no controlling consciousness, but Cody's seems the most observant, and he opens and closes the narrative. He is, in some sense, the villain of the family, full of grievances and meanness, unhappy and unforgiving, always replaying his old contempt for, fear of, and resentment of Ezra. A turning point in family history is when Cody, who is, like Beck, successful with women, steals the only girlfriend Ezra ever has and marries her, though they have nothing in common. Pearl, who realizes what is going on, can't stop it. But eventually this betrayal is incorporated into the family history along with every other misadventure and mistake.

泰勒的小说跨越了大约四五十年，通过一系列家庭事件，以每个角色的不同回忆展开叙述。小说没有统一的叙述视角，但科迪的视角似乎最为敏锐，他负责叙事的开头和结尾。在某种意义上，他是这个家庭的反派，充满怨恨和刻薄，郁郁寡欢且难以释怀，总是重温他对埃兹拉的蔑视、恐惧和怨恨。家族历史的一个转折点是，科迪——像贝克一样在女人缘极佳——抢走了埃兹拉唯一的女友并娶了她，尽管他们之间毫无共同之处。珀尔察觉到了这一切，却无力阻止。最终，这段背叛与其他的不幸遭遇和错误一起，被纳入了家族史之中。

Tyler is subtle and retiring as an author. Her style is precise and insightful, her incidents are full of interest and psychological weight, and her structure works to lay bare the workings of the family. But what is her point? Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant is Jamesian in the sense that it reads like very advanced gossip: all of the ideas it explores are about personal relationships—what they feel like, what they mean, how they work—but nothing about their larger political context. In the background I sense all sorts of psychological theories that exist in the culture but are outside the purview of Pearl and her children (even Jenny). In some sense, Dinner at the Homesick Restaurant stands as Tyler's answer to Freud, Jung, the behaviorists, the attachment theorists, and the ranks of therapists and clinicians. She is saying, here is a family; here is a bad mother; here is dysfunction. But the meaning of their family life is not in any theory about it, but in the details of what happened, how they experienced it, and what wisdom they took from their experience. She also excludes other forms of self-improvement, such as religion. The Tulls are entirely secular and not intellectual. They don't seek to know themselves through God or through ideas. Tyler seems to be saying that a good memory is enough for some measure of redemption as long as someone, in this case Ezra, has the right attitude.

泰勒的写作风格含蓄内敛。她的文风精准而深刻，笔下的事件引人入胜，心理刻画入木三分，结构巧妙地揭示了家庭运作的真相。但她究竟想表达什么呢？《思乡餐厅的晚餐》颇具詹姆斯式的风格，读起来就像是高雅的八卦：书中探讨的所有观点都围绕着人际关系——感受、意义、运作方式——却丝毫没有涉及其更宏大的政治背景。我隐约感觉到，书中充斥着各种存在于文化之中，却又游离于珀尔和她的孩子们（甚至珍妮）认知之外的心理学理论。某种程度上，《思乡餐厅的晚餐》是泰勒对弗洛伊德、荣格、行为主义者、依恋理论家以及众多治疗师和临床医生的回应。她仿佛在说：这是一个家庭；这是一个糟糕的母亲；这是一个功能失调的家庭。但他们家庭生活的意义不在于任何理论，而在于事件的细节、他们的经历以及他们从中汲取的智慧。她也排除了其他形式的自我提升，例如宗教。图尔一家完全世俗化，不追求知识分子式的修行。他们不试图通过上帝或任何理念来认识自我。泰勒似乎在说，只要某人（比如埃兹拉）拥有正确的态度，良好的记忆力就足以带来某种程度的救赎。

But, of course, Tyler does have theories, like any other author. She does not overtly display them, but she constructs her story so they are demonstrated. Ezra, for example, is not typical of a successful adult. His restaurant is not a great success, and he lives at home with his mother. He has no artistic aspirations, though he enjoys music. He is not physically prepossessing, nor is he universally appreciated by anyone but the author. Nevertheless, his kindness and patience supply the Tull saga with its redeeming moment, which takes place after Pearl becomes blind, during a period when she asks Ezra to read her youthful diary aloud to her. Other than that, I am not going to give the moment away, but it constitutes Tyler's idea about what is moral and of value in ordinary human existence. In other ways, too, she orchestrates the action of the novel to demonstrate a certain theory about how to live a good enough life even with flaws and vulnerabilities. While Tyler is remarkably self-effacing for an author—always writing in the third-person limited point of view and never digressing from the story or taking any opportunity to comment on the historical or social context of the story—the reader comes away from the novel with a strong sense of her presence and her take on life—clear-eyed but benign, principled but full of good humor and insight.

当然，泰勒和其他作家一样，也有自己的理论。她并不直接展现这些理论，而是通过巧妙的故事结构来加以阐释。例如，埃兹拉并非典型的成功人士。他的餐厅并不成功，他和母亲住在一起。他没有艺术追求，尽管他喜欢音乐。他外表并不出众，除了作者之外，也没有人欣赏他。然而，他的善良和耐心为图尔家族的故事增添了救赎的瞬间。这个瞬间发生在珀尔失明之后，当时珀尔请求埃兹拉为她朗读她年轻时的日记。除此之外，我不会剧透，但这个瞬间体现了泰勒关于普通人生活中何为道德和价值的思考。此外，她还通过其他方式精心安排小说情节，来阐释一种关于如何即使有缺陷和弱点也能过上足够美好的生活的理论。虽然泰勒作为一名作家非常谦逊——总是以第三人称有限视角写作，从不偏离故事，也不借任何机会评论故事的历史或社会背景——但读者读完这部小说后，会强烈感受到她的存在以及她对生活的看法——目光清醒但和蔼可亲，有原则但充满幽默感和洞察力。

86. Milan Kundera. The Unbearable Lightness of Being

86. 米兰·昆德拉。《生命中不能承受之轻》

TRANS. MICHAEL HENRY HEIM (NEW YORK: HARPERPERENNIAL, 1984), 314 PP.

译者：迈克尔·亨利·海姆（纽约：哈珀出版社，1984 年），314 页。

Kundera is a philosophical novelist in the tradition of Hermann Broch, and like Broch, he likes to break up the narrative in several ways to give the themes primacy over the story and characters. Whether this works is, I think, more a matter of taste with Kundera than with other novelists of the same turn of mind, because Kundera's tone is not charming, like that of, say, Italo Svevo, but cool and even condescending.

昆德拉是一位秉承赫尔曼·布洛赫传统的哲学小说家，与布洛赫一样，他喜欢以多种方式打破叙事结构，使主题凌驾于故事和人物之上。我认为，这种手法是否奏效，对昆德拉而言，更多地取决于个人品味，而非其他同类作家，因为昆德拉的语调并不像伊塔洛·斯韦沃那样充满魅力，而是冷峻甚至带有居高临下的意味。

The protagonists of The Unbearable Lightness of Being are Tomas and Tereza, a couple living in Prague who begin their relationship not long before the Prague Spring and Soviet invasion of 1968 . Tomas is a doctor who has left his wife and young son because he doesn't like them and prefers the life of a libertine. Tereza is an unhappy and vulnerable young woman who more or less gives herself into Tomas's hands after one or two meetings. She has some talents and a love of books, but it is not what they have in common that appeals to Tomas, rather Tereza's capacity for grief and suffering (most of it self-imposed by means of terrifying nightmares). Tereza is jealous and insecure, but Tomas does not give up his persistent womanizing—he justifies his “epic” pursuit of sex with many women as a separate category of connections and emotions from his feelings for Tereza. The two other characters in the novel are Sabina, an artist who has been Tomas's mistress, and Franz, a lover she meets in Geneva after she emigrates from Prague following the occupation. Franz and Sabina are not capable of understanding anything they experience together in the same way because of the wide differences in their previous lives, nor do they seem to be able to communicate these differences, but after Sabina leaves him, Franz remains attached and loyal to her as a kind of larger conscience or perspective that reminds him that his life is trivial and unheroic. When he does make a small attempt to do something heroic, he is accidentally killed, and his whole life disappears as those around him interpret it for their own benefit. Sabina, too, eventually dies in alien territory (California). Her vocation, painting, is portrayed more as a way to make a living than as an expression of her inner life.

《生命中不能承受之轻》的主人公是托马斯和特蕾莎，一对住在布拉格的情侣。他们的恋情始于1968年布拉格之春和苏联入侵前不久。托马斯是一名医生，他因为不喜欢妻子和年幼的儿子而抛弃了他们，更喜欢浪荡的生活。特蕾莎是一个不快乐且脆弱的年轻女子，在与托马斯见面一两次后，她便或多或少地将自己交付给了他。她有一些才华，也热爱读书，但吸引托马斯的并非他们之间的共同点，而是特蕾莎承受悲伤和痛苦的能力（其中大部分是她自己通过可怕的噩梦造成的）。特蕾莎嫉妒心强，缺乏安全感，但托马斯并没有放弃他持续的拈花惹草——他将自己与众多女性的“史诗级”性爱行为合理化为与他对特蕾莎的感情截然不同的情感体验。小说中的另外两个人物分别是萨宾娜和弗朗茨。萨宾娜是一位艺术家，曾是托马斯的情妇；弗朗茨是萨宾娜在布拉格被占领后移居日内瓦时遇到的情人。由于两人过往经历的巨大差异，弗朗茨和萨宾娜无法以相同的方式理解他们共同经历的一切，他们似乎也无法沟通这些差异。然而，在萨宾娜离开弗朗茨之后，弗朗茨仍然对她保持着依恋和忠诚，仿佛她是一种更宏大的良知或视角，提醒着他自己的人生是多么渺小和平庸。当他试图做一些力所能及的英雄之举时，却意外身亡，他整个人生也随之消逝，因为周围的人出于自身利益而曲解了他的一生。萨宾娜最终也死在了异乡（加利福尼亚）。她的职业——绘画——更多地被描绘成一种谋生手段，而非她内心世界的表达。

The one thing Tomas and Tereza share is a dog, Karenin, who is a female, but has a male name and is always referred to as “he.” The action of the novel more or less spans Karenin's life, and after he dies of cancer, Tomas and Tereza are killed in a truck accident.

托马斯和特蕾莎唯一共同拥有的就是一条名叫卡列宁的狗，它是一条母狗，却取了一个男性化的名字，而且总是被称作“他”。小说的故事大致围绕着卡列宁的一生展开，它因癌症去世后，托马斯和特蕾莎在一场卡车事故中丧生。

The gist of Kundera's theme is that the continuous falsehood of life under Soviet communism renders every action, emotion, and aesthetic response empty and meaningless. The great drama of Tomas's professional life occurs when he loses his career as a surgeon because of a letter to the editor of a newspaper written during the Prague Spring. The entire experience of the letter, printed in a truncated version that distorts Tomas's point, makes no sense because there is no action Tomas can take sincerely—everyone involved wants to use him and his prestige for purposes that do not originate with Tomas himself. Even though he loves surgery and knows he saves lives, he soon realizes that his only choice is to give up every form of success and privilege in order to remove himself as a tool for others. When he then becomes a window washer, it turns out to be a wonderful vacation, because he now has access to many more women than ever before, and he is shielded from Tereza's unhappiness by the mismatch of their daily schedules, since he is out all day and she works all evening. After two years, though, this life, too, becomes untenable, and Tereza persuades him to move to the countryside, to a collective farm. In the end she decides that he really does love her because he has given up everything for her, and he pretty much decides the same thing, though they differ in their estimations of what he has given up.

昆德拉作品的核心主题是，苏联共产主义统治下生活的持续虚假使得一切行为、情感和审美反应都变得空洞无物。托马斯职业生涯中最戏剧性的转折点发生在他因在布拉格之春期间写给报社编辑的一封信而失去外科医生生涯之时。这封信的内容被删减，歪曲了托马斯的观点，因此整封信都显得毫无意义，因为托马斯根本无法采取任何真诚的行动——所有相关人员都想利用他及其声望来实现并非出于他本意的目的。尽管他热爱外科手术，也深知自己能够救死扶伤，但他很快意识到，他唯一的选择就是放弃一切成功和特权，让自己不再成为他人的工具。后来他成了一名擦窗工，这反而成了一段美好的假期，因为他现在能接触到比以往任何时候都多的女人，而且由于两人作息时间错开——他白天外出，她晚上工作——他也因此免受特蕾莎的不快。然而两年后，这种生活也变得难以忍受，特蕾莎劝他搬到乡下，去集体农场。最终，她认定他是真心爱她的，因为他为她放弃了一切，而他也几乎得出了同样的结论，尽管他们对特蕾莎所放弃的一切的理解有所不同。

The salient characteristic of all four of these figures is that they never share their inner lives and that in fact it is impossible for them to do so. Tereza's grief is private, lived out mostly in dreams and in her relationship to the dog. Tomas can't communicate to anyone either the nature of his feeling for Tereza or what he thinks of his own epic womanizing. Franz and Sabina don't take the time or make the effort to connect—she seems to forget about him, and he internalizes an image of her that may or may not have anything to do with her. It is only by coexisting in Kundera's novel that they become available to anyone other than themselves, but while that may be enlightening for the reader and a good occasion for Kundera to make some points, it does the four of them no good.

这四个人物最显著的特点是他们从不分享彼此的内心世界，事实上，他们也根本无法做到这一点。特蕾莎的悲伤是私密的，主要体现在梦境和她与狗的关系中。托马斯既无法向任何人倾诉他对特蕾莎的感情，也无法反思自己风流成性的过往。弗朗茨和萨宾娜没有花时间或精力去建立联系——她似乎已经忘记了他，而他则在脑海中形成了一个关于她的形象，这个形象或许与她本人毫无关系。只有在昆德拉的小说中，他们才能彼此接触，而这或许能让读者有所启发，也为昆德拉提供了一个表达观点的契机，但对他们四个人来说却毫无益处。

Kundera's method is to remove the veil of verisimilitude from his characters—to treat them as characters and talk about them as characters rather than pretending that they are real people. He then defies his own assertions about who they are or are not by evoking their inner lives and external circumstances as if they were real, but as soon as those begin to solidify, he speaks up again (his intrusions don't seem intrusive because his tone is conversational and because he prepares the reader early on for his method) and reminds the reader that these are just characters. There is a certain degree of playfulness in this, but Kundera's style is so humorless that the playfulness doesn't come across very well.

昆德拉的写作手法在于揭开人物的“真实性”面纱——将他们视为人物，以人物的身份谈论他们，而不是假装他们是真实存在的人。然后，他通过描绘人物的内心世界和外部环境，仿佛它们是真实存在的，从而反驳自己对人物身份的断言。但当这些内心世界和外部环境开始逐渐成形时，他又会再次开口（他的介入并不显得突兀，因为他的语气如同对话，而且他很早就向读者交代了他的写作手法），提醒读者这些人物仅仅是虚构的人物。这种手法中蕴含着某种戏谑，但昆德拉的文风却缺乏幽默感，使得这种戏谑难以被读者充分理解。

The Unbearable Lightness of Being is openly a novel of ideas, but ideas, or themes, are the most time-sensitive element of any novel. Kundera's ideas about communism became outmoded and of current relevance to groups of people growing smaller by the year within five years of the novel's publication, when Eastern Europe threw out the Russians, and then the Russians threw out the Communists. As themes lose currency, the narrator's authoritative tone comes to seem egotistical rather than insightful, and seems to prevail at the expense of his characters rather than in support of them. It is possible that The Unbearable Lightness of Being will emerge from history like The Sleep-walkers , which has a large thematic investment in changes wrought in the human psyche by the First World War, but Kundera is much less interested in ideas of good and evil than Broch is, and it is the evils that the characters do, still shocking after more than eighty years, that furnish The Sleepwalkers with its engine. Kundera also, in this novel, contrasts with Arnost Lustig, another Czech writer, who focuses on the Holocaust rather than the Communist period. For Lustig, the Holocaust is an example of the nature of humanity, and therefore worthy of interest both as circumstance and as theme. For Kundera, the nature of humanity is influenced or even altered by communism. One of the problems with this idea is that when communism vanishes, Kundera's insights into humans under communism lose immediacy, too.

《生命中不能承受之轻》表面上是一部思想小说，但思想或主题却是任何小说中最具时效性的元素。昆德拉关于共产主义的思想在小说出版后的五年内便已过时，其现实意义也仅限于那些人数逐年减少的群体——东欧推翻了俄国人，随后俄国人又推翻了共产党。随着主题的衰落，叙述者权威的语气与其说是富有洞见，不如说是自负，而且似乎损害了人物的利益，而非支持他们。或许《生命中不能承受之轻》会像《梦游者》一样，在历史长河中留下深刻的印记。《梦游者》着重探讨了第一次世界大战对人类心灵造成的改变，但昆德拉对善恶观念的兴趣远不如布洛赫，而《梦游者》的动力恰恰来自于书中人物所犯下的罪恶——即便在八十多年后的今天，这些罪恶依然令人震惊。在这部小说中，昆德拉也与另一位捷克作家阿诺斯特·卢斯蒂格形成了对比。卢斯蒂格关注的是大屠杀而非共产主义时期。对卢斯蒂格而言，大屠杀是人性本质的一个例证，因此无论作为一种事件还是一个主题都值得关注。而昆德拉则认为，人性受到共产主义的影响，甚至被共产主义所改变。这种观点的问题之一在于，当共产主义消亡后，昆德拉对共产主义统治下人性的洞察也随之失去了现实意义。

87. Jamaica Kincaid. Annie John

87. 牙买加·金凯德。安妮·约翰

(NEW YORK: NEW AMERICAN LIBRARY, 1985), 148 PP.

（纽约：新美国图书馆，1985 年），148 页。

Annie John is a narrowly focused and intense portrayal of the inner life of an adolescent girl growing up in Antigua in the 1950s and 1960s . It begins in paradise. Annie is ten years old. She lives an orderly and affection-filled existence with her mother and father in a small house he has built and that her mother keeps perfectly in order. Annie adores her mother and loves being in her presence, helping her with her daily tasks, dressing like her, being made to feel cherished and protected by her mother's knowledge and special rigor. The next nine chapters detail Annie's simultaneous disillusionment and quest for independence as she becomes “a young lady” (a very suspect category), a star student in a rigidly British educational system, and her mother's loved and hated antagonist. The last chapter details Annie's vivid ambivalence about her departure from the island and from her parents. She is now taller and stronger than her father, disdainful of her mother, and in a fever to leave the island, but the reader knows through the very richness of the novel she has just read that Annie can never quite leave behind the sharp combination of pleasure and pain that has been the strongest feature of her passionate childhood.

《安妮·约翰》以细腻的笔触，刻画了20世纪五六十年代安提瓜岛上一位少女的内心世界。故事始于天堂般的场景。十岁的安妮与父母生活在父亲亲手建造的小房子里，过着井然有序、充满爱意的生活，母亲把房子打理得一尘不染。安妮崇拜母亲，喜欢待在母亲身边，帮她做家务，模仿母亲的穿着打扮，感受着母亲渊博的知识和严谨的管教让她倍感珍惜和呵护。接下来的九章细致描绘了安妮在成长为“淑女”（一个颇具争议的称谓）、成为英国僵化教育体系中的佼佼者以及成为母亲既爱又恨的矛盾体的过程中，既对现状感到幻灭，又渴望独立。最后一章则生动地展现了安妮对于离开岛屿和父母的复杂情感。她现在比父亲更高更壮，对母亲不屑一顾，一心想离开这座岛屿，但读者通过刚刚读过的这部小说的丰富内涵知道，安妮永远无法摆脱她充满激情的童年时期最强烈的特征——快乐与痛苦的强烈结合。

The spread of general education after the Second World War swept all sorts of potential novelists, male and female, into the net, and one of the special features of the generation of novelists born in the forties and fifties (Kincaid was born in 1949 ) is its range of national and ethnic diversity. Kincaid has said that she became a novelist almost by accident—after leaving Antigua to work as an au pair in New York City, she went to college for a few years and began meeting up with writers and writing herself. But her education in Antigua, based on English classic literature, was both a perfect education in literary taste and a perfect education in political ambiguity.

二战后普及教育的兴起，将形形色色的潜在小说家，无论男女，都纳入了文学创作的范畴。出生于四五十年代的那一代小说家（金凯德生于1949年）的一个显著特点，便是其民族和种族的多样性。金凯德曾说过，她成为小说家几乎是偶然——离开安提瓜岛前往纽约做互惠生后，她上了几年大学，开始结识作家并进行写作。但她在安提瓜岛接受的以英国经典文学为基础的教育，既培养了她对文学品味的深刻理解，也让她对政治的暧昧性有了更深刻的认识。

Kincaid's only apparent subject is the evolution of Annie's emotional state as she is growing up. Her style is precise, ironic, and evocative—Annie's world is full of people and places that intrigue her, draw her, or alienate her. She is full of appetites and hates to be crossed. The reader quickly has the sense that her mother's standards of doing everything according to plan and order have created in Annie a felt but not quite articulated aesthetic—different from her mother's but equally powerful—and that this difference in taste is added to the other, more common rivalries of mothers and adolescent daughters. Annie's maturation is objectively the most routine of processes, but it is so strongly felt by the child herself, and as narrator she brings such a wealth of inference to it, that it seems to be the paradigm of tragedy and epic. It does not overtly remind the reader of other deeply felt tragedies and epics as much as it resonates with similar vibrations while purporting to be nothing more than a very particular record of a very particular childhood.

金凯德唯一显而易见的主题是安妮成长过程中情感状态的演变。她的文风精准、讽刺且引人入胜——安妮的世界充满了吸引她、令她着迷或令她疏离的人和事。她欲望强烈，却又痛恨被人冒犯。读者很快就会意识到，她母亲凡事都按计划和秩序行事的标准，在安妮心中塑造了一种虽难以言表却又清晰可辨的审美观——与母亲的审美观不同，却同样强烈——而这种审美差异，又与母女之间常见的其他竞争关系交织在一起。安妮的成长过程客观上是最为寻常的，但孩子自身却感受得如此强烈，作为叙述者，她又赋予了这段成长历程如此丰富的内涵，以至于它似乎成为了悲剧和史诗的典范。它并没有直接让读者想起其他感人至深的悲剧和史诗，而是与类似的情感产生共鸣，同时又声称自己只不过是对一段非常特殊的童年经历的非常特殊的记录。

In later works Kincaid expresses more specifically political ideas and emotions about Antigua, class, race, illegitimacy, colonialism, AIDS, and other topics that some readers may find informative in the context of Annie John or of Kincaid as a writer who is also a representative figure of her time and place, but the genius of this particular novel is that whatever those ideas are, the author doesn't use them as any kind of explanatory reference in accounting for Annie's successive states of mind. Like most children, she exists outside of time. Her life is all of life and her world is the whole world. Her view of things recapitulates the way the world works and the way human psychology works, and subtly comments upon political and social ideas if the reader wants it to. Like The Trial, Annie John expands into larger meaning or doesn't, depending upon the reader's frame of reference. It is more likely to expand than not, but it also works on its apparent terms—a simple story of a particular girl in an out-of-the-way place.

在金凯德后来的作品中，她更具体地表达了关于安提瓜、阶级、种族、私生子、殖民主义、艾滋病以及其他一些主题的政治思想和情感。一些读者或许会觉得这些主题与《安妮·约翰》或金凯德作为她所处时代和地域的代表性作家的身份有关。然而，这部小说的精妙之处在于，无论这些思想是什么，作者都没有将它们作为解释安妮不断变化的心境的参照。像大多数孩子一样，她存在于时间之外。她的人生就是全部的人生，她的世界就是整个世界。她对事物的看法概括了世界的运行方式和人类心理的运作方式，如果读者愿意，她还会巧妙地对政治和社会思想进行评论。与《审判》一样，《安妮·约翰》的意义是否能够扩展，取决于读者的参照框架。它更有可能被扩展，但它本身也具有内在的意义——一个偏僻地方的女孩的简单故事。

Annie is a figure of both sympathy and empathy—even when her emotions seem inappropriate, she is so honest about them and she evokes them in such detail that the reader stays right with her. In some sense the flowering of the novel around the world in the seventies, eighties, and nineties stands as the fulfillment of the potential of the novel as a social document, if not as an artistic document (the potential of the novel as an artistic document is always equally fulfilled and unfulfilled). Of this flowering, Annie John is an especially excellent example. The superb precision of Kincaid's style makes it a paradigm of how to avoid lots of novelistic pitfalls. By staying very close to her protagonist, always moving the argument and the narrative forward, choosing concrete incidents and examples to portray, having a goal but not anticipating it, and knowing her subject in such depth that every episode seems to distill many other episodes that have to go unde-picted, Kincaid never allows the reader to either wish for something more or to wish for something less.

安妮是一个既令人同情又令人感同身受的人物——即使她的情绪有时显得不合时宜，她也坦诚得令人难以置信，而且她对这些情绪的刻画如此细致入微，以至于读者始终与她感同身受。从某种意义上说，七八九十年代小说在世界范围内的蓬勃发展，标志着小说作为社会文献的潜力得以充分发挥，即便它并非完全是一种艺术文献（小说作为艺术文献的潜力总是既有得到充分发挥，也有未能得到充分发挥）。在这一蓬勃发展的时期，《安妮·约翰》便是一个尤为杰出的例证。金凯德精湛的文风使其成为避免诸多小说陷阱的典范。她始终与主人公保持紧密的联系，不断推动论证和叙事向前发展，选择具体的事件和例证进行描绘，设定目标却不预先设定，并且对笔下人物有着深刻的了解，以至于每一个情节似乎都浓缩了许多其他未曾描绘的情节。金凯德的这种创作方式，既不让读者感到意犹未尽，也不让读者感到遗憾。

# ↩

88. J. M. Coetzee. Foe

88. J. M. 库切。《敌人》

(NEW YORK: PENGUIN, 1986), 157 PP.

（纽约：企鹅出版社，1986 年），157 页。

J. M. Coetzee is a winner of the Nobel Prize, and best known for his novel Disgrace , which was published in 1999 and won the Booker Prize. A novel of his that I especially like is Waiting for the Barbarians , which evocatively explores the question of how a man of good will can negotiate daily life in a tyrannical world, portrayed in the novel as hypothetical, but clearly based on anticolonialist ideas growing out of Coetzee's life in his native South Africa. Even though Foe is not one of his more famous novels, I was drawn to it through my admiration for Defoe, and my fascination with his life, which Coetzee seems to share. Like Wide Sargasso Sea, Foe is the meditation of a modern author upon the power of a classic author, in this case Daniel Defoe, and upon the history and tragedy of British colonialism. The premise is that a woman, Susan Barton, has come to London with a story of being cast away on a tropical island. She hopes to persuade the famous Daniel Defoe to write her tale and make her fortune, but “Mr. Foe,” as she calls him, has his own troubles—he has fled from his house in an effort to escape his creditors. Much of the novel details her attempts to communicate with him by letter, explaining her situation and making suggestions about the writing she hopes he is doing. She is accompanied by a wordless Friday, whose exact relationship to Cruso (the original of Robinson Crusoe) she doesn't have any means to understand, because Friday has either lost or never had the power of speech—Cruso has told Susan that slavers cut his tongue out, but in fact Susan doesn't know whether this is the case.

J·M·库切是诺贝尔文学奖得主，他最著名的作品是1999年出版并荣获布克奖的小说《耻辱》。我尤其喜欢他的另一部小说《等待野蛮人》，这部小说生动地探讨了一个善良的人如何在暴政世界中生存下去的问题。小说中的暴政世界是虚构的，但显然源于库切在故乡南非的生活经历，并由此萌生了反殖民主义思想。尽管《福》并非他最知名的作品，但我出于对笛福的敬仰和对他生平的着迷（库切似乎也抱有同样的感受），而被这部小说所吸引。与《藻海无边》一样，《福》是一位现代作家对经典作家（在本例中是丹尼尔·笛福）的力量以及英国殖民主义的历史和悲剧的沉思。故事的开端是，一位名叫苏珊·巴顿的女子来到伦敦，讲述自己被困在热带岛屿上的经历。她希望说服著名作家丹尼尔·笛福将她的故事写成小说，从而发家致富。然而，她口中的“笛福先生”却身陷困境——他为了躲避债主而逃离了住所。小说的大部分篇幅都描写了她试图通过书信与笛福沟通，解释自己的处境，并就她希望笛福创作的内容提出建议。陪伴她的是一个不会说话的星期五，苏珊无法得知星期五与鲁滨逊·克鲁索（鲁滨逊·克鲁索的原型）之间的确切关系，因为星期五要么失去了说话的能力，要么从未拥有过说话的能力——鲁滨逊曾告诉苏珊，奴隶贩子割掉了他的舌头，但苏珊并不知道这是否属实。

Foe refers nearly as much to Roxana and several of Defoe's other works as to Robinson Crusoe —for example, Susan is pursued by a mysterious girl who claims to be her lost daughter, just as Roxana is pursued by the daughter she abandoned after the departure of her profligate husband. What Coetzee seems to be getting at is the disorder of a writer's themes and subjects before he orders them into separate books. Whereas life is a mishmash of events, books are ordered and sequenced; whereas life is rather dull, books are exciting—one of Susan's observations is that Cruso's real life on the island contained neither cannibals nor introspection. Mr. Foe will have to make up something in order to give the island any interest for a reader.

福伊在《鲁滨逊漂流记》中引用罗克珊娜和笛福的其他几部作品的次数几乎与引用《鲁滨逊漂流记》的次数一样多——例如，苏珊被一个自称是她失散女儿的神秘女孩纠缠，正如罗克珊娜在她挥霍无度的丈夫离开后被她遗弃的女儿纠缠一样。库切似乎想要表达的是，作家在将它们整理成书之前，其主题和题材往往杂乱无章。生活是一团乱麻，而书籍则是有序排列的；生活平淡乏味，而书籍引人入胜——苏珊观察到，鲁滨逊在岛上的真实生活既没有食人族，也没有内省。福伊先生必须编造一些东西，才能让读者对这座岛屿产生兴趣。

Foe has several gamelike features—Defoe's disappearance, Susan's pursuit of him, the basic proposition that among the three characters, they are producing a work that is to be entertaining as well as enlightening—but the tone of the novel is oppressive. Instead of discovering something or achieving something or, at least, coming to a degree of self-knowledge, Susan grows more confused as she becomes less and less able to clearly remember her own history (part of Coetzee's theme about the costs of novel-writing). As she writes about herself and Friday to Mr. Foe, she becomes more and more uncertain, especially about who Friday is and what his capacities are: Does he have language and feelings? Does he understand what she is saying to him? What should she do with him? (At one point she is about to send him away on an English ship when she realizes that the captain is actually planning to sell him into slavery.) Friday's wordless suffering also serves to root the novel (and, by extension, all novels) in pain.

《福先生》具备一些游戏般的元素——笛福的失踪、苏珊对他的追寻，以及三个人物共同创作一部既要娱乐又要启迪人心的作品这一基本前提——但小说的基调却令人压抑。苏珊非但没有有所发现或有所成就，甚至没有达到某种程度的自我认知，反而随着她越来越难以清晰地回忆起自己的过往而愈发困惑（这正是库切关于小说创作代价的主题之一）。当她写信给福先生，讲述自己和弗莱迪的故事时，她变得越来越不确定，尤其是关于弗莱迪的身份和能力：他有语言和情感吗？他能理解她对他说的话吗？她该如何处置他？（有一次，她正要把他送上一艘英国船，却发现船长实际上是打算把他卖为奴隶。）弗莱迪无声的痛苦也使整部小说（以及所有小说）深深扎根于痛苦之中。

Coetzee's points are all thematic—Susan's adventures are not fleshed out; very little action and process are supplied to go along with the dissipation of certainty and meaning. Coetzee is South African, and what he really wants to emphasize is the central mystery of Friday, who could be anything and could mean anything. The novel is short because Coetzee wants to make a certain point—that the usual novel-istic tricks of the trade, such as detailing the setting (London in the early eighteenth century), fleshing out the characters, and filling in the gaps of the story are exactly the parts of novel-writing that, according to Foe , are dishonest and suspect. Since Coetzee does not have a playful sensibility and has written other novels about the moral compromises of writing novels, such as The Master of Petersburg and Elizabeth Costello , he is not the sort of novelist to simultaneously perform the tricks and send them up.

库切的观点都围绕着主题展开——苏珊的冒险经历并未得到充分展开；几乎没有提供任何情节和过程来配合确定性和意义的消散。库切是南非人，他真正想要强调的是弗莱迪这个核心谜团，她可以是任何人，也可以代表任何人。这部小说篇幅很短，因为库切想要表达一个观点——小说写作中常见的技巧，例如详细描述背景（十八世纪初的伦敦）、塑造人物形象、填补故事空白，恰恰是福伊认为小说写作中不诚实且可疑的部分。由于库切缺乏戏谑的特质，而且他之前也写过其他探讨小说写作道德妥协的作品，例如《彼得堡的大师》和《伊丽莎白·科斯特洛》，所以他并非那种既会运用这些技巧又会讽刺它们的作家。

In the latter third of the twentieth century, European literature itself came to seem coercive to some readers, especially for promoting the white male Christian supremacy that even when not its subject has been its assumption. The women's movement proposed the principle that the personal is political—that is, all personal choices have their source in power relationships (a principle that was gleaned from the nature of the novel as well as 250 years of novels about choices made by and about women). This principle became a useful lens for looking at how all power relationships work—always a subject that the novel is interested in—but it doesn't always make for readable and compelling novels, especially if the novelist is preoccupied with the problem of subjectivity. Susan Barton, for example, spends very little time depicting her activities around London and a lot of time depicting her doubts and fears. Her thoughts go round and round about the same moral concerns without resolving them, at least in part because the author hasn't constructed a plot that organizes and carries forward their resolution. The lesson is that characters in a novel must keep on doing and interacting or the novel will sink under the double weight of its inherent subjectivity combined with the theme of subjectivity. Infinitely nesting thoughts eventually get tedious, even in only 157 pages. If we look at Roxana or Defoe's other novels that play with subjectivity, we see that in them survival comes first and is of intense interest. Moral considerations follow, and when they sometimes conflict with the means of survival, that is fascinating, too. Coetzee can't reproduce Defoe's characteristic practical, clear, and generous tone or his illusion of real concrete life, so his accusation against Defoe—that he exploited and misrepresented the “real” subjects of his work—falls flat. Defoe was a novelist; he exercised a rich imagination and wrote novels that were compelling to read. That's all, in the end, that the reader holds him responsible for.

在二十世纪后三分之一的时间里，欧洲文学本身对一些读者而言开始显得具有强制性，尤其因为它宣扬了白人男性基督教至上主义——即便并非其主题，这种至上主义也一直是其默认的前提。女权运动提出了“个人即政治”的原则——也就是说，所有个人选择都源于权力关系（这一原则既源于小说的本质，也源于两百五十年来关于女性选择或与女性相关的各种小说）。这一原则成为审视所有权力关系运作方式的有效视角——而权力关系始终是小说关注的主题——但它并非总能创作出引人入胜、通俗易懂的小说，尤其当小说家过于关注主观性问题时。例如，苏珊·巴顿很少描写她在伦敦的活动，却花费大量笔墨描绘她的疑虑和恐惧。她的思绪在同样的道德困境中反复徘徊，却始终无法得到解决，这至少部分是因为作者没有构建一个能够组织并推进这些问题解决的情节。这部小说告诉我们，人物必须不断地行动和互动，否则小说就会因其固有的主观性和主观性主题的双重重压而变得臃肿不堪。即使只有157页，层层嵌套的思绪最终也会令人感到乏味。如果我们看看《罗克珊娜》或笛福其他探讨主观性的长篇小说，就会发现，在这些作品中，生存才是首要的，也是最引人入胜的主题。道德考量随后而来，而当它们有时与生存手段发生冲突时，也同样引人入胜。库切无法重现笛福特有的务实、清晰而慷慨的笔调，也无法复制他对真实具体生活的描绘，因此他对笛福的指责——即笛福剥削和歪曲了其作品中的“真实”主题——显得苍白无力。笛福是一位小说家；他拥有丰富的想象力，创作了引人入胜的小说。归根结底，读者对他的评价也就仅限于此了。

89. Toni Morrison. Beloved

89. 托妮·莫里森。《宠儿》

(NEW YORK: NEW AMERICAN LIBRARY, PLUME, 1987), 275 PP.

（纽约：新美国图书馆，PLUME，1987 年），275 页。

It is clear from Morrison's dedication (“Sixty Million and more”) that she intends to embrace the social-document potential of the novel, as, indeed, any novel that treats injustice and its effects must do. This acceptance of the novel's power to shape opinion actually frees her to do anything she wants artistically—novelists who are careful to avoid social questions tend to limit their subjects to personal relationships or aesthetic questions that seem, on the surface, to be perennial, though in fact the novelist is usually simply avoiding the social and economic implications of what he or she is saying. For Morrison and most other writers of the 1980s , though, everything about the novel, from plot to style to characterization, that had once seemed fairly neutral was seen to be fraught with political implications. Like Tolstoy, who also embraced the novel as a social document and openly used the novel to express his opinions, Morrison had a theory—a vision of slavery and black/white relations in America—that was in some ways old hat, but still inflammatory and unresolved. The task was to remake the old story in a compelling way, and also to separate her own telling from that of earlier writers, especially Harriet Beecher Stowe and possibly Harper Lee as well as several male writers.

从莫里森的献词（“六千万及以上”）中可以清楚地看出，她打算拥抱小说的社会文献潜力，事实上，任何探讨不公正及其影响的小说都必须如此。这种对小说塑造舆论力量的认可，实际上解放了她，让她可以随心所欲地进行艺术创作——那些小心翼翼回避社会问题的作家往往将主题局限于人际关系或美学问题，这些问题表面上看似永恒不变，但实际上，作家通常只是在回避其作品的社会和经济内涵。然而，对于莫里森和20世纪80年代的大多数作家来说，小说的一切，从情节到风格再到人物塑造，曾经看似相当中立的元素，都被视为充满了政治意味。就像托尔斯泰一样，莫里森也把小说视为社会文献，并公开地用小说来表达自己的观点。莫里森也有一套理论——关于美国奴隶制和黑白关系的见解——这套理论在某些方面已经过时，但仍然具有煽动性，并且尚未得到解决。任务是以一种引人入胜的方式重述这个古老的故事，同时也要将自己的叙述与早期作家，特别是哈里特·比彻·斯托，以及可能还有哈珀·李和几位男性作家的叙述区分开来。

Beloved is not as easy to read as, say, To Kill a Mockingbird , but it is easy to get used to, and once the reader begins to distinguish among the elements, they fall into place quite clearly. As it opens, Sethe, in her late thirties, is living with her eighteen-year-old daughter, Denver, in a house that the neighbors avoid because it is haunted. The time is the early 1870s , right after the first wrenching dislocations of the Civil War and its aftermath. Sethe and Denver live in an uneasy truce with the ghost until the arrival of Paul D, one of Sethe's fellow slaves on her former plantation in Kentucky. Paul exorcises the ghost, but then a mysterious female stranger shows up. She is twenty years old and strangely unmarked—she has no lines in her palms, for example, and her feet and clothing show no signs of hard traveling. She calls herself “Beloved,” and Sethe and Denver are happy to take her in.

《宠儿》读起来不像《杀死一只知更鸟》那样轻松，但很容易上手。一旦读者开始区分各个元素，它们便会清晰地呈现出来。故事开篇，三十多岁的塞丝和她十八岁的女儿丹佛住在一栋邻居们避之不及的房子里，因为据说这里闹鬼。时间是19世纪70年代初，正值美国内战及其后续影响带来的第一次剧烈动荡之后。塞丝和丹佛与鬼魂勉强维持着一种不安的和平，直到保罗·D的到来。保罗是塞丝在肯塔基州种植园的奴隶同伴。保罗驱除了鬼魂，但随后一位神秘的陌生女子出现。她二十岁，身上没有任何奇怪的痕迹——例如，她的手掌上没有皱纹，她的脚和衣服也看不出长途跋涉的痕迹。她自称“宠儿”，塞丝和丹佛欣然收留了她。

Sethe, Denver, Paul D, and every other character in the novel live simultaneously in their present and in their history—the chapters of the novel alternate between the two stories—that of the growing contest between Sethe and Beloved and that of Sethe's life on the plantation, her escape, and the traumatic events that followed her crossing of the Ohio River and her appearance at the home of her mother-in-law, Baby Suggs. A crucial, revealing, and in some ways impossible to assimilate event takes place about halfway through the text—Sethe's former owner shows up with some officers to recapture the escapees, and Sethe attempts to kill her children. The two boys and the newborn survive, but she succeeds in slitting the throat of the two-year-old.

小说中的塞丝、丹佛、保罗·D以及所有其他人物都同时生活在当下和过去——小说的章节在两条故事线之间交替展开：一条是塞丝和贝拉维德之间日益激烈的争斗，另一条是塞丝在种植园的生活、她的逃亡，以及她渡过俄亥俄河后出现在婆婆贝比·萨格斯家后所经历的种种创伤。一个至关重要、发人深省，且在某种程度上难以理解的事件发生在小说中段——塞丝的前主人带着一些警官前来抓捕逃亡者，塞丝试图杀死自己的孩子。两个男孩和一个新生儿幸存了下来，但她成功地割断了两岁孩子的喉咙。

Everyone is astonished and appalled by this turn of events (which Morrison discovered in an old newspaper account of the period). Baby Suggs is never the same again; Sethe is shunned by her fellow citizens; Denver grows up isolated and suspicious. Morrison is careful, though, to indicate that while this is a pivotal event in the lives of everyone, it is not, in spite of its shock value, either the climax, or the worst thing to have happened to Sethe and her loved ones. The climax of the historical narrative is, in fact, the night of the escape, when several of the escapees were hanged and mutilated, while the present-time narrative builds to Denver's decision to separate herself from what is apparently a life-and-death struggle between Sethe and Beloved, and to go out and find work and friends that will help her save herself.

所有人都对事态的转变感到震惊和恐惧（莫里森在一份当时的旧报纸报道中发现了这一点）。贝比·萨格斯从此一蹶不振；塞丝被同胞们疏远；丹佛在孤独和多疑的环境中长大。然而，莫里森谨慎地指出，尽管这起事件对每个人来说都是人生中的一个转折点，但即便它令人震惊，也并非故事的高潮，或者说并非塞丝和她所爱之人遭遇的最糟糕的事情。事实上，历史叙事的高潮是逃亡之夜，当时几名逃亡者被绞死并遭受酷刑；而现代叙事则着重描写丹佛决定脱离塞丝和贝拉维德之间看似生死攸关的斗争，外出寻找工作和朋友，以帮助她自救。

One of the reasons Beloved is a great novel is that it is equally full of sensations and of meaning. Morrison knows exactly what she wants to do and how to do it, and she exploits every aspect of her subject. The characters are complex. Both stories are dramatic but in contrasting ways, and the past and the present constantly modify each other. Neither half of the novel suffers by contrast to the other. Especially worth noting is Morrison's style, which is graphic, evocative, and unwhite without veering toward dialect (which can strike the reader as unintentionally humorous if the writer isn't careful). Even though Morrison rejects realism, using a heightened diction and a lyrical narrative method returning again and again to particular images and events and adding to them so they are more and more fully described, the reader never doubts the reality of what Morrison reports. Just as Sethe recognizes Beloved toward the end of the novel and knows at once that she has known all along who she is, the reader is shocked at the sufferings of the black characters and the brutality of the whites, but knows at once that every torture and cruelty is not merely plausible but also representative of many other horrors that go unmentioned in the novel and have gone unmentioned in American history. Harriet Beecher Stowe was accused in her time of exaggerating the cruelties in Uncle Tom's Cabin , and she replied that in fact she whitewashed events to render them publishable. Morrison is her heir, in the sense that she dares to discuss and publish more (though certainly not all) of the truth.

《宠儿》之所以伟大，原因之一在于它既饱含感官体验，又蕴含深刻意义。莫里森清楚地知道自己想要表达什么，以及如何表达，她充分利用了题材的方方面面。人物形象复杂。两条故事线都充满戏剧性，但风格迥异，过去与现在不断相互影响。小说的两部分并不因对比而逊色。尤其值得一提的是莫里森的文风，它生动形象、引人入胜，且不落俗套，却又不流于方言（如果作者不加注意，方言可能会让读者觉得滑稽可笑）。尽管莫里森摒弃了现实主义，运用华丽的辞藻和抒情的叙事手法，反复描绘特定的意象和事件，并加以补充，使其愈加丰满，但读者却从未怀疑过莫里森所叙述内容的真实性。正如小说结尾处塞丝认出贝拉维德，并立刻明白自己一直以来都知道她是谁一样，读者也会对黑人角色的苦难和白人的残暴感到震惊，但同时也会立刻意识到，每一种酷刑和残忍不仅合情合理，而且也代表着小说中未提及、在美国历史上也鲜为人知的诸多其他恐怖事件。哈里特·比彻·斯托在世时曾被指责夸大《汤姆叔叔的小屋》中的残酷情节，她则回应说，事实上，她为了让作品能够出版而粉饰了某些事件。莫里森可以说是她的继承人，因为她敢于探讨并发表更多（当然并非全部）真相。

Beloved has held up quite well over the years in spite of the fact that Morrison was as much a product of her time as any other novelist. The novel seems, for example, more current and compelling than The Unbearable Lightness of Being. One reason for this is, of course, that racist attitudes in the United States change very slowly, but another is that Morrison is far more subtle in her exploration of her ideas than Kundera is. Morrison depicts every incident with such concrete expressiveness that the reader takes it in willingly as truth. She is also entirely matter-of-fact in her assertions—equally so about the presence and identity of the ghost as about the character flaws of whites. No aspect of the novel is presented as speculation, and so to read on, the reader suspends disbelief. In this, Beloved works something like The Trial or “The Metamorphosis.” With a tale, the reader is asked to suspend disbelief completely and at once. If she can't do it, she won't read on; if she does do it, she is in the mood to accept everything the author asserts as true. The bonus of the tale form, for Morrison, is that she is also tapping into a vital store of black folklore that feeds her style as well as her story.

尽管莫里森和其他小说家一样，深受时代局限，但《宠儿》多年来依然经久不衰。例如，这部小说似乎比《生命中不能承受之轻》更具现实意义和吸引力。原因之一当然是美国种族主义态度的转变非常缓慢，但另一个原因是莫里森在探讨其思想时比昆德拉更加微妙。莫里森以如此具体生动的笔触描绘每一个事件，让读者心甘情愿地将其视为事实。她对所有事件的描述也完全基于事实——无论是关于鬼魂的存在和身份，还是关于白人的性格缺陷，都同样如此。小说中的任何情节都没有被当作推测来呈现，因此，读者需要暂时放下怀疑才能继续阅读。在这方面，《宠儿》的叙事手法类似于《审判》或《变形记》。在阅读故事时，读者被要求立即完全放下怀疑。如果读者无法做到这一点，他们就不会继续读下去。如果她真的这么做了，她会欣然接受作者所断言的一切。对莫里森而言，故事形式的妙处在于，她还能汲取丰富的黑人民间传说，这些传说不仅丰富了她的故事，也塑造了她的文风。

Beloved is one of the few American novels that take every natural element of the novel form and exploit it thoroughly, but in balance with all the other elements. The result is that it is dense but not long, dramatic but not melodramatic, particular and universal, shocking but reassuring, new but at the same time closely connected to the tradition of the novel, and likely to mold or change a reader's sense of the world.

《宠儿》是少数几部将小说形式的每一个自然元素都充分运用并加以发挥的美国小说之一，同时又与其他所有元素保持着平衡。其结果是，它内容丰富而不冗长，充满戏剧性而不矫揉造作，既具有特殊性又具有普世性，既令人震惊又令人安心，既新颖独特又与小说传统紧密相连，并且很可能塑造或改变读者对世界的认知。

90. A. S. Byatt Possessior

90. A. S. 拜厄特 占有者

(NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, VINTAGE, 1990), 545 PP.

（纽约：兰登书屋，Vintage，1990 年），545 页。

Possession begins with the theft of a document from the London Library. A young researcher in the 1980s happens across the draft of a letter written in the 1850s by a Victorian poet whose relationships and activities had been thought to be perfectly understood and accounted for. Investigation reveals the poet's great secret—a love affair with a rather obscure poetess. Through straight narration, poems, and fictional documents such as diaries and letters, Byatt develops the parallel stories of the secret affair, the scholarly detective story, and the growing attachment between the researcher who found the document and a famous scholar who is a specialist in the life and works of the poetess.

故事始于伦敦图书馆的一起文件失窃案。一位年轻的研究员在20世纪80年代偶然发现了一份维多利亚时代诗人于19世纪50年代写下的信件草稿。这位诗人的人际关系和生活一直被认为已被完全了解和掌握。调查揭开了这位诗人的惊天秘密——他与一位名不见经传的女诗人之间的一段恋情。拜厄特运用直白的叙述、诗歌以及日记、信件等虚构文献，巧妙地展开了三条平行叙事线：一条是秘密恋情，一条是学术侦探的探案故事，还有一条是发现这份文件的研究员与一位研究这位女诗人生平和作品的著名学者之间日益加深的情感纠葛。

Possession is a remarkably rich novel, so painstakingly constructed and so multivoiced that it is hard to believe it is the work of a single novelist. It is a true example of astonishing inventiveness but also astonishing insight, thought, and research. George Eliot appears early on—evoked as a shade in the stacks of the London Library—and surely she is Byatt's model and muse. Byatt's prose has a deliberate pace and imaginative density that is reminiscent of Middlemarch.

《占有》是一部极其丰富的长篇小说，其结构精巧，叙事多线交织，令人难以置信出自一人之手。它不仅展现了惊人的创造力，更体现了非凡的洞察力、思考和研究。乔治·艾略特在小说开篇便出现——以伦敦图书馆书架间幽灵的形象出现——她无疑是拜厄特的创作原型和灵感缪斯。拜厄特的散文节奏沉稳，想象力丰富，令人想起《米德尔马契》。

The nonscholarly reader, though, may wonder at first whether she cares about this subject. Victorian poetry, the works of Tennyson and Arnold, don't have much appeal for the modern audience, at least in comparison with the Romantics and the moderns. Possession may seem so erudite as to be inaccessible, but Byatt is deft with her modern and her Victorian characters. Although Roland and Maud (the modern scholars) are fairly standard, virtuous, and well disposed, their supporting characters are eccentric and appealing—Roland's testy girlfriend; Maud's overbearing American lover; and Roland's employer, who is named “Blackadder.” And the Victorian characters seem authentically Victorian—Ash, the poet; Christabel LaMotte, the poetess; and Blanche Glover, Christabel's artist-lover. One theme that interests Byatt is the differences in the ways the modern era and the Victorian era experience passion. Although the novel implies that there is something deeper and bolder in the Victorian manner, it is the modern characters who achieve the happy ending, with satisfying connections all around and the ever-pleasant infusion of plenty of money.

然而，非学术读者起初可能会怀疑自己是否对这个主题感兴趣。维多利亚时代的诗歌，如丁尼生和阿诺德的作品，对现代读者来说吸引力不大，至少与浪漫主义和现代诗歌相比是如此。《占有》一书或许显得过于深奥，难以理解，但拜厄特对现代人物和维多利亚时代人物的刻画却十分巧妙。尽管罗兰和莫德（现代学者）相当典型、正直善良，但他们的配角却个性鲜明、引人入胜——罗兰脾气暴躁的女友；莫德专横跋扈的美国情人；以及罗兰的老板，名叫“黑爵士”。而维多利亚时代的人物则显得真实可信——诗人阿什；女诗人克里斯特贝尔·拉莫特；以及克里斯特贝尔的艺术家情人布兰奇·格洛弗。拜厄特感兴趣的一个主题是现代和维多利亚时代体验激情的方式的差异。虽然小说暗示维多利亚时代的方式蕴含着更深层次、更大胆的东西，但最终获得幸福结局的却是现代人物，他们拥有令人满意的关系，并且不断获得丰厚的金钱。

I mention Byatt's use of names because she is openly cluing the reader in to her use of the tradition of the romance and the epic. Ash is a poet in the epic tradition—his major work (of which Byatt supplies a lengthy selection) is titled “Ragnark.” He also writes about science and history, all male subjects. The ash tree, of course, is an ancient representation of male potency and strength. “Christabel” is a reference to Coleridge's famous poem of the same name, and “LaMotte” refers to medieval fortifications (Christabel is not easily won). Roland, of course, is the subject of the French chanson de geste The Song of Roland. “Maud” refers to a Tennyson poem. Through her poets and scholars, Byatt manages to introduce a great deal of European literary history. Possession is not weighted down by it—it is more like music in the air. As the interlocking stories proceed, the reader begins to sense a grander, more intriguing, and livelier atmosphere than she has sensed in other novels. With its wealth of references, Possession successfully throws off the customary novel-burden of linearity and succeeds in expanding in a new way. The names, the references to other authors, the layered narratives, the poems, diaries, and letters begin to reside together in the reader's mind—not, in the traditional way, creating a self-contained world, but in a new way setting up the resonances of many imaginative worlds coexisting together.

我之所以提及拜厄特对人名的运用，是因为她毫不掩饰地向读者暗示她对浪漫史诗传统的借鉴。阿什是一位史诗诗人——他的主要作品（拜厄特提供了其中的长篇选段）名为《诸神的黄昏》。他还创作关于科学和历史的作品，这些都是男性主题。当然，梣树是男性力量和能力的古老象征。“克里斯特贝尔”指的是柯勒律治的同名名诗，“拉莫特”指的是中世纪的防御工事（克里斯特贝尔并非轻易就能攻克）。罗兰自然是法国英雄史诗《罗兰之歌》的主人公。“莫德”指的是丁尼生的一首诗。通过这些诗人学者，拜厄特巧妙地引入了大量的欧洲文学史。占有并没有因此而显得沉重——它更像是空气中飘荡的音乐。随着环环相扣的故事展开，读者开始感受到一种比其他小说更为宏大、引人入胜、生动鲜活的氛围。凭借丰富的典故，《占有》成功摆脱了传统小说线性叙事的束缚，并以一种全新的方式拓展了故事的边界。书中出现的人名、对其他作者的引用、层层叠叠的叙事、诗歌、日记和信件，这些元素开始在读者的脑海中交织融合——并非以传统的方式构建一个自成一体的世界，而是以一种全新的方式，展现出众多想象世界并存的共鸣。

Possession is a novel of ideas, and illustrates some of the joys and the pitfalls of using the novel to put ideas across. Byatt tries to construct the novel as an example of her ideas, while for the most part avoiding overt comment upon them. She wants the reader to feel the ideas as they shape the characters’ lives and to accept the rightness of how they feel. Possession has held up fairly well because Byatt's ideas are expressed through traditional forms and styles—her choice is not to create new forms and styles but to add layer upon layer of readily understandable forms and styles (and if a reader chooses not to stick with the lengthy poems, she can still enjoy the prose). If and when Byatt's ideas lose their currency, the novel can survive as a story without them. Even though the central modern relationship seems a bit thin and tentative, and the villains are a bit too villainous, the whole is so various and full that everything works well enough as a story and marvelously as a display of literary virtuosity.

《占有》是一部思想小说，它展现了运用小说这种形式来传达思想的乐趣与陷阱。拜厄特试图将小说构建成她思想的例证，同时又尽量避免对这些思想进行直接的评论。她希望读者能够感受到这些思想如何塑造人物的生活，并接受他们感受的合理性。《占有》之所以经久不衰，是因为拜厄特的思想是通过传统的文体和风格来表达的——她没有选择创造新的形式和风格，而是层层叠加易于理解的形式和风格（即使读者不想阅读冗长的诗歌，仍然可以欣赏散文部分）。即便拜厄特的思想日渐式微，这部小说本身的故事依然可以成立。尽管小说中核心的现代关系显得有些单薄和摇摆不定，反派角色也略显邪恶，但整体而言，这部小说丰富多彩、包罗万象，既能构成一个完整的故事，又能精彩地展现文学技巧。

91. Nicholson Baker. Vox

91. 尼科尔森·贝克。Vox

(NEW YORK: RANDOM HOUSE, 1992), 165 PP.

（纽约：兰登书屋，1992 年），165 页。

Vox seemed like a shocker when it came out—the premise of the novel is that a man and a woman are having a transcontinental bout of anonymous phone sex, through a calling service. Although their purpose is to arouse each other, their conversation repeatedly digresses, and although they do arouse each other periodically, the more conversational sections are meant to be compelling as well, luring the reader into empathizing and sympathizing with them as characters, and into possibly even having a few vicarious wishes that two people as compatible as these (it is a costly phone call, after all) might overcome distance and anonymity and get together happily ever after.

《Vox》出版时着实令人震惊——小说的设定是，一对男女通过电话服务进行跨洲匿名电话性爱。虽然他们的目的是互相挑逗，但他们的对话却不断跑题；尽管他们偶尔也会互相挑逗，但那些对话部分同样引人入胜，旨在引导读者对书中人物产生共鸣和同情，甚至可能让读者产生一些间接的愿望：希望像他们这样契合的两个人（毕竟，这是一通昂贵的电话）能够克服距离和匿名，最终幸福地在一起。

Baker is trickier than that, though, and far more austere. Whatever the reader takes away from Vox is the reader's responsibility. There is no reassuring frame saying what happened before or after the events of the novel, and absolutely no indication of who these two people are outside of their phone call, or of whether they are as they present themselves. The phone call itself may well be a work of collaborative fiction in which both assume personae and false presentations of self. Vox is a tour de force of a kind—a genuinely intriguing and unique premise that, in my opinion, had to be executed exactly as Baker executes it in order to be interesting at all.

然而，贝克的笔法远比这复杂，也更加冷峻。读者从《Vox》中能领悟到什么，完全取决于读者自身。小说中没有任何令人安心的框架交代事件发生之前或之后的情况，也完全没有暗示这两个人在电话之外的真实身份，或者他们是否如他们所展现的那样。这段电话本身很可能就是两人合作虚构的作品，他们各自扮演着不同的角色，并伪装出真实的自我。《Vox》堪称一部杰作——一个真正引人入胜且独一无二的前提，在我看来，只有贝克以如此精准的方式呈现，才能使其如此精彩。

The originality of Baker's work lies in its meditative nature. My favorite of his novels is A Box of Matches , in which a man comes down every morning and lights a fire. The novel records his thoughts as he lights the fires and day by day uses up his box of matches. He ruminates on all sorts of things, but there is a cozy quality to the situation— the family is asleep, he is inside the house, it is winter, and so forth. But Baker brings his meditative nature to all kinds of subjects, and it transforms them. When Vox was published, it was considered especially bold, but the story, such as it is, progresses too idly and too routinely to be pornographic and thereby comments on the artificially lurid quality of pornography. No matter what is happening in Vox , the reader has the underlying sense that the author is a decent, normal person, just the sort of person who could ponder a box of matches or a punctuation mark (The Fermata) at length and in an intriguing way.

贝克作品的独创性在于其沉思的特质。我最喜欢的他的小说是《一盒火柴》，小说中一个男人每天早晨下楼生火。小说记录了他生火时以及日复一日用完一盒火柴时的所思所想。他沉思着各种各样的事情，但场景却有一种温馨的氛围——家人都已入睡，他待在屋里，正值寒冬，等等。贝克将这种沉思的特质运用到各种主题中，并赋予它们新的生命。《Vox》出版时被认为尤其大胆，但就其故事而言，其发展过于闲散和循规蹈矩，以至于无法称之为色情作品，反而讽刺了色情作品人为的耸人听闻。无论《Vox》中发生了什么，读者都能感受到作者是一位正直、正常的人，正是那种能够长时间、以一种引人入胜的方式思考一盒火柴或一个标点符号（例如《延音记》）的人。

In 2004 , Baker published a much more controversial novel even than Vox , titled Checkpoint: A Novel , in which two men discuss the assassination of George W. Bush. One of the men talks through various schemes and the other tries (apparently successfully) to dissuade him from acting out his fantasy. Checkpoint was denounced in the New York Times Book Review as a betrayal of liberalism, and it was seen in other publications as a joke—after all, there is no indication that the would-be assassin in the novel can even begin to carry out his notion. Both Vox and Checkpoint , I think, are daring moves in the novel-as-a-game genre of experimental fiction. What differentiates them from racy popular bodice-rippers and political thrillers that have similar themes is Baker's refusal to situate them in a recognizable genre and give them the trappings of commerce, such as suspenseful plots. The reader is asked not to go along for an exciting ride but to meditate along with Baker upon ideas of phone sex, politics, and assassination. He also refuses to add flourishes of obfuscatory literary style (la Joyce) that serve to deflect all but a select audience. Baker's style is always plain and clear. It is also sometimes tedious and even dreary— intentionally so, since fidelity to the conversation of average people sometimes requires that they seem tedious and dreary in order to seem average. Baker also never communicates his own feelings about phone sex and assassination to the reader, as political thrillers and bodice-rippers do—he presents the conversations and the ideas. The reader meditates upon them. The author seems to be absent, or, if not absent, then morally neutral.

2004年，贝克出版了一部比《Vox》更具争议的小说，名为《检查站：一部小说》（Checkpoint: A Novel）。小说中，两个男人讨论刺杀乔治·W·布什的计划。其中一人滔滔不绝地讲述各种方案，而另一人则试图（显然成功地）劝阻他不要付诸行动。《检查站》被《纽约时报书评》谴责为对自由主义的背叛，其他一些出版物则将其视为一个笑话——毕竟，小说中那个潜在的刺客根本没有可能实施他的计划。我认为，《Vox》和《检查站》都是实验小说中“小说即游戏”这一类型的大胆尝试。它们与那些题材相似的、迎合大众口味的言情小说和政治惊悚小说的区别在于，贝克拒绝将它们归入任何可识别的类型，也拒绝赋予它们商业化的外衣，例如悬念迭起的情节。读者并非被要求体验一段惊险刺激的旅程，而是与贝克一同思考电话性爱、政治和暗杀这些话题。他拒绝使用故弄玄虚的文学手法（如乔伊斯那样），以免将读者群引向歧途。贝克的文风始终简洁明了，有时甚至略显枯燥乏味——这正是作者有意为之，因为忠实于普通人的对话有时需要显得枯燥乏味，才能显得真实可信。贝克也从未像政治惊悚小说和言情小说那样，向读者表达自己对电话性爱和暗杀的看法——他只是呈现对话和观点，让读者自行思考。作者似乎置身事外，或者即便并非缺席，也保持着道德中立。

Baker's strong suit as a novelist is that he is intriguing. No one else's mind works quite like his, and he never seems in any way to make apologies for it or to try to be a different kind of writer. When we read his books, we are only in part reading them for themselves—that is, as individual narratives. What we are also reading for is just to find out what Nicholson Baker has been thinking about lately.

作为小说家，贝克的优势在于他引人入胜。他的思维方式独树一帜，而他似乎也从不为此感到抱歉，或者试图成为另一种类型的作家。我们阅读他的作品，一部分是为了欣赏作品本身——也就是作为独立的叙事故事。另一部分则是为了探寻尼克尔森·贝克近来都在思考些什么。

92. Garrison Keillor. WLT: A Radio Romance

92. 加里森·凯勒。《WLT：广播罗曼史》

(NEW YORK: VIKING, 1992), 401 PP.

（纽约：维京出版社，1992 年），401 页。

If Garrison Keillor were not a radio personality famous for his smooth, good-natured delivery and generally good-humored skits and anecdotes on A Prairie Home Companion, WLT might not have been such a surprise when it came out in 1992 . WLT is both dark and funny—it is as dark as it is funny—and lots of Keillor fans, used to the lighter, more rueful tone of his earlier collections of pieces, were put off by the novel. Nevertheless, it holds up very well thirteen years later. Keillor's vision is all of a piece, and his style is supple and provocative.

如果加里森·凯勒不是一位以流畅、和蔼的语调和在《草原之家》节目中轻松幽默的小品和轶事而闻名的电台主持人，那么《WLT》在1992年出版时或许不会让人感到如此意外。《WLT》既阴郁又滑稽——它阴郁的程度与滑稽的程度不相上下——许多习惯了凯勒早期作品集中轻松、略带忧伤的基调的读者，对这部小说感到难以接受。然而，十三年后的今天，它依然魅力不减。凯勒的视野浑然一体，他的文风流畅而富有启发性。

The novel begins in the 1920s with Ray and Roy, two brothers from Minneapolis who start a radio station in a small lunchroom and quickly discover that the eagerness of listeners to devote themselves to the radio is matched only by the eagerness of “personalities” and musicians to get on the air. WLT becomes popular and powerful—the signal can be heard throughout the American heartland, and Ray, Roy, and their sister Lottie (who sings old standards on a show of her own) get rich enough to indulge their eccentricities. Ray happens to be a ladies’ man, who samples the pleasures of most of his staff over the years but has a jaded view of both humanity and radio. Roy is a frustrated inventor who retires to the country and invents things such as “the radio chair”—an overstuffed prototype of “surround sound.” Lottie, who is wheelchair-bound, lives near the station and sings as “Lily Dale” for fifteen minutes a day, spending the rest of her time speaking well of others and trying to maintain a cheerful attitude. The other writers, singers, engineers, and actors who work for the station come and go over the years, putting out an always wholesome product (except for mistakes) but otherwise living by principles of self-interest, self-deception, and lust. Ray, who benefits the most from the hypocrisy of broadcasting (especially broadcasting to middle America) has the sourest view of it.

小说以20世纪20年代为开端，讲述了来自明尼阿波利斯的雷和罗伊两兄弟的故事。他们在一家小餐馆里创办了一家广播电台，很快便发现听众对广播的热情丝毫不亚于那些“名人”和音乐家们渴望上节目的热情。WLT电台迅速走红，信号覆盖了美国中西部地区。雷、罗伊和他们的妹妹洛蒂（她主持一个演唱老歌的节目）也因此变得富裕起来，足以满足他们各自的怪癖。雷是个风流成性的花花公子，多年来与他手下的大多数女员工都交往过，但他对人性和广播行业都抱有愤世嫉俗的看法。罗伊则是一位郁郁不得志的发明家，他退休后隐居乡下，发明了诸如“广播椅”之类的东西——那是一个填充过大的“环绕声”原型。洛蒂坐轮椅，住在电台附近，每天用“莉莉·戴尔”这个名字唱歌十五分钟，其余时间则用来赞美别人，努力保持乐观的态度。电台的其他作家、歌手、工程师和演员来来往往，多年来他们制作的节目总是健康向上（除了偶尔出错），但除此之外，他们都奉行着自私自利、自欺欺人和贪婪的原则。雷是广播行业（尤其是面向美国中部地区的广播）虚伪现象的最大受益者，他对这种现象的看法也最为愤慨。

About a third of the way into the novel, Keillor introduces Francis With, who turns out to be Keillor's real protagonist. Francis is a young boy living in a small town in North Dakota, whose father is killed in a railroad accident and whose mother thereupon falls into unredeemable despair. Francis changes his name to Frank White and finds occupation, love, and eventually success at WLT and then, as radio goes into decline, in television.

小说大约三分之一处，凯勒引入了弗朗西斯·怀特这个人物，而他才是凯勒真正的主人公。弗朗西斯是一个住在北达科他州小镇的男孩，他的父亲在一场铁路事故中丧生，母亲从此陷入了无法自拔的绝望。弗朗西斯改名为弗兰克·怀特，并在WLT电台找到了工作、爱情，最终获得了成功。后来，随着广播的衰落，他又转战电视行业。

Keillor's style is fast-paced and lively, full of jokes, set pieces, and anecdotes quickly and vividly sketched in. It takes a while for the main characters to come alive because the author's first task is to give a sense of the sociology of the radio station, which he does in an informal and colloquial style, very evocative of both the way midwesterners use language (full of colorful expressions) and the way they confide in one another and gossip about each other. The reader must infer the author's point of view and themes entirely from what the characters do and say.

凯勒的文风节奏明快、生动活泼，充满了笑话、场景和轶事，笔触简洁而鲜活。主要人物需要一些时间才能鲜活起来，因为作者的首要任务是展现电台的社会风貌，他以一种非正式且口语化的风格来描绘，生动地展现了中西部人使用语言的方式（充满了丰富多彩的表达），以及他们彼此倾诉和闲聊的方式。读者必须完全从人物的言行中推断出作者的观点和主题。

Most of the characters’ lives are marked by foolishness, mistaken choices, and tragedy. WLT is a collection of knaves and dupes who happen to be able to sing or act and who, in addition, often hate or envy one another. Original sin abounds, as with the child stars Little Marjery and Little Buddy, and the Shepherd Boys’ gospel quartet, and where sin doesn't obtain, sheer wretched luck does. The afflicted get more afflicted, and the unafflicted get pretty afflicted, too. Fans of the shows, who are full of admiration and affection for the characters, are shown to be gullible and easily manipulated, always ready to send in a dollar or a letter, unable to tell the difference between fiction and reality.

剧中大多数角色的生活都充斥着愚蠢、错误的抉择和悲剧。WLT 汇聚了一群只会唱歌或演戏的无赖和傻瓜，他们之间往往互相憎恨或嫉妒。原罪无处不在，比如童星小玛杰瑞和小巴迪，以及牧羊男孩福音四重唱；而即便没有罪孽，也难逃厄运。受苦的人更加痛苦，而那些原本无辜的人也难逃厄运。剧中的粉丝们对角色充满崇拜和喜爱，却又显得轻信易受摆布，总是乐于捐款或写信，根本分不清虚构与现实。

Keillor's style is the backbone of the novel. He constructs his story and his characters out of a mix of colorful expressions and conventional wisdom, often contrasting the cynical with the wholesome and thereby skewering the native hypocrisy of American conformism, midwestern variety. He doesn't always avoid mean-spiritedness by any stretch of the imagination. In some sections, as in those about Lottie and some of the other women, it is hard to tell what it is about them that is being satirized—that they are ugly or that they are silly.

凯勒的文风是这部小说的脊梁。他以生动的语言和陈规俗语交织构建故事和人物，常常将愤世嫉俗与纯真质朴进行对比，从而讽刺美国中西部地区根深蒂固的循规蹈矩的虚伪。他并非总是避免刻薄。在某些章节，例如描写洛蒂和其他一些女性的章节，很难分辨她究竟被讽刺的是什么——是丑陋还是愚蠢。

Satire, of course, is often a sour dish. Jokes depend on the teller of the joke and the listener sharing enough values and references so the double and triple implications of the words can be understood. The theory of life evident in WUT is that nature is bad and nurture is worse, and efforts to avoid this truth are at best forms of delusion and more likely forms of calculated corruption. Beyond that, the broadcast media, in particular, can't help but exaggerate and consolidate the inherent evils of human nature, disseminating them into every corner of modern life. The reader has to wonder: Is this what Keillor really meant? Did he mean it in general, or was he just going through a bad period?

当然，讽刺往往是一道苦涩的菜肴。笑话的魅力在于讲笑话的人和听笑话的人拥有足够的价值观和共同的背景知识，才能理解话语中蕴含的双重甚至三重含义。WUT（《世界末日》）中体现的人生观是：先天本性是邪恶的，后天教养更甚，任何试图逃避这一真理的努力充其量只是自欺欺人，更有可能是蓄意腐败。此外，广播媒体尤其热衷于夸大和强化人性的固有弊端，并将其传播到现代生活的方方面面。读者不禁要问：这真的是凯勒的本意吗？他是泛指，还是仅仅处于创作低谷期？

Dark satire is always problematic in the novel because the novel is so long and often the reader can't tolerate, or doesn't care to tolerate, such a sustained cynical tone. One of the difficulties with WUT , as with other satiric works, is that the author's integrity, as he presents his vision, doesn't allow for much variety, but the reader, who finds herself in the presence of the author for hours on end, yearns for variety and even relief. Wit works to a certain degree to carry the reader through the novel, and WUT is indeed exceptionally witty. It helps that Keillor's insights into hype, self-aggrandizement, and pomposity, not to mention capitalism, are uncomfortably astute. But an entertainment this is not—it is a polemic with an entertaining demeanor.

在小说中，黑色讽刺总是会带来问题，因为小说篇幅很长，读者往往无法忍受，或者根本不在乎这种持续不断的愤世嫉俗的语调。《WUT》和其他讽刺作品一样，难点之一在于作者在呈现其观点时所秉持的原则，使得作品缺乏变化，但读者却渴望多样性，甚至渴望得到一些喘息之机。机智在某种程度上能够引导读者读完这部小说，《WUT》的确妙趣横生。凯勒对炒作、自我吹嘘和自负，以及资本主义的洞察，都敏锐得令人不安，这无疑也为作品增色不少。但这并非一部娱乐作品——它是一部带有娱乐色彩的论战之作。

93. Kate Atkinson. Behind the Scenes at the Museum

93. 凯特·阿特金森。《博物馆幕后》

(NEW YORK: PICADOR USA, 1995), 333 PP.

（纽约：PICADOR 美国，1995 年），333 页。

On the second page of her novel, Kate Atkinson acknowledges her source of inspiration in the line “and the scratch-scratch of the Reverend Sterne's quill.” Indeed, the narrator begins the novel as Sterne begins his, with her conception, which coincides with the chiming of the hall clock (in Tristram Shandy , the source of all Tristram's troubles is his father's distraction when the clock chimes just at the moment when the “homunculus” is setting forth). Ruby's locale, like Tristram's and Sterne's, is Yorkshire and the city of York. One of Atkinson's themes is that York is not the same England, even in the twentieth century, as London and the South. And just as Sterne focuses on the male members of Tristram's family—Father and Uncle Toby—Atkinson focuses on the female members of her family: her mother, Bunty; her grandmother Nell; her great-grandmother Alice; and her sisters Gillian and Patricia.

在小说第二页，凯特·阿特金森以“还有斯特恩牧师的羽毛笔的沙沙声”这句开篇，承认了她的灵感来源。事实上，小说的叙述者与斯特恩一样，以她的受孕为开端，而这受孕恰好与大厅钟声的响起同时发生（在《项狄传》中，特里斯特拉姆所有麻烦的根源在于，当钟声在“小矮人”出发的那一刻响起时，他父亲的注意力被分散了）。露比的居住地，如同特里斯特拉姆和斯特恩的居住地一样，是约克郡的约克市。阿特金森的主题之一是，即使在二十世纪，约克也与伦敦和英格兰南部截然不同。正如斯特恩着重描写特里斯特拉姆家族中的男性成员——父亲和托比叔叔——一样，阿特金森则着重描写她家族中的女性成员：她的母亲邦蒂；她的祖母内尔；她的曾祖母爱丽丝；还有她的姐妹吉莉安和帕特里夏。

Theirs is not a happy family and has never been a happy family. Atkinson alternates Ruby's narrative of her childhood with chapters that jump around in time and show the larger background to the small incidents she remembers and that account for the inability of the family members to enjoy and value one another. Bunty is a cold and unaf-fectionate mother, much put upon but also unaccountably nervous about every little thing. Father George, it turns out, is habitually unfaithful, but in fact no one's affections work as they ought to, beginning with Alice, whose fate is a mystery to her children (they think she died in the night, but actually she ran off with an itinerant French photographer) and a family curse—Alice is quickly replaced by a wicked stepmother who actively abuses the children.

他们家并不幸福，也从未幸福过。阿特金森以露比的视角交替叙述她的童年，穿插着一些时间跳跃的章节，展现了她记忆中那些小事背后的更大背景，也解释了为什么这个家庭成员之间无法彼此欣赏和珍惜。邦蒂是个冷漠无情的母亲，她饱受折磨，却又莫名其妙地对每件小事都焦虑不安。父亲乔治原来是个惯于不忠的人，但事实上，家里每个人的感情都无法正常运转，这要从爱丽丝说起。爱丽丝的命运对孩子们来说是个谜（他们以为她夜里死了，但实际上她跟一个四处游荡的法国摄影师私奔了），而这似乎也成了家族的诅咒——爱丽丝很快就被一个恶毒的继母取代，这个继母经常虐待孩子们。

But Atkinson's exploration of the family's history and circumstances is not confined to domestic particulars. The history of the family is profoundly intertwined with twentieth-century British history. Each generation's youth coincides exactly with the onset of a world war, and the decisions each character makes about whom to love, whom to marry, what to do, and where to go are shaped and distorted by who lives, who dies, and who is injured in the wars. Atkinson has none of the sentimentality about the wars that other English writers show. She counts costs very carefully—dead soldiers, dead suitors, maimed bodies, and maimed hopes. She seems to be saying that the same English intransigence that won the war makes intimacy and simple familial attachment impossible, either because affections are repeatedly betrayed or because no one has the occasion to practice any form of relating besides resentment.

但阿特金森对这个家庭历史和境遇的探索并非局限于家庭琐事。这个家庭的历史与二十世纪的英国历史紧密交织。每一代人的青春都恰好与世界大战的爆发重合，每个人关于爱谁、嫁谁、做什么以及去哪里的决定，都受到战争中生死存亡的影响。阿特金森对战争没有其他英国作家所表现出的那种感伤情怀。她仔细地计算着战争的代价——阵亡的士兵、死去的追求者、残缺的躯体和破碎的希望。她似乎在说，正是英国人赢得战争的那种顽固不化，使得亲密关系和简单的家庭纽带变得不可能，要么是因为情感屡遭背叛，要么是因为除了怨恨之外，没有人有机会去实践任何其他形式的人际关系。

For Ruby, the first and strongest object of resentment is her sister Gillian, four years older. Ruby's resentment is a reciprocation of Gillian's intense sibling rivalry, which at first seems to have no larger implications. Ruby comes to be fond of the oldest sister, Patricia, who returns her affection, but Patricia is unnaturally self-contained, as if planning her escape from the family from her earliest moment of consciousness. And, indeed, one by one the sisters disappear, leaving only Ruby and Bunty and Ruby's increasingly avid excavation of the family history.

对露比来说，她最先也是最强烈的怨恨对象是比她大四岁的姐姐吉莉安。露比的怨恨是对吉莉安激烈的姐妹竞争的一种回应，起初这似乎并无深意。露比渐渐喜欢上了大姐帕特里夏，帕特里夏也对她有好感，但帕特里夏却异常内敛，仿佛从她记事起就计划着逃离这个家。果然，姐妹们一个接一个地消失了，最后只剩下露比和邦蒂，以及露比越来越热衷于挖掘家族历史。

Behind the Scenes at the Museum sounds depressing, but Atkinson's lively and idiosyncratic style and irreverent tone make the novel work brilliantly. Her take on family life and English history is deeply and consistently ironic. She banishes sentimentality from the novel—no being sentimental about absconding mothers or dying children or war heroes or a fire in a pet shop, no being sentimental about an uncongenial childhood, about not achieving one's heart's desire, or about the blows of history. Better to make a joke out of it all—to detach and observe—than to lament. In the end this is as much a characteristic of the English, and the English novel, as Atkinson's portrayal of coldness, intransigence, and resentment. But in her use of language, Atkinson plays exuberantly over her subject and illuminates it with profound wit and pleasure.
